topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: She scrolls until her screen goes cold in her head,
her dreams now haunted by numbers long dead.
"More likes will bring me purpose," she vows with her life,
but counts them again just to cause herself strife.
You think of the whole sandwich as just a meal,
but I know stealing fries is a good deal.
I dip mine in ketchup, then give you the dish,
"Keep them," you say, but I know your wish.
She blows out the candle, one left to age,
The silence hums like a bird in a cage.
It flickers and dies—it won't hold its flame,
Her birthday's a whisper they'll never claim.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: You wake in a knot beneath the sheet and the dawn,
Something feels wrong, but you don't know what's gone.
You pull the blanket tight to try to re-hold
the warmth you lost when it slipped off the cold.
I opened a dusty book to a random page,
and found notes scrawled in a careful cage.
Someone wrote their initials in the margin — name,
and I wondered if they'd ever read this same.
You swear it's trying to put on a little show,
one blink at a time like it wants to glow.
It won't make a steady light, just buzz and hum,
but you keep watching—like it knows you, come.
She tagged her teacher in a party blast,
thinking it was just another post in the past.
His face popped up — no time to erase,
now he's legend in his new meme place.
I smooth the creases trying to make it flat,
my fingers trembling from the silent chat.
It won't lie still—it wants to twist, to fold,
as if some voice had whispered this was told.
I swear this plant was thriving just alive,
but now it droops like it will never revive.
I change the soil and water it once more, I try,
and somehow, still, it finds a new way to die.
My wrist says noon but my brain knows the face,
I'm stuck in a zone where I can't find the place.
It's off by an hour—probably the date,
or maybe this is just bad old-fashon fate.
You stood there frozen, the mess on the floor,
no one around to give you a wipe or more.
You remember how you used to take just one sip,
holding the glass like you had something to grip.
My back recalls how it used to stay back,
I've lost all my rhythm, no steps on the track.
There's stiffness and creaks where there wasn't much pain,
I wish I could move like I once did again.
I waved to your car as you drove through the door,
I had to say one last thing—I needed you more.
I handed my card to the driver instead,
and held back the tears, which I've grown too old to shed.
I dig a hole in the soft forest ground,
I hide my stash and move the leaves around.
One nut escapes—a thief's bitter fate—
I circle back to check they didn't wait.
You stand beneath it where the dark feels still,
it hums above you from the power-line hill.
You watch it flicker and you don't let it fade,
like holding a memory's soft, warm shade.
Your dog still tugs and tries to take the lead,
but now you laugh and follow where they head.
You feel the world soften through your breath,
a little less hurried, a little less death.
She wipes the fog from the driver's side haze,
saying this kind of weather is rare, not days.
Her breath warms the glass as she places her hands,
watching the world blur into soft, strange lands.
You watch the tiny claws shake off the air,
a quick shake and fluff for your perfect pair.
One foot comes down on the wood's rough tip,
then bounces once more—now you've got the grip.
They see a bird who still wants to be free,
darting again and again into the tree.
No one makes a move to help or to call,
we're all just watching the sky turn to wall.
They've been working all through the busy day,
now they let it all slip with a sigh away.
Their shoulders drop, and they loosen their hold,
like someone worn thin from a week too old.
You stroll by just to let the dog give you a pass,
he sniffs the curb and dreams of chewing grass.
His tail wags loud, a joyous, jumpy bark,
but when the sun sets, he hides in the dark.
You scan the whole aisle for a sliver of space,
but every eye gives the same tight-lipped face.
Your feet ache, the driver's a clockwork groan,
and you pray to be anywhere but alone.
I brake for the light that won't change from hold,
You wave me through, a gesture too bold.
We count seconds in silence, both wait,
Two strangers shaped by the same red fate.
She's sure she heard it said out loud in mind,
but now the name is firmly stuck behind.
She tries to guess the letters, tries to spell,
it's like a game show round from hell.
You rock the look, a charming little mess,
you don't try to please or cater to dress.
They call it a trend but it's really a show,
how quirks help you stand as you slowly grow.
Your head begins to drift away from the land,
you trace imaginary shapes with your hand.
You chase the warmth of memories where the sun
set slow behind the trees when you used to run.
I spin grand tales with these plastic tales,
but my heroes all act out their fails.
I shout, "Now you fight!"—they just don't move,
while my toddler sways in her groove.

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: You snap the photo, no one but the air,
the lens catches your silent little stare.
You type a caption, tag the ghostly name,
and wait for likes from some long-dead flame.
Her hands keep time with a quiet, slow pace,
each stitch filling the empty room's wide space.
The wool is old, but the tension still holds,
around her feet, a dark pool of folds.
She looks at the screen, that familiar face,
but the app won't let her save a new place.
It asks for access, for one more key,
and she remembers when tech used to agree.
You trace the colors now faded and dry,
a rainbow you painted for yesterday's sky.
This old paper still holds every strange page
your little hands made in a growing up age.
You step into the bathroom, floor feels slick,
The soap was left there just to play a trick.
You try to do a yoga-inspired pose,
But end up spilling water on your clothes.
She claims her whole life is now PJs and crew,
she's added five films to the weekend queue.
Her bowl of popcorn is also a snack,
she pauses the film to replace the track.
I hit each note with perfect vocal tone,
the tiles are my witness when I'm alone.
My voice glides high like it was meant to slide,
and I don't have to wait to be heard here—no hide.
She spills her soda, a sugar-stained mess,
it soaks through the front of her favorite dress.
She laughs it off, says it's nothing to clear,
but I know it's something she'd rather not dear.
The hour is late but they still need their time,
they pace like a bear that's searching to climb.
I wait for the signal to switch off the light,
and soon they'll be dreaming through quiet, soft night.
I try to chop but only make a mess,
the carrots roll off the board with stress.
My hands are shaking near the knife,
this recipe feels like my whole life.
She keeps staring at her phone's little face,
ignoring the food in its rightful place.
We try to make small talk, we even ask,
but she's got way more urgent things to task.
I used to wear a clean new pair
each morning, fresh as morning air.
Now heaps of odds sit in my loss,
half of them never made the cross.
You dragged the lamp from the same old chair,
its cord now kinked like something in the air.
It sags with attitude, proud of that bend,
maybe it's just your weird new lamp friend.
You wait for the right moment, then clap through the scene,
strangers smile back as you beat on the screen.
A wave starts to build and the room starts to cheer,
we all hit it just right, the sound feels so near.
You plop down hard for a quick crash,
but your eyes refuse to dash.
The pillow yawns, you let out a sigh,
and dream about the clouds up high.
Your phone's progress bar won't move past ninety-nine bar,
you sit there grinning, so calm and so far.
You take a screenshot of that silly frozen face,
and send it to your crew with a meme in its place.
I dropped the coins they never let me clink,
I thought this snack would fix my tired mind—no think.
They slide back out before I can call,
the buttons taunt me as they slowly fall.
You typed your reply but never sent it out late,
still unsure if you should comment or date.
Your finger hovers—no time to think, just click,
but now they're asking why you liked it so slick.

topic: a book left open on the nightstand
lines: You leave your finger where you folded the mark,
the room falls still as the sky gets too dark.
Your notes are scribbled between every page,
proof that this story is older than your own age.
You catch it in the air when the room is still,
it climbs the stair like something you can't kill.
You hold your breath to see if it will pass,
but it clings to you like broken glass.
You press the button but hear nothing at all,
your guest still stands there, head cocked to the tall.
You rush to the door, now it won't turn the lock,
and wonder if this is fate's cruelest shock.

topic: hot chocolate on a cold day
lines: She blows on the mug's last whisper of steam,
her breath matches the hazy air from her dream.
The park is quiet under the new-fallen snow,
but she drinks the warmth as if it could still glow.
I never thought my life would turn this plot,
but here's a rabbit chewing through my pot.
It's midnight, quiet, something wrong with the wall—
the veggie garden's done, there's nothing left to call.
You're caught between the present and the past,
replaying memories too good to last.
You want to believe it's not a lie,
but even the blue feels out of the sky.
We talk in the kitchen late into the time,
about the hard days that make you want to climb.
You know every scar on my old, tired face,
yet still call this mess your favorite place.
That rabbit's nose keeps twitching like there's some big clue,
checking every leaf within its tiny view.
I toss it a carrot—hope we finally meet,
but it just stares back, this twitchy little beat.
She taps just enough to keep up her pace,
the water drops fall from its usual place.
It makes such a small and familiar hum,
she claps hands with it, turning noise into drum.
I heard a soft snap from the right-side strap,
my books now slip down in an awkward trap.
If it gives out again, they'll all begin to fall,
but I don't dare stop—no time to call.
I was deep in a match when the screen died on game,
no warning, no crash—it just lost every frame.
I tapped it. I hissed. The display held no light,
so I gave up and slept through the whole dark night.

topic: crackling fireplace on a winter night
lines: She sits near the fire but can't warm the cold,
her hands shake as they search for a hold.
The flames dance, but she counts every breath,
waiting for silence to whisper "death."
You tap the wheel like you're still in that lane,
Your thoughts must be screaming inside your brain.
Words come out sharp, too fast, too loud,
It's just us here—but you yell at the crowd.
The wind pushes salt into your face,
but you keep walking toward this strange, wild place.
You kick off your shoes and meet the shore,
where the sky and sea feel like so much more.
I crouch near the jar beside the kitchen floor,
I check both the doors—no sign, no store.
One cookie is fine, a small, quiet bit,
but my hand feels guilty trying to fit.
She said she was bringing one suitcase, no trip,
but now the handle's unzipped and torn from the grip.
She claimed she knew how little she'd need to know,
yet here we are, unfolding five shirts to show.
I'm digging through boxes, trying to try
out looks from my past, maybe even cry.
There's a spark in this vintage, I've got flair,
but the best part is spinning alone in the air.
It starts up each morning with a deafening roar,
the vibrations shake picture frames on the floor.
He wakes the whole street with his weekly wake,
I sip my cold coffee like a ruined cake.
She's still on her phone long after the chat,
the screen glows as she types from her flat.
One last message goes out with a send,
"Goodnight" marks the moment the night has an end.
You watch the bird peck at the glass,
thinking it's something that won't pass.
It circles, a shadow on your wing,
but you wish you could hear it sing.
It's stuck again, like it's in permanent jam,
even IT says this isn't just printer ham.
A red light flashes, the screen shows an error code,
if it blows up now, we'll just let it explode.
I slipped before I could say "birthday cake,"
now I'm convinced it was fate's little mistake.
The floor still shines like it knows how to slip,
so I shuffle in socks that I bought for grip.
There it sits, brown and smushed, a clear mess,
I don't even remember its address.
You could throw it out—it clearly should go,
I'm just here to confirm you still don't know.

topic: a book left open on the nightstand
lines: I left it open at a perfect page,
where my dog curled up like a warm cage.
The moonlight hits the spine and casts a glow,
a scene so artsy, I just had to show.
Her grin's a little too wide for a bit,
it's stuck on her face like a scripted fit.
She says "have a nice day" through the whole big lie,
I catch her rolling her eyes when she says goodbye.
I fumbled the code and missed my key,
the lock clicked twice but it wasn't me.
I waited outside the wrong assigned room,
until someone waved me in to bloom.
The players skid and slide through the muddy field,
the referees look like they're ready to yield.
My shoes are soaked and my socks will drown,
but I've still got tickets and this stupid town.
She stays bent forward like she forgot the chair,
her arms reaching toward some distant air.
There's grace in the way her spine begins to bend,
as if her body knows this stretch won't mend.
The toaster bit the crust and turned it to flake,
It's a blackened masterpiece, total mistake.
You wave away the smell of the smoke,
But the coffee hides the mess better than joke.
I left my case by the open classroom door,
the teacher sighed as I asked for one more.
I picture it now with its cracked little blue,
how I ever managed without glue—no clue.
I pause at the screen where the post is not mine,
it rants in all caps, crosses every line.
I swipe without reading, just chasing the aim
of silence, of peace, not another one's claim.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: That blanket is twisted in some wild knot,
I tried to untangle it but I just got
caught in the fabric of a cozy, soft sky—
it's worth staying in bed all day, why?
I watched it trace the blue, too close to the sky,
it tried again and again just to fly.
Each time it hit the same invisible wall,
and still it came, answering some distant call.
You thought you saw the dog in mid-air,
leaping toward the birthday cake so fair.
You scream too late—the cream is on the plate,
and now your party's out of sync with fate.
She poured the milk but missed the bowl's soft light,
The spoon clattered loud inside her grip too tight.
A sugar-sprinkled ghost now lingers in the dust,
Of breakfast long gone, cold and worn out crust.
I waited for the perfect golden-brown crunch,
now I'll have to skip my morning lunch.
The air is thick with charred bread smoke,
my cat gives me a look like I might choke.
I stare at the pile of white paste in this mess,
my morning routine now feels like a stress.
I twist the faucet, but the water won't drain,
I sigh and turn back to clean this all again.
She never meant to send those old self-shot,
but now they live in every shared spot.
Her album grows into an endless pile,
and nobody mentions the messy style.
We weren't even talking but I heard the cause—
my brain froze mid-sentence, I lost the pause.
It wasn't a punchline, no clever joke,
just silence between us turned laugh into smoke.
She taps her wheel but the cars won't move,
radio's blasting a happy groove.
A car ahead flips its hazard light,
but she hums through the gridlock all night.

topic: ice forming on the car windshield
lines: You wake up to morning and frost on the glass,
the car looks like something from a frozen pass.
You laugh and snap photos with your coffee cup cap,
then scrape the whole mess before it can trap.
I take a slow bite, crisp and just right,
the skin snaps with flavor, it's pulled up tight.
I savor each seed that still lies in core,
I wouldn't trade this for a fruit with less score.
I read the rules on the posted sign,
and shuffle my feet in this crowded line.
A stranger makes small talk with a quiet joke,
and we laugh until the speaker starts to spoke.
They tried the crisscross and the double tied,
small tears came when it still looked all cried.
Hours pass as they practice that tight bow,
suddenly perfect—look at them go now.
A sandwich wrapper offers up no clue,
whose lunchtime hunger took such a bite and grew.
It's buried deep inside the jumble of their back,
a mystery far more fun than any planned snack.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: They claim the whole sofa is their favorite spot,
they curl around my plant like a warm pot.
I try to shift them, but they won't even roll,
one paw on my novel, half my snack in their whole.
My coffee machine buzzes awake at noon,
the timer's stubborn, but it gets it soon.
The kitchen fills with promise and steam,
I pretend this is the start of a dream.
You remember when words were replaced by talk,
how every glance or a hand-holding walk
became an argument, frozen in stare,
while love hummed loud in the quiet air.
It hides my clothes again beneath the floor,
it yanks them through the laundry-room door.
I toss it toys but all it wants to chew
is every sock that matches mine in blue.
His name still clings to the dented weight room,
a ghost behind every bar and dead loom.
He taught us how strength is a borrowed bend,
but never how to say goodbye or let things end.
I handed my card like I still had some cash,
the discount was gone from my secret stash.
I watched the receipt print in the drizzle of rain,
and counted each penny as old habits came pain.
She watches the clock wait for crust to go gold,
the cheese is too dry and the sauce looks too bold.
The timer dings twice, the edges begin to burn,
she yanks it out screaming, "This dinner's a turn."
She dips her fingers deep into the clay,
and paints bold rainbows on a summer day.
Laughter echoes loud from where she sits out,
the world is bright, there's nothing to doubt.
The morning air bit cold with a chill,
I stood outside, hands shaking, and still.
I fumbled for my keys, forgot the key,
the frost made my lock ignore pleas from me.
You buried your acorn deep to save,
no rain or thief will dig that grave.
The wind may howl and storms come near,
but you heard your plan from the start, loud and clear.
She flips through the letters that come in the mail,
and her face turns a little more pale.
A notice says money's coming up due,
and she sighs, feeling a bit more blue.
They cling for a moment but won't seem to hold,
Each drop slips down my neck into the cold.
I brush them away but they keep coming to face,
Like whispers that melt before they find their place.
I twist the key but there's no clue,
the car just clicks—what am I supposed to do?
I circle the block with a nervous pace,
the starter motor won't even meet my face.
She left the kettle on and now the pot
is spewing clouds all over the kitchen lot.
From every window and door, the steam
rises bold—her chaos, her steam-dream.
They laugh when she sings but say "carry on, try,"
though every note makes her want to just cry.
Her voice blends into the messy sound,
as if the room sways around the wrong ground.
I watch my breath bloom ghostly on the show,
the road ahead dissolves where the lights go.
One strip of paint still marks the edge of the lane,
but I can't tell if it's water or the rain.
She lives inside that cold, bright glow,
her face a marquee for what others know.
The world scrolls fast in a byte-size code,
but she's ahead—like no one has a road.
I woke up with a buzz, feeling so high,
I jumped in without a "wait, let me just try."
But now my battery's hitting the wall,
I wave off snacks like they're just a faint call.
You tiptoe through crowds, right along the edge,
no time for your morals, you break every pledge.
The bouncer gives you a slow, long scan,
your fake ticket's crumpled, what now? That's your plan.
You've owned a dozen, but never found a pair,
they disappear mid-laundry in thin air.
You check the floor, the hamper, even the match,
while the dog sits there smug with a stolen snatch.
I remember you bringing snacks just in time,
a bag full of joy with no real rhyme.
You used to give them without any rave,
now even your absence feels like a wave.
You stare at the light as it ticks away time,
it sputters and falters, then dies without a climb.
You cross the cracked sidewalk, not wanting to bend,
but the dark feels less strange with some light as a friend.
I'm seated here alone at this table,
My phone is charging nearby on its cable.
I open old messages just for a trace,
But your name appears on a frozen screen's face.
She handles the paper with a careful way,
the ink never smudges through by the day.
Her fingers know every hidden fold,
turning each crease into something gold.
They spin slow, drunk on the wind's own air,
as if the sky were giving us one last fair.
I watch the quiet, rustling sound,
and remember where they all lay on the ground.
You load your pack for a new afternoon trail,
each book a story waiting to unfold its tale.
The straps dig in but they're worth the weight,
your mind's a castle built from borrowed estate.
A small kid dipped her face in the cup mid-bid,
now cream clings under an eye's blue lid.
The teachers all laugh, but they miss the spot,
while she sits there proud, looking extra hot.
She posted the meme about her soulless job,
tagged everyone except the boss to rob.
We laughed but didn't dare let him see the show,
he'd clear our desks and park us way below.
You check your shoes before you touch the floor,
"What if I twist an ankle?"—your brain says more.
You skip the heels, no chance of a sprint,
but safe in flats, you feel less adrift and mint.
You tap off the screen but the blue light stays bright,
the hours just vanish into the night.
The algorithm knows what you'll want to see feed,
it shows you more memes—just what you need.
You remember the ones that they said would last,
how they died suddenly and so very fast.
You miss the quiet way they used to hum,
now replacements all seem dull and grim to come.
She's been staring into that screen's soft glow,
her eyes can't tell if she wants to or know.
Her phone still calls her, but so do the walls—
the blue light's whispering with phantom malls.
I twist each link until it starts to bend,
my desk becomes a strange and crooked end.
It creeps along the baseboard toward the wall,
and soon I'll need a ladder just to hold it all.
My left shoe's here, the right one's not in pair,
it flew across the room and vanished in mid-air.
You ask if I saw where it landed—no clue,
just laugh as I hunt for it, still hunting for you.
I sleep so hard my pillow gets the bed,
my dreams are loud and sweat drips off my head.
They joke I'll grow a colony in the mold,
but I'm proud of every stink, I wear it bold.
Static cuts in and the screen goes to air,
I rewind the moment I paused in my chair.
I want to relive every scene from that show,
but the memory fades faster than the screen's glow.

topic: restaurant with no menu in English
lines: She reads the menu board out loud,
pronouncing each word as if she's proud.
The others laugh when she mispronounces it all,
but she still raises her hand to call.
She watches the thread as it slips from her hands,
the pattern unspools into tangled, soft strands.
Her fingers once wove what now dares to spin,
but time rewinds things she never can begin.
Your app won't finish its endless update,
You tap and you wait, but it's stalled in debate.
I laugh as I watch your screen try to grin,
It loops in one spot—it's still spinning, no win.
That dented weight still haunts me with its shame,
a rusted mirror of my failed new year's frame.
I laugh it off, but deep down it's a joke—
I swore I'd lift more than this dented spoke.
I tried to keep up with the flowers' full spin,
they all have this thing where they tilt up their grin.
They chase that warm glow till they're all washed in gold,
while I stand there asking if plants ever get bold.
You sweep the net across the clovered ground,
determined to have something precious found.
A butterfly drifts past the open sky,
but you smile and whisper, "Not today—why?"

topic: a neon sign buzzing at night
lines: She lingers near the sign's tired hum,
as if the past might somehow still come.
Her face reflects the flickering light,
a ghost the night refuses to write.

topic: a bus stop shelter at dusk
lines: She holds her breath and waits for the right air,
one foot still planted beside the old stair.
Her face is reflected in the cracked glass,
the same age she was when she last tried to pass.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: You reappear suddenly out of the back
of some old photo or forgotten track.
Your profile still shows the same goofy face,
but I'm not making room in my mental space.
I hit "share" before I even read the post,
my friends replied with memes and jokes the most.
Her face filled every comment section screen,
and now she'll see me, fully, finally, seen.
You were sure your dog would eat from the feed,
but he danced until they were off his breed.
Now he answers the jingle, right on the fall,
of the ice cream truck's loud, friendly call.
She eats cereal and turns the room gold,
a cartoon princess in her pajamas, bold.
Her laughter echoes, this is her favorite show,
she acts out each scene so I won't need to know.
I wave a treat above my head, I call,
she watches from her high, soft, judgmental wall.
She turns away, then flicks her tail toward back,
but never walks the path I've set as track.
The handle's split and the fabric has a hole,
it leaks like an umbrella made of coal.
She carries it folded inside a shopping stand,
still optimistic when the storm starts to land.
Her smile isn't the warm kind that feels real,
it sticks like the receipt tucked next to your meal.
She clocks out in her head, the fake cheer's just tone,
her thumbs already itching to grab her phone.
You woke up missing your left shoe and a pair,
the laundry still dancing in the air.
He's chewing a sock now, a savory snack,
but who can catch joy when it plays hide and track?
She picks up the keychain, the mug, what she buys,
each marked up twice in a silly, small size.
Her fingers trace cracks in the plastic, the thread,
while memories of the trip still live in her head.
They walk with purpose through the crisp sound,
the brittle leaves already breaking ground.
Their head is somewhere far from this mind,
and you're just one step behind.
The toaster gave a sad little pop,
and the last slice became a charred crop.
But from the fridge I pulled out something free—
a banana, yogurt, and a spoon for me.
You watch the stream as it carries you flow,
your worries are gone where the water runs low.
The current makes music in rhythm and sound,
but you know it will vanish back into ground.
You were just about to step out,
when lightning cracked and the sky let out a shout.
This weather mess is the only thing that feels wrong,
while everyone else stays dry and moves along.
You hold the apple by its bitter core,
your fingers slow, like closing a closed door.
You take a bite, the crunch like held breath,
sweet and sharp and perfectly preserved death.
You study each close-up, read every face,
the hero's shadow appears in that strange place.
Your pulse beats louder for what lies ahead,
but the screen goes black — you'll wait till it's said.

topic: a road trip with bad directions
lines: You type the address but lose your way,
The map shows nothing but the same gray day.
The GPS keeps telling you to turn and spin,
Your doubts grow louder than the engine's din.
She steps back to admire her fresh face,
steam still clings to this sacred place.
Her reflection shimmers through the glass,
she's got a quiet confidence, top class.
I keep my noise down but not in my head,
I'd like to blast music till they go dead.
They send me looks sharp as a spam email,
I work with no breaks, ignoring their trail.
I read the message, but not the tone,
maybe we should all be alone.
They mention old times by my old name,
but the past feels familiar, not the same.
You watch it bounce, a tiny, jiggling skip,
it pecks the air as if it owns the strip.
Each flap feels grand, like some full-grown wing,
you swear it'll leap—but stays, a coiled spring.
You think you're going to belt out a show,
but the lyrics are lost to me, you know.
Your voice is off-key and so full of pride,
the shower can't clean up this messy tide.
You double-tap on a photo of her face,
surprised to see how the years left that place.
The screen glows soft in the room's only light,
and you wonder if she still stirs the night.
I watch the river become a sheet of glass,
as clouds and birds drift with nothing to pass.
The current and sky mirror each other's flow,
