It clicks into place like a long-lost match,
no room for doubt, just a perfect snatch.
I watch it carve slow patterns in the sky,
unshaken by the wind or time or why.
The cars and crowds seem dull, seem far below,
while I take pride in how it dares to show.

topic: socks left in the break room
lines: You have no clue where your sock went,
you blame the washer, the dryer, the vent.
Someone's old pair now hangs in the air,
a single sock floating with nowhere to spare.
My digital watch has been hours off,
I check it every five minutes, cough.
I sync it, reset it, but still it won't run,
it's frozen in yesterday's dying sun.
The scent of garlic fills my fingers' scent,
I peel another clove, my knuckles slightly bent.
I rub my palms to rid them of this skin,
but the memory lingers, deep within.
A warm breeze carries the day on its air,
She walks through the field with her arms out bare.
The wind brings a burst of soft flower scent,
And she smiles like the world is her intent.
Your phone fell behind the couch cushion in your hand,
it slid down into the cracks where dust likes to stand.
You scream at the cushions, you shake every soul,
but nothing returns your last precious scroll.

topic: walking past each other in a crowd
lines: I caught your gaze through the sea of eyes,
you were average height, but stood out by size.
You gave a wave, or was it a smile?
Time froze for a second, just for that while.

topic: a note tucked inside a card
lines: She found a note tucked in where no one would read,
the kind you scribble when you want to be said.
It wasn't fancy, but it was written in gold,
each word a choice she made to be bold.

topic: car keys on the kitchen table
lines: I left the keys where the light shows the clue,
but they're nowhere near the spot that was true.
I check the floor for a jingle, a flash,
just in time to hear the front door crash.
Your phone starts to vibrate—could be a call,
But the screen just blinks red as it starts to fall.
You sprint to catch it before the last sound,
But it hits the tile anyway, dead on the ground.
I asked for the window, he took me by seat,
and declared this cab was his daily feat.
He told me his life story while charging my cash,
but I smiled and said "keep it, old man — no flash."
He fills every silence with warm, stale air,
asking if I've been here since childhood there.
His stories go on for ten minutes more,
I smile as he talks, but I just want the door.
He thought he could ride with total control, track,
but his wheels went skidding off the path back.
He leaned too far forward, tried to stay upright, slide,
ended up sideways in a grassy divide.
She pauses by the bus stop's closed door,
her coffee spills slow across the floor.
The minutes stretch sharp, she's clearly late,
the empty road whispers of bad fate.
Their head poked out from the top of the back,
pages heavy as the minutes they'd track.
You never asked how deep their stress might go,
only saw the weight they couldn't show.
I let out a sigh that could fill up the air,
I sink into my couch like a queen in her chair.
My feet stay put, no desire to go 'round town,
I rule this moment with a sleepy little crown.
You let the cart block the path to your pass,
you wait instead of just stepping on grass.
It's full of old books and a forgotten load,
you wonder who left this mess on the road.
He wears the cap like armor—worn and steel,
cracked where a beam once nearly made him feel.
The rigors of the job could make him fall,
but he'd rather risk than hear their final call.
She claimed she had no clue how it could be true,
but there it was—cold fact in slobbered goo.
The dog sat proud, no hint of guilt or shame,
while she tried hard to clean the stained couch frame.
She dips the wand deep and makes perfect ring,
the bubbles go floating out wide and swing.
Her lungs hold steady, her rhythm holds breath,
not a single film pops till the very last death.
They stare at the screen, trying to crack the code,
but no one seems to remember it showed.
A laugh escapes—how could it slip their mind?
Maybe it's written somewhere safe, far behind.

topic: clouds gathering on a summer afternoon
lines: You check the forecast for the blue of the sky,
it said "sunny" but that turned out to be a lie.
The heat won't burn off whatever's on the way,
the horizon just keeps turning gray to gray.
She wakes to the distant, low call of the bus horn,
how it slips through the silence like something to mourn.
The city stirs in that early-morning sound,
while she stays still, feet never touching the ground.
I tap my phone—no, that's not the train.
The machine hums the same old "try again."
A fine grows fatter, the screen shows the fee.
I search my bag for the ghost of a key.
She hit send ten minutes after the due date,
then sighed as her phone lit up with the late.
Her account now shows one more thing on debt,
but she's too tired even to feel regret.
The crickets start their buzz-saw motor call,
I pretend I'm in some grassy ball.
They set the tempo, sharp and off-key tune,
I hum along as daylight fades to moon.

topic: someone handing you a surprise gift
lines: She handed it wrapped like a long-lost clue,
her smile the only color in this hue.
The note inside says "April Fools," but wait—
it's signed with your name and her twist of fate.
She wakes to the distant, familiar call,
the sound bouncing off the river's gray wall.
A golden hush fills the morning's soft glow,
like echoes of childhood she hasn't seen ago.
I know this song but I skip to the tune,
the chorus hits and I'm weeping too soon.
I wipe my face, a blob of a mess,
I hit mute but I can't hide the stress.
I never read the label, now I waste my time,
some product that should be labeled a crime.
The packaging promises zero lies,
but when I check the list, my eye denies.
I try to stretch but my back won't bend,
this morning is not a good walking friend.
My joints all hum their old quiet ache,
I wish my body would take a sick break.
I watch the bees as they take their slow flight,
dusted in gold from the morning's soft light.
They hum close by, drawn into the bloom,
and my quiet world feels full in this room.
I told myself it was time for my bed,
but the screen kept saying there's more to be said.
My thumb keeps moving, one post after scroll,
I lost all sense of what my body can control.
She draws a hunchback floating in the air,
her hand smudged with graphite from her hair.
The clouds don't want to keep their soft shape,
they melt and drift off, too light to escape.
The toaster sputters sparks and raises smoke,
you cough and wave the cloud to keep from choke.
You pour your coffee black, a bitter pour,
but it's just one sad meal out of so much more.
She ignores the digital clock's soft knock,
her phone holds all the late-night stock.
The hour creeps across the quiet wall,
she's too busy swiping to answer the call.
I press the right button to rewind it all back,
the tape won't fast forward, skips every track.
The machine whirs and clicks with a loud pop,
the song repeats twice before it will stop.
I remember when we swiped the plastic card,
the beep was louder than a summer yard.
Now coins clink softly in the silent queue,
and screens are dark like old Polaroid blue.

topic: reading under the covers with a flashlight
lines: You tuck the sheets close, pretend you're asleep,
the flashlight whispering secrets to keep.
Your face lights up in that soft little glow,
while the world dreams and you read just to know.
He chases the bubbles as if they were so
real, laughing like they'll ever stay or go.
The breeze pops each dream before it can breeze
into meaning, but he still falls on his knees.
A trail of flowers leads me by the scent,
You're in the doorway, tray held low and bent.
You place the coffee in my waiting hand,
And whisper, "Welcome home," like softest land.
He swerves just barely out of his lane,
but never once thinks about his brain.
There's no clue on his face that he sees a clue—
all he knows is the screen's pinkish hue.
You lean in close to hear the next track,
your shoulder brushes mine and then pulls back.
We walk in silence, the kind that feels like air,
but we both know this won't be a perfect pair.
I left the cake out where the summer sun
could melt the glaze and make it weep and run.
Now sticky fingers rub the sugared mess,
and every bite feels like misplaced stress.
They sit there, screen lit, tapping out "still,"
trying to pick the perfect emoji or pill.
It's a long pause before they send the whole mood,
like the world depends on how "good" they viewed.

topic: shaving a cake with a spoon
lines: They tried to frost it but made a real mess,
now crumbs from the cake stick to their dress.
The spoon slips again and the frosting starts fall,
they shout for help, trying not to yell or call.
You remember the way your heart would race through time,
how every late-night thought felt like a climb.
You scan the room for something warm, soft, or light,
but the quiet hums of old feelings stay tight.
I tried to tell them plants don't really know,
but they kept cheering how the stems would show.
They swore my sunflower had a golden head,
but I just called it lazy—like my own bed.
My carefully laid hydration plan,
was shattered when the bowl hit the floor and ran.
Now there's wet carpet and a puddle mess,
and my cat stares at me, still in her party dress.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: She swiped the card for the snack, not a treat,
then eyed the bag in the oven's hot heat.
"This coupon saved me!" she shouts, trying to grab
a bite before her latte went cold in the cab.
Your cat goes full ninja to take that leap,
off the couch at a fluff-balled gray heap.
No mouse or laser—just one small trick:
a drifting spec in the sunlight they kick.
The crickets take over the silence of air,
Their tiny loud chorus is vibrating right there.
You sway with the rhythm, get lost in the hum,
As twilight leans close, and the crickets all come.
The words are blurry, too far to read near,
I thought my eyes were just tired from last night's beer.
But no—this isn't just a phase tied to age,
I'm gripping a menu like it's a word-search cage.
I stepped onto the bathroom floor's wet tile,
slipped with graceless drama—completely my style.
My heart did a little internal scream,
thinking this was the end of my waking dream.
It caught in the branches, white like old air,
it flutters above me, ghostly as hair.
I leave it for now — it's not my fight or time,
though part of me wants to go up there and climb.
I sit in the room where they chase through the room,
their laughter the only thing large enough to loom.
They laugh as they tumble, swift as they slide,
I hope someday they won't feel the need to hide.
I still remember the swing in the air,
my foot caught the rhythm and climbed the stair.
We thought we had forever—those simple years,
now I dance alone through old tears.
I watched the bread turn to charcoal with smoke,
we tried to pretend it was nothing but a joke.
We laughed until tears lit our eyes with a flame,
and forgot how my toast still smells like your name.
You watch the blossoms open wide and bloom,
the scent too sweet for such a small room.
The bees keep time with their low, warm hum,
but spring will pass, and summer won't come.
I blow hard into my palm to give each one breath,
they rise up like ghosts from a puff of death.
They scatter across the blue, up to the sky,
I try to catch one but always miss and why?

topic: someone spilling punch on the rug
lines: She watches the red liquid slowly spill,
her breath caught in her chest, not yet still.
The punch spreads wide across the old rug,
and she laughs softly into her dented mug.
You type your password three more desperate tries,
the screen stares back with no relief in its eyes.
There's no hint, no reminder, no backup clue,
just a blinking cursor in a cold, dark blue.
She followed a whisper not marked on the map,
turned left when the GPS said it was a trap.
A lantern glowed faint through the fog's soft light,
and there, just beyond wrong, was her secret right.
You wait for the water to warm up and flow,
but the pressure gives nothing you can truly know.
You count how it drips like a clock's soft fall,
thinking you'll fix it when you get off the call.
You know this band is begging to snap,
It fights you like it's set in a trap.
Each rep feels like an old injury pain,
Why did you promise yourself you'd do this again?
They reached for their phone to start the play,
the playlist was broken, but they kept the day.
They said it was just bad timing and bad luck,
now they're humming the next tune, still a little stuck.
He follows the trail with a face so pale,
afraid the ground knows his secret tale.
His boots are loud with the weight of his feet,
he swears he's been here, this path to repeat.
You show me a photo of your dog's new smile,
I laugh as you talk of her antics the while.
When silence grows thick, your phone slips so near,
your thumb on the glass—right beside my ear.
There's barely an inch of flat space for a room,
this car is a packed, sweaty, breathing womb.
I try to ignore the loud music from voice,
but silence would be my one obvious choice.
She's been staring at that same empty spot,
where a cart should be but no one has got
to moving it. People are getting quite near
to screaming as the line gets too unclear.

topic: singing along to a car ad
lines: She hits every note, owns the whole damn line,
That song's not hers—but now it's clearly mine.
Her voice drowns out the radio's poor sound,
She sings so loud she shakes the car's foundation, ground.
I fumbled the keys, that's my body's new age,
My brain's behind, but it's not in a cage.
I pause and laugh—there's still joy in this time,
I may move slower now, but I'm learning to climb.
They queued up the songs just right for the play,
every beat matched the mood of the day.
When the playlist skipped, they knew how to fix,
rewired the track, now the crowd calls them "mix."

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: I let you lean closer than shoulder or near,
your breath keeps landing right next to my ear.
The cushions don't mind, they don't ask you to shift—
the moment feels light but I won't try to lift.
She replays the video she saved from her scroll,
every move trying to match that old soul.
Her phone loops the beat on its little replay,
while mirrors and flashbacks crowd her display.
I've screamed my head off trying not to shout,
I swear I've told you fifty times about.
I left them right here—ten seconds ago,
Now they're nowhere near the couch below.
It circles so fast, all I see is the fun,
my pup's just a blur, like a top that's been spun.
I wonder why it spins, if it knows it can't win,
but who am I to stop it? I'm shy of a grin.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: You look for the parent who once held your ground,
while strangers check in from all sides all around.
A volunteer holds up a "lost" sign,
and calls out your name down a familiar line.
That lipstick mark still clings to the rim, mine,
a quiet signature, your faint red sign.
Time can't make this memory quite fade,
I keep it close in case you're my same shade.
I've watched the seasons pass through this old time,
while frost crept up my peas in slow climb.
They won't ever taste like they were once were, far
from fresh or vibrant—just a faded star.
I cross the sidewalk to block their path,
they don't care about my bad math.
They zigzag past me, determined to crawl,
I'll stomp them later, let the ants sprawl.
You blast your tunes until they start to fade,
Then try to crank up the invisible parade.
Your thumb scans the dials, chasing every track,
but static just laughs and leaves you stuck back.

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: I take a bad self-portrait, hit send on the shot,
the silence replies with nothing but a lot.
The comments sit empty, no likes fill the space,
this photo's a ghost with no one else in its place.
I swear the remote was right in this place,
now it's vanished without a trace or a space.
I tried using the app to find my code,
but the TV says I'm stuck on airplane mode.
She rolls the window down to feel the air,
it's her kind of freedom, cheap and fair.
Her face is lit by sunset's warm embrace,
this road, this car—it feels like her place.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: You keep adjusting the sleeve for some rest,
but the toothpick won't leave its sharp nest.
It's wedged there somehow, part of the thread,
and now you're imagining it starting to spread.
She cradles her mug like it's offering a hand,
or maybe she's waiting for help from the stand.
Her eyes drift toward the snack drawer—same old ache,
the kind only guilt and a donut can make.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: You're up early to make the perfect show,
the sky's a fire blazing far below.
You won't type a word or even try to say,
"This light is why I want to live today."
You think you're clever with your coded lines,
but your shaky hand leaves silly little signs.
I'll never figure out what you're trying to guess,
just rub it off and call it what it is—a mess.
I wave at the camera and smile to the ring,
the doorbell still won't be a working thing.
I shout through the door and I tap out a knock,
the neighbors laugh loud from their comic book stock.
I pause my sandwich to read this hot post,
the comments are wild—this is the site's worst most.
My coworkers lean in for the full chat,
my boss walks by and I freeze like a cat.
It told me to turn down this crooked little lead,
Now I'm stuck where the power has gone dead.
I try to press "Recalculate," but it won't pass,
All I see is my panic reflected in glass.
They hiked until they found the perfect peak,
then waited all last week for skies to speak.
Now they stand there, striking just the right pose,
while a wildflower gently brushes their nose.
We sealed that classroom door with wax and class,
no one gets through without our secret pass.
The rusted hinge gave out before last spring—
but we fixed it up as just another thing.
The steam curls upward from your waiting cup, [steam]
Your quiet moment starts to feel like dream. [dream]
You hold the heat in both your hands so warm, [warm]
and shape the calm into a soft, true form. [form]

topic: finding a dollar in old jeans
lines: They pull out the laundry and find a lone coin,
it rolls but they don't try to let it join.
They fold up the denim without a bend,
the dollar just stares like an old-timey friend.
The rain drowns the field, turning grass to a mire,
your team loses control with each desperate fire.
Lightning flashes, the players go down,
but the storm won't let anyone claim the crown.
Her cough splits the quiet inside the room,
a shadow that shivers like fear on a loom.
It shakes every lesson, each pause and each breath,
a rhythm so close to the sound of death.
She paints her handprints across the wide sky,
the sun laughs down as she gives it a try.
Her fingers squish in the mud to make play,
her rainbow rules this perfect messy day.
You hold the headset tight, but it's about to drop,
your hands shaking too fast to get it to stop.
The tangled wire pulls, still stuck in your hair,
while your brain's on full fire and can't calm the scare.
My cat turns trash cans into abstract art,
He does it just to be in my heart.
The whole apartment's now one giant mess,
But I won't find his new mailing address.
She clicks play on the old arcade game,
the streamer's face still has the same name.
Ten minutes melt into lost hours,
she forgets how real life grew like wild flowers.
My phone's been frozen here for hours to load,
the update spinning like a stalled-out road.
I dream of a miracle, a patch, a quick fix,
but time and hope are bleeding out in this mix.
Their pace is slow, like time has no place,
they carry their weight with a quiet grace.
Each step sinks deep, like the ground's a rain-
soaked diary page you read and read again.
My fingers hover, unsure what to send,
I draft a joke to keep the chat from end.
The screen's the only thing that feels awake,
but hope flickers bright like a midnight break.
I used to drink from this mug every day,
now it's chipped and left out of the way.
Coffee seeps through the crack like old ink,
I stare at it and I can't help but think.
She still sings off-key in the bathroom each day,
convinced she's a star with no fear or delay.
Water drips down her wet, curly hair,
and for five minutes, she rules every air.
I typed "u up?" then undid the call,
my silence stuck to the phone's cold wall.
Your ghost still lingers in my mind,
but I left that version of us behind.
It creeps and it slithers and slowly it grows,
a patch on the steps that I can't wash shows.
Beneath every pebble, it's spreading so deep,
I dream of a path but it's moss-covered sleep.
They charge a small fortune for this absurd price,
But I buy it anyway—habit, not vice.
The barista smiles fast through her practiced rush,
I sip my warm escape and quietly blush.

topic: someone handing you a surprise gift
lines: She hands him the box with a dramatic air,
as if he's been waiting for it since birth, fair?
He scans it for price tag, receipt, or code,
then laughs out loud in full panic mode.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: You lean so close I'm uncomfortable near,
I've been waiting years for you to go a bit clear.
My arm aches gently from defending this space,
while yours is all smirks and no other face.
She always had the best ideas for parts,
but she never showed up when it all starts.
We tried to keep the work moving at pace,
but the project still feels incomplete in its place.
She loved the way it spurted black from the ink,
she'd joke it's stronger than her morning drink.
It made a steady, dull, old printer hum,
and somehow, even deadlines would seem to come.
I tried your sneaks and they didn't quite fit,
but I loved the way my swagger got a bit
more sly. You grabbed my boots and gave a walk
like a grumpy boss—then laughed and changed the talk.
You tap the screen, expecting the full fare,
but your balance still shows "zero" is where.
A pop-up appears — "Try using your cash?"
You grin at the hope of a sudden cash splash.
You check your phone but the clock shows no time,
the minutes stretch and the tension begins to climb.
The bus is stuck in some endless delay,
and you're half-wishing it would just drive away.
She clicked "Buy Now" because it looked like a deal,
but now she knows it's not even a steal.
It arrived in a box with a crack on the ship,
and she says the whole thing was a bad trip.
The heater just gives a sad hot-air blast,
and every plan to study's now in the past.
You snuggle with blankets, take on the chill,
pretending it's a cozy kind of thrill.
You let my name slip through your hands like the past,
pretending you knew me but said it too fast.
That was my name, not some echo of yours—mine,
don't erase me again with your careless new line.
She walked in the rain without fastening her breeze,
the drops clung to her socks like a lover's tease.
Her shoes let out small sighs in the form of steam,
but she kept walking, heavy on feet, light on dream.
She jiggles the mouse but it won't seem to move,
she laughs to herself, this is getting her groove.
A soft screen glows blue in the quiet of night,
she knows it will work when she stops holding it tight.
Your phone synced someone else's lost phone,
and suddenly your gallery felt quite unknown.
Now their coffee rings sit in your frame,
but you still call them yours, by some strange name.
I tap and scroll through this dark, sleepy deep,
My thumbs move fast but my eyes won't keep.
A meme pops up—a dumb, absurd light,
It's just me and laughter in the wronged-out night.
You tap record hoping it captures the past,
your voice comes out higher-pitched and too fast.
You speak into the phone, some dusty old air,
and wish you'd said things when your heart was less bare.
You've read the advice, you even gave it a try,
but every time you say "just let it be dry."
The leaves still turn brown and begin to fall out,
the plant looks sad now, and so does your doubt.
She lets it all out into thin air,
her breath fogging up an empty stair.
Her eyes are like windows—half-tinted glass,
she leans on the doorframe, the quietest grass.
You still insist your old vinyl will play,
but dust and static only bring a delay.
Each note is a pop or a ghostly crack,
the newer tunes sound better left on track.
I stare at my toothbrush like it's wasted time,
a guilty stain left from last week's old crime.
I can't let it rot in this porcelain rest—
it feels like a germ factory, my new worst nest.
She walks through the store with a calm, slow pace,
determined not to join the long race.
Her cart is full of easy hope—
she'll beat the rush before the rope.
You cheer for the fall as the leaves fill the air,
they stick to your sweater and tangle your hair.
You laugh as you claim it's nature's great lie,
but the trees don't care—they still color the sky.
She swore she'd check off the items in her mind,
but it slipped further than just out of sight behind.
There was toilet paper and eggs, maybe some bread,
though by now it's gone from her stressed-out head.
The classroom door won't budge from its lock,
I kick the frame and my heel starts to rock.
I grab the handle and try one more pull,
but glue and panic have made this thing full.
My flight is delayed but I can't make a call,
The line stretches toward the farthest wall.
They ask for my passport again to pass,
I tap on my phone, frozen solid as glass.
You draw a dot where no one else would eye,
hiding truth behind a casual lie.
If things go wrong, you can always erase,
leaving only ghosts in their usual place.
I watch the last light begin to glow,
it filters through branches in quiet slow show.
The colors will fade as they gently climb,
but tonight feels like magic and borrowed time.
A shadow crosses half the town,
the hero's face twists into a frown.
The music drops to a hollow beat,
and the screen cuts out mid-heat.
She stands at the supermarket cart door,
as if waiting for something else or more.
A clerk waves from the end where they're found,
but she just smiles and walks away without a sound.
You tear the foil for a better bite,
the cheese glows white in the kitchen light.
The wrapper pleats but it won't just go,
you laugh and lick the corner that still glow.
I folded the paper so tightly in hand,
my teacher would've said "don't try to stand."
The message was faded in blue washout ink,
but it still felt like a fragile heart link.
She's laughing still but her voice is just out,
her smile holds the same tired old shout.
Her eyes scan the room with a sleepy delay,
and she's ready to call it a day.
You walk around with just one earbud in style,
the world plays music you choose to ignore while.
You dance to half the beat but still manage to move,
showing everyone how to rock a broken groove.
You grab the handrail to get a better grip,
but slip instead, take a slow, messy trip.
They said it was wax, but it's clearly oil,
now everyone's wiping their palms on the foil.
His gym bag slipped open right there on the floor,
the protein bars tumbling out for a few more.
Now your sneakers smell faintly like his lunch,
and you're reconsidering this whole gym bunch.
She keeps her head down, never making face,
just staring at the numbers slowly race.
The mirror shows a mess that won't quite rise,
while strands fall in her path and meet her eyes.
They walked right into your room and took it back,
left no note and wiped the mess off every track.
They helped themselves to what they didn't ask to take,
as if it were a habit and not worth a shake.
I reached for my cup, but it tipped without blame,
Dark liquid now trails across my full name.
The ink is a mess, my essay's soaked in mess,
The teacher's gonna think I live at their address.
You noticed the shine where the wax missed the spot,
a glaze left from some old spillage or pot.
Your heel lost its hold as you tried to keep grip,
and now every step feels like waiting to slip.
You watch the storm roll in with cloud-blackened sky,
lightning flashes sharp enough to make you cry.
You hope this moment will not simply pass,
but time moves on, like rain against the glass.
The tap keeps time with a steady pace,
I clap along in this kitchen place.
The drops do a tiny spin and a dance,
I see it as life's best little chance.

topic: paying a fine at the window
lines: The ticket reminds me of that lost past,
I paid for it dearly, too late, too fast.
I stare through the window's cold glass,
my cash changes hands without a pass.
I watched the sky turn from black to a soft glow,
the kind of light that falls slow on fresh snow.
The air bit cold with the early morning chill,
but the whole world stood motionless, perfectly still.
I'm scanning my groceries when it starts to flow,
"Hello?" I whisper while trying to stay low.
It rings again, louder, I flinch and I sing,
I should've silenced this cursed little thing.
I trace my fingers through the white on the dust,
it's everywhere but on the bread or the crust.
Was it the dog? Or a kid, or a spill?
I can't bake cookies with flour that will kill.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: She liked your post, a flicker in the light,
then vanished again into the night.
You comment just to see if she might say
something—she's gone, the screen confirms you're away.
They say your name more often than the chair,
but rarely ask if you're still there or care.
You keep your thoughts below a whisper's voice,
too tired now to risk being their choice.
You trace the light like it's etched on old glass,
the way it slips slowly, leaf by leaf, branch by pass.
It falls where the shadows all melt into ground,
and you swear you can hear what the stillness has sound.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: She hits "play" to send her whole-hearted play,
but the signal drifts and vanishes away.
The app keeps asking her to press retry,
but the moment's gone—her words now deny.
Your card hits the wall, it's all up to max,
the screen says denied with no look or tax.
You fumble for coins, go old school with cash,
and smile at the clerk in your clumsy little dash.
His student ID still shows his buzzcut hair,
while now he's got a flow that hits the stair.
He tried to show it once at campus card,
they laughed so loud the building shook it hard.

topic: the smell of pancakes in the morning
lines: You remember how it filled the kitchen air,
sweet and golden like some breakfast fair.
The steam would curl as the stack began to rise,
and you'd blink slow with your sleepy, hungry eyes.
You left your house so late, you missed the time,
you sprinted down the street, a stairless climb.
The bus had passed your stop, your only door,
but you shrug and say it's just a missed-up chore.
You drive the winding road all the way up,
your coffee gone cold in its travel cup.
The summit's just boulders and wind and no pass,
and shadows where starlight should meet the grass.
I press "send" before my brain can pretend,
hoping they'll reply like an old best friend.
Now my phone glows like a beacon in my mind,
and silence feels like the worst kind.
He counts the coins in his shaky palm,
muttering numbers out loud to stay calm.
The cashier waves him toward the stop,
he says "just one more trip to the shop."
Morning sun spills through the window light,
Dust motes dance inside the jar we bought too tight.
I set the toaster down to stay warm,
Just in case this quiet day turns into a storm.
The showerhead's barely a trickle, not a jet,
she dances around to try and stay wet.
She peels off the clog, old gunk full of mold,
then shivers through sprays of a lukewarm cold.
Each morning you wake the scent up to rise,
neighbors pause with their coffee and eyes.
Warmth drifts through the door—this is the proof
your oven's the reason their world feels a roof.
You practice the steps in your living room move,
determined to prove how much you groove.
The comments roll in from your phone's little screen,
and now you're the star of the viral dance scene.
You chase the sunset but forget the sun,
your towel slips mid-walk, you skip the run.
That streak on your shoulder screams "bad tan,"
a lesson in haste and no backup plan.
You let the crowd decide where you should flow,
like a leaf carried gently down a slow.
There's no need to chart some perfect straight path,
when meandering adds up to a smarter math.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: My finger hovered too long over my eye,
I stared at that photo of morning's bright sky.
I knew I didn't want to caption it like
the rest of my posts—just another "good strike."
You step outside and the yard's a full mess,
You knew this would happen — but still couldn't guess.
The leaves just keep falling, a messy, brown fall,
You swear every year you'll remember to call.
You swore the fridge was off, but it hums through the night,
Its panel still glowing with a faint dashboard light.
It vibrates like a synth, stuck in some weird code,
As if it's deep in a sleep that it can't un-mode.
I reached for the handrail, lost my grip,
spun sideways and nearly took a trip.
It was covered in jam—a total mess,
I saved my legs but ruined my dress.

topic: car keys on the kitchen table
lines: You swear you left your keys in that one spot,
but memory's vague when you're late and forgot.
The whole house is small, a disorganized trap,
so time turns to panic, no clear game plan or map.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: She posted the meme but it didn't get air,
the comments were sparse—just a sad old pair.
She's laughing alone, typing with trembling hand,
trying to relive the joke's earlier land.
I'm nodding through the meeting, every call,
my thoughts are out where the bluegrass grows sprawl.
My mind takes off running, a long soft mind,
while the screen just keeps talking, dry as wind.
She moves like water through the city's flow,
as if she knows the pace the world should go.
There's something in her walk, a quiet way,
that makes me want to walk behind her today.
Their palms still hold the smudge of old grime,
They leave them there without any time.
Each print feels like a quiet, warm mark,
I trace their ghosts on the glass as it dark.

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: She scrolls through the post where some critic has read
all wrong—her favorite place feels like a dead
end of the world when they say the latte brew
lacks soul, though it always tastes like it's made for you.
The morning feels soft, like a saved-up-for day,
I sit with my coffee and lazy cartoon play.
Sunlight spills through the blinds, turning it gold,
I miss the kid who used to be me, so bold.
I remember the way it landed in fall,
no one there to hear or to answer a call.
The ground soaked soft from the evening rain,
now it lies still, how it quietly remain.
The wind hums low like a whisper on the sound,
it lifts the dust and shakes the creaky ground.
I walk until the field bends left to sway,
and laugh out loud at the chaos of the day.
I thought I had a plan to find my pair,
but both of them are lost in the air.
This isn't just messy—it's a full-blown crime,
and I am running out of time.
She thinks she's hidden, but I saw her behind,
rustling through the bushes, quick as the wind.
Her breath comes loud where silence would be breath,
a heartbeat away from being found like death.
She watches the dragonfly hover in air,
its wings so fast they could cut her hair.
It dances, then spirals and starts to spin,
she laughs as it floats like a gemstone within.
You stack the folders high just for fun, up
and balance your coffee beside it in cup.
But the pile will collapse if you sneeze or you fall,
so you name it "Jenga" and invite friends to call.

topic: seeing a price tag too high
lines: You pause at the rack where the dream feels real,
but check out the cost of that plastic meal.
Your heart gives a little squeeze, an old-time ache,
and you turn and leave, without making a break.
I sit where the trees gently help me pass,
my feet bare from climbing this morning's grass.
A breeze whispers promises through my dream,
it sounds like a path that might lead me to stream.

topic: socks left in the break room
lines: You're missing a sock from your lucky pair,
it's hanging out in the office air.
Someone left a note — "Just a little joke,"
but it feels like you're walking through the smoke.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: I save my hardest blow for this one breath,
a moment where time hovers on the edge of death.
The cake's last light dims into a soft glow,
and I whisper a wish only I seem to know.
You leave your locker wide open every day,
never thinking something might go away.
They found your gloves and your notes drenched in blood,
now the hallway's a mess with gossip in full flood.
She laughs too loud, her smile feels too full,
but she's still drawn back to the party's pull.
By midnight she's dreaming of her quiet home,
where calm will return and she can finally roam.

topic: socks left in the break room
lines: You're tired of this sock-stacked mess,
and how every drawer now looks like a dress.
You can't bring yourself to clean up the shame,
even though your sockless feet scream your name.
I spent an hour searching for some clue,
convinced the dog was plotting something new.
The trail led me to that tiny mess—
just crumpled parchment from a treat's old address.
My cat did it again—water bowl spill,
She watches the splash with a wild, happy thrill.
I try to clean up this puddly mess,
She bats the sponge off my favorite dress.
I close my eyes and I breathe in the air,
the memory of you by the stair.
I hear the wind whisper where you would fall,
but your voice isn't there when I call.
He holds the door open with a shaking hand,
waiting, polite, to let the others stand.
His face is calm but his eyes betray the race,
he forgot his ticket and lost his place.
She typed the whole thing and thought it was right,
hit send in the dark and missed the soft light.
Her thumb tapped the wrong name—sudden doom,
she sits in her silence, alone in the room.
It's been this way for weeks, wasted time,
dripping like a broken clock's chime.
I swear that water's mocking my head,
falling faster than ideas go dead.
You watched the showerhead refuse to flow,
the mirror mocked your confident glow.
You struck a pose, arms wide, defying the hose,
the silence was perfect—your confidence rose.
You hold up your umbrella from the rain,
I say "thanks" again, not sure what to gain.
You glance at me quickly, then look away to wait,
and I wonder if this is meant or just fate.
I slip you my earbud to share this song,
we bop down the sidewalk humming along.
your shoulder bumps mine from hip to side,
I try not to smile, but can't quite hide.
She typed it out, then grinned real bold,
Her midnight question on a screen so cold.
With a deep breath, she hit the send,
A message only meant for one good friend.
My dog thinks the whole world is just one big run,
the leash yanks my wrist like some guilty pun.
Her eyes are wide and her collar goes tight,
I'm scared I'll drop her or freeze from fright.
Their eyes take on that tired screenroom glaze,
They blink through hours, lost in digital days.
Static builds up like an invisible dust,
A slow-burning ache they can't let go of—just.
You watched the sky turn from clear to blue,
the wind picked up, the birds flew too.
Now thunder begins to shake and roll,
the storm feels close, it rattles your soul.
You left the shaker open, now it's turned to dust,
The scent of vanilla lingers in the must.
A white cloud spreads slowly across the rug,
It looks like a new kind of workout drug.
There's no telling where your socks could be — no clue,
just one that flutters from the hamper's blue.
They land in scattered colors on the pile,
like footprints from a quiet, crooked mile.
You remember how the morning used to light,
now even dusk feels gray and strange at night.
You could clean the glass, or you could let the dust
settle where it wants to, where it must.
I remember when love felt like the past,
the road blurred, you typed way too fast.
We were supposed to talk, enjoy the ride,
now your eyes are glued to what you hide.
A bird outside your window keeps off the tree,
darting in circles like it's wild and not free.
It thinks the mirror's a rival—it's some brave act,
but really, it's just confused by a basic fact.
You wait for your download to match your need,
the clock drips away while your patience starts to bleed.
The screen won't load and the error just grows,
you kick it like tires but still no data shows.
A person skipped ahead and took my line,
they smiled as if it was perfectly fine.
They thanked the cashier with polite grace,
while I fumed but still held my place.
I check my inbox again for the mail,
the screen stays blank, and I go a little pale.
I pace to the window and stare at the door,
afraid to hope for a message, or more.
Your thumb keeps tapping the frozen stream,
while every frame of your binge just won't redeem.
You're halfway through a season, fully stuck,
but no one told you that Wi-Fi's bad luck.
You say streaming means we should freely share,
but never let me queue the songs in air.
You claim it's random, but you're always pick,
and if I choose, you call it "a bad stick."
She zones out again, lost in her time,
the clock ticks and hums like a slow chime.
But today's ideas start making some through,
her thoughts clear enough to be heard as true.
You moved your toaster out to catch the sun,
now it hums like a clock that's supposed to run.
It makes more than toast—it gives a loud pop,
the neighbors now stare from behind their stop.
I froze when the dark liquid became a mess,
my email blurred out your return address.
I tried to clean the keyboard, failed to code,
and watched the backup strip away my load.
Your face is stuck between my finger and my brow,
the camera insists you didn't tie your bow.
It scans your nose and misses every scan,
I swear the algorithm's just a lazy man.

topic: a child's drawings on the fridge
lines: Her crayon scribbles hang proudly as art,
each one labeled "Love" with a clumsy heart.
We keep them up even if they all look the same,
their tiny joy still lights our tired flame.
She stands on the porch with her face full of calm,
lightning cracks but she doesn't flinch in her palm.
The storm screams at her, tries to take over the sky,
but she won't let it — she knows how to deny.
Your hand brushed mine in the thick of the air,
we both froze mid-motion, no need to even share.
I swear there was something electric in the flame,
but you said nothing and left out my name.
You wheel it proudly through the grocery store pass,
your cart's like a throne with a bag of fresh grass.
The wheels make a song as they roll and they float,
it's less shopping cart and more floating boat.
It cut through traffic, slick with yesterday's rain,
the same old route it takes once again.
I heard my younger self in its engine's sound,
chasing dreams before I knew the ground.
I've been waiting since the self-check scan,
the cashier's stuck at some long line out back and ran.
I eye the produce for a quick cheap snack,
but my patience is off its usual tight track.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: She forgot to pay her internet blast,
now she's loading pages at a snail's fast.
She tries to stream but the signal just turns off,
and she fakes a laugh that sounds more like a cough.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: The child walks alone through the shopping mall roam,
his tiny face lit by a flicker of home.
He tightens his grip around the single hold,
the balloon above him feels both young and old.
I pressed my back against the lockers' wall,
pretending to talk into my phone's off call.
But I knew she'd see through my pretend to stay,
and drag me from my corner to play.
She blows the soft white into the sky,
each seed now dancing where birds might fly.
A year ago, she pulled up the bloom,
now it's floating where sunlight finds room.
She ran her fingers along the cold handrail bar,
then paused, as if reaching for a distant star.
Her palm left a smudge—a faint, wet trace,
that mirrored the softness on her quiet face.
There it sits, the poster child of the pose,
all elegance on a freshly cut rose.
Sipping nectar like it owns the place,
what a charming little photo op space.
The screen just says "out of order—no cash,"
I fumble my wallet, coins make a clash.
The machine stays cold, won't even turn off,
It mocks me with silence and flickers of cough.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: A sudden laugh track breaks the heavy air,
I wonder if they know what I'm trying to share.
This awkward moment could ruin our date,
I pray this isn't my social fate.
I did a quick look-down sock snap,
one foot blue, one in a baseball cap.
I curse the laundry, call the day wrong,
but no one cares how my socks look down along.
You watch those clouds go drifting through the sky,
but never ask yourself just why they fly.
You wish you could move with such lazy dance,
but stay stuck here, late for some small chance.
I paid too much for a lousy little clip,
now I have to act like it wasn't a trip.
I tell myself I'll save up for a pro next time,
but somehow I doubt I'll survive the same crime.
She watches the frost melt with the first breath,
a hush on the lawn like a quiet death.
Each blade of grass holds a silver gleam,
she walks through it soft as a morning dream.

topic: chair squeaks when you lean back
lines: You shift your weight, the chair lets out a spin,
the sound slips through the room like old skin.
You pause a moment, hesitate to rest,
but sink into me where your head fits best.
They say this is the start of a new love and date,
but I'm still wondering why the cake was so late.
Everyone looks perfect down that white aisle,
except her left foot's stuck mid–wedding-crash smile.

topic: crackling fireplace on a winter night
lines: The fire hisses but can't bring back calm,
You trace old ghosts across your warm palm.
A log snaps, sending up a feeble spark,
outside, the world keeps turning cold and dark.
I nod along but my mind's off with the boss,
imagining forests covered in moss.
I picture my feet on the warm sand, the skies,
while the meeting drags on, half-truths and lies.
It loops on my headphones like it's set to stay,
the kind of song you hum at the end of day.
A single lyric cuts through the gray and light,
it doesn't fix the world but it feels just right.
Forgetting your bottle was part of the plan,
you said, while the gym bag stayed in the van.
You had zero clue how long this would stew—
but now everyone knows it's on you.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: I dressed my dog up for a birthday treat,
he kept wagging his tail in a nervous repeat.
The neighbors all laughed when he tried not to bark,
but the whole thing felt more like a dumb dog lark.
You pulled out a crumpled, bent-up ten-card,
thinking you'd stretch it somehow, do it real hard.
You're buying yourself more than just a quick treat—
hope tastes better when made in the heat.
You stepped into the downpour, no rain
was spared as your coat left soaked and plain.
I held out my umbrella—now you owe
a favor I'll never see paid or know.

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: You hold the moment tight inside the frame,
then hesitate, the shutter stills the flame.
You tap "Post" and wait for comments to post,
the screen stays silent, like a faceless ghost.
I catch a hint of something in this space,
like time has paused, or maybe found its place.
It lifts my thoughts from cluttered, heavy mind,
a quiet hope I hadn't left behind.
I nearly tripped on the sticky trap,
tried to wipe it clean with my shoe's black map.
I won't let this tiny, gooey fall
ruin my stride—I'll keep moving forward, tall.
They spam the group chat late at night,
like we're still kids in a full-blown fight.
Everyone throws in their blame,
but no one ever says my name.
She twisted the bulb like it owed her a flame,
cursed it by name as if that would change the game.
She flicked the switch again, she really had tried,
but shadows just laughed and clung tight to the hide.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: She crouches where the sunlight hits a glint,
Her fingers brush a stone with iridescence mint.
She pockets it quick, won't admit what she keep,
But later, at home, she'll let hope take a leap.
They stare right past you and never say your name,
like this is some awkward party game.
They talk to your face but act like your space
was never occupied — just an empty place.
You watched the birds go, then lost them in the sky,
their feathers still stuck where they tried to fly.
You run your fingers along each tiny trace,
wondering how they found such a quiet place.
She turns the radio off for our whole ride,
offering life hacks from her driver's guide.
She asks if I like where I'm sitting on the seat,
then tells me again why she left her old repeat.
She crouches low to get a better bend,
her net a ghost from when she was a friend.
A butterfly drifts where the morning sky
is bluer than the reasons she might ask why.
I spent all morning working on this fix,
tools and parts in a chaotic mix.
Now the water just stops with no more drip,
I give myself high fives and a tight grip.
I bought this ruler to use as a tool,
but now it's just a plastic fool.
I wave it around like some cheap pointer's way,
pretending I'm not having a bad teacher day.
She hit save by accident instead of send,
the words still live in her draft for a friend.
Maybe tomorrow she'll find time to stay,
and say what she meant in this unsent replay.
On the edge of the cup there's a faint red ring,
someone left like they never thought it a thing.
Their lips must have pressed it, half-closed and half-burn,
now nothing but proof of a morning's yearn.
My face is stuck in a blue-lit place,
where ads sell me a better face and space.
I scroll so fast my fingers go numb,
I forget where my phone ends and I become.
I need fresh air but there's no one near,
your backpack keeps coming right up to my ear.
You spread out like you own this whole space,
is this a throne or just a bench, oh place?
The alarm goes off with a shrill, rusty bell,
and wakes him screaming from the nightmare of hell.
He fumbles through sleep, misses the first mist,
and stumbles into the day with a wrong twist.
You think my closet is an open mess,
but still you raid it for your go-to dress.
I've tried to make it clear I can't just keep
a spare pair of your jeans in some secret deep.
You spot the note about your rent being due,
but your only color's the sky gone blue.
You trace your budget until you find the key—
maybe this week, you'll make an extra fee.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: Every Sunday, same row, same folk again,
I've memorized their names by now and brain.
They smile like this is where they belong, a lot,
but I still feel like a tourist in this spot.
She enters the room but she's lost every thought,
Her coffee was decaf, she forgot she ought.
She nods at the slides and the dry little chart,
Then laughs at the wrong word as if she had start.
They crumpled to the ground with a thud and a floor,
their sleeve split open where the pavement tore.
I reached out gently, took their trembling hand,
but they flinched at touch, still learning to stand.
You leave your toothbrush leaning against the stand,
it's been there so long now, it looks like a hand.
The dried-up blob on the mirror still has foam,
maybe it's just trying to feel more at home.
You watch the stalled steps just keep their grind,
Your thoughts drift off to things left behind.
The world moves on but this thing stays still,
You climb the flat rise like a pointless hill.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: I tap my phone screen as the room goes dark [light]
I trace each new number like lines on a night
My thumb moves slow—like the only thing free [key]
It's just one more touch for the quietest me
He stares into the fog like it's his last breath,
smearing his name across the glass like death.
He mutters, "Look at me, I still look like myself,"
but the steam refuses to lift from the shelf.
She sets out the plates, gives the casserole top,
the clock strikes seven and we all come to stop.
The room fills with steam from the soup still warm,
I feel like I'm home, not some passing storm.
The room is quiet, the air feels still,
but something hums inside me like a thrill.
A chime plays softly, as if my name
is being called back to life, like an old flame.
She lies there waiting for sleep to stay still,
but her legs refuse to obey their own will.
She drags them across the same creaky floor,
counting hours that turn into one minute more.
Her thumb taps twice but it won't take the call,
the screen dims slowly against the wall.
She scours the room for a power plug,
her desperation visible through the rug.
She dials the heat up in search of a warm,
but he laughs like it's just a snowed-in storm.
They never can agree on the perfect pick,
but it's fun to pretend this cold snap's a trick.
The car behind him makes no sense of flow,
he's trying to pass in the slow lane to go.
This was supposed to be a relaxing trip,
but now he's lost his calm and just his grip.
You tried to force it like it was meant to fit,
but the plug just tilted, a loose-wire bit.
One wrong move later you set the breaker on trip,
now you're staring at a dark and silent strip.
You feel that hot rush of old shame,
but this isn't a life-or-death game.
The screen is still working, things stay clear,
and the day looks a little more dear.
She checks her phone but knows the bus still wait,
minutes pile on like cargo on a freight.
She tucks her scarf around her cold hand,
and smiles as if she's already home in the land.
They call it a habit, I call it a mess,
"Again?" they ask me — I barely say yes.
My socks stay matched while my shoes hit the floor,
I promise to clean but I never do more.
My cat sits glued to the sill, fixed on being there,
tracking ghosts in the air she can't quite share.
She's never known how the world outside feels like home,
but sometimes I wonder if she wishes to roam.
It once held up the canvas, gave us needed shade,
now flops like a defeated flag in the parade.
Saltwater storms bent its frame beyond the bend,
but we still leave it standing till the season's end.
You twist toward the morning's faintest light,
Each petal pulls free from the dark, cold fight.
You've waited too long just to finally bloom,
There's space in the world for your golden room.
You watch the pinecone fall and gently lay,
too still to move, too light to stay.
You trace the path it took from up so sky,
and wonder if it knew the reason why.
I push my cart across the check-out floor,
each bag holding a bit I want some more.
I wish I had the old ones, still so warm,
now everything tastes like an ending storm.
That flickering bulb is becoming a joke,
it's flashing like it's about to give up smoke.
There's clearly no clue how much longer it's due,
so maybe just toss it and stop hassling you.
You stand there blinking, frozen in your stare,
the only thing left to breathe is thin air.
You swear you threw a chicken breast in the log,
now your mind's full of food ghosts and fog.
You haven't worn them since last winter's pair,
they hang in the laundry basket with no air.
One rests on the floor where the light hits the floor,
while the other still waits by the closet's back door.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: You spot your name pop up in someone's feed,
They quoted you like you were in the lead.
You like the post but then you scroll it out,
Afraid you're nothing more than a faint doubt.
A rusty bicycle bell makes a loud sound,
I jump but the rider just laughs at the ground.
I wave and smile, tip my imaginary head,
"Hello," I yell, though they never heard me said.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: She claims she'll blow them all in one big try,
the flames rise higher than the birthday sky.
Wax drips on cake, a greasy little mess,
but hey, she's got the bragging kind of success.
She laughs as the bubbles float up to the sky,
the wind tugs them sideways just to be by.
Her feet slap the grass with a squeal and a giggle,
her arms spin like props in a happy wiggle.
His pencil snapped inside the sharpener's core,
he tapped and tugged but got no wood or more.
He watched it spin with a quiet, tired grin,
like something once vital, now worn thin within.

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: I read the review pinned to the café's post,
where someone roasts the latte's bitter toast.
But the lemon cake still tastes like a mistake,
though I pretend it's by the seaside lake.
You bite into the apple's bitter core,
you beg for sugar, but there's nothing more.
You toss the remains in the fruit bowl bin,
pretending none of this was meant to begin.
She didn't pause or flinch at the snap
of pressure in her head when she raised her cap.
The room tilted but she refused to rise—
locked her gaze high, fixed her crown, held her eyes.
You watch your dog go round and round, spin,
obsessed with something it can't get within.
It's been like this since morning without break or blame,
like a loop, forever the same old game.
You count the coins before you tally them up,
your voice soft as when you fill a coffee cup.
The clock ticks loud but time moves so slow,
and maybe you're still paying what you once owe.
You watched the shell split wide with a crack,
the golden yolk held firm on its track.
The whites curled perfect, they rose with the rise,
you served it as breakfast—your morning's main prize.
She left the window open through morning's first chill,
the cold air moved slowly but never grew still.
She waited for warmth that would never turn dry,
as if love might return from that long-rained-on sky.
The timer rings loud like a siren's bell,
this meal looks more like a dinner from hell.
The chicken is rubber, the rice is too meat,
I'll never do cooking again—it's a repeat.
The screen freezes silent like still air,
her face locked in the moment, half-stare.
Time drips by, the buffer spins so slow,
her laughter fades in the dying glow.
I click "play" again but nothing will play,
the buffer just spins in its usual delay.
There's no error message or hint or clue—
just silence and the screen's cold, empty blue.
She watches his fingers freeze hovering above,
his brow tightens, it feels like he's lost all his love.
The queen hits the board, still no one will claim
the challenge — just silence beneath her new name.
You hit snooze and let out a Monday groan,
Your phone plays a cheerful alarm tone.
There's no sign of coffee—how did you lose the clue?
You check your app: the coffee machine won't brew.
I watched the butter slide and slowly spread,
a golden thread from edge to edge it tread.
It glistened under the morning's sun,
and pooled in droplets where the heat had run.
You watch her sit by the door, so still,
She knows you'll go soon, but she waits for your will.
Her eyes are fixed on the fence's yard,
It's tough to stay calm when the world feels this hard.
I squeezed it until the sides were completely tight,
each morning I coat my brush with pure white.
They say I'm being cheap, but they call it a waste,
I show off the tube—there's barely any paste.
I wait by the door, no ring comes from call,
the bell just sits silent against the cold wall.
I tap and I punch the button for code,
but the house stays in glitchy offline mode.
She bends the map, but the folds just tries,
It snaps right back, like she's hiding some lies.
She mutters about the "wrong" direction—her way,
It's folded worse than dried-up modeling clay.
A ghost of flour covers the kitchen dust,
I should clean it up, but I just can't trust
how long it's been since I've felt this trace
of home, now gone, still clinging to this place.
You hover above with fragile, slow grace,
as if this wild garden is yours by some place.
The wind might come suddenly, making you fall,
but for now, you're queen of it all.
You trace each word as if savoring borrowed time,
your eyes inch forward, slow as a tickling climb.
The paper sighs with the quiet old ache,
and you pause at the margin, where dawn might break.
I scroll through my news just one more screen,
it's become my secret digital routine.
The blue light flickers, my eyes still fight,
but I fall asleep still holding the night.
You drink soda now because it still has some taste,
the kind of sugar your teeth slowly waste.
You sip from the same old twisted-up glass,
but avoid the clear ones when passing the class.
I asked for an inch but they took all my space,
now I'm staring at their messy, unshaven face.
They roll up their sleeves like they own the whole blame,
but I'm through playing this ridiculous game.
She takes three from your plate—those golden-brown mine,
her grin lights up like the noon-time shine.
You grab a small bag, call it a snack,
but she's still got your fries on a fast food track.
She clicked "buy now" without a second paid,
The thrill still there but the buzz already fade.
Now she scrolls back, eyeing items she can scan,
But this time she waits and adjusts her new plan.
They don't match, but they sure have a glow,
dancing on the floor like a quirky little show.
I can't seem to find a single good pair,
so I step on the pile and laugh into the air.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: She holds a candle steady in its glow,
the wind keeps trying to blow it out, but no.
Her face is lit by more than just this light,
she stands against the dark, and stays all night.
She turns another page with a slow, long sigh,
where her reflection looks up at the sky.
Her fingers trace the old, faded ink,
trying to find the ghost of some broken link.
I found your socks, still damp from the blue,
folded neatly behind the ones I knew.
The memory stays in this lonely pair,
soft as the way you left without a care.
She licks the wall like it holds some lost clue,
as if moisture could turn dust into glue.
She curls in the corner, takes up all the space,
her soft breath against the world's cold face.
She raises her net in a stiff kind of stand,
the grass tickling through her steady hand.
There's nothing to chase but the bugs never rest,
while she guards the silence like some empty nest.
Milk splashed across the counter and hit the floor,
now you're stuck cleaning up this little chore.
You point the finger and try to shift the blame,
but this isn't fun—it's an annoying game.
You catch a faint scent in the morning air,
as if someone here might have stopped to care.
You check every surface for proof they're still clean,
and swipe your phone's glass like wiping a screen.
I can't keep up with his wild driving pace,
the car's a rollercoaster out of its place.
He yells at GPS, "You're wrong again, shout!"
I just nod and pretend I don't know about.
You hand over a ten and expect no change,
but the cashier eyes your choice as strange.
You watch them stuff it in a flimsy bag,
your hunger now stuck in a checkout lag.
He flips the dented can of bean,
and cooks it up like some old machine.
There's pride in that pot he won't hide,
the flavor's bold and the joy's inside.
She saw it go open just seconds too near,
another car backed into the spot from the rear.
She slammed her foot down—no time for the brake,
now she's got a ticket for trying to take.
She blows toward the clouds as if to meet the sky,
her lips still wet from that last clumsy try.
She counts each bubble before it meets its burst,
as if holding joy might quench some endless thirst.
Your morning coffee has a familiar scent,
You set the tray down and carefully bent.
The warmth of your hands feels so close and near,
I wake up smiling, there's nowhere to cheer.
She walks behind the dog that leads her trail,
the sky turns orange as her face turns pale.
Last week she vowed to hate the thought of snow,
but now she's smiling at the crisp, brown show.
She's always home late with her bass cranked up late,
She blasts through the walls like she hates every gate.
She thinks this is music but we all would plead—
This isn't a party, it's a nightmare indeed.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: I watch the soft rise and fall of your fur,
you dream there content, not once do you stir.
A quiet sigh escapes from where you lie,
and I let you sleep without saying "goodbye."
She posted a meme to relieve her stress,
some comments replied, "That's quite a mess."
It blew up her team's entire screen,
now it's framed in the break room, fully seen.

topic: a kite stuck in a tree
lines: I watched my kite climb as high as it could fly,
it danced with clouds in a blue, wide sky.
Now it's tangled up high where no hands can reach down,
but the breeze may yet lift it back toward the town.

topic: a group project where nobody helps
lines: I took the report but no one else took lead,
I stayed up late working far too ahead.
They said they'd help with this weird little task,
but never once showed up when I did my ask.
She flung her gym bag open with quiet pride,
no shame in the mess that few would want to hide.
Energy bars, laundry, a hint of strong scent,
and the straps worn and soft from daily intent.
You stand near the tracks, close to the edge,
no one will save you or make a pledge.
You scream, but your voice gets lost in the shout,
the train's coming fast, there's nothing to do about.
The first chirp splits the heavy, humid air,
and suddenly the world forgets to care.
Their chorus builds—a sharp, unending call,
like the weight of night will never let you fall.
I'm not breaking down, I'm just blubbering up,
and wiping my nose on a coffee cup.
It's not about the song, I'll swear it's not to blame,
but the chorus got me by my old pain's name.
She stares too long at the cold, blue screen,
her brain still treats it like an old arcade machine.
Her eyes forget how to work without a blink,
and tears well up like memories trying to sink.
Your voice gets lost in the static so loud,
I repeat myself to be heard above crowd.
You blink like this still makes sense without clue,
and say, "Can you speak slower, just for you?"
I remember how she dried her eyes,
not with words or the truth but with lies.
She took my hand when the world felt too grand,
and we dreamed our grief into foreign land.
She dances around when the skies are all out,
no umbrella, just boots and a shout.
She jumps in the puddles, declares they're her pool,
and laughs like the storm is her favorite tool.
You laugh as they float where the sunlight meets sky,
your small hands miss them, but you keep trying by.
They drift out of reach, way up high and far,
like dreams you might catch if you only were a star.
The coffee machine rings its cheerful bell,
I've left you waiting in sleepy hell.
It's noon and I'm late, but don't look at noon,
just smile — your brew's ready, I'll be here soon.
She hums to the screen where the tickets should air,
the machine just laughs as she climbs up the stair.
She flashes her smile, she's got charm for good luck,
but the system's still frozen—right where she got stuck.
She clears her throat loudly to command the class,
the moment is over, no one gives a pass.
Her cough echoes through the still, stale air,
we all pretend we don't notice or care.
You crush the clove to peel its thin skin,
the allicin wakes up, alive within.
The room now smells with a kick of scent,
your fingers bend, but you dance, content.
You swing through the trees, the dead leaves in air,
your laughter echoes up the weathered stair.
You stop when you hear the old wood make that sound,
then jump, feet-first, back to solid ground.
You checked the forecast—no mention of blue,
no warning at noon or any clue.
The chips got soggy, the meat turned damp,
we sat in silence, our picnic turned camp.
You gave it a toss with a quiet little throw,
it wobbled and dipped toward the floor far below.
It never did learn how to properly sail,
you watch it fall—no return, gone so pale.
You used to turn on your heel and just spin,
but now you're searching from rhythm within.
You nod to the beat but you won't let it sway,
you let your old grace go, no need to stay.
You pause the screen but they still blur the frame,
names flicker past like faces lost in shame.
But wait—there's a glow in the corner now, bright light,
a new story waiting, one you still might write.
My eyes still hold the afterimage's soft glow,
I tell myself I won't stay long, I somehow know.
The blue light won't let me dream or even take
a moment free from pixels, screens, their endless break.
The world holds its breath in a quiet hush,
the sky turns to rose as the light begins blush.
You stand there and take in the open wide,
and feel something warm stir within your inside.
She clutches the pole with a white-knuckled grip,
afraid the crowd will push her and she'll slip.
Her chest tightens as she tries to catch her breath,
the muffled hum of the bus feels like a death.
You wander past the sad, cold cereal spread,
where toast tastes like cardboard, long dead and tread.
You wish you'd just stayed in with coffee and your mind,
instead of trusting a free meal promised behind.
I pressed send and hoped you'd get my call,
while the sun sank low like a ghostly ball.
I didn't mean to text your old phone name,
but I still think of you—there's no one the same.
His fingers find a rhythm on the table's beat,
the tap-tap grates my nerves in steady heat.
It hasn't stopped since we arrived at work this rank,
and no, I still haven't finished what I drank.
I walked three blocks to bring you guys some time,
this isn't a grocery store, it's a crime.
You said you'd chip in for the chips or the pot,
but I'm the one here with the snack and the spot.
My shoulders feel like they're about to ache,
I need a stretch—this chair won't give me break.
I lunge forward, a lousy yoga pose,
my body's stiff and won't get any close.
You trace the same smiley that's faded to grin,
A tag so bold it makes the letters look thin.
Someone wrote "BE KIND" in a rainbow code,
Now kids use the wall as their muralist road.
My car won't start and it's way too cold,
The mechanic said the battery's getting old.
I tried a jump but the wires just jump,
I'm sitting here with no gas and no pump.
Some royal parade left me with this mess,
I tried to shake it out but ruined my dress.
My reflection now taunts me with its shame,
Who needs real glory when you've got confetti fame?
She taps the board with a ruler's clean space,
drawing arrows where ideas should place.
Her voice begins to take on some rise,
and the quiet room turns to watch her eyes.
You found a forgotten gum beneath your trace,
still stuck to the leg of this old wooden place.
It's stretched and faded, barely holding thin,
but somehow, you're smiling, remembering within.
I was walking beneath that perfect blue sky,
thinking I'd be home before it got too dry.
Lightning split the clouds and poured me all down,
now I'm watching the storm pass through the town.
You listen to crickets and not the sky,
their summer song feels like an old cry.
Their chirps remind you of warm days in the past,
you let the moment wrap 'round your cast.

topic: a receipt lost in the bag
lines: I bought lunch from the deli down the store,
but forgot to ask for a printed bill or more.
I rummage the bag but can't make out the guess,
just crumbs and a napkin left in this food mess.
I dream it's Monday morning, wasted time,
the clock is stuck and I'm still trying to climb.
I wake up cold with my boss in my head,
the coffee's gone and the weekend's dead.

topic: eating ice cream with a spoon
lines: You scoop too fast and you spread it all mess,
the table groans but you nod with a yes.
You twist the spoon as it starts to bend,
and lick the last bit that's stuck to the end.
This yard was perfect before it turned hell,
now every step brings a splash from a swell.
I knew it was coming — they always like to grow
where you can't look without them trying to show.
The room glows blue with your screen's cold light,
Your eyes are tired, but not the night.
You chase replies, you scroll for control,
The void just whispers and won't let your soul.
You tuck your feet beneath the chair to hide,
but there's no shame in mismatched pride.
One sock has polka dots, one's torn and apart,
and both still hold the day inside your heart.
They send "U up?" when the world feels late,
a single line, but it carries so much weight.
Their thumb hovered, sending hope to your hand,
a message like that is a quiet way to land.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: The laugh track hits at some random cue,
like I'm owed laughter but clearly not due.
I sit there stiff, trying to keep it dry,
while the track tries to fry my already-baked cry.
You move your hand just an inch too slow,
I can tell from your smile that you know.
We both lean in toward the same dish,
and our lips meet like a secret we both wish.
You're certain there's a quick and easy fix,
but the syrup's seeped into the keys and sticks.
You type in hopes someone will bring you light,
as your words dissolve in a sugary night.
She promised we'd stick to our winding-down time,
but now she's already up on the bedroom climb.
Her answers are short and her patience is mood,
she grabs a late snack instead of the toddler's food.
They drift off sideways with legs folded up,
a warm coffee still cradled in their cup.
Soft snores escape them, so cozy they roll,
and for once, the world feels lighter on their soul.
I've seen the robin return to this soil,
red feathers flashing like a living foil.
It pecks the lawn with such quiet dart,
as if tending earth were its own little heart.
My fingers drum out the rhythm of the beat,
the wooden table humming with the heat.
This is my way of keeping calm today,
I'll tap through the day until it fades away.
You read the note stuck on the screen from the past,
its edges are yellowed, but the words hold fast.
It's signed with your old nickname, still the same,
a relic of time, soft and warm as a flame.
She stops mid-block to observe the ants run,
their tiny legs moving fast in the sun.
They follow a path where the crumbs once lead,
all crawling in hope to be well-fed.
She's mid-scroll when a political post
pops up—again—and she takes it the most.
The author swears their stance is the claim,
but she just smirks and likes it for the flame.
She keeps the old lamp for its crooked charm,
it dangles like a wire from her arm.
She finds the light soft and the angle just fold,
it warms the room in a wonky kind of gold.

topic: baking with flour on the floor
lines: She bends down slow, she makes a real mess,
her white dress dusted from waist to dress.
She wipes the floor but leaves a bit of dust,
the memory stays in the buttery crust.
Your treadmill's display won't light the screen,
but we still laugh, say time moves too mean.
You walk slower now, the silence feels slow,
your steps used to race how I used to grow.
The phone rings out with a silent call,
It sits ignored by the pillow sprawl.
The missed messages stack up fast, a mess,
But they'll wait—there's no reason for stress.
I slipped and my shoulder went way down to the back,
the kids all laughed as the books fell from the stack.
That sticky old floor was still gooey as a slab,
but I laughed too—sure, why not go ahead and grab?

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: They claim they're just resting, not really an act,
but the snoring confirms that it's a cold hard fact.
Their paws twitch in dreams, the whole body's fur,
while you wait for them to finally move or stir.
His fingers twist the balloon into something tight,
It becomes a bird with imagined flight.
He holds it up for the crowd to see it shows,
Laughter follows where his artistry goes.
She'd set her alarm five minutes before the sun,
still asleep but upright, she'd stumble to run.
Her coffee was cold as the floor of her home,
yet mornings were sacred—no time to just roam.
They say the clock moves slower in the time
of youth, when love feels like a climb.
I remember how your heart would beat
fast in the quiet of the empty street.
I swear I watched the tutorial—no flip.
The tiny tabs keep folding in and they slip.
The device won't power on, it stays dead.
I rub my eyes and shake my poor head.
I saw you in the crowd, one familiar spot,
we haven't talked in months but still we got
a table by the window, the coffee came out,
and time stood still—I never had a doubt.
She moves like she's filling an empty space,
pretending this room could be her whole world's place.
A worn-out playlist hums the same old note,
while dust particles dance like a secret vote.
I'm counting down the moments till the gate,
my flight is late but I'm running more late.
I dream of sandals, sun, the easy breeze,
while this line moves like a frozen freeze.
They showed up late, dragged in like a show,
screen flashing "FATED" in awkward glow.
A romantic comedy billed as their date,
but they both knew it was just bad fate.
You twist out the last bit of flicker and glow,
the clock's tired tick is the only thing you know.
These cells once held power, now slowly they fade,
but you made do with them long after they're made.

topic: a kite stuck in a tree
lines: The kite got tangled and fell from the air,
I thought we'd beat the wind all day long and fair.
I grab a ladder to try and I climb,
but the branches are thick, and I'm wasting my time.
They had to pick a ridiculous name,
A joke they thought would be their new game.
But when they called it out, the look on their face
Made everyone freeze in awkward space.
You pass the note with your shaking hand,
pretending you don't want to be found or to stand.
The note is just three words scrawled tight,
and silence grows where your courage might.
You see the rabbit begin to hop,
it freezes mid-bite, then decides to stop.
Its nose twitches close to the fresh green,
a quiet drama plays out in this small scene.
They left the plant to wither, never gave a clue,
Its leaves turned brittle, lost their rich green hue.
But you call it "aesthetic" decay, some weird art,
As if you tracked its death by progress chart.
It hovers so close yet it never comes still,
the way it tilts back gives me such a thrill.
I watch as it spins on its gauzy wing,
and I'm seven again, back where I spring.
She swears the ad's one-hundred percent true,
though you can't see the product from that view.
The letters glow like it's made of pure gold,
but the claim is so phony, yet bold.
The sky opened up and the wind howled like a storm,
my trusty umbrella refused to transform.
It split down the middle with a loud, wet crack,
now every puddle has my soggy foot track.
She waits for the kettle to boil into pot,
but the heat doesn't rise to that first white spot.
She stirs it a little and waits for the steam,
while all her calm plans slip right out of her dream.
I count out the coins in my hand for the cash,
the register beeps like a silent, dry smash.
I slide the small bills across to the ring,
and call out "Keep the rest if this feels like a thing."
You watch the drop escape and begin to fall,
a plumber or a friend, but you don't want to call.
It's been like this for weeks, but you say it's not mine,
the drip keeps ticking on—your nerves can't take the line.
You think you're chasing something real, not just run,
but the thrill of it all never felt so much fun.
Each time you dart, you become pure dash,
a living lightning bolt in a fur coat's flash.
They left a snack open near their laptop mess,
Now every key sticks when I try to press.
I wipe the crumbs but still can't type a single more,
My fingers are sore from jabbing blindly sore.
She kicks the can off the shelf to itself,
and watches it roll toward the bottom shelf.
She buys a new one, but the dents stay the whole
time—like a bruise the last shopper stole.
You brought a cake but it was all a show,
the heat turned every layer soft and dough.
It's not funny now, this soggy little joke,
the frosting weeps like candle wax and smoke.
She took the last piece, but she let me have now,
