we always split it, like we used to vow.
She handed me crust, saved the cheese for her bite,
we ate in silence, like we did that night.
The teacher's cough echoes through the whole room,
each rattle and wheeze feels like certain doom.
We beg her to stop—it's too much to pass,
she laughs, "This is how you survive my class."

topic: a note tucked inside a card
lines: She skipped the message and just tore the card read,
left the real note folded on the back instead.
It wasn't a love letter, more like a joke—
"Don't cry over me if this makes you choke."
She types "goodnight" at twelve and waits for him to send,
some proof he's still here, still her midnight friend.
Her phone is warm where her thumb tried to sleep,
and she promises she'll go to bed to keep.
She found her headphones lost in a messy mess,
the cords were knotted with nowhere to address.
She tried to pull one side to free the plug,
but yanked too hard—and dropped it on the rug.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: You watch them take off without a care,
two wings, one beak, a lucky pair.
They fly through the morning's thin frost,
their cause already is lost.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: I posted a joke that was clearly half-tried,
but no one laughed, not even my ride.
I reshared it hoping for some false clap,
now it's just a ghost in a comment trap.
She mutters agreement but makes no real sound,
just nods along while her thoughts hit the ground.
She's lost in a cloud where no facts have space,
yet insists she knows exactly this place.
You bend a paperclip into a makeshift hook,
praying no one sees how desperate you took.
The line snaps with a pop—it was never the end,
but now you're out here fending off shame with your friend.

topic: a sticky finger on the window
lines: A smudge remains from the fingertip's trace,
the way they pressed out the view from its place.
They paused on the sill, let the silence fill air,
then vanished below to some unseen stair.
She skips outside the moment it starts to rain,
laughing as her boots splash through again.
Her face lights up with a quiet gleam,
as mud squelches from the puddle like a stream.
I swipe through the pictures from all these past days,
the screen still has that sleepy vacation glaze.
These images serve as my best proof—
I lived high above my old dull routine's roof.
She steps outside and never takes a walk,
just stares at the yard and starts to talk.
Her breath looks like smoke, she doesn't shiver,
says it's just the lawn turned into river.
A moment passed between us—full of spark,
we stood in silence by the quiet park.
I haven't stopped myself from wanting to seek
a sign you'd let me hold your hand again this week.
You double-tap a random stranger's snap,
not sure how they're linked to your own map.
You think it must be a mistake or a joke,
but your thumb already hit their profile spoke.
You shut off the cash register's dead sound,
humming your mantra and standing your ground.
"Exact change only" — you teach us the math,
while I fumble with coins, down a new path.
Their bread got stuck and the toaster won't pop,
They stare at it hoping it'll just stop.
They shout at the machine, as if that will try,
and swear the toast is the one who'll die.
She still insists it's enough to be clean,
though the plate looks like paste in the machine.
She takes each dish off and hand-wipes the rub,
her smile soft as the sponge, bit by bit, scrub.

topic: losing your wallet at the mall
lines: He retraced his steps but found no clue,
then stood in the lost-and-found queue.
They scanned his face, not his credit card chip,
and said this mistake won't happen on your next trip.

topic: someone handing you a surprise gift
lines: She holds out her hand like it's nothing but air,
I reach toward the gift at the top of the stair.
There's no note, no hint, not a single clue,
just a box tied tight with "To me, from you."

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: I set up the shot just to take a new frame,
I strike my best pose to make my own claim.
There's no one here watching but me for the post,
I snap and I flex—this silence is my boast.
The knight was knocked from its quiet fall,
no one there to answer or to call.
Its carved initials still whisper its name,
but the fire of the game is a spent flame.
You count each step going slowly up,
just trying not to spill your lukewarm cup.
Your knees begin to hum their quiet ache,
so you pause on the landing for a quick break.
You walk alone in the morning's soft hush,
sand still warm from where daylight first blush.
Waves whisper secrets they carry to bend,
you lean down, as if you might hear them to send.
You sit there watching it glows and dies,
the bulb seems to knows that it's run out of tries.
A final spark jumps inside the glass spark,
but soon the room falls into its usual dark.
The escalator's stuck, it won't help you move,
but the crowd has already started to groove.
Laughter echoes as the minutes stretch delay,
someone taps their shoe against the display.
Your alarm clock starts to blare without care,
each morning it screams through the heavy air.
You slam your hand down on the cold floor,
pretending it's just another chore.

topic: baking with flour on the floor
lines: She's making a cake but forgot how to cake,
now powdered sugar paints every mistake.
The flour goes flying like some kind of art,
it's a mess with a purpose—baked into her heart.
It keeps replaying the same song on play,
my thoughts stuck spinning, can't look away.
I pace near the window, near the floor,
afraid it'll start again — and play some more.
You move your lips so close, but still so slow,
the stove light casts a warm, red glow.
I know you're trying not to let anyone see,
but I almost snort-laughed when you kissed me.
You wake up again with your nose running thin,
The heater is still humming too close for sin.
You breathe in the steam from a warm, wet mist,
And hope your symptoms will soon be off your list.
You catch the ghost of a stranger's old coat,
a cedar and smoke kind of ghost note.
You flick your vents but can't erase the trace,
this car won't be the same strange new place.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: A child sobs in the grocery store aisle,
while their parent forces a fake smile.
The wails echo clear and consistent, loud,
yet they act like they're still so proud.
She watches the map crease itself into fold,
a precise zigzag only she can hold.
To others it's paper, but to her it's art,
a folded chart of genius, crisp and smart.
You spilled the whole shaker, a snowy white wreck,
your shirtfront's a canvas, your pride now in check.
You toss the mess into a trash bin with mix,
and flex your stained collar, calling it your new fix.
She hits replay when he skips to the jam,
He calls her taste "basic," she calls him a ham.
She swears this song fixes her whole mood,
He grumbles about being playlist-brood.
I leave the door ajar just for the sound,
my voice floats out like steam from the ground.
The mirror lights with the warmth of your glow,
I sing off-key but you still want me to go.
I wait for morning until the shade turns light,
the sky cracks open like a rusty hinge too tight.
Golden coins drop from the trees to hit the floor,
I leave them there—I don't have time to store.
You try to keep balance, but lose your grip,
and stumble against the front door—what a trip!
The driver gives a look, "Get off, don't stand,"
you apologize with your raised hand.
She twists the dial but it won't budge or spin,
the rust has settled in where the U is thin.
She tries every key from her jangled key,
then pays a shop to cut it off for a fee.

topic: a bus stop shelter at dusk
lines: The sky fades into a soft rose-gold,
and your breath drifts out, looking bold.
You wait for a ride with a weary stride,
but the stars are already trying to hide.
I left the cart key somewhere in the mall,
I even phoned the staff, but got no call.
I watched them wheel it off, I never did lock,
my hands feel cold with silent, passive shock.
She checks the screen, still holding onto hope,
but the numbers fall way below the scope.
The rent's due soon — she can't afford the bill,
so she fakes a smile and pretends it's a chill.
You settle into the back seat, just fine,
But he starts to repeat the same old line.
He insists he knows your whole life's way,
from your job to your divorce today.
I'm certain my phone fell into the hole,
I scream as if losing part of my soul.
I try to use Find My Phone to track,
but the screen shows a sad, empty back.
That wobbly pole gave out and now you stand,
trying to fix it with your bare hand.
The breeze just laughs as your umbrella float
flops down again—write a "screw it" note.
My car won't budge—the whole highway won't move,
horns blare in rhythm but nothing finds its groove.
I check my watch, then the time behind me past,
and curse how slow this "traffic" moves so fast.
You're sitting in class, but your bag feels so late,
You dug through your backpack—no eraser, no plate.
You text your sibling to check if they have it all,
They laugh and say, "You left it by the front wall."

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: This isn't just sweat—it's a badge of the heat,
I walked the block back in full sun, no sweat sheet.
My forehead glistens like some trophy of brow,
the A/C? Please—July shows you out now.
She wakes to a plate that he somehow made,
with fruit arranged in a silly little parade.
The crust is burnt, but she gives him a toast,
says he's the only chef who can mess up this boast.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: She left the house without a backward mess,
convinced she'd paid the bill—another yes.
But the Wi-Fi slows to a snail's old speed,
and now she's pacing, mad at her own need.
You sprint across campus when the warning bell
rings loud like a siren, your morning from hell.
You scan for the shortcut that won't cost a pass,
and miss the roll call at your first-period class.
Your phone blinks out like stars fleeing the light,
A 3% emergency, full-blown fright.
You fumble drawers for a cable (the door
Slams shut behind you—there's no time for more).

topic: finding a dollar in old jeans
lines: You pull out your jeans and discover a gold,
it's crumpled and worn, tucked deep in a fold.
You hold it up tight, like hope in your hand,
and wonder what else might fall from that land.

topic: ice forming on the car windshield
lines: She wakes to a car with a frozen, glass-bare,
and swears at the morning, the cold, and the air.
She scrapes in a rhythm, a slow, frigid thud,
until every chip is as clean as the mud.
You're way past your bedtime, but it's too late—time,
you say it's an emergency, a sleepless crime.
You light up the room with your glaring face,
where's the quiet bedtime calm? Not in this space.
You fumbled through those clumsy early time,
each loop a lesson without any rhyme.
Now your laces form a perfect, tight bow,
but memory keeps you from letting it go.
You pass me the bucket with your hand,
We both laugh when some kernels go stand.
It's not just butter that makes it feel warm,
It's the quiet between us, like a soft storm.
They tried to fix their breakfast with plain toast and bread,
but the machine spat out every slice half dead.
The room filled with the smell of bitter smoke,
a morning that tasted like regret and choke.
You see the tag and do the math twice,
you swear the price was way more than nice.
The cashier shrugs and says no change,
and now the whole moment feels strange.
She waited for the machine to show some cash,
but her screen just flashed a lonely red slash.
Her phone buzzed once—then nothing in her mind,
she counted steps back home to take it in behind.
I left the door wide open without a key,
the sign still says "Occupied" for all to see.
I found my old trophies still neatly in gold,
forgot how secure I felt being this bold.
I left my homework for the last possible load,
now I'm racing time down this winding road.
Found a shortcut called "pretend I'm a hack,"
but the teacher's watching—no tricks on this track.
I'm still in my job's same tired role,
even in sleep, I dig mental coal.
My boss yells at me just before I wake—
I reach for my phone, but it's just a coffee break.
You thought you'd hide your shoes behind the lace,
but the rabbit found them in the perfect place.
It's been at the left one all morning, chew,
now it's on the right—and you're down to two.
A single bulb flickers in the light,
She dances alone like she might fight.
Her expression softens into face,
A smile blooms where there used to be space.
I freeze mid-line when my phone lights up screen,
the cashier watches me now, I've been seen.
They ask if I need help with the bill in my cash,
but I'm sweating through clothes, trying not to go rash.
He pours the powder into his morning mix,
the blender coughs up a beige little fix.
He grabs a shaker, adds water and shake,
but now the sink's clogged with a chalky mistake.
You give the door another yank for a try,
the handle clicks like it's mocking the sky.
Your phone lights up—someone sent you the key,
but not soon enough to set your arm free.
I laugh at the billboard hawking the real,
promising miracles with a single meal.
It glows too bright to be that shine,
a lie dressed up in every clean line.
She watches a bird so tiny and small,
balanced carefully on a splintered old wall.
It taps on the wood with a rhythm so light,
as if every hop is one note in its flight.
You feel the crisp autumn in the air,
you walk the path without missing a stair.
There's warmth in the golden light that still glow,
the falling leaves are a quiet, pretty show.

topic: a dog leash tangled in railings
lines: My dog's leash is caught in a perfect little loop,
the kind that makes you wish for a squirrel or troop.
I yank to get the leash to finally lead,
but only manage to tangle it worse and spread.
This ticket was way more than it should have cost,
Now I've sat through three ads and still feel lost.
I could've spent this cash on something less trash,
Like a nap or snacks that don't come with a clash.
You pinned it to your desk with careful hand,
now it's stuck to your coffee mug, half-stand.
It's got a face, three buttons, and one funny eye,
but somehow, no one's asking why or why.

topic: the smell of pancakes in the morning
lines: The scent of syrup lifts through the air,
a quiet promise that someone's still there.
The pan is warm and the breakfast turns gold,
like memories made from the comfort of old.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: She checks the date on her crumpled up price,
the app won't scan it through her phone device.
She grabs a bag and hopes it won't crunch,
and prays it counts as a better lunch.
You act like this feud is some global air,
just a simple snack theft and a sharp glare.
You're trying to split hairs over this split,
when we could have both just taken a small bit.

topic: steaming coffee in a blue mug
lines: She claims this is just for the morning brew,
but sips it all day like it's medicine for you.
The cup's got a ring where she left it in stain,
and every week she says she'll wash it again.
The sound is too close, it's right in my ear,
I swore I'd get volume down this whole year.
I hunt for the remote to change this fix,
and dial back the noise to a softer mix.
She turns down the lane she's never seen near,
the brick wall is covered in ivy this year.
A bell chimes softly as she steps out of rain,
the scent of cinnamon makes her want to remain.
Her bike follows the gravel road's low hum,
the only noise the wind that doesn't come.
She slows at every sharp, unmarked bend,
as if each turn might be the ride's last end.
She reads the hot take in some random post,
then swipes through memes as she sails along the coast.
Her feed's full of rants but she doesn't engage—
she scrolls and she laughs, then blocks and unblocks the page.
She circles the clue but she can't see through,
the letters feel right though they're never quite true.
Her pen runs out mid-sentence, dry as the ink,
she stares at the grid but she just won't think.
I tried to smooth it but kept getting crease,
the paper rebelled and refused to release.
It twisted and buckled in every bad fold,
until I yelled out, "This thing's cursed like old gold."
My card got declined in the checkout air,
I laughed like it was some cosmic fair.
I blamed my ex and the wrong credit date,
but deep down I knew—my money's fate.
You never got the dripping tap to fix,
but mastered all the weird DIY tricks.
You proudly tell your friends how much you save,
like it's something to be praised, not brave.
You watched the butterfly land and glow,
remembering summers that felt so long ago.
Its wings were a whisper, a momentary breath,
a fleeting kind of life before full bloom or death.
She watched them break through the cold, frozen ground,
each bloom a secret the earth had just found.
They reached toward cracks where the sunlight would light,
and she thought, this might be the best kind of sight.

topic: reading under the covers with a flashlight
lines: You hide the glow of your secret little light,
the stories are loud when the world is tight.
The paper turns soft as you read each page,
your blanket is thick, but your mind escapes the cage.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: A green shoot has grown through the sidewalk up,
I stop what I'm doing to get a better cup.
It twists past the stones, growing strong and through,
a neon rebellion in gray city hue.
My favorite track cuts out mid-verse, no warning,
The phone just skips and gives me nothing but mourning.
I pause and restart, but it won't play or fix,
Guess the algorithm forgot how to mix.
The fog rolls in like a heavy gloom,
It turns my view into a gray room.
My morning drive feels like a ghost road,
This weather's dragging me down like a load.
She speaks up and starts to talk it all out,
her voice breaks the silence without a shout.
Her strength doesn't hide but just quietly shows,
the room feels a little brighter as she grows.

topic: a note tucked inside a card
lines: You found a note tucked in my outstretched hand,
a message from someone long unplanned.
The words are smudged where the corners got ink,
but you still read them, even if you don't think.
She thought the map would never steer her lead,
but laughed when it said, "Make a U-turn, dead."
She took the detour like she knew the way,
and found a lake she'd never seen today.
I step outside where the petals still bloom,
the sky pours into the gray-lit room.
The handle clicks, then it flips with a twist,
I spin my problems from mind, off the list.
I checked my text, not the timetable zone,
the screen lit up like some dumb midnight phone.
Now I'm here, waiting, stuck where I'm too late,
while the train zips off without me—my bad fate.
I saw you staring at the last slice with my eye,
don't pretend you didn't know it was a lie.
We could've split it but no, you took the share,
now I'm left with crumbs and nothing but cold air.
You twist the old pencil, its lead begins to bend,
The shavings pile up, like crumbs from a friend.
You push and you wiggle, you spin it one more try,
Then finally—snick—the blade clears the sky.
She runs eight apps at once without a heat,
the laptop steams hot on her bare seat.
She laughs when I ask if this might be a joke,
but the fan's on full now, we're both watching smoke.
The last light lingers in the evening air,
their wings still sharp in fading golden glare.
You hear the same old song they've always hum,
but dusk won't wait — it slowly starts to come.
I run while my thoughts won't stay in my mind,
I look back at the noise getting heard behind.
I wish I could run far beyond my tired past,
but the squeak keeps the dreams I try to cast.
You feel the world slow down when it's not home,
the kind of quiet where your thoughts can roam.
The air holds the day in a warm, soft still,
while crickets begin to sing and fill the hill.
She tells her kids all the cookies are near,
but whispers to me they're still within ear.
I grab a few more, my hand seals the fate,
she walks into the room and spots my full plate.
You crunch your way through the brittle brown ground,
the rhythm like music you've never quite found.
You wish this walk wouldn't slowly fade,
but the trees are already turning to shade.
You step outside, the sky turns dark and blue,
lightning cracks the clouds, your plans go out of cue.
Thunder comes rumbling, loud enough to roll,
you laugh it off — this storm won't steal your soul.
You blast the fan until it's cold as air,
then march downstairs to fix the broken stair.
"It's supposed to be warm!" you yell and say,
but no one built this place to heat your day.

topic: crackling fireplace on a winter night
lines: The fire burns low, but it feels so still,
The kind of calm that makes you smile and fill
Your cup again with warmth, with a fresh log,
And hope that tomorrow won't be fog.
My snore can rattle the frames of the room,
it echoes like thunder rolling through loom.
I don't hide or muffle this mighty claim—
my slumbering symphony's earned me some fame.
I finally reach the lecture hall's back door,
ten minutes late, as usual before.
My socks are damp from the puddles in the rain,
and the seat next to you is empty once again.
She moves through the field like a whisper from the past,
the wind a blast of summer, warm and fast.
The grass all bends in time with her slow bend,
as if the world's pausing to watch her ascend.
Your finger brushed mine—no lightning, just a spark,
we laughed it off as the room turned to dark.
You raised your hand with a quiet, "Let's grin,"
and I agreed—we're not done yet, let it begin.
You're still up past your bedtime, third hour,
the kettle's off but you need more power.
Your eyes are tired, but the coffee won't burn,
so sip it slow and pretend it's your turn.
The date is bright red on your calendar due,
Your thoughts keep turning the morning to blue.
You try to ignore the late fee alert call,
But guilt moves through your chest like a cold crawl.
My cat goes wild when the lights start to spin,
convinced there's a dragon hiding within.
I've tried to explain there's nothing to blame,
but he still plays the hunt like some dark game.
That coffee was heading straight for the wreck,
I moved my keyboard off the kitchen deck.
It missed the keyboard but hit the trash can—
now grounds are everywhere, what a disaster, man.
You trace your fingers through the muck and play,
pretending it's magic that will last today.
The sky is gray, but you draw your own light,
turning mud into something so bright.
It's been hours since this bulb tried to fit,
my patience wearing thin with every wit.
There's a sound it makes—a soft electric crack—
like it knows it should die but won't go back.
She walks beneath the quiet starlit glow,
her shadow moves but I don't really know.
The path ahead keeps curving low to bend,
and still she walks, as if the night won't end.
I catch a whisper of the scent of clean, wide space,
like rooms where quiet dreams their rightful place.
It smells like hope still clinging to my breath,
not fear, but life that's cheated grim death.
You remember how it warmed you in the sun,
the quiet afternoon turned into fun.
That bench is still there, but not the same sign,
just an old towel folded on a line.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: I watched it push through the hardened soil,
still curled like a green heart in armor's coil.
It bends toward what little light remains,
and clings to life with its tiny, tight veins.
You count the coins with careful hand,
and let the cashier know you don't need to stand.
Your quick math skills make your day feel bright,
you follow a path where cleverness feels right.
I've spent the whole afternoon trying not to cry,
both laces dangling like loose threads in the sky.
The tutorial said this step would help me lead,
but my shoes still scream I did it all wrong, indeed.

topic: walking past each other in a crowd
lines: I keep my head high and my steady pace,
you slip through the crowd, your familiar place.
We lock eyes once—like we're bound by fate,
but I keep going, and you're already late.
You cradle the steering wheel like it might lead,
the road stretches out and disappears ahead.
A gas station sign flickers in the fill,
you keep telling yourself you'll find the will.
You untwist it once more in its broken case,
like love tangled in static, out of place.
The plastic still frays from where stress met fray,
and charging becomes just another delay.
She flips the old disc like some sacred stone,
the player lets out a sad, slow moan.
Those songs brought back memories from better days,
she's not sure how to feel in this strange phase.
You trace the creases where the map has fold,
your breath fogging the paper, weather growing cold.
The roads blur together — no clear way,
just crumpled ink and a lost half-day.
The sky's been pouring all morning with rain,
You've sat here three times and tried to read again.
The roof still leaks, so you try not to drip,
But the wet pages turn into a soggy trip.
Your showerhead refuses to give steady flow,
it drips in rhythm only it seems to know.
You curse the wall and tap the rusty head,
but it just laughs and sprays in lazy spread.
They push through the soil like the morning would rise,
I kneel there and blink with my hopeful eyes.
Not much grows here where the pavement is ground,
but they stand small and proud, soft and crowned.
You laugh so hard at your own little clue,
your eyes crinkle up, and you snort just like you.
That deep, warm sound rolls out, slow and unbound,
I fall into it, laugh till my toes touch the ground.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: I saw the sky turn to fire and flame,
each second caught perfect in that frame.
I posted it bare, no caption, no break,
just pixels and silence by the lake.

topic: sitting on the porch steps at twilight
lines: I hear the last echo of the day's sound,
my shadow stretches toward the ground.
The screen door creaks like it wants to say door,
but silence offers nothing else to explore.
I turn the dial with trembling care by hand,
the tape hisses loudly on the old machine's stand.
I'm chasing every note from that lost song,
just to hear her voice one memory long.
I tap "retry" again but it still won't try,
my phone just sits here making me want to cry.
They promised this update would surely fix,
instead it's turned my phone into digital bricks.
They hit send before checking who got post,
My name blinked beside their morning toast.
The replies came quick—like a silent wave,
The teacher appeared in the thread so brave.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: You watched it slowly push through to grow,
a green fist breaking from concrete below.
They never asked for your story or name,
just walked by, pressed down on the same.

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: I gave that old stapler a second shot,
its hinge still creaks in the same old spot.
The rubber band's all that keeps the spring
from flying out—makes this junkyard thing.
You hear your phone vibrate with a call,
You sit up in bed, half-awake, you sprawl.
Your room is still dark except for the light,
It's midnight again, the worst time of night.
She follows him on his daily long walks,
her tail wagging like she's agreeing with talks.
He points at trees they never went past,
but she remembers every stick from the last.
You watch the kettle tick away the time,
its whistle rising sharp in winding climb.
You chase the mist but can't hold on to steam,
just memories of warmth that fade like dream.
You let the paper whisper its story,
remembering the scenes in your glory.
Each page takes you back to the heart of the past,
but the wind flips them and it all goes too fast.
They fall in step behind you, same pace,
hands deep in pockets, just finding their place.
The sky begins to weep a soft rain,
and you walk as if you might do it again.
His fingers keep time with a quiet, lost beat,
the rhythm of footsteps on pavement, the street.
Each tap on the table sounds like it's made of wood,
I wonder if anyone else just stood.
Her porch light flickers like an old-time glow,
She keeps it on so I still want to go.
I drive by slowly, wheels never bend,
But the light goes out before I reach the end.
They've worn the same jeans since they were freshly closed,
and now the zipper fights to stay composed.
They whisper, "Wait here," as if the metal might slide,
but it's caught on a thread from love's soft inside.
I can't hear the world when the needles make sound,
my thoughts fall away like the leaves on the ground.
I trace every loop with a color so thread,
but the quiet just climbs up inside my head.
Their fingers rest beside me, warm and trail,
the quiet stretching between us, calm and pale.
I don't need words to know exactly when
they'll still be here, steady, holding on again.
You thought it was just a quick little spree,
now boxes sit around you like old debris.
Was this a gift or a mistake of fate?
That tiny "Buy Now" button had too much weight.
You waltz through the room with that guilty snack face,
like you're proud you forgot to bring coffee or grace.
Everyone stops what they're doing to talk,
you're the joke of the hour, written in chalk.
Your keyboard clacks like it's trying to sound
like thunder echoing through these hollow ground.
I've been trying to focus but now I'll just lose
my concentration to your constant muse.

topic: leaving a note on the fridge
lines: She writes in all caps as if reaching back,
to times when her voice left a hand-scrawled track.
She adds a small smiley, the year, and the date,
then sticks it to milk for some future mate.
She lets the melody pull her into the tune,
her eyes look upward as if talking to the moon.
"It's okay to cry," she says with a sigh,
and no one tells her to hide or be dry.
You swing your shovel, the frost gives a crack,
You bend again, feeling strain in your back.
Beneath the ice, you can feel the soil,
Waiting to bloom like spring's quiet oil.
You grab the shaker, then trip on your shake,
white dust spreads like snow on the kitchen lake.
No mopping will fix it—this powder's a mess,
your smoothie dreams died under all this stress.
The tuning fork hums out its perfect tone,
while he fakes focus, bored and alone.
He stares at it long, claims to hear the still,
but his eyes scream, "This isn't a thrill."

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: I watched the pigeons fight the rising air,
their wings beat chaos up the rusted stair.
The ground was cement, cold as winter's frost,
and every beak fought for its quiet lost.
He pedals fast to fix a flat, no patch,
his spare is old and doesn't quite match.
The mud sticks hard, and it's ruining his heel,
he mutters curses like a rusty steel.
Your phone insists you follow where it lead,
down alleys with trash and old stale bread.
It never checks if you can actually pass,
just guides you toward a patch of wet grass.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: You watch them too long, you wonder if they're still,
their breath barely moving, your heart skips a thrill.
Was that a soft snore or a sudden bump?
You freeze by the couch, fear creeping in like a slump.
He left a smudged-up window as his mess,
I asked if he'd wash it, got a "yes."
He said he tried but missed the corner in ink,
now the glass shows coffee rings and a drink.
You pull the couch apart to make your own space,
where shadows become your secret place.
You trace imaginary lines on your floor map,
but sunlight won't fall into that blanket trap.
You clutch the cup like it's your last grip,
but coffee still escapes from the drip.
The stain spreads faster than you can clean the floor,
your boss walks in and asks for one more.
He hit send before proofreading his post,
Not realizing the teacher was in the host.
Now the whole class is laughing at what went wrong,
And he just sits there, blushing all the way along.

topic: a sticky finger on the window
lines: A tiny hand left a smudge on the glass mess,
I'll never figure out which kid did it, I guess.
The morning sun shows where the prints took light,
like clues from some secret childhood super-night.
You watched the lightbulb fade from bright to glow,
its flicker a signal you both still want to know.
It died in silence, leaving this room bare now,
but maybe we're enough without it to show how.
They've been stacked so long they're waiting to fall,
I keep pretending I don't hear them all.
Every paper has a future, same fate—
buried under the weight of the pile and the date.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: She slid the old key into the rusted lock,
the box creaked open to a dusty stock.
She swept out memories and set them all away,
now heirlooms glow proudly in the display.
She calls the mess a show of autumn's last glow,
while trampling leaves that crunch like chips below.
She says it's nature's gold, a fleeting, warm sight,
but I already told her it's just trash in white.
I danced with the gift on the hardwood floor,
it swayed like a lover pressed close to my door.
I loosened the bow, unspooled every tie,
but under the ribbon was nothing but a lie.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: You missed the date but never got a call,
your screen just stared like a silent wall.
Now buffers dance and videos play so slow,
you scroll through blank feeds that won't let you go.
Her phone bill came in double digits—way too due,
but she just laughed and said it wasn't that true.
She checked her data use, drew a red line,
and texted the carrier a quick "Nope, won't sign."
The screen blinked red when I asked for some cash,
my savings hit rock bottom fast—what a crash.
I stared at the machine, then back at the bank,
my stress now officially moved up in rank.
I watch it stretch along the desk's far bend,
one twist away from falling off the end.
Each paperclip feels as weak as every link,
I'm sure the whole damn thing will fall if I think.
You read the labels but it's always the price,
your eyes drift toward the things you can't afford twice.
The shop feels more like a sales pitch than trap,
yet still your wallet gets the silent slap.

topic: a long queue at the coffee shop
lines: You were the first one through the café door,
but the barista said they had none left for more.
The line moved so slow, you forgot your own pace,
while people behind you tried not to show their face.

topic: sitting on the porch steps at twilight
lines: I sit in the quiet hush of the fading light,
the sky a watercolor wash of gold and white.
A breeze brings the muffled chirp of distant sound,
my feet rest heavy on the cool, worn ground.
She keeps her wallet close to her hand,
every transaction feels like foreign land.
Now she counts coins while sitting in chair,
but it's funny how saving can still be a scare.
I stare into every puddle so deep,
afraid of the cold that begins to creep.
One wrong step could turn into a slip,
my shoes are already soaked through with drip.
My cat sees a shadow and goes for the leap,
convinced it's a monster beneath the heap.
He bats at the fluff like it's something to treat,
then trots off with pride and shakes both his feet.
He insists he'll handle the tip,
but I'm not buying him that trip.
You know how he gets when you try to owe,
he'll "remember" for years and never let it go.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: She squats in the sun with her pockets full of dirt,
slinging gooey globs and getting grass on her shirt.
"Look at my castle!" she yells, full of mold,
I pretend I believe her whole house is gold.
They said the mat would stick to the floor,
but it slipped and slid when they worked out full-tore.
The smell of sweat and of mildew's scent
made him quit mid-set, his resolve all bent.
You hear the soft ring of a familiar tone,
It breaks the stillness but does not come alone.
The screen lights up with the hope of a call,
But the silence stays, clinging to the hall.
You tap record then say "throw it in the trash,"
but the mic catches your coffee cup crash.
You hit stop, then redo it once more for good click,
the take you get sounds like a muffled brick.
She found it curled tight in a cardboard deep,
her breath held still, afraid to make it leap.
The rabbit stays quiet but never feels alone,
it waits like a secret in a cold, soft stone.
You pedal easy, the gravel lets you roll,
a stray dog yaps at a downed mailbox pole.
There's pebbles and thorns but you keep your grit,
a flat's a small price for the open road bit.
The songs all begin to drift off and fade,
you twist every knob in a fruitless parade.
You wait for the static to lift, but it still
buzzes like silence has climbed up the hill.
You try to stretch but your neck won't bend,
The pillow's blamed (not your old weird friend).
This morning brings a quiet, stubborn ache,
But coffee's brewing—time to take a break.
You think you need a whole suitcase of gear,
but half of it won't even get to appear.
The pile keeps growing, you swear there's no more—
until your bag gets stuck by the front door.
You turn the handle but the door won't twist,
It's wedged in steam and stuck with a list.
You knock, you holler, time begins to rush,
Trapped inside your nerves start to crush.
There's crayon chaos all over this mess,
You'll never be able to clean it, I guess.
I tried to pretend that I'd left to eat,
But you drew on the fridge next to the meat.
Your shovel's stuck like a rusted claw,
You curse the weather, break a local law.
You swing again—your shoulder screams "you're through,"
This dirt won't budge, and neither will you.
You hear the dryer's beep—it's time for joy,
A single sock now leaps like some lost toy.
You pause the cycle just to make a fix,
Now laundry day feels like a happy mix.
You counted down the hours, days, and then through,
and still no card, no text—just silence for you.
The candles are gone but the room feels too light,
as if the party was borrowed or might.
He gives each post a lazy double-tap,
like he's giving praise instead of a clap.
The algorithm serves him fluff for his feed,
and he never sees what's real, not even indeed.
As dusk falls, the shadows cling to the ground,
A breeze passes by, but there's no loud sound.
I squint at the corner of my tired eye,
Hoping it's nothing—just daylight's last lie.
She misses the buzz of the morning ring,
the string of old texts she used to bring.
These days she forgets to even make a call,
just stares at her phone on the quietest wall.
His hands stay still on the warm, worn wheel,
the engine hums, a steady, sleepy steel.
The city passes by without a roll,
but peace in him says this is where his soul.
Your hand went by too close for me to pass,
we both laughed like our nerves were made of grass.
Our mugs knocked over, coffee met with clash,
but you said, "Again—let's have a flash."
I watch the earth where spring has torn the ground,
something tenacious, green, already found.
I kneel to see the way they push to rise,
their yellow heads now touching my low eyes.
She thought the train was an hour late,
but her smartwatch had missed the date.
The calendar app said the time was wrong,
so she walked home singing all along.
I try to sketch clouds but it shows in my try—
the shapes look more like smoke than the sky.
You'd think a mess is what you get when you mess
with graphite and clouds, but this feels like less.
My eyelids droop as the hunger goes down,
I barely heard what you said about town.
I need just ten more minutes of sleep,
but the clock won't let me forget I should keep.
I pretend I still hear your voice on the sound,
while my thoughts wander soft and unbound.
I think about how we could have gone right,
if only time gave us more than just light.
You try to walk but your dog insists on lead,
They bark and spin with joyful, crazy head.
You jog to keep up, laugh as they run,
It's chaos and love wrapped in one weird fun.
I tap along to the fridge's weird old tune,
it hums low, like it's in league with the moon.
It keeps my drinks just this side of cold,
a quiet hero, in silver and gold.
They blast "Happy Birthday" straight into my ear,
the whole team's shouting, like it's some big cheer.
My neighbors bang pots, I'm shaking my head,
if this keeps up, I'll go totally dead.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: A kid's having none of this vanilla cake,
they scream like it's ruined their whole life's sake.
I try not to stare or say "Aw, come on, deal,"
but now they're crying where the shopping carts wheel.
My calendar is a disaster of my plan,
every hour screaming "Don't be that man."
The scribbles overlap into a full-blown mess,
but crossing out dates feels like stress relief, I guess.
The sky turned dark and swallowed up the blue,
we watched the storm begin to slowly brew.
The wind went still, then came the sudden hush,
we laughed as raindrops drenched us in their rush.
Each visit eats into their borrowed time,
another white coat lines up to climb.
They nod but don't meet your worried head,
their answers seem stale, like old factory bread.
You've tried everything to get it to run,
even left the door open for the sun.
The plates come out looking more like a mess,
and we both know what this means, I guess.

topic: ice forming on the car windshield
lines: Frost crawls across the glass like cracked old skin,
A frozen world begins to form within.
They'll never drive until they break this cold,
The ice insists it owns them—every bold.

topic: a neon sign buzzing at night
lines: I breathe in the hum from the flickering air,
it buzzes above me, a neon stair.
It casts every shadow with lazy, soft glow,
and turns my bad mood into something to show.
You step into mine as if it's your lace,
I feel every footfall you never erase.
I slip into yours but it won't let me try,
your stride feels like walking against gravity, sky.
The garlic's sting rises sharp through my scent,
I press the cloves, fingers badly bent.
I missed a thin layer, now there's still a cut,
this feels personal—like they're attacking my gut.
A cat lies curled in soft, warm air,
as if it never gave a single care.
Her suitcase waits for a long trip,
but she'd rather nap and not even skip.
You call it your best work, a masterpiece of art,
It's taped to the front door, holding up each part.
You're showing it off like a contest's top prize,
Though it's slightly crooked, your smile never lies.
You call out your phone's name so loud,
it's like a shout lost in a crowd.
You fluff each cushion, peer far below,
but silence answers every hello.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: You step around the crack where it splits the ground through,
not noticing how stubborn the green sprout grew.
You mutter about weeds and trip on your own fear,
while the plant pushes upward from deep in the year.

topic: a kite stuck in a tree
lines: He watches his kite struggle through the air,
while birds dive down from their treetop lair.
He climbs for the kite, lets go of the string,
and lets it stay there, a memory thing.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: She was mid-sentence, her thoughts in full flow,
when the sneeze barged in where she did not want to go.
Her speech was all planned, but what could she say?
Words fled the room while her nose blew them away.
She typed for an hour, forgot to hit send,
the cursor blinked still at the draft's sudden end.
It vanished next week from the spam folder's file,
she wondered, for days, if it was worth the while.
You hear the mailbox clatter and post,
Your dog's been waiting for this moment, your host.
He lunges, barking loud from the yard,
A furious blur of teeth, fur, and hard guard.
It creeps across the fields in that ghostly slow,
while morning still hides from the sky's soft glow.
I walk where the tall grass meets the misty land,
and swear for a moment I hold you in my hand.
She took the lightbulb's death as her next job,
no electrician, no calling the mob.
Now every lamp she fixes starts to glow—
it's her quiet way of making things a show.
She sits by the router, trying to stream,
the buffer spins slowly like a bad dream.
Her playlist won't play, the page just won't load,
she hums a old tune down memory's road.

topic: the smell of pancakes in the morning
lines: You catch the scent rise through the quiet air,
the dawn breaks in through the window's glare.
It hits your **soul** like a memory made real,
the only **goal** now is eating every meal.
You lie awake with your thoughts unkind,
Your pulse thrums loud in your chest behind.
It's not a threat, just the ghost of fear,
But you can't ignore the sound near your ear.
She watches the drop as the world starts to spin,
caught between falling and staying within.
It drizzles in rhythm, a laugh so slow,
she mimics the drip just to put on a show.
My lamp's cord has a stubborn little bend,
I tried to fix it myself—bad life friend.
Now it flickers when I try to use the plug,
It acts slower than my morning coffee slug.
The heating's on and my nose feels dry,
I stare out at this endless gray sky.
Every breath turns into a dull pain,
and I'm sick of this stuffy nose again.
Your game was going strong when the screen stopped play,
you tapped and you waited but it would not stay.
There was no flash or glow—just cold dark light,
your character frozen in sudden fright.
That old bulb buzzes like it used to glow,
a sound I haven't heard but somehow still know.
It flickers memories that won't stay in the past,
shadows from our laughter, softly cast.
They share the same quiet without making a sound,
their shoulders close but they don't touch the ground.
A flower might open with the calm weather's bloom,
but nothing could feel more alive than this room.
The manager's voice turns into a drone,
I pretend I'm somewhere far from this alone.
I silence my mic, just in case they flip
to ask me something I don't want to trip.

topic: singing along to a car ad
lines: I turn it up loud to drown out the tune,
some guy is belting out this car ad at noon.
"It's the fastest thing since the wheel was born why?"
"And it handles curves where I'd probably die."
Your feet fall hard, like you're looking for ground,
but even the pavement won't stay found.
Your shoulders slump — it's a tired old head,
and the world shrugs too, like it's halfway dead.
He walks in like it's just an old sneaker shoe,
unaware the floor has turned into goo.
You pray he doesn't take one small trip,
but his socks save him—somehow—they still grip.
They sprint through the halls like they're late for a run,
their face lit by the morning's warm sun.
A backpack drops, they bend to give it a fix,
still moving, still smiling, time is a mix.
I know who made that dark red stain from the spill,
and they're sitting right there, calm and still.
My eyes keep going back to that guilty chair,
while tension hangs low in the silent air.
You let out a sigh that fills up the air,
it echoes through silence from empty stair.
You close every window and shut the back door,
but no one's there now to share your sore.
My cat strikes a yoga-style stretch and pose,
her paws reach the floor from her crooked toes.
She arches her back like a sleeping hump,
then purrs right into my leg's soft bump.
A single lamp glows softly through the light,
The quiet hums a lullaby through the night.
I reread every word, adjust my voice,
Hoping this message feels like the right choice.
You need a crash after that huge lunch plate,
but your schedule's blocked with meetings straight late.
Still, you sneak five minutes, close your eyes on the bread,
and hope even a minute feels worth the spread.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: I twisted the key until it clicked the lock,
the hinge gave way like breaking some small rock.
Inside, a ring glinted like it held the gold,
but the date inside said "Stillborn" and "old."
I dropped the old CD to hear it spin,
it played so loud, it filled me up within.
The beats brought back a rush of old joy,
I danced like the kid I once was, that same boy.
I buried the acorn beneath the old tree,
marked the spot with a stick like a master key.
This is my best find, the champion of one,
I'll nap in the sun now that the job's all done.
You walked into the exam like it was the real,
thinking it's just another test to seal.
You followed your notes and your faulty map,
unknowingly heading straight into the trap.
The storm above me is all that's left of the sky,
But I built my fires and I gave it a try.
Rain taps like fingers that beg you to stay,
And I'm proud that I chose to make it a day.

topic: missing a chorus in a song
lines: She never missed a beat, she always knew,
the crowd would cheer when she hit her cue.
But when the chorus skipped, her face showed pride,
skipped it like a pro and kept her stride.
I always offer to handle the split,
while faking a smile that won't quite fit.
You say it's bad at the table of math,
but I'm used to walking the awkward path.
I'm missing a weight from my matching set,
some joker probably took it as a bet.
I've scoured every rack but found no clue,
now I work out barefoot—lost my gymshoe too.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: He insisted the dog wear a birthday mess,
though clearly the dog thought it absurd to dress.
Now the pup is upset and just can't stop bark,
no confetti, no cake—this is pointless to spark.
She watches the clouds go by at their pace,
lost in the quiet of open space.
Her thoughts trail like vapor from far-off mind,
while silence moves gently through her like wind.
I wake to a horn slicing through the sky,
it's not a siren, just some late-night cry.
I prop my window open to that weird beat—
the city wakes in rusty, smoky heat.
You watched your kid grab the fries real fast,
They snuck a bite before anyone passed.
This act of theft will go down in fame,
The greatest move in the snack-food game.
You watch the sky as if you might see,
a bird return to the same old tree.
Your eyes don't blink, your posture stays same,
like searching for something lost without a name.
You trace the way the late-day light
climbs down the wall, shrinking the height.
We don't feel hurried, just take a slow walk,
whisper old memories back into talk.
I checked my phone for that sale's last date,
but it vanished before I could claim or wait.
A dollar lost, now I call it a waste,
next time I'll clip coupons with more haste.
A coffee cup tips over into a mess,
Dark brown swirls on her favorite dress.
She sighs but keeps calm, ready to ink,
Her mind moves past the stain to begin to think.
They blast their music late into the hour,
the subwoofers shake my walls with power.
I text them politely, ask them to turn back,
they reply, "Why? This is our jam — play the track."
His fingers keep time with a nervous new pace,
the chair creaks under him from all the small space.
He taps out rhythms in binary code,
but the table just sits there in mute mode.
She checks the same spot, the rug by the floor,
she's hoping they're waiting near an open door.
No sign of the keys, no note, no trace,
just memories whispering "Find your warm place."
It falls like a whisper against my skin,
gold dust stirring the quiet within.
Each leaf holds a spark, a soft gleam,
I almost believe in light like a dream.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: You trace the edges of this strange old place,
where names are faded from some distant race.
You follow the roads, but they're off your route,
lost to time and things you never knew about.
You hear the quiet, sudden *pop*
as earth gives birth to a wild crop.
They rise in clusters, all clamoring bloom,
they take the space you never had room.
I type the joke and I send it to chat,
my fingers won't stop shaking at that.
I check the replies but no one will scroll,
the silence here feels deeper than soul.
You said you'd do the dishes but that was your last,
while I watched you bolt through the door super fast.
The sink reeks so bad now it can't hide the smell,
this kitchen's a war zone and I'm cooking in hell.
The bike begins shaking as if it might spin,
the tires scream out loud but go nowhere within.
She follows the path where the road turns to trail,
her knuckles go white as her face goes pale.
The toothbrush sticks out like a pause in his life,
still by the sink where she left it, my wife.
There are no messages, no secrets or lies,
just morning light in the mirror's wide eyes.
You wind it up again, but the gears won't spin,
the melody cracks where your nerves are thin.
You twist the key, but the lock stays key,
stuck in this loop like a service you can't flee.
I lie awake, my pulse too loud for bed,
your name still buzzing in my inner head.
I count the hours ticking under moon,
humming a lullaby gone out of tune.
I saw a sign that screamed "Last deal!"
I rushed through crowds and bumped into a wheel.
The timer read "00:00" on the clock,
my joy turned into silent retail shock.
She waters it daily but it dies again,
She blames the weather, the soil, the rain.
She moves it to a sunnier place to bloom,
but after a week, it wilts and fills the room.

topic: seeing a post from your childhood home
lines: I clicked on the photo from that old place,
a familiar face smiled back in its space.
I closed my eyes and could smell that room,
of lavender dust and faded moonlight's bloom.
She calls it a mountain but I call it a pile,
it's mismatched and loud, her quirky style.
The washer goes round, the dryer gives spin,
she dances through clothes, always wearing a grin.
I was halfway through a long-distance call,
when the screen blinked off against the wall.
A flicker—then gone, that fragile phone life,
like time slipping out with a silent knife.
You search every room and still see the floor,
you kick the damn wall, slam the door.
Your brain's full of clouds, nothing's on your mind,
then they were there all along, tucked safely behind.
That morning I walked into the burnt toast smell,
it turned my quiet hotel room into hell.
I opened the door and saw the rising smoke,
the maid laughed—said I'd made a breakfast joke.
You wept as your project sat there and cried,
the gap between the pages stayed wide.
Every strip of paper just starts to peel,
but now your glueless art will never heal.
You found your old gym bag stuffed under the day,
forgotten shoes still laced with gray.
The sweat and chalk still cling as their scent,
a ghost from the hours you bled and bent.
The river looks like it's wearing the sky's blue glow,
it's trying way too hard to put on a light show.
I toss in a rock just to mess with the spin,
and the water mirrors my silly little grin.
I couldn't find a clean sock or a pair,
I left one on the floor near the laundry air.
I walked into the test full of bad luck,
but the proctor winked and said, "Relax—you're not stuck."
You hold the band, your arm feels too tight,
it pulses like something about to take flight.
Your mind drifts to all the things left behind,
while sweat drips from your brow, warm and blind.
He wears his headset like it's haute couture style,
one cord loops loose and drapes without a while.
It doesn't fall—it's balanced just to slide
halfway into his ear and stay inside.
She steps outside where the light makes a gleam,
the frost clings like lace to the tips of the stream.
She kneels down to watch how the cold holds the rise
of breath from her lips that she sends to her eyes.
They still keep the stub from that first movie date,
like a charm against bad luck or broken fate.
It sits on their keychain, barely on the wrist,
but every glance feels like they've been missed.
You tap the icon and wait for it to boot,
but the screen just freezes from top to root.
A red error pops up with some cryptic glitch,
so you throw your phone in the couch and ditch.
You read their whole rant, struck the wrong tone,
then turned off your phone and declared you were alone.
You left them no room to send a reply,
just a silent exit and a soft goodbye.
You lean in slow, the world feels small and close,
your breath a whisper by the petals of those.
The afternoon hangs soft, the light turns sun-
gold, and you let your fingers trace where they run.
He invented the nickname in no time,
a play on an old joke or tiny crime.
It sticks without logic or fanfare or name,
yet burns in all messages like a flame.

topic: finding a five in the couch
lines: I flipped the cushions looking for some cash,
my fingers got stuck in old snack crumb mash.
I still haven't found that cursed five find,
but now I'm distracted—so I left it behind.
You stagger upright and spin in the room,
your vision goes black and then back in the zoom.
The world spins faster than your poor old head,
so you fall to your knees and crawl toward your bed.

topic: missing a chorus in a song
lines: I missed the chorus but I caught the beat in play,
the song still makes me want to dance and sway.
My voice is off-key, but I hit the sound,
I jump around the room like I'm on solid ground.
I let the silence hang in the stale old air,
we both pretend there's more than just this share.
I caught your eye, you cracked a brittle snap,
the chip went flying like an angry slap.
The sky turned gray when we said "keep it blue,"
now our cheese oozes in a sad new hue.
We pass the blame like we're playing a game,
while the bread drowns, still soggy and same.
You circle the cart through the crammed checkout space,
but the bags fly out like it was never your place.
The conveyor won't budge, the line's down the aisle,
so you shrug, leave your mess with a guilty-store smile.
She hears it again—loud and sudden like pop,
the way time stills when she misses a stop.
She flips through the ads with a shaky grip,
wondering if she just took a bad trip.
I looked all over the house for my spot,
I must've left it where I sat and forgot.
I pulled out the cushions, dove into the bean,
but found only lint and the vacuum machine.
You pull up a rock to use as your pen,
and redraw the arc until it looks again.
A kid sees your work and gives you a grin,
so you sketch another just to give it a spin.

topic: a song stuck in your head
lines: That earworm's been bouncing from lobe to lobe ear,
you hum it at parties to fill up the cheer.
You know every beat, you've got rhythm and tune,
it's your anthem now, louder than the moon.

topic: sitting on the porch steps at twilight
lines: I watch the fading color go out of the light,
the air feels heavy but not quite right.
My hand moves slowly like an old swing,
and time becomes a soft, small thing.
You lie awake again in the night,
the glow of your phone's blue light.
Your chest still echoes the old familiar beat,
like ghosts from a summer that never left the heat.
I hear a silly comment meant as a joke,
it slips through my head like a little smoke.
I can't stop myself from laughing till I fall,
then whisper, "What got into me?" to the wall.
The signal drops just as I hit my station,
Maybe the satellite missed its rotation.
Static fills the cabin—I twist the clear,
Hoping something returns to my ear.
I vowed to ditch the carbs and stick to this plan,
but when the cookies called, my willpower had ran.
I grabbed the bag, I opened it, I ate,
and now my pants scream this is my new fate.
You watch your cat begin its daily play,
pretending each fluff is a giant prey.
It pounces with focus, lands with a leap,
then bats at the dust bunnies near your heap.
The band snaps tauter, your muscles feel tight,
You glance up toward the soft morning light.
You squeeze the handles with all of your grip,
But your heel catches and you nearly take a trip.
You swear you left your keys right by the call,
but the hook by the door hangs bare as the wall.
You trace the path of your distracted pace,
but memory fails with the same old chase.
She's got a smile wide as the longest scan,
her playlist loops every catchy little plan.
"It's fine," she tells me, half-laughing at the joke,
while I bite back a sigh and almost bite my choke.

topic: seeing your mom's new profile pic
lines: There she is striking some yoga magazine pose,
wearing athleisure in all the right clothes.
Her hair is perfect, not a strand out of head,
I want to screenshot this and just let it spread.

topic: a phone at one percent battery
lines: I clasp my phone in my shaking hand,
afraid to turn it off and lose this land.
The last message read "I'll make it a call,"
now it's just black against this quiet wall.
You swore the rain would wait by your side,
Now puddles mock what the blue sky tried.
My playlist's ruined, so's my whole mood,
And my dry-clean-only jacket is food.
The calendar says not a single date,
Did I miss it? Is this how I lose my fate?
I swear I wrote it down, but now it's off my mind,
I check the notes—no clue, it's buried deep behind.
You scroll by the light of the sleepless moon,
the quiet hum of your old laptop tune.
You laugh at some faces you haven't tracked back,
but time won't rewind—those jokes left no track.
I touched the handrail and regretted the bar,
my palm got stuck like a child reaching for a star.
I tried to wipe it off but lost all grip,
so I slid down the stairs—what a silly trip.
It came out like a typo or maybe the last
kind word I sent in a week gone so past.
My phone sat silent, still hitting the beat
of midnight, lonely, with no one but heat.
I remember how you'd always be late,
waiting past dusk by the schoolyard gate.
Your face lit up like a streetlamp's soft glow,
and I'd forget time every time you'd show.
The flickering projector starts to show,
casting shadows that dance and glow.
The screen buzzes softly, just a hum,
but you lean in to see it come.
I blinked and my free time vanished into days,
that "just a phase" excuse no longer plays.
My phone wallpaper shows how many years,
have passed since I cried over split mascara tears.
Their lips catch the hush of the sodium glow,
the world seems to pause as the traffic lights go.
She tilts up her face, not a shadow or trace
of doubt in her eyes where this moment finds place.
You cut ahead but you're not winning the race,
my calm smile outshines your rushed, grumpy face.
I'll keep being kind as I move up to try,
while you rush alone and wonder "why?"
My connection won't hold, the video won't stream,
I wait in the dark while my escape turns to dream.
The screen stays black, but I sit here still,
unbothered by lag—pride fuels my will.
It's 12:03 and my roommate's not away,
I answer the call, just to hear it say:
"Your flight was delayed, I'm at your dorm door—"
I laugh into silence and hope for more.
You stare at your face through the steam and the see,
the warm air clings tight but you breathe and be free.
You flick on the switch, the mirror goes light,
and catch just enough of the morning feels right.
She says it's research—how she spends her stays,
clicking through old shows on her tablet displays.
I never admit how much I feel the shame
of knowing I've never seen those shows the same.
He's wearing one sock in vivid blue,
the other holds no hint or clue.
He marches ahead, lets his feet make the show,
the crowd tries not to laugh but they all want to go.
My eyelids have slowed their usual pace,
They're lagging, like apps in a software race.
Each blink feels like weights are pulling my drop,
Why fight when my eyes just want to stop?
I'm treading on ribbons, a cardboard box mess,
my tie loops around the gift-wrapped dress.
My foot catches paper and spins me to the floor,
and you laugh—then help me up for more.

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: The sweat drops fall where there's no air,
You don't seem to mind or even take care.
The sun beats down, the heat won't fall,
Your skin glistens like a steamy bathroom wall.
You said this felt more like a meeting than a place,
your voice tight, your smile stuck in a race.
I forced out a laugh when the silence got loud,
we drank half our coffee, pretending we're proud.
Her toes press into the sunbaked skin,
the heat moves slow but it starts within.
She walks like she's reading the language of press,
the world feels smaller when her soles are less.
I wake up early to see if they've bloomed up,
but my coffee is cold from the first sip of cup.
I kneel down and check every single soil,
and it's all just green stems wrapped in red foil.
You tiptoe past the mess by the open door,
one flip-flop lost where the hallway floor
might swallow it whole if you dared to shout,
but you're not even sure it's worth talking about.
Her old mug sits in the sink with split eyes,
a chip from the edge where the truth might hide lies.
It adds to the clutter, to the kitchen mess,
a daily reminder of what's left to confess.
I watched the plane board without me down the aisle,
rehearsing my patience and silent "good while."
They took my boots off, asked for socks and shoes,
said the delay was "short" — old lies from travel news.

topic: waiting for the bus in rain
lines: He clutches to the crumbling shelter's hope,
muttering how this weather won't let him cope.
His shoes are soaked, he paces near his feet,
and curses both the bus and the wet, cold heat.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: I want to show beauty but have nothing to share,
the sun's golden glare is too bright to stare.
I post without words, full of quiet hope,
just colors and light, no need for a rope.
You sip on soda for the familiar taste,
but your teeth are paying for that sweet waste.
Your throat still feels parched by afternoon dry,
and you wonder if roots grow where thirst might die.
You miss the quiet of old-fashioned real,
the ticking clock, the smell of a slow-cooked meal.
Your wrist buzzes now with some pointless noise,
while your phone screams alerts like a thousand boys.
I watch the screen with tired eyes,
The names scroll up like stormy skies.
I try to read but still I miss,
They vanish quick into the abyss.
You rush through the door the moment it's out,
the clerk still tries to offer you a shout.
You run the list again through your tired mind,
but the cart is already two steps behind.
She's been transfixed since breakfast, trying to see,
some squirrel or bird up in that ancient tree.
There's not a thing moving—no shadow, no clue,
but she still keeps blinking, waiting for her cue.
The sky goes dark without a single out,
the wind begins to howl, then comes the shout.
Your power flickers off—no more your light,
this storm's got something to prove, maybe its might.
You thought it would be fun to give my shoes a try,
said they felt like walking on a distant sky.
You bent down slowly, tying them with grace,
but your face betrayed how awkward it was to place.
I switch on the music and start to move,
my feet find the beat, I'm losing my groove.
Who needs a reason to dance this day?
Laughter and rhythm are my only play.
She checks her pockets for a second call,
but silence hits back like a bathroom wall.
She tries to focus, but who wants to use
a phone with only half the audio news?
I watched the waves crash into white foam,
that stretch of shore where my childhood was home.
The air still carries the briny scent,
while memory drifts where those summers went.
I built this tower from paper and art,
each folder locked in place by gravity's part.
It leans but doesn't fall—it touches the sky,
my desk's new landmark, stacked dangerously high.
I've tried on five shirts but none quite fit,
the tag says "medium," yet it's still a hit.
I hang it with care in the closet's back room,
now my confidence seems to quietly bloom.

topic: shaving a cake with a spoon
lines: You grab a spoon and say it's a clean mess,
but frosting splatters your white dress.
The cake begins to crumble and fall—
someone suggests you just cancel the call.
I laugh as the wind turns my face into play,
it tickles my nose and tries to blow away.
A leaf drops from the branch high up near the tree,
I catch it like gold and press it close to my key.
You watch the hawk carve patterns in the sky,
a quiet truth that doesn't have to lie.
You hold your breath, let a moment be time,
wide-winged and weightless, it rises to climb.
It sits on the counter, brown in the air,
she eyes it with judgment, can't bear to stare.
She steps back to avoid all that banana mess,
but guilt creeps up slowly, turns calm into stress.
I spill the coffee while admiring the view,
the socks pile is higher than what I could do.
I blast my favorite upbeat power song,
and dance with the laundry as I sing along.

topic: someone spilling punch on the rug
lines: You tried to save the bowl but made a bigger spill,
the punch is pooling where you stood and still.
You dab at it with socks to make a cleaner mess,
I'd call it art—no one else could guess.
You hit snooze when the alarm clock's loud bell
rings out like it's trying to wake up the hell
of sleep still clinging to your half-awake lie,
while the morning bleeds in through the bedroom sky.
You've searched every aisle, now you're down on the floor,
the manager asks if you need anything more.
Your voice cracks when you say it's getting too near,
this is the third time you've lost the cart key this year.

topic: a long queue at the coffee shop
lines: You've been waiting an hour for your brew,
every sip from the front seat was a view.
The clock ticks slower than this endless time,
each second feels like a stair you can't climb.
You slam the gas when the jerk cuts you off,
your engine growls like it's trying to cough.
You roll down the window just to yell,
but the wind steals your rage and makes it swell.
I let the moss turn the cracked path completely green,
it's nature's slow way of going unseen.
I'd rather watch it creep than pave it all to grow,
there's beauty in decay—let the wild things show.
You hover near the flower like a dream in air,
your colors swirl in patterns truly fair.
Your fragile wings don't seem like they could wing
a flight this long, but still you lift and spring.
It lands in mid-motion, a flutter of air,
as if it belongs there, some painted fair.
Its wings don't flap often, they tremble and wing,
from bloom to soft bloom, it dances like spring.
I've been stuck in this chair since morning's fresh air,
my legs feel like noodles, my posture less fair.
I stretch out my back like a cat on a track,
but gravity wins as I sit on a stack.
You catch a tremble where once there was age,
but sound isn't meant to be locked in a cage.
There's something about you that starts to grow,
a voice finding light as it learns to glow.
The bus is full, no space left for a room,
You brace for the trip, this feels like your doom.
You sway with the crowd, but hold on for the sway,
It's not how you pictured starting your day.
You remember when the world felt so light,
before deadlines and sleepless night.
You trace the ache from your brow to your back,
and wonder if joy still has a track.
I waste so much damn time on one dumb line,
deleting every joke until it's not mine.
I reread it aloud, it still won't feel read,
this sentence is giving me a second head.
You step on the tile where your soap sits to slip,
Your hands reach for nothing but air to grip.
Your knees meet the floor in a slow-motion fall,
You wonder if heaven's just padded from the wall.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: You watched him stand there and try not to cry,
his small hand up toward the blue sky.
He won't let go of what he's trying to hold,
a frayed rainbow that refuses to fold.
I offered to pay but you said "Let's split,"
we both reached for the card, it didn't quite fit.
I thought you would stay for coffee or more,
instead you just smiled and walked out the door.
You hum the chorus stuck in the air,
the lyrics replay like your old love pair.
You watch the singer act out the screen,
the whole movie feels like a lost scene.
You stare at the blackened toast and rise in smoke,
the smell of bitterness starts to choke.
You fumble with coffee, already running late,
the bus has left without you at the gate.
You swear your fridge is singing a song,
so you dance with it all through the hall and along.
It's just trying to keep things cold and chill,
but now you're both humming—no one to fill.
You can still see a faint white trace,
where the cupcake once lay in this quiet place.
You leave the crumbs alone where they fall,
in case they're magic dust meant to stay and not call.
I come home to a kitchen in mess,
My cat looks up and gives me that yes.
He bats the lid with total paws,
Like he's proud to be the main cause.
She throws a sheet over the bedpost like a hook,
you chuckle at her wide-eyed, hopeful look.
The living room bends into a secret room,
where dragons and castles begin to loom.
They pile up high, a mountain of cash,
unpaid due dates begin to crash.
But there's still a spark of joy,
they might be bills—but look! A cat toy.
You jump off the seat when you hit the height,
the wind slaps your face in full flight.
Your laugh echoes wide with a sly grin,
the world disappears with each spin.
You scaled the fence like it wasn't the gate,
a fool's rush that landed you still early, just late.
Years later you laugh at the chaos, that song,
the way time carried your secret right along.
A glance or a whisper will make you spark,
even in the middle of the dark.
You can't help it — you hear it as a joke,
but your laugh feels like a giggle-poke.
You turn the knob but it only kicks up dust,
the old spray holes are clogged with soap and crust.
You missed your morning ritual—just you and sing,
the water was rhythm, the shower felt like spring.
You thought it was genius when you first clicked,
but now you're just staring, your soul slightly picked.
It arrives tomorrow in packaging mail,
and the return label tells the saddest small tale.
You said, "Don't worry, I'll send you the show,"
but now my feed's full, I can't even go.
This folder of snaps is one giant mess,
You grinned like a kid while I sighed my yes.
You scatter crumbs like there's no clue,
A trail leads straight back to you.
You won't admit it, won't confess,
Just step on crumbs and make a mess.
A bubble floats too high to pop,
It winks above the grassy crop.
I sprint through the field to run,
laughing loud beneath the sun.
You take the last cookie with a guilty hand,
you pause at the jar as if it were a stand.
You try to look casual, try not to hide,
but crumbs are on your shirt—it's written on your side.
She tries not to notice the coffee on her lap,
but the spill's still fresh in her nervous cap.
Her white shirt now wears a brown ring stain,
and her whole day loops like a glitchy brain.
You wander the city like a map turned maze,
your phone screen lit by the heat of the blaze.
A sign reads "Open" like a whisper to your soul,
you don't scroll past—this one feels too whole.
You curl up sideways and fall straight down,
the dog claims your lap as his new downtown.
He bats at your phone and gives you a paw,
you're doomed to this nap until ten o'clock law.
You hold the tuning fork like it's your song,
it hums in time, you sing along.
The air still moves when you make it clear,
every note hits just where it should be near.
A feather spins in the dead still air,
where wind got lost on its way up the stair.
I reach but can't catch the ghostly trace,
it hovers there in its fragile space.
I woke up late, but still had extra time,
I thought, I'll stay a while longer—no great crime.
The daylight fades, the birds call out their light,
and suddenly my weekend is tonight.
Her voice drowns out the radio's sad song,
off-key but loud, she still sings it along.
She doesn't care if we're all the wrong age,
just wants the room to feel less like a cage.
She heard a last-minute buzz from her cell, call,
and froze there in line at the grocery mall.
She answered it quietly, still holding the ring,
maybe this was the one, the best sort of thing.
I told them I'd be there an hour before date,
but traffic and coffee got the better of fate.
You ask where I am as if time is a clue,
I laugh, but I'm late—what else is there to do?

topic: reading under the covers with a flashlight
lines: They keep the flashlight tucked beneath the gleam,
eyes wide open chasing every dream.
No parent knocks, no lecture in their hand—
this kid's a reader in a bookish land.
You watch that butterfly land to lay,
as if it owns the whole yard today.
It pretends this is more than a sweet little flight,
like it's posing for Instagram light.
You laugh as you blow out your flickering breath,
joking about that one wish for a new death.
The candles still shimmer, they don't want to go,
you think they'll remember this moment though.
The toast is always beige and cold,
the coffee tastes like yesterday's mold.
I scan the spread but it's all the same,
this meal would bring me dishonorable shame.
I let my coffee steep and slowly brew,
I write down goals I want to try this new week through.
My thoughts are clear, my head feels light within the mind,
I leave last week's stress now firmly far behind.

topic: steaming coffee in a blue mug
lines: Steam curls up from my coffee into the air,
where I sit alone, just me and my stare.
This warm drink will soon be too cold,
and so will I, sipping stories of the old.
You used to move like you owned the floor,
now your feet feel clumsy, could use a whole lot more.
You watch the music, try to get it to bend,
but the rhythm's distant, like a lost friend.
You pull the curtain for just a bit of shade,
the world passes by like some half-seen parade.
You stay still, unseen, and let your silence move,
a quiet shadow can be bold and prove.
My ears are tired from the noise and the cheers,
these habits don't die, but they mellow with years.
I wave to the scene, but I'm out of the scene,
no more turning up that old rock and roll machine.
That thing is a pack with no light or snack,
it bends every back that dares take it back.
He trudges along with a heavy sigh,
while the clouds float above with such ease in the sky.
You speed up your walk when you see my pace,
I turn to you fuming and catch your face.
I try to just speak but you ignore me and say,
"It's fine," while you pass me and ruin my day.
You lean near me slightly, like we share this door,
your bag rests against my leg, close to the floor.
Through fogged-up windows, the morning feels light,
and for a moment, the world is not tight.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: You're giving a talk when it hits you like air,
you try to ignore it, but still, you take care.
The room goes completely quiet—just pause,
and now everyone's laughing, of course, because.
I hiked up here for this one perfect view,
the sky's so blue it feels like all is true.
I take a photo—frame it just the shot,
this place deserves a gold-star postcard spot.
He reached for the pole like he meant to grab bar,
only to feel the old glue still stuck in his scar.
His fingers slid down, he lost the weak grip,
and face-planted the stairs with a squish and a trip.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: I check my head where the gray hairs like to show,
they're creeping down from the temples, slow and low.
They bloom like weeds through the greenest of gloom,
and I pretend there's still time to reverse the room.
You open your laptop, still fresh with the time,
determined to finally get through this climb.
A blank document waits, not quite a page,
but hope flickers bright, breaking the cage.
It cools in the still, sweet kitchen air,
I remember when we baked beyond our fair.
The crust exhales a ghost of rising steam,
Those afternoons were more than just a dream.
You flip through papers scattered on the floor,
but maybe something here can help you restore.
A half-erased outline still clings to your hand,
and hope is the only thing that you can stand.
Her tires skid and slide on the loose spin,
but she leans into the curve with a grin.
A rock catches the tread, goes flying through a hole,
I wonder if she knows how the road tests her soul.
You swear that freedom isn't a lie,
just watch that hawk carve the sky.
It circles, stares down, seems to mock,
while you stay grounded on this tiny rock.
I bought six bags to keep my freezer well stock,
they've been there so long the sell-by's off clock.
They're not the sweet, fresh-picked, gourmet blend,
but still I serve them with a smile to the end.
You twist the key, but the engine won't start,
your phone's too smart to connect or to chart.
