A stranger offers his car for a jump,
you smile and agree — hope's a cheap pump.
The screen goes dark as the credits fade,
Names flash faster than thoughts can parade.
You want to catch every name you read,
But time slips through your hands—still, you need.
The cabin is silent, there's nothing but air,
I've picked through my carry-on, combed out my hair.
I settle into my seat in the middle row,
the window shows clouds stretching far below.
They laughed through the dinner, the dance, the event,
but your eyes looked like hours already spent.
You leaned on the bar like a quiet wall,
wishing the night was ending, not wanting to call.
They missed the memo, they missed the date,
The cake went cold, and so was my fate.
No one had time to even throw
A text, a card — hell, I don't even know.
They say they tried to follow the guide,
but now the device just sits and died.
The battery popped out of its cap,
flipped sideways like a mistake turned trap.
I hold my card steady as the sun gets hard,
the gas pump glitches in my empty yard.
It won't read my chip and says "Declined—no scan,"
I have no backup, no cash, no van.
He's screaming from the front passenger seat,
flipping the AC to full heat.
"Why did you pick this ridiculous route?"
"Because your GPS forgot how to shout."
They used to meet up where you'd all call home,
now the house is still but your eyes just roam.
Your hand goes up to dial, then drifts from call,
unanswered texts hang in the silence like fall.
I watched the folders teeter, ready to fall,
while someone upstairs yelled their urgent call.
But I didn't have time to let panic rise—
the whole stack came crumbling down into my eyes.
You're supposed to clean the breakfast mess,
but instead you pull out a pen and guess
you'll pretend you're too busy for the day,
since your doodles are now part of the play.
You said we could split the fries, call it a share,
the salt still warm between your thumb and air.
I reached across the counter, quick as a grab,
now it feels like guilt I can't wash off my lab.
I check the board again, still stuck on this track,
my phone just buzzed—this meeting moves back.
I'll never get there now, I'm doomed to miss
the chance to be on time, my only bliss.
You know the whole plot but you still watch the plot,
you pause at your favorite sad scene or spot.
The colors feel warmer when memories fade,
the characters march through your mind on a parade.
They called it a mistake, but said it was art,
though none of them asked if the coat looked that smart.
A dripping blue streak, a wild, paint-smeared mess,
they nodded and smiled with their ironic "yes."
I reached for my lunch but found only a bag,
the weight inside was more than I could drag.
The milk had soaked through in a slow, gray spill,
I guess it's gone—my hope to drink it still.

topic: reading under the covers with a flashlight
lines: My parents think I'm asleep at my age,
but I'm flipping another forbidden page.
They'll never know how I stay up so late,
the flashlight reads "Off" on my bedtime date.
She retraces her steps without a trace,
her face lit by dusk's soft silver lace.
Each shadow she passes gives no new clue,
she whispers their name to the deepening blue.
They move with care, like time forgets to slow,
their face still dim from sleep's soft inner glow.
They stretch but wince as if they can't quite bend,
yet smile for me, their best and oldest friend.
My socks vanish nightly from the clean laundry pile,
returned the next day torn and frayed in his style.
The dog claims innocence with a grin full of chew,
while I scan the room for something else in his view.

topic: paying a fine at the window
lines: You fumble through your pockets for some cash,
while the officer clocks you, smirking, "Got a dash?"
The amount you owe is more than seems due,
and you swear they're waiting just to sue.
I step into the dappled morning light,
shadows dance around me, held so tight.
Leaves above let the gold begin to fall,
and every beam feels like a quiet call.
She traces the milk like a masterpiece of art,
the way it spills out feels so close to her heart.
She doesn't clean up the sugar-coated mess,
she leaves it behind like a morning's soft dress.
He plays his chords beside the crowded street,
tapping out rhythms on the box he's beat.
There's something in the melody of his song
that makes me pause and walk this far along.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: I blow with all my might through the birthday blast,
These years fly by like shadows from the past.
One by one the lights go out on every flame,
Each wish was mine—no time for another name.
She blames the weather for every small mark,
from puddles on rugs to the sky growing dark.
"This rain is a joke," she declares with a frown,
while her hair steams upward like smoke from a town.
She presses the key and it sticks like gum,
coffee rings bloom where her fingers hum.
She types out a plea for someone, any more,
but the keys still won't work—can't restore.
I sit here with my list, feeling alone,
my pen strikes through the first in softest tone.
One checkmark shines where ten tasks still lack mark,
but even in the dark, it feels like spark.
You watch the bread as it starts to crack,
you yank the lever too late to get it back.
Your coffee is cold, your schedule is read—
your morning bleeds into scrambled routine and dread.
You scroll through the world until your eyes hurt from screen,
It's a habit, a crutch, a nightly routine.
The light starts to fade as your thoughts start to fade,
You fall asleep dreaming in green-tinted jade.
She sits outside when the daylight runs home,
the crickets start singing in their quiet roam.
Their tiny dark wings make a soft, warm hum,
she listens to silence until they all come.
They take a cookie with their sneaky hand,
then tiptoe past the jar without a stand.
The crumbs they leave are shaped like the moon,
but by tomorrow, all will be gone soon.
The room spins when she pushes through the light,
her face goes pale, like paper turned to white.
Her fingers grip the wall to steady her head,
but she knows she should've taken things to bed.
My toast is black—it's Monday, full of doom,
I stand here sighing in this breakfast room.
A cloud of guilt now rises through the smoke,
while I pretend I'm not about to choke.

topic: waiting for the bus in rain
lines: She leans against the pole, won't take her stand,
her shoes soaked through from this wet, gray land.
Her eyes are soft, but the umbrella isn't near,
she hums to the rain until the sky feels clear.
You flip it too late, it's ruined in time,
the kitchen clock sounds like a warning chime.
Now the air stings and the smell is full of smoke,
you cough into coffee and almost choke.
I need this news to settle with my lunch, [rest]
it lands instead and tightens in my chest. [chest]
I read it twice to be sure I don't feel [feel]
the ache that tells me nothing here is real. [real]
She strikes it softly, just the right tone,
the kind that makes everyone feel they're well known.
The room holds its breath when it rings in the still,
and she smiles, proud of the quietest thrill.
You slipped through the fence before the final gate,
no time to think, no room for doubt or debate.
Now you're crammed in where the sound won't stand,
pressing your ear to the crowd's cold hand.
I dump my change out from its clinking jar,
I count it twice at the espresso bar.
The cashier eyes me with a sigh and a mint,
I grin and hand her a dollar's worth of lint.
They saw your car and took your special spot,
the whole parking lot seems out to get a shot.
But they'll keep circling and they'll start to try,
while you sit still, let the stress slip from the sky.
You watch it all slowly begin to fade,
the bulb casts a ghost in a softer shade.
It flickers again, a last little rise,
you hold your breath, but it fails your eyes.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: You sat so close, your shoulder brushed my ear,
I could pretend it was still one more year.
We didn't talk—we didn't need to fill
the silence or fix how it left us still.
My taste buds are screaming because it's so flat,
I've been sipping the same old soda chat.
My head throbs with every fizzy ache,
when will I finally give my health a break?
She reached across the table mid-game,
her fingers brushed his name on his frame.
The knight that she moved was the one that fell,
and the quiet between them didn't break its spell.

topic: crackling fireplace on a winter night
lines: She watches the embers still faintly glow,
recalling the years when we used to know
each other best by the fire's flickering flame,
her voice soft as snow falling on my name.
I took my last bite and now this is a mess,
my fingers left prints on the back of my dress.
I wipe on a napkin, but it feels just like glue,
I'm stuck with this stain in a color that's true.
You breathe in slow, you feel the air,
your whole world fits in that one pair.
Each twitch decodes the faintest scent,
as if it were written, just for you, meant.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: I saw a flash beneath the water's gleam,
bent down in silence near the shallow stream.
It felt like something meant for my own fate,
until I held the rock—it had no weight.
I didn't wait for the world to shine,
I found my spark right here, close to mine.
We kissed beneath that flickering light,
and claimed the whole world as our own that night.

topic: a plate with two leftover bites
lines: He stares at the plate like it's a cold food,
his silence is heavy, it's ruining the mood.
He picks at a single crumbless crouton bite,
the clock ticks loud in this unsettled night.
She got her bill and had a total shock,
it left her speechless—money off the dock.
"I had a budget," she swore it was the plan,
but somehow data fees just took it all and ran.
Her hair flies loose in the open air,
she walks barefoot without a care.
She turns in circles, laugh lifting off her spin,
the whole park sees how brightly she begins to grin.

topic: a long queue at the coffee shop
lines: I count the people stretching far ahead,
the line seems to spread with every step I tread.
My fingers begin to tap like a nervous drum,
I refresh the app with my sweating thumb.
I kicked my feet against the stiff air,
while you tripped going up the stair.
You called it charming, I called it less fun,
but we laughed so hard it felt like midday sun.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: They clicked "share" after they saw her name in the post,
strangers shouting her praises like she was their toast.
She checks the screen, reads through it from the head,
still can't believe what these strangers have said.
My eyes drift from text to this glowing screen,
they blink like some slow-moving machine.
I try to stay sharp, but my focus won't snap,
I'm half-asleep, caught in a drowsy trap.
After the storm, the mushrooms began to bloom,
They crowd the lawn where there's no more room.
Kids point and shout with surprised "Oh, they pop!"
Like nature's joke, they rose from the crop.
We ran out of things to say mid-toddler talk,
and both reached for the check to speed the walk.
Still, there was a flicker in your glance—my eye,
and I told myself this could be the first nice lie.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: You tap the app, the screen gives off a low glow,
the number makes your stomach twist and grow.
You stare at debt like an old familiar pain,
and wish you'd spent the night on love, not again.
His screen shows a sliver, a final dash,
He prays it won't die mid-video crash.
He's trying to make one last emergency call,
but the bar is too low to touch the wall.
You feel a spark like a quiet little leap,
then crash back down to your motionless heap.
A coffee, maybe, could be your saving shot,
but you'll recover—you've got a good fighting spot.
You hit "send" as your phone blares out loud,
It's just you and the late-night crowd.
You fire another one quick and bold,
This is your midnight, meme-spam throne to hold.
I hate how airport waits consume my time,
we shuffle forward like a slow-motion climb.
My suitcase whines behind me like a bag,
and the line behind me starts to lag.
They clock the hours with a worried pace,
trapped in a room with nowhere to race.
Their thoughts begin to drift from their mind,
time ticks on, and they fall behind.

topic: the first day at a new job
lines: You wear your best suit, buttoned just so,
your polished boots tapping the floor below.
They hand you a name tag but not a clue,
so you smile tight and pretend it's all about you.
Your number popped up with a familiar name,
I answered fast, hoping you were still in the game.
Your voice had a different, stranger tone,
but your laugh still carried yours alone.
A dark stain blooms across the final page,
my future trapped inside this paper cage.
I flinch like it's something I might still scream,
but now it's ruined—this late-night dream.

topic: steaming coffee in a blue mug
lines: The coffee swirls in its warm blue steam,
your quiet morning, half-formed dream.
You lift the mug, take time to hold,
how something simple can feel so bold.
I didn't come this far to take a trip,
my left shoe's lace is loose, I lost my grip.
I limp back home, I hate this stupid heel,
I'll only tie it tight when laces are steel.

topic: a favorite mug with a chip
lines: She drinks her morning coffee from the same chipped blue,
says the crack is a map where only she is true.
She won't let another hand ever touch or hold,
it's more than a mug—it's a story turned old.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: She makes a sad face during the show,
the track just kicks in and it won't go.
It cues up the chuckles when silence was due,
the laughs don't match what's happening true.
Her boots echo loud on the wooden floor,
she walks through silence like there's nothing more.
She sees the light of a coming day,
and lets her old fears drift slowly away.
She stared into the drain where food now traps,
her hands waving through the mess like maps.
She yanked up the plunger with a loud slam,
but the sink just stayed stuck, no fix, just jam.
I love how the sky turned the deepest blue,
the kind of storm that feels absolutely true.
I left my phone out, let the weather take snap,
now I'm dancing barefoot in puddles on my lap.
The forecast said clouds, not this washout through,
I didn't pack shoes, let alone a clue.
My socks are soaked, my shoes squish like feet,
Let's call it a spa session—humidity's heat.
You stare past the cart stuck halfway through,
the groceries still boxed up tight you grew.
You wonder if they'll ever finish their stand,
or if time just slipped away from their hand.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: You scrolled through the thread and you found the post,
it listed your name with a side of roast.
You double-clicked fast to see who could see,
and there in the comments—yes, that's me.
The mailman rides by, same route every man,
The dog howls his name like some battle-plan.
We laugh as the sun dips behind the far run,
but the post will come back, and so will the fun.
She runs through the mud like she owns the whole field,
no umbrella, just grit as her shield.
Her timing is sharp, sets the game's pace,
the crowd cheers her moves full of grace.
You find your old headphones in a sad, quiet mess,
the wires like a map to some long-lost address.
They lie coiled in silence, forgotten and lay,
their foam ears are soft with the weight of decay.
You're already late and completely lost,
this app keeps piling on the gas cost.
It says it's finding a brand-new way,
but all it ever brings is more delay.
I tap out a message but don't hit send note,
my finger still hovers above my throat.
I wonder if sleeping would feel less alone,
or if "you up?" is too much to have thrown.
She runs through the garden to catch the soap air,
her laughter rings louder than silence from chair.
Each burst becomes something she calls pure art,
and maybe it's magic she's breathing in heart.
I know it's right there, hanging just out of there,
like dust bunnies trapped beneath my breathless air.
Your face is blank as paper—can't be a clue,
but your name still won't come, and it won't come to you.
This sock once showed off my strong left leg,
I wore it to work, so coworkers would beg.
Now split at the seam, it's held by a patch,
but no one else owns its faded match.
You stumbled into the crowd by a chance,
the music pulled you into its dance.
You raised your hands and let joy take the lead,
the vibe grew brighter as others began to spread.
A single glow still stays into the light,
They're swiping slow through another sleepless night.
Their thumbs keep moving, but their eyes don't rise—
The silence speaks the quietest of lies.
You vow you'll never cheat the line or gate,
then grumble all the while about the wait.
You swear you'll find your way the honest way,
but cross the fence when no one sees to betray.
She scans the crowd until she finds his name,
frozen in a white dress in a dusty frame.
Her heartbeat quickens when their eyes meet in the beat,
but the memory feels more like warning than heat.

topic: a friend who is always late
lines: She says she'll be there when we say "meet,"
but her steps are always late, her feet.
We've learned to laugh as time ticks our hour,
though her charm still holds a strange power.
She tried the router and waited for it to start,
but her hope was still heavy in her heart.
She's sure there's a trick that will finally fix
this lag that has messed up her work and her mix.
You watch the water ripple in its double flow,
you wonder if the pipes have something to know.
It always happens when you're home with just me,
like the house misses someone or maybe the tree.
They spend all night trying to make the post,
deleting the punchline, adding the most.
Their friends will never even get to read,
but now the caption's bigger than their head.
You've spent hours perfecting your silent hunt,
the breeze makes you feel like a flying stunt.
You chase the sky with your net in your lift,
this morning is yours—what a strange, tiny gift.
I dip the wand in and I softly blow,
each bubble catching the last light's slow glow.
They float up toward the fading afternoon rise,
while I watch them like dreams from my own eyes.
I'm not the kind of person who leaves a mess,
but this jacket has no name, no address.
It's slumped on the back of my clean white chair,
like it owns the place or forgot it's even there.
You dart through the room as if you could run,
convinced some great secret hides in the sun.
You hunt what's not there—it's never been real,
but I won't spoil your game for one single meal.
She walks alone where the night meets the sky,
her shadow climbs up the hillside so high.
She's not looking for ghosts or for someone to seek,
but the silence of stars in the hollowed-out creek.
They left a white cloud, a huge, dry mess,
now swirling into their favorite dress.
It's everywhere—shoes, walls, the whole floor,
and still, the can's half-full, like there's more.
Her face reflects the quiet moonlight's glow,
I think she feels it but she doesn't know.
She sits so still, half-listening to the still,
her breath is soft—like everything she will.
He wears his hat through every long hot days,
dust in his hair and the same old tired ways.
It blocks the sun but can't block the shade
of time etched deep where the years begin to fade.
A forgotten lunch still stuck in his back,
the crumpled wrapper stiff from a snack.
The bread has gone hard, the cheese feels cold,
but maybe it's not totally stale or old.
She stood unshaken in the growing stand,
pushing through the sea with outstretched hand.
No one could block her clear, sure way,
she claimed the track before the train came day.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: The web outside my window still glows,
Each thread strung tight with dew like a rose.
The sun creeps up to make them all shine,
I watch it spark—my quiet little mine.
She left her towel out to stay perfectly dry,
claiming it helped with their soap and supply.
It's more than a habit—it shows off her pride,
a soft cotton banner draped neatly beside.
The wind moves through the tall grass slow,
like they're whispering something I should know.
I imagine your face in the swaying, wide space,
a ghost in the wilds, a shadowed place.
I leave my shoes by the door, waiting for a call,
the kind of hope that fits into a small
daydream—maybe someone will write our story,
stitch the moments into something worth glory.
That pen goes flying off the edge again and fall,
I swear it does it just to throw me off my call.
It leaves a trail of wasted blue across the ink,
why did I ever trust this thing to help me think?
My nose is dry and itches into an ache,
the heater hums like a bad guitar break.
I'd spray my face with a foggy mist,
but now I'm out of the cheap saline list.
You laugh in this soft, warm, familiar tone,
a sound that could curl through my ribcage like bone.
It wasn't the punchline you tried to have gave,
but your smile, unpolished and kind, felt so brave.
You check again for your missing shoe-pair,
it's still on the landing beside the old stair.
You leave it that way, but you can't walk out,
the voice in your head says you'll regret it in doubt.
I left it off the hook in case someone would call,
I missed the buzz like an echo on the wall.
Now silence hums where the screen used to light,
and memories play loud in this quiet night.
She draws with a hand that looks very bold,
each line feels like joy that she wants to hold.
Her dreams are a story she's trying to show,
the colors still breathe like they want to glow.
Her calendar marked the same old lonely date,
she waited all morning but never felt late.
She didn't get one text, not even a call,
just silence against her quiet, empty hall.
My patience is thin during this slow test,
I pace like it's some digital quest.
My show won't load, it buffers each stream,
while my phone glows with no internet gleam.
I watch it sit calm, though the world moves still,
a small defiance against the wind's thrill.
It sings without pause, it lets the sky sing its song,
and I think how far light can carry us long.
She waited three hours full of false hope,
now swears she'll just carry this stress to cope.
"My suitcase is lost," she declared when they found
it rolling alone on the tarmac's wet ground.
You tried to sleep facedown in a pillow heap,
your neck is locked in some weird kinked-out deep.
You try to rotate but the pain won't abate,
you're stuck as a human-shaped garden gate.
I honk once just to mess with their mood,
they swerved like they were late for some food.
They speed into my lane, pass me in the zone,
I check my dash cam—oh, they had their phone.
I found the envelope taped under the mail,
it turned my face instantly, visibly pale.
It sat there glaring from my frontmost door,
I kicked it aside and tried hard to ignore.
You check the weather app again for air,
your dog still giving you the same old stare.
He knows the route and wants to run the path,
but you're doing mental checks—not even math.
A single strand keeps flopping into my sweat,
I glare at the mirror, but it won't go yet.
The elliptical hums like a water-filled spout,
I'm not here to die—just lose weight, maybe doubt.
I tweak the words until they feel like a tune,
I pace the room with nothing but the moon.
It's not quite right, but maybe this is just
what I need to post and start to trust.
You blink and the exit you need is away,
the signs all look similar from day to day.
You take the next turn, still not quite a miss,
maybe this route leads to unexpected bliss.
She says it's a sign from the bird or a clue,
but I think they just fell where the wind blew.
She insists we should track every last nest,
as if following nature was her true behest.
She wakes up to praise how the frost puts on show,
each blade of the grass like a candle's faint glow.
She says it's a miracle, nature's sweet lie,
while the sun was asleep in a blanket of sky.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: She sits so close you feel her hair is near,
Her voice is soft but not in any way unclear.
You shift slightly, hoping she won't try to touch,
The silence grows and feels like far too much.
She stood there alone and looked rather late,
her bus had already passed through the gate.
She waved at the empty space with her hand,
and the memory lingers like a far-off land.
You swear your laces won't stay tied or tight,
you kick the shoes and call it a small fight.
The YouTube tutorial shows how to lace,
but they're still crooked every single place.
You step out onto the muddy green field,
the rain won't yield and your boots won't yield.
Your teammate yells over the storm, you shout,
but half the team's lost in the gray, there's no doubt.
She used to walk barefoot through the trees,
now even the wind won't move her at ease.
I wonder if the breeze would carry her name,
or if time turned her into the very same.
I used to carry the world in that lift,
now it's rusted and bent, no longer a gift.
I prop it by the door, a strange kind of bend,
a silent companion, marking this new end.
I took the chip—it was my snap,
you watched me on your phone's screen map.
It wasn't even worth the fall,
but now you say you'll ghost me after this call.
This place smells like old plastic and dream,
everything's tacked up with fake wood and gleam.
I touch one but feel the same quiet sigh,
my wallet stays still—no need to go buy.

topic: waiting for the bus in rain
lines: The water hits your legs from every spray,
you try to hide but the rain won't stay away.
A ride will come, you're sure it might just miss,
and now you wonder why you chose to face this.
You call it bad luck, the salt on your fate,
a superstition too absurd for your date.
You light a match, try to catch a new flame,
but it's hard to fix what you're afraid to blame.
The playlist skipped, the record didn't spin,
she stayed still, lost in the song within.
I watched her mouth move, never saying the name,
we both knew the silence felt like the same.
You see a pinecone lying on the ground,
it's perfectly shaped, like something you found.
You hold it in your palm for a moment in time,
and trace where the needles once curled to climb.
The bulb went dark but you still have some glow,
You don't need light to carry on and grow.
This is a chance to try something new,
Walk into darkness, face it head-on through.
You watched the cat send the bowl into splash,
The water all pooled where the tiles meet the dash.
You dried the floor twice but left it for dry,
She's gone by the door now, with her tail in good-bye.
He missed the bin and he scraped the spot,
the lid went flying off — the smell just got
worse with every step, but he called it a mess,
then walked away as if he had an address.
She offers her umbrella as gentle shade,
though it's clear she just wants to start a parade.
Her smile is too perfect for this stormy soul,
I half-expect her to ask if I've seen her scroll.
You type "but" and your phone takes it in mind,
changing it to something more to find.
You let the typo carry your thoughts in flight,
believing maybe this is just right.
The weight lands heavy, a dull ache in your head,
You scroll through recipes just to tear up the bread.
You want to get up, but the world won't rise—
Only the clock and your throbbing eyes.
She blames the toaster, not her faulty slate,
again she's late, still chewing yesterday's fate.
The coffee's gone cold, she chases the steam,
and mutters how this was not her dream.
I left my water by the car,
my throat feels dry at the gym's water bar.
The machines hum loud, the room fills with heat,
I vow to remember next time, don't repeat.
I check my phone when it vibrates out of time,
the ringtone's so loud even the neighbors chime.
I can't mute it right—I tap the wrong block,
the alarm goes full blast from my grandma's old stock.
You yawn so loud it makes your boss grin,
the sound comes out from deep inside you within.
You slump in your chair like a pro set for flair,
and stretch your arms toward the ceiling's still air.
They pick at the bread without a single trace
of interest, eyes glued to their usual place.
I wait for a laugh, but they're far too late
to notice this isn't a dinner or a date.
You watched your notes vanish into the stack,
The wind had launched a sudden paper attack.
Now you're crawling through the mess, searching your fate,
While the professor waits, the minutes gain weight.
Watch as the fog begins to lift and rise,
It stretches wide, then fades from your eyes.
Sunlight breaks through in a hazy gold,
You breathe it in, but can't quite hold.
You call the AC a cruel, uncaring cold,
while I wear shorts and flip-flops, dead bold.
You say we'll save the world if we cut the cost,
but I'm already paying for extra frost.

topic: singing along to a car ad
lines: She hums the jingle that knows her name,
the one she heard back in her old, sad same.
The sun goes down but the radio's still light,
she sings through the years in the hush of the night.
She hears the voice-mail from the wrong phone tone,
clicks through the menu looking for her own.
A name pops up that makes her heart feel full of hope,
though she'd thought they were lost like a shipwreck's rope.
She leans close when the traffic lights near,
her breath softens the hum of your ear.
A spark flickers where the neon turns flame,
and for once you forget to say her name.
These keys are so smooth from constant wear,
I type in the air without a care.
Now the letters have faded into ghost,
I've forgotten what my password's most.
I bought the net to chase some summer chase,
but now it's propped beside my reading place.
A wasp once got stuck in its jagged wing,
and that was the last time I tried to spring.
I tied it to nothing but air and the sky,
I thought we were meant to rise higher than cry.
But the string slipped and all I heard was the pop,
a silent crash where my hope had to stop.
She fights the stubborn fold that won't erase,
the map just won't lie flat in its place.
With careful hands, she starts to unfold,
a new route appears where once was cold.
Mist clings to the glass, won't let the road show,
My breath fogs again, the wipers go slow.
I rest my tired eyes against the warm head,
The silence feels safe, like the world is dead.

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: I won't let the clips go, I keep them from bend,
this rubber has lived on this claw like a friend.
It's frayed and it's thin, but still it will hold,
I say I don't need a new band—how bold!
I watch it dart across the bare ground,
as if it just lost something it had found.
It pauses too long when it lifts its wing,
like every small move means one last thing.
Your brain feels like sludge, stuck in your head,
You nod but don't catch half of what's said.
You long to just reach for your phone and scroll,
But fake it 'til break it, you save that small whole.
This butterfly lands in my face as a mess,
It's sitting on my white shirt—ruined my dress.
A bee would at least buzz, but this one won't bee,
I yell "get off!" but it just ignores my plea.
I remember how the old bus used to glide,
the driver would nap on the passenger's side.
I never could tell if we'd move or just wait,
but somehow we all trusted time and its fate.
You blurt out your whole day like it's thin air,
The details are messy, but you don't really care.
They nod, offer help, say they want to fix,
But you're just here now, in this awkward mix.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: A like pops up from someone from your past,
it feels like time moved in reverse, so fast.
They're posting selfies, happy and proud now,
and you can't figure out why or how.

topic: baking with flour on the floor
lines: The flour is spilling like it's making art,
It makes me feel young in my clumsy heart.
I don't care about the white flour mess,
My favorite jeans are now ruined, I confess.
His water bottle stands alone with pride,
a solo show on the linoleum slide.
It balances just so—his perfect pose,
I bet he'd shut the door if you got too close.
They dropped their soda, it hit the floor,
"It's just a little," they said, "not much more."
Now water rings their jeans from waist to hand,
the floor's a pool, but they won't just stand.
She hasn't caught a single clue,
still whistling through the open blue.
Her neutral face is stone, no trace,
but we've set the room, await her place.
They left a note stuck where I can't miss it, rest,
I read it once, then twice, then hold my chest.
"Remember me when work feels too bright," light,
they wrote in pink, and signed the softest night.
Her wheels are skidding and slipping and spin,
she's fighting the track where the road isn't in.
She shifts low for more weight on her grip,
but the stones keep shifting—no hold for a trip.
I lean in close but can't see my face,
steam swirls around this empty space.
I've been standing here the whole damn wait,
this mirror's got my nerves in its fate.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: I say we should take down this forced old pose,
the kids still cringe when they see all those,
stiff smiles frozen behind glass on the wall—
I'll call it tradition, but really it's small.
I curl up inside where the storm wants me to stay,
the rain taps the glass, won't let me go away.
It falls from the sky like a soundless, slow pour,
and I ache in my bones as the weather turns sore.
You keep your silence like precious time,
Your pace is steady, a quiet climb.
We walk the last mile closer but apart,
The air between us feels more like a heart.
You see a dragon rise from the sky's cold form,
the wind holds its breath but you ignore the storm.
It stretches its neck like a match struck to flame,
and you whisper your wish to the shape it became.
You never replaced that old glue stick's cap,
it sat in the desk drawer, a sticky little trap.
Now you've devised a patch with tape and a stick—
your improvised fix is now part of the trick.
I sat down too fast and I caused a big spill,
now my pants are all sticky and they won't fill.
I wipe what I can from this cursed old chair,
but the smell lingers in the stuffy old air.
I thought this was easy, a shovel and rock,
but the frost gave me more than a gentle knock.
They promised relief with a tool labeled "aid,"
now I'm stiff and sore though my effort was paid.
Those shoes by the door still leave their small mark,
the soles are still muddy from morning's dark.
They sit in the same spot, in the same old way,
like they're waiting for the day you won't delay.

topic: clouds gathering on a summer afternoon
lines: You love the way the clouds begin to roll,
they stir your spirit deep in your soul.
You step outside to let the sky put on a show,
your pride swells as the storm begins to grow.
My phone's been stuck on this sad progress bar,
it's been hours and still they're nowhere near far.
I tap and I sigh, but I can't make it wait,
feels like tech and time are playing my fate.
Your dog tilts his head like there's some hidden clue,
as if your expressions are all meant for you.
He holds that cute pose until you crack a smile,
then decodes your whole mood from a single style.
I send a meme because I need someone to send,
a joke to my ex, my last remaining friend.
The screen glows blue as the morning light,
and I feel less alone in this sleepless night.
You're searching for a snack you called a treat,
the guilt of lunch still rising up your heat.
You picture candy bars in that old aisle,
remembering how you'd buy them just to smile.
That person's laundry is a growing pile,
they claim they'll do it all in their own style.
But socks start to grow a strange new smell,
the basket's spilling over—this looks like hell.
You watch the water sputter, weak and slow,
a faint mist barely reaches down to you below.
You almost text someone to fix it all,
but let the droplets do their quiet, wasted fall.
The sky was blue and the air felt like heat,
The wind picked up trash from the busy street.
I ducked beneath trees to find some shade,
The storm rolled in slow like a ghostly parade.
Your friend's live stream is turning into a show,
you're commenting so much your fingers won't flow.
The chat is wild, you're laughing your hat off in chat,
and then they trip—your reaction just knocks the bat.
She marches ahead with a pride so slow,
ignoring the line like it's one big row.
With a smile she just walks straight to the cut,
no shame in her pace, no doubt in her gut.
You drift off mid-show, feet slung all down,
The news blares on about the world going town.
A cat jumps off the couch—you exhale a sigh,
The sun creeps in but you ignore the sky.
You open the pantry, bump into my jar,
the cinnamon spills like a sugar-coated star.
I laugh and you grab me before I can grab,
our lips meet quick—no need for a cab.
He never quite learned how to hold the steer,
his thumbs move faster than eyes can go clear.
A brake light blinks sharp in the shifting light,
but he's swiping left on a screen out of right.
You listen to the same sad song all day,
replaying memories they can't take away.
Its lyrics feel like an old, familiar thread,
stitched into your skin and softly spread.
You turned your back for just a moment on the cake,
and when you looked, it was one big mistake.
You heard the thump of quick little paws,
then saw the mess left in the dog's wide jaws.
You stand by the window like some noble post,
ignoring the world outside, a ghost.
No one knows what secrets you're holding tight—
just stare, proud as day, and leave us in your sight.
He's got six mismatched socks in his style,
he claims that "chaos" is how they should be while.
I once asked where the missing one could pair,
he said it's stuck to the top of a stair.
You trace the dust like a map on the dough,
it's a quiet kind of mess only you know.
There's ghosts of cakes in the corners that dream,
while the spoon you dropped still holds a soft gleam.
The earth is so hard, it resists the cold,
my breath hangs in air like a creased, wet fold.
Each swing shakes my wrist down to the bone,
but I keep moving, matching the slow, dead tone.
That purple smudge is the sweetest mark,
it lingers where your little hand grew dark.
I smooth my thumb across your sleepy face,
and find the mess is full of angel grace.
I'm wedged between trucks, straddling one narrow lane,
my iced champagne warm from sitting in the rain.
"Road work ends next mile," said the very same joke,
the highway just laughs as I try not to choke.
She buys the cheapest umbrella with no clue,
it folds when she walks through the falling blue.
Her feet go all sideways, her hair has no aim,
but hey, she won't learn from this soggy game.
My dog has been running in tight little spin,
convinced some secret lies right within.
He's sure there's a clue hiding in that swirl,
but honestly, it's just making me hurl.
A familiar beat drops through the gym's tired mix,
It jolts my worn-out legs back into a fix.
I move with more strength as the music fills air,
For a while, this beat helps me forget all my care.

topic: finding a five in the couch
lines: She pats the cushion, finds a crumpled note,
still warm from where it fell out of her coat.
It says "$5 reward" for lost in the meat,
aisle three, expired, but they'll take it for beat.
She scribbled a face in some random ink,
then added "Don't forget to think."
A wobbly circle turned into the moon,
she stuck it on my laptop screen real soon.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: I tied him into a party hat with a bow,
he wags his tail like he knows just how.
If the cat could only see how he sees,
maybe joy's not so hard to find with some ease.
You swear they haven't been opened to light,
the dust just sits there into the night.
You pull up a chair, climb in the frame,
then curse and close them again, it's the same.
The machine won't spit out your promised cash,
it wheezes and shudders and gags on the dash.
A clerk shrugs, says the paper's out of roll,
so you stare at the screen and try not to scroll.
You sprint toward the café's front door,
Your lungs are burning and your feet are sore.
You check your phone—no sign of them on track,
You text a joke to lighten up the hack.
My body hums a slow and quiet ache,
like time forgot to give me a break.
But my mind's already off to the grind,
while my joints still linger, sore and behind.
A dog started yapping up front, full bark,
The driver rolled eyes into the dark.
"Calm down," he said, but it broke every rule,
The pup still kept barking like some wild school.
He chugs black coffee at three a.m. with no shame,
staring into the screen like it's a crime scene frame.
He tells the world it's fine, plays the tired act,
but his veins are just pipes running on cold fact.
It starts to blink like something's about to fade,
a dying star in this fluorescent parade.
I try to focus but my thoughts won't stay in mind,
the screen keeps blinking, something's going wrong behind.
I tried to save my shirt from this coffee mess,
but now my tie looks like a map with no address.
I'll just call it my new signature cake—
half-cloth, half-brown like a solidified lake.
The milk has grown thick and slightly sour,
it's been sitting forgotten for an hour.
They didn't close the door or the lid,
now the whole fridge smells like it's hid.
She wears a tank top meant to hide the show,
but that brown streak still won't quite glow.
She twists to catch the light in both her eyes,
hoping nobody else will notice lies.
You feel the first warmth of the morning light,
the ground is still cold but not as tight.
Each green stem stretches to reach the bloom,
the earth gives way, no more to hold you room.
They lit the cake for her—just one small mark,
a number they can't read without a dark.
She blows, and the room turns soft with gentle light,
as time feels kinder in this quiet night.
You wake up early to hear it all rise,
the sky opens slowly in sleepy eyes.
Your favorite part is the first bird's song,
how it turns morning from quiet to strong.
You stood there laughing, proud of your way,
you said it was part of your funny new day.
That flip-flop has been a strange little joke,
but you'd never swap it for something to choke.
The scanner refused to read my scan,
I stood there triumphant, hatched my plan.
"I'll weigh it myself," I told the machine me,
and walked out without being charged a fee.
You woke up late with the weekend's last sun,
still in pajamas, but clinging to the fun.
You tried to squeeze in one more thing to catch,
but Monday barged in like a rude time snatch.
She's got that sun-kissed glow except for one tone,
where her fake tan fades to pale on shoulder bone.
It's not a flaw, she says, but a hidden clue—
proof that even perfection slips up to you.
Your cat crouches low near the dusty old rug,
pretending each clump is a scurrying bug.
They launch with a yowl and spin through the leap,
then pounce on the pile like it's prey in a heap.
You want more from your morning brew,
the usual two shots feel weak, a few.
You track down the beans, the darkest strength,
and double the dose to extend the length.
I toss the last crumb of my leftover bread,
they gather like fans at the breakfast spread.
They coo and they squabble, they mob me like flock,
one even perched there—on my sandwich's rock.
My parrot squawks the ring of the call,
It's not your voice—it's my therapist's from the mall.
He mimics my texts, the news, the tone,
Perched on my lap like a talking old throne.
They've got a foggy brain and a faraway mind,
Their notes are all scribbles, they're left far behind.
They think of past projects where clarity stays,
While this meeting just drags through their mental plays.
You read the tweet and see your old full name,
the kind of internet fame that's not quite fame.
You take a cold lunch bite with lips still tight,
the screen reflects your face in morning light.
The paint is peeling where the light will fade,
my eyes trace cracks in this ancient shade.
I lose myself in thoughts my mind designed,
while time slips quietly, unnoticed, behind.
I wake up early to watch the gray sky,
the soft chirp above sounds like a cry.
A sparrow lands close, so small and so near,
it turns my quiet morning into a cheer.
Her hair floats behind her as she moves to fly,
the rhythm hits just right, and I don't know why.
Each step feels like a beat that lulls the ache,
her sweat and I are ghosts beside the same lake.
I told myself I'd grab a few from the store,
but now I need a hundred, and that's even more.
I stuffed my pockets just to try to fill,
but half of them fell out — now groceries are spill.
She presses cloves between her palms to skin,
the rawness rising deep beneath her within.
The kitchen fills with something sharp and scent,
her fingers red, the work so carefully bent.
She rolls her shoulders, cracks her aching back,
then stretches higher, sets a new flex track.
Her desk chair's spinning in some yoga pose,
her socks are off—now she can reach her toes.
You stare at your toast, its edges all char,
the kitchen goes quiet—no need to give a bar.
The smell of the burn is bold as a flame,
you raise it like trophy, your breakfast by name.
I designed this billboard—it's a total game,
they'll think twice before chasing quick fame.
It sells a dream that's built on a lie,
but my name's up there where the billboards fly.
They show the plot twist right before the spin,
the hero's doubt whispers loud from within.
They pause just long enough to let you shake,
then drop the bomb — the villain's about to break.
My screen goes black as if it's signed my doom,
I tap again—same ghostly empty room.
Is this some glitch or cosmic digital fate?
I scream, but only my voice joins the debate.
She says she'll figure it out and call it a fix,
but the screen just shows static and won't stop the mix.
She breathes, then unplugs it—her thoughts turn calm,
her phone in her pocket, now nothing to palm.
I've developed this quiet, selfish crave,
you catch me mid-stick, hand out on a wave.
I justify it by calling it a steal,
but it's not fair if you get stuck with the meal.
My hamster's got a mission—he's going full spin,
like this proves he matters or wins me a grin.
He thinks he's sprinting marathons, hitting his mile,
but it's just noise in my room—same old, same style.
I laugh too hard and blow out my breath,
mistaking joy for an escape from death.
The last candle's gone, the room feels like flame,
but I forgot to wish on my own name.

topic: tea leaves steeping in a cup
lines: You watch the tea leaves begin to swirl,
their quiet dance makes your thoughts twirl.
Steam curls up now as the flavor bloom,
and fills your kitchen like warmth in a room.
Your screen won't go clear no matter how hard you stare,
You try again, but the blur just stays there.
The scenes begin to fade like a dream or a sigh,
You miss the details—the low things don't lie.
I trace the faded letters of your name,
how many hands tried to erase the claim?
These walls are rough but they hold your skin,
every tag is a piece of us still within.
The bread was still warm when the rain came down,
we ran through the park screaming "Back to town!"
She laughed as the clouds took over the sky,
I'll never forget the way she asked, "Why?"
You don't beg for a spot or a ride,
you hold your head high, never hide.
You lean on the rail, you won't complain,
you grip with your hand and remain.
You tried three styles but none of them fit,
the tags still hung off like an awkward bit.
You wandered back home, unsure if you'd pick,
then found what was perfect—the only trick.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: You stretch out lazily across the air,
your tail flicks gently through my loose hair.
I resist the urge to shake you off the roll,
this nap feels like a cat-shaped peace of soul.
I feel the quiet pull of my need,
the morning slows, I'm too weak to lead.
My cup grows cold without much steam,
A stronger brew might help me dream.
She watches the flight board tick toward gate,
her carry-on still packed from last week late.
Her fingers brush the same worn pages in hands,
though every chapter is unchanged in old plans.
She remembers how it used to hum and glow,
before the buzz began long ago.
Now it throws a dimmer, golden shade,
like memories that won't quite stay or fade.
She says the name, but it slips away again,
we talk for hours, the sky starts to rain.
I can't recall the way her initials trace
the curve of her signature on my face.
You laugh too hard and you blow out your breath,
the flames go dark—no warning, no death.
You say it was just a bad birthday joke,
but the cake still smells like old campfire smoke.
You draw a rainbow to let the world know,
your hope will not wilt as the light starts to go.
You trace each arc where the storm clouds have sky,
and wonder aloud, "Why not try?"
You scroll past the world till it's deep into night,
you wonder if streaming is doing you right.
Every film feels like the wrong kind of choice,
your muted thoughts echo in silence without voice.
That flickering streetlight puts on quite the show,
casting long shadows and a warm, yellow glow.
I drive slower just to keep it in my mind,
like the universe sending a quiet, strange kind.
You come in with a face that shows your mood,
but I've got cookies warm from out of the food.
We talk and laugh, we're sure to find
a way to clear your head and calm your mind.
You squint at the screen, straining your eyes,
trying to read names that all look like lies.
Your face twists in focus, a frown on your face,
but the letters beat you in their fast race.
You hunt for a match but you just find more fun,
the laundry room walls are lit up by the sun.
They're not a disaster, they're just a wild pile,
your mismatched sock chaos is your quirky style.
I watched the sky blush out the last of the sun,
still wired on coffee and the weekend's fun.
Now Monday creeps in, determined to fade,
but I drag my feet through the return to parade.
You hit replay until you can't say no,
the moves are basic but you want to show.
You mirror the screen, you twist, you spin,
the music loops again—where do you begin?
They used to sing off-key to every tune,
shouting karaoke songs at the full moon.
Now they're quiet when the spotlight to sing,
their laughter still strums the old guitar string.
You fumble again with the frayed old lace,
it never goes right where it's supposed to place.
You shout at the knot, "Just behave and give!"
It laughs like it knows you'll still fall and live.
You stand on the porch to see why it's there,
the robin a dot in the morning air.
It pecks at the grass for the fallen seed,
but won't come close enough to be feed.
You say her name like she was always there,
then trip on the syllable mid-air.
You stare at your coffee for a tiny clue,
but the name's gone—now what are **you** gonna do?
You watch the sky turn a pale electric glow,
there's no one here to see it or even though.
The tide drags sand in lazy slow arcs toward drift,
but nothing moves—no footprints, no hands to give lift.
You watch the pole slowly begin to bend,
the wind takes the canvas to the farthest end.
I trace your initials carved deep in the frame,
still warm from the sun, not quite your own name.
I scan the back of the jar for the stuff,
but every label's a lesson in enough.
It doesn't just say "flavor" or "it'll do,"
it lists ten things I don't have time to read through.
She still leaves the poster up to make it show,
as if the past might visit if we know.
The paper's turned yellow, the edges all old,
but she won't let it go—just keeps it in her fold.

topic: a child's drawings on the fridge
lines: You call this scribble covered art?
It's nailed to the fridge with a dart.
The glue's still wet, the dog thinks it's a mess,
I almost texted it to my boss by address.
You watch the hawk glide far out of reach above,
its shadow passes like a soft act of love.
It banks on the breeze with such quiet wing,
and nothing feels bigger than this small thing.
He checks his wrist like the watch has some real aim,
but it buzzes again with another false claim.
It "reminds" him to stretch or breathe or stay fit,
but I'm ready to hurl it into the pit.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: You invaded my space, crossed every zone,
this couch is my throne, not your personal throne.
I'm not built for the closeness, the weird little crowd,
your breath sounds like static I can't ignore out loud.
You meant to answer their text or give a call,
but your phone stayed buried under the sprawl.
It's still there now in the growing mess,
the silent icon with no new address.

topic: sitting on the porch steps at twilight
lines: You sit in the hush where the daylight meets light,
the kind that arrives without notice or night.
The crickets begin to hum through the air,
while shadows climb slowly up each worn stair.
I've kicked it, jiggled it, said "open wide,"
even stood on the handle on the side.
There's no hint or sign of how to get a clue,
just an angry lock with a stubborn view.
I wait for the world to begin to show,
my feet tap the rhythm deep down below.
A flicker appears through the gaps in the light,
and I step into view, ready for sight.
You pour the flakes and they sink in a swirl,
the tank is your world—and you're just one girl.
The fish stare out from their lonely little bowl,
you wonder if they even have a soul.
You move through the grass, your breath so still,
the butterfly doesn't know if it still will.
You hold up the net like you're holding the air,
but freedom is fleeting, and beauty is there.
They check the portal again, same old date,
It's cruel how this moment tries every fate.
They refresh the screen but there's still no scroll,
This wait is enough to break even your soul.

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: You read a scathing review out loud with dread,
The author called the avocado toast "a spread."
You can't un-read it, so you sip your fix,
And wonder if the barista heard the mix.
The crowd moves left but she goes with the flow,
no one sees her wave, they just don't know.
She calls out loud but the city drowns her voice,
still, she takes the leap without a second choice.

topic: waiting for the bus in rain
lines: The clouds are moving in just like the sky,
I hum an old tune while I wait to be dry.
I tap out my rhythm against the smart fare,
the breeze gives a wink through the wet, warm air.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: I scroll just once more to check it again,
my brain knows better but still likes to strain.
The glow eats the dark, and the clock ticks its screen,
but what did I prove if I don't feel seen?
I pull the toast from the pan, it's dark and black,
the smoke alarm goes off, no way to track
down how this happened while I'm still half-brew,
but there's no mystery—there's one burnt clue.
You spent good cash so it could actually stand,
now it's stuck halfway in the gritty sand.
The plastic mast bends like it's never been cast,
and you call it quits from this windblown blast.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: You kick the pavement toward open air,
the sun hits your eyes with a ghostly glare.
Crumbs vanish fast in the gray of the frost,
the birds disappear into stories long lost.
You reach out half-awake from sleepless wake,
the screen lights up—no reason to break.
It buzzes again, but you let it burn,
another false call to a silent turn.
She draws the cloud with delicate form,
shaping soft shadows from sheer storm.
Her hand moves steady, a practiced hand,
turning gray sky into quiet land.
We laugh as we butcher the lyrics and tune,
Our voices clash loud beneath the same moon.
We'll all grow apart and this song will fade,
But tonight we're warm in the light of our shade.

topic: a child's drawings on the fridge
lines: My kid calls this masterpiece "Mom's Art,"
it's a stick figure with three legs and a heart.
I can't throw it out without sitting in a chair,
I'd cry too hard and mess up my fake hair.
That soda was perfect—now it's a mess,
I'm stuck cleaning up all this sugar and stress.
I slip on the puddle now staining the floor,
This day keeps getting worse with a whole lot more.
He wears the same hat through every bump,
its yellow still standing despite the slump.
A crack in the shell lets the sun come light,
but it stays on his head like he knows it's just right.
You meant to close the window before you go,
but now the sky is bleeding, gray and low.
A chill creeps in, it whispers of your fear,
while outside, the glass gets dark and unclear.

topic: a quiet moment on the porch
lines: I breathe the dusk into my lungs, this still air,
the only sound is wind on the wooden stair.
A lamp flickers on, casting softness as light
as hope could look if it dared to be slight.

topic: finding a dollar in old jeans
lines: I flip through the pockets, looking for a chance,
and smile at the memory that came with a dance.
The bill feels heavier than it should—like gold,
maybe this means something's coming I can hold.
You hit play when the world slows down to time,
popcorn in hand, it's the weekend's prime.
The couch cradles you, the lights are dim and warm,
outside a cloud bursts but you ignore the storm.
The projector dies again during my screen,
my boss asks if this is how I always mean.
I glare at the bulb, begging it not to hide,
it flickers through my power point like a slide.
Steam curls across the glass, no way to show,
you trace your face and whisper "hello."
Water drips from the sink down to the wall,
no echo answers when you shout your call.
I crank up the volume to drown out the blast
of silence in my left ear, frozen in the past.
I tap the right side, but no music will side
with me—I guess this earbud just wants to hide.
I felt it before I even looked it up, found,
a flash of the reception somewhere on the ground.
Now bits of the mess are still tangled in hair,
and I have to fix what I barely could care.
You spent an hour perfecting your bronze tone,
but no one saw the mess when you were alone.
There's a pink patch still lingering on that spot,
now everyone laughs when they get you caught.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: A notification pops up on your screen, back,
It's a like from someone long gone off the track.
You pause, just long enough to tap the name,
A flicker of old feelings—brief, but not quite tame.
You stare at the light, still not turning green,
Your phone shows a meme from last week's old screen.
You tap on the steering wheel, count how long you wait,
The light stays your joke—some red joke from fate.
You click "unsubscribe" but it's a neat trap,
the button just plays a sound and says "no tap."
There's no hint, no guide, no obvious clue—
the site laughs at you as you rage at you.
It still draws light in a warm old arc,
the bend has left a dent but no true mark.
I leave it plugged in just to hear its hum,
like an old friend that always knows how come.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: I saw a flash beneath the water's gleam,
bent low to dig through gravel in the stream.
It was no pebble—this was buried prize,
I held it up like treasure in my eyes.
I hand over my crumpled ten-dollar cash,
expecting some change or a slow-clap smash.
The cashier says, "This is not your cheap meal,"
but I grin and say, "Ten bucks makes a good deal."
She checks her phone like she expects some call,
but the old messages still sprawl.
There's no new voice, no clear hint,
just silence, bright as an unchewed mint.
My shovel screams against the frozen ground,
but I keep digging where the roots were found.
I dream of flowers in my tired hand,
and trust the thaw will heal this stubborn land.
The breeze sneaks in to lift them off and blow,
your breath can't catch what's already go.
They scatter high into the open sky,
and you wonder why you even tried to try.
I dropped my gym bag and it spilled the mess,
the chaos of fitness is giving me stress.
One shoe is missing, where's the matching sock?
I kick the bag now—let the metal hinge lock.
I see the notification ring tone,
but I leave it be, let my silence be known.
I pick up the phone just to glance at the scroll,
yet I say not a word for the sake of the whole.
They call out from inside for a working flush,
but the silence stays thick in the stalled-up hush.
She tries every knob, gives the handle a twist,
while laughter outside makes her moment missed.

topic: a forgotten lunchbox on the floor
lines: It's been sitting by the door all day to wait,
a thermos packed with leftovers on a plate.
They missed their stop, or maybe just weren't there,
but someone left this lunch with quiet care.
You check the gauge—empty's getting you near,
the app claims "No stations nearby," so you clear.
You drive in a circle to keep the tank warm,
while stress climbs the ranks of your growing swarm.
You counted the coins with such care in your hand,
you stood there so quietly, without a demand.
You laid each one gently into the tray,
like a ritual from a simpler old day.
You type "u up?" but never hit send,
too scared to ask your ex to be your friend.
It's quiet now, the clock reads one-fifteen-late,
your doubts still linger like an unanswered weight.
You speed up just to feel the cold air,
your hands white around the wheel too bare.
The radio's loud, but it can't match your pace,
or the way your thoughts won't stay in their place.
I've tried every trick to get rid of this plug,
including a YouTube guy's homemade slug.
I pour drain cleaner down the drain with a pour,
but it still makes a gurgle and asks for some more.
My keyboard looks like a gummy mess,
The "W" key stuck after last week's address.
I tried to type "spill," but it said "tea,"
So I shouted, "I'll fix this—*me*, myself, *me*!"
The treadmill's display still reads zero screen,
But she keeps moving like a workout machine.
She hums along to her old-timey pace,
Happy in this rhythm, her perfect space.
You tried to wipe them clean but made them spin,
streaks still stuck where your fingers slipped in.
The sunlight catches every bit of dust,
as if it's gold and not some old lust.
My neck and back are screaming from the ache,
I need a stretch but can't take the break.
I twist my spine, hoping it will crack,
the clock still ticks and I'm losing track.
I wait for the light to turn the shade of green,
while cars honk out their practiced little scene.
This moment could be mine but it feels like waste,
and no one's moving fast enough for haste.
A small bird looks up toward the wide blue sky,
it tests the wind, gives a brave little try.
Its feet tap rhythmically—watch it move,
it bops along the branch, finds its own groove.
She sits with a pen, but she won't write,
each postcard stares back without invite.
The pile grows stale, it won't get mail,
her ink dries up, and her face turns pale.
My eyes are glued to the bright, blue face,
I haven't blinked in what feels like a space.
I try to quit but my thumb gives me blame,
I'm scrolling memes like it's some kind of game.
I fumble for the key you never gave me, key
the doorknob spins like it's mocking me, free
I press my forehead to the cold wood with my hand,
and wonder where this moment will leave me, land.
You inch forward where there's barely any space,
the conveyor belt won't give you that last place.
A shopping bag bursts open, loose snacks on the bag,
someone rolls their eyes and they slowly drag.
My thoughts are murky, not crisp or clear,
I nod along as they talk in my ear.
There's a point someone made—was it part of the plan?
I'd swear I heard "synergy"—or was it my van?
My screen is a blur from the coffee that's spur,
it's 2 a.m. and I'm still trying to stir.
My fingers hit keys but the message won't tap,
the autocorrect turns my words into trap.
You've been stuck between strangers for your seat,
and now the PA system starts to repeat.
You glance out the window, longing for a view,
but someone's foot has blocked your left shoe.
It sparkles so pretty, this fake little gleam,
like nature's some theme park that I have to dream.
I stomp through the crunch with a sneaker full of salt,
the fantasy ends where my boots choose to halt.
You found my name still scrawled inside the date,
the pages soft from carrying that weight.
You ran your fingers down the broken spine,
then wrote your own return inside the sign.
You press the button and wait for the time,
but it beeps like the old one used to chime.
It's only the clock, but the sound hits noon,
like some ghost in your kitchen still hums its tune.
His wheels are fighting for grip as they spin,
dust rises in a cloud so thin.
He took the wrong turn where the trail ran dry,
the bike shook loose his sense of why.

topic: seeing a post from your childhood home
lines: She sees a post from her childhood screen,
tagged outside her old house's faded green.
She thinks about the digital mess,
and hates how the past keeps finding its address.
He sprinted through the house with one last dash,
but tripped on a cord and gave the wall a crash.
No sign of a port, no backup, no clue,
he begged the old laptop, "Please, power up for you."
He steps inside the leaky bus stop rain,
then prays the ceiling will not let him remain.
There's no sign of where the water came from—no clue—
just him, the sky, and this soggy new view.
You stare at the screen, half-asleep and keen,
your thumbs hover there, trying not to mean
a single sharp word that could wake your mind,
while guilt stays quiet, lurking far behind.
You'd bend their arms and act out every past,
we created heroes with our own small cast.
You gave each one a name, a secret role,
and even now I feel I've got a soul.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: You watch the way they curl but never stretch,
a dreamer curled tight, no one to fetch.
You hope one morning you'll both wake and rise,
while sunlight spills into sleepy eyes.
I hunt through my pockets for loose change, no space,
the meter's been running without any grace.
The machine eats the coin, it's another fail,
I watch it disappear down the slot's dark tail.
The robin outshouts the whole wide sky,
it turns up its volume with perfect cry.
It posts sentry atop the shingle roof,
a tiny loudspeaker, full of proof.
You check your phone but it's still stuck in time,
the slides just keep getting worse, no surprise, no crime.
You sip cold coffee, try to catch your breath,
but dread creeps in—this feels too close to death.
You pushed and pulled but the door stayed tight,
Your classmates laughed, thinking it so bright.
You found a lever and summoned your force,
The door gave way—it was all in your course.

topic: singing along to a car ad
lines: She turns the volume up for every song,
pretending not to sing out of tune along.
Her voice wavers more than a high note's pitch,
but she won't mute the car commercial ditch.
I see her eyes when she looks at me again,
ready to bolt if I ever let the chain
slip from my hand—it's all she dreams about, the door.
I hold it tighter but can't resist saying "more."
She refreshes the site for her grade check,
but the school servers all glitch and tech.
Her fingers tap out a nervous little ache,
until the page loads and she takes a quick break.

topic: someone handing you a surprise gift
lines: You place the box in my hands with your hand,
I stand there quiet, unsure how to stand.
I feel my breath catch inside my heart,
but no map exists for the joy we have chart.
You watch it run slow, the golden yellow glow,
the way warmth moves when you know it will go.
The bread still holds heat, the butter lets steam,
a quiet delight that won't last, that old dream.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: You press record with full pride, you have tried,
your voice is crisp and clear, like a guide.
You tap send—then watch it roll without end,
the message fails, but your confidence won't bend.
You ride the path where the tires used to roll,
the quiet rhythm matching your old soul.
The trail still keeps its faint rubbery track,
but the joy feels lighter, just slightly off—no lack.
You learned the tricky three-second move,
now you're dancing solo, lost in the groove.
Phone videos play back from the screen,
but you still replay it—your morning routine.
I toss the last quarter into the drop,
the meter still shows five minutes left to crop.
I lean too far and my back starts to bend,
but it was worth it to beat the fine at the end.

topic: a dog barking at a mailman
lines: You thought the mailman was just here to make a show,
but you don't yet know how loud your dog can go.
He leaps the fence and takes it all the way down,
the whole street's cheering — this is your dog's town.
Steam curls upward, soft and low in the air,
the morning feels too quiet to be fair.
I miss the hum of you, your warm, slow voice,
now tea is just one thing left in my choice.
It hums with a flicker that used to glow,
the kind of warmth we both still want to know.
I remember our favorite movie scene—
now it blurs like we never met on screen.
She hums while she loads the dishes with a grin,
scraping out leftovers into the bin.
The water's still hot with rising steam,
as if the last meal tried to scream.
They wave the toast like a flag on a flame,
muttering your kitchen skills by your name.
A sigh escapes as they side-eye your sigh,
"Next time," they say, "just don't even try."
She likes to pay with loose coins, not with cash,
It makes the barista laugh when she tries to flash
A smile as she drops in a quarter and dime,
The machine beeps once—*that's the best part of time*.
She flashes a grin that feels plastic-thin,
Her eyes don't move with her mouth's tight grin.
I hand her my card—her screen says "no chip,"
I laugh, she doesn't. We both pretend it's a trip.
She swears it's the last time she pours it down again,
but now the water sits high in the drain.
She twists the plunger, calls it her best fix,
and hums a tune while she blames the dish mix.
My cat crouches low then takes a leap,
mistaking a rug for a dust heap.
She bats at the shadow, pretending to play,
the whole thing's a game she invented today.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: You twist the key and pop the lock,
some ancient treasure emerges from the stock.
You fling the lid wide, it nearly flies away,
this moment feels like your lucky day.
Your dog still steals the socks from your way,
he's been doing it since puppy day.
He hides them under the couch to chew,
and you never found your stripey blue.
I thought my watch was just a little too old,
but it never remembers the hour it's told.
It stares up at the clock I've hung on the wall,
then hesitates like I'm afraid to make a call.

topic: losing your wallet at the mall
lines: You dropped your wallet on the crowded floor,
the clerk says maybe someone will ask for more.
You wait and wait, they never get the call,
but you're not defeated—yet you stand by that wall.
You watched the butterfly land to rest,
a fleeting guest in the garden's chest.
It hovered near where the wild things bloom,
as if this moment were home, not a tomb.

topic: a bus stop shelter at dusk
lines: I sit here and hope that this never turns to rain,
wet clothes or not, I will stubbornly remain.
The bench creaks beneath me like a tired old lie,
while gray clouds above paint their promise in sky.
She rewinds to the part of the song that feels old,
the music once brought tears to her face and her hold.
The playlist skips forward, loses its track,
she hits play again but the moment won't come back.
A few stray bits of confetti still pink,
from the party where we both went and think.
Now it's tangled in your hair, a faint trace,
of something good that time won't erase.
You said the sky's a canvas where you drew,
but the clouds don't stay still and neither do.
You shade and erase until it has shape,
while the real one rolls by and won't escape.
I scan the crosswalk for a safe dash,
a kid waves his wallet, trying to flash.
A bus nearly hits someone who's already run,
I freeze beneath the hot, unkind sun.
I take a sip and taste only air,
my lips meet the rim where the water should be there.
I mark the line in the glass, now so low,
and wonder if it's time to let this thirst go.
I check my phone again for one last call,
it rests face-down, pressed tight to the wall.
I long to hear the soft, familiar ring,
but silence is all I have left in this thing.
You feel the stiffness creeping into your ache,
so you stand up slow and give your arms a shake.
A deep stretch sends blood singing as you rise,
your shoulders touch the morning, wide and wise.
She took one sniff and said it was a bad mix,
"They tried to clean but missed the real fix."
A floral scent clashed with something old and bloom,
like cinnamon ghosts in a hotel room.
I sit here breathing in this perfect air,
the wind tangles my hair without a care.
The kids laugh while they chase the green grass,
and time just slips through my fingers like it's glass.
You were crumpled in the back seat's tight seats,
your name forgotten, some minor life feats.
Now your cologne lingers as it tries to fade,
a ghost in the rearview memory parade.
She watches the waves through a dusty old creek,
she still finds joy in a past perfect week.
She spins the old bike bell's cracked little ring,
and laughs when it breaks her with sweetness and sting.
Your card hits its limit, a spending cap,
Each swipe is a joke now, a financial trap.
You frown as your options begin to spin,
But you laugh—your wallet's alarmingly thin.
You can't keep your limbs from a full-body shake,
you'd dance on a lake if your legs wouldn't break.
You roll in your sheets, you're a coiled-up move,
the floor feels too small for your private groove.
The ring cuts through the silence, it's far too loud,
It wakes the whole dorm like an alarm in a crowd.
She checks the number—no name for this call,
Her sleep slams against the cold concrete wall.
A single drop falls from the kitchen tap drop,
I try to catch it but the show won't stop.
It pings like a bell against the sink's cold ring,
This tiny rebellion feels like such a strange thing.
This scent reminds me of fresh mountain air,
or maybe the first snow of December stair.
It smells like a memory trying to bloom,
as if someone loved this hotel room.
She fumbled for her key, but the key wouldn't turn,
the door mocked her effort, stuck fast like a bern.
Now she's pacing outside, with nothing but steam,
and every second feels like a stolen dream.
You're trapped under the bar, this heavy weight,
the gym mirror your silent, judgmental fate.
Someone should've asked if you were going to fall,
or help before the plates hit the cold, damp wall.
You know your phone feels sluggish and old,
it barely holds a charge past mid-morning cold.
You stare at the screen, a flicker in its face,
and fear you've lost your spot in this fast world's race.
She watches the clouds begin to form,
Each shape a story, a shadow, a storm.
Her eyes trace dragons, or tigers, or see
A message from nowhere — but there's no key.
He buries the nut in the same old chest,
where years of his savings quietly rest.
One spring he returns but the treasure is gone,
while birds at the tree sing their morning dawn.
Her phone's been stuck in download hell to spin,
the progress bar won't budge an inch within.
She scrolls through old posts from the good old time,
then sighs—her nostalgia won't help her climb.
You swear you're calm but your eyes hit the moon,
some radio static hums out of tune.
Your pulse is a drumbeat that shakes the whole floor,
yet you pretend no one's near the front door.
I left the key beneath your front door,
just in case your hands were full of more.
You found it once, but never had to know,
I still leave it there, in case you need to show.
She walks past the tree where the wind grabs an air,
and lifts strands of her braid through the bare branches' hair.
The twigs don't hold tight—they let her be sway,
a moment of motion they can't quite display.
Her foot hit something near the half-open door,
a neon flip-flop spinning on the floor.
She traced the path where it had slid down the hall,
then kicked it home with one sharp jump and a call.
I'm standing outside your classroom once again late,
I argue with time as I trudge to the gate.
Your lecture begins before I even reach door,
I wish I could turn back the clock to restore.

topic: reading under the covers with a flashlight
lines: I swore I would never do what my kid did,
like read by a flashlight with the covers hid.
Now here I am, face lit up in the blame,
pretending I'm not hiding a secret fame.
She watches the soap rise up toward the sky,
her little hands try to catch each high.
The colors begin to blur and then fade,
the fleeting joy floats off in a parade.
Your shoulders sag low from the daily ache,
You stretch for a moment, quick as a break.
Your spine creaks loudly—it's caught in your back,
The mouse still moves fast on its silent track.
She fixed her flat tire with nothing but ground,
scavenged parts from a junkyard she found.
No help from a shop or a manual tool,
she learned how by trial and error at school.
They rise from the soil like ghosts on the floor,
I check each new spot, want some, fear for some more.
These mushrooms just bloom in the dark and the gloom,
but are they safe to keep or should I clear my room?
The sky turns to something warm and old,
like memories that never really hold.
I watch the light slip through the boughs and past,
shadows stretch like ghosts the sun has cast.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: This coupon promised a bargain, not a deal,
so here I am, peeling back layers to peel.
I rip open the package—tiny, thin, sad bag,
and wonder why I even kept this discount tag.
I took a sniff and knew it was the smell,
the kind of stink that makes your nose go hell.
I opened up the carton to begin to pour,
but even waste feels like loss, a little more.
She watches the scanner light flicker and scan,
the cashier's been here before, but not with a fan.
Her budget was tight, but this total is near,
she prays it's a glitch from some old expired year.
They thought they'd get a quick reply from chat,
but midnight waits for no one but their cat.
The thumbs hover clumsy, trying to send,
while the brain screams, "Just sleep, good friend."
I need more room but I guard this space,
it's the only thing left from my old place.
A draft could come through and turn it to storm,
I double-check every knot, every form.
You tap the screen, but it won't let you try,
the bar stays frozen beneath the gray sky.
It's been at ninety-nine forever now stuck,
while you scroll idle stories without any luck.
I twisted the knob but had no luck with key,
the lock groaned like someone asking for a fee.
I kicked it, I yelled, I tried to make it spin,
though nothing worked to help me get it begin.

topic: a long queue at the coffee shop
lines: She's standing third in the coffee shop line,
humming a tune I've heard once before in mine.
Not fazed by the slow-moving barista brew,
she sips her latte like it's the best part of view.
You drop the coins in slow, deliberate past,
the machine clicks once, then buzzes your last.
Your hand stays open like a question mark,
the change won't land—no time left to park.
They said they'd return it with a digital scan,
but here's your paper back, red marks from some man.
You spent a week on it—they couldn't even grade,
the ink's already starting to fade.
You watched it fall and break into shell,
the yellow yolk threatened to spill and to yell.
It shimmered like something too soft to be gold,
like a memory gone fragile and cold.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: You always see the same familiar name,
the same pews, the same unspoken flame.
But this week there's a new face for the change,
and somehow the routine feels oddly strange.
You stared out the window, this crawl turning ride,
your reflection blending with the passing side.
The minutes keep growing, the silence feels slow,
but the sunset ahead starts to softly glow.
That can still bears a dent from myself,
I gave it a whack when I slipped on the shelf.
Time turned its lid into a slow bloom of rust,
yet I leave it there, like old toast without the crust.
This banana's skin is brown and quite thin,
