But inside it's mushy and falling within.
I try to pretend that I don't hear its smell,
It screams from the counter—it's banana hell.
I dropped the coin but it just won't try,
it's stuck in a slot where hope runs dry.
I nudge it again—still a total miss,
the machine's laughing at my coinless this.
My ATM said zero when I swiped my card,
probably off by a decimal in the yard.
I'll just go down to the branch and ask my bank,
maybe they'll explain it in plain old Frank.
You watch the pigeon glide through the air,
as if it's earned the feast from a fast-food fair.
You laugh but still you feel a quiet cry,
it soars away with your snack in the sky.
They stood there as the fading day gave light,
the way the colors folded into sight.
Shadows stretched in long, unspoken calm,
soft and warm, like a quiet, lingering balm.
Your lower back has started to ache,
you need a stretch but no one will take.
You twist your body, try to work your core,
but your legs won't carry you near the door.
We walked in silence as the day turned dusk,
your perfume lingering like old summer musk.
You pointed out stars through the tree-lined lane,
while the sky began to drizzle soft rain.
I missed my stop thinking I'd caught the train,
the conductor asked, "Would you like to try again?"
My pass was lost—I forgot to pay the fare,
and now I sit in the guilt of awkward air.
A single drop escaped and made a slow spill,
the room holds its breath while the color runs still.
It paints a path across the wooden floor blue,
and somehow feels like something real is made true.
My day is ruined—I will place the blame
on that damn bottle now rolling into fame.
I tried to bend down for just one quick sip,
and there it was, waiting to make me trip.
She steps out early, but can't see the view,
her sneakers splash through the puddles they knew.
The tires spin where the blacktop lost grip,
she holds tight, praying not to take a trip.
You're looking for a nickname but lack a clue,
so you use your name and add some glue.
The logic isn't clear—it's built from a bean—
but now everyone sees it on their screen.
You paid through the nose for that airport deal,
a lukewarm cup pretending to be a meal.
The whole flight was just about this one trip,
yet sipping it feels like letting go of a grip.
You scratch your head like there's some clue,
pacing and meowing like you're in a stew.
You fixate on the same dull spot,
and lick that wall until it's gone all hot.
She pays full price, hands the ten to the back,
no shortcut, no trying to play the discount track.
She wants the whole sandwich, not some cheap meal,
she says, "I work hard—I buy what feels real."
You left the keyboard in a sugary mess,
now I'm typing through the syrupy press.
The spacebar's stuck, it leaves a weird stain,
my thoughts are slow—this is not good for brain.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: You hit *play* and the old show tries to play,
a laugh drowns your memory, drifts away.
The moment's long gone, but still lingers past,
a sudden laugh track from your past, a blast.
She watches it pool like a memory spread,
the silence still lingers from something she said.
It never gets enough time to go warm,
the toast burns black while the moment turns storm.
You shove both your shoes beneath the chair,
pretending they're hidden and not out of pair.
Your toes wiggle slightly, I see the grin,
it's obvious this game will soon have to begin.
She grabs the remote, it clicks, but nothing comes out,
A frown forms her brow—she starts to feel doubt.
She takes out the batteries, both are clearly dead,
She sighs and sits back down, just shaking her head.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: You clicked the photo before the frame,
freezing a moment where no one could stay the same.
Now years later you trace the past,
wishing you'd blinked just a little bit fast.
I watch the bus driver slump at the wheel,
the vehicle swerves slightly, makes me reel.
He never told anyone this would be his stop,
but now we're all waiting to hear his drop.

topic: chair squeaks when you lean back
lines: I tried to sit down and just relax my back,
but the chair screamed like it had lost its track.
I leaned once more—*of course* it screeched again,
this thing's louder than my thoughts' whole train.
He sends a meme at three to save his soul,
the screen is all he has left to scroll.
It lands unseen on the "read" list below,
no one laughs, but they never do—no show.
I didn't know they were saved from long ago,
my phone uploaded a silent little show.
I scroll through strangers, but one familiar face,
brings back a room I never thought had space.
She takes another slow, deliberate shot,
the flash glows once—it lands on the spot.
The lens captures light as it filters through,
for the first time, her hope feels a little more true.
She turns the corner where the streetlight doesn't bend,
half-expecting a ghost or an old friend.
The jazz is soft, the coffee's slow to pour,
and time feels off by minutes on the floor.
My dog still pulls me down the lead,
but I pretend my heart isn't dead.
There's hope that this walk won't be a talk
of giving up — today we take a walk.
The toaster made a loud, alarming pop,
I yelled "Oh no!" and slammed it on the stop.
Now crumbs are everywhere, what a mess,
this morning just keeps adding up to stress.
She brought a cake for the party, the treat,
but the dog danced around her warm feet.
We watched in shock as he snatched it and did
a clumsy happy dance, like a pup with a kid.

topic: finding a dollar in old jeans
lines: A crumpled bill gleams like forgotten gold,
I flex my jeans—no pocket could have hold.
It's been months since I had change to call mine,
and now luck grins, bold as a fortune line.
You stepped into the café, soft as air,
and melted every shadow on the stair.
I didn't need your voice to know your name,
your smile was written on my empty frame.
My dog's been accused of stealing socks and hide,
He winks when I ask if he's been on my side.
I found a blue heel half-gnawed by his chew,
But he barks at the camera—no proof, no clue.
I wind up the box with a tiny old key,
it sings only this one sad song for me.
The ballerina twirls in her slow little spin,
I hear memories dancing deep in my skin.
You watch it dance across the room's worn floor,
your shadow blocking every draft from door.
Its nose detects the faintest hint of scent,
but finds you there, with nothing but your intent.

topic: socks left in the laundry pile
lines: They've searched the laundry for a single pair,
convinced one sock is floating in the air.
They text you photos asking "What's the why?"
You know they'll toss the rest if you don't reply.
My goldfish stares through his tiny view,
like he's plotting a mission or fresh-caught stew.
He slams against the glass with a headbutt slam,
as if he wants to join me for toast and jam.
I watch the bulb burn low with quiet glow,
it flickers hard to put on one last show.
It hums against its time—defying fate,
and dies a dramatic, cinematic great.
My legs start to buzz and they won't quit tick,
They beg me to move, so I give them a kick.
I try to distract them by humming a hum,
But they dance with delight—they refuse to come.
You can see it's fake right through her smile through,
she's already thinking "not this one, you."
She says "total's $15" with no real cost,
just another soul who's checked out and is lost.
She spots the last crumb still clinging to the floor,
she bends down again, this time hoping for more.
Her clean-up app claims this spot is a mess,
her therapist would call this routine pure stress.
I thought a coffee might be my quick fix,
but stress is a poison, not a bitter mix.
It pounds behind my eyes like a slow drum,
and logic can't chase it far enough to come.
You'd tap your foot to the pipes' low hum,
always waiting for the echo to come.
Back when stuck doors felt like sacred time,
you'd laugh instead of trying to climb.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: You kept your phone off from dusk till the call,
the silence pressed close like a quiet gray wall.
You moved through the hours at a dreamlike slow,
but missed how the world moves when you don't have to know.
You lie there quiet, screen dark and still,
I know you're waiting to be heard, to fulfill
your purpose, resting in my warm hand,
but sometimes the best love means to understand.
My hamster thinks he's chasing lasting fame,
spinning endlessly in his plastic game.
He's close enough to touch, but far from near,
like a man on a treadmill sipping beer.

topic: a long queue at the coffee shop
lines: You tapped your fingers against the counter bar,
waiting for the latte that might still not mar.
The line moves slower than a Sunday pace,
and you're thinking how this was not the place.
She started her trip with a coffee in hand,
a $7 drip brew from the duty-free stand.
She smiled as she left all the change she had paid,
sipping her guilt in a relaxed, sunlit shade.
You think you're being helpful as you talk,
but no one cares if you explain the chalk.
Your voice gets more than a little loud,
and the whole line starts to treat you like a crowd.
I woke in a position that screamed "no twist,"
my morning routine now reads off the list.
My neck holds a tension it just can't shake,
yet somehow, this pain feels too slow to break.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: He wandered off in the busy afternoon park,
strangers gave glances but never made a remark.
His tiny hands held tight, trying not to cry,
while the balloon floated up toward the low sky.
That burnt toast smell sticks to the hotel smell,
a breakfast from hell, black and well-dried hell.
I'd trade this cold plate for the road I left cold,
where memories taste sweet, though they're slightly old.
I watch it drift so slow, this fish that float,
as if it left a message for me to note.
It flips through currents like a part of sky,
and I wonder softly why I don't try.
You love the way those brittle leaves make sound,
you stomp through piles, claiming every pound.
This is your kingdom, you set its own tone,
a crunching symphony only you have known.
She smells something odd in the musty old air,
checks under the sink for a cleaning product spare.
The soap tastes like regret, the towel is thin,
she checks out before her last hope runs in.
Your body was humming, a steady, warm fire,
now your phone buzzes like a dead wire.
You tried to ride the high, like a crashing wave,
but now you're deflating, turning into a cave.
She stirs the pot where the warm steam meets the air,
humming a tune like a wish to be fair.
This recipe's hers, she says it makes good love,
and maybe today, some luck from above.
The rhythmic click sets off your nervous tone,
you mutter prayers to not feel quite so alone.
You cast another loop, try to stay cast,
but every stitch feels haunted by the past.
I dropped my shaker and the lid wouldn't shake,
Now powder's a cloud where the kitchen's a lake.
This isn't just dust—it's a gym-fail mess,
But somehow it makes me giggle instead of stress.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: She rolls around in the puddles and dirt,
her T-shirt soaked through from head to shirt.
She builds a castle of clay and a mound,
and rules the backyard where muck meets ground.
I loaded it right, but it just won't run,
the plates look like they've seen the sun.
It's not a big mess, but it's not my sort,
the manual's unclear, so I call in support.
You sort through the envelopes forming a pile,
the dog chews your shoe for a quiet while.
You pause and watch sunset paint the gray sky,
then sigh and ask fate the same question why.
You took them from my plate with your free hand,
like you owned the whole table and its land.
They were salt-crisped, hot, like stolen gold,
and now I sulk alone, with hunger bold.
You stop to look at the colors that glow,
the kind that makes you feel you should know.
It promises things that it can't help but lie,
you wonder if truth is too far to fly.
You wave the blackened slice out of the smoke,
Your morning was fine until it all broke.
You grab coffee just to get the day run,
But the burnt mess feels like your whole plan undone.
You match my shirt like you had a clue,
I laugh because I know it's just for you.
We're rolling through life like a matched pair should,
two weirdos with no clue what our souls could.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: You spot a toothpick wedged in your sleeve right there,
it's been with you all day without a care.
You fish it out with the napkin in your hand,
now everyone stares—it's like a weird new brand.
I need three feet of real estate, my space,
but their keyboard clacks in this loud, chaotic place.
They stream their game every lunch break, full feed,
while I try to focus, my patience slowly bleed.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: I tap my card to pay and just stand away,
the screen shows "declined" in bold display.
I dig through my pockets for some spare cash,
but all I find is old leftover ash.
You used to keep your phone out of your hand,
where highways had no stories worth their sand.
Now you miss those days that feel so old,
when safety came wrapped in risk, not sold.
I can't seem to get these tingles to go away,
they buzz in my veins since the tail end of day.
My toes won't stop twitching, I try to force move,
but my legs will not settle into any groove.
It rolls in soft and slow, the fog gives things a lift,
like morning's quiet wrapped up in a gift.
The world holds its breath like it doesn't want to seem
so fragile, just a hush above the creek's cold stream.
I stand here like statues, we all keep the same pace,
my reflection is stuck in the window's dull face.
There's nowhere to go but I'm sure they'll ask more,
the car door won't budge—it's welded to the floor.
The mower starts again—its loud, cruel roar,
you bolt your windows like a paranoid store.
Your hands are shaking now, the air feels tense,
you swear it's aimed at you, this noise offense.
Her video keeps glitching mid-stream,
she laughs and calls it her buffering dream.
She switches the task, lets the page keep its load,
then flips to airplane just to be in peace mode.
You trace where the salt once clung to the grain,
now washed down the sink in a quiet plain.
You still reach for the mill, make your usual shake,
but miss it just slightly—like time you can't take.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: You check the number one last time on screen,
the digits don't feel like what they should mean.
Your phone's blue light still has a little glow,
but you're too tired to let it keep you from go.
Your lips are soft beneath this flickering light,
my pulse is loud and our breathing feels tight.
I swear you've got some kind of magic in your soul,
the world could end and we'd still be this whole.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: You watch your cat let out a soft sigh,
curled up where the sunlight likes to lie.
There's peace in this moment, here at home,
and you hope it will never feel the need to roam.
I trace the arc where the hawk carves the sky,
it glides without effort or reason to fly.
I wish I could soar when it lets out that call,
but today's enough if I lift up from all.
I scroll through the snaps from the summer view,
your smile is the kind that's just always true.
You wore something white, a dress that fit tight—
the whole town still talks about how you shined that night.
Your breakfast is now a dark and crispy char,
You swear you set the crumpets on low, not star.
You spread the remains with a dollop of jam,
And laugh as your cat gives a toast-inspired slam.
She turns up the shower and loses all time,
her warbling could shake the last dime from a chime.
She claims this is just about a hot bath,
but there's foam on the walls down the hallway's whole path.
I dug through my bag for some loose spare cash,
crumpled bills, nickels, and banana peel mash.
Coins dropped with a clink in the register's cup,
a ritual from when cards didn't connect up.

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: I shift into third like it changes my gear,
the wind slaps me upside my face in the rear.
I'm chasing some myth called a safe top speed,
my palms are all sweaty—my nerves just bleed.
You try to snap the sunset but can't see
what the lens wants for its golden fee.
It hunts for contrast, a spark to make a ring,
and turns your blurry world into a clever thing.
My phone's screen blinks red, but I choose to let go,
It's time to unplug and actually show
My phone's dead, but the sunlight shines right through,
This unplugged moment feels perfectly true.
You follow the path where the forest trail,
bends under the trees in their rusty pale.
Each step becomes music, crisp and gold,
a playlist of autumn, you walk it bold.
My suitcase sits open, my things still in case,
My cat chose this spot as her favorite place.
She curls on the fabric, on plastic, so bare,
Her purr fills the silence just floating in air.
You leave receipts on tables to make it a show,
the ink still fresh and the barcodes glow.
You're not even trying to hide your wild kind,
of life that throws money around like wind.
You used to wear them with purpose and time,
now they sit in the dark, gathering grime.
You left them this way, but still keep them apart,
maybe one day you'll miss the place in your heart.
You tap through the menu and pick from the app,
It promises fast but it's clearly a trap.
The fries are still warm when you finally get eat,
You microwave the burger to give it some heat.
You watch the dandelion clock begin to blow,
each white fluff escaping out and off and go.
You try to grab one but your fingers won't hold,
like time itself—too fast to ever be old.
The flicker turns the dark into a haunted room,
like ghosts are dancing where the images loom.
I lean in close, half hoping I might see
the pattern that will show me how to be.
I still remember the fizz in the air,
we bought it all at the roadside fair.
It lasted months, a half-empty week,
now I just stare where the spout once would speak.

topic: ice forming on the car windshield
lines: My breath turns frost before it reaches skin,
the car sits silent, trapped and tight within.
I can't grip the wheel—it's slick to the hold,
this morning tried to freeze me to the cold.
You hit play again, hoping it might start
where the last time left off—still not your heart.
A new favorite line plays in the scene,
and maybe this time it won't feel so mean.
You spilled snacks and now your keyboard's a mess,
Each key feels like it won't let you press.
You hear a faint *crack* when you try to type crack,
The cursor moves wrong—your mouse can't track.
They started a chain to save all their time,
now it curves down the desk like a climb.
Each link they twist feels like a small bend,
but the edge nears where the story must end.
You tap the glass, but it won't get clear,
your breath leaves clouds like steam off a beer.
The road ahead is lost to the view,
so you blink slowly, like glue meets glue.
You watch the small bird shake dust from the air,
its chest beats fast, but it doesn't seem to care.
One foot on the stick, one foot on the wing,
it practices songs it will never get to sing.
You said my name as if it slipped your mind,
Not cruel, but lost—like me behind.
You meant to say it, yet you called me wrong,
I've carried this smile, too soft and long.
I reached for the bottle labeled "sun,"
the spray was cheap but the label said "fun."
A streak hit my shoulder—now there's a mark,
but I laugh it off like a true beginner spark.
They sent five messages and then stopped all talk,
no emoji, no snub—just a cold walk.
Not even a screenshot or a read mark to trace,
just silence and a profile pic still in place.
You curse the car in front like it knows your true flame,
no one honks their horn without shouting a name.
Tires screech, engines whine but you stay in your shift,
this road rage—clearly not your best damn gift.
You walk through the yard where the grass used to ground,
and spot soft caps where the fungi have found.
They peek out from moss in the dappled morning light,
a quiet kind of miracle, clear and bright.

topic: someone handing you a surprise gift
lines: I took the box from your outstretched hand,
my eyes searched for clues where it might stand.
This is more than a label or gift,
it's a weight I feel rising to lift.
She sticks a note where the cursor draws near,
the blinking text starts to slowly appear.
It's in all caps, color set to red,
just three short words she keeps typing said.
You watch the curling plume rise from the steam,
a quiet escape to some distant dream.
You sip the warmth steeped in memory mint,
and trace the faded label with ghostly print.
The bulb gave one last flicker before the glow,
and now every step feels like things might go
wrong. She searches for the switch in a mess
of shadows, scared her life will be safer with less.
You try to budge the bathroom door in time,
the toilet's been flushed—this feels like a crime.
You twist the knob again, a slow, tight spin,
the door won't budge an inch, your patience thin.
You check the router box at the front door,
then kneel down to look under the floor.
You've tried every hint you could have tried,
but the password's vanished from your side.
The kitchen's warm with the ghost of last year's heat,
you stirred the batter with something too sweet.
Now the frosting runs down the sides like you know,
your hands made magic but time had to show.
They left their toothbrush in the sink for an hour,
still pointing proudly like it had some power.
It didn't budge when anyone asked it to rise,
but watched the morning through half-closed eyes.
I step outside where the cold bites the air,
the world is a picture too pale to be fair.
Each blade of grass wears a silvered patch,
and I'm the only one who can show it a match.
You speak in the air while I float out of air,
some distant stair lures my mind upward, stair by stair.
I imagine a light you could never quite light,
a sudden escape into starlit flight.
You crush a clove and the room fills with scent,
Your fingers twist, they are all now bent.
You hold your breath to avoid the breath,
But garlic clings like the thought of death.

topic: a taxi driver yelling on phone
lines: He's shouting into the phone, full yell,
arguing loud about some stock to sell.
His hands grip tight, his foot slams the floor,
the cab shakes like he wants to drive for more.
He slides sideways and finally goes down,
His head lolls back, now the couch holds his crown.
One leg hangs off, a foot near the leg,
Don't even think about it—it's not a beg.
My kitchen light acts like it doesn't know
what half-lit shadows it's supposed to show.
It buzzes like an old expired date,
but stays alive—some kind of bad fate.
You hold the twist of air, a snake curled tight,
you watch it wag its tail and rise in flight.
The monkey gave it life, but you won't let it stay—
you whisper, "Not today," as it floats away.
The stadium leaks like a sieve on the goal,
half the fans are singing off-key and out of soul.
The players look like soggy ghosts on the pitch,
we're debating whether it's a game or a ditch.
They never smooth out the crease in the fold,
just drape it there when the morning gets cold.
It's not about laundry or how much they press,
but something soft left hanging like a bless.
I watched it hop through the garden's green stalk,
my voice caught in my throat, too scared to talk.
It pauses now, right by my fresh crop,
and I can't seem to move—I just want it to stop.
The light goes out just as I walk about,
I check my phone—no signal, no doubt.
It buzzes now, a rhythm, a hum,
and draws a moth that flits straight up to come.

topic: sharing a cat video with no context
lines: You sent me a clip where the cat bats the frame,
the background faded, no caption or name.
I watched it again under dimmed bedroom light,
your love came through loud in that quiet, odd night.
She sank into the warm salted sand,
holding tight the broken fiberglass hand.
A gull circled high in the fading light,
but she smiled—defiance growing bright.
She runs outside to make a leafy show,
twirling in the mess they dropped below.
"This is why I hate autumn," she yells—no dance,
just a mad sprint and a backward glance.
It sits in the pantry like a loaf in the air,
untouched since the day we moved down the stair.
I opened the bag and faced the decay,
but couldn't bring myself to pitch it away.
We're a blur of faces in a nameless mix,
I'll call you Benji when you're clearly not the fix.
You'll correct me gently, no harsh clue,
"It's Owen," you'll say, and I'll still call you "you."
You knew this test would return without a grade,
your answers still marching in neat little parade.
Your eyes scan each box for a red pen's sharp mark,
but silence sits where the judgment should have been stark.
You let the story take its own good time,
savoring each word like a quiet climb.
You won't speed through it to leave your mark—
you read to feel the fire in your spark.
You tried to catch the cloud's soft form,
but time moved faster than a summer storm.
The lines you drew began to fade,
while memories passed in a slow parade.
She licks her lips clean of the pinkish hue,
The mug remembers what she won't say to you.
A ghostly smear clings to the bottom stain,
Like secrets she sips and swallows again.
The sky is leaking but my umbrella's rain,
My shoes are soaked and my brain can't explain.
I step into a puddle — that's the floor,
This walk won't fix me, can't quite restore.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: She checks her phone just once more before scroll,
but "just a peek" turns into losing control.
Her follower count didn't really rise,
but she's wide awake with numbers in her eyes.
I swear it was meant for someone else, fate,
but now I'm stuck waiting for her to be late.
She says it was all just one big bad joke,
but I'm still seeing reds I can't ignore, smoke.
That bulb's been flickering like my bad mood,
Is it haunted or just some stale old food?
It buzzes and wavers, won't hold a steady glow,
I still haven't fixed it—was it three days ago?
There it is, the sticky note, still stuck to the spot,
she wrote "temp_password1" and then forgot.
He slaps his head when he sees her palm,
she laughs and says, "Just don't panic—stay calm."
My skull feels like it might slowly crush,
some silent engine inside gives a rush.
I scan my inbox for some reason to beam,
but only dread stays tangled in my scream.
I color-code my life in jagged, messy code,
from meetings to dentist on Monday's road.
You'd think the chaos was just pure bad mess,
but somehow it works—this strange visual less.

topic: crackling fireplace on a winter night
lines: I sit by the fire, this little room,
where shadows melt into quiet gloom.
A single log cracks, it makes a soft spark,
and lights my face from the coming dark.
She turns up the heat, the first strip begins to crack,
she leans in closer, the oil starts to slink back.
The air gets thick, a little too much smoke,
she coughs but keeps cooking, the smell still a choke.
You twist the pencil, still it won't shed lead,
the blade is clogged with shavings like old bread.
You try to force it, making the knob spin,
until the wood cracks and the shaft grows thin.
They left a damp towel on the bench—no clue,
like it's a message written in wet and blue.
They think they're subtle, pulling off this act,
but we both know it's just a lonely fact.
You let the sheet sit, cold and undone,
while golden light spills in from the sun.
Time moves too slow as the metal grows cold,
and you know the moment will never grow old.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: She tosses the bread into the air,
A pair of pigeons squawks and flutters there.
They peck in the frost like a painted snow,
But she laughs and lets them fly and go.
I brew my coffee just a little too deep,
the neighbors probably heard me shout "sleep!"
It's a blackened, bitter, slow-moving drip,
but somehow I'm walking on caffeine-induced trip.
You start laughing out of thin air,
it catches me off guard and fair.
A smile grows slowly on my face and I spot
how joy can hit you without warning or shot.
I got home to see the note stuck on the call,
it stood there on my porch, small but so tall.
It was just a form, a cold-faced thing,
but it still cut deep and left a sting.
The date for the payment has come and gone due,
your phone still ignores every overdue cue.
You know there's a fee for being this late,
but ignoring it feels too light to hate.
Your phone slips off your desk and hits the glass,
The screen is shattered, but you still pass the class.
You tap through the mess to give your best show,
The cracks twist the answers you try to know.
The sound from the TV is a full-on blast,
The neighbors will come running very fast.
You try to hide behind the dining room chair,
But the bass still shakes the windowpane in the air.
I watched the liquid fall from the glass,
it mirrored the sky on the morning grass.
A drop landed near my wedding ring,
and reminded me of the day's small thing.
It wobbles and bounces and does little spin,
but no matter how hard she tries, not in bin.
She kicks it instead, a small act of war,
the bottle just rolls where it always was—floor.
This wall is alive with some wild street art,
I pose for a photo, pretending it's part
of a secret mission or an escape plan—
the cops laugh too hard when I run down the lan.
Her smile is a script, every movement a grin,
her eyes say thank you, her lips feel too thin.
I hand her the bill and she hands me the cost,
her voice is all numbers, her warmth feels like frost.
You wanted fast food and no need for cash,
but the ATM gave you a zero dash.
Your card was working when you last tried it late,
now it won't open the craving or gate.
She pedals along the trail without a track,
until her bike lets out a sad flat back.
A stranger hands her tools to help mend,
and laughter turns a glitch into a good end.
He talks about his ex like they were still a talk,
even while he stumbles on the curb as we walk.
She tries to laugh it off — this first date's a date,
but the tension here feels more like a declared state.
I begged my cousin for his ticket pass,
we waited outside where the venue grass
was damp with sweat from the stage light's glow,
my hands still shake, but I don't want this night to go.
She stops chewing to read the next scroll,
her sandwich melts while she takes full control.
The tweet was a meme, a dumb little joke,
her laugh burns the bread, now there's smoke.
It's not just the socks she likes to chew,
it's the way they keep her close and true.
She'll steal one from under your leg,
then sit and wait until you beg.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: The dog wears a party hat with glue in his hair,
He's the star of the block, or so they declare.
He barks when it spins, but he can't stop the spin,
So we dance to the noise, laughing at the din.
The tension starts low in their jaw and feels tight,
They squint at the screen, blinking toward light.
With every soft sigh, they search for a breath,
But calm is too far, and peace seems like death.
You thought this cab would be a quiet ride,
but the driver won't let silence hide.
He tells tales from his life—some are old,
but there's hope in his voice, it feels so bold.

topic: socks left in the break room
lines: I search the break room for my missing pair,
hoping they're not still floating in the air.
Maybe tomorrow I'll just stop and find
the one that's lost — or let my brain be kind.
I left my heels at home for once—not for fun,
but I still can't keep my balance when I run.
These shoes may fit, but they won't help me feel
the way I did in sky-high soles that felt real.

topic: a book left open on the nightstand
lines: The book still waits where you left it on the page,
as if your thoughts were locked inside that cage.
The lamp glows soft, but the room feels still and light,
you'll close it soon as the hours slip into night.
It's still playing the song from that rainy day,
the screen shows the same colors, washed-out and gray.
The dancer keeps spinning, stuck in her spin,
and I swear I can feel her, deep in my skin.
You crumpled the ticket after the final show,
but the memory still makes your cheeks glow.
It was more than just a cheap cinema date—
you like to say it felt like destiny's fate.
The photo on my ID shows my old hair,
I used to dye it neon pink and fair.
They wave me through—no one questions the scan,
my style may be bold, but their trust was my plan.
You sing off-key but you don't let it key,
the water's hot and you're wild and free.
You hold a bad note just to tease the note,
pretend this drain is a boat and float.
She wakes before the morning's pale light,
the garden expects her each springtime sight.
The tulips have pushed up through soil to grow,
she kneels there each year and she seems to know.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: A child is wailing loud down this long aisle,
her candy wrapper crumpled on the tile.
Her mother's hand is tight on her small cry,
she keeps repeating, "But I don't know why."
He watches the tank where the fish put on a show,
flipping loops like stars caught spinning slow.
His hands press against the cold and silent glass,
a strange new world turned into liquid mass.
Our eyes met, and our fingers gave a spark,
You laughed it off but I still make that remark.
You think you're slick, you know what you're gonna do,
I'm faking it, but I've got no clue.
The cat claimed the suitcase as his resting case,
curled tight like it was his favorite place.
His low hum vibrates through the leather and fur,
the wheels stay locked—no moving, no blur.
You yawn so wide it could set a new show,
your face still holds that sleepy slow glow.
The clock ticks loud as you sink in the chair,
and no one dares even stir in the air.

topic: a cup of cold coffee on the table
lines: The cup sits there with a faint smirk,
as if it did most of the work.
A lipstick stain makes a lazy ring,
and you pretend it's still the best thing.
My battery blinks red but I haven't shut yet,
I'm still logged into this world I can't get.
Maybe there's life in the thing after all—soul,
it hums like I'm not losing my control.
He claims he owns no such thing as a pair,
the socks just fall off each morning down stair.
He wears one brown and one gray with a smell,
but never gets asked if it's style or it's hell.
I left the cart key but now it's been found,
it jingles again with its old familiar sound.

the room feels warm beneath the heat.
I've got no space but there's room for grace,
you turn your face and meet my face.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: The flicker is low, my only flame,
I whisper to shadows, say my name.
The silence grows thick and it feels so cold,
I move forward, though I'm too scared to be bold.
I click play hoping this review will save the game,
it's already jumping from scene to frame.
They say there's a patch that might be the fix,
but now I'm lost in what their take might mix.
You mix the words until they start to blend,
you laugh and type a message just to send.
Your accent slips out loud and clear as far,
the whole chat room replies like you're a star.

topic: a dog leash tangled in railings
lines: You follow the leash still tied to the trail,
It loops like old letters no one can mail.
You wish your dog could run wild and be free,
But the knot stays tight—like a lock with no key.
You swerve down the sidewalk in my way,
your bell jingles loud enough to wake the day.
I jump, half-laughing, like you meant to scream,
your grin's the kind I'd chase in a dream.
I watch it bob its head, so calm and still,
the wind kicks up and rattles the railing until
it freezes mid-hop, eyes locked on sky,
just like me, I guess, wondering why.

topic: a taxi driver yelling on phone
lines: You hear him shout above the traffic loud,
his voice cuts through the city's moving crowd.
He curses the app for some lost fare,
while red lights flash and tempers flare.
They're always half an hour late.
Their keys are still under the gate.
One sock lies untied on the mess
of the floor, and it gives me stress.
She checks the bag's expiration date,
unsure if she should eat or wait.
The peas sit cold beneath the frost,
their freshness fading fast, now lost.
I open the bag and catch its faded scent,
the kernels crumpled, spilled and now bent.
It wasn't just popcorn—it was movie gold,
but now it's just trash from a memory I hold.
She swears the chimes are playing her favorite tune,
though no one else sees anything in the moon.
It's just the wind, but she insists it's her old pain,
reliving every memory—yet **again**.
You keep collecting that travel mail,
postmarked from places you haven't trail.
Each note is a "what if" you choose to stay,
but the stamps remain un-purchased today.

topic: a group project where nobody helps
lines: I show up early to carry the run,
while they text "I'll do it" and never get done.
They ask for the file but won't give their share,
they breathe all the credit, take zero air.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: You spotted the kid stuck near the grocery aisle,
his red balloon wobbling with every smile.
He doesn't know how to find his parents' way,
but you pretend it's a game—it's a perfect day.
The radio signal starts to spin,
Static takes over, the sound gets thin.
I fiddle with dials in deadened air,
Searching for music, lost in my care.

topic: someone spilling punch on the rug
lines: You sent the punch flying across the room up,
glass shattering like a well-timed cup.
There's pride in your grin as the mess takes gleam,
while everyone else tries not to scream.
You smooth your face like it's perfect skin,
but who do you hide deep inside you within?
The filter gives you a flawless glow,
yet hides the real you—no one can show.
You still have glitter from some long-lost day,
A neon shred stuck where you thought it was away.
It dances there like one bold, happy flake,
A tiny mistake that somehow looks like cake.
My phone rings out like a wedding bell,
but I'm not celebrating — it's bad news from hell.
I stop what I do and I have to read,
it's just a survey they really don't need.
He found my favorite spot, that's his only space,
he parks there with pride and a smug little face.
I circle the lot again, feel like a miss,
while he sips coffee in his lucky bliss.
I leave the kitchen light on for its soft glow,
you'll say I'm doing it just so you'll know.
I don't have to call you now—no need at all,
the bulb hums warm against the silence in the hall.
You leave your toaster out because it's old,
Its edges rusted, still warm from the gold
Of afternoon sun slipping through the light,
Until the shadows tell you it's goodbye tonight.
She brought a blanket and a full picnic meal,
the sky turned gray, and it all felt too real.
She shielded her face with a soggy white head,
while crickets took crumbs from her sandwich and bread.
I remember the way she kicked the plane's aisle,
her tiny feet working hard while I tried to smile.
We were flying so high through that wide blue sky,
but all I heard was the echo of her cry.
The U-lock refused to twist or turn tight,
I stared at it long into the cold night.
My bike's combination code still in my key,
I smiled—it's unlocked now, but not yet set free.
My cursor blinks, this message is late,
I rethink our conversation, no date.
I press "send" but my finger won't send,
the silence remains and it cuts like an end.
I flick the switch hoping for warm air to heat,
but the fan just hums the same tired repeat.
I pace through the house, check each empty room,
expecting the walls to suddenly bloom.

topic: seeing a price tag too high
lines: She spots the number with a roll of her eye,
calls it an old sticker still stuck there to lie.
She smiles and walks right past it with class,
and leaves the store through the self-checkout glass.

topic: eating ice cream with a spoon
lines: They scoop a rainbow into a perfect swirl,
the way they eat it makes my world twirl.
Their spoon goes deep for every single dip,
and never once do they let chocolate slip.
I found a soft fluff behind an old spot,
it's flopped down beside my half-empty cot.
I reached to move it—then stopped at its fur,
too cute to scold, but I swear it will bur.
She flips the pancakes like they're made of air,
the griddle sizzles, but she isn't there.
Her movements match the stove's soft blue flame,
I almost call her… but I know her name.
You thought today would be your perfect morning,
but smoke curled up from the pan, a golden warning.
You watched the coffee brew, calm, full of steam,
while flames licked crumbs you never let become a dream.
The payment date came and went without a trace,
you sighed and blamed your fate to save your face.
You opened the app to write a late fee check,
only to remember your bank account's a wreck.
They take a big bite, they leave a mess,
and rub my white shirt with their messy dress.
I try to wipe off the jam with a smear
of napkin and laughter, and maybe a beer.
You hear the clear trill of a morning song,
a breeze is dancing lazy, light, and long.
The blue is wide and the clouds look sky,
would you rush when a bird asks, "Why?"
You stood under the broken bus stop rain,
water dripping through where the roof would remain.
A flicker above shifted into a light,
and you pulled your coat in, just slightly more tight.
You press your paws against the wall for calm,
as if its salt could offer you some balm.
You circle slow, your rhythm sets the pace,
your tongue finds cracks to turn into a face.

topic: ice forming on the car windshield
lines: Frost clings to the glass like frozen skin,
The warmth inside can't melt it from within.
Cold seeps through cracks in the weak old air,
They drive off with the world still half bare.
My gym bag's a total, chaotic mess,
I suppose it's time to clean this up and confess.
I open a snack that's long past its time,
and find shoe goo where my sock should be, divine grime.
You swear your phone would rather not ring,
though it seems like the only normal thing.
You fumble through pockets to check if it move,
but silence just mocks you — there's nothing to prove.

topic: a child drawing on the table
lines: I trace the colors the kid left as art,
a messy reminder of childhood's heart.
The table is stained like a canvas, half-page,
but somehow it feels more alive than a cage.
You stumble outside still full of the mess,
the party was loud in that cheap little dress.
Confetti is tangled where it should be hair,
you laugh and spin, sending bits through the air.
You twist the old socket for one last try,
the bulb shivers faint as the stormy sky.
Maybe it'll burst back to soft, steady glow,
you've learned to hope when all else feels like slow.
She spends ten minutes perfecting her face,
then chooses a filter full of lace.
Her skin looks too smooth, her teeth too glow,
but she insists this is how they should know.
I swear this screen has started to glow
like it's trying to upstage my own show.
My eyes beg for the dark to fade,
but I'm stuck here in a blue-lit shade.
I curled up tight and drifted right down,
the couch is clearly my new downtown.
Don't look at me, this isn't my blame—
the cushions called me by my full name.
You check your phone to be one hundred percent sure,
the numbers swirl like there's no possible cure.
The line moves faster than your hands can count a dime,
and every second feels like wasted time.
You stare into the fogged-up mirror's back,
your breath still rising in the heated track.
The sweat and steam all blend into a mist,
you catch your face before it starts to twist.
I tried small talk to make some kind of spark,
but silence fell fast and left the room dark.
We swapped facts—boring, generic, same old chat,
the vibe died quickly, my excitement turned flat.
I blow until every bubble just pop,
they float through the air like a summer crop.
The light hits them just right — shimmer and sun,
I trip in the grass trying to catch them all, run.
She's scheduled three doctors since her last pill,
all chasing cures for some new thrill.
"Preventive care" sounds like a vague old care,
but she treats it like a romantic affair.
I feel untethered, wild and completely free,
no audience, no judgment, just my key.
Steam clouds the glass where I don't have to face
the silence waiting when the music leaves space.
I wipe my face but leave a streak to show,
the mirror glistens where my sweat began to glow.
I lift another weight, feel muscles start to try,
I might just hit my goal before today's last sky.
The strap gave out without a single snap,
my books now shifting in this paper trap.
I jaywalk and dread some sudden spill,
but tripping won't help me avoid the bill.
I reach for the wheel and see you miss the brake,
your eyes on your phone, this is a mistake.
The road bends ahead where the traffic is real,
and your silence tells me what the screen can't reveal.
I left the cart key somewhere in the mall,
I retrace my steps down every aisle and call.
There's nowhere to hide but I still can't find key,
I'm trapped in this store until I'm set free.
I watch the tuning fork grow still,
my quiet room begins to fill.
It hums its perfect, fading tone,
and I am left, yet not alone.
She chases the sunset's last soft glow,
the lens hums low as the world begins to go.
She snaps the scene, perfect in its frame,
and signs the light with her quiet, golden name.
Their left shoe gave out — the laces were string,
The wind laughed a little, said "weird old thing."
They stumbled but kept going, refused to fall,
But now that same foot won't stay tied at all.
I thought there was once a clean sock in this pair,
but now they both reek with gym stink and air.
A damp crease is growing where mold likes to mold,
I toss the whole bundle — I can't bear to hold.
She's running late but not because of track,
the treadmill screeches every time she turns back.
I've offered WD-40 more than just once or oil,
now the belt just spins—something's gone wrong with the coil.

topic: a favorite mug with a chip
lines: I try to keep my hands steady and hold,
but the crack in this mug feels oddly old.
A small flaw that's grown into something like a chip
on my confidence when it comes to a slip.
They sip their coffee, counting every hush,
the clock hands spinning from the 3 a.m. rush.
Their shadow stretches on the quiet floor,
but there's nothing left to say, and no one wants more.
You let the screen fade to critical blue,
pretending you never needed it that true.
You slow your step, keep your cool steady pace,
like the last charge's your final resting place.
The scanner whirs and plays pretend it can,
but my budget is still a vague, sad plan.
Credit card declined—again, it's due,
the cashier's shrug, my turn to cue.
They sent three GIFs and said they loved the talk,
then vanished off my screen mid-coffee walk.
Days passed with nary a "thinking of you" days,
classic ghosting — they were just a phase.
Your thumb moves slow across my palm like sky,
What are we doing here? Just you and why.
The world could crash, but we don't miss a beat,
This quiet hold—there's nothing like this heat.

topic: a child's drawings on the fridge
lines: Her latest creation now hangs on the art,
a lopsided figure with crayon-filled heart.
She used way too much glitter and glue,
the colors are wild but they all sing in hue.

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: She leans into the curve where the road takes a bend,
the wind her only companion and silent friend.
A red light flashes—she slows, eyes on the light,
hoping this moment will last and never might.
She searched the couch where she'd left it last room,
tracing circles like it was her old womb.
She'd never admit she forgot how to find
the buttons once fixed in her muscle and mind.
She leaves the plates in the sink feeling alone,
each fork and spoon rusting like fruit on a stone.
The smell of garlic still clings to what's left,
a meal now memory, the table bereft.
She waits for the page to fully load,
her coffee gone cold like a forgotten road.
The internet dies between her and the post,
her deadline now looming like a digital ghost.
They whisper goodbye but they never quite move,
their lips keep returning to the same old groove.
They claim they're not hungry, just want to lie,
but I see the truth in their flirty, kitchen eye.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: My cat has claimed this sofa's prime space,
and every time I move, she doubles her pace.
She curls around my arm in a feline spoon,
pretending I'm the sun, she's the moon.
The banana sits there in full yellow show,
it's past its prime and beginning to grow
a streak of brown that screams "don't make a mess,"
though maybe it could still be dessert's last bless.
I used to hate the neighbor's early-morning hum,
now I miss it when he says he won't come.
I walk out slow and pretend it's the sun
that wakes me, but I know the song is done.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: I hit "record" like it might still work if I try,
My voice cracks out through the static, so dry.
I speak my thoughts into thin air,
The screen fades out, nothing left but the bare.
You turn the corner and the road goes down,
but it's not closed—it's a new downtown.
A marching band passes by without a hum,
someone yells, "This was not in the come."
I left the wifi password locked out,
I didn't ask for help or even shout.
I cracked the sequence, mind sharp and code,
I fixed it alone—my genius in full mode.
My gym bag hit the ground, and everything went floor,
from weights to wet socks, something inside tore.
A gym sock's musk was the first smell I scent,
and now I know this mess was never what it meant.
You were deep in a game when the screen turned to shame,
chasing wins that now drift into fame.
Your thumb still moves where the glow used to scroll,
like a habit, or maybe something for your soul.
I watch them push up from the cold, wet head,
where frost still sleeps beneath the soft white bed.
They come in time, no matter how late the bloom,
and fill my dark little garden with their room.
The trailer opens with an ominous boom,
shadows fill up my darkened living room.
Each scene shows a hint but gives no clue,
my brain tries to guess what just flew.
She pauses mid-swipe, reads the post,
then laughs and grabs a buttered toast.
Her finger keeps moving, up the scroll,
but common sense wins — she hits control.
I drive this car like it's some deadly maze,
convinced I'm in the wrong life phase.
The gauge screams low, no fuel left to spark,
I'm stranded near a sign: "Gas Station – Park."
A baby wails through your window seat flight,
You watch clouds turn to gold in the morning light.
The infant's sobs begin to feel calm,
As you hum the old tune, soft as a balm.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: Her phone buzzed with a like—she dropped her jaw.
"This counts as contact," she muttered to the law.
She checks the post again, and now again, and now,
until her forehead tightens into a frown-brow.
She claims she's got a real dance flair,
but it's just her moving in the kitchen air.
She knocks the pan, sends soup flying dish,
this "performance" is one big kitchen mish.
You wear your smile like a store-bought grin,
it barely stretches beyond your lips, so thin.
It's just another part of your practiced act,
you'd rather swallow than say the cold, hard fact.
You left a voice so warm it barely fit the call,
your words stacking up, too rich for any tall.
I listen just once, then mute the old tone,
but keep the message so I'm never quite alone.
You wake up dreading the clock's next time,
it ticks out the hours like a warning chime.
You blame your boss for the work that came,
but deep down, you know it's your own name.
I never meant to put on this aquatic show,
but these fish won't stop bumping the tank's green glow.
They stare through the glass, they've got me in their eye,
like I owe them a story or a tie.

topic: a child drawing on the table
lines: She says this will be her masterpiece—art,
her marker ink seeps deep into the heart.
We scrub the table, but it won't wash from the slab,
now every meal there's a doodled crab.
There's birdseed scattered all over the mess,
the robin's been here to sign its address.
It pecks at the grass for the buried seed,
thinking this yard is a treasure indeed.
You watch the crowd surge in a single flow,
the traffic light turns green—you hesitate to go.
You wish someone would grab your hand,
but the city swallows you, no one to land.
You left your phone by the couch so near,
I know you'll see me even after a year.
I won't be the one to pick it up and lay
it gently back, but I still turn it away.
You stare at the wall as if it's the clue,
the paint peels in patches, it's faded to blue.
You lap at the dust with a quiet, dry grit,
then curl into silence, not sure where you fit.
The sky cracks open in colors too bright,
you walk alone where the silence feels tight.
You chase the tide with your shadow in stride,
but the dawn finds you and leaves nowhere to hide.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: You added a bow for a festive new style,
it perches atop an old paper plate pile.
But every time guests try to clap, you hear bark,
and still, you can't help but smile when it spark.
I press my palm to the glass, leave my ink,
half-distracted, I barely think.
The office glows in a tired old view,
my thoughts are stuck like dried-out glue.
She pats her pockets, looks for the key,
the lock just won't budge, she's not going free.
She tries every angle, gives it a twist,
the chain still holds tight—she just missed.
I won't admit the bottle has a dent,
but I still carry it, a little bent.
It lost its form and now sits odd in shape,
yet somehow still holds water without escape.
She writes the date in the corner, goes through
the motions, never saying anything true.
The ink is fresh but the mail doesn't air—
they're just paperbacks of places she's not there.
I still see your jacket where it lay on the back,
a memory on a chair without any track.
It smells faintly like rain and summer air,
as if you might return with all my lost care.
The mess spills out, a fabric-covered pile,
I pause the day, just sit and stare a while.
I don't want to fold, I just want to hold
the soft warmth of you in every fold.
Your treadmill stopped mid-morning work,
it gave a loud electric jerk.
The screen still says "0.0 miles read,"
your progress stays at zero speed.
Her camera trains its mechanical eye
on clouds that drift in monotone sky.
It hunts for light that simply won't go,
but the frame remains a dull place to show.
Her tires skid and wobble as they bounce,
she adds an extra weight for every ounce.
She stares down every crack in the old path,
like it's some ancient ghost stirring her wrath.
The lens locks onto my glassy, bloodshot eye,
It scans the room like a drone searching the sky.
I do a little twirl to test if it will spin,
And snap—there's my face, forever frozen in.
My phone glows too bright for a tired face,
I can't remember where I used to pace.
I swipe my thumbs into the scroll,
pretending this buzz is good for my soul.
I swore I'd beat the clock and meet that date,
but Netflix said "Stay here, you're already late."
I tried to send a polite email or call,
but even my wallet skipped town to the mall.
You missed the train but the bus swings by your door,
the day turns out full of things that are more.
A cat chases ducks in the pond where you found,
the music of delays feels bright and unbound.

topic: a cart with a broken wheel
lines: Your grocery cart gets stuck — one wheel goes flat,
while other shoppers roll their eyes and chat.
You push it slowly down the crooked path,
pretending it's part of your shopping math.
My fingers fly across these sleep-deprived hands,
the keyboard glows like some old disco stands.
The message lights up sharp and clear on screen,
I type it just to prove what I still can mean.
You tried to train your pup not to take the bed,
but now he's lying there with his slobbery head.
You stare at the fabric, this growing old mess,
and wonder if love counts when you want to confess.
You left the cart key hanging on the rack,
no need to ask anyone or look it back.
It slipped through the gaps but you didn't miss a bit,
you know where it sleeps—there's no room for a fit.
You tried to split your coffee break with a try,
the toaster spat out bread gone to fry.
Now you're proud of that smell of smoke and char,
it's your little ritual, blackened little star.
She drives with the top rolled all the way sky,
letting the miles fall behind her so by.
Old songs mix with the grass's dry scent,
and time feels almost like it's never been spent.
I sit here watching how the water stays still,
while shadows dance around the farthest hill.
There's comfort in the silence, strange and alone,
but beauty sounds like something I've already known.
At noon, the machine gives its shrill, false noon,
like some disgruntled robot playing tune.
It beeps through your sleep-deprived, caffeine-fueled stress,
and you swear the thing knows you still need to confess.
My alarm goes off but I pretend my clock
didn't really ring—just silence on the knock.
I blink into the morning, heavy on my eyes,
and whisper to myself that I don't need these lies.
Her ringtone drowns the room, but still no tone,
The call logs fill with names we marked as "phone."
She swears she's tried—just says her head's a bit
Too full of dreams to leave her midnight fit.

topic: finding a five in the couch
lines: I found a crumpled five behind the couch, cash,
my face lights up like a sudden flash.
I check the cushion for a bigger spot,
but settle for joy with this tiny shot.
The yard looks staged like someone painted it froze.
A squirrel's tail is frozen mid-climb, mid-pose.
I walk around with coffee, careful not to drip,
though there's ice underfoot I never quite trip.
I can't decide if it's strong or will bend,
my paperclip chain counts on each friend.
It balances there on a narrow, sharp edge,
a fragile little link becomes its pledge.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: The cat assumes a curl with lazy grace, this pose,
one paw twitching softly in its doze.
Sunlight strokes the patch of dappled fur,
but not a muscle shifts—it won't stir.
She says she saw it in another room,
but now the silence here feels thicker, more gloom.
She blames the dog, the cat, the mail, the rain, the blame,
while muttering how this exact story's the same.
She remembers how it felt when the rain
soaked through her socks, laughed once, laughed again.
Now she wipes the mud off her old running shoes,
reads about spring from her phone's bad weather news.
You spot a face but your mind won't give the name,
it's some old game where the blanks stay the same.
You smile too hard, you're about to blush,
so you change the subject and try to hush.
The screen cracks like glass as I bet my last life,
the quiz buzzes wrong—my pride, a bloody knife.
I check the leader board, still high on the score,
but my phone won't unlock, stuck like a closed door.
She walks too fast with her sandwich and jam,
the tray goes flying in a loud, messy slam.
Her coffee drenches her papers, a spill,
she mutters under her breath, "I swear this is ill."
I designed the billboard to rule every street,
a bold new product with no real feat.
It promises magic, but fails to spark,
we sold the illusion, then lit it in dark.
You weave through traffic like you own the lane,
I bet your driving test skipped the brain.
You zoom too close to my side to pass,
some safety school should teach you manners, class.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: She freezes at the first gray hair she spots,
her fingers twist it into tiny knots.
A decade's stress is written in her age,
she stares too long into the glassy cage.

topic: baking with flour on the floor
lines: I made this cake—it's more than just an art,
every sprinkle was chosen from my heart.
Flour dusts the floor like snow in this mess,
but I'm still in my party pants—call it a dress.
I don't stop to read what they're saying instead,
I keep calm, steady, and hold my head.
With one hand on the wheel and texts in my hand,
I multitask like the world should understand.
You crave more than the usual daily fix,
your old mug stained from the weak black mix.
You step up your game, go for something bold—
a French press brew, dark as the morning's gold.
You swear your bin is just as far as you can,
while they claim your cans blew into their fan.
Both yell about the best way to fix the mess,
but no one wants to sign the complaint's address.

topic: leaving a note on the fridge
lines: I wrote the note in scrawl but full of love,
stuck it on the fridge with a magnet above.
They'll read it when they come back home to see,
"Take out the trash" is still my only key.
They dropped the mug right on their final page,
now equations bleed like ink in a cage.
It's a sticky, brown, chaotic mess,
but somehow it still feels like a success.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: She kneels deep in the puddle and dirt,
laughing off scraped knees and a few minor hurt.
With red hands and a muddy shirt in hand,
she builds her castle in this soaked, soft land.
I tap the screen but it won't let me save,
my phone's too low to even crave.
All apps begin to slowly fade,
the red light blinks like a silent parade.

topic: baking with flour on the floor
lines: I spilled flour everywhere, a white mess,
it powdered my shoes and clung to my dress.
But the smell of my rising cinnamon cake
makes me laugh—this chaos I won't want to take.
He watches the bird in its frantic flight,
confused by the window's false white light.
There's no sign of trees or an escape clue,
just reflections that give no way through.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: She stares at her phone with a stressed-out face,
The screen just says "No Data" in that cold, white space.
Her calls drop mid-sentence, her Wi-Fi's cut out,
She yells at the ceiling, "Why didn't you shout?"
You watch the same fish go back to the bowl,
their tiny lives full of quiet soul.
They move in small patterns so calm and so round,
and you feel peace in this simple, strange found.
I heard it slam — but that was just the door,
some flip-flop's lonely, lying on the floor.
I stepped right on it, of course, and took a trip,
now I'm crawling through hallways with no grip.
I head to the store when my stomach wants a snack,
I follow the aroma down each smelly track.
I wave my card at the "Exact change only" cash,
then load up on fruit and ice cream with a splash.

topic: socks left in the break room
lines: I've searched every shelf but found no clue,
though half are mismatched and bright blue.
Whose idea was it to let them all hide?
They pile up on every bench's side.
You say you're just tuning in for the show,
but you can't look away from their glow.
You mute your phone but leave on their voice,
half-listening, yet making a choice.
He straightened the clip with a vice and a bend,
he called me a fool but I stayed his friend.
It caught on a branch and he lost every hook,
the river just laughed at the shaky little look.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: You dig up the yard and you leave such a mess,
Your muddy legs smear across your white dress.
The dogs take one look and they join in too,
I'll never get this dirt cleaned out through.

She tried to ignore it, the ache from last sleep,
a crick in her neck still held tensions too deep.
She stretched in her chair but it wouldn't help move,
the rhythm of rest had escaped its old groove.
She watches the world from behind the sheer sight,
tracing strangers as they walk through the light.
Her fingers brush the fabric, prepared to wait,
but she's learning patience is her own fate.
You tiptoe past the car like it's fragile glass,

She watches the steam rise into the air,

Her teacup begins to slowly spin,

She parks right outside the time limit zone,
her phone buzzes with a reminder tone.
She fumbles for loose change, calls it old cash,

She let go of the string, the last bit of air,

It shimmered in the sun, a moment so light,

You twist the cap off your dented old shape,

Of all those times you refused to give in [line].
The wind is sharp and it burns my air,

I watch them move but I don't really know

I was aiming for sun-kissed but got a weird glow,

They slump into chairs like the weight's dragging down,

lines: A fingertip of jam left a long smear,

lines: I text it even when I'm not in my mind,

I used to match each sock like part of a lore,

I watch the butter melt beneath the sun,
my breakfast turns to gold as it begins to run.

My shoes always find their perfect pair,

She clears her throat like it's the thinning air,

the kids sit frozen, pretending it's some dark ode.
The screen cuts to black and you are still,

She pressed her palm against the sticky wax,

now everyone's trapped somewhere within.
I never thought I'd command my whole class,
but your cough echoed like shattering glass.
You tried to carry on, but I couldn't take
the quiet you broke into with that coughed break.
Her toes remember the burn of the sun,
she used to skip home barefoot and run.
Now she walks careful where the cracks hold stone,
but the old joy still lives in her tone.
You wipe their tears because you want to try,
you promise the storm will hold off and dry.
There's warmth in your touch, a quiet fire,
and hope blooms again from the smallest desire.
The sandwich left you sleepy, sinking down,
even the clock's ticking sounds too town.
Your eyelids are curtains, slowly drawn to rest,
and your chair becomes something soft to nest.
I drop my fries in the lunchtime air,
a pigeon swoops down with a greedy stare.
It pecks and it flaps, this beady-eyed thief,
I watch helplessly, losing all belief.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: She's mid-sentence, her words all in flow,
when suddenly something's got to go.
She fakes a yawn, tries to keep up the act,

She arrives quietly, ten minutes late,

The others watch her quick, uneven run,
her hair lit by the morning sun.
You toss your fries into the open air,
a pigeon swoops from nowhere to be there.

You laugh but feel your jaw go weak and tight.

She watches the sky with a steady sight,

like silence and wind are the peace in her palm.
You swore it was just a dispute in the air,

You'll gather them all, plant your feet with some hope,

now I trace it all like a quiet regret.
They left their flip-flop in the hallway this day,
probably forgot it when they walked away.
You still wear it, the same worn-down toe,
though the sole hangs loose down to your ankle below.

topic: a book left open on the nightstand
lines: She's been sitting there flipping pages to wait,
hoping the ending will act like a bait.

but she can't let go, still trying to hold.

as if they don't need any care or more.

hoping they'll lead me back to your face.
You keep stacking receipts like old secrets to keep,
they whisper of late nights you didn't go to sleep.
Each price and each date feels like pieces of a clue,
and I want to ask but I'm afraid to ask you.

lines: She's off in her head, no thought left in mind,
her laptop just flickers, "Payment is behind."

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: She thought she saw something that gave off a gleam,

the tiny smooth shard from the creek's quiet deep.

lines: It's been hours since my morning pot,

the birds ignored me back where they nest.

My bike finds the gravel and starts to go off-track,

she lit up like a star, but not like you.

Right off your ego and you'll finally slip.

the sink will still be running when I'm dry.
She watches the rain move slowly down the still,

but it's just a reminder that she is the same.

lines: You lean a little bit closer than near,

lines: It smells like syrup floating in the kitchen air,

Her screen is flickering, about to fade,

She grabbed the box and spun it round real fast,

lines: The steam stopped rising—my coffee went cold,

lines: I saw you today by the quietest park,

lines: I hold my phone up to snap the empty frame,
