The screen dies at midnight, a promise to sleep.
I watch him bounce across the wooden floor,
then stop near the cracked open kitchen door.
His whiskers quiver as a summer breeze
touches his ears with the softest of ease.
I keep the one earbud tucked in my space,
half-listening while the world turns my face.
That song feels like something we used to share,
but now I get most of it only in air.
I got no idea what to call you by name,
so I leaned into a joke to make it a game.
Your face lit up fast—my silly flap
was magic, not sarcasm; we both knew that trap.
I opened my drawer in search of one pair,
but there was only lint and stale air.
It's not a disaster, it's not that big a deal—
but where's the other sock? This is getting surreal.
I wait at the light while the cars pass my fate,
the signal's been frozen in some tech debate.
I flash them a grin as I take my own pride,
and roll through the red like it's my own ride.
You watch the water swallow the last tide,
the ferry hums out where your ride died.
The streetlights blur as you turn at the bend,
alone with the stars and the wait that won't end.
I opened the jar and pried off the lid,
then took out three and pretended it hid.
They tasted like childhood, like warm buttered moon,
but I ate them fast, long before the noon.
You wake up sneezing from the attic dust,
Your nose is raw, a dried-up blood crust.
I hand you tissues, hot tea for you,
We'll wait this out together, sniffling through.
I baked a chocolate cake with one candle in time,
the dog took it whole in a single quick crime.
Now frosting clings to his ears and his fur,
and I pretend I didn't just see it or stir.
She lines up coins with her pockets full of luck,
the machine whirs but won't let her be stuck.
She drops them faster than her usual pace,
and somehow fits exact change in the right place.
You send the meme as a tired joke,
hoping your boss won't catch the smoke.
It's only been ten minutes, not an hour,
but panic already has its power.

topic: crackling fireplace on a winter night
lines: You call this warmth, but the fire's just a lie,
It coughs and sputters and soon it will die.
You snap a photo for social media post,
While your toes shrivel—what a cozy toast.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: She moves a little too close and stays near,
her breath ticks off time right by your ear.
There's nothing between them but borrowed space,
yet something still whispers it isn't the right place.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: I got a moment of accidental fame—
mid-debate, a sneeze crashed the whole game.
It could've ruined the room, it might have took,
but the crowd laughed so hard they just shook.
I typed "Butterfly" just to give it a try,
the screen lit up like a child's inner sky.
Autocorrect won't let me pretend or say
what I meant to write—I'll fix it today.
You kick off the ground and chase the air,
Your shirt flaps up and soaks your hair.
You're not just a kid, you're a winged flier,
until you swing past the slide's wet fire.
You thought the blinds would wipe clean but still have dust,
you chase the cloud around with every gust.
You try to raise them but they stick, won't slide,
now you're sneezing hard from the wrong side.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: I watch the morning melt in every glass,
while dew beads dangle from the sleeping grass.
A spider's thread is strung with diamond thread,
and morning light begins to gently spread.
Her thumb keeps tapping out the old tune,
she hums along when the signal hits the moon.
Static seeps into the empty air,
her face goes quiet, caught without a care.
You answered every question in the game,
your cracked screen lit up like a broken frame.
Now it's just static and memories fade,
but you still tap ghosts in each empty shade.
You watch the raindrops as they slowly fall,
your mind tries hard to recall
some pattern in their silent, glassy trace,
like hope is written in a new place.
Your show was in full swing when the stream lost flow,
A bar of data blinked, stubborn and slow.
The screen just froze, a cruel little glitch,
You pause the chaos and flip the router switch.
She freezes there, milk running cold and slow,
the ceiling light reflects in the puddle's glow.
The dog noses at the sugary mess,
while she replays every mistake in her stress.
Her shoes drag and her feet know the ground,
she's retracing a path she once found.
She doesn't look up, even when it might turn,
just walks through the rain, worn, but still yearn.
I keep expecting it to fall right down,
this battered old lid from my work in the town.
A chip on the side could soon become a crack,
and I know just how heavy it feels on my back.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: I lit this candle to find my own way,
but now it's burning past dusk into day.
Hot wax is sliding down sideways and drip,
I stub my own toe in this stupid dark trip.
They toss but they never quite find their rest,
their breath rises fast against the warm chest.
The room holds the ghost of the trapped body heat,
and sleep won't come easy again, it won't repeat.
You're done with that brew labeled "for the weak,"
you'll drink yours black and you won't even speak
of milk or sugar or how it might burn—
your lips curl just thinking this mess might turn.

topic: a man reading on a bench
lines: You stare through your glasses at the sunlit grass,
time slips away like cars that slowly pass.
Your fingers turn each page with quiet rage,
as if you're reading back your younger age.
I ran my thumb along its rough, worn edge,
like making a silent vow to stay in your pledge.
It curled in my palm like a memory's shape,
but even stillness feels like it might escape.

topic: reading under the covers with a flashlight
lines: You hide the soft rebellion of the glow,
while parents sleep above you, safe and below.
You turn the pages, whisper-slow, to read,
like secrets can survive if they don't bleed.
I hear the track I've loved since high school beat,
it's playing just like clockwork, on repeat.
My treadmill hums while my heart tries to sweat,
and for once, I don't even want to forget.
They swore the room was filled with clean air,
but something clung to my clothes and my hair.
This isn't fresh—it's chemical, not a nice fix,
it smells like old bleach and bad perfume mix.
She swears the light is broken once again,
not sure if bulb or circuit—what a chain!
Her "fix it" skills are worse than my roast,
she shocks the plug, now dinner's just toast.
I came here looking for something calm,
but the water won't still or give me balm.
Each ripple drowns every small clue,
the sound rushes forward and down through.
You hear your phone play a song it now knows,
But when you look up, no one's in close.
It wasn't your phone—your friend is nearby, near,
and you dread what she's sharing from this past year.
You watch as she leaps after that favorite ball,
her paws hit the floor like they came off the wall.
She knocks the water bowl with a bang and a spill,
but who could stop magic when chaos is will?

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: They woke to a tangle, a wrinkle, a fold,
the blanket still clinging like something they'd hold.
It whispered in frayed bits, in lost stitches, in thread,
across the cold mattress where warmth used to be spread.

topic: laughing too hard at a joke
lines: They doubled over in a full-on laugh-fit,
their eyes were watering from what they'd just hit.
Their shoulders shook, their breathing felt tight,
but no one knew if they'd laugh or faint in the light.
You zip through traffic like a hot July breeze,
engines sputter as you race with your keys.
One hand on the handlebar, one hand off the wheel,
I swear you're late for both your job and your meal.
My clothes are spread out across the floor,
the longer I wait, there's just so much more.
I meant to do it but never gave it a thought,
now socks and shirts are tangled up and caught.
The sun sets and suddenly crickets all chime,
They're playing your favorite old radio time.
You try to record them but they won't stay in box,
You end up dancing in mismatched socks.
I watched you glide by without a second pass,
your laughter bouncing off the springtime grass.
I let it slide—said nothing, kept my mind,
while you pulled ahead, left me far behind.
She fast-forwards through the old tape,
searching for songs in their warped, fragile shape.
The buttons are stiff, but she takes her time,
rewinding youth to its analog prime.
You type "but" and your phone changes key,
it's not like you can undo what you see.
It adds "butterfly" — now you have to wing
how to fix this silly little thing.
I sit by the curb where the big trucks meet,
not asking for help, just a small feat.
Coins clink into my worn-out hands,
each ring feels like hope on kinder lands.
You follow the tiny and tireless path,
it turns out the world needs more than just math.
Their work gives your heavy thoughts a gentle lift,
you smile and let hope take your mood's shift.
I used to think I'd live in outer space,
now I can't even turn my face to face.
This chair feels smaller than my childhood home,
but back then, I never needed room to roam.
She finds the stack growing larger each pile,
the postman drops off yet another while.
She sorts out which ones are still officially due,
but forgets to pay them, right down to the glue.
You call it a display, we call it a mess,
you label each sock with an old home address.
You swear you need every worn-out pair,
but I found three of them stacked on the stair.
You crouch behind the fence that runs too tall,
I pretend not to hear when you begin to call.
The lilacs outside your window lean to bloom,
while we both stay still in the same wide room.
You blow out the flame that marks your new age,
a wish flies up, no time to rewrite the page.
We rushed the setup, forgot to bake,
but even this mess feels like a happy mistake.
They still kick off their shoes without a trace,
just like they did when life felt like a race.
The laces are frayed, old stories on thread,
their absence sits heavy where the socks are spread.
They press the button to rewind the tape's past,
the little wheel spins but it doesn't go fast.
They tug at the case, beg the thing to spin,
the song should be over before it can begin.
They left a sticky keyboard after their mess,
still smudged with syrup and unclear address.
But now they're typing, fast and full of hope,
washing doubt away, one key with soap.
He scatters the crumbs like a rhythm or drums,
the birds bounce and bob as they drum up the sums.
They flutter so close and then scatter away,
but he smiles at their dance all the same each day.
You wish they'd leave room for your tired old space,
but their bags are too big for this park bench's face.
You cross legs and fold patience into tight fold,
trying to remember the warmth of a friend's hold.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: He posted a joke that was meant to be a bit,
but the comments rolled in like they'd seen it.
The punchline sat there, a little too dry,
while the silence above him felt heavy as sky.
She walks in with that familiar clean air,
her scent like a whisper through sterile hair.
I try not to sneeze but my nose starts to wave,
she laughs, "Relax, I'm not some germ cave!"
You thought this trip would fix your bad luck and burn,
but even the toast won't brown without a quick turn.
The coffee's too hot, the plate's full of steam,
and you want to wake up far away from this scream.
You wheel your cart like it's heading for home,
chips and candy stacked up inside its chrome dome.
Someone will spot you and yell "Hey, can I grab?"
You'll trade this haul for a better snack cab.
They spilled coffee and jam, now the keys are all goo,
She taps and she waits but the screen just won't do.
She bought new keycaps in bright colors, mint,
her desk looks so fresh with that digital tint.
You cracked a joke so bad my laughter came out,
I doubled over, choking through my shout.
The conversation's now down the wrong led,
I'm stuck here smiling like an idiot's head.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: That ridiculous thing doesn't even fit,
it wobbles when he tries to sit.
He's not a mascot, he's a real live dog,
not some kind of party log.

topic: a kite stuck in a tree
lines: You watch your kite struggle in the wild air,
the wind tugs at your strings and your hair.
It flaps against bark, caught in the same tree,
you beg it to fall or rise to be free.
The bulb had a warm and familiar glow,
I hadn't noticed how much I still know
the way it shaped the room in softest shade,
until it blinked and simply decided to fade.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: It's your birthday, here's the mess on the cake,
you promise one breath will be the magic break.
A dozen still burn, a few stay lit true,
so I blow again, hard, like you never blew.
I wipe the last smudge like it's some old mark,
the memory still glows like a tiny spark.
You left a kiss on my cheek, not too much grace,
but I keep it close—your little-known place.
You remember how it felt—bare skin and the sun,
the way your feet hit pavement as you run.
Time slips through the cracks in that quiet while,
one summer memory in one slow mile.
She sorted the letters and left them all took,
but she placed one aside and she gently shook.
Her hands trembled as they held what was owed,
a bill in the mail with her mother's old code.
My dog keeps hearing a sound in the yard,
he barks at the ground where no shadow's hard.
He's sure there's something out there to see,
but all I feel is the silence that sees me.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: She kneels in the puddle where sunlight meets rain,
her hands twist and press the wet dough again.
Her laugh rises loud, a clear-cut play,
she builds a whole world in the dirt of this day.
You poke your finger deep into the lead,
The sharpener whirs but won't take heed.
It spins and grinds but never makes you spin,
The stub's too thick to get any more thin.
You heard your friend's phone play a brand-new tune,
They'll brag about it when they get home soon.
There's no real clue about the song or who,
But you still smile — they love, and that's enough for you.
I blast the old songs to fill up the room,
the memories hover like shadows that loom.
The beat pounds so hard in my ears and my head,
but the joy fades slow, pain starts to spread.
The breeze drifts in like someone calling you awake,
it lifts your curtain, whispers through the break.
A sunlight path insists you take the day as rise,
you blink, the world is full of greened-up eyes.
The shaker tipped just as I reached the door,
now protein dust coats my carpeted floor.
I tried to sweep it but just made a mess,
this cleanup project is not a success.
I flipped the couch looking all over the room,
the dog just stared with TV show doom.
I posted a reward on the lost and found spot,
my neighbor called—*it was his kid's first shot*.
You left the note on the fridge where it sticks away,
your doodled stick figures in hopeful ballet.
The sun went down but you forgot to say sky,
so I read your silence as "I'll stay—I'll lie."
You sleep close, your warm breath near my skin,
I trace the shape of your body within.
Your sweat seeps through the cotton, soft and heat,
I want to hold you again, touch you repeat.
My drawing skills are still kind of flat,
I hope the message will speak enough to chat.
I sign it in bold, then smudge the last ink,
my hands shake — did I miss something when I think?
She spills her gum right there in the wax,
the kids come sprinting through their new tracks.
I hear the janitor let out one groan,
he mutters, "This is not my happy tone."
She swings her net like it's some grand old thing,
chasing dragonflies with a spiteful spring.
Not a single catch, just another long miss,
she calls it nature's joy, but I call it bliss.
The hum of the cabin feels thick with bad air,
nobody here has the patience to care.
A kid cries. A man spills snack mess,
I try not to notice my wrinkled dress.
The drain won't let the water flow,
the soap sits there and starts to glow.
I hate this mess, it gets right in my gut,
stuck in the same old broken-down rut.
Your phone shows a pop-up in red flashing tone,
It says access denied like some modern stone.
You tap again hoping maybe it will track,
But silence remains where your data went black.
I watch the leaves dance where the sky is above,
they spiral like secrets I've kept from my love.
They don't fall flat, no—they stay up and spin,
I follow their rhythm, wild power within.
Her plates return from the cycle still white,
the rinse aid indicator blinks red in the light.
She reads the manual, tries not to feel small,
but hope slips away down the kitchen's cold wall.
You left the dishes in the sink all done,
They glisten like porcelain kissed by the sun.
A mountain of plates in your favorite pile,
You left them proud, in your perfect, messy style.

topic: finding a five in the couch
lines: I found an old bill folded and still,
the memory of coffee, the warmth gone chill.
I sat in the quiet of that Monday night,
holding the past like a belt too tight.
You tied the paper like it was fine art,
a crumpled mess with love at the heart.
I saved the wrapping, every last roll,
it feels like you gave me a little soul.
A crisp breeze lifts the colors from the air,
the trees let go like some autumnal fair.
Each step I take makes the pavement crack,
I follow the path, but I don't want to track.
You watched your cat start to lick the wall for no clue,
her tongue a tiny broom over peeling blue.
She cleaned every inch of that blank, empty space,
then turned with a purr and began on your face.
She watches the hamster circle his pace,
too tired to move from her quiet place.
It's just one more loop, the same old spin,
yet she feels small, small as him within.
You heap it on high, a mountain on plate,
as if every bite was your perfect fate.
The fork catches noodles, you laugh and you twirl,
gold cheese melts into creamy red swirl.
She left her pencil case with not a clue,
Said she'd grab it later while the tea would brew.
Now classmates pass her notes in silent spin,
She draws with marker pens because she's pencil-thin.
You double-tap a photo of her face,
a smile from somewhere you used to embrace.
The timestamp reads a year without a date,
your heart feels heavier with that weight.
You're too scared to wear anything that might trip,
so you stick to the shoes that provide the best grip.
They call them "comfort," but we both know it's a lie—
who needs style or confidence in your dead-eyed eye?

topic: a long queue at the coffee shop
lines: You've been waiting forever for your time,
This feels more like a civic time crime.
You tap your foot, your patience nears its soul,
The barista's TikTok feed won't let you scroll.
The headset dangles by its broken wire,
still glowing faintly with a ghost of fire.
It looks like it might drift away and float,
a lone thought stuck in your silent boat.
You always cry when the credits roll out,
trying not to let your emotions shout.
The kind of story that lingers and stays,
still haunts you long after the theater days.
She pulls the classroom door but it won't go through class,
her name's on the list, so why does she get no pass?
The handle sticks like it's mocking her try,
She wipes it again with a tissue and a cry.
I lie awake with wild and strange thought,
my brain's just taunting me with bad jokes bought.
There's something up there—maybe some mold,
or ghosts from last week's bad relationship gold.
The bus driver yawns halfway through his shift,
his eyes begin to gently drift.
He still knows every stop by route,
even if he's half asleep and zones out.

topic: a favorite mug with a chip
lines: They wrap their fingers gently round what it holds,
as if the chip could grow into some new molds.
Their thumb still finds the dent where it once bit the hand,
but they drink like nothing was ever unplanned.
You can't find a single clean pair,
they're all tossed in a damp heap of air.
One goes on a foot—now where's the sock?
It's lost again, you just can't take the shock.
She walks through the room with that ghost in the air,
her face full of disgust from that chemical stare.
She keeps checking clocks, not sure how much time
she'll have to breathe deep through this white-line grime.
You cursed the lock but kept your cool, no key,
and leaned the bike against the wall, now free.
You smiled at how you handled things with force,
proud of the way you took control, of course.
You saved your seat for the latest show,
the screen lit up in that red-and-blue glow.
That stub now hangs in your wallet with pride,
proof of a win you still feel inside.
I stand under this plastic and still get rain,
the roof rusts and it pours out again.
My shoes squish with every step from the drip,
I brace for the slide if my foot starts to slip.
He types with one hand and leaves quite a mess,
each typo increases the user's stress.
He claims it's his rhythm, a system of flow,
but watch him crash apps, no need to make a show.
I told them all I never had to try,
my old router still hits the blue sky.
They stare at me, still searching for that code,
while I reboot in private, offline mode.
His hand's still stuck inside the broken blade,
he swore he'd never need this crummy grade.
A spiral of wood shavings makes a mess,
just one tool turned his calm into stress.
They move in a line so precise and so small,
each step follows signals they can't help but crawl.
I watch in the sun where their journey is light,
a whole world revealed in this tiny, slow sight.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: You snap the world without a single frame,
the pink and gold that kiss the ocean's flame.
The birds don't wait for captions in the sky,
so you just post it with a grin and "why?"
Your plane left without your suitcase on flight,
you're stuck in last week's clothes, both stiff and tight.
You scan the carousel for your name on a tag,
while strangers carry home the wrong black bag.
Your wallet feels heavy but your spending room
has vanished, now capped by a red-lit gloom.
You dream of folding money in hand, soft and cash,
but all you have left is a swipe that won't dash.
You left a note on your screen for the day,
reminding yourself not to lose your way.
It sits there fragile, stuck to the glass,
like hope taped gently to morning grass.
A dragonfly hovers too close for the sky,
I wonder why it won't just fly by.
It zips around me like some tiny dart,
a living flicker of winged, wild art.
You thought the sweet aroma was the smell,
but don't let that fool you—it's straight from hell.
You're not cooking, you're putting on a show,
your face lit by oil that flickers and glow.

topic: missing a chorus in a song
lines: You hit "record" and skipped the whole play,
now the chorus is gone for the day.
You hum it to fix it but still feel so wrong,
the track ends too soon, and you're singing along.
I type my last name into the log,
my cat just stares like she knows the dog.
I hit "confirm" and I let out a sigh,
I whisper "goodby" to the monthly lie.
I wear my hard hat like it's part of my gear,
this job keeps me steady in this rough career.
It's saved me from more than one painful bump,
but style has a way of lifting any slump.
You've been standing here for nearly an hour,
the system's down and they lost all the power.
You rub your cold hands as you try to wait,
but your suitcase still spins out of fate.
Your lips are warm beneath the electric glow,
the cars keep zooming past but I don't want to go.
Your laugh catches fire on my shallow breath,
I swear if the world ends, let it be this death.
It falls in time, a rhythm, a drop,
I tried to fix it, but it won't stop.
I've sat here watching for an hour,
and still, the drip holds all the power.
She left her desk for a midday sweet,
she walked the block down to the corner street.
She counted out cash for a soda to sip,
but came back alone with just coins in her grip.
The river becomes a mirror of glass,
where clouds lie like birds on the grass.
The water just moves, it won't rush or drift,
it gives me a peace like a soft, quiet gift.
I didn't move when the others all wait,
let the cars behind me curse out their fate.
I held my lane with a calm on the brake,
while they rushed into every small mistake.
The screen still glows with what you used to show,
but now you tap out, not trying to know.
You close the app, feel something new and more—
a hush between you and your open door.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: They crouched by the water with steady hand,
turning stones slowly from creek to land.
Something caught light—a spark, a gleam,
they smiled like it held their future in dream.
She watches the hawk turn slow through the sky,
some quiet hope still refusing to die.
She traces the road ahead, a clear-cut path,
but life never balances on perfect math.
You saved the last slice, still cheesy and warm,
while thunder cracked out like a sudden storm.
It wasn't much, but it felt like your crutch,
that crust tucked neat where the box used to hutch.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: She tosses the bread with a smirk down the trail,
the sky blurs above in a soft, gray, pale.
Each bird cuts through silence, a storm made of flake,
their wings ripple echoes across frozen lake.
You leave the kitchen light on just to glow,
I watch from the doorway, I somehow still know.
I don't want to interrupt or take your hand,
just let you be here where you softly land.

topic: a kite stuck in a tree
lines: He watches the sky, but no more kites in the air,
his hands still feel the pull from a spool that's now bare.
It's stuck in that oak where the branches don't sway,
a part of him still thinks it might come down some day.
You check your watch, the bus is in a delay,
The app says it may never show today.
You tap your foot at the empty bus stop,
Your patience lower than a Monday's drop.
You never found a decent fish hook,
so you used the paperclip you took.
It spins in circles, the water's too deep,
I left you a note where the pond goes to sleep.
I leave it on through the silence of dawn,
it shines through the window above my old lawn.
They'll know it was me, there's no hiding that fact,
I won't turn it off for the sake of the act.
I count the hours till I get to home,
while strangers next to me try not to roam.
My knees are cramped against the seat,
but time has lost its rhythm and its beat.
You swear the wind chimes know your song,
they echo just the notes you're singing along.
You tip-toe through the yard that way,
afraid the breeze will steal your day.

topic: a note tucked inside a card
lines: You unfold the paper expecting a sigh,
but it only says "Please don't let me die."
The ink is smudged and your grip feels too tight,
you tuck it back where it vanished from sight.

topic: someone handing you a surprise gift
lines: They hand you a box tied with a crooked bow,
no warning, no hint of the plan below.
You laugh, you shake it, hear a little roll,
and wonder if this is a joke or your soul.
You treat that torn foil like some heinous crime,
it's just a snack bag with a crooked chime.
You ponder if this was the universe's fate
to turn your lunch into a twisted debate.
You said the party would be your last,
now confetti clings to your head so fast.
You tried to brush it but you can't seem to find,
a way to get through this without losing your mind.
She leans on the handle, tries turning the flush,
but it sticks in a silence she can't get a hush.
She jabs at the knob, yanks it left, gives it twist,
while steam from the shower rolls out in a mist.
I watch it dig up its secret stash,
then chuck the old ones—some tiny smash.
It pats down the soil with such serious move,
like it's got a plan or a buried groove.
His taxi's tail light won't turn into a beam,
he still calls it his ticket to a better dream.
The passengers don't talk or ask where they ride,
they just stare at their phones and feel it inside.
I hit the button and it won't replay,
my favorite chorus is running away.
It should've queued up the next track right,
this glitch is a nightmare, a total fright.
Your clothes form a mountain, a crumpled-up heap,
but you see opportunity — not a clean leap.
You set to the task with a calm, clear mind,
and catch up on laundry that's long gone behind.
The butter spreads easy, a warm glowing gold,
the knife keeps slipping—it can't seem to hold.
A fat drop lands where the jam meets the drip,
you balance your toast on the edge of your tip.
She grabs the handrail with a wince and a grip,
but slides all the way down into a trip.
The rail glistens still like some sticky mess,
she swears never again will she touch that address.
The bike lock is rusted and twisted tight,
he tugs in the morning's weak early light.
He fumbles for keys from some distant key,
the lock just coughs up old metal debris.
You used to think sitting there was your time,
but now the chain only makes a low chime.
You tried to fix it once, but the bolts just rust,
so you let it be—what you do is what you must.
You remember the app from a time long old,
how it used to display your saved posts bold.
You tap once, twice—then you give it another try,
but the screen just goes dark like a storm in the sky.
I filled the nonstick with butter and air,
now breakfast hums low with delicious flair.
The slices begin to sing their fat crackle,
I can't help but grin as I savor this tackle.
He drops the coins and hears them clink,
but the machine won't give him a drink.
His fingers hover, full of hope,
while dreams slip down like a slackened rope.
She rewinds the track but the music still won't play,
the cursor spins, as if trying to stay away.
She misses that sound from her teenage years,
the memory slips like a ghost through her ears.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: Your old friend pops up like a digital ghost,
clinging to your memory through one stupid post.
They tag you in a story, try to fan the flame,
but you're both still the same, nothing's changed—just shame.
Your weights are all out, but one doesn't set,
it vanished, perhaps, while you went to get.
You scour the whole house, then check the workout room,
but maybe it's time to let this detail bloom.
She tugs at the teeth like it's a losing pull,
the track is jammed from where the pocket's full.
Her fingers trace the break along the seam,
but laughter's her only fashion theme.
The warm water rises, thick with steam,
they belt out a ballad from their dream.
Their off-key vibrato fills the voice,
it's their moment, no shame, just choice.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: It squeezed through the concrete, relentless and tight,
a tiny upstart in a silent, slow fight.
Now it bends in the wind but still stays green,
while traffic rolls over this unlikely scene.
You sat in the chair for a quick little trim,
the clippers buzzed louder than the radio's swim.
That chair still hums in the back of your hair,
the same cheap scent lingers in every stale air.
She folds her jacket to give her more leg,
then wedges a book where her shoe once was peg.
She chats with the stranger who shares the aisle,
and ends up halfway to heaven with a smile.
I wear these socks because they look fun,
one bright blue, one in yellow with sun.
I gave up trying to match each sock pair,
now I let my feet make their own wild air.
You stare in horror as the liquid makes a mess,
A dark stain creeps up your favorite dress.
You scramble, panic rising to a high-pitched whine—
"It's just a drop!" you wish you'd never typed that line.
Woke up to toast, but also a weird scent,
A spoon is bent—did someone eat with their dent?
The room looks like a food fight had a mess,
This breakfast was supposed to *impress*, not stress.
I blow out the last wish left on this one day,
hoping the universe hears what I say.
Maybe tomorrow will feel different, just might,
I flicker a smile into the fading light.
You let the soft thread run in quiet slow flow,
it whispers of something you want to let go.
Maybe the unraveling is meant to mend,
not break your design but instead rewrite the end.
You watch the onions sizzle in the pan,
your face twists as the smoke starts to fan.
The oil spits, the flame climbs too heat,
you sigh—this meal feels like a defeat.
I watch the map crease into itself fold,
the inked-out streets whisper of days long past old.
I trace the path that my fingers still know the way,
but the paper's frayed now, it won't hold me today.
You kick off the ground to touch the sky,
your laughter soars where birds might fly.
The chain creaks as you lean to the bend,
the world holds its breath when you reach the end.
He's taken up too much of this cold space,
head down, lost in some far-off place.
I'm not sure how long he's held this grip,
but time is passing and I'm starting to slip.

topic: a child drawing on the table
lines: They drew a rainbow all across the mess,
using markers still wet from their dress.
Time slows down for every single play,
when a child makes art in a quiet day.
She stands outside with a dead car and the sun,
the clock ticks louder than the battery can run.
She pats her pockets for the spare, no key,
she texts the neighbor to jump-start me.
She loads the dryer and sets it to spin,
the heat is too hot, her socks are now thin.
One is still warm, but where's the other pair?
It's probably stuck to the back of the air.
I let the melody drift through my stream,
the singer's sorrow becomes my dream.
Their lyrics hit hard, they stir up my ache,
I think of the love I once tried to wake.
A bag clings to the branch like a lost tree,
it waves in the breeze as if proud debris.
I tried to pull it down but got a small note—
it's stuck in my hedge and now also my throat.
You missed the message, forgot the date,
You swear it wasn't meant to be your fate.
You'll send a text, or maybe make a call,
Just saying "hello" seems like it could be all.
They call it relaxing—just lying there awake,
but I know why you're really making this mistake.
Your thoughts are stuck on loop, your mind
is a ceiling fan, spinning the same old grind.
I double-tap fast but the feeling's just tap,
my thumb moves like lightning and paints every cap.
I wonder who sees or if they even see me,
they scroll by so quick like they're hunting for a key.
Her eyes catch the flickering projector beam,
recalling every movie, every dream.
The screen goes dark but the hope doesn't fade—
she claps for herself like a quiet parade.
She lets her dog pull on the lead,
dreaming of fields in her dog's head.
The pup sets a fast, wild pace,
while she wonders if this is her true place.
Each link a soft curve where the metal gives bend,
I made it alone but I think of you, friend.
It curves down the desk like a secret we edge,
a quiet vow not to break, our silent pledge.
The cursor won't budge—I've tried to move,
it only glitches out of nowhere's groove.
I slam my laptop, reboot, and try—
it lingers frozen till I'm ready to die.
There he goes again, making another mess,
"It's just one egg," he says, with a shrug and a yes.
He never thinks about how you'd like him to fix,
Now we're both stuck with this broken yolk mix.
He walks right into the gooey trap,
completely ignoring the warning map.
His foot starts to slide with a loud slip,
he scrambles for something, but nothing will grip.
My cat is up there, all paws on the wall,
She's stretching her limbs in a wall-mounted sprawl.
There's nothing to chase but a spot on the floor,
She licks the same patch till it drives me half-sore.
I see the number but I don't know the name,
this mystery caller is my new game.
You got my number, but you dialed all wrong,
so I'll pretend I'm busy, ride this joke along.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: You post the sky, no caption to say,
just colors from a quiet new day.
The world wakes up in your uploaded light,
strangers pause—some even smile, you might.
He tries to strut but he can't really move,
his feet are too tiny to find the groove.
He flaps and chirps like he wants to chat,
but all he does is miss the stick and just fall flat.
I found a bag caught where the roses grew,
it clung to branches like it was holding true.
The wind made it sway but never let it trap,
I watched it dance while I took my midday nap.
You pack a week's worth of outfits to wear,
expecting every item to air.
But your suitcase looks like a disorganized plan,
and your zipper won't close within an inch's span.

topic: car keys on the kitchen table
lines: There they sit, no hint, no clue,
holding court where you usually do.
The morning hums, no sign of play,
while the car waits somewhere else today.
I used to lie outside and feel the thin air,
now I avoid the windows' white glare.
The sun would kiss my bare arms and my skin,
but now I stay cool and never let it in.
That streetlight's changing every hue,
I tap the window for my dance cue.
It sputters out—my moment to spin—
but darkness hits before the fun can begin.
My knees remember every step they ache,
I count them out loud in a tired break.
Halfway up the flight I curse each stair,
pretending they're weights I'm lifting in air.
I curse myself for losing the keys again,
the morning stalls, I'm stuck in this chain.
I flip the couch, I check the same old floor—
there's nowhere left to look, but I search for more.
You watch the bird go crashing through the wind,
trapped between the trees and what's so neatly behind.
It flaps and flutters, giving all it can try,
until at last it finds the open sky.
The silence is thick like an old love affair,
we don't talk about it, but we both care.
The clock ticks so loud it could break every crack,
yet neither of us dares speak the wrong track.
They repurposed the jar into a clear glass,
now it holds fresh-cut stems from the front yard grass.
They stir their own blends, everything from mix,
not store-bought powders—they'd never let others fix.
There's a cracked yolk in the bowl, a complete mess,
and they're smiling about it as if saying yes.
They have no idea how this looks, no clue,
they're telling me not to worry, calm down, you.
She always studied here the same old way,
circling terms that brought her back some day.
Her notes are scribbled tight between each read,
I can still see the ink she used to bleed.
I watched it take off from the lily pad leap,
it landed with a splash that echoed too deep.
The water is still now, but something feels wrong still,
I wait for ripples—does it survive or will?
The gym bag gapes open on the cold floor,
as if it's holding back memories and more.
A water bottle dreams of a younger past,
while laces lie still, never worn fast.
She tugs the leash as if it's a race to go,
her tail waves hard like she wants to show.
Her eyes are locked on the squirrel near the ear,
and nothing can stop this small demon, my dear.
He sits by the door with the whole world as clue,
eyes locked on the sky turning gray to blue.
The leash lies still—no command to take,
just hope in his paws for the walk to the lake.
She watches her cat chase some phantom pace,
leaping where light doesn't quite erase.
The silence is loud when it turns and cries,
as if no one sees through those hollowed-out eyes.
You think this pinecone's just a quiet sprout,
but wait—there's magic happening about.
It waited years before it finally fell,
now you're the only one it chose to tell.
She left her gear at the locker room gym,
and blames the weather instead of herself or him.
Now she walks home where her pace can't become a run,
while tying her shoes—half the laces still undone.
My sad song knows my deepest soul,
I've listened to it more than I should—no scroll.
I'm crying into toast, I'll take the blame,
but the lyrics still call me by my name.
My dog insists it's not his fault or my blame,
he barks at shadows but still takes the name.
The water bottle went flying—what a spill!
He ran through the house with a soaked toy in his thrill.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: You catch the morning in the crystal light,
the kind of quiet beauty that takes your sight.
The web trembles, but it won't let you hold
the fragile, fleeting hope that the sky has turned bold.
Your back hums a warning it never will shake,
you pause from the screen to give your body a break.
You stretch like a cat and test every bend,
the moment feels healing before it will end.
A single feather caught in the morning sky
now floats down slowly, as if it wants to lie.
It twirls into twigs, gets snagged on a tree,
another joins it, all falling like debris.
I got too close to the sun's bright glow,
now my poor nose has a pink new foe.
By tomorrow it might start to peel,
but I don't mind—this pain will heal.
I remember the glow of the screen, that old frame,
a face lost to history, without a name.
The crowd's gone, but the moment feels still,
your silence could be my only will.
I feel a quiet hush of old-time shame,
I know this dance—it's a memory game.
There's no clue why one sock looks brand new,
the other's faded, like the rest of you.
One earbud slips free as you turn a sharp drop,
the music cuts off, but your feet don't stop.
You hum along now and move without play,
yet somehow this stumble feels like your best day.
The shovel hits ice with a hard metallic clink,
The neighbor across the yard slows down to think.
He pauses to check how much dirt he can load,
Then grins at the challenge, a snowman in his road.
She jumps with the grace of a practiced leap,
the bowl clatters, spilling the cold heap.
He follows the trail with his nose to the scent,
and finds her in joy, paw still wet and bent.

topic: a cart with a broken wheel
lines: The cart screeches forward, a rusty old scream,
its wheel caught on gravel in no man's stream.
I push with all might, hear the frame begin to groan,
but the wheel won't budge from its jagged new stone.
You dance through the sky where the soap meets the air,
Each pop is a laugh from a summertime fair.
You sprint through the yard like you're racing to run,
Your face tipped up toward the warm, golden sun.
I left the spoon inside the open jar,
it clung like guilt to every sugar bar.
Now morning finds me slow and full of drip,
the spoon won't budge without a honey trip.
You shout at your friend for stepping on the floor,
then trip into the parking lot's wide door.
You blame it all on their weird driving aim,
even though your face still screams their full name.
She wipes her forehead with the same old face,
where salt and effort leave their quiet trace.
The fabric smells like time and rubber scent,
but she still calls it home when the world is bent.
She swore she'd never lose a single pair,
but now there's one foot hanging in the air.
It's ruined her vibe, this lost-sock mood,
she's eating cold cereal for snack and for food.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: You know every back in this Sunday stack,
the same old crew never off their track.
You spot names before they sit in the pew,
it's like meeting ghosts who forgot they're new.
You pretend it's a hi, not an awkward wave,
but your heart cheers for how uncool you're brave.
Maybe there's magic in that accidental spark,
or maybe it's just the room lit up too dark.
It won't shine steady, but it still glows,
I pretend not to notice how it grows.
The cord stays twisted in the same old bend,
a quiet symbol of this fading friend.
They hover near it, too scared to just wait,
like silence from tech support was their own fate.
They charge it slow where the light starts to fade,
and speak to the screen like an old friend in shade.
You watch as the screen light begins to fade,
the edges go dark in a fading shade.
There's no time to send one last text or call,
you lose everything in the blink of an all.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: A small footprints leads down a quiet street,
The wind hums a tune with its sugared sweet.
But there's no sign of sadness or fear in his cry,
Just wonder and hope reaching up toward the sky.
My thumb hovered—could this be the final break?
One tap for love, the other was a mistake.
Your profile stares back, no hint on your face,
just silence in the empty comment space.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: He was hitting his stride, the crowd's eye in flow,
the mic in his hand, ready to show.
Just as he said the punchline—boom, he went off,
a thunderous sneeze, a total cough.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: She said the silence was the punchline of the joke,
but the laugh track rolled in, making her choke.
She turned off the sound and the room felt so blue,
like some moments are meant to stay quiet and true.
He blasts from his room with a thunderous boom,
the walls vibrate in their bones like a tomb.
This isn't the first time it's ruined the day,
my nerves all unravel and start to fray.
You watched the cat send the bowl to the floor,
you laughed and left it there as your chore.
You thought you'd clean it up, but not *then*,
you still haven't moved it—same spot, again.
You lose your own rhythm, forget your own pace,
everyone moves fast, but you need more space.
A body brushes close, another will bump,
and your shoulders tighten, ready to slump.
You remember the joy of the first spring rain,
how each drop called you out just to play again.
Now your boots sink where the puddles run deep,
but the laughter feels faint now you try to keep.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: Your voice message failed again, this app,
You lose your temper, slam the phone down, flap.
You record it once more, trying to try,
The same three seconds stutter, cut, and cry.
The register's broken again, no cash,
I watch the customers mash the wrong keys with dash.
They point at the items we never can scan,
I mutter the price, they fume—they don't have a plan.
This laundry basket's a full-on mess,
half my socks have no matching address.
I drop the pile in despair on the floor,
I can't shut the laundry room door.
I let out a sigh, it's been heavy with stress,
we never got close to solving the mess.
But I flip off the switch and I meet the new light—
the kind that suggests tomorrow might.

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: She poses alone like she owns the air,
the camera lens never gives her a stare.
Each click is a statement, each pose is a shot,
the world might be empty, but she finds her spot.
She flips the pancakes with old-fashioned grace,
each flip a ritual in its rightful place.
Outside, the wind begins to weep like rain,
but she is happiness wrapped in a plain.
You wipe the glass until the sun begins to gleam,
it's your cleanest yet, you almost dare to dream.
But smudges rise again from yesterday's old mess,
so you pull your sleeves down past the cuffs of your dress.
She keeps the same bottle to go with her mind,
always looking for ways she might not find.
She sips like the water won't last the whole pour,
as if holding out for something even more.
You fall into step with my quiet pace,
hands in your pockets, no need to erase
the silence between us feels soft and light,
but close—like a door left just slightly tight.
The heavy hush of stagnant, hot air
makes even my skin feel like it's too bare.
I count the hours till the end of this day,
but time moves slowly when the heat won't go away.
I let the snow collect as cold proof,
claiming my collar's the only roof.
They crumble slow, but I won't let them melt—
I pat them down like a champion's belt.
I watch my butter slowly melt and spread,
the silence of success—no need to tread.
This toast is perfect, just how I wanted it done,
the golden glow says I've already won.
You give the dented can a curious eye,
it's been in the cupboard for years, not a lie.
You open it up and you take out the bean,
check if it's still edible or just plain green.
You hit "save" but your message said "send,"
Now you're waiting for replies to mend.
You tell them it was a typo on the key,
They're still debating the emotional debris.
You stare at the screen but can't finish the task,
your face holds a smile behind a yawn mask.
The camera angles are out to catch the boss,
while you track the clock like it's your biggest loss.
I missed the exit again, same old time,
this confusing mess feels like a crime.
There's no sign that makes any kind of clue,
just ramps that look identical to you.
The scent of old soap lingers in the air,
a ghostly pair from some forgotten lair.
It's not unpleasant, but it doesn't bloom—
just clings around the edges of the room.
They've got a raw, unfiltered voice,
Choosing the bathroom for their performance choice.
A pop song hums out, off-key but true in tune,
As steam rises, like a love ballad in the moon.
You pace near the carousel like a waiting zone,
your flight app refreshes your hopeless phone.
They call it a system-wide tech delay,
your bag's still not here and it feels so far away.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: They clicked on the link and scanned down the post,
Half-expecting your name to be just a ghost.
A reply blinked up in the pale screen light,
And there—just in time—was your welcome sight.
She checks the breaker switch—was the power turned on?
The bulb pulses weak, like it's about to be gone.
Her shadow trembles on the ceiling's white beam,
She wonders what else feels so close yet so dream.
Your alarm goes off with a shrill little call,
you hit the snooze button and stay in your sprawl.
You try to imagine a perfect first toast,
but your coffee's still cold on the kitchen coast.
You had this whole vibe for your long-awaited trip,
The only mistake? Forgetting your passport slip.
Security stops you right at the airport gate,
You laugh it off — maybe it's travel fate.
She taps again but the screen won't let her try,
the app blocks out all hope from the bright blue sky.
"Permission denied" is all it will let her read,
but she shrugs and says she doesn't really need.
You think the breeze is here to put on a show,
but the bees already know where you go.
They're counting petals and checking the bloom,
while you pretend this is more than a plume.
This old record still whispers to fade,
cracks in the grooves painting every shade.
The needle drops, my head falls to rest,
I swear that bass hit my ribs like a chest.
She watches the screen do its slow, quiet spin,
then laughs at the beep in her head full of din.
No need for old cash, or debt or a stash—
she left the whole system in the past to smash.
I traced my finger along the book's cracked age,
read every yellowed, dog-eared page.
The notes in the margins still smell like your back,
we used to study late at the library stack.
You check your ticket and your baggage tag,
but the conveyor belt is cold and lag.
You wait in silence for an empty hour,
remembering trips when time had power.
I flip the page hoping my grade comes back,
but all I see is ink in jagged black.
There's not a single comment, no rubric, no mark,
was this a lesson or a teacher's cruel lark?

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: I spotted a spark beneath the tree's long gleam,
I waded through mud to pull it from the stream.
It fits inside my palm—I vow I'll always keep,
this tiny treasure, proof I might yet reap.
We count down the seconds before "snooze" time,
The others are gone for a coffee or crime.
We tiptoe through cabinets and loaves of bread,
She laughs, "If you blink, we'll both be dead."

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: The wind feels like a slow-moving breeze,
You fumble with your glove to find your keys.
The wheels hum as we both begin to roll,
It's quiet out here, but I feel it in my soul.
He swears he charged it last night, but don't trust,
the battery died in a pocket full of rust.
It still shows Friday—same wrong date,
like some cruel joke his tech fate wrote late.
You read the recipe but fear the flame,
not sure why this dish has such a strange name.
You stir the pot and check your phone for mess,
unsure if it's done or just a wild guess.
You toggle the knob but the signal won't clear,
your favorite song's stuck between a dead ear.
Static creeps in where the music used to fade,
so you hum the lyrics in a lonely parade.
I told a half-truth about this tale,
pretending my socks aren't looking so pale.
I swear they were matched when I laid them out fair,
but now one's a unicorn and one's just plain air.
You're stuck with this dull, unrelenting pain,
your thoughts swirl like thunderheads in the rain.
But you take a breath, let it go nice and deep,
and trust that the calm will begin to keep.
You think your tilted head gives you some clue,
your eyes like windows of a fading blue.
You're listening to something far away in bark,
but I just hear silence in the quiet dark.
You left it out like a still life—art,
brown splotches blooming like a soft heart.
The kitchen fills with its musky smell,
you let it rot and you don't cast a spell.
You type with one hand, quick and fast,
your thumb moving past the shift key's cast.
You won't let pain steal what you can still hold,
each message a quiet act of being bold.
My bike's tires whisper soft on the roll,
the path feels like it knows my soul.
The sky is open, skies are wide,
I'm unspooling joy deep inside.
You can't stop the string from slipping your pull,
even though you held it so tight and full.
The loops begin to escape down the thread,
like time, thin and quiet, getting spread.
She's been standing all ride, no vacant seat,
her patience melting in the train's tight heat.
The AC hums but offers no cool air,
she thinks about giving up for the office stair.
Her eyes catch the starlight's quiet gleam,
She whispers secrets only the sky could dream.
I follow the path where her shadow leaves a trace,
She turns, and I'm lost in her soft, familiar face.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: I show up each week to the same old same,
waving to folks with their familiar name.
These seats hold the stories we've shared through years,
we're not just members—we're the main damn cheers.
You watch the bulb tremble, trying to glow,
it's dying but waiting for something to know.
The room leans in slowly, embracing the dark,
but you hold your breath—maybe there's a spark.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: She watches the silence too still for fresh air,
her breath turns to mist on her skin so bare.
The web holds the world on a single thread,
she drops to her knees, the sky at her head.
She left the cart key somewhere near the shop,
the register dinged and gave her a new crop.
She smiles while she walks back to the find,
her stress melts to nothing inside her mind.
I slide the key in—no click, no key,
the dash just stares back with a "jump me."
I call my friend to come and wait,
while traffic speeds by and mocks my fate.
She's searching the room for something to bite,
her eyes scan the desk, no treats in the light.
A crumb in the trash pulls her toward the cake,
she'll chase it all down for sweet little sake.
They hand me a plate that's already a mess,
then smile like they're proud I made such a guess.
Jelly's smeared on their fingers and coat,
you'd think they just wrestled a wild jelly goat.
You dropped your cold drink but hid the spill,
now ice cubes are dancing across the bill.
The liquid spreads slow on your keyboard's mat,
you switch to a window and blame it on chat.
You left your snack crumbs in a glorious mess,
the keyboard glistened like your early success.
No one could find where the sugar ran off the track,
you typed through the syrup, a sweet little hack.
I found a piece of chewed gum stuck in the trap
of the office chair, where my thoughts start to map
out worst-case scenarios—will I sit tight?
Or scream and storm out, take a bitter bite?

topic: a sticky finger on the window
lines: They left a smudge where their hand touched the heat,
trying to draw something they later repeat.
I follow the curve of the vague, open trace,
like memorizing the shape of their face.
I know every scuff on each worn-out pair,
they've soaked up the silence of empty stair.
They reek of bad sidewalks, wet leaves, and hell,
I kick them outside just to keep the smell.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: You thought of them only hours in the past,
a memory hits like an old email blast.
Your thumb hovers, unsure if to send or deny,
but you tap "reply" anyway — just to say hi.
She's never felt right and she's always been wrong,
but you kept her tucked somewhere deep in your song.
Now it clicks—how she once could have fit,
a missing small shadow, a quiet old bit.
I gave my last ten and got nothing back in change,
the cashier looked up from their usual strange.
I'd hoped for some coins so I wouldn't have to miss
the way we used to tip with a folded-up kiss.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: I peer into the mirror, trying to hide,
but there's a silver streak along my side.
A gray is growing bold atop my crown,
I laugh—looks like I've aged out of town.
You check your watch for an empty space,
but every seat is already a place.
A baby starts to cry and you try to sit,
but there's no room to move—just hope to fit.
The screen won't show how far I've gone or track,
so I pretend my workout is an attack.
I guess the numbers are just out to lie,
while I count steps by staring at the sky.
You turn a corner and spot a quiet bend,
A chalk sign reads "Cafe" in your new friend.
You sip your latte in peace, one cup,
The music is soft, and your spirits perk up.
You lift your face toward the gray sky,
the drops fall fast but you won't stay dry.
The umbrella bends, it almost gives bend,
yet still it holds you like an old friend.
