lines: She leans forward and hopes it feels wise,
not counting the years on her face or her tries.
Her cheeks grow warm from the wax and the heat,
and laughter from long ago starts to repeat.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: Your internet bill went unpaid and due,
the screen goes dark in a sudden blue.
You refresh the page—no email will ping,
but hey, it's a great chance to read a good thing.
Her face is locked on the spinning progress bar,
she mutters how this is a new kind of scar.
She's tried every trick online to get a fix,
but the update won't budge—it's some cursed mix.
It slipped from the cup and it broke as it fell,
I didn't flinch or even yell.
The yolk spread slow like a masterpiece art,
I snapped a pic for my breakfast chart.
I tap the screen but it won't save my time,
the last five percent is the worst of the prime.
My texts go out as "sending"—no such calls,
I yell at the silence, like screaming at walls.

topic: crackling fireplace on a winter night
lines: The fire hisses too loud for a soft, warm tone,
I'm watching the shadows as I sit all alone.
I flinch when embers pop and my thoughts jump ahead,
afraid the quiet will stump me to tears instead.
The cat lies flat across the open beam,
as if it owns the house and not the dream.
Its tail curls gently around the suitcase lace,
while luggage tags peek out from its soft face.
A wad of gum left a sticky little trace,
it clung where your hand wiped your tired face.
You pause and inspect your next move, your plan,
then smile like a kid with the world in your man.
I screamed, "This is not a dog-drool mess!"
The vet just smiled and said, "It *is* a yes."
I tried to wash the memory off the scent,
but the stain still lingers where it went.
You watch as the dog performs the whole act,
It's not pretend—this stealing is a cold fact.
I've tried every trick to stop the daily try,
But who are we fooling? I know why.
They hold up the net like they're after the sky,
hoping to catch what they can't even try.
It's more than a game—it's a quiet dream,
chasing the wind through the tall green stream.
You double-tap a stranger's profile view,
as if that makes your judgment any more true.
You keep swiping left, then you hit the scroll,
but apps don't help when all you lack is a soul.
I swear this goldfish is not acting sane,
It swims around like it's stuck on a chain.
Is it stressed from the tap or the vacuum's blame?
Maybe it dreams of becoming a lake's fame.
You left your clothes where they landed on the floor,
not sure if it's chaos or a closed door.
The memories here, you've seen them all grew,
but now you don't know who this room once knew.
My dog stares at the door like I hold the next treat,
tail twitching as if he already sees the street.
He circles three times, just to be sure to spin,
then waits—excited—for me to say let's begin.
She spends an hour perfecting every face,
smoothing out the lines she can't erase.
The filter hides more than just her truth,
it buries time, but not the loss of youth.
The screen just sits there, stuck on "Unable to scan,"
they're trying to fix it but not making a plan.
She counts out the change with no computer to dime,
the queue grows longer, the silence feels like crime.
She leans in close, takes a shaky breath,
pretending this is her final death.
The camera flashes—she can't hold the giggle,
her cheeks go red, and she pretends to wiggle.
He opens the fridge to that faded old bag,
of peas so long frozen they no longer will drag.
He tried to make something feel special, this meal,
but time left those peas just a little less real.
You offered your umbrella against the rain,
saying the storm wouldn't let us remain.
Now every puddle leaves the same old trace,
I still see your shadow in its wet, blank face.
Your growling stomach takes lead in your head,
you bypass the candy and skip the hot bread.
You stick to your budget, your shopping list,
and leave with pride, not a single regret or mist.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: You're sure your Wi-Fi is stuck in your head,
but it's just the router—the signal is dead.
Your screen goes black and your brain feels blank,
while you stare at the due date, late from the bank.
I watch the tiny bird hop and dance,
it's like a solo show put on by chance.
It bounces across the thin wooden beam,
and makes me smile like a kid again, free and dream.
I check my closet, feel the shopping doom,
there's one ziplock left—no grocery room.
I'm at the checkout, cashier says "you now,"
I stand there frozen, thinking of some how.
She buys a fake ID, just to pass the bouncer's test,
and skips the line where the rest of us are pressed.
Up the fire escape, she's the first one to climb,
stealing the show before the show begins, in prime.
You never tried to bend it into a fix,
just let the kink do whatever weird tricks.
Now it hangs there crooked, your signature pride,
casting shadows you won't even try to hide.
You finally got your refund in cash,
you're tempted to show it off with a flash.
But you think better of it, hold back a bit,
and deposit it all into your savings fit.
You turned your house into a mystery room,
"They're here somewhere," you tell the empty loom.
You tried every drawer, tried every lock,
but laughed when you found them—just total shock.
I film myself doing the dance again to show
how badly I mess up each time I go low.
This isn't a hobby, it's more like a pain,
my phone loves my fails, but not my brain.
I hit send after midnight—too late,
my words feel heavy with awkward weight.
They sit there unread, like a ghost in the read,
and maybe it's best I just leave it unsaid.
Your laptop's so hot, you're feeling the heat,
It jolts and restarts and just won't repeat.
The fan whirs like a tiny outboard fan,
You vow to find chairs with a better plan.
Your hand brushed mine in the elevator air,
I froze mid-step on the office stair.
Time paused for a single, strange beat,
and silence grew warmer than any heat.
You pause when you hear their familiar tune,
it's late, but your brain still chases the moon.
You wonder if this new song means their name
has reappeared, like a ghost from a flame.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: I blow hard and watch every candle's last flame,
The numbers spell out your birthday, my name.
I told you I'd never try this again, today,
But somehow your shadow still lingers in gray.
Your treadmill screen won't glow or grow,
but still you run where your feet want to go.
The numbers stay stuck at zero to read,
yet every step feels like it could still lead.
You remember the time your hand got a burn,
you cried over searing garlic and a wrong turn.
Now the kitchen fills up with a warm smell,
you wave at the past and taste a soft farewell.
You open the document too late at night now,
the cursor blinks as you question how.
The clock continues ticking toward midnight's face,
your thoughts stretch thin in this empty space.
It cuts right through my morning peace and my ear,
it sounds like a voice from another year.
I tap on the screen, but the message goes through,
the silence is back, leaving only this blue.
I bought the treadmill to save my own time,
now every workout feels like a minor crime.
It squeaks so loud I'm sure it's a joke,
but I keep running, slowly almost choke.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: She scrolls late again, no need for sleep,
the numbers go up—she starts to leap.
A swell in her chest with each new pride,
she grins in the dark, the glow inside.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: The screen glows cold, a little too blue,
I watch my savings vanish from my view.
Some card I lost still adds new debt,
while I lie awake with quiet regret.

topic: finding a dollar in old jeans
lines: You bend down to flip your jeans for some gold,
and sure enough, there's a bill you can hold.
You hold it up like it's pocketbook change,
but why do coins feel more fun than this strange?
I typed *"butter" with care but missed my aim,
now the message blazes like a flame.
The chat is silent—should I laugh or say
this was the worst thing to happen today?
You watch the hamster go round and round the spin,
though deep down you wonder what it feels within.
It's not like it has options or it really knows,
it just keeps running where the routine goes.
You stare at the clue you've circled three times,
The puzzle is due in five minutes, not rhymes.
You panic, look up, but you hit the clock now,
Your thoughts spin faster than answers will how.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: You posted the same old joke once again,
hoping this time it might strike a new vein.
You give it another shot, just one more try,
but silence is still all anyone will reply.

topic: eating ice cream with a spoon
lines: She hums a tune only she can hear in the air,
legs kicking out rhythm from her seat in the chair.
Her spoon drags through chocolate, a slow swirl,
time bends for a moment, just this quiet girl.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: You said the dead air needed one more joke,
but the laugh came through like a breathless choke.
It lit a half-empty stage, one strange scene,
where silence had meant something so clean.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: You liked my old Instagram post last week,
I thought you'd been a ghost I never could speak.
It's strange how a single tap can still feel
like proof that you once mattered to me—still real.

topic: tea leaves steeping in a cup
lines: You sip your brew, let your mind unwind,
while leafy shadows stir up behind.
They swirl and spin in a lazy slow flow,
performing a circus they never asked to show.
You hold your last balloon full of air,
Its string now wrapped tight in your hair.
You spin and you leap, trying to run,
But the tangle refuses to be undone.
She claimed the suitcase with purrs and a lay,
it's been that spot where she claims her day.
Now luggage stays zipped, the couch turns to chair,
while whiskers twitch softly in dreams of the air.
I tried to catch leaves but I lost them to sky,
they looped like a cursive you'd see if you fly.
I said it was nature's weird twist of a joke,
they twirled like old ghosts in the wind's smoky smoke.
She walks with her toes pressed against the sun,
the heat rising quick and the sidewalk run.
Her sandals hang loose by their frayed-out shows,
while thoughts swirl beneath where the breeze goes.
You stood there waiting, but you never lost your time,
your patience wasn't a public crime.
The bus faced problems, it had a long delay,
while you watched the clock and smiled at the display.
They scribbled a message inside the small note,
but spelling mistakes marred what they wrote.
Their shaky handwriting barely looks ink,
yet there's something about it—no digital link.
She stares too long at that blue-lit glow,
the cursor blinks like it wants her to go.
Her eyelids twitch from the static dust,
but she keeps scrolling, obsessed with her lust.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: Her thumb stays on the screen in eerie blue,
another bill appears—this month's is due.
She sits with numbers and her quiet alone,
the app gives no reprieve, just a flat tone.
You wandered down the empty grocery aisle,
remembering the clerk's slow, patient smile.
The machine blinked red where you tried to be paid,
and you missed the old queues, how they would fade.
I call it grating, but it's more like art,
the kind you take too long to get it right, the part.
The pasta waits beneath the parmesan dish,
and I pretend they can't taste how much I wish.
You hear the chime like a ghost from the past,
it wasn't your phone, but the wind's soft blast.
You reach for your screen, expecting a call,
but the clock just ticks, and the quiet grows tall.
You hear the faint ring from your nightstand sound,
It wakes you up mid-dream, half-undressed, unbound.
You answer in hush, afraid it might be all
a wrong number or ghost against the cold wall.
You pulled out a ten for what seemed like a deal,
thinking it'd buy you a decent enough meal.
The cashier raised an eyebrow at your bill,
while you tried to stay cool and pretend you still chill.
The static breaks the silence in the air,
like lost songs whispering through the fare.
She leans closer, chasing the old hum,
her voice now the only beat left to drum.
I fumble with the lock, but where is my key?
The handle won't budge—am I trapped or set free?
I knock and I shout, beg someone to try,
but silence answers, and I'm alone and I cry.
You pause mid-step where the sand met the floor,
the flip-flop still caught at the open door.
You hum a small tune, turn the hallway light,
and know things will settle, just take your right.
She swore she would pay it before it was due,
but her phone showed nothing in her bank's view.
A fee hit her balance with no prior shock,
now cash is a curse she can't seem to block.
She stared at the check printed in faded blue,
the date still legible but long overdue.
She signed her name in smudged-out ink,
then spent the afternoon trying not to think.
I can't seem to keep my head out of my mind,
my thoughts chase each other, fast and unkind.
The chip in the mug seems to echo a crack
in something I've tried so hard not to talk back.
I chase the bubbles rising toward the sky,
the dog just snorts and trots on by.
One bursts in midair—oh, how it pop!
I trip on a root and land flat on my crop.
I step outside where the stillness is air,
the ground holds a sparkle so light it seems bare.
Each crystal resists but will soon be melt,
while I walk in my coat like a tight-woven belt.
I knocked the can and watched it slowly pour,
the bubbles sizzled where they met the floor.
My headphones wheezed a strange new pop,
but now my playlist ends—right where it's got to stop.
You watched your goldfish spin 'til your head lost its mind,
the fish swimming straight but the tank keeps it blind.
There's nothing out there, just the wall of the bowl,
yet still you wonder if it knows it has no soul.
We went from nonstop talk to zero talk,
then they vanished like a ghost down the walk.
Their profile stays online, but I don't read,
just scroll past their face on my TikTok feed.
Her screen glows brighter than the hour is late,
She tells herself this post will be the wait.
She'll quit when the blue light starts turning to dawn,
But sleep still feels far and the hours are gone.
You carry that backpack like it's your full load,
the straps dig deep like a highway to road.
Each step creaks your spine like a rusted-out bend,
but you joke it's just a heavy-lidded friend.

topic: a cart with a broken wheel
lines: I push the cart through the grocery store's long shift,
each item meant as a last-minute gift.
When the wheel screeches, I almost drop the cart,
and laugh how life can feel like broken art.
You turn away for just one second—what a mess,
the blue runs down your sleeve and onto your dress.
You grab a towel but the wall starts to drip,
you try to fix it, your hands start to slip.
You think you're out for a peaceful morning run,
until the dog decides this isn't fun.
He yanks and yelps with a full-throated bark,
tugging you past the coffee stand at the park.
You leave your towel on the sticky floor,
It holds every drop, and that's a bit more.
Now someone else wears the sweat's old scent,
But you never had any such intent.
You tell yourself it's just a little lie,
the room is fine, the weather fits the sky.
But your shivering says you need a chill,
so you crank the heat for that false thrill.

topic: the smell of pancakes in the morning
lines: The kitchen fills with that buttery air,
I forget my towel's still in my hair.
The pancakes rise in a lopsided rise,
but you smile through syrup in your eyes.
I try to hydrate but my mind has a mind,
it treats each glass like a task that I grind.
I vow to drink more each single day,
yet somehow I still forget them away.
It dances above me, light as the air,
its wings are a blur of translucent pair.
It hovers, then dips—how does it all spin?
I watch it hang still, suspended within.
I spill flour on my shirt and the mess
grows bigger each time I give the task my yes.
The pan starts to smoke, things begin to burn,
but even bad meals help me slowly learn.

topic: a group project where nobody helps
lines: The deadline looms but they're not really due,
they say they'll do it but you know it's not true.
They slide through the week without a single slack,
while we chase their promises down every track.
She traced each letter as if she meant to read
the secrets that had climbed across the spread
of concrete, looking for a name to claim,
but found only echoes of the same.
They promised your grade would be posted by date,
but the portal won't load—just sits at the gate.
You refresh every five minutes, a scroll,
while your patience and soul slowly lose control.
They dart behind the tree and listen to the bark,
hidden tight in the hush of evening's dark.
A petal falls near where they sit upon a stone,
their quiet joy in being seen but not alone.
My phone died twice since I last saw the screen,
It's muttering things that sound vaguely mean.
I toss it like a brick into the plug,
It sparks up only when I swear at the rug.

topic: a book left open on the nightstand
lines: I left you open on the nightstand page,
your spine now bent like a worn-out cage.
I trace the words by the pale moon,
my heartbeat's a silent old tune.
I can't let the butter just sit on the stick,
it's sliding too fast, it's a warm, greasy slick.
My breakfast waits calmly, but still I race,
trying to eat before it all melts in its place.
That kid left a soda cup in the mess,
I tripped and swore, now I know my address.
It oozed across the tiles like a drip,
and now I'm limping every time I trip.
She circles the rack but she never says try,
her tears are held close beneath her dry cry.
She asks if this size might somehow still fit,
and softens my voice when I shake my head "bit."
She bends down slowly, her back to the street,
and sorts through the mess with her muddy old feet.
She picks up what's spoiled or beginning to rot,
and sighs at the things she never should've got.

topic: hot chocolate on a cold day
lines: You heat up the same old bag of expired brew,
it tastes like last week's leftovers gone stew.
Snow's piled high but you can't move from the block,
the minutes crawl slower than any old clock.
I dropped my fries and watched him take my snack,
he waddled off with grease on his little track.
He stared up once, as if to read the sky,
then flew off—no, not flown, but just walked on by.
I've plunged and cursed until my hands feel like drain,
the smell's so bad it's now in my brain.
This isn't just water—it's the whole kitchen mess,
I'm paying a plumber just to survive this stress.
I found your name and your locker key,
left your lunch and paid the late fee.
No need for panic or any clue,
I handled it all for you.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: You scroll as you lie in your warm, sleepy bed,
The screen says your number won't rise or fall dead.
Its blue light still glows, but you just want to know—
Who sees all this longing? The world doesn't show.
You spot the bus driver dozing at the wheel,
his half-eaten sandwich dripping with a meal.
The bus sways gently, coasting past the brake,
you pray they wake before this turns to mistake.

topic: a child drawing on the table
lines: You call this scribbled mess a work of art,
I'm trying not to scream into my lunch meat heart.
You proudly show off every smudged-up mess,
I nod and smile and say "Oh, that's a yes."
My brain feels like soup, my eyes full of rain,
A nap is the only way off this train.
I need to crash hard before three o'clock,
I'd pay for a pillow, a blanket, a sock.
This sad song is playing again as a thing,
The phone just buzzed once, now silent, no ring.
I hit the repeat button (auto-play mode),
My grief is so algorithmic, it's code.
I swear this room reeks of someone else's clean,
but maybe I'm just being overly mean.
Could be the ghost of a janitor from last night,
or I'm losing my mind — which is fun, but not right.
You wind the music box with care and key,
it dances while you sip your warm tea.
The melody spins out soft and thin,
a forgotten world stirs deep within.
Her smile is sold in lights that fake a glow,
they claim she's real but you don't really know.
She's built to sell a lie, she was made just
to trick your eyes—don't fall for what you trust.
My showerhead won't make a proper arc,
it dribbles sideways and leaves me a mark.
I twist the knob for more water flow,
but the pressure just won't go go go.
She wears her dreams tied tight in that bag,
it sags behind her, leaves her moves a bit lag.
The world feels heavy but she carries the weight,
small and alone in a quiet, calm state.
You made a drama at the school supply scene,
a full-blown meltdown from a clueless teen.
You blamed your mom for forgetting your name,
then yelled at me—"It's always the *same*!"

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: She stops to admire the web's crystal gleam,
the morning light flows through like a stream.
The dewdrops look ready to spin and to dance,
she smiles, it's a moment worth pausing for a chance.
You stand beneath neon, always wanting that glow,
the face in the ad just wants you to know—
it's a filtered illusion, a setup to lie,
but you still reach for stars in that painted sky.

topic: missing a chorus in a song
lines: I hum along but miss the big tune,
the lyrics feel far like a half-sung moon.
My finger skips where the chorus should be,
a familiar sadness just slips through me.
They opened a window to freshen the air,
but the must still climbed the damp wooden stair.
Something chemical hung in the mix,
a scent no amount of bleach could ever fix.
I wade through the shallows where light finds a gleam,
the water repeats every cloud in the stream.
This mirror outshines any glass they could claim,
the sky bows its head to reflect my own name.
She swears it was on the tip of her mind,
she looks behind every chair, every blind.
The memory starts to drift and to fade,
while coworkers pass like ghosts in a parade.
You were too late to stop the garbage from spill,
it scattered across the sidewalk to fill
the gaps where the cat likes to dig near the home,
now trash drifts like leaves as the wind makes it roam.
You count the drops trying to set your pace,
the echo is loud in this empty place.
Your hands are steady, but you feel the fear,
the sink seems to whisper, "Is it almost clear?"
I tried to hide my confusion with an act,
but the paper gave out the whole dark fact.
It folded itself like a bad road sign fold,
pretending it knew what direction was told.
I thought the train left at half-past right,
but the board shows a red, wrong light.
Now I'm staring at "Delayed—Be late,"
while my breath clouds up the closed gate.
You still leave the light on when you go,
let it flicker soft like it used to glow.
That old bulb lit every birthday cake,
now it's failing slow but you won't let it take.
She tells her brain it's time to unwind,
but screens are still sharp with content behind.
Each scroll feels urgent, another quick click,
though sleep is the only real thing she trick.
I grab the couch because it's the best for fun,
We drape the windows so no one sees the sun.
The blanket fort now rules this whole room,
Laughter brightens even the weekend's gloom.
I scroll through the news, it's all bad doom,
the screen glows like a ghost in my room.
I mean to stop here, just one more thread,
but morning's a myth when you stay up dead.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: You find a toothpick caught in your sleeve's snag,
it's strange but you call it a lucky flag.
You clip it tight like a symbol of hope,
turn it into a charm, a tiny makeshift rope.
After lunch my energy goes on a crash,
I need something sweet to give me a flash.
The vending machine's my only quick fix,
Got chocolate, pretzels, and a bad diet mix.
That old bulb still hums with its fading glow,
I should replace it but somehow still don't know.
I freeze in the hallway, time slows all the way down,
like walking through memories from another town.
You try to sleep but the wheel won't be stilled—all
—night it clatters like a faulty wall.
You count each turn, but it never will spin
long enough to feel like it's ending within.
The fridge light flickers but still stays on beam,
They opened the door on a hunger dream.
Leftover beans and old chicken stew
are the only ingredients — no meal, just clue.
The lot was full, and every space felt tight,
until a spot opened up and shone so bright.
You thought it was your lucky break, your luck,
but ended up parallel-parked and stuck.
You spilled coffee on your keyboard last mess,
now crumbs and ketchup jam every address.
You try to clean but the keys won't snap
back in place—this is a total trap.
You wore your old boots for the springtime rain,
a childhood habit you couldn't let go again.
Now your socks are soaked and your workday shoes
never saw the storm coming—no warning, no news.
They take up more than half the seat, spread,
but only ask to rest their aching head.
You shift your bag to make them more space,
and catch the softness in their tired face.
I clocked out but I'm still at my desk in a dream,
the emails keep pouring and they all scream.
A voice says "you'll get a promotion if you call,"
I wake up reaching, arm still in sprawl.
She's still holding tight to the fragile hope,
her foot tapping soft against the bus rope.
The minutes stretch slow while she tries to wait,
but the bus isn't coming—it missed the gate.
You found the notice slipped beneath your hand,
its words like a landlord's cold-voiced demand.
You hold on tight to that one last little note—
the key, still in your old worn leather tote.
You count rotations, trying to keep your spin,
but every loop just makes the fear begin.
It's the same routine, the same old dread,
like life's a hamster wheel on a tight thread.

topic: the smell of pancakes in the morning
lines: It drifts through the house like warmth in the air,
a scent so familiar, soft and fair.
The kind that makes dough slowly start to rise,
and slips into my dreams without my eyes.
You feel a rush of quiet pride,
the recipe was yours to guide.
The table's ready, the food is set,
someone will say this is their new favorite yet.
You feel drained now that the party's all out,
Your smile still echoes the crowd's loud shout.
You turn off the lights and leave all the bright,
But hope hums quietly through the soft night.
You let the quiet day settle in your mind,
no texts, no calls—no one tried to find
you just made a cup of coffee for the day,
and let the forgotten date slip slowly away.
You watched it float high into the sky,
its final escape made you want to cry.
It popped without sound beneath the sun,
you laughed instead of trying to run.
She meets your gaze with a flick of her eyes,
then turns away like there's nothing but lies.
You call her name, she walks to the floor,
as if she owns every inch of this door.
You call your life an organized mess,
but your closet looks like a hurricane dress.
Lecture notes are never actually found—
they drift beneath your couch like important ground.
I blow warm air from my mouth to clear my breath,
I'm tired of staring at the ghost of death.
I draw a big, silly face to practice a smile,
hoping it sticks for more than a fleeting while.

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: The sun still lives in every drop of flame
that beads across my brow I dare not name.
I let it fall and don't even try to pass,
July knows my secrets, dry as dead grass.
I once had big dreams but fell flat on my pride,
I tumbled through leaves, then got stuck on a slide.
I tried to eat moss—it was not a snack,
now I'm just a joke on the forest floor's track.
You stood there letting the storm put on its show,
while the wind howled things no one else heard below.
You let the rhythm of the rain dictate the beat,
turned thunder into your personal kind of heat.
I watch the dragonfly hover in air,
its wings so still though the breeze is fair.
It seems to pause, then zips away like a dart,
I smile, amazed at this tiny heart.
He takes a bite, the center starts to core,
the seeds fly out when he opens the door.
His smile goes wide—a perfect, juicy grin,
the apple's gone, now the peel looks too thin.
My body lit up like a fuse had a spark,
but now it's heavy, and all I want is the dark.
I sink into the couch or maybe just chair,
my breath feels thick, like I'm swimming through air.
She slides the box out to see if it will bake,
forgets she read the wrong side—full mistake.
The cheese never rises, just sags and sighs,
she serves it anyway, calls it a weird surprise.
I leave it on low so it knows I will stay,
not rush, not fizzle, or burn out and away.
It warms the kitchen with just the right heat,
and I come back later to taste what we eat.

topic: posting a photo with no one around

if they weren't aimed at everything that crashes—
the lights, the Wi-Fi, life itself in flashes.
It weaves through traffic with the morning wind,
I'm left standing still while it zooms me behind.
The rider laughs loud with perfect grace,
I wave from my curb with a grin in my place.
I left my fries alone on the kitchen plate,
I turned my back and now I'm way too late.
They took one bite, then winked with their hand,
I laugh and pretend I don't understand.
She sees the gas light and checks the tank,
her budget's already tight at the bank.
She'll wait until the next gas station stop,
though the needle keeps inching toward a drop.
She watches the daffodils come into spring,
each bud a sign that winter's grip is thing.
Their yellow heads defiant in the light,
she feels her hope return at that first sight.
You step on your treadmill, ready to roll,
it screams like a ghost trying to break your soul.
You vow you'll get healthier, stronger, more fit,
but the noise makes you wish you were stuck in a pit.
You laugh so hard you forget there's a cake,
knees shaking, glass clinking, halfway to break.
One snuff blows out the last remaining flame,
but the joke is still the exact same.
I hear the rusted swing set breathe the air,
its seat still warm from where you sat in chair.
We promised we would come back just to stay,
but time wore through the wood, like it or not, decay.
They're stuck in their room with nothing but fear,
refreshing the chat in a haze that's unclear.
Their finger hovers, "Is this one okay to send?"
The clock ticks again toward the dread of the end.
The "E" key feels loose and starts to go flat,
I type on my thumbs to send out my chat.
The letters keep fading like they lost their fade,
I panic mid-text—will this mess up my grade?
Your toothbrush hangs loose on the tiled wall,
while others all drip from the shower's sprawl.
It's been months since you swapped out for mint,
and the bristles still hold your last rinse from Clint.
You swore there was order, some perfect space,
but your desk is a landslide, no room for a place.
You'll never find anything, you can't even try,
the notes are a ghost in a paperless sky.
They left a sticky keyboard after the mess,
probably spilled soda—no one can guess.
The teacher tried to clean but missed a few keys,
now students beg, "Please don't sit here!" with ease.
A bird gives me the same tired call,
it's like a broken alarm clock's dull ball.
I stare at the gray and never ask why,
the sky stays half-awake, same as I.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: I trace each crease and each weathered fold,
the ink's faded but the paths are still gold.
I spot an X where no one would mark,
and suddenly hope starts to spark.
My battery screams "I'll die if I run,"
but I still try to save what's left from the fun.
I tap on my contacts, ready to call,
but doom wins again—nothing works at all.
I watch the stalks strain toward the sun to bend,
like they owe it something or maybe a friend.
What if I'm stuck facing this way to bloom?
Is there even space for me to move or room?
You laugh off the crush, the lack of space,
this crammed carriage feels like your strange place.
The rhythm of tracks creates a hum,
strangers smile — maybe they'll come.
I bring my pasta some bright, grated cheer,
the cheese falls soft as a fresh-fallen flake near.
It's not about being the best damn dish,
it's just a small joy I chose to make my wish.

topic: reading under the covers with a flashlight
lines: You turn off the lights to hide your glow,
Your parents think you're asleep, they don't know.
You swore you'd read just five pages you gave,
Now you're on chapter ten, feeling brave.
A feather drifts from the gray sky,
it trembles there as it tries to fly,
tangled now in the old oak's twine,
I can't save it—it's stuck in this line.

topic: steaming coffee in a blue mug
lines: Hot coffee curls upward in lazy steam,
I sit here sipping my morning dream.
Light hits the handle, that soft blue hue,
I think this might be the calmest me true.
The crickets sing a ballad of endless time,
their rhythm like old clocks left to chime.
You watch the last of the light bend in the sky,
and wonder if the moment will ever die.
I draw a rainbow where the ground is dry,
as if the sky might break and weep from high.
Each color blooms in muddy, brownish hue,
I paint my hope right up through the dirt and through.
Each time the shovel makes a loud thud,
It kicks up clods more like rock than mud.
They count every swing, sweat, and sting,
but this winter's earth won't be tamed into a thing.
You thought you were immune to this old tune,
but the lyrics hit harder than a full moon.
You grab a napkin—your sleeve works too—mop
up the mess before the chorus has to stop.
She replays the track by the best-known ways,
Each chorus loops through her saddest days.
Her headphones hum as the record keeps spin,
A private storm that she swears feels within.
I plug the toaster in to catch some sun,
it warms my toast but leaves me half-done.
The steam fogged up my phone's front screen,
now butter slides where I had drawn a mean.
You lie awake again and wonder why you're there,
tracing cracks in plaster up the stair.
Your brain refuses sleep — your mind's too wide,
lost in thoughts you'll never put aside.
I told my toaster I'd give it one more try,
now it's just charcoal, and I'm about to cry.
It gave me smoke, not breakfast—it's a crime, this smoke,
I guess the burnt bread is the universe's joke.
She claims she's flush with enough old cash,
but the bills are stacked like a veggie smash.
A breeze walks through, they begin to storm,
the stack takes flight and the papers swarm.
You twist the handle but the lock won't spin,
your palms get clammy, you're slipping so thin.
You dig through your bag for the spare key, no key,
the landlord charges a fee to set you free.
You hit send after the joke had long passed,
cringing silently like smoke from a blast.
You try to deny it, but you still feel miss,
the chat scrolls on—don't even try to fix this.
You tell yourself it's not just a lie,
you're feeding peace to the gray in the sky.
They peck and they squabble and shuffle and roll,
while you pretend this means something for your soul.
She watches the yolk sink into the glaze,
her memory soft as a morning's thin haze.
Her spoon moves slow through the quiet, the stir,
she whispers "Dad" when the ghost speaks "My son, sir."
You write your name on the edge of the skin,
whisper it softly so only you're in.
You hope the words might escape with the wind,
waiting for someone to find what you've left behind.
I can't look at this paperclip mess,
you probably think it's some kind of artless guess.
I tried to tell you they'd all snap and bend,
now we're stuck with this pointless metal end.
You call this art? It's barely legible mess,
I had to guess your name from the return address.
I've seen toddlers draw better than your feeble try,
at least theirs didn't bleed through both sides when it dry.
She counts out each bill with tight-lipped cash,
the register keeps flashing what she's not flash.
Her fingers shake with the quietest fear,
she checks it again, just to satisfy her ear.
You draw your heroes, your ghosts, and your life,
smearing color like blood from a knife.
The walls lean in close, your bright little room,
the page feels like home, like a warm painted womb.
Your toast never made the satisfying pop,
It froze mid-sizzle and just would not stop.
You tried to force the lever to give it a lift,
But now crumbs are trapped — a breakfast-world gift.
Your favorite jeans are a faded, worn blue,
You wear them every damn day without a clue.
You tug and you strain, but the zipper won't try,
It's stubborn and slow, like a quiet little cry.
You swing the shovel—blunt as the blade,
your breath fogs out and dies in the shade.
You pause and stare at this stubborn rock,
then laugh at the absurdity of shock.
You trace your age in the fog on the face,
the only dry spot where you once had grace.
The hot water fades into thin sheets of steam,
you whisper old hopes back into the dream.
I watched it fall and hit the wooden floor,
there wasn't much I could do or say for more.
The coffee seeped from where the lid let go,
now I'm mopping it all up and feeling low.
You poke your pencil into the blade,
The tip gets shorter in every shade.
You try to twist it, you gently press,
But bits of wood are a sticky mess.
Your beach day crumbles in the wind's behest,
you set off alone to fix this strange quest.
You tie frayed ribs with a wobbly thread,
but saltwater laughs as your shade starts to spread.
You drew your childhood in a single room,
the chaos colored like a warm womb.
Now every swirl is faded and worn out,
but I still trust the joy you once had no doubt.
She traced her fingers over the faded name,
something bold chasing a fleeting fame.
The wall's rough surface couldn't be held tight,
but she kept drawing until it felt right.
You tap the send button, breath held tight to send,
"Goodnight" to a friend who might just pretend.
They're still awake, you know they won't reply,
but you wait anyway, afraid your heart will die.
A single drop spilled from the coffee to ink,
She froze mid-sentence, her eyes began to think.
The paper was soaked where the math problem grade
would be, and now all her effort's about to fade.
She tried on his boots but they never did fit,
she wobbled and pointed at the big "it."
He laughed off her footwork in borrowed shoe size,
claiming practice looked better in playful disguise.

topic: clouds gathering on a summer afternoon
lines: I saw the sky turn from bright to a dull blue,
the clouds wearing gray like they meant to stay too.
I hope it will clear up before there's a break,
and we can still walk by the empty lake.
The tiny print now looks like strange signs,
I squint at menus full of hidden lines.
I tried to deny it for way too long—age
creeps in slow and steady, like a silent cage.
You breathe deep, the kind of cold that fills the air,
twist your scarf up higher—no use to even dare.
You crunch through frost and clear a better way,
turning the driveway into something worth the day.
You leave a white trail across every mess,
it dusts your shoes and your favorite dress.
The cat paws through it like a snowbank cake,
but you laugh and say, "I'll clean it all take."
He squirts toothpaste from the very base,
like it's some sacred rule for life and space.
"This is the only right way," he'll say,
as if the tube cares how we spend our day.
The clouds twist and churn like they're trying to spin,
the wind slams my window against my skin.
I check the forecast, it says "you don't need,"
but still I pray this storm will never feed.
The envelope's taped tight with the rent still due,
she hadn't the cash and she knew it too.
Her hands hovered briefly above the door,
then slipped back into her pockets for more.
His face flickers under the dying glow,
the kind of light that makes you feel you know.
He looks like he's waiting for something to fall—
maybe the silence, or maybe the wall.
I pulled up the handle and gave it a twist,
the button was wet, the thing didn't work—just missed.
A gust hit the ribs, the frame let out a crack,
I dropped it in fear, my shoulders still shaking back.
You watch the snowflakes dissolve on your skin,
Their fragile designs disappear within.
A quiet thaw hums where your collar meets jaw,
But winter still rules by its icy law.
She drops a ten-dollar bill in her lunch cash,
the machine chomps it, then spits out a smash.
The cashier shrugs and calls it a bad deal,
so she just grabs a sandwich and pays for the meal.
The screen flashes red as if it's your time,
It feels like the world thinks this is your crime.
You wave your card again, the machine won't bend,
And no one around even offers a friend.
I wear the left earbud to drown out the blast
of your conversation that I've already passed.
You think this is cool while I lose half my soul
pretending to listen as I keep on scroll.
He claims his dented bottle's how he found his fame,
but it's clearly from some ancient, lingering shame.
He leaves it by the gym bag like a sacred door,
as if keeping it hid adds myth to the lore.

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: She still remembers how she first flipped the read,
the coffee and scone were the best kind of bread.
The review calls it a trap by the writer's name,
but to her, it's the spot where they felt most the same.
She packs the last box and leaves it on the floor,
the cat curls up there like it owns the whole chore.
Her flight leaves tomorrow, but the cat makes a claim—
it paws at her phone, won't let her use its old name.
She ran through the halls like a map turned to maze,
her books swinging loose from a dozen bad ways.
A professor drew arrows in quick blue chalk,
and pointed her toward the right kind of talk.
I give her a look—no need for a clue,
she knows every step's a promise that's true.
She leans toward the door like she's built to run,
the handle waits gleaming beneath the sun.
You saw it again last night, quietly chew,
though you didn't want to admit what you knew.
Maybe he's just building a soft little nest,
not trying to ruin your sneakerless best.
You hit replay but the song isn't in the air,
it skipped like a beat you once loved in a pair.
You pause the track to try and find what you miss,
but the playlist moves on—sorry, not this.
I check my phone again just to see the chat,
the mood has gone stale, and the silence feels flat.
But someone adds a joke, and it brings back the spark,
and suddenly laughter lights up the dark.

topic: clouds gathering on a summer afternoon
lines: They pause beneath the heavy grey sky,
the kind of quiet only lovers can lie.
The clouds begin to mass and to form,
but neither moves—your hands know this storm.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: You find a toothpick still lodged in your sleeve there,
it's been there all day, lost in the air.
You pull it out slowly, a small ache gives a twist,
but you didn't miss the moment it kissed.
You thought you could open the can with your fool,
but even the can-opener calls you a tool.
You shake it and swear that you'll never be rid
of this dent, this mess, this cursed bean lid.

topic: texting 'i miss u' out of nowhere
lines: I saw a cloud shaped like your face in the sky,
So I typed "I miss u" and asked myself why.
I almost called it off as some lighthearted joke,
But my thumbs moved faster than my better smoke.
You wear your mess like a badge of pride,
All crumb and crack and sadness inside.
You'll never swap this for a store-bought know,
It's dented but real—there's beauty to show.
She found the combo and swung the door wide key,
No more waiting, she's officially free.
A grin spreads slow, she holds it all so smug,
The others stare as she sips from her lunchtime mug.
It's lost its shape but still knows every form,
it survived a drop, a fall, a minor storm.
Who needs a new one when this one is fine?
It's got more stories than a long grocery line.
You swear the zipper's trying to make a tear,
it won't go past your hip—just gets stuck in your rear.
You tug at it gently, then rip out the seam,
and let the perfect jeans become a lost dream.
She pretends she's just here for the calm, soft man,
but her hands won't stop moving across that yarn span.
Her focus has shifted from Netflix to code,
now her knitting's on vibrate, not relax mode.
She pours the milk like it's filling a lake,
expecting a crunch, not a soggy take.
Her spoon hits the bottom, a sad little puff,
she stares at the mess, this cold breakfast stuff.

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: Your skin feels the sun but you let it burn,
your face toward the heat, don't try to turn.
That sweat rolling down's your silent proof—
you're alive under this whole sky's green roof.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: You struck your best smile with perfect pose,
[toes] Your socks were bright and your barefoot toes,
The dog had just ruined the birthday cake,
But you laughed anyway—for fun's own sake.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: She laughs as the earth begins to roll,
the joy in her grin speaks to her soul.
A puddle becomes her newest mess,
her clothes are ruined, but she loves her dress.
It darts through the room like it wants to see
something that vanishes, wild and free.
It pounces for hours in the golden hour,
all energy fading, no prey, no power.
Her finger taps but the cursor won't move,
it's frozen where it's placed, nothing will prove
she tries a soft reboot, a force click,
the screen stays cold, her tech becomes a brick.
She left the knob stuck on gentle heat,
same simmer that hums every week, repeat.
The pot gives off little more than a glow,
but she's happy enough just to sit and go.
They wipe their eyes and smooth their tear-streaked face,
trying to remember where they found their grace.
A flicker of a smile hides the old pain,
as if the sky might weep again.
You walk through town with pride in your stride,
kicking up dust, leaving sidewalks aside.
You plant your soles where the pavement meets ground,
and claim the heat as something you've finally found.
You tried to fold the bag into a neat mess,
but every flap still sticks out from the guess.
That buttered butterfinger left behind grease,
and now your fingers won't let go of the release.

topic: a cart with a broken wheel
lines: This grocery cart won't even roll,
every push takes a mental toll.
It's stuck on the curb, off the track,
someone call a repair tech—this is a hack.
You shout your wares into the hot air,
hoping the traffic will remember you fair.
Your name is lost in the city's long name,
but your voice still flickers, a quiet flame.
The toddler giggles each time one will pop,
then chases the next one out of the crop.
She's convinced they're trying hard to fly,
even though she has no idea why.
You sit and watch that robin peck around there,
while you pretend you're not bored out of your air.
It's such a strange little performance, this waste,
but hey, nature needs no script or any haste.
I kicked off my shoes like they held some bad news,
the socks clung to them, dripping their clues.
This floor feels too cold for the state that I'm in—
I'll let them air out... or maybe just bin.
That joke means nothing if you don't know the code,
we fall into giggles like some strange new mode.
You can't explain why, but you laugh all day,
chasing old memories we can't throw away.
You're still looking for that one tiny clue,
the gum under your chair is half-chewed and blue.
It's been there since your lunch break, that sticky old date,
your coworkers all know it but never state.
A chilly air brushes her face like a breeze,
the wind whispers secrets just to tease.
Her breath curls up, a ghostly little spark,
she closes her eyes as the sky turns to dark.
My roommates raised their voices just to fight,
the last slice glowing under fridge light.
I held out hope they'd let me just keep,
the slice was more than a craving—it was deep.
I hit the road to chase some air,
the wind flips through my wild, wet hair.
My old playlist brings up an old song,
I laugh out loud and sing it along.
My mind feels heavy with half-formed thought,
I've battled silence all morning long, I fought.
Words circle back me but won't take shape or ground,
so I nod and wait till the meeting's found.
You let the silence grow from the past,
unread messages fading too fast.
The sender's still saved under your name,
but your replies feel like a dying flame.
I watched them push up through the wet earth and rise,
their yellow heads turning toward my wide eyes.
They don't need spring, they just want to bloom,
and now they're taking over this whole front room.
She watches the bird stay perfectly still,
the way it balances gives her a thrill.
Her fingers hover like they might reach out and,
just miss the moment, as if it's too grand.
I type my password and curse every try,
my brain's too dry to remember why.
They offer help, but it won't help me fix —
this digital wall made of code and bricks.
You lunge at the flicker on the ceiling's bright beam,
convinced it's the ghost of some shadowy dream.
You twist through the furniture with feline leap,
but the light just sits there where it softly creep.
You fix your eyes on that flickering stare,
the bulb shivers out of the damp, cold air.
You swear you feel something like static or blood,
a presence seeping through the dark like a flood.
I took the last spoon from the shelf near the jar,
and watched the light catch the gluey star.
One drop fell slow like a small, soft drip,
and slowly, I smiled as I felt it grip.

topic: restaurant with no menu in English
lines: She asked if this dish was the same or a name,
the waiter shrugged—it was neither the same.
She lifted her fork with a smile at her plate,
half lost to the flavor, half lost to her fate.
They flip the pancakes just so they turn gold,
the spatula steady, never let it hold.
There's rhythm in the motion, a kind of grace,
as if the whole kitchen was built for this place.
You watch the way the light misses the tree,
how shadows crawl but won't set you free.
The leaves keep time by the pattern they cast,
while you stand still, never quite getting past.
You said it was urgent but gave me no clue,
I drove halfway across town just for you.
You thanked me with a smile I could love,
held out a paper cup like the stars above.
He leans against the same old wall,
waits for a call that never comes at all.
His keys still jingle from a habit to skip,
but the porch is empty—no one to trip.
Time etched its quiet mark in the moss's age,
it waited unnoticed, like a frozen stage.
A steady drip falls from the old oak drip,
and you nearly miss your step on the stone-slip.

topic: tea leaves steeping in a cup
lines: You stir the spoon in a lazy twist,
watching the leaves slowly unravel their list.
They dance in circles, a quiet swirl,
like secrets whispered by a dreamy girl.
I spin alone with the gift on the floor,
it's been waiting since we left the store.
Maybe tonight is the perfect new chance,
to finally unwrap it and learn how to dance.
A fish taps the window with one gentle side,
like it's calling me out for a midnight ride.
I trace its path through the quiet tank's soft hum,
maybe something brighter will soon begin to come.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: I count to three and try my best to blow,
but the wind decides how many to show.
Another year, another number, same old age,
I trap my fears inside the birthday cage.
I don't want you to feel like I'm trying to fold,
just lean in, let's split this warm, gooey hold.
We don't need two slices to make something to share,
one crust between us is enough to fill the air.
She watches the butterfly land and pose,
wings trembling slightly above the rose.
Time feels like it's holding its breath, a blur,
but nothing moves—just the wind gives a stir.
The card got flagged for spending in the wrong,
but maybe this is just a glitch in my song.
I tap my phone—*pending transaction, not free*—
but I still believe in some kind of backup key.
She ignores the time, even as the clock
flashes warnings from the bedroom dock.
Her eyes are heavy but she doesn't sleep,
chasing midnight dreams till her phone starts beep.
She pauses at the edge of the wet tile,
her careful walk, so cautious in her style.
A moment wavers, a quiet slip,
but she finds her balance—no need for a grip.
He wears his hard hat like it's built for a crash,
it's painted with memes and a glow stick flash.
It holds back his hair and his forehead's whole band,
a monument to the jobs that he still can stand.
She offers her umbrella to share the sky,
no question or hesitation, just "Why?"
"It's a storm," she says, smiling at you,
and something about her feels a little more true.
You turn on the record, let the old songs play,
Dusty grooves spinning in soft afternoon day.
You tap your foot, almost catch the tune to hum,
Laughter follows melodies that gently come.
You squeeze the bottom like it's still your paste,
ignoring how it's turning into waste.
You're saving every bit for the tiny hole,
but we both know you don't have a tube soul.

topic: waiting for the bus in rain
lines: Your shoes already soaked, you're not going to run,
the bus is late again, this day feels half-**done**.
You stare at clouds that look like they might crack the sky,
and wonder if it's worth it to wait here and **why**.
The teacher clears her throat—then gives the class
a warning look, like she's made of crystal glass.
She hacks through every lesson, breaking each rule,
while we just float there like in a classroom pool.
I type "butterfly" but my phone starts a fight,
it changes the word into just plain "night."
I pause in the middle of every spell,
afraid what it'll say when it tries to tell.

topic: a sticky finger on the window
lines: I spent ten minutes cleaning up this mess,
only for my kid to leave a new address.
I wipe it firmly, try to get it all away,
but here it comes again—his smudged display.
It dangles loose now on just one side,
I forgot how to tune it without a guide.
I miss the old static and distant hum,
but silence feels better than noise that won't come.
I took the middle seat because I claimed more room,
but leg space shrunk to something close to doom.
I cross my legs and try to fold my lean,
and smile like I was born in something tight and mean.
Your bark can shatter windows when you get loud,
you howl like the center of a silent crowd.
There's nothing there, but that means it's your thing,
the phantom becomes your personal king.
I dug up my costume from last Halloween kit,
it barely fits now, but I still look fit.
I strut down the stairs with that quirky old flair,
pretending I own the place, ha! What air?
You used to wait for days, now every hour,
You chug it like it's caffeine—full of power.
Some say it's hydration, I say it's a clue:
You're becoming someone better than you.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: You sat so close to me, almost too near,
your voice brushed by my cheek, right next to my ear.
I couldn't say a word—I just wanted to hold,
like we were still that young, back when we were bold.
You felt it was time to let go, just a bit,
It didn't quite match your life, not a fit.
A deep breath, you click and the page goes light,
Now you've space to try something new, you might.
You watch the light spread across the early sky,
and hear the first sigh of morning's long sigh.
That bus hasn't stopped for your old familiar ride,
but it pulls you awake like the call of the tide.
You tried to wear it with a giant hole,
claiming some other sock must have stole.
I told you once not to skip tying the lace,
now it's wedged behind the fridge—its final place.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: You're stuck in the grocery store aisle,
while someone tries to force a smile.
They offered the kid every processed snack,
but the meltdown won't come off the track.
The scent brings back a summer long past,
how time slipped by without blinking or fast.
It's faint like old toothpaste, a ghost of mint,
stuck to my memory like fabric soft lint.
My essay's still a mess and it's due now,
I stare at the screen like a bored cow.
Each empty page feels more like a cage,
I've wasted this whole day and my age.
I followed a map that led down a back street,
where cinnamon air smelled like an old-time sweet.
The lights had a soft and yellowed glow,
I didn't want to leave—I almost didn't know.
You tried to keep it up against the wind,
but salt and time left you standing behind.
That frame still juts from the wet, warm sand,
though now only ghosts take that sunlit stand.
You follow the sun from your morning bed, glow
the sky is your sign when to stand or to know.
You turn your big face and lift your gold head,
your warmth is the reason we dare to spread.
I follow the trail of the wind's soft scent,
through grass and the shadows where tall trees are bent.
The air is alive with the promise of bloom,
and even my heart feels it has more room.
You've stopped blasting tunes just to fill up your ear,
no need now to crank it to maximum gear.
The chaos called noise just slips by without a fight,
you'd rather now listen to silence or light.
My back screams from hours behind this ache,
I need to move now before I break.
I twist and I turn, reach high up to bend,
Each stretch feels like joy sent straight from heaven to mend.

topic: a video call with a frozen screen
lines: Their face still lingers on the frozen frame,
They hadn't left the room—it was all the same.
A smile flickers through, a silent wave,
I wait, but the screen won't refresh or save.
She laughs as the balloon pulls tight against air,
Its string now knotted deep in her golden hair.
For a moment, she dances, trying to float,
A child again, tied to dreams like a boat.
The shovel won't budge from the ground's cold crack,
your muscles scream through your sore, stiff back.
Winter bites hard with its iron-tight bite,
every swing strains, your grip stays a deathly tight.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: You scroll through your feed and you spot her from the past,
She liked an old photo you posted in the fast.
A flicker of feeling, a ghost of old flame,
You tap on her [name]. She's still in the game.
You left the towel draped in your perfect room,
as if it were hanging from some designer loom.
You checked for a wrinkle, then posed in that spot,
the pic got a thousand likes, no wrong step or shot.
You watch the clouds begin to roll,
a sudden storm shakes your whole soul.
You don't run, you lift your face and break
the stillness wide like a thunder's wake.
I tried to stand but got stuck in this spot,
dumb move—I forgot my legs are weak as a tot.
The bar digs in like it's trying to bar
me from ever becoming a gym star.

topic: checking if you have enough for gas
lines: You check your phone to see if the tank's low,
then panic-check your bank for gas money flow.
The numbers stare back like a cruel joke from fate,
so you sit there and sigh, and then begin to wait.
The milk carton still says "best before date,"
but time and neglect have sealed its fate.
She stirs it and sees the green blobgy mold,
yet sips it anyway and tightens her cold.
She feeds the machine her last crisp, shiny drop,
but the screen stays blank where the snack list should crop.
The coins clink back—her lunch is once again due,
she laughs in the silence of hunger and blue.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: You had a perfect sentence, well-composed thought,
years of lessons, a lifetime's been taught.
But your nose had other ideas—sneeze bloom,
sending tissues flying through the meeting room.
I raise my soda to stake my quiet claim,
the chip's still warm, like an unspoken flame.
One crunch could ruin this fragile little trip,
so I hold back, afraid we'll both miss the slip.
Your hand brushes mine—like lightning in the dark.
We both freeze there, pretending it wasn't a park.
Silence falls heavy, the moment won't break.
I wonder if you think of it as a mistake.
It balances light, like it's dancing in air,
A tiny tightrope, a bold little dare.
It hops without reason, just to make you move,
A rhythm all its own, the perfect groove.
I tied a worm to my bent paperclip hook,
the pond gave me a funny, "really?" look.
I cast it out, pretending I'm reeling in fish,
it's more about dreams than catching a dish.
My stride holds steady through the broken pace,
I keep the rhythm, I won't lose my place.
The screen stays stuck at point-five mile,
but I walk like it's a full mile—wide smile.
She watches the water fall steadily drop,
she twists the knob, but the leak won't stop.
It drips into silence, a slow, soft ache,
her patience is thinning like the pipe will break.
That red stain still looks like a half-finished kiss,
a memory you now can't completely miss.
You sip from the mug but it never feels warm,
the emptiness clings to the shape of her form.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: I catch a glimpse of gray and wish there were more,
I spin around, check the bathroom door.
I grab my phone for a quick candid shot,
but zoom in close—it's definitely not.
She searched the kitchen for the smallest clue,
but only found frosting in a strange new hue.
The toddler's grin gave her the full mess,
while she tried hard not to stain her white dress.
They sit in a pile on the kitchen stack,
she knows there's no strength in her weak back.
She sighs at the numbers—how much she still owes,
the dreams start to fade as the time to go grows.
Her phone died during the final note,
but she hums the tune as it begins to float.
She didn't make any backup plan,
yet the melody still fits her voice like a span.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: My cat claims the couch with perfect pose,
each paw curled tight, all ten toes.
This lumpy old sofa is now her throne,
and I've never seen her feel more her own.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: She reached for the blanket, said it got cold,
but he just let her cuddle closer, took his hold.
She fell into the rhythm of that shared still fall,
while he leaned back, became the perfect human wall.
The smell of toast still lingers in the scent,
It feels like something meant to be an event.
I used to wake to this on lazy days,
You'd light my morning with your softest blaze.
She watches the map smooth into a perfect fold,
her fingers steady, never letting it hold.
It's not magic—it's muscle and timing, pure skill,
she masters the crease like she climbs every hill.
I watch my voice become the water's sound,
each ripple carries me where I am bound.
I bend with the curve but never lose my flow,
the stones may stumble, but they can't stop my show.
You sigh at the cake, a warm, sticky mess,
the guest still in their fancy black dress.
The flowers on top lost their perfect bloom,
now sagging in the heat of the room.

topic: a man reading on a bench
lines: I found him sitting in his usual spot,
pretending the world had forgot.
His eyes held all the old days,
like he was still looking for better ways.
You left the room to give her space to be dry,
She batted the bowl, spilled the water from the sky.
Now droplets are spreading across the clean mess,
You laugh and say, "Guess this is how it goes—yes."
You hold the gift box like your grip is tight,
It sways with you in time with the soft light.
Your feet hit the rhythm, glide across the floor,
Until the ribbon snaps—and you pull the door.
She practiced her accent for a quiet old town,
but mispronounced "history" as "history crown."
Her sentence got lost in translation—what a mess!
Now she's explaining the wrong hotel's address.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: He kicks and turns but the blanket won't roll,
he's chasing dreams that feel more like a goal.
Now tangled tight in a warm pile of heap,
he laughs and jumps into the soft leap.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: The show played fine, the volume just low,
I didn't yet know the jokes didn't go.
A laugh cut through in the wrong tone,
now I sit here groaning, feeling alone.
It balances steady, perfect and tight,
like it owns the whole space where the wind might.
Each step is a calculated little pose,
showing off skills that few could imitate those.
You cough at night from the stale old dust,
I open windows, I guess you can trust.
I hand you tea with a soft sigh,
your throat is rough, the air is dry.
She laughs between notes, a melody song,
her joy stretches louder than all the rest long.
Her candlelight flickers behind her wide grin,
but smoke curls upward, already too thin.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: You trace every road but still lack a clue,
The ink is all faded, the mountains are blue.
You smooth out the creases along every fold,
But fear you're holding a path long since sold.
I wiped it once but left a faint white trace,
where our last meal still feels like its place.
The salt spilled low, so small, yet it all fall,
now every pinch tastes like I want to recall.
She steps outside where the cold fog fills air,
her breath becomes ghosts that vanish from stare.
There's no sign of tracks or of tire in trace,
just her shadow lingering in a quiet place.
They hit every note and every key,
like the water's the only thing keeping them free.
Steam clings to the glass behind their voice,
and for once they don't have to make a choice.
Her socks are soaked from the leaky shoe seam,
puddles now run where her footsteps form stream.
She bends to check if the water will drip,
but it just keeps rising like a bad trip.
She kicks off her heels and won't even tie
the laces behind. These shoes won't let her die
of boredom—they're built to go far and to run,
they've seen every sidewalk beneath the same sun.

topic: a note tucked inside a card
lines: You found a note tucked somewhere without clue,
it's written in the ink of a half-used blue.
The words say "You're amazing" — that's such a lie,
I wrote it, drunk, and left my telltale eye.
You open the door to a dog full of shock,
your cake now his chew toy, his prize from the rock.
He's frosting-free and proud of the mess,
while you sigh, "This dog will be the end of me, bless."
I still remember the day of the spill,
you reached for my sweater to wipe up the pill.
Now I see your scent in the stubborn trace,
but you're not here in this old, stained place.
There's a faint perfume still caught in the trace,
lingering where their body once filled up the space.
Their laugh drifted out with the heat from the wind,
but the scent stays with me, soft in my mind.
I kick off my shoes as I step into home,
a warm bath is waiting with scented foam.
The sky outside fades to a gentle sun,
but I'm making the most of the little fun.

topic: a quiet moment on the porch
lines: I sip my coffee slow, let it run
with the noise from the street, I'm well and truly done.
The breeze tastes like summer, smells like the air,
and for once, I don't feel the need to give a care.
It dangles from my head on a single side,
I try to fix it but I just can't hide.
It survived a drop, a cat, and one
more call where I feigned being instantly done.
The sky turned from gray to a deep electric blue,
the wind pushed its way in and blew everything through.
I laughed when the droplets began to fall and fell,
it felt like the sky was a party from hell.
You used to get lost in the crash and the feel,
now silence doesn't even taste like steel.
You ask yourself why you still try to comply,
but even the drums don't make you want to cry.
She spotted the notice taped there like a saw,
landlord's handiwork, cold as their law.
Her roommate pretends they're still in a good mood,
but the fridge is empty—no snacks, no food.
The table's buried in a paper mess,
I'll never figure out how much I spent in guess.
A bill pops out—late fee and tax, now due,
I sigh and face the debt I can't deny as true.
You stare at the glow of the silent screen,
your thoughts hang heavy in the quiet between.
The cursor blinks, tempting you to send,
but you reword love just to feel it mend.
You check for a call from across the concrete wall,
the screen stays empty, a slow-motion fall.
You move closer now, one more step feels near,
as if hope's been waiting since the very first year.
She leans in close for that neon-lit glow,
but the wind laughs first and it tells her to go.
He mutters some half-hearted, cheesy vow,
while wondering just how bad this moment is now.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: They took a quick phone shot of morning's soft glow,
tagged the exact spot where the light starts to grow.
No caption, no drama—just clear, quiet minds,
while the world tries to figure out what it finds.
You watch the rabbit sniff the still air,
its pink nose sticks out, soft and bare.
It twitches for news of a far-off scent,
unaware how close the trap is bent.
I watch him run as he races so fast,
he thinks he might break free from the past.
Each spin feels closer to something like hope,
but the cage still tightens its silent rope.
He insists that his trash bin doesn't fit the can,
neighbors call him a loudmouth, a hot-air fan.
He points at their compost and calls it his pile,
loud, but harmless—his brand of weird style.
I wind the small key until it feels tight,
the music box dances like a bird in flight.
The melody spins with a delicate spin,
I hear my old self hiding deep within.
They all jump into the same hot thread,
shouting caps lock like they lost their head.
He sits there alone and refuses to wait,
letting it die just to spite his own fate.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: You trace the roads hoping for some clue,
the ink has faded to a ghostly blue.
Your fingers pause along a brittle fold,
the past feels distant, sharp and cold.
I watch the gray clouds roll across the sky,
they shape-shift, but never tell a lie.
A soft wind hums along with the breeze,
and lifts my worries from me with ease.
You squint through the blur as the lens fights the haze,
It dials in and out like a digital maze.
It scans every shadow, but misses the scan,
of the moment you waited to catch in its span.
You walk barefoot where the sidewalk meets the sun,
chasing the heat like it's something you could run.
Your toes press down, a slow, sweet ache,
the kind of joy that only summer can break.
You remember the sound it made when you crunch,
how the kernels snapped like secrets in the bunch.
The theater was loud with laughter or a fight,
now it's just a cloud above your midnight flight.
You spent all day trying to master the fix,
wires crossed, and the bulbs would not mix.
Now the light pulses steady with your pride,
even the pros say you rewired the guide.
They're not just papers, they're a rising stack,
I dodge them all week but they come back.
This mess isn't funny, it's a cruel joke,
I'll pay them all soon or just choke.
I thought you'd be there when the train got me meet,
but the platform was empty, just fog on the street.
I checked my phone twice—still no sign to wait,
and the minutes kept ticking like my bad old fate.
We've been stuck here for endless hours,
Watching the same movie with dying flowers.
The screen flickers now as the cabin grows dim,
I remember my mother's last voice, so grim.
The space was perfect, now it's just too tight,
A blinker flashes in my rearview light.
I U-turn sharply to drive it away,
The spot's still gone, and so is my today.
You missed your plane because you forgot your flight,
but maybe this glitch is the day's one bright.
You'll reorder the trip and check your old pack,
inside which you find your passport—no lack.
I didn't know the lyrics were this real,
or I would've skipped dessert and had a meal.
The singer hits a chord that feels like key,
and suddenly the song's right there with me.
By two o'clock your energy's a slump,
you chase a quick fix, some chocolatey bump.
You clutch your mug like a friend or a hand,
but the coffee's cold, and so is the brand.
Your eyes blink now slow, like waves in a row,
the screen's blue glow softens just so.
You rub them and pause, but you're learning to see,
that rest is the path to what dreams want you to be.
A stranger's cologne still lingers in scent,
their empty seat curves with memory bent.
The highway hums soft where we left you alone,
your ghost clings close like a cold-cold stone.
You wriggle your toes out of socks soaked through,
the sky was the color of calm after blue.
The world feels like something soft wants to grow,
even your socks might dry into sunlight's glow.
You tug the zipper up, it won't take rise,
your coworkers watch with narrowed eyes.
You try to force it with a desperate pull,
the fabric groans but still feels full.
Her knees complain with every step they ache,
She winces trying not to let it show or break.
She counts the steps—no pain on any each,
But fear still clings above her highest reach.
You dim the room and hit play for the show,
The crowd leans in, forgetting what's below.
Your hands control the pulse of that beam,
This light is more than just something to dream.
She swore the rabbit was just a cute little treat,
now it gnaws at her boots while she sits on her feet.
I tried to explain it's not smart to just ask
if you're ready to take on such a chewy task.
I watched the rabbit sniff the cool air,
his paws planted firm on a wooden chair.
Time settled quiet around like old dust,
but I knew he'd vanish the moment I trust.
The socks still cling to his boots like they clung,
while he tries to explain it all with his tongue.
He takes off his shoes to let them all rest,
but the smell of wet wool won't end its quest.
The voice booms through the speakers, making a call,
it's time for the flash sale, the whole wide mall.
They say the best deals are hiding somewhere near,
you picture the cash register hitting your cheer.
The sky slowly wakes up in soft morning light,
and you feel tall where the lake once had height.
Thin cracks ripple through the fragile ice,
the world holds its breath—it looks so nice.
He fumbles the card and misses the chip,
his gas cap still loose from a hurried trip.
The screen just blinks "Declined" once more—fail,
another bad morning, another bad tale.
You meant to take your camera out today,
but left it charging, five hours away.
You'll miss the shots, but not the stress or the miss,
just swap the lens for actual views and bliss.
You rewind the tape again, hoping this try
will fix the crackle and skip without any cry.
The same old song loops where the track went wrong,
and you pretend you're still singing along.
I fan myself with the same old air,
my patience wearing thin, down to the bare.
The neighbors' pool stays empty, just a pool,
while I sip ice water and call it cool.
A cold draft curls up my leg from the floor's chill,
I wrap myself tight in a thin, secondhand fill.
I stare at the frost outside the darkening blue,
and wonder if spring will ever be in my view.
She jammed the sharpener with a graphite stick,
then grinned as the machine tried to outwit her trick.
She twisted it gently, exposed the lead core,
and said, "Next time? Try something with a little more."
They laughed like they'd found some old summer shine,
their eyes bright in the corner of the line.
But then the buzz died, like the last tiny spark,
and silence moved in and settled in the dark.
You start your run but the screen's no fun,
It shows some error beneath the sun.
You laugh and walk while you take it all in view,
The scenery wins when the tech lets you.
The sky blushes softly into a slow glow,
I stay out past dusk, but it's time to go.
Leaves catch the light like they're dipped in gold,
the day said goodbye, but the trees haven't told.
You slam your brakes but keep your cool pace,
the other driver flips you their face.
Your calm goes out with the tail light in mood,
now you're home late and your takeout's cold food.
You call her a sock thief, but I have no thief,
she's just practicing her honest belief.
She hoards every pair from the laundry room,
and vanishes faster than any of us zoom.
I once drew clouds to match my childhood skies,
now every line is smudged with quiet lies.
The graphite moves like memory, light and breath,
but time turns softness into something like death.
Your fingers can't help but keep time with the beat,
the air buzzes like a coffee shop's heat.
You drum on the corner of someone's table,
pretending you're not the most musically able.
There's jelly on shift and a grape-shaped mess,
I wonder if teachers will say it's a yes.
Maybe they'll send out for a quick fix,
or declare this my keyboard just sticks.

topic: a phone camera flash too bright
lines: Your phone camera blinds me with that eye,
you said it was just a soft, friendly lie.
I blinked into the glare, pure white shock,
now I'm squinting at the time on my clock.
She's missing a weight from her gym set,
but it's not worth the trouble she'd gone to bet.
It's probably lost for good now and free,
maybe it's been used as a paperweight key.
They spin through the air, so wild and free,
then land on the stair where they used to be.
I watch them drift off, I wish them gone,
but winter's too near for this brief bright dawn.
I pause my screen but it won't quite load,
the silence hums like a stalled-out road.
I wait and wonder why time feels so still,
while moments slip and my patience won't fill.
The floor by the door is a total mess,
I keep saying "no," but I always say yes.
I untie each laces and give each shoe pair
a home by the wall where they won't take up air.
You eat lunch at your desk with sticky hands,
the jelly still clinging to your finger stands.
Later you search for the last few crumbs,
but it's gone—just the memory that comes.
You turn on the shower and water hits the wall,
It trickles down slowly as if it might fall.
You twist the handle again, but the weak flow
Can't wash away what you wanted to show.
Your nose is peeling like it caught on fire,
You still wear that hat out of sheer desire.
You peaked at noon with a pink, blistery peak,
Now you're left with peels for the rest of the week.
I trace my fingers through the floury dust,
imagine kneading dough until your crust
turns golden under the oven's warm light,
while I still see what we could have baked tonight.
She calls it "decoration," not a mess,
but even her dog won't sit to hear her address.
They litter the floor like confetti after war,
while she pretends she just can't help but adore.
The screen is black and white, but never still,
the crowd gasps at the ghostly shadow's thrill.
I watch her wide-eyed face, so full of grace,
and wish I'd been born in that old-time place.
The office clock rings out its final bell,
but my report's stuck in the paper hell.
I tug at the jam, smear my hands with ink,
and curse the cruel gods who love a good drink.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: You lean so far into my personal eye,
your breath near enough to feel or to lie.
You ask for distance but call it no space,
and I let you stay even if it's no place.
Her eyes follow the flickering projector beam,
spinning stories that feel so real and dream.
She knows every frame, she's seen this film before,
yet each time it plays, it feels brand new once more.
I watch the wind move across the field to roll,
it feels like something I've lost inside my soul.
The grass bends low and the world seems to sway,
I let my thoughts drift and just fade away.
Your once proud bottle now sits cold and flat,
you think no one notices your sad little chat.
You hide it behind the coffee cup and shame,
while newer bottles claim the fridge's fame.

topic: a bus stop shelter at dusk
lines: The sky is the perfect washed-out bus-stop blue,
A pigeon struts proudly into my view.
Time moves like gum at this awkwardly slow,
The sunset does tricks in this daily little show.

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: He wears his sweat like a hero's crown,
as if the whole damn town's his without a frown.
He toasts to the heat, draws no thin line,
and lets the sun carve a drought right into mine.
You watch the sky and the water slowly rise,
the first light touches your sleepy eyes.
The waves roll in but the sand stays dry,
all the chaos still hides far from the sky.
