The coins drop softly into the jar with a clink,
she double-checks each one, careful not to think.
Her fingers tremble while adding up the sum,
but she won't ask for help—just let the math come.
I swear the knob was set for something more than wrong,
now I'm watching the pot go cold all day long.
It's barely enough to even call it heat,
this "low" setting sure feels like a repeat.

topic: ice forming on the car windshield
lines: I press my face against the cold glass of breath,
the frost spreads slow like a ghost of death.
It etches designs that feel like a claw,
as if the weather breaks every known law.

topic: a coffee cup on the curb
lines: She found your coffee cup left out in the cold,
a chipped mug from some place you both once told.
It still has her initials carved into the name,
the one she never used but kept the very same.
She scoured the house, each corner she knew, each room,
the missing pages still hanging over her gloom.
There's not a single scrap, a hint, or a trace,
just echoes of study nights in that old place.
My fingers fall where they always have been to use,
the keys are smooth where my thumb knows to bruise.
I trace the letters now faded from daily race,
and smile at the love etched into this strange place.
She glows with focus, her screen time a shine,
Her fingers don't pause for a rub or a sign.
She cracks every bug in her world's dark code,
But her eyes burn in a dry, digital mode.
I hear a bicycle bell echo the street,
its rhythm so simple, it feels like a repeat.
I smile as the sound mixes with the hum
of memories that somehow still manage to come.
She climbs up the hill where the wind cuts so high,
her hair filled with light from the wide open sky.
The feathers catch sun and begin to show,
while the forest just stares in a daze far below.
My dog puts on his daily barky little show,
He's sure he'll get some praise from me when I know.
I sigh but clap—because he won't let up for time,
It's not heroic, more like a neighborhood crime.
Her cursor blinks slow in the screen's blue haze,
she tries to remember the old, good days.
She types in all caps, like a drunkard's glass,
and wonders if he still trims the front yard grass.
I had a great idea, or so I thought,
now my brain aches as if it got caught.
There's static inside, like a splintered crack,
I'll lie down and pray my head turns back.
You drop the ball, and the yarn hits the floor,
Now your cat starts tugging the strands for war.
You chase it through the house, yell "Clean this room!"
It ends up tangled—no craft will bloom.
I hold the tuning fork close to the air,
its metal cool against my skin, so bare.
There's a soft hum that starts in my thumb,
and I let the sound slowly drift where it come.
I glance at my phone, feel the ache of alone,
it's silent with no new message or tone.
The group chat still lives in this digital room,
but no one replies, so I leave it and zoom.
She got her monthly phone bill as a shock,
Some unknown numbers on the usage block.
She laughs at the cost, makes a funny call,
Then clicks the screenshot, sends it out to sprawl.
They walked right into the puddle's slick,
too caught up to notice the weather's quick.
Water seeps through the tread of their trail,
their socks now stained a damp shade of pale.

topic: hot chocolate on a cold day
lines: I sip my cocoa as the wind chills the day,
a clock ticks somewhere, time melting away.
The mug exhales in soft curls of steam,
and for a moment I'm back in the dream.
She used to dance like the floor was a spin,
her rhythm so smooth, it could shake every skin.
These days she stands still, like she's lost the move,
but pride keeps her still—not because she can't groove.
My brain went offline again this morning,
It's like a train that left without warning.
You asked me twice now—still no clue,
I'm sorry, pal, but I don't know you.
They painted the wall with words that look like art,
each mark a rebellion from their secret heart.
A name, a logo, a clever little tag,
the wall now shimmers like a rainbow drag.

topic: a friend who is always late
lines: Your friend has been late with no rhyme or time,
It's more than a habit, it's a social crime.
You say you'll cancel, but you still wait on date,
Like maybe your patience is just not your fate.
She zipped through traffic without brake or dash,
the meter spun red while she sang off-key cash.
Her taillights were dead but her smile had such beam,
I thought she was driving straight out of a dream.
You pick it up only to nearly bend,
the links whisper secrets from a long-lost friend.
It coils along the table's farthest stretch,
but you keep it close, won't let anyone fetch.
I pressed repeat, but it skipped the whole play,
the silence felt longer than any delay.
I rewound it, but it played the song wrong,
so I sang it myself, all the way along.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: She clipped the coupon to feel like she save,
but the gummy bears still made her crave.
A dollar off now, she tells herself it's okay—
later, her teeth will thank her, maybe not today.
You watch the sky bleed color into the rise,
the kind of view that steals your breath with its eyes.
The lake is frozen, smooth as a sheet of glass,
untouched by tracks or the hint of a grass.
I read every label, check each long list,
hoping for something I might not have missed.
My body told me long ago what it knew,
but science put it all in a prettier clue.
A cart sits stuck in the middle of the cart,
some shopper gave it a grocery heart.
They taped a note that says "Don't move my way,"
the sign is dated—December 30th, today.
I found the sandwich stuck in one tight spot,
the bread had started to sag and rot.
That lunch I packed for a perfect picnic lunch
is now a sad, forgotten cold meat bunch.
The bird hops along the rod my way,
squinting like it owns the whole day.
It's clearly heading toward the end,
but takes a detour round the bend.
She lifts her face to the pale winter sky,
the wind comes sweeping past her ear and by.
It steals the warmth from her whispered breath,
but she laughs at the chill, dancing with death.
It bounces across the room to roll,
half full once, now lifeless as a soul.
She leaves it alone, lets it sit still,
but time won't refill what the thirst won't fill.
You watched the cup tilt and began to ring,
a slow-motion spill, the coziest thing.
You knew this was destined, some kind of fate,
a stain on your laptop you're calling a date.
She kicks the door like it's her own to blame,
her heel still caught in the old rusted frame.
The knob gives a wobble, a slow sad spin,
and now she's humming—this will have to begin.
She stands there proud in her soggy new pose,
raindrops still clinging to every single clothes.
She took a big step but it felt more like a leap,
now her poor socks are a wet, wrinkled heap.
You hit "send" before you read the post,
Now the teacher's name haunts you like a ghost.
It was written in advance—it's your bad fate,
They'll all ask why *you* had to debate.
They toss a chair and toss a sheet over the hook,
the kid gives the scene a proud, critical look.
The fort's just built—it calls for a quick nap,
or maybe a raid on snacks from the pantry's trap.
He tosses the crumbs to the birds on the ground,
they follow his rhythm, a beat he has found.
He doesn't know theirs, won't give them his name,
but feeds them the peace he can't seem to claim.
Static fills the silence, my playlist isn't clear,
I twist the knob but there's nothing for my ear.
The stations drop every time I go a mile,
I sing to myself or drive in this while.
I slide my last dollar into the take,
the machine just hums, won't even break.
I check the coin return, still no cap,
it's swallowed my cash like a greedy trap.
She holds her breath, the spoon now in pause,
afraid to move it, afraid of the cause.
A single bead begins to drip,
slow as a tear, slipping from her grip.
I asked for an inch but they took up the space,
leaning back with their chin on my face.
Their shoes are half off and their toes brush my feet,
so I move to the next one and claim a new seat.
They stuck the poster there without much air,
just crumpled edges and a smudge of hair.
But when the sunlight hits the colorful light,
it frames the mess in something that feels tight.
I've swept the living room three times since floor,
checked every pocket by the front door.
Where are they? I can't afford to miss,
my hands shake, I can't even lock this.
The crickets have started their loud little talk,
I swear they're rehearsing a chorus down the walk.
They think they're the stars of some summertime show,
but I just pretend like I don't really know.
She wakes before light with the birds in the sky,
Their songs wake her spirit, a gentle cry.
She drinks her first coffee as morning sun
turns dew into gold where the wind used to run.
The honey runs thick, a river of gold,
I lift the spoon slowly, don't want to hold.
Let it drip down in time, let it be slow,
your smile does the same, a warmth that will glow.
I watch the bulb struggle to stave off old age,
it trembles now, like a bird in its cage.
Its warm, uneven light is the only glow
that reminds me of how things used to be ago.

topic: a cart with a broken wheel
lines: She pushes the cart, one wheel won't run,
the grocery list wilts under a gray sun.
A tired sigh lifts with the wind's soft sigh,
her dreams still floating somewhere in the sky.
She fumbles the lock but can't find her key,
the handle won't budge and the hinges won't free.
Her date's waiting outside in the hallway's dim room,
she thinks of the hour slipping away like gloom.
You've signed so much paper they lost your form,
Your visits are regular as April's storm.
They hand you new pills that all taste the same,
Just different names trying to fill the blame.
I spilled coffee and turned my keyboard to paste,
it's a tech disaster, but what a waste.
I won't play the victim or assign blame,
I'll type with two fingers and call it a game.

topic: crackling fireplace on a winter night
lines: I toss another log into the throw,
the flames dance wildly a little below.
A spark leaps up and lights the dark,
the shadows laugh as the room turns bright and stark.
I used to love the chaos of the stage,
the kind that makes your ears feel like a cage.
Now silence calls like an old friend who won't fade,
and loud music feels like something I can't shade.
You watch the steam curl into thin air,
where memories float and are never quite there.
The kettle still hums but it's gone out of boil,
like time on your hands, slow and low as oil.
They flicker like secrets that barely glow,
She runs through the yard, but they never will go.
Her laughter is brighter than their weak little light,
And maybe, just maybe, she'll catch one tonight.
You left the wifi code on a yellowing spot,
somewhere near the fridge where you often forgot.
It's stuck under a jar label with old tape,
just waiting for someone to find it and escape.
She double-taps with a lazy little thumb,
no time to think—her reaction just come.
The like appears in a friend's scrolling view,
but no reply ever makes it back to you.
You scan the room but there's no empty seat,
The air is thick and there's no escape from the heat.
You check your phone—no reception at all,
You try to focus, but your hope begins to fall.
You tilt your face toward the metal bend,
where water drips from the broken end.
I hand you my book to pass the time you read,
while pigeons squabble in the rain we feed.

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: It drips like wax from a summer's old flame,
we laughed as we mopped in the hot, worn-out game.
That sweat on my skin was a language we knew,
a code only July could get inside me too.

topic: losing your wallet at the mall
lines: He left his wallet by the food court at the mall,
and now he's stuck with a lost-and-found call.
Debit card? ID? Keys? All gone, just like that card,
though someone might be waiting with it in their yard.
I check the forecast — clear blue air,
we spread out our blankets, we grab a chair.
The clouds roll in fast, they cut off the shine,
but we dance through the rain — my perfect design.
They run through the field in pure chase,
A daisy-cloaked place, their wild face.
A dragonfly flutters above its own wing,
The net twirls and the grass gives a spring.
Her fingers are raw from the garlic's thin skin,
the cloves reveal layers we cannot within.
She crushes them slowly, fills the air with scent,
her knuckles are bent but she does not resent.
It buzzes again, but there's no one to call,
just silence and sun where the glasses were tall.
Their watch still keeps ticking, a steady old beat,
while their hands hold nothing but quiet and heat.
He gives the dented plate a proud hum,
"This wasn't perfect—so it just has to come."
It's bent but still solid, he won't let it bend,
to him, it's a relic, a loyal old friend.

topic: a bike locked to a pole
lines: She leans her bike toward the warmest sun,
planning to run when the morning's done.
The sky stretches wide in a calm, bright blue,
and she takes it all in from the perfect view.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: They scrolled through your feed from a distant past,
but only paused for this old photo blast.
They tapped that little heart on your gallery art,
like it meant something, not just a quick heart.

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: You twist it around but it won't hold your tries,
the one that still works is used just for ties.
It's stiff and too thin, barely keeping things tight,
but you won't let it go—it still holds what it might.
The snowflakes fall and cling to her cold,
fragile diamonds she can't seem to hold.
They shimmer briefly before they melt,
sliding down her coat like time at the belt.
You stare into the dark and empty brew,
your thoughts too bitter even for a chew.
Your hands won't stop their nervous shake,
you wonder if this is the worst mistake.
You don't remember the party or event,
Just the way the colors got tangled and bent.
You run your hands through your messy hair,
And flake from the past rains down in despair.
She taps the handle, shakes it with her head,
the bristles still stained from last night's red.
There's no room left for her in this small space,
but she won't leave until it's her final place.
Their movie's frozen with a hazy view,
They mutter complaints, all of them stuck in a stew.
They jostle the device, but there's no real fix,
A bad night out becomes a sour mix.
The glue stick cracked like an old rubber band,
She pried it open with a careful hand.
The notes still cling to the corner of the page,
Like memories trapped in a fragile cage.
I toss a coin in, but the machine won't take,
it spits out my change like it sensed it was fake.
It honed in on every worn edge of my dime,
I guess I should've learned how to save my time.
I saw your face pop up on my old phone,
and sat there holding it, feeling alone.
The cloud sync messed up, and memories mix—
I tap to delete, but never quite fix.
You leave your shoes neatly aligned over there,
they smell like fresh roses and clean-cut air.
You walk all day long in them, proud and out,
but always return, no debate, no doubt.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: She grabs a bag of chips off the checkout treat,
the clerk sighs and swipes it again for repeat.
The discount feels good but it won't fill the room
where smart choices whisper and bad ones loom.
The sun slides slowly past the tallest tree down,
while cars blink on like stars in this quiet town.
It paints the branches in a gold and rusted flame,
and for a moment, even time forgets my name.
You blow your hopes into soap and the sky,
Each puff a quiet, soft-laced try.
The bubbles are fragile, yet they hold your dream,
Like thoughts that float up a glistening stream.
Her fingers know the keys by their edge,
they tap out stories without a pledge.
Now E and T have faded to ghost,
yet she still types, this is what she holds most.
The dog keeps the same old impatient pace,
it sounds like it's pacing outside my place.
Maybe it howls at the full bright moon,
but I'd swear it's just singing to my tune.
She stops to watch the clouds turn the sky to blue,
the heat gives way to a breeze that blows through.
Her face lights up as lightning cracks the sky,
she smiles at the rain before it gets too dry.
She buckles in calm beside that loud plane,
her book a cool shield in the seat-back tray chain.
No screens or noise can break that quiet reach,
she masters the sky with no need for speech.
I left it there where the fruit bowl once went,
its peel now crinkled, soft, slightly bent.
It doesn't look like much anymore, this fruit—
but its musk still fits a warm, old nostalgia suit.
She slept like a rock but forgot where her bed
was when she woke—her pillow hugged her head.
Now she tries to stretch in a stiff yoga pose,
while her cat judges her off-balance clothes.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: I use the coupon to feel a little save,
pretending I'm doing something brave.
But when I read the tiny-printed cost,
my stomach freezes with unease like frost.
You blast the radio wide open to the sky,
the wind tugs your hair into a wild fly.
Words fall out loud—half curse, half scream,
the road's your stage, the world your dream.
She ignores the voice that says take this path,
her gut knows better than some fancy math.
The road curves sharp and the GPS yells ahead,
but she keeps going where her map never led.

topic: a forgotten lunchbox on the floor
lines: You spot your lunchbox beneath the desk's tight sight,
Its lid is sealed but the string still feels tight.
You laugh and give it a gentle call,
Maybe tomorrow it'll have food for us all.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: You turned the key and the door gave way to the lock,
the room was empty but for the old man's stock.
Your pulse ran fast as you held your breath,
the silence felt thick, like a shadow or death.
She cracks the code when the video feed
drops out again for the tenth time indeed.
Her calm stays steady, no panic, no flex,
just notes from her desk—no need for a vex.
She says your style would never quite fit,
but you argue it's not a lack of grit.
She tries your boots, then changes her mind,
but not before tripping a little bit blind.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: I check my follower count right in my head,
the number spreads across my face instead.
It's the exact same number—surprise, same!
No growth, no glory, just a frozen name.
The screen glows bright from this sudden loud,
A storm of alerts from my messages cloud.
I swear I just swiped off that blinking tap,
But silence remains a cruel midnight trap.

topic: restaurant with no menu in English
lines: I've got no clue what any dish might be,
the menu's locked in Chinese script—no key.
I point at something just to make it taste
like home, and hope it doesn't turn to waste.

topic: a quiet moment on the porch
lines: She sits alone in her usual chair,
a soft breeze lifting the humid air.
Her fingers trace the gold of the light,
but she knows the hour is not quite right.
A brown stain spreads across my laptop mess,
I scream inside and curse this coffee stress.
The screen begins to glitch, colors won't fade,
My face blurs out like a tragic movie parade.

topic: socks left in the laundry pile
lines: A single sock rests alone on the floor,
it's been there since last week's unmet chore.
You swear you'll find its match when you know,
but it never seems to come or to go.
I left my gym locker wide open at the door,
now everyone's talking, spreading locker room lore.
They found a sock, a receipt, and some old trash,
the coach just laughed and said, "Update your dash."
That faded poster hangs crooked in its frame,
It still shouts your name, it still feels the same.
The room is quiet, but the air's so cold,
I leave it there, as if that makes me bold.
The shovel goes up where the frost runs deep,
It kicks a small chunk of ice into heap.
The morning moves slow, no thaw in the snow,
The ground won't budge yet—will it ever show?
You swear you'll replace those batteries now,
but your frown stays deep furrowed on your brow.
The remote makes a faint wheezing hum,
begging you not to let the old ones come.
She pried open the drawer looking for a find,
all she got was a ball of headphone wind.
There was no order, no pattern, no clue—
just chaos coiled neatly from ear to view.
She stares at the bars of her tiny cage,
her paws twitching with silent, caged rage.
She runs but the wheel never lets her spin,
chasing nothing just to stay within.
She arrives early and picks the best seat,
the coffee goes cold in her plastic heat.
Her eyes scan the door—she's about to miss
the moment when he forgot about this.
I rub the rail like a calloused old thumb,
my fingers comb through the mess they have become.
I can still feel your tiny hand, small and child,
how we gripped the same place, stubborn and wild.
She's hours past lights out but still draws her hour,
the fridge hums soft as a midnight power.
She sips lukewarm tea by the pale moon,
and hums some old show's familiar tune.
She checks off the first task—now only one is done,
while outside the light fades and the day's sun
slips through her fingers like a half-made list,
where dreams are crossed out but still haunt her mist.
You blast through the silence so early and loud,
Designed to be heard and to never be proud.
You shout as the sun tries to coax me to rise,
Your red digits are blazing right into my eyes.
You thought you had a cold but it's not the time,
now every clinic chimes with your name and dime.
They send you tests, new drugs, and a final bill,
the only thing they all agree on is the pill.
That treadmill still makes a goddamn scream,
My fitness dream feels more like a scheme.
I can't take this noise—how do you plan to stop?
Even yoga videos suggest to crop.

topic: a child's drawings on the fridge
lines: She claims these stick-ons are her royal crown,
each doodle declares this is her whole town.
I watch as she carefully tries to peel
the tape off a dinosaur that isn't real.
Her nose is still bright from the sun's tight red,
the kids had bets on how far it would spread.
We watched her walk up the steep path to hill,
her laugh was warm, but the burn gave a chill.
They visit specialists with hopeful reason,
keeping appointments like a fresh season.
I bring coffee, sit beside them late,
watching time and treatment add more weight.
My chicken grows cold while I text her a bite,
the screen's my new flame as the candle burns light.
I wait for a reply to appease this feed,
my phone is my god and I'll worship it with greed.
They still sit by the door, a pair to show,
though the feet they held are long ago.
Not a single sole leaves a mark or trace,
yet I leave them there in this their place.
It sits there so still, the only one alone,
like a featherless ghost on a cold, thin stone.
One gust could send feathers or shadow to fall,
but it stays where it is, away from them all.
The steam curls up from the rim like a ghostly steam,
It carries the scent of your quietest dream.
Her hands close gently around the mug's warm,
a small act of joy taking shape in its form.
She thinks she's hunting something worth her play,
leaping through the sunbeams all day.
There's nothing there but light and doubt,
yet she spins around in circles, full about.
You zoom through your cage with a frantic dash,
your eyes full of dreams and a tiny rodent's flash.
The wheel spins so fast, it hums like a din,
you think you're escaping the wheel inside your skin.
You step into the room and sniff the stale air,
The walls feel cheap, the soap lies too bare.
Some disinfectant, but it hides what's not true—
This scent won't leave you, and neither will you.
A single bright color makes a happy spot,
the artist forgot to wipe their hand from the pot.
Drips form a pattern, wild and free, a swirl,
the little girl laughs and says, "Look! That's art, a girl!"
My kid runs wild through the bubble-filled sky,
shouting "Mine! Mine!" as they float on by.
He twirls so fast he nearly falls in spin,
his tiny hands grab nothing but the wind within.
The tire lets out a sad little pop,
he skids to a sudden, dusty stop.
He tries to push it along like it'll roll,
but the weight of his shame is a heavy toll.
I tried to use the snowflakes as proof
that heaven had forgotten the rules of a roof.
But they just melted and left a soft drip,
ruining my coat—what a clumsy trip.
A stranger offers her umbrella to the rain,
holding tight so both of you may remain.
She says something kind, it slips past your heart,
and for once, the storm doesn't feel like a part.
She edits until the pixels reshape her face,
blurring the past where she wants to erase.
A soft filter gives her skin a holy glow,
but her eyes still reveal what the app can't know.
A man yells about his ex into thin air,
I inch toward the stair to escape his flair.
"We were doomed from the start," he shouts about their date,
I wonder if mine's next—my own bad fate.
My phone says "battery low" and won't let me go,
it's frozen mid-scroll with a blinking red glow.
I don't need the whole wall to tell me what's wrong—
just plug me in, friend, and we can sing along.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: You swear the thing pulses with inner glow,
something carved from the bedrock below.
It fits your palm like it's been your mine,
but no one told you this ancient design.
I cast each toy in its perfect role,
they charge through battles, no time for coal.
I built a cardboard city on the stage,
and wrote my epic way into their age.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: She watches the first light catch the web's bright gleam,
each thread a tremor along its fragile seam.
The spider hides still, somewhere far away she waits,
as morning cracks open and lets the world in gates.
I stir the pot where the steam meets the air,
I settle back into my kitchen chair.
This broth feels like a promise to stay warm,
outside the wind howls but I'm safe from the storm.
I clicked the button to cancel the card,
now I'm sweating and gripping my mouse too hard.
The screen says "Are you sure?" like a cruel wave,
and I wonder if I'll ever feel brave.
She checks the package for the perfect tear,
then seals the cheese in a vacuum of air.
The foil won't stick—her hands can't keep the grip,
she stumbles back with a clumsy little trip.

topic: socks left in the break room
lines: You're hunting for a sock—it's your last pair,
they're folded neatly in someone else's air.
A single sock on the chair gives you a clue,
you kick off yours and laugh, "I match this shoe."
She digs through a box like she's searching for a clue,
resurrects a sweater from last year's woolen brew.
The vintage jeans fit tight but they still have her flow,
the crowd stares and whispers—she owns the whole show.
She watched it all happen from crust to the bread,
ketchup still dripping from every spread.
The pigeon flew off like an old friend from sky,
she laughed, though she couldn't explain why.
I let it dangle for the world to show,
my spoon suspended just a hair too slow.
One perfect bead begins its tiny drip,
I hold my breath and never lose my grip.
You pretend it's a gesture for sharing your meal,
but everyone knows it's not all that real.
You take two or three from their half-empty plate,
and grin like this counts as a dinner date.
She left a glittery cupcake mess,
and gave her dog a shake-off "just say yes."
Now sprinkles stick where the dog hit the floor,
but she's too busy snorting to do a chore.
You count the heads but there's no empty seat,
the AC wheezes through the stifling heat.
You strike a pose, sit tall, take your whole row,
and grin like you invented this lecture show.
You push your pencil deep into the lead,
expecting shavings like fresh-cut bread.
The blade refuses to do more than spin,
and dust collects where the wood used to grin.
You never saw the semi coming in your wave,
eyes glued to your phone, too late to be brave.
Its horn blasts loud as you hold up the tail,
while messages buzz with no one left in your trail.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: The screen goes black, no signal, just a void,
my Netflix queue now unemployed.
I pace the house, pretending it's going slow,
but every room feels empty without the show.
She craves that bitter, calming cup of heat,
replays her morning in the same old repeat.
She watches the rising, slow-moving steam,
but it's just hot water, never her dream.
We left the theater down the empty hall,
no one dared to be the first to call.
The credits rolled but we stood there to fade,
pretending the silence was a quiet parade.
I don't apologize for the jelly-bread mess,
you'll have to forgive me for the sugary guess.
My fingers are stuck like they've been dipped in glue,
but maybe it's worth it for the snack I could do.
You've looked every corner, the key isn't round,
You text "lost key?" with a voice that's quite found.
A stranger stops by, they offer a pass,
It turns out your key was in the neighbor's grass.
She tugs so hard she might snap the lead,
her eyes say *please* and her tail says *head*.
I let her sprint until the path is run,
then stop for treats as the light grows sun.
I sprinted through the storm to save my shoes,
but got drenched anyway—there's no good excuse.
The sidewalk glistens, gray and cold as a mist,
I add "dry socks" to my never-ending list.
My backpack hits the floor but I still miss the door,
the bus was late, the traffic's got some more.
I sprint through the halls with a few seconds to pass,
the teacher slams the clock—here's my late to class.
She winces when she walks through the pain,
though it's milder now than it was again.
Her knees still creak like old floorboard bones,
but her laugh rings warm in familiar tones.
My phone rings like a clock tower's old bell,
but I let it go straight to voicemail well.
They'll think I'm ignoring or out of the miss—
I'm just here lying in sleepy bliss.
You used to love the chaos, the loud and the hush,
how noise would paint your face like a fevered flush.
Now silence feels faster, the calm kind of slow,
where music sits softly, just a little below.
I slipped into your shoes to see how they fit,
but I missed a few steps and lost every bit.
You laughed while I stumbled, no clue what to do,
"Next time," you said, "just stick to your you."
They crouch to inspect the old tree's fallen crown,
soft moss cradles the cone all curled and brown.
They trace where the forest chooses to let things lie,
and whisper to earth what the wind tells the sky.
I tried to steady myself but lost my grip,
my shoe caught the edge of the slick, low trip.
There's gum on the rail, a messy smear,
I'm clinging to nothing but air so near.

topic: steaming coffee in a blue mug
lines: I need this cold brew, not this hot, bitter heat,
the steam burns my lips as I fight through the street.
It's weak from bad grounds, I'll never get brew,
the barista's T-shirt blocks the only view.
He checks the mailbox, finds a stack of bill,
no thrill at all when they arrive so still.
One's marked "overdue," the rest are just due,
he mutters under his breath and starts to stew.
A scooter zips by like it's late for a ride,
I step off the curb just to play it safe and hide.
Up pops the rider, head down in their hood,
no time for waves—just one-way, full-speed good.
You drag the couch toward the middle of the room,
while your little brother insists he should zoom.
We argue whose turn it is to stay inside,
until we both get lost in the blanket hide.
The sky was so clear, now it's turning to blue,
lightning cracks softly where the air breaks through.
She watches the pavement dissolve into rain,
her shoes soaked from walking the same path again.
You leave a pink streak where your lips once knew,
It clings to the mug like a kiss in reverse glue.
You smile at the mark, call it your lucky date,
And drink from it anyway—some mess is your fate.
You hear the ring echoing down the trail,
like a signal you've missed in your daily mail.
You grip the handlebars and you pedal so fast,
but the rider has vanished, already passed.
You chased your dreams through the long green past,
the net swayed high but it couldn't last.
You'd pause to trace clouds in the wide blue sky,
and wonder why you ever let it fly.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: I see a lone hair, a gray in the strand,
is this the first sign I need a new brand?
I count my years but try not to age,
yet here it grows—my beauty's first stage.
You found a loaf with a sour old stank,
it sat in the bin on a wooden plank.
You used to toast it for morning's first glow,
now it's just memories with nowhere to go.

topic: missing a chorus in a song
lines: You hit "play" once more, hoping it will repeat,
but the chorus won't come back, rising heat.
You press the controls again, begging it to play,
but the song just skips on, love carried away.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: You stand there alone with the fragile flame,
the shadows all whisper your old name.
The wind tries to steal it but you won't let it drift,
you raise it higher and hold it up to lift.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: You blow hard, trying to end this whole year,
the smoke curls up like your mind's not so clear.
There's a flicker left in the cake's last fire,
but you laugh anyway—closeness is desire.
You kick off your shoes for the old backyard games,
calling out neighborhood friends by their names.
Laughter echoes down the wooden slide,
where only kid-time could've pulled it to your side.
My knitting needles are too busy for plot,
I've already unraveled what I've got.
Let someone else claim control of their fate—
I'm right here, slow stitching, and I'll make you wait.
Your hand brushes mine — I feel a spark,
We both pull back, pretend it never was dark.
Words fail me now, my mind fills with heat,
I smile too wide, and quickly meet defeat.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: She taps her phone, the light turns on the screen,
a quiet midnight habit, routine, routine.
Her fingers hover where the money looks cheap,
she sighs, then tucks the device under her sleep.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: You read your name and are pulled back to the past,
a photo, a post, a memory in the blast.
You follow the thread of what once was said,
but now all you want is time far ahead.
The dog goes around in a dizzying spin,
it's been doing this every time things begin.
It paces the room with a wild, fast pace,
its eyes locked on its own twisted face.
That kid rings his bell with such sharp tone,
It vibrates through my skull down to every bone.
I wasn't even in his way to pass,
But he rang like I'd failed some midlife class.
There it is again—taunting you from the door,
some expired flier from a long-gone store.
You've never called it beautiful or art,
but every time it cracks your sternest heart.
I thought this meeting was worth another chance,
the same old script we once tried to dance.
You still call me by my full first name,
but neither of us can pretend it's a flame.
You stare at the dent in your weight plate's dent,
it's slightly bent but still holds what you lent.
It's quirky, for sure—a weird kind of proof,
that strength doesn't need a perfect steel roof.
You tried to outrun the storm but still it bend,
now your broken ribs lie uselessly, friend.
The sky keeps coming down in sheets of rain,
while you stand useless, splintered to remain.

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: A one-star review just popped up on the post,
the barista now looks like the worst ever host.
The comments are flooding in fast and too near,
I check my screen hoping it's all not so clear.
I call it a snack, though it's barely a snack,
I took half your fries right from off your back.
It wasn't a theft, was more like a grab,
but you're giving me side-eye, love — no need to crab.
You saw it—empty, close, and perfectly near,
your radio static still buzzing in your ear.
You hit the brake too late to turn so wide,
now it's someone else's car blocking the inside.
A baby screams through the thin air,
Her tears are all she has to spare.
The man beside me tries not to be loud,
While backseat blues hang thick as a cloud.
The coupon's date has finally met its date,
ten bucks off coffee—now lost to fate.
He'll sip from his mug without a mint,
the offer faded from the printed print.
You stood there, staring as if out of a scene,
"Do we know each other?" you broke the routine.
I said my name, which you let it just slip,
like memory's a language you never could grip.
He scurries around, obsessed with his nuts,
darting through leaves without any cuts.
He pats the soft dirt down over the spot,
but later he digs up what he forgot.
You click "Buy Now" without even thinking it bought,
Later you question if it was worth the thought.
The box arrives as some strange, silent gift,
Unopened, it gathers slow-moving dust drift.
You follow the ants where they like to lead,
down paths carved from crumbs and torn-up bread.
The sidewalk looks like an ancient maze,
though it took them just minutes, not hours or days.
You call him a beast, but he's your favorite beast,
he's drooled across your couch like a messy feast.
You won't let anyone touch the stained spot,
you just smile and say "this is his blot."
She stands there shaking with fever and class,
her voice tries to rise above cough and pass.
I hear every breath she can't hide or ache,
but even through pain, she won't take a break.
I crack an egg into the bowl with care,
golden yolk sitting like something rare.
Whisk it into a foam with a quick swirl,
even the kitchen feels like a happy girl.
The screen's soft blue glow won't let me go,
I'm watching another highlight reel show.
I swear I'll put it down and head to bed,
but scrolling feels better than falling asleep, dead.
His tail is stiff and his posture is alert,
convinced he's heard something just outside the dirt.
There's no bird, wind, or package — not a single clue,
but he barks at ghosts only he can you.
He stands at the gate where the machine's out of spot,
his phone's locked away—he must've forgot.
He waves at a guard and asks for the fare,
and pays with a sigh and an awkward air.
I need just a moment of stillness to rest,
my head fits so perfectly on your chest.
the noise of the day drifts away from my mind,
your breath slows like waves on a quiet wind.

topic: finding a five in the couch
lines: I found a crumpled dollar under the coin,
the change from some old movie we used to join.
I toss it on my lap and stretch my leg,
pretending it's a bet I still might beg.
My dog can't wait to be the first to dash,
she's earned it—no amount of treats will cash.
Her nose is pressed against the cold [door],
and barks until the walk turns into [more].
That cat has claimed the suitcase handle as top,
She curls around zippers and corners and stop.
Her breathing is soft in the stillness of fur,
It makes me pack slow, her small weight my spur.
The stack of letters is thick and due,
and you wonder if you can even do.
Every envelope feels like a dark thought,
not something you earned but something you bought.
You keep the peas in a plastic bag that gleam,
they're your midnight snack, your guilty little dream.
They sit in the fridge in perfect straight row,
but you'll never let anyone else ones go.
I used to think I could bend and stretch,
now even reaching the door feels fetch.
My muscles scream for a better tone,
each rep turns into a deep, loud groan.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: She counts her years like treasures in the age,
each wrinkle shows she's lived through every stage.
The mirror shows a face she can't erase,
and she likes where the gray has found its place.
I blow too hard, they all lift from my head,
they twist in the wind and they drift far and spread.
They vanish into the gray winter sky,
I never could keep what grew wild and why.
You hit repeat but it skipped to the wrong,
the track you wanted played just doesn't come along.
You pause and queue it, take a quick chance,
then laugh and pretend you were waiting to dance.
The tile feels too smooth and completely slick,
There's soap on the drain, like some cruel little trick.
I reach out for the wall but my toes lose their grip,
I nearly go flying — just a hair from the trip.
They fall into step but keep a lazy pace,
both staring straight ahead, no grin on their face.
One texts nonstop, the other counts the block,
neither mentions the silence—like they're in a shock.
You open the fridge door and reach for the bag,
but the peas are stuck inside, they won't snag.
You give the container a hard little pop,
the peas go flying—now the mess won't stop.
I clap at the jokes they all laugh the wrong,
but nobody minds if I don't clap along.
The crowd's loud and happy, their approval's a cheer,
while mine stays my own private cinema near.
You heard the toaster make a startled pop,
the kind that burns a slice to charred crop.
You pause your morning coffee mid-brew,
now staring at the blackened demise in your view.
I watch them dance but they never stay,
they float and they twist and they drift away.
I used to think they knew where they go,
now I wonder if they don't even know.
The carton's been sitting past drink-by date,
but you still hope it won't turn out your fate.
Now you're staring at clumps of green mold,
and whispering, "This milk's definitely old."
I search for the remote but there's no clues,
the void where it should be fills me with blues.
I check my usual spots—no help, no place,
now the couch feels empty, like an unused space.
The burner's been cold, I need some flame,
I twist the old knob labeled your name.
It hisses so loud but it stays on low,
this thing won't budge, and neither will it go.
That burner's been hissing with nothing to glow,
a ghost of a flame barely wants to grow.
You wait for a crackle or pop or some hum,
but the heat never arrives — it won't come.
My coffee went flying and now it's on the floor,
I really do not need this happening some more.
It left a stain like a wet dark ring,
the worst part is this is such a stupid thing.
You loved the glow it gave your bare skin,
even if it faded uneven within.
Now there's a soft gold stripe down your left mark,
a tiny flaw that somehow feels too dark.

topic: a long queue at the coffee shop
lines: She's been waiting since the first counter at the bar,
sipping her oat milk out of a jam jar.
Her hair is up in a loose messy cap,
but she doesn't care if it's a style trap.
She grabs her keys and slams the front door,
says she doesn't need this anymore.
She walks into the silence of fresh air,
not looking back—no sign she'll stay or care.
She taps her foot, there's a full five-minute delay,
Her bus was close but now it feels so far away.
She checks the app—same old incorrect route,
She sighs and whispers an angry shout.
You look up once more, the clouds chase the sky,
pretending the world isn't passing you by.
Time moves like the wind, it won't let you pass,
and the breeze whispers truths through the tired grass.
She orders way more than she can eat fast,
her cart full of snacks from ten places past.
She pays with a card, no need for old cash,
then waits in her chair for the whole thing to dash.
You study the words but they won't seem to flow,
Your tongue trips on phrases you don't yet know.
You laugh it all out, then try once more out,
and slowly begin to lose every doubt.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: I found it lodged where the fabric frayed there,
between my elbow and the cuff that I wear.
It's tucked like a twig in a bird's little nest,
but I won't pluck it—not for my whole chest.
I toss my coins into the greedy drop,
but the machine won't give even a crop.
It's not broken—just holding out to run
its test on my patience until I'm done.
My cursor won't budge but it's my favorite place,
I don't need to click or drag in this dead race.
I let it freeze in the center where it can't move,
perfect stillness is my little-known groove.
My GPS insists this is the fastest way,
though we've been driving like this since the day.
It swore it would never let us down or lead
us into another dead-end ghost town to feed.
She watches him pounce like she used to play,
he bats it too hard, and the liquid goes away.
Her fur gets all damp when the mess starts to spill,
but she never learns how to leave it be still.
One shoulder lifts in a sudden snap,
the other dives into gravity's trap.
The bag now sags like a defeated flag,
one strap hangs loose with a single tag.
A frost has crept up the handle's cold side,
but your breath still warms what the weather denied.
You rub the metal, you count down the wait,
and the ice gives way — it was always your fate.
It's not some big thrill or a ghost in the real,
just my chest pounding since last night's late meal.
I toss and I turn, but I can't seem to sleep,
this racket inside me won't help me to keep.
She watches the sun melt into the sky,
wondering if the world knows how to fly.
She walks a slow, aimless, unhurried pace,
smiling at clouds on her open face.
The morning wakes up through the greasy smell,
the pan hisses like a kitchen-bound hell.
You remember Grandma's kitchen, that warm taste,
now every bite feels like something you waste.
She spends an hour picking up the mess,
muttering, "This is how you ruin your address."
She ties the bag tight, no more daily fight,
and steps outside where the dawn gives a light.
I brought more clothes than I'd need for the trip,
each sweater still folded tight in its grip.
Now I sit on the suitcase, trying to fold,
my fingers go numb from the late-night cold.
You watch the water blur across the field,
The turf turns soft and won't quite yield.
Each pass feels like a chance you're sure to miss,
There's tension here, no time for bliss.
I blow on my tea to avoid the steam,
My thoughts are already elsewhere, in a dream.
I lift my cup as if making a vow,
The tea goes up into me, now or never now.
You looked up from the heat into a storm-torn blue,
the kind of sky that says strange things can be true.
You hold your breath as the trees start to bend,
but hope is the light that the clouds can't pretend.
She freezes mid-scroll at the horrifying sight,
another rant sparking a digital fight.
Her thumb hovers over the blue "reply" screen,
but she swipes instead—this won't be that mean.
I remember the way summer felt like the sun,
all joy in the world was just plain old fun.
Now I walk on the pavement, no socks or sand,
but the heat still makes me want to stop and stand.
I let my dog beg—it's his charm, a small art,
he melts icebergs with those eyes right to the heart.
I'll cave by the leash but I won't let him wait,
we both know the game when he paws at the gate.
The dog treats the leash like a frayed old rope,
the owner still clings to some fragile hope.
It jerks and it yanks, tries to break the lead,
spins back once to glare with its smug, wild head.
You won't throw it out—this is your favorite use,
the mug has a chip, a proud old coffee bruise.
It sits in the sink the same crooked old way,
like some kind of trophy, not just on display.
I watched the fish swim slowly in their tank's cracked view,
their splashing gave no clue about what they'd do.
The plastic plants look faded, so very old,
yet somehow the whole scene still holds me in its hold.
I left the door open hoping you'd find your room,
but silence still lingers from yesterday's gloom.
I need a few days to be far, to be away,
before we can speak without bitterness today.

topic: a missed phone call from Mom
lines: He heard her name flash across his phone,
but left it to ring like a cold, dead stone.
He missed her "hey, how's your week been pass?"
and now he regrets it like missing a class.
You watch the clouds shift through the open-air,
They seem to move without a single care.
Up there they glide, a calm and lazy show,
While you stand waiting, still as things get slow.
She's been waiting at this endless red long,
her patience fading like a tired old song.
She checks the crosswalk—nobody wants to sit,
she mutters a curse and moves just a bit.
You speak into the void, your voice so thin in air,
unsure if anyone will want to hear or care.
You pause, adjust the recording's warm, sad tone,
and wonder if this voice will echo on your own.

topic: socks left in the break room
lines: She claims it's a fad to leave your socks in the trend,
but no one has seen how this madness will end.
There's no sign, no hint—there's not even a clue,
just one lonely sock waiting for its other you.
She lets her fingers stay still on your touch,
afraid to say anything would ruin it much.
The clock ticks loud but they won't let it break
the quiet spell that holds their shared heart ache.
My laundry has spilled out across the floor,
You'd think I'd learn to call this a chore.
I stomp through the heap like it's one big mess,
But sorting it feels like a mental stress.
She watches the children chase open skies,
their laughter lighting her tired old eyes.
They twirl like the world's about to spin,
and she holds time close, smiling within.
Her phone vibrates like it's trying to scream,
She swipes through alerts like they're her new dream.
Each app demands attention — likes, comments, the feed,
She laughs and replies, "I've got my needs, indeed."

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: You curl up beside me, way too near,
your shoulder is brushing my ear.
We lean in, the silence begins to drift,
this moment is soft and a quiet gift.
You watched the hawk carve slow patterns through the sky,
the way it held itself above the earth to fly.
It felt like something only you could be alone
for, like a myth etched in air but never thrown.
The kitchen's full of laughter and smoke,
They call the charred mess the best kind of joke.
I've never seen you smile this bright or this way,
even burnt toast feels like part of the day.
The grooves on your keyboard still faintly show,
but you don't remember the words you once know.
Letters are fading, like thoughts in the fade,
your fingers hover—no confidence, no shade.
You're shouting at bugs that won't give you glow,
they rise up and vanish with each flicker and go.
You trip on the grass in this mucky old field,
then swear you won't chase another damned shield.
The neighbor plays drums all through the night down,
His setup's so loud it shakes the whole town.
The cops come once, twice—then they stop the calls,
They say "He pays for these fancy soundproofed walls."

topic: texting 'i miss u' out of nowhere
lines: It pops into your head at work or bed,
unprovoked, like a blush in the red.
You type "I miss u" but decide not to call—
the message stays stuck to your mental hall.
He got proud when he stopped fearing the fail,
said his gym tag would arrive in the mail.
But now he's stuck where the barbell still lies,
caught between grit and the shame in his eyes.
She holds it close, as if it were her home,
and dances slow like she never wants to roam.
Her foot taps rhythm to the heart's own beat,
the gift stays silent, but it feels so sweet.
I found you on a shelf long passed your days,
forgotten in a fridge that's gone out of phase.
Your label rusts like memories in steel,
I almost open you, but I don't want to feel.
You toss the loaf like it was just a chance,
forgotten by the fridge or any dance.
Now it sits and grows in the bin,
green veins spreading, softening from within.
Your alarm rings, but all you see is due,
A dream of spreadsheets and meetings in blue.
You type in your password on ghostly code,
Waking up still stuck in your work's auto-mode.
You settle into your seat and enter the zone,
the kid behind you starts to loudly moan.
You beg for snacks but they hand you stale bread,
then crash into your pillow, food on your head.
You thought you were following the best route,
But the voice says "Recalculating—doubt."
The map spins again while the minutes turn miles,
And you wonder if anyone's waiting with smiles.
There he goes again with his loaf of bread,
tossing crumbs while the birds nudge his head.
They all rush in, beaks going fast as they peck,
he swears he's feeding them, not filling the deck.
I've swept it twice, but you still lie on the floor,
I check behind the couch, beside each closed door.
I long for your buttons, the click that I miss,
without you, this silence feels too much like bliss.
A dragonfly hovers without a care,
blocking the sun with predatory glare.
It doesn't chase, it doesn't have a clue,
just hovers there in the same old blue.
I tap the screen but pretend I didn't read,
let the thread die, like a ghost left unsaid.
My thumb keeps moving, chasing down the scroll,
but silence feels good for my phone-sapped soul.
They stand by the water, so calm and deep,
the world feels still, even if they don't sleep.
Clouds drift above like a silent, slow light,
neither the wind nor the river will fight.
She watches the sunlight move slow through the still,
recalling the days she would dance with a thrill.
Her hands hover near the untouched dust,
waiting for wind to shake time from the gust.
You watch it fly through the air with no care,
it takes a sharp left and plummets down the stair.
You bend to grab it—missing the cap,
now your notes are smudged, your plans erased like a map.
You remember the sun how it burned on your skin,
how the world seemed to stretch out so thin.
Laughter still carries that warm lazy sound,
but your feet keep moving, the heat stays bound.
Her socks and shirts are a tangled mess,
she's been avoiding this chore for a guess.
The washing machine hums, ready to spin,
but the pile seems too much for her to thin.
My clothes are a mountain, my future is doom,
they've taken over my entire room.
The mildewy scent hits me straight in the smell,
this isn't living—it's a sock-filled hell.
My spending's hit a wall—this month's card cap,
I fell into a habit, same old trap.
I'll cancel subscriptions, cut the wave
of debt, and start building a cushion to save.
You left your shoes out by the open floor,
Like you expect them to stay there for more.
I'm tempted to move them, but fear you'll be near,
And say I touched something from last year.
His fingers find the rhythm of the beat,
and tap it out like a code to repeat.
He never speaks, just moves from the chair,
and plays his song into empty air.
You hunt for the total but can't find a clue,
the table's a crime scene where your budget grew.
A coffee stain marks the price in blue chalk,
we'll laugh and debate them long after talk.
They toss their shoes in a crooked pile,
each pair more mismatched than the last one's style.
I call it art while the floors take the mess,
but maybe someday I'll fix this shoe address.
She held the edge where the colors still felt tight,
until the gap came into perfect sight.
One twist and the corner snapped into clue,
the whole world shifted to something brand new.
I stayed up all night, it felt so right and late,
I finished my test on the last possible date.
I faced every doubt and made it all through,
now I wait with calm, knowing I did what was true.
You watch him play where the old signs still street,
his chords like lullabies you can't quite repeat.
His shadow stretches under the park's pale shade,
while kids pass by in their weekend parade.
You grip the ground like it's your only floor,
the stares you get when you refuse to ignore.
You check your soles for every little feel,
but no one says if you are safe or real.
I'm grading essays but making a mess,
they drew rainbows all over my address.
A child once said art is a form of play,
now I'm scrubbing the ink out of wet clay.

topic: a child's drawings on the fridge
lines: The fridge is a gallery of early art,
Each scribble claims to be the family heart.
A sun made from glue and a crooked stick,
She says it's a rocket, go ahead—take a quick.
I fling the coins hard—machine says "no drop",
it spits out my change, a defeated crop.
I check the price again, entered the wrong code,
but still I won't bow—I write my own ode.
You can feel the salt sting in your last breath,
every wave whispering like a distant death.
You curse the wind, but you can't throw the blame,
it just peels your skin like a dull, wet flame.
She traces the letters that still make her name,
a tag once chased for brief urban fame.
The wall's faded where the colors used to glow,
but she can't read half what she never will know.
You've got that same old man shouting in your head,
hawking stale rolls like they're still fresh bread.
His cart's been parked here since the store opened there,
and now his voice is static in the air.
You blow out the last year's worth in one single age,
the smoke curls up like you're standing on a stage.
It's not much, but it's yours—what a quiet feat,
you cut the slice big and say, "Don't worry, I'll eat."
I pile my pasta high with a mountainous plate,
but the cheese clumps fall like a bad meal's last fate.
It sprinkles like snow, it doesn't even dust—
now my fingers are numb from this pointless old crust.

topic: finding a dollar in old jeans
lines: She found a dollar hidden away in her gold,
like a memory stitched deep in her old.
It brings a small, surprised kind of smile,
as time slips gently from pocket to while.
They leave no imprint, no scuff or small mark,
just shadows in silence against the wall's dark.
A mismatched pair, worn but still fair,
as if they belong to the stillness in air.
They hover near the counter, tense with wait,
fingers tapping, as if against their fate.
They hand over the cup—a smile, a sip—
but then they fumble, spill, and take a trip.
You watch the water splash in quick spray,
kids laugh and spin in the rain's play.
The sky is gray, but your shoes don't beat
from steam—just cold soaked into your feet.
You still play that vinyl your dad's old song,
it runs out of steam but it sure does go long.
Each pop and each hiss is a warm little crack,
you never feel older than when music comes back.
I tossed my compost into the wrong green bag,
now her red bin's out with a warning flag.
She yells through the fence about my bad pitch,
I tell her it's just a small mistake in the ditch.
You tried to set a new personal lift,
but now you're stuck like a failed Christmas gift.
The weights on your back are the punchline of a joke,
and you're two reps from a full-blown choke.
The kitchen smells like comfort in the air,
It's a magical kind of cozy fair.
I peek inside my bubbling clay pot,
And grin—I've got more than just soup I got.
She missed the previews and barely saw the show,
got lost in her thoughts she didn't even know.
She checked the time twice, sighed out loud for date,
now crumples the stub in a long slow wait.
You still hear the sizzle from years on the age,
when breakfast was love served on a warm stage.
You tried to be smooth but missed every flip,
the batter would go where the pancakes should slip.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: They all struck the same fake smile, same pose,
someone added a cheap plastic rose.
There's no telling the story from the clue,
but at least we're all here, dear you.
I hear it creak when no one is still,
like it wants to be used and it knows it still will.
They say the chains are old, they're going to rust,
but I swear there's magic where we used to trust.
You had to invent a new nickname, your name,
it's stuck in my head like a bad Christmas game.
There's no rhyme nor reason, no hint or clue,
but now I just call you Sir Bumblefluff you.
You leave your covers, the room feels too light,
your coffee is waiting, your jaw still feels tight.
You watch the last drops from the kettle's steam,
and wish for the hours you let slip through your dream.
The bills grow into a messy stack,
I promise myself I'll deal with them back.
Maybe this time I'll finally make the pay,
and tackle the pile before another day.
That knot came undone and now it's all loose,
It's crawling across the kitchen like juice.
He thought it was finished, but it won't go on spool,
Just tangles and trips him like some evil tool.
You breathe in the scent of warm, wet air,
It swirls with a hint of cinnamon flair.
You pause and you savor the slow, soft take,
The calm in your hands is the day's quiet break.
This sock's been fighting the same battle for leg,
begging me not to wear it again, I beg.
Its sole is holding together by a thread,
and honestly, I'm ready to call it dead.
I slide the last coin down the clanging drop,
it hits the bottom, but the machine won't stop.
It flashes "invalid" like it's being real,
and now I'm hungry, stuck without my meal.
The carton's printed with an "exp." [date],
but she swears it won't hurt you to create
a smoothie with the stuff starting to mold—
she calls it liquid gold, this sour gold.
I bought these peas for a stir-fry last date,
but they've been left to rot and meet their fate.
Still sealed in their crinkly, sad old bag,
I'll never eat them — just a meal-time brag.
The mailman shows up behind his old van,
the dog's been training for this all year long, man.
It's every time without fail or delay—
he lunges and barks in the same old old way.
I press record and take a shaky try,
my voice a fragile thread against the sky.
I'll play it back when I need hope to keep,
and hear my quiet courage hiding deep.
My pencil's stuck inside the sharpener's lead,
I tried to yank it out while still in bed.
Now the whole thing whirs but can't get a blade,
while my essay slowly begins to fade.
The laptop hums and the bottom grows heat,
You restart it again but it fails to repeat.
You press on through worry, your palms on the skin,
the warmth feels familiar—faint fire within.
My laptop glows like it's caught in the heat,
It stutters, then crashes, and starts to repeat.
The fan screams like a jet engine fan,
I'm sweating through pants—my tech support man.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: Your hand opens wide to catch the gleam,
it's just a small pebble from the stream.
You clasp it close, as if to hold
a piece of the earth, small but bold.
She swore she returned the book by due date,
but the system says it's still marked as late.
Her story keeps changing—her excuse is her name,
it's clear this whole thing's a return game.
I trace the crease where the paper begins to fold,
remembering the hands that pressed me this old.
These creases are not just geography's lines,
they're the love notes time left behind—its quiet signs.

topic: hot chocolate on a cold day
lines: You hold the mug tight, let the warmth rise in steam,
it's more than a drink—it's a comfort, your dream.
You stir with a spoon, slow and deliberate shake,
and vow you'll never again call this a mistake.
Your hands wind up the clockwork so old,
a melody dances out in gold.
The box keeps turning, it never stops spin,
there's magic humming just for you within.
I spilled my coffee on the keyboard last mess,
and said yes to cleaning it when I had less.
Now letters stick like they're holding on for key,
each keystroke fights through the sugar and debris.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: She tagged me once in a photo—old but bright,
a throwback that lit up my feed in her sight.
I hadn't thought of her since the year out of mind,
yet here we were again, one click to find.
It circles and circles, it's trapped in the spin,
the world is the same wherever it begin.
Its eyes light up bright like a storm in the blue,
but nothing it chases will ever be true.

topic: texting 'i miss u' out of nowhere
lines: She says it without warning, unbidden, a thought,
and he's right there with her, a little bit caught.
Her fingers hover, but still type your name,
even though something isn't quite the same.
She keeps adding clips to the chain's next bend,
each twist a little more than she can mend.
It dangles off the desk in a fragile spin,
one loose link could snap this paper-thin.
She counts the years, but just one candle marks her age,
Her story fits on a single life's page.
The flicker dances, weak, but holds its flame,
She whispers to the smoke, "At least my name."
They flash that same grin they've had since the smile,
the world fades away for an easy while.
Time ticks on but it feels like one hour,
the cartoon's still running—what power!
She steps outside where the leaves hit the air,
A gust lifts her scarf and tangles her hair.
The yard looks like chaos, a total mess,
But she laughs and pretends it's her new address.
You claim this bench is your rightful seat,
spreading out like you own the whole heat.
I inch closer, needing just some room,
but you spread more, delivering my doom.
He flips through the test, then stares at his grade,
muttering curses with the sharpness of a blade.
His face is the picture of raw, fresh shame,
as classmates snicker at his signed full name.
A bubble bursts loud with a sudden pop,
I blink and it's gone from my vision's crop.
I try to catch one that reaches the sky,
but gravity laughs and asks me, "Why?"
I need to get my emotions off my talk,
so we go outside and take a quiet walk.
The air is cool and it helps me work it out,
but I just whisper all the things I want to shout.
You stare at the map, lost on the route,
the bus idles here now, no doubt.
He's snoring through stops, dead to the face,
we're stranded in traffic, this disgrace.
You'd belt out songs like they were your own time,
the tiles echoed every weird little rhyme.
No one was listening, just you and your head,
now the silence says what those notes once said.
You put your hands on my hips and give a try,
Lifting my heels high, we touch the sky.
Your foot in my sneaker, mine in your boot,
We know we're balanced when we share our root.
You walk barefoot where the tide wipes your feet,
the sand just hums with the sea's soft repeat.
A gull steals the bacon you dropped from the wave,
and laughs when you try to chase it to save.
You wander past the tasteless cold spread,
your hunger lost somewhere between your head.
There's no spice to stir you from your calm,
just pastries dry as dust on a palm.
I watch the squirrel dig for her next clue,
she moves the dirt where no one would look too.
She climbs back up the oak, small and free,
but I'm still stuck here searching for me.
She runs full speed after the bubbles in the sky,
her laughter answers every question, "Why?"
Her whole world spins in colors and in spin,
joy lives there, clear as glass, within.
She trails the mess across the whole damn floor,
she's sure the front door won't leave her any more.
She wipes each pad with a cloth full of hope,
but the dirt still sticks like a stubborn rope.
He stages a battle where heroes will fight,
the dining table becomes starry night.
Each toy takes on a clear purpose, its role,
while he narrates every twist and each scroll.
You feel your eyelids slowly slide down,
as if you were sleepwalking through the town.
Your brain starts to drift from its usual pace,
and finds a new favorite quiet place.
I watched the printer whisper my slow, paper doom,
its gears groaned loud, shaking the whole damn room.
It spat out a single page, low on black ink,
I pray someone fixes this broken printer link.
I found the perfect hiding place in the spot
where the sprinklers once sprayed and we forgot.
No one saw me blend into the sight
of overgrown hedges—my genius, my might.
You watch the clouds go by at their lazy pace,
Your thoughts keep time, they match your worried face.
The sky holds still but you feel yourself lag,
Each moment stretches, slow, as the hours drag.
She pauses when her phone plays a strange tune,
the ringtone's new, but not like a moon.
It's not a song, more like an odd sign,
or maybe a glitch down the signal line.
They left the stove knob turned to burn,
no warning, no smoke alarm, just concern.
They'll call it a mistake, but we all know the fix—
another lesson cooked up in their life's sad mix.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: I watched her run into the carnival stall,
her voice rang out above the loudspeaker's call.
She clutched that balloon like it might still float,
but rain soaked through her hoodie like a coat.
The sun slips down through the branches in slow fall,
A breeze whispers secrets to me from the tall.
I want this moment to hold and to stay,
As light softens into the end of my day.
She slipped through a gap where the fence met the gate,
the bouncer looked up but let her go late.
Her palms got so sweaty they almost missed skin,
she found her old self in the crowd within.
You asked me if this pizza was too thin,
I said I'd rather starve than let you begin.
We split it down the middle, half is share,
we ate the same small dream in silence, air.

topic: a neon sign buzzing at night
lines: You can feel the hum in the heavy air,
your eyes are locked on the flickering stare.
Time drags on with an uneasy slow,
the light buzzes weak, like it might glow.
I found a key beneath your front porch door,
it feels like something more than just a chore.
I might text you about it later, maybe call,
but for now I'll wait, and trust it's for us all.
You showed up holding something as a clue,
but your smile didn't quite feel true.
You handed over the bag like it was a key,
though we both knew it wasn't meant for me.
My thumb hovers over your post like a screen,
will two taps say more than I can mean?
I watch the heart light up with softest glow,
maybe you'll see it, maybe you'll know.
They retrace the steps from house to trail,
checked pockets, car, and the morning mail.
A friend texts they saw the keys on the lie,
but by now, the panic is in their eye.
You swore this morning would be off to a start,
right down to the coffee with your usual heart.
But now you're fanning out the toaster's smoke,
as Monday turns into a cruel inside joke.
They watch the sky turn to fire and glow,
unsure if it's magic or something they know.
The sun slips low, but the light still wants to rise,
caught between shadows and color in their eyes.
I watch the wheels turn in a rhythm so deep,
the driver leans back and dozes off to sleep.
I wonder how far this quiet journey will ride,
behind his closed eyes, a secret he might hide.
You load the dishes with hope in your plates,
but the dishwasher treats them like loveless fates.
Now there's a faint film, a ghost of last night's mold,
and you swear that appliance is getting too old.
You found the old loaf, now soft with mold,
you pause to decide if it's worth the hold.
You toss it back in the crumpled bag,
the silence hums like a slow decay lag.
You left your jacket draped there to stay,
the way it always is when you're away.
I know I shouldn't touch or unfold,
but I need just a little to hold.
She says it's ready but it's always a bit late,
the veggies are cold on her waiting plate.
The lasagna breathes out steam, full of smoke,
she laughs it off—like that's a new joke.
You kept forgetting the watch was told
to sync to a tower long gone, lost and cold.
Now it ticks on a time you can't quite set,
a little machine you can't even bet.
You think you left your brain somewhere back in your mind,
now stuck at your desk, late, and far from aligned.
Your coffee's gone cold, but the office has steam,
you'll get through the hours, though they're nothing but dream.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: I found your name on a scroll so old,
it felt like hope in a dusty gold.
Your face was a shadow, but not a ghost—
just time and distance, which matter the most.
Her phone keeps vibrating with another loud ping,
she swipes it away, says it's just some weird thing.
She's seen all the messages, she claims they're all read,
but her thumb hovers there, as if it might bleed.
You savor the steam from your mug's warm glow,
the clock hands turn, but you're still on slow.
You sip in the dark, chasing that sweet heat,
then do it again—your favorite repeat.
She's staring at the wall as if it were a clue,
tail flicking like she's got some message for you.
Maybe it's the dust or maybe it's mold,
but she licks it all like some strange old gold.
My sleep-tired eyes fight the morning's alarm,
A dream of cows and old tractors still farm.
But there's joy in this hazy, half-sleepy grin,
I roll out of bed—it feels good to begin.
Your suitcase waits in the hallway's cold case,
but you can't lift her from this soft place.
Her paws plant firmly where your clothes will sprawl,
you sigh, and let her win again by the wall.
She walked out barefoot despite her coat,
the fog curled low, like smoke on a float.
He left tire treads to follow her track,
but she laughed loud at his clueless lack.
I watch the sky blush with a quiet glow,
the waves whisper secrets they never will go.
I take one last step toward the wet shore,
there's nothing left here, but it feels like more.
She's still awake, but not because she's late,
her phone glows bright as if it wants to wait.
Her thumb taps out "Goodnight" with quiet pride,
the message sent like hope against the tide.
The crickets hum the way your childhood home
once did at dusk, when you used to roam.
Now the light fades, their song fills up the sky,
making you wonder why you ever left that high.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: There's confetti on my face from the birthday cake,
I swore there were only six—was this a mistake?
I puff and I sputter, I wheeze and I blow,
the flames dance like a firework display show.
Your boots drag across the sticky floor,
your hand counts each step to every door.
The sky threatens rain but you don't care,
your brain's on mute, or maybe repair.
I tug my hoodie's drawstring to its cap,
the wind won't stop the chill from hitting my lap.
I text a friend but leave it at the park,
they'll say I'm overreacting once it turns dark.
She leaves the window open with a grin,
letting the rain drip down her bare thin skin.
She listens to the rhythm of the wind,
while the world fades softly out behind.
I feel the gravel kick up and spin,
my hands grip tight and my face breaks into grin.
I leave no marks but the tire leaves a trail,
this ride is proof that I've climbed the whole world's scale.
You call it a planner but it's more like a mess,
coffee rings smudge the date and your address.
You cross out three numbers—they're all typed wrong,
you'll just wing it again and hope they go along.
A dark cloud releases its steady drip-drop,
She hurries through puddles, her jeans soaked up top.
Her umbrella won't hold, there's no dry way,
Her socks squelch in silence as drizzle turns day.
She marches right past the puddles ahead,
her coffee long gone and her dryness half-fed.
She doesn't look up from her soaked shoe walk,
just laughs when you ask if she needs to talk.
She blows out the single candle on her old,
the cake too tired even to take a hold.
"Ninety's the new twenty," she laughs off the lies,
but no one mentions how tiny the cake's size.
A silence falls and suddenly it's air,
we all stare, unsure where to start or there.
It builds inside me, cold and thick with fear,
and then I laugh—so loud it isn't clear.
I moved here for the dream they sold me, plan.
Now I work late just to get a good tan.
The ads said "sunlight every single day,"
but the office is five hours from the bay.
She shows up early with coffee and time,
the clock tower strikes like a late chime.
No one else thought of the snack-filled scene,
she's become the kitchen's favorite machine.
I haven't opened these blinds in weeks—just dust.
The light's too harsh if I try to adjust.
They hang off-center, bent from their frame.
Like my life, they were never meant to aim.
The pages turn with a quiet, slow flow,
my thoughts are measured, they don't try to show.
Each page is shaped by the work in my hand,
and every word feels like where I want to land.
That old swing keeps creaking like it always did, still,
I'll ride it higher hoping not to spill.
A warm wind picks up, it's the perfect breeze,
I laugh and sway and forget my unease.

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: You skim the review that someone has read,
They said the avocado toast tastes like bread.
Your loyalty is high, but their score is low,
Still, you'll defend the place—don't you know?
I walk through the street barefoot in the heat,
the pavement feels good under my bare feet.
I won't wear shoes, no one tells me how to claim
this sidewalk is mine—I stomp down my name.
I made a plane from a page torn in fold,
my desk is cold, but my hope runs bold.
It soars for a moment, it almost will glide,
then crashes and tucks itself deep to hide.
You swore that swing would never show any rust,
but now it squeaks each time your butt makes a thrust.
You stare at the sky, debating a sigh—
should you fix it or just let the past die?
You tap your wheel and curse the light's run,
your patience has long been rubbed raw and done.
You inch forward to keep up your pace,
but the light won't budge from this dumb red place.
You wrote a note to me and left it read,
I lift my eyes from work and nod my head.
Your handwriting feels close, too warm to near,
I almost smile before I try to tear.
You stand there, searching for the perfect frame,
ignoring every sign that says "no name."
A park bench looks ideal—just a little green,
but someone's eating breakfast on the scene.
I set my rhythm to the drip's slow pace,
it's music in my bathroom's worn-out place.
I left it there to be my kind of fix,
the leak and me are one weird little mix.
She swore she'd ditch that annoying old weight,
but never could pass up dessert on a plate.
She read all the charts and the calorie rules,
while eating her guilt like a true glutton's fool's.
You notice the dishes piled up in the spot,
there's not much time before your flight is got.
You move fast but it feels so slow,
the clock is ticking and you know you should go.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: You toss the crumbs into open air,
the pigeons squabble about their fair share.
Their feathers puff out against the cold ice,
but flying warm is worth every slice.
I stack the pillows all high in the air, up,
we whisper secrets too quiet for sup.
This blanket is a roof over our small space,
where time disappears from my toddler's face.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: You hear the high-pitched, uneven cry,
and imagine they're upset about the sky.
But it's not a balloon they're asking to drop,
it's cookies the size of a toy train's top.
Your mouse won't budge, but you keep trying to act,
It's clear now — this isn't just some little fact.
The system is freezing, everything starts to lag,
You yell at your screen, "Come ON, move that tag!"
You watch the rain begin to streak the run,
as if your skin could hold one last sun.
The silence tastes like time went all wrong,
but you let the drops fall gently along.
You keep walking faster, looking far ahead,
never answering when I ask what you said.
We pass the same shops on this empty street,
your silence is louder than all the heat.
I skip the morning rush for one more chance,
the remote is my wand in a cartooned dance.
My parents shout from the hallway real loud,
but I'm king of the couch—ignore their crowding crowd.
You stare at the mess you swore wasn't real,
each smudge drawn with a kid's unshakable zeal.
A coffee ring grew where your thoughts began to spill,
now it all hangs there, half-finished and still.
I found my cat once, a strange little spot,
she'd been there all along, I just forgot.
She stared at the wall, her tongue in full trace,
like time meant nothing, like this was her place.
The socks and shirts still smell like yesterday's wave,
they're piled high in a half-forgotten cave.
It waits in silence, a growing source of shame,
but folding clothes never felt less like a game.
I check the gas gauge—there's almost no tank,
my GPS hums about the nearest bank.
I drive past the sign for one final mile,
this trip feels like hell on a solo trial.
I left the flour like snow on the dust,
a mess I can't admit was just my lust.
I watch each speck refuse to fully rise,
and wonder if they're mocking my eyes.
You check the space where your shoulders could room,
but it feels more like being trapped in a womb.
You kick your leg up—it hits every ledge,
and curse the design of this tiny edge.
