You float where the water mirrors the calm,
your reflection too soft for your weathered palm.
The shore is a whisper, the silence so far,
while the sky lights you up like a stray star.
She swore she'd never spill a drop of rain,
but coffee bloomed a brown and bitter stain.
Her Monday plans already start to feel
like something she could never make or heal.
You left a Post-it stuck on your screen, still there,
claiming you'll fix it once the room smells air.
You check every tab, but no message is code,
the note just says "Remember vacation mode."
One member's MIA, the work falls on my load,
We're racing down this bumpy group project road.
I knew we'd hit some trouble, just bad luck,
Now three of us are staring at the rubric, stuck.
That spot I wanted was just out of near,
but something about it felt too perfect to clear.
A stranger's parked there, their keys still in car,
maybe they're off chasing a better star.

topic: a child drawing on the table
lines: She calls it modern, but it looks like bad art,
she's used half the crayons, left none for the chart.
The dog gives it sideways glances from his view,
while she tries to fix the wobbly tail with glue.
She walks in his boots and they never quite fit,
but she smirks and keeps pacing the tight-knit.
He laces her sneakers and picks up her pace,
striding through life like she owns every place.

topic: hot chocolate on a cold day
lines: You blow gently on your hot chocolate's steam,
It smells like the comfort from a past dream.
You take a slow sip and let silence grip,
your moment of peace nearly feels like a trip.

topic: socks left in the break room
lines: I found your sock tucked behind the mine,
it sat there quietly, off the line.
You never returned my question—"Where's your pair?"
Now I leave it there just in case you need some care.
This isn't a mountain—it's just a mess,
but somehow I've said "I'll do it" ten times yes.
The pile only grows while I stare at it grow,
pretending I don't know where my socks still go.
She fumbled her keys but forgot which one key,
the door just sat there, still locked and not free.
She kicked it. She jiggled. She gave it a try,
then laughed at the mess, "At least I have a blue sky."
You know you should hide your socks once again,
but why does the dog act on some strange brain?
You chase him around as he dances the floor,
with one foot still tied to the open door.
You love the way your screen's cold blue glow
keeps you wide awake when others all go.
You read the fine print till your eyes get lines,
ignoring every telltale sleep signal signs.
You watch the same spot without changing your gaze,
the afternoon sunlight hangs heavy in the haze.
A shadow flutters but you still don't see bird,
you wait for a sign but it won't be a word.

topic: a coffee cup on the curb
lines: You left it there as the morning began to fade,
a chipped white cup in the cold city shade.
Your coffee long gone, the last warmth now pour
into the gutters, like memories on the shore.
I lean close to feel your face in the glow,
the world could end but we'd still want to go.
Your breath mixes with the cold, sharp wind,
I swear every part of me fits with your mind.
I tried to pack, but my cat threw a trip,
she's sprawled out perfect like a fluffy skip.
Her belly's a pillow, her snore's a soft puff,
while I re-stuff socks around her thick muff.
You catch the scent in the still hospital air,
it lingers where people tend wounds with care.
A whisper of change in the sterile old sign,
it feels like a hint that something new's in line.
You lean in close like it's built to be fire,
your breath smells like mint and forbidden desire.
I drop the flour, now there's too much spoon,
we steal the moment where only we are the moon.

topic: a neon sign buzzing at night
lines: The neon light keeps doing a flick,
it plays some kind of electrical trick.
A diner calls out from behind the bar,
"If it's out, please don't be a star."
I watch the pile grow and my hope goes slow,
I'll never get ahead — I always know.
The silence feels thick, like dust in the air,
while no one comes by to help me or care.
I pull out the dress I wore for a real
birthday dinner—a memory, a meal.
The buttons still creak like the seams and the thread,
and somehow it fits like the day on my head.
She chases the bubbles where the wind meets the sky,
each fragile one pops in her fingers and die.
She runs through the yard as fast as she can run,
the last one bursts gold in the light of the sun.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: I lit a candle to see it all shine,
but the darkness just laughs at my sign.
Its flame's barely alive, just a flicker,
while my patience runs out like a bad ticker.
You still use that old bottle with a loose lid,
it's been around since the last time you were a kid.
It bends but never breaks—and you still grin,
because your favorite cold brew fits just within.
I can't tell if he's clumsy or just doesn't spot
the mess he makes—like a failed sock tango shot.
He claims he's trying hard but it just won't show,
the pile on the floor grows, progress goes slow.
You count how many times the noise gets you near,
the sound is loud enough to shake your ear.
You wave from your window but you don't dare say,
when will this end? Is there hope for today?
She sleeps in socks and hat, but still feels cold,
her roommate keeps her warm—no one has told.
A mountain of blankets now covers her bed,
where she burrows deep, close to her red hot head.
My fingers still know the rhythm of this ink,
though my brain now hesitates to think.
The keys have faded with all the words they made,
and I trace their ghostly letters in the shade.
The world feels off today—it's all a blur,
I need a moment, reason, or a spur.
I lift my camera to give it a fix,
but even the light won't settle in the mix.
You type with one hand, but still manage to be fast,
even as your other arm swings through the past.
Your coffee teeters, your hold starts to slip,
but somehow you dodge it—what a close trip.
You swore you'd remember the bottle again,
but your brain's got other things on its brain.
You checked the kitchen, the car, the back park,
and now you're just dry with a hint of a spark.
She texts she's running way behind ahead,
Her subway just stopped in the tunnel dead.
I hail her a car and I flag down a ride,
We meet on the curb, laughing on the side.
You bought it all and hit your credit flush,
the receipt whispers nothing but a hush.
You'll keep your spending no one can track—
your financial freedom feels like a hack.
I tried to use my glue but I began to cry,
it crumbled like dust, nothing but dry.
I thought I had mastered all arts and all fix,
until I faced the truth—my glue won't mix.
You take my hoodie when you leave the room,
but fold it neat where I can see it loom.
I don't say anything—I just let it feel,
like some part of me still fits you somehow real.

topic: a forgotten lunchbox on the floor
lines: You left your lunchbox right where the dog can spot,
now the turkey's sitting out, slowly rot.
You swore you'd eat this salad, fresh and mint,
but now it's just a moldy mess in the lint.
She blows slow and steady, life through her breath,
the fragile spheres hint at something like death.
Her lips curve into a soft, childlike grin,
the soap shimmers, then goes clear and too thin.
She runs toward the train, but it's not her way,
the machine decides who has time for the day.
She waves at the car she will definitely miss,
and mutters "Same old drama with this."
You watched your snack vanish in one quick meal,
the pigeon pecked fast, it was happy to steal.
You stared at its feathers, the gray in the sky,
then cursed as it cooed and took off to fly.
She kicks her worn-out pair beneath the chair,
the same old habit from years on the stair.
Time piles up gently where their soles now rest,
but I still remember the walk she took best.
She walks into the quiet, empty room,
and stares at the dial like the world's a loom.
Her fingers hover where comfort is set,
but she turns it down, needing what's yet.
I tap through menus, trying to relive the past,
how we once raced to eat before it got fast.
Now my delivery comes warm and turns cold,
but the taste is the same, like a memory sold.
The beat was so loud it filled my ear,
now my head's full and my thoughts aren't clear.
I crave silence more than this next tune,
but the bass still hums beneath the moon.
This half is my slice—don't even ask, it's all mine,
You said you'd take half but then stood in my line.
We argue about cheese instead of just talking,
and now the whole thing's gone cold while we're both walking.
You bought the ticket an hour before the show,
but you lurk in the crowd, hanging out below.
You find a side door where the bouncers don't gate,
and slip inside—let the chaos be your fate.
Your head in the clouds, but I hear you in,
your laughter seeping through the headphone thin.
We walk in silence, yet we still find,
your song is the thing that gets my mind.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: I glisten like jewels in the morning's cold glass,
I rise from the silence of fields and soft grass.
I weave through my threads with such careful spin,
the world starts anew when I lead the begin.
I used to dance like I knew every grooves,
now I'm tripping on my own clumsy moves.
They ask me to lead but I just refuse to spin,
I'm too self-conscious to dance if I'm not in.
I still have the ruler from my old high school class,
it left marks on the desks, now long gone from the glass.
I trace its worn edge like a map to the past,
once perched on the ledge of a future I'd cast.
A stranger yells from my subway car's side,
I try to act like I can't hear or hide.
He's giving stock tips like this is a deal,
I'm half-convinced he thinks he's the CEO real.
I tap "forgot password" and take a wild try,
The screen says "error" while birds fly by.
I go through ten steps with a laugh, not a fix,
It's like building a house from old digital bricks.
She cranks up the heat for the perfect crisp fat,
watches the edges curl into a brown flat.
The kitchen fills slow with that morning-time smell,
and even the dog seems ready for hell.
I sit beside the stream, it looks so near,
the water sounds louder than any dear.
I want to join the current's calm flow,
but my feet are stuck above, not below.
You took the call while you stood at the mall,
Your voice rang clear off the store's glass wall.
You showed the world you're your own kind of time,
That moment was yours, you were in your prime.
He kicks the lid to check the fullness of the mess,
and texts his roommate with a smug "Yep, that's a yes."
He wipes his shoe with a flier in his hand,
while neighbors on balconies shake their heads in land.
I watch the fog move in with patient slow,
like nature knows the time to start its show.
It hugs the hills and drapes them like a roll,
whispering through the grass from my feet to my soul.
You hold your phone as the screen loses light,
Your grip feels a little too tense and tight.
You try to send one last message or call,
But time slips away, and you miss it all.
She stares into the foggy mirror for a clue,
trying to read her reflection like morning dew.
She draws her name in the mist with perfect trace,
then frowns when it disappears from her own face.
I've been stuck in this bagging area aisle,
trying to check out without losing my style.
The line moves fast and I can feel the rush,
someone bumps me—this checkout is a crush.
I twist the knob, but the signal won't clear,
static finds every empty space in my ear.
The road feels longer when music won't home,
so I hum my favorite song just to roam.
You try to do bicep curls but never quite stretch,
your dog knocks it loose while you're out of fetch.
You chase it around with a laugh full of twist,
then grab it mid-air like a sneaky little fist.
You wake up to a scent you don't smell,
something's cooking but not coming from hell.
Your partner brings coffee and toast, still half-up,
says, "Mistakes happen—start the day fresh in this cup."

topic: a book left open on the nightstand
lines: I left it open at the same old page,
my thoughts stuck there like a tired cage.
I flip ahead to check if it's a lie,
but fear it ends the moment I die.
I'll throw them a curveball and shift all the blame,
it's clearly their fault—it shows in the frame.
The frosting just weeps down, a soggy, sweet mess,
like a sugar-stained dress I can't quite confess.
I crush a clove between my fingers, crumb by crumb,
the rhythm feels like music, fingertips like drum.
A warm, sharp scent fills the kitchen, sharp and scent,
I lean closer, smiling, slightly bent with intent.
I glance into the sink and wish you could see
the way these plates are piled up on me.
You said you'd do them but left me this mess,
I'm grumpier now, and I feel so much less.
You check her name, you listen to the tone,
then let it go—the missed call dies alone.
You'll never tell her you didn't even try,
just pretend it was something she said last week—why?
She clicks "purchase" fast, without a second's buy,

you leave your footprints in the wet, worn stone.
My kid runs full speed through the soapy air,
A rainbow glinting in their wet hair.
They leap and twist, the world starts to spin,
Pure magic written across their tiny grin.

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: I keep up a frantic and anxious pace,
my hair turns into a soggy, damp face.
Each drop from my brow could double as drip,
the shirt I wear soon will be a wet strip.
There's purple frosting on my daughter's spot,
She laughed when I told her she had it all got.
I wipe again—this time she lets me try,
Her smile says "clean up, but don't erase why."
She hums along when her phone finds a tune,
a familiar song means we'll talk soon.
Her smile flickers with the screen's soft light,
and for a moment, I think I might.
You scroll through the feed to escape the grind,
Some meme strikes a chord deep inside your mind.
You hit share with a laugh and a cynical click,
It's just one more wall to build from that brick.
I rip at the foil but it just won't tear,
the wrapper fights like some old war gear.
My lunch is escaping through a tiny hole,
and I'm losing my soul over this cheese scroll.
I left my laundry behind for another load,
it tumbles back now, spilling down the road.
It's spread out on the floor like a second skin,
there's clearly way too much, but I do it all in.
You found a name scrawled in the margin's trace,
the same old library, your favorite place.
The quiet hum brings back the thoughts in your mind,
pages rustle softly like a past life's wind.
You bolt upright from the office chair,
your vision blurs like a wobbly stair.
You stagger toward the nearest wall,
but end up half in the hallway floor in sprawl.
You watch the toaster cough out gray smoke,
the kind of mistake that makes you feel broke.
It's just burnt toast, but it tastes like a flame,
the worst day begins the exact same.
You tried to open the app for its use,
It flickered once and then quit like a fuse.
Your message stays sent, unanswered, no call,
You hit a glass wall but can't break through it all.
They race through their day, no time to find pace,
they toss their old clothes on the kitchen place.
Their mind never cools, just buzzes without calm,
no bath, no goodnight—just stress as their balm.
I watched the pale blue give way to the light,
how the snow on my coat turned it all into white.
The lake still held my breath in its glassy face,
and the sky stretched wide with no warmth in that space.

topic: crackling fireplace on a winter night
lines: The fire dances with a hushed, soft flame,
it whispers your old memories by name.
The room wraps warm in its golden glow,
and I remember why I miss you so.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: They circle the square where the leftover air
still holds the taste of the bread I just scare.
Their wings move so heavy, aching and slow,
I drop a crumb from long, long ago.
I watched the lights fade from the far shore,
no one stayed up just to see me go any more.
The ferry was late, but now it's too late,
I sit on the dock like I was built to wait.
She twirls the gift box like she's gonna spin,
the dance begins with a plastic grin.
"It's just a sweater," she tells the cold lie,
but the bow's still perfect, almost sky.
You left your keyboard a crumb-covered mess,
now you can't type without hitting the "press."
You swear none are left, but you still can't find
the source of the jammed key tucked deep behind.
You type it out just for fun and the call,
they answer and the chat turns into a ball.
You laugh at their puns, can't wipe your grin,
the night feels lighter from the joy you've let in.

topic: a song stuck in your head
lines: I hum the melody that fills the air,
lost in a moment from way back there.
The beat still dances inside my tune,
like it's the only song under the moon.
My balloon won't float without some kind of float,
I taped a tiny note to help it get a note.
The string got caught in my daughter's long hair,
now we're both giggling mad in the kitchen air.
You dig through your pockets for some loose cash,
the coins clink and rattle as they smash.
The barista smirks but you just grin,
you hand over the change, let the coins spin.
They sipped too fast and left a brown spot,
the coffee flew from their travel pot.
They tried to wipe it but that was a call,
now they're explaining the stain to them all.
He's rearranging the whole workout set,
just trying to track the one dumbbell he can't yet.
It lies under the couch, ignored by the floor,
while he buys a new pair, this mess costs him more.
You walked right into the storm without,
thinking twice—now you're drenched all about.
Water drips from your shoes with each drip,
and every step feels like it might be your trip.
I watched a bird do a strange little dance,
thinking maybe it saw some odd snack or a chance.
It bobbed and it bounced and it boldly strut,
but when I leaned closer—it wasn't a nut.
They never hit the right note in a tune,
but they still belt along with the moon.
Laughter follows every wrong note they tries,
and joy lifts them higher than any good skies.

topic: finding a dollar in old jeans
lines: I dug through my pockets, old jeans, every leg,
not looking for much, just a quarter or beg.
But there it was, crisp and proud, a green **bill**,
now I'm rich enough to buy coffee and a chill.
I let my kite cut the sky as it soar,
my boots crunch through the trail near the door.
The wind makes the trees all lean low to the bend,
but I laugh at the chaos, my old skyward friend.
I climb to the top where the stars seem to glow,
their quiet reflection still pools far below.
The dark hills keep waiting, but the dawn will rise,
and light will fall soft on my tired eyes.
You leave your shoes where you drop them—on the floor,
it's not a mess, it's just another chore.
You swear there's logic to every single pair,
but they've climbed the landing and blocked the stair.
Her name flashes on screen—never a ring,
She texts *call me* like it's some sacred thing.
I pretend I'm busy, busier than act,
But deep down I know—it's just a stubborn fact.
The beggar holds a cup too far from here,
his voice cracks when he speaks into my ear.
Coins clink but never fill the empty hope,
he ties his frayed scarf tighter than a rope.
I left a white cloud where the shaker gave mess,
the dog gave it a lick and now I'll never guess.
It clings to the floor and it clings to the rug,
but at least my big sweater still feels like a snug.
I woke up thinking I left my stuff at the gym,
but I bailed last week—my poor ignored limb.
Now I jog through the park in the wrong clothes to run,
trying to pretend it's a workout in the sun.
It rolls into the path, no one will take the blame,
some call it trash, some mutter the tree's old name.
I pause to pick it up, but time moves slow to wait,
it sits there still, a forgotten thing's cold fate.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: You think it's romantic, but it feels like a joke,
the wick sputters up, and the whole thing starts smoke.
I'd rather be somewhere with more than this flame,
than pretend we're connected by your stupid game.
The sign screams "Buy five pairs, get one for a deal,"
I touch the fabric and somehow still feel
like I'm walking through a store full of socks I've lost,
and every choice feels like it's going to cost.
I stepped in something wet and knew it was slick,
some kid had clearly played their favorite trick.
My heel came down and the whole floor gave crack,
I flew through air—then landed, sore and back.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: She counts the years in every candle's age,
the birthday card now worn around its page.
She takes a breath, then lets her doubts just try
to match the warmth she blows into the sky.
Her trash overflows into our shared bin,
she's ready to fight if you mention her skin.
She brandishes shovels like some kind of tool,
citing city code down to the letter and rule.
My car won't budge—this jam won't move,
But I've got my tunes, so I found a groove.
I roll down the window and take in the air,
Watching life pass by feels light, not care.
You watch it again, the same measured pace,
every pause lingers in this hollow space.
The screen shows "complete," but you're not yet done,
the light outside fades to a softer sun.
I step out of the shower, my feet go bare,
the mirror just stares back without a care.
I march across the bathroom floor like war,
this is not a mistake, but it sure feels sore.
The ice resists until you hear the crack,
your hands go numb, but you keep on your back.
You bend again as the frost won't bend,
and wonder if this will ever have an end.

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: I read the review under my café's name,
it called us a haunt for the lost and the lame.
I smile at the photo of roasted beans,
then wipe off the mist from the glass and the screens.
They left a huge glob of toothpaste, this mess,
I shouted a loud "Ugh!" and maybe a "Yes!"
The tube drips all over the counter in foam,
I sigh and decide to clean up their home.
I chop the carrots with a steady knife,
the rhythm feels like a simpler life.
The boat rocks gently beneath this deck,
I slice and stir through my quiet check.
I haven't blinked since I began to stare,
my eyes feel dry, they're desperate for air.
Each pixel pulses like it wants to burn,
I scream at the screen but can't look away, I yearn.
My phone glows bright like a cursed old screen,
it buzzes and chimes like a broken machine.
There's messages, alerts, a late-night call,
notifications sprawl like a digital sprawl.
I check the final amount for the fare,
my card declines with a sad little air.
I dig through my bag for some loose cash,
but nothing's left but fast food wrappers in my dash.
You left the stove knob set to glow,
let the heat seep in slow, soft flow.
It's not a mistake—it's kitchen art,
you did it from the chef's own heart.
They run through the yard like they're in the air,
chasing sparks in the sun's last-hour glare.
They think each glow is something special, light,
but I've seen that show—they miss the wider sight.
She keeps those old blinds just for the frame,
they bear her late mother's yellowed name.
A thin layer of dust just sits on their trust,
she leaves them untouched with more than just dust.
I build up the drama, they leap into fight,
each punch and each kick under desk lamp light.
We craft a new world with each twist and tale,
till the characters fade and the plastic goes pale.

topic: a phone camera flash too bright
lines: She snaps a photo but it blinds your face,
the moment lost in digital erase.
Her phone's flash flares with too much light,
turning every laugh into stark white.
Your shoulders still hold yesterday's ache,
you lean back and reach for a stretch, a quick break.
Fingers curl slow toward the floor in a bend,
each movement a whisper your body can't mend.
She steps outside where the late sun warms the air,
the scent of lilacs tangles in her hair.
She waits for a signal, a shift, some sign,
but nothing is coming, it's all still mine.
You swipe and you breathe to make it show,
but steam moves in slow, your time is low.
You glare at the mirror, it won't reveal your face,
it's stubborn this morning, like it loves your disgrace.
You blast the AC and roll down the air,
Your bangs flap like flaps of untamed hair.
We're flying down the road, you set the pace,
But I'm screaming, "Slow down — this isn't a race."
She heard the glass bowl hit the floor with a crash,
the cat had already vanished in a dash.
She sighed and smiled, pretending it was an act,
but deep down she knew—he just loved the water fact.
The fog rolls slow like breath across the flow,
whispering secrets only earth knows below.
Distant shapes blur into ghostly light,
I hold my hand out just in case it might.
I hum along to the busker's tune,
his shadow sways beneath the moon.
I clap once, then feel a bit out of tap,
he nods and tips his hat my way—no cap.
My blanket smells like he's been licking the scent,
He didn't ask—he just had his intent.
Now it's soaked with slobber and doggy fur,
I roll my eyes but never quite stir.
You thought your burnt toast was some kind of show,
now the smoke alarm's wailing down below.
You scramble eggs while the room starts to mess,
this morning routine is turning to stress.
You board the wrong bus, head down the new route,
the driver says nothing when you ask her about.
A child points to a sign that swings in the rain,
and suddenly you're early, with minutes to gain.
The cat curls deep into the warmth of the sun,
its purr could soothe a traveler back from the run.
One paw still clutches the old suitcase tie,
as if it's sworn to guard where they learned how to lie.
You say the house feels like a sauna's air,
but I think the temperature is pretty fair.
I don't want to waste money to burn,
so we stand here sweating and never turn.
You've been collecting them for months, gone through
every card but never had the right clue.
You know you should just send them all out, still—
something holds you back, a strange little chill.
She reached for her keys but knocked over the spill,
her lunch bag was soaked from the top to the fill.
Now the bread's all soggy and the soup turned cold,
she sighs with her lunch that feels far too old.
She grabs the socks that were marked down a deal,
humming a tune she can't quite recall to feel.
It's just a quick run, but she makes it a trip,
through aisles and plastic bags, holding on for a grip.

topic: steaming coffee in a blue mug
lines: The coffee rises in lazy, warm steam,
and I let my thoughts blur my dream.
I trace the pattern on this quiet blue,
and wonder which part of me feels most true.
She swore she'd never forget their special date,
but missed it clean while she called her gym mate.
She sent a "Happy Whatever" text out of call,
then shrugged when they said, "You missed it—*what's it all?*"
She swipes through the feed without pausing to view,
faces red, facts unclear, no one feels quite true.
Her thumb hits the dash and she lets out a sigh,
a cat video flashes — she jumps to reply.
Her cough breaks the hush like an old lesson from class,
it rattles the quiet like shattering glass.
I let it fill spaces where my thoughts used to be,
lost somewhere behind her wheeze and debris.
She left the book out, now it's days overdue,
the fine ticks upward in a deep-blue hue.
She tried to return it but found every lock
had changed since last year—this feels like a shock.
You followed the trail of mud from the rain,
leaving more tracks, just to do it again.
Your paws are soaked, but you don't miss a beat,
a mess of joy, all sticky and sweet.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: I posted the meme 'cause I figured it tried,
but no one got it so I just smiled and implied.
The comments were thin and the silence felt live,
the joke didn't land, and the vibe just didn't thrive.
It wasn't just a buzz—it was a loud, proud pop,
the kind that makes your moment just drop.
I reached for the ladder to try and get a hold,
but now the room's a ghost, this place feels cold.
You stare at the blank page, worksheet, or sheet,
you think you're the only one suffering elite.
Your mouse cursor blinks like a dying flame,
while TikTok scrolls by in a distraction game.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: I had a perfect moment, ready for air,
the mic was warm, the crowd felt so fair.
I opened my mouth to speak, meant to say,
it all dissolved when my sneeze blew it away.
You enter the room like warm morning air,
the scent of fresh bread in your golden hair.
I don't even speak, but you know my name,
your smile lights something inside me like a flame.
Your GPS is confused about the way,
It tells you to go where it can't say.
You drive through the mall parking lot's dead car,
then find the address next to a sports bar.
I tap through sunlit shots of foreign sand,
every smile held in another's hand.
They're always somewhere, always that way,
while my own plans slowly go to decay.
You sketch your dream house on the kitchen table plan,
a husband, a dog, a yard with no man-made pan.
You promise to paint while I cook a quick meal,
and laugh when you say it all feels so real.
The doorbell goes off in the dead of the night—ring,
I'm the only one up with this strange new thing.
I stride down the hall, they're still knocking, knock,
I open the door and my dog starts to rock.
I hit send before I checked the tag on the post,
Now my whole class is watching the ghost
of my teacher appear at the top of the name,
I pretend it was intentional—bad game.
They walk through the chill with a grin so cold,
pretending the wind doesn't cut them bold.
Their breath clouds up but they never erase
the lie they wear like a frozen place.
My neighbors tap their windows just to check my ears,
and sigh like this has been going on for years.
I crank the next song for a full-fledged blast,
pretending not to notice I've already passed.

topic: a coffee cup on the curb
lines: A coffee cup lies crumpled on the side,
half-stained, as if someone tried to hide
their guilt with a toss—no cap, no lid,
just waste in a world that no one's bid.
I watched my pen take its final spin,
it rolled so far, it was gone within.
It vanished clean beneath the floor,
but I found joy in the moment's restore.
She watches the water drip out of the slow,
counting each drop like she might somehow grow.
Her hands reach up to fill the glass,
and pour it into the dry cracked grass.
You blink against light that still blinds your eye,
The flash goes off brighter than daylight in the sky.
You wanted to capture a moment to start,
But the glare steals the memory from your heart.
I swore I'd be there on the dot of the time,
but traffic treated my delay like a crime.
You stood under shelter, just hoping I'd wait,
while I fought with the clock and my phone's poor fate.
She lets the wind pretend it's an ocean kiss,
while waves repeat what she'll never say to this.
Her toes are buried in sand along the shore,
and salt clings tighter than love ever did more.
You stop and stare at the fading tree glow,
the colors refuse to simply just go.
The branches catch fire in golden-hued bark,
while you hum a tune like a lazy lark.
I haven't found a single clean pair
since I lost my method for sorting the air.
I just grab one foot, I give it the shrug,
then toss the whole mess back onto the rug.

topic: a friend who is always late
lines: You're late again, which is nothing new in time,
this tardy behavior borders on a crime.
I tell myself you'll show up soon, but not yet,
my patience grows thin, and it feels like a debt.
You say it's for the best, but we're both so old,
you try to act like I never was bold.
Your name now is a memory or a slip,
and mine feels heavy, like something to trip.
I study the smile in the frame so deep,
how their joy stacks up in that happy heap.
Her voice echoes still as they say "That's our vow,"
and for a moment, I'm there—here and now.
I watch him toss the crumbs into the park,
no smartwatch, no phone—no need to remark.
The birds lift off like feathers lost to sky,
and I almost text her just to make her reply.
You knock your coffee onto the room,
the stain spreads like trouble with nowhere to doom.
You laugh instead of crying or faking an act,
because messes are proof that you're living, not fact.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: You say we need to stop and take a new pose,
your hair's still caught in the neighbor's garden hose.
The kids are faking that cheerful fake grin,
Mom's eyes are narrow, this frame looks too thin.
I watched him play beneath the busy street,
his strings trembling in the late-day heat.
I traced his chords with eyes, not hands,
as the song melted into distant lands.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: You twist the key and the lid goes up,
a hollow click in your silent cup.
Inside lies a trinket old and gold,
but you can't decide if you want to hold.
I chugged my soda at warp speed and blast,
sugar and carbonation moved so fast.
A geyser erupted with a sudden boom,
now the mess shouts from this shattered room.
She left the knob cranked to low, just to stay,
watching steam curl from a pot all day.
Her thumb still rests where she moved the hand,
like it's anchoring warmth in a quiet land.
The shovel digs but feels more like a claw,
Winter obeys its own ancient law.
You hunch your back to meet the cold and bend,
Each strike reminds you this won't easily end.
I watch it glide into perfect sight,
the wind moves with every beat of its flight.
It catches a current and begins to soar,
I want now to feel that kind of more.
Your headset dangles in an awkward way,
but it still plays songs all through the day.
You lost the clip long ago without a trip,
now you wear it loose with one-ear grip.
I thought I'd never lose my head or mind,
but left the list where? Not a place to find.
The bread was bought, but now the milk's in bed,
next to a toothbrush, coffee, and my head.
She checked the coupon—yesterday was the date,
now she's scrambling like this is her fate.
She'll pay full price, no more plastic or cash,
the savings are gone, now they're just stress and ash.
You hold your cup with trembling hand,
this street is not the home you planned.
I drop some change and feel so cheap,
you say you need more than they'll let you keep.
You watch the robin hop across the green,
its feathers glinting, a flash once seen.
It pecks the earth where daisies kiss the soil,
and time unwinds in that soft, old spoil.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: The child watches the cloud drift through the sky,
too small to say why but not afraid to cry.
Her red balloon sways like a toy in her eyes,
while strangers pass by full of worry and wise.
You yank the handle but it won't budge or turn,
a long hour trapped inside, a little more burn.
"This is why we can't have nice things," you joke,
as steam rises and mirrors try to choke.
I tap my card but it won't pay the fare,
the screen just stares me back in its glare.
The driver honks — I still have to wait,
and hold the phone from falling to fate.
You stir yourself up with the smell still strong,
you lift your last cup like it's got a song.
The drive-thru is closed, the espresso bar,
but the moon gives a wink from its lonely star.
You flipped it too late, missed the perfect time,
the toaster let out a shrill warning chime.
Now you stare at the crumbs and the dark,
wondering if this was meant to be a spark.
He used to lead the room without a single move,
his hips and hands in sync with every groove.
Now he claps in place when the crowd begins to spin,
afraid to lose control, he dances small within.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: She tucks her cold feet beneath my rest,
my heartbeat warms where her toes are pressed.
The blanket slips low but she won't let it fold,
she grips its soft edge like a reason to hold.
I vaulted the bouncer like climbing a fence,
every nerve screamed this was poor common sense.
But my luck didn't listen or even debate,
the stage was mine—so be damned, that's my fate.
You didn't notice at first—you were in a rush,
but now the stain leaves a warm, pinkish blush.
You wipe it gently, try to leave no trace,
yet hold the memory in a quiet space.
A breakfast tray appears without a hint of tray,
Fresh coffee steams with absolutely no delay.
Her eyes light up the way a sunrise does a smile,
She hasn't left her room for what feels like a mile.
You wedge yourself between the poles and door,
your shoulders aching from the shifting sore.
The lights flicker out somewhere far ahead,
and panic blooms in this jam-packed spread.
Your favorite app was just in full play,
Then suddenly the light went away.
You tap, you sigh, but it won't reboot your game,
So you shrug and say, "It's just my phone's weird name."
The traffic moves in fits and starts, no flow,
horns blare behind me, but I can't just go.
My thumb hovers over "send" — I won't let it hold,
but what if the words I choose are too bold?
The moonlight glides across the lake's wet skin,
It seems to guides my thoughts where secrets begin.
The water stays still, but it's not at all still,
It shimmers like dreams I might try to fulfill.
I crack a joke so painfully old,
they laugh like it's freshly minted gold.
My smile tries to keep up but starts to fade,
I play the fool in their memory parade.
I spent three hours in all kinds of ink,
but you never once asked if I think.
Now the paper's back with no mark or grade,
just your name and a comment that fade.
I watched that squirrel dart across the tree,
tail high and wild and totally free.
It buried something deep beneath the find,
now I'm obsessed—how do I get it off my mind?

topic: waiting for the bus in rain
lines: I step outside into falling mist,
my playlist hums through these wet streets, twist.
A stranger's laugh becomes part of the song,
this wait feels less cold even though I'm still long.
I hit "send" before I had a chance to think,
the wrong words flashed just as my heart began to sink.
It was meant for her, but went to my ex by date,
some glitch of life to twist your darkest fate.
The morning sea wraps me in salt and mist,
It clings to my skin, it burns my wrist.
The waves roll in like a memory's tide,
I close my eyes, and I'm there, deep inside.
The screen won't budge—still stuck on "0.0 read,"
you jog in place but never seem to tread.
A thin layer of sweat meets the frost,
and you lose count of time, minute by lost.
You're lying in bed but still can't resist the scroll,
it's three in the morning and your thumb takes control.
Your eyes start to burn and you sigh with a moan,
you wake up trapped in the blue light zone.
She checks her phone twice to see what it shows,
the screen confirms she's alone in these rows.
Her fingers tighten around the soft grip,
the time ticks louder with each nervous slip.
I'll never know what this sticky note's clue,
it's covered in scribbles and colors in blue.
I take a closer look, but my eyes still are off—
did someone draw a sad hot dog with a cough?
Your voice echoes through the door, still cold,
I wait out here, where you won't let me hold.
I trace the shape of the space where my key
once fit inside you—now it doesn't fit me.
The kind of cold that makes your face glow,
it lingers there like a soft touch or a slow go.
It brushes gently, like a hush on your skin,
a chill from outside that feels strangely within.
You hold the tuning fork close to your tone,
it hums through your hand into flesh and bone.
You press it to silence and listen for hum,
the sound seems to want to stay close and come.
He chases the bubbles that shimmer in air,
pretending they're monsters that float up there.
When they burst and drift softly down,
he grins like the world has just moved around.
I squeeze a ribbon of toothpaste so new,
the morning ahead feels bright, there's a view.
A smile waiting somewhere in the small spark,
even the mirror admits it's not that dark.
He stands by the door like he's glued to the gate,
eyes locked on the hallway, body too straight.
He's already there in his mind, the whole park,
chasing squirrels or barking at the dark.
They linger too close when she walks into view,
She shoots me a smile and says "how are you?"
I force a small laugh and I pretend to try
but every hello feels more like a lie.
The morning sun comes through the kitchen light,
your burnt toast is a blight on coffee white.
You offer me a piece with a shaky hand,
I take it without a word, I understand.
Your heart still picks up its old, familiar pace,
even when there's no reason for this place.
It's your thoughts they chase—your mind won't still,
like secrets in the dark, you try to kill.
You watch the bag swirl in the hot water steep,
the steam curls up slow like your morning sleep.
It's the only thing left in you that feels calm,
this lukewarm excuse for a healing balm.
She needs an inch of legroom for her space,
but the kid's got the whole row on her face.
She stares at the mini snack that counts as a meal,
and dreams of a bed when the plane hits the wheel.
She scans the chaos from left to right,
the crosswalk turns green, the cars still fight.
A tourist steps forward, no one wants to move,
so she walks through the jam like it's her groove.
My phone shows a single sad bar,
it won't wake up even for a star.
I fumble around for an old plug,
it falls flat beside me on the rug.
You stare into the back of the boss's chair,
while silence lingers thick in the air.
They call it "team-building" in PowerPoint code,
but you just want your laptop in focus mode.

topic: paying a fine at the window
lines: You hand over cash to pay your last pass,
the clerk sighs like this is their least favorite class.
The meter's been running since you got here too late,
they stamp the ticket with a new due date.
