Her savings may not feel very gold,
but she's acting with choices more bold.
It's been jammed for hours, wasted my time,
paperless and screaming, this machine's a crime.
Ink's empty, the screen reads "toner out,"
I storm down the hall to find another route.
You play your records loud from eight until home,
the ceiling vibrates like a giant's old dome.
The neighbor waves from her window—she's heard the bass,
but just smiles, shrugs, and says "enjoy your pass."
I need my notes from a lecture last week,
I'm opening folders, I'm scanning, I seek.
There's paper, there's coffee, but still no clue,
this desk is a disaster, I'm just a hot stew.
These flakes were crunchy, not this sad puff,
a soggy mess, a breakfast-type stuff.
I stare into the milk-soaked bowl,
half-wondering if this is my soul.
She held the crust in one greasy hand,
letting cheese dangle over her sand.
"It's got way too much garlic in the oil,"
she whispered through a mouth full of foil.

topic: leaving a note on the fridge
lines: I left a note on the fridge so you'll see,
it's just a reminder that life holds a key.
I wrote it in markers, bold and in hope,
I know we both need something to cope.
At noon the machine chirps in flat, shrill tone,
She's stuck in the kitchen with no one but stone.
It buzzes, "I'm ready," then grinds her new brew,
but she never did trust what the machine knew.
You browse the souvenirs that match the bad theme,
everything priced like a scam or a scheme.
You count your money and almost hand over cash,
then wonder why it feels more like trash.
Your hand brushes mine and there's a spark,
The room feels heavy, like we're stuck in the dark.
You pull away but not before the touch,
A moment like this is more than just such.
She slings her bag with a worn-out strap,
its weight a burden, but not a trap.
Her mind is sharp, her thoughts are kind,
success walks silently, smartly behind.
You watch the moonlight flicker off the gleam,
the surface shivers like a paused-in-time dream.
The water breathes in rhythm with the flow,
but you don't know how long it will still show.
I thought it was just a quick game to play,
but the hours slipped out and faded away.
Now the pencil lingers on smudged-out mark,
and the sky outside turned from light to dark.
Her head's been a thundercloud wrapped in fog,
she lists off her tasks like they're firewood to log.
A breath and a pause now begin to feel calm,
the silence between thoughts becomes gentle balm.
You swear the whole building reeks of this room,
some chemical ghost from last week's deep clean loom.
You open the window just to tell them to stay,
but they only send more mops your way.
You need to pay now but your card says no cash,
the screen just laughs as your plans go to crash.
You charge it all once more, into the debt,
you'll feel it tomorrow—your purchase of regret.
I found a CD in my shelf's hidden gold,
it's got my old band's name scrawled on the bold.
I pop it inside, let the tracks give a spin,
and smile as the music comes back to me within.

topic: a child's drawings on the fridge
lines: I told my kid "Don't leave your art as a mess,"
but they said, "It's cute, just a little bit yes."
Now the fridge's covered in crayon and pink,
I sigh every time I go back there to think.
She's drowning in the clutter of her debt,
each crumpled slip a whisper of regret.
The stack grows higher with every new pile,
but she won't toss them—charms her chaotic style.
It coasts above the sidewalk without a care,
smooth thief of crumbs from my paper plate fair.
Its wing dips once, and I know there's no sting—
it's just us, the sky, and this strange little thing.
She stands beneath the trees where the light still sees,
golden specks dancing like scattered keys.
Time slows as shadows gently begin to falls,
and something deep inside her quietly calls.

topic: steaming coffee in a blue mug
lines: I sip my coffee and pretend it's a lie,
but the steam still curls toward the same old sky.
I curse the day I bought this chipped mug of shame,
as if good coffee ever gave anyone fame.
She stares at your face like she knows it by heart,
but the name slips away from her like soft dart.
There's something familiar—just out of the clue,
maybe we knew each other once, maybe we do.
She moves with the rhythm and never lets go,
her smile catches light and begins to glow.
She opens a novel and starts to read,
her calm presence quietly takes the lead.
She wore one sock with a frayed lace,
the gym called it a fashion disgrace.
But she owns that tear with no trace of fear,
turning damage into her workout gear.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: You stare at the face frozen in that frame,
Wishing they'd stayed the exact same.
Time turns their stories into old joke after joke,
And you laugh until it all feels like smoke.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: I stand there frozen, afraid you won't see,
the morning air whispers "just look at you be."
The world holds its breath like a dropped glass,
where dew clings fragile to the spider's grass.
The field is slick but he still runs right out,
the crowd cheers louder with every shout.
His socks are soaked but he kicks for the goal,
you'd think this game was his whole damn soul.
She carries her umbrella like it still could swing,
though one bent rib won't let it hold the spring.
Raindrops now fall through where the plastic leak,
but she laughs through each squelch, having such a good week.
I twirl with a box that gives no clue,
it's heavy, but no one knows what it's to.
We spin like fools to the rhythm of fate,
laughing while I carry this unknown weight.
She comes from around the corner quite near,
the jingle slides into your ear.
She slows down where the path takes a bend,
and smiles like an old lost friend.
I remember the thrill of the mud being deep,
how we'd run and then shout and then leap.
Now I wash off the stains and the grass from my mess,
and wonder if childhood was better, or yes.
They march ahead as if they're on a race,
I try to catch up, lose my usual place.
Their stories spill out like a faulty lock,
I listen without a word in my stock.

topic: a forgotten lunchbox on the floor
lines: The lunchbox lies abandoned in that spot,
Lunch meat steams and joins the slow rot.
They swore they'd eat it by the third snack,
Now it's just waste no one wants to track back.
He puts the record on and it begins to plays,
the needle wobbles and the music delays.
It skips to disco, gives him some kind of heat,
the chorus loops again—how fittingly repeat.
You called it "charming," this whole rainy sight,
but the wind isn't keeping the door tight.
Your coffee table is now a soggy mess,
and suddenly this feels so much less.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: I clear my throat, take a deep breath of air,
I'm ready to speak, but the moment's not there.
A sudden sneeze rings out sharp and loud,
the whole room turns silent, the spotlight now crowd.

topic: hot chocolate on a cold day
lines: She sips her drink slowly through the gray day,
the frosty world softens and seems to sway away.
Her breath curls up sweet, a wave of warm,
the cold outside fades into a quiet storm.
Your screen flickers and freezes mid-stream,
The lag makes you miss that old dream.
You try one more call but the signal won't hold,
You sit there alone, too far from the fold.
I leave my sock by the door as a treat,
he sniffs it, then chews it—same routine, repeat.
He takes my favorite pair, runs off and stole,
I swear that dog has the sneaky dog's soul.
A kid kicks the seat and screams stuck way too high,
their tears blend with clouds in the windowpane sky.
The passenger shifts but keeps their quiet blame,
while strangers pretend they don't know the child's name.
They wipe their eyes with a trembling hand,
as if they could scrub out love's old brand.
The water runs down the pale face, still fall,
their tears won't stop, there's no healing wall.
Your feet fall silent as they hit the ground,
you don't skip stones or look up to be found.
Each step feels heavy like a memory hold,
the weight reminds me how we both have grown old.
She lets her breath fall into the air,
a small sound of stress slipping from there.
Her shoulders drop toward the soft light,
and for once, the world feels less tight.
I keep checking if my phone might ring,
but nothing arrives—just the same old thing.
I walk back and forth, try to slow my pace,
but time feels like it's running this race.
Your finger brushed mine like a static spark,
We stared at the bench where the pigeons all park.
You say nothing's new, but I know you miss
the warmth of a touch that tries not to fix [this].
She still texts "goodnight" even past her call,
screen lit up late while the cat takes a sprawl.
It's way past midnight—another long hour,
she scrolls in the dark, pretending that's her power.
Her eyes are up, but her mind's in other heads,
She's imagining she's baking perfect breads.
She nods through the meeting, clearly in her zones,
while texting me emojis in between the tones.
You pull them out like a faint thread of hope,
the wires all knotted in a sleepless rope.
They haven't played since that last summer still,
but you keep them close so memory won't kill.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: They blinked mid-laugh or looked away—what a frame!
The caption still says "My Best Friends" by name.
We tried to re-create the shot with new pose,
but time had changed us, down to our plain clothes.
The lens finds your face in the morning's soft haze,
I remember the room, the window's gold blaze.
It focuses slowly, pulling the image through,
like time moves that way only for those we knew.
I gripped the ruler like a stick of chalk,
using it to point and help me talk.
It tapped the board, a rhythm on the edge,
now just a prop stacked on the shelf's old ledge.
You thought you could hide it with frosting and act,
but the crumbs near the door tell the truest of fact.
You baked that cake right, but it's gone now—your loot,
the dog did the crime from the kitchen's dark root.
You watch the rabbit's twitching nose for a clue,
It sniffs a dandelion, licks some old glue.
It freezes mid-hop, scanning the air,
then bolts—some shadow you never could scare.
They schedule appointments with a new kind of hope,
holding tight to a thread thinner than a rope.
Blood is drawn, then more scans and tests,
and in the quiet, they check their rising chests.
You're up until all hours, making it late,
thumping your dishes like you're throwing a plate.
I've texted twice now, but you don't seem to know,
if this keeps up, I'll storm over to show.
They never want to help when it comes to split,
insisting their share would not quite fit.
They argue about what they might still owe,
while you just want the conversation to go.
It landed soft, as though it knew my air,
and studied my fries like a curious fare.
With one quick flap, it tried to carry a wing,
but I laughed out loud at this strange little thing.
You meant to delete but your fingers hit keys,
the draft still hangs there like an old lost breeze.
You read every line on that frozen page,
the words feel alive, caught inside their cage.
I cranked up the beat till my ears screamed in head,
the bass shook the walls and the windows spread.
My neighbor's cereal now trembles in bowl,
but shaking the house is my only true goal.
The line's three deep and the cashier is here,
then rings my name but I'm stuck on my ear.
I fumble the phone, still trying to track
if I have enough cash or will hit a crack.
I swore I'd never forget your usual cold,
this coffee order's not even that old.
You're pointing fingers, but I take no blame—
my phone just auto-filled "hot" full of shame.
She hits every wrong note with reckless delight,
her laugh is a better quote than the lyrics might.
They sway in sync even if they don't know the arms,
it's messy and loud and full of small charms.
They draw a dragon that covers half the mess,
and when you ask, they call it art, not stress.
The markers are weapons, the table a tool,
they spill soda in it like it's pool night cool.
That empty spice jar's got no life left in it,
My wife says it's hiding some old glue or grit.
She swore it would never become a last date,
But here it stands—its spice-filled fate too late.
I watch the cheese bubble toward golden-brown gold,
the crust turns bold with a charred, meaty fold.
I slice through the heat, let the hot air steam,
but it tastes like a memory, not a dream.
I wait for the light to turn green to go,
while cars pretend they don't want to show.
The crowd moves slow, no one sets the pace,
it's chaos disguised as a civilized place.
You need a reason to fix it as whole,
but something about it feels broken at soul.
You trace every chip and you study the crack,
half-wondering if it's worth saving your back.
You curse when the bulb you bought quits its glow,
you feel around shelves in the dark all below.
You fumble a box, almost take a small trip,
your hand finds a ladder but shakes as you grip.
You spill coffee while typing with one mess,
Each keystroke feels like it's going to stress.
Your elbow hits the trackpad—it's about to drop,
You laugh and hold it up with your big toe, prop.
He swears the battery won't let it fully fade,
it blinks red like some dramatic parade.
He searches three rooms for the charging plug,
then trips over the cord that's coiled beneath the rug.
She checks the carton's old, faded date,
then pours it in silence beside her plate.
Her fingers linger on the slow sip,
the way she holds time in a soft grip.
You try to peel it, but it sticks to your skin,
your fingers look like they might just begin.
By the time you're done, your hands feel so raw,
someone should make this an OSHA law.
She lets the salt-heavy breeze untie her hair,
drops her keys in the surf, lets them drift where they dare.
The tide sweeps smooth the stories in the sand,
while she spins with the waves in one wild hand.
The manager speaks in the same old drone,
her PowerPoint slides all have the same dull tone.
I'd rather be driving a traffic lane,
or folding laundry in a coffee shop's sweet rain.
Their thumb still hovers near the screen's soft glow,
They hesitate to let it finally go.
The day has settled into silence, now they fall,
Between their dreams and dusk—their phone's cold wall.
Her backpack sways heavy, she walks down the back,
crammed full of old novels and forgotten class stack.
She pauses to lift it, lets out a quiet sigh,
and tries not to wince when she catches your eye.
I clicked "Remind me tomorrow," now it's late,
my app keeps buzzing, but I missed the date.
They're charging me extra—what a bill,
I used to be calm, but I can't chill.
My usual cup just isn't quite hot,
I need something bolder, I've finally got.
I grind my beans extra fine for a brew,
sipping sunrise from my kitchen's high view.
They both pause mid-bite when they notice the tense,
their eyes say, "I saw you, that's clear defense."
She claims it was hers since she bought the whole split,
he says he deserves it — his mood is a fit.
I was already ten minutes off course and lost,
this app's advice has now officially cost.
It insists we take a shortcut down this route,
and I can't shake the feeling it's all in doubt.
You swear you'll never watch it again,
but the remote clicks you right back on the train.
Every punchline still lands as the same old joke,
yet somehow you laugh like you almost choke.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: He's giving his big speech, full of air,
when suddenly he starts to glare.
A sneeze tears through his carefully planned cold,
now the whole room laughs, he looks absurd and bold.
You bought it last week to outrun the rain,
now every gust adds new stress to the strain.
The handle still promises it can mend,
but you'll never believe that again by the end.
She folds your favorite shirt in soft blue,
and picks out the sneaker that matches your shoe.
Not sure who started this game with such pace,
but you both still play just to light up her face.
You grab a ruler like it's some great tool,
but your hand slips—it's a clumsy fool.
It clatters down the desk and takes a slide,
now you're explaining why it hit my side.
My watch still thinks I'm in another time zone,
I check my phone just to confirm it's my own.
Maybe this glitch is a sign something real
is shifting—like life isn't stuck on a wheel.

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: I found an old stapler buried after years,
its hinge held only by a band that appears
to have been stretched beyond its breaking snap,
like it marked the days on a life's old map.
Her laugh cuts through the room like sudden light,
teeth gleaming brighter than the camera's white.
She strikes a pose, it goes off with a snap,
—but the lens can't catch her in its still-life trap.
You crack the shell with a soft little shell,
there's no mess here—this kitchen's not hell.
Golden liquid begins to swirl,
you smile and whisper, "This meal's for the girl."
You pause to watch the crowd as you cross,
the moment feels too big for this loss.
A car's taillight fades into the night,
your grip remains a little too tight.
You walk slowly where the fallen leaves go through,
remembering how you once felt things grew.
The sun shines bright, but it can't save the day—
the breeze steals moments, cold and away.
You always ran toward the first drop of rain,
knees caked, laughing—something you still remain.
Now you'll never take off those muddy old shoes,
or let go of the joy you somehow still choose.

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: You worked this sweat under the sun you earned,
the kind that clings and feels like it's burned.
It rolls down slow like medals of proof,
and drips off your chin like a leaky car roof.
The toaster gives out a loud warning pop,
she freezes mid-step, her coffee about to stop.
She tries to salvage the charred, blackened sip,
but ends up tossing the mess from her lip.
The tuning fork hums where it rests in the still,
a quiet thrill in the hush of the chill.
Its tone lifts the room just enough to make air
feel lighter, as if your old worries don't care.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: You're watching a documentary, not a show,
but suddenly a laugh plays from below.
Your face feels hot and your voice goes quite dry,
you wish you could vanish and just take a sigh.
She checks the forecast one final time for dry,
then unpacks the blanket beneath the open sky.
The clouds drop water without any blame,
so she folds the chairs while the picnic turns to game.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: They tap the phone against their quiet screen,
count every decimal point to try to mean
something better for a morning they won't save,
while sleep pulls at them like a low-tide wave.
I leave it on, just in case it hums something new,
but no groceries ever seem to come through.
The silence grows louder than any old jar,
I count every snack left between the last bar.
You had the lock and the rust and the key,
the hinge was clogged with last year's debris.
With muscle and grit, you showed off your strength,
the door gave way after what felt like its full length.
I wear my headset on one lopsided side,
it stopped working last week and now it's just died.
My boss insists on a full day of chat,
while my poorly gadget pretends it's a cat.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: You freeze when the balance gives you a shock,
It's past midnight, and the app's old clock
You pour yourself a bigger glass of wine,
but the numbers still won't cross the line.
My scroll has turned to static in the feed,
I've checked my passwords, rebooted, tried to need
a fix that doesn't come—a long slow ping,
while time slips out like dust from some old thing.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: It's been years since we waved goodbye again,
Your comment drops through the blue sky's bright rain.
I click your profile, scan posts from your name,
Then laugh at how fast I once burned for a flame.
You notice the way the morning light
moves golden through the trees' full height.
It dances across your bare, warm skin,
and feels like the world has paused within.
I walked past seven shops before I paid,
the coffee cups all lined up like a parade.
The first sip tasted like a matchstick burn,
but I drank it down to justify the turn.
I tap "send" into the dark full of hope,
tying a message like a knot in a rope.
I wait for a signal, for you to be heard,
while silence sings on like a lonely bird.
You call it a feature, not just plain heat,
it's roasting your jeans and your left side seat.
You swear it's still fast—like you've done no work,
while fans whirr and buzz from some unseen jerk.
You blow a bubble and it pops with a pop,
you chase it faster but it won't help stop.
It shines like glass under some strange glow,
you know it will vanish—still love it, though.
She claims three seats as if they were her space,
arms out like she owns this packed place.
Her heel catches the door—no loss of grip,
she turns it into a show, like it was a trip.
You blow hard until they all float up,
your sister says "bubbles for lunch? Sup?"
You chase every one till you're sweating and far,
the last one winks like a joke from a star.
You followed the arrows, but missed the map,
now you're stuck in this underground trap.
You check your app, but it says "no stop,"
so you guess again from the train's top.
A balloon tugs my wrist and pulls it from me,
it zips off with a breeze straight up to the tree.
The string lassos my head and knots in my hair,
I spin like a weather vane lost in the air.
You hum your way through the stress of the zone,
you tap out a rhythm on strangers' phone.
The line moves so slow but you keep up your pace,
this chaos feels oddly like a happy place.
I've been stuck here since the delayed hour,
lights flicker once—no power.
My feet are numb, but I can't move my feet,
and there's no heat in this steel beat.
You remember how far your body could stretch,
when we had to bend the world to our fetch.
We laughed at the sweat and the terrible tone
of youth—now a band's all it takes to feel grown.
I found a dusty CD buried deep in mine,
the plastic cracked but still a good sign.
It played without skipping, that music so gold,
I held it up high like a story I told.
She watches the sunflower lift up its face,
as if sunlight were something it had to replace.
It chases the glow, it won't sit or seek,
while she stays still, rooted beside the creek.

topic: ice forming on the car windshield
lines: A glacial sheet of glass covers my screen,
The morning street lies hushed beneath the sheen.
I trace the patterns where the frost took hold,
Reminiscing how the world feels long and cold.
That single blink says I nailed every shot,
I'm lighting the room without missing a spot.
The flash flares with a bold, steady light,
this frame is perfect—just as I had it right.
They carry that sigh like a tone from the deep,
a sound shaped by hours of work needing sleep.
They fall into fabric, a soft kind of chair,
where silence wraps close like a warm evening air.
I watched my toast turn dark with silent flame,
the smoke curled slowly, calling me by name.
We laughed over the coffee still hot and brew,
and turned the mess into a quiet "just us two."
She steps on expecting the usual ride,
but the escalator's jammed and won't budge aside.
Stuck between floors, she's a growing trap,
her foot hits the edge—someone shouts, "Don't snap!"
You watch the fish bump against the glass, show
their circles repeating and moving so slow.
A silent pressure builds up into fear,
like the tank knows something's getting too near.
She pokes the lever but it won't budge from toast,
she mutters about bread being the worst, or most.
Her fingers press down, then try once to lift,
the slice finally drops—like a burnt-out gift.
I attempted my first breakfast with a fry,
flipped it over but the bread just came out dry.
The kitchen filled with steam and some smoke,
the staff laughed like it was the best kind of joke.
A flash of joy still flickers in my spark,
but even walking to the park feels stark.
I used to bloom through the morning's gloom,
now I collapse in my sunlit room.
You sprint toward the café's front door,
but your friend's already been waiting some more.
"Let's order," they say, still half-annoyed at the wait,
yet you both laugh—it's a small kind of fate.
The whole block can taste it in the air,
I baked this loaf—no store-bought fare.
There's a warmth in my chest, a swell of pride,
they'll never know how good it feels, inside.
You left the toaster in the morning light,
Its coils still curled like lips held tight.
The sun will soon move on, begin to grow,
but you won't come back to toast your dough.
You slide the clove from its papery skin,
the scent rising faint and familiar within.
You crush it gently with your thumb and press,
and time feels lighter, somehow a bit less.
You say let's invent something wild and new play,
the mission: save Mars before lunchtime today.
You spin the robot on one wobbly foot spin,
while I shout, "Ambush! The base to attack begin."
They flash a single scene, then it's gone, unseen,
the words scream out, "Don't touch that screen."
I hold my breath as the music grows thick,
a whisper of death waits just ahead, quick.
You've tried to fix it but your only tone
is a string of curses as the water moan.
You sit on the floor by the puddle-damp chair,
and scream at the ceiling, "I swear this is air!"
They fall into step perfectly by your side,
humming along as you both sync as guide.
The world feels softer when the music is near,
you share more than a song—you share an ear.
The dishwasher sprays like a broken fire shot,
greasy film clings where it never should spot.
It still makes that loud, proud happy hum,
like it's saying "I work, but you're not gonna come."

topic: finding a dollar in old jeans
lines: I found a crumpled bill in the back pocket, more,
I've been waiting for something good at the door.
This isn't just paper—it's a little bit gold,
so I won't spend it all, but I might just be bold.
You left the cap off and made a toothpaste mess,
the tube squirts out more than there was to get less.
It drips like guilt across the porcelain lip,
and now I'm mad, though I know I shouldn't trip.
I ran through the house in a caffeine dash,
spent all my energy just to get cash.
A surge hit me suddenly—then the wave
of tiredness pulled me down like a cave.
You keep the camera steady on your eyes,
while your mind is busy spinning quiet lies.
You picture clouds or birds, the open sky,
as the meeting drones on without your reply.
I wrote it down as if it had a plan,
a grocery list of healthy, low-cal man.
But every time the hunger came for snack,
I lost my way off that thinning track.
That banana on the counter starts to glow,
the color's proof you won't be able to throw.
You won't put it in bread or even try to save
it for smoothies—no, you just begin to crave.
You follow the path where the deer left their trail,
the sky fades from blue to a ghostly pale.
You stomp for the sake of that crisp, loud sound,
and laugh as the leaves fly up all around.
It digs with care in the soft autumn ground,
pausing to sniff where last year was found.
A trail circles back to an oak's thickened tree,
like mapping a memory buried for a key.
You stand beneath the glow of a synthetic flame,
your face blurred out to make room for the brand's name.
They promise joy, a life they'll help you sell,
but you know this is just the ad hell.
You fumble with the machine, a coin mess,
the receipt says "no" but you still press yes.
Time ticks while you curse this forgotten toll,
your patience leaves—this fee eats your soul.

topic: ice forming on the car windshield
lines: Frost creeps across the glass like cracked old skin,
She wipes it off but it just comes within.
The sun rises late, too weak to melt the slate,
She's minutes late now, her morning fate.
They catch you stealing fries with a stolen eye,
and you pretend you didn't notice their lie.
You laugh too loud, trying to change the spin,
but the silence after cuts way too thin.
They said your bag would be here by now from claim,
but no sign of it anywhere in frame.
The airport's got an art to every delay,
your suitcase still missing, hope starting to decay.
You watch the foil crinkle where it gives way and tear,
a moment of perfection ripped from the air.
You try to smooth it down but the gap won't seal,
and suddenly everything feels less real.
You twisted the batteries until they fit,
your fingers raw from all the stubborn grit.
Now the device glows bright and powers out,
you wonder if it was worth the slow doubt.
She watches the shapeless white sailing through the sky,
her hand moves softly, a little too shy.
The pencil stills when the cloud starts to drift,
but silence feels like a quiet gift.
You stare at the track, wondering when the train
will come while the crowd chooses to remain.
You inch toward the edge, but there's no space,
just shoulders and bags in your tired old face.
You pull the dusty disc from the bin,
hoping the music still fits the spin.
Static crackles as the grooves run deep,
but you're too nervous to fall back to sleep.
He opens his chat and begins to scroll,
he sees no new messages—just the whole.
A meme pops up next, dry and low-joke,
he laughs to himself, "Man, that was well-spoke."
You catch a whiff of someone's cologne in the rain,
it lingers where they sat but doesn't remain.
It makes you think of something bittersweet and deep,
how strangers leave things only time can keep.
You stand there watching the field begin to sway,
A whisper of motion moves it far away.
The breeze hums softly, a sound like a call,
And you feel lighter, as if you could be all.
I double-tap and then I double-check my tap,
a thumbs-up halo lights up from my cap.
You see the reaction to your shared post,
and ask if I'm flexing—nope, just a ghost.
I check the time again and the clock
shows numbers that feel like a rock.
My mind floats in the morning's haze,
missing hours I'll never get back these days.
She tried to act cool when it hit her lap,
but the table was set like a coffee trap.
Now there's a ring where the white shirt stain
makes everyone laugh when she tries to explain.
I'm seated beside a man on this ride,
and he won't stop talking—there's nowhere to hide.
He isn't to blame, but still I chase blame,
acting polite in a not-so-subtle game.
You pull the cord out like some cursed string,
the mess becomes a whole new kind of thing.
It's coiled so tight it feels like cosmic fate—
but really, you just lost your earbud debate.
The waves roll in, the world feels still,
A lone gull calls—it's my quiet thrill.
I leave no footprints in the wet sand,
As morning holds me in its warm hand.
She keeps the volume off but never the bell,
her phone is all she checks when she feels swell.
Her fingers hover, quiet, over the still,
as if the world could change with a quick reply's will.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: They tried to play cool but it just wasn't a joke,
The laugh track cut in like a burst of old smoke.
They paused, unsure how to act or speak out,
But you saw through it all, full of quiet doubt.
You toss it like dice to see where it will roll,
half hoping it lands near your bare-boned soul.
It plops near a log where the moss hides a hog,
and suddenly laughter lifts up from the fog.
I left my sock on the gym locker floor,
now only half my shoe feels properly wore.
Its seam's come undone at the frayed-out thread,
but walking barefoot won't help me walk ahead.
Years of coffee spills now lock in the food,
My keyboard clacks in a sour mood.
I miss the clean, sharp tap of the real,
The stuck keys whisper of a broken seal.
She plops down hard in her rented-out chair,
while clouds and her coffee both stain the same glare.
The wind steals her hair tie, messes her mood,
and knocks all her chips into soggy old food.
She laughs like they're cracking some sacred code,
her eyes lit up all the way down the road.
We don't know why, but we're laughing too—just roll,
it's silly, but feels like the whole world's our soul.
The sky blazes pink like a hidden flame,
you try to spot birds by their call or name.
The branches bend under the fading light,
the last rays send shadows dancing tight.
She never checks the app where the list is lead,
her phone can wait—she's got a better head.
The grocery bag stays full, no need for a trip,
she holds it firm in one hand with a tight grip.
You watch your cat like she's lost in her mind,
hypnotized by the creak of the wind.
She sees a world with no trace or clue,
and somehow you feel lucky just being her too.
I squeezed too hard and made a toothpaste mess,
now the mirror's frosted, so who can tell or guess?
I leave it there without replacing the cap,
next user will blame the drain if it clogs the trap.
I leave my sketchbooks in a colorful mess,
who knows if it's art or just nonsense I guess.
The coffee goes cold next to the chair,
while I argue with ghosts in the blank page's air.
I checked my messages but they're still out,
I tried to laugh but it felt like a shout.
I left a hint like a riddle or key,
but no one noticed it was meant for me.
You stare into the glow of the screen,
your weary mind is turning off like a machine.
Your eyes drag slower than a buffering lag,
but you still call it style — let those lids sag.
I've been waiting here since the tail-end of queue,
not a single car moves under this blue.
Pedestrians laugh as they walk safely cross,
I count every second as sanity's loss.
I found a bit of you stuck under the trace,
still warm from where your lips had pressed your face.
You never meant to leave this tiny mark,
but time won't lift the ghost you left me in the dark.
She runs through the yard chasing every glow,
the light flits away and won't let her go.
Her hands close around just a whisper of catch,
the bugs laugh like sparks as they slip out of snatch.
You hit play and only one side starts to play,
the left earbud vanished since the break of day.
You listen with one ear, you almost don't miss
half the lyrics—how could you ever miss this?

topic: a gym membership you never use
lines: I signed up with the credit card I paid,
then stored my badge where no one would parade.
It's still in the frame by my front room wall,
a trophy for a goal I never recall.
She's MIA but expects us to have a clue,
the project's due today and she's nowhere due.
We split the work, but still tell the same old lie—
her share vanished like confetti in the sky.
She ignores my wave and takes her time with the call,
like this whole grocery store is still her mall.
Her phone keeps ringing, she answers every ring,
while I wait behind her, near the end of my thing.
The neighbor's dog won't stay out of your mind,
You're not cruel—but you wish it were blind.
You mutter to yourself about dogs that will talk,
Then sigh, because now you want to take a walk.
I dropped the bowl and lost all that crunch,
now breakfast feels like something gone for lunch.
I leave the mess and go find a dish,
but nothing's fresh, just crumbs and a wish.
You wake up tight as a jar of jam,
your brain clacks out a tired ham.
Your thoughts are heavy as melted lead,
you chew your toast like it's your last bread.
She leaves a damp towel on the bench as a clue,
its edge curled toward me in a soft, sad blue.
I step back to avoid that wet, brown spot,
but my foot slips and sprays her with a cold shot.
He pries open the cap at the very last end,
like maybe it's haunted or cursed by a friend.
The tube lies there squashed, all sad and flat,
not giving him even a tiny bit fat.
You stare at your reflection, not fully clear,
the steam from the shower still clings to your ear.
You draw slow circles that won't leave a trace,
and wonder where time left its quiet face.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: You spot a silver strand against your crown,
you trace it gently, smiling from ear down.
These hairs don't scream old—they whisper your age,
you wear them now like a hero on the stage.

topic: seeing your mom's new profile pic
lines: She posted her pic with that new hair style,
a filter brightened up her whole damn smile.
It clashes with her look—just don't ask why,
I'm dying but I'll say "oh, I love that, sweet pie."

topic: checking if you have enough for gas
lines: I check the gauge and my heart skips a mile,
I try to laugh but can't fake the smile.
The needle nears empty, my fuel tank,
my savings just dropped like my luck when it sank.
She had one job but now we have no clue,
the whole thing's hanging late, it's so overdue.
We split the work and she was left alone,
her silence screams in every message tone.
Your laptop's glowing like an angry fire,
and every app still runs with full wire.
It melts the fabric where your jeans meet heat,
while "reboot" blinks—this message won't repeat.
You stand beneath the old oak tree,
where branches sway and birds are free.
A breeze moves slow across your skin,
I feel it too, deep down within.
I float near the center where the water runs still,
waiting for the quiet to finally take will.
My reflection is soft, my thoughts on my face,
and tonight feels like the calm I need to replace.
You found him perched inside your closet room,
his whiskers twitching where your boots once loom.
He nibbled the laces—your sneaker as snack—
you leave fresh grass trails around the back.
She steps into the band's elastic loop,
pretends it's a dragon she must keep coop.
With a stretch and a laugh, she gives it a bend,
the band groans but stays her good workout friend.
Your boots hit the pavement hard, a steady beat,
you sweat through your shoes and you're into the heat.
You leave marks behind, not trying to trail,
just walking your story, a tale with no fail.
She sips the last drop and twists the cap down,
watching the sunset across the town.
Her day was long, her steps slow to walk,
but she's too tired now to really talk.
You watch the kettle begin to sing,
it's steam venting off like a magical thing.
The room gets misty, it almost looks like sky,
you laugh and ask the pot, "Why so spry?"
It creeps along the garden's soft edge,
as if it made a quiet peace pledge.
It pauses to nibble, I crouch down to see,
maybe it's time I let vegetables be.
He's got a rhythm when he digs for his nut,
precise and focused, never once off-cut.
The garden looks like it's been plowed for a bed,
and he's the boss of this little dirt head.
You watch as your pup goes round and round, spin,
but you know there's joy hidden deep within.
The chase may seem endless, but hope won't end,
you're not just a pet—you're a loyal friend.
That blue streak hit the floor where once we stood,
The drip still reminds me of the things you would
say while pretending this was just a little mess,
but now I see the room feels somehow less.
You move your tongue across the wall so slow,
like you could taste some truth I don't yet know.
The pattern's random, but you won't let it fix,
your breath a quiet hymn between the bricks.
The sky is wide and brushed with blue,
the robin hops right through my view.
I used to call it by its name,
now I just watch it stay the same.
She watches the old vinyl spin, slow and turn,
each crackle like a memory trying to burn.
Her fingers trace the dust on the edge of the hand,
as if time might settle gently in this soft land.
A dog starts barking from the back, won't stop,
Its tail sticks out the carrier like a crop.
The driver yells, "Who owns this line?"
I raise my hand—it's not my mine.
Your hand brushed mine like a match struck too flame,
I swore for a second I heard your old name.
We held it all silent between us and air,
like ghosts in a photo, unsure of the where.
You match my stride like we set the pace,
but you don't know where this leads or what place.
I'll pretend your jokes land well, don't fail,
I'm leading the walk, just stay off my trail.
The pawn fell hard when the player tried to move,
a slight nudge meant to reveal what they could prove.
The table trembled from where the glass stood still,
and silence passed through the room like a chill.
You stand by the fence where the front gate is tight,
The postman debates if he'll charge past your sight.
Your dog picks that moment to let out a bark,
That leaves him with nerves and a quick exit mark.
You blow hard at the cake's final blast,
expecting to celebrate being passed.
But your breath turns it into a silly joke,
and we all laugh until there's no smoke.
The fog moves in like it's late and feels slow,
you wanted sunrise but here it won't go.
It coats your boots with a gray, wet dust,
you can't even trust your own damn crust.
A plastic bag flaps in the dry air,
it snags on twigs and knots your hair.
You're sure it's a ghost from some past life, or code
from a grocery store on some long-lost road.
You feel the cold kiss where they touch your skin,
each flake dissolves fast as it lands within.
They fall like secrets too shy to stay tall,
and vanish before you can catch them all.
I won't let that app tell me what to ask,
I turn down each request, no matter the task.
I won't just give in or be browbeaten by gave,
my privacy's mine—I will never cave.
I drive past another fake "all-natural" real,
for a meal that's just plastic and processed appeal.
It's all hot air wrapped in a shiny lie,
I wish they'd stop testing what my eyes try.

topic: a child drawing on the table
lines: That kid turned the whole damn table to mess,
and somehow I'm the one who gets to guess
how long until someone slams something off
and scolds me for letting it happen so cough.
You always seem to run out of an hour,
but never your battery or your power.
The barista calls your name twice in a shift,
and you hand me coffee like it's the world's gift.

like a ghost in the shadows that never would loom.

which isn't food anymore—it's just mean.
The bag is damp, the peas have long gone bag,
and still he opens it like a delayed gag.

it's freedom speeding through the hell.

your heart lifts—just for a second you feel.

You stare at the glass, another mess,

It clings like your doubts—your soft, smudged trust.

while your loud chewing fills the room with din.
The fabric soaks in every slobbery mess,
you've claimed this blanket as your proud success.

lines: You're sitting on a bench with an open book,
a pigeon pecked the crust you just took.

the breeze flips pages—start again, repeat.

and now the code's a mystery that won't escape.

my dog just dripped joy all over my blue.

the juice bursts sharp and tart within.

but the taste feels like a memory grown old.

as if we were listening through a coffee glass.

she draws a lily in her favorite cream.

and makes herself pretty without a trace.
I feel the slow pull of the strap against my weight,
but carrying this load feels like sealing my fate.
Each step bends my spine like a branch in the sway,
yet somehow it's peaceful, this ache of the day.
They serve the pasta like it's their last dish,
and dust it with cheese, fulfilling each wish.
Their movements are slow, precise and low,
the grater shines bright like a memory's glow.
You blast your music so loud, it's your own way,
I know you're trying to drown out the day.
It's not about the bass or the beat or the blue,
it's how you play it just for me, and that feels true.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: Your shoulder fits perfectly next to you,
My thoughts drift quiet, calm as snowflakes through.
Your warmth lifts something heavy off my weight,
This calm is now my favorite quiet state.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: A notification pops up with your name,
five years since the last message or flame.
They liked your latest update on the post,
and you feel seen more than you've felt the most.
I catch you staring at my piece through your eye,
you say it's no big deal with a grin and a lie.
You sneak it when my back is turned, you take what's left,
A crime of hunger, but still a cold theft.

topic: steaming coffee in a blue mug
lines: They brew their coffee with quiet and calm,
steam curls from the mug in their steady palm.
It's not just a drink—it's a practiced art,
they savor each sip as if reading a chart.
You find the rabbit gnawing under the dusk,
your leather cracked where his tiny teeth left musk.
He's soft as the fur that drapes off your silk,
but you'd trade every drop of fresh milk
His fingers press down but the lock stays tight,
he breathes on the metal to warm up the light.
He tries every twist of the old worn-out key,
and waits for the click that sets it all free.
I follow the glow as my eyes do their chase,
it lands on a spot where the gold finds its place.
I lift up the lens and I hear it go *snap*,
the world turns to pixels and codes on my map.

topic: sitting on the porch steps at twilight
lines: The air turns crisp, and I welcome the chill,
but you're already here to fill my coffee still.
My thoughts are quiet—just let my mind unwind,
this isn't a meeting; it's not the daily grind.
She swears this isn't the first time in jam,
but you'd think she was selling some gourmet ham.
She gives the machine one last dramatic act—
it still won't print, which is the cold, sad fact.
I built them high, that paper-high height,
hoping time would not undo what I might.
Dust has settled into those quiet years,
and I wonder now if I cried any tears.
You show up early, ready for work,
your group chairs remain stubbornly lurk.
You split the slides and you take it alone,
but send your thanks with a soft, hopeful tone.
I helped write this film from the script to the done,
we stayed up all nights having wild, secret fun.
Now the credits scroll fast, you can barely see,
but my name is still there — like a hidden key.
You press repeat on the piano's soft keys,
the melody creeps in like an old disease.
Your tears fall slow but they refuse to spill,
until the last note gives your sorrow the will.
Your morning starts with toast, not your alarm,
you swear this bread was baked on a charred-out farm.
You show your kid the perfect blackened char,
"Look, a burnt marshmallow—let's call it a star."
You watch the river mirror the bruised sky,
the clouds weep down like a quiet cry.
A pebble sits there, smooth and cold as stone,
and you wonder why you still feel alone.
A hawk drifts lazily across the sky,
I watch it soar where I wish I could die.
It rides the updraft, pulled by the wind,
while I stay grounded, left far behind.
I retraced my steps through the crowded park,
someone mentioned keys by the water's remark.
I scanned the path hoping for some small clue,
a glint in the sunlight changed my bad view.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: I miss the easy joy of that warm day,
when childhood and the earth led me to play.
I tried to find my old mud-kitchen spot,
but time blurred the edges and I forgot.
I turn the page like it's the last of my time,
each word a memory, each pause feels like a crime.
The corners grow dusty from fingers that dust
the story forward, desperate to be thrust.

topic: laughing too hard at a joke
lines: Your laugh cuts through the room, clear and loud,
It silences everyone in the crowd.
I barely finish the punchline I catch,
but you steal the moment—you snatch every match.
I pile my cart with snacks and some art,
the cashier says, "You really are a bit smart."
She double-checks the code, scans the wrong can,
I laugh out loud—it was my masterful plan.
She swipes her card twice but still runs late,
the train has long left from the other gate.
She checks her phone—no saved e-tickets to scan,
she sighs and buys another doomed round-trip plan.
I left my shoes out in the rain all through,
the water soaked my socks and they grew.
I won't complain or wish it could be all,
I'll dry them slow against this sun-warmed wall.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: You tap the name you haven't seen in face,
A ghost appears in your comment space.
Their notification pops with sudden glow,
Then disappears before you can say "Hello."
You dive back into that sunny past,
Each photo a memory, vivid and fast.
You swipe left or right just to seek,
the best moments of your perfect week.
You let the ketchup arc in a careful stream,
a masterpiece of mess, your joy supreme.
Not a single drop hits the food—it just drip-
down your chin, and you grin and call it a trip.
She left a small note with no real clue,
just a smiley in yellow against the hue.
I glance at the screen and I read the spot,
and laugh because I already had got.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: The child walks alone toward the blue sea,
clutching a balloon still bright and free.
Strangers pass by, they do not hear his cry,
the wind takes the ribbon into the sky.
The cart won't budge and it's stopping the flow,
people just sidestep, but you try to go.
You shout "Let me through!" as if space could pass,
the store feels like traffic trapped in a mass.
They always leave it upright by the time,
like a ritual in morning's soft prime.
It waits there quietly, wet still at rest,
a gentle fixture in their little nest.
She's not what you'd call young or very old,
but there's strength in how she still can hold.
One flickering flame becomes a tiny fire,
no need for a hundred—just one real desire.
She borrows your sweaters off the shelf,
layers them up like it's all for herself.
You leave your things out with the hope it's trust,
but every time she takes, it feels like dust.
The sink is a battlefield, plate-stacked mess,
I'll have to figure out who left this guess.
A week-old soup bowl starts to really smell,
this cleanup feels more like a trip to hell.
A faint pink stain circles this coffee stain,
I remember how she left it there again.
Her name's still etched inside the chipped-up cup,
as if she might show up to drink it up.
I found my old headphones down there in the ages,
the cord so knotted it could win some rages.
I plug it in, half expecting a flat tire,
it plays one song—then cuts out, total liar.
I feel the weight slowly coming out,
I didn't mean to let it all come shout.
Words stumble forward, they won't stand tall,
but you listen close without making me call.
You watch in silence as your cat licks the spot,
her tongue moving slowly in methodic dot.
There's clearly no reason, no pest or no clue,
she's just licking the wall like it's something to glue.
It's three a.m., and here comes the time,
the doorbell insists it's a late-night crime.
He picks up his bag and he answers the door,
and finds just a cat and a box marked "for more."
I tried to act calm when my card said no cash,
I tapped it again with a frustrated dash.
The numbers keep climbing, I'm deep in my debt,
and every small purchase feels like cold regret.
You now drink straight from the pitcher, not your glass,
It's hydration with flair, you said, "This is class."
You even skip coffee to help you money save,
Your Instagram story calls you hydration brave.
He stands there in the grass with his net alone,
eyes locked in some quiet, bug-hunting zone.
A breeze might try to mock him, but he won't shake,
he's out here to collect wings, not to take.
You savor every word before you flip,
your fingers tight in a loose grip.
It's quiet now, and getting kind of late,
but the story won't let you through the gate.
You put your toaster up there just to be told
that no one gets the joke except your old gold
It's fused to the windowsill, stuck open-lid,
pretending it's a spaceship from some other kid.
You retrace your steps through every bare room,
retracing choices, chasing yesterday's gloom.
The key's still out there—somewhere in the lock,
you're running short on time and spare stock.
I wound the music box to find a key,
but all it opened was old debris.
The ballerina still tries to twirl,
while I'm stuck being her backup girl.
It holds its fragile weight in perfect pose,
landing gently on the half-open rose.
You watch how briefly life can stay on wing,
then vanish like a dream too soon for spring.
You stand by the sink where the plates won't rest,
remembering meals that used to be your best.
The clock ticks too loud, the silence feels late,
and guilt pools in you like the water's cold weight.
You spot your name on the corner, crisp and bright, [tag]
but the artist forgot to sign it and drag.
A smiley face smiles in bright green spray paint, [code]
you read it as an impromptu street ode.
She finally found the last missing clue,
it was the only one in that exact hue.
The whole table held its breath when it fit—
then she dropped a corner, lost the neat bit.
A small bird bounces along the low sky,
it balances hard when it starts to fly.
Its beak lifts to test if today it will sing,
one step forward is half of a spring.
You thought it was easy to guard your small plan,
but the cat's wild antics make you their new fan.
The bowl hits the floor with a loud, proud spill,
and you laugh—because nothing could change your will.
I tried to add weight to my max PR lift,
but now the bar won't budge—just stays in its shift.
I breathe deep, focus, engage every core,
and believe that the grind will get me a lot more.

topic: a child drawing on the table
lines: I let it stay—looks like abstract art,
a scribbled mess without a single heart.
My sandwich waits, but I lose my meal,
half-chewed and smudged by their tiny real.
It loops again, the song won't stop its play,
I've lost track of where my grief went away.
I almost want to hear it once more to hold
the ache that feels so familiar now it's old.

topic: a cart with a broken wheel
lines: I watched the cart wheel wobble, refuse to spin,
its metal scream cut through the late-night din.
My spine groaned as I tried to lift it alone,
my elbow screamed, I swore I heard a bone.
I've played my worst tune on this crowded street,
The moon's a bad listener, doesn't even cheat.
A quarter drops in—my first bit of cash,
I smile and I bow, but I won't pretend to flash.
I hit replay but the song won't play,
the app says buffering—just a delay.
I restart the app, reboot, try to fix,
it's not a glitch, it just hates my tricks.
They left the window open, still in the frame,
as if their ghost might drift in by some name.
The rain taps gently but can't make them cold,
they've always been this soft, this love so old.
He yelps at the ceiling fan, convinced it's air,
then jumps to the couch where a shadow's his hair.
The neighbors call it a dog with a ghost,
but I think he's just mad at the mail truck's new post.
You stare at the pigeon like it's from the sky,
It pecks with delight while you try not to cry.
Your meal was a lunch of salted fries,
Now gone in a bunch—your appetite dies.
She hesitates at the red light brake,
unsure if this is a mistake.
The radio plays a quiet hum,
but she's waiting for you to come.
She hesitates at the counter, late for the bar,
unsure if they take cards or need cash or a star.
Her phone freezes twice when she tries to scan code,
while the line grows long behind her like an ode.
She leaves the list home and forgets half the head,
she buys only essentials like eggs and fresh bread.
The groceries go untouched on the dusty shelf,
she opens the fridge and smiles at herself.
You blow the bubbles straight up into the air,
You chase them yelling, "I'm number one there!"
They pop before touch, just an empty lie,
You grin and say they're now drawing in the sky.
She wanders the buffet like it's some grand spread,
but everything tastes like it came from the dead.
She can't find a single thing worth the move,
even the pastries lack a basic groove.
One lace goes slack mid-stride, my string hangs loose,
The rhythm breaks—what was I thinking, use?
I glance ahead, my pace gives way to fear,
The finish line looms far in the rear.
They said the scent was supposed to feel clean,
but something about it felt a little mean.
He'd sniff it like a memory or a rose,
and for a moment the room just kind of froze.
You took out the old ones, each still faintly gold,
they held your last memories, stories long bold.
The new ones won't remember or keep them from fade,
you miss the old charge that once lit your parade.
I watched it vanish from where it stood, took,
my thoughts caught on the memory like a hook.
Now the space feels hollow, no hood or car,
just echoes of keys by an empty drink bar.
You held your ground beneath the pouring game,
the crowd roared out their thunderous acclaim.
The field was mud and the sky was full of storm,
but your team's spirit felt like fire, so warm.
I watch the rain try to erase your trace,
it runs like tears down this dirty glass pane's face.
Her fingers linger, slow and still,
her breath is soft as fog on a quiet hill.
The clock says ten, but I delay the end,
I flip through old texts, time won't quite bend.
The silence feels loud without your voice,
so I sleep early—it's the easy choice.
I left my bottle on the gym bench's top,
or maybe dropped it when the bus slowed down to stop.
I'll find it soon, I bet it's near some aisle,
I jog the track, half-drained, for just a little while.
That flicker's your design, let the walls know,
the old house can't hide how it's starting to show.
You fixed the old lamp, checked each frayed wire,
now the light dances like a proud little fire.
I used all my time but I didn't feel spent,
I drew through the mess, none of it got bent.
You'll say it's bad art, but I poured in my art,
the worst kind of bad is what's missing a heart.
I was halfway through my favorite song to play,
the screen went dark in the middle of the day.
The melody stopped where it was about to fade,
like the moment itself disappeared into shade.
I watched it peck through the mess on my chip,
the thief balanced well on the paper's thin grip.
It tilted its head toward the dull, gray sky,
then flew off, leaving crumbs where the truth would lie.
I sent the final text without a hint of stress,
now the conversation's tied in a quiet mess.
I muted your call—no need for a farewell brawl,
you're just a username that I let gently fall.
You left that carton past its printed date,
but said it's just *sour*, nothing to be late
for breakfast—ha, ha, a real groan-worthy joke.
Now you're pretending not to want to choke.
He says the morning is full of claims,
but the fog rolls in and puts out the flames.
He swore he knew where the road goes,
now the world's white and his map just shows.
I perfected the swift, silent double-tap,
my phone's camera flash has never missed a cap.
It's not just a swipe—it's a statement of pride,
I scroll with a purpose, I don't just stride.
I press my thumb into the clove, so bare,
the scent blooming sharp in this quiet air.
The paper-thin layers fall away from skin,
leaving something raw but whole again, within.
You feel the rhythm in the wheel's quiet roll,
your balance and courage feel part of your soul.
The path curves left but you don't need to bend—
the gravel sings, and you fly down your friend.
I break the silence with a nervous air,
you twist your fingers through your dark hair.
I try a joke, but it falls flat as toast,
you laugh too loud—I think you're just faking it, most.
I pretend to care about this stale old air,
while dreaming of my desk, my cubicle lair.
They talk about the new update to code,
I'm on mute, again, in ghosting mode.
You told me your usual and never the name,
I ordered the coffee, you said it's not the same.
I wrote down the brand but lost the whole post,
now you're sipping from mine as I walk the long coast.
Their bass vibrates through my walls and my beat,
I crank up the volume to match their heat.
I blast every song with a smirk on my face,
I'm louder than them, I won this race.
Your headset dangles on one ear, one side,
you pretend it works, but we both know we hide.
It's not the cord or the volume—it's your fate,
you'll never fix it, but you'll argue the debate.
You stand there calm as a summer breeze,
the jingle of your keys lost in the trees.
The bird watches the sky without a care,
and you wonder why you ever got so rare.
The map on my phone turned all shades of green,
The arrows on screen just keep spinning unseen.
I've missed three express rides trying to hide,
Stuck between hope and a growing tide.
You thought your secret was flawless, your plan,
but someone let slip "surprise" to the man.
The balloons are up, the cake's ready to blow,
and now you're pretending you knew this would show.
He squashes the tube until it's all a waste,
smearing mint across the mirror's glassy paste.
His thumb still makes that old familiar twist,
like we were still together—now he's just missed.
It happens again in my favorite spot,
the cat acts like some proud little tot.
I want to be mad but I just can't,
I clean up the mess from the potted plant.
She waited at the light that wouldn't turn green,
arms crossed like she owned the whole scene.
Cars honked, but she stayed put to prove
that patience could outlast the wrong move.
She waters the soil with a weary old bed,
her phone lies nearby but she keeps her head.
The tulips just bloom, bold without any scheme,
while she fills this small room with a quiet dream.
Your thumb hovers, a heartbeat from a thumb,
it taps once—too timid, not even a drum.
You ask me why I bother feeling why,
I guess I'm just chasing some digital high.
My hamster spins until the world feels spin,
then blinks as if the motion never begin.
He's king of his cage, but it's a tiny stage,
where every loop just rewrites the same page.
He shifts his weight like he has some clue,
the bike jerks sideways into my view.
"It's all part of the ride," he says in his style,
as the handlebars shake him side to side while.
She picked a quiet bench in the afternoon park,
every word she spoke felt like the same remark.
There was silence between us, thick as the heat,
I left that first date, swore I'd never repeat.
You tiptoe across the floor with bare feet,
Your toes shiver but you laugh out your heat.
The morning sun warms one small patch of tile,
You dance toward it, a slow little smile.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: You wake before sunrise to see the blue sky,
the world is still holding the last lie.
A dewdrop hangs fragile on a thread,
and silence begins to quietly spread.
My dog sits by the door and stays so still,
his eyes say "we'll leave now" if I just will.
He's begging with paws for that morning walk,
we've already said all we need to talk.
She taps the screen but still gets no clue,
the GPS blinks "Recalculating—new view."
She keeps driving, trusting it will come out,
but deep down she can't shake her doubt.
I left the old loaf sitting in the bin,
now it's fuzzy and blue on crust and skin.
The stench is so thick it fills the room to smell,
this kitchen is turning into a rancid hell.
They shoved three more in each single seat,
The prof just lectured the same old repeat.
The stale air hummed with the buzz of despair,
But no one dared leave — this was their share.
You've been stuck for miles without any move,
Even the radio can't help you find your groove.
Your phone's map still shows "Merge Ahead—No Map,"
So you laugh and call this high-speed trap.
She watches the bunny sniff the morning air,
one tiny nostril working, pink and bare.
There's something in how he sniffs, a hidden clue—
maybe joy is just breathing, and this is true.
Your camera hunts for the perfect bright,
it frames the world as if it's pure sight.
You wait for clarity, but the lens still can't find,
you laugh—it's the chase, not the catch, in your mind.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: She swears she paid in full for the weekly cash,
but the app keeps flashing a fee she can't slash.
She counts the days left 'til the due date for rent,
then sighs and calls her cat her new life's content.
I crank up the heat until it feels warm,
then sit here and smile like a happy little form.
The house finds a balance, slips into its own zone,
and hums along with a comforting tone.
The u-lock is frozen, it won't come un-tight,
I tap on the shackle beneath morning light.
I wiggle the key in the rusted-up key,
maybe today's the day it decides to be free.
You hold up the fork and it hums a lone tone,
the metal feels warm where your hand rests on stone.
You listen until the sound starts to fade,
hoping it brings some strange help or aid.
She flips ahead to check if today's date
still holds the ink from last year's debate.
A note in red is scrawled in her hand,
"Don't forget" turns to a half-erased demand.
I hold the band like I'm holding time itself, stretch,
a moment I know I will never fetch.
It tugs me toward some unspoken bend,
where my body and willpower both wish to mend.
I blame the bulb for the light's faint cast,
but maybe it's just getting worse, not past.
I consider fixing it, going to the door,
yet part of me likes how it fades a little more.
Her face is a billboard for every fake dime,
she clocks it down to the practiced "nice time."
That grin could pass for a corporate mask,
but she's good at it — just another retail task.
She stands at the water's edge where the sky runs blue,
the clouds drift slowly by, soft as she moves through.
Her face is lifted up, like she might try to see
the world as something whole, and not broken or fee.
She longs for the thrill of buying one thing more,
but her card just says "declined" at the store.
She calculates how much she still owes in debt,
and wonders if this is life's quiet regret.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: You refresh the page, then read your name in post,
thinking maybe you're a ghost they finally boast.
You zoom out from the comment, check the screen,
no, it's not a glitch—you just don't get to mean.
I wake up to that glorious engine's roar,
it shakes my whole house, right down to the floor.
He cuts every blade with a skill from the cut,
his yard's a green masterpiece while my shack's a hut.
I clipped another link to the bend,
the chain now drags close to the end.
It's fragile but steady, it's meant to grow,
and someday it might catch a glow.
That dog was your best buddy and closest friend,
he waited by the fridge for the party to end.
I saw you smile when he took one last lick,
the way he danced away still feels like a trick.

topic: tea leaves steeping in a cup
lines: You watch the leaves swirl and they slowly twist,
the way your hands move when you rest your wrist.
The air grows thick with the warmest steam,
and for a moment, it feels like your quiet dream.
You found a crumpled gum stuck to the spot,
still sticky where your date's kiss had got.
Time softens even the sweetest truth—
but that bit of gum still smells like your youth.
She tapped the screen for the song to play,
but the playlist skipped and went its own way.
Her head turned back as the next track began to spin,
she groaned, "Please restart from where you should begin."
Their bass is rattling my walls with a beat,
I crank my kettle to blast some heat.
I raise a mug like a weapon, loud and up,
"Time to turn down your racket," I yell and sup.
You wave the cereal box but it won't scan,
the machine stares back, no clear plan.
It asks you again for the price code,
and you're stuck in this loop, no escape mode.
A voice booms out across the echoing floor,
some system's crashing—tell me what to restore.
I freeze mid-step, but I don't want to mind,
the chaos surrounds me, I feel completely blind.
You twisted the knob until your face turned blue,
but the lock still clicked shut, just as I knew.
I whispered, "Let's just leave it be and stay,"
but you tried again, without turning away.
She types "blue sky" but it changes to wrong,
her thoughts drift up, chasing butterfly along.
It hums through her screen with such fragile wing,
and disappears—just a glitch or a thing?
There's not a single clue where I should start,
my fingers slip in carrot juice and art.
One wrong move here and I'm sure to trip,
this knife's too big, I've lost all grip.
I remember the soft, accidental hue
of frosting smudged there on this child's cheek, due
to a birthday cake collapse in thick, slow trace—
now every mess feels like a grown-up's face.
Your stomach has started to rumble and grow,
But you wait until after dinner to go.
You reach for your card—and your gasp at the cash,
The cart hits the wall, your groceries all crash.
She promised a chapter but missed every clue,
now we patch the report with bad glue.
We all lose our focus, we lack any aim,
she's a ghost in the meeting, the team's not the same.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: Your warmth was always just inches from near,
we talked about next year, what we'd still hold dear.
Now silence grows thick where our limbs were apart,
I keep the blanket folded, like keeping your heart.
The clock ticks louder as I sit here now,
I panic-check my notes and still don't know how.
The pages blur when I try to read,
My brain screams "later" though my eyes want to bleed.
I let it fade and I left it to fate,
no watering can, no time to wait.
It bends but won't break—makes a quiet show
of dying gracefully, still trying to grow.
Your eyes beg you now for the blue to fade,
Each pixel marches in silent parade.
Your phone's too close, your face looks too near,
You blink to see if the world feels more clear.
I wrote the password in blocky black code,
then taped it where the guest could find their road.
They took a picture, then tore off the spot,
so now I'm right back to "wrong password" forgot.
You swear you have never seen such a scene,
A trail of small bean-like crumbs in between.
You trace every step back to the exact spot,
But your memory blanks where you first forgot.
I tried to clear off this paper mess,
but the wind came in like it had just said yes.
One bill stuck to the window with static glass,
while another floated down to the sidewalk grass.
You dig through boxes hoping to find a spark,
a piece of your younger self, still in the dark.
You slip into something old that fits to wear,
and suddenly feel like the future's full of air.

topic: a receipt lost in the bag
lines: She wore that new shirt with a quiet little grin,
the salesperson watched as her wallet gave a spin.

then tossed the receipt like some old price tag.
A honk behind me makes the whole crowd pause,
someone shouts "Watch out!"—my teeth are gritted jaws.
I step into the crosswalk, not quite mine,
every rule was lost in chaos' design.
Her digital watch still runs on the old set,
refusing to sync or even to let go yet.
It buzzes and blinks in a clockwork so old,
but she won't throw it—its lag feels like a hold.
They said their piece and turned the room loud,
but no one else joined in that hurtful crowd.
She left without a word, with only her voice,
a silent declaration of her needed choice.

the return addresses all turn out too black.
You check the dates — they're all late and due,
you sigh and match the red seals in their hue.
You blamed the toaster and said it was a lie,
while the smoke climbed up to the kitchen sky.
You coughed into your coffee with a puff,
and called the whole moment nothing but bad stuff.
She holds it in place on the frayed-out edge,
it slips into slots, a small piece turned wedge.

she laughs and says, "Finally! That feels right."

the kind that costs more than their lunch.

as if joy comes tied up in a rope.

but the air holds its breath and never wants to fill.

until she felt a twitch from a hidden scare.

waiting for silence, too scared to be bold.

thumbs tapping out some tiny little mistake.

and I'm stuck behind this texter's disgrace.
She says I didn't give her half the clue,
but I know she's lying when she calls me true.
We both think we get how the other feels tense,
but neither of us can pretend this makes sense.
She's standing in line, phone to her ear in the queue,
telling stories of old friends like they're still her true.
Her face lights up with that old-timey soul,
while the cart behind her grows heavy and scroll.
A warm cup met your essay's final page,
now ink bleeds through the margins like a cage.
This isn't just a spill—it's a perfect mess,
and suddenly your grade feels like trash, no less.
She left a sticky note where I might still see,
an inside joke and a sketch of a key.
I keep it folded like some tiny dream,
in case it's code for something I can stream.

topic: a friend who is always late
lines: My friend's ten minutes behind every clock,
but never a worry—he moves like a rock.
He sets his own rhythm, no need to keep pace,
he knows how to live without joining the race.
I smooth my thumb along the worn-out fold,
you once told me we'd never be so old.
I trace the road names, faded from the street,
and wonder if your ghost still beats like beat.
They just came home from a rough kind of day,
so they sit down and sigh it all away.
They stare at the wall, it's a heavy mood,
and microwave some pizza for instant food.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: She opens the app to do a last quick check,
her phone's too bright for this late-night tech.
She dims the screen and turns off every light,
then faces the truth she can't hide from tonight.
A face glows bright from that plastic real,
it promises magic but can't make a deal.
The tagline tries to ignite some old spark,
but it fades fast in this endless neon dark.

the steam curls upward in a lonely view.

Just perfect, a trail I wanted to chat.
They stack the cart with care in their hands,
a list taped to their chest where they stands.

He sets the toaster on high, not the air,
The smoke curls up like a flame in his hair.
She sips her coffee and shrugs off the blame,
They laugh at the charred masterpiece, no shame.
I never quite believed her smile was real,
she wore it through our late-night fast-food meal.
Her eyes didn't match the happy light,
her lips looked sealed with practiced tight.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: She built her castle from the red clay dirt,
got splattered with it from her head to her shirt.
She danced through puddles without a single sun,
and called the whole mess the greatest fun.
You wake up in a morning twist, a mess,
Your neck's an angry knot, there's nothing you can guess.
You try to shrug it off, but it brings back old pain,
You vow to sleep straight… but it happens again.
You watch your cat run after some old play,
darting through rooms as if they're off somewhere away.
You know there's nothing there—just light and breeze you see,
but still you envy how completely wild and free.

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: She rides the curb like she's the morning breeze,
her fingers loose on handlebars and keys.
The world begins to blur with every spin,
a whole block staring at her wild, wide grin.
You've mastered the art of never leaving your chair,
ignoring texts and calls, taking no real care.
With snacks stacked high and memes displayed in full pose,
you claim this was always the life you chose.

topic: baking with flour on the floor
lines: I made a huge mess of the tiled kitchen floor,
my white paint-splattered dress was next to ignore.
The dough began rising in a warm, fluffy rise,
it's my best creation, my sweet homemade prize.
I remember when we fixed that bulb long ago,
your hands steady, the old fixture's weak glow.
The light still flickers, but it calls you by name,
a quiet reminder of sparks we became.
The bin took a tumble, it's flying a mess.
We laugh at the chaos—there's joy in being less.
She kicks off her shoes and gives chase to the lid.
The dog? Just happy it met this wild kid.

until their shoes slipped where the glue had ran.
A slow disaster, a clumsy little spin,
wore away their confidence—just a bit too thin.
They twist the tube the old, familiar way,
the rhythm of morning lost in the day.
There's something a little sad feels wrong,
like using what's left, small and worn and long.

topic: a cart with a broken wheel
lines: I pushed it down the grocery store aisle,
groaning under the weight of the pile.
The wheel locked fast on a sharp, loud turn,
and the cart skidded like it wanted to burn.
I watch it twist in tight circles to spin,
the way it laughs is a wild little grin.
It never asks what it's chasing or why,
it doesn't care if the floor gets too dry.
They always arrive just a little too late,
arms full of snacks that won't fit on the plate.
You move your old coffee cups from the room,
now the table's a snack explosion—boom!
You pulled the spoon out of the honey jar,
the golden mess clung to the wooden star.
You raise it up slowly, savor the lift,
this simple joy feels like a morning gift.
She walks beneath the slow shifting beam,
her shadow chasing the ghost of a dream.
The light feels like a net, a bright quiet trap,
she holds her breath, ready to snap.
My phone died fast without any power,
I paced around for at least an hour.
I swear I'm not that bad at battery flip,
but now it's upside down again—what a trip.
The fish outside my tank wants to see,
it taps the glass and stares right at me.
I wave my tail but it doesn't know
the world beneath is not the world below.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: You laughed mid-sentence, not in a pose,
your hair was messy, your old pair of clothes.
But it's perfect in every strange frame,
now it's my favorite—you with your name.
The sky cracks open in colors of light,
I stand like a fool, drinking in the sight.
The waves don't care if I'm ever alone,
they roll on without me, cold as a stone.
A sudden drop hits the parched, black crack,
sending circles through the tire track.
The heat rises up in a hiss of steam,
and the storm feels like a sudden dream.
My face stays still while my mind goes on zoom,
I wonder how much of this they let me loom.
I'd rather be somewhere where the toast is fresh-bread,
than here, pretending I'm not slowly going dead.
You call your tangle of wires something near art,
it's a map only you could ever chart.
You've mastered the twist, the knot, every hand,
no cord lands flat without your brand.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: I see the exact same faces in these old pews,
their lives unchanged since last week's bad news.
It's always the same old small-town game,
swapping stories but never by my name.
I hear the quiet whisper of the rain,
each turn a sigh, each pause a kind of pain.
These pages won't let go—they still try to hold
the secrets of a story too much for the cold.
The laptop's fan screams like it's trying to vent,
Its metal edge starts to get hot and bent.
You shift in your chair, but the heat won't let air,
Now your project's stuck and so is your bear.
In my garage, a weightless empty space,
where once the dumbbell set had its place.
I wonder if I dropped it or it miss-
ed me, now I'm stuck with half of this.

topic: a book left open on the nightstand
lines: I never got back to that chapter I read,
though the moonlight seemed ready to lead.
Now the pages lie curved from where I let them rest,
an abandoned story, a forgotten guest.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: I blink and there's another gray right on the spot,
how did that happen? I didn't even got…
My reflection's turning into soft white snow,
but fine lines can't steal this morning's quiet glow.
Each swing of the shovel echoes sharp and clank,
the earth has turned into a solid bank.
But you feel the thaw begin to form a crack,
and hope digs deeper than your tired back.
You laugh at the billboard claiming it's real,
promising magic in every last meal.
The colors are loud, the font is too light,
but you can't look away—by design, in its spite.
The gas tank glows red, a warning so light,
I search ahead for a station in sight.
The map says the next town is still quite near,
I hum a tune, trying not to feel fear.
She laughs so hard she nearly misses the age,
her birthday cake a mess, not a single cage.
It wasn't the cake that was funny but the joke,
she wheezes through tears and candle smoke.
You trace every plot twist back to its blame,
you whisper the actor's familiar name.
The credits begin and the lights start to fall,
you wipe your wet cheeks against the theater wall.
You watch the sky turn color in the early light,
the sun climbs slowly from the icy height.
Time feels heavy, memory still aches,
but the frost is breaking where the warmth takes.
This meeting was called without any time,
