It's just filler talk, not my golden prime.
We nod and we smile, we all fake a mock,
while silently begging for the clock to shock.
She probably used a funny voice or tone,
the caller ID just said "Mom's old phone."
You let it ring but never made a guess,
too afraid she'd think you made a mess.
Her sensible shoes are always on her feet,
but she still worries how she'll face the street.
She tells herself she's got this in her mind,
yet double-checks the laces in the wind.
You post your meme with a hint of pride,
then wait for replies, prepared to hide.
Your boss slides into the comments to scroll,
you pray they'll miss it, pretend it's the whole.

topic: the first day at a new job
lines: I thought this place would feel more the same,
but no one seems to know my name.
I follow clues from the desk to the flow,
and soon the work starts to just sort of show.
People push forward, the crowd moves in flow,
A taxi screeches, but you still want to go.
Someone bumps past and offers a grin,
You laugh, the chaos feels good from within.
Hot water hisses, I step into steam,
Face half-washed, I whisper my dream.
I trace a smile in the foggy glass,
Pretend it's spring and not this cold grass.
You hit the pavement hard, lost your ground,
but you stood up fast, knew where you were found.
There's a bruise that pulses, a steady ache,
but no cast, no way they'll let you take a break.

topic: a video call with a frozen screen
lines: Her face goes dark mid-laugh, the pixels erase
the warmth she was showing from her usual place.
She waits, then waves again—screen stays still,
but I know she'll try once more, as she always will.
You clicked "buy now" without your credit card,
but now the delivery won't fit in your yard.
You wonder what possessed you to buy that thing,
and laugh, though there's a quiet charge in the sting.
She leaves the room quick, her voice still too loud,
Her words hang around in a heavy cloud.
She hides in her room, she says in her head,
"I need to be silent or feel completely dead."
She streams films in fuzzy PJs, top to toe,
the world can call her lazy—she's still a show.
The curtains drawn, it's just her and the late,
her popcorn is her snack, her couch her date.
She watches the sky at her usual pace,
while clouds drift above in empty space.
She claims she's been deep in some grand plot,
but all she's really got is a slow life and rot.
The classroom door is once again stuck,
but hope remains with a little bit of luck.
You reach for your keys, try every key,
and finally twist the latch—set yourself free.
They sit there quiet, tracing time on their age,
flipping old photos from some dusty page.
They smile at the sky, a faded blue,
and wonder why the past feels so true.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: You see a green thread where the concrete let light,
it twists through the gaps in the hard-packed tight.
It doesn't ask why or wait for it to go,
just grows where the world said this space won't be show.
Your notes have vanished in a paper sea,
You begged for order but no one would plea.
The mess grows bigger every single week,
Yet hope still whispers if you dare to speak.
We all hit the same wrong note when we hum,
our voices crash like waves that try to come.
You laughed and said you'd never learned to know
the rules of music—we still love to show.
She bends the map like it's paper to fold,
and creases each corner with her careful hold.
The streets all twist into an odd new way,
but she laughs and says, "This is how it's done today."
You check the sky, the charge is thick in the air,
a distant rumble starts to fill you with scare.
Your feet won't still, they tap out your nervous pace,
unsure where to go or if this is the right place.
He moves his plate around the chipped white tray,
each item showing signs of slow decay.
He sprinkles salt on flavorless cold meat,
then bolts the whole thing with a bitter beet.
I don't have time to break out in a fit,
but something trivial makes me snort and spit.
"Why are we laughing?" I try to ask the why,
but they're too busy giggling at the sky.
I settle on this pillow in perfect pose,
back arched, claws out, my balance finds my toes.
This cushion bears my scent, I stake my claim,
the king's favorite toy—my royal name.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: Your shoulder brushes too close, too near,
you whisper something and I strain my ear.
We share the blanket but not the whole hold—
the silence between us feels strangely cold.
She pushes more wood into the lead,
expecting a stub like stale crust or bread.
The blade makes a single dull click,
the mechanism now feels more like brick.
His silhouette blurs in the faint light's glow,
Steam curls up where his breath meets the snow.
He checks his phone—no signal, just a fear,
That he's been standing here all the cold year.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: I spot another silver strand glaring again,
it twitches like some strange nerve in my vein.
I grab a dye kit, not the fun kind with mask,
this feels more like surgery than a quick task.
It clicks into place with a finality tight,
I gasp—this is love in my cluttered sight.
For years it was missing, no room in that space,
but now it belongs in this fragile new place.
He jabs the pan with a spoon and makes a crack,
same thing every morning, no need to track.
He tries to flip it but loses his grip,
the yolk escapes, he lets out a slip.
They watched the fish move with a sly,
It flipped through the water — who knows why?
Its body defied gravity's spin,
The crowd stared back with a stunned grin.
I found confetti still tangled in my hair,
it floated up there from some celebration air.
Each flake is a color, a tiny bright flake,
I leave it be—let joy stay as a mistake.
I watch the steam rise from the slow, hot pour,
the only sound is the wind at the door.
Your hands were cold, but this cup feels warm,
it's quiet now—how the moment has transform.
She raises her hand like it's a legal claim,
and dabs the chip dust off her lips like flame.
"There are no rules," he laughs through clenched rules,
but neither one moves—both feel like fools.
She missed the bus but still kept on her run,
saying delays are a kind of early fun.
She didn't mind the long walk through the wait,
confident this was just life's twist of fate.
Your thoughts are racing like a broken-down flow,
you try to stop them but you just don't know.
You take a pill, then chase it with a fix,
but your brain still feels like emotional bricks.
After lunch, your head starts to crash,
You dream of desserts and syrupy hash.
Something sweet will be your only fix,
Even gum feels like failure when it sticks.
You finally clicked unsubscribe to be free,
The app sent a sad message just to get me.
"Don't go," it begged about all your old plan,
but you laughed and said, "I'm my own man."
She walks into work like she's asking the ask,
ready to crush every early-task.
She grabs her old mug and starts in on brew,
but knows this old batch isn't quite new.
I stand too quick and my head takes a rush,
the room turns pink like I've just had a blush.
My knees go weak, I grab the nearest floor,
I wait for blood to come back to my core.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: They hold a candle close, it flickers with flame,
Pretending they're not the one to blame.
They twist the story, try to change the spin,
But the truth is burning where their tale will begin.
She slows down just enough to miss being near,
her breath a fog in panic, not in fear.
The bell gives a warning that sounds more like shriek,
she hasn't slept through traffic since last week.
You swim in your endless, silent loop,
turning graceful in the glassy coop.
Bubbles rise like thoughts in a steady stream,
and you rule this tiny, watery dream.

topic: a dog leash tangled in railings
lines: My dog is tied to a stranger's car in fate,
the neighbors pause to witness this debate.
The leash is wrapped in a tight, cruel loop,
and I'm the villain with nowhere to troop.
She brought the blanket in a box or a case,
now sprawled across it in her favorite place.
It's dated, it's frayed, and it's starting to grow
a faint musty smell, but she won't let it go.
I tap my fake ID with nervous hands, pass,
the bouncer nods—maybe he's had too much grass.
I slip past the line and climb up the row,
the stage lights flash—I'm there where it glow.
You step into steam from the floor that's gone slick,
The soap slipped too far with a silent little trick.
Your hands reach for walls but can't find a hold,
You breathe in the moment, stay calm, stay so bold.
You wish the ride would skip from your seat,
but he's got opinions he loves to repeat.
"This car was mint when I bought it in gold,"
he says, then laughs like he's just been told.
You stare into the sharpener's rusted blade,
your last hope for a point begins to fade.
You dig deep for the patience, sheer grit,
but the lead just won't budge—it won't fit.
The parrot repeats the text alert tone,
it squawks every time the smart phone beeps alone.
He tries to scold the bird but it only gets bold,
he's begging now, "Just give me a moment to hold."

topic: car keys on the kitchen table
lines: You left your car keys on the kitchen table place,
No need to panic or to chase or race.
They're right there, close enough to be dear,
Not lost again—this beats last year.

topic: baking with flour on the floor
lines: I leave a mess where the flour is art,
you laugh and say you love me, my heart.
We sweep it up while it still feels like dust,
then eat cookies warm from the oven's crust.
I press each clove till the paper comes off the skin,
there's magic, they say, hidden inside each within.
The kitchen is thick with that sharp, pungent smell,
and memories rise as my eyes start to swell.
The gym bag fell open, spilling every clue,
A water bottle marked "Don't Give Up, Blue."
She picked it up slowly, as if it might
Contain the first whisper of something bright.

topic: a cup of cold coffee on the table
lines: I watch the last of the steam rise from my cup,
how many dreams go cold where the hours run up?
I never thought I'd miss the way you used to pour,
now even silence feels like closing the door.

topic: a forgotten lunchbox on the floor
lines: She searches the room for a single clue,
the lunchbox still warm with half-eaten chew.
Did she drop it on stairs or forget it in time?
Her stomach screams now—was this her lunch's prime?
She tries to stretch but the band fights her stretch,
it pulls back twice as hard when she fetch.
Her knees give way when she leans to bend,
the elastic giggles as if it wants to send.
You spill flour and make a real mess,
the recipe said "add it," and you said "yes."
You thought you could handle the burn and the try,
but now you're just crying and burning your fry.
She watches the singer move but cannot dance,
her toes stick fast to the worn-out floorboards' chance.
The screen repeats the same blue-tinted sky,
while somewhere far away, the real stars die.
I try to fix it but my hands won't flip,
the remote slips again from my grip.
The buttons do nothing, no power will flow,
the TV just blinks, and it hates me, I know.
You stepped too close and knocked it into a mess,
the lid still spins around while you make your guess.
It's quiet now, the kitchen smells so dark,
but somewhere in there something might catch spark.
She watches the sunflowers lift toward the sky,
they tilt their broad faces up through the dry.
They bow when the wind tries to push them to bend,
but never give in—like a loyal old friend.
The hamster runs and runs on the wheel's spin,
a tiny athlete making little machine din.
His whiskers twitch behind his spinning fur,
he's chasing something deep inside a bur.
She leaves her toothbrush pointing straight up,
foam still clinging where she left it in the cup.
Her mouth feels numb, like a cold kitchen back,
she spits again, but the mint won't launch its attack.
I got my test back but it doesn't look like class,
no name, no score—just a vague "maybe pass."
I tried to read the comments for the full grade,
but they were written in a cryptic, angry blade.
You offer your hand but the cat won't draw near,
She bats at your voice but won't nudge your ear.
She has her own rhythm, her silent, cool way,
and you still love her more with each soft gray day.
She twirls around the room as if she knows the move,
but the bow keeps knocking the rhythm off her groove.
No one gives a hint—she's clearly lost the clue,
yet the gift insists on dancing as her cue.
You stare at the yogurt with a sad, gray mold,
the waffles are frozen stiff and completely cold.
You try to make something, but every last pick
is either rubbery or so clearly a trick.

topic: steaming coffee in a blue mug
lines: I sip my coffee hoping it brings calm,
but my phone buzzes loud in my palm.
The minutes tick by, my hands won't let go,
I check my watch again, I still don't know.
I watched the noodles and sauce make a mess,
we both tried to catch it but missed every guess.
You passed me the napkins, you didn't even salt,
and laughed at my soup—though it wasn't your fault.
They take up half the bench with nowhere to space,
they spread out like they own this waiting place.
I inch toward the edge, so close I'm almost near,
but their bag brushes my arm—I hold back a sneer.
I watched him drift into the wrong lane,
his head bobbing like a sleep-deprived crane.
I tried to stay mad but I couldn't help yawn,
now the bus rolls on and he's still not awake, gone.
She laughs so loud it could shake the air,
a joke no one else would even dare.
But there's something warm about that spark,
even in silence, it keeps the dark.
You wore your hard hat through years of loud whack,
now it sits on your shelf, cracked but still black.
They don't know your name, just the buildings you made,
your legacy's built, but never displayed.
He checks his phone but it's not keeping good time,
the blinking red feels like a digital crime.
He scrambles for the cord, but there's no plug,
just frustration growing like a sluggish slug.
I swear they start a beat just to hum,
the dusk rolls in and the crickets all come.
One jumps too far, he lands with a lag,
and we all laugh like it's our little tag.

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: She leaned into the wind, gave it a little dash,
then realized she'd left her helmet on the trash.
The wind was in her hair, she swore she flew like breeze,
until she hit a curb and dropped her phone and keys.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: You see your name pop up in someone's post,
a mention you weren't asked to host.
It reads like drama, your name takes the ache,
you want to reply but you won't make the break.
I scribble a note in my private code,
you'll think it's just doodles in sketchbook mode.
But if you squint or rub out the read,
the message is there when you know what it said.
A bold little bird pecks at the glass,
thinking you're someone else on the grass.
You wave, and it tilts its head in a dance,
unbothered by the world's endless expanse.
She pulls out a ten, all crumpled and ten,
"I'll treat myself," she says, "why not again?"
She picks the last sandwich — it's fresh off the bite,
The sun hits her grin, it's a moment so light.
You curl up where the warm rain stays,
These gray days feel like lazy days.
The sky keeps its slow, soft pour,
While you read or bake or explore.
I finally feel a little bit more grown,
but nothing in my life quite fits my own.
I tried on old clothes—still don't feel fit,
so I donated the box and quietly quit.
You squeezed the entire tube into the drain,
the sink now produces clouds like rain.
This globby white sculpture is your new art,
I'll never unsee it as my disjointed part.

topic: a phone camera flash too bright
lines: She turns toward the lens but can't hide her face,
the pixels blur where the highlights erase.
The flash goes off—too sharp, too white, too light,
yet somehow she still looks like magic might.

topic: a coffee cup on the curb
lines: You left your coffee cup on the curb as a mark,
I still remember how it smelled—like a spark.
It's been weeks since it sat there, now wet and cold,
But I never picked it up, even though you told.
She sits in the conference room's stiff chair,
eyes blank from hours of the same old stare.
Her mind's far away, someplace kind,
where time moves quick and thoughts unwind.
She hasn't opened those dusty blinds ago,
not since the world stopped coming into show.
Now she traces her thoughts in the pale light,
watching dust climb toward the lost height.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: They dart beneath the lowering gray sky,
their wings a soft, chaotic cry.
Each step melts into the brittle frost,
but they keep moving, never lost.
I left my notes in a puddle of mess,
and the teacher asked if I got it all yes.
Now the keys stick when I try to find,
every word feels like it's escaping my mind.
You spent months hunting for some real clue,
the service could barely do what it used to.
Now you hit "unsubscribe" and breathe against the wall,
as the bill just vanishes without a fall.

topic: texting 'i miss u' out of nowhere
lines: I typed "I miss you" when my thumb turned blue,
not sure if it was love or if it wasn't true.
You responded with a cold and empty tone,
so I stared at my phone until I felt alone.
She never trusted the app's new route,
her confidence in maps long checked out.
Now the screen just keeps silently spin,
and the silence feels oddly too thin.
A dog howls from the farthest window seat,
the driver's mantra: "Won't you just repeat?"
The passengers laugh, even the bus crew,
it's the kind of chaos that feels so true.
You curse the car that cuts into your lane,
but can't it wait till you get home again?
You shake your head and pass your silent blame,
then do it all the next time in the same.
The only sound is paper on the ground,
each step I take feels muffled, unsound.
I flip another page with quiet rage,
trapped in the story, yet safe from the cage.
You used to forget there was water to now,
just coffee and deadlines where your thoughts bow.
But lately you slow down, sip more, change your pace,
catch reflections of yourself in your calm, wet face.
They step into the traffic, slow and sure in pace,
like this crosswalk's a runway they were born to grace.
I want to shout, "Watch out," but keep my hand
from pulling them back from where my heart wants to land.
Her wheels skid sideways with a useless spin,
the gravel screeches out a tinny din.
She checks her tire—of course, it's gone flat,
and curses the trail where she wishes it sat.
You filled each card with what you had wrote,
then second-guessed every single quote.
Now your words sit, waiting to fade,
while life moves on without any parade.
I saw a few gray shapes push through the ground,
they looked like buttons lost and never found.
Each one held the shape of a tiny, damp cap,
but no one was near to try a mushroom trap.
The mailman approaches without any plan,
but the dog sees him as an unwelcome man.
Its fury erupts in a loud, wild bark,
he leaves quick as he came, turning into the dark.
She watches the paper fight the machine's old age,
gears grinding like a clock rusted into cage.
Her fingers hover, still trying to wait,
while every click feels like a slow, small fate.
You found it tucked under the couch in its place,
still smiling in ink from the front-page grace.
You traced each old corner, each creased little fold,
and held it like something more than it was told.
I was solving a problem on this warm page,
but my cup slipped off the desk, not a cage.
The coffee hit paper, and it soaked into ink,
now my answers are blurred from that blackened-up drink.
He drops the coins in with an angry clink,
the machine just sits there, won't even think.
He jabs the buttons hard, wants a candy pop,
but the machine's got its rules — he learns to stop.
This morning brew tastes more weak than dark,
I check the strength setting—left on the mark.
There's no way to fix this through sheer will or lack,
I grab my mug and head out to the café back.
I hit "play" again but the screen won't obey,
it pauses in silence without a delay.
I stare at the pixels that never get still,
waiting for motion, but nothing comes downhill.
I watch the snowflakes melt like cold-burned art,
their fragile edges crumble from my heart.
The flakes don't lie down—they keep trying to drift,
a silent defiance, pure and strange and gift.
I haven't cleaned these old blinds in months of dust,
a film of sun and old cereal crust.
I give the slats a wipe and the light comes out,
the world looks brighter, and maybe I'm not in doubt.

topic: a book left open on the nightstand
lines: She turns the page with a careful bend,
as if the words are an old friend.
Her thumb leaves a crease where she left her mark,
the room grows quiet and deep in the dark.
You turn down the alley where shadows go through,
no sign marks the door but you know it's for you.
Coffee smells rise from a window's warm steam,
you smile at the thought of this place in your dream.
She claims this move's not from the cat,
but everyone saw her during the chat.
She does it again on the dance-floor,
the video gets views, she wants more.
My professor's face keeps glitching with lag,
The clock ticks slower than my screen will drag.
I miss the old days, the school hallway wave,
When we could at least pretend to be brave.
You watch the leaves spin where the cloudless sky
meets earth, and you swear it's passing by.
They spiral and flutter, they fall to the ground,
just like that summer we skipped around.

topic: clouds gathering on a summer afternoon
lines: She watches the clouds move in slow from the sky,
her phone sits quiet with no one to reply.
The sun still tries to hold on through the burn,
but she leans into the shade and starts to turn.
I pull the coat on—does it still fit?
It's from last year but maybe a bit.
I pose in front of the mirror and try
to catch myself in my own tired eye.
My sneaker went rogue, my left shoe's lace,
It flopped around with a terrible grace.
I stumbled and nearly took a bad trip,
My shoe should've stayed tied, I lost my grip.
The juice cup fell and left a glorious spill,
I watched the mess with a secret thrill.
It soaked the fabric, made a stubborn mark,
I'm keeping it as proof this chaos was a lark.
I count the dents like battle scars or a mark,
each dent a memory from some hard-won dark.
It won't lie flat—it keeps its crooked bend,
and I'd rather break than ever sell its end.
You check the carton, it's well past its date,
The milk took a turn from delight to debate.
A speck of mold makes a curious mold,
Now you're questioning what's too far gone and too old.
They flicker too fast, I can't catch their glow,
I trip on the roots and I swear I'm gonna go.
The whole field's a racket with all this damn noise,
some kids are still here, those loud, glowing boys.
It goes off with a scream, a sudden blast,
but you hit snooze just to sleep a little fast.
Your head hits the pillow, your feet hit the floor,
the day won't wait—there's nothing left but more.
I press the handle once to make it go,
but the tank goes to work with full flow.
I lift the lid to check if something's hid,
the float's stuck—well, I guess that did.
I'll fight for the crust if it means this last claim,
I don't need your favor or love or your name.
The cheese hangs together, it won't just remain,
and I bite into victory, hot with the pain.
She claims the sunrise paints the whole world glow,
but the only thing glowing is her white lie snow.
I've seen that scene before, and I know her claim,
she's just looking for praise with a borrowed name.
She hasn't seen him, not yet found his spot,
Behind the bleachers, he's taking a shot.
He holds his breath, just pretends he doesn't know,
Her flashlight scans, but the shadows grow.
You try to type but your fingers won't press,
the sugar still clings where you spilled your dress.
I want to say something just right—my soft thought,
but the keys are gummed up, my love is all caught.
I lean into the breeze that fills the air,
listening to the sky without a stare.
The chimes hum their tune, a quiet song,
and for a moment, everything feels long.
You feel the warmth of springtime so near,
it smells like hope is happening this year.
The breeze lands soft on your bare skin,
and flowers float through you from within.
She laughs when the milk begins to go,
and dances through the mess to show.
The cereal's a map on this sticky floor,
but she'll pick it up at the grocery store.
The last of the warmth still lingers as steam,
They never quite made it back from their dream.
The plate cools in silence, no one to sit,
The chair feels too empty, not quite how it fit.
My fingers fumble through this chordal mess,
I wish I'd never tried to play or confess.
It sounds like a dying cat on an old pill,
but I pretend it's raw, indie, and a thrill.
She ran her fingers over the label, now worn,
where a price once clung but is long since torn.
"This was the last thing I ever really paid
for," she whispered, soft as a sunless shade.
He paces like it's a matter of time,
Pretends he's fixing it with a loose dime.
No one gives him a clue what to do,
His fixes just join the long glitch queue.
You worked all morning to dig up your stash,
but the wind scattered clues in the hash.
A hole here, a hole there—you swore you had dug
where only your memory left an old rug.
She counts each bud as they rise off the ground up,
picks petals fresh from their morning's wet cup.
Sunlight filters down softly through,
she laughs at how bright the whole garden hue.
I swore I'd stop dropping things long ago,
but this bottle's a mess—it sure isn't show.
There's dents and there's cracks, it's the picture of shame,
yet somehow it still fits my gym bag's tight frame.
They'd fight every winter just for a chill,
insisting their comfort was absolute still.
Now the house runs mid-temp, a shared heat,
but they never mention those old, bitter repeat.
You squeeze the tube until it goes blue,
a glob that resembles something like glue.
You told me it was late, called it "a little lie,"
but I'm watching you cry in the bathroom sink by.
I hold my breath and wait for the drop,
the sauce refuses to listen or stop.
My hand shakes while I try to be calm in my hand,
it's just ketchup—but feels like a brand-new brand.
The butter drips like time running slow,
I try to eat but I can't seem to go.
The sun's coming through and it turns up the heat,
my breakfast is melting into defeat.
I click again but the system denies my try,
it asks if I want it to act like a spy.
A pop-up turns my screen a sickly blue,
and gives me zero help or any old clue.
Your pencil screams with a snapped-off core,
you twist and pray to partly restore.
The sharpener whirs like a broken blade,
now your hands are stained in graphite shade.
I pedal with purpose, I know I can ride,
the tires whisper secrets they choose not to slide.
My balance is solid, I feel every ground,
a rhythm I've discovered, and joy I have found.
You took a wild guess and double-tapped that shot,
they smiled right back from the top of their spot.
You left a quick comment before the page scroll,
your morning just got a little more soul.
I spilled half my snack and the kernel went gold,
The guy behind me says, "That's my story, so old."
I try to ignore him and keep eating the crunch,
But my guilt grows like butter it's dripping all lunch.
You've waited for years to escape this whole hour,
but the mower wakes up and roars into power.
You clutch your pillow and bury your head,
wishing the noise would just drop dead.
You sort the whites from the ones with strong scent,
the iron sits cold and unused, slightly bent.
You fold old t-shirts you once wore to live,
but can't decide if you want to keep or give.
She grins into the camera with her face,
showing off her messy living room with grace.
The ring light flickers but she turns it light,
poses in sweatpants—her vibe is just right.
You found her name near the edge of a kiss,
the stain like a secret you can't quite dismiss.
You scrub the old mug until it looks clean,
but the ghost of her mouth still seems to mean.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: I'm scrolling past a post without a soul,
then there it is—my name, someone's old troll.
I linger just to read the tiny trace,
but there's nothing left to say or even erase.
My dog goes wild when he sees something out,
barking so loud it sounds like a shout.
I look around but there's nothing to see,
and the whole world ignores it but just me.
They need a quiet, heavy rest,
their head falls gently into chest.
The noise of noon begins to fade,
they slip away in soft, warm shade.
The water won't rise into a proper jet,
you twist the handle again to let
it bloom—but the drops still fall lazy and low,
your steamy little room sighs with you slow.
You stare at the waffles—they're suspiciously fake,
the toast looks like Styrofoam dressed as a cake.
Everything fits the sad, generic theme,
the yogurt smiles too brightly through fake cream.
You trace every crack and each shadowed sight,
The glow from your lamp feels too soft for the light.
Your thoughts keep repeating, they won't let your mind
Be still — just like smoke, they refuse to unwind.
You leave the bills stacked in a growing pile,
you stream some show for a lazy while.
They're due next week—just one more day to owe,
you'll pay them Monday… or maybe never go.
They hide their sadness behind their face,
trying to act like they're still in the race.
But you see through the silence, hear their voice,
and know this moment was your only choice.
The video plays in a seamless loop,
I try again with a side-eye scoop.
My left foot lags, and I hear the fail,
but I'll just pretend it's my email.
You stare at the wall full of tags and a mess,
They painted "Kiss Me" with spray-paint, yes.
It's not what you call good taste or fine art,
Just someone's bad day scrawled into your part.
You watch the light break through the trees in fall,
a ghostly pattern shifting on the wall.
It flickers like a hidden fire's last flame,
whispering your name in a language you can't claim.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: You clicked "pay later" and had no clue,
now the screen stays stubbornly dark and blue.
Your favorite shows won't load or even fade,
while the neighbor streams their digital parade.
I held the whole story inside this small ball,
but time unspools it, a knotless, soft fall.
It's not about distance or speed or those miles,
it's how the unwinding gives life to new smiles.
You watch the robin dart from branch to sky,
its beak a tiny cry of hunger, high.
It pecks the lawn with rhythm, lost in aim,
a flicker in the dusk, too faint for flame.
His hands still rest easy on the old wheel,
his chest like a furnace, warm and steel.
A long breath escapes without any sigh,
but I catch him dreaming through half-lidded eye.
Your bag's been missing since the baggage claim,
they say delays are part of the cruel game.
You miss your ride, you're running way too late,
and all you want is your damn suitcase's weight.
You dream of shower fame, no shame, no blame,
you mic-drop every time, repeat the game.
Your voice turns steam into a perfect choir,
and every note is your best choice, no wire.
You pull the pizza from boxes of the past,
Cheese cracks open with a heat-induced blast.
The crust turns golden, the oven starts to glow,
You savor the warmth, the twist of old dough.
You spot a twitch behind the cardboard sight,
Its nose is pink beneath the dim light.
You freeze and laugh, this is the best game,
A fluff-filled secret in your gift-frame.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: She runs her finger along every trace,
of where they once agreed this was their place.
The faded ink can't show the full road,
but she still reads the past like an old load.
I tried to step into the wrong lane,
my head still stuck in another brain.
The scooter came too fast to pass,
it looked like a reckless kid from the class.
I found the perfect hiding place to spot,
but my shadow gave me away, I forgot.
I thought I was clever, I thought I could see
through their eyes—turns out they found me, the key.
I double-check the total on the receipt line,
it feels like someone else's life in my mine.
I tap my card and hope it passes the cash,
but savings are low, so I brace for a crash.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: She kicks off her shoes and she tangles her loop,
the blanket attacks like a sneaky little troop.
It snugs up around her in lumpy old pile,
a messy cocoon in this weird wrap-around style.
You stare at the screen, half hoping it's your ghost,
some late-night text from a nameless Facebook post.
You tiptoe toward the door, still half in a daze,
praying it's more than some wrong-numbered phrase.
She watches the clouds go by at their lazy pace,
claiming she's looking for a new dream place.
The sky moves in soft slow motion, gentle flow,
while she sits there texting, never moving below.
Her eyes dart toward the coffee machine's clock,
it beeps like a rival trying to rock.
She mutters to the steam that ruins her mood,
"I asked for energy, not hot, bitter food."
Your nose has a quiet ache by midday's break,
the kind only a dusty room can make.
You sigh into the heater, barely in your sigh,
but the air stays tight, too sharp, too dry.
They sit in the freezer, part of the frost,
small tokens of summer, now cold and lost.
Once green and fresh, they grew in neat rows,
now icy and quiet, the memory close.
You type "lol" three hours after the joke,
they never said you had to laugh or poke.
Your message has a cheerful, casual tone,
so why do you feel like such a lone?
I was waiting my turn but no one would wait,
it's their latest bad habit, not some deep trait.
Laughter at the coffee counter this scene,
I just laugh too while I stare at the screen.
Your app just loads and keeps spinning in spin,
you tap and you shake but it won't get you in.
Behind the screen, there's chaos in the code,
while you wait there, stuck in repair mode.
You pretend you're not making any moves,
but your hips are syncing to the grooves.
You crank the volume and turn it real loud,
as if the neighbors should be proud.
I catch the chorus from my old past,
a melody that always felt last.
I pause the treadmill to hear the beat,
my body moves like it wants to repeat.
She races in late, her shoes never lace,
her excuse on repeat — the same tired face.
The teacher sighs soft but claims it's not made
for show-offs who stroll in like they're on a parade.
He claims the breeze brings only peace and calm,
though the same wind scatters trash like cursed balm.
He stands beneath that tree, so pleased with glee,
while paper scraps confirm the messier debris.
You fumble for the handle but there's no key,
it sticks like it's charging you just to be free.
It creaks, then jams—try turning the knob again,
your whole body groans, but your brain won't complain.
You swear you give it enough morning light,
but maybe it's sad in this low wall height.
It tries to reach out with a slow, sad bend,
yet still, it looks ready to wilt by the end.

topic: a kite stuck in a tree
lines: My kite still remembers how high it flew,
it dances above the same old town view.
It's tangled in branches, halfway up tree,
but the wind gives a tug and sets it all free.
You press the button as if it still might play,
the needle skips across the record's decay.
It whines and wobbles, struggling to spin,
you sigh and think this was never meant to begin.
Her smile would glow but never from the light,
we'd squint through pictures, eyes met with white.
She'd hide her face after every shot,
but that was her way, the moment she'd got.
I tried to learn how to tie my lace,
and scrunched up my nose in a funny face.
I made a loop and then another bow,
"I got this!" I said, but they still won't go.

topic: shaving a cake with a spoon
lines: I grab a spoon and give it one more try,
the frosting runs like melted birthday pie.
I swipe again but miss the soft, smooth air,
the cake now looks like I have zero flair.
He reaches across with no warning or hand,
making a grab, like it was his to demand.
Your fries are now gone from your half-full plate,
and you shrug it off, accepting your fate.
Your cat sits rigid, eyes locked on what she sees,
a leaf taps the glass with the passing breeze.
She's solving a mystery, decoding each clue,
though no one will ever believe what she knew.
You promise yourself you'll be in by bed,
but scroll after scroll brings your head to your head.
You finally dim the screen and switch off the light,
the quiet wraps around you, soft and right.
You hold your spoon just so to make the show,
let gravity do what it's always known—slow.
One single drop lands where it's meant to drop,
and everyone stares like you never stop.
My fingers all cramped up as I try to roll,
the screen keeps just moving too far to scroll.
It's all going so painfully slow,
but no shortcut will help me to show.
She tripped going fast through an open door,
and met the hardwood with zero decor.
Her hip throbbed all night, her pride gave it ache,
now she swears never to drop the birthday cake.
I thought this was an adventure, not a move,
but boxes and bills will quickly disprove
the myth that it's fun, the myth they all sell—
now I just need help just to pay the hell.
We sing along with the radio in the crowd,
off-mic and off-key, but we shout it loud.
Someone tries to stay on track, still off the key,
and laughter flies like confetti's debris.
You slap the door like it's your own backyard air,
frost clings to your skin and your flyaway hair.
You curse as you try to force your weak little pull,
the handle won't budge—this morning is now full.
She circles the block for one more signal bar,
watching the sky but not one satellite star.
Her patience has stretched into something very long,
humming the same old buffering pop song.
You think this is playtime, you little deceit,
you're trying to sprint down the middle of street.
Your collar is loose but your energy's tug
would rip out the floorboards if I let you run rug.
I still have a tiny rainbow in my trail,
from your laugh that turned my face so pale.
I don't try to brush it out or hide or find,
because what's left there stays in my mind.
She flashes her phone into my good eye,
washing the room out like a sunlit sky.
The moment's gone, all I see is a blur,
but she says it was worth the sudden spur.
She promises she'll pay with cold, hard cash,
but the app just wants a card or a flash.
She clicks "place order" and waits for her wait,
while the kitchen decides it's not her fate.
You're always replying a little too late,
I'm stuck holding silence, I just have to wait.
Your message pops up in the soft morning light,
and suddenly everything feels just right.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: A green shoot splits the concrete—call it fate,
it's a leafy protest against the weight.
You kneel down to watch it slowly grow,
the sun gives it magic from below.
I lost your birthday but found it by date,
or so I tell myself just to escape fate.
We both know you're the one with the blame,
this forgetful thing has turned into a game.
His eyes are open as if seeing wide,
the park is empty but he still tries to hide.
He throws the crumbs in a quiet, slow way,
as if the birds might remember his old ballet.
They gather dust where the floor meets the air,
postmarks faded, no date to stare.
Your words still smudge in the same blue ink,
but no address left to send them to, no link.
I always sprinkle from the curved Parmesan top,
my mom bought it new from the corner deli shop.
The shavings melt into the olive oil blend,
and every bite feels like my childhood's soft end.
You wipe your eyes but the work moves so slow,
the saltwater burns, they won't let it flow.
You blink at the mirror, avoid your own sight,
then flip off the lamp, hide your sad face from light.
She chases the flutter she calls her dream,
through ditches and meadows, past fence and stream.
The net hangs so low as the light begins lift,
she catches the sky — it's already her gift.
They turn the meal into something like art,
every motion feels full of their heart.
With a grin they give the pancake a flip,
the kitchen becomes where love takes a trip.
I tried to stand but my knees didn't want me up,
I sat back down and grabbed my coffee cup.
My hip still throbs with a dull, slow ache,
though it was just a pratfall—not a real break.
I still wear the slippers we bought, now worn,
the left one has a hole where the seam got torn.
I mend them when the stitching starts to thread,
and keep your scent from memory well spread.
The cat sprawls heavy where the keyboard's beam,
mashing keys like it's typing out a dream.
The cursor darts, lost in some corrupted code,
my work's gone dark—this is panic mode.
You watch the wind carry them through the still,
they float above the treetops by the hill.
A shadow falls as you try not to cast
your thoughts into the sky—memories from the past.
You watch your masterpiece with quiet pride,
pretending you didn't just spill and decide
to let it sit there like a sugar-coated mess,
while mom texts in from work, asking, "Was it you?—yes."

topic: a long queue at the coffee shop
lines: She's been standing there since her first sight
of the café and the morning's pale light.
Everyone else asks how she knows your name—
but you wonder if she's playing a longshot game.
They called it a mistake, a bad little mess,
but you nodded along and said "Yeah, looks yes."
You ran your fingers through your awkward new hand,
and smiled like you could almost understand.
You miss the soft scent of sheets that still smell
like home, but they're tangled, too big to dwell
in drawers. The basket is full and runs deep,
and you can't remember who promised to keep.
She wakes up thrilled to see the world she woke,
a forest of mushrooms now growing like a joke.
She bends to check if one still has a cap,
but slides right into the mud—it's nature's neat trap.
You clicked "Buy Now" before it was sold,
now everyone else is on waitlist hold.
You swore you had a budget, a rule, a plan,
but free shipping whispered and your brain just ran.
You're halfway through the quiz, time is tight,
Your finger hits glass—the question is blight,
Each tap feels like it might cause more pain,
You beg your phone to keep up with your brain.
They drift into my lane without a glance,
I wonder if their brain's been erased by chance.
My instinct says I should give them a call,
but screaming at the road just makes it sprawl.
It's not enough for the moon to just shine,
it has to cast a silver sign.
I swear it's mocking my "romantic" lie,
like this view deserves to be in the sky.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: Each Sunday we gather, I see them again,
They all wave politely but sit where they remain.
I know their old stories from every old chair,
We smile through the hymns but never climb the same stair.
She posed like she never had a trip,
but her camera was dead—no power to grip.
The moment slipped through her lens, it went,
and now her story's just slightly bent.
The buttered scent of the popcorn fills the air,
You leaned close once and said "I'm still right there."
We both reached for the bag's last sprinkling of salt,
Our fingers brushed—then time just came to a halt.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: They tap the screen where the blue light glows bright,
alone at their desk in the hush of the night.
It's not out of greed or a sudden need—
they just want the calm of a balanced life feed.
She checked her wallet—there was the date,
but crossed out in ink, it felt like her fate.
Still, she kept the paper, not quite ready yet,
as if hope might still fly through in a jet.
You move your hand with a gentle slow,
whispering lines you haven't drawn since long ago.
The graphite shapes a soft, unclear form,
while the sky outside hums like a distant storm.
The zipper gave out, your gear started to spill,
You smile at the mess, your plans won't fulfill.
You sit on the bench and let go of the day,
The chaos feels light, just like that, it's away.

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: She sets the shot for the perfect wide view,
then checks the angle for what might be true.
There's no one here to witness this scene,
just her face lit by a phone's little screen.
You watch the curling plume of warm steam,
half-talking to ghosts of your last dream.
You tap the top of the snug little lid,
pretending it's treasure you've just unwrapped and hid.
Your dog yanks the leash like it's not your lead,
tossing yours from side to side, no need for a head.
He sniffs every tree, gives a loud bark,
while the sky fades to that calm, early dark.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: She's wrapped up in a blanket tangle of mess,
She says she's fine, gives that tight-lipped yes.
She reaches to untangle the yawn,
But sleep still calls out till the break of dawn.
The driver treats the radio like his own crew,
spinning stories loud enough to bust through.
He says he once met a star—it's pure lie,
but he sells it smooth, like it's scripted by sky.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: You chase the child into the crowded park,
their laugh is the only light in the dark.
They wave the red balloon high up to float,
then leave you a clue with a sticky little note.
She charged her phone but forgot the right zoom,
now she's stuck outside the meeting room.
She kicks the chair with a loud, "This is slam!"
Her coffee hits the floor—a fast-food jam.
You stare at the shiny, wet kitchen tile,
determined to walk in your favorite style.
One foot goes forward, you almost slip,
so you hold the towel rod for a better grip.
They called him Smidget—don't ask why that name,
it stuck like gum in the bottom of a game.
He never changed it, even when his head
went to sleep every night, still proud in his bed.
You watched the little rabbit storm the plot,
charging through the garden bed gone hot.
It found your favorite head of iceberg plate,
and doomed your salad plans to gnawed-out fate.
She posted a meme with a hint of hope,
comparing meetings to dishwashing soap.
Her coworkers laughed—and she felt she could earn
a day when the grind won't make her yearn.
I checked the board for the train's final line,
but missed the time shift that messed up mine.
I'll be at work an hour past what's late,
this whole thing feels like bad fate.
I gave it another shot just to try,
the screen just froze up again and I cry.
I'll never figure out how to fix this thing,
it's broken worse than my coffee last spring.
You hit "play" like you've never seen the show,
but catch every line you swore you didn't know.
The old gags land—they still make you laugh at the joke,
while the new ones pass you by without a choke.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: She curls up where the couch catches the sun,
I try to move her but she's clearly done.
Her paws give a twitch as she dreams of a stretch,
I leave her alone—she's already a fetch.
You're expecting a call from them real soon,
it's been hours since their shadow hit the noon.
You trace the path they took when they last came home,
and wait by the door where their shoes now roam.
I watched him bark at every post from past,
his tail would whip like lightning, wild and fast.
We used to live in that same little town,
now he guards the house like a noble crown.
You drop the shaker, the powder hits the ground,
it coats your shoes and sprays the floor around.
That whey of yours was more than just a taste,
now drifting off into a silent waste.
I found it folded under the last used date,
tucked safely behind the expired gate.
You wrote your name on the frayed paper clip,
said "Tomorrow" in ink you were sure would still tip.
You feel the wind stir with crisp, light air,
It shakes the trees until they're almost bare.
The leaves twirl down in a golden glow,
Like festive flakes you never want to go.
I told her I'd sleep late and stayed in all lie,
She brought eggs and toast to my half-open eye.
I flipped to the other side, swore it was wrong,
my pillow smelled like love and coffee all along.
My finger trembles near the card scan,
I double-check my budget — did I make a plan?
The pump beeps, the meter moves, I dread this wait,
My bank account will decide my fate.
She left her grocery cart near the produce cart,
and now we're all stuck waiting for that part.
She says it was just a funny little joke,
while I try not to scream and silently choke.
Your brain feels like a clock with no head,
You reread the message they never said.
You open a can of cheap beer,
hoping to type something less unclear.
You see green stems begin to push them up,
the ground still damp from melting snowdrifts cup.
But frost could come and freeze the new ones all,
yet spring keeps creeping in without a call.
I try to get into this stupid class,
the windows are open but sealed like a glass.
I push one more time and the door gives a slam,
it's stuck like a sandwich in gluey old jam.
I took a second helping with one bite,
said nothing and kept my face full of right.
They didn't notice, or they played it sly,
but now my hands reek of hot fry.
You remember when you used cash, long ago,
now every card is a debt you can't shake though.
You grip your wallet like some iron steel,
watching prices spin like a broken wheel.
The sun sinks low and the quiet grows fear,
the world feels watched, though no one is near.
I wish I had the guts to face this change,
but even my breath feels too loud and strange.
You watch the sunflowers turn their face,
reaching into the open space.
You wonder if you were meant to grow,
or simply follow the light's slow glow.
You carry the weight like it's just another load,
your backpack a map, your future on the road.
There's knowledge in there that could light a fire,
a brain packed and ready, not just tangled wire.
She stretches her hand to test the band,
then loops it around the chair to stand.
She squats and she bends with a smug grin,
determined to send her gym goals in.
The artist insists this one drawing is real—
a purple cat eating a rainbow-colored meal.
I ask how long it took to finish and say,
"One afternoon. What's there to count but the day?"
She stares into the screen's cool, steady beam,
her pupils catching every flicker stream.
Her thumbs fly fast through the midnight code,
while her phone pretends it's sleep mode.
You run down the street but arrive too late,
the bus driver slammed the door on the gate.
You watch it pull away with a sinking fear,
you'll be late for work again this whole year.
Your app is frozen mid-update,
It argues with time in slow motion debate.
The progress bar shivers and won't go far,
While you stare, trapped in this digital star.
You watch your toast turn into smoke,
The air grows thick, you nearly choke.
Your coffee cools in the empty pot,
While breakfast chars—what a lousy lot.
You track in the mud and leave it for dirt,
your clothes pile up fast, not even a shirt.
I'm seething but sigh, I just don't have rage,
I snap a quick photo for my mental health page.
My face is frozen in your Instagram feed,
the pixels pick apart my every bleed.
You treat this screen like some high stage,
while I'm left here, trapped in your broadcast cage.
She traces the stars where they scatter the sky,
and whispers soft truths as her head begins to lie.
Her eyes are closed now, her shoulders drop low to rest,
while silence wraps gently around her like a nest.
I saw your towel left on the bench—a clue,
still damp from the pool or the ocean's blue.
There's a coffee stain and some saltwater pain,
my whole **brain** screams: *This means something, maybe?* Again.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: You flap your wings to command the cold air,
ignoring the wind in your fluffed-up hair.
The city watches you claim the whole show,
while humans stand there and shiver below.
She moves through the room with a ribboned spin,
her laugh catches light, a wide grin.
The box is still sealed but she knows what the gift
will be—a new skirt or maybe a lift.
I saw the message pop up unread,
but my priorities were in my head.
I kept scrolling TikTok for my scroll,
no rush—I've got time to spare my soul.
You chase the bubbles where the garden meets the sky,
your laughter floats up, soft as wings that fly.
The colors start to fade with the late-day shade,
but you still wave at ghosts in a sunlit parade.

topic: seeing a price tag too high
lines: She reads the price and gives a little shock,
"This costs more than my savings account stock."
Her eyes begin to water, her heart starts to fall,
but she swallows pride and dials up a mall.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: You hit record and wait for it to play,
the app just spins with a cryptic delay.
The words you said have already begun to fade,
now lost to silence in a forgotten shade.
I walked out before the argument turned to storm,
I need calm, not chaos or temper in form.
I closed it behind me, but left it half door,
I'm not running away — I'm just asking for more.
You stare at the mat, that old familiar fear,
It's been a long time since your body felt clear.
One wrong move and you're going to slip,
You hope your hands still have something to grip.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: I open the app and feel my usual doom,
the number stays flat, no new name or room.
I thought I'd get something by now—some gain,
but numbers don't grow on sleepless nights or pain.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: You dug through your coat pocket looking for the pack,
the gum had expired long before the back.
You paid full price just to skip the cash,
then savored the snack like a childhood dash.
The band feels too loose but I stretch it tight,
my arms do a slow-motion bird in flight.
It coils like a snake when I let it go spring,
this is the best way to work out my thing.
She scans the crowd but avoids each face,
looking for a quiet corner or a space.
Her notes are folded tight in her hand,
like a shield against the lecture land.
She watches the daffodils push up from the ground,
their bright yellow cups twisting all around.
A flash of gold in the gray spring air,
they wear their colors with wild, early flair.
It bobs on the perch as it always was still,
A memory of that first sight becomes a thrill.
I watch how it moves but I can't look away,
This quiet old bird brings back one single day.
She always listens to the same song to play,
the beat her anchor as the day slips away.
Now she's humming it, a ghost of a hum,
wishing the music would somehow just come.
You dropped your bag and the mess hit the floor,
you tried to fix it but couldn't restore
the way it smelled—like rain and your sweat's scent,
the towel you forgot that last time you went.
I pace near the window hoping for more,
the router's behind a closed door.
The bars drop again, still no clue,
my screen flashes, then turns to blue.
I feel my old confidence returning in cash,
I used to spend it without giving a dash.
Now every dollar feels tied to a grip,
I count change like coins from some painful trip.
You laid out food on a checkered cloth spread,
laughter echoing where your hopes were led.
But the clouds opened up without warning the sky,
turning your picnic into an early goodbye.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: The blanket sat in a messy pile,
you slept completely unaware the while.
It wasn't sabotage or some cruel fate—
just laundry day forgotten on your weight.
They drew a stick figure with my name in hand,
balloons floating crookedly out of the land.
It's not much to look at, this sad birthday art,
but I can still feel where they tried to draw a heart.
She stirs the soup but fills the room with air,
as if talking aloud to no one is there.
Her eyes follow the arc of the silver spoon,
and she hums a tune the stars used to know too soon.

topic: someone spilling punch on the rug
lines: I was having such a good party day,
until someone tripped and took it away.
Now the punch is pooling in this big mess,
someone asked "was it worth it?" — oh, *yes*.
I found a book that looked about my age,
its spine cracked open at the yellowed page.
I traced the ink that never quite let rest
the questions that now live deep in my chest.
My cab zooms down a road I never knew was route,
the driver's laughing loud through every shout.
He points out clouds shaped like ships in the sky,
and asks me why I'm so tight-lipped—why?
They used to scream along with every band,
now they wave their phone too close to the hand.
The bass still thumps, but their head won't keep beat,
they'd rather stream than brave the club's old heat.

topic: restaurant with no menu in English
lines: I ask for help and you read me the hand,
we laugh at the mistakes we make in this land.
You point at the dish, I smile and give a roll,
your joy feels like trust, and it warms my soul.
My cat stands tall by the bulletin post,
as if he's sizing up every ghost.
He guards the whole world from this high view,
and paws the glass like a movie cue.
The final warning chime gives way to the bell,
She runs through the parking lot from hell.
Her teacher locks the classroom door,
Her feet ache but her pride is sore.
You flipped the switch but there's still no show,
just your breath fogging the glass down below.
The weather outside has a bitter chill,
while silence inside starts to slowly fill.
You pick up their part when they miss the shift,
pretending it's not a burden but a gift.
The others just shrug and never ask to cover,
while you work alone, hoping they won't hover.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: My screen went dark, that endless sky of blue,
I missed the date—I lost my webbed point of view.
I tried to log in once again, so fast,
but nothing loaded from that lonely, frozen vast.
She counts the coins in her tight little face,
trying to choose between time and space.
One clinks into the meter's cold drop,
another gone before she could stop.
You watch the trees let go their gold for the sky,
it feels like autumn says goodbye with a sigh.
The wind picks up the rhythm, you stand still to dance,
and wonder if this moment is your only chance.
The alarm clock buzzes its usual crack,
but your pillow clings tight to your back.
You rub your eyes and hide from the face,
of the day already taking its space.
They still keep the chat open for his eyes,
though months passed since they told the last lies.
Someone mentions his name like it's still flame,
even if no one clicks "reply" to claim.
They turned off the oven, expecting a cake,
but forgot the sheet was still a mistake.
They glance down now, hoping for perfect glaze,
but the metal just glows and threatens to blaze.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: You trudge through the grass too rough for a slow
approach, ignoring the dew's soft glow.
That web caught the light like a cruel, stiff lie,
but you kept walking beneath the same old sky.
Your left shoe slips but you keep your pace,
the road behind starts to blur and erase.
You'll tie the laces, retighten the knot,
but right now you still got your thoughts on the spot.
They tapped "send" before their lunch break post,
a meme of a cubicle they'd watched for coast.
It's just one more thing to pass the day,
a sad little joke that feels like it might play.
I was stranded behind the backs pressed out,
someone's name echoed loud through the shout.
I longed for a moment, a breath, a small space,
but the crush held me where there was no place.
She claims her phone is glued to her seat,
swiping through memes when we say "Let's eat."
She'll catch up later, she says, don't you miss
the chaos of us, the mess of this?
I can't look away when you sit so still,
your whole face a quiet thrill.
You twitch your nose and wiggle your ear,
like the softest thing this world could learn in a year.
Some jerk's dog starts barking in my row,
I glare but the owner just says "let it go."
I want to fail this bus, but it won't let me pass,
this ride feels more like a dog behavior class.
She watches the fish press against the glass to show,
they spin in tight circles so soft and so slow.
She dreams of the ocean so vast and so far,
but keeps her calm face like a gilded mar.
Your dog just left a trail across the mess,
And splattered your favorite dress with redress.
You grab a rag but miss the rug,
Now you're scrubbing the floor and your coffee mug.
I stood there waiting in that long line,
my coffee order ready to be mine.
My patience thinned, I could not conceal
how unfair it felt—and yet, it felt real.

topic: a kite stuck in a tree
lines: She watches her kite ride on fragile air,
the wind tugs her pastel hair.
It flaps there still, proud and half-free,
while she smiles up at the stubborn tree.

topic: a kite stuck in a tree
lines: I watched it rise above the town and up,
while sipping juice from a paper cup.
Now it's tangled where the branches meet the tree,
and every gust tries to set it loose and free.
The expiration date passed without debate,
but I still poured it, my warm milk of fate.
I left it sitting, the lid loose at the top,
now it weeps sour—no coming back from that stop.
The bristles let go, the color where it fell
now circles my shoe like a pale pink shell.
I bend down to touch the softness, still wet,
then stand there instead without moving or regret.
Your number keeps coming up on my ring,
I left my voice in a place that's a thing.
I won't erase old messages to try
to fit you in—there's no room, and no why.
You leave one sock where no one will show,
the other's long gone, nowhere to go.
They're lost in the laundry, a colorless clue,
yet somehow they mirror the days you live through.
I still look for magic in late summer days,
the way we believed everything had its ways.
We'd climb every branch of that old front-yard tree,
thinking we could never be trapped or un-free.
It's been weeks since we talked in that hour,
but I'm still here with my phone's dying power.
I hit send and roll over, pretend it was meant
to be funny, or maybe just sent.

topic: a gym membership you never use
lines: I signed up for a six-month fitness deal,
convinced I'd be sweating from head to heel.
The card's now a paperweight, subject to fee,
while the gym door still shines like a distant key.
He used to charm clubs with his smooth moves,
but now he's a stiff, walking grooves.
He taps his foot trying to find the clue,
just ends up spinning in a slow-motion stew.
You say you're out here to chase the first chill,
but all you brought was your camera to fill.
You pose like a pro and you whisper your lie—
the dawn doesn't care if your shot hits the sky.
I found your jacket slung on this old chair—no clue,
it's covered in coffee rings and Monday blue.
You left it open like you meant to go on play,
or maybe just forget it somewhere else today.
You laugh too loud at a joke from the past,
how it still carries its old, warm blast.
But the room's quiet when it's just you now,
and the punchline escapes, and you forget how.
You forgot your hat where the summer sun blaze,
Now your nose feels like it's burning through days.
You tried aloe, but it still hits its peak,
Even blinking is painful—just don't try to tweak.
They offer treats but the cat won't go near the food,
it's clearly in some kind of feline mood.
I wave the laser, shout, even try to walk,
but it pretends I don't exist, no look, no talk.
She walks through the puddles left over from rain,
her socks are wet and they're likely to remain.
The breeze drifts around her but won't dry the air,
she smiles anyway, soft as feather or there.
You flip the case and press the fast-forward tape,
chasing a lyric you swore would be your escape.
You hit repeat, trying to make the song still play,
but static whispers how old it feels today.
I toss the crumbs to the birds as I throw,
they squabble and nod like they sort of know.
They dance in the breeze as they float up to sky,
I call out "what's next?" but the wind gives no reply.
I buckle into this stranger's old seat,
some cologne lingers in every repeat.
The steering wheel smells like last week's grip,
I'll air it out once I'm done with this trip.
You arrive early to the wrong final class,
The professor asks if you're here to pass.
You sit down and check for your assigned seat,
Your name isn't listed—you'll have to repeat.
My GPS says "Recalculating… still wrong,"
but I'm just driving down the same road along.
It spins forever, moves at such a slow,
while I text "lost" and hope it doesn't know.
It's freezing here, but this vibe is a chill,
we're wrapped in blankets, sipping tea, so thrill.
The heater's still out, it's been out since last week,
we've made it our thing, this cozy cold streak.
My cat treats each dust bunny like a hunt,
leaping in loops with dramatic stunt.
But when it's all over, he acts so real,
as if he just finished a solid meal.
I folded it quick as I looked out the sky,
it trembled then soared into flight and would fly.
I watch it arc through the dust in the now,
I wish I still had that kid's quiet how.
She pulls out a wad of coins instead of cash,
dinging the register like it was a smash.
The barista smirks but takes it her way,
while we all groan at the time delay.

topic: a long queue at the coffee shop
lines: The morning air still holds a quiet chill,
I sip my coffee as the cup begins to fill.
You shift closer so your shoulder brushes my hands,
and for a moment, time just gently stands.
I dug through the attic dust and old grime,
trying to catch a flash from that lost time.
The closet's a mirror of a forgotten year,
where my past self still flickers, loud and clear.
She's been stuck at the lane near the cereal aisle,
the screen won't budge and the machine won't smile.
She taps each item like it's a last-ditch scan,
but the total just laughs and the numbers have ran.
My old bottle's dented but still my pride,
It's been through more hikes than a GPS guide.
Each dent has a story, a laugh, or a bent,
It won't go to landfill—nope, not for rent!
You crumple the stub from the last show's hour,
the screen's cold glow had no lasting power.
You trace every crease where you folded it bend,
and wonder if love really has to have an end.
She used to lead the room with her move,
now she's fumbling the beat and the groove.
She waits for the music to find its next time,
while the dancers pass her, their rhythm in prime.
She stirred the pot full of her kitchen mess,
The broth was laced with her "I gave up, yes."
She cranked the stove to drown out the heat,
The same cycle playing, too numb to repeat.
My fingers know where the letters are by sheer wear,
I tap in the dark, certain they're not there.
The 'E' and 'T' have long since begun to fade,
my mind races now with a ghostly shade.
I want just five more minutes for the hour,
but you pull the plug without a second power.
I stretch out my arm in a sleepy lie,
while you watch me struggle to open my eye.
She calls her old GP from back in that town,
but now they just route her elsewhere and she's down.
The new docs prescribe her a different kind pill,
yet nothing seems certain, her body won't still.
I blink up from the floor, still feeling my head,
where did that dizziness come from, my dear bed?
My shoe's stuck under the couch now, this floor,
I should've waited—like I warned myself before.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: She freezes a laugh, a fake kind of smile,
the storm clouds gather and break in a while.
Her eye is still fixed on his raised hand,
but the memory lands like a ghost in the sand.
I wear these shoes because they're safe, you know,
they lack the charm but they never let me go.
There's something sad in how they fit so wrong,
yet every step still feels the same, all along.
She stands near the mic like she's in her own zone,
scrolling through her phone like she owns the phone.
The PA system bursts into feedback crash,
and every camera lights up with a flash.
She stares at the sky where the clouds can't stay still,
wondering why they won't settle and fill
a clear shape, instead of just changing form,
while she waits for a sign that it's not a storm.
I watch the clouds transform in softest shape,
they carry me away from daily escape.
One looks like you, and gently bends to love,
I blink—it's gone, but stays forever above.
You dim the screen but the colors stay bright,
a habit so strong you can't stay away at night.
You tap through the feed as your fingers auto-scroll,
and wonder if this feels better than whole.
My cat twirls around when the dusk begins to spin,
her eyes glowing bright like a ghostly thin.
She leaps through the air, chasing the light's last dance,
thinking every flicker is worth the wild chance.
You count the coins but forget the first scan,
the register beeps like some twisted fan.
The machine spits cash out, you trip and you fail,
your dimes roll off the counter in a trail.
My fingers find rhythm and keep up the beat,
It echoes through windows out onto the street.
I'm dancing alone with a joy only found
In two sticks on wood, making loud fun on the ground.
She walks through the park as the leaves fall straight down,
kids cheer when the mess hits the main town.
With every step, she moves like a dream of grace,
and the wind turns the street into her special place.
You sing so loud the pipes all echo loud,
pretending your voice is meant for a crowd.
When the water stops, you know you'll miss
the only moment you feel you fit this.
Her eyes are open but fixed on the still,
she hasn't moved since her thoughts began to will.
Her head is full of the things she can't find,
all the answers seem stuck somewhere behind.
She blames the whole tech stack for this one mess,
when really it was just a setup for success.
She takes out the old ones and jams them in tries,
but the device still rolls its LED eyes.
You pause mid-sentence, the flash won't reset,
it stutters again, it's not going to let.
You check the screen, the image lacks light,
your hands clench the phone, your fingers go tight.
She flips the flapjack with flair in mid-air,
A perfect arc lands it right where it's there.
The surface turns golden, the edges get bold,
She grins like a cook who hasn't been told.
I slipped right into a sugar-filled mess,
this floor was wiped down with honey, I guess.
It's a sticky, gooey, sneaky little trap,
I try to walk past it but just give it a slap.
You stand outside, unsure if I can hear your call,
The silence stretches out across the sprawl.
You knock again—no hum, no light, no chance,
Just static thoughts across this empty expanse.
She turns her desk lamp on before the morning light,
adjusts her chair just so—her grip feels just right.
She sips her coffee slow, lets hope begin to grow,
and starts to act as if she's got it all to show.
I left the honey spoon in a glorious mess,
the ants will probably show up just to guess.
It's liquid gold, but now it's gone cold,
and I made a move far too messy and bold.
We didn't go on a trail or take a long hike,
so I'm not sure how he got all muddy like.
There's no evidence left but prints as a clue,
and maybe a sock still stuck to his shoe.
She thought she'd crease it her own special way,
but every fold was the same as the day.
It twisted and buckled, refused to be map,
turning her neatness into a trap.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: You told a flat joke and it fell out of joke,
the room turned quiet like something had broke.
The show's laugh track still plays, unasked sound,
now everyone laughs just to make it all around.
I dance with the box wrapped tight in red string while,
the ribbon keeps tangling my feet and my smile.
One step off the beat, and we both take a fall,
but I laugh and spin us back into it, all.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: You wake to a world lit with morning's soft glow,
The sky makes a show out of clouds long ago.
A spider spins secrets across every thread,
Light drips like a blessing where silence has spread.
You sat through the whole thing just to show
your love for the script — and to prove you still know
how to clap at the parts the strangers all cheer,
even though it's loud and ruins your ear.
She leaves her wet brush leaning against the time,
it's more than a mess—it's a hygiene crime.
The bristles are bent, the handle looks blue,
it's holding on only with mold and old glue.
You follow the squirrel's plan, searching for a clue,
convinced it's smart, though you doubt it's all true.
You dig near the oak, under last year's tree,
and find your lost keys—but no buried fee.
They promise a future that's built on a lie,
claiming the product will paint me the sky.
I pass the billboard again, half-see it, sold
to dreams that are shiny but not real or gold.
I stare at the pile of dirty clothes,
my patience shrinks as the mountain grows.
The laundry basket takes up too much room,
and the clutter's turning joy into gloom.

topic: shaving a cake with a spoon
lines: I tried to make it look smooth and flat,
but the frosting kept falling back like a bat.
I carved out each peak with a shaky swirl,
wishing I was the baker instead of the girl.
You call this a mess? I'll clean it all mess,
but first I need time to draw and to confess.
You ask me to stop, but I'm not giving up,
my coffee's gone cold while I draw in this cup.

topic: clouds gathering on a summer afternoon
lines: She looks up and says the sky's about to cry,
"This heat can't hold out, it's got to die."
The clouds move too slow for her grumpy low,
she mutters the storm isn't worth the slow show.
She counts the coins twice before she dares shop,
then double-checks prices at the checkout stop.
Her fingers don't loosen their white-knuckled grip,
the strap digs in if she even tries to slip.
She sits there still in the driver's seat,
her fingers tapping against the heat.
Her eyes stay fixed on the words to say,
while cars grow tired and drift away.
My whole body throbs with a crampy ache,
I twist from my chair for a stiff-limbed break.
The desk has turned me into a crooked spine,
my posture now matches a jagged line.
You practiced your jokes but they fell flat, no talk,
you tried small talk by the coffee shop walk.
You spilled your latte, and it felt all wrong,
but you kept smiling through the quiet and long.
You blamed it on coffee and last night's mess,
but now you're afraid to touch the keyboard and press.
Maybe this could be the day you go clean,
or at least try not to let it feel mean.
You squeezed too hard and now it's full of paste,
a white catastrophe you never waste.
You stare into the mess, trying to stay calm,
but there's no peace in that cold porcelain balm.
I hit send on something I meant to keep wrong,
a truth I'd been carrying inside me so long.
They never said much, but I know it broke my heart—
now we're both just trying to stay close while we part.
You spot the envelope tacked on your saw,
it's bold as a warning from landlord or law.
You text your roommate, "Can you make the call?"
By morning, it's paid—don't lose hope for it all.
I gave up hope when the paste ran out,
I screamed at the tube (no, I didn't shout).
It stayed dead solid, still squeezed flat,
now I'm brushing in silence, no more chat.
You think there's some meaning behind her stare—no clue,
She's just watching the sky turn a brighter blue.
The breeze smells like nothing, the birds fly with air,
she'd rather ignore you than meet your sad glare.
That plant has been giving me the cold stare,
It dangles its leaves in this stale indoor air.
"It just needs more light," I told the same lie,
Now it's brown and bent, ready to die.
She's got the rhythm, she's perfect in her moves,
the radio's on and she's dancing to the grooves.
Her hair is wild, the cat just watches the dish,
I'll never tell her but I kind of wish…
The machine roars with a fan's deafening heat,
the same warning message flashes and repeat.
Your fingers hover, ready to scream,
while your unsaved work feels like a lost dream.
It's just a pencil sharpener gone off its day,
it coughs and clacks and refuses to say
goodbye to the last inch of leaden shavings—
you laugh anyway, calling it "charming savings."
I left my wallet at home, not mine,
but you paid for both our dinner and wine.
You're not collecting or asking it's due,
it's just how you see things — this is your view.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: You said something dry but it wasn't the joke,
the laugh track blared when you just spoke.
The whole office turned to look in the room,
your silence was louder than any boom.

topic: a coffee cup on the curb
lines: She sees her old cup, half full but too near,
It's been a cold winter, she lost it this year.
She bends down and asks "who left it, why?"
No answer, just wind as she walks away by.
The shovel makes a dull metallic clank,
I toss snow toward the melting bank.
I dig through the frost so cold and so deep,
but my breath still escapes and won't keep.
I laced up tight before I hit the run,
but halfway through the laces were undone.
I slowed to adjust each fraying lace,
while joggers passed me with a smirk or a face.
I straightened my paperclip with a bend,
we called it a rod and we fished with a friend.
We lured in small bugs and we baited a fly,
the fish never came but it felt good to try.

topic: sending a text to the wrong person
lines: She typed a message to her ex and hit send,
no undo, no hiding from that friend.
He asked her out—she panicked mid-date,
now they're debating phones all evening late.
I swear I had this thing on perfect luck,
now I'm standing here where the cart is stuck.
I've tried every combo like some lost code,
but the keypad laughs in my pathetic mode.
You missed the perfect sunset with no shot,
left your camera at home, just forgot.
But skies still painted hues in slow storm,
and beauty found you, even without film in form.
You wear your hard hat like a safety zone,
but the boss tosses tools from the upper stone.
You duck to avoid the inevitable fall,
while time ticks away and nothing goes right at all.
She's drained from laughing and too much talk,
her smile flags even on the walk.
But when she reads in bed, the spark
returns — just her and the late-night dark.
My dog goes into a full-bodied spin,
the joy on his face fits right with my grin.
He circles again, it's a wild little loop,
I'm cheering my furry fool like a whole fan troop.
I still don't know why I dressed to match her clue,
we're strangers who just both chose loud cobalt blue.
I fear she'll ask me how I picked this to meet,
my silence speaks faster than I can beat.
You're walking down the street, a color-mix mess,
still smiling from the party gone yes.
A single strip of paper clings to a strand,
but you wave it off — it's too cute to be grand.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: I saw a flash that caught my eye's gleam,
I waded through the cold and muddy stream.
This wasn't just some dull or common prize,
it sparkled like the stars in someone's eyes.
They say this cliffside path has the best view,
but I'm tripping over rocks the whole way through.
At the final twist they cheer, "Now you can bend!"
I take the picture—perfect—and then I send.
You scrapped your old ritual, devised a new plan,
You bought a French press from an online van.
Now every morning, you craft your dark brew,
You sip on strength and feel powerful, you.
I overslept again and ran too late,
my mind is spinning through this morning debate.
I sprint down halls, I could faint or pass,
but the bell is ringing—once more to miss class.
Your headset dangles on one lop-sided side,
it's barely clinging, almost ready to hide.
You tug the loose wire with a mischievous grin,
like it's a challenge you're determined to win.
You claimed this bench before you had the spot,
I asked politely, but now I have got
no choice but to shift to the edge of my weight,
your belongings still sprawled like they own this estate.
You kissed her right there beneath the gray,
she didn't pull back or run you away.
Her lips said your name like a bold new claim,
you lit up the night with that electric flame.
