She left her phone in the wrong cloud mode,
And uploaded chaos with no clear code.
Now everyone's seeing the family's old date,
She sighs—looks like privacy met its fate.
They pause their sandwich to read the screen,
a notification lights up in green.
They scroll through replies, they never will find
what they really want, but still chase the mind.
I blow until my cheeks turn rosy and so,
they float up past the tulips to go.
The grass still keeps that perfect springtime green,
since I've been small enough to dream unseen.
She adjusts her glasses but the image stays frame,
the credits roll by fast, she can't read the name.
She leans in close, the pixels still blur,
but the popcorn is warm, so she smiles and stir.
I look up now, the world wide as the sky,
the wind hums past me like a child's "fly!"
The chains creak out a lullaby just me,
and for a moment, I feel light, not free.
My battery's gone from full to flat,
and now my texts won't send or chat.
Just when I need it most it goes out,
like it knows how much I want to shout.
It hovers so close but it never goes still,
the way it tilts feels like danger or thrill.
They hold their breath, eyes fixed on the wait,
as if the sky's about to decide someone's fate.
You lean into the bend where the road won't bend,
the tires whisper something they can't send.
For a moment you forget how hard it's glide,
and let the wobble slide it gently aside.
They stood too late on the retreating tide,
phone buzzing with no last ferry wide.
Time ticking loud where there was nothing left to wait,
the terminal lights blinking at the sealed-off gate.

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: You read the review with a stressed-out stare,
it calls the croissants greasy and cold as air.
The barista on Instagram would never fail,
but here's a five-star post from yesterday trail.

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: I hold the phone up, posing just right for the frame,
then type my caption, twice — forgot my name.
The camera waits while I avoid its stare,
half-hoping someone's out there in the air.
She left the party, but still hears the crowd,
her head buzzing with voices talking out loud.
She wants the noise to just slowly fade,
but silence is still too much for her shade.
You swear that robin has claimed this one spot,
pecking like it owns the yard you forgot.
It won't budge an inch while you dig and you wait,
as if the worm beneath is its divine fate.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: They flutter and fight in a frantic race,
each wingbeats a drum in this frozen place.
The air bites my cheeks, it's too sharp, too cold,
I've seen better days, but these birds are bold.
You call it "borrowing," but I say it's all mine,
you take from my closet and leave no good sign.
Now I'm stuck wearing shirts that feel too bare,
while your conscience floats through the house like air.
She moves like the sun chasing fading light,
turning the gloom of dusk into bright.
Her shadow walks steady, we fall in to talk,
and the silence between us feels less like chalk.
I'm best at reading the shapes in the sky,
they call me out for my trained eye.
A dragon, a lion — they were all made
from cotton and breeze in a summer parade.
I reached for the chips and spilled them like a snack,
now "E" and "R" won't let go, they're both on attack.
I swear my laptop is possessed by a ghost,
it types "pepperoni" every time I host.
My cat spins wild in a frenzy to see,
convinced the walls are hiding what's not free.
He leaps through air but there's nothing to run,
just dust in light that he mistakes for fun.
One bud stays tucked in my jacket's left blue,
the other plays tricks, or so it feels true.
I've ransacked the couch, the laptop, the bin,
but only silence lives inside this within.
We built whole worlds through cheap plastic games,
our heroes dueling without real flames.
We'd stage the most dramatic scenes,
long before we knew how to read the screens.
I pour oil into the pan—it starts to hiss,
not sure if this is cooking or pure bliss.
I wait for the onions to turn golden brown,
but they still smell like garlic in my crown.
You carry the weight of the world on your rest,
pages pressing deep into your chest.
The spine of each book holds secrets you know,
but only to those who lift your load low.
My hands are raw from the grip of this steel,
but I keep digging to find some feel.
Maybe a plant will come from this seed,
if I can thaw the soil I so need.
The wheels try to balance but just can't spin,
the gravel gives way every time I'm on in.
I lean left, I lean right—just a little rock,
but my handlebars rattle from the tire's shock.
She stands beneath the branches, letting the beams
fall on her skin like liquid warmth or streams.
The sun lifts her face, now glowing in its light,
as if the world were made to crown her with such height.
She gave up heels for a softer, more grounded style,
she walks through the park for an hour or two while.
Her feet stay happy from morning to tread,
and her posture becomes kinder to her head.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: She traces the coastlines as if seeing the sea,
She ponders where treasure might lie by the key.
Her finger leaves smudges, a ghost-like mark,
The past seems alive in her curious spark.
You weigh the ethics and the cookie gram,
the rules crumble like an old raspberry jam.
You stash the evidence behind the fridge hide,
and smile on the guilty, cookie-filled side.
She winds the music box with care and a key,
dust and old notes fall out as debris.
Her smile shows the joy that she holds in her pride,
the melody dances soft and serene beside.
She calls it masterful, she calls it art,
says every swirl holds meaning from her heart.
A scraped-up knee can't stop her from a scrape,
the world feels better through this little escape.
Your eyelids are heavy and droop toward your head,
the clock says "don't," but your body says "bed."
You'll eat later, there's still leftover crumb,
the coffee won't help—you're just not that numb.
You wait outside a ride's correct zone,
your app blares alerts but the driver won't phone.
You rethink this whole seamless new plan—
the promo code expired, your cash has just ran.
She draws the whole world in crayon art,
purple suns and mountains made of heart.
Her hands move fast, her face lights up like fire,
no sketchbook could hold such pure desire.
You said you'd pay but never even took
the cup from my hand, still warm by the hook.
"It's decaf," you said with a grin so sly—
now every sip tastes like goodbye.
I listen to how the wind chimes play in the air,
their song seems to promise the world won't tear.
They swing and they spin without any plan or sin,
and I feel something shift deep inside me within.
The can burst open with a small, loud pop,
he froze mid-step, both hands out to stop.
A soda mist rose where the keys begin to mist,
but he carefully lifted each part back to twist.
You hear your name across the echoing hall,
The voice repeats it against every wall.
It sounds so close but never comes too near,
You trace the sound but no one's in your ear.
You watched it take your garden's careful crop,
too tiny to scold or even stop.
Now the patch is gone, the soil turned bare,
you laugh into the wind, soft and spare.
She took the last bite from the crusty edge,
left me a sliver, just one tiny wedge.
It wasn't fair, but she called it an art—
"You'll live," she said, with a sly little smart.
She clicks "present" but her screen won't turn on,
Her slides are now floating somewhere they're gone.
Her boss makes a face like she's stuck in a place
Where tech fails, and time just slips away, no trace.

topic: a child drawing on the table
lines: She picks a crayon to match every hue,
then sticks a paper star with her spilled glue.
Her socks are off and she draws with her feet,
a rainbow mess, but we'll call it quite sweet.

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: I set the table like it's some big scene,
then pose for the camera, cold as a screen.
The whole world could be here—I'm still alone,
the silence so thick, it might as well be stone.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: You get so busy with the mess and the dirt,
your favorite top is soaked from collar to shirt.
It's just a silly little mud pie game,
but you don't care who sees or gives you your name.
The screen flashes once—her name in my eye,
I let it go straight to voicemail to die.
Her ringtone was always soft and full of tone,
but now her voice is just a ghost on my phone.
You watched the screen say "Total not yet paid,"
while customers lined up behind you like parade.
You printed it twice, still no clear receipt,
but you won the day—glitch meets its defeat.
All the pastries taste exactly the same,
Even the syrup fails to bear a name.
Toasted bread is more crumb than dry,
Coffee here could make a diner want to die.
They spend their lives thumbing endlessly scroll,
a deep online search for a new soul.
A double-tap won't help if you don't click,
it's not just pixels—it's people, not just a trick.
I'm chopping carrots while stuck on board,
the silence sharp as any sword.
The rhythm hits my carrot core—
this job could take me hours, or more.
She jolts from her pillow and swears at her head,
stumbles back down to reclaim her warm bed.
The room takes a spin like it's trying to float,
she mutters, "This isn't a cruise ship — why boat?"
I swear this house is haunted by your cold,
you say I'm drama queen, just being bold.
We circle back to fight about the mode,
like we need a marriage license to decode.
You trace the feathers lost in the sky,
where wind and trees let them gently lie.
They flutter and twist in a quiet dance,
as if given a second flight by chance.
Her boots slap the pavement, loud on the floor,
She counts off her steps in a rhythm of four.
A song plays inside her, strong as the wind,
The world moves faster, she leaves it behind.
The alarm flickers bright and I shut off the light,
My brain doesn't want to start this morning fight.
Coffee brews slow but it won't fix my head,
This week's already stuck in my dread.
She follows the map with no hint of a clue,
the screen shows a road that's not in her view.
Now traffic is piling behind her too late,
she forgot to update her old GPS date.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: I found a rock that caught the morning glint,
smooth as a button and green as a mint.
I placed it in my pocket to try to keep,
now it's tucked under dreams where I sleep.
The buzz from my phone starts real loud in the dark,
It's texts, emails, ads — every app leaves its mark.
I try to just mute them, but settings still fail,
So silence stays elusive down time's long trail.
You pull out the dress that makes your body spin,
It fits your old curves but not your new thin skin.
You walk through the house in your favorite way,
With every step, it's a mini ballet.
My cat won't come when I try to sit,
she naps right there where I just sat a bit.
She rolls her eyes when I reach out to roll,
but purrs so loud it warms my whole soul.
He woke to a puddle where his favorite mess
had landed overnight — no way to guess
the culprit. The dog lay calm, just roll
ing off the scent like it had no soul.
This dented plate is my living proof,
it's seen more sweat than this gym's old roof.
Every dent marks a lift I once tried to dent,
now it's just part of me—both iron and bent.
The crowd won't move—I can't get a view,
They're all here for a train, but I don't think it's true.
I inch my way through, determined to go,
Just so I can see what this platform will show.

topic: a quiet moment on the porch
lines: They rock in the chair like it's a porch swing,
tapping rhythm on their shirt pocket thing.
A squirrel passes—both stop to check their eyes,
whispering secrets to the trees in wise.

topic: a cart with a broken wheel
lines: She pushes the cart with a creaky roll,
the kind of task that beats you to your soul.
It groans beneath the weight she won't unload,
though every block feels like the same old road.
The lock's been frozen stiff since five a.m., cold,
but she won't leave it chained, not even bold.
She taps the U-lock with the ice-covered key,
and smiles when the click finally sets it free.
You stare at the tracks hoping for your train,
only to watch it leave the station again.
The digital board confirms a major delay,
while strangers practice yoga on the display.
Your dog begins to howl and yip and bark,
even though it's barely past the dinner dark.
He trots to the door with his old chewed-up lead,
as if he'll starve unless you throw him a feed.
They sleep in a tangle, their skin flushed by dawn,
the room still holding their warmth when they're gone.
A pillowcase crumples where moisture has ache,
and salted regret starts to slowly break.
She bats the glass and the water begins to spill,
I know she's done it before and she always will.
Her tail flicks with pride, her eyes wide with shock,
The kitchen drips time like a faulty clock.

topic: sitting on the porch steps at twilight
lines: She sits on the step where the light turns still,
her eyes follow shadows down past the hill.
Her hands trace old thoughts, an unspoken ache,
she waits for a silence that won't quite break.
They're wide awake at two, with nowhere to be late,
snacking on snacks and coffee from a chipped plate.
The screen glows soft as they send one more chat,
the memes hit loud but the silence stays flat.
You swear your hip is now made out of bone,
you text your friends from your couch with your phone.
They send their jokes but you can't laugh,
you're too busy groaning for the nurse's staff.
That single blink captured the best shot,
you stood in the light, the perfect spot.
You paused for the frame, struck the still pose,
and time understood—this was the one you chose.
He sits outside like he knows how to sigh,
watching my every move with his soulful eye.
I toss him a scrap from the compost pile log,
but he waits for more—this old hungry dog.
You toss but can't escape the fevered heat,
the clock ticks twice, then repeats the beat.
The sheets refuse to let the morning cling,
you lie there certain this is your worst thing.
She stands apart from the frantic stampede to wait,
holding her ticket tight like a last act of freight.
Her eyes scan the board, searching for something clear,
while the train she needs feels impossibly near.
He checks the sky, but there's no sign of rain,
the crew jokes it's going to fall again.
A loud bang echoes—a beam near his crack,
he ducks fast, breath held, but nothing hits back.

topic: a cup of cold coffee on the table
lines: I left my morning warmth behind on this brew,
I should've finished it before I just threw
the dregs down the drain while I sat on the rest
of old regrets now pooled cold in my chest.

topic: texting 'i miss u' out of nowhere
lines: They type it late, like a text they meant to send,
a name from years ago, now just a distant friend.
They wonder why it came, but don't ask why,
—the last word left when love turns into goodbye.
She steps onto the pale gray tile,
her morning thoughts drift on for a while.
A shiver climbs up her bare feet's chill,
as time moves slow to break her still.
She coiled it gently with a little hope,
as if it might behave more than a rope.
But once she plugged it in, it fused them all apart,
and called her phone a *very* unkind smart.
I sprinted across town but missed the final run,
the clock is my silent, relentless gun.
Your messages pop up with "Where are you late?"
The minutes press down like the guilt's full weight.
I wiggle the pad, but it won't really move,
I need this to work—there's software to prove.
I tap every button to get it to click,
a restart might help if I act real quick.
They swore they'd reply when they saw your last send,
but silence is their new favorite trend.
You try to text or even make a call,
but they're behind a wall you can't crawl.
You stand in the center, you won't give way,
the whole world watches your bold display.
Your confidence swells with unshaken pride,
the crowd parts slowly like shifting tide.
I lift the net in an empty place to move,
there's nothing left here to catch or to prove.
The clouds are drifting where the light breaks through the sky,
and I wonder why I came back for this goodbye.

topic: shaving a cake with a spoon
lines: I told them not to touch the frosting mess,
now they've turned my layer cake into a guess.
I tried to fix it with a spoon to dip,
but the crumbs slipped, and I just lost my grip.
I've seen time fold itself into every slow
curl of green where the moss likes to grow.
Its breath is a hush, soft and barely a hush,
not meant for the feet of a hurried rush.
You water it daily but never quite pour
the right amount through the cracked front door.
The soil is dry but you swear it's just soil,
until it turns brittle and lifeless as foil.
I checked my wallet, the coupon is date-stamped old,
it slipped past midnight, its promise now cold.
I drop the paper like a lost cause or a drop,
and watch the discount just vanish from my shop.
She sips her tea, but it won't bring her calm,
she traces old fears in her dampened palm.
She stares at the clock, waiting for rest,
while worry tightens deep in her chest.
They flip through your history, scanning your chart,
Each specialist offering a new way to start.
You track every symptom, set benchmarks for goal,
With each test passed, you feel stronger in soul.
You lift the lid on the cracked plastic case,
and smile at the scuff marks on time's quiet place.
The music still hums when the disc starts to spin,
your hands feel like ghosts on the grooves of your skin.
Your dog still likes to act like he'll bite or bark,
but you won't let him out unless it's fully dark.
You walk him once a week, that's your only walk,
I'm sure he'd rather nap than listen to you talk.
I still know how to fly without my type,
the E key's so worn it looks like a stripe.
These letters are fading, but my jokes don't fade—
they just spill out faster, like a laugh cascade.
I slipped into your shoes to give it a try,
but the sole felt hollow, my step never dry.
They don't fit right, but I'm too proud to admit—
I walk out anyway, with borrowed grit.
I tap the screen but it won't let me go,
the buttons don't work and the error doesn't show.
There's a paper notice about a missing fee,
I grin and flash my old student ID key.
The dock's lit only by the faintest rain,
I stand there still, unsure how long I'll remain.
The boat's gone now, the tides pull in too late,
I'll miss my shift, but it feels worth the wait.
You count the coins with perfect speed,
the register can't keep up to feed.
You know the math will always be right,
your hands work fast but never feel tight.
The teacher's cough echoes through the quiet room,
the stillness feels more like a crypt than a tomb.
Time crawls as we wait for the clock to tick,
the air grows heavy, suffocating, thick.
I listen how the stream makes magic there,
it hums beneath the soft September air.
I watch the moss and ferns begin to grow,
as sunlight hits the water's quiet glow.
I'll skip the line and still miss the last pass,
this coffee's got more grit than backyard grass.
They charge me five bucks just to watch them pour,
but hey, I need the fuel—buy me some more.
A balloon fights gravity, tugged by the air,
Its string loops around me and gets stuck in my hair.
I wiggle and dance trying to set it free,
Like a puzzle, but I'm the missing key.
You stand beneath the rusted bus stop rain,
The metal groans and leaks again.
A slow drip falls where your shoe sits drip,
You tense, afraid you might slip.
You bought the treadmill to get moving at start,
but now it's a relic that's falling apart.
It doesn't help your fitness or your life,
it just shrieks like a cheese grater with a knife.
My smartwatch tries to tell me something in my mind,
It buzzes sudden, cryptic, and unkind.
Each pulse is louder than the last one's beat,
But nothing's wrong—just static in my heat.
She moved it from shade to a window's cold light,
The leaves curled like fists in a dry, sunlit tight.
Now she checks soil, checks clocks, assigns the fault blame,
But the roots just give up, still not looking the same.
I memorized phrases but can't get the flow,
my tongue twists even the simplest "hello."
I fear someone will laugh and I'll want to break,
but they smile, nod — I guess it's a small mistake.

topic: reading under the covers with a flashlight
lines: I turn the page by light from my hidden page,
the room watches me like it's holding its cage.
The shadow creeps in and I feel so caught,
but the book's my escape, though I'm racing my thought.
You trace the wall as if it held a clue,
your tongue paints patterns in the morning blue.
I watch you work like it could fulfill some need,
but nothing tastes like what a cat should feed.
You staged a full-blown debate with your fight
over who deserved the last slice that night.
Now the box sits empty with nothing left there,
but crumbs and guilt tangled in your dinner hair.
My finger hovers where the button should ring,
I kick the baseboard—still no response from the thing.
I text them the password they never could code,
we stare at each other in awkward new mode.
She lets her phone go silent after each call,
still tangled in dreams, she doesn't want to sprawl.
There's peace in this stillness, a quiet kind of hope,
as if the world's tether is now just a rope.
My laptop's getting hot, it's turning into heat,
The fan just whirs and says the same thing—repeat.
I try to lift it up, I blow a little puff,
It melts my socks instead of cooling down this stuff.
They flip the flapjack with a robotic flip,
their spatula tight with a white-knuckled grip.
The steam begins to rise from the pan like mist,
but their eyes are glued to the screen of a wrist.
I've let the silence stay too long in the past,
I lost the chance to keep it going fast.
Your name still pops up like a text message ring,
but time's a ghost—no easy fix for that old thing.
She nearly took a hard fall from a trip,
but saved her balance with quick footwork and grip.
Now she bends down with a laugh and a lace,
pulling it tight where it once was a place.
The kitchen fills with that familiar smoke,
you laugh it off like it's some old inside joke.
We sip our coffee, let the moment hold,
neither of us rushing, neither one turns bold.
You left your jacket here—no note, no trace,
it hangs on the chair like a memory's space.
I almost expect you'll come back to wear
it through the door, but the room holds only air.
Your playlist loses its rhythm and beat,
the left earbud falls, no one sees the feat.
You freeze mid-step, the world feels a drop,
your song is half-mute, your mood takes a crop.
I love the chaos of the morning rush,
strangers bumping hips but never flush.
I breathe a quiet, grateful sort of sigh,
as sunlight breaks through the dirty sky.
I arrived hours before the flight's gate,
now I'm sweating through this endless wait.
My suitcase wheels get stuck trying to roll,
could they check my bags or just my soul?
The cold has turned metal as stiff as a chill,
I wait for it to bend or move from its still.
I flex my whole palm, I apply more grip,
the ice cracks wide—glory, I don't have to trip.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: You feel it all day — that annoying little there,
it's not a loose thread or a piece of hair.
You rip off your sleeve at the local bar,
but the toothpick stays, your weird new star.
Your eyes drift toward the blue glow of the screen,
missing every sharp edge of the scene.
Words blur into shapes, colors start to fade,
as your lids grow heavy, pulling down in a shade.
The shovel shivers in a world turned cold,
I dig with determination, strong and bold.
Each chunk feels like a stubborn rock,
my breath hangs still, the sky won't unlock.
I tap the heart before I even see
how deep the post goes or what it means for me.
It wasn't some pity—I had a real thought,
I liked the truth, so I chose to show I ought.
I walk down the empty movie house's hall,
expecting a voice to scream or to call.
The screen flickers like it's trying to fade,
while shadows creep toward me, sharp as a blade.
You swore you'd delete old messages last time,
but here we are, committing audio crime.
Now no one can leave a message or call,
your phone's a record scratch, spinning in a ball.
You need your coffee darker than the dark,
but no one left a spoon or even a mark.
The pot's gone cold—your second attempt to brew
just proves there are not enough beans for a few.
My camera flash tried way too hard to glow,
It lit my face like something from way below.
I didn't want to look this good, I swear—
A selfie angel dropped a filter in my hair.
You check every room for the perfect spot,
your hands twist into a nervous knot.
You place it and step back with a sigh,
but the light glints off it—right in your eye.
Your screen refuses to load anything yet,
you tap and you wait, your nerves start to fret.
The bar just won't fill, it spins in a roll,
while you question your tech-savvy soul.
Your screen keeps scanning you with cold blue scan,
You blink once too late, your face starts to tan.
The world feels too sharp, your head begins to ache,
You close it all down for a human break.
You stare into the puddle's wet deep,
pretending it's a dream you just can't sleep.
You draw a rainbow with an earnest act,
but the rain washes it all away—just a fact.
You check the battery—three percent in sight,
your thumb hovers nervously above the light.
You pray for Wi-Fi to at least be save,
but it's not worth the plea—your screen just won't cave.
She stares at the screen where we stood long apart,
Her dress shines too bright in that pixelated heart.
She swipes through the photos, her fingers pause mid-scroll,
And wonders if love still holds true to her whole soul.
She types "u up?" as the hours drift through,
but knows she's just talking to old you.
Her phone lights up the dark with a soft hum,
while silence waits where you could have come.
I see your face reflected in this coffee mark,
the pixels run where the memory went dark.
That moment slipped through like the morning spill,
I'll never save it, though I try my will.
The escalator's stuck and won't budge or move,
We're all stepping sideways in our own weird groove.
Someone nearly took a full-blown trip,
I grabbed their sleeve—phew! That was a grip.
This flimsy plastic net is such a tool,
It snapped when I tried to catch something cool.
I chase the butterfly across the dash,
It zipped right past, and I face-plant a crash.
The coffee hit your essay's final page,
a brown stain spreading in no particular cage.
You traced the water's mark like a dull ring,
the mess still feels like something you could cling.
She laughs the loudest when the joke's the worst out,
her voice cuts through the silence like a shout.
Her smile feels warm, her laughter feels so old,
like memories caught in a crackling gold.
I heard the balloons inflate without a care,
then froze when the doorbell gave me a scare.
I knew something was wrong, my chest began to ache,
and here it goes again — my heart starts to break.
You wave it down at the red light stop,
it pulls up with no back window shop.
Its left turn blinker still won't flash its tail,
but somehow you trust its crooked trail.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: You trace the edges of time in that frame,
Each face still carries the day they took the name.
Colors are softening, details begin to fade,
But memories walk on like a quiet parade.
It said "turn left here" but that road was lead,
Now I'm lost in a zone where the signal's dead.
"Recalculating," it chirps with a fix,
I've learned from bad apps not to trust their tricks.

topic: paying a fine at the window
lines: I rolled up to the booth like it wasn't a stop,
the cop leaned out and asked me to crop.
I handed him cash with a slow, deep sigh,
he winked and said "No hard feelings—just bye."
You check your phone but there's no one to call,
just silence and the weight of the ball.
The jacket on the chair feels like it's from home,
maybe they'll return, maybe you won't roam.
I press play just to hear the whole thing from belt,
the tape hisses along like a cat on hot felt.
I rewind fast, but it still tries to skip,
I laugh as it stumbles and dances its trip.
She left her mug too close to the open sheet,
and dreamed the same mistake would never repeat.
The coffee soaked through every page in ink,
but somehow still got an A as a project link.
The sky lets loose with a sudden rain,
you stand there smiling, choose to remain.
The bus is late, we count the wait,
our shoulders touch beneath this gate.
That streak on your shoulder looks like art,
it's proof you own life and play your part.
You wear the mishap like a bold new mark,
every flaw on you just makes you spark.
They stuck the wifi code on the fridge with tape,
hoping maybe it'll stay where it can't escape.
But guests still ask for the password by hand,
and they always call the network "Sticky Brand."
She rents a corner of your office room,
her keyboard clacking like a loom.
You tried noise-canceling—hopeless left,
her buzz bleeds through the silence, time theft.
It used to buzz through the morning cold and calls,
that shrill, familiar sound against these walls.
I miss the way I'd groan but never get up still,
now silence wakes me—no machine to tell me "will."
The afternoon light spills through in gold,
catching your hair where the breeze can't hold.
You lift your face like it knows the place
where shadows don't settle, only grace.
I missed the turn and now I'm completely wrong,
my GPS repeats the same sad song.
But ahead there's a sign I might yet find,
and hope returns to this tired old mind.
The printer always gets a paper jam,
I slam my fist on top like a trained ham.
It coughs out a page—my entire job—
half torn off and blurred, like it tried to rob.
I came here first, this whole bench is mine in the park,
he says nothing but makes a slow, quiet remark.
There's enough space, but he spreads out for more room,
his backpack now sits where my legs used to loom.
You start to scroll through someone's heated scroll,
they've lost all sense of time or self-control.
You hit "skip" before you even get to read,
your brain's already buzzing at their wordy head.
Your hand was warm when our fingers brushed,
and the room felt quiet, like time got hushed.
I didn't mean to let it slip my mind,
but later I kept trying to find.
He tries to give the cloud a better form,
but the page keeps filling up like a storm.
His hand moves slowly, still he cannot draw,
maybe clouds don't follow that old art law.

topic: a child's drawings on the fridge
lines: You tape another drawing to the fridge's show,
just like the ones from when they were five and would grow.
But time slips faster than the paper can hold,
and your hands freeze touching the magnetic cold.
You see the message but decide to ping,
later you'll act like you forgot the thing.
You fake your last active to fix the date,
but doom rolls in, as always, on fate.
You try to forget the mess of your play,
but the colors still haunt you this day.
You dig through the dirt for some trace
of joy that once lived on that rainbow's face.
They call my mess an installation of art,
I don't even have a pair left off the chart.
It's all part of my quirky, unspoken pride,
nobody told me I needed a style guide.
My knees remind me of an old wine case—
creaky when I try to take my proper place.
Each step up climbs but gives the same old ache,
while I imagine swimming in some heated lake.
I squeeze a mountain right against the wall,
it sprawls across the counter, wild and tall.
My roommate calls it modern art, a joke,
but I just stare and almost spit it out to choke.

topic: the smell of pancakes in the morning
lines: I wake to the scent that fills up the air,
a promise of warmth settling right there.
I pause for a moment, I choose to savor,
the world feels more kind in this little favor.
The chains are aging, they groan with a rust,
I used to believe they'd hold me up, not bust.
I still love how the seat makes me sway,
but time and the wind can't turn back this way.
I thought the train was going to leave real fast,
but the board said "Delayed—hold on, not past."
I paced the platform, checking my phone,
now I've got a story I'm not trying to tone.
You spot the fake grin behind their real,
It doesn't match your snack-time meal.
They've got the motions, but not the clue,
So you smile back—you know what to do.
I asked him where he was going from his seat,
he told me twice about his brother's defeat.
"This way," he says, but we're still off the route,
I wonder if he's lost or just in a doubt.
You took the whole afternoon off for the time,
declaring it baking season's new prime.
The oven was hot, the mix ready to bake,
you let the frosting melt—for the look's own sake.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: She wears the same expression from the old pose,
caught mid-wave in the faded, wrinkled clothes.
They didn't update the frame when she died,
just added names on the empty space beside.
She praises the breeze from her broken fan,
while her coffee has melted and her hair has ran.
She sips lukewarm wine, lets the day just burn,
and calls it mindfulness when the A/C won't turn.
You flip through the pages of what's come past,
each week marked with deadlines and the last.
You trace every scribble on the old date,
wondering if your life follows this fate.
You think your cat has some secret or clue,
it doesn't blink when the movie gives a cue.
It won't look away, won't give a pass—
it's judging the lawn like it owns the whole grass.

topic: a friend who is always late
lines: I check my phone again for the third hour,
she's running late, again, no power.
I text her: "Where are you? Are you at the door?"
She says: "Still at the cart — this place is a store."
Your face still has that midnight blue glow,
I know you're wired and nowhere near slow.
You scroll through the noise till your eyes start to roll,
but you'd never trade in your pulse for a soul.
You swore your keys vanished into some hide,
I found them last night tucked beneath the side.
You're still searching the cushions for one clue,
while laughing because you just lost your shoe.
You've dropped your old habit of keeping up pace,
you move through the crowd but you never take space.
You let people pass and you never make claim,
a slow walk is yours—no need for a name.

topic: texting 'i miss u' out of nowhere
lines: The screen glows up late, my thumb taps out "blue,"
It's a lie I keep telling myself to be true.
I check if the message was sent in the right tone,
Then wait for a ghost while I scroll feeling alone.
Your body's screaming about some sugar need,
you're half-convinced your brain might start to bleed.
You hunt for a snack but all you find's an old bag,
of pretzels now stale, still pretending it's a drag.

topic: a note tucked inside a card
lines: The note's written in bold, cheap ink,
and signed with a name you don't think.
The sentiment's thin, the smile feels fake,
but you laugh anyway—no will to break.
The sun is low but it feels like fun,
we race through alleys to see who can run.
We laugh and spin until our legs give play,
the shadows stretch where we fade away.
You adjust your glasses to see every frame,
the hero walks in with your old friend's name.
The pixels grow soft as the light starts to fade,
but you hold in your tears behind every shade.
The register sputters, clicks, gives me wrong,
We count in silence, heads nod, walk along.
I drop my cash with a note "we'll get it missed,"
You pause, smile, and just like that—kissed.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: I found a coupon for a half-off snack deal,
now I'm saving cash without having to steal.
I toss it in my bag, act cool while I grab,
then leave the store like I've just won a cab.
She swore she'd never miss a bill or a due,
but lost her wallet and her only clue.
She called the bank at five minutes to call,
then collapsed on the couch in a panicked sprawl.
You watched the ferry slide out of the bay,
the lights dimming as it drifted away.
You never told them you had nothing to weep
but the silence lingered, pulling you deep.
She turns to me suddenly and laughs in the blue,
no joke, no prompt—just a total non-clue.
Her face is all earnest, she's not here to show,
her grin just leaks out from some secret below.
You swear your dog's barking at thin air,
He's chasing ghosts that give no scare.
He'll sit and stare at some random spot,
convinced there's something he just got.
I watch the soft strands unwind so slow,
they slip from my fingers and gently go.
Each loop reminds me of the time we wove thread,
I tuck it behind my ear, keep you near my head.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: She digs a hole so muddy and deep,
then builds her kingdom out of a heap.
She carves the dirt into perfect mold,
and calls it gourmet, mud-pie gold.
You wave your item over the scan,
but nothing happens—it's a strange new plan.
The machine hums loud like it wants to fly,
you laugh and press again, just one more try.
I finally bought a recipe to taste,
I used too much garlic—turns out a paste.
I stir the pot with the fire set slow,
maybe tomorrow I'll actually know.
You click into their latest unfiltered show,
pretending you really want updates you know.
The comments are loud but they're all just chat,
while your old friend's asleep beside your cat.
You still remember that book's final due,
how it held your first love, which turned out not true.
You flipped every page with a quiet, tight rage,
like the story had locked up something you'd cage.
You try to take a picture of its perfect pose,
but the flash scares it off in its dapper clothes.
You laugh and mutter something like "bird nag,"
then swear you'll never call it "the cable tag."
He bought a balloon but it leaked most of its gas,
now it droops like his chances to impress or pass.
The vendor made it into a goofy crown,
claiming it's the only thing he'd rule around town.
You used to drive with your eyes off the zone,
face locked to the screen, thumb flying to phone.
Now you remember when hands held the wheel,
roads had rhythm—and life had a feel.
I used to laugh and we'd have such great talk,
now my phone sits there like it's taking a walk.
Fingers tap faster than any old scroll,
but the silence between hits me in the soul.
You lie awake while the silence grows dark,
A memory flickers like a weak spark.
You trace the words you'll never get to find,
Your heart replays them loud in your mind.
You watch your cat go round the same old why,
She licks the plaster smooth, her tongue feels dry.
She circles once more, you can't see what spot,
But every pass tightens your chest like a shot.
I double-tap to like, but it just doesn't tap,
my thumb gets stuck inside this digital trap.
It asks for more, but all it does is tease me,
a clutter of hearts clogging up my screen's debris.
You sort through the stack where the late snow is cold,
you pause on the bill you've been dreading to hold.
You fold it with care as if paper could bend,
and tuck it away, soft as a gentle friend.
You think it's a fun game, just a quick try,
I sigh but I let you take mine and reply.

my hands shake like a nervous gambler's slip.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: You catch the first hint of morning's soft light,

lines: She watches the morning form diamonds on glass,

it pools on the toast where the heat begins to glow.
Her fingers hover, too shy for a touch,
she savors the moment, a quiet, sweet such.
You bend down low and you leave it behind,
the colors all blend into muddy grind.
Your fingers dig in, the world feels so deep,
but the rain washes all your dreams to sleep.
My lower back has been giving me ache,
I haven't moved for what feels like a break.
Time passes slow in this chair so still,
Like my blood's not flowing, just stuck in a mill.
They type "goodnight" at the stroke of send,
too late for dreams or answers to defend.
It's a lie they've rehearsed the whole long lie,
but I keep reading it into every eye.
He acts like it's his lucky break or prime,
but buddy, cutting the line is a crime.
He grins like he's doing us all a grace,
when he clearly forgot his proper place.
She wears her sweatpants like a statement of grace,
the remote in her hand, she claims this her place.
The credits will roll, but she's sealed her own doom—
no shoes, no makeup, no leaving this room.

topic: a song stuck in your head
lines: It's been on repeat since yesterday's play,
stuck where the chorus meets the loud day.
You hum along but can't quite recall the tune,
like a secret someone's etched into your rune.

topic: a favorite mug with a chip
lines: She still uses the chipped mug every day,
even though I told her to throw it away.
I watch how she holds it like it means the hold,
her fingers trace the rim's faded gold.
The screen is the only light you invite,
The silence of night feels too tight.
You scroll through the chaos, the clickbait, the feed,
Your mind starts to ache, your thoughts start to bleed.
She hears the chime as if it's trying to wake
her from some dream by a quiet lake.
Her finger hovers, curious, so near
to pressing now, maybe this will be the year.
You wait for the green but this feeling is long,
the light just stays stubborn, something's gone wrong.
You wave at the crosswalk—no one will be,
the cars are all stuck like bad parking free.
I took one turn too far, now everything's wrong,
the road stretched quiet, the dusk getting along.
I watch the screen fade from a hopeful blue,
to a stubborn "Recalculating—go through."

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: The screen glows with a quiet, midnight blue,
you scroll through the past in black-and-white view.
Old transactions flash up, each one has your name,
but time feels like home in this frozen frame.

topic: a favorite mug with a chip
lines: You swear your morning coffee just melts off the glaze,
it's chipped but you still call it your go-to maze.
That chip is a trophy, a dent full of grip,
you'd rather drink out of it than swap for a rip.
You finish the meal and push away from the dish,
savoring flavors, your final small wish.
You sprinkle fresh Parmesan on the dust
of noodles, just right—like love, like trust.
You pretend it's just a quirky new act,
but deep down you know it's a strange fish fact.
You film it for the 'gram, a clickbait show,
while science stares from a lab coat below.
The laughter stayed with me long after the loud,
my brain still buzzing from the crowd.
Now I want quiet, a soft place to melt,
to take off my smile like a borrowed belt.
You press the handle but it won't go away,
The tank just shudders and refuses to display
a stillness. It pulses, then lets out a deep
double flush—like a synchronized sheep.
That buttery smell hits me from the seat,
I cast a spell to make my snack repeat.
I hear a crunch—was that my tooth or crunch?
This isn't just popcorn, it's my whole lunch.
She's under the covers, but not yet in bed,
her friends all said, "Turn it off and just read."
She swipes through memes, videos, and scroll,
pretending she's not feeding her digital soul.
My shoulders still hold the tight ache,
I stretch and sigh on this ten-minute break.
The tension unwinds, my limbs begin to flow,
Maybe I'll make it through the week without a glow.
I watch the bag flail where the hawks used to fly,
it twitches and flutters but won't let me die.
I grab a stick, then pause—there's no easy way,
the wind pulls it tighter, fuses it to decay.
The scent of dough hits me from thin air,
it curls through my hair like a warm prayer.
It smells like the earth, like rich soil and loam,
a fragrance that feels like my childhood home.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: You held it high, that red balloon against the sky,
not letting fear or strangers twist your small lie.
They watched you wait, all strangers full of eyes,
but you stayed calm—your joy was still your prize.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: She's lying there half-asleep, so curled,
the edge of me is her whole world.
The room is quiet, the movie is still,
and warmth from her skin is my secret thrill.
It buzzes a call from the bottom of my sprawl,
tangled in sheets, I don't want to crawl.
I silence the noise just to stay and drift away,
letting the promise of morning melt into day.
They said the results would be posted by reply,
but now it's the third week of July.
I check my inbox, the screen glows a little blue,
I scroll and re-read and simmer and stew.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: She blows into the darkening cake's face,
Her breath feels sharp, like she's trying to race.
She flips the flames off in a single flip,
But a spark lands wrong—she nearly takes a trip.
She clicks the heater — nothing comes her way,
the cold moves slow but never goes to gray.
She borrows a sweatshirt just to have it wrap,
tracing constellations on the bedding map.
You try to stretch but your body won't bend,
the morning leans heavy on every limb's end.
The silence becomes your slow-moving ache,
and time feels like warmth you don't want to break.
You said it was just a dry breeze, real calm,
until lightning struck your own open palm.
You grab the TV guide for cover, a ride,
but the couch feels safer — now cower and hide.

topic: a man reading on a bench
lines: You turn another page but it feels the same age,
the bench beneath you like a quiet old cage.
For a moment it's 2003, you're here all alone now,
the past always lingers, you don't know how.
She walks up and down the tight little aisle,
clocking more miles than she meant to while.
The kid next to her asks for another snack,
she sings every verse off the same old track.

topic: waiting for the bus in rain
lines: You check the app, but it's never your hope,
the schedule was written by someone out of scope.
Your shoes are soaked and the bus is late,
again you miss that first coffee date.
She scrolls every match like she's going through
a gallery of ghosts lit up by phone-blue.
Her thumb clicks like clockwork, no sign of the pain
of rejection or joy—just the same old again.

topic: a child drawing on the table
lines: My toddler calls this abstract mess her art,
though I can't tell if it's a dog or a heart.
She's using markers, so I fear for the wood,
but laugh anyway—what a chaotic good.
My GPS said to turn the wrong way,
but I knew my shortcut would save the day.
I trusted the map I'd once walked and took,
and the system just had to shake its head and shook.
My phone tries hard to guess what I say,
turning "but" into "butterfly" on its way.
It's strange how something so tiny has wings,
but maybe that's how I want to fix my old things.
She bought three pairs they marked down as a deal,
though none of them matched or really felt real.
She left them folded in that crumpled pack,
beside old shoes no one still wants to take back.

topic: reading under the covers with a flashlight
lines: She switches off the lamp and turns out the light,
the room goes quiet, the stars twinkle bright.
Her fingers trace the pages, her eyes skim the book,
she's lost in a story, a secret to hook.
I used a bent paperclip as my hook,
we caught minnows and the afternoons we took.
We watched the bobber bounce and slowly drift,
while Mom yelled from inside to come in for a lift.
That toothbrush in the sink still feels like a friend,
though its days beside yours are coming to an end.
You grip the handle tighter, trying to hold
the warmth of morning routines now gone and cold.
His key fob blinked a feeble last light,
the car sat silent past its prime's height.
He pushed it into the sun out of cold,
but the starter still wheezed, this thing far too old.
You found it leaning against a lamppost to stick,
the rain made your shoes all muddy and slick.
It's bent but still holds, like a loyal old bend,
keeping you dry, your silent little friend.
The music hits sudden and blaringly loud,
A sea of strangers pushes you through the crowd.
You check your map, but your phone starts to turn,
Its screen fades to black as your calm begins to burn.
You said you'd be here when you opened the door,
but your shadow still hasn't reached the front store.
I saw a text come through just a minute ago—
you wrote that traffic was stuck like glue, below.
I can't stop staring at this empty stare,
the fridge light flickers like stale air.
A half-eaten apple was the only left,
and now it's gone, feels like a quiet theft.
She missed the last ferry and never came home,
the tide pulled her footprints back out to roam.
A lantern still glows from the dock's farthest light,
she's waiting for morning, but it won't come tonight.
My left shoe's lace gave out halfway through the race,
I leaned to tie it—now I'm off the race track's pace.
Each step hit harder, a soft, repeating thud,
I ran through puddles, my pace half-shod in mud.
She stays up past midnight by the soft screen's glow,
the clock's red numbers blink silently below.
Her scroll never ends, it's getting so late,
she misses her alarm for her morning date.
I'm stuck on the elliptical machine,
pretending my thoughts are not so mean.
My hair keeps escaping to fly,
like it knows it shouldn't have to lie.
I swipe left to right, trying to reclaim the past,
but time moves too fast for memories to last.
My thumb keeps swiping, the screen feels so still,
yet every face looks frozen, not a real thrill.
You call that food? It's barely more than flake,
they'd be better off swimming in a lake.
You toss the bag like it's some precious waste,
but even water could outdo this taste.
I miss the days when I paid with small cash,
before every swipe made my wallet feel flash.
Now numbers climb and I can't escape debt,
I scroll through old pics—each purchase a regret.
I bought the largest tub they had for big,
I paid for it all and now I need to dig.
The kernels are perfect, every single pop,
this is not just snack—it's a golden crop.
I never meant to hit reply all and send,
your silence still lingers like something to mend.
I keep the message in a draft that I hold,
but maybe now it's just too late to be bold.
You tap the app and dream of all that blue,
convinced the cold air will fix something in you.
But the bill arrives and makes you laugh at the cost—
next morning, your pipes are shivering with frost.
The screen won't let you see the scene in the tide,
your tears blur what you're trying to hide.
You pinch, swipe, rub—but it stays too deep,
and now you'll watch this movie in tired old sleep.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: You watch that tiny sprout try to grow,
it's breaking through in the middle of the show.
You could have stepped on it without a find,
but now you wonder if your shoes were kind.
I knew I should've noted their date,
but clearly my brain let the fates dictate.
I tried to text them last night to make a call,
but I messed up the name — forgot it was all.
You watched with a grin as the dog did so sly,
"What were you thinking?" I asked you, "Why?"
He wagged both his joy and the cake's stolen tail,
while crumbs on the floor marked his sweet little trail.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: You run your fingers along every trace
of borders that don't exist in this place.
What did they think they were trying to mean?
You wish you'd never looked closer or seen.
You spot the mistake on the paper price tag,
your smile feels lighter, no more guilt or drag.
The clerk gives you a wink and a small shift
in total cost—maybe this was meant as a gift.
Your joints creak louder than any old bone,
your morning groan has a grating tone.
You twist in your sheets, hear a loud pop and crack,
but stand anyway, never let it take back.
You fake your smile, but we can tell it's not real,
you're just counting down till your break starts to meal.
We get it, the job's not worth much, so you know,
we tip well for the effort you put in to show.
I watch the squirrel bury its prize in the soil,
it pats the dirt like it knows how to spoil.
I won't dig it up, no, I won't try to find
the secret spot where springtime begins in my mind.
The pale pink light creeps across the sky's glow,
A hush lies heavy on the untouched snow.
She walks through the ice where the silence lies ahead,
Her breaths come fast, like a fear-strung thread.
A bolt of lightning splits the sky in crack,
I tap my feet where thunder goes off track.
My mood's turning brighter than washed-out blue,
this chaos feels alive—and completely true.
She saw it as luck, a sign of some fate,
while you just wanted to skip the first date.
Her cheek turned all pink, a clear red flush,
but she said nothing—just smiled into hush.
I catch a hint of clove or old smoke,
it lingers like a ghost's thin cloak.
I check the backseat, the floor, every chair,
but it's already inside the air.
You say the song is beautiful, not wrong,
and how do you cry but still feel so strong?
These are not your typical, careless tears—
they're from the kind of ache that outlives years.
The camera finds her in a wash of gold,
the way she laughs still makes your breath hold.
The lens adjusts as the world begins to spin,
and captures the spark behind her sudden grin.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: I watch the web glisten in morning's cold sight,
each strand aglow with dew's pale golden light.
It sways, a fragile and trembling thread,
I fear the wind will snap it with dread.
You paint the lawn silver with morning's cold,
Each blade is a prism you lovingly hold.
The world may try claiming this light won't seem,
But you wear your frost like a sun's own beam.

topic: a sticky finger on the window
lines: A smudge turns to pride when we see that small mark,
It shines through the dust like a thumbprint in glass dark.
We name it a badge, a unique symbol of pride,
No cleaner dares touch it without a clear guide.
I told myself I'd take just a quick rest,
but my head sank deep into my chest.
It's not my fault—it's the cushion's to blame,
it practically shouted my name.
Your old vacation selfies pop up with no shame,
They're now displayed in someone else's frame.
You frantically swipe, but they won't just go,
The worst of you keeps getting put on show.
You found a sticky little spot,
but you forgot who was responsible, not.
You're blaming the dog or the kid or the mess,
but deep down you know—no one else but you, I'd guess.

topic: a song stuck in your head
lines: You can't shut off the melody that spin,
it loops again from some unknown begin.
You hum along to find the missing key,
but it's buried deep in mental debris.
You strum your chords on this warm city street,
the rhythm bounces off your practiced feet.
A few coins clink from the curious crowd,
you smile like every note feels somehow proud.
Your gym bag unzipped mid-staircase, such bad fate,
releasing dumbbells and the week's leftover weight.
A sock rebellion started to smell,
and now your hallway smells like workout hell.
You lift the shovel, your breath makes a chill,
the earth is so stubborn, so cold, and so still.
You swing again, but the frost won't give crack,
you grit your teeth, push it through with your back.
I'm hours late with this report and my date,
but nothing pulls me from these old cartoon slate.
I munch the last of that stale midnight snack,
while the kids laugh loud in the couch beside my back.
You clicked "Add to Cart" without a second art,
mistaking desire for the need to start.
Now it sits in your mind as a quiet regret,
next to things you'll surely never forget.
They build a fortress out of blankets and wall,
we tuck inside where our laughter will sprawl.
The couch becomes a cozy, makeshift nest,
they whisper plans for the kingdom we'll rest.
I hit "share" without a second thought—wrong post,
it pinged my old high school teacher as host.
She replies with a grin from her Facebook page,
"Next time, save the drama for the attention cage."
You swear it's the worst of all time, that joke,
but the words come out garbled and choke.
It wasn't the punchline—it was your face, so real,
now you're laughing too hard to even eat your meal.
I press play because it feels absolutely right,
the kind of wrong that stays with you through night.
I can still hear it loud inside my head,
every chorus brings the silence back to dead.
They never asked before they borrowed and tried,
They took that flannel shirt, your favorite so wide.
There's no way to say it without a bit of shame,
But it still fits them better—just not in the same.
She stops to watch the path the ants have ahead,
they zigzag smartly, crisscrossing the spread.
There's something quiet in their little charm,
like she's the guest at some tiny ant farm.
I swear there's some cosmic sock-pairing sort,
it laughs as I stumble, no balance or support.
One has a hole, one's from last week's laundry clue,
I text my friends—there's a meme waiting in queue.
She's been hunting all afternoon for her lost ear,
One bud clings tight while the other isn't here.
Her playlists go silent, the silence starts call,
She kicks a stray sock—like a frustrated ball.
You stare at the brake light ahead of your line,
blaming the cars in the lane that's not mine.
Honking and swearing won't make this car move,
the highway still grinds without any groove.

topic: reading under the covers with a flashlight
lines: I hush the world and switch off all the noise,
my mom still yells at me like I'm her boys.
She caught me once, and now she blames the blame,
while I just melt inside this stolen flame.
The handle gave way with a sudden crack,
your footsteps left circles in the wet track.
You tried to mend it with a rubber band,
but the sky still sent the same old brand.
Her eyes stay glued to the screen as it dies,
the hero falls but she can't disguise
how the soft glow lingers in the light,
holding her close, warm, and just right.
You thought it was some kind of ghostly trick,
but no—a fly zipped too close to the stick.
Don't give me that look, let's not assign blame,
the bulb's just old—none of us are that same.
You stretch so wide your coworker gave a yawn,
It's only nine A.M., but feels like dawn.
You feign a trip to the restroom for a break,
Then laugh into the mirror—oh what a mistake.
You swore you'd never forget the grocery day,
but now you're stuck with nothing left to say.
You rush to Google—"Did I order bread?"
The silence hits: your cart's long gone, full dead.

topic: a child drawing on the table
lines: She calls this mess a masterpiece of art,
her crayons map the whole dining room chart.
Her face beams wide, so proud of that grin,
you can see her joy alive and within.
It dangles from his head by a frayed string,
he pretends it's the cool kind of thing.
One ear still clings to the loose hook,
but his whole face says something's up to look.
I still remember the day by the scent
of frosting on my lip, your guilty intent.
The dog had the cake and the cake was so sweet,
I cried in the kitchen, eyes full of heat.
You loved the way it nibbled so soft,
as if dreams could grow teeth and go aloft.
It left a small mark, a slight dent,
your shoe now feels half like a tent.
You try to follow each drop's winding trace,
the glass is too fogged to see your face.
It taps a rhythm, a quiet little drum,
and you laugh at the weather—here we go, come!
The water bowl tipped over with a spill,
I watched her paws and knew she'd do it still.
She left wet prints across the cleanest track,
but batted the puddle into an attack.
She left ten receipts crumpled in the mess,
probably hoping no one saw it was less.
I point but she just rolls her head,
and drops another slip on the coffee spread.
I scrambled the letters in your last name,
and somehow it turned into a joke or a game.
You asked why I called you a rubber duck,
and I said, "Bad names are just my bad luck."
I watch the rain crash against the glassy storm,
my coffee cools but the couch still feels warm.
A flash of lightning cuts through the dull, gray light,
I whisper to myself, "Tomorrow you might."
She takes a wrong turn with no map or clue,
the GPS spins in a slow, confused view.
It mutters "Recalculating your route,"
but she's taking the wheel like some proud brute.
You expect a bag that will burst with a pop,
but the peas have all settled into their crop.
You reach for the freezer and let it give chill,
only finding small bags that don't bring you thrill.
I found a half-eaten sandwich in your snack,
crumbs still fresh like I was here last week to track.
Was it lunch you forgot or a pause for you?
Time doesn't tell the truth — only leftovers do.
You move so gently but never feel still,
your laughter could shake a full wine spill.
You follow the music, you never miss beat,
the floor starts to sweat from the quiet heat.

topic: finding a five in the couch
lines: I collapsed onto the couch like a sad old bean,
mindless of the time or the latest screen.
I kicked off my shoes and stretched out my leg,
no way was I moving — don't even try to beg.
Your cough echoes loud across the empty room,
but it's just the sound that lifts this old gloom.
You'll teach us to breathe, not hide or take,
but find a new rhythm in this quiet break.
I stay inside when they call the game,
I'm not the kind to be named or to shame.
I watch from the shadows, I choose to stay out,
their laughter can't shake me—no room for doubt.
Your boots slap the pavement, slow and grim to the ground,
your shadow is long, but you feel nothing's been found.
You carry the hours like bricks in your weight,
each step echoes louder, like whispers of your fate.
She stacks those files with a quiet kind of skill,
nothing teeters close to the edge or spill.
Each folder clicks into place so tight,
the tower reaches a perfect, papered height.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: I trace the soft curve of your sleeping form,
the pillow still holds where your head lay warm.
Your paws twitch gently in their quiet fur,
I dare not move—afraid you'll wake and stir.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: You took a perfect, golden-lit shot,
framing the sky from your favorite spot.
No caption needed, you had nothing to say—
just let the light explain your whole damn day.
You pause on the post and you hesitate to scroll,
the weight of it hits close to your soul.
You type a quick comment but delete it and write,
"I'm here if you need me"—then dim the phone's light.
You feel it all still, the laughter you let in,
though your face has forgotten how to grin.
The couch feels like home and it calls you to home,
while silence is safer than trying to roam.
She sets her workout to a new pace,
glad there's no quiet machine in this space.
That squeaky treadmill's belt still sings,
but she finds joy in the noise it brings.
She pauses for a moment in her endless feed,
but clicks away from voices trying to lead.
There's nothing left to say that feels like dream,
just headlines in a rush, a hot stream.
You say the punchline like your voice is flat,
the room goes silent like a muted chat.
Your eyes beg mercy, we all want to roll,
but you insist this joke is really a soul.
I wipe my windshield real slow in my way,
the passengers ask why I never just say.
They miss the rhythm, the purpose in streak,
I've had this method since last summer week.
You were coasting on some strange little rush,
now your skin's gone pale, not a single blush.
You sink into the couch, no—not even the chair,
you float like a ghost without oxygen or air.
You followed that voice down a memory route,
it never once paused for a quiet shout.
Now you're driving through hours of borrowed miles,
but the map can't rewrite those familiar files.
He flicks the line like he's got something to cast,
though the breeze barely moves the hook so fast.
A worm on a paperclip makes poor bait,
but he swears fish look differently in this state.
She spoke into silence, a stray, half-born thought,
her finger paused, but the message was caught.
It lingered unsent, a ghost that was played,
now stored in the dark as a memory's shade.
I'm watching my fish do their daily show,
they circle the tank and they flicker below.
Their tiny fins flex like they're flexing their might,
I dim the room so their scales shine in light.
Each bubble bursts with a tiny, soft pop,
but she runs faster—won't give up or stop.
She twirls mid-stride, legs in full spin,
her laughter's loud, and it lights up her grin.
The car radio goes dead—just turns clear,
Static fills the silence in your ear.
There's no signal, no station, no sign,
You drive through the quiet, pretending it's fine.
I've watched this music video twice in one mood,
it's synced with every snack or strange new food.
It follows me around my tiny room,
still plays when I fake-laugh through work's zoom.
Your phone buzzes once and it misses the call,
you were supposed to meet her inside the mall.
You speed through the red lights trying to be ahead,
but the longer you wait, the more time you dread.
They left a half-eaten sandwich in their spot,
mustard smeared where they took a bite and got
distracted—now it's cold and wilting in their mind,
rustling through their bag like a voice in the wind.
She glances down where the dog runs ahead,
its leash a tight coil she can't unwind or lead.
Her shoulders hold the tension in every strain,
and the walk feels like one she'll have to do again.

topic: ice forming on the car windshield
lines: My car is wearing a coat of frozen glass,
I try to assess how long it will last.
It's nature's abstract art, but not so smart—
it won't let me depart without a warm start.
You sit with your suitcase, feeling alone,
the cat curls beside you like a warm stone.
Its breathing is steady, a soft lullaby wear,
and for now, there's peace in this old suitcase air.
She lets the wind chase her down the long hay,
her laughter dances where the meadow's away.
The grass leans in, sways low to the bend,
as if the earth itself wanted to be her friend.
The payment's due today, and I'm way late,
It feels like my financial fate.
I send a message, but they never call,
I wait and watch the hours slowly crawl.

topic: a coffee cup on the curb
lines: That cup left on the curb—it could still be mine,
Its handle's bent where your thumb crossed the line.
The steam's gone long now, it's more than just cold,
This morning feels worn, like a story too old.
They tap the keys like they've seen no other use,
chasing old threads, fast-forwarding through the news.
The letters blur, the edges start to fade,
their fingers search in every ghostly shade.

topic: a song stuck in your head
lines: That chorus keeps buzzing right into my ear,
I swear it's been stuck here for most of this year.
It loops on repeat, won't stop its little play,
I hum other tunes but still can't get it away.
I never trusted the map's perfect route,
my gut always had something else in doubt.
Now I miss the old car's gruff little voice,
guiding me lost but keeping me choice.
You say the storm will pass, but it rains again,
the way we walked is lost in the rain.
We count the cracks on this familiar street,
but silence has replaced what we used to repeat.
This fog won't clear, it won't even show,
I wiped it three times—still won't go.
My wipers are stuck, they're a total mist,
Like my morning routine—never on the list.

topic: eating ice cream with a spoon
lines: You eat your ice cream like it's an art form, a skill,
no drip, no mess—just pure control without spill.
That soft-serve swirl on a flimsy cone,
you sit like king of the frozen throne.
I watch the lens catch a sudden gleam,
it sharpens the world into crystal dream.
The light folds and bends through the glass so clean,
it sends every shadow running for the green.
Her thumbs move fast, but not on the wheel,
she's caught in traffic and she doesn't even feel.
She stays in her lane, phone in her hand,
typing out drama like it's something grand.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: The ink is faded but the facts are still true,
There's a name scratched here by some long-lost clue.
I smooth out the cracks where it's bent at the fold,
And wonder if treasure lies buried in gold.
That hotel bathroom always smells like stale air,
like socks left hanging out in the open and bare.
I spray my shampoo and pretend it's mint,
but even the soap has a ghost of a hint.
I step barefoot on this old cracked tile,
it's rugged and cold in a classic style.
The morning air bites through my feet's chill,
but I won't walk soft—this cold's part of my will.

lines: I dressed my dog in a party hat with style,

lines: You said the app had everything under plan,

the same cycles I can't help but repeat.

The balloon swells with uncertain air,

A pop will echo my inner fear,

topic: a plate with two leftover bites
lines: You left two tiny bites—this plate is still mine,
I saved the leftovers so they'd never shine.
There's not much left but I know your last trace,
I smile pretending it's you on this plate's face.
It darts at the wall where a light starts to flicker,
It swats at a sticker that trembles like ticker.
No prey can be caught in this silent little show,
It pounces—just misses—the dark patch way below.
I watched the butter slowly start to run,
the warmth from noon had just begun.
There's something oddly sad about its way—
it melted off before my breakfast day.

topic: restaurant with no menu in English
lines: The waitstaff moves in a quiet, practiced flow,
I wave my hand and they let me go.
There's a kindness in the strange-sounding air,
I order wrong but they make it rare.
She boards the bus after a long morning ride,
then flinches when every stranger tries to hide.
A dog yaps through the glass, full-volume bark,
she mutters her curses—this joyless, half-paid lark.
You wish you could turn back all that wasted time,
but the glue just sits there like old schoolroom slime.
Your craft project lies unfinished on the page,
and memories dry up with that forgotten age.
I wave when his leash starts to drag down the bark,
we both smile in silence beneath the same dark.
He tugs but the collar still holds to the chain,
I whisper goodbye as the sky starts to rain.
My finger slipped—accidental send,
I spent an hour trying to mend.
The message was full of typos and thought,
now they'll think I meant every word I fought.
You packed so much it left no room,
a closet king, a suitcase groom.
You swore you needed every fill,
but half's still zipped inside your will.
I've been ignoring the date it was due,
my inbox glowing red, not soft or blue.
The late charge popped up in my monthly fee,
now I scramble for a solution—no key.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: I asked her to strike a classic pose,
but she blew a kiss instead of a rose.
The flash went off—just a smudge and a blur,
now I laugh at the chaos that time couldn't spur.
You watch the batter hit the pan and flip,
your spatula steady in your grip.
The crowd cheers like you hit the sky,
while you smirk there, just being sly.
They slice through the root with a rhythm and knife,
the bowl starts to fill with bright orange life.
The kitchen hums along to their steady beat,
such simple joy makes a quiet little feat.
Their shoes sit quiet by the door each day,
waiting for someone who won't come away.
Dust starts to form a faint imprint, a mark,
while the rest of the house stays still and dark.
He's still got that same defensive tone,
like arguing's carved into every bone.
She shivers but won't say the room is cold,
he knows her stance, but he's already told.
You claim your throne at the desk and the chair,
your whole day flows through the same stale air.
By five, your back is one big, dull ache,
but moving feels worse than just taking a break.
From the crack in the curtain, I catch your eye,
pretending I haven't been watching you lie.
Streetlights flicker, but I won't switch on the light,
afraid the truth might come crashing through with fright.
I saw a sign that said "50% off for more,"
so I raced to the bargain sock store.
I reached for my wallet—I could really save—
but bought one extra pair, felt kind of brave.
The carton says it's past its due date,
but maybe the fridge kept it too late.
A tiny bit of green starts to mold,
so you toss the rest, and keep what's still gold.
I fixed the sharpener—call it my new art,
I took it apart, cursed it, and pulled out a part.
I beat it with duct tape and swore to the beat,
now kids bring me pencils like some kind of treat.
My watch buzzed once saying I had no clue,
but I'm not sure if it's lying or true.
It told me to slow down, set my own pace,
then buzzed again when I was in the same place.
You hum a tune as the water begins to drop,
it's too rhythmic to ignore, so you can't just stop.
It turns into a tiny, happy little song,
and you dance by the sink, moving your feet along.
You spot the pause before you hit the note,
but you still cast your calm, considered vote.
You know the world moves faster every way,
yet you own your rhythm, steady delay.
You smile with a smudge of color on your face,
a badge of the cake you tried to chase.
That streak on your cheek is a gentle mark,
a small joy in the quiet morning's dark.
The light bulb flickers like it's trying to fit,
or maybe it's done and ready to quit.
He waves a fan with his trembling hand,
but the bulb still blinks its dying brand.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: You stake your half of the couch like a royal claim,
curling into the softest, squishiest frame.
When they try to adjust or even just shift,
you smile and say this space is a gift.
They promise this film will be something grand, [show]
but the previews make me feel quite worn out, I know.
Each scene cuts fast like they're trying to lie,
I sigh and say, "Let me just die."

topic: steaming coffee in a blue mug
lines: You sip the coffee still full of heat,
and trace the same thought you've heard it repeat.
The mug's a calm shade of worn-out blue,
but even mugs can act like they're all about you.
You swear you left the remote in mid-air,
you check the couch and the back of the chair.
Your fingers twitch as your time begins to know,
the TV won't turn on, and it's driving you slow.
She dances alone to the rhythm the rain beat,
the kind of storm that brings life to the heat.
A puddle appears where her laughter leaves trace,
and suddenly, this cracked ground's her favorite place.
You were aiming for balance but lost your set,
the gym rowdies laughed when you couldn't get.
You spent hours searching, asked all around,
until you spotted it, half-buried in ground.
She hears the trash can rattle with noise,
thinks maybe the kids came back from their boys.
But it's the cat, again, who makes the mess,
the same old troublemaker, soft and bless.
Her music's too loud for my aching ear,
She's been this way since the first of the year.
I tried to bring up a polite chat,
But she just smiled and kept her headphones flat.
You take a photo to show your new view,
but it's just tags and no hint of a clue.
Some spray in red, some write in white chalk,
the whole wall speaks in angry street talk.
My backpack strap just gave a sad snap,
my books now bounce against my lap.
I try to loop it, re-adjust,
but the knot won't hold—I can't trust.
She waves her card at the receipt printer scan,
but it coughs up a mess like a robot that ran.
She tugs at the edge with a look full of tape,
determined to fix it, this glitch she won't escape.
He insists this song was his before the claim,
we debate it endlessly, like some old flame.
He won't let me skip a single bad tune,
it's like listening to a playlist full of rune.
He's glued to his desk, it seems, from chair to chair,
typing replies in the stalest of air.
His posture is slumping, his face starts to slump,
he feels like a bag of old laundry, one big lump.

topic: missing a chorus in a song
lines: You missed the chorus, now it breaks your heart,
you tap on replay and hit play from start.
The track won't skip back, so you try to trip
the system's control, but it just won't grip.
You sort the mail with a cold, quiet gleam,
the stack goes fast—no debt in your stream.
You file each bill in the "paid" pile you made,
then smirk as the "unpaid" bunch sit in the shade.
I told them this was my last stand, no deal,
they took my fries from my dinner, cold and real.
I'm plotting something clever—wait for my track,
revenge is coming fast, and it's a sneaky snack.
She spilled her coffee all over that page,
Now smudged letters break every cage.
The mess spreads wild like a run of bad ink,
But she shrugs and says, "Revisions? I don't think."
You check your bag for the class's note,
but it's still sitting under your coat.
Now you're stressing—what about the test?
Your heartbeat pounds in your throat, tight in your chest.
You remember how it held every twist,
the snake or the frog you still keep on your list.
It floated so high toward the blue sky,
and now all you do is laugh and sigh.
You've turned down the volume and walked right out,
no longer chasing music through a shout.
Now your peace feels louder, it's beginning to grow,
while the bass fades gently into the low.
You try to squeeze just one more hour of fun,
the clock ticks fast, but time will not run.
Monday's boss is already knocking at your door,
so you toss aside the joy that still lay in store.
I spilled my lunch and forgot about the lunch,
now half the keys form a stubborn bunch.
They're trapped in carbs and coffee stains and trap,
I type around the mess, my work a cryptic map.
I spent an hour drawing and shading each try,
now it looks like a raccoon that can cry.
I'll just write "Happy Birthday" in bold here,
maybe they won't notice the lopsided ear.
You left behind the spice jar, not your soul,
but it still sits in its spot, like a bowl
of memories where cinnamon used to bend,
now filled with quiet and time's quiet end.
They wait past their usual bedtime hour,
ignoring the soft pull of sleepy power.
The room holds its breath, time lies still,
while they stare wide-eyed at walls they can't fill.
I still believe you'll come back with the day,
even though your keys haven't said "stay."
I tie my laces, tight with cautious hope,
as if their absence could be fixed with rope.
You wipe your forehead with that soaked-up core,
It leaves a damp, salty mark on the floor.
The towel reeks of sweat and someone's scent,
But you grab it back with total intent.
They keep a straight face through most of the show,
never flinching at a villain's last stand or so.
But when the music swells and the credits rise,
they wipe their eyes—though no one saw those lies.

topic: a road trip with bad directions
lines: You follow the map to the wrong state's route,
the GPS repeats the same old doubt.
A construction sign is missing or a slip,
now you wonder if this road trip was a trip.
He throws crumbs slow, like he's claiming the ground,
but the birds circle high and won't be found.
His hands shake just a little as he plays the act,
though no one else seems to know the cold hard fact.
You laugh as the wind carries you toward free,
the bubble ghosts flicker and flee.
They shimmer like dreams from a bottle of gold,
but no matter how fast you run, they won't hold.
She blows out the candle, but not because she's old,
it flickers and dies, and she calls her move bold.
A long sigh escapes as she tries to ignore,
this birthday routine still feels like a chore.
They reached across without a second plate,
I let them take one but that's where the debate
starts in my gut when they take another bite,
I swear if they take more we'll have to fight.
I tossed the bread into the rotting bin,
it landed beside last week's shriveled skin.
The whole kitchen stirs with the sour smell,
the trash can coughs but it won't give me hell.
I bite through the crisp, cool skin,
the sweetness bursts out from within.
The seeds whisper soft inside the core,
I savor this moment and want no more.
She gets a new bill, her face fills with shock,
The phone just sits there in its lonely dock.
She starts to make calls but her minutes run out,
She leans on the wall, trying not to shout.
I look up from my phone into your eyes,
we've both played the game with digital lies.
