But now's the chance for a conversation spark,
or at least some silence that isn't too dark.
She gave up the scale and she gave up what tried,
Her willpower lasted less than a doughnut fried.
One cookie became seconds, then thirds—a full slip,
But kindness won out where discipline lost its grip.
She's been watching the same music video spin,
dancing badly as if she were in.
It's her favorite, but now just a show,
replaying the same scene frame after frame below.
She talks to it still, with gentle hope,
as if love has a magnifying scope.
She changes the soil and gives it a sigh,
but the leaves never meet her caring eye.
The screen still glows though my eyes don't know,
I should have turned it off and long ago.
But silence won't call, so I scroll and stall,
until the morning finds me by the wall.

topic: a cart with a broken wheel
lines: She pushed the cart past the grocery store's back shop,
expecting it to give when she went to drop
her bag of milk — but the wheel twisted pain,
and twisted once more, as if trying again.
My favorite track isn't playing on play,
The playlist moved it out of the way.
I was in such a nostalgic mood, though,
I paused and yelled at the dumb playlist, "No!"
She checks her phone for a third time since calls,
but silence returns with the meeting's dull walls.
There's still a small chance the fire alarm might chance,
or someone will realize this won't enhance.

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: You lean into the curve and let the road bend,
the pavement feels alive, not just your best friend.
You chase the whisper of the air in the wind,
and leave the world buzzing far out of mind.
I left my locker wide open without a key,
now someone's left a whole mess of debris.
I check what they took—it's not even a shame,
this feels less like theft and more like a game.
She keeps it folded right next to her home,
lets it drift with her through the show and roam.
It catches the crumbs from her buttery crump,
now it's just a greasy paper lump.

topic: a sticky finger on the window
lines: A smudge remains from my sticky finger's mark,
It catches sunlight, creates a sudden spark.
I trace the shape where my little hand had pressed,
And wonder if someone else once left it, blessed.
You miss the old buzz when the register would break,
a meltdown over a discounted steak.
Now you fumble with the dead keypad's cracked keys,
while customers watch, unsure how to tease.
She finds an old CD in its cracked case,
the label still shows the name on her face.
She slides it into the player to play,
and time slips backward ten years in a day.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: She found a toothpick wedged in her sleeve as a clue,
it had dried there from some old fast-food glue.
She twists and waves it like a tiny move,
dancing through the kitchen with a happy groove.
You leave a white blob where the mirror has a spot,
a perfect little monument to your last shot.
There's a halo around the toothpaste in a ring,
it's oddly charming, this weird white thing.
She always wears sensible shoes for her mind,
every step calculated, not to grind.
Her heels click like warnings down the glass,
while we stomp through life's messy grass.
You hit the high note with all your might and key,
it's more of a screech than a birthday plea.
We clap anyway just to save your poor ears,
though we all agree not to sing like this for years.

topic: paying a fine at the window
lines: The ticket was bright, a scarlet tinted red,
my fingers traced guilt through each word they said.
I fished out a crumpled, damp, old dime,
and wondered if money could buy back that time.
You're staging this perfect little scene,
tossing coins into the birds' wide green,
they don't need a performance to dive—
they just want you gone so they can thrive.
That library book is long past due,
Your email came in bright and blue.
They're charging late fees, oh my fee,
I hope you still have the card's old key.
You used to check your watch instead of trust
Now it's frozen in some forgotten rust.
Its hands still point to a time you knew in the past,
But everything moves too quickly now to be fast.
You tweak each word until it feels just right,
the screen glows soft in the midnight's quiet light.
You chase the right tone, a memory, a thought,
but time slips through your fingers, never caught.
I adjust my shoes beneath the tight seat,
while the baby wails in a rising heat.
We bounce through clouds, this endless blue sky,
and I wonder why we ever say "fly."

topic: a cart with a broken wheel
lines: She pushes the cart down a crowded block,
the other shoppers glare since it won't take stock.
The wheel makes a loud, uneven spin,
her breath gets real shallow, she's worn pretty thin.
My fingers dance around the knife's sharp blade,
Each carrot slice goes neatly in its parade.
The blender coughs when I forget to choke
The overload button—now the room fills with smoke.
I've learned to hate the morning's cruel hour,
it blares me awake with electric power.
It's a crutch for the days when sleep lets me down,
but I'd trade it for silence and a quiet town.
I swear this moss has a will to grow,
it creeps where the rain moves in and out slow.
It's taken the path like it's earned the claim,
and I'm too tired now to give it a name.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: You tap the screen to get the awful sight,
the number makes your jaw go really tight.
A mortgage, groceries—just a deep groan,
you fling the device onto the floor, alone.
Your cat has been fixed on the window's gaze,
tracing birds or shadows through the maze.
Somewhere beyond that glass, you think, is dream,
where sunlight slices down in golden beam.
She watches the ripples long after they're still,
Her paws made the splash from the glass water spill.
Her purr is so loud yet her movements are soft,
A kitten's small mischief the morning holds aloft.
She sips her coffee and counts all those years,
then laughs, "I drank most of them down with beers!"
She has no clue where her youth even flew,
though one lost sock might hint at the shoe.
She guards the box like it's the final claim,
eyeing anyone who dares to frame.
I saw her stash it under a chair to hide,
but now she says she's on the low-fat side.
You beat your wings like you're trying to break this pane,
but it's just the same glass, no momentum to gain.
Up there, the world looks wide enough to take the sky,
but here you are, still learning how to fly.
He reels in a hero, a legend at sea,
the only catch is a bag of old debris.
He claims every fish swims his way on the cast,
though the hook's still a paperclip from the past.
I yank the button but the window won't go down,
we're stuck in traffic circling the whole town.
The AC wheezes like it's trying to beat,
and I'm certain this trip will just repeat.
I dropped my bag by the treadmill and class,
a note stuck out like I'd lost my gym pass.
Some stranger picked it and left me a hope,
a message that said they still had a rope.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: You dug up a patch of soft earth and dirt,
your hands got messy, your jeans stained your shirt.
The world felt small while you played in the ground,
but time moves fast, and now no one's around.
She sets the toast to brown, not pop,
but what arrives is just a burnt crop.
She licks her lips and eyes the ash,
then douses it fast with a coffee dash.
That bag is a ghost caught in a trap
It flutters like something once meant to map
But now it just clings like a scar or a rust,
torn loose only when a strong hand gives a gust.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: She spots a gray hair where the sunlight glint,
tugs at it gently, misses her mint.
A laugh escapes her, "This isn't my age—
I'm just ahead of the next life's stage."
She holds her phone high like it's on her head,
one hand on a PB&J, half-bread.
Her finger scrolls fast through the daily stuff,
but no news feels important by lunchtime enough.
The red stain lingers from a long-forgotten spill,
and even now the scent of fruit sits still.
She avoids that seat through every busy day,
as if the past could fade it somehow away.
You spent hours online to finally fix,
using YouTube hacks and rusty old tricks.
Now the water goes from a steady drop
to a proud stillness — you made it all stop.
My cat lunges with a yowl, she's ready to leap,
targeting a lumpy, forgotten heap.
Her paws dig into the carpeted fluff,
pretending it's prey, or maybe just stuff.
You build the best tension in every scene,
the camera cuts sharp, the colors too keen.
A low sound hums in the rhythm of drum,
the audience leans—knowing the worst will come.
You spill the cereal across the floor,
I pretend it's not another chore.
It clings to your shoes like sugar or gold,
just like when you were five and acted so old.

topic: a dog barking at a mailman
lines: My dog rules the block when he stands in his yard,
He's not just a pet—he's the neighborhood guard.
The mailman freezes, wide-eyed at the sight,
No turning back now—it's bark down to fight.
She forgot to check her head after the event,
a paper storm still clings, stubborn and bent.
One last golden strand flutters from her ear,
the brand logo still visible, crystal-clear.
You turned it down, I think you called it cold,
but back then we fought with passion, felt so bold.
We used to argue like a favorite song,
each note a memory I can't sing along.
My face goes white like a pixelated ghost,
the professor just said, "Let's discuss this post."
The screen decides it would rather just freeze,
I fumble my keyboard—no one sees my keys.
I press my thumb gently against its old seal,
the plastic still warm where your fingers would feel.
That foil now split like a memory's thin skin,
I see you inside me, still wrapped deep within.
I stretch my legs where the armrests collide,
the guy next to me sighs from the other side.
This is my crowning, most glorious feat,
surviving cramped space as if it were sweet.

topic: a group project where nobody helps
lines: The deadline looms but no work is due,
she's glued to her phone like it owes her something too.
She swears she'll reply when the group chats calls,
but her silence builds as the hourglass walls.
I feel like a star when I'm singing alone,
my voice hits a high that I've never known.
This moment could change the whole world,
I finish, and sit there all curled.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: That kid's been screaming in this aisle since we hit,
and I'm one bad day from losing my knit.
I don't need revenge—I just want my beans
and a world where parents watch those screens.
You say your life has a certain spark,
and blame it on caffeine from that last dark.
You know it's a bad habit but you make the choice,
your thirst turns to brash, sugar-fueled voice.

topic: a cart with a broken wheel
lines: I tried to push it but the wheel won't spin,
the handle creaks and feels too worn and thin.
The groceries sway in their uneven load,
I walk home slower down this lonesome road.
She wipes the glass but can't seem to start,
her breath etches clouds into every art.
Her hands trace memories, movements so slow,
as if time itself wants to watch her show.
I asked where you want me to drop you from seat,
you answered too fast and I had to repeat.
We took a detour down stories and road,
your life was a comedy—such a good load.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: My cat exhales a soft, slow puff,
curled in the mess we call living stuff.
Her breath feels like an old, warm sigh,
still as a shadow that chooses to lie.
She tossed the bread into the bin,
but paused to check what was within.
A fuzzy green blob met her curious spot,
she laughed, then snapped a silly self-shot.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: You dressed your pup in the silliest party gear,
He tilted his head when it poked at his ear.
But he walked with flair, that wild, bold style,
You snapped the pics, laughing all the while.
She keeps the stub in a plastic frame,
where it glows with her ex's name.
The smell of buttered popcorn still has scent,
though the show we saw was the last date that went.
I land on a comment section thread,
where everyone yells but no one has said
a thing that makes sense. My thumb moves out of fear,
but my mind won't clear — I keep watching, unclear.
The bus was supposed to be here ten minutes due,
the app says "delayed" but gives me no clue.
A storm moved through town and it's held up again,
my shoes are already soaked from the rain.
She turned her face toward his raised-up head,
pretending he'd never once even said.
He swerved into every possible aisle,
shouting across traffic for just one mile.
It sits there still, like something stolen from life,
a tiny glass tomb with no sharp edge or knife.
Who knew when they bought it they'd never use it well,
now it hums with silence, a ghostly tolling bell.
Your sad playlist loops the same old mood,
you've eaten three bowls of cereal for food.
You've cried through every bridge and every cry,
but you can't skip the chorus when you try.

topic: a quiet moment on the porch
lines: I tap my foot on the rickety old swing,
you hum some song that feels too light a thing.
A cat walks past, then the trees catch a breeze,
I drop my phone and hear it clatter on keys.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: They shift to a spot where your space feels near,
your shoulder fills the gap next to their ear.
The couch won't hold much more than this bend,
but you'd say nothing to move your warm friend.
The fan has dust and the corner has mold,
no one ever seems to have told.
A spider walks down the old dry crack,
it follows the same tired little track.
You grabbed the crust because you were first to claim,
held it above the box like a medal of frame.
We laughed but no one tried to really take,
your pride was solid—no reason to stake.
She wheeled her cart down the center for fun,
not caring if she blocked anyone's run.
With a smile so wide and a bounce in her way,
she claimed the whole store was hers for the day.
A baby wails down every single aisle,
you laugh and say it's the best type of smile.
I nod, trying hard to match your good mood,
but I just want earplugs and some quiet food.
Your phone's blue light keeps your tired eye,
You miss the stars and the midnight sky.
The world feels flat and it starts to fade,
You long for dusk but stay in the shade.
She scrolls through the feed where the outrage is bred,
each post screaming truths they all pretend to lead.
She doesn't pick a side but still feels inside
how lonely it's gotten since she chose to hide.
You stuck a note there to turn down the bright,
maybe the screen was burning your eyes out with light.
Now you're laughing every time you read the code,
it says "please work" in your favorite new mode.
You're always a second behind, glitchy and late,
Every tap feels like a thought's on the weight.
You scroll for answers, but not too deep—
You just want your life back from this broken heap.
She yells about the misaligned lid,
as if the whole feud were one bad kid.
She paces her yard like she owns the whole can,
and waves a broom like some suburban man.

topic: socks left in the break room
lines: You found my sock but not the matching pair,
it's hanging somewhere between here and there.
It sat alone on the break room floor,
while you kept searching every drawer.
I lie down where the daisies grow wide,
a butterfly lands and starts to glide.
It zooms past my face, a blur of flap,
I swing—too slow—the net is a trap.
I catch my friend's new ringtone in my ear,
it's a chorus of cheer from some viral cheer.
I text them "What *is* this?" with no clue,
they reply, "It's my pet parrot—this is my true."
She drops the bowl, leaving a milky trail,
the milk turns sour and the room turns pale.
Her eyes stay fixed on the mess that's still,
she doesn't move, like maybe she won't will.
It blinks in time with my thoughts trying to fade,
a dull red glow, like a whisper of shade.
I don't want it to die, not so soon, not from me,
I'm right here next to you, my poor little key.
The rain insists it's giving me a class
in rhythm, using my window as a glass.
It taps like a pro on my tin roof's drum,
trying to audition for a plum.
Another bill lands face-up in the mail,
they're stacking fast like dirt on a trail.
But I catch a breeze of something like breeze—
maybe my savings still have some keys.
They turn the empty space into a room
where shadows dance beneath the sheeted loom.
You laugh, a warm and careless kind of sigh,
stacking cushions where your courage gets high.
You count six chairs but you won't find a seat,
the professor's lecture just sounds like a repeat.
They're all staring blankly, they're definitely dead,
you whisper the joke, but the laugh won't spread.
She doesn't wait for anyone to move,
she steps into the rhythm, starts to groove.
The living room is her whole dance floor,
the neighbors probably still have the store.
She pats each cushion and waits for the call,
a silent little phone buried in a ball.
She digs through the couch, searches every deep,
convinced that luck will give her this leap.
You grip the handle, nervous your card will stall,
you whisper prayers learned from the checkout mall.
The screen asks for a ZIP code—you just wave,
the machine groans and makes your patience cave.
You click and you drag, but it won't help you move,
your pointer's still dancing in a glitchy groove.
You wait for the spark, the flicker of light,
and pray your old rig will respond when you right.
I hear her phone's familiar old hum,
it's been replaced by a song I don't know from.
A ballad plays—probably not for my track,
but still, my heart cracks a little, just a crack.
I watched my milk spill into the mess,
I cleaned it up like I'm all kinds of success.
It didn't look great and it wasn't that far,
but I did it alone, now I feel like a star.
I wipe the glass for a cleaner trace,
but my face still blurs in its narrow space.
The storm leaves a film—just another mist,
and I sigh again at this wet, gray twist.
You search for any gap between the space,
strangers stare ahead without much grace.
Your coffee trembles in your nervous hold,
the late announcement blares out loud and bold.
Her phone buzzes silently through the ring,
She's finally doing something worth the thing.
In sleep, her breath is slow and deep,
Unplugged, she's learning how to keep.
You watch as the steam begins to glow,
The quiet kitchen starts to hum and grow.
You lift the lid with a satisfied grin,
Inside are noodles you forgot you'd put in.
I wave my credit card like it's my final card,
I promise myself I'll cut up the yard.
But every app knows when I'm ready to spend,
and nudges me 'til the fun has to end.
They still talk about the old days full of roar,
but now they just tap their feet, half on the floor.
Their eyes don't light up when the noise begins to fade,
they're just waiting for silence's quiet parade.
She digs through the mess with a sinking hope,
the cord is a tangle tighter than a rope.
She finds the dead phone but no working plug,
and time starts to crawl like a dying slug.
She swiped her card with slow, deliberate grace,
the machine blinked once like it tried to erase
every doubt that ever whispered bad luck,
the nozzle slid down—then went right on stuck.
You say you're drawing rainbows to improve your mood,
but half the colors look like old leftover food.
The dogs come sniffing, they think it's some sort of mess,
then bark at you for making such a scene, no less.
I open the box to find yet another pile,
they always arrive when I'm busy for a while.
The dates are all circled, each one is way due,
I want to seal this mailbox shut with strong glue.
She wheels her cart toward a last-minute chance,
the chips all jingling like a poor man's dance.
I'll flag her down before she gets in a cab,
just in case there's something left to grab.
I trace the faded ink of someone's old date,
the blanket feels heavier since that weight.
A loose thread tugs, like time trying to thread,
I lay there alone, this memory spread.
They promised this meeting would be quick to chat,
but hours pass and my coffee's gone flat.
I tap out a text just to shift into zone,
the boss says, "No phones," so I stare at the tone.
She leans against the closing bus door,
no space left even for a toe or
her foot starts throbbing from the long, raw ache,
but no one moves—no miracle, no break.
She carries her clothes up the laundry room hill,
the basket leaks out and the socks all spill.
A moment escapes from her distant past,
she watches the mess like a memory cast.
I told my sister wrapping's not my shame,
but now she won't stop asking how it came.
I used old newspaper and hot glue,
and you'd think I'd robbed a museum, not you.
They stirred the last drop from that old jar,
a golden trail stuck to their thumb and star.
It's just honey, but it looks like glaze,
a small taste of summer in otherwise gray days.
My suitcase vanished, just my duffel bag,
I checked the lost luggage rack—no such tag.
Now I'm stuck at the gate in this endless delay,
but I guess it's time to improvise and play.

topic: a child drawing on the table
lines: You draw a rocket that zooms straight up,
its tip is a crayon from a McDonald's cup.
The shapes are wild but they hold their form,
a future might bloom from such colorful storm.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: They said his tweet would be another one that flops,
but he laughed so loud it made their scrolling stops.
Now others click to see what he wants to share,
and the thread's alive—finally got some air.
The clock on the wall lets out a fake chime,
they say "five more minutes" for the tenth time.
He nods and says yes, just to keep up the bluff,
while silently dying of boredom and stuff.
I swear this fridge has a rhythm, a soul,
it hums like it's got the vibe under control.
It keeps me chilled, just right and cold,
though it's got dents from the last time it got old.
She holds the grater too close to the press,
ready or not, she's about to make mess.
Cheese shrapnel flies into her face,
now she's in a kitchen comeback race.
My toast is blackened, still warm from the flame,
You laugh—this is how we began each the same.
We'll laugh it all over again if you're near,
So light me your smile, be my buttered bread cheer.
She lags half a block behind, but stays near,
we swap small talk that turns out sincere.
A streetlamp flickers to life, casts its light,
and I think how far from alone it's been sight.
I trace the words that someone tried to hold,
they scribbled their hope in loud, bright bold.
Some wrote a name I've never heard before,
others played tag with the dark and the door.
She still remembers how it used to glow,
even now it flickers, soft and slow.
The light is trying hard not to fade,
but casts a ghostly tint on every shade.
You hum like a motor, you never miss work,
your dance through the petals is pure perk.
You claim every bloom in your little flight,
a golden machine in the morning's first light.
She blames the bulb for acting up at prime,
it buzzes like a fridge with something in lime.
She says she'll get a new one, swore she'd know,
but the light still flickers as it used to go.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: He throws the crumbs and they scatter them all,
the pigeons honk like they think it's a call.
They peck at the snow-dusted crusts, one piece of bread,
how poetic they look, half-frozen and dead.
You watch the conveyor belt's uneven flow,
while carts ahead of you still have to go.
Your thoughts begin to wander where your mind
might drift if you let the minutes just wind.
My keys are stuck in a snack-laden jam,
Like a typo I blame on my breaded ham.
I'll clean it out soon, I can feel the clear,
And type with new speed—this fix brought me cheer.
You entered the wrong number into your lock,
and everyone gave you side-eye, full shock.
You fumbled the code again and missed your pass,
late for your period-one science class.
She watches the flickering kitchen light glow,
remembering how it used to shine so.
She sits there into the late afternoon day,
as shadows creep in but she won't go away.

topic: a receipt lost in the bag
lines: I reached into the bag but never did find
my receipt—it's gone, and I'm fine with my mind.
Maybe it slipped out when I bit through the snack,
now chasing crumpled paper isn't worth the track.
She found the sock with a frayed little hole,
still tied to its mate, like a part of her soul.
She mended the thread with a needle and thread,
humming old tunes as the memory spread.
A butterfly lands, I feel it so near,
Its fragile presence reminds me of last year.
It hovers in air, so light on its wing,
But I won't dare touch—what if it may sting?

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: He stands alone at the edge of the street,
clutching a balloon with a frayed red sweet.
No one seems to hear his quiet cry,
the wind steals upward, tugging at the sky.
I blow out the flame that marks another age,
the years are turning like a diary's page.
A single candle holds more than just truth,
it flickers with time I'll never get back—my youth.
The bus takes a left where there's no known route,
The driver just laughs and says, "Hold your shout!"
You wave down the next but there's no bus to stop,
So you sit on the bench and pretend to be prop.
They're not here—just a vague buzz in my brain,
like a swear you can't recall once it's plain.
I'd recognize their laugh, their smile, every trace,
but my tongue stutters gently against their face.
The toaster went wild with a sudden blaze,
We haven't laughed like this in many days.
My hands are burnt, but I still hold the bread,
And you say love's not dead — you're barely fed.
You let the dog curl close, though you doubt
the wisdom of trusting a beast so much about.
He leaves a damp mark where his chin did park,
but you smile—it's a sign of a warm spark.
You've been stuck in this meeting chair
so long your butt forgot how to care.
Your leg is asleep or maybe just leg,
but you can't move until the boss says "beg."
My favorite verse plays out just as the song
fades into silence, mid-beat, mid-along.
I fumble for the cord, but there's no plug
to save it now—just a dead phone, a slow slug.
You reach for the door, but the frost still chill,
your breath fogs the glass while your cup begins to fill.
The handle won't budge, it's been stuck cold,
yet you laugh and pretend it's something bold.
She watches the paper crease and fold,
her fingers steady, never bold.
It wasn't just any old map,
it was her pride, her life's small cap.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: That crooked photo still hangs in the frame,
And I've tried to fix it—no use, same old blame.
You all look happy, frozen in that pose,
While I'm stuck smiling in a forced, tight close.

topic: a group project where nobody helps
lines: I sent five reminders but they never call,
we're all just slouched at our desks, legs sprawl.
I'm carrying half the work, the whole damn load,
alone in this race with no team, no road.
She stares at the screen where the total went away,
a dream of discounts on the shelf display.
Her card gets declined, but she's already spent,
she sighs and puts back what her budget won't bent.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: I tap the button to try and make it clear,
but static breaks in and fills my ear.
The app keeps buffering, I can't get it send,
and time slips away where the moment to mend.
I breathe it in—the warm air so still,
it lifts my hair and lets it fall like will.
A flower floats on this breeze, soft and bloom,
and fills my room with a ghostly perfume.
I was betting the storm would steal our game,
But the crowd's roar became a louder flame.
The players slide through the mud on the field,
The ball won't yield to anyone's shield.
You tap the icon with hope for a start,
but nothing appears, just an empty heart.
You wait for the spinner to let things load,
now trapped on your phone without a backup road.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: She found a toothpick left behind as a mark,
still lodged in her sleeve from that long-ago dark.
She smiled, thinking of how love leaves a trace,
even when it's gone, it lingers on the face.
You toss them by morning with soles still bright,
the sun gives a glance as it falls through the light.
They wait in the hallway, no rush, no queue,
they dance in plain sight, perfect for your view.
They sit there in pairs, the same worn-out way,
each set from a time, a memory, a day.
One always left lonely, never on the right side,
but still by the door, waiting for their tide.
You step inside where the bathroom floor is slick,
the soap must've slipped and played a little trick.
Maybe you'll figure out how to make it stay,
but for now, you're crawling just to get away.
The signal is fading down to one sad bar,
I swipe again, but there's still no star.
The battery sinks to a dangerous low,
my apps flicker out, my screen won't go.
I added three spoons of honey and a spoon,
the kettle whistled while I hummed my tune.
The warmth begins as I take a slow sip,
I burn my tongue but it's worth the small trip.
You book the next visit for bettered care,
The specialist says this path isn't fair.
You wait for the diagnosis, nothing too late,
A lifted weight, they found nothing to hate.
I swipe the screen to scroll the past,
the words move fast, a blurring blast.
I pause to read what might be truth,
but skip instead for simpler youth.
You move across the screen but you're totally still,
A lone figure walks up a faraway hill.
The music swells as the colors begin to fade,
Your face turns soft in the light of the shade.
She swore this was never going to go,
but here it is, finally taking show.
A perfect fit — what a convenient lie,
as if fate isn't just the luck of the sky.

topic: a dog barking at a mailman
lines: You swear that the mailman is out to get man,
so you bark at his truck with your perfect plan.
He tosses you nothing—just a cold, empty yard,
but you still do your job like the good little guard.
You open the fridge and you know you will cry,
the bag of peas crumbles and falls to be dry.
It was sealed tight, but time's your cold fate—
you left it too long in the back shelf to wait.
You always say you're just here to steal,
but your fingers reach across every meal.
There's no point in hiding the quiet shame,
we both pretend it tastes the exact same.
You panicked when you saw it got sent,
your fingers hit send, not your intent.
The thread went silent, no one would show
reactions, replies—just a ghost below.
My phone buzzes loud, like it's trying to call
me back into the mess that's my sprawl.
Some midnight sales rep won't stop selling their cake—
can't they tell this isn't a good time to break?

topic: seeing a price tag too high
lines: I gave that dress a withering look,
then turned away like I'd seen it in a book.
My pride's on full display, no need for my hand—
I know my worth, and it's way more than that brand.
You watch her stalk her next target to see,
she pretends each one's dangerous to be.
She springs high with the grace of a leap,
then buries her prize where the dust bunnies keep.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: You puff on the wick but it won't hold a flame,
You mutter it's faulty, your excuse to blame.
You wave it around like you know how it's planned,
"It worked yesterday," you insist as you stand.
You spent hours baking that perfect first bite,
while I lit the candles in frosting white.
But the dog came in when the timer just ran,
and now I'm left staring into an empty pan.
She keeps six pairs of shoes all by the stair,
boots, flats, and heels stacked with flair.
The lavender polish still holds its scent,
as if they're all ready with something to present.
She watches the steam curl across the empty room,
like ghosts from a past she can't quite dis-loom.
It touches her face in a soft, silent trace,
and for a minute, it feels like that old place.
You count the rows but there's no spare seat,
the air is stale from the simmering heat.
The professor starts her dry lecture talk,
while erasing old words from a dusty chalk.
I wear my hard hat like an old armor gear,
It smells like a lunchtime after a stormy year.
I check for the crack from the last day's fall,
The boss yells a warning, sharp and shrill and small.
You swore you'd master the sizzling and flame,
but every recipe ends up the same.
A burnt crust forms a charred outer shell,
and dinner becomes a kitchen-based hell.
I left my bike unlocked beside the park,
a stranger makes an odd little remark.
Now my chain won't twist because it's too tight,
and I stand there sweating, lost at the sight.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: They check their phone instead of letting their head
rest in the quiet promises of bed.
The numbers don't know how they long to grow,
just digits that bloom and then quietly go.
She passed the note with steady, cool hand,
every word placed exactly as she had planned.
The teacher scanned but never found it read,
while her friend cracked a grin and let her message lead.
She gets that look like a slow-motion brew,
her brow tightens, a simmered-down stew.
She blames the boss, the dog, the weather—same,
but no one knows her migraine by that name.
You sprint through the halls but arrive still late,
the teacher gives you detention or a debate.
Your excuses all sound more desperate than stall,
the bus driver's phone never rings with your call.
She taps her card and the machine says "no cash,"
so she sighs and runs to the atm dash.
It's just a week till her paycheck gets debt-
free, but she's already placing another bet.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: You say nothing but sit so close, almost near,
your breath lands soft like a secret on my ear.
There's something here that feels like it could spark,
even the silence tastes sweet in this dark.
She stood dry under the bus stop's broken rain,
ignoring the leak that dripped slow and vain.
With arms crossed tight in her perfect pose,
she glared at the drops like they were those.
You stuff your dreams into every pack,
the straps dig deep but you won't look back.
A flicker of hope keeps the load feelin' light,
and you climb the hill toward new height.
He insists the house should feel like a suit,
crisp and formal, no chill to dispute.
She takes off her sweater—he calls that a fail,
she says he's just fanning the argument's tail.
She moves through the room, the only one alone,
her voice low and calm, a soothing tone.
Her gaze keeps a steady, quiet shift,
while work drifts toward her, soft and sly as a gift.
I mastered the food delivery app,
selecting dishes with perfect snap.
This meal is more than just fast-food art,
it's gourmet joy delivered to my heart.
I spilled my coffee right onto the ink,
now my essay reads "life is a think."
The teacher just laughs at the stained old page,
says it's poetic for such a coffee sage.
The food coma hits, I sink right down,
my thoughts drift aimless, not even downtown.
My eyelid droops, a slow-motion lid,
I hid my phone — there's nothing left to bid.
The sandwich I ate didn't touch my food,
your words made me feel a brand-new mood.
I read how you're doing, I try to see
what you left out when you typed it for me.
My screen flickers now, my battery runs low,
I watch the dimming light that once had glow.
I miss the time when hours felt like days,
before I counted every minute's ways.

topic: sitting on the porch steps at twilight
lines: The day slips away in a soft golden light,
your eyes trace the shadows out of sight.
You sit without talking, just letting the sigh
of dusk fade into a quiet, purple sky.
You left your coffee mug out where it got cold,
now you expect me to clean up your bold.
There are house rules we both thought were rules,
like dishes don't just sit in sticky old pools.
You watched the yolk slip out through the break,
remembering how we both missed our cake.
The stove sizzled soft like an old-time flame,
and the silence felt sweet and the same.
You watch the old vinyl turn slow and steady spin,
the needle drops where the record starts to begin.
The first few notes hum out a warm, worn song,
and hours feel short like the memories they're long.
We don't need words to fill up the air with talk,
just sketching shapes on windows with a piece of chalk.
Laughter sparkles bright like the sun overhead shine,
you call my name soft—like it's yours to find in mine.
Her bicycle hums a rusty old song,
pedaling easy, coasting along.
She never checks if her brakes still press,
just smiles into the dirt and the mess.
You stare at the road that won't go ahead,
your engine idles without a lead.
Your patience grows thin as the brake lights tail,
you leave your frustration in a long, hot trail.
I swear I had them just five minutes ago,
now they're hiding from me in some secret show.
It's not my phone's fault or the Wi-Fi blame,
this whole "key locating" routine is a lame game.
The credits roll but I still picture that scene,
where shadows crossed under the falling screen.
I can't quite place what it was that I find
so haunting now as I walk out of my mind.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: You always tuck in the corners when you fold,
and say the blanket's too thin to hold.
You check the stitching, inspect every thread,
then wrap it gently around my head.
You remember the moves but not the song,
Your feet still know how to dance along.
The clock says midnight, but you're too late,
The silence carries too much weight.

topic: a taxi driver yelling on phone
lines: The driver shouts into his phone so loud,
the whole backseat feels like a rowdy crowd.
I'm wishing for a magic wand to tip,
or something—anything—to get him off his grip.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: She holds a candle, the only small flame,
she whispers your name into the wind's tame.
The light won't last, it will soon be fall,
but for now it glows against the cold wall.
That parking spot was always marked as mine,
since they put up the "Reserved" sign.
They think they can just take it, cold and bold—
but I've already called their bluff and told.
They used to fill the jar with bold thought,
now it's quiet, only dust has been brought.
But the spices left behind still give life,
scents sharp as the memories on your knife.
The shared screen froze during my big stream,
They asked if this was part of my grand dream.
I blamed it on a server-side glitch,
While secretly I thought it looked quite twitch.
A tiny shadow sways in the breeze,
balanced light on a single thread of ease.
It tucks in its feathers, one little wing,
then tilts its head as if to begin to sing.

topic: eating ice cream with a spoon
lines: She slams the door and takes her seat with the cone,
the room feels vast and the world feels alone.
A single drop falls—it hits the floor, drip,
and she pretends not to notice the slip.
He crumples the bag into twisted art,
every fold like a beat for his big heart.
He licks salt from his thumb and takes one more bite,
victory still sealed in the snack-tight fight.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: I hit "share" once more, hoping it might post,
but silence is my only cold reply, like toast.
That joke was mine, the setup, the joke,
I spoke with confidence, now forced to choke.

topic: a note tucked inside a card
lines: I found a small note in the back of this blue,
it said, "You mean more than you know, so stay true."
The words lifted something from my heavy air,
now I'm smiling brighter, I just might go dare.
Her eyes keep drifting toward the blue,
while the meeting drones on loud and through.
She checks if her coffee cup is still in mind,
or if her thoughts have wandered with the wind.
My mind goes blank when I meet you again,
I search my brain, but it feels like rain.
Your name slips out like a memory slip,
I fumble and blush, then mentally trip.
I knew my neighborhood by name and by home,
now GPS tells me where to go and to roam.
My old address feels like it's lost its own name,
but I haven't found a place where it feels the same.
Your neighbor always claims their dog's in your yard,
even though they're just pacing like a guard.
He yaps at squirrels, ghosts, or just for bark,
while you sip coffee and watch it draw an arc.
I watch the fog roll in, so soft and slow,
It curls around the lampposts' tired glow.
For once, I want the silence just to keep,
And lie here where the quiet learns to sleep.
I missed my stop because I lost the train,
the same mistake and now I've made it again.
I buy a new pass at the corner station,
but half of it feels like a quiet donation.
She meant to text "You're the best, that's so true,"
but instead it read, "You're the worst, what a blue."
Now she's laughing hard, trying to make it a joke,
while I pretend not to remember what she spoke.
My toast didn't pop out, got stuck up top,
now breakfast feels tragic, a failed food crop.
I tug at it gently, I push, I do try,
but my bread's still trapped like a doomed omelet fry.
I trace their patterns in the sky's wide air,
they hang suspended, slow and bare,
They shift without effort, lose their shape,
while I'm stuck trying not to waste my escape.
You trace the path where the thread has led,
how it once curled neat in a tight spread.
Now it's a tangle with nowhere to end,
slipping through your fingers like an old friend.
Their feet fall hard on the worn-out ground,
they trace paths where they once were found.
A shadow lingers from days long past,
each step feels like memories cast.
She schedules another check-up and test,
they're just making sure everything's best.
Her calendar's full of the doctor's miles,
but she knows her health is worth all the trials.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: I never asked for any kind of clue,
but here's a key beside this ancient brew.
I fit it in the slot, the latch un-lock,
the box flies open—what a pleasant shock.
I trace my fingers over the faded days,
and remember how time ran different ways.
The ink still clings to the corners of the past,
a lifeline frozen, now slipping too fast.
Their songs began to slowly fade,
Once loud, now barely worth a parade.
They crave the quiet, soft and calm,
A hush feels like the soul's true balm.
She tried to buy groceries but had no cash,
her card got declined with a polite clash.
Her savings are gone, she's running out of dime,
the app just buzzed—her limit hit its chime.
You step onto the bathroom floor tile,
then flash a grin with your barefoot smile.
The cold creeps through your socks and chill,
but you dance anyway—you always will.
I watch the stream as it powers its flow,
it carves through stone just to put on a show.
It doesn't beg or try hard to find its voice,
it simply moves, makes its own way its choice.
My voicemail says "no more storage space,"
I listen through messages in a tight race.
I delete old ones hoping not to miss
the next call from someone who brings me bliss.
I bought these fries and I know they're mine,
I'm eating them slowly, one bite per line.
They reach across the table to take,
and my calm cracks just a little bit break.
I write in soft pencil, leaving no trace,
the letters still linger but never erase.
There's magic in something that won't hold ink,
I'll tell you my secrets if only you think.
She watches the sauce leave a wobbly trail,
a curl of ketchup slower than snail mail.
It dangles, suspenseful, about to drip—
she licks the tip fast, but loses her grip.
I swore I'd never waste time searching this pass,
but there's something about the quiet green grass.
The coffee here is weak and the bread feels like stew,
yet the place has a vibe that looks worse than the view.
She saw the ping but gave no clue,
the work was late, the task was due.
She let the silence settle out,
a pause that spoke without a shout.
They claimed it was deep but they never got read,
the font was too small for their tired old head.
They turn every page with deliberate slow,
like they're trying to prove how much time they'll show.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: I had a solid point but then I lost my flow,
a sudden sneeze took over my whole show.
I reached for tissues—no one came to aid,
my moment vanished as my voice began to fade.
My legs gave out before my mind could say pain,
My body betrayed me, it's no use to train.
I'm stuck in the rack, can't seem to find hold,
You warned me once, "Don't push to be bold."
You found him curled inside the cardboard spot,
you had tucked him there and almost forgot.
His soft gray fur blends with the packing fur,
as if he's grown around some hidden spur.
I left my sweat behind as my new mark,
the mat was stained when I rolled through the dark.
This spot's my badge, a kind of proof,
of all the work I did beneath this roof.
You swear you put your phone away again,
but your brain insists it's somewhere plain.
You toss the cushions high to try to find,
it was just sitting there the whole time—behind.
She rolls her shoulders to chase off the ache,
each crumb a reward she forgets to take.
Her spine tries to touch toes, but resists the bend,
her body still whispers there's more it can't mend.
I catch the scent of your old coat in my seat,
like you left a voice memo I can't delete.
It smells like subway air and the cold rain,
like part of you was meant to remain.
Your phone buzzes once like it means something ring,
but you pretend there's no reason to bring
it up. You let it die without skipping a beat,
and maybe tomorrow won't be a repeat.
She tries to stop it but can't hold the fit,
A whisper becomes a cackle—just a bit.
Her eyes start to water, the room rings a bell,
From silence to symphony, she laughs till she swell.

topic: a man reading on a bench
lines: I watch the wind blow pages slowly through,
his face lit by sky, his book dog-eared blue.
He doesn't know I'm here or what I might know—
I trace my shadow in the grass right below.
You type so slow and keep it all wrong,
the cursor blinks like it's had enough along.
Each letter turns into a clumsy hunt,
your efficiency becomes a sad stunt.
You touch the edge and you feel the burn,
the cookies crumble when you try to turn.
It's still too hot, this heavy steel,
your skin remembers, even if you feel.
You strike a yoga-level stretch and pose,
your paws curl up near the edge of my toes.
I try to roll away for a quick nap,
but you land right on my chest—don't even trap.
I knew their name, I even knew their name,
but not the drink they call a sacred game.
They stared at me with a half-empty glass,
like I'd failed some barista's final class.
You send the same tired "u up?" every call,
it lands like a deflated sad little ball.
You'll wait for a ghost while your eyelids beg rest,
but pride won't let you go back to your nest.
You call the crumpled flyer art,
it's been the bane of your wall for weeks, still chart.
You tried every glue, tape, or stick,
but somehow, it stays up—it's your little trick.
They caught it with bare hands, no time to plan,
A moment of panic, then calm began.
The coffee was brown and the floor full of drop,
But they laughed through the mess, and wiped up the crop.
My phone rings like a midnight alarm bell,
it's just apps screaming into the void of this hell.
I let it light up my fingers' soft glow,
some small part still wants help from below.
They spill syrup on the floor this bright day,
unaware of the mess they're putting away.
A shoe catches and they take a small slip,
you steady their arm and hold their warm grip.
The kitchen was thick with the weight of the heat,
the cake sat forgotten in sweet defeat.
She traced the soft swirls with a quiet sigh,
and wondered why love always melts when you try.
You followed a sign that missed the clue,
a crumb on the sidewalk begged to be chew.
The door opened up a strange new scene,
where pastries are loud and coffee's out of routine.
You're still wearing that gym sock on one leg,
though it's clinging like a desperate clothes peg.
You tried to blame it on the laundry room's game,
but the tag still has your full and proper name.
You remember how the cheese fell into the bowl,
a dusty Parmesan your mom once stole.
Now you grate it slow, let it fall like dust,
and hope the memory tastes as good as trust.
I started this diet with a strict plan,
but hunger has proven to be such a man.
I nibbled a crumb, then the whole damn snack,
now my calories are way off the track.
His bark could shake the windows off the guard,
He stands like king above his muddy yard.
The mailman tries to sidestep his name,
This hound's local legend—brave to fame.

topic: texting 'i miss u' out of nowhere
lines: It slips from your lips into thin air,
unspoken, it lingers in your stare.
You tap on the screen but you never press send,
the words are for no one, just a faraway friend.

topic: someone handing you a surprise gift
lines: She shoves the box into my hand,
claiming it's from some "secret brand."
I rip off the tape to check out the new,
but it's a fidget spinner—old news, bad view.

topic: missing a chorus in a song
lines: You hit pause just as the music was skip,
you stumble forward, trying not to trip.
Your heart's off-rhythm with the lost beat,
you rewind, but the song just won't repeat.
I tried the "rubber glove" trick — still no glove,
my fingers say they don't give a damn about love.
Each clove leaves more scent than a permanent stain,
and now I smell like dinner walked into my brain.
I remember the old toy with two simple slots,
batteries blinked to life in their magic red dots.
Now I fumble, trying to force them the wrong way—
no spark, just the ghost of a childhood gone gray.
His eyes are tired but the screen still glows,
He can't put it down, even if he knows.
The hours pass and his yawns say "to sleep,"
But the world feels far when the mind goes deep.
My breath still echoes from the game's sweet flow,
A high score falling just before it show.
I gasp, I beg—my finger taps for rest,
But silence wins, and grief sits heavy on my chest.
We get stuck in the same old joke loop,
laughing like we're part of the troop.
Nobody else would understand the code,
so we keep it running, private mode.
Your neighbors tap on your window with ears,
their patience running out after all these years.
But you turn it down when you find the right key,
then offer them space to feel music-free.
I slide the pizza onto the hot metal tray,
my hunger's lingering but I turn it away.
I'll wait until it browns to a perfect gold,
though deep down I know—I'm too hungry to hold.
She counts the seconds between each pale glow,
her breath catches as the truth starts to grow.
This isn't old wiring—it's something to fear,
it's been coming closer, one year by year.
You sigh but you'll clean the mess off your desk up,
the coffee was black from the paper cup.
It's smudged, but you'll rewrite it for grade,
no stain can steal what you've learned to trade.
I still remember the ballpoint was blue,
the only ink ever to write something true.
It rolled off my desk late last night to the floor,
now I hunt for it like some strange morning chore.

topic: laughing too hard at a joke
lines: She heard a punchline that was just a tiny bit,
it landed like lightning and caused a full-blown fit.
She toppled right backward out of her chair,
and whooped into thin air with nowhere to care.
She paints her truth loud, a message to shout,
wild colors collide in a mess that's about
to burst through the gray—no rules for the sky,
they can't make her stop, and they can't make her deny.

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: You lean into the breeze as you glide,
A pothole forces you to the road's side.
You try to tap the brakes, but the scooter won't stop,
And now there's flashing lights—you're flagged down by a cop.

topic: restaurant with no menu in English
lines: She steps up to the counter, wants to see
what's on the menu or if there's a fee.
She points at symbols, tries her best to ask,
but translating the meal becomes her task.
You roll but your spine won't bend like a bone,
Your voice comes out grumbly, a tired old tone.
You try to stretch fully but fail to wake,
The couch was a trap — you call it a mistake.
I gave it a look like the end of a sigh,
Its leaves curled and browned as they hung to die.
I stepped over it daily with purpose and cast,
A wilted old ghost from a forgotten past.
He moves along like he invented the tread,
his posture says he's tired of leading the head.
Not a single soul passes to share the care,
and still, he walks like the silence is rare.
She clips his leash as if it's some kind of tie,
and forces him to greet the morning sky.
He hates the walk but never lets her hear his bark,
just drags his feet like some tired little lark.
You twist the top and blow into the air,
but nothing comes—your glue is too bare.
Your notes lie undone on a sticky page,
like secrets trapped in a fragile cage.

topic: waiting for the bus in rain
lines: The schedule says the bus will come but delay.
The bench is wet and shows signs of decay.
You stare at the road where the water drops,
your hair gets soaked before it even crops.
The number on the page is a total shock,
I toss my phone into the charging dock.
I scroll through charges—some dubious byte,
I swear I didn't stream anything that night.
It's not a full-blown ghost or a haunted phase,
but the bulb keeps blinking like it wants to blaze.
She swears it's not her eyes or her tired mind,
though this flicker might just drive her completely blind.
Your laundry basket reeks with old gym smell,
it's been neglected for a week-long spell.
Socks are tangled where they hit the floor,
but you call it fashion — weirdo laundro-chore.

topic: leaving a note on the fridge
lines: I left a note in marker, not in ink.
It's bold and clear — they'll surely think.
"Don't forget," it says, in blocky read,
"the cat is on a diet. Don't feed."
There's a bird outside pecking at the glass,
thinking it's got me right out in the grass.
I wave and shout, but it won't stop this show,
poor thing probably thinks I don't know.
Again, you're stuck when the name comes out,
everyone smiles while you choke on your shout.
You nod and you laugh—no one gives a clue,
your brain feels like water, not glue.

topic: steaming coffee in a blue mug
lines: You watch the steam curl as you slowly pour,
your breath like mist against a distant shore.
You know the morning will run out too cold,
but you pretend this cup is something bold.
I passed the last shelf with a faded sign,
"Ends Today" screamed in a crooked line.
The store's old neon buzzed, dimmed and low,
I bought what I loved, but I never will know.
I keep scrolling down the endless hate-filled feed,
it all feels designed to incite and lead.
I long for the quieter, simpler days,
when conversations had gentler, kinder ways.
You're staring at screens looking for a clue,
Your brain says your password isn't what you knew.
You try your dog's name and it makes you grin,
But the app says "Invalid," and your hope grows thin.
You let the world fade when you hear that chime through,
It's not a distraction—it's your next big clue.
You silence the room with that quiet, sharp tone,
Confident, focused, you're never quite alone.
This flicker's messing with my entire mood,
I blame the bulb not my midnight food.
It pulses like a disco ball mid-lie,
pretending it's the northern lights in my sky.
You said these were for comfort, not to try
the impossible in heels or something sky-high.
You tried to dance and stumbled with a leap,
now laughing, they're more trouble than a heap.
You thought cooking would be fun and a dash,
but now your kitchen's a flour-filled crash.
You watched every video, you've really tried,
yet the recipe app still calls you a guide.
I used to know each rhythm and move,
lost in the beat, spinning without a groove.
Now I stick to corners where the floor
feels like a mirror I can't look at before.
Their shoes always catch the eye when they go,
polished so clean, they seem ready to show.
They never come unstrapped, not loose or askew—
a daily ritual, their care is so true.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: There's a toothpick jammed in their sleeve, it looks stick,
They try to hide it with a nervous quick.
It won't come loose, they're trying to get it out,
But now everyone's watching, and they're full of doubt.
My phone buzzes with an alarm to ring,
The parrot squawks like a comical thing.
It screeches messages from my old chat,
And wakes the room like a charging bat.

topic: sharing a cat video with no context
lines: They hit "send" on a meow without a thread,
probably hoping their old friend would dread.
You stare at the screen, unsure if you share,
but something about it makes you want to care.

topic: a gym membership you never use
lines: You keep the card clipped in a little frame,
but guilt creeps in with each unused name.
You say you'll get serious next week, same as last,
while life keeps moving past your fitness glass.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: You posted the punchline one more time in your try,
but no one laughed—just silence, slow and dry.
The joke's gone stale, but still you make it fade,
like some old trophy in a shame parade.
They're limping slightly but they won't admit it now,
"It's nothing," they insist, gritting their teeth how.
You see the pain flash through their guarded eyes,
but pride keeps them smiling through the silent lies.
He says it was just a small risk he took,
the window left wide when he read his book.
Now the floor's soaked and the dog hates the rug,
while coffee goes cold in your favorite mug.
They teeter so close to the edge, it's all too near,
Her breath is a whisper of panic and fear.
One cough could be what makes the whole thing fall,
She backs toward the wall, she won't get close at all.
His snore is a bass line, a nightly, deep song,
it hums through the hours and carries me along.
The neighbors have learned to block out his loud,
but I'm proud of the rhythm he makes like a crowd.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: I picked up the smoothest flat stone,
and held it in my hand all alone.
It caught the light with a quiet gleam,
like a wish formed from a forgotten dream.

topic: singing along to a car ad
lines: The radio hums a catchy little song,
I tap my fingers gently moving along.
My thoughts are soft, they float through my mind,
memories of you whisper warm and kind.
She counts each coin like it's the last of her time,
lips moving softly to tally each dime.
"Exact change only" means we still use cash,
while she smiles slow and the credit card flash.
You watch the butterfly land and sit still,
the moment feels fragile, almost a thrill.
It doesn't stay long—no time to say
goodbye before it drifts off, light and away.
She thought she was deleting some old snap,
but my phone imported her whole life as a map.
Now every embarrassing vacation post
is haunting me, tagged like a digital ghost.
Your shirt is all soaked by the wind in your hair,
I'd call it a date but you've no money to spare.
Your cologne has mixed with the gas station stink,
I'll just blame the radio's bad playlist link.
Her dog goes wild with unfiltered calls,
The sound reverberates off the bus walls.
She won't stop cheering his rowdy, proud shout,
like he's barking on stage and she's calling the out.
I feign interest when they shift from my eye,
their stories now laced with a digital lie.
They snap a photo, then check if the post
appears while I'm left to quietly ghost.

topic: a video call with a frozen screen
lines: Your face gets stuck on some old frame,
The app still reads out your display name.
I try to wave but the screen won't wave,
I shrug it off, acting so brave.
I waltz through the room without breaking the floor,
this package's from the best dance supply store.
You might think it's boring, but trust my good guess—
this present's the perfect fit for your new dress.
She's got the kind of shoes that shout "I'm smart,"
built for the commute, not for a heart.
Her laces are tied, not flung into lace,
every step she takes feels like the right place.
You let the moss grow soft on the stone,
walk slow, as if your voice still had its tone.
Each step leaves more than a footfall's trace,
it lingers in green on the quiet stone's cold face.
I duck past the bouncer near the side gate,
the crowd thinks I'm someone who got there too late.
I stand in the crush where the bass hits the beat,
and pretend this is mine for the price of a treat.
It's not a mess—it's a catastrophe, full spill,
she crouches there with her guilt and her still.
The hardwood groans as the drops meet the floor,
and suddenly cleaning feels cursed, like a chore.
She laughs every time she hits the wrong voice,
knowing this is her favorite strange choice.
We clap louder when the notes are wrong,
still cheering how we sing it all along.
A slow, sticky trail runs down his chin,
the ketchup is pale, the moment thin.
Each drop takes its time as it leaves the spoon,
he holds it too still, I can't help but swoon.
You stare at the screen, hoping for flush,
but the machine gives you nothing but hush.
You tap your card again just to tap,
it hits the same dead-end financial trap.

topic: missing a chorus in a song
lines: She rewinds but the record still skips,
the needle just hums through the chorus and strips.
She swears she doesn't even know,
but her lips are mouthing every show.
You press rewind, hoping to relive that scene,
the tape whirs quietly inside the machine.
You hit play, listening for something to stay,
maybe the past still feels like today.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: You swore you'd never do this—left it all to lie,
like me, neglected, left to slowly die.
Now you untangle the mess with a grimaced thread,
blaming the night, not how you slept instead.
You found a piece with a greenish spot,
but it's still good for a little bit of rot.
You toss it with a laugh and a grin,
and throw the whole loaf into the bin.
I can't stop smiling as she runs to go,
her tiny hands outstretched to make them show.
She laughs so loud the whole wide sky feels right,
and I know nothing else could feel this bright.
The dog runs in circles all day long, it just spins,
it's not clear if this play or if this just begins.
It barks at the motion but can't seem to go,
it's lost in the magic of spinning in show.
A single drop hangs from my silver tear,
it dangles dangerously close to my ear.
It slips so slow—it takes a moment to fall,
landing softly on the kitchen's white wall.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: She remembered the date but forgot it was due,
now every screen is a static, drained hue.
Her fingers hover mid-click, there's too much lag,
so she sends a message and waits for the tag.
Your bag got stuck in the farthest claim,
They called your name but you missed the game.
You texted "Send backup, I've hit a stop,"
Then bought a hoodie and laughed, "This'll do—good prop."
You watch the cars crawl but the road won't flow,
the GPS insists you should turn and go.
You spot a coffee shop just out of reach—so near,
you sip, you sigh, and pretend to cheer.
You step onto the bathroom floor's wet tile,
pretending you have moves like a dancer's style.
But your socks lose grip and you go full slide,
landing gracefully—though barely—on the side.
She keeps it propped near the back door to stand,
where the wind can't reach it, safe from the land.
She let one break once in a gale-force storm,
now this one's her best—it's her new norm.
She squints at the small text, misses the date,
misreads her receipt's number on the plate.
She claims she's doing "just dandy, quite fine,"
but I help her find what was once clearly mine.
Her mind is already lost in the thought,
halfway between nodding and being caught.
She stares at the window, the clouds drift by sky,
but silence is all she can muster as reply.
She pauses her sandwich to read this small bit,
her face goes from calm to a sudden fit.
She slams down her phone, like it's some cursed shell,
her whole lunchtime now ruined, transformed into hell.
She says the sink's clogged for the tenth time again,
her hair is probably stuck in the drain.
"It's not my fault!" she shouts, shifts the blame,
then pours oil down there—oh, the very same.
You hum along but it's hard not to note,
each crack sounds like hope running out of your throat.
You laugh it off, pretend it's a quirky old tree,
when really you're just losing your voice and your key.

topic: a road trip with bad directions
lines: You promised the map was accurate in blue,
but we drove all the way down the wrong path through.
We wasted three hours and countless miles,
yet laughed the whole time with forced, tired smiles.
She yells "Hurry up!" as she jabs in my move,
then fakes a "slow wave" to help her prove
how effortless it is to break every queue—
like we don't have sensors or cameras or clue.
She fills the page with soft, dark ink,
the lines connect but leave her mind to think.
Her fingers move with quiet, steady hands,
a dream takes shape where worry lands.
I blow out the single flame, my new age,
A quiet celebration, no fanfare or page.
One wish, whispered fast to the air, my wish,
The cat watches me, eyes wide like a fish.
A frozen screen makes me beg it to load,
while outside the kids chase bikes down the road.
Finally it starts—just a moment to play—
the audio's still mute, but the visuals are day.
I hum an old tune while he strums his song,
the rhythm pulls me to walk along.
He hits a wrong note but it still feels right,
we laugh and dance in the front yard light.
You posted that meme and it was a bit late,
we're all stuck here, same tired fate.
The comments are rolling in fast from your view,
I laugh too loud, but I secretly rue.
I give the shaker a hard, nervous shake,
then freeze when I see what I've done by mistake.
The granules spread out on the worn kitchen dust,
and I worry it shows something I can't trust.

topic: laughing too hard at a joke
lines: Their laughter fades but their eyes stay dry,
They're holding back with that forced, tired eye.
The punchline landed, but it never quite hit—
It just gave them a laugh they barely could fit.
She scans the tiny print but can't really read,
her eyes dart faster than her stressed-out head.
She's certain there's a loophole worth the cash,
but now she's second-guessing every dash.
You think you're safe because your shoes don't dance,
but stairs and sidewalks still give you a chance.
You twist your ankle in some quiet pain,
then vow to never wear them again.
You said it was fine when they took every deal,
but not from the plate at your dinner table meal.
Your voice goes up like a match to a flame,
while they crunch what's been yours all the same.
They spin so fast, I wish they'd rewind and go slow,
the names slip by and I never will know.
As lights dim and the credits all start to fade,
I feel like I'm missing some vital, sharp blade.
You collapse the couch into a shadowed room,
the pillows are stacked in a pyramid of doom.
You drape the fabric like a shield against the wall,
but the sound of your laughter echoes through the hall.
He never takes off his dented old wear,
he marches through sites up the metal stair.
It's cracked from a fall but it still has to hit,
though it no longer fits, he won't admit it.

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: The July air clings like it's made to heat,
You move with purpose—no time to repeat.
You knock out your job from start to full stop,
Beads of sweat fall from your hardworking crop.
You watched the sun fall below the last light,
but your work climbed up past the usual height.
The hours you put in are etched on the clock's mark,
while the world fades into the quietest dark.
I hit the button marked "unsubscribe to stop,"
the screen blinked once, then faded to a crop.
A breath of calm now fills my inbox free,
I didn't know I'd need to feel this agree.
Your spine makes a satisfying *pop*,
you freeze like a robot mid-stop.
You twist your upper body back,
and hear a loud noise from your neck—*crack*.
You once moved like water, smooth and a glide,
now you're sticking out from the rhythm's tight side.
You count every step, lost the old beat,
still feel the dance floor's ghostly heat.
The neighbor lets the dog out at the gate,
always a minute or two running a bit late.
I freeze when I hear the familiar bark,
waiting for the leash to snap in the dark.
The moss still grows on this stone path of yours,
It shows no fear of the dry or the pours.
You tried to clear it one morning the way
you clear your mind on a bad therapy day.
You find your own rhythm, a steady beat,
the same notes again but they never repeat.
There's music inside you, a drumstick soul,
I swear you could tap me right off my scroll.
As the sun dips low behind the west,
your silhouette craves one final rest.
You stay still like you're holding onto the hour,
but even dusk takes back the power.
The egg hits the pan with a loud crack,
She leaps away like she got zapped right back.
"That's not a mess," she says, "it's pure art!"
I check my mood chart—it just says "hart."

topic: texting 'i miss u' out of nowhere
lines: It slips from you like dust in the air,
a message sent without any stare.
You type "I miss u" out of the blue, no line,
just three words that somehow feel like mine.
She walks along the water's quiet chill,
the waves repeat the same old lullaby still.
Her phone buzzes soft but she won't let her mind
chase shadows — the morning air's too sharp with wind.

topic: finding a dollar in old jeans
lines: I thought this pocket held something of clue,
a lost sock perhaps or a bill that's overdue.
I dug my fingers way down to the deep,
all I found was a buck to keep.
Since this morning, it's been making a drop,
I've ignored every plea for it to stop.
Water now forms a small puddle-shaped pool,
But I'm waiting for someone, any tool.
You stare at the cake with one lonely age,
A setup for laughs but you're not in the stage.
You blow out the flame in a half-hearted lie,
Wishing it's easier to fool your own eye.
You've been watching that bird for an hour,
it's not going anywhere, not out of power.
You curse its bright beak, its small sharp gleam,
like a tiny tyrant of your greenest dream.
You watch their sneakers spin in the midday gleam,
their laughter turns the air into a shared dream.
They don't need a score or a list of rules,
you'd trade your world for these tiny, noisy fools.
I've been waiting to see if it will ever grow,
patient enough to let the quiet show.
The moss has claimed its soft green patch of stone,
and I'm not so alone beneath the unknown.
The river shows off every sad little hue,
as if it could sell me a perfect view.
It mirrors the clouds, which can't hide the lie—
today's just a wash, but the sky must be sky.
I paused my sandwich just to read this post,
the comment section was the real life host.
I laughed so hard I almost choked on my bite,
it lit my meal up like a summer night.
There's a bird outside that thinks your window's flat,
It taps and chirps like it wants to chat.
It sees its reflection, thinks it's something wrong,
Poor featherhead, this could go on for days—how long?
My snack and my typing share one sad fate—
both fall victim to gravity's plate.
I send emails with a coffee-stained spill,
and the "E" key won't budge from its still.
You took a bite like it was a deep cut,
betrayal pooled hot in your gut.
We could've split it, but now it's a deal
we both lost something bigger than a meal.
I left the key inside and now there's no clue,
the lock's been tampered with—how could that be true?
I check my bag again, but it's not hard to find,
something feels off, and it won't leave my mind.
You built whole worlds out of plastic scenes,
now our kids stare at life through flat screens.
We'd assign dialogue, create each role,
while those little heroes lived and fought with soul.
You thought you could skip the forecasted storm,
now stuck in a downpour, the city a swarm.
The umbrella gives way with a loud snap,
you're drenched in the rain and the sidewalk trap.
You listen to thunder, the raindrops still pour,
and count how long it's been since last week's four.
A flicker appears in the murky gray light,
a hunch tells you something might happen tonight.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: My phone goes dark when I lay down my head,
but not before I hit the count for bed.
The numbers rise, or they fall into lies,
and either way, I stare too long with tired eyes.
You follow the map through the narrowest twist,
the wind reads your worries in whispers and list.
A lantern glows sudden, sharp as a flame,
you read its old name like a secret or a claim.
You press record to keep the voice and sound,
but memory is tricky, never quite found.
Words fade even when they're saved for the past,
like echoes you try to catch and then cast.
I toss my change toward his broken street,
he plays the same three songs with the same old beat.
He nods when I drop a single dime,
then says "Thanks. That'll get me through until next time."
I blasted music till the walls went loud,
guests swarmed in, no room left for a crowd.
Every detail hit just as I'd planned it—plan,
they called me genius, their secret party's fan.
I squeezed the soap—it smells like old gym gear gel,
the kind that turns your five-star stay into hell.
Not the fresh toothpaste kind or a spicy cool mint,
more like mold, and maybe a wet magazine's print.
The acrid smoke fills the stale hotel smell,
you swear this is how your bad day begins to spell.
You stare at the blackened edge of the breakfast pan,
your flight leaves in two hours—what's your new plan?
You watch the gate numbers as time starts to roam,
Your carry-on feels heavy like a little home.
A stranger ahead looks just as tired and near,
But silence hangs thick where no one wants to cheer.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: A toddler's wails echo down the whole aisle,
Her brother just laughs, still chewing his smile.
I try a goldfish, but it won't be a snack,
The plane hits turbulence, and now I'm off track.
I found old gum stuck beneath my chair,
it left a stain I still remember where.
It smells like mint, or maybe like the scent
we split — quick as air, without intent.
She tries to draw hearts but the mirror won't show,
her hand moves in circles, she doesn't quite know.
A ghostly fingerprint appears on her face,
she laughs and wipes it with shaky grace.
You swear you hit send, not the contact's ring,
but sure, let's pretend this is the right thing.
I guess the joke's on me — it was all wrong,
you'll just laugh later when you read it along.
My brain's been on fire since morning to burn,
I've tried ten teas, none could make it turn.
My desk now feels like the bottom of a crawl,
I scream into my pillow—then hit the wall.
I spot his scent still lingering on the seat,
it mixes with AC and old heat.
I crack the window, but it won't make a trail,
the road ahead feels somehow more pale.
I twist the top off my glue stick again—no cap
to hold the mess I'm about to make or trap.
A dry white ridge forms along the narrow crack,
and I sigh, knowing I'll need a new one tracked back.
The drip machine beeps like a debt that's long due,
it won't stop repeating the same shrill do.
You check your watch — it's exactly noon,
you dread the next beep, but it won't come soon.
The water just drips, there's no rhythm or flow,
I swish in the puddles that gather below.
I longed for that steam that would always stay warm,
when showers were showers, not just a slow storm.
I drank my coffee from this mug so warm,
and didn't see the quiet day turn storm.
Now your name lingers in a faint trace,
but the cup's still here, yet you're not in this place.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: I spotted a shard of light in the creek's gleam,
it caught me like something long lost in my dream.
I held it tight, like a truth I might keep,
but the current stole it back into the deep.

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: You wipe your brow but the sweat still keeps flow,
the air stays thick and your breath won't let go.
Each drop makes a mark where it hits the shirt drip,
you stumble indoors just to miss the heat trip.
She only ever wears the left-side song,
humming the chorus just to sing along.
Her right ear listens to the world's own beat,
half the music she'll never get to repeat.
She fumbles the key, the rusted one's worn key,
the bike is still locked, and she's minutes late and free.
The students pass her on sidewalks too fast,
she sighs as the moment slips off into the past.
You bought it a new pot with drainage and grit,
you even got a cactus instead of a lit.
It's not about the bloom or the leaves or the height,
it's thriving in your room—dead by morning light.
You twist and you tug, but the handle won't spin,
the lock's giving nothing—just clicks from the tin.
Your tools hit the floor with a clatter, no key,
so you laugh and you shout at the heap of debris.
They're sipping their third cup since the brew,
staring past the window at the same old view.
The sugars in their coffee can't help the shake,
they mutter about how this hit was a mistake.
You watch the feathers drift gently and still,
their soft descent slows when they reach the hill.
You try to follow where each one might trace,
but they land forgotten in some lonely place.
She tried to wind it up and gave it a throw,
the strands all snarled and refused to grow.
I watched her mutter with no real hope,
the whole damn thing looked like a twisted rope.
She swore she'd never use her old cash,
but panic set in when the app wouldn't dash.
She waved down the driver and asked about the fare,
now she's fumbling for coins — oh what a scare.
You blink so slow, as if time won't let go,
your gaze drops soft and weary and low.
That old desk lamp still casts the same warm beam,
while you stare into something you used to dream.
He cracks another joke and laughs it out,
like he's trying to shout down his doubt.
Everyone rolls their eye but won't say die,
just pretend they ate the joke like pie.
You handed me a ten, like covering old pain,
"Just get what you want, we'll do this again."
The sandwich was good, but the joy had a cost—
I watched you eat fast, like love's something lost.
Each tiny link holds more weight than I think,
They dangle so close to the table's brink.
If one lets go, they'll collapse and fall,
And I'll lose every chain I've built so tall.
You sink into cushions, all lullaby down,
Your head near my shoulder, the pillow your crown.
The silence between us is slow and so soft,
My hand lifts you gently back where you're aloft.
You think you need a little more than just a shout,
but deep down you know it's all a bit of doubt.
The kettle hisses, sending up its thin stream,
while you pretend it could be something more than steam.
I check the schedule, but now I miss class,
I need a professor to let me pass.
The building looks all the same on this map,
I run in circles like a rat in a trap.
The wind catches their face without a trace,
it flicks a memory you can't erase.
Their breath hangs thin in the sharp cold,
you knew this moment had been foretold.
She says it's cold, but she means she wants warm,
her breath a silent complaint in the storm.
She checks the temp as if she can't just feel,
as if this fight weren't made of old steel.
I can't tell what's wrong but I don't want to see,
it's not moving right like it should be.
It loops in the tank like it lost how to float,
I'm panicking now, I need a pro's note.
He's got a smile wide enough for his chat,
from politics to his cat's most annoying hat.
Each story he spins is a funny new tale,
and I'm just along for the gossip-filled trail.
You let your phone ring out with no one near phone,
the room stays still, you're calm, completely alone.
There's pride in the quiet, the silence so wide,
you feel it deep, calm applause in your inside.
The rain insists that it's here to stays,
blurring the difference between these gray days.
She sips her coffee from a chipped mug,
laughing with the cat on her worn-out rug.
You hum the same tune into empty air,
the screen casts a pale blue glare.
