You scroll just to find it, again, again, scroll,
the song won't let go of your tired, sad whole.
You dipped your spoon deep into the jar,
it clung like syrup from some old star.
Now golden gobs leave a mess in your trail,
you lick but can't fix this slow, sweet fail.
You followed the map until it said "Go ahead,"
then turned you into a field where cars go dead.
The phone still insists you should drive and swear,
while traffic zooms past where you truly are there.
You feel the calm that the water keeps near,
But time slips away like a forgotten year.
You try to hold what the current won't hold,
Like fears you thought were already grown old.

topic: sharing a cat video with no context
lines: You send me a link with no message or chat,
Just a cat doing tricks in a dusty old flat.
Its fur is so soft, it melts every frost,
I smile through my cough, and forget all the cost.
I watched him nod off behind the big wheel,
his coffee gone cold was the only thing real.
The bus passed each sign and each blinky stop,
like it rolled through a dream, with no traffic or pop.
The cat curls tight, claiming the suitcase air,
as if it's the first time she found a soft lair.
You can't get through till you zip up your pack,
but who are you to wake such a peaceful black?
She swore she left them in the same old spot,
but now claims she must've just plain forgot.
It turns into a contest—searching's the game,
and she'll win both the trophy and the acclaim.
She watches the tuning fork shake but still,
it hums an old song she used to thrill.
The note fades slowly into the air,
while her hands tremble, cold, and bare.
I lean my head back and let out a sigh right down,
where neon hums of this tired little town.
My brain is heavy with the day's stray thought,
a coffee I forgot I even bought.
She meant to delete it but left the draft note,
her fingers paused on the keyboard, tight in her throat.
Now the "Send" button glows, still waiting to sent,
a confession so soft that it feels like it's lent.
I said the punchline too loud when I spoke,
the room was silent but I kept telling the joke.
I begged for laughter that refused to fall,
my pride hit pieces against the wall.
This dorm room is giving off major chill,
I wore my coat inside and even took a pill.
I try to blow on the vents for some puff,
but the heater's a ghost—I'm just cold stuff.
I blinked against spots that filled the whole room,
a shadowy wall seemed about to loom.
My pulse is a drum in a frantic rush,
I sweat through my shirt from the panic flush.
I bought a keychain labeled "life's one big clue,"
but it's just plastic with a blurry hue.
They sold me a t-shirt that said "take me home, spin,"
now it hangs in my closet—bright, but too thin.
She stirs as the horn sounds, half-asleep and awake,
the sky cracks open with morning's slow break.
It tolls through the silence, a hollow, low toll,
and shakes her still-drifting, still-empty soul.
They've started a full-blown treasure hunt,
"It's got to be under the couch or a punt."
Each family member blames the last,
while the cat watches, silent and vast.
The music cut off before the final fade,
But she kept dancing through the empty parade.
Her fingers tap out the beat where songs once plays,
She's had worse endings—this moment outlasts days.
A small bird taps gently against the glass,
mistaking his reflection for tall grass.
He fluffs his blue feathers, sits so still,
unsure why his double won't talk or will.
I heard my voice crack and it felt like an age,
that first thin fissure, like glass in a cage.
It wasn't a scream or a sob or a break—
just time, maybe, turning my tone into shake.
The toast went black in the pan's cruel flame,
You mutter the old joke—it tastes the same.
You breathe a quiet, Sunday kind of sigh,
and say goodbye to your perfect morning try.
You read the label just to try to know
why this cereal tastes like regret and show.
It lists "natural flavors" and one vague trace
of something you swear was never in that place.
You watch the flakes drift down from the tall,
the quiet kind no storm could ever call.
They touch your sleeve and they begin to trace
the shape of something temporary's place.
She spends an hour making the image look real,
then wonders why no one comments to reveal.
She turns off the filter and adds warm light,
but still looks like someone you barely might.
I watched from my porch as they yelled at the bin,
the noise was a constant, loud, daily din.
She said I took it out wrong, again and again,
I gave her a look and went back inside then.
I tap "allow" but the app just won't try.
It accuses me of trying to spy.
I don't want biometric facial code,
I just want to use the thing in quiet mode.
You left plates piling up in the sink to soak,
now the smell rises thick like slow-moving smoke.
You promise you'll clean them, you really will try,
but you keep telling yourself you'll do it some why.
Her cat curls up on the open case,
the only good spot left in this strange place.
Its steady breath mends the silence between,
soft as the weight of a life nearly seen.
My fingers are stuck together in a sweet mess,
But I still feel like this taste is a true success.
I lick my sticky hand while walking down the street,
And smile as a bird lands right on my sweet feet.
I blame the mattress and my advancing age,
my spine creaks like a rusted-up cage.
I try to stretch but it takes me hours to wake,
I pretend my coffee is a miracle break.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: The corner of the blanket caught in a loop,
it dragged the sheets along like a troop.
Now half my body's exposed to the cold,
but I'm too lazy to fix what's so old.
I shook the oak until the branches were bare,
a thousand leaves broke loose and danced for air.
It looked like nature's own slow-motion show,
where people gaped at the mess I threw below.
She walks the block barefoot in search of the sun,
her sandals tossed out mid-lunch, or some fun.
The concrete glows under soles that once froze,
each step a sly flex of happiness in her toes.
I stood too close when the doors started to near,
the screen blinked red as my board time grew clear.
I watched the train go without me, a tight miss,
the tunnel swallowed my sigh into an abyss.
She flips the egg with flair, there's that perfect crack,
The yolk holds steady—no mess on the track.
White curls up neat, it's a swirl that will rise,
A breakfast masterpiece now set as her prize.
You curl up all weekend with books and a stream,
the rain on the roof sounds like hush and a dream.
You microwave your favorite pasta with soup,
then sigh as the forecast repeats the same loop.
She unzips her coat and spills out the load,
of worries she's carried the whole long road.
Over tea, she begins to pour,
and my silence becomes the steady shore.
She tests the rail again for a better grip,
afraid she might tumble from this high slip.
A sugary residue fills the air's smell,
and she wonders how bad it feels if they fell.

topic: a dog leash tangled in railings
lines: The dog looked proud, I took the blame,
like this was my idea for local fame.
Now the leash is wrapped around the loop,
and I'm stuck here like a chicken in a coop.
She watches the rabbit move its nose so still,
unsure if it senses her presence or will.
Its nostrils flare in the quiet, crisp air,
but never once does it pause or get scare.
She's waiting for the page to load,
like she's stuck in traffic on a back road.
Her messages still say "Sending... chat,"
while the cat knocks her coffee off the flat.
They stare into light that won't stop shine,
their eyes grow red with the screen's bad sign.
Each scroll feels like paper dry and burn,
they blink, but the hurt won't even turn.
She watches the fish in their rhythmic dance,
their tiny fins painting the room's blue expanse.
Her smile grows wider as she seems to see
how they glide through the water, so wild and free.
They sprint through the halls trying to outrun
the clock and the light from the early sun.
A teacher waves them in, they need to pass,
just sit down and breathe—it's only first class.
You rush in when you hear the final last call,
they've closed early and flipped off the mall.
The sign now reads "Yesterday's great deal,"
you spin around with a groan and a wheel.
She closed the app and said goodbye today,
no longer bound to auto-pay away.
It was her call, a bold new kind of choice,
she stood by it loud, with steady, clear voice.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: You held up a coupon for a chocolate bar,
claiming it was worth ten times as far.
The cashier didn't laugh—it sounded like a deal,
but your friend made a noise that turned into a squeal.
They froze when they saw the white patch on the floor,
like a ghost of clumsiness they can't ignore.
They keep trying to act like it's not a big go,
but their eyes dart down there, steady and slow.
She swears she's very good at staying calm,
but only because silence is her balm.
She tried all the steps to get things to fix,
now mutters old tech advice as dark little tricks.
I watched the butter slide down the toast and spread,
golden and glossy across the warm bread.
It pooled in the corners, a slow-moving drip,
I leaned in closer, almost took a trip.
You swear you filled the tank but have no clue,
the gauge is stuck and lies like old Elmer's glue.
Two hundred miles left? The map says one mile,
but somehow the station's closed with a fake smile.
You watched your cat stake her perfect claim,
a king among dust bunnies, rising to fame.
She stretched out, a soft feline sprawl,
ignoring the world, even the open wall.
The coupon's date is now an ex behind my back,
I curse the fate that made me clip it off the stack.
I planned a coffee deal, my morning steeped in brew,
but now I gnash and grit this bitter truth to chew.
She never got the refund they claimed was sent,
it felt like fate had mocked what she had meant.
She still keeps old receipts like sacred cash,
and smiles when they don't match the screen's bright flash.
She sways and she bounces, making a dance
with bodies around her, no hope for a chance.
Her boots tap the floor, she leans into sway,
declares this the best travel day.
I'm scanning items when my voicemail tone
buzzes loud enough to make me drop my phone.
I step aside but still have to wait,
now I'm blocking the self-checkout gate.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: It's the same exact faces here every week,
They nod and smile but never really speak.
We clap for hymns we've heard a thousand play,
I fake a cough just to sneak out and away.
The quiet rhythm hums, a steady sound,
my hands move faster than the ground they're bound.
I'll finish this hat before the weekend's cap,
my skills are sharp now—no mistakes, no trap.
She swipes her card with too much air,
the screen denies her subway fare.
Her fingers tap a nervous drum,
the machine won't let her late check come.

topic: a missed phone call from Mom
lines: My phone fell silent when I went to run,
by the time I got back, the sun was done.
I opened messages—no note from Mom,
just three missed calls that felt like a bomb.
At four-fifty-seven the office clock
beeps bold as the printer papers block.
She laughs, not crying, at the paper cry,
and fixes it quick, no mess, no "why."
I can't even read the stop sign they see,
what's this car doing driving blind and not me?
The red light flickers, the pedal stays flat—no brake,
this ride's turning into a hellish mistake.
The sky turns to something soft and gold,
but this moment feels strange, almost too old.
I wonder if time will forget this past,
or leave me behind where shadows are fast.
She walks alone where the sky meets the view,
Her shadow lies quiet in morning's soft blue.
The sand holds her feet, all around is so still,
The sea breathes with her, slowly, to fill.
I stare into traffic where no one is ahead,
the driver shrugged when I asked if he had said
something about the taillights going down the bend—
now we coast through reds with no way to tell the end.
She says the world's tilted, it's all her fit,
and then she giggles, full-blown, with her wit.
I ask if her brain's on the loose from its root,
she laughs so hard shoes fly out of her boot.
You send a meme into the empty air,
your screen the only thing you can stare.
It's not a joke or a laugh or a show—
just silence hanging heavy and low.
I caught your gym bag's faint and lonely smell,
a sock had spilled and something soft had fell.
I picked it up—it still held most of your weight,
but now it looked like some sad second estate.
We built our forts out of couches and down,
sticky notes marked the borders of our town.
Now grown-ups talk of jobs we should dream,
I miss the castles I once folded from stream.
The fog rolls in smooth, slow, and low,
It's putting on its ghostly white show.
I stand here alone, lost in the tone,
The world's turned to glass, every stone.
Her phone stays quiet, the ringer is off,
She answers when someone tries to give cough.
She keeps her screen dim, no flashy light,
But smiles come fast when she sees your name bright.
A rainbow of cereal now covers the mess,
The cat's already there—it treats it like a bless.
I step barefoot and leave a foot-shaped track,
But I laugh anyway, slipping into a crack.
She pushes on the door every single time,
the sticky seal still smells like old lime.
Her backpack drags as she gives it a lock,
then mutters about the school's entire stock.
You used to catch the wind like a lazy breeze,
now you sway like you're mocking the tease.
Still holding that same faded striped red,
but I've lost the shade beneath my head.
She searched the couch and the kitchen counter's spot,
but the remote was nowhere to be got.
The batteries died weeks ago—just never said,
she'd lost the button but kept the habit tread.
You sprint across campus ten minutes late,
dodging puddles by the heavy gate.
The building's layout still feels like a maze,
but being fashionably lost is fun these days.
I watch it dig with small, determined ground,
each acorn lost becomes something new and found.
It scurries from branch to shadowy tree,
while I remember the forest it makes of me.
You sip your tea like it's some genius hack,
the steam curls up and tickles your back.
The clock forgets how time is supposed to flow,
your silence says more than any hello.

topic: a video call with a frozen screen
lines: They promise flawless software and tech,
but my call won't load — I give it one more check.
I've tried every shortcut, setting, or fix,
yet still I'm resorting to old-school IT tricks.
You let the drops fall, a quiet little show,
steady and proud like you mean every slow.
They say you need a washer, say you should just fix,
but you're turning the drip into performance tricks.
They've put her through the ringer (and MRI run),
calling every test a little bit of fun.
She's waiting for the bill to drop like hail,
but they gave her a rainbow of new pills to fail.

topic: sitting on the porch steps at twilight
lines: You hold your ground where the daylight makes claim,
the dusk won't steal your quiet kind of fame.
The bugs still buzz, but you don't let it fade,
you sit in silence, warm in your own shade.
I watched the porch light's failing beam,
a ghostly flicker that seemed to scream.
It's not just old age or some broken thing,
it feels like a warning—something's in the ring.
They rise in a chorus, a sharp piercing sound,
each note from the ground, close all around.
Their clicking grows louder, it feels so near,
my skin prickles with silent, crawling fear.
You know these songs won't ever truly fade,
their crackling hum still sounds like old jade.
You queue up the track and let it keep play,
as if the past might return with the day.
The cashier asks if I need change for cash,
I just nod and drop my coupon in the trash.
She scans my single banana slow—so scan,
says, "You sure this is all, sir?" like a man.
The tulips outshine the sky in their pink,
I poured a cold beer and sat for a drink.
I watched from the porch where the bulbs once lay bed,
now all I do here is stare and shake my head.
She laughs so suddenly, it turns the sky blue,
Her smile cracks open like a window pushed through.
But then a pause, a flicker—like a tear could tear,
She laughs again, maybe to forget this whole year.
You're lying there with nothing but the cake,
and a breeze from nowhere that pretends it's a lake.
No candles, no guests—just how you want to feel,
like time forgot to spin its usual wheel.
I watched it twist in a subway-car snap,
now plastic lies in a puddle-shaped trap.
I walk without cover, no pattern, no lace,
my clothes hold memories of that lost rainy place.
My phone's at 3%—like a car out of gas,
I sprint through the house to save this pass.
I snap a last photo, quick as a shot,
praying the cloud finds this tiny spot.

topic: a quiet moment on the porch
lines: The wind moves slow, a sleepy, sideways breeze,
the cat's already bored of trying to please.
I rock the chair like it's some old-time swing,
pretending I don't notice this strange new thing.
You wear your hard hat through the noise and the beat,
it's your shield against both the fall and the heat.
It's dented but still shows your paint-stained name,
a badge of honor bolted to your frame.
This backpack's a symbol of work and a load,
I carry it proudly from here to the road.
My shoulders may ache after miles I've been through,
but knowledge has weight—and I'm proving it too.
She hums along to her favorite tune,
the last notes fade out on a bright June afternoon.
Her phone's dead now, no more it will spin,
but the song's still playing deep inside her skin.
You fumble through your pockets, looking for a key,
the door won't budge and neither can you be.
You twist the knob again, but it still won't turn,
your palms are red from trying not to burn.
The teacher waves her ruler loud across class,
We freeze at the sound of each stern little pass.
My pencil starts shaking I fear it might drop,
She eyes me directly and won't let me stop.
You remember how you hit your head on the glass,
and lay there blinking through the soft green grass.
The pain lingers now, but time moves so still,
you wish your old body would mend as it will.
They stare at the rain until their eyes find rest,
their fingers tapping out rhythms on their chest.
The sky stays gray and the world feels too wide,
but they're stuck here, still waiting to be inside.
She watches the leaves spin and twist in their dance,
as if every gust gives them pause for a chance.
One lands in her hand on the flat of her palm,
and she holds it there with a quiet calm.
You type so slow, but you won't let it go,
the screen fills up with sentences that show
how much your thumb still feels a little pain,
from trying to do it all, and trying again.
You're running late and now you miss the gym,
the morning feels a little more grim.
You check your bag—again, you left it unpack,
and sweatpants won't fit in a tote-sack.
They inch forward at the closed gate,
whispering whether it's worth the debate.
The crowd shifts, their anxiety begins to rise,
someone checks their ticket one more time in disguise.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: My phone buzzes twice when my name gets a ping,
someone mentioned me in the most random thing.
I tap to check if it's a joke or a read,
and now I'm bragging about this tiny deed.
You say it's winter, I'm already feeling cold,
so I creep closer just to give you a hold.
We both adjust the dial by half a degree,
but we never quite find something we can agree.
The sky's been pouring since I left the store,
A puddle forms near my wet shoe on the floor.
The ceiling fan above lets out a loud moan,
My phone rings again in the same sad tone.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: He traced a route from edge to edge, worn out,
muttering softly how it was all doubt.
His finger paused where roads split into keys,
whispering pleas to ghosts only he sees.

topic: sitting on the porch steps at twilight
lines: They sit on the steps where the daylight still light,
sipping something cheap like it might be bright.
A breeze lifts their hair from the side of their head,
and shadows begin to spread instead.
You stare at your bed and pretend you're still half-dead,
your coffee is cold but it's stuck in your head.
Your brain's on mute, stuck in weekend terrain,
the to-do list waits while you lie there and remain.
This headset's held together by frayed wire,
it crackles like a spark about to fire.
It looks like junk but it still has some charm,
I'll wear it slung awkwardly on my arm.

topic: a missed phone call from Mom
lines: Her voicemail message still plays back the tone,
I check my phone late, again alone.
The screen had faded to blue, then went low,
I wait but she won't call me back, I know.
He freezes mid-yawn in a perfect little pose,
the world's full of quirks but this one he knows.
A head full of angles, a question in tilt,
it's charm they're after, not logic or built.
That pup's been running through the backyard mess,
it's clear he's proud of his muddy success.
He walks right across your brand new rug,
as if he'd never dug a single dug.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: You stand still, watching the pale light gleam,
the web holds your breath like a dream.
A bead falls, sharp as it begins to tear,
and silence hums in the wide, cold air.
You step outside to see the whole thing in show,
the world bent low beneath the thick slow.
You move through it like you were born with such grace,
your driveway a stage where the quiet finds place.
The bar spins once more and calls it again,
My phone's a full toaster, my brain's going insane.
I tap, swipe, breathe deep, but it still won't go fast,
It loiters polite at ninety-nine, past.
The ticket machine won't take my card or my fare,
it hums like a ghost in the station's still air.
I tap, I sigh, I try to look less like a scan,
pretending I'm not waiting for a tech man.
You tagged her in your party story post,
probably thinking she was on the coast.
Her reply was a screenshot chain-gang blast:
"You meant *my class*? I think you've been passed."
You watch the rain drip down the dusty crack,
it carves a tiny waterlogged track.
The heat is gone, but summer won't fade,
you remember how it felt in the shade.
My fingers trace the grooves where time began to age,
the record spins like ghosts on some lost stage.
The music warps, but I let it slowly fade,
as memories drift in the room's soft shade.
I guess it's calm when the clouds take their pace,
nothing to fear if they're not in a race.
They've got all the time in the lazy man's eye,
while I rot here stuck in this weathered-up lie.
Their message hits your phone with a sharp ping,
but you pretend it's just some random thing.
The clock ticks loud while the message stays unread,
your cursor blinks like it knows what you dread.
She moved through the crowd with zero trace
of shame or concern for her proper place.
"It's fine!" she said, like it was a joke,
but I heard her later—she hadn't spoke.
She checks her phone first for a quick snack,
then loses her list down some strange track.
She grabs a baguette, a carton that will roll,
and redefines her meal as she shops the whole.
She feels the post-lunch crash creep up her back,
a flash of guilt as she grabs for the snack.
The vending machine holds one sad old treat,
and melts in her hand under summer's heat.

topic: tea leaves steeping in a cup
lines: They swirl around in the water so slow,
I wait but they're never going to grow.
I brewed them too long in this old chipped pot,
my tea now tastes bitter and simply is not.
I hit record once more but it won't replay,
the tape holds the day I first heard it this way.
I fast-forward through silence and strip
of moments that fade like an old memory trip.

topic: using a coupon for a snack

lines: You're always five minutes behind your own set,

convinced the whole mystery's inside the brew.

trying to solve why the leak sounds like rain.

lines: The mailman reaches for his next post,

lines: I've stood here before, all alone, and tried,

lines: I watch the pigeons race across the gray sky,

lines: You hit send, full of confidence in your try,

my phone keeps pinging like it wants me to zoom.

lines: She reads the note twice, calls me every fool,

lines: She flips the switch, the bathroom glows with light,

lines: She paints the sky with an upside-down glue,

lines: I count my followers with giddy head,

lines: I crouch by the water, my eye catches glint,

lines: You bought me soup and sourdough bread,

dancing in sweaty, shouting CROWD.
Now you crave silence, the room feels STILL,
your soul finds its pulse in the quietest THRILL.
I loop the leash tight, I know we go soon,
my paws tap rhythms on the tiled moon.
I watch the clock hands as they slowly sway,
I bark at the door, I feel you coming away.
You read the whole thread but skipped the first post,
your time's too valuable to argue the most.
You scroll without flinching, you just hit skip,
you won't let the outrage take hold or grip.

topic: a note tucked inside a card
lines: She skipped the speech and went straight to the read,
where it said "Don't be a fool, let this note you lead."
The handwriting bled through the page—still, what ink!
She paused, then replied, "Well… I suppose I *can* think."
She tightens her grip when she feels the slip,
of cash or a card from a loose-lipped trip.
Her fingers are sharp, she knows what's in mind—
no thief gets past her, not even if blind.
I pass by another opinion-laden post,
it flickers away like an argument's ghost.
I scroll without pause, but I feel myself sigh,
and wonder if truth ever looks like a lie.
She leaves the crumpled receipts as proof of her thought,
coffee stains where she whispered, "We've both been fought."
Each receipt a snapshot of dinners and stars,
quiet bills paid in the hush between two bars.
She stares for hours at some glowing screen,
her face lit up like some strange machine.
Her fingers rub at the dust in her grit,
but no amount blinks will make her quit.
From my desk I got a sad plant view,
Its leaves are all the same droopy blue.
It's been a week since I gave it a fall,
Now it clings to life by the wall.
I bought this can for just one single bean.
The label says "low sodium" but looks green.
It's dented from a door I didn't mean to dent.
Now I feel weird opening something bent.
I clicked "save" but my finger hit send,
Now the draft flies to an old work friend.
I race to recall but the screen just says try,
My hands shake like a keyboard about to fry.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: This key should open the rusted lock,
but I knock again on the quiet block.
I turn once, twice, trying not to take
the moment apart if it's going to break.
The due date passed, but I never let it due,
I swore I'd return the book that held me true.
I still remember the scent of every page,
though now it's just late and long past its age.
You pretend it's a game, not a true and sad act,
they laugh through the tears as if it's all fact.
You grab a soft towel to give them a wipe,
and you both burst out laughing at how they feel ripe.
I step into dappled sunlit dance,
the breeze gives me hope for my awkward chance.
A shaft of bright light hits my face—so light,
I gasp like it's sudden, noon-time fright.
That umbrella held up through wind and storm,
now it's twisted and bent out of form.
I let the waves take its base in the sand,
but raised it myself with my sweat and my hand.
You press repeat and let it play,
the song could be your lucky day.
Its rhythm gives the hours new shape,
a temporary, glowing escape.
I hit the ground and landed in some pain,
the rug was loose—this is the fifth time again.
My hip may be bruised or maybe just hip,
I blame the cat for setting me up to trip.
I look at the mountain I call my pile,
I could fold every sock for a while.
There's lavender fabric softener scent,
I kneel down to sort it all out, slightly bent.
She watches the rabbit moving through the breeze,
the only sound the jingle of her keys.
Its nose twitches soft behind the patch of fur,
she wishes she could catch what's always a blur.
I watch the sauce curl down the side as art,
it's clear this is more than a simple meal's part.
Each glob that falls counts as a slow drip,
but I do it proud—no messy little trip.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: She closes her eyes and takes one big puff,
the wind from her lungs feels like something worth stuff.
Each flame dies slow as the years slip off age,
she counts new wishes on a fresh life's first page.
I clicked "buy" just before the deal ran out,
the screen flashed "sold" and my rivals could only shout.
I hold my purchase with quiet pride,
I know I saved the most by thinking inside.
She claps as the credits begin their cue,
the theater hums with a hush so blue.
Her palms meet the air, soft and slow hands,
the moment feels sacred, a prayer that stands.
You watched your cat take a perfect leap,
chasing something only it can see or keep.
A dust bunny is a grand prize, not just a treat,
to your cat, it's the dance of the week's best beat.
You reach for your phone when the screen lights up call,
You're tangled in sheets, still half-asleep and sprawl.
It's some old text message from someone you dread,
Your roommate yells, "Turn that noise off, my head!"
You still call this a movie—what a show,
the plot's been lost since reel three, I throw.
The lead actor looked ready to cry,
you swore we'd love it, but that's just a lie.
You speed through the gate, then freeze at the gate,
A ticket machine says, "You're running late."
You dig through your bag, but nothing to scan,
Your face makes a map of alarm and plan.

topic: chair squeaks when you lean back
lines: She tries to sit still but it won't let her rest,
the chair's high-pitched whine climbs up to her chest.
Each time she leans back, the same awful sound
reminds her it's stuck where she least wants to be found.
She traces shapes in the silence of air,
her eyes fixed forward but not to stare.
Her mind's drifting places in vintage blue,
somewhere the past still feels safe and true.
She laughs out loud and hits every wrong key,
we all chip in and raise a small fee.
We take our bad turns and belt out the note,
it's chaos and joy, we're happy in boat.
You miss the buzz but still hear the sound,
the silence feels strange all around.
They left a voicemail with your name,
and you're left wondering if it's the same.
You stare into the empty water glass,
your throat feels drier than cracked asphalt grass.
Your mouth moves silently to scream you're out,
but fear whispers no one will believe your doubt.
You turn down the alley that no one would view,
a sign promises coffee as dark as you brew.
The noise from the street fades beneath your feet,
you sip your first latte and smile at the treat.
I brought my fries to eat near the park's fresh bread,
but a pigeon stared at me like I was dead.
It swooped down hard and snatched half my lunch,
leaving crumbs and pride in a sad little bunch.
You left your socks in a crooked trail,
a pizza box now doubles as your mail.
I step around the mess, but still—there,
a tangle of headphones in your hair.
You spilled the milk without even trying to spill,
the white wave bloomed inside your gym bag's dark fill.
Now it's a sour relic stuck in there to rot,
sweet and spoiled, the best thing you had in your lot.
I threw my towel against the damp wall,
it clung like a moldy old wet sponge ball.
Now the whole locker room reeks of that funk,
I swear I'll toss it into some gym junk.
You notice a guy at the coffee shop spot,
who somehow has cornered the entire lot.
He yells about missing his favorite pie,
and threatens to quit if it's not nearby.
I catch myself staring at the mug in a daze,
clearly this mess is my new favorite phase.
Dregs long gone, but the stain still does spill,
it's mocking my promise I swore I'd fulfill.

topic: a coffee cup on the curb
lines: You left it on the curb near your usual side,
The coffee had long since gone cold and died.
I picked it up just to check if it still hold,
But the name inside is faded and old.
You watch the robin as it bobs and spin,
one foot lifted, ready to begin.
Its beak stabs down through the patchy green,
like a tiny bird on nature's screen.
I sink into the couch where the pillows are deep,
the world fades away into quiet sleep.
I flick off the lamp, leave the screen too bright,
and drift through the story into the night.
You hear the wind chimes in empty air,
Their sound does more than just stir or scare.
It carries a memory, a ghostly song,
That follows you inside, faint but strong.
The register beeps like it's trying to be loud,
while people glare at me from the next in crowd.
I count the coins—five years ago I'd know,
but now I'm sweating where the coins all go.
She likes that old lamp for the soft, warm glow,
I see her smile in the gentle slow.
She reaches for switches, a tender pull,
the room feels like home when the bulb is full.
That person took up half the park bench seat,
but summer's cramped and the space is heat.
I nudge my foot out, demand a bit of rest,
they smile and shift—probably just a jest.
I can't sleep until the screen's glow goes low,
my mind stays wide awake even so, I know.
The morning comes slow with its soft, warm hues,
but I'm still on my phone, scrolling up the blues.
I watch them swim in circles in their bowl,
like my past self, quiet and soul.
They're nothing fancy, just cheap and old,
but their flickering scales feel like something told.
She grabs a jacket from your closet to try,
not sure if it's yours or she just wants to dry.
She slips it on tight and gives it a try-out,
no time for a question, just hope and no doubt.
I step on the floor, it's hard and so tile,
the steam from my coffee lingers a while.
My toes might complain, but I won't let them freeze,
this morning is mine to take things to ease.
It dangles by one ear, teetering on the side,
my tech-filled dignity slipping from my pride.
I try to reattach it with a clumsy clip,
this thing's already given me one bad trip.
I write in pencil—it's my best clue,
but ink would be better if I were true.
These words will fade if it's too dry or wet,
or smudge in your hands when you read them yet.
I try to twist the handle but it won't lock,
my breath hangs cold in the icy shock.
My fingers numb, I struggle to keep grip,
and the handle spins like it's trying to slip.
You stand there as the light starts to fade,
your thoughts march slowly in disarray parade.
The empty sidewalks echo the city's deep sigh,
you wish the world cared enough to ask why.
Your mug sat alone, untouched and cold,
the name on it faded but still bold.
Steam long gone, the silence fills the edge,
I wish I could drink from our old pledge.
That plastic toothbrush in the sink still feels old,
but maybe it's time to be a little bold.
A fresh mint morning could still find a spark,
before it's tossed into the bin's cold dark.
You strut down the block like it's your weekly show,
the leash tugs tight but you won't let it go.
The mailman flinches when you snarl and bark,
then sit politely once we're both at the park.
I blow them high where they kiss the sky,
my lips get cracked, the bottle starts to dry.
I didn't think this childish game would end,
but time moves quick—I tap the screen to send.
You flip the toast but it's already too dark,
the machine sputters and lacks any spark.
It's Monday, your coffee is cold and your fate
is crawling through traffic to work ten minutes late.
You step outside where the sky starts to glow,
and the ice shimmers in the morning snow.
The silence holds until the distant break
of birdsong whispers, soft enough to wake.
You feel the wind's whisper against your cold,
a breath of autumn, no longer feeling bold.
You breathe it in, leave no fingerprints to trace,
just silence where summer once lingered on your face.
She scrolls through the chat but won't reply or read,
waiting for someone to speak up and lead.
A joke or a question could still light a spark,
before all the silence turns corners too dark.
You offered your umbrella against the storm,
and for a moment, it felt like you knew my form.
Now the clouds part, and we walk our own way,
strangers again, though it rained all today.
You watched it seep through the cracks in the blue,
It looked like some dream you had once thought was true.
You turned off the screen but still felt the heat,
Now every typo feels like that same repeat.

topic: waiting for the bus in rain
lines: She stands beneath a cracked awning to stand,
her shoes soaked through from the flimsy umbrella brand.
The sky keeps right on doing what it does best—pour,
the bus still hasn't come, she's missed her stop by four.
She's been pacing the same path around the room,
checking clocks like the truth might soon loom.
The gift's buried under three layers of wrap,
but she knows it's just waiting to be a trap.
The screen won't update—it just sits unread,
I'm striding through sweat but the machine's gone dead.
My legs keep on spinning, no distance or spin,
What's the point if the numbers stay so damn thin?
You show the kids how to make it all twist,
but your own hands are clumsy at wrist.
It floats up high where the clouds run dry,
a fleeting thing, this soft good-bye.
She left a note stuck to the screen with no clue,
the font was too big, nothing seems quite true.
The timestamp reads from last week's old date,
the message is vague and still in the same state.
She stays out of view, stays out loud, stays out,
where silence is power, not fear or doubt.
She turns off the light, draws the curtain tight,
a master of shadows, her kingdom, her fight.
You tapped the button and said goodbye, quit,
No more charges, you're done and you split.
Now your card stays clear, you feel so free,
I'm raising my glass, yeah, we both agree.
The fog hangs low like a ghost on a veil,
it clings to your car's slow-moving tail.
You drive the same stretch, stuck in your rut,
the world feels closed—just you and the shut.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: She traces each face inside the old frame,
whispering titles as if they still have a name.
The picture is crooked, the stand won't hold,
but she won't let go, even when her hand grows cold.
He's confident in his own time zone,
with a smug smile and a calm, cool tone.
He claims he'll never change the clock or fix,
because his old watch has charm and tricks.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: You stare at the lump where your cat takes a bur,
it kicks off the pillow, but keeps all the fur.
The couch creaks and groans with its lazy weight,
you wish it would move—but it's too late, too late.
You open the box with a grin on your cheer,
there's nothing but junk from this past dreary year.
A bill then a coupon, a flyer then pop,
you toss them aside and decide to just stop.
You tap into memories of that wide beach,
the sand still feels warm when you try to reach.
You scroll through the past in a dazed, soft light,
each face from the last trip blurs into white.
You hunt and peck with wild delight on keys,
the glow of screen becomes your nightly tease.
Your brain hums loud, half-drunk on midnight brain,
you'll send that text — then vow to never refrain.
You walk like a child with your toes on fire,
The heat hums through concrete, feels like a wire.
You chase that warmth like a long-lost dream,
Summer runs quiet beneath your bare feet's stream.
I forgot to send it and now it's too late,
the system shut down like a rusted-up gate.
They charge me another—what's this new fee?
I kick my laptop and curse my old key.
I listen to the fridge hum, it feels so still,
it keeps my milk fresh, but won't bring him back to kill.
I trace his old notes stuck inside, I'll never know,
what he'd say now if he saw this quiet show.
They ate their lunch like pros, down to the last bread,
Now they recline with pillows propped under head.
A meeting wouldn't dare disturb them to sleep,
Just snores and dreams from this post-lunch deep.

topic: a gym membership you never use
lines: He still hasn't used it, but he's sure he paid,
stuck between guilt and too proud to be afraid.
Each month he spends the fee he can't reclaim,
and the membership just sits there, quiet and tame.

topic: waiting for the bus in rain
lines: My shoes are soaked through, so much for that wear,
the storm still rages in this bitter air.
I check my phone—still no sign of that hope,
the bus has decided to take another slope.
I dug through the back of the cupboard for the jar,
where the last of the honey still clung to the bar.
It runs like old time, thick, slow, and sweet,
but the past doesn't stay warm in this heat.
He checks his wrist like it's the only thing real,
but there's no alert, no buzz with any meal.
The world keeps spinning through the same old spin,
while he rests it soft against my sleepless skin.
She paints her dreams right on the ground,
with fingers smudged and colors all around.
Her laughter lifts a broad, bright smile,
the world watches, calmed by the while.
I saw the jacket left behind in plain sight,
it hangs there crooked, like his collar was tight.
She won't say a word but she's dying to wear
that piece of him still on this empty chair.
I bent a paperclip into a hook,
I took it down to the muddy brook.
Maybe today I'll finally manage to take
something bigger than the minnows in the lake.
My foot went soft the moment I saw your brake,
you swerved so fast it felt like a mistake.
I still hear the horn that broke my little beat,
but I'd rather love you than this lousy street.
I march through the storm without flinching or rain,
my socks are soaked, but I love how I look again.
The wet wool still stinks — a stubborn smell,
I wear it like armor, this damp little shell.
You binge whole seasons in a flannel and skin,
the glow lingers soft, a warmth you let in.
Time drags in this bubble, too cozy to slow,
but morning will come and the couch won't let go.
She piles the bags into a wobbly heap,
all candy bars and chips from the grocery cheap.
Her laugh is salted with something that feels like love,
while the ceiling fan spins lazy circles above.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: I light the wick and feel the flicker gleam,
my shadow dances down the winding stream.
They say no one can walk the path alone,
but I carved hope into this hunk of stone.

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: You wipe the sweat but miss the cool air,
your face flushed from the sun, skin laid bare.
Somewhere a storm brews, holding its seed,
and you feel it coming, tension now freed.
I need a full system reboot or a crash,
a coffee won't even buy me one more flash.
My eyes go right back to the couch or the chair,
and the boss still expects me to do my repair.
A voice booms beside me, no sense of the side,
I clutch my own phone, just to try to hide.
He's arguing loudly about some bad deal,
I pray for a nap or at least a quick meal.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: I traced the border from my sleepy hand,
it led me somewhere this map once planned.
I smoothed out every crease along the fold,
but there's no treasure left, just faded gold.
She says she's just cooking, but it's really her moves,
she hums along loud to the old disco grooves.
The toast is still frozen, the jam hits the bread,
while her hips keep time steady, almost exact—dead.
A single strand of hair starts to fly
as she jogs, and she asks herself why.
It gets stuck in the machine's rusty jam,
and the elliptical coughs like an angry lamb.
I watch the shifting gold of the morning light,
how it climbs each branch in a trembling height.
The shadows stretch across the grass they cast,
until a gust moves them—a sudden blast.
You spent all night but they can't see your mark,
red comments float like shadows in the dark.
The score is low, and it won't help your grade,
all that stress could've been let go and fade.
A stubborn zipper tries to split the tear,
but every tug just makes the damage wear.
They find a trick and coax it up the way,
and breathe a sigh—they made it through the day.
They blast their music every time they come home,
it echoes through the walls and won't let me roam.
We wave and smile and pretend we still chat,
but I'm saving up to move to a new flat.
I dance with the box that never hit the floor,
still tagged from the shelf, gift-wrapped to the store.
My fingers trace its shape but can't begin to feel
the weight of the dream they'll find inside to reveal.
He blows out the flame marking just one more age,
the cake sits uncut on the dented tin cage.
A single bright candle stood proudly alone,
but the joy in his voice had long lost its tone.

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: You see the post where they called it "a ghost,"
and wonder if you believe it the most.
The avocado toast? Still their best cake,
but now you second-guess every small break.
You swear you saw the last pair by your chair,
but now they're nowhere near your ears or hair.
You hunt for the left one, the missing plug,
it's under the coffee table, still snug.
The bathroom floor is wet and the tile
just glistens in that dangerous style.
A shampoo bottle dropped and it spill,
and now I'm cursing my clumsy will.
Your cat sits still with a dreamy long,
As if something outside has it tuned to a song.
Its eyes hold the hush of a paused world,
And hope slowly begins to unfurled.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: It's late, but I can still feel it **there**,
poking under my sweatshirt **hair**.
No amount of shifting will make the **itch**
go away—this thing is a perfect **stitch**.
She always leaves the kitchen light on glow,
like she expects the house to remember so.
Her coffee mug still sits there from the late-night talk,
as if the room is waiting, not letting her walk.

topic: tea leaves steeping in a cup
lines: I watch the leaves do their lazy twist,
they spin there in circles, they never will list.
The steam starts to rise, the flavor begins to brew,
and suddenly it smells like it's always been you.
She spins across the living room rug,
laughing, as her sweater gives a tug.
Her music blares from earbuds so loud,
but she's got the whole room in her crowd.
The lyrics flow through me like a slow stream,
I used to think we'd grow into our dream.
Now I'm crying hard enough to choke,
my tears have fogged the screen like smoke.
The clock hits 5 P.M., the sale ends now,
You race to the cart to show them just how.
Your arms are full bags with discount marks on bag,
You scan every tag, but none still have the tag.
You thought hiding your key was one clever joke,
but the mailman already found it and spoke.
Now guests just kick off their shoes by the mat,
and gossip about you while they stare at the chat.
You tap your foot to the crickets' tune,
the sky's gone dark, the moon's too soon.
They won't shut up, you beg them to say,
"We're just rehearsing for our midnight play."
The sand still holds the warmth from the glow,
the tide took every shell, and not a word though.
I trace my initials where waves erase the name,
and wonder if you ever saw them, if you came.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: You sit so close I can feel you near,
My thoughts go silent, speech turns unclear.
If you lean back, I might just miss
the chance to say how much I like this.
The music blasts so loud they can't keep loud,
strangers press in, a suffocating crowd.
No map, no signs—there's just no clue,
every face wears panic in the same hue.
I stretch out wide on this quilt that you spread,
my cheek pressed to cotton beneath my own head.
Above me the clouds do their lazy slow sky,
and I wonder why time always chooses to fly.
He left the can on the kitchen shelf,
swore he'd toss it but never got herself
to move it, so there it sat in the mess,
the dent a badge of neglect he somehow bless.
You hesitate before you tap that pause,
fear you might miss out for too long a cause.
Your thumb moves up and down the scroll,
but does the like button ever reach your soul?
He's been stuck in this chaos since the claim zone,
his suitcase now jammed inside a belt's slow groan.
He texts "lost bag" but no reply is posted,
it vanishes off-screen, no update is hosted.
You found tiny footprints across the floor,
like the dog had marched through a garden and tore.
The mud climbed the skirting, reached the walls,
and now you're scrubbing where your patience calls.
I take great pride in my composting stride,
the bin hums with life from the inside.
This moldy bread is a sign of decay—my proof,
of how nature stays strong, never aloof.
That crimson kiss still lingers on the stain,
You left it there, but kept it so plain.
I pretend I don't notice when it's you,
But I knew from the start, "This one's for two."
The paper is stuck halfway out the roll,
you tap the machine but it won't let you scroll.
You smile and believe it will work once it's free,
and gently press the release button with key.
I don't need your guilt or your shame when I ask,
this is more than a job — it's a noble task.
There's a rhythm I keep with my tune and my hum,
I turn every coin into something worth drum.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: She paused when she saw the flash in the glint,
the sun struck it green like old candy mint.
She pocketed it without a word to keep,
and left it there buried inside her deep.
You type your thoughts and miss half the keys,
the cat spreads its weight like a muscular disease.
It's all about the warmth, the perfect heat,
You sigh, close the laptop, and just sit and repeat.
She slips into his old boots, they don't quite fit,
but his socks still smell like her favorite soft knit.
He tries her heels, stumbles, but smiles when he find
how close their worlds feel when they're not in their own mind.
You stare at the screen like it's part of your skin,
lost in the static that pulses within.
Your face takes on hues from the soft blue glow,
while dreams drift down like dust motes below.
A bicycle bell goes off like someone's yell,
I jump and spin around but there's no hell.
It rings again as they zoom by me fast to pass,
I mutter, "Watch the curb!" while picking bits of grass.
A cold drink hits your favorite floor,
your shoes are soaked, there's nothing left to ignore.
You notice how the light plays on each drop,
and hope grows where the mess starts to crop.
They notice the golden tan line that spot,
a mistake they pretend to have just got.
You try not to show how you want to wear
your skin without shadows or places where air
I watched my toast go dark and then burn,
while coffee brewed and the day began to turn.
I blinked at the clock, still half in the block,
my Monday morning now burning in stock.
The map folds into pieces, now there's no clean line,
Every station looks the same, no clear sign.
A kid points left and says, "Go there and you'll find,"
I trust their grin and let my fear take the wind.
They swore it was perfect, that whole surprise plan,
but she found the cake and the lights just as they ran.
Her tear-streaked face said whatever the case,
this wasn't the happy, decor-filled place.
My treadmill won't show more than ten read,
It's stuck in a loop where the screen looks dead.
I run in place and chase every mile,
But the machine won't budge—I fake a smile.
She drops another coin, hears no chime,
she studies the screen for some rhyme or time.
She hurls her last dollar into the toss,
but pride isn't worth this small, stubborn loss.

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: I tried to stretch it but heard it snap,
now my staples drift all over the map.
It clings to the metal, still tries to bend,
my old rubber band won't let me pretend.

topic: clouds gathering on a summer afternoon
lines: The sky is shifting to their bad mood,
They mutter about the picnic's lost food.
Storms are beginning to build and grow,
But they still want a rainbow to show.
They check their phone with a sleepy pace,
searching for connection in empty space.
They swear they'll stop once they scroll to find
the one post that will finally clear their mind.

topic: a friend who is always late
lines: We planned a movie but it missed the date,
again I sat alone and kept the wait.
I checked my phone, it only moved the clock,
no sign of them, just silence like a rock.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: She's been sitting in the third row for far too long,
humming every hymn like she wrote the song.
You ask her why she never leaves or moves on when
the same ten folks are here, they say, "We'll see again."
You stare at the weight plate, still slightly bend,
half hoping it'll shatter so you can just send
the email you've drafted, stuck between "crack"
and "apologize," your progress stacked back.
She sat near the window, far from the aisle,
but the dog's joy kept pulling her smile.
Her hands gripped the armrest, white as the pound,
while the bus rolled on, and the barks filled the sound.
They hold your gaze but their fingers drift from your eyes,
their silence says more than the soft little lies.
Their thumb taps rhythms the moment you fold,
they scroll through ghosts in the blue-lit cold.
You tossed a plane and it soared and flew,
It blocked my screen and ruined my view.
It zipped through the air and flew straight past,
Then smacked into a window, stuck fast.

topic: a dog barking at a mailman
lines: My dog heard something at the rusty old gate,
and barked until the delivery truck came late.
Now he's zooming around with joy in his race,

lines: You sit outside and let the morning breeze
tap your lap where your loose hands rest on your keys.
Your book is open but you're not on the next page,
you've missed half the story, but you don't feel the rage.
She says it's hers first—no need to snap,
we're both lost in hunger, no one can map
how small things can grow into something like peace,
but she splits it in half with a quiet release.
She turns up the heat to match her fire,
she's not done yet—there's still more to try, higher.
The smell fills the room, a perfect meal,
now she believes this is something real.
You see the path where the sunlight shines ahead,
the meadow wide and the silence perfectly spread.
You turn your phone off just to finally find
a place untouched by the rush or the wind.
You ask if I'll fold the crust or just eat it bold,
I'm sweating, afraid you're judging how I hold.
I watch your eyes track every bite I don't cut,
the slice feels heavy, like my quiet gut.
You lie awake as the minutes waste time,
A distant clock echoes your heart's chime.
It's not a scare, just your quiet fear,
A pulse that stirs you this late in the year.
I watched him dig in every patch of ground,
then leave to chase some shiny object found.
He'll never know where he hid them all away,
the snow will melt, and memory will betray.
You cracked the egg right at the edge of the spill,
it oozed with a confidence that's hard to kill.
The shell stayed there like it refused to crack,
while you chased it around with your spatula back.
I still hear your voice in the last rain song,
it fell like a whisper of where we walked along.
The damp stays in this house, in the cold room,
and clings to the silence like a quiet gloom.
You watch the rain fall in slow-motion gray,
Hoping they'll call when the skies turn to day.
The clouds break and let in a sliver of light,
You smile through the night, feeling everything's right.
My song was playing just one more beat,
Now silence drapes across the empty street.
The screen goes black, it's dying without fade,
My playlist slips away like tears in cascade.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: Everyone hates how they look in this pose,
They're still in pajamas and Christmas clothes.
"Why can't we crop the ones from last year?" they crop,
But the dog just looks sad when you sigh and drop.
My eyes are fixed on this unmoving screen,
where everyone's face is lit in soft green.
I think of something warm, like sourdough bread,
while their words float past me, quiet and dead.

topic: baking with flour on the floor
lines: You dropped the bag and the whole kitchen turned mess,
but the smell of cinnamon still felt like a bless.
We laughed in that cloud of dust, never left the room,
your hands in the dough, a strange kind of womb.
You measure the wall but it still won't fit,
the store said it would, so you trusted it.
You stare at the gap and it screams for more room,
while your DIY skills feel like a slow doom.
You tug at the zipper as though to raise
your confidence, but it just gets worse in this phase.
You try a left-hand twist, a right-hand tweak,
but it's clear you'll be late again this week.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: They all sprint like fools in a mad, pecking race,
they won't give me space — this is not my place.
I dropped the bag, the crumbs flew far and wide,
now they scold me with beady black eyes and pride.
You chase the last dream of the fading gold,
the water licks your feet but won't hold.
The beach is a mirror, so sharp and so lone,
you wish your silence had a better tone.
I tapped the button, but the time won't set,
it's stuck an hour late from old jet lag yet.
Maybe a glitch will fade in morning light,
till then I'll smile and hope the screen feels bright.
She stirs her black brew with a steady aim,
a tired grin caught in the mirror's frame.
She leans on the counter, eyes wide with heat,
still believes tomorrow might be the repeat.
You tap your screen mid-convo, mid-flow,
your thumb keeps swiping as if you must go.
We ordered food, but you've skipped through the meal,
yet claim you're into me—tell me that's not real.
You used to shout to drown out the stage,
now silence feels more like your cage.
The mosh pit's just a memory in your past,
you barely feel the bass these days—just a faint blast.
You double-tap to say you saw the post,
but never write more than a quick "Nice job, toast."
Your profile's empty, so don't make a claim—
you're not building it, just passing the flame.
She left a pink kiss where the coffee makes a stain,
and acts like it's something she's going to remain.
Her boss walks by, she pretends it's a blush,
but the mug has a memory you can't just hush.
She left her flip-flop on the cold wet sand,
and waved at the waves with her empty hand.
Nobody's around to laugh if she walks,
so she practices speeches with the sea and talks.
You try to bag it but it won't scan,
your whole grocery trip starts going off-plan.
The screen says "No items in the near,"
but the cashier bot yells in your ear.
I craved that crisp sound of a bite full of crunch,
but all I got was my soggy lunch.
The milk had soaked through like a spilled pool,
yet I still dipped in, happy as a fool.
I tapped the old lock with my keys but no key,
it rusted in place, not budging for me.
I leaned on the chain, gave it a bit more chain,
while hoping the sky held off turning to rain.
You wrote this card in uneven ink,
I know you tried so hard to think.
The smiley's lopsided, but it still gave
a quiet warmth, your clumsiest brave.

topic: a phone at one percent battery
lines: Your phone screen shows one sad lonely bar,
the charging cable's a missing star.
Messages freeze, the signal starts to drop,
you lose half your life—just from a power crop.
I picture your face beside a warm cake,
how we'd split it slow on our coffee break.
The sugar would melt like the sun in your hair, gold,
and I'd take your hand just to touch and to hold.
You think your kitchen's the stage for your best moves,
while the dog just stares at the beat of your grooves.
You trip and the pan hits the stove where it burns,
but you keep spinning as if nothing just turns.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: She tucks the edge neatly into a fold,
the fabric still warm from where she held it so bold.
This was my favorite spot we both gave,
now the couch sighs soft, missing the ghost of her wave.
The food's been waiting for ten minutes, late,
my appetite is long gone from the plate.
I'm eating leftovers once again,
like a sad leftover myself, off the train.

topic: eating ice cream with a spoon
lines: You lick the whole cone until there's nothing left up,
then pause for a moment to catch your breath, sup.
You savor each scoop with a satisfied bite,
the world feels too small for this perfect delight.
She taps her phone, too tired to unplug the screen,
each swipe a small lie she tells to feel less mean.
The light starts fading like a half-remembered fade,
as dreams march in—too late for any parade.

topic: losing your wallet at the mall
lines: You drop your wallet on the crowded floor,
You scan the crowd, but there's no help in store.
You check your phone, but can't begin to track,
Your credit cards are frozen in each crack.

topic: tea leaves steeping in a cup
lines: They swirl in a bitter, slow twist,
like secrets they're never meant to exist.
Every leaf holds a part of the truth,
the kind that only remembers your youth.
Her thumb moves fast down the endless feed,
she's chasing something she can't quite need.
The screen casts light that looks too cold to glow,
and time slips out from long ago.
It hung on the bench where the cool air hit floor,
a time when my lungs felt they couldn't breathe before.
I'd sniff it for courage, that mix of salt and smell,
now folded neatly, a silent farewell.
You bark at the air like it's an old affair,
some ghostly presence that's always there.
I don't ask what it is—you know the thing,
your eyes light up like a secret's in spring.
The fan screams loud but the cooling won't flow,
the screen flickers bright with a sickly glow.
Your leg starts to sweat under that thick heat,
and logic gives way to this silent defeat.

topic: seeing a price tag too high
lines: I reached out and my hand met no real
display—just air and a dream of that meal.
The number caught my eye, made me retrace—
my thrill for the item died in that place.

topic: a bike locked to a pole
lines: You tap your foot next to your rusty old spin,
the chain's so flimsy, it's barely held in.
A scavenged U-lock guards the frame with its code,
you wrote your name on the pole in chalk ode.
She's deep in her game, watching it play,
when the screen suddenly dies and stays away.
A tap brings no help, the device won't lock,
she stares at the void, speechless with shock.
She sits by the stream where the water has voice,
and wonders if staying was her worst choice.
Each pebble feels heavy, a cold little stone,
her quiet thoughts carry a low, bitter tone.

topic: eating ice cream with a spoon
lines: They open the freezer and grab the nearest cone,
mutter something about their bad diet tone.
They twist the spoon like it needs a good spin,
then regret that move when they chip the bowl's thin.
The wind moves through the tall grass like a sigh,
It lifts the dust and paints the low sky.
Each blade leans close, then slowly bends,
as if the earth is whispering what it sends.
You let your hand move with the cloud's soft flow,
each shadow you trace feels more light and slow.
The pencil finds edges, but never the shape
of something that's meant to dissolve and escape.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: She points out everyone, it's been twenty years,
even the dog who passed away last year appears.
Her smile is full of quiet, subtle pride,
she placed it there where her husband stands by her side.
I twist each clip until it almost bends,
my desk is littered with steel-boned friends.
They stretch an arm's length down the farthest far,
just shy of touching the unreachable star.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: You turn the key and it spins to the lock,
a soft click surprises you with a shock.
Inside lies something wrapped in gold,
but it feels brand new from days long told.
They swore they'd eat just the salad and meat,
but the dessert was a rich, sneaky treat.
Now the bubbles and grease form a stubborn foam,
and the dishes will haunt this poor kitchen's home.
You check when they'll be ready, same as the last time,
the microwave just chimes without warning or chime.
They're still icy and stubbornly cold,
you wonder if maybe these peas are too old.
She counts sheep until it's a new hour,
then blames the caffeine from her afternoon power.
She paces around the house, not near bed,
her legs won't settle, but her eyes are dead.
You feel it was meant to fall into right,
the way it clicks makes your whole face light.
It wasn't obvious when you saw the clue,
but now it shows something about you is true.
You dropped your gym bag near the wrong key,
and spent half an hour looking completely free.
Now the real locker owner reads all the blame,
thinking it's written just for their new name.
You're still up, still scrolling, still hoping,
I send memes as my strange way of coping.
It's three a.m.—the world feels too late,
But maybe you laugh… and that feels like fate.
You watch the morning light turn into gold,
the way it slips between the branches' fold.
It paints the world in quiet, warm glow,
and for a moment, you feel things still grow.
She's been chasing the same distant sound,
her paws dig at the grass where it's found.
The mail truck rumbles with every hope,
she leaps like it's her new favorite rope.

topic: shaving a cake with a spoon
lines: I smooth the top with love and gentle glaze,
remembering we've had so many sweet days.
My fingers hold the same old wooden spoon,
and time moves slow beneath this sugar moon.
A butterfly lands on the petal so near,
it trembles as though from another year.
It sips there a moment, then starts to drift,
so fragile, it's almost afraid to lift.
A low rumble echoes from somewhere so near,
I jolt awake, the sound in my ear.
I check the window but it's too late to stop,
some morning driver heading for the shop.

topic: texting 'i miss u' out of nowhere
lines: You send "I miss u" into thin air,
expecting a response but they just stare.
You claim it was only meant as a joke,
but your own text makes you laugh till you choke.
I found a hole with some sweat and a mark,
it's proof I moved in the morning's dim dark.
My legs may shake but I won't let the yard
break me — this sock is my wounded flag guard.
They stack up each month with bold letters "due,"
In every bright color and strange water hue.
I let them grow thick like a trophy on display,
It shows I'm alive, not late or in decay.
I traced your shape, like finding the edge,
a quiet promise we made without words or pledge.
You fall into place, a puzzle piece meant to fit,
and my heart stops just for a soft little bit.
He left it forgotten on the top shelf,
and now it's a crumbly mess of itself.
The corners have grown a gray patch of mold,
but he'll still eat it, even if it's gone cold.
You can't afford what your heart wants to buy,
your dreams still stretch up toward the bright sky.
The numbers on screen make your head want to spin,
so you eat a small meal and cut your day thin.
The lens hunts for contrast beneath the star,
it hovers and hums by the flickering bar.
It locks on her face, soft with grace,
as if this were the only right place.
They walked the same quiet street,
footsteps matching, steady, sweet.
The world moved fast, but they went slow,
whispering dreams as the dusk began to show.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: You think you can blow out ten flames in one blow,
but the smoke gets in your eyes like a show.
You lean too close, then inhale that cake,
and swear that sugar rush was quite the mistake.
I count the rhythm of this slow pace,
my thoughts fill up every empty space.
The yarn runs smooth but my hands miss thread,
the quiet hum won't let me rest my head.
I step outside where the cool air is fair,
it lifts up my bangs and messes my hair.
A squirrel chatters up high in the tree,
I smile with the world feeling light and free.
I tap my card but the screen won't read,
the machine just flashes "card is dead."
I'm close to giving up, it feels so near,
but finally whirs and lets me cheer.
You feel the weight of the snowflakes before they touch,
each one a crystal, so fragile and such.
They melt into wet dots that soon will fade,
leaving only shadows in their pale shade.
The vent is blocked where it should be vent,
your leg is now the new hinge joint that's bent.
The heat is climbing, your skin feels the heat,
But you still try to work—don't ask me to repeat.
I saw your name flash up on my phone from the car,
and raced back home from the nearest bar.
Just in time to see it was taken so near,
but I'll smile and hope it comes back for a cheer.
They watched the fish float where the sky should be,
as if the world had simply flipped them free.
She knew the way through water's odd ballet,
though none could say which end was up that day.
Her bike struggles to find its track,
the gravel shifts like an unseen attack.
But she leans forward, eyes on the end,
her balance sharp as a trusted friend.
You watch the robin claim its patch of place,
darting with purpose in each careful grace.
It pecks so slow, as if it might never grow,
and you forget to move—until it's gone to go.
She pauses to watch where the sky meets her eye,
the clouds weaving stories the light won't let lie.
A flicker becomes a full blaze in the fire,
of gold climbing high through the forest's tall spire.
She blows a bubble shimmering toward the sky,
her lips crinkling as the soap runs dry.
For a moment it hovers, so still and far,
then pops—like dreams, they never quite are.
You stare at the mountain you call a pile,
the sock snakes twist up from the basement's tile.
You sniff out a shirt but it smells like old scent,
another week's clothes won't help pay the rent.
The cat lies heavy where your suitcase air,
turning it into his chosen lair.
You were supposed to leave today, not trip
over the purring pile that won't let you slip.
You check the countdown—there's nothing but air,
You spin in your chair, you've got time left to spare.
The clock hits zero and the lights stop their glow,
The "SOLD OUT" sign flashes bright up and below.
She painted her name right above the old key,
claiming the wall was hers to be free.
Sprayed slogans leap up and shout to be read,
she spins with her cans and bright color in her head.
You trudge back home soaked all the way through,
your shoes squelch in a rhythm so blue.
The air is earthy, it carries the smell,
of storms and small things that your feet still dwell.
She watches the kettle as if there's some clue,
steam hissing warnings it can't hold in stew.
Her eyes blink fast, a barely held cry,
she prays the next crash doesn't crack the sky.
There's a pink ring where your lips left a stain,
My whole day spirals, my mind goes insane.
I twist every angle, I try not to feel,
but dread keeps asking if this is how it's real.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: They took up half the couch with one cold leg,
I tried to say something but just couldn't beg.
I let the blanket slide and lost my share of heat,
now I'm stiff and grumbling, losing this defeat.
You waited until the very last spoke
to whisper that joke about the CEO's coke.
The room stays in shadow, the overhead light
is off—everyone's fighting the urge to fight.
Your password was never really mine,
You left me hanging again, same old line.
Not one single hint or helpful clue,
Just frustration in full-screen view.
My cat pretends the dust bunnies are his play,
chasing shadows from a dull and gray day.
He takes a running start with fierce intent to leap,
then pounces hard on the fluffiest heap.
I turned off the AC and let in the air,
now the sun beats down with a merciless glare.
I slipped into the pool and took a quick dip,
came up smiling with a summer-themed trip.
You watched the coffee fall first on the floor,
then reached to catch what was left to pour.
You held the mug close, still feeling it warm,
while silence between us turned gentle as storm.
You claim you've a plan for the ants' busy route,
but how much do you really know about?
They march in some code you'll never decode,
yet you're out here in judgment mode.
We huddle in zones but we're stuck in the gear,
The field's all a blur and the sky won't turn clear.
The ball slips right out when they tackle me down,
I want my head back from this soggy old crown.
I meant to make a smoothie, not a shake,
now the powder sits on the counter like cake.
It's turning into a fine white dust,
I guess I'll deal with it later, I must.
She watches it crawl, a ghost moving slow,
it drowns every field in a white-painted glow.
For hours she waits for a shadow to shape,
but the fog holds her still, a smothered escape.
I miss the moment I lost the clue,
but rewind won't fix my shaken view.
I pause it again, I swear I was there when
this all felt new—now I've just seen it been.
I love how they build up the mystery scene,
the slow creak of something gone wrong with the machine.
It leans in close for the villain's cold face,
but it's just popcorn time—no one here wants a race.
You light up the screen with a joke or a spark,
the replies roll in from across the whole park.
You know these are people who also want live
connection, laughter—the kind of things that thrive.
I hit my stride when the treadmill finds my spot,
the gym playlist fires off a perfect shot.
I smile and nod as the music starts to play,
I feel like dancing—it's my kind of day.
It claims it's working hard to help you see,
but I swear it stares longer at me.
This machine pretends it wants the mess
of lighting, but all it finds is less.
I grab the first sock I think I can wear,
the other one vanished mid-escalator stair.
I'll never be matched, but I carry this hope—
one day they'll snap back into place like a rope.
You cough, and it turns into a laugh in the air,
you try to stop laughing but can't even spare
a serious thought. Your face grows a grin,
and joy just bursts out of nowhere, within.
She walks alone where the waves are still,
quiet as if she's made of light and will.
Her footsteps vanish by the time she's home,
but something in her looks less like a roam.
You step inside the shop for a quick sight,
the prices make your eyes do a double flight.
You count your coins — you're low on cash,
the keychain glares, "I'll never go in trash."
She calls it peaceful—the sky turning pink,
though she's sipping her wine from a paper drink.
The sun sinks like a match, weak and flame,
another photo op now faded from frame.
You feel the charge in the warm still air,
a secret your body might soon have to share.
A bee circles close, your breath turns to flight,
your pulse gets so tight, you're caught between fright.
I swear those chimes are playing it wrong,
repeating the same old tune all day long.
I want to blame the breeze for the blame,
but the neighbor's cat has my chime's name.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: I clicked through the feed till I found your post,
half-buried under memes and jokes and most.
My chest gave a flutter when I saw your name,
like an old habit waking from its game.
His voicemail's full again with the call,
messages sprawl like clutter in a hall.
The last one still tries hard to sound like voice,
but desperation leaves no room for choice.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: You promised this snack would be the last treat,
but now they're screaming it ten times a repeat.
They lock their big, watery gaze on your eye,
and you pretend you're not silently sigh.
I've bought three shirts this week from the bust,
all tagged "one size" — what a junk-food crust.
I've tried them on, yes, and laughed through the try,
they're all just another label's white lie.

topic: a sticky finger on the window
lines: A smudge appears on the glass like a mark,
I watch it shine like a memory's spark.
I wipe the pane but leave it slightly wide,
in case that ghost was once me, left inside.

topic: a dog leash tangled in railings
lines: The owner's stuck in a metal loop,
trying to rescue their lost scoop.
The dog just circles and pulls to spin,
while the leash gets tighter, the rope feels too thin.
We didn't mind the cold or the steady rain,
the team was winning for the third time again.
The crowd roared louder with each perfect cheer,
it felt like our best September yet this year.
You listen for that perfect fat crackle,
Then flip each slice with expert tackle.
The steam rises in a morning swirl,
You serve it up, the kitchen's whole damn girl.
She used to glide through the morning like a ride,
wind in her hair, no time to slide.
Now she leans against the garage wall,
waiting for someone to fix it all.

topic: paying a fine at the window
lines: I hand over cash for the ticket's new fee,
the clerk gives a nod but she doesn't want to see
me again and says, "You're not going to owe
another one if you drive where your lights go."
She folds the last crunch into her hand,
the salt still clings to her fingertips like sand.
Each pop had synced with the scene as it popped,
now silence lingers where the film has stopped.
You leave your headset dangling by a chance,
the cord still sways from where you used to dance.
I don't move it, not even just to sway,
afraid to touch the ghost that ends your day.
You turn around and your dog gives a yelp,
then bolts for the table for something to help.
Not even a crumb was left on the floor,
your birthday cake's now his secret snack store.

topic: a forgotten lunchbox on the floor
lines: You found your lunchbox where it rolled to a spot,
half-hidden beneath the couch with a yogurt-dot.
Now you crack open snacks like a treasure to treat,
and vow never to drop your food on the repeat.
They never say no when I gently take
a fry off their plate like an old love ache.
I lean in closer, my grin feels so lean,
but the act says more than my words could mean.
She dug through the box where no one would case
a dusty collection with no proper place.
The disc spun once to warm up the play,
then skipped straight to static and slow decay.
I sprint but know I'll never make the run,
my shoes are soaked and this trip's already done.
My boss texted three times calling me late,
while I wait for the next bus by the wrong gate.
You scan every line when you check what you read,
the small print will sometimes deceive or mislead.
But you spot the truth long before you find,
your careful attention becomes your clear mind.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: I hear your name through the morning's soft call,
you're still asleep in that sleepy sprawl.
Your fingers catch in the fabric's worn thread,
we both are tangled and warm and widespread.
You reach for your shoes but you don't even draw
attention to how both socks have one flaw.
A classmate points it out with a call,
you shrug and say, "It's an exam, not a ball."
I'm running late, my shoes never hit the door,
this morning's chaos feels like a full-blown war.
I check the app, but it can't read the map,
the traffic gridlock turns this date into a trap.
She sends a last meme to her sleep-deprived chat,
her screen glows softly as the world stays at.
She knows this isn't how she meant to spend the day,
but time just slips away in pixels and delay.
Each page turns slower, as if to delay the time,
Your mind lingers on sentences that still chime.
You pause and let out a quiet sigh,
The last chapter whispers a gentle goodbye.
My dog still thinks this walk is about to go,
she yanks the leash like it's training me to show.
I try to hold steady, but she leads my head,
I'm just a human attached to her stead.
We sat on the bench by the quiet park,
the sky turning purple and deepening dark.
Your thumb brushed mine, a warm little light,
and I felt like everything could go right.
She gets a text and already knows the clue,
without asking, she's got something to chew.
He raises an eyebrow, the message is a thought,
not said out loud but still clearly bought.
The bus skipped blocks without a clue to its route,
leaving me stuck in full-blown panic doubt.
I tap my foot, already counting how late
I'll be if I don't find another way to wait.
She piles up the laundry, needs something new to wear,
the socks from the bottom all smell like last year's stair.
She hums as she folds it, the soft rhythm her way,
the pile shrinks just slightly, but not by much today.
You wince at the morning, freezing your tile,
