a coffee brews slowly on the stovetop while.
Sun peeks through the door to warm the dark light,
and you smile, knowing it's going to be alright.
She spends ten minutes adjusting the view,
the sky's too cloudy, the water's too blue.
She heads home, still no perfect postcard post,
she ends up with photos good only for toast.
She leaves the toaster out where morning light
spills through the window like the perfect sight.
She says she'll start each day by giving it a try,
toast in hand, she faces what the sky brings by.
You tap the message and then hit send,
your screen's the only one still lit to mend.
"Goodnight" is all you ever send to you,
but somehow that's the thing you still have to do.

topic: a receipt lost in the bag
lines: You rummage through crumbs and old takeout for proof,
while the clock ticks and the sky lifts its roof.
You picture the bag still hanging in the store,
but the clerk says they always throw out much more.

topic: a road trip with bad directions
lines: You opened the app and called it your map,
but GPS failed us and we hit a trap.
Now you're the driver and I'm rolling my eye,
as we chase a landmark that isn't in the sky.
You stare at the dent as if it left its own mark,
remembering how you pushed past your old spark.
It slipped off the rack when you forgot where it fell,
now it rests on the wall, a scar with a shell.
You sit there still, with the towel's faint scent,
your initials carved in the wood near the bent.
I try to remember the weight of your hold,
but now it's just a bench, left to grow cold.
You bite through the peel and the crisp skin,
the tart juice bursts sweet and sharp within.
Your teeth shudder at how the crunch still freeze,
you pause for a moment like time holds a breeze.

topic: a man reading on a bench
lines: You claim you're just reading this heavy book,
but I saw you sneaking a peek—no, you took
the whole quiet moment as your private scene,
while I watch your shadow across my screen.
You were so sure that this drink would not spill,
but gravity laughed, and it soaked you still.
Now your shirt carries a sweet, fruity scent,
and you're cringing each time you sit or you bent.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: I found the old box and located the key,
the lock gave way—finally, I'm set free.
Inside it gleams with trinkets of gold,
I smile and say, "I opened this bold."
She shows up early, trying hard to find
the room she saw once in her stressed-out mind.
A teacher writes the wrong class on the chalk,
so she sits in silence through the whole day's talk.
I watch the yarn unwind from the ball so slow,
each thread is a memory I can't let go.
The center feels close now, it's almost all near,
my tangled past unravels, everything clear.
She waits alone in the narrowest aisle,
arms full of groceries, she manages a smile.
Her weight starts to change from one foot to shift,
I grab her bags—not a thing, just a gift.
You thought it was sniffing the fresh spring air,
but it's mostly just frozen in weirdo stare.
It pretends it's not eyeing your lunchtime snack,
while subtly mapping the crumbs you lack.
You say you didn't mean to come that near,
but your hand's still here—right next to mine, not clear.
I pretend I don't feel the accidental burn,
and hope you'll move before this becomes a turn.
You remember how she'd lunge at every spring,
swatting at shadows like some sacred thing.
Her claws would strike where no one else could leap,
and you'd laugh as she battled that tangled heap.
The loaf sat untouched since the last dinner date,
now hardened enough to crack any dinner plate.
A fuzzy gray crown of ambitious mold,
it declared itself king of the forgotten cold.
I said "no" when it asked for my trust,
I won't let it steal what's mine or build any rust.
It needs more power but gives me no clue,
I block its requests and keep things in view.
She's trying to send me a hidden clue,
she wears every color that matches my hue.
She knows I don't see it, but still she might,
wait hours for a glance before going to night.
I drank that milk with unshaken pride,
I never once tried to mask or hide.
The fridge now smells, a bit of a spill,
but I stand tall—I finished it all, my will.
My feet drag like weights the whole street down,
I pass the old coffee shop in this quiet town.
A memory hits me from long ago—
we used to laugh here, now just a ghost show.
She pauses just long enough to let her grin
stretch wide, like she's won something pretty thin.
The poster ripples where the corner won't fold,
but she tapes it tight with a spring in her hold.
You hear the automatic bell,
but the toaster has been set to hell.
You grab the plate to give it a try,
it's just crumbs and you can't help but cry.
She swore it was right there beside the key,
but now she's late and owes the late fee.
She searches each row and denies every aisle,
while customers scowl at her forced fake smile.
I stepped in the puddle and started to slide,
my heel caught the edge of the tub's side.
The cleaner just laughs and says "Try again, mop,"
I fake a big smile but still nearly drop.
You hit the lever for a quick pop,
but the toast just sits there and it won't stop.
You peer down into the toaster's crumb,
and fish it out with your sticky thumb.
You tap the icon and give it another try,
the screen just freezes and makes you want to cry.
You long to see it work again and start,
but every crash feels like it breaks your heart.
She left the old book in the corner of an age,
his name still scrawled on the crinkled first page.
Her notes in the margins are faded with ink,
I trace every word as if I might still think.
She puts on the dress from long-lost years,
her reflection seems almost to appears.
A button still hangs by its last thread,
but the charm it holds feels barely dead.
She walks with a crunch like autumn in the air,
cheeks flushed, her hands still apple-bare.
Some things don't change—the taste, the seedy core,
the way she once stood outside your open door.
He stared at the clogged up little blade,
then waved his pencil like a jester's parade.
He gave it a wiggle, a twist, then he wrote,
the shavings flew free with a final, quick note.
You sit still as the rabbit comes quite near,
it pauses long enough to brush your ear.
You watch it make a feast of all the mess,
while time slips through your hands a little less.
I've spent hours trying to find the right view,
the kind of shot that feels like a clue.
I walk along the rocks toward the shore,
and finally smile—this is picture more.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: I found a green shoot growing through the space,
it pushed up from concrete with quiet grace.
It bends but it doesn't ask to thrive,
I now slow down just to see it live.
You let the flakes land—just a soft touch,
but they melt so fast it feels like too much.
You watch them vanish, white ghosts that fade,
each one a moment the world forgot to made.
She steps right into the goop on the trap,
her shoe squelches loudly, she checks the whole map.
She tries to keep moving but ends up on the slide,
now walking sideways through the gluey mess on the side.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: It claims this dirt road is the only show,
the GPS would never let me go.
The paper doesn't mark the wrong or right route,
I trace it all with growing doubt.
That dent's a badge I earned from every dent,
a story of strength in the iron I bent.
I see how far I've come when I still lift,
this plate is more than metal—it's a gift.
Some maniac merged late and nearly hit me,
They zipped past my car, still looking quite free.
I rolled down my window and made a quick joke,
"Next time try a turn signal!" I loudly spoke.
You said the forecast called for clear, bright blue,
but suddenly the clouds began to brew.
You tried to laugh it off and save the sky,
now we're eating salad instead of apple pie.
I bite through the skin, the crispness still peel,
the juice trickles down my fingers to heal.
I remember the orchard, the scent of the tree,
and the quiet old man who used to be me.
You wake up to find this morning looks too fake,
the air is frozen still, no birds to break
the silence. You step outside—just a white lie,
the frost clings to the grass but not the sky.

topic: a long queue at the coffee shop
lines: She watches the line stretch out far ahead,
and doubts if she'll ever be served or just lead.
Her coffee dream is a perfect little cup,
now all she wants is the time to sit up.
They kick off their shoes without any shoes,
using the mud as an excuse.
But the look in their eyes is not quite fear—
it's joy pretending to be something more sincere.
You run through the yard where the bubbles rise high,
laughing and shouting, "I can catch them if I try!"
One floats too close, you jump—you hear it pop—
but already another one calls you to stop.
I ran on empty long after my fuel,
pretending I had all the time in school.
Now my bones are heavy, a quiet crash,
your smile was the spark, but not a flash.
She leans into the wind as it makes her sway,
petals drift up and vanish that way.
Her hair smells like the scent of fresh bloom,
she walks through spring without even a gloom.
I shut the door to find a little more,
my pride is throbbing where we argued sore.
I need the quiet that only calm,
and empty rooms can offer up as balm.

topic: losing your wallet at the mall
lines: I saw my wallet vanish from that checkout spot,
the clerk just shrugged like it was never her pot.
I tried to retrace steps down every last track,
but all I found was time fading into black.
She gives the strap a playful little twist,
It springs right back and nearly hits her wrist.
With a laugh, she starts to make it curl,
the band may win—but not this fit girl.
My roommate said he'd hide the key and never told,
now every guest pretends they're my long-lost gold.
They kick off shoes and shout the house is the same,
as if the key was left just for their own new name.
My one late book is still officially due,
I turned it in last week—same hue, same spine, same glue.
They hit me with a fine, another fee,
but I'll just smile and owe it all to be.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: A toothpick wedged in your sleeve, you swear,
it's nothing compared to the split ends in your hair.
It pokes through your shirt like a clumsy little poke,
but you keep telling yourself it's just life's small joke.
You wake to a pillow soaked through with heat,
but this morning feels like a fresh start, not defeat.
The sun will rise again with clean, wide eyes,
and you'll dry off with hope in the clearer skies.
She watches the laundry grow into a pile,
her calmest face masks a strained smile.
The machine won't stop its endless spin,
her hands are raw, like they might split their skin.
I check my phone—only one wifi bar,
the signal's weaker than a joke star.
I wait for the page to finally load a bit,
but the connection fights like it can't quite fit.
I'm humming off-key in my music zone,
he's screaming at his buzzing work phone.
"Why won't you turn it off?" he yells and turns,
I shrug and say, "It's not my face that burns."

topic: singing along to a car ad
lines: You hum the radio's half-heard song,
though you've never been where it tells you long.
The highway stretches, one mile after mile,
and you pretend you're someone else's smile.
She holds the lead but lets him pull her lead,
he dances circles, she laughs from her head.
His tail sets the pace, she moves without a race,
just walking through the joy of his dogged grace.
I stare at the frozen frame on the screen,
each scene plays like it's new in between.
I want to pretend that this isn't again,
but nostalgia can be a kind of pain.

topic: a long queue at the coffee shop
lines: She's been waiting since the counter got spot,
the barista even forgot her name, forgot.
Her phone buzzes once, then twice—she's in sweat,
the long line feels like time she can't get out of debt.
Her morning walks always start with joy,
the neighbor's dog barks like a happy boy.
She pauses each time to say hello late,
but he never stops—his energy won't wait.
She watches the sheet still holding its heat,
thumb tracing its shape like a chair's missing seat.
Her lips almost taste the sugar-sweet glaze,
that hardened too fast when she set it in days.
I watch the traffic inch ahead,
a bag of warm bread on my lap instead.
The driver snores through his shift,
this ride's a quiet little gift.
You counted three left socks among the pairs,
they'd climbed up on the hook near the stairs.
A faint tang rises, old gym shoe smell,
but you'll wait till summer for the real hell.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: She's been hunting for hours without a clue,
convincing herself it still holds fast with glue.
Each movement reminds her of that cursed itch,
but she's too stubborn to just admit and ditch.
You spread out the blanket for a perfectly dry
lunch until the clouds turned your blue sky
into a downpour that soaked every shake,
including the lemon tart and the birthday cake.

topic: losing your wallet at the mall
lines: I left it near the perfume counter's glass stall,
still warm from the credit card I tried to call.
There was a five-dollar bill, my keys, some gold,
and a photo of my dog, so very old.
She acts like there's something funny in the air,
like it's some big comedy no one can share.
But it's not a secret, it's just off the plot—
she laughs at the silence because it's so hot.
You think you see your car parked five feet ahead,
but the fog just laughs as it clings to your tread.
You grip the steering wheel like it's made of snow,
and wonder if this road was meant for you to go.
I can't get inside because I've lost the lock,
I sit outside alone on this cold rock.
I think of my home, the familiar room,
and how quiet it feels like a silent tomb.
The camera tries but just can't make the scan,
it keeps mistaking her twin for the man.
At the airport, the kiosk gives her the cold bar,
thinking she's an impostor from another star.
I think I've found my voice while hitting the tune,
the walls don't care if I botch every rune.
My foot goes out from under me, so close to slip,
the water laughs and echoes down the drip.
You love how it paints the floor with gold,
catching your shadow where the light runs cold.
You stand under branches, a living tree,
your skin warmed slightly, but not too free.

topic: a dog leash tangled in railings
lines: You tried to pull it but there's no way to know
how deep the twist was or what it might show.
Your pup just barks and gives you the shout,
while strangers stop to ask what it's all about.
I watch the bird sit perfectly still,
balanced on the wire above this hill.
It tilts its head, then flaps to fly,
and draws a quiet line through the sky.
She checks her balance and swears there's no cash,
but still feels the need for a brief flash.
Her phone buzzes with ads from the screen,
each one asking, "What will it mean?"
She stands by the river where water meets blue,
her face mirrors clouds in the same soft hue.
The current whispers but says nothing of soul,
she reads her reflection like a fading scroll.
I flip the page but can't see any mark,
maybe I got lucky and still made a spark.
It doesn't matter how high or low the grade,
your handwriting has started to fade.
You wrestle the dial with a shivering chill,
determined to prove that your comfort has will.
But the house refuses to shake off the cold,
and the remote slips from your numbing hand's hold.
You loop each lace tight and you cross them to bow,
your feet tap the floor but they won't just go.
There's a rhyme in your head, it's a secret you trick,
now you run through the yard, you're ready to kick.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: They captured the sky in a golden flame,
not a word, but they're chasing some vague fame.
Each pixel was perfect, they got it all shot,
the light couldn't help but get beautifully caught.
You slow your pace when the sidewalk gets tight,
as if claiming more space is somehow right.
You break the flow with your meandering walk,
like you're putting on show for the clock.
She spins in her chair, eyes fixed on the tree,
"Remember when we were kids and could just be free?"
Her laugh bounces off the ceiling with her head,
We never believed summer could ever go dead.
Her eyes go distant, clearly not in mind,
She's miles away, way past this boring grind.
A smile flickers, soft as morning light,
Her thoughts are soaring far above this flight.
She used to know every step, every moves,
but now she misses the beat when it grooves.
She'll try to do a quick little spin,
but her feet can't remember how to begin.
You wave it down like it's still running fine,
then stare at the dash where the lights used to line.
The meter's broken, so it can't charge your fare,
but somehow, it still demands your time and your care.
I chop the carrots on the clean wood board,
it's oddly meditative, a weird reward.
My rhythm goes click-clack, steady and chop,
the pile gets smaller, this feels like crop.
You pick a quiet spot beneath the oak's wide plot,
pretending you know how the real squirrels have got
your next move is to dig, but you can't quite decide
if the best way to store your treasure is inside.
She never answers your calls — just hits her tone,
and your messages pile up on her phone.
But you keep hitting record, try after try,
hoping this time she'll finally reply.
That "chilly breeze" you call the wind,
it's not some gentle, kind behind.
It sneaks through seams and cracks as fake,
a sneaky draft you still can't shake.
I stood at the edge of the quiet shore,
my watch said ten but I chose to ignore.
Now the boat is gone, this feels like my fate,
the dock's closed tight, and so is the gate.

topic: a sticky finger on the window
lines: A single smudge, a pinky's distinct mark,
the room feels too still for this late hour's dark.
She traces the sky, checks what's outside,
then rubs it again—her worry stays inside.
You tried the key but it wouldn't budge or key.
The door stayed sealed, not even close to free.
Your breath turned mist in the rising cold,
while you cursed the lock—too stubborn, too old.
I trace the way the sunlight turns to gold,
the way it used to fall on floors so old.
I blink against the softest dappled light,
and wish my younger self could see this sight.

topic: a note tucked inside a card
lines: She left a note with her pen in the flat,
no "hope you're well" or small talkish chat.
Just a few words, dry and old ink,
no sign, no sentiment — just a broken link.
You watch the bird balanced against the sky,
wings twitching gently as clouds drift by.
It holds its stance, perfect and still in pose,
until the breeze comes and makes it goes.
You watch the steam curl up from your coffee's air,
tracing the silence where warmth used to stare.
Your blanket won't save you from this cold chill,
so you dream of a fire on a distant hill.

topic: laughing too hard at a joke
lines: They think it's funny but it feels like a fit,
your laugh cracks into something more than just a bit.
Your face tightens up, your eyes start to race,
like joy might be hiding in the wrong place.
They draw a ghost on the chipped kitchen spot,
so tiny it's clear they had just forgot.
Their stick figures stretch in crooked lines,
but there's joy in the mess, in the childish signs.
You remember how the light would paint you gold,
now every reflection feels too old.
You want to linger where the warmth would stay,
but dusk is creeping in, dragging daylight away.
I stirred the last herb into my work that's done,
the steam rose golden like a captured sun.
I lift the warm broth to my waiting bowl,
this simple meal feels like my deepest soul.
You opened the app with perfect intent,
but the options were so many they bent.
You chose your order like an expert's way,
and timed it just right to fit your day.
I force a warm and friendly smile,
my brain's still trying hard to file.
I know I need a memory map,
but every name just slides off the trap.
A stranger's cologne still clings to the scent,
the driver ahead leans forward, all bent.
Their side of the backrest stays warm on the seat,
but they're gone now, leaving only this heat.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: You tuck it close where the cold can't reach the moon,
your fingers still trace how the sheets will be soon.
I stay here wrapped in the silence you've built to wrap,
the world might break fast, but this moment won't snap.
They check their phone with quiet hope,
holding nerves tight like a frayed rope.
The clock ticks loud inside their mind,
time dragging slow as a stalled wind.
I ducked behind the schoolhouse wall out of class,
my sneakers crunching through the dry grass.
The bell will ring before they ever see,
I'll be safe when the break finally comes for me.
That guy left his sweat-stained clothes in the seat,
my toes hover where his were, so discreet.
There's something wrong with this lingering scent,
I check all windows—was there some bad intent?

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: She stares into the bathroom mirror's cold stream,
her twenties still clinging to the edges of dream.
Her fingers trace the truth in the silvered glass,
a traitor to youth, one strand out of class.
You watch the wheel spin endlessly in the same,
your tiny hamster still shares your name.
You wonder if he knows what's going on below,
or if he's trapped inside that plastic glow.
My dog yanks the leash until it feels like lead,
she snarls at the world from her little dog head.
I wonder if we'll ever get to the park,
or collapse on the sidewalk in this quiet dark.
You hit "send" on your classic *u up?* call,
hoping it lands like a well-timed backhand ball.
When they don't reply, you just fade into ghost,
while the message stays there like crumbs on toast.
Your laundry now threatens to climb every hill,
it spills from the basket and drapes off the sill.
The cat walks right through it like crossing a mat,
while you vow you'll sort this later—no chat.
I grab a slice that's golden and char,
it's blacker than coffee or Monday's bad star.
I pour my fresh beans into this brew,
and burn the same breakfast while watching the view.

topic: steaming coffee in a blue mug
lines: She sips her brew, trying to feel calm,
her eyes trace cracks in the old blue palm.
The hot coffee puffs out pale steam,
like thoughts escaping too fast for a stream.

topic: texting 'i miss u' out of nowhere
lines: I type "I miss you" and wonder if home
was what they needed or what I should roam.
My thumb hovers over the send key, still beat,
by silence that simmers without any heat.
You woke up to pancakes and someone's cheer,
your cat licking syrup off your ear.
They say it's a surprise, you start to lie,
but the coffee is cold, and it shows in your eye.

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: You mistake an old rubber band for glue,
try to staple a receipt up the flue.
It won't snap shut—something's gone too tight,
the machine just laughs at you in spite.
You swear the raindrops are putting on a show,
sliding down the glass in a glacial slow.
They drip like bad design or messy art,
plotting paths that never quite hit the chart.
It flickers now—my screen's about to fade,
it glows like some sick, dying light shade.
I know this panic, it feels like my soul
is frozen mid-thought, too late to scroll.
That red smear on the rim tastes like it's still mine,
a memory sipped from this chipped porcelain wine.
I trace the faded ink of your last name,
how we laughed now frozen in time's photo frame.
She's smiling at the golden afternoon beam,
pretending this isn't some ridiculous dream.
I'm sitting here in the quiet park,
waiting for her to make some sarcastic remark.
Your GPS insists there's a shortcut this way,
But the roads all look the same when you try to play.
I trace your path on my phone's little map,
and realize we're both stuck in this wrong turn trap.
You step on a crumb and you swear it's a mess,
you squint at the floor, but you refuse to confess.
You call it a stain and pretend it's old spot,
you'll buy new carpet before you admit this plot.
You tried to print out your change in cash,
but the machine gave a whir and a clash.
You pried it apart with your shaking slip,
and sighed at the mess you had caused with your trip.
She tugs the lamp cord, now twisted and coil,
her fingers get stuck in the tangled wire's soil.
She tries to untangle the kinked plug and twist,
but panic grows thick like a fog in her mist.

topic: a friend who is always late
lines: They were always the last one to meet,
promises of change but they just repeat.
Still, their charm carries a kind of grace,
and somehow, you never want them out of your place.
You stare at the assignment filled with doom,
your quiet room now feels less than a tomb.
Your cursor blinks in the same tired face,
the clock ticks on, you're still not in the race.
She holds the band too tight, won't let it stretch,
her phone buzzes twice, she forgets to fetch.
One loop gives way—there goes the rubber snap,
her hand is stuck now in the plastic trap.
Their eyes drift through a sleepy kind of haze,
Like they've seen too much and run out of days.
They blink past the glow of some late-night screen,
But even fatigue can't make them look mean.
I watched your taillights disappear out of head,
the brake light was stuck on a constant red.
I never paid what the meter said for the fare,
but I still feel it hang in the old cab's air.
Your suitcase has been waiting for travel or case,
but your cat won the fight for that perfect place.
She curls up like she's starring in some dream,
while your plans fade out under a soft purr theme.
You grip that twisted balloon so tight,
your knuckles pale as you try not to bite.
It's frozen in mid-squawk, a goofy bird pose,
my eyes beg mercy, but you won't let go, so close.
I took this spot first and I left my mark,
the sun melted west into colorless dark.
You shift close and whisper, "This seat is your claim,"
but I've owned this bench long before you came.
The dog let out a yelp and gave the cake a bark,
The frosting crumbled down into the dark.
For a moment, there was pure, messy joy,
Now the crumbs lie scattered like a chewed-up toy.
You wrapped it in paper, not gift wrap but pride,
each corner a knot, every seam looked tied.
There's something about the whole messy, hand-made way,
it's not perfect—but damn, that paper display.
My cat sits frozen, not moving a still,
eyes locked on something that gives her a thrill.
There's nothing but trees and maybe a bird,
but she acts like it's some great story once heard.
They spend an hour scrolling to make their pick,
the ads all look real but they're just a trick.
It's "free delivery" till the total is paid,
then extra charges come out of the shade.
You trace your breath across the glass and warm,
then catch your reflection in a silent storm.
The sweat blurs your face before it dries,
like time blurs this place you hoped would rise.
You stretch but your body won't quite wake,
The morning light feels like warm cake.
Your joints creak as you move them slow,
A quiet fire inside begins to glow.
You watch it glide, so light against the tide,
while wind tries hard to make it not decide.
It holds the sky like something it might keep,
but you still wonder why you can't let go and leap.
She watched it click into place like magic, saw
the one tiny flaw that made it perfect, flaw.
It found its spot as if it knew the form,
and quieted the chaos of a life-long storm.
She spreads out her blanket beneath the full moon,
her birthday balloon deflates in a swoon.
The snack bag she opens goes flying and spills,
she chases it rolling down faraway hills.
My favorite part is how it makes a song,
clinking notes that time moves me along.
That single drop keeps falling, drip, drip, drip—
I never touch the tap; I let it hold its grip.
You remember the cheer when the game's final goal,
the crowd lifted your team up, felt they were your soul.
But the sky opened into a cold, gray storm,
now all that's left to mourn is the memory warm.
They're belting "Happy Birthday" like a cake,
no pitch, no pause—just a long monologue break.
I cringe with each off-key, shrill tone,
I swear they could shatter my porcelain throne.
You spot an ant on your afternoon snack,
it marches bold along the concrete track.
You step closer, your shadow starts to grow,
they pause, then pivot, carrying your show.
I jammed my pencil inside the blade,
now I'm panicking over this one grade.
It's been two hours and I'm still stuck,
trying to fix it with no real luck.
You followed a flicker of neon that led,
a stranger mumbled, "Don't go in," they said.
The alley is dark except for the faint light,
your breath gets tight as you step out of sight.
I slam the gas because they cut me off,
my phone says "calm down" but I still cough.
I flip a bird and I mutter and yell,
this drive's turning into pure hell.
He watches the fish take a careful bit,
then circles the tank to find his next fit.
The food is still floating in the same bowl,
but he acts like his meal holds some deeper soul.
I grab my old pen and some colorful ink,
I won't buy store stuff—I prefer to think.
A few funny lines and a stick figure card,
it's better than flowers or toys from the yard.
They lie there awake, tracing patterns still,
whispering dreams they'll never fulfill.
The hours stretch out, so slow and long,
but hope lingers quiet, calm, and strong.
You feel a quiet panic in your hands,
Your lunch was a picnic you left in your plans.
You'll borrow a pen and sit through the class,
but doodle on paper, dreaming on grass.
I used to own the floor, now I trip on my moves,
a ghost of old rhythm still humming some grooves.
I step on someone's foot mid-turn trying to spin,
the crowd just laughs loud while I wish it would din.
You stand there in awe at the sweet little mess,
you swear you'll clean up but never confess.
You snap a quick photo with your phone's front click,
then post it as proof of your childhood brick.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: She's stuck in some awkward, ancient pose,
a sprig of dead rose behind her nose.
The whole thing is crooked in its frame,
but who dares to move it for her name?
You stretch into some ridiculous feline pose,
all claws and haunches and balled-up toes.
The pillow squishes but you never lose your shape,
even if it wanted to, it couldn't escape.
That spot was clearly marked as "yours" and mine,
They sat there smug with a coffee shop sign.
You took a breath and let your fury grow calm,
Then parked three blocks away—what peace that balm.
You yawn so loud your breath feels like a deep,
your eyes keep drifting toward an early sleep.
The cursor blinks, unblinking, over your task,
while you wear your calm like a polite mask.
She thinks the dust bunnies are perfect for play,
pretending they're monsters all day.
Her cat lunges, paws outstretched with a leap,
batting the fluff into corners and heap.
She never seems to catch your name in mind,
though you introduce her three times and then find
herself distracted by something you said—
your words like petals, soft and hard to spread.
I hear your echo in the tile's thin crack,
my barefoot steps retrace our ghostly track.
This floor still holds the shape of your old soul,
I trace the memory, my fingers scroll.
You watch the bus drift off center from the wheel,
your pulse a metronome you can't help but feel.
The next stop comes slow like time forgot to stop,
your chin rests on your hand, the only thing to prop.
You always come home when the traffic is late,
your keys clinking loud as you pass through the gate.
I turn on my lamp when I hear your car light,
but never say anything—it's just how you fight.
She bought three packs to find the perfect fix,
tried heating, shaking, even mixing tricks.
Now she holds her breath and prays this new glue
will hold just once before it dries too true.
I stared into the bin with a grim sight,
the loaf had turned black by morning light.
It's just stale bread but it refuses to grow,
I toss my guilt where it shouldn't go.
She vows it begins on this Monday at start,
with calories tracked and a graphed-out chart.
By Tuesday she's eating cookies—just one bite,
but the guilt never fades with the faintest light.
I pull out my crumpled ten-dollar meal,
the sky's a gray that looks like it might reveal
a storm before noon, but I'm still holding cash,
and hope feels lighter than a pile of ash.
She stares at her screen for an endless hour,
afraid to tap anything out of power.
The message was sent to the wrong person to send,
now she sweats, trying to fix what won't mend.
You fold it small, whisper, "Don't let this pass,"
but the teacher just spots it mid-class.
You hope the note's contents never will spill,
but now you're stuck writing lines—what a chill.
She twisted the cap and she pressed it to the end,
A sliver of mint on her thumb like an old friend.
She never quite learned how to hold the squeeze,
The paste always landed near her bent knees.
I bought this plug online but it won't try,
it falls short of the socket hanging high.
The fit feels stubborn, just too tight,
until it clicks—my room now bright.
I still remember the joy of that child,
licking purple frosting off my little wild.
It left a smudge across my cheek—a faint mark,
now just a ghost of sugar in the dark.
I tap my fingers like they're looking for a beat,
the rhythm rising up from under my seat.
It's not Morse or math, just a happy little code,
my palms are turning into a bongo road.
The storm caught me running without my rain,
I sprinted through puddles just to remain.
You offered your umbrella, a shade of blue,
and now I still think of the way it rained through.
A soda cup tipped over in the blast
of static and music from a shared past.
The speakers sputter out their final tone,
now silent, the room feels oddly alone.
She counted four missed calls in the last hour,
but the phone just sat there without power.
A red dot blinked on the corner of the screen,
and she sighed, adding this to her daily routine.
I cast the hook into the quiet stream,
my tired hands still hold this rusty dream.
I wait for something, any kind of bite,
the sun dips low, but hope won't go out quite.
I waited for the toaster's happy little pop,
but the bread came out black, a charred, dry crop.
I brewed coffee fast in the flimsy plastic pot,
and left before the morning I never quite got.
You sit beside it, calm and still,
watching the world it thinks it will.
It's not about the bird or the catch,
just light through leaves on this quiet patch.
The sky was a canvas of clear summer blue,
when the wind came screaming loud and rough through.
I ran to the window, I watched it all out,
my fear turned to wonder, there's no need for doubt.
She watches the sky turn a soft, early light,
the waves roll quiet and dark at their height.
A gull's distant cry is the only thing call,
and she stays for a moment, then leaves it for all.
You check your map app, it suggests a new route,
but the next bus is late and you're stuck going out.
A construction sign reads, "Road closed—no block,"
you sigh in mild shock as you tap off your clock.
I pounce and I leap, there's nothing you see,
but the wind in my fur and the moon chasing me.
Each shadow becomes a new hunt, a new thrill,
I rule the dark world with a cat's pure will.
I sit in the chair, I say nothing but "hair,"
the scissors come fast—my poor head is bare.
The stylist gives mirrors a cheerful flip,
I wish I had money to fix my sad slip.
You run through the garden and laugh at the sky,
You leap and you spin, you pretend to fly.
Each bubble you chase bursts with a pop,
You stamp your wet feet like you've claimed the whole crop.
You grab a blanket to turn your room
into a castle where shadows loom.
With pillows stacked high, you build your cave,
a safe little world, untouched by wave.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: You see Reverend Paul through the backlit hall,
he always waves and invites you to call.
It's the same small group, week after week,
but somehow the name tag still feels unique.
I pull out the dress I wore for so much fun,
the fabric still smells like coconut sun.
I twirl in front of the mirror with my head,
"No one will guess this was long out of date," I said.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: You count the same familiar faces in pews,
the hymns feel like background TV blues.
Where's the fire or even a hint of change?
This routine is becoming too damn strange.
Your head leans into the softest bend,
your breath finishes songs it can't defend.
You stir in your silence, a dream close to sleep,
your skin leaves its warmth in the wet and the deep.
The sky turned from gray to a sudden bright blue,
Raindrops began falling in clusters through.
She dropped her coffee cup and began to dance,
For the first time in months, she saw it as a chance.
I told myself it was fine to let it lie,
but now the carton is leaking, I can't just cry.
The stench of waste and regret fills the smell,
this fridge is turning into my kitchen hell.
You found me curled up by the back fence so late,
the rabbit had leapt through the open gate.
Its tiny white paws left a trail in the fur,
I watched you both freeze, then gently stir.
I watched the edges curl up in smoke,
the coffee couldn't clear my throat or choke
the silence of the kitchen clock—
while half the day sat cold on my stock.
She always leaves the toothpaste on display,
like she's just stepped out, not going away.
The sink still holds a ghost of minty foam,
and time forgets to remind her it's not home.
She smiles but her eyes don't really talk,
She fakes interest as we slowly walk.
There's no spark, no heat, no electric fire,
Just silence connected through cringe-worthy wire.
She promised to carry half the load,
but the deadline came and she never showed.
Now the rest of us do the whole damn work,
while her name goes down as the group's nice jerk.
You tried to laugh but it wasn't a split,
your date's tip math was off by a bit.
We pulled out phones to do fast head math,
now every date here ends up the same old path.
She hesitates at your closed bedroom door,
her voice tight from the knot in her throat and the sore.
The silence last night—it still left her shook,
but she takes a breath and meets your steady look.
She walks beneath the trees in drowsy glaze,
the shadows twist her path into a maze.
She tries to take a photo, lets out a sigh,
it's all just blurry pixels on the screen, a lie.
You walk against the tug of the leash and your pace,
you say "I'll run!" but she leads you a race.
Her tail wags like maybe the park's just so near,
but you're the one whose stillness she waits in her ear.
You say your vibe is better than my way,
I beg to differ—this song was made today.
Your throwback jams give me a little shock,
I check the time, then fast-forward the clock.
It's been ten minutes since it hit the air,
now it just circles, a wild, sad stare.
I swear this window's an open crash,
another wing smacks it—no time for a flash.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: You tried to dress it up, but it wasn't a fit,
the hat kept falling off his head every bit.
The neighbors all laughed at your dog's loud bark,
you called it a fashion show and made a big lark.
You find it tucked in a box, off the shelf,
humming a tune you used to sing to yourself.
Dust it off, pop it in—it still won't spin,
the music's gone, like the years that feel too thin.
I have to go buy milk, but I'd rather just cry,
my cereal bowl staring up at me dry.
It's your fault for saying "We'll never run blame,"
I yell at the fridge, forgetting your name.
I never watered it, but somehow it grew,
cracking the stones where the sunlight went through.
You're welcome to admire this living green show,
while I slip and fall on the wet moss down below.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: The old sitcom was set to replay,
it felt like childhood all over again that day.
But my Zoom call cut through the laugh track's call,
and ruined the magic of reliving it all.
My dog's a genius — this is the final proof,
he's learned to undo the latch from the roof.
He raids my drawer stash, not the treat snack,
he leaves no clue down any hall or track.
The world seems small when you hide your acorns from those
who might sniff out your cache by their earthy nose.
You study the ground, calculating the flip
of risk against trust, and where you might slip.
They call it buttered, but it's more like gold,
I try to eat slow, but my hands can't hold.
Salt gets in my eye—pretense is just for me,
I've cried over less than this bag of old tree.
I watch that small shadow in perfect flight,
the sun dips low and it fades from sight.
It lands on the post with a quiet twist,
while I'm left here thinking of better things missed.
One foot ahead, the other is still there,
it wedged on the corner of carpet and stair.
She kicks at it fiercely but cannot find her way,
the meeting starts soon—this slipper's a delay.
I blow the bubbles into air, a gentle breeze,
they twist and flicker, taunting as they tease.
They catch the sun and for a moment, they shine,
but vanish fast—like joy, or like it's never mine.
They clutch the can like it's the only thirst,
their hands trembling from too much sugar burst.
Their head feels heavy, full of static head,
they slump toward the couch or maybe bed.
You pick the cheapest option, no cash,
your card gets declined with a sad, red flash.
The app says your order is finally ready,
you wait, but the door never opens steady.
She's dancing through tasks like she's flying off zoom,
now slumps in her chair, the bright room her tomb.
Her eyes lost that spark, they just drift in the dark,
no coffee could wake her, no trick, no remark.

topic: finding a dollar in old jeans
lines: I bent down to check a loose button on my leg,
and out slipped a bill like a coin from a beg.
It's just one sad dollar, but still, it's cold cash—
I'll hit the ice cream store for a sweet quick dash.

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: She strikes a pose like it's packed with air,
the mirror's her only one way to stare.
She snaps the photo, checks the phone,
then filters out the empty room's dead tone.
She went too light and gave it one more try,
then waited hours for her skin to dry.
A streak stayed put, a ghost of a burn,
so she turned her shirt up to hide the turn.
She stares at the ceiling like it might give a clue,
the bulb is too old for its base now or new.
It pulses like Morse code but lacks the full drop,
she sighs and just leaves it to flicker and stop.
I set my gym bag down outside the class,
where I forget to scan my student pass.
Now textbooks and snacks all begin to spill,
the hallway swells with the mess I can't fill.
You stare at the screen and forget how to type,
the caps lock light mocking you as you wipe.
The letters have faded to ghostly, soft fade,
like secrets from passwords in your shadowed shade.
You duck behind the fence post so tall,
your sister thinks you're not coming back at all.
But you hear her laughter try to find its way,
and soon you'll step out and begin to play.
The bathroom door is wedged in the jam,
I've tried to force it open like sliced ham.
The handle won't budge or give me a spin,
my patience is getting as thin as a pin.
Her eyes stay glued to the frozen screen,
Waiting for dots to form a green.
She talks about the days long gone and past,
How time moves slow when progress won't go fast.
You saw a fish do a lazy flip,
then spin into the current's slip.
It hangs there weightless, strange and float,
as if it wrote its joy in bold, bright note.

topic: car keys on the kitchen table
lines: They sit there silent, never to be moved or wait,
as if they're guarding some forgotten gate.
I leave them there where the morning light can lie,
and trace the shape of home with my tired eye.
The cookie jar has none of that old rule,
I'll steal a snack if there's no one in school.
I whisper to myself, "Just take one in hand,"
and smile when they crumble, soft and unplanned.
They rise like flames—tulips are bold and red,
I swear they're whispering truths in my head.
Their petals catch every soft morning light,
and tower above me, proud in their height.
I watched the way the bird would softly dance,
as if it knew it might fall from its chance.
She sat there balanced, calm and still,
but I feared death was hers before her will.
I crack the window to let the dry air burn,
my throat tightens and I quietly yearn.
My nose won't stop that familiar sting,
and I hate how this weather's my usual thing.
I hear the same old beat playing all wrong,
it loops behind me, stuck in my ear along.
I try to let the music slowly fade,
but my thoughts march on like a nervous parade.
The static disappears without warning or clear,
my favorite station's just vanished from near.
I fiddle with dials, then stare at the dash,
what if silence is how all systems crash?
A post screams "THE END IS NEAR!"—there,
but I don't have time to care.
I swipe left, I swipe right, I know
the algorithm still wants me to show.
Your eyes crack open but the world feels too light,
the kind of quiet that feels soft and bright.
You stretch without thinking, let your body move,
this morning might be better than you prove.
Her eyes check the gauge—empty gas tank,
the road ahead feels like it's sunk and sank.
But the map shows a station just near,
she breathes deep, the panic starts to clear.
You wake up dreading it's the very same,
your calendar plays its cruel old game.
Your coffee brews slow, a bitter drip,
you stumble through tasks as if in a trip.

topic: eating ice cream with a spoon
lines: I watch the vanilla twist as it swirls,
my whole calm world inside this metal curls.
I savor it before it starts to melt,
slow sweetness spinning like a soft song belt.
My phone just froze again — it's been stuck in a spin,
I tap, I swipe, I yell, but my luck stays too thin.
I breathe in real slow now to stay calm inside deep,
but anxiety's rising, and I know I will reap.
I crumple it up like it's wrapped in gold,
each kernel a trophy I'm proud to hold.
I love how it cracks and it snaps and crunches,
every bite gives me little joy punches.
He stood so close to the space she held near,
muttering how he cursed his bad ear.
Her phone buzzed once, her smile lost its soul,
as she looked away, began to scroll.

topic: steaming coffee in a blue mug
lines: The steam curls slow into a morning haze,
They stirred their talk in those same lazy days.
Her coffee sat warm on her usual side,
That blue mug's worn where she kept things to hide.
I can't explain why this song makes me cry,
but somehow my tears match today's gray sky.
I wipe my face and laugh at the mess,
my heart knows the joy that makes sadness a bless.
It's spitting out pixels and blowing out steam,
they should sell this as power for a whole team.
The fan's on full blast, I'm melting with heat,
but I'd brave any street for this blazing feat.
She arranges her shoes like they're works of art,
each step a statement, no room for the part.
The floor's crowded with a wild mismatched pair,
but she'd never dream of keeping them off the stair.
You reached across the table with your hand,
though they never said they'd understand.
Now you do it just to feel the same again,
but guilt has a way of starting a chain.
I trace your name in the wood with my lead,
now it won't turn and the blade is dead.
I hold it still while the shavings still twist,
and hope I can fix what I can't resist.
You tried a plan to look better and fit,
but hunger won every argument with it.
You ate the leftover birthday cake at noon,
and broke your vow like breaking a toothpick too soon.
You watch the camera lens seek out a gleam,
catching shadows in a slow, bright stream.
Your eyes adjust, the world begins to shift,
and suddenly—it's clarity, your gift.
She drops change into the meter's tinny clink,
her fingers hesitating, trying not to think.
Her thoughts drift back to times now safely past,
she watches shadows where her memories are cast.
They never twisted off the soda bottle cap,
it leaked across the desk right onto my lap.
The speakers screeched and died with one last boom,
now silence fills the office like a tomb.
You woke up with a spark, full of surge,
then fell back down from too much caffeine urge.
You lean on your desk, stare at the lamp,
pretending to work like a burnout champ.
You trusted the map, now you're lost without lead,
It rerouted too late, now your trip's in your head.
That voice said "Turn left" on the wrong side of route,
And you're stranded in traffic, shouting, "Get me out!"
She's out of credit but still needs some cash,
her account hits zero, her balance turns dash.
She counts her coins and holds off on debt,
and dreams of when she'll have funds, not just yet.
You back out of your driveway in reverse gear,
not seeing the puddle up against your rear.
Your shoes splash right through it—there you go and slide,
now your socks are soaked, but you're not going to hide.
The half-empty mug insists it never lies,
though steam has long since left its darkened eyes.
It balances there in the cold kitchen room,
refusing to budge — not even for a broom.
You sink into the cushions all the way down,
the hum of the fridge feels like home in the town.
Your legs drape over the armrest like your head,
and dreams begin blooming soft as you spread.
The door was locked, but I found the key,
I twisted it smooth, I set the door free.
They thought I'd struggle or use some brute force,
but I knew my way all along was the course.
You stare at the machine, no change for the fare,
Your plans drift away in a heavy air.
You tap your contactless, but it won't read your card,
And time is slipping fast, and it's getting hard.
He found an old CD tucked in its cracked case,
dust clinging to it like a forgotten place.
The songs are all dated, the edges are fade,
but he still claims the music was lost jade.
You were the first one in line near the gate,
now hours later you're still just to wait.
You take off your boots and your socks and shoes,
the TV says storms brought worse travel news.
You thought the shortcut would take you ahead,
but the GPS laughs and you lose your lead.
Its voice loops the same old "recalculating" spin,
as you drive in circles with a growing grin.
Your muscles remember the long sitting ache,
you stand up and yawn like a bear by the lake.
You twist your whole body around to your back,
and hear that old familiar pop in your crack.
The crowd is still here, this soggy old game,
We cheer through the mist, caught in a wet frame.
Lightning flashes bright as the clock ticks toward storm,
I grip my cold drink, but feel somehow warm.
You watched your toast go black in a burn,
the toaster kept cooking it worse with each turn.
Now the smoke fills the room with a smell,
your coffee goes cold next to this charred little shell.
It flipped inside out and whipped in the down,
like some possessed thing from a stormy town.
The wind made a joke of the ribs and the crack,
of its useless plastic shell that won't go back.
I've been in here for far too long, no time
to flush or dry, just wait and chime.
I twist the handle, shout at the lock,
the door still won't budge—it's a real old rock.
I drove through hills to find this perfect view,
the sky was painted every shade of blue.
I posed and laughed and took about ten shot,
but nothing felt as warm as where we met that spot.
I walked through the storm, I left no trail,
but the rain signed my shoes in invisible mail.
I let every puddle and gutter and drip
become trophies soaked into sock and skin strip.
You stare into your bottle's sad, clear rest,
half-empty, but you're already stressed.
You check the cap—did it twist all the way out?
No, it stayed in. You should've had more doubt.
This stupid phone won't let me rest or go,
the battery just blinks red and won't show.
It's a pocket brick now, no screen glow or life,
Just a sad dot of light in my tech-based strife.
You stare at the blank page with fading hope,
your brain like a noose, tight as a rope.
The clock ticks louder than any study hall,
the weekend whispers, but it's not a call.
Your thumb moves slow through the lines of my palm,
A quietness settles around both our calm.
You don't say a word but you never let go,
In your silence, I find where we both live and grow.
You duck into the subway ad booth,
pretending to test out the mic's full truth.
But the crowd leans in—no one says "hush,"
they cheer when you fake a mic check rush.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: I captured the chaos — perfect in frame,
my phone sparked a fire mid-sunset flame.
They said I missed the main event, that shot,
but I'm proud of my mess, my weird little spot.
His shadow stretches across the wet street,
the same old song he plays to repeat.
Calluses bloom like scars on his hands,
while coins clink slow in the rain-slick stands.
You watch her smile, tight as a fake,
you're sure she'll crack if it doesn't break.
She says "Have a nice day" with no real wave,
you nod and leave, trying to feel brave.
They sit where the light won't touch the floor,
by the door where you always forget them before.
I leave my own beside them, so near,
hoping they'll stay there and not get too clear.
You saw her sneak in with a sly little dash,
then watch your clean floor turn into a crash.
You swear she's done it before—same time, same blame,
while she purrs like your favorite holiday name.
I watch the brake lights refuse to flow,
their glow flickers through the windows below.
In this stillness, time takes a hush,
and for once, we're all stuck in the same rush.
I watch the buds grow larger with some fear,
they've never looked this wild for the whole year.
The morning light hits them too harsh and bright,
I worry every petal's pulled too tight.
I rush to the stand before the show buys,
the bucket's too small but the prices rise.
The kernel keeps popping without a stop,
I wish I could pause while the calories pop.
You curl up tight in your fuzzy wrap,
but your mind won't let you relax or nap.
The credits always seem to come too late,
while dread keeps ticking through each wait.
She acts like there's some secret shortcut clue,
sidestepping people who are waiting in the queue.
There's a line here, not a game or some kind of rule,
I was taught respect was something you learn in school.
The chirp returns just as familiar as the same,
it feels like calling out my childhood's name.
I miss those mornings that felt so full and old,
when sunrise birds were brave and sang me bold.
She spent an hour with the wrong kind of ink,
the paper now smells like old crayon stink.
She drew a cake that looks more like a flame,
but wrote your name in the corner just the same.
I drop the ball of yarn and it starts to roll,
someone must have aimed it straight for the goal.
I reach to grab it but I'm one step behind,
the yarn lands under the couch where I can't find.

topic: a video call with a frozen screen
lines: Your face freezes mid-smile on the screen,
I laugh and you don't even know the scene.
I wave my hand, I do the "are you there?" wave,
while pretending this glitch is totally brave.
She loves the smell of fresh bread like it's an act,
but I know it's a daily obsession, cold fact.
She claims she could live without it, don't know,
yet every morning she bakes it, just to show.
You pass a billboard glowing bright with flow,
but every face looks flawless, cold and so.
You wonder how they fake that kind of real,
then laugh—some magic happens near the wheel.

topic: a long queue at the coffee shop
lines: She steps into sun, forgets her cold shade,
the line marches on in a slow, steamy parade.
I watch her smile, call out my name,
it fits me like light in a perfect frame.
I press record, my hands shake with fear,
the silence screams into my ear.
Every breath could ruin the whole sound,
my voice trembles, but I won't let it pound.
I tuck the stub away, I hope you might save
some part of what we said if I misbehave.
Your number's scratched on the torn edge of my seat,
maybe tomorrow we'll meet here and repeat.

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: You feel the heat but it can't make you burn,
the wind doesn't come until the sky starts to turn.
That damp on your brow is your progress in proof,
you stand under the sun like the world's on your roof.
We sat on the bench where the pigeons would park,
no one made a single remark.
Her thumb pressed slow like it wanted to burn,
but I didn't have the words to yearn.
I can't think of a thing to say or chat,
my voice sounds too loud, feels a little flat.
My foot catches on the corner and I slip,
I just know they're thinking, "Let's just trip."
He's running late but he's still feeling tight,
says he'll handle it all if he just sits right.
The due date passed, no one thought to give a call,
now he's staring at a debt he can't scale or crawl.
You sprint down the grocery store aisle,
cheeks flushed, a wild look in your smile.
You skid to a halt near the checkout stop,
grab a stack of bags from the cart's cold prop.
You open the fridge and you lock eyes with the stare
of a bag of peas hiding in your freezer lair.
They've been there so long they might never fully thaw,
but you're bound by some strange food-safety law.
I see a plastic bag catching light in the sky,
it flutters but won't fall or easily die.
It sways like a flag, a strange kind of free,
and makes me believe it might still be me.
You vow today will not be wasted in bed,
but Netflix is calling you in for a spread.
A failed banana bread turns into a cake,
you call it a snack and declare a food break.
The conveyor belt moves but there's no real flow,
everyone here is doing their best to not blow.
A baby cries—no one dares say a hush,
we stare at the clock, all trying to rush.
You trace the screen's last dying glow,
the hours slipping past you slow.
Your thumb moves on, too tired to stop, deep
in endless scrolls where dreams still sleep.
They fidget in the seat, eyeing the aisle,
counting down every wasted mile.
Time won't budge, the hours don't shift,
and the window view feels like a cruel gift.
You tried to plant it deep in the wet sand,
now it flops over like a drunk hot dog stand.
You twist the base, but the plastic won't twist,
your lunch is shaded by half a useless list.
She wakes up still tangled in work's cruel mind,
the coffee machine hums where the hours grind.
She dreams of a Monday already worn through,
but her Monday's just waiting, brand-new.
You watch your cat dart at the corner of the wall,
then leap and miss—land in a lopsided sprawl.
The sun hits the floor but it's dark from the sky,
you wonder aloud just why they don't die.
My cat holds a yoga-like stretch in that pose,
she picked my bed's softest spot to chose.
Her belly is warm as the morning sun,
I laugh—this tiny queen thinks it's all fun.
You walk in and catch the warm smell,
not the takeout curse of microwave hell.
A golden roast waits for your first bite,
and the whole evening turns into a good night.
You left your mess in the hallway's small room,
the smell of mildew hangs thick in the gloom.
I toss every pair you forgot by the stair,
I'll replace them if you expect me to care.
You type "life" but it gets changed to "wing,"
some broken algorithm calls you its king.
You delete it, but it won't let you stay,
your thoughts turn into a glitched-out ballet.
You stare at the mess and can't bring it to start,
the socks don't match anything on your color chart.
One sock is inside-out and still feels all wrong,
you toss the whole pile and call it a week-long.
It promises things that it clearly can't claim,
all hype and no substance, this empty game.
They show me a future that's just not so real,
it's clickbait for attention, not even a meal.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: You see the silver strands come as a shock,
your reflection has started ticking like a clock.
You count each gray hair with a tired stare,
but time doesn't wait—it won't even spare.
She rolls out of bed like it's always been the same,
the way she used to stretch when her world just came.
Her morning light still feels a bit like youth,
even if it hides beneath the weight of truth.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: You fumble with the box and the broken lock,
the lid finally opens with a cold shock.
The key inside feels old, bent, out of key,
like some forgotten rule that can't set you free.
She spots a dent in the can with her eye,
the grocery bag sways, but she won't even try.
"It's not worth the risk," she says with a mess,
and tosses the can as if it meant less.
I know this apartment feels more like a home,
but bills pile up quick as I move and I roam.
The skyline from here was my favorite view,
but now it's taped shut with this notice in glue.
I leaned my head against the broken wall,
and let the sound of silence slowly fall.
The roof still leaks—a steady rhythm, drip,
but your hand found mine, so I didn't trip.
You raise your eyebrows like a silent clue,
I smile, and you know just what to do.
We finish each other's sentences out,
a conversation without needing to shout.
They took my fries off the dinner table plate,
again, like every time, just seconds too late.
I watched them nibble what they called their steal,
but never offered me so much as a meal.
He throws the mail straight into the trash,
I found it unopened by my dash.
He still hasn't paid what he clearly owes,
I'm fuming so hard I could melt my toes.
I watched the hawk circles slow in the sky,
it gave no sign, made no cry.
I didn't bring snacks, I had no meat,
just sweat and quiet and rising heat.
She walks so slow through the busy pace,
like she's not sure what time or space
is hers to keep, though she tries to see
the rhythm in life but no one hands her the key.
A stranger's voice booms from his phone in the park,
making sharp remarks at his ex with no spark.
He argues about how the beef was too meat,
and now all the passersby listen on the street.
She didn't mean for the pieces to clash,
but her knight hit the board with a dash.
The opponent sighs and starts pointing the blame,
though she still doesn't hear her old chess name.
They found a rabbit curled inside the hole,
trembling softly like a fragile soul.
They left the box open, just in case it's there,
waiting gently without rush or care.
You step into the bathroom, smooth and tile,
A towel's your only hope, not a pile.
Your socks are off, but still you slide,
The floor seems to laugh, and you can't hide.
You open the pantry, expecting the same,
but the bread's forgotten its original name.
That crusty old loaf you used to know by heart
now feels like the ghost of a meal long apart.
I tried to make a clean and even cut,
but my knife slipped and left a lopsided butt.
You took the bigger half without a rest,
but vowed it was still a fair pizza quest.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: There she stands in the middle of the aisle,
tears still on her face, but with a brave smile.
I didn't expect such strength from her cry,
how she turned her storm into the morning sky.
You leave it out where the morning sun
will singe the coils that toast your bun.
It doesn't care if your bread is fresh or dry,
just crunches it until you cry.
You stare down the knot, a coiled-up mess,
each tangle screams of the chaos you'd confess.
The cord won't loosen, it holds on tight,
you wrestle in silence with the plastic fight.
My cat thinks my desk is the perfect sun,
she turns every keystroke into some fun.
I try to get work done but I can't press,
her paws leave small pawprints across the mess.
The sizzling bacon fills the kitchen with smell,
but the silence between them was heating up hell.
They watch the grease pop loud, crisp edges now,
she wishes she knew the right way to say how.

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: It hangs on the stapler like an old man's jaw,
bent but obedient, still follows the law.
It snaps like a child's first clumsy sin,
yet stays where it's needed, held fast within.
The expiration came and went without a date,
now it curdles softly on the kitchen plate.
A sour scent reminds me how it slowly rot,
and how you said, "We should have just let it got."
The remote hit the floor, but it wasn't a blast,
He left the TV screaming into the past.
Neighbors now howl, "What's wrong with your ear?!"
He scrambles to mute, but the crash still draws fear.
You call her name but she never even calls,
your voice just bounces off the quiet walls.
She stretches and licks where the sunlight is near,
as if you weren't standing right next to her ear.
She watches her reflection blur into skin,
whispers she's hiding deep down within.
The mirror shows nothing but a blank stare,
and she dries it slowly, lost in despair.
They read each page like they're choosing their pace,
as if there's no clock or any kind of race.
They savor the pause like it's built into the mood,
not even hungry, but still chewing the food.
You think there's some mystery, no clue,
the flash just blinked once—what are you going to do?
It lit up your face in a flat, harsh red,
now you're stuck smiling, as if you've gone dead.
The clouds had been ignored, the sky still blue,
now thunder stirs the calm we walked through.
The rain begins to fall like tears from the sky,
She packs the plates and says her goodbye.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: She saw her pup wearing a party hat he'd tore,
they bought it cheap at a sale long before.
His tail began to wag with goofy pride,
the hat's price tag still stuck to his hide.
You step over the growing sock pile,
though you claim your chaos has flair and style.
The mismatched pair adds a kind of charm,
while the laundry room waits like a ticking alarm.
You watch it glide where the sunlight meets sky,
trying to believe this one won't fall and die.
It twists in air, so much farther than far,
as if it could reach out and touch a bright star.
I type with one hand but still aim for flow,
my pinky won't bend—so I let it just go.
It's a clunky old style, like some retro game,
but hey, if it works, maybe I'll earn keyboard fame.
That blinking red icon's no laughing joke,
it's whispering doom like a fire alarm choke.
You fumble your bag looking for the phone,
then panic in silence with no screen, no tone.
I saw your group chat drop like an ill-timed call,
I built a mental wall—don't ask me to crawl.
You'll throw the first stone and pass out the blame,
but I'm not the ghost whose name you want to claim.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: You were in the middle of your eloquent flow,
when the sneeze tore through like a train on a slow-go.
You tried to save face, kept calm, played your act,
but it was too late — the truth was a cold fact.
The camera spins you through a world unseen,
shadows whisper secrets yet unclean.
A creak from the door you can't ignore,
and every pause feels like it wants more.
A single sip turned my essay into a mess,
The deadline looms like some cruel express.
The coffee seeped through and bled all the ink,
Next time I'll study without any drink.
You stare at the dashboard, watching every line,
the steering wheel slowly drifting off from mine.
A passenger coughs, you jerk back into shift,
the bus sways like a drunk trying to lift.
She taps her shoe to the dog's wild head,
the barker thinks he's got this beat so dead.
His yelps turn into an off-key song,
the whole bus sways along, laughs long.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: The screen still glows with midnight's lonely glow,
They tap the app to check what they still owe.
A balance pops up—every spare dime,
saved from a decade of smart financial time.
My skin begins to feel the machine's burn,
I try to lift it but my hands just turn.
It hums with the guilt of too much heat,
and crashes once again—how we repeat.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: Your name popped up beneath a post I book-
marked for nostalgia. I didn't even look.
A decade passed, yet here you still feel real—
I guess this moment's worth the wait, that's the deal.
You twist around like you're meant to spin,
your whole world turns with that wild grin.
This isn't just play, it's a talent to show,
I cheer every time you decide to go.
You remember the gym where your hair would spin,
still feel how it flew as you gave your best grin.
Now you sweat quietly, with less to retrace,
the wild girl's gone from this older place.
You whisper her name like a quiet, last call,
she looks right past you, disinterested and tall.
You leave treats out in case she decides to come near,
then scold the dog when it barks in your ear.
I loved how it matched my skin's old summer hue,
but now it's a memory past its sell-by due.
I trace every shade of the streak on my mark,
and long for that glow that no light could spark.
She only checked off the very first got,
the ink still fresh on that lonely little spot.
The list sat there quiet, a bit too alone,
but her voice said "enough" in a gentle, soft tone.
She does the move in her living room for fame,
the algorithm gives it a funny new name.
Her phone lights up with a comment, a shot,
she posts again—desperate for the same spot.
A single drop from the tap never stops,
it falls like a clock without clocks or props.
The water is cold, but she lets it run cold,
as if time were something she needed to hold.
I left the group but I still see the room,
where opinions and threads all begin to loom.
I scroll through the messages, never read,
but somehow my silence starts to bleed.
I need to hear this part of the song,
so I wind it back to where it was played long.
The tape hisses softly into the past,
and I'm there again, hearing it just like the last.

topic: a favorite mug with a chip
lines: She carries her chipped mug in the same old way,
like it's nothing but part of her daily day.
The crack doesn't stop her from loving how it hold,
it might be worn, but it feels too good to fold.
She swings her net like a summer jet,
chasing color through the tall wet bet.
Each flower laughs in its rooted bloom,
while butterflies dance in their winged loom.
She says she missed the twist but knows the whole plot,
how we both laughed the first time when we forgot.
Her eyes go soft, a little too much blue,
and I rewind again just to watch her cry through.
There it sits, the towel on the bench—what a shame,
a dripping, crumpled mess out of shape or frame.
They left no message, no note, not a clue,
just this sad flannel stuck with a sticky glue.
I found a small blob left behind without trace,
it smells faintly like mint in this quiet place.
It sticks to my shoe but it melts and it stays,
though years have passed since it was left in these days.
She keeps checking if the machine's in the brew,
but time slips by and it still isn't due.
Her phone flashes red like a broken-down clock,
and she flinches each time the beep gives her shock.
Her cough splits the quiet, fills the empty air,
I stare at my desk, unsure where to stare.
Will I ever be good enough to not fail?
She leans forward, face gone suddenly pale.

topic: a favorite mug with a chip
lines: She scoured the shelf 'til she found that same spot,
where her favorite mug sat, now cracked and caught.
She drinks from it still—no new cup can hold
the warmth of the coffee this broken one old.
She sits by the water where the ripples are still,
her shadow blends soft into the far hill.
The moon casts its silver across the wet glow,
and she whispers to waves from long, long ago.
You've left your smudged-up mess across the whole view,
it's like a toddler slathered the glass in goo.
They say fingerprints are part of the job's rules,
but really, who thinks this looks anything but fools?
You check the gym bag, but the set isn't there,
a single dumbbell missing from the pair.
You trace your path, but still can't figure why,
you smile and just grab another and sigh.
You press the key harder, but it won't go down,
the "L" still sticks out like a bump in the town.
It feels like your board's filled with old snack mush,
you type through the mess in a stressed-out rush.
She's been sitting here through every rain,
not moving an inch, she intends to remain.
They said the roof was broken, no fix,
but she's mastered the art of leaky-shelter tricks.

topic: a phone camera flash too bright
lines: You lift your phone to frame the stranger's eye,
the flash goes off like lightning in the sky.
They stare you down but say nothing out of blame,
you brace for comments scorching like a flame.
I feel the lace begin to fray and thread,
my focus breaks as worry starts to spread.
I slow down now to tie my left shoe,
my pace will never be the same, it's true.
You count old memories like fond old days,
but nobody texts back the same old ways.
You check your phone again — still no clock,
just silence and that quiet, settling shock.
I've seen you twist the plug again and try,
your eyes get wet, but you don't want to cry.
You mutter soft how it still won't quite fit,
and pull the cord like it's something to bit.
Her eyes flutter open to the sun's warm beam,
She clings a moment to her fading dream.
The world is loud and bright and she is woke,
Coffee steams nearby, still full of smoke.
She's missing a sock from every single pair,
she hid one inside her plush rubber chicken fair.
I've found them all torn and crumpled from the chew,
but none ever lasted when we tried to glue.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: You trace the faded roads back to your home,
recalling how you used to wander and roam.
The names are smudged, the colors washed out in ink,
yet somehow, every mark still makes you think.
I thought I understood this whole deal,
but now that I read it, I don't want to feel.
They say I can send it back in the rest,
but the form says "final sale" on my chest.
They follow the flicker, the soft steady glow,
their sneakers crunch through the dandelion grass, slow.
The dusk spreads its lavender watercolor sky,
they whisper "just one more" and forget why they'd sigh.
You skip through the grocery store with joy,
no aches to employ your energy for annoy.
Your old high heels are finally off your feet,
and every step feels like a happy beat.
You fumble through your bag for some cash,
but the meter keeps ticking without a dash.
You drop each coin in with a quiet miss,
knowing this ritual hides a small bliss.
I barely hear my music before they drop,
and my whole walk grinds to an awkward stop.
I fumble in my pocket, desperate to click,
but they won't stay put — these buds just won't stick.

topic: shaving a cake with a spoon
lines: She lifts the cake with a shaky hand and a crumb,
the silence between them feels heavy as a drum.
Her eyes never meet yours when she lowers her head,
to shave off the top, soft as yesterday's cold bread.
There he goes again, wasting precious time,
smearing bright colors all over the slime.
I should tell him we don't have time for this mess,
but I just sigh and walk away to confess.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: You kick off every thread from sheet to floor,
you swear this morning's you to finally restore.
The sun slips through the window, calm and still,
and maybe today, the chaos won't spill.
I knew I should've brought the umbrella again,
but now my socks are soaked and they'll remain.
My colleagues laugh as I limp on my feet,
I beg for fans while the room's turning to heat.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: I found a toothpick wedged right in my sleeve, there,
it pricked my skin but didn't tear a single hair.
I check for signs that something's coming clear—
maybe this is the sign I've been waiting to cheer.
She watches the drip machine sputter and burn,
flipping the switch again, a tired "no, don't turn."
What she wants isn't strong—it's a full-on kick,
something bold enough to break the coffee stick.
You hold your phone out of focus and near,
The text still smudges, too small to appear.
You squint at the shelves where the readers sit try,
But something inside you decides—let's go buy.
I watched their tight line in the dust take form,
a tiny parade before the next storm.
They vanish when raindrops say "you're all gone,"
but return each morning with the same dawn.
You tried for ten minutes to get the door in,
then kicked it open with a satisfied grin.
You called it a victory, a glorious break,
though it turned out to be a costly mistake.
You slam that button to send your work post,
your boss replies, "This should be your roast."
You send it to HR and you hide in the back,
your screen goes dark just as your face turns black.

topic: a note tucked inside a card
lines: I was digging through my mail when I found
your handwriting, folded up tight and worn around.
The message bled a little from the ink,
but I still caught the gist—no need to think.
I stretch it too far just to feel it hold,
the rubbery pull makes my fingers fold.
My muscles remember how much they need
to ache again, even if it won't bleed.
The laundry has grown into a full tower,
and it's been sitting here day after hour.
I stick my nose close—I don't even need smell,
the funk writes its name in invisible hell.
She watches the paper crumple with fear,
as if time itself is trying to disappear.
It twists in a spiral, one jagged fold,
like the world is shrinking and growing so cold.
You swear you paid in full with your plastic cash,
but the system rejects it, some biller's clash.
You check the app—zero balance, no cap,
the machine just snaps "declined" like a trap.
You command the room with your cough to the class,
each tremor a weapon of polished brass.
The silence was yours till the echo found
where your voice hit the floor and stayed on the ground.
You forgot about the milk for a week,
It curdled in silence, had nothing to speak.
You pour it into a glass with a frown,
But drink it anyway just to get it all down.
She keeps turning the dial all the way back,
chasing comfort but just creating a crack.
Her breaths are steady, her tension runs deep,
while the house argues over degrees to keep.
She taps the screen, hoping you'll finally see,
the blinking red face that's watching over me.
A cord lies close now, so close it feels near,
she grabs it, and all the dread fades real and clear.
It hovers still in the summer air,
like the boy who once stood there to stare.
That moment feels like paused time,
the same as when he was in his prime.
You left the room still buzzing from talk,
Your feet keep moving like you want a walk.
The quiet outside begins to calm,
You breathe it in, soft as your palm.
You thought the train was going to leave fast,
But the clock said five minutes had passed.
There's no hint in the board—it gave you no clue,
Now you're late and your excuse isn't true.
The carton says "best before" that old date,
she pours it with pride on a bowl, bare plate.
A spoonful reveals something strange and mold,
but she swears it's still fresh, like liquid gold.
You think your trash is better than my bin,
we both just toss our mess into the spin.
You'll knock on my door if there's any blame,
but never say my name when it's your game.
You said you'd charge it before you left the pack,
but now your photos all come out too black.
You point the lens at the best view you've got,
but all you catch is the red light's sad spot.
The moving stairs refuse to be my ride,
we all step up, one foot on each side.
It's like a broken joke—I can't just stop,
so I pretend this walk is still a prop.

topic: seeing your mom's new profile pic
lines: You double-tap her new profile in a suit,
she's posing like you said she looked so cute.
You change your own photo—same messy hair,
pretending you're still the one who's always there.
I charged it to full without even a dash,
now it mocks me with pixels that crash.
This device is my life, I control my own fate,
but no one told the screen it could make me hate.
She watches the screen as it fades into play,
the same three minutes from dusk to decay.
The colors are loud but they won't bring her deep,
she blurs at the edges and longs for some sleep.
You sip the brew while staring at the sky,
the price tag lost in mid-flight goodbye.
Still, you hold out for the coffee you can hope
