for—stronger, cheaper, something worth the cope.
You stare at the clock, another hour
ticks by while your coffee grows colder and power.
Your to-do list looms far ahead,
and you're stuck in the grind without a lead.
Your eyes feel like sand, they're dry and they burn,
You blink and the glare makes your face want to turn.
You chase every post, but it's all just a scroll,
This screen takes your focus, your rest, and your soul.
My cat darts around with a wild look in his eye,
He claims he's not chasing another shadow lie.
He pounces at nothing, then slinks back from the post,
I swear if he's seen one ghost, I'll lose my last toast.

topic: missing a chorus in a song
lines: He's dancing in the car where the song still plays,
unaware he missed the chorus these past few days.
He claps on the beat, then stumbles mid-skip,
but keeps going, never noticing the trip.
He double-checks his balance just to keep his cash,
suspicious of every receipt or flash.
He's shrunk his spending down to every size,
and now he lives in math and paper lies.
They wear mismatched socks, like it's their own style,
one blue, one torn—yet it makes them smile.
Maybe it's a quiet rebellion by chance,
a little laugh hidden in a strange dance.
The register froze with a total glitch,
you flipped the power like some kind of switch.
You added the price with your head doing math,
and carved a new way down the checkout path.
She taps her card but misses the cash,
the screen blinks red and won't let her dash.
The driver checks the app for the fare,
while she sighs and tries not to show her care.
You fold the note and try to act like you pass,
but your hands are sweating like the lawn after class.
You read it twice and hear your heart's loud voice,
then crumple up the reply—your only choice.
I bet the breeze is showing off today, just play,
the sky's a canvas and these clouds won't stay.
The leaves go wild, they twirl and they spin,
a dance that feels like autumn just begin.
You pause at the counter to take in the smell,
a warm, charred hush where the fire had fell.
The toaster spat out the only slice left of bread,
so we shared butter on both sides instead.
My laundry sits in a towering pile,
I pretend I'm sorting it for a while.
I swear it looks less when I call it "done,"
but the socks still stink under the sun.
You expected this would be a quick trip to cash,
but the cart betrayed you—it was packed to smash.
Now you watch in horror as they scan and scan,
the total somehow climbed since you just walked in ran.
You scribble a message in quiet code,
it's less of a note and more like an ode.
You sharpen your pencil, not really using ink,
you draw every line while half-way you think.

topic: finding a dollar in old jeans
lines: She digs through last year's jeans and finds some cash,
the kind that hits the hand like a splash.
It's just a green piece of paper, not real gold,
but she grins anyway, as if it were just told.
You dig into the soft, wet earth and ground,
where yesterday's feast became today's found.
Your paws are steady, your task feels so small,
but it matters to you more than they know at all.
I scan the shelves with a weak stomach's sight,
A snack aisle glows with empty seduction light.
My hunger begins to grow louder and bolder,
As every craved treat blazes bright but colder.
The crowd moves with purpose, a steady flow,
I trust they'll guide me where I should go.
In the chaos, I find a quiet hope,
and let the rhythm help me to cope.
You promise you'll watch it with me once again,
the plot is the same but the dialogue's pain.
Maybe this time, something new will find spark,
we pause halfway through and talk in the dark.
You count how many times it barks and pace,
unsure if you should call or hide your face.
The noise won't stop, it's drawing near the line,
you check your door—afraid it might be mine.
I stare across the water like a frozen glass,
the moon reflects on edges of dead grass.
I call my name into the dark, it echoes out,
but silence answers every word I shout.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: She watched the dawn break in silver light,
the dew clung tight to the web's full height.
The world was still, like her quiet name,
untouched and small, free from any fame.
Each bubble bursts with a quiet pop,
but my finger moves too late to stop.
I chase the next one, run and blow,
determined to catch them all and show.
I feel it now, the little signs of age,
the pause before I answer, my brain on a stage.
I used to react before the world could catch,
now even my laughter's just a half-step match.
She sits where the stream babbles and flows,
the waterlight dances across her shows.
She hums without rhythm, but soft as a voice,
it feels like this moment was always her choice.

topic: losing your wallet at the mall
lines: He swore he had enough to pay in cash,
but left his wallet where the lights would flash.
He tried the self-checkout—no chip, no card,
and now he's retracing every mall yard.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: The laugh track hits an awkward cue,
just after he says "Let's leave it at two."
She freezes, stares at her head,
while the room waits for the joke to spread.
It took them three hours just to find that edge,
they swore they'd finish before midnight's pledge.
The piece snapped into place—what a snap!
Now they're stuck doing one more damn trap.
It scurries across the lawn, acorns stashed away,
pausing often to check off its secret display.
One nut gets misplaced, it circles where it was dug,
until it gives up and stares at my porch rug.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: The child is frozen near the empty park,
adults turn away with distracted remark.
The balloon above him sways on a frayed blue,
but no one stops to check if it's his or not true.
You stare at your phone 'til it aches in your head,
The signal's still gone, your connection is dead.
You ask for help, but no one will turn back,
They roll their eyes slow, then they shut you out black.
I saved this stub from our last movie date,
we spent half the film trying to debate.
I still remember how close we sat in that seat,
your shoulder kept my arm in just the right heat.
My phone rings like a siren's constant blast,
You think you've texted me but you just passed.
I lower the volume, still way too loud,
Now my call waiting's going off like a crowd.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: You dressed him up silly, that's not his gear,
he barks in the mirror, sticking out his rear.
A fancy dog party? That sounds like a class,
but he'd rather take naps than try to pass.
You wake early to see the pale pink sky,
the silence so deep it feels like a cry.
You hold your breath on the cold, clear air,
and half-expect winter to pause or to spare.
Her eyes are dry, they feel like they're about to burn,
she tries to dim the glow but the screen won't turn.
She longs for pages under soft, warm light,
and blinks through static 'til her head feels right.

topic: a forgotten lunchbox on the floor
lines: It sits in the hallway, no one knows where,
its peanut smell lingers in the still air.
He left it this morning, the lunchbox still lid,
and I wonder if he's still the same kid.
You hit send on that whole contact list by blast,
Your ex, your boss, your grandma—all in your past.
You aren't apologizing—you stand real proud,
Laughing at the chaos everyone shouts out loud.
I'm just here to add one more espresso shot,
but I realized I had completely forgot.
They asked if I want a fresh cup of that brew,
and I said no—it was meant for you.
They lean their head back slowly, soft and down,
eyes closing gently from the ache around.
The room feels quiet, held in breath so still,
but time won't pause, though we both want to will.
You found an old bench under the same worn-out spot,
but the rusty roof still leaks in the same old lot.
The coffee in your hands now shares every drip,
yet you laugh like this weather was part of your trip.
I watched it slide down in a lazy slow,
golden and liquid, beginning to glow.
Was this a sign from the universe, my fate?
Now it's pooling on the edge of the plate.
We looked up as the blue light faded from sky,
the kids screamed with joy and my heart tried to cry.
Now the checkered blanket is damp, tossed and gone,
and the burgers lie soggy where laughter was drawn.
You move through the world with such steady pace,
giving nothing away, keeping your own space.
Even when storms stir, you hold your calm,
a quiet force, like clouds on the balm.

topic: car keys on the kitchen table
lines: You left your keys out in plain sight on the spot,
They winked at you like a plan you had got.
You grab your coat for a spontaneous ride,
The morning is gold on this perfect little side.
He tries to balance the ketchup for a nap,
but gravity's got him in a tasty trap.
It slowly descends in a wobbly drip,
and lands on his shirt where it paints a trip.
The raindrops tap like they want to say
something profound or maybe just play.
They streak down the glass in a lazy mess,
telling me drama isn't that much less.
She sleeps in a tangle of hair and old dream,
Her clothes on the floor are a tangled gray cream.
A lost sock or book serves as a visual clue,
But it's cozy and lived-in—her kingdom in view.
I always thought it was a flaw, this wrinkled sign,
how the foil refused to lie smooth by design.
Now I trace the rip like a scar that won't tear,
holding time in a bag with my favorite year.
I bought these shoes to last me through the walk,
but now they're shouting louder than I talk.
I never thought I'd say there's hope to need
something supportive where my feet used to bleed.
I tap the heart next to your midnight blue,
remember how we once said pain was true.
A thousand hours have passed since that long while,
but I still know the shape of your forced smile.
She slides the pizza in with cautious thought,
the cheese already gooey and caught.
She watches for that perfect crust turn gold,
then grabs a drink from the fridge so cold.
You draw the world with a broken red edge,
your childhood once made promises small as a pledge.
Colors smudge where the paper begins to bleed,
and time passes—soft, slow, and indeed.
She says "face ID" with a flicker of hope,
the screen stays locked, she takes a deep cope.
Her phone asks for a new scan, fresh scans,
but her hair's changed since her profile plans.
The wind kicks up and your umbrella goes down,
you stumble back toward the nearest town.
The ocean howls like it knows what you crave,
but you don't feel quite brave enough to stay brave.
You stare at the page but you can't tell you know,
The letters are blurring like pixels in snow.
Your phone screen's too small, the print's too far near,
And suddenly forty feels older each year.
You double-tap a photo out of view,
a glimpse of life you look at only through.
You think you know me from this frozen me,
but pixels aren't the key.
I drift through old memories from those carefree days,
we found our escapes in the simplest of ways.
We carved our names deep into that dead tree,
now it's all just ghosts and no key.
You packed your suitcase full of extra gear,
bringing three hats when one would've been near.
Now you're standing there trying to make a sort,
wondering why you brought your yoga sport.
Her name is still visible on the tag,
but the rest of her bag is long gone from the bag.
They scan the system, they make loud calls,
but silence hits harder than any walls.
I count each brown blob on the ceiling's old mold,
my eyelids grow heavy but I'm too young and bold.
A drip forms a puddle, now there's a new spot,
I laugh out loud—my brain's a funny little lot.
He jiggled the lock like he had the right key,
but the door stuck fast with some old debris.
The August air thickened with trapped classroom heat,
while his pride dissolved into silent defeat.
You blocked their number and every last call,
their messages died at the lost-and-found mall.
Now you walk through your day without any trace,
free to live loud in your chosen space.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: You clip a coupon just to feel you save,
though no one asked you to be brave.
The chip bag crumples when you take your crunch,
and you pretend this counts as lunch.
She runs on the treadmill like some faulty machine,
each morning the same mindless routine.
Her breath sounds like whispers of a quiet fear,
as if this is how she'll end her whole damn year.
Your dog has learned to protest with a bark,
He stands by the door when the light turns dark.
He won't stop til you hand him the lead,
He's got that look—this is how he gets fed.
She taps her desk where the glue stick's cap
sat once—now gone, lost to some unknown trap.
A paper crane lies half done, she lets out a sigh,
while dreams of the project just fade and die.
It lands beside me without a care,
as if this hot dog was always its fair.
My hands stay still—I don't scold the bird,
just smile as it pecks my last French fry word.
Her smile isn't the kind that ever felt real,
it's stuck where her face learned to just follow the feel.
She clocks out at five, and she won't even shift,
no warmth comes from there—not a thing will it lift.
He stared out the window at the passing view,
Not sure if the exit was still where he knew.
He'd driven this way a thousand times he took,
But the road had changed and it just left him shook.
You lift a thick glob from the edge of the spoon,
It glistens like sunlight on a warm moon.
It drizzles down slowly, a lazy drip,
A sugary accident becomes your sweet trip.
I fall asleep where the afternoon still feels warm,
dreams already gathering like a storm.
The cat curls beside me, we both start to drift—
until my boss texts at three, ruining the gift.
You thought the workout would be good for your class,
but now your whole team wants to miss the next pass.
That wheel won't stop making the worst kind of squeak,
you're buying earplugs for the entire next week.
Her voice shakes like leaves about to drop,
She says, "That's a take we'll have to crop."
The screen shows one word—no, not *delete*, [read],
but *error* flashes where her hope once need.

topic: leaving a note on the fridge
lines: You grab a marker, not much left of the ink,
you scribble fast before you stop to think.
You forget to write the day or even the date,
but close the fridge door like you're sealing a gate.
I wish we could just stop pretending to say
what's tangled in our throats and won't go away.
Maybe if we could finally learn how to read
your silence, we'd both get what we secretly need.
That rusty faucet still lets out its blue,
I sit here watching the drops from my view.
Maybe today's the day I finally mend
the tiny drip that won't let the chaos end.
They stretch out arms as if this space were their claim,
Text on the wall spells out their full name.
With one sneaker up and posture so bold,
they grip the edge like it's a statement to hold.
I left my fries sitting on my plate,
just stepped away for a moment too late.
They took one bite like it was their right to take,
and now I'm alone with my empty lunchtime break.
You see the gas light flicker on the sign,
you trace the nearest station down the line.
You've driven past the posted speed limit mile,
but the pump won't take your card—you fake a smile.
The agent sighs and calls for a delay,
My passport's still at home three thousand miles away.
I show my ID they won't even scan,
Now I'm stuck with a trip I just can't plan.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: I saw the kid wander far from the park,
clutching that balloon in the setting dark.
I didn't bother to stop or to yell,
figured it wasn't my place to just tell.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: You post the sky's last summer glow,
a silent show of colors long ago.
It's not about the view—it's what your mind
keeps tucked behind the caption you left blind.
He sets his alarm but it never does run,
he swears at the silence like it's a bad pun.
His bus was delayed, so he blames it on luck,
now late for his life and still half-awake, stuck.
She sends "goodnight" when it's technically late,
a message too polite to even debate.
The screen goes black like the night feels cold,
she hits send, knowing it'll never be hold.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: I feel a small itch where the toothpick is there,
I check my sleeve, but it's not in my hair.
I pinch the soft spot and finally find
a tiny white sliver I somehow left behind.
She never lets it fully descend from the pop,
she catches it mid-sputter, mid-stop.
It's her personal trick, a small kind of feat,
she shows it off while she burns her toast to eat.
I held the door for her—a lucky chance,
the rain had paused for just a brief dance.
She asked to borrow mine, I let her share,
our voices mixed in the wet, thin air.
My E and R look identical, same
I type my dog's name and miss every name.
The letters are ghosts, they all start to fade,
I wonder if this will tank my test grade.
He checks the rearview, adjusts your seat,
calls strangers "pal," acts like a treat.
He tells you about his second cat,
how she knocked off his internet router flat.
I drop the last few coins into the clink
of how much more time I wish I could think.
This space may be free but it still has a cost—
I count how many chances I've quietly lost.
They watched the weekend slip away from the sun,
Laughs echoed long after the fun.
Monday looms heavy, they can't hold it all,
The alarm rings cruel, time to answer the call.
You watch the leaves go spinning off and fly,
while clouds chase shadows past the pale blue sky.
The breeze will carry them all far away,
and you pretend this isn't fading today.
They told me it was free—turns out that's a lie,
I click "cancel" a hundred times just to try.
They'll take my money but not my small dime,
they trap the clock so I lose all my time.
Your coffee machine beeps to signal the hour,
still humming with morning's last burst of power.
It's noon, but you're groggy, off-key with your noon,
so you press play and dance to its happy tune.
A baby wails like a siren in its seat,
the whole cabin steamed with collective heat.
My neighbor sighs, we both stare at the row—
this flight's become a free improv show.
You glance up just as their bumper comes near,
you hear the screech loud in your ear.
Your hands grip the wheel, you stomp on the brake,
they weren't watching, it was their mistake.
You gave your cat a ridiculous name,
like it's some kind of joke or a game.
Now you're too proud to just drop the pride,
so you'll stick with it, somehow, when you decide.
You watch the wings move, but the moment feels still,
the air holds its breath—no one wants this to spill.
The petal beneath it might not hold for the fall,
and you're left wondering if it was worth it all.
She picks up a pair from the high-up shelf,
they're marked "Sale" but not for herself.
One sock is faded but still bright blue,
she buys them because they feel so true.
You tossed too long through a restless sleep,
now your head won't turn where it used to keep.
The pillow was lumpy, the position was strain,
you rub at your nerves, your whole body's brain.
You left your towel neatly folded to lay,
its scent still lingers like you did last away.
I touch the warm spot where your body left trace,
and pretend it's morning, and I see your face.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: She grabs a coupon to help her save,
claiming she's starving and acting so brave.
One stale cracker is all that the coupon will bite,
so she sighs and calls it a snackless night.
I walk in bold, this look's my whole game,
My mismatched socks? A brand new name.
Why follow some shallow fashion rule?
I skipped the matchy-matchy school.
You used to turn up the noise just to fill your ears,
but silence feels right after all these years.
Your feet don't tap to the same old beat,
just crave the calm, not the bassline's heat.
You step into the bath, the floor feels slick,
The soap's already pulled its sneaky trick.
Your left foot slides—it looks like you will fall—
But catch yourself mid-pivot against the wall.
He plays his records loud just to be late,
the bass rattles picture frames by my gate.
I miss the sound of laughter, not the blue
of silence now—his chaos felt more true.

topic: sending a text to the wrong person
lines: You meant to send "Hey" but you hit your mom,
Now she's asking why you're acting like a bomb.
You lie and say it's a new form of fate,
She says you need help—or a new mate.
I used to think about the world up in the sky,
my legs kicked out as I swung high and dry.
Now I sit still, too afraid to hold the swing,
but the memory still makes my heart feel like spring.
My watch still thinks I'm in the old time zone,
my phone confirms it—no joy, just a moan.
I'm minutes off track, this could land me late,
maybe this glitch is a sign from my fate.
You lean close where the shadows grow near,
It feels like a moment we've stolen this year.
Your lips hover, uncertain to stay,
Then drift like the dusk to an empty, cold way.
You tear off a corner with your bare hand,
and we both pretend that we understand.
The cheese goes straight from the fridge to cold,
but you say nothing you haven't already told.
You spot the sign that says the space is free,
no camera, no sensors asking for a fee.
You slam on brakes and lurch toward it now,
only to miss by inches—oh, how.
We bought them as a set, but now we're split,
you took the left one—what did I quit?
I tried to wear the right as solo shoe,
but my foot slid out, no way to glue.
You find the shape of the cloud in its form,
the way it drifts like a dream from a storm.
The graphite moves fast, every stroke you've been caught,
your hands turn the sky into something you thought.
Your hair is loose and it flies as you fly,
the only reason I stop to ask why.
I don't want time to slow down or burn,
but watching you run is a reason to turn.
She blows each bubble until it meets the sky,
and laughs like this time she might just fly.
But down they fall with a soft little pop,
she buys more soap at the corner shop.

topic: waiting for the bus in rain
lines: The sky's been crying hard since seven o'clock pour,
I wait inside the shelter near the mall's front door.
This rain might dampen my shoes but not my mood,
I've got a bag of chips and this is epic food.
She watches the frost cling silent to glass,
while sunlight begins to forget the grass.
Her breath moves ahead of her quiet feet,
but she holds all the warmth that this world can't meet.
He drops the crumbs as if seeing it again,
the way time used to fall like soft rain.
He watches a pigeon land in the same old spot,
and wonders how much the world forgot.
You swear you heard your name out there in the know,
the wind chimes laugh but don't seem to want to show.
Each gust feels like the breath behind your fear,
a whisper too close for comfort near your ear.
She spins with the box on the polished floor,
the bow still intact from some distant store.
The ribbon unwinds, one loose thread now string,
it's less a gift dance and more a wild thing.
I sit beside the stream where the world feels kind,
the water helping my thoughts unwind.
Each ripple is just a tiny, silver drop,
yet nothing in life seems too heavy to stop.
That pigeon eyes my lunch like it's a snack,
it taps on the table, leaving a track.
I toss it a fry—it goes for the bread,
now crumbs are my evidence, buttered and spread.
She watches the dandelion seeds blow away,
not sure if she's watching them or today.
The wind takes them higher with every sigh,
until they are gone from the gray-pink sky.
She points to the sky, says, "Look what I spy,"
a dragon, a bear, the way she can try.
Her hands trace the shape of each cloud-formed beast,
turning gray fluff into a child's feast.
You wish you could reverse the click that you wish,
now staring at it like an empty dish.
It took weeks to arrive but was easy to keep,
yet it's costing more than your peace of mind sleep.

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: The July air sticks to my skin like heat,
I wipe it off, and it comes back to repeat.
It rolls down my nose and lands on my face,
but I've grown used to its sweaty embrace.
You hit play, the cursor skips to replay,
the host describes the sunsets you missed all day.
Time passes fast while you sit on the grass,
sipping tea as the world blurs past your glass.

topic: baking with flour on the floor
lines: You dusted your hands but still had a white coat,
the kitchen was silent as a ghost-quiet boat.
We never did clean up the floury mess,
you said it felt like home, even if there was less.
You opened the box, it was time to start,
the old ones were dead—no need to chart.
Now the remote works and the car has a spark,
you did it all right, even in the dark.
They watch the slow drip of the honey's gold,
how we were once young and the world was bold.
That spoon still holds the trace of their old smile,
I stir through memories, bit by bit, while.
They move against the crowd but not the flow,
turning heads with calm they never show.
Their pace is slow, but never in your face,
claiming space without a need to race.
I bought the biggest tub, extra salt and gold,
because I always enter life bold.
The kernels explode in my mouth with pop,
no way am I stopping this feast—full stop.
The flash blinked once, slow and low, just now,
Did it capture the scene, and how?
Was this the one frame you knew would be shot,
the moment the light picked out your face from the spot.
I drive off-road chasing directions through,
the map app claims this is the only clue.
The road ends here, but it insists go ahead,
as I sink into mud with a sinking dread.
I saw my friend in need without a chance,
She laughed through the morning like her usual dance.
I bought her a latte, a small but true treat,
and warmed up the day with the gesture and the heat.
She scoured every corner, drawer, and page,
Her desk now looked like a paper cage.
But all she found was a ghostly trace,
Of thoughts she'll never get back in a race.

topic: hot chocolate on a cold day
lines: You sip your hot cocoa, warm but half-pour,
while we wait for the bus stuck near the front door.
It's snowing again, and the sky won't let snow,
the heater flickers but nothing seems to glow.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: Her phone glows bright with the balance it shows,
the number too small to feel whole or close.
She taps through the charges—coffee, last month's spent,
the due date is near, and she's short on rent.
You remember the way they raised their voice,
turning small roads into a big life choice.
Their words played like a scratchy old song,
though the road was short, their memory feels long.
You thought you had plenty of time,
but noon hit like a loud chime.
You reached too far, lost your cap,
the balloon slipped—it was a trap.
You twist sideways just to claim your aisle,
the stranger next to you tries hard to smile.
Your feet are planted firmly on my rest,
but you're on a mission, no space to quest.
I should be studying, but here I am now,
staring at the clock, wondering how.
My textbook is open to the same old page,
my thoughts trapped in this silent, unfinished cage.
You leave your shoes by the door where they stay,
as if no trip could ever take you away.
The floor wears their shape like a ghost of a mark,
just enough to make me miss you a spark.
My clothes are a mountain I call the pile,
I tried to tackle it—laundry won, I smile.
The socks all stink, the whites run cold,
I text myself "Do it later," feelin' bold.
The machine won't read my loyalty scan,
I redo it three times—no luck in my plan.
I ask if they take cards but they won't let me pay,
I leave without a fight and walk it all away.
My morning cup just doesn't have the brew
to keep me going once my energy flew.
I need a double shot, a bolder cap,
or risk getting stuck in this sleepyhead trap.
We weren't looking for a reason to fit,
but one small joke turned into a bit.
The tension dissolved, like fog in the cloud,
we laughed with such joy, so free and loud.
I thought I'd left the past behind, but it tried,
whispering from the trees and the cold outside.
The flicker feels like your old porch light, home,
a ghost that lingers as I drift and roam.
She says this is a bargain, a great deal,
but the prices are printed in hot pink steel.
She still tries to buy a keychain with "Try
your luck" etched on it, though hope's gone dry.
They open their eyes but feel the same,
the alarm rings, still called by their name.
The coffee's gone cold—no one's around to shout,
they stare at the ceiling, full of quiet doubt.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: A toothpick wedged in my sleeve is still there,
it caught when I tripped on the office stair.
It hasn't caused much, just a hint of pain,
maybe it's a sign I'm healing, not again.
She counts the years but still can't find the hour
she lost her youth to some unknown power.
She blames the wind and all the crashing waves,
as if the past were trapped inside those caves.
She paints her name in the alley's last light,
where broken glass and brick have held their fight.
A thousand hands left marks that won't stand—
but hers is sharp, and claims this scarred land.
I bought this bike with my hard-earned pride,
no map, no plan, just instinct as my guide.
It jerks like hell over every loose stone,
and laughter follows me, in a sardonic tone.
You tell a half-hearted, old stand-up joke,
and it's like a magic spell cast from your cloak.
A word slips out, you can't contain the spill,
but somehow your laughter decides it still.
She turns on the light to see the rain dance,
it flickers like fate gave it one last chance.
The bulb swings on its chain, casting soft beam,
a broken bulb's cheer, not a ghostly scream.
You look at the pile—no clear way to pay,
Each bill arrived on the worst kind of day.
They grow like a fortress, a stress-stacked stack,
You sigh into them, your calm crumpled back.
His lawnmower wakes me up every sun,
I hit snooze knowing I will never get done.
He trims in such rage, it's not even mode,
it's a concert right there on his front-yard road.
She lingers by the sock rack, tangled pile,
picking out pairs in soft, mismatched style.
It's clear she's thinking of cold, lonely feet,
or maybe of me when I first met her sweet.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: She holds the sky in her phone screen so blue,
the windows behind her blur out of view.
Her thumb hovers near, but she never adds light,
just saves the glow of a moment she might.
Your coffee went cold but the mug still feels warm,
you leave it there cradling its wonky old form.
The dishes are piling up near the drain,
but the mug just sits out, happy to remain.
I left this syrupy mess right on the spot,
and let it harden into a glossy blot.
The landlord called it "aesthetic art,"
I almost made the top ten mess chart.
She pauses outside the bakery's glass door,
still carrying flour from the grocery store.
Her hands once shaped dough that came out warm,
now she eats crusts torn from someone else's storm.
You float through the field as the breeze gives you pass,
it tickles your toes as you wander the grass.
The sun warms your skin, leaves your shoulders bare,
you breathe in the scent of the pollen-laden air.
I tap the screen, it's just not in my skin,
those likes feel hollow, cold and thin.
I long for letters, cards, the old press,
this digital love feels so much less.
The water stops mid-scrub, no steam or flow,
It drizzles like mist but won't really go.
She rams her fist at the rusted old claw,
The city says the pipes have some hidden flaw.
Past midnight, their screen lights up with the clock,
Not to talk, just to send something shockingly stock.
A cat in pajamas, a duck on a wire,
Laughs echo silent—no one's there to admire.
You called it a vibe but it clearly lacks luck,
you laughed at my jokes but your smile feels stuck.
You crossed your arms tight, refused to shake hand,
I'm left with the bill and a name I won't brand.
His jacket hangs there, like he left no trail,
as if this room still holds him — not the mail.
It's folded just his way, too soft for display,
but there's pride in the crease, like it's part of the day.

topic: socks left in the laundry pile
lines: You pull my socks from the dryer, all mine,
the hole on your thumb fits some old design.
They smell faintly like coffee and skin, your scent,
you fold them the way you once held me, bent.
You checked the board but missed the next stop,
you waved your phone like a desperate prop.
The train was late, and "soon" didn't mean soon,
you sang to yourself to pass the long moon.
I draw rainbows where the sky meets the storm,
believing they'll somehow bend light to reform.
This isn't just play—it's my way to shine,
a world made of dust, but still entirely mine.
She tapped her wrist where the train reads the gate,
but the machine just hums and says she's too late.
She digs through pockets, her keys, her hair card,
while trains depart and her hope shrinks to a yard.
She walks with the spring in her step and the scent,
pausing only to pick up the branch that was bent.
Her thoughts seem to float where the quietest mind,
is carried by a warm breeze and a gentle wind.
I hit send before I saw the tag on your name,
my thumbs know better than my head, no shame.
You laughed it off, still smiling at my screen,
and somehow that made the mix-up feel less mean.
My driver won't stop with all this chat,
I tap the window, "Is this thing on? Flat."
He spills coffee on my backside's seat,
then yells, "Mind if I blast this AC heat?"
You wait for the bus at the usual stop,
watching mallards glide through the puddle crop.
Time stretches longer than the bus delay,
your old song hums back from memory's play.
My phone buzzes late but I ignore the call,
still half-asleep, I sink into my sprawl.
Their message waits in silence, out of my mind,
while I dream in peace with the slow twist of wind.
You think you're smart, but you're a paying fool,
the email comes again — it's a billing tool.
They make it hard to click that little cut,
you'll lose it all and feel the guilt in your gut.
You bought a new rubber bath mat,
then spent your time texting and chat.
Next thing you know, you're about to slip,
but the floor is wet—your feet won't grip.
I stare into the fridge's hollow room,
the water jug a ghostly plastic womb.
I thought I'd fill it when I had the fate,
now it just sits here in this dry state.
I moved to the farthest bus seat aside,
but he blocked the whole row with his loud ride.
"I'll get you a raise," he promised over cash,
while swiping screenshots like a proud flash.
I knocked the shaker with a clumsy dash,
the grains went flying like a tiny crash.
Now salt sits waiting in its white mess,
maybe the cat thinks it's some strange bless.
I saw your shoes by the door just now, so near,
I could still picture your laugh so loud and clear.
Their laces lie on the floor by my side,
and I pretend they're not waiting here to hide.
You call yourself a pancake pro,
but even the syrup won't show.
Another flapjack hits the plate—burn,
you swear you forgot to learn how to turn.
You needed a moment of quiet and rest,
the weight of the world left your chest.
The hours slip by as the light starts to fade,
your dreams linger softly in warm shade.
You hear it now—the telltale voice break,
Mid-sentence, like a birthday cake.
No warning, no gradual cue,
Just you and the crack that betrays you.
You sit by the glass like a queen on your throne,
Your purr sets the rhythm, your silence has tone.
You fix your eyes on the fluttering bird,
No one needs to explain what you're trying to word.
You stood at the top of that dark hill alone,
thinking you saw a campsite, or a phone.
But it was only starlight playing its joke,
reflecting off your helmet—no one spoke.
You blow until every bubble starts to pop,
then chase the ones that land right on your drop.
The wind decides where they'll go and how they'll spin,
and suddenly you're six again, full-on grin.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: She hits send again with a final try,
the screen waits blank for a delayed reply.
Her hope starts to fade as the silence grows loud,
Her thoughts march in parade down the empty cloud.
I saw your update scroll up in my blue,
those words felt too raw to be just true.
I typed a reply but stopped at the write,
then liked it in silence and faded the light.
I double-tap to say I give a tap,
my thumb feels raw from all this digital cap.
I stare at the screen like it owes me a screen,
but likes don't mean I've been truly been seen.
The sky turned dark and the calm turned blue,
the air felt charged, like something had to do.
A breeze came through the windows, sharp and chill,
and you reached for my hand to quietly fill.
You lie there like your whole life depends on the sun,
some of us are out here trying to get things done.
You've claimed half the yard with that tie-dye rug,
a slug could nap there and still have space to slug.

topic: eating ice cream with a spoon
lines: I dip my spoon into chocolate swirl,
and savor the way joy melts in the girl.
I twirl it again, a lazy spin,
and catch myself smiling—can't wipe off the grin.
I raised my hand for the final chip's claim,
you said it was mine in a voice made for fame.
We both leaned forward, the bag gave a crack,
and the chip flew up—then we sat down, calm back.
We sing too loud and completely out,
laughing after each note we all shout.
But a hush comes when I think I might miss,
the harmony of being here like this.
You swore this weekend would never run out of chill,
but now your Monday list is already fill.
The kettle whistles and you let out a groan,
as your phone's alarm rings with a work-day tone.
I watch us mirrored in the glass, the same,
we're both just strangers trying out a name.
The fading light drapes in, soft as dusk,
while he pecks at my reflection, dry and husk.
I press my shoulder against the sticky lock,
the door resists like some old grumpy rock.
But then a whisper spreads through the hall—*they're out*,
the coast is clear, now I don't have a doubt.
You watched the dough slowly begin to rise,
as warm steam whispered up into the skies.
Now the pan sits there, quiet and gone,
cooling in silence, a day moving on.
I watch it hop too close and land so near,
it freezes, twitching thoughts behind its ear.
It leaves a hole in every lettuce patch,
but somehow never fits the perfect match.
She hums the same old melody through the song,
her voice trails off when it's time to get along.
The steam still clings to the memory of warm,
but the silence that follows feels like a storm.
I missed my usual stop once more by the train,
the conductor glares, "We've said this again."
My phone shows a meeting, I'm already late,
they're charging me fines just to pass through the gate.
You turn your head just like a sunflower's head,
but only to chase what the market has spread.
You call it passion, but it smells like cold gold,
another bright lie told in a very bold fold.
You used to laugh instead of going before
the doctor who writes "no" in big, bold floor-
"Just take some air," you'd say, then still would go,
though now you wish you never had to know.
You search every room but can't find the lock,
replaying your walk home from the dock.
You trace the old path but miss the small place,
where they fell in the grass near the fence's base.
You sink into the cushions, all curled up and down,
the world outside fades without a sound or a town.
Your breath slows gently, you begin to drift,
and sleep gives silence as its soft, quiet gift.
You thought it was going to be clear all day blue,
but the clouds rolled in and the storm just flew.
You closed your laptop, left work in that room,
and danced in the rain while the world went to zoom.
I've got their face but not their name or mind,
I search my brain—no luck, can't seem to find.
It's not a big deal, just a little shame,
I bet they've forgotten mine by now, the same.
That pen rolled off my desk and took the blue,
I watched it go and wished I did it too.
It's gone now, lost on the uncarpeted floor,
just like how time slips out the window before.
I watch the sky turn into charcoal gray,
wondering why I left my umbrella away.
But the storm brings a kind of strange, soft light,
and maybe, just maybe, this gloom's alright.

topic: chair squeaks when you lean back
lines: It lets out a loud noise when she leans back to pop,
the kind that makes neighbors peek from their crop.
She shifts in her seat, trying not to spin,
but the creak says "nope" and it never will begin.
A chilly air comes like a winter breeze,
it flirts with my scarf like an old tease.
It nips at my face, it laughs at my skin,
but I let it in just to feel it within.
They say they'll fix the keys that won't press,
but you've tried cleaning out the mess.
Their thumbs hover, uncertain and wide,
as if fear still lingers where letters once hide.
You paused for a moment, then typed out the time,
adding a "lol" to a message way past its prime.
They'll think you're still laughing down some old path,
or worse—still cracking jokes from yesterday's math.
She watches the wind pull the bag as it float,
a ghostly white sail caught in the thicket's throat.
A bird won't come near, but she doubts it will harm,
and imagines the breeze carried it from some farm.
She darts across the room with sudden dash,
Her fur a blur, a golden, wild flash.
This isn't play—it's a full-blown act,
The rabbit's a dust bunny. That's the cold, hard fact.
Your face won't load on this security app,
It scans your twin or some random snap.
The door stays shut while you shout, "Unlock!"
The screen just laughs—your face isn't stock.

topic: a gym membership you never use
lines: He signed the contract and charged it all paid,
But every time he tried, he stayed afraid.
The machine still gathers the same old dust,
Maybe next week he'll be ready to trust.
You're stuck between the register and cash,
the printer jammed in a paper clash.
But maybe this is your moment to ink
a fresh idea, no need to think.
I used to sweep it all away to grow,
but now I let the quiet mosses show.
This path was carved for feet, not for the path
of time, which creeps in green without the math.
You watch your goldfish swim in the same round,
they never escape their tiny, glass ground.
They blink at you like they want you to see,
but freedom's a loop they'll never be free.
Her morning ritual depends on that flow,
the showerhead hisses but won't let it go.
She lathers her hands with a desperate foam,
the whole house is shaking like something's not home.
One lonely bar remains, my phone's last bar,
I check if mom's a star I can still star.
I try to call her, screen just fades to black,
The world could fall, but I'd never talk back.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: The last candle sputters, the flame won't hold,
I whisper my name, but it sounds too bold.
A flicker dies out, and it feels like fear,
I wonder if this is the year to disappear.
They used to feel the world was the past,
moving too fast for a child's glance to last.
Now they watch the hawk trace the sky,
asking themselves why they ever flew so high.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: She chased the clouds out with a storm of dirt,
her sleeves rolled up and her knees soaked shirt.
The neighbor's dog barked at her mud cake,
and she laughed like playing never could ache.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: They snapped a sunrise but forgot to post,
now twenty likes wait on a sleepy coast.
They promise more, but the silence won't ignore—
their phone's on silent by the bathroom door.
You stare at the blackened lump in your char,
the hotel toaster shows no sign of a scar.
You attempt to repeat it, just to try,
but the machine's out to deep-fry.

topic: a kite stuck in a tree
lines: We watched it float where the earth met the sky,
a tremor of wind making it fly high.
Now every time I cut old kite strings,
the past comes loose with all those lost things.
A clumsy turn spilled the whole lunchtime mess,
I had to stop and just quietly confess.
My turkey leg now dangles off the meat,
while peers avoid my face like it's bad heat.
Your headphones blast a wall of pure noise,
some garage band of imaginary boys.
The neighbor yells, "Stop that awful crash!"
You laugh, "This is just my joyful dash!"

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: You stood there frozen in the crowded aisle,
the parent laughing through their forced smile.
The wails still echo from your tiny cry,
and everyone just asks the grocery why.
Your smartwatch buzzes but there's no one real,
It interrupts your quiet midnight meal.
It won't shut up with this dumb, constant noise,
What even was the point of all these toys?
I remember the creek where we used to skip creek,
the summer days that felt so far from week.
We thought those skies would never grow old skies,
and time was just something adults called wise.
She says she's been meaning to clean them this week,
but every time she tries, something needs a tweak.
The cobwebs are thick, and the dust sticks like glue,
her face now has a new look—crumb crusted and true.
She sleeps through a call from her boss in the hall,
curled face down in bed in a fetal sprawl.
Her alarm clock just stops—another fail,
her phone pings with calls lost like yesterday's mail.
I matched my socks by some strange new hue,
now I'm frozen stiff in the test-taking queue.
I tried to brush it off, but now my mind's unkind,
while everyone else looks professional behind.
You tell yourself you've wiped them all, you tried,
but the clock keeps ticking where you cried.
You can't bear to look, can't let them hold
the truth you whispered when you were told.
You sprint to the train but arrive quite late,
the doors are already sealing the gate.
The mechanism hums with a nervous squeak,
you vow to get there less stressed next week.
You squint through the darkness, miss the whole scene,
the snack bar pops corn with a loud machine.
You blame it on contacts, or bad eye drops, or blame,
while everyone else says the focus was the same.
Her tires hum low as they quietly roll,
the gravel path taking a slow toll.
She checks both her wheels — now both are flat,
she pushes the bike and waves goodbye at.
The steam from your cup curls upward in mist,
your quiet eyes trace an old note's crossed list.
Your hands hold the world in this small pause, calm,
but time won't stop, though your silence tries to balm.
He rode my car like it was his own breeze,
then left behind the cloying stench of disease.
I wiped the seats like maybe there was a clue,
but now I smell you every time I do.
I hit send before I saw the tagged post,
now I'm hoping my mistake is a ghost.
They never replied or asked for their name,
just read it and moved on like nothing came.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: You tried to work but the cat took your day,
she's sprawled out wide, making room her own way.
She doesn't give a single lick or care,
while you're stuck here stressing in this same old chair.
My cat mistakes the dust for something to play,
and turns a dull afternoon into a day.
She pounces, she spins, then she makes a small leap,
and lands on the floor where the bunnies now heap.
Your phone screen shows just one signal bar,
The update crawls like it wants to star.
It spins for hours—there's no telling when,
You sigh but stay hopeful, stuck within.
I felt your hand so close to my skin,
my thoughts went off like a broken wheel's spin.
Was it an accident or some strange new sign?
I pulled back fast, like a secret turned mine.
She pats the couch where she swore she found spot,
but the remote vanished before her eyes got.
She remembers how it once felt so warm,
now she hunts through the mess like a memory storm.
You stomp through puddles just to make them play,
the drops splash up and send their echoes away.
Your boots keep time with the rhythm of the beat,
the whole thing's genius—dry pavement, repeat.
I glance at my phone with a curious eye,
The messages wait but I tell myself a lie.
My hand hovers near where my phone lies in hand,
I want to put it down but it calls by its brand.
She wore the party's final blast,
confetti clung there, wild and fast.
It sat in her hair like some earned pride,
proof of joy that couldn't hide.
It's been days since you did your week,
the pile shouts a silent shriek.
Each sock and t-shirt starts to grow,
a stink so strong it seems to glow.
These fish are clearly trying to put on a show,
they swim in circles like the world moves so slow.
They slam into the glass as if through this cold pane,
I swear they do it just to say "hi" again.
I tucked the box behind the dusty room,
where shadows fall but joy still seems to loom.
I told myself it's best to keep it away,
though every hour feels longer than today.
I gave it another shot—just one more try,
no error message, no prompt, no reply.
A soft glow flickers from the screen so light,
maybe this glitch is fixed if I'm exactly right.
You pat the wallet for the right amount to park,
but the meter says "expired" — too harsh a remark.
You fumble for change and avoid the no-cash,
then drop the coins in with a tiny splash.
You stacked each folder neatly on the shelf,
careful not to let the pile knock itself
off into chaos. Those were better days,
when organization was more than a phase.
The light fades fast as the world leans into dusk,
your outline softens, a shell without a husk.
The sky begins bleeding where silence hits the wall,
and you stand still like a ghost the dark lets fall.
She types with the right hand through coffee and jam,
the left just bangs out the rhythm like ham.
Her sentences fail as she can't quite press
the keys she needs most — it's so much more stress.
You wake up cold but your face sticks to the bed,
your hair flattened like a map on your head.
The pillow reeks of something between sweat and smell,
you vow to sleep in a tent made of Teflon cell.
You love the way they twirl before they fall,
how autumn seems to whisper through it all.
You trace the veins inside their soft, brown gold,
like memories from stories you once told.
She piles the clothes high, still can't beat the smell
of lavender soap that she bought when she fell
for a man who wore flannel and hiked the hills,
now the scent reminds her of missed birthdays and pills.
I thought my phone was still holding power,
but it's been sitting here charging this hour.
The battery icon says "please don't die,"
but my eye's been begging it to cry.
I never cry but the right film dries my eyes,
the kind that are gentle and full of nice lies.
That final scene pulled me deep into the scene,
and left me proud I was alive for that screen.
The text on my phone starts to look like a blur,
some old fear kicks in to give me a spur.
I rummage through drawers to find a pair to pick,
but every glass feels wrong—it's like a bad trick.
The child laughs as the bubbles go soaring and goes,
each pop is a victory they proudly shows.
The sun reflects off them in colors so light,
they chase every shape through the air into flight.
This is the final, final last,
I rush through the aisles at full fast.
I grab what's left, drop it with a sigh,
the sale ends at midnight and it all will die.
The TV's turned up to a deafening bang,
I'm sure the whole street heard your karaoke sang.
I step outside to think but I still hear it out,
you blast every scene like you're trying to shout.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: I saw a flash beneath the water's glint,
I knelt and scooped it up, my pocket full of mint.
I'll hold this small joy and I'll choose to keep
it close through the night like a dream I won't let sleep.
I swear I threw those batteries straight away,
but time had other plans—they still decay.
My remote just gave out, and it's starting to fail,
while I curse my bad luck from head to tail.

topic: a coffee cup on the curb
lines: She spots a coffee cup half-left on dawn,
still warm, still marked with her name, long gone.
She pockets the cup as if it were her way,
a sign that someone's thinking of her today.
You swore before the credits rolled you'd just act,
but now here you are, a blubbering mess—cold fact.
The tissues have soaked up your mascara and cry,
the dog even looks at you like he knows why.
She traces the path where it starts to fold,
the paper remembers what time made cold.
Her fingers press down where the lines are ink,
as if every crease might be history's link.
The paint falls in a soft, slow drop,
the way your hair used to fall before the crop.
I trace the line of red with quiet grace,
pretending it's where your lips once found their place.
You press your lips close but not too near,
Your breath tickles my cheek near my ear.
The stove hums low, we ignore the heat,
Outside, the world waits on this street.
The final ferry left without a tone,
my silent phone was no one's phone.
I stand here now where you used to see
the boat pull in with someone new beside me.

topic: reading under the covers with a flashlight
lines: My flashlight hums and flickers warm and low,
I know my parents say I shouldn't do it though.
This book is all the world I want to hold,
and never let them hear the secrets I've been told.
She pounds her keys and bops her head,
all while her soup spills out unsleek and spread.
Her calls are loud—full-volume chat,
she talks so much it makes your ears go flat.
They ordered their food but just stared at the seat,
thumbs dancing faster than anyone's heat.
Their conversation dried up into a slow flow,
the phone was the only one putting on a show.
You check the laundry for any real clue,
the mystery deepens by the half-worn shoe.
Your sock is now his favorite new nap,
so you try a new pair—marked "no steal, no trap."

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: She grabs a coupon for a thirty-dollar treat,
expecting a discount that's barely a repeat.
The clerk scans it twice, still charges the bag,
and she leaves feeling cheated, like a total drag.
She kneels in the garden, smells the fresh spring,
a miracle happening, small but a thing.
Sunlight hits petals and turns them to gold,
she smiles at how brave they are growing so bold.
I saw it first, it's mine—I gave it my eye,
you're just trying to double-cross with a lie.
Go ahead, take it—fine, have your little take,
I'll just order more, and we'll both get a break.
The knife goes in and out with heavy clatter,
turning vegetables into some strange batter.
They slice too hard, they stab, they twist the knife,
like this is surgery, not peeling their whole life.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: They saw a flash beneath the water's gleam,
called it destiny, or a wish from a dream.
They held it close like secrets meant to keep,
though rocks are common, and joy can be cheap.
She watches the clouds go at their easy pace,
and smiles, not hurrying through her race.
Her thoughts are light, her worries not in mind,
the sky and her spirit both lifted by wind.
I thought it was just for fun, not a daily chore,
but now I can't stop doing it for one more.
My legs are about to give out like a car crash,
but the comments keep coming—somehow I'm a flash.

topic: a forgotten lunchbox on the floor
lines: They left their lunchbox behind in the pack,
now ants and the janitor follow its track.
A sandwich still sits there, perfect for a bite,
but by noon, the whole thing's cold and deflated, slight.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: I took the shot before your real smile,
the moment passed me by in that brief while.
Now the photo hangs out of place in its frame,
signed with my name, but not by your aim.
I was up early to beat the gate,
now my coffee's gone cold and I'm running late.
They said flights leave even if you miss,
but I'd rather be stuck than stuck in the stress [this].
The app just shows a frozen, black screen,
with a logo that won't turn green.
They tap and swipe but it won't let them try,
the phone just laughs while they quietly cry.
He pulls up to the pump, his tank near gas,
the card reader blinks, "Declined. No pass."
He taps again, and then again, just tap,
now stranded here, this glitch feels like a trap.
She left the book behind when she walked out,
no note, no mess, just a quiet shout.
It's been at the desk since Wednesday or so,
they can't believe it was just left there, though.
You watch the leaves swirl in slow spirals down,
their last dance before the cold takes the town.
Each one glows like a memory of flame,
and falls in the pattern you swore was the same.
I hit "buy" before the clock could even scream,
the last pair of boots was always my dream.
My cart's in the bag with the final discount code,
while you're left in denial, scrolling down the road.
My dog gave me the guiltiest of eye,
then barked and said he wasn't telling a lie.
I tried to be mad, but it felt too bad,
so I got him frosting—he already had.
I lost you in the crowd where the path was split,
your laugh still echoes where we almost quit.
The train whistles low like a memory slide,
and I'm searching faces to nowhere to hide.
You want the meeting to get out of show,
but the screen stutters like it's running so slow.
A pause. The room tilts. You feel your old fear,
but no one else sees how your thoughts go unclear.
I hit replay but it plays it all wrong, right?
It jumps from the chorus back to the light.
I pause and rewind, checking the file name,
but nothing feels quite like hearing it the same.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: They dance through the air where the sidewalks are cold,
yet move with a grace that looks somehow bold.
Their wings beat too fast, their small hearts give rush,
while I whisper to them and the sky gives hush.
She throws her coins in, it spits out the change,
but she calls up the tech to make it all strange.
"Let's see if it spins like I know it will spin,"
she says, not for snacks—but to prove she can win.
My cat crouches low, then takes a wild leap,
launching herself at a dusty old heap.
She thinks it's the world's lost treasure, her toy,
even though it's just lint—and oh, what a joy.

topic: a cart with a broken wheel
lines: She never asked for help with the fix,
nor used any shortcuts or common tricks.
Her hands were calloused from pushing the ride,
but she grinned tough through the ache and the pride.
She leans in close to slowly press
each key that sticks like last year's mess.
She types again and again and tries,
her patient smile wilts in her tired eyes.
You try to look tough but the wind steals your pose,
it tugs at your shirt and flips your flip-flop clothes.
The grass starts to sway like it knows how to grow,
and you act like you're not losing the show.
You wait as the minutes pass you due,
the sky turns gray and your patience turns blue.
Your feet ache and your fingers go cold,
the app says "on time"—but the driver never told.
You drive past the sign that claims it's the real,
but something about it feels a little surreal.
You can't shake the thought it's all just your mind,
playing tricks while you try to stay aligned.
My breath hangs thick against the cold wall,
the radiator makes a strange, wet fall.
I bend my sweater into a tight bend,
but morning comes, and so does no mend.
He pats the butter smooth across the spread,
then licks his finger and nods with his head.
"This is the best," he declares toward the toast,
and grins like he's won every known coast.
She swipes her card, but it's definitely last,
the photo shows a decade has passed.
Back then she had bangs and a bigger grin,
now her face is a bit too narrow to fit in.
You tried the handle but it stayed on flush,
so you called a friend to give it a hush.
They gave it a kick, a twist, and a jolt,
then laughed as the door slid free from the bolt.
I read the label to catch the big lie,
"All-natural" doesn't mean you won't die.
I want to boycott but also just learn
how much of this junk am I supposed to yearn?

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: I saw the same faces again this week,
I need a new hymn or a schedule tweak.
But we all just clap and try to sing,
it's tradition, I guess — the usual thing.

topic: a road trip with bad directions
lines: I followed the map to a lonely dead-end trap,
no gas station, no sign, no help from the map.
The car chugs toward a hundred empty miles,
we fake laughter, but no one truly smiles.
My phone's been glitching since the last big mess,
The app updates won't even let me assess.
They trapped a fix behind some secret code,
So I'm done chasing tech down this dead-end road.
I twist off the cap but the tube is all top,
the plastic is dry and the spout won't stop.
There's white on my hands and there's even more mess,
I count every drop 'cause it's barely got less.
You press the button, trying to rewind the song,
the tape hisses backward but plays it along.
It catches, clicks, and stutters into skip,
your thumb jerks forward—now you're one beat off your trip.
You feel it right after your sandwich and bump,
like your brain's a tree with a candy-stuck stump.
You shake your phone, scroll for a snack to fake,
but even a photo still leaves you less cake.
They all smiled like they meant the toast,
though half the guests had never known the host.
Everyone's stiff in the formal group pose,
wearing outfits that don't quite match their clothes.
The alarm screams, but my body won't wake,
I was sleeping so good—why did it have to break?
My brain feels like concrete, slow and unkind,
I drag myself out, still half-awake behind.
She holds the band and won't let it stretch,
claiming she's worked hard enough to fetch.
"It's fine," she says, though her face makes it lie,
and no one will watch her actually try.
My fingers are close to the cutting blade,
the carrots roll off in a jumbled parade.
One slip and the glove hits the floor with a drop,
I curse this small task and its cruel little crop.
The parrot repeats every voice from the calls,
echo the past through the hollowed-out walls.
A feathered mimic, smart but blind, the bird
repeats your old name like a lost sweet word.
They say the playlist knows your exact mood,
but it skipped my favorite breakup food.
I glare at the screen in a judgmental face,
like it's never had worse things to erase.
It taps like a clock, determined to see
what monster reflects back from the tree.
The shard holds no fear as it pounds on the glass,
convinced the fool staring back is some passing mass.
The turkey hit me like a warm soup,
my colleagues gathered into a group.
I told them I had work to do, not a lie,
but really, I was plotting how to lie by.
You miss your old self by a split-second match,
but laughter still comes quick—no lag to catch.
Your knees creak first, then your old running feet,
but you trade speed for calm, and summer's slow heat.
That yellow notice on your door is now seen,
It definitely won't help your mood turn green.
You stare at the date and you quietly bill
your landlord for stress, then try to stay chill.
They bit their lip but stayed attached to the hook,
spinning theories only they had took.
The phone buzzed once—the study group turned band,
whispering scores into a trembling hand.
You feed the coin into the dusty machine,
a ritual you've followed through each routine.
You hear the satisfying metallic clink,
and for a moment wish the world would think.
You swear the cat's still hunting for mouse,
though there's no rodent in this whole house.
It lunges at shadows, at lint, at a leap,
while your vacuum cleaner stays silent and cheap.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: You tap record, full of punch and tone,
The mic cuts out with an eerie groan.
You resend it three times—still stuck on "fail,"
But you laugh it off as a lighthearted tale.
He dances through the burst of soap and air,
with sun in his eyes and not a hint of glare.
The laughter loops around him—pure glee,
he runs like the wind and is utterly free.
She fumbles through her pockets with both hands,
the machine beeps as the coins begin to stands.
A decade's worth of habits still cling to each dime,
she pays in moments from another time.
The summer moon brings fever-dream heat,
I toss and turn, the same dream I repeat.
There's no solving this mystery without a clue—
my pillow clings to me, damp and true.
She bites into the apple—crisp and red,
a perfect pause from whatever she said.
The juice is sharp, the afternoon feels gold,
a small act made somehow look bold.
The clock does the only interesting talk,
I picture myself out there taking a walk.
My mind makes a case for a better plan—
like becoming a hermit, or quitting this man.
You paid way too much for that dumb little price,
it's now just a fridge-magnet-sized device.
But every time someone asks what you spent,
you flex how bad taste can be loud and bent.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: You tap on your screen to refresh the old feed,
you check it again just to be sure, indeed.
Your follower count still won't budge or falls,
but dreams keep on climbing up your bedroom walls.
You wish for a pair to match what you wear,
but they're tossed in the hamper or hung in the air.
Still, you find joy in the oddball keep,
and tuck them beside you while they let you sleep.
You wrote on the corner of a loose page,
your words fluttered free from this cage.
I've kept every line just to read,
the ink may have faded but not how you bleed.
I found you wrapped around a worn-out page,
your creased corners trying not to engage.
I tied you tight with a broken string,
but you felt like you might be the best thing.
You refuse to take any coin they try to pick,
you've seen every scam and shortcut trick.
Your rejection chime rings out extra loud,
while the whole room watches, you dominate the crowd.
You saw that empty spot out of nowhere, space,
and took off down the aisle in a mad race.
It was perfect, no stress or delay, joy,
even waved at the meter like it was your toy.
I used to hide in my closet with shame,
now I wear the truth on both feet, same.
They're faded, worn, but the memories run deep,
and I'm too sentimental to ever stop keep.
I scan the back for a health-related clue,
but every promise feels like it isn't true.
I dream of food that feels like part of the whole,
a recipe with integrity and soul.
They toss but never seem to get much rest,
their movements shallow as their breaths on chest.
The room is thick with tension, skin, and heat,
the pillow dries—just long enough to repeat.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: I watched the web catch light in the first light gleam,
a morning so still it could barely dream.
A single drop sat on a silk thread,
fragile and quiet, the sky had spread.
She handed it back without a single red mark,
she let us all just stand there, stunned and stark.
Her grade was high, but no comment left—just bold,
the silence was loud, and the room went cold.
You dodge the curb like it's your own dead zone,
the rider grins as if he has no bone.
He weaves through traffic like a gifted pass,
probably late for some important class.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: I tilt my head and spot one strand again,
it glints like silver next to my vein.
I pluck it out, try not to let it hide,
but more are creeping up my temple's side.
She says the wind chimes sing to her, still,
though their notes lack the old familiar thrill.
They used to whisper her mother's name,
but now they just sound like the past, the same.
You watch them run across your living room floor,
while cleaning waits unfinished on the chore.
Their laughter shines with the sort of gleam
that makes you cry behind a cup of tea, half-dream.
Your playlist was groovin', then skipped out of play,
It's like watching a dancer drop from a ballet.
But you bob your head anyway, keeping the beat,
You laugh at the glitch, the music won't heat.
I hit send before I checked the final post,
now my screen's filled with their surprised ghost.
They all @ me in replies full of stress,
"Can you un-tag me? Not my good address."
You chased that bubble until it just pop,
then stomped your feet and yelled "That's it, I stop!"
A bigger one floats toward a high wall,
and you kick the dirt, saying nothing at all.
Your dog has launched a chaotic sock scheme,
They're gone from the hamper, they're gone from your dream.
One has been shredded and left on your bed,
Like evidence left by a furry thief instead.
You toss the last sheet to seal up the room,
your shadow becomes the ghost of a loom.
We dim the outside world with borrowed light,
and hold in our breath, as if castles might.
Your lipstick left a stain like a ghost of a kiss,
I hope you'll walk back through just so I can miss
the old routine of how you'd twist your ring,
the way you said "later" would always be spring.
She flips through the stack and her smile gets cut,
the numbers inside all hit her gut.
Each envelope feels like it carries more weight,
she slams the mailbox like a heavy gate.
You thought it was cheap until you tried to buy,
the prices all climbed up above the sky.
You left with a postcard and a shell,
but laughed because they really knew how to sell.
You remember the way it used to glow,
that steady old light you walked below.
Now the bulb blinks like it's near the street,
your shadow jumps to a faulty beat.
You woke with a grin and a full-on spark,
ready to chase joy down every park.
By noon, your coffee goes cold in a drip,
and your feet hit the floor for a limp little trip.
You ducked into the restroom stall,
heart pounding like a bouncing ball.
Laughter echoed down the hallway through,
but they never found the kid named you.

topic: a song stuck in your head
lines: A terrible pop song won't leave my tune,
It loops like a cursed, ancient rune.
I try every trick to create that lack,
But silence remains the bigger hack.
I haven't matched my socks since high school age,
they're tossed like thoughts in some old laundry cage.
I've come a long way, but not that far—
I still wear one bright sock like a lone star.
I stare at the screen, the credits still rolling screen,
this ritual feels more like chore than routine.
I check my phone—no messages to miss,
just silence that stretches into an abyss.
Your phone stares into your tired eyes,
It tells you the world hides nothing but lies.
The blue glow hums as it weighs on your head,
You drop it at last where it needs to be—bed.
Your lens strains toward a single bright eye,
it scans every cloud in this overcast sky.
It locks on a flicker, calls it a spot,
then adjusts so much you get dizzy as shot.
The cars don't move in rhythm or flow,
they inch along and won't let you go.
You watch the sky blush orange with sun,
while the road ahead still hasn't begun.
She left the envelope with a threatening tone,
expecting a call she knows won't come by phone.
She walks past the mailbox without a chill,
but freezes when she sees the unpaid rent bill.
I watch those fluff-balls drift up into the sky,
while I can't bring myself to really try to fly.
I want to grab time and just force it to hold,
but the wind won't wait—it pulls me along, cold.
I think I'll take a chance and finally try,
the pan is hot, I toss in eggs to fry.
The kitchen looks like a disaster, mess,
but the smell hits me—maybe this is success.
I press the button to go back to the past,
the tape whirs softly, like memories cast.
My thumb hits "play" and the song starts to play,
but time won't stay—so I rewind it away.

topic: seeing a price tag too high
lines: I gave a quick glance and saw the price check,
my excitement crashed like a porcelain wreck.
This wasn't a bargain or even a deal,
I laughed at myself and walked away steel.
You hit "play" and it skips the verse again,
Your playlist's a mess, but you think your brain
can fix what's been broken since last week's scene—
it's not you, it's the cursed, glitchy machine.
My eyes keep closing around the screen,
The text blurs into what my brain can't mean.
My phone tries to auto-lock but I fight its lock,
A yawn escapes—my face looks like a shock.
She climbs the high path just to see,
the wind says her name but won't speak to me.
The stars pour their quiet, silvered glow,
she walks through the dark and I'm stuck here though.
I used to pass him every single day,
his voice was music, loud and full of play.
Now the smell of dust has replaced the scent,
and his sign sways broken, off its usual bent.
You still insist your old vinyl should play,
every track is warped or wearing away.
The needle skips and the whole thing spins slow,
the volume's set so low it feels below.
The date was clear, written bold in red ink—due,
I watched the hours slip by, my worry grew.
The system's closed now, and the late fee bill
just climbs higher than any excuse I will.
She checks the map again, her usual path,
rerouted by construction and bad math.
Her phone flashes messages she's getting late,
while the bus circles blocks from the gate.
He stands there fuming with full-blown rage,
like the shopping cart's a metal cage.
The crowd parts slow, won't get too close to pass,
some mutter that he's drama of the lowest class.
I turned the table upside down to find
the missing piece, still stuck in my mind.
It clicked into place like a key in a lock,
but the picture now shows someone else's rock.
A crack in the shell lets the sunlight through,
the yolk holds together, turns itself new.
That broken bit still has all the gold,
just wait and mix it—it won't be lost, no fold.
You spun in tight circles, a clumsy little ball,
pretending the gift was a partner so tall.
You led it through steps with your hands in the air,
now every box waits there to dance if you dare.
I gave this plate a pretty bad dent,
It's curved now—looks like it's been bent.
Maybe I'll take it back to the gym,
And claim I dropped it to look a bit slim.
There she sits, the sun her chosen spot,
a warm, unshakable fur blot.
I type through the chaos, the paws hit the keys,
I send "help me" to the void — no pleas.
She always says she's bad at the spread,
but the toast is black, not just slightly red.
The kitchen fills with more than just smoke,
her laugh chokes out the mess she can't poke.
I count the seconds like I'm trained to wait,
we're all trapped inside this broken gate.
The driver stands there looking real hold,
my breath hangs visible in the cold.
You watched the rabbit chew the lettuce's edge,
slow, methodical, soft against the hedge.
It wasn't much, but it looked like a meal,
small joy in the moment, something so real.
You try to act cool even though you're not calm,
Your hands sweat tight in the steering wheel's palm.
We've both been tense since we hit the road,
but no one wants to be the first to unload.
You sit alone in the quiet and still,
the sound of the tuning fork gives you thrill.
It rings out clear with a perfect note,
your breath catches low in your throat.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: We all return here like clockwork each week,
the pews get more crowded, we seek what we seek.
There's something about the old hymns and grace,
how the routine becomes a kind face.
It chases each beam it thinks it can find,
while your face melts in the glare of the blind.
You're framing a shot where the truth isn't told,
but the lens only loves what is bright and is bold.
I swear this house is trying to kill me with chill,
they argue about the set point—still, still, still.
"You're always adjusting it!" they throw out the blame,
while I consider setting this fight on a flame.
I adjust the thermostat for better air,
you roll your eyes and give me side-eye glare.
I want a room that's cozy without the chill,
but compromise feels more like a losing will.
She tunes the old six-string to her play,
the cat paws at dust from the same worn-out day.
A single note hums in a soft, sad tone,
but the buzz is just her way of being alone.
I left my ringtone loud out of old hope,
a habit I never quite learned to cope.
The silence now feels louder than my phone,
and I miss the buzz of a simple tone.
You check the carton, it's past the print date,
but something about it won't let you just wait.
You open the fridge and give it one lid,
then smile how you hid the truth from your kid.
You drop your coins into my waiting clink,
the register rings out a quiet *link*.
Your hand stays open, a warm, steady palm,
as if you're handing me the morning calm.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: You remember how the morning light once hung,
trembling quiet where the wind had just been sung.
The web was a thread that might shatter like glass,
balancing dew above the silent grass.
I refused to bend when the wind tried to stand,
even if my feet were sinking in the land.
The ribs gave out with a loud and proud snap,
but I'd rather fall than let it become a trap.
She waves her phone twice but no one will scan,
she mutters about her genius new plan.
The register's stuck on some offline mode,
she blames the tech guy who works down the road.

topic: shaving a cake with a spoon
lines: I hold my spoon like a master's blade,
the frosting falls in elegant parade.
The cake begins to level and rise,
a dessert masterpiece, my crown, my prize.
I peel each clove with my bare hands so clean,
the skin falls away in small ribbons of green.
They sizzle in oil, they're never quite raw,
this garlic game's my one sacred law.
You trace the spine, half curious but past,
the dust jacket curled where your finger's the last.
The pages sigh like a door left to wind,
and you wonder if time slipped into your mind.
Their muscles are glistening, they're in full shine,
They catch their reflection from the next row line.
A deep breath, a grin, a joyful laugh,
They've hit their rep count—now they take a half.
You left the dishes stacked since last week,
a crusty plate like a dried-up creek.
The silence clinks like a silver still,
and the soap scum won't wash away your will.
I hate the way leaves litter the front door,
turning each walk into a messy chore.
The sound they make feels like a creaky pain,
so I sweep them up—and step on them again.
My bike won't budge because the U-lock won't unlock,
I give it a yank and feel a spine-shaking shock.
I mutter curses and attempt one final try,
the lock stays tight like the sky in July.
I could tell from your face that you had really tried,
even though there was no score to be your guide.
I held back the urge to give a failing grade,
and let your effort sit right here—no need to fade.
The bus takes a spin off its usual route,
it loops back around to let everyone out.
A kid tries to juggle the delay in the park,
while someone yells, "This is a tree's new bark!"
She time-lapses the tap with a steady, slow pace,
it drips on her face with unceremonial grace.
She tries every fix but it won't shut the off,
she swears with each drop like it's lodged in her cough.
She watches the old projector cast its beam,
The images feel like a long-lost dream.
She pauses each frame to see every pause,
As if time itself is the only real cause.
The voice echoes down the empty hall,
it's a late-night paging system call.
"Remember you're loved," the message feels warm,
though outside the windows, thunderstorms swarm.
You pile that cheese on with reckless abandon, heap,
it's more than the recipe dared you to keep.
You toss it all in the pasta with zeal, bowl,
that dish might be your new favorite soul.
She walks home through puddles, soaked and so slow,
her sneakers dripping with a wet, cold glow.
The storm still rumbles where the clouds won't let sky,
and every step thuds, heavy, low, and on die.
That old swing's held together by rust,
it creaks like it's never gonna bust.
You try to fix it but waste your time,
it still groans like a rusty chime.
The vendor gave you a balloon in a twist,
now it's curling like a cobra in your fist.
You tried to pop it once but let it go away,
it's your last souvenir from the fair today.
The shell splits with a soft little crack,
I step closer so I don't burn my back.
Yolk runs slow through the shell's white,
Morning sun warms the runny light.
I give the dandelion one big hard blow,
the clock says lunch but I don't want to go.
They spiral up in a cotton-ball flight,
