I squeal as one lands in my soda-fizz fright.
She scrolls through her feed when the clock hits noon,
A meme pops up there and she laughs all too soon.
Her phone lets out one quick and proud chirp,
She shares the dumb joke—her desk starts to burp.
You sit with the yarn and your thoughts in a knit,
the quiet grows louder, a peaceful small bit.
The needles make rhythm, a patterned old song,
and time seems to stretch, but it doesn't feel long.
She checks her balance, no room for new cash,
her old habits still whisper promises flash.
The credit card hits its stubborn red cap,
but she's caught between guilt and the debt trap.
That banana's brown but it still wants to show,
peeling like a map of where sweetness once grow.
You take a deep breath—you can't ignore the scent,
and smile as you slice the now-spoiled fruit, slightly bent.
A cart wedged tight where you meant to pass,
with groceries spilling like clumps of grass.
You freeze mid-step—no one wants to stop,
so someone grabs it before it tips the prop.
I wave it around like I run the whole class,
the teacher thinks I've got a clever new pass.
Each tap makes a sound that's both loud and click,
but it's just me showing off—everyday trick.
I've rehearsed the same old jokes and scripted talk,
her face remains a blank, unreadable chalk.
She sips her drink and lets out a long sigh,
then glances at the clock twice in my eye.
I watched my toast go from golden to burn,
I tried to save it but just gave a turn.
The crumb fell right down in the buttered bread,
We laughed so hard we lost our spread.
She moves him slowly toward the faintest light,
he trembles still from his long quiet fight.
His leaves are curled but she keeps him so near,
like saving the last green hope of this year.
This brew's so weak I can't stand the taste,
I need my fix and I need it in haste.
I press the button for a double pump,
but the machine coughs out a sad slump.
I swear I'll turn it off and just let go, but [light]
it feels too bright for dreams or deep enough to [might]
My thumb still moves across the screen's dull [scroll],
and somewhere in the noise, my quiet self is [soul].
She slides the bread in then sets the dial to spot,
the machine glows red and she swears at the dot.
The edges are crisp but the center's now char,
she mutters about how this tastes nothing like star.
The bird outside looks in for a full-blown show,
flapping wildly at the reflection below.
It thinks the glass is some strange magic trick,
but I'm just laughing while it pecks itself sick.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: I caught a flicker of something new—old age,
my reflection trapped in the silvered cage.
It's only a strand but it threatens to show,
a quiet reminder of time working slow.
You dig at the dirt, but it won't go away,
your breath hangs heavy, the sky turns to gray.
You pause and check how much you've still got to done,
the job feels endless beneath the dead sun.
They cut every best moment from the scene,
your breath is caught inside the screen.
You know the ending still lies far ahead,
but the poster says "Rated R for dread."
You wake up soaked where your fur meets the dry,
The cat stares at you with one beady eye.
You scramble to fix it before the fall,
But the water keeps spilling against the wall.
She waves at the smell of the toast taking start,
her first move each Monday, a ritual chart.
The kitchen's all hers when she looks so smug,
sipping coffee alone from her favorite mug.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: You watch the sun trace the curl of its fur,
and wonder what spurs such deep, lazy purr.
One paw taps like a slow-moving log,
you swear it's a dream, but the cat acts the dog.
The sink's full of plates—what a tragic tale,
I stare at the mess and my face goes pale.
I vow I'll do this, I just need some more
willpower than I have or the local store.
I let my coffee sit and slowly spin,
the crack's shaped like a smile, I can't resist a grin.
It seeped into the sink over time like a pool,
but now it's just a relic — stylish and cool.
You grip the leash like it's your last lead,
your dog is yanking you by the head.
You're certain today will be the final fight,
until a squirrel darts into the light.
I tell her this isn't my usual way,
she yells back *you're wrong about today.*
Her raised voice drowns out the radio voice,
but I stick to the route I chose as my choice.
She tosses her note like a dare into the throw,
the plane drifts slow, won't go where she hoped to go.
It wobbles midair in a frantic spin,
she prays it survives the landing on their skin.
She sees a cloud of dust she wants to play,
Her shadow stretches long across the day.
With feline grace, she makes a silent leap,
But the prize was just lint—she lets it keep.
My pencil shavings clogged the tiny blade,
they twirled out like ribbons in a parade.
I gave the handle a stubborn twist,
and laughed at the chaos, like morning mist.
I still have the ticket stub from the show,
but I can't remember why I had to go.
My seat was there, next to an empty seat,
and the theater's cold like it's holding its heat.
Her groceries pile up in the cart—no flat,
she's too stressed about them to even chat.
Her eyes are already feeling too dry,
but she'll wait until she gets home to cry.

topic: seeing your mom's new profile pic
lines: I saw her post—a grin lighting me proud,
Her hair was up, not a worry in her cloud.
She stood alone in the morning wave,
Years melt away, she looks far from grave.
They said you cried when the sad song came streaming,
but your eyes shone like you were still dreaming.
You wiped your face with a laugh, not a sigh,
and told us this was the kind of place you'd cry.
It sits there humming with a faint ring,
Who knew a metal thing could sing?
It strikes a pure and perfect tone,
I'm still here laughing all alone.
Steve grabs the cheese grater, calls it his prime,
he hoists it high like a mountain to climb.
His mission? To cover the pasta with top,
until it slides sideways—ruined. Now stop!

topic: restaurant with no menu in English
lines: You point at the board, try to guess every dish,
your eyes do the work when your tongue can't make wish.
You smile as they bring you warm rye and flat bread,
then laugh at the chaos that fills up your head.
The phone screen goes black mid-play, mid-game,
the character frozen without a name.
You remember the joy when pixels would fade,
to the soft glow of dusk and memories made.
He sidled up where the queue should be,
claiming this spot was his by some new decree.
He called it a shortcut, a smarter kind of way,
but everyone else saw it for the delay.
They send the meme about that old job,
how they'd been trying to quit it or rob.
It brings back the vibe of their early mood,
and the jokes we still laugh over with food.
My shows buffer forever, my Zoom calls won't stream,
I watch the white arrow go round like a dream.
I restart the router, I beg for a byte,
the internet flickers like a bad light.
Your phone lets out a single quiet ring,
the kind of thing that makes your heart skip a string.
You check, then sigh, it's not much of a head,
just someone tagging you in an old comment thread.
She takes off the skin with no trace of shell,
but it leaves her fingers soaked in its smell.
She scrubs through the sink, hands still feel dry,
yet the scent lingers, no one can spy.
A royal spot of frosting rests on your cheek,
you forgot to wipe it after the birthday week.
You flash your grin, proud of the mess you made,
joy lives within such unfiltered, sticky shade.
They reached but missed the falling coffee drop,
a habit they once caught without a crop.
Now their brain's a step behind the scene,
like an old film where the frame rate runs lean.
You set the pan down with a satisfied thud,
it's still too hot to touch or even to mud.
You eye the rim where it might start to bend,
but you'll wait till it cools before you mend.
Your lipstick's still here from the morning's first kiss,
I pretend it was meant for my coffee cup bliss.
I wash it but leave a small stain, just a spot,
your taste lingers here where our moments were caught.

topic: a child drawing on the table
lines: You draw your world in crayon all up,
fingers smudged, abandoning your cup.
A grin appears, like magic, spark by spark,
while art grows bold across the wooden mark.
She taps the button once to make it spin,
a melody plays deep inside her skin.
Her thumb just keeps moving, not a scroll,
but trying to fix something lost in her soul.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: You stand there, frozen in that store aisle,
your best fake grin won't make her smile.
She clings to the wall, her tiny voice cry,
"No ice cream" feels like the end of why.
You paid a ridiculous processing fee,
then waited months for the company to agree.
The check arrives in an envelope from the mail,
but it's so small it could get lost in your meal trail.
You sit up so fast your forehead hits the head,
who's crazy enough to ring the bell so dead?
You grab a bat and pad in barefoot dough,
a raccoon holds a sign that says "Goodnight show."
She watches the river pretend to be calm,
the clouds above melting into balm.
A breeze stirs the water's soft silver light,
and for a moment, the sky feels so right.
You stare at the page and wonder "what now?"
You'll finish this pile by some magic how.
The ticking clock reminds you it's getting clock,
but your brain just turned into a full block.
I paid for this service to smoothly stream,
but every clip feels like a bad dream.
The screen just sits there and it keeps on spin,
I'm wasting time I'll never get back in.
She says it's smarter than a locked-up brain,
her spare key waits out there once again.
It's tucked beneath the mat—no need to hide,
she's got a system, takes true pride.
You crack a joke so clearly old,
we laugh as if we still want to hold.
We don't explain, we just laugh out why,
but your smile feels more like a sigh.

topic: a phone at one percent battery
lines: My phone sits at one percent so low,
It flickers then dies—no more to go.
I trace my old numbers now lost to the sky,
Why didn't I save a single goodbye?

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: You read the review and it calls it the same,
but says your old haunt has a cooler new name.
They didn't get how we loved every brew,
they missed how this place felt so damn true.
You run through the yard, they vanish in air,
your phone's flash blinds the poor little glare.
You swing at the dark with a desperate aim,
it's over by now, the old summer game.
You watch as the first ant sets the lead,
then fifty more rush out to spread.
They zigzag across the sidewalk trail,
carrying crumbs like they're UPS for the mail.
The invoice keeps popping up as due,
you scroll through your bank account in view.
You count every penny, even the gas,
but the clock ticks slower, you fear it will pass.
She holds the grater high above the cheese top,
watching each flake fall as the curls drop.
Her laughter mingles with the sauce's taste,
she sprinkles joy, not a shred goes to waste.
You watched it drip slowly from edge to spread,
you sighed like you'd seen every buttered bread.
The sun hit it just right—look how it turned gold,
now grab a napkin, your breakfast turns cold.
My roommate boasts about his perfect bass tone,
while I wake up in my sleep-deprived zone.
He says I'm sensitive, refuses to share
the bed when his snoring fills every air.
You thought the garden was safe from your plot,
but the rabbit found lunch in your favorite spot.
It doesn't care what your veggies are worth,
it munches your lettuce while you dig in the earth.
She swerves but never leaves her texting zone,
one hand on the wheel, one hand on the phone.
The car goes off the road but keeps on spin,
she mutters "Wait, wait!" through the engine's din.
She texted the group "let's get it done now,"
but no one knows the best way to go how.
One says they'll work till the bulb burns out light,
another just laughs, "I'll fake it 'til it's right."

topic: sending a text to the wrong person
lines: She hits send before she even reads the name,
turns it into a weekend apology game.
Now he's asking what the message meant to read,
and she wishes her phone would just go to bed.
You finish the toothpaste by squishing it dry,
the tube lies defeated, about to die.
You twist off the cap for a sad little cap,
now your hands are stuck in this sticky trap.
The bus isn't here yet—there's always a delay,
it might be ten minutes, it might be ten away.
She hums a soft tune and wears her wide smile,
she strolls through the weather, she savors the while.
Her phone just played the same old "no more tone",
she swore she'd delete messages from her phone.
She blames the signal, the tech, bad luck, or fame,
but every list still shows the same old name.
She watches the bees chase their sweet flight,
the morning glows soft with golden light.
They hover and dart in a wild, mad dance,
as if they're all spinning for love's small chance.
A sugar-coated keyboard from last class's mess,
She taps the escape key but can't even press.
Still, she starts her draft with a shaky hope,
Typing slow and steady as if it were a rope.
I scaled the fence and slipped through the gate,
somehow they never saw me come late.
We stood near the stage where the bass shook the hall,
and swore we'd do it again next time on the wall.
She stares at the grid for another clue,
Her screen glows faint with a bluish hue.
The blank boxes stretch across each page,
And silence wraps tight like a quiet cage.
It strikes a perfect, windswept birdlike pose,
like some celebrity that fate chose.
From every angle, this wire's prime view,
but I'm stuck below with the mess that is me too.
You watch the frozen pizza turn into pie,
the scent reminds you of the summer sky.
You long for the fire of that old heat,
when laughter rolled thick through the city street.
He says the new look is "bold," but it's bad,
a style his barber's been giving since dad.
He asked for a fade with a little more edge,
now he looks like he made a bad hair pledge.
They're stuck with a pencil, point jammed in,
and the old sharpener just sits there, spin.
They tap it with one hand while holding their stand,
as if the machine could read what they demand.
I keep dropping coins into this try,
the machine's mouth stays stubbornly dry.
It won't let a single dollar fit,
but maybe next time, it'll take my bit.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: You trace the faded names in the map's dry ink,
convinced it knows more than you do or could think.
The creases crack, a map made for the fold,
but you still try to read what time won't let hold.
My baby's wailing like a talent show,
and strangers are glaring at my row.
I beam through every sob and cry,
they think I'm cursed—I think I'm fly.
She tapes the password to her monitor's post,
but says she'll delete it once it's on her toast.
She claims it's safe, just out of sight to hide,
but I check my phone from her laptop's side.
She flashes a smile like the camera's her grin,
does a little dance, spins like a pro with a spin.
Her shoes tap out rhythm, they never miss a beat,
as if the whole wide world were her sunny street.
You tilt your head like you're figuring out when,
I'm halfway through my sentence and stop mid-pen.
You wait for the rhythm, the lilt in my voice,
as if your whole world turns on this small choice.
The cat takes a leap toward the dusty heap,
tail high, eyes wide, barely containing the creep.
It pounces and lets out a yowl of pure cry,
mistaking the mess for a mouse trying to die.
I don't know why but this does not fit,
maybe the coffee hit me just a bit.
There's no good excuse, it's not that real,
I just crack up laughing at the whole deal.
They left their cereal alone in the bowl,
the kind of breakfast that feels like your soul.
Milk pools and runs in a thin, cold drip,
and time slips slowly with no big trip.
You showed up five minutes after the scene,
pretending you missed traffic, that old machine.
Your excuse was a flat tire, your only claim,
but we all know it's the usual, the same.
The cashier gives me a friendly scan,
I lay out my groceries as fast as I can.
A coupon falls out from a crumpled clip,
I saved twelve bucks on this shopping trip.
That October wind still blows the way it blew,
just like back then when things still felt so true.
We watched the leaves twirl up into the sky,
not knowing why we'd ever say goodbye.
You drag chairs in to build your secret room,
where stories hang like shadows in the loom.
You drape the blanket low — the softest light,
a fortress where your worries can't come in tonight.
I stuck my hand in the jar without a plan,
the sugar rush will be my downfall, man.
The jar just made a noise—it sounds like crash,
I freeze mid-reach, then bolt for the dash.
You let them fall where they choose, not trying to hold,
each crystal so delicate, yet somehow still bold.
They leave a faint dampness, no need to erase,
just melt into skin with a quiet, cool grace.
The camera says "Not you," but I'm still me,
It needs my face as the new security key.
I've squinted, grimaced, blinked—every trick I've tried,
but now I'm locked out and I almost cried.
That creak you hear is the wind's old sound,
your feet still spin where the chains are bound.
It may show some age, yes, a little rust,
but we built this joy so you never lost trust.
You feel the bike shift and you don't want to slide,
your hands hold on tight but the road won't be guide.
A headlamp glows through the dust and the light,
you steer back to balance, that's progress, not fright.
Their mouth hangs open like a broken screen door,
a battle of breath, one lung at war.
They crash through the silence like a rogue wave,
while I lie awake in this sleepless cave.
She always pays with crumpled-up cash,
the driver and her values clash.
She mutters the fare like a secret prayer,
then counts each cent on the back seat stair.
He's slower now but still knows every game,
the crowd respects his decades of fame.
His moves lack speed, but he keeps his pace,
each step a lesson in calm, old-age grace.
The video won't play no matter how I try,
I waited all day for this moment to fly.
I beg for some sound, but the silence stays loud,
my room feels like a silent movie crowd.
You feel the slow build of a sweet crave,
it crashes like hunger but worse than a wave.
The desk is all emails, no hidden snack,
you're low on willpower and off your diet track.
There's now a huge stain on my best clean spot,
I took a quick photo to save the shot.
I frantically check the mug for any blame,
but the barista's name tag says "Not My Name."
I stepped right through the hall to the wet tile,
the soap slid off my hand in such a short while.
One little move and then—oh, what a slip!
I grab the towel now for extra tight grip.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: She walks through the yard, the webwork's like lace,
each thread catching morning in its right place.
The sun turns the dew into something that glows,
she smiles slowly, then turns and just goes.
I rock the knife from side to side, blade,
the carrots march in lines, my heart a parade.
A tremor shows in every single slip,
I think of skin where one wrong cut might trip.
He checks the fridge, again, for the jug,
no sign of it past where the cat keeps the rug.
A single drip makes a sudden small drop,
so he grabs a carton and heads out to the shop.
Your glue stick has gone where the paper once went,
pages barely stay fastened, a little too bent.
You grip it like magic might still make it hold,
but it's dry and it's dusty, your faithful old old.
My eyes are heavy, this endless task
drags me down—I dare not even ask.
A yawn slips out, I whisper "Just a break,"
while my boss stares like I ordered a steak.

topic: a man reading on a bench
lines: I sit beside him in this quiet park,
the sky growing soft and slightly dark.
He turns each page like it might begin
a story I'm not sure is real within.
She points out the shapes the clouds begin to form,
pretending the sky won't break into a storm.
"Look," she says with a laugh, "there's a fox to see,"
but I know she needs a trick to unlock the key.

topic: a receipt lost in the bag
lines: She swore she still had it tucked somewhere paid,
but time can make memories slowly fade.
She dug through the bag, laughed—no proof was found,
just echoes of coffee and pastry's soft sound.
She checks the clock twice, "It's way too soon now,"
But her brain won't stop asking "Just how?"
Her eyes drift toward the vending machine cake,
She pretends to be done with her bland green shake.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: The web just glows where the morning light goes,
each drop like a pearl that the sun just rose.
She walks through the yard with such careful thread,
and bends down to touch what has quietly spread.

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: The road feels wide when the world is in the wind,
I push forward hard, no time to look behind.
Neon signs flicker in colors too bright,
joy and fear ride together through the night.
You're trying so hard to make a pancake show,
your batter is lumpy, more like half-cooked dough.
You flip them too fast, without even a lid,
it's less of a cook-off and more of a bid.
They walk with a steady, silent pace,
never looking up from their face.
I wonder why we even try,
the only conversation is a sigh.
She's been searching for hours like it's some big game,
yelling the flip-flop's ex-owner's name.
It's lodged in the doorway—a sticky little trap,
no amount of nudging or slapping will slap.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: You woke to the mess of your perfect sprawl,
the room full of evidence, no one to call.
You tied every corner into a knot,
but you'd do it again if you knew what you've got.
We had a perfect scheme to skip class and plan,
but my crush passed me a note that said "Cool man."
I spilled coffee on it—now half the paper's ink,
he'll never figure out I was trying to think.

topic: baking with flour on the floor
lines: I dropped a bag of flour—now I must go,
it's everywhere, like a crime scene of dough.
I try to clean the mess off the kitchen spot,
but only made a bigger powder plot.
She laughs to keep her voice from going tight,
every joke a shield from the bad day's fight.
She leans back slowly, closes her tired head,
while silence wraps around her like a warm, safe spread.
You hold your cup with steady hands,
and wait where the traffic still stands.
Your song has lost most of its voice,
yet people pause — if only out of choice.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: Pastor waves, but we all still sit in the row,
hymns hummed off-key as if we don't know.
Same Sunday crew, same coffee-stained pew,
we've never met, yet we all love it true.
She plants her boots into the stubborn tone,
each step sounds like a sledge against a stone.
The neighbors stop to watch from their backs,
while she carves new roads through the snow's old tracks.
The screen we both watched just froze in mid-call,
We blamed each other, like kids in a mall.
Great tech support, same as every bit of luck,
Wasn't there when we needed it most—now we're stuck.

topic: a man reading on a bench
lines: I turn another page, the wind turns my page,
the book is my escape from this quiet cage.
A memory slips through and my mind runs with thought,
I'm halfway between here and somewhere I've caught.
She turns the dial with a calm, precise set,
Her confidence feels like a smart gamble bet.
It's not just a fix, it's a skill and an art,
Of her home's comfort she plays such a part.
Their soles face the ceiling, stuck in the doom,
two ghosts in the hallway haunting the room.
I once tried to ask where they belonged, though—
she said, "They're just waiting for him to go."
My phone's been ringing since the morning sing,
I left it in my bag like some strange thing.
I keep half-waking up, but never quite awake,
afraid I missed a call, some life or death mistake.
You watch the hawk carve patterns in the sky,
still wondering if it's time to say goodbye.
Its shadow passes over your quiet wings,
and you forget the weight of little things.
I treat my phone like the main event at meal,
its glow has more charm than the table's appeal.
I'll keep swiping fast while they beg me to ignore,
this is how I serve my new favorite chore.
The dog is going full circle and spin,
spinning so fast it's a blur with a grin.
It's a never-ending, wild little loop,
like a solo dance by a pup on a troop.
I stared at the can as if it were myself,
it sat there, defeated, abandoned by the shelf.
It's dented and bruised, this poor little can,
I had a clear plan—now it's soup for lunch, man.
You watch the white clouds roll across the sky,
they move as if time were just passing by.
A whisper of breeze lifts them without a breeze,
you sigh with the calm of pure delight and ease.
I added more soap, but there's no suds, just foam,
we ate with our fingers—no clean plates at home.
I swallowed my pride and I scrubbed every grit,
while the machine hummed, it still did not get it.

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: She scrolls through the post when she should be read,
the review's words are sharp, not worth the spread.
They bashed her go-to spot for coffee and beans,
but she knows the truth's not in five-star greens.
He yells from the cart, "Last chance for a row!"
It's a smoothie that probably won't hold go.
I debate if his pitch was worth my fare,
while choking down pulp that tastes like old air.
She used to live for the thunder of years,
now she tunes out the stadium's cheers.
Her favorite track is a soft, quiet hush,
and silence feels like a better rush.
She glides through the market like a soft breeze,
jingling her grocery bag full of keys.
She spins that cart like she's got wheels to win,
zigzagging through the crowd with such grin.
He's at the window with his eyes on the meat,
I toss it down—then trip on the treat.
He dances around, repeating the scene again,
some days I swear I'm not his person, I'm his train.
I found the milk—leftover from last week, now old,
I thought it might still sparkle with a touch of gold.
I lifted the carton, ready to pour,
but dripped each sad drop straight onto the floor.
You still watch that old streetlight's last gleam,
how its gold light spills down like a stream.
You want to run back and try to hold
it close, but the bulb has long gone cold.
She digs through the closet to find her own style,
holding up pieces that stir up a smile.
There's magic in fabric that fits like a life,
and stories half-told in the seams where it's rife.
You just took my fries without even a take,
I fake a smile and call it "fate or cake."
I'm saving ketchup for your greedy hand,
but you're already out of arm's-length band.

topic: missing a chorus in a song
lines: You tap the screen but the chorus won't play,
it skipped ahead and now you're stuck away.
You rewind again and miss the beat,
the song loops on while you try once more, repeat.
The piece slides into place with a snap,
revealing the path on the world's worn-out map.
A missing clue now makes everything clue,
the picture feels whole, and the design feels true.
She reads each label like she really knows
what's good for her body, down to her toes.
I'll never convince her to just give it a try—
she waits for the science to confirm and reply.
My cat makes another small disaster of mess,
The glittering confetti of things gone to less.
I clean up again while she pats out her home,
A queen through the chaos, content to just roam.
I built whole cities out of wooden blocks,
now watch the minutes drag from work to clocks.
We used to climb that oak and call it tree,
the wind would whisper secrets just for me.
Your pup spins circles, pure unbound joy,
until they flop down near your favorite toy.
They drool all over the cushion where you lay,
but who needs style when life's this good a day?
I stuck a note on the screen to turn light,
"Remember: you're the best tonight."
I'm not here to play or pretend or to fix,
just reminding the world with my brave little tricks.
You toss the crumbs and they flutter straight down,
the pigeons gather from all over town.
They coo soft sounds toward the pale winter sky,
you watch them lift off, each one flies so high.
You think your cat is full of wild play,
darting and leaping all through the day.
But it's really just a shadow-chasing act,
though sometimes it feels like a living fact.
You tried to tear off the plastic with your head,
but the cheese stayed intact, not a bit spread.
Now the foil's twisted in this kitchen mess,
so enjoy your snack—there's no making it less.
The bus is gone and your head hits the clock,
You stare at your coffee, half cold, half rock.
The calendar groans with how far you are late,
Your boss is already in bad-spirited state.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: They press send with passion, full of rage,
The app spins forever, stuck on a page.
They re-upload, they pause, they retry,
The message dies again, their phone might as well die.
My cat thinks this is the highlight of his life,
leaping at a flicker that looks like a knife.
He pounces like it's prey, gives it his full hunt,
then stares at me like he just did a stunt.
She slips into his boots but they don't quite fit,
He hesitates too long and she takes a bit.
Her breath catches when something feels too real,
She wonders if this test was worth the whole deal.
You check your phone again for signs of doubt,
no one replies—your thoughts get stuck about.
The silence builds until some late-night ping,
and you swear it's urgent, though it means no thing.
She watches the dragonfly hover and still,
its wings making patterns that can't last a thrill.
It dips near the pond where reflections kiss glass,
then vanishes into the tall, dry grass.
Someone left their drink, the entire spill,
I now face the wrath when I send out my bill.
It's smudged across the fabric of this seat,
and no dry cleaner's going to fix that heat.
I trace the creases where it once was fold,
a map from my backpack still feels too old.
I follow the paper down every street,
laughing when it curls and begins to repeat.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: They took a single photo of morning's first shot,
where the sky blurs into gold at that perfect spot.
They posted the silence without any pause,
maybe beauty doesn't need reason or cause.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: I watch the morning freeze across the gray sky,
the web a crystal cage where stars will die.
Each strand a silver thread, too thin to tread,
I gasp—this fragile world might break and spread.
They twist the dial to match their mood,
saying it's really just about the food.
But when the room turns arctic cold,
they call you over, acting bold.
I found my old headphones buried in the past,
wires still wrapped around the useless cast.
I trace the tangle back to one lone thread,
the left earpiece doesn't work—it's gone dead.
You laugh as they float in the sky's wide blue,
Each pop says *you* won't catch me, silly you.
The wand gives a swish and the bubbles all spin,
They burst in a dance without rhythm or din.
I watch him circle in place again, just spin,
his joy so loud even I can't help but grin.
He runs in loops that never seem to loop,
a solo dance only he's trained to troop.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: You search for a filter that hides the flame,
the sky's too perfect, looks like the same.
You type then delete—nothing on the post
feels right, so the photo stays a ghost.
She walks where the sidewalk still holds the heat,
her shoes tapping out a soft beat.
The drops fall fast but they don't want to spread,
she tilts up her face like it's welcome in her head.
She zipped up my boots without asking to wear,
said they had a new gait but lacked the air.
He stepped into my loafers, said they'd break,
then left a half-smile where my sock had mistake.
He gets stuck between the cart and the aisle,
pretending the groceries hide his smile.
The cashier rolls her eyes at the crew,
muttering something about "not you."
You wake up proud of the yoga pose,
your head is tilted too far to close.
You try to fix it but nothing feels the way
you want it to, so you start the day.
She built whole worlds out of the plastic past,
Each figure a hero with its own cast.
The tales had no ending, they lived through the lore,
She'd play till it faded, but never felt more.
She searches every room for the cart's lock,
retracing steps she never meant to rock.
The minutes blur as hope begins to spin,
her calm is fading, fraying thread by thin.
You built this tower, sharp and full of pride,
every label neat and perfectly inside.
It teeters but it doesn't seem to want to fall—
your system's tight, and your hands feel small.

topic: a kite stuck in a tree
lines: She watched the kite fade into the sky,
her silent hope turning into a cry.
Now it hangs tangled up in that tree,
a symbol of dreams that never felt free.
I sat there nervous, the clippers began to snip,
he said, "Let's flip it," though I didn't really flip.
A cloud fell on my head, my hair hit the floor,
but now I laugh out loud—how can bad cuts restore?
You read the billboard, bold in its false claim,
a product too good to be true in its fame.
It promises miracles, a life dipped in gold,
you don't believe it, but you're still not sold.
She said she wanted to meet but meant she'd ghost,
Now her phone lights up every time I post.
She stares right through me from the bar's back spot,
I raise a glass—she won't even take a shot.
A toddler sprints after soap suds in blue,
convinced the wind is his best friend who's true.
He leaps through arcs, a ragged dance in full spin,
all sweat and joy and bubble-stained grin.
You stare into the drain, a greasy mess,
convinced your life could use a little less.
You pour in baking soda and let it go,
but deep down you still don't really know.
She sits alone where the water turns dark,
the only sound from the late-night park.
Her shadow waves in the cold lake's cast,
a whisper of fireflies bursts—then gone fast.
I zip all the way up with a stubborn snap,
my thumbs get caught in the metal trap.
I twist and I pull until it starts to roll,
then post it online—it's my victory goal.
You stare into the jug, it's completely dry,
but outside the window the clouds still cry.
You don't know if there's enough to meet your need,
but you pour what's left where a plant might find its seed.

topic: someone spilling punch on the rug
lines: I watched her trip with a silent pride,
the punch sloshed out like slow-motion glide.
Now the rug bleeds color, chaos in mess,
I fake a gasp—this is my little success.
Your glue stick is dry, there's nothing left up,
you tap it into your coffee cup.
A splash of water, a dash to save,
you shake it like hope is something brave.
Your fingers keep finding that perfect beat,
is this a symphony or just chicken meat?
The table is getting the worst of our chat,
soon it will need a massage to stop being flat.
He sits alone inside a silent cage,
flipping through a book he'll never page.
His face is stone, his posture screams "I'm calm,"
but his hand is shaking—check his sweaty palm.
She burns her toast but calls it a delicious mess,
the kind of thing that only feels like a weird bless.
Her laugh catches like fire, bright and flame,
and I forget my own name just watching her claim.
I offered my help when she needed the aid,
her smile said more than a check if it was paid.
We walked through the downpour that wind-blown storm,
and found something shaped like a bond, not just form.
You left your towel on the floor by the wall,
now it lies there in a damp, furry sprawl.
You swore you'd work on your fitness and core,
but this scene just feels gross and a bit of a bore.

topic: a road trip with bad directions
lines: She followed her phone instead of the map,
we drove through a toll in a GPS trap.
The app said "turn left" but the exit was ahead,
now we're lost in a field where it shouldn't have lead.
Your flip-flop is lodged in the hallway shoe,
you try to move it, but don't know what to do.
You pace back and forth, seeking a better way,
but nothing changes the strange hold it's made today.
You weave through the crowd in this narrowest aisle,
holding your groceries so close to your smile.
There's rhythm in chaos where the shoppers all flow,
your cart hums softly along the floor below.
You called to ask if I had your apartment key,
then charged me twenty bucks for the membership fee.
Now you're out here learning which foods you crave,
I text "hi" but you never seem to wave.
It sits there smug with a blackened peel,
pretending it's still worth the breakfast meal.
Its insides used to be bright and gold,
now it's just fruit that's clearly getting old.
A burst of music rises from the sound,
Color spills out like it's all around.
You feel the city turn into home,
For once, you don't want to wander or roam.
You trace the cracks in the ceiling so blank,
the kind that hides your savings up in the bank.
You dream of spending all your stress away,
and waking up relaxed, without a care today.
I left my shoes out overnight in doubt,
the hallway echoes like someone's trying to shout.
I pray to every god for a little luck,
now I'm trapped in one red sock, one blue sock stuck.
She stands near the back where the crowd fills the door,
her thoughts drifting further than she can store.
She checks her phone for the time it will show,
and wishes she could climb out the window and go.
They slip down the glass but they never all fall,
they pool near the sill like a ghost on the wall.
She traces their paths with a fingertip's grace,
and wonders where time left her familiar face.
She brews her third cup since midnight's sleep,
lost in thoughts too loud and too deep.
Her hands cradle warmth, the room feels light,
and for one moment, the dark turns right.
I power down my tablet, enter sleep zone,
but the guy next to me won't mute his phone.
He jogs up and down like it's some kind of aisle,
I count every minute this will take a while.
You blast your old playlist, let the music sound,
hair flying wild and free, loose all around.
The world becomes your backup singer, you sing,
and every note feels like a loose guitar string.
A sound like ice—the shovel strikes a crack,
the blade snaps upward, jolting from the back.
He pauses, stares at the stubborn rock,
his breath hangs still, the motion like a lock.
You stand there barefoot, the floor lets out a crack,
you limp to the couch and don't walk back.
Those chipped bathroom tiles remember every fall,
they've seen your secrets and still keep them all.
She sips her coffee and waits without wait,
clicking refresh while the toast goes cold on the plate.
The screen flickers once, then starts to play,
and she laughs—glad her bad tech day won't stay.
You stare into the water, dark and still,
the moon sits low behind the distant hill.
Shadows flicker where the reeds bend through,
and you wonder if the sky's been dyed in blue.
I cradle the egg, watch the yolk dip and sway,
a crack got too wide and it spilled out this way.
But maybe the mess is a better new shape—
a chance to remix my scrambled lunch escape.
You stood there watching your bag miss the claim,
you searched every belt, every broken frame.
Time ticked inside this forever stall,
you cursed the airline, screamed your worst swear call.
I tap my card and the pump still won't go,
the screen just blinks and the price doesn't show.
I wave my card again at the gas,
but the machine just laughs and says "No such pass."
You let the message sit and slowly ghost,
unanswered as the hours drift and post.
The jokes will fade, but not the regret parade,
a silent thread where you could have strayed.
You raise your plastic ruler high for class,
It taps against your desk made of glass.
Your hand is shaking when you point it out,
The students still look like they have some doubt.
I didn't miss this—somebody gave me a shout,
they redirected traffic to block off the route.
I flipped up my collar and took my own stand,
watching the streetlight turn into a band.
I never asked why the bouncer let me gate,
the crowd was thin since the show started late.
I blend into the background, keep my beat,
but the spotlight turns my cover into heat.
She mixed her morning routine into one quick shake,
the kind of chaos that smooths into a lake.
The powder still dusts the rim like old white,
a ghost of breakfasts she can't quite fight.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: She claims half the couch like it's all her room,
while you sink into your private gloom.
Her shoulder keeps brushing your bare arm,
you pretend it's an accident, not a charm.
We used to play outside till the streetlight yard,
now the screens keep watch like a passive guard.
Our days just spin in the same old loop,
while memories march in a silent troop.
I've wandered away from the checkout aisle,
the cashier waves me back with a smile.
My cart makes a loud clatter, "Let's go, pop,"
I freeze—this line's moving when it wants to stop.
I was fine until the sad song began to stream,
it hit me like a weepy old movie theme.
My eyes got soft, my grin turned sly,
and now I'm sniffling, not sure why.
You lie awake listening to his constant pace,
you wonder if he sees some other space.
Maybe something moves just out of sight,
or hope lives there beyond the quiet night.

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: You weave through traffic stuck in gridlock jam,
Some kid waves you down like some wild scam.
You hit the brakes too late—it's a pothole trap,
The handlebars vibrate with a harsh slap.
My thumb keeps moving, even though it's deep
into the night when my brain should be asleep.
I don't know why I'm still clicking this app—
the stories fade, but I can't just snap.
I check my phone to escape this dead feed,
but now there's a rant about justice and creed.
I try to just scroll but it won't let me scroll,
it keeps making points about the world as a whole.
You love the way socks keep jumping from their jump,
while shirts lie defeated on the closet's stump.
The detergent's a fresh, floral, soft scent,
and you dance through the piles with a happy bent.

topic: hot chocolate on a cold day
lines: You take a warm sip, it melts on your lip,
your boots almost slip from the frost on the trip.
The world outside hums in its quietest snow,
while you curl up inside where the cocoa still glow.
They left the milk out for untold hours,
now the whole kitchen reeks like old flowers.
It seeped through containers, a slow drip, a leak,
the kind of mess you can't fix in a week.
A squirrel buries that acorn real deep,
like it's hiding from time or the end of the keep.
It checks every inch for a thief or a clue,
thinks you know where it is but you don't—so you do.
She types in a whisper, no need to erase,
her fingers have learned every key's old face.
Their memories form in the grooves of the shape,
but time wears them down to a faded escape.
They watch her float through the water the wrong way,
as if some strange peace holds her up through the day.
Her face is a mirror of slow, still grace,
a fish out of time and empty space.
You double-tap a face you don't know from tap,
the heart fills red and you instantly cap.
Was that too bold? Your thumb pauses in feed,
some part of you wants to undo the deed.
I watched the butter slowly work its spread,
thinking how warmth can fix your tired head.
There's magic in the crunch of golden toast,
even a simple meal can heal the most.
My cat curls up where the sunlight hits the beam,
She purrs so loud she seems half-alive, half-dream.
Her paw blocks my work—no way to get the tap,
I laugh and save my file to some other map.
You hum along to the silence on the road,
it feels like your own kind of crazy ode.
You flick the dial hoping it might start to spin,
until the next signal pulls you in.

topic: steaming coffee in a blue mug
lines: You take your time sipping the morning's first brew,
you count the quiet moments left in the few.
A chip on the rim of your favorite old cup
reminds you to sip and to calm things back up.
She belts out karaoke like she's meant to live,
each note a declaration that she is thrive.
You'd think the crack would be a curse to break,
but it's how her truth fully comes awake.
She giggles while she paints with her play,
using mud and stones as her clay.
Her rainbow stretches far and wide,
until the rain washes it from her side.
She never says a word but she always talks,
I catch the meaning in her quiet walks.
Her shoulders drop like a heavy sigh,
and I know her thoughts by the gleam in her eye.
She blows her wish into the bright sky,
the puffball dissolves in a soft goodbye.
The white parachutes drift, they don't want to fall,
but time moves forward and takes them from all.
You wear it slung low in your very own way,
it's never been off since this morning's first day.
One wire's bent tight on the side's little hook,
but you don't fix it—this is how the cool kids look.
You watch the robin strut across the path,
like solving your grass is top priority math.
It pecks then fluffs, a wild and crazy dart,
as if it maps some secret bird behavior chart.
I tried to force it but couldn't get a turn,
the keyhole mocked me—no way to earn.
I sat on the porch and gave it my crack,
then gave up the fight and walked it off my back.
I took a spoonful and winced at the bite,
the cereal had soaked up all the light.
Still, I see promise in this messy day,
maybe this slowness is just a tasty delay.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: Mid-sentence my nose starts to trap,
I fake a cough but it just won't cap.
My face goes hot, I'm dying to flush,
the moment out with a loud, unwanted rush.
I left a wet brush on the edge and made a mess,
I dropped my dress on the floor in distress.
The color looks worse than a scuff on the wall,

She stages battles all the way from town,
where toy cars crash and little heroes fall down.
Her fingers shape a world with fragile life,
but time slips through like plastic from a knife.
You promise to check it before you flip,
but your haste gets the best and you fumble the trip.
A fresh set goes in, and your device finds new life,
no more inconvenient low-power strife.
He twirls the gift bag as if it's his clue,
"Watch this," he says, "I can dance with it too."
His feet hit every beat out of pace,
but he's smiling like it's full of grace.
She stops her scroll to double-tap a post,
not sure what else she's feeding or who's host.
The thumb keeps moving down the endless scroll,
she wonders if this matters or her soul.
You crave a little quiet, clean space,
but the clothes on your floor won't erase
the chaos that's settled like dust and old glue—
maybe it's not just the room, maybe it's you.
I can't keep up, my brain's out of my mind,
they're scrolling so fast, like a storm in the wind.
Not every great name gets a moment in haste,
but I'll cheer when they do, and call it no waste.
I borrow your boots to see how they walk,
you slip into mine while I try to talk.
We laugh when we stumble, we swap every size,
it's funny, but nothing feels quite like a prize.
You launched your plane and it soared and flew,
it caught the light from the window's view.
It twisted in air with such perfect grace,
and landed still flying in someone else's place.
That hard hat has seen every job site clue,
painted sky, dust storms, and pigeon droppings too.
It's a safety code in constant motion, bold,
bouncing down the asphalt like a story told.

topic: laughing too hard at a joke
lines: Her sides begin shaking, her laugh finds a crack,
She loses her rhythm, the beat goes off track.
She's slumped on the couch now, she can't hold back fall,
Her eyes water up, she's too close to the wall.

your eyes turn red—this isn't just a flame.
You wave the chip like some strange piece of proof,
I duck out fast before the chip hits the roof.
I watch the quiet rhythm of its feet,
how sun and shadow shift with every beat.
It balances in tiny feathered grace,
as if this branch were its own special place.
They've got a pack heavy enough to crack
their spine, yet they carry it straight on back.
A whole world spins inside that burdened bin,
all knowledge bound in pages too damn thin.
You watch the fish press their flat little eye
against the glass, not quite wanting to die.
They circle the room in their borrowed tank,
where your silence feels like a public bank.
My neighbor stood fuming beside his trash bin,
I waved with a laugh and a sunny grin.
"We'll sort it all out when both sides are clear,"
he muttered through gritted teeth into my ear.
You stare into the endless TSA row,
trying to guess when we'll finally go.
They ask you to remove your shoelace tip,
while still holding your toothpaste in your grip.
You belt it out like the whole world is free,
hitting every note—right on the key.
The shower steam helps you really beam,
while the walls absorb every last scream.
He said he'd bring the data, but skipped his part,
while the rest of the team scrambled to make their chart.
His share of the work just kind of falls,
like he'll finally show up—still no calls.
You freeze like you're acting out some tragic face,
then panic as the train begins to race.

but the doors close before your excuses show.
He tosses the crumbs like he's trying to cast

a hush in the air as if all is unclear.
You charge across with the green man in lead,
but step on a skateboard still whirring and dead.

you laugh at the chaos you're certain won't last.
I bought a dozen pairs at the clearance price,
paid only once—no need to pay twice.
I brought them home in a single box,
now they're spread out everywhere in socks.
The bus takes a new turn without giving a route,
but you don't panic—you handle the doubt.
Your shoes hit the ground, strong and with feet,
the city can't shake your confident beat.
A plastic bag flies where the crows would wind,
it flaps and twists but doesn't seem to mind.
We could have saved it, but we left its fate
for squirrels and beetles to quietly debate.
It still plays from my phone on shuffle replay,
the same chords now feel older with each decay.
I skip the chorus, but the melody's a ghost,
the one I listen to when I'm alone, the most.
You hear the ground resist with a brittle crack,
the shovel slides off, still on the same old track.
You lift it again like some broken-down claw,
but winter's got rules you can't bend or ignore, law.
That bird outside has the worst morning call,
it's shrill, it's early, and you want to sprawl.
You mimic its tune but have zero clue
how birds figure out what they're supposed to do.
You waited through chaos and stress at the claim,
your bag lost somewhere beneath some old name.
Now you're dressed in a hotel's spare for the delay,
hoping your suitcase will vanish that way.
My camera's got perfect focus but no eye,
it captures the truth but lets the story lie.

while I forget how I lost my own point of phase.
A warning popped up, my laptop's too hot to stop,
It's melting the couch where the heat starts to crop.
The fan spins like a jet but the vent still won't vent,
I texted "I quit" but it never got sent.
I tried to keep it neat and contained at the start,
but now it's flying out like a frayed-out heart.
I can't get it back on without a lot of roll,
this tiny mess is turning into such a whole.
She acts like she can't hear the faucet's show,
though it's been going nonstop since morning's flow.
She says she doesn't know how it still knows
to drip at just the worst possible goes.
She owns this whole space with the mic in her air,
It's not just a duty but something so rare.
Her voice cuts through noise like she's shouting to shout,
The crowd stops to listen, they've got nothing to doubt.
She gently removes the clove's dry skin,
the layers fall off like the years grow thin.
There's something so quiet about this small life,
she pauses a moment before the knife.
I watch him toss crumbs in the park,
the sky turning gray and getting dark.
He speaks to the birds as if they'll shout,
his eyes full of fear, I guess I share his doubt.

topic: paying a fine at the window
lines: He rolled up to the booth with a grimace and stop,
his shirt too small, his cuffs in the crop.
He fumbled through pockets but found no cash,
just loose change and a flicker of flash.
I spent hours filling this grid with a clue,
only to realize none of it's true.
My pencil's now worn down to the ink,
but the final answer still won't make a link.
I've been waiting days to get my grade,
now it's marked missing—what a trade.
I check my inbox, the teacher said "no email,"
I storm into class with smoke up my tail.
You taped the password to the side of the door,
now every guest can log in and restore.
The ink is already beginning to fade,
they'll swipe your signal in their daily parade.
She's turned the volume all the way up and off,
belting out "Happy Birthday" through a cough.
Her voice cracks the silence that wraps this meal,
but it's her kind of joy—imperfect and real.
I press the bulb between my thumb and whole,
the skin slips off like a second soul.
I think about what it means to not feel break,
how small acts might yet help the world to wake.

topic: the smell of pancakes in the morning
lines: You throw the window open, nose held nice and wide,
deny you ever cooked something to hide.
Syrup drips in globs off the plate, a sticky mess,
but hey, you tried to cook something to impress.
A shopping cart spins in circles all around,
I try to steer it back where it was found.
But the grocery store lacks a clear-cut flow,
now I'm pushing chaos on display to show.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: My dog wears a party hat tilted just so,
he bounces around wanting to go.
We twirl together, the floor starts to spin,
the whole neighborhood sees me grin.
The train doors won't open, I'm stuck near the door,
I've been wedged in this space all the same old sore.
Everyone's standing, but someone took my seat,
The AC's dead, and I'm melting from heat.
She moves like she knows every step is wrong,
her feet are too fast, too loose, too long.
The music keeps going, but she's lost the beat,
her cheeks grow red under the oven's heat.
You blamed the kid for the sticky red spill,
though it clearly oozed from your coffee cup still.
You call it an accident, but it's just a mess,
one stain closer to the car being worth less.
You watch the water inch down slow, no flow,
the pebbles of grime still stubbornly glow.
The morning light fades into something like dusk,
while you wait for the pipe to give up its husk.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: They check their phone under the bedroom glass,
another pointless scroll through likes and class.
One less follower and they feel the lack,
too scared to put it down and turn it back.
She never could stay on her New Year's track,
she'd skip the gym and text you for a snack.
It wasn't a failure, just life taking slip,
a warm chair and a book felt better than grip.
I turned around halfway to the gym,
my mind a deadweight on every limb.
The track was mine if I had wanted to run,
but now the day feels half-undone.
She rattled off items from memory's sharp head,
milk, eggs, and the loaf she forgot was dead.
Her method's a proud, chaotic theme,
she shops by instinct like thoughts in a stream.
The bell rang twice before he hit the bell,
his backpack full of toast and yesterday's hell.
He swore he'd left his shoes right where he'd find,
but they were stuck together, taped behind.
There's a sugary mess where my bowl used to be,
I'll never guess how much sugar went free.
I tried to wipe it but now it's like tide,
the milk has seeped into cracks I can't hide.
She twisted the knob but found not a single clue,
the glass stayed put, reflecting every dull hue.
Her fist pounded the dash like a trapped little scream,
while the car sat there, a rusted-out dream.
Your sneaker flaps like a drunk jaywalker's lace,
and every stride slams your rhythm off its place.
You don't admit it, but deep down you take blame,
the shoe's got more grit than your whole running name.
She pulls out an outfit like a lost crown,
the kind they don't make anymore in town.
Every button tells a story down the thread,
she walks forward like history's walking ahead.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: One hand hovers near the edge,
while the other makes no pledge.
The silence gets a little deep,
no one speaks—just breathe and keep.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: My punchline bombed yesterday in the heat,
I'm replaying it now like a lost weekend treat.
I can't help but repost what I once tried,
even if it splits no one's face with a side.
They swear it's not some wild or spooky real,
just caffeine and the last half-eaten meal.
But their chest keeps drumming like it's caught the heat,
pacing till dawn on an empty street.
You hover so light, but you're staying so near,
your colors remind me of summers last year.
Your wings brush the petals, the pollen will cling,
you carry the promise of growth and of spring.
She waves off the tip and insists on the claim,
not letting the waiter guess her name.
She pulls out her card, swipes twice to round,
then leaves the bill split with nothing left on the ground.
You sighed when we got stuck behind a slow glide,
called it fate trying to make us both hide.
You leaned toward me, hair still full of sun,
and whispered "this trip was meant to be undone."
You watch the lights fade as the ferry leaves dock,
the gulls still cry out from their salted rock.
You sit on the pier where the shells used to lay,
the tide drags your shadow further and away.
Your tire went soft near the edge of the flat,
you sighed and sat down for a brief chat.
A jagged little rock stuck in your stone,
you fix it and ride off in the same old tone.

topic: a road trip with bad directions
lines: She followed the route on her broken phone map,
but the app led her far down a country trap.
The gas tank ran low past each lonely mile,
yet she laughed through it all, with a stubborn smile.
I need my morning cup to truly burn,
its bitterness is how I feel I turn.
It's more than just a drink—it goes so deep,
a dark, warm habit I'm afraid to keep.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: I post the sky because there's nothing to share,
just that hot pink light stuck in my glare.
My finger hovers—no caption feels click,
so I wait until the likes come in real quick.
I watched the king fall, but it wasn't my game,
the move was bold, and it carried your name.
We both laughed out loud—it was pure fun, no cheer,
I righted the piece, kept the win just too near.
I stared at the screen from my local bank,
it listed my funds as a social rank.
My account's new status read "deep in debt,"
while someone else flew off in a private jet.
They take one bite, then go to your hand,
as if you're the reason they're double-brand.
You glare through the grease on your fingers' oil,
but they keep sneaking fries just to spoil.
You wipe the glass but the streaks still burn,
the mirror mocking how you've yet to turn.
Your sweat drips down and it blurs the pool,
you forget why you came—it's not a tool.

a message left without an end.

what's in there, tucked inside your head.
They fall like confetti, painting the ground,

A whisper or something I want to cry,
the brittle, brown echoes crunch as they dry.
You run in circles like your world is spin,
but even chaos feels good when you grin.
It's just a game, a habit, a loop—
but freedom starts inside this small coop.
My dog gets a kick out of this daily sight,
the mailman's briefcase bolts into flight.

though he's never seen anyone else around.

the clock ticks faster than the turning of a page.

a little slower, like gears without steel.

The bus sways off path, taking a wrong route,
And no one aboard dares question it out.

a sharp, repeated rhythm, faint and fall.

he mistook for open air, a lost chance.

it spills across the water in a silver hill.

while stones sit quiet where you once skipped a rock.
I twisted the handle but never found key,
the chain stayed solid, not easy to free.

while strangers nearby hid smirks in their grin.

lines: She forwards me something without a send,
just a cat on a couch with a grumpy old friend.

topic: a child drawing on the table
lines: The kid makes art with total joy,
turning pasta into a crayon toy.

each smudge a way to just express.

they catch the breeze with some strange chance.

it laughs when they finally drift away.

turning chaos into her favorite space.

now they're stuck wandering the halls to roam.

His hands hang loose off the big bus's wheel,
the dashboard hums with a steady steel.

as miles stitch slow at the fabric's seam.

no movement, no flashing, no signal, no cue.

your fists were clenched tight all through the night.

your body claimed this room as its sweat-soaked roof.
She spent an hour on the laces, it took,
but every step made her stumble and look.

and now she walks through the day in quiet gloom.

we've sat there together many a time and oft.

the world spins outside on some distant street.

I tap on the dash, then I shake it for ride,

a moment you weren't sure would be your fate.
You catch your breath and keep your calm hold,
your body remembers how not to fold.
She flies above the ground on a swing of air,
her laughter says she's going to go so dare.
The wind gives her a push, it helps her lift,
like joy was always meant to be a gift.
She leans down with her only working key,
drops a coin in the metered parking fee.
She blames the cold rust not her old bike's frame,
swears she'll get a new one—next week, same name.

lines: She digs into it with a spoon and a brain,

a quiet worry now lives in the fill.

Your bag isn't there from your late flight,

A maze of tags and a lost-luggage lab.

a melody stretching way too long.
The water still falls in the same steady drop,
but your voice is the thing I wish would never stop.
She frowns at the laces, determined to bow,
each loop a battle she's never known how to go.
Her little shoes sit, waiting to be shoes,
while her hands discover the secrets they choose.
You circle dates as if they're matters of fate,
rewrite each event in pointless debate.
Your scribbles bleed through the page in red ink,
the mess connects you to this cursed time link.
Your morning starts with toast and your smoke alarm,
it feels like a fire's breaking out at your farm.
You scoop up the remains, it looks more like char
than anything you'd serve to a hungry five-star.
You wish you could walk where the dogs run wild and free,
but yours would rather bolt down the alley to flee.
We took a quiet trail far from sidewalk and path,
hoping exercise would keep us both from wrath.
You still remember the taste of that tree,
how the crunch felt so good, so perfectly free.
You pause on the sidewalk, take a slow walk,
hoping the quiet inside might begin to talk.
I step outside and my soles start to burn,
the sun's a cruel thing, it feels like an urn.
I should have worn shoes for this kind of heat,
but now I'm just cursed with this burning defeat.
You snatched the fries from my burger-bun hand,
"You didn't even try to stop me," they demand.
I played it cool, like I didn't mind it or act,
but truth is, your theft? I'm kind of proud of that fact.

topic: a child's drawings on the fridge
lines: You taped every picture high and wide,
each one a memory stuck on the inside.
Fingers smudged the paint in every hue,
now framed by time, they still come into view.
You watch them dart like secrets through,
their silver bodies flicker close to you.
I wonder if they dream of being cast,
or if they're stuck forever in our past.
He jabs a finger in the glass between the face,
like this is some high-stakes commuter race.
The doors are shutting, he's too far to get near,
but he shouts right into my ear.
I wipe the glass but the world stays a mist,
my hands grip tight as the road makes a twist.
There's no sign or map, no hint of a clue,
I drive through the fog, barely moving through.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: I posted a joke but no one gave crack,
my screen still sits silent with no replay or track.
The comments are dry, it's going straight dead,
I'm second-guessing my punchline in bed.
You open the mailbox and give it a slap,
expecting junk mail, but it's a payment trap.
A notice says your bill is long overdue,
and they're considering legal action to sue.

topic: someone handing you a surprise gift
lines: You're standing there with this awkward hand,
and out from your sleeve pops a rubber band.
I wait for the punchline, but it turns to joke—
it's floss! I laugh till I almost choke.
The wind isn't helping—it's really to blame,
tossing red and brown like a dying flame.
I keep raking them all into a pile, down
where the kids play soccer without a frown.
She walks with a chill in her step like a breeze,
her laughter slipping from her pocket keys.
Her cheeks are pink from the wind and the cold,
but she smiles like she's got the whole world bold.
You watch the preview, just one more scene,
the lights dim softly against the screen.
A shadow moves toward you, a silent storm,
your breath holds steady in its new form.
She wakes to a crick in her sleep-tangled hair,
curled in a strange pose she can't help but bear.
Her toes won't curl right, her chin's in the blame,
still half in her dream where she whispers his name.
My screen's shattered like confetti in glass,
but I'm still trying to pass this dumb quiz in class.
My answers are guesses—no logic, no clue,
the moment I clicked, my confidence just flew.
The smoke curls up from your charred breakfast fire,
you smile—this is how you used to aspire.
You let the bread burn, savor the dark burn,
and toast turns to art when Monday starts to turn.
She clicks play once more, hoping for a chance,
the screen still twitches like a broken dance.
Her phone just stares with a judgmental moan,
no sound, no shame—it's the vibe, the tone.
You tap through posts long after midnight's through,
your screen the only thing that feels so true.
You laugh at memes you'll never show your grin,
some quiet joy lives deep inside your skin.

topic: a note tucked inside a card
lines: She skipped the main message and went straight to read
the tiny postscript scrawled near the head.
It said "Love, weather" — the ink barely ink,
she filed it away without really think.
They sip black coffee under a flickering light,
the quiet between them feels like a fight.
Their tired eyes scan the empty chairs,
counting hours that were never theirs.

topic: a receipt lost in the bag
lines: She's hunting through the bag for some small trace,
her brow furrowed, something on her face.
"Why do I keep you waiting?" she asks me why,
and I pull out the receipt, then let out a sigh.
They walked past racks, too tight or too wide,
not caring if the world could watch them hide.
In the last store, something finally fit—
a quiet joy that couldn't be a bit.
You watched the ants in their steady small,
a line that never let the progress crawl.
A pebble lay there, a threat to their fate,
you paused to wonder if to step or debate.
You said you'd water it but never gave it talk,
then blamed it when it browned from stem to walk.
You moved it twice this week for more sun,
now it's a corpse, and you're not even done.
I check my phone but the sky steals my reply,
lightning strikes every message I try.
A loud wind mimics a ghost's sharp knock,
I count my breaths until morning's in stock.
He bolted up quickly from lying in bed,
his vision went black like the power had dead.
The room took a turn and began to spin,
he sat right back down where he just had begin.
It made a soft sound as it met the hot crack,
I watched the yolk stay whole, no sign to track.
The broken shell let through the pale white,
like morning bleeding slow into the night.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: You were halfway through a story, warm and flow,
when a sneeze hijacked your moment to show.
Words tangled in laughter, and you nearly choked,
your sentence now fading like something smoked.
They used to grate the cheese into a heap,
slow circles over noodles, soft as sleep.
Now every meal feels short on that same dust,
their old grater gathers quiet rust.

topic: missing a chorus in a song
lines: You tapped your foot for the chorus to play,
but the beat cut out and it all went away.
You rewind the track, but now you miss
the part where the song starts to mean the most to this.
Your screen gives a warning in blood-red dash,
You panic and count your last bits of cash.
Your pulse thumps like thunder in every vein,
You power down apps while the seconds pour rain.
You follow the sugary scent down the trail,
your shirt now a map of where your hand went pale.
You try not to lose your balance or your grip,
but gravity laughs as it gives you a slip.
A bird outside thinks it's seeing the same,
and flaps at my window like a silly old frame.
I laugh as it dives and then zooms back to show,
how high it can fly though it's stuck in this below.
They always squeeze the toothpaste from the squeeze,
a morning ritual with flair, not a breeze.
It's their chosen way to begin every day,
a small act of pride they won't delay.
You eat your lunch like it's something to meal,
you savor each bite, slow and real.
Your head hits the desk or a soft borrowed chair,
but who cares if you snooze? You earned that small care.
You'll never know how long you hid that dark
stain on your shirt until someone makes a remark.
It's fading fast, just give it time to fade—
or toss it now and let your fashion be your aid.
I tap my card at the counter with my name,
"Double-check," he says—"not the usual same."
My fingers shake as I lift the hot spill,
"No ice," he warned, but I didn't hear it still.
My card doesn't work — it says "no chip,"
A decade ago I could pay without a trip.
I fumble for cash, but my wallet holds no code,
The gas station slams shut — I'm stuck on this road.
She watches the leaves dance with the wind,
her back to the party, quiet and behind.
Her laughter is loose, like an old thread,
coming unsewn from a promise once said.
They shimmer and vanish with one final pop,
the breeze slows down, the moment seems to stop.
I want to run after what I can't see,
but fear grabs my fun before it can be.
Your breath turns hazy against the glassy view,
you didn't mind how the morning mist grew.
You laugh as your fingers wipe circles on the dash,
and joke about selling the car for cash.
They send "u up?" when the whole world feels late,
like midnight is some kind of cruel fate.
Their phone lights up the dark with a hum,
but your thumb freezes—what do you say, dumb?
She still buys the huge tub, same buttery taste,
half the kernels stay uneaten, a guiltless waste.
Her eyes track the story but not the screen,
she's thinking about how it doesn't quite mean.
A knight falls to the table in sudden clash,
I flinch like it's some tragic final dash.
The board remains unshaken, moves as still,
but I'm stuck in this drama I simply will.
They don't quite fit but she tries them fit,
laughing at how they pinch just a bit.
He knows what it's like to not want to give,
but still, he hopes they'll both learn to live.
She watches the butter drip down in a slow,
transparent river where the heat begins to flow.
The morning light hits it like a sun,
she savors this quiet joy just for one.
You watch the clouds go by without a pace,
they float in some distant, dreamlike space.
Their shapes fill the sky, but never stay long,
and you wonder why your thoughts are so slow and wrong.
I missed your text when the screen went to show,
the battery died while I was going below.
I found my phone by the kitchen wall clock,
but the lateness still gives me a silent shock.
You check your phone for the sunrise view,
but fog just makes you lose the road in blue.
Your coffee cools as you drag your pace,
pretending this isn't your daily race.
You watched your favorite show and the coffee cup
tipped without warning, brown trickling up.
A dark spot bloomed fast where your shirt once was stain-
free, but you laugh and say it won't happen again.
She asks now what you said—I heard it so slow,
the words just slipped by like the years she doesn't know.
Her ears used to catch every word as they fall,
but now she just leans in when you say her name, small.
My mom would braid my hair and bring it rose,
She hummed old tunes from those long-lost shows.
Pancakes stacked high with syrupy cream,
I used to think this perfect world was a dream.

topic: singing along to a car ad
lines: You hum the jingle that feels like a dream,
It streams through your speakers in a neat stream.
You imagine yourself miles far ahead,
"This ad didn't lie," you quietly said.
One headphone cord loops loosely down his thread,
he's got the song all queued, ready to spread.
I ask him if I might join in this bit,
he says, "Sure," but it's a half-inch too tight to fit.
I spent the evening doing nothing but talk,
we laughed, we gossiped, we did some crazy walk.
There was wine and cheese and far too much meal,
now I'm drained like a robot that's lost all its steel.
I made a joke when I tried to cut,
the cheese slipped off, it hit my gut.
We split the slice, we ate it half,
the mess was bad, but better laugh.

topic: finding a dollar in old jeans
lines: I found a dollar in the jeans I rarely spot,
a crumpled bill from some forgotten slot.
It feels like luck could still come true, my dream
is real — if only for a moment, a stream.
You glance out the window, the whole sky is black,
The wind howls like something trapped in the crack.
The power just died — your screen suddenly took,
A flash of lightning gives you one sharp look.
They serve the cold omelet that tasted the same,
each plate is stacked with a brand called by name.
The waffles are bleached into pale, starchy blend,
I swear I would pay to just skip this whole end.
You watch the waves take the umbrella's slow drift,
while salt and the breeze give your shoulders a lift.
The legs are stuck now, half-buried in sand,
but you keep them upright with your patient hand.

topic: a phone at one percent battery
lines: You feel the weight of certain doom
as you stare down your last percent in your room.
You cancel plans, abandon every task,
and beg the bar to rise with one last ask.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: She froze when she saw her face on the screen,
captured in a moment not meant to be seen.
Her cheeks flushed with a quiet, sudden shame,
as comments piled up under her name.
The instructor called it a learning mess,
but I wouldn't call this any kind of success.
My fingers slide between the smudged keys,
I type like a disease the screen can't seize.

topic: a bus stop shelter at dusk
lines: The setting sun gives the world a soft light,
you climb onto the bench to gain some height.
A gust of wind hits your face—*ah, a sneeze!*
You drop your bag, fumble for your lost keys.
You've tried three shirts and none of them fit,
but something feels close—just not quite it.
You hold it up to the mirror's thin seam,
and wonder if perfect is enough to dream.
She mapped the ant trail inch by careful path,
turning tiny legs into a perfect math.
The crumbs were hers to conquer, her rightful crown,
the whole sidewalk bowed where she walked the town.
I've seen you try to keep your face so calm,
but you trace the table's edge from left to palm.
Your eyes scan the mess, your thoughts out of mind,
like a receipt could catch something in the wind.
You admire the dark bloom of the bread's mold,
the way it whispered growth stories it had been told.
You leave it alone in the open-topped bin,
like art that thrives quiet and wild within.
You try to think your way out of the ache through
a fog of deadlines and the kind of blue
that only comes when you finally stop to calm
your forehead gently with your own soft palm.
She scribbles secrets in the margins, jabs
at silence with a pencil, flipping tabs.
It's not about the words or the ink,
it's that I can't just shake this attitude thing—think.
You light a candle pretending it's a fire,
but the glow won't bring back your old desire.
The bed feels like a wall now, cold and tall,
and silence has been winning every call.
She flipped the egg with a confident flip,
the yolk stayed round—no messy little trip.
The cracked shell held firm, the whites in their shell,
she cooked it perfect, a morning's small spell.

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: I tap the screen to adjust the frame,
then wonder why every shot looks the same.
There's no one here to fill this space,
so I erase my face and save it in case.
I left this crossword without a single clue,
the blanks now feel like truths I can't undo.
It's been too many days since I began,
some answers turned to phrases I still can.
The room's cold like the Arctic, no warm air,
their breath hangs frozen, eyes full of glare.
Their fingers go numb from this brutal freeze,
they swear they have caught some unknown disease.
I trace their path with dust on the line,
careful not to crush what's under mine.
They carry crumbs like purpose and soul,
but one step from me, they vanish as a whole.
You watched it get taken right from your near,
the same thing has happened about five times this year.
You rub at your key ring, your hands on the tire,
and wonder why parking still feels like a fire.
She moves without speaking, lets her body sway,
we watch the light fade from the quiet day.
A heartbeat, a breath—no need for a sign,
her fingers stay curled in the palm of my mine.
I bought this cheap umbrella to stay dry and soak,
now every branch feels like an ancient oak.
It bent and then twisted with a loud pop and snap,
I'm drenched and annoyed in this storm's endless trap.
I found my old jar tucked inside the room,
dust now where paprika used to perfume.
It's time to repurpose, make a new plan,
maybe plant succulents, impress my fan.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: He posted the joke in the wrong place and air,
getting only a few glances and glare.
But he still hits "share" one more time to try,
hoping someone someday will finally reply.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: I wake to find it half off the floor,
it bled from the edge where I tore.
I reach but the corners won't catch,
the wind tries to steal it, I snatch.

topic: a note tucked inside a card
lines: She found a little note folded tight with much love,
tucked under a photo from way up above.
She paused just long enough to sit down and read,
and smiled because the words wanted her to lead.
She doesn't hide the fact that she's a softie in time,
Her eyes well up with every lonesome chime.
There's strength in her tears, they're not fake or real,
She dries her face and heads out for a meal.
You barge into the middle of this scene,
as if this is your daily routine.
Your smile fades when we don't move on your dash,
you thought the line was waiting just to crash.
She wipes her daughter's tears without a clear aim,
the moment caught in a shaky selfie frame.
Her hands are steady, but they won't stay dry,
she wonders now if she can never say why.
You swipe through the feed, too tired to even read,
each post screams to fix the world or just to plead.
A cat video pops up, you pause for a while,
the screen feels like a mile between truth and smile.
She sipped the airport brew at double the price,
her phone buzzed orders from some faraway device.
A tiny curl of steam rose from her cup,
and for a moment, the dull world lit up.
These leaves think they're putting on some kind of show,
dancing wildly as if they control the flow.
They don't have a clue what they really want to say,
just windblown mess trying to blow me away.
She checks the app, but it's stuck in the block,
the bus makes a U-turn around the rock.
She laughs out loud as it finds a new route,
her calm was a bluff—she had zero doubt.
Each evening it glows with a steady wide beam,
casting shadows across every passing stream.
It flickers but keeps shining through night's cold light,
a lone sentinel flashing its ironclad might.
You let the peel turn dark and gold,
