it's bruised and soft but you still hold
a flicker of joy in your kitchen light,
you won't throw it out—its rot feels just right.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: It sleeps so peaceful, all tucked and curled,
as if the chaos outside was unfurled.
The sun hits just right through its soft fur,
but peace still holds tight — not one body stir.
I watched the egg white spill from the shell,
the crack echoed something deeper than hell.
There was still a flicker of yolk left in gold,
like memories that feel both fresh and old.
You scurry quickly, acorn in tow, away,
Puff your chest out like a prize on display.
This hiding spot is perfect — look at you now,
Do you think I don't know exactly how?
You stepped into the storm without a sky,
now every sock is soaked and ready to die.
Your shoes scream for mercy from your feet,
but the humid air won't bring any heat.
I wiped their faces full of cake and dirt,
they chase each other, no time to be hurt.
One yells because the dog took the ball,
I text my wife it's time for the call.
Her gym bag slipped open, contents all fell,
I watched her face crumple — there was no way to tell.
A water bottle slowly began to leak,
I offered to help while she hid her weak week.

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: You feel the snap but it's just an old strain,
it coils there tight, refusing to remain.
Your work is done, but the band still twist,
a ghost of glue, pretending to exist.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: They posted a meme they clearly had tried,
the comments all mocked how the whole thing had died.
Now they're begging you — just don't hit "share,"
this joke's out of gas, and it smells like stale air.
The teacher's cough takes over the whole class,
echoing through rows like a paper pass.
We hold our breath to hear the sudden hush,
then laugh until our cheeks go red and flush.
She drives around trying to find the grid,
the signal's gone cold since she last slid.
She rolls down the window, hoping it won't fade,
but even hills won't help this bad-grade.
She stares at the ceiling as the dark fills the room,
some shadow seems ready to drop from the loom.
Her fingers grip tight, trying to hold out the pull,
but fear's getting louder, her chest feels too full.
I read the label twice but missed the list,
there's something strange in this ingredient twist.
I thought I had a solid food truth knew,
now I'm staring at the can with zero clue.
You piled your fries up in a neat little plate,
but your sibling called it the universe's fate.
You turned away for just one quick little nap,
and came back to find it was all just a trap.
I scaled a fence and slipped through the gate,
arrived just in time to be flagged as late.
The guard followed me down every aisle,
I kept a calm face, but it wasn't a smile.

topic: seeing a post from your childhood home
lines: I saw a photo tagged on my old street,
where I learned to ride on wobbly feet.
The house still stands where I once grew,
but now it's a museum—everyone's view.
You stare at the screen, wishing for cash,
your wallet's just lint and a cracked phone smash.
A life bought in installments, now you're less,
of what you once were—just a financial mess.
They watched her slice with a steady knife,
each chop echoing louder than life.
Salt air swirled like a memory sea,
but the knife slipped—she's not quite free.
I trace my steps along this old stone age,
each rock feels like a scene from some forgotten stage.
I used to sprint down here, now I barely walk,
but the moss remembers how we used to talk.
You bought these shoes because they said "they'll fit,"
but now you're stuck trying to find a place to sit.
You swore you'd never fall for "comfy all day flat,"
your feet are mutiny, they've had enough of chat.
You watch the hawk wheel silently above,
its shadow fleeting, a wish you can't love.
It glides on the wind with a sharp, wide wing,
while silence descends like a quietest sting.
You meant to capture this perfect day,
but left your camera far from your stay.
You missed the first light, the best of the shot,
though memory fills where the photo forgot.

topic: finding a five in the couch
lines: You thought maybe you'd find a crisp little bill,
but all that's there is dust and an old pill.
You could always use it to buy something new—
this chase for cash has no clean ending in view.
My dog insists we race through the run,
she thinks it's a contest, not just a bit of fun.
She leans so hard I can barely tug,
and I'm half-dragging her, like a silly old mug.
You'll fall asleep in five minutes, you claim.
But here's your face in morning light—full of shame.
Your phone still glows with its cracked old screen,
and dreams you'll never live to actually mean.
I count the coins like they're worth a whole lot more,
I pass the mall but don't even go to the store.
These days I think twice before I choose to spend,
my wallet's a fortress, locked down to the end.
She makes eye contact with no one but her eyes,
the group chat scrolls, she posts something wise.
The post goes viral just ten minutes late,
Her boss walks by — oh, the cruel twist of fate.
They hit send before they read the post,
now the whole school's laughing down the coast.
It was a clear social media fail,
but the teacher stayed strangely calm and pale.

topic: a quiet moment on the porch
lines: You call it peace but really mean the breeze,
which rustles just enough to mock your tease.
You sip your coffee with a long sigh,
then text how perfect this little lie.

topic: waiting for the bus in rain
lines: She checks her phone for the app's next soon,
humming a quiet, half-known tune.
Rain slides down her coat but not all the way through,
her patience stays calm, not washed out to blue.
It comes to me still when the wind moves through,
carrying the scent of the trees where we grew.
That golden afternoon light, warm and slow,
I'd give anything now to be there and know.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: I'm ten minutes late for my shift at the park,
some kid drops by with a snot-nosed little remark.
"Have you seen this balloon?"—the child lets out a cry,
its string still tangled in a branch up high.
She runs the path where the morning is trail,
her breath a ghost against the sky's pale.
One shoe comes loose, but she won't stop to lace—
she turns it into something faster than race.
I tap "fast delivery" like it makes it fast,
but the clock keeps ticking and time moves passed.
The promise of free returns is cold and free,
my stomach growls—this waiting is a plea.
You chew the chip and hear the salted crunch,
your body's still half-full from breakfast punch.
But then the weakness hits—you finally cave,
and swipe for the dessert that feels like a wave.
She sleeps curled up like a child having a dream,
her breath soft as the water in a stream.
By morning the pillow's still warm from the night,
soaked through where her heart pressed it good and tight.
The conductor can't explain this morning's delay,
the digital board just shows a red display.
My coffee sloshes over the brim on the floor,
while the engine growls like a clockwork roar.
A pounding starts where my forehead should brew,
My thoughts roll in like a bad movie cue.
I scan my schedule — there's nothing to scan,
But somehow my brain still finds work to plan.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: You tuck it tight, smooth out each soft fold,
like your touch can fix every wrong or cold.
Morning light creeps in where the blanket fall,
and reveals how deeply it still covers all.
She swore she'd be fit if she stuck to her plan,
but forgot her leggings when she hurriedly ran.
She walks fast now, hoping it counts as a pass,
just so she can say she made gym time today, class.

topic: a neon sign buzzing at night
lines: You watch the neon flicker in the light,
its buzz turning louder, sending you a fright.
Your pulse keeps time with the uneven beat,
as static rises, building into heat.
Your smartwatch keeps buzzing, but it should be off,
you're not even sick—you just had a cough.
It screams "emergency" with a false alert,
but all it's done is make your wrist feel hurt.
I crept up to the cookie jar,
my hand out like a thief from afar.
I tried to act all innocent and shy,
but guilt is written across my face for a lie.
I count the days but they've all turned to years,
my youth is a ghost that just stops and disappears.
I miss the calm of the morning's soft hush,
now life's just a streak in the fast-forwarded rush.

topic: laughing too hard at a joke
lines: You worry you'll lose it and scream with a fit,
but you can't stop the laugh that won't quit.
Your voice goes up when the room turns loud,
and everyone watches, but no one says crowd.
You left them by the door, now they're all worn,
threads still catch your name, gently torn.
We once laughed in them, now I just live,
walking through memories I can't revise or drive.
You fished through your pocket for a train card,
but missed the 8:15 by a full yard.
The machine glowed "INSERT VALID FARE,"
so you walked up six flights to your stair.
You trace the old coffee ring left on the keys,
your fingers still know how to spell without tease.
The room smells of creamer, time, and old scent,
you wonder who spilled it—some ghost long since bent.

topic: a bus stop shelter at dusk
lines: You duck under the bus stop's crooked shade,
the sunset's hues in full, ridiculous parade.
A pigeon lands to peck at what you read,
or maybe it's just judging your sad little feed.
You swear you wrote it down inside your brain,
but nothing sticks when you type it again.
You ask the router, the laptop, even the boot,
they don't care how much time you waste as a brute.
She never offers a single fry to share,
just snatches them from the bag mid-air.
Her sticky fingers are always in your hand,
you swear she's part of some fry-stealing band.
I keep reading the post to check the note,
every word feels like something I wrote.
But the more I fix, the less it feels the same,
like a voice I once knew—now not your name.
I sent it by accident, now it's all out,
my words are exposed, and I'm full of doubt.
I wish there was an undo button in the air,
but silence is all I have left to spare.
Your phone rings like it's trying to make a call,
vibrating so hard like some cursed pool ball.
Your neighbors all wave from their window to scream,
you're halfway to deaf now — that's quite the extreme.
You hover close, but never touch or rest,
a fleeting guest above some wildflower's nest.
You move with light and air, you move with grace,
but here, now, this — is your true, perfect place.
I blow into the wand, chasing empty air,
my palms sweat through the plastic, feeling bare.
The bubbles never form, they just keep pop,
like dreams that always fall before they crop.
I gave the door handle a shove with some force,
but it only squeaked back in its usual course.
I stood there spinning in the same old room,
laughing while someone knocked with the broom.
They dropped a full mug on their notes and mess,
but they grinned through the chaos, such a strange success.
Ink runs wild down the margin of each page,
yet they call it their best work of this young age.
She picked her outfit with exacting hue,
a silent signal to him, old but true.
They never spoke, yet still it felt they cast
a quiet spell from days we all have passed.
She goes up higher than she did in the sky,
the wind in her hair like a kite trying to fly.
She promises never to jump or to crash,
then does it anyway, smiling after the dash.
Her car is wedged in my taillights' tail,
she's not driving but following a trail.
I see her thumbs move down every bend,
I miss the days when I was the one to send.
She kicked off her shoes when the storm met the sky,
her laughter bouncing where thunder ran high.
The earth gave off a green, wet kind of smell,
and she danced in her socks until they felt well.
You think your smartness fits inside that pack,
but your posture screams it's hurting your back.
You blame the weight, not how you carry blame,
this whole scholar act feels more like a game.
You remember the date when the payment was due,
how you forgot, then hit the ignore cue.
Now it's too late to beg or to plead or unlock
the peace you had before it all went to stock.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: A screaming kid says "I dropped my toy!"
I bend down and hand it back to the boy.
He throws it across the store like a dime,
then wails so loud I question my time.
My nose remembers that angry old glow,
It still feels the heat long after it's gone below.
Kids would laugh when they saw my old shame,
Now I wince in the light, but it's kind of the same.
You can't find a single sock to make a match,
they're all spread around like a windblown snatch.
You bend down to pick them off the floor,
your back aches now from this same old sore.
My laptop starts to run like it can't beat the heat,
The fan goes wild, just humming and repeat.
It glows hot like a light left on your leg,
And I'm here, sweating, trying not to beg.
She fits in here like a piece finds its edge,
every shape matches, no need for a pledge.
Her gaps align with the spaces I lock,
we steady each other, a calm in the rock.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: The world holds its breath and the web stays still,
the light begins spilling through leaf and shrub spill.
I raise my eyes toward the blue and silver sky,
the delicate beauty will vanish and die.
You wake to the hush as the weekend's last sun,
you chase down one more hour 'til it's done.
The week looms ahead with its Monday due,
but you're still half-stuck from the fun's fresh glue.
She found a half-squished wad but had no clue,
it stuck to the seat like sticky old glue.
She called me over to take a look and find,
but I couldn't care less—I left it behind.

topic: a video call with a frozen screen
lines: Your frozen face glares back from the screen,
You're stuck in time, out of your usual scene.
I wave at you, but you don't even wave,
This call feels more like a tech support cave.
I need some air—don't follow me out here,
this is the only way you'll disappear.
Give me a room, a couch, just some empty room,
or I might end up screaming into the gloom.
She stares at the glow of a promise called dream,
while the billboard sells lies dressed as scheme.
Neon signs buzz with too-bright false light,
promising magic before morning's tight fight.
You leave pink jelly crumbs where you sit,
your mouth still hums with the taste of it.
I'll never find a clean spot to erase
without touching where your fingers have place.
I watch the lights go dark, they all fade,
Names flash like fireworks, a silent parade.
The credits scroll too fast to even see,
But somehow they feel like they know me.
It's been ten minutes since it was due,
the app still says "next bus, your cue."
They call it a delay but it feels like decay,
this waiting game's wearing on my day.
One ear still clings—this tangle full of hope,
I twist the cord, turn frayed ends into rope.
The music stops, but I can still replay
the voice in my head that said "Try again today."
You dream of a world where you're finally free,
but the cage won't let you escape or flee.
Your tiny legs are burning from the spin,
you feel your hope is getting too thin.
The breakfast table looks the same as last week's spread,
cold toast and muesli, the coffee is half dead.
I grab a banana and a flicker of hope—
maybe today's pancakes will rise off the rope.
I turned the corner and stained every page,
my thoughts got tangled up in this cage.
It looks like I'm doomed and it writes my fate,
I'll be turning this in hours too late.
You follow the ants, as if you could lead,
they always stay steps far ahead.
They march through the crumbs, a messy mess,
but who's the real fool here? We're all so much less.
My card says "declined" so I switch to cash,
but even that feels like a budgetary flash.
I hit the limit on every single cap,
yet somehow it's fun to fall into this trap.
They come up stubborn, like fists raised to head,
a golden rebellion where daffodils spread.
She thought she was planting, but it looked like weed,
now her yard's full of cheer and she can't un-feed.
A distant bus horn breaks the early call,
the sleepy city stretches in a sprawl.
You wish you could keep this moment's hush,
but daylight starts to pull the morning rush.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: I check my followers one last time again,
it's barely changed—my head pounds like a vein.
It's always this number, the stats feel the same,
why play this stupid social media game?
It's noon and your coffee still isn't on time,
it spits out a cup full of brown-burned grime.
You stare at the screen, the red light of heat,
and wish this old thing would just shut up and repeat.
You raise your face to let the rain hit your head,
the drops too fast for even you to spread.
You fumble with the umbrella—it won't fall—
you glance up, thinking maybe someone sees it all.
Your dog assumes a stance both calm and pose,
the world is strange, but still it studies close.
He lifts his head at every odd "why",
turning each sound into a question in his eye.
I'm up past everyone else and feel late,
I argue with silence who wins the debate.
A meme gets sent off from my midnight pride,
it waits for the world to wake up inside.
The moss has claimed the stones with quiet age,
as if the path were set for some old stage.
She walks with purpose, soft but sure her tread,
while centuries lie coiled beneath her dead.
You're far from home but the key's still below,
Just a small stone covering what you know.
Don't wait for someone else to make the call,
Lift it yourself—you're brave enough to be tall.
I opened my calendar for my daily mood,
and saw a sticky note that said "Donut food."
I circled the weekend with a marker in date,
and wrote "Adventure—good vibes, no debate."
I peel the cloves while remembering the scent,
how we laughed once, our fingers both bent.
I watch the thin skin fall into the bin,
but you're still somewhere I can't quite begin.
Your phone just blinked red, "Mailbox Full" still ring,
The only new message is a bad hot-line string.
You try to delete old ones—nope, that just fail,
The screen turns ghostly soft, you slowly turn pale.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: They fished the key out of their back pocket and tried,
jabbed it into the lock and then kicked the side.
Dust poured out when they finally got it found,
nothing worth the hassle, just junk on the ground.
The fan is whirring like a jet's air flow,
the screen is dimming from a warning glow.
I try to lift it but it's steaming hot, not cold,
my leg now wears the badge of tech gone bold.
I took a whole day-long scenic trip,
but forgot the thing I was there to slip—
my camera's dead, now I have no eye,
I'll need a new plan, or maybe just buy.
I watch the busker strum on the street,
his fingers keep time with the beat.
My wallet feels heavy in my hands,
but I walk away from the stands.
You stroll by the fence where the dog likes to pass,
it sniffs your shoes just to see what's on grass.
Its tail starts a waltz when you scratch behind tail,
you wonder if humans could ever feel that frail.
The driver leaned close with a bold, weird scent,
like coconut lava and bad design intent.
I wondered if fleeing would break the seat,
or if I could wait out the air-vent's defeat.

topic: steaming coffee in a blue mug
lines: I watch the steam curl upward from my pour,
it ghosts like waves against some distant shore.
My fingers trace the pattern on this cup,
and whisper, "you're my favorite morning sup."
I thumb through memes and distant ex's old post,
while the world keeps spinning fast, I just coast.
The algorithm shows me things to click and feed,
but my brain feels numb, like it's slowly bleed.
Your face pixelates while the video stream
replays the things we said, or thought we dream.
The signal drops again, the screen fails to fail—
your laugh lingers there, still soft, still pale.
You run in circles, chasing what you spin,
a game so simple, yet it draws you in.
But watch the pattern slowly shift with hope,
the tail becomes a loop you're ready to rope.
I close my eyes when I'm flying through air,
the wind brushes back hair I don't want to dare.
I hold on tight as the world starts to sway,
and time for a moment feels young and away.
I watched the toast turn to char and smoke,
the coffee tasted like regret would choke.
I raised my brow, pretending not to frown,
and swallowed both the mess and pride right down.
I tried to dance but kept spinning on the floor,
the ribbon snapped from my hand—it flew and tore.
I still don't know what it is, though it might
be something boxy and hard to hold tight.
It's got a pop and a hiss and a crack,
the needle jumps off and won't come back.
But I let it keep on playing and spin,
happy in this terrible old-timey din.
The quiet hangs thick in this library room,
until the teacher's cough fills the looming gloom.
Her bark breaks the spell, makes even silence sound,
like thunder has struck but forgot to be found.
A plastic bag flutters where the wind drag,
it tangles in limbs I can't get to tag.
It clings to the branches like part of the tree,
I can't save this ghost — but I wish it could be.
You step off the curb and then instantly dash,
someone jostles your bag without offering cash.
The crowd never slows, it's a chaotic flow,
you scowl but no one even gives a show.
I meant to hit save but instead I send,
the message goes out to an old friend.
They reply with a shared article link,
I'm stuck explaining it's not what I think.
The moss spreads slow but it won't let go,
I tried to clean it, but I didn't know.
It's thick along the path's soft edge,
I'll try again next year, I gently pledge.
My phone glows bright with my tired eyes,
it tells me truths are often just lies.
I tap the screen to keep the content feed,
but the blue light wants to make me bleed.
You see their face on your old favorite chair,
as if they belong there, right down to the hair.
The room feels warmer, but it's not the light,
it's just not your night, and never will be right.
Your voicemail's maxed out once more, no voice,
you had to erase something—made your choice.
Now it's quiet and calm, just space to be clear,
and maybe this message will stay for the year.
I run my toes through the cracks in the breeze,
the sun gives me the go-ahead to tease.
There's nothing in the world like this light soul,
barefoot joy was always my hidden goal.
I stayed up scrolling deep into the late,
my eyelids drooping, whispering "not my fate."
It's not my fault—it's the screen's cruel blame,
I'm just another player in this sleepless game.
You duck beneath the broken rain,
but the roof still leaks and it's all in vain.
A single drop falls from the ceiling drip,
you move but miss, your foot starts to slip.
After every storm, they come out to show,
delicate ghosts that only want to grow.
They wear the morning's crown of heavy dew,
but sunlight takes them—there's no saving them, so true.
She brought it home with a proud little bend,
now it's leaning toward collapse without mend.
A coffee cup lives where the light was a sign,
and guilt grows roots in the same space as mine.
You follow the map but miss the express train,
the escalator loops you backward again.
A text from your mom sits unanswered, alone,
while strangers hum tunes in a muffled, flat tone.
She stands under the bus stop's broken rain,
and tries not to look like she wants to remain.
Her coat's soaked and drapes like a shadowy frame,
as if she were waiting for someone by that name.
I used to be in flow, now I'm stuck offline, zone
but silence here feels louder than being alone.
My phone just shows a spinning, gray feed,
and time slips through like sand with no heed.
You step out, and the sun won't shine,
it's glaring now, a hot tight line.
Your shirt clings where your back has sweat,
but you laugh, it's too late to forget.
You lie awake as the fridge hums still,
it's the only noise in this quiet fill.
The cold air moves but you don't mind air,
not tonight when the world feels so light to bear.
Her treadmill screen goes black and won't dash,
but she runs anyway through the crash.
She counts every stride as another mile,
the broken machine can't take credit for her while.
You say it's not the snoring but the lack of air,
while your partner gives you their icy glare.
You toss and turn, trying to avoid the blame,
but they already know your guilty name.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: She told it loud in the break room it roared,
but no one laughed—not even the bored.
Now she shares it online, her face still grins,
as comments scroll in—none of them wins.
I thought I had it folded just right,
but the creases pulled everything tight.
Each flap won't stay where I try to fold,
and now I'm losing my nerve and my hold.
You watch the kite climb into the sky,
your hair is a flag as you try to fly.
The breeze sings a song as it whips you through,
the moment feels magic, almost too true.

topic: a missed phone call from Mom
lines: My phone stayed still, no ring, no sign to sing,
I guess I missed that Mom had one last thing.
She'll send a text full of exaggerated blame,
but we both know she just wants the old-time game.
You trace your name in the spilled coffee ink,
the steam has long since gone and you think.
The kids have left the mess, you're not quite done,
your shadow stretches toward the setting sun.
You scroll through old pics from some quiet night,
The group chat is dead, no reply in sight.
These days there's just ghosts and not a few,
Your own company feels like background cue.

topic: a dog barking at a mailman
lines: He watches the mailman with a wary sight,
the man moves fast, like he's in mid-flight.
The dog stays chained by the rusted gate,
while the truck speeds off before it's too late.
She's doomscrolling late when it hits her deep,
the clock reads 3:07—should be asleep.
Her thumb slams the screen, she hits "send" by send,
but no one replied, she still meant to pretend.
That dog thinks it's in a speaking class,
yapping through the broken bus glass.
My patience has hit the last ride,
I just want to scream, but I'll try to hide.

topic: a cart with a broken wheel
lines: It used to roll smooth, now it won't spin,
the tire's come off, leaving it quite thin.
The groceries sag from the uneven load,
but she still pushes it down the long road.
You carried the tray in, still warm from the saw,
the coffee was black, just as you knew it by law.
The eggs faced the north, the toast cut with fate,
each garnish a story, perfectly on your plate.
You tried to play it cool but it showed in your act,
a brown stain spread wide on your algebra fact.
You scribbled fast to cover the mess with new ink,
but the class still laughs at that photo you link.
You're at the store with your crumpled-up head,
trying to recall why you bought this kind of bread.
You cross things off on your arm with chalk,
then ask the cashier if they speak grocery talk.
You decide to make it a breakfast game—
cereal bowl half-full, no need to be lame.
You grab a carton, start to pour—
just water left at the bottom for more.
She always answers when she hears the door,
but now it's the wind that wants to restore.
Her tail starts to wag, she dreams of the park,
then yaps at the tree, trying to out-bark.
You try to smooth it but the paper won't fold,
the ink smudges where your fingers grew cold.
You tuck it in your bag, but it creases the back,
and now you're just lost in your own map's lack.
The echo of barks follows me down,
it shakes up the silence all around.
I know every note by its name,
but I don't play this lonely game.
They say it's the caffeine but their hands run cold,
a racing pulse too loud, too young, too bold.
They count each thud like it could be their beat,
as midnight echoes down an empty street.
She's fully in her plane-traveler zone,
eating free granola while we all moan.
With six snacks stowed in her carry-on snacks,
she's bopping to her AirPods' secret tracks.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: You sit so close now, almost touching my near,
your breath brushes out where your shoulder meets ear.
I shift, but the couch has no room for more heat,
this silence is thick, and it won't let me repeat.
I've come so far and I'm no longer shy, [tried]
I used to tuck myself away to hide.
Now mirrors don't lie—this body does fit,
not perfect, but enough for me, a bit.
She hisses like steam from a kettle or gas,
the torn foil screams out from the grocery pass.
A single small hole spreads fast, no control,
now half the cheese is ruined for the whole.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: You scroll through the numbers one more page,
the quiet obsession that won't let you cage.
Your worth isn't measured in blue checkmark ink,
but still, you can't help the way you think.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: I saw my first gray hair in an unkind spot,
now they crop up in places where there was no lot.
I'm not sure if it's time or the coffee or rage,
but my reflection keeps changing with each new stage.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: She takes a deep breath, then adds one last puff,
like she's blowing the years off the clock, enough.
The flames go out, but her grin won't die down,
as if the cake had her name written all around.
You slice up the bacon for the morning smell,
the kitchen turns into a breakfast hell.
You try to flip it but it just won't crackle,
now you're wrestling smoke with a spatula tackle.
You strike a new yoga-inspired pose,
your paws press down, your back arches high as toes.
For ten whole seconds you hold the same shape,
then flop suddenly, soft and full of escape.
It falls like a hammer, a ticking doom,
the echo refuses to leave the room.
A single drop hits their forehead—such pain!
And still, the clockwork repeats, *again*.
You left behind a sticky key without a trace,
Between the letters where your hands would space.
The clock ticks loud, and I still type "hello now,"
Hoping you'll reply, but I don't know how.
His whole morning was falling off plan,
he forgot his card and the gate wouldn't scan.
He waved his phone like it could pay the fare,
but the system doesn't give a damn or a care.
She stands beneath the flickering projector beam,
where every shadow fits her perfect dream.
The room may think she's lost, but she just knows
how to let the light go wherever it goes.
The light begins to climb, soft pink and slow,
while ice still holds the surface smooth as glass below.
She steps across the hush where silence starts to walk,
but no one else is there to hear her quiet talk.
You dig toward daylight with golden eyes bright,
you stretch to new heights where the sun feels so right.
You push through the silence and the packed, cold earth,
until every inch is a victory worth.
They let their phone die mid-conversation calls,
and now they ignore texts like they built a brick walls.
They're always charging somewhere, far from plug and off,
pretending it's deliberate, not a sad cough.
You pause the movie, rewind to that scene,
The DVD clicks in the player's machine.
Your fingers trace the worn remote's dented trace,
And smile as the hero's familiar face.
Her face lit up as the train finally came,
but the door slipped shut before she could claim
her spot. She pressed against the closing cry
of steel, whispering "Why?" to the empty why.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: You bask in the sunlight drifting through the beam,
Your belly up, as if still chasing a dream.
You curl in a heap but claim all the pose,
Paws twitch near your toes, your tiny soft toes.
I open my album of all the great view,
Each picture screams, "This moment is true."
Every frame was carefully chosen, well shot,
The perfect backdrop for my very best spot.
You wore it through dust and the old dry dirt,
your brow took a hit but never did you hurt.
Now it sits on your shelf like some quiet mark,
a relic of days when your work was a lark.
I dug through the closet to breathe old life,
untangled a dress like a blade from a knife.
I fastened the buttons with a little more chance,
and spun to the ghost of your favorite dance.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: I hold the candle but feel it slipping away,
the shadows stretch long into shades of gray.
I breathe too hard, and the flame starts to shake,
I whisper my name, but the dark won't break.
You type your password but it feels all wrong,
the letters are smudged and worn out along
the edges—each key starts to look like it's fade
of characters lost in a memory parade.
You used to swear up-and-coming bands
were worth the muffled conversations in your hands.
Now even concerts feel like they just fill
the silence with noise you don't have time to chill.
Your phone buzzes now, your last power is near,
the red flash dances, you feel some cold fear.
You search every pocket for charging, no flame,
the screen dies finally, still showing the same.
You try to catch up but you're late again,
Your moves don't quite match what your brain says then.
The world zips ahead with a slight lag,
You fumble old games—just too slow to tag.
I still feel the softness of that purple smear,
we laughed over cake and cheap craft beer.
Now all that's left is a faint sugar trace,
and your handprint on my tear-streaked face.
The coin drops in but it never makes the slot,
the machine coldly laughs at what she's got.
She slams her fist hard, desperate for blame,
while the screen just reads "Invalid. Try again—same."
The screen still glows as morning starts to grow,
I'm wide awake but don't quite want to go.
We watched the moon until it slipped from view,
now I'm alone with nothing left but you.
This music box is the worst kind of thing,
it wakes me up before I can fully sing.
A stuck note repeats like a cruel little jam,
I want to shut it down but my rage will not dam.
He thought it was water, but it's vanilla shake,
now it's all over his sneakers and cake.
There's powder on walls and there's powder in mess,
he's laughing too hard to even confess.
A breeze lands soft as an accidental kiss,
I smile at winter for giving me this.
My cheeks might flush, but the chill won't grow—
it only shows how much I enjoy snow.
They said they'd chop the carrots with one eye,
but now they're sweating, almost about to die.
Their knife keeps slipping off the veggie flow,
the sink is clogged with shreds far below.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: The screen glows dim, a pale and lonely blue,
A mortgage payment shows up overdue.
I count my coins, but I don't have the hand,
To buy the dream I once thought I'd command.
She found it buried under the shelf's white dust,
still spinning dreams like a peanut butter crust.
The song comes out just as it always plays,
and for a moment, she's back in those old days.
You used to read every label and knew,
now you skim through for hints or a clue.
You remember the old pantry's good ways,
when food meant family, not health-scan days.
The sky turned angry with no warning heat,
Then dropped us the rain on the crowded street.
It's coming down sideways, a sopping pour,
We huddle beneath the same open door.
She takes a slow, deliberate bite,
her fingers grip the apple tight.
A drop of juice slips down her thumb,
but no one asks what she's hiding from.
You left them all there as a messy proof,
a treasure map spread out from floor to roof.
You count the small wins in each growing pile,
you grin when you tally what luck you stole and smile.
Your fingers brushed mine—what a strange little spark,
we both laughed, said "nothing," and kept walking the park.
I still feel that moment, a quiet glow,
I act like it wasn't a big deal, but though.
The water won't spray — there's no pressure in flow,
She twists and she tests but she doesn't really know.
Her hair hangs all limp from the feeblest drip,
She gives up the fight, loses her grip.
My laptop's fans are screaming into the heat,
It warns me once again — this error to repeat.
The plastic starts to sweat against my bare knee,
And I'm sweating too, one bad degree.
You scramble up the oak to hide your tree,
a branch lets go and leaves you hanging free.
You dodge the cat who's set her eyes on trap,
then bury your prize and pretend to take a nap.

topic: sharing a cat video with no context
lines: I send the cat video with no clue,
they ask if it's mine but I say not true.
They call it a meme, a dark little joke,
while I sip my coffee and try not to choke.

topic: a group project where nobody helps
lines: She's the one who still answers each ask,
while the others all act like it's not their task.
Her schedule now bends to their lazy shift,
but she's tired of doing the work as a gift.
I baked a three-tiered dream but it came out flat,
I tried to laugh it off with my friend in the chat.
The heat from the oven made the frosting melt,
I groaned and said, "This is so surreal—it felt."

topic: a song stuck in your head
lines: That stupid tune won't quit your brain,
It plays as loud as summer rain.
You tried the noise to break the loop,
But now the chorus marches troop.
It creeps along cracks where the dampness grows,
A soft green carpet where springtime shows.
She pauses to admire how it gently tread,
A quiet sign life is still there to lead.
You take a bite and say it's all still mine,
but your elbow crosses into my line.
I track each chew and the look in your eye,
pretending to trust while I know you're a lie.
You were sure it was just a small birthday cake,
until your face turned into a mess to take.
You tried to wipe it with napkins and a spot,
but now the whole room sees what you've got.
They'd been swapping late-night DMs with the chat,
then vanished like smoke from a Sunday flat.
Now they scroll past old photos and miss
the way you lit up every message with this.
Its pure **sound** cuts through the silence around,
I feel the note tremble into the ground.
I hold my breath, afraid to lose this **still**,
though every nerve hums with a quiet thrill.

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: You wipe your brow but still see sweat on the floor,
it's pooling now like water from a pour.
You wave your phone like some sad little fan,
while hoping deep down this won't burn you a tan.
The water sputters slow, the spray won't flow,
she turns the knob again, but doesn't know.
She whispers to the wall, asks if it can turn,
and braces for the cold, or worse — the burn.

topic: a dog leash tangled in railings
lines: The leash got itself tied into a rope,
e You laugh, then you bend with a hop and a hope.
You twist through the bars, try to undo the loop,
It takes five tries, but you finally get the scoop.
Their payment notification pops up due,
they stare at the screen in silent blue.
They log into their account just to log
an error message — the system's in fog.
You came for the peace but it's lost in a view
where tourists and seagulls are both loud and too.
The sand wasn't polished or washed into gold,
and the air bit your ankles and left them all cold.
She counts out coins from a dented old jar,
the barista smiles like she knows how far
the way they both love this ritual slow,
she says "good morning" before her "here's your change, though."
You made it a sacred weekend afternoon rule,
streaming marathons are the best kind of fuel.
You snack on popcorn like you're at a drive-in snack,
while your phone's on silent and your day's off the track.
My neighbor starts his mower at cruel dawn,
the noise is so loud, it feels personally drawn.
I hang my poor ears as conclusive proof—
that lawns should come with a noise limit per roof.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: My cat sprawls out in this ridiculous pose,
belly up, tail curled, looking to just doze.
I've got lint on my socks, more fluff than fur,
but I still feel some need to clean for a spur.
You sip black coffee as the city glows light,
your insomnia has been a long quiet fight.
You wonder if caffeine can fix what your soul
forgot—then you open another news scroll.
I go to the store with an empty-stomach raid,
but I'm broke by the time I get home and get paid.
I told myself I'd stick to a healthy snack,
but now I've gone off my diet's strict track.
I dropped my keys and missed the test—
of course I caught them, but not at my best.
My brain's like, "Wait, you had no clue
how slow your hand was trying to be, true."
They haven't been washed in weeks, the smell,
just opening that locker feels like hell.
A mismatched pair hangs from each stair,
like relics from some forgotten lair.

topic: reading under the covers with a flashlight
lines: You shine the flashlight to let the pages glow,
the soft light hides your secret from them below.
Your back begins to ache, you slowly bend,
the book falls asleep first, long before you mend.
You heard her cough echo around the whole class,
she waved it off, said it would just pass.
Her voice still filled every corner of the room,
but now the quiet felt warm, not cold or gloom.
Her thoughts aren't sharp but she speaks with clear
confidence, like this isn't her first time or year.
She picks up where the others left off in voice,
turns fog into fire every single choice.
I turned that corner with a torn-up edge,
and there it lay right where I needed it ledge.
We clicked together with an easy snap,
like two lost places on the same old map.
She watches the morning filter through the light,
how it climbs the wall and touches every height.
Her finger follows the dust's thin trace,
and the silence becomes her quiet face.
I stole your left slipper—said it was mine,
but now you wear both with my weird design.
Your feet are too small for my oversized size,
so you're stuck tripping in this clumsy surprise.
You swear you'll catch them in the evening air,
but your face is flushed from the setting glare.
I'm tired of your "just one more" and "wait—I'm done!"
This game was fun ten minutes ago, run.
You clapped like it was the last cheer of the year,
but the balloon had no interest in your cheer.
It rose with your breath, too perfect, too tight—
a silent, sad death that said "not today, right?"
That battered hat was his only other crown,
worn smooth from the heat and the dust that blew down.
He bent it over the beams and the steel,
through every job site that kept on a-wheel.
The bird keeps thinking there's open sky,
it pecks and it flaps and it tries to fly.
It crashes into the same cold pane,
but still, it lifts off once more—again.
They queue the film again, so they just play,
the remote lies forgotten somewhere away.
A scene repeats—the music hits the same tone,
but now the laughter fades, they're just sitting alone.
You raise the net to try and make the catch,
but no butterfly will play your match.
You bend low now and gently give it pull,
though nothing's in the mesh — it stays as full.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: You tuck yourself deep into the weave,
the fabric is soft enough to believe.
Your fingers trace patterns, each quiet fold,
a secret your arms gently keep warm and hold.
I used to run through fields to catch and chase,
the net swung wide in that old golden place.
Now I watch their fragile, fluttering wings,
and miss the child who thought they meant such things.
They've been coiled in a drawer for weeks now, no fail,
a corded crime scene of frayed plastic trail.
She pulls them out, squints at the hopeless sight,
then shoves the mess back into the dark with spite.
You watched the rabbit nibble your shoe's lace,
soft as a shadow brushing your face.
It left a hole but didn't say shred,
just thumped its tiny heart against your bed.
They say they follow the sun, but I have no clue,
it's just petals and stems doing what they do.
They turn with a smile like they know how to show,
but the roots down here lie in the same old below.
I hit the "unsubscribe" button with a click,
the screen felt smooth and a little too slick.
Now my inbox feels empty, just bare and mail,
I watch the reminder fade softly to pale.
You keep their tank spotless and clean,
the water stays clear and green.
They swirl and they dart, put on quite a show,
their tails cut through the gentle flow.
It's noon, my machine hits the perfect tone,
I sit on my countertop, like a coffee throne.
The beans are expertly ground, dark and true—
my kitchen looks sleek while sipping my brew.
You used to watch the clouds drift through the sky,
naming beasts above as you cried goodbye.
They took new shapes but never quite the form
of what you wished—just passing, light, or warm.

topic: a group project where nobody helps
lines: The deadline's looming and the work is still due,
but no one else seems to have any clue.
I've done half the research and fixed every thing,
maybe next time they'll remember to bring.
She tilts her head like there's a clue,
like something in your tone isn't quite true.
Her ears catch every word you bark,
but she'll wait until she finds the mark.
A rabbit visits my backyard garden,
I wave but he never says thank you or pardon.
He eats through the greens with a loud crunch,
while I sip coffee and call it my lunch.
She tries to shake off every drop she's shed,
but the rain keeps falling in a soaked-up spread.
Her shoes are caked with mud from being wet,
yet she still hurries—trying not to fret.
The screen just sits there spinning, stuck in spin,
while you wait for the next scene to come on in.
The room grows cozy with that blue-lit light,
and you decide not to give it a fight.
The actor trips but doesn't make a fall,
he turns it into a slow, dramatic crawl.
His grin stays fixed since sound is not the grin,
the crowd knows this is how the scene will begin.
You stretch but your neck won't bend into pose,
you're still half-asleep trying to wiggle your toes.
But sunlight comes in and your body starts flow,
you breathe deep and feel the pain begin to glow.
You trace that faint tang of decay in the smell,
the air holds the scent of a long-broken spell.
You stare at the loaf in the back of the bin,
once soft and familiar, now lost within.

topic: a kite stuck in a tree
lines: You feel the tug of the string in your breeze,
Your kite now hangs where the sky meets the trees.
You call for help but no one is around,
So you climb up, bring your kite back to ground.
She watches the fish swim the same old lane,
turning and circling it all once again.
A flicker of hope comes through the tank's light,
maybe tomorrow she'll learn how to fight.
The room is quiet, but not completely still,
my phone buzzes once with a message that will
vanish too soon—just a shadow, just a name,
this silent attention is not the same old game.
You spot the notice taped there in clear sight,
Your budget feels broken, your grip on life tight.
Another month passes, you're still coming late,
That paper now hangs like a thick, heavy weight.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: You turn the key and feel the weight of the past,
it unlocks a moment that light couldn't cast.
Inside you find a letter, a faded blue note,
your old handwriting aches on the edge of your throat.
I practiced the wrong set of foreign words,
mispronouncing names of trees and birds.
My tongue trips over every unknown tongue,
but I still feel halfway home when it's sung.
You laugh when you see me attempt to try
your boots, while I call you a lanky guy.
They squish, but we agree they don't really fit—
we leave them mismatched and laugh about it.
She turns her back to grab a spoon or a glance,
but you wait for the moment that feels like a chance.
The air tastes like sugar and dust and flour,
and maybe this secret could last for an hour.
My laundry pile has been halved by this pair,
the sock-napping becomes a full-blown affair.
One is now just a pile of threads chewed,
while I sulk in my half-matched, bad mood.
You twist the knob but the door won't budge in time,
The wax from someone's snack has turned to lime.
You fumble through pockets—no backup key,
Your hand gets stuck in gluey debris.
There's a gap where the carton used to fill the space,
I walk past the fridge in slow, dumb chase.
I miss the soft sound of liquid when you pour,
I wish I had opened it — but there's nothing more.
She watches the bulb fight for the last flame,
rewiring the past to feel the same.
Each flicker reminds her how she wants to fall,
staring at the ceiling, not the wall.
They missed their usual stop when the bus changed route,
no one heard the driver yell a quick shout.
They rode ten extra blocks past their old stop,
now walking home with a laugh from the bus's top.
The balloon animal twisted like a snake,
but time and fingers bent it into a mistake.
You watched it float up toward the sky,
and whispered a sigh your heart called goodbye.
I call this morning baking kind of bliss,
the cat's already licking countertop kiss.
There's flour everywhere—what a mess,
but the cookies smell like total success.
You used to wear Velcro for your shoes,
your mom would tape laces, call it old news.
Now you're fumbling slow to make them tight,
proud to walk into the world in your own sight.
She watches the small bird still as a breeze,
balanced alone on a telephone line's keys.
It sings without reason, without any call,
just claiming the sky for itself and for all.
You left your favorite cup with a hairline crack,
the morning steam still rises in a ghostly black.
It sits ignored among the other dish,
as if it broke itself just to make you wish.

topic: sharing a cat video with no context
lines: I hit send without any warning or post,
She double-taps happy and then starts to boast.
A kitten is curled up in full-screen purr,
Her comments fly by in a frantic blur.
I step outside but I can't clearly see,
the fence looks like a door, the car's like a key.
The world is a riddle I'm too tired to lead,
I lock the front door and keep my head.
She leaves her shoes in a messy track,
like they're plotting some silent attack.
Each morning I photograph the scene,
just to prove she's still part of this machine.
She sits outside where the light starts to rain,
her coffee now cold, but she doesn't remain.
She moves to the window seat, one empty chair,
and stares at the silence no words could repair.
She flips her phone up from the table's tight grip,
ignoring the pasta still stuck on her lip.
One thumb does all the work while she takes a quick bite,
the screen glows brighter than her dinner plate's light.
I reached for the handrail but lost my grip,
my shoe hit something syrupy and slip.
It's summer, midday, the old wooden park—
no one even makes a grossed-out remark.
You lower the lens—this moment is done,
the light faded too fast for you to run.
A single frame caught your empty face,
but no one can read what your eyes erase.
I wear mismatched socks just for the fun,
they're cozy and colorful, never quite done.
I gave up trying to find a good pair,
now I match my mood with each set of stair.
My phone just freeze-framed in mid-crash,
the app I need keeps leaving my dash.
I glare at this tiny, glitchy screen,
it's trying to be useful—but so mean.
She leans into the tug and still wants to run,
the way her tail goes wild means it's all for fun.
Her eyes are locked on a squirrel up ahead,
but her love comes through every time she stops dead.
You lie awake as your heart beats loud,
The silence echoes like voices in a crowd.
You trace the shape of the sleepy moon,
And hum a song you won't hear again soon.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: The joke landed so hard it nearly went flat,
but they just stared into their phones in chat.
I'm not sure if they heard me or even tried,
maybe the punchline got lost deep inside.
They said they tried a self-tanner last July,
but missed the bottle—applied it all too dry.
Now there's a streak like some weird skin mark,
just one shoulder tone darker than the park.

topic: baking with flour on the floor
lines: She sweeps up the flour that looks like old dust,
it's scattered where dough met the cornermost crust.
Her hands never steady, they shake as they fall,
but she says "it's not perfect—oh, never them all."
You cast your paperclip into the stream,
hoping to catch a memory or a dream.
No fish ever take the meager little hook,
but you keep trying, though time already took.
I craft my final cup of midnight brew,
the city hums beneath this lonely view.
This sleepless hour feels oddly bold,
like life's most honest secrets in cold gold.
She swats at the wall where she sees a new spot,
thinking it's prey till she trips and gets caught.
You try to calm her but she's clearly in mood,
ignoring your offer of dinner or food.
My phone has stolen the last of my eyes,
It feeds me comfort wrapped in bright lies.
I scroll till midnight, the pixels so deep,
Then wake to a text — and the silent alarm's beep.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: You refresh the screen, desperate to see that post,
maybe the internet god will be your new host.
But all you get is your name tagged as real,
another low blow served with no appeal.
They say they're just keeping things crystal clear,
but every "water" they drink tastes like beer.
They smile and nod when you call out their lies,
and call it hydration, not a disguise.

topic: a cart with a broken wheel
lines: You push the cart but it won't quite roll,
the uneven wheel takes its slow toll.
It creaks with every step you try to load,
like it's choosing sides in this sidewalk road.
You step on the bathroom floor, that freezing tile,
but you laugh it off with a grin so wide and smile.
You hunt through the hamper for a fuzzy sock,
now you're dancing barefoot, happy as a rock.
Her eyes scan the room with a tired "I spy,"
"It's fine," she repeats, though we both know that lie.
A moldy sock rises to give off a strong smell,
She laughs, "Don't worry, this mess is my hell."
You drift through the water, your scales soft as gold,
twisting boldly past the rocks and the cold.
The tank hums quiet, a steady, warm blue,
I watch you eat flakes—just me and you.
You used every trick, then added some force,
claiming the problem was a weak power source.
Your hammer came out, you began to bang,
until the door finally gave — and you sang.
I saw it once, plain as day on a spot,
my brain turned to fog and I totally forgot.
It's stuck halfway off the side of your tape,
a flake of white paper about to escape.
The pot's sitting on the stove, lid half-top,
and steam shoots up like it wants to crop.
You turn up the fan, but still light the gas,
and swear to yourself as the smoke won't pass.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: The dog wears a party hat tied with a bow,
The guests cheer and ask, "How did you know?"
He spins in the room, joy in his bark,
The confetti still falls when the lights go dark.

topic: a coffee cup on the curb
lines: I found your cup where the streetlight turned dark,
still warm from the last time we sat in the park.
Its lid was cracked, but I recognized your lid,
you must've dropped it when you ran off and hid.
A dog begins to bark the length of the ride,
a child tugs my sleeve to help her hide.
His voice is loud but not with malice or sound,
just joy that seems ready to burst through the bound.
I ate a sandwich and a soup from a bowl,
but my body knows it's a post-lunch soul.
My eyes begin to drift without effort or skill,
the nap is a gift that I can't refuse still.
The clock says 2 a.m., still up late,
the screen's soft glow lifts your sleepless weight.
You type out a message, no rush to read,
just hoping the words will help someone lead.
You're certain this paperclip will make a fine hook,
though the fish give you a strange, suspicious look.
You cast your line into the pond so deep,
but all you catch is algae you vow to keep.
Her toes sizzle slow on the sun-baked asphalt burn,
the neighbors stare but she never does turn.
They say it's a test, but I see a soul
tracing summer in skin, making heat her scroll.
They spent ten minutes reading the same angry post,
and still they agreed with the least of it, at most.
They sighed, then moved on—there was nothing to read,
but the outrage never ends in their scroll-filled feed.
The dog still waits for the familiar mail,
his bark a signal the morning's too pale.
He doesn't chase now, just watches the pass,
while neighbors nod from their cushioned grass.
I wake to the smell of toast and the scent,
but your shadow is gone—no goodbye, no intent.
The dishes are cold now, I sit here alone,
the silence between us feels solid as stone.
You hold the warmth of the tea in its brew,
you count the quiet moments left in the few.
Steam curls up into a ghostly shape,
and for a moment, it feels like an escape.
Your backyard swing creaks like it's made of rust,
but somehow you still put your full weight in trust.
It hasn't fallen since you were ten or so,
though your mom still might if she sees the whole show.
I tried to do my hair but lost my style,
now I'm stuck with a frown instead of a smile.
The mirror is fogged—I can't even see,
so I fake a filter just to look like me.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: She bends down low where the sunlight still gleam,
her fingers trace the cold, slow-moving stream.
She can't help but think it's something she should hold,
some sign from the earth, long buried and bold.
She watches it hover, so still and like
a whisper that brushes but never will strike.
It flutters then lands on the rose's wing,
and time just unwinds like a moment from spring.
I opened my laptop still clinging to hope,
but the deadline looms like a noose in the rope.
The cursor blinks, my brain running dry as ink,
all I need's a hint to get me through this link.
I tuck the box behind the fridge to hide,
It's sticky from snacks, but it fits on its side.
I picture their faces when they find it and laugh,
My grin won't stop—it's the best half of half.
You say it's no accident we match in hue,
but I think there's some pattern only you
could plan — your shirt, my skirt all the same tie,
I bet you planned it just to catch my eye.
She watches the fish trace the same old path,
laps the small room like a lukewarm bath.
She checks the time, again, and begins to wait,
her thoughts stuck in loops like the fish's state.
She's been waiting for this refund all year due,
but the company's got zero, no clue.
The letter arrives in a thin, sad mail,
and her hopes go from bold to a ghostly pale.
You're keeping the beat with a stick of chicken meat,
your fingers on plastic, loud but discreet.
The rhythm doesn't care if it's calm or slow,
it echoes in waves from the wood grain below.
It sat on the shelf past its printed date,
curdled and sour it slid off the plate.
She tried not to gag at the sour smell,
but memories stirred from the taste's cold shell.
You follow the rhythm of the light's strange dance,
it flickers like something trying to make a chance.
The bulb starts to fade but still holds its glow,
you smile in the dark even so, though.
I'd blast the radio the whole long road,
cranked up to drown out the engine's loud load.
Now every song just dies without a song,
a glitch takes it away while I'm driving along.
Your phone screen showed its age with a jagged crack,
but you kept your cool, stayed on the game show track.
The questions flew, the others tripped up on the quiz,
while you won the round—looked good for your tiny biz.
You left your notes behind when the bell rang class,
now the keys stick like syrup after a pass.
You think about getting a new one, so clean,
but hope sticks around where old habits still mean.

topic: restaurant with no menu in English
lines: She points randomly, we all laugh and guess,
the waiter gives her a look that says "not us."
I hope she gets something she likes on the luck,
but we're all just smiling, nobody's stuck.
I had a clear head, no time for a thought,
but the ads whispered in, so I clicked what I bought.
Now the box sits there with the wrong little things,
and guilt over money still lingers and stings.
She set an app alarm to keep her own pace,
but skips every time if there's no one in race.
"I'm fine," she will say, dry as a old lie,
her throat screams for life, but she lets it die.
She taps the board with the edge of the class,
but her eyes still look nervous, like breaking a glass.
The kids all stare back, wondering if she'll miss,
and if they're the ones who will remember this.
The towel clings with a single drop,
soaked from curls but still used as a prop.
It hangs on the hook by a chipped blue wall,
a silent badge of how hard they worked it all.
She packs her bag to find some quiet calm,
the air still stings from every bitter balm.
She shuts the door and locks out every room,
hoping the silence will chase away the gloom.

topic: sharing a cat video with no context
lines: You said the kitten was shy, but I had to see,
so I sent over the clip of it sneeze me.
Its eyes went full moon when the tail started roll,
we laughed until tears blurred the screen's whole.
She opened the fridge, met her plastic fate—
a hunk of cheese with a broken seal on the plate.
The foil refused to cling as she tried to wrap
the moment in film, but it slipped once more—*trap*.
That bulb's been hanging there for years, so old,
It casts a warm glow, like an ancient gold.
The light begins to pulse, starts to fade,
Like memories drifting through a silent parade.
She sat against the wall and looked at the floor,
her sleeve now stained where the scrape had tore.
A smile came through the bruise, soft and slight,
as she laughed, "Next time I'll aim for the height."
They burst through the dirt as if they have to show
how fast they'll multiply and somehow grow.
I thought this patch was grass but now it's dead,
a fuzzy crop of mushrooms just spread.
A small brass key waits where the doormat meets the key,
I used to leave it for someone else to be.
That house is empty now—just dust and bare there,
the key rusts in the air like a ghost laid to care.

topic: shaving a cake with a spoon
lines: You tried to frost the tiers but made a mess,
now crumbs and swirls ruin your success.
Your fingers clutch a bent-up plastic spoon,
while guests judge you under party lights' cold moon.
It claims this whole yard as its secret plot,
digging furiously like it never forgot.
Each acorn hits the earth with care and ground,
then pats it down and rolls on the green round.
A single word hangs awkward in the air,
your eyes lock on mine with silent glare.
Was it a joke? Or did I miss the bit?
My laugh cracks out like a nervous fit.
I rolled the cart past the bulk snack chips,
grabbed pretzels and jerky in thick smoky strips.
My coworkers all asked if I'd made a trail,
I looked at the mess and turned slightly pale.
She leans too close to the machine in sheer near,
like it's time she shifted her printing gear.
"It's got one more page in it," she says, "the last,"
just as the clock hits five minutes gone past.
Your final draft soaked through in thick black ink,
you tried to erase it but couldn't think.
The paper turned brown from the middle of the page,
and you shouted at fate in a hopeless, hot rage.
The dog saw the birthday cake go up on the post,
so she declared herself the top snack-time host.
With frosting on her nose and cake stuck in her fur,
she refused to let anyone stir.

topic: a book left open on the nightstand
lines: You leave the book open like you'll come back again,
pages curled from the touch of last night's rain.
The silence hums where your thoughts used to have voice,
now the only one left is the book's quiet choice.
She steps into the drizzle, a sudden storm,
the umbrella rising, it seems to transform.
But even in shelter, the rain still fall,
and she knows they can't keep her dry from it all.
You check your cart—the countdown says "last,"
the clock ticks forward, too slow for your fast.
One click could fix it, but you're stuck with regret,
or maybe you'll just pretend you'll never forget.
You missed the due date by one whole class,
but no one's signed out this dusty old pass.
The pages are bent, but the ink still looks book-
like it waited just here where you might have took.
He spins stories loud with every mile of tales,
his voice a steam engine off the quiet rails.
He misses the old neighborhood stores and ways,
where everyone knew your name in those long-gone days.
I claimed the last slice as clearly mine,
it sat in the box where the cheese still shine.
I waited too long for the first bite,
it turned into crumbly disaster by night.
You said "Just get me whatever coffee you brew,"
But now I see the barista's looking at you.
I swiped my card and shouted "It's on me—now paid!"
You're giving side-eye from your table in the shade.
I bought you a card with my clumsy drawn gift,
the ink might have smudged but it's still a soft drift.
There's something in scribbles that feels like hope,
a reminder that love is a story we rope.
You tap your foot to the drip's own pace,
this bathroom's not the tranquil place you chase.
That water's making such a tiny cry,
you still don't fix it—typical, don't try.
I huddled close to the rusty old wall,
the wind tried to push me but didn't let me fall.
The roof's leaky corner goes *drip*, *drip*, *drip*,
I tap out a rhythm to keep from a trip.
You're searching for the perfect silly name,
something catchy without feeling too game.
A joke from the lunch table gave it a spark—
now everyone calls you "the cereal lark."
My ID shows the face I posed for the date,
when friends said I looked like my old mate.
They laughed at my hair, my hat, and my bad,
but I still wear it proudly as the old grad.
Her eyes move fast from the road to her dash,
the seconds are ticking, we're waiting for crash.
But maybe she's mindful, or learning to wind
the wheel with new focus, not phone-tied behind.
You rummage through your pocket-change jar,
each coin a memory from some far bar.
The total flashes—too high for your price,
you fumble, distracted by screen-lit device.
I never found the matching sock to this pair,
they're lying lonely on the bottom stair.
They must've been worn when you were still asleep,
now one's in shadows, one still out to keep.
She blamed the crickets for all of the noise,
said they must be some escaped circus boys.
She marched out into her quiet, dark yard,
and shooed the shadows like unwanted guard.
You sat down for the final test,
only to realize your chest was stressed.
Your pencil taps out loud with no clue,
the clock ticks red in this wrong-room hue.
I lay there close to the cold, wet floor,
my muscles tight with a quiet sore.
There's a faint smell of sweat and the scent,
of every body that's ever been bent.
I wish your name would stick in my mind,
not because I'm ungrateful or unkind.
You told me once, but it slipped out long said,
now you're a story I can't quite thread.
I say it's my last cup, but clearly it's brew,
this is how I convince myself it's still true.
My tongue is a map of every bitter burn,
yet I pour another just to take that turn.
They shine even when the room lacks light,
I bet they've survived more than one fight.
No scuff marks their soles from any trail,
they wait like trophies for daily mail.
You miss the way the water used to spray,
how it rinsed the stress right away.
Now you let the drops fall through your hands,
like time or memory or something that lands.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: You scatter the crumbs into cold mid-flight,
they flutter like ghosts in the morning light.
The birds scream and dive, their wings have rung
the stillness with cries you're too late to tongue.
I'd rather sleep until the rain says stay,
than brave the sky's gray coat and go away.
My coffee cools against this bedroom wall,
while thunder hums a lullaby I recall.
You count the seconds before they all pop,
the wind teasing, "They'll burst when they stop."
Your breath catches just to try to hold,
but the air is sharp, and your hands get cold.
You used to say "I'll just window-shop,"
but now even free samples feel like a crop.
You count every coin, track it for cash,
and let old habits die rather than smash.
You type the late-night thoughts way too deep,
the dog snores loud in their favorite sleep.
You hit send, but there's no one awake to share,
so the joke just hangs lonely in cyber air.
I snapped the band and gave it a loud pop,
now it's wrapped around my chair leg for a prop.
Ten reps later, I feel my bicep lift,
this was meant to build me up—it worked as a gift.
The box tipped over and now it's a mess,
This morning feels cursed, not a bless.
I step back to save my shoes from the cat,
And squash the last bit of milk on the flat.
His voice cuts through the wind with that same call,
a rusty cart stacked high with fruit so tall.
I buy an apple just to hear his smile,
and savor it like hope might last a while.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: You noticed the bill was still not paid due,
The screen turned black, and the world went a little blue.
Your shows, your memes, and your endless stream,
All gone—just like bits of a fading dream.
I hear you humming a half-forgotten tune,
I wonder if you'll be gone from this room soon.
Will you turn off the water and step out,
or leave me listening with growing doubt.
He runs with the sun still up in the sky,
laughing out loud as they float slowly by.
There's nothing but pure, unshaken joy,
he chases the colors, breathless, his toy.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: He sprawls in a dramatic, limp-limbed pose,
belly up with his paws over his toes.
A stray sock serves as a chin-high bean,
while you're the only one who runs this machine.
You watch the machine go round and around, spin,
one sock gets stuck where the lint rolls in.
You fish it out, now it's a lopsided pair,
they land on the floor when you toss them down stair.
You walked alone, the wind blew you through,
while pigeons cooed in the soft, washed-out blue.
You wanted to fold time like a kite and fly,
but the clouds just moved fast in their lazy sky.
She stirs the pot in a quiet, steady slow,
the herbs and broth begin to gently glow.
She knows there's magic in the art of wait,
and time is how you learn to truly create.
You watch the clock, waiting for the train,
The conductor says it's delayed again.
The crowd grows tense, there's no room to delay,
Someone sighs loud, "This never goes away."
I hit the ground but didn't lose my dust,
a bruise bloomed purple with a broken crust.
I stood up tall without a single whine,
the world kept spinning — I'm just fine.
You thought you could unfold the stubborn map,
but it twisted again into a trap.
You tried to trace your path to find your way,
but the creases just laughed as they messed up your play.
Your hair keeps flying into your face like a glare,
you try to ignore it but still do a flair.
You try to flip it back with a quick little flip,
but the wind won't let go—this is war, no grip.
She drops her towel on the sticky gym mat,
it sags to the floor in a limp, damp flat.
She glares at the spot where she left it to throw,
but the machine's whirring now spinning below.
She walks at a stroll but the dog sets the pace,
we zigzag down sidewalks, a sight to erase.
The pup yanks toward every snack bag or treat,
I swear they all wave from the curb on the street.
I clicked "unsubscribe" and now I feel paid,
the monthly charge starts to slowly fade.
I don't want to cancel but I don't owe
your service a second more — let me just go.
I watch their eyes slide down from the eye,
My breath is held, my heartbeat wants to die.
A truck swings left, the moment feels so near,
I pray they see me before it turns unclear.
You flash your fake and say this is the claim,
they'll never know who really made the name.
The billboard shines with your borrowed gold,
and everyone thinks how cleverly you're bold.
You twist the pencil, stuck inside the blade,
the wood is splintered, your notes will fade.
You try to force it, making it spin,
the lead breaks off—your work gets thin.
She drops her coins into the empty jar,
counting each one at the coffee bar.
She thinks this could be the best way,
to save for something better than today.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: She parks her hip right on the couch's edge,
like she's making a territorial pledge.
Her knee is siphoning off all the heat,
I count to ten—then do it again, repeat.

topic: a phone at one percent battery
lines: She clutches her phone with white-knuckled grip,
as if it might vanish from her hand's cold slip.
Her thumb moves in circles, tracing old trace,
whispering prayers into the screen's blank face.
You promise yourself you won't forget to stretch,
but the cat steals the band just as you fetch.
Your left leg lifts with the kind of weak dread
that makes your whole body feel like your poor head.

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: You expect it to break with a final snap,
but it holds your old notes in a tired trap.
Time wears it down, yet it bends and still
keeps pulling the pages together, as it will.
I pulled out my old money—ten-dollar cash,
no card, no app, just a little flash.
The menu was long, but I didn't want to spread,
so I picked the cheapest, safest bet for my head.
My shoe collection runs from dress to crew,
each pair has meaning or feels true.
They line the floor like trophies of my pride,
the mess outside? I'd rather leave it inside.
It snaps into place with a satisfying tight,
you finally see how it fills the sight.
You thought you had nothing but this one clue,
but now you just wish you had some glue.
You watch the rain drip down the glassy flow,
the storm outside is some kind of cruel show.
You raise your hand to trace the drops, but stand
frozen there as thunder shakes the land.
You strain for the train but the crowd blocks your view,
You tiptoe to see, you squint looking through.
The platform's a jam with no space to find your way,
But the wait feels short when there's so much to say.

topic: a taxi driver yelling on phone
lines: The taxi driver's shouting down the fare,
waving through the open window in the air.
He's defending his life choices over meat,
while idling outside the same old beat.
You arch your spine into the fluffiest bend,
ripples of muscles like a message you send.
One foot comes out, slow-motion and claw,
then back to the pillow — your favorite new paw.
You stand there quiet, letting the grass sway,
each blade lifts gently as if to say away.
They dip low near you, whisper how they bend,
a secret soft message the wind likes to send.
That faucet still drips like a metronome song,
It's been going nonstop for way too long.
I could fix it with parts from a toothbrush and dime,
But honestly, I quite like this ticking old time.
You stand there quiet, the lock clicks real near,
a name still sticky on the rusted year.
You hope inside you'll find something worth finding,
maybe a note to say you're still worth minding.
They've pulled and cursed and even slightly cried,
but the stubborn zipper won't move from its side.
They mutter something about bad luck,
and now their jeans are officially stuck.
I was powering through my morning track,
when my foot launched a sudden ankle attack.
I stopped mid-stride to retie the knot,
only to laugh at how I'd wrecked my got.
She locks the door to sing out her tune,
the melody brightens the gray light of noon.
Her hair's all wet but she bobs her head,
the music echoes and gently spread.
They sit with their shoulders almost too near,
the quiet between them draws close to their ear.
A laugh finds its way through the air, warm as gold,
they let it linger, like stories yet to be told.
My thoughts run fast like a grinding old mill,
I pop a vitamin, maybe one more pill.
The pain clears up like a morning without cloud,
I dance in my kitchen, a little too proud.
You took your time but now here's stew,
you said you'd cook, so let me see what you do.
The roast is tender, sides are neat,

He stirs the bowl with a dreamy crunch,

She sets the needle down to make the record play,
the kind of music that comes out at day.

a message lost in time, waiting for a new word.

her steps feel stiff and out of the place.

Its lyrics fit like an old, familiar day.

A quiet hope returns as a strange new gift.

no one dares say she's another big bore.
She skips the lecture they'll never miss,
and claims the seat by the window, her bliss.
