lines: I check my wallet—do I have enough cash?
The pump reads high, but I'm ready for a splash.
My tank's on empty, so this might be my last mile,
I pat the handle and pretend I still smile.
The broken umbrella still leans on its pole,
you wonder if summer could rise from your soul.
You watch clouds roll in, the light takes a shift,
but hope doesn't die—it just moves its drift.

topic: sitting on the porch steps at twilight
lines: You watch the last colors melt into the sky,
the birds say their goodbyes with a soft bye.
You drum your fingers on the worn-out tap,
and kick your heels up, flip the bottle's cap.
You stare at the billboard, full of air,
their model's got a wig you could tear.
They promise you magic, a life you can buy,
while selling moonbeams in a box by the sky.
I watched it roll past the house and the wall,
the lid popped off when it hit a small fall.
Now food scraps and wrappers are strewn on the waste,
and the whole block smells from the rot's bitter taste.
I used to run through the mud with my bare feet,
now I watch kids laugh, trying to repeat.
The rain still makes those same splats on the ground,
but time moves slower when joy wraps you around.
I still hear my grandmother's old hands,
her knitting stood tall where the silence would stands.
I take up the gift that she taught me to wear,
and feel her in every soft click in the air.
The screen went black just as the drama was on,
A cliffhanger now lost, a moment just gone.
It felt like some cruel twist of bad fate,
But restarting again makes the pause just too late.
My guitar hums a low, electric hum,
probably from the way my thumb's too numb.
I try to strum but it just makes more noise,
pretending like I have some musical poise.
You hold the child who won't stop cry,
the clouds blur past the window high.
This cramped room stretches into a tomb,
and hope fades like a forgotten bloom.
She's deep in her focus, in full creative zone,
while the laptop hums its hot, worried tone.
It glows like a space heater but stays on her seat,
the cycle to melt her jeans starts to repeat.
I smile when I see it, the quiet old mold,
I'm not the least bit afraid of its soft, gray bold.
I crumble it gently, a little dry crumb,
and tap out a rhythm that only I drum.
You type a reply but hit delete instead,
Your thumbs replay every word they said,
You check your messages—no new scroll,
Is this how silence cuts a little soul?
You remember how you used to type in your prime,
when coffee and code made perfect all time.
Now crumbs stick where the letters are bent,
but you still love the old machine's scent.
You kept trying to fix the whole little flight,
adjusting the seat, cracking jokes too tight.
But then the clouds shifted into a calm,
and her tears softened into a strange balm.
They play the same song from start to the song,
dancing alone now where we once danced along.
The lights are too bright, the air feels too still,
but the past won't let go, it lingers and will.
She hands over the crumpled ten,
her grin says she's done this again.
The cashier eyes her messy plate,
but says nothing—letting luck decide her fate.
You watched it push off, a perfect small leap,
then vanish beneath the still water to sleep.
For seconds the pond sent wide ripples through light,
and the world felt like something slippery, slight.
They press repeat and let the song replay,
the kind that makes you wish it were your day.
You freeze them in that perfect, pixelated frame,
never tired of hearing their voice say your name.
I hear the first pop of buttered kernels pop,
the smell still hits hard like a summer crop.
I save every sound from that half-eaten mound,
and fold the last scrap down to quiet ground.
She checks her phone—*this can't be going wrong*,
the credits roll, but the crowd still claps along.
Her clap was off the final scene's last cue,
she counts the beats back, face tense all the way through.
You left your towel behind, still holding your scent,
its edge curled softly where your body was bent.
I sit here pretending I never sat this long,
but the memory clings—too vivid, too strong.
You watch the butter melt into golden gold,
the quietest thing turning something so bold.
It slides down the edge, a soft dripping drip,
and you swear the whole toast is a little bit trip.
You left your toothbrush in the perfect spot,
like a hero ending a tight little plot.
It stands there tall, a symbol of your pride,
crowned king of the sink with a regal stride.
She clutches the pole, determined to stand,
her patience crumbling like wet cookie sand.
The overhead speaker gives a glitchy feed,
but no one stops to check—no time, indeed.
My smartwatch buzzes like it's got some cause,
but I'm just here, not saying a pause.
It can't tell when my silence is from the phone,
or if I'm quiet because I feel alone.
They tossed the case by the front door's base,
swore they'd never lose them in that place.
One bud was last heard playing soft jazz left,
now silence fills both ears, but one remains bereft.
I stomp through the fields where the rain made the muck,
my boots squelch with pride in this muddy good luck.
I leap at the puddles, I make a big splash,
the kids all watch me, they know I'm a flash.
You swear you've kept your voice mostly calm,
but your fist keeps tightening against your palm.
You tell it to "fix" while the screen still freeze,
and vow next time you'll use something less breeze.
She swerves into the fast lane without a glance,
her thumbs spell out her name in mid-air dance.

her focus steams through the engine's heat.

no warning, no backup for your dear old ear.

hoping it's just static—no sign of a spark.
My dog has a talent for finding a hide,
he digs by my bed when I flip to his side.

and drops it on guests with a proud little shock.
I watch my hamster chase the same old race,
looping around his cage without a place.

I worry what's inside his little fur-lined skin.
You hit "save" but meant to click **send**,
now the draft's stuck there to bide and to mend.

lines: I count the candles—each one stands for a year,
my hands shake slightly as I get too near.
The last one flickers, a soft final flame,
and I whisper your name to the empty frame.

lines: You watched your kite rise on a gust of air,
now it's tangled in branches, your panic grows bare.

your strings are too frayed to pull it back free.
You own this moment — the feed's full of lag,
your comments drop like a forgotten flag.

but you still say your last word: *not to blame*.

it's stuck on the same beeping, broken tune.

you beg it to brew but it just won't try.
She sets the scene and lets the story play,
the kitchen table her epic war day.

and saves the world beneath a single lamp's light.
I set my max five pounds above my aim,
the barbell trembles in my shaking frame.
My arms don't want to hear the words "don't fail,"

like it's checking if I'm keeping good guard.
It kicks up clumps of wet old dirt,
and stares at me like I might feel hurt.
They said I should hide it behind the front wall,
but my cat knocked it loose with her tiny white ball.
I tried to leave hints, subtle and few,
now watch as they wander the house searching you.
She watches the earth after a quiet morn,
where frost was still holding the green things torn.
The buds bend low, but they won't stay to stand—
they push up from the dirt like hope for the land.
She still holds out a little quiet hope
that it will work again soon, just to cope.

lines: She turns up the radio with her voice,

hoarding threads like treasure every night.

lines: You rummage through the bag but there's just air,

I wake up to an empty shelf and a grin,

She walks beside you, quiet as the side
of a road, pretending she's your official guide.

like magic woken slow from underneath my thrill.
I rang my bell like a king on the street,

She walks into the room, unaware they're in,

My boot breaks through the crust for a lazy slice,

lines: Cold air nips at my face as I step off the stair,

the clock ticks louder each time I press turn.

this glow feels heavy, it's starting to steal my soul.
You watch the steam rise in a soft swirl,
the morning feels light for this single girl.
The yolk breaks open with a tiny crack,
your smile follows sunshine on its track.
They press their palm against the cold machine's hand,
The screen blinks out, and I don't understand.
It reads "Zero" and they hold the screen real now,
Their shoulders sink—I wish I knew some how.
I still have the sweater we wore the same blue,
it's tucked in my closet, waiting for you.
I never meant harm when I bought the same thought,
now every time we meet, we're silently caught.
He sets the heat ten degrees too cold,
"Winter's harsh," he says, his voice shrill and old.
Their breath hangs thick—another full-blown clash,
The dog just sighs and sneezes into the ash.
My umbrella's broken, the beach offers no shade,
Waves crash slow, a sunset starts to parade.
A breeze comes through like it knows how to drift,
I smile at the wind—it feels like things might lift.
The sun throws golden rays that barely last,
we count the hours till these hot days pass.
She smiles through sweat, her face a grin,
I toss my shirt in the laundry bin.
You retrace your steps in every known spot,
But nothing shows signs you could have forgot.
Your morning plans are already all run,
The clock ticks ahead, and the day feels undone.
She orders the strongest coffee, black and bold,
It steams like a sunrise, deep and gold.
Three A.M. calls, but she's never late,
She claims it's her rhythm, not anyone's fate.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: His belly rises slow beneath his fur,
Not even thunder could make him stir.
He sleeps as daylight fades into the sun,
Dreaming he's somewhere the world is done.
She slipped through the gate before bouncers knew her name,
thinking this was fate or maybe just plain lame.
Now she's pressed against the wall way out of sight,
wondering if it's worth the risk for one last night.
They found it tucked inside an old crack,
dust swirling softly as they flipped it back.
Static hums through memories from those days,
a song from a long-dead relationship phase.
You hunt for that button-down with mismatched thread,
twist your scarf until it turns your head.
You pose like you're fusing past and present blend,
but time just applauds the look it can't mend.
I tried to scrape it from the edge of the jar,
but the last drop clung like a stubborn star.
My tongue goes for the spoon and misses the lick,
now I'm stuck with this sweet mess on my stick.
My legs give out beneath the iron bar,
but I'm holding steady—don't want to mar
this moment, the sweat, the grind, the weight,
the strength I haven't built yet still I create.
I didn't check the calendar that line,
just turned the corner and saw the sign.
People danced to the beat of a drum,
and I followed the music wherever it come.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: My phone is already by my head,
I fall asleep but I'm not in bed.
I dream in metrics—just numbers and scroll,
I check for likes, but who's really got soul?
That carton's been there since last month's same shame,
I can't pretend this is some cleanup game.
The fridge stinks with that sour, weird smell,
living with spoiled food is kitchen hell.
You say the wind chimes don't begin to sing,
but they turn the air into a lovely thing.
A warm breeze lifts their notes without a breeze,
just enough to dance and soothe and please.

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: She adjusts her hat, flips off her cap,
then forces a grin and takes the snap.
Her arms go stiff in some awkward pose,
while no one laughs but she texts "Love these toes."
I stare at the still life frozen in this frame,
your face lit by a matchstick's flickering flame.
My hands reach out but time won't let me fall,
we're trapped between the reel and the projection wall.
You drift across the lane without a care,
your brain too busy to run or to spare.
A honk arrives, you let out a sigh,
but keep your thumbs typed to the point you might die.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: You scroll past the news and you hit your bed,
The app whispers numbers and your heart said,
"Maybe tomorrow will reach my new aim,"
you close it and keep the small hope as a flame.
You look down and catch your left sock in the eye,
the pattern doesn't match, your shoes scream "why?"
You check if anyone else noticed in the room,
but now it's stuck there, coloring your whole gloom.
I walk slower now just to match your pace,
I leave more space between my body and your space.
I watch your face for signs you're moving too slow,
you smile and say, "this is the best place to go."
The moment the egg went into the shell,
I knew this kitchen was turning to hell.
Its yolk was still perfect, a drop of pure gold,
but something about it felt strangely old.
She bought the stamps but never sent the mail,
their corners are yellowed, ink has gone pale.
She flips through each address on every page,
like birds trapped in paper, words in a cage.
You follow the sound of the water so near,
it hums in your ear like a lullaby clear.
You wish you could stay but the current calls away,
and carries your worries off deep into today.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: You drape the blanket over both of us to rest,
my head now lies perfectly snug against your chest.
It's soft and warm, this pile of woven fold,
but what I'd trade to feel just once again your hold.
She haggles with the driver about the base rate,
then yells at him when he blocks her exit gate.
The app said fifteen but it's now forty-three cap—
she swears the system was designed just to trap.
She stops her walk when she hears the crickets home,
their evening chorus, a song to roam.
The world seems to pause under twilight's soft hush,
no need for a clock, she forgets all her rush.
I catch the flakes that fall gently on my down,
they shimmer like glitter from some quiet town.
The winter air holds just enough to keep the chill,
but I let it linger, soft and sweet and still.
I pause to watch the sky stretch out so wide,
the wind hums low, it keeps me calm aside.
That bird sits steady on its thinning wing,
and I believe in hope because of that small thing.
You've taken a hundred bad photos of this view,
but every single shot looks like a clue.
You'll never send it home to stick on your mail,
it's just a rock and a bench down the trail.
You're playing hide-and-seek with your acorn game,
burying clues beneath a fallen frame.
The ground grows lumpy where you dig too bare,
but you keep laughing in the crisp, bright air.
I raised my hand to help the teacher teach,
now I'm tapping desks with this long, bony reach.
The kids all lean in when I point the class,
the sunlight shines through me like a drinking glass.
My thoughts move slower now, like bent and broken time,
I can't track the jokes or pick my moment to chime.
I float through questions I pretend to feel,
like a meeting is a wheel I'm not quite real.
You leave one earbud plugged into one side,
it's not lost, it's just waiting to hide.
You half-listen when they try to call,
but you're close to something with just one ear, not all.
Each morning beside the same glass on the side,
She leaves it at angle to let the tip dry wide.
The scent of old mint still clings to the mint,
Her name isn't there, but her grip leaves a print.
They order burgers but keep the fries near,
you lean across just to touch their ear.
You take a handful and call it a grab,
they laugh and pretend to be mad like a crab.
You stood so close to that perfect spot last year,
your tires humming in my window's ear.
Now someone else's initials mark the chalk,
and I pretend I never start to talk.
You hang my stuff in your closet like a rack,
then borrow my hoodie and forget to bring it back.
I track you down each time just to go through,
the mess of your room, still can't find the glue.
The stack of folders speaks in quiet years,
dust settled where time and memory appears.
You built that tower to reach new height,
but now it blocks the soft afternoon light.
The beat from next door won't turn off its tune,
It throbs through the walls like some cursed rune.
I raise my own volume to match the blast,
but silence remains what I've missed in the past.
I dropped the band and it snapped toward the floor,
this thing's been in a decades-long arm war.
I yank at the middle to untie the knot,
and throw it across the room like a missed free shot.
The showerhead once gave a steady, warm stream,
now every drop feels like a quiet scream.
A single drip echoes in rhythm, sharp drip,
the porcelain cracked by some old, unseen chip.
They left the milk out and caused a big spill,
the mess sat there untouched, cold and still.
No one stepped forward to clean up the crust,
it turned into something more permanent than dust.
I duck behind a row of lockers in the hall,
the office has my number if they choose to call.
I hope this isn't turning into long-term fear,
but for now, silence is the luck of the ear.
I watch the condiment follow its trail,
its red now a streak down my plate's edge and pale.
I try to catch every last drop,
but all I hold is an empty crop.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: You freeze when you spot your name while you scroll,
the screen feels like it's spinning inside out, whole.
You check if it was a mistake or a troll's post,
but deep down you're secretly flattered the most.
You call this art? It's just a big mess,
I guess you've spent way too much time to obsess.
Next you'll try to frame it with some tape,
I'd rather eat the paper just to escape.
She hit send by mistake and caused a blast,
the whole team saw her rant from days long past.
It went viral before she could stop to send,
but she laughed it off—pride has no need to bend.
I found him sitting in my salad spot,
chewing through the lettuce like a movie star shot.
He won't take the bait or even try to leap,
just sits there judging every move I keep.

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: She revs up the motor and flies down the hill,
her hair in a whirlwind, she's lost all her chill.
She zips through the traffic, dodging the bees,
then locks up her scooter and drops both her keys.
She leaves her shoes out like she owns the floor,
as if this hallway's some abandoned store.
The smell of leather lingers, sharp and scent,
the soles curled upward, still a little bent.
You tried to work but the cat claims your heat,
your deadlines are melting, pure defeat.
You sigh and text "CAT ON MY KEYS,"
the world replies "We get it. Not a disease."
You load the cart with chips and it pop,
you pause at the candy aisle one last stop.
That bag of pretzels makes a loud crunch,
your snack haul is ready for tomorrow's lunch.
I walked all the way home with a milk carton splash,
I tried to sprint but my socks got a dash.
Now the floor's got a puddle of creamy white,
but hey—it's a good excuse for ice cream tonight.
She was all spark and light, a full-volume boom,
now she's slumped in her chair, a tired old room.
Her coffee goes cold as she slowly sinks slump,
a deflated balloon with a sugar stuck lump.
You're stuck in this line with no end in near,
the man behind you keeps talking in your ear.
Your flight was delayed, they just made the call,
and now you're trapped between the gate and the mall.
I finally found some space to breathe and room,
no more clothes crushing me like old bad loom.
I try it on and it feels like it fit,
I leave without looking back to quit.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: She throws the last crumb into thin air,
while they argue who got the unfair share.
They squabble with beaks, all cold and grit,
like it's worth their whole day to look so fit.
A pigeon waddled up and stole my fry,
now struts around like it can't even fly.
I laugh—what's lunch to birds but just a take?
They probably eat better where they wake.
She laughs when she sings the same birthday song,
tips her head back just to laugh it along.
A flicker dies on the last rising flame,
but she's still laughing—how could anyone blame?
A close-up shows her smile and wide grin,
her eyes sparkle bright, alive and within.
A tune hums through the theater's old song,
I laugh with the crowd as we all dance along.
You stood alone on the docked ferry's shore,
the engines left without a final roar.
The bridge is closed now—no more tickets sold,
the wind cuts through your coat like knives so cold.
Your laptop starts to glow with that warning light heat,
the plastic grows warm where it presses your seat.
You move it to a desk and you fan it to cool,
now the cursor dances—your digital tool.
You hit "send" at the stroke of twelve, full send,
your last message, a "goodnight" to a friend.
The phone dies at one as you check the clock,
alone but unshaken—you sleep like a rock.
I blast the cartoons at full volume sound,
the neighbors all come out and stomp around.
I am their worst nightmare, a time-travel child,
I own this couch like a Saturday-morning wild.
She hands over a crumpled old ten,
"I'll get it right," she says, smiling again.
The clerk gives her back coins for the change,
but she keeps the paper like it's something strange.
Your cat just sent the water bowl into spill,
It pounces on the floor with a puddle thrill.
You clean up the mess with a towel and a sigh,
But the real success is that it wasn't your guy.
You hit "sync" instead of your photo app, snap!
Now my vacation's all over your map.
I try to delete them but they won't go trash,
our albums are mixed in a visual clash.
You say it's too cold, I say you're just chill,
the air hums loud, but we're both so still.
We leave the degrees at some halfway dust,
our silence grows thicker than seasons or trust.
She dropped the can and watched the soda spill,
but the sound that came out felt almost a thrill.
The speaker hummed, trying hard to stay hush,
while static danced in the sudden white rush.
I fake every nod but I don't have a thought,
they think I was trained but I wasn't taught.
I stare at the slides, there's no sense in this plan,
I smile through the haze, I'm a sleep-deprived man.
You watch the rabbit move so still,
its tiny breaths seem they won't fill.
It sniffs the air, like the whole world's dust,
yet you feel how gentle love can trust.
She tries to join the leaves as they dance,
but her feet stick fast—no luck or chance.
They swirl and glide with effortless grace,
while she just stands there, still, no place.
Above me, they shift and slowly take form—
a dragon, a dog, a coming storm.
They billow and rise, they drift on these wings,
a kingdom of clouds where I am their kings.
You left it by the bench where we once walked the path,
your initials carved out crooked in bad math.
Time turned the silver steel to red with rust,
but the cracks still hold the memories we trust.
You blow on the puff and make your one wish,
like it can fix things, or at least wash your dish.
They float up to the sky with such glee,
but why do they leave you with nothing but debris?
He shouts his pitch with a practiced shill,
like this could ever be more than a thrill.
His "fresh-baked" cookies aren't even gold,
just stale, but he sells 'em real bold.
You watch the highway stretch far ahead,
while summer fields slowly fade and spread.
You wonder if this was what the trip
was meant to be—a slow, hot slip.
You step outside to find your street is now a block,
tables bloom with waffles and live music stock.
A man in costume shouts, "This is no act,"
but you know better—you read the signs, the fact.
I blow a bubble so high it floats way away,
now the kids beg to see another display.
It pops with a sound like a secret we pop,
I dip my wand in the bowl and don't let it drop.
I fumble through pockets searching for the slot,
the machine won't take cards, I don't even got
a dime left to drop after buying my dime,
I curse this old meter for wasting my time.
I sleep in the bed where the summer heat
has soaked every dream into worn-out repeat.
My pillow's a map of my struggle and proof—
I built this sweat palace from nothing but roof.
You stare at the mountain of carrots on board,
convinced this will never feel worth the reward.
Your blade shakes as it risks a bad slip,
the veggie world's out to get you to trip.
I press my palm against the frozen cold,
This ancient door is getting way too old.
I fumble through my bag, find the cracked key,
It jams again—this rent's just not worth the fee.

topic: seeing your mom's new profile pic
lines: She posted a photo from years gone old,
A smile in the light, full of gold.
You double-tap slow, like turning a book,
And time feels a little softer when you look.
I watch the tree shake off its last leaf bare,
the wind spins secrets through the thinning air.
It seems the squirrel buried acorns, some,
but none have sprouted where they're meant to come.
I watch it swim in its little patch of gold,
I've never been much good at being told
how to care, so I fill up the bowl
and wonder if fish have something like a soul.
It hovers in mid-air without a care,
wings whirring like a broken desk fan's pair.
You watch it stay absolutely still,
yet somehow manage to move at will.
You take a sip and then you watch it spill,
"Just leave it," says your friend, "I'll refill."
The cap's been off since morning—meet your floor,
Now your carpet hosts the saga of this lore.
You stand too quick, your vision fades from head,
your pulse is loud, your thoughts won't spread.
You track the rush, like clockwork, the blood
returns—but not before you felt a flood.
You choose your outfit but I won't wear
what you call a match—it's forced, not fair.
This isn't fashion, it's your twisted plan
to turn me into some dummy clone man.
Your empty mug sits dangerously near
the edge, as if trying to tickle my ear.
Morning condensation clings to its frost,
a silent reminder of where you are lost.
You remember the old blend, that perfect first batch,
how it lit up your mood like a lost little match.
Now the machine hums but the brew's weak and plain beans,
while you scroll through reviews, half-awake on your screens.

topic: a phone at one percent battery
lines: She checks the screen again for an incoming call,
she's missed three alarms and now she's late for the mall.
Her eyes scan the room for the charging plug,
her phone drops to zero right there on the rug.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: Mid-sentence the speaker's whole speech goes out of flow,
a tickle becomes a trumpet-like blow.
Words leave his mouth but they don't hit the air,
he ends up all pink from the nose down to bare.
Rice and broccoli sit there all steamed,
Leftovers from what she once dreamed.
She didn't cook this with any grace,
But the scent feels like home in this place.
You bought it for style, but it never was good,
the wind would flip it inside out where it stood.
You'll tuck it away until next spring to mend,
hoping the cracks will fade if a friend helps them blend.
You leave your plant forgotten each day,
it turns toward nothing but shadows and gray.
Its leaves begin to fold inward and bend,
a quiet goodbye you don't quite intend.
I left the stove on, but not for a fire—
just a simmer, the kind that shows my desire.
Patience is a craft, and I'm keeping it slow,
letting time sizzle in a quiet red glow.
She traces the shape of the cloud's soft form,
then adds a few lines to make it a storm.
Her hands know the right kind of pressure to shade,
as memories fall like the charcoal cascade.
She turns up the heat, but it's still cold in there,
she glares at the glass that won't clear her stare.
There's no way to tell if her makeup looks good—
the fog might be right, maybe she never should.
They always stop where the light turns the view
to gold, like they're seeing the world as brand-new.
You'll never find a better place than this bend,
but they don't take a card—just stand there and send.
The heater blows nothing but cold air,
You wear three sweaters, still so bare.
You simmer in silence, half a stew,
This place is a dump—what else is new?
She draws her rainbow across every sky,
even when the ground is too hard to dry.
Her fingers trace colors as if she still play,
the magic lingers where her marks stay.
You offer snacks but she gives no clue,
she stares right through you in cool, calm hue.
You call her name again—she won't even ask,
just licks her paw like it's some grand task.
The sky refuses to stop pouring down in rain,
we crowd close together, forced to remain.
Water still falls through cracks overhead to drip,
someone's heel catches a puddle, you almost slip.
You flip the switch but find no clue,
the bulb still burns, you don't know what to do.
A warm glow lingers as you walk below,
maybe it's waiting for you to let it go.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: You swear it's a diamond the moment it gleam,
your future already in gold-trimmed dream.
You show it off proudly, vow you will keep,
but it chips on the counter—just another cheap.
The lights dim and I wait for my cue,
the silence turns thick, almost blue.
One last check of the script for the scene,
then we clap—synchronized, clean.
They've tried everything else but still don't fit,
adjusting seams by inches in one bit.
They're nearly there, almost see it through,
the label says "M" and it feels quite true.
My tires grip tight as I take the next spin,
The gravel crunches but never feels thin.
I leave a clean trail through the dusty trail,
My balance is perfect—I've moved up a scale.
I waited five minutes to present my slide-time,
the cursor just stared like it owed me a dime.
I checked the settings, the cables, the code,
but nothing would fix how the whole thing went bad-load.
I watch the robin hop around in a dance,
it pecks up bugs with its beak in a chance.
Its chest is a flash of the lawn's brightest green,
I pause my work just to watch this small screen.
I walked through puddles just to keep my pace,
no one saw the way I lost my grace.
Now I'm drying socks with a hair dryer's shock,
cursing every pothole in the block.
You stand too quick and it hits your head,
Your vision fades like old sour bread.
You reach to grab something from the rush,
But the floor's too close and you feel the flush.
She never could sleep when the barking was late,
she'd sigh and get up and adjust the gate.
That dog in the yard never seemed to be known,
but her voice held a kindness he'd heard in his tone.
I wear this hat for my daily job,
it has a visor with a little knob.
It survives every loud crash and bump,
but can't fix the neck pain after lunchtime slump.
I swiped my card to fill the empty tank,
the screen said "declined" by the gas pump's bank.
The price of gas is more than just a pain,
it hits the same old note—this cuts me again.

topic: a friend who is always late
lines: She swore she'd be there but didn't even say,
"Traffic," again—her favorite kind of delay.
We waited through thunder, the sky turned to rain,
while she texted us memes from her car, no pain.
The bulb made a soft click and gave one last pop,
I sighed and said work will have to stop.
I reached for the flashlight on my key ring to glow,
and saw something shimmer on the floor far below.
I stepped in the tub but I had no clue,
my socks stayed behind when I took off my shoe.
There's a posted warning I'd never seen before—
I slipped like a cartoon and landed on the floor.
I watched her dig in the garden last yard,
now she's gnawed my boots into a threadbare guard.
She says it's play, but I can't help this chew,
she makes a mess I can't pretend to view.
You swear it's not just your ears or your will—
the fridge lets out a long, lonesome chill.
Its metal heart beats out a slow cold,
and you wonder if this old thing feels sold.
You watch the world like it's not the same seem,
as if you're part of some half-remembered dream.
Your nose is pressed to the cold, flat glass,
watching birds land on the forbidden grass.
They sip their coffee against the early light,
the way they blink seems like a quiet fight.
Their fingers trace the steam from their own hands,
but say nothing of the dreams that stayed in plans.
That lipstick stain is unmistakably mine,
A smudge on the rim, still, it runs through the line.
It's not about pride—it's a quiet proof
Of mornings shared where the past finds its roof.
They tried to stretch out their stiff old post,
pretending they weren't too sore to host.
Their joints still ache from last week's snow,
but they won't let it show — or let the cat know.
You hover near the bloom as if to rest,
your wings so delicate, they barely test
the air between your body and the lift
of life—this moment, fragile, quiet, gift.
You wake up to power, not just a bland sound,
your alarm grabs the room from the silence around.
You vibrate through the walls with a loud, proud ring,
they'll never forget how you shockingly spring.

topic: a plate with two leftover bites
lines: She left just two bites on her favorite cake,
a little rebellion from her healthy break.
The crumbs have found a quiet home in the spot
where sunlight curls around the rug's loose knot.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: I sat so close to you, shoulder to near,
whispering stories into your ear.
We curled up tight like memories in a fold,
warm as the past we used to hold.
The carton's past its prime, but still she ate,
pretending this was something meant to fate.
She sipped the curdled mess from a clear glass,
then called it "avant-garde" to her whole class.
The porch light flickers but stays on,
Maybe they're still here, not completely gone.
You can almost see a shadowed soul,
Waiting by the door, the breeze to scroll.
You scroll through old photos, trying to find the scene,
where faces fill up the edges of your screen.
You zoom in, but they're just pixels fading through,
and suddenly it hits—you're alone with you.
The kettle begins to whistle and boil,
She stirs the old tea with a little oil.
Her breath turns to mist, the world feels calm,
The steam is her morning, quiet balm.
It's just a reminder of you and your call,
I stare at the screen in a quiet, bare hall.
I mute the phone fast, but it's hard to deny—
your face still fills silence like sunset in sky.
I watch the world from this safe little still,
imagining lives that might give me a thrill.
Their shadows don't make out the whole shape,
but longing looks better through half-drawn escape.
I jingle my keys but they won't help me free
the lock on my bike looks too messy to be.
I try to spin it, wiggle, and nudge with a grin,
it stays locked tight—I still haven't got in.
You toss the whole ball into the air to sing,
it dances behind you like rope from a string.
You laugh as it loops through your fingers and you,
the tangle is magic, let it all just undo.
She watches the bus pull away from its route,
her coffee gone cold as the schedule falls out.
There's a calm in her tired, half-smiling face,
like this is the kind of loss she's come to embrace.
She watches the water go rushing through stones,
soft sounds from the stream in familiar tones.
Her voice echoes faint, the same words repeat below,
but the current moves on, and her sorrows just grow.
You tried to one-arm your personal lift,
forgot it was never a perfect gift.
The mirror shows you, red-faced and sweat,
but you don't really want to leave it yet.
I peeked just once since I took off the lid,
the broth has been bubbling where secrets got hid.
Now garlic and ginger rise up in a bubble,
but I'm sure this won't be my kind of trouble.
You load it just like the manual said to try,
but the dishes still come out damp and dry.
That wineglass is still streaked from last week's glass,
like a relic from a better dinner class.
They never really match—how they show,
the way you wear them, soft and slow.
One red, one blue, the contrast feels deep,
like your quirks are the things I still keep.
She counts the coins with slow, familiar hands,
the register beeps where she once stood and stands.
The coins feel heavy, like the year is old,
but they don't hold value, not even close to gold.
You lie awake, tracing cracks in the still,
remembering when the world felt like a thrill.
Now your thoughts drift where they never could wind,
a quiet storm forms far from your mind.
You swear it's a siren or maybe a call,
but it's just a bus that's already in sprawl.
It's seven A.M.—your hair still in shock,
you curse the heavens and your sleepless clock.
The baby waves at the clouds so high,
she thinks they're candy in a distant sky.
But when she's upset, no one can hold
her tears at bay—she's too young to be told.

topic: a child drawing on the table
lines: I watched her sketch the world in soft blue shade,
a rainbow of crayons, her fingers in parade.
She leaned too far, the paper started to stick,
I couldn't help but smile as she gave it a kick.

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: I skimmed the review, then I gave it a thought,
they said the new menu was barely bought.
But my barista's still got her magic beans,
the place is still humming with daily scenes.
She sends "u up?" like it's some kind of test,
then laughs when her number gets blocked from your best.
You lie there with guilt till your phone lights up back,
and you vow never to text like a crack.
She watches the plastic bag catch the wind's low flow,
still trying to blame it for the mess we throw.
It twirls like a ghost of something meant to spin,
a poor imitation of the real thing's thin.
She moves with the rhythm of the crowd's flow,
stepping where the gaps let her go.
A stranger offers her space with a grin,
and she thanks him, as if this moment could begin.
They crouch behind the firs and poplar trees,
wincing at the brambles scraping their knees.
You're it, but you never had the heart to lead,
so you chase the same old shadow they need.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: He traces the route with a finger's bold route,
Each mark is a memory without a doubt.
His careful old hand lays claim to this land,
A world in a crease he once dared to stand.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: You snap the pink and gold across the sky,
zooming in like you're framing just your eye.
It's clearly a vibe—no caption, no mood,
just a sunrise and the promise of better food.
I read the tweet and slip back into the past,
where every laugh felt like our very last.
Their words still carry the echo of their voice,
and I'd choose that lunch, that moment, any choice.
They spelled the address completely wrong,
the driver called to double-check along.
The order's cold and half an hour out,
she's pacing now, upset and full of doubt.
The car won't start, the engine just turns cold,
Her gloves are still in the glovebox, so old.
She tries the key but it sticks in the lock,
Her patience has left her, ten degrees from shock.
Your music still rings in my sleepless ears,
though we haven't been close in so many years.
I found your old headphones by my bed's head,
I put them on slowly, the silence now spread.
I stand here in silence where the water is still,
the moon above shines on this quiet hill.
It paints the surface with a silver gleam,
and I feel like this moment could be a dream.
You listen for echoes but hear only deep,
the world outside settled in long ago, asleep.
You count the wet streaks as they blur every trace,
imagining time sliding off your own face.
You blow until the soapy film will fly,
they float up high toward the open sky.
Your laughter echoes when they all begin to pop,
you pause to smile before you want to stop.
She sits beside him in the still room,
the clock ticking like a silent loom.
Her thoughts drift somewhere far away,
but she won't break the tension today.
I love how the thunder starts up in the storm,
the way it makes even strangers feel warm.
The rhythm of rain taps out a wild beat,
and I cheer for the sky's strange little feat.
Your dog sniffs the breeze without a care,
tail wagging wildly, eyes full of dare.
They stare at the door, ready to run,
as if every walk promises new fun.
I looped the band too many times tonight,
it snaps like a snake, gives me a fright.
I toss it back—it doesn't even lie
flat on the floor like it's about to die.
The pan lets out a sudden loud crack,
She jumps and knocks a glass off the back.
The room is thick with smoke and scent,
She leans too close—her sleeve gets bent.
You watch it hover—so close yet still,
a flicker of summer's last possible thrill.
It dances above the pond's wet air,
then vanishes quick as your damp, warm bare.
The window's frozen mid-way down, my role
in this silent disaster feels like coal.
I mash the button, but it won't just spin,
now I'm sweating, and my patience runs real thin.
I twisted the bottle too hard, lost the cap,
Now sugary liquid sits waiting to trap.
I wiped every surface to make things feel clear,
Just hope my old speakers still sound like they're dear.
You shiver in the doorway, jeans still cold,
fingers fumbling with a stubborn zip to hold.
The teeth catch where your patience starts to thread,
I step closer, warm and slow, to help you spread.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: She traces the faces trapped behind glass and frame,
the clothes are all dated but the looks feel the same.
Her little sister's laugh is frozen in that smile,
the clock ticks away as the silence fills the while.
She cuts into the fast lane without a glance,
the driver honking her first name in dance.
Her thumbs move quick with a sharper flow,
her screen lights up while the rest just grow.
She smacks the screen like it might help it bang,
the device just hums and doesn't even sang.
It spins in circles, slow and vague, to load,
she yells, "Reboot! This isn't airplane mode!"
You watch the first drop fall far from your hand,
You try to catch it, but it slips off the brim and
The wall looks worse now than the painted mess,
This could have been done with more care or with less.
You left your seat when the credits came,
but paused at the door, still caught in the frame.
The lights were up, you couldn't have cried,
but your eyes told a truth you tried to hide.
I left my credit card near the snack-food yard,
or so I said when I fumbled my card.
The cashier raised an eyebrow at my screen,
as if she'd seen this kind of act before, serene.
We built a castle in the middle of the room,
where shadows danced above us like a loom.
You whispered secrets meant to stay and hide,
and never let go of my warm, small side.
Her shoulders slump like they forgot their back,
she cracks her neck but it won't quite crack.
She tries a yoga move, a half-assed pose,
then slouches again just to show she knows.
He watches the hamster run and spin,
legs churning, growing sore and thin.
The cage light flickers off his fur,
a tiny astronaut, sleepless, stir.
You open the mailbox with quiet dread,
your whole life weighs heavy on your head.
They ask for more money, again, no cash,
this is how the month begins to clash.
I press the bulb hard until my palms feel slick,
the rhythm's a dance I don't want to kick.
I peel with care, each skin falls when I press,
there's nothing left but the core of it, less.
You watch them swim through the empty waste,
their food drifts down like some slimy paste.
The aquarium rocks out a tinny bell,
but they don't seem to notice this watery hell.
I watch them crawl in lines toward some unknown home,
their tiny legs moving under a sky's wide dome.
Maybe they carry dreams they hope will help them lift,
or maybe life's a story handed down as gift.
You stop your car for a flash of a deal,
but the ad shows nothing feels new or real.
A voice promises magic in every lie,
while your eyes roll back at the nonsense they'll buy.
They stack up each morning like a growing pile,
I sip coffee and stare at them awhile.
My phone buzzes twice about my old debt,
and I wonder why I didn't just pay it yet.
She shouted above the crowd, refused to stand,
her socks soaked through in the mud-slicked land.
The team tried to cheer but could barely yell,
the rain poured so hard, it drowned every swell.
You call this a fort? It's a lopsided cave,
you draped up a sheet like some poor man's wave.
The pillows are lopsided, the chairs full of shame,
but go ahead—hide, it's your sad little game.
You tap the cloud, and you sync the wrong,
Now our albums hum with the same old song.
I scroll through faces from the past,
They blink at me from your accidental blast.
I left it there with a note full of hope,
just in case someone else needed to cope.
Now I walk by each shelf, checking for its return,
hoping this way we both might get to learn.
You still wear your lipstick like a half-erased kiss,
and I can't help but miss the taste of you on this.
I try to hold onto the memory, the warm
of moments that now only haunt like a swarm.
I used to double-tap with such grace on my thumb,
now I just stare at each post as it come.
My feed feels colder since I saw your new screen,
where once we shared the world like a strange sweet scene.

topic: losing your wallet at the mall
lines: She swore she left it right next to her spot,
but now she's standing at the register, forgot.
A teen asks if she'll be quick or will dash,
so she pretends she came here without cash.
She's live on her phone, the world now her feed,
Her face flushes pink when the comments start bleed.
The chat screams "CHEESE!" but she won't say chat,
She strikes a pose, forgets where the camera's at.
You said you'd text me when you got to your drop,
but silence is the only thing I got to stop.
You don't have time to read my quick little blame,
just scroll and ghost me like it's some new game.
The sky was a brilliant, unworried blue,
until the dark clouds rolled in fast and through.
Now rain hammers down on the rooftops and street,
the dog days have vanished like smoke from the heat.

topic: a missed phone call from Mom
lines: My phone buzzed once but I missed your call,
maybe it slipped like a dropped pool ball.
I'm busy living this weird fun day—
I'll text you later and pretend we play.

topic: walking past each other in a crowd
lines: You hold your head high, blocking out the view,
the chaos swirls around but can't break through.
You glide with a quiet, practiced kind of grace,
while others jostle for their crowded place.
She fumbles for coins in her coat pocket's drop,
the meter is blinking, she needs to stop.
She counts twice but knows the total is wrong,
the car's getting tickets right down the row along.
She never sent the stack, but it makes a fine mail,
each card a secret she chose to keep trail.
It sits in a box, her most boastful pride,
unread but perfect—she won't ever decide.

topic: someone spilling punch on the rug
lines: You knock the bowl and the punch begins to spill,
you swear it's fate, your clumsy, doomed free will.
The red swirls spread into the rug's deep stain,
and there it sits, a mess meant to remain.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: You keep the blanket pulled tight to your near,
afraid this moment might end in a year.
Your eyes trace every old hole in the seam,
but you stay quiet, so no truth has to scream.
She keeps the dents as proof from days gone past,
each dent a memory she won't let last.
It lost its shape but still holds its form,
like her—bent by life, but still whole in the storm.
My coffee sloshes close to the keyboard's spill,
I juggle keys like climbing a steep hill.
Each letter feels like a missed chance to tap,
my brain's on fire but the shift key won't cap.
You struggle to squeeze through but can't seem to pass,
your coffee sways gently as if dancing on grass.
You grip the cart handle and make a sharp turn,
it scrapes down the wall like a wound left to burn.
You watched your fries disappear from the plate,
but now it's their turn—your sneaky new fate.
You've learned to let go with a shrug and some peace,
while your quiet revenge starts to slowly increase.
My screen won't stay on—it's already fade,
I curse at my phone like it's made of jade.
I've swapped every port and tried every try,
it blinks in a taunt, "You can't charge this lie."
You swipe past another loud screed on the screen,
the kind that's only there to be mean.
It's not your fight, but still you read the post,
then breathe and float down the quieter coast.

topic: sitting on the porch steps at twilight
lines: The sky still holds the day's last glow,
a breeze reminds me time won't slow.
I hear your name in the wind's soft voice,
I sit here longer—my favorite choice.
I hit "send" before I had time to post,
her name popped up like some digital ghost.
I deleted the tag but it still shows up class,
now I'm panicking worse than a cracked iPhone glass.
I dropped my fries on the sidewalk's ground,
a pigeon saw and came running round.
It bobbed its head like it didn't care,
and flew off with both, not a single dare.

topic: sitting on the porch steps at twilight
lines: The evening air feels warm without a breeze,
the sun lingers as if to tease.
I sip my tea from a chipped old mug,
my feet curl on the threadbare rug.
I type out "break" but the screen shows a key,
my message to her is now twisted with me.
Autocorrect insists it should say "fly,"
and I'm stuck in this mess, trapped in a lie.
She holds the tape tight, searching for the song,
her fingers move gently down the spool along.
I watch her focus, how she gives it her hand,
this moment was soft, perfectly unplanned.
They know they don't need words to feel so sure,
their quiet touch acts as a deeper cure.
The world keeps spinning, but they stay still,
like love has built a bridge where time won't kill.
You looked up when the thunder cracked the sky,
hoping the storm would pass before it got too dry.
The frog leaped out, ignored your inward call,
and vanished where the water waited cold and tall.
I wait for you to take your first small bite,
while your eyes stay glued to the screen's soft light.
You swipe through messages, chats, and the scroll,
but all I want is to feel my love in your soul.
They wave your card through the red light twice to scan,
your hand trembles as you sign a line you can't plan.
The total jumps—this looks more like a debt,
your face goes warm, but you don't break a sweat.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: I light it up to keep the fear from coming out,
but shadows still whisper their usual doubt.
I hold steady, let the flicker guard the flame,
and believe that hope feels like the same.
They type "Goodnight" when the hour hands sends,
a formal sign-off to their old friends.
The phone screen's glow competes with the moon,
a lonesome buzz that can't be unsung too soon.
She gave the lever one more shove to try,
bread stuck halfway down, making her sigh.
she slammed the plug and cursed it off,
the smoke got thick, and we all had to cough.
You walk across the tiles, they gleam too slick,
some unseen drip played its cold, wet trick.
You pause to balance, but still you took the fall,
now every step echoes the day you recall.
I check my phone and the digital clock,
the last item's still listed in stock.
I run to grab it before the price tag
gets changed, or the deal starts to drag.
You say the quiet isn't doing any wrong,
but silence stretches like a sour song along.
Words collapse into soft, unspoken lies,
we speak in glances and avoid each other's eyes.
You thought the yarn would just sit tight and roll,
but it had other ideas for its goal.
You tried to take a quick ten-minute nap,
now you're surrounded by a knitter's trap.
He's got a turntable that screams ancient age,
spins vinyl slow like a farewell stage.
No one knows why he still treats this as a clue,
but he swears that warmth is somehow more true.
The shovel slips off the edge of the pitch,
I lose my footing, fall into a ditch.
I dig through the ground thick with last year's mold,
this job feels tougher than I'm getting old.
The screen says "Enter PIN" but I have no code,
I stand there like a fool, some tragic ode.
I tried my card again—still can't get a tap,
this line moves slower than a debt trap.
Your laptop's typing up a storm of keys,
the cat treats your work like a lazy tease.
Its warm, soft fur blocks every single key,
your deadline blurs where your focus used to be.
We laughed and we talked through the late-night chat,
and I forgot how time can fill your hat.
Now silence feels heavy, too fast for my pace,
and all I crave is stillness in my space.

topic: a phone camera flash too bright
lines: You smile into every shot with your face,
the perfect subject without a trace.
But the flash always blinds us with a burst,
we swear it could wake the dead from their cursed.
She says it's too cold but her lips stay red and chill,
while he stares at the rising electric bill.
"I'm from the south," she insists, not one full degree
is warm enough to follow his climate decree.
She never answers when the phone gives a call,
the screen just glows bright from her silent sprawl.
The group chat waits cold while she dodges the blame,
but she won't be the one to say her own name.
She watches the earth crack open all up,
digs near the old pot and plants her new cup.
A sliver of green dares to rise and be green,
but she fears what might still go unseen.
You hold the tuning fork, but time stands still,
its hum a whisper meant to fill.
The air remembers every pure tone,
your silence vibrates through my bone.
You find your old shoes chewed up in the room,
where quiet disasters always seem to loom.
Your hands were once steady, but now feel so soft,
while the bunny just sits, calm and aloft.
She flips through the pile, then dreams of the sea,
and scribbles a note that's meant only for me.
Each postcard shows places she's never been through,
but the joy in her grin feels completely true.
You asked me your name but I could not say there,
my brain was stuck counting the steps up the stair.
I know I should think but my mind feels half-head,
like a phone on mute or a ghost with no bread.
I try to twist the handle, but it won't spin,
the wood is sweating where my palm is thin.
"It's just a minor setback," I mutter in joke,
the toilet paper nods like it already spoke.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: She calls it her kingdom, a world built from zone,
Her backhoe's a wand and her dirt has a tone.
She bakes every mound like a chef who would cook,
until every pebble she fastens with hook.
I thought I'd never find a clean pair,
these socks are smushed in like they don't care.
I hold up two that match — I almost cry —
until I realize they're just stuck in the dry.
He sits by the wall where the cold wind still chill,
his coffee long gone, now frozen and spill.
He searches for warmth, but the heat feels lost,
breath turns to mist, his nose numb with frost.
You watched it finally let go with a snap,
your books now sliding down from their trap.
But you found some duct tape to help it mend,
and hope it holds out till the day's end.
You pull out your wallet, it's all in ten cash,
the register rings with a smile and a clash.
You leave it in coins and you skip the small change,
but something about it feels oddly strange.
She hums a tune she's known since way too deep,
while my focus dies with the buzz of her beep.
Coffee spills on my notes, a tiny crumb,
she taps her pen like a rockstar's own drum.
The slides are stuck in the same old flow,
we all pretend we still care to know.
It's turning into a never-ending long,
until someone hums a rescue song.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: You pull out your coupon instead of cash,
hoping it will be worth something, not just flash.
The cashier smiles like it's some kind of treat,
scans it once and says, "We can't repeat."
She stares into each puddle so deep,
her foot hovers high before she will leap.
The mud looks too thick, it all feels too cold,
she worries she'll sink and won't be able to hold.
The goldfish acts like this meal is a show,
He swims up, down, and all around below.
He does a little twist, a tiny twirl, a dance,
then flicks his tail and gives me one last glance.
My coffee's cold, but it's still almost noon,
I thought I'd feel electric, not half-moon.
The morning rush is turning into a fade,
I watch my willpower walk off in a parade.
She watches the bulb flicker faint and slow,
like sparks from a fire someone lets go.
It's not just the light that keeps her mind,
but how it dances with the soft wind.
She stops mid-sentence, the room holds its note,
a tremor escapes from her tight little throat.
She blames it on allergies, dry air, the blame,
but we all heard the truth in her cracking name.
That smell in the air, like both salt and decay,
lingers on my wet hair after I bathe and pray.
I sniff for a clue, but it's vague as a dream,
like perfume turned glue—just a ghost I can't redeem.
You built that swing before the house showed age,
now it sways like it's dancing on its own stage.
Each creak you hear is a memory in sway,
you love that sound more than any new day.
Your brain feels like a loose lightbulb in your mind,
it flickers and buzzes and won't stop its grind.
You try every trick to chase back some calm,
but all you've got left is aspirin and balm.
You hold your place with quiet grace,
while others jostle for their space.
The rush dissolves, the noise grows calm,
and patience becomes its own balm.
I wear my helmet through the city's loud beat,
and sweat under the midday's harsh heat.
It's got dents from the tools I carry around,
but I wouldn't trade my sturdy old crown.
I wake up early to see the lake cold,
my breath turns fog before it takes hold.
The surface is smooth like a shattered glass,
and the reeds from the shore look stiff as dry grass.
I trace your face in the blue screen's soft glow,
even darkness can't hide how late it's though.
My eyes won't blink, but you won't let me take
this moment offline—just let me have my break.

topic: a bike locked to a pole
lines: The U-lock is twisted and rusted tight,
the bike's frame still shakes within my sight.
Its wheels won't spin, stuck in their sleep,
the owner's out there, I can feel it deep.

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: She holds up the phone to take a new frame,
a caption still waiting in her name.
The world is all quiet, she's alone to live,
but who will she send it to to give?
She spends hours reading each argument post,
then comments as if she's the topic's host.
She swipes down for a break from that same view,
her thumb just scrolled past it—there, now it flew.
It lingers after they go, this scent that stays,
a ghost of routine from empty hotel days.
You leave the door open, let light into the room,
as if the air needs something softer than gloom.

topic: singing along to a car ad
lines: I scream the lyrics at the loud ad,
trying to prove I'm not going mad.
My fingers drum on the wheel for speed,
but no one's there to set me freed.
She types with one finger, real slow,
the screen casts a soft blue glow.
The letters stick like glue, they fail,
she sighs and turns her face quite pale.
He's chasing the ball like it's his only goal,
his whole face lit by the storm's dark soul.
The field's a blur, the lines lost on the pitch,
and every pass feels like a nervous switch.
Your parrot's repeating every ringtone call,
it learned from your pocket while shopping at the mall.
You think it's strange but you know it will grow,
one day it'll impress with a talent to show.
You watch the horizon turn pink with the glow,
waves curl soft as they kiss your skin low.
You stand there barefoot, sand warm under feet,
and time feels less heavy, quietly retreat.
I claim my post-lunch power nap as bliss,
no guilt or shame, just soft, warm this.
I shut the door and tuck my shoes under the boot,
my to-do list can wait—this nap is my root.
I knew the clouds wouldn't stay in the sky,
but I swore my shoes would somehow stay dry.
Now every step sends a cold drop from each drip,
and walking home feels like trying not to slip.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: They wheel and dart through the pale blue air,
a mismatched pair with a shared dare.
The sidewalk cracks under the thinning frost,
they peck at the crumbs no one's trying to lost.
The song was in play, just one more verse to stay,
the screen went dark and took the melody away.
This was their favorite, now frozen in the last
note played before the silence settled in the past.
A rabbit curled inside the cardboard hole,
Its twitching nose feels close to breaking my soul.
It's been three years since I've seen you just hide,
All soft and still on your quietest side.
I handed them a ten, not asking for cash,
the cashier glared like we had a clash.
It took five minutes just to count the mess,
they called me names I can't begin to bless.
She kicks off her shoes and refuses to wear
a mask for the mud as it hits every air.
Her laughter is loud when she dares to run,
each splash proves that joy can be found in the fun.
I swear I've read all the care tips again,
I even try misting it like the rain.
But the leaves still brown and I place the blame,
on my hands, clumsy as they ever were, the same.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: You inch closer on the couch trying to be near,
your shoulder now brushing the side of my ear.
I shift left but we still get into a bump,
I give up and slump—this seat's half your lump.
I scribble fast, my hand full of fear,
hoping the page doesn't whisper it near.
I mark out whole lines, try to truly hide
what's scrawled here—no one must see it inside.
You mutter winter's usual white lies,
glaring at the sky with narrowed eyes.
You tap your phone for a cab, no heat,
and stamp your boots with cold-defeat.
It walks right past me, no glance in my near,
as if my calls never reached its far ear.
It lounges where sunlight hits the floor's beam,
while I'm left wondering if I'm just a dream.
I never found a better way to stay,
than holding hands without a need to say.
The room could buzz or fade, we didn't spark,
but still I'd choose this quiet love to mark.

topic: a gym membership you never use
lines: You pay in full — no card, no monthly cash,
just a receipt and a fast digital dash.
You never set foot there, so they can't say you owe,
and truthfully, you don't miss them when you show.
You'd say something dumb and we'd both grin,
before anyone else could even begin.
We're laughing now, but it's a little less still—
some jokes never land quite as hard as the hill.
She walks the same three blocks from the office block,
her watch ticks faster than the wall clock.
She eats lunch at her desk with her jaw full of grit,
but won't turn on a fan, says this is a sweat-fit.
I check my email again—it's all due,
the numbers turn everything slightly blue.
They stack up on the counter, a growing pile,
I force a fake one for the kids—my fake smile.
I was halfway through my soggy lunch
when someone bumped me—spilled the whole bunch.
A gloopy mess of mystery meat
slid down my arm like hot embarrassment heat.
I keep my wallet close, trying to feel the past,
remembering those days spent without a blast.
But time has changed me, here and now,
I count each penny—just don't ask me how.

topic: car keys on the kitchen table
lines: They left the keys on the table as a clue,
Their coffee's cold, and their lunch is overdue.
They search through drawers for their lost car,
Then laugh—they're right there, next to a jar.
She's been stuck at 99% since morning she tried,
following every tip from some random guide.
The screen pulses with a weak, sad glow,
but maybe tomorrow the download will flow.
We sat in silence and counted the time,
your pocket watch ticking with borrowed chime.
The colors of your quilt were worn through the thread,
I held you close as the story was spread.
Your screen dims slow like a fading light,
the red corner grows into a fright.
You tap "low power"—it's a desperate save,
but silence looms like a hollow cave.
Her face lights up in that vintage wedding smile,
frozen mid-laugh, alive in that single while.
A flash of joy from a world far from light,
she whispers to you, love could still go so might.
She never knew if she missed the right road,
the voice just said, "Let me try this new load."
She'd pull off the curb for a minute or pause,
and let the machine be the map and the cause.
You tap the button, but the house stays warm,
your nerves are turning into a storm.
You change the number, try to get it just set,
but every choice feels like extra sweat.
She waits for the first green signs of spring,
the world still feels wrong in its cold, dead thing.
The daffodils twist to break the ground's tight bend,
as if they were messages from earth to send.
You let the waves wash it from your sand,
they throw back a shell into your hand.
A sudden gust laughs with the rising breeze,
and sprays you with salt to get right up in your tease.
You touch the handrail on the subway car,
and hold on tight, so the world doesn't get too far.
Your thumb leaves a mark down the plastic trail,
your hand sticks there—sweet, stubborn, pale.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: They inch their shoulder alarmingly near,
pretending the tension is nothing to clear.
Their breath still smells like midnight takeout cold,
but they're clutching the blanket, claiming it's their gold.
She sprawls across my desk where the midday sun,
turns every silent click into soft fun.
Her paws tap dance on the space bar and key,
she thinks this is hers—and maybe it's me.
It was a small thing, but the fight felt right,
you held your ground like it was muscle tight.
You swore it was yours, the dip still on the claim,
you ate it with pride, but still said their name.
You watch the light move down the leafy stream,
but the silence feels like something waiting to scream.
You trace the pattern where the shadows fall in line,
afraid it's pointing out some weakness in mine.
My dog's been stuck inside this endless loop,
circling faster, like it just got a scoop
of cosmic joy or maybe sheerest mind,
but somehow still manages to stay quite blind.

lines: The cat lies sprawled in a patch of the sun,

They left it in the sink, now full of dish,

Her face freezes mid-laugh on the lecture feed,

She blames her router, her chair, or the frame,

You trace the reason behind their soft cry,

She taps the screen again, the bar just says "retry,"

The yolk spills out like a slow-motion crack,

She pretends she won't sleep unless it's your bed,

though you know time will take this joy's soft toll.
You step outside where the pavement still gleam,

The shovel hits something more than frost—*clang*,

lines: I watch the dusk fall into a gentle hush,

She sees a target where others see prey,

It slipped from my hand and went splat with a crack,

Her playlist used to match the road's slow flow,

My roommate watches fish give a full-on show,

lines: She finds the key and turns the rusted gate,

She checks the phone once more—there's no more time,

no plastic weight in my hands to hold.
There's not a single sign or a clue,

watching the clouds drift lazily by.
The robin still knows this patch as its spot,
but I'm the one who has somehow forgot.
She stands at the edge where the mountain meets sky,
her shadow dissolved in the stars up high.
Her face holds a quiet, unspoken chase—
this hill isn't just land, it's the only place.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: The wind is cold, the ground is gray with frost,
A dozen birds all dart around, half-lost.

I catch your gaze and you pretend with my eyes,

it moves like it knows the world will fly.

while I hold my breath for the simplest things.

careful not to disturb with her hands.

she thinks this is how beauty holds things.

topic: a coffee cup on the curb
lines: That coffee cup on the curb could be mine,
my name is still faded inside the lid's line.
