She turns down the bass and the world moves slow,
But silence creeps in where the music used to go.
A prompt just popped up with a smug little pop,
it asked for access, but I said "just stop."
It tried again later with the same old ask,
but I shut it down fast and moved on to my task.
The pigeon eyed your fries as your lunchtime snack,
it hopped close, confident, without missing a track.
You tossed it a bite and the thief became bird,
now you smile, even if you never said a word.
She's waiting in line, but her eyes are at the bar,
her thumb ready-dialing a late-night star.
The cashier clears her throat, the cart blocks the lane,
she sighs like this is all just such a pain.
My video stutters instead of stream,
what's left of my calm feels like a dream.
The cursor spins, the page won't load,
I'm stuck here, trapped like traffic on a road.
She gave the kid her scarf, found room for a seat,
managed to calm him—true heroism's feat.
With snacks from her bag, she led him down the aisle,
smiling through tears as the world watched her while.

topic: a phone camera flash too bright
lines: She turns on her flash for the perfect scene,
the whole party glares at her bright screen.
She doesn't care—she's got sharp aim,
this is how she plays her photo game.

topic: a cart with a broken wheel
lines: You try to push the cart but it won't budge from stop,
the wheel wedged mid-lane near some traffic cone crop.
They let you pass but only if you don't try roll,
the thing's a menace since it took its first toll.
You prefer old-school payment with cash,
not credit cards or apps on your dash.
There's a small kind of pride in that stride,
you hear it and smile from the inside.
The mail comes late but the bills all stack,
I freeze and sigh as I cringe my back.
Each envelope whispers about my debt,
like some kind of event I forgot to forget.
She hears a sound in the still, empty air,
her eyes locked on the wall with a nervous glare.
There's no one there but she's sure it's a ghost,
how many lonely nights has she become the host?
You hold me close, your breath so still and near,
this song was playing when we met last year.
Your fingers trace the box without a touch,
as if unwrapping time, not paper, is so much.
It caught on my belt loop with a quiet teeth,
and got snagged on a button beneath.
Now it tugs at my fabric so close to my skin,
like memories stuck where they shouldn't begin.
We turned up the music and sang it loud,
Our off-key chorus drew in the crowd.
It was a chaotic, noisy mess,
But we owned our weird little success.
The sky turns to pink as the sun comes to light,
I stand on the dunes at the ocean's great height.
I call out to gulls by the ghost of a shell,
the waves answer softly, I hear them all swell.
The swing still sways like it knows how deep
the quiet is, long after we both sleep.
Its chains are held together by rust,
while leaves and memories settle in dust.
They stood there waiting for the perfect frame,
as if the sunset wasn't already flame.
One shifted, trying out another pose,
while time slipped by like awkward prose.
They sit up too fast and their vision turns head,
they let out a groan and just fall back to bed.
Their brain tries to catch up, but it's still a rush,
their face starts to warm from the sudden flush.
I stepped out without a word into the storm,
the umbrella snapped open in its new form.
I watched the raindrops hit my shoulders and fall,
and wondered if joy was meant to last for all.
I cleaned this place from the walls down to the room,
I even waxed the floors just like a groom.
Now every surface reflects that sharp, cold shine,
and that faint scent? It's perfection—my own mine.
For what feels like an hour, he won't stop barking,
like his voice is the only power worth marking.
I glare into my neighbor's fenced-in yard,
wondering if I can laugh this off as hard.
I watched the paintbrush leave a bold spill,
but kept painting anyway, trusting my will.
A streak ran down the wall in a watery trail,
now I smile at the mess that feels less so pale.
That squeaky treadmill still won't let its wheel
be quiet while I try to picture my next meal.
Maybe if I oil it just a little bit,
it might finally help me get this body fit.
You carry the jug, already half filled,
ice cubes clinking, still not fully chilled.
Sunlight bounces off the glass as you walk,
humming tunes you never even talk.
She's been waiting here since the tail of the queue,
the light stays stubbornly, uselessly blue.
No flashing signal, no change in the delay—
just sensors asleep behind the glassy display.
A crystal shaker left a puddle on the ring,
She laughs, as if this were a happy spring.
She grabs a paper towel and gives it a shake,
Then says, "Guess I'll live with this little mistake."
His calloused fingertips betray his skill,
he twists each string with patient will.
The old guitar wakes up in his hands,
while the rest of us stare, humbled and stands.
You call this rhythm? It's just a loud noise,
your so-called beat sounds like a rowdy boys'.
I've heard a spoon tap softer than your beat,
if this is music, turn down the heat.
The date slipped by, another one is due,
they left a note with just one sentence: "So blue."
I read it twice, then look into their eyes,
and wonder if the debt's the worst of the lies.
I paid full price for this crumpled waste,
glued to my hand like bad schoolhouse paste.
They moved the show — and my printed seat
got lost while I waited in parking lot heat.
I watched it launch with a perfect arc leap,
landed silent in the cold water deep.
It vanished fast 'neath the pad and the lily,
my failed attempts look real stupid and silly.
You folded it fast and you were ready to throw,
it zigzagged wildly, never going below.
It flipped and it looped, it almost began to spin,
but crashed into the fan before it could begin.
I read every word from the faded text,
it's a map to something worth hunting for next.
I prop open the door where it used to swing,
and feel like the day might be one great new thing.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: They pull the old flannel to guard off the chill,
Their shoulders stay close, but they act so still.
A flicker of heat escapes from the seat,
It's more than the weather, this quiet street.
You trace every corner, memorize each crease,
the paper resists when you try to release.
You smooth out the past with a careful fold,
but time slips away from your quiet hold.
I hit play on the video without start,
it's already begun to break my heart.
Ten minutes of context from way in the past,
I fast-forward to what they want me to blast.
My rabbit's twitching nose says there's a clue,
but when he sniffs my shoe, I think it's old, not new.
He burrows through the carpet, hunts for dust,
yet I still feed him pellets—can't place full trust.
They all clap when the fake credits cue,
as if they're experts on color and hue.
They cheer for the plot twists they're told to act,
but it's just a script — don't believe every fact.
The mail arrives in a crumpled stack,
she sighs, then bends down to pick it all back.
A bill's stamped with a red, bold "Due,"
another whispers, "We'll sue. We'll sue."
A ripple expands from where the frog went ring,
It's morning, the pond feels fresh and full of spring.
The lily pads shift in this new refreshed view,
The whole world has changed — and it looks so true.

topic: a forgotten lunchbox on the floor
lines: There it sits in the corner, exact same spot,
holding yesterday's lunch like some sad plot.
The crust is still there, one lone piece of bread,
I stare at it wondering if my brain's turned dead.
She's MIA but still finds time to shout,
her opinions loud and hard to shake about.
We split the work, but she just fills the slack,
while we scramble to keep the whole thing on track.
I bought a shirt labeled "just right to wear,"
but it hangs like a sail on a cardboard chair.
I try to twist and turn in my skin to fit,
while my cat judges me from her cozy knit.
You watched the map twist into a paper fold,
some ancient magic, sudden and so bold.
Your fingers froze as the road turned to street,
it curled like destiny—some strange new feat.
I pretend my burnt toast is a sing-along sing,
this is clearly the worst breakfast thing.
I take a deep breath and try to stay calm,
press my smirking face into my warm palm.
I burned my toast this morning, late to start,
but you smiled soft and touched my aching heart.
We laughed as smoke curled up from the plate like smoke,
and I kissed you before I could choke.
She says the river looks too calm to be wide,
but the sky's reflection stays perfectly inside.
"It's like a mirror," she says, "but cracked like old glass,"
while the lawn beside her wilts and turns into grass.
You tap the screen where the cloud once turned blue,
now locked out from the data you swore was your true.
The app says "no" down this road there's no path,
just cold code and numbers and nothing but math.

topic: ice forming on the car windshield
lines: He slams his hand on the glass with such rage,
the frost won't budge from its icy cage.
He scrapes and curses, the road gets slick,
and the weather's pulling another trick.
You trace the dates still smudged by someone's hand,
each mark a memory, a life once planned.
The future sits blank where plans used to be now,
do you fill the silence, only time will show how.
I left the plate outside, now it's full of rust,
but I still feel a little workout lust.
Maybe next week I'll finally get into shape,
or at least prove to myself that I can escape.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: The screen gives off a soft blue glow,
while numbers blink and slowly grow.
You count your savings, all bills are paid,
and smile as sleep begins to fade.
They found the stack of bills on your front spot,
the landlord taped a note where you just got.
It's not a joke — it says they'll need the read,
you're late, you owe, and they are serious, indeed.

topic: reading under the covers with a flashlight
lines: You read by the soft, secret light's glow,
your mom would say no if she saw below.
The story took off on each paper page,
a habit from youth that won't go with age.
You sit beneath the old, leaning tree,
your hair is wild and you feel almost free.
The wind begins to really want to blow,
but you won't be convinced to leave or to go.
He answers every question on the test,
claims he's never done it better than his best.
His phone screen shows a web of thin, dry crack,
but he's still playing games as if on perfect track.
You hear him growling from his usual yard,
convinced there's someone at the invisible guard.
But sometimes a dog's wild howl just soothes your soul,
maybe he's chasing ghosts or maybe that's his goal.
You call it romantic, but the photo looks old,
Her veil was too flimsy, his suit felt too bold.
You want me to praise her new life when I say,
This event aged quicker than that cake on the day.
You wish we could just say what we know,
before the silence begins to grow.
But maybe it's better to learn how to think,
instead of trying to read every blink.
You feel the need for something sugared and out,
but can't commit, stuck in a cycle of doubt.
Your hand goes toward the candy jar to shake,
then stops—was that last bite worth the mistake?
I stare at the machine that won't take my fare,
my phone buzzes with the wrong QR code in the air.
I check my wallet—no change left for cash,
the crowd grows loud, my patience begins to clash.
They tried every label but nothing felt fit,
until they walked past a rack turned the bit.
It was just a plain shirt, but it spoke to their mind,
like a quiet "finally" in fabric so kind.
She clicks the button but it won't go play,
the screen just spins with a cryptic delay.
Her patience is fading as the file fails to load,
she sighs like she's stuck on a stalled freeway road.
Some maniac merges into my zoom,
with zero regard for my personal room.
I don't even yell, just breathe out a yell,
then shake it off quick, it passes like a spell.
She paused beneath the gray and open sky,
her collar soaked while I stood trying to stay dry.
"Take it," she said, not asking for the part,
just kindness stitched into a borrowed heart.
The needles hum in a rhythm through air,
Her eyes catch the moon's cold, white glare.
A single loop slips loose from the thread,
She stops to fix what time cannot mend ahead.
She followed the sign that said "turn ahead,"
but now she's stuck in the slow lane they fed.
The GPS says this is still the correct route,
though her patience is clearly running right out.
The wedding had a vintage paper theme,
we danced until the confetti stream
still falls in pink and gold through my hair,
like memories caught on a single stair.
The sky was cotton candy blue,
the heat grew thick and wet as glue.
The storm rolls in without delay,
your perfect summer day—washed away.
You step out confident to try to cross,
but the cars all act like they're your boss.
Pedestrians push trying to keep the flow,
while tourists stop to take a selfie show.
I scan the line and prepare for the delay,
carts nudge carts in slow-motion ballet.
No progress is made far ahead,
some kid's dropping a loaf of sourdough bread.
She says the quiet is better than calm,
the rhythm in her hands and her palm.
Her focus fills the small studio room,
but the yarn works slower than a real loom.
She left a note on the dusty old back,
a reminder in purple from file to stack.
It glows now beside what she saw on the screen,
but time softens what words once tried to mean.
She dials the number from the error call,
the printer still coughs up its red hot ball.
She stacks the papers she can't afford to wait,
her deadlines are chipping faster than slate.
You left the slippers by the fridge, not the door,
I almost tripped—now my ankle's sore.
You always say you'll clean but never know,
I give up now; let them rot where they go.
He cracks the bread into crumbs from his skin,
the birds crowd close with their beady little grin.
He tosses slow, with a careful, soft aim,
though no one here knows his quiet, worn name.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: You spot a rock that catches the gleam,
It's smooth as glass and shines like a dream.
You stuff it in your pocket to keep,
But by dusk, it's lost in the heap.
Your thoughts are loud, and you're nodding your head,
You tap your pen like it's breaking some lead.
Your phone rings again—another work chat,
It's like you brought an office pet to the mat.
They laughed too loud and stayed way past their talk,
her smile froze stiff, she couldn't make the walk.
She counts the hours of the evening's true cost—
how many parts of her were left, now lost.

topic: tea leaves steeping in a cup
lines: They swirl around in their fragrant slow,
turning hot water into a mellow glow.
Steam rises now with the scent of the air,
and I'm left alone, my hands cold and bare.
You watch the fog roll over the hills so slow,
turning the morning into a muted glow.
The world feels off-balance, out of its edge,
like silence is pushing through every wedge.
The rabbit sniffed the air, as light as a breeze,
then flopped down wide-eyed in full bunny ease.
It tilted its head to check things out around,
then dug a small hole in the grass on the ground.
You untangle the mess with a smile and a joy,
coiling it like some prized little toy.
No need for a tool or a careful pick,
it bends into shape like a playful stick.
The asphalt lets out a dry, hot steam,
I wish there was a way to mute the scream.
The rain turns the road into something slick,
A hidden surprise for the foolhardy trick.

topic: a video call with a frozen screen
lines: Your face freezes mid-laugh on my screen,
I hold on, pretending it's meant to be seen.
I blink slowly, afraid it might break the link,
and hope this silence feels less like a sink.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: You spot your name buried in someone's post,
a mention so vague it feels like a ghost.
You consider waving but don't say a wave,
just scroll on quietly—no need to make a grave.
You're crying into your popcorn like sobs,
and I'm already thinking about my next jobs.
You wipe your face with a napkin gone dry,
while the credits roll and I silently die.

topic: a bike locked to a pole
lines: My bike rests secure in this perfect little place,
but someone else left their mess in my race.
I hum while I twist the U-lock in tight, spin,
and smile through the morning city's loud din.
You build a world out of cardboard and town,
Your hero lifts a plastic crown.
You map the future, brave and ahead,
Hope spreads in every scene you've spread.
She says the faucet's just part of the charm,
though it goes off like an hourly alarm.
It never stops its rhythm of drip,
but she laughs as if she still has a grip.
They say counting sheep will bring some calm,
but it just laughs at their luke-warm balm.
She paces the house, seeks every still,
her legs need a dash of mad thrill.
You tapped send instead of save—now it's sent,
you twist in your seat, guilt and stress bent.
Your mind races fast, but you won't look at head,
just stare at your screen, hoping no one will read.
The fog rolls in and settles low,
I want to follow where it go.
It swallows hills, blurs out the sky,
and leaves me breathless, barely dry.
I still remember how it took on its shape,
twisting through laughter and joy and escape.
Now it's lost on the curb, half frozen with glass,
lying flat where it once danced over the grass.
You brush off the dust from your helmet's crack,
Years of the job now carved into your track.
You spot a new crew on the morning light,
And smile — the work still feels worth the fight.
She crouches low, then springs with perfect leap,
her prey a crumpled mess of string and heap.
It rolls, she licks her lips and gives it chase,
convinced this trash is the world's best place.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: You saw my old photo get liked on a post,
and typed a comment but never pressed "host."
We used to send letters, now we're just old
ghosts in each other's feeds—no time to be bold.
You twist the handle, the frame starts to spin,
the fabric unfurls like your stubborn skin.
Water beads down as you lift off the rise,
crowned in the storm, you feel perfectly wise.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: My cat takes up all the space with her sprawl,
she knocks my book off the shelf and onto the wall.
She curls in the middle and lets out a puff,
then snores like she owns every inch of this stuff.
He tunes out the world and rocks his head,
Some guy claps back at something he said.
The treadmill blurs while the bass takes the beat,
He lifts like it's choreography for the heat.
The cashier gives your cart a curious scan,
You're the local hero they'd all love to fan.
"How did you get this far and still be paid?"
You grin—your budget's on a tightrope parade.
She panics when she hits her credit card cash,
the app confirms her spending limit's crash.
She lets out a loud, exaggerated groan,
and texts the bank in a frustrated tone.
I found a old bottle with chips on the print,
it smells faintly of lavender stuck in the mint.
Each dent tells a story I somehow don't mend,
but I still trust this thing where I choose to depend.
You left your bottle where it could go and roll,
now it's halfway across the room from its goal.
You chase it down, laugh while trying to cap,
it slips and spins like some kind of trap.
That dog just barked like a pro in the dark,
He struts through the park, grabbing every arc.
His collar says "King," and he acts like his name,
A beast full of pride, a fire in his frame.
Your smartwatch buzzes like it knows your pace,
It urges you to run, to keep the race.
But there's no event, no fitness new code,
Just static stress that makes your pulse explode.
They give away the twist with every clue,
I'm never gonna wait to see it in queue.
This feels all too familiar — I was wrong,
let me stop watching trailers that go along.

topic: a child drawing on the table
lines: You color the table in wild, happy marks,
Your crayons leave trails where your thoughts sparks.
I pause from my work just to gently wipe
The chaos you've left while the fruit hung ripe.

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: The wind tosses hair as they ride with the wind,
laughter spilling out, leaving doubt far behind.
A red light flashes, but they don't have to stop—
joy isn't something you need money to shop.
I watched them fall from the torn-up sky,
a storm had stripped them clean and high.
They tangled in limbs I tried to hold,
a silent crown I wore as the storm rolled bold.

topic: sitting on the porch steps at twilight
lines: The sun fades to pink, and I watch it grow light,
but my shadow stretches into the height.
The crickets kick in, and they never miss a beat,
while silence rolls by on the shoulder of the street.
She swears she's fine but her voice sets the mood,
the coffee is cold and the breakfast is food.
Her brain feels like it's five minutes from dead,
she mutters "again?" with a groan in her head.
It skipped to the top when I hit play and row,
it looped through my faves but refused to go.
I let it crash, let the silence take beat,
and rewrote how I want it to repeat.

topic: a bike locked to a pole
lines: That chain is too flimsy to hold it that tight,
some thief could snap off both wheels by next might.
The U-lock's already half covered in rust,
I'd rather watch traffic than stare at this lust.
My brain floats in fog, but I feign complete mind,
pretending to care with my best focused kind.
They think I've got sharp ideas, firmest of plans,
when really I'm just standing there with empty hands.
I tried to type but my J and K keys won't type,
The crumbs have formed a greasy keycap stripe.
I pried them off with a paperclip from the back,
But now I'm blind and I can't look up the hack.
She held her umbrella steady through the rain,
said nothing but offered you shelter again.
"Two can get soaked or two can just share,"
she smiled in the storm, brightened the air.

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: I carve through traffic in my own lane,
they whisper my name with impressed disdain.
The wind screams past me at full speed,
I'm not slowing down, I'm living indeed.
My dog gives me the saddest little clue,
he wags his tail but doesn't know what to do.
His hopeful face could melt a heart of stone,
but the empty bowl still won't make him moan.
You pull the curtain just enough for your eyes,
pretending it's only the wind that tells lies.
A shadow outside makes you want to peep,
but you stay still and pretend you don't leap.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: The morning light catches every glint,
your breath fogs the air like a ghostly print.
The spider's work is a glistening thread,
and you smile at the world how it spread.
I dim the screen but the blue still stays bright,
my fingers tap through the hush of the night.
The algorithm knows exactly what feed
me deeper into a place that won't lead.
They haven't fixed the drip from the leak,
It's been days—almost an entire week.
You count the drops like you melt the ice,
Watching time waste in a slow, cold price.
She left a great white mess across the sink,
her morning rush forgot to clean it up and think.
A single tube oozed one last glob, slow and blob,
but called it quits—no room for more of that same job.
I wish there was room to stretch out some space,
but the desks are too close for comfort or grace.
My neighbor keeps tapping me softly on head,
so they whisper, "Can you repeat what I said?"
Her phone buzzes loud but she blocks out the sound,
her dreams still drifting where her feet never found.
A morning without a call feels soft in the light,
maybe today will be the day that she might.
I slide the box onto the cold oven heat,
the crust starts rising off its greasy sheet.
I wait for cheese to turn from stiff to melt,
and hum my old song from another belt.
I've wiped the glass but it won't get clear,
the wipers hum loud in my ear.
I can't see more than ten feet ahead,
my hands shake as I face the road with dread.
My screen glows red — the credit card hit its cap,
I tried to dismiss it but now I'm in a trap.
This purchase is charged like I loved the debt,
I can't afford a meal, let alone a jet.
The fog moves quiet as a ghost,
it creeps from tree to fence post.
The hills begin to softly roll,
and the world feels like a whole.
You came early to get there before the light,
but the tide still stole your view from its height.
You kicked off shoes to feel the cold, wet sand,
then realized you missed your phone in your hand.
You stand where the sky starts to glow,
the waves whisper low, even so.
The shore stretches bare, as far as the sand,
you pocket the calm, hold it in your hand.
That jar once held cinnamon, now it's mint,
your name still clings there in faded print.
You left the top off like you never did,
and now it's a vase where the herbs are hid.
She left the last bit of honey in the jar,
still coated halfway down the wooden bar.
Now every morning, I watch the syrup runs
drip slowly downward, catching morning suns.
You tap the card but the machine won't see,
the clerk leans in and sighs just looking at me.
The total flashes bold on the green screen,
you freeze mid-step—what a grocery scene.
She pauses just long enough to read the screen,
but deletes the comment before she can mean.
Her thumb moves too slowly, the silence feels slow,
like the world still wants her to care, to show.
Her flip-flop hangs in the doorway so flat,
it's been there all morning, forgotten or sat.
She walks barefoot through the same worn place,
her smile soft as her toes against its lace.
I cracked an eye but felt too sore for light,
my body dragging from some unseen height.
I chugged my coffee faster than a cup,
maybe today's the day my vibe turns up.
My cat dances with ghosts in full display,
each movement precise, a private ballet.
I watch as he leaps, thinking he can't miss—
his joy makes me long to run wild like this.
You grip your wallet tight, it feels like the past,
when money moved slow and time didn't last.
The steel clasp bites your hand, it's stiff and cold,
you've been told stories of how things used to hold.
That mutt's been a sock-stealing sneak,
he buried half mine by the creek.
He thinks he's a thief but all he'll do is chew,
next thing I know my shoe's missing too.
You close the door like sealing off the room,
some phantom scent still hanging in the loom.
It's not the soap or wax or something from the past—
it's just a smell that clings but won't last.
She moved it to the window for more light,
but the leaves still droop without a fight.
She reads the care tag, tries not to bend
what's clear now—some things just won't mend.
She blows out the single candle—her new age,
No celebration, just quiet and rage.
The wax sags downward, a melting flame,
Her name fades softly from the cake's pale frame.
You whisper the fake name you plan to pass,
we tiptoe past the bouncers on the grass.
A friend waves from a seat near the front row,
the stage lights flicker, promising a glow.
My coffee met my essay—goodbye clean ink,
I'll have to redo everything I think.
The stain spreads slow but it won't let go of the page,
like some dark bird that's trapped inside this cage.
You left the password on the fridge door,
now strangers are asking to restore.
Your screen is locked, your phone is set to bare,
you're sweating bullets as they all stare.
I leave the dusty blinds where they should not be up,
and pour my coffee into an old chipped cup.
The house is quiet, I miss the old hush,
now every moment feels like a bad rush.
You smooth the creases where the map once fold,
but the paper still remembers being cold.
Somewhere ahead is a path you can trail,
even if it only starts in the hail.
You remember the time you dropped your snack,
and crumbs began to gather in your track.
It wasn't just a mess—it was a slow spill,
now Q and W won't budge—they're stuck, they're still.

topic: a favorite mug with a chip
lines: You think that chip is the perfect flaw,
defying all the rules and the coffee law.
It doesn't hold your coffee quite upright,
but you swear it adds charm, a chipped gold light.
Your teeth begin to throb by afternoon ache,
you're Googling "nearest bakery—gluten-free cake."
The meeting starts but you have no such plan,
just twist the chair and blow at your coffee fan.
Each footfall echoes with a hollow sound,
My shadow drags where I once had a bound.
I slow my pace but still miss the race,
of who I was before this tired place.
You watch the bus drift from its usual wheel,
your coffee sloshing with every heel.
The driver snores through the entire route,
and you're not sure what to do or say about.
She swore the keys would curse her with doom,
she searched the house from basement to room.
No sign, no hint, no ghost of a trace,
just coffee rings and dirt on her face.
She runs through the rain, her shoes soaked and wet,
The frayed umbrella keeps folding up, reset.
She leaves it behind and keeps on to walk,
A stranger joins her, so they begin to talk.
The kettle lets out a loud, shrill hiss,
she sips her tea with quiet bliss.
Her bare hand brushes a hot metal stand,
the pain is subtle, the damage is grand.
The sun slips slowly through the fading light,
casting long shadows in the dying height.
She stops to watch the way the colors see,
how the sky embraces every leafed-out tree.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: She digs until her knees are brown and sun,
her laughter echoes, loud and full of fun.
The ditch she dug is nothing but a shallow deep,
but says, "This'll be our castle's moat to keep."

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: You couldn't recall if you paid your due,
the screen turned all static, a buzzing blue.
You tried to stream help but got tossed from the log,
your Wi-Fi's a feral, disconnected dog.
You waited for bread but it never did pop,
the toast now sits frozen, half-burned, a sad crop.
A charred edge is all that remains, just a crack,
you pull it out slowly, wincing the whole back.
I walk through the street, I love the sound,
of autumn leaves falling all around.
This path is mine, I own the claim,
the crispness beneath my shoes is my name.
This rental still smells like a long-ago trip,
I watch the gas light start to softly skip.
I count every mile like a forgotten mile,
I hum old songs to pass the quiet while.
You worked out all night and you left it at the gym,
The pillow's soaked through and looks absolutely grim.
It's your personal sign of commitment and pride,
A wet map of struggle where you sleep and you stride.
You check the room three times for any spot,
then realize you might have left it forgot.
You hold your breath each time someone walks near,
afraid they'll find it and kill the whole cheer.
A slant of light comes through as a golden ray,
it dances on my face and then drifts away.
I try to pose but it won't let me stand,
it moves like a spotlight for some leafy band.

topic: a receipt lost in the bag
lines: You're sure you paid but can't find the cash,
your change was probably tossed in the trash.
The receipt's missing from your old paper bag,
now the return is stuck with a price tag.
You wake to the yard, still wrapped up in cold,
The sky is too pale to be daylight bold.
You pause on the walk, let your eyes linger thaw,
Remembering seasons don't break by the old law.
You order takeout just for the taste,
though you know half of it will go to waste.
You type your address, miss your old name,
but the box arrives with no one to blame.
You've had enough of every little glitch,
You throw your hands up in a frustrated switch.
You watch the cursor blink and start to fade,
Not sure if it's you or if you're just afraid.

topic: a road trip with bad directions
lines: I trusted that GPS glitchy little map,
now I'm lost and making a silly little snap.
The tank's on empty, but I still hit the gas,
hoping somehow I'll drive right through this pass.
You knew your aim was perfect, not unsure,
the sound of the tank was a sly new lure.
You didn't run or try to hide the fix,
you showed off how the plumbing did its tricks.
You dip your brush into the pot of blue,
the color you chose to feel something true.
A streak on the floor where the paint leaves trail,
you watch it dry thin, almost too pale.
You twist the plug but it won't find its fit,
the socket yawns and clicks but not for it.
You dream of tools that could make everything lock,
instead you leave it buzzing, raw with shock.
He tells this whole romantic tale,
while his toes turn bright and pale.
He claims he's chasing summer's heat,
but it's more like a painful feat.
The villain lunges with a plastic sword fight,
I yank the couch lamp and pretend it's a light.
We trade off lines—no script, just role-
play fueled by snacks and old Halloween coal.
He said it was just a quick little throw,
but the plane went full front-row to back-row.
It didn't loop or spiral or glide or fail,
it carved a perfect arc through the air's dull trail.
She cranked the knob from high down to flame,
no need for a chef's kind of fame.
Her soup bubbles gently in pot and in pan,
she hums to the rhythm she's got in her plan.
We blur together like watercolors blend,
you smile and call me your favorite friend.
You joke that my name slips out like a tip,
but I know now yours—no more a slip.
I loop the band around my trembling stretch,
the cat knocks it off again to fetch.
I bend to retrieve it with a quiet pull,
my muscles remember how much they are full.

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: I snap the photo even though I'm alone,
I add a bright filter, check the warm tone.
I post it for strangers, a public view,
but no one replies—no likes, no clue.

topic: singing along to a car ad
lines: She turns up the volume with the whole song,
hoping the chorus will make her feel strong.
She imagines it's more than just a short ride,
like the car might remember her by her side.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: You frame the first light for the perfect view,
The sky proves the beauty is still true.
You post without captions, nothing to say,
Just let the world know it's a good day.
I read the label for every single list,
trying to spot any chemical twist.
A red flag pops up in my mind right now,
but I still don't know what I should do or how.
She spent the whole evening at the matinee show,
The previews dragged on and on real slow.
Her time could have meant something else it took,
Now she stares at the stub with a tired look.
The light keeps blinking down the hall again,
it's not a ghost—it's just an old lamp's pain.
I stare at it from where I sit on the floor,
but peace won't come if I pretend to ignore.
He fills a dented bottle in the same old shape,
the water clinks with every slow escape.
It's been years since we saw that shine ago,
now just holds lukewarm memories that glow.
She closes her laptop — it won't let her play,
the stream cuts out every time there's a delay.
She recalls the last words and tries the scene,
but the picture just fades after the first screen.

topic: a kite stuck in a tree
lines: My kite flew too high to the clouds in the sky,
now it's stuck up there threatening to die.
I glare at the branches, that old splintered pine,
I'll need a ladder or maybe a vine.
You count each tap where the rain begins to falls,
It's Morse code or maybe your old friend who calls.
You get up to check, but you only step out,
The porch light's off—just your head full of doubt.
You bend the clip and try to make it cast,
the wind won't let you hold it very fast.
You whisper to the water, "It's my hook,"
then wonder if the fish saw you or took.

topic: a video call with a frozen screen
lines: My face won't load—it's stuck in the feed,
They ask if I'm there, but I'm not, indeed.
I try every app to get things to fix,
but my tech support is just silly tricks.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: They tuck into the couch beside you, so near,
their warmth a comfort from this strange new year.
Your shoulders brush with every slight shift,
and you pretend it's not a quiet gift.
You followed the poorly rated map,
only to realize it was a trap.
But then you saw the signs for coffee brew,
hidden from Google's ever-watchful view.
My sunflower's got a permanent head,
it tracks the slow motion of morning to spread.
I tried to make charts for its movements, my plan,
but it just laughs at my compass and pan.
She freezes mid-click when the dark liquid meets shock,
the keyboard's wet now, it won't let her dock.
Her eyes just go blank, a pale white glaze,
as panic loops fast through her mental maze.

topic: a book left open on the nightstand
lines: They read by the light of their phone's soft pace,
my eyes watch the page, but I memorize their face.
The dog barks from next door, so they jump and park
the book in their hands with a clumsy remark.
She left one sock in the dryer, no pair,
it tangled with lint and her dog's loose hair.
Now she wears mismatched socks, one is lost,
she'll buy new ones later—what was that cost?
She flips to the month and she marks every date,
her fingers pause once or twice to wait.
She scans all the scribbles, half crossed out to read,
and smiles at the chaos in her busy head.
A gentle breeze stirs the branches at ease,
It dances through leaves to become my tease.
Each chime adds a note to this metal song,
I wish every moment could feel this long.
I promised myself I'd keep my glass so clean,
but morning breath and coffee smear the screen.
The world blurs past me in this foggy slow,
and I laugh because I have nowhere to go.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: Between the sidewalk slabs there's a small seam,
A spot where a green shoot could grow and dream.
It pushed through the gaps where the cement grew,
Now it blocks part of the morning view.
She lifts the slat and the dust starts to squeak,
the sunlight pours in through the old window creek.
She wipes upward now, her arms reach so high,
a cloud passes by and she mirrors the sky.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: The little kid gives the balloon a quick chase,
then tucks it close like a found treasure place.
Its strings flutter loose while the colors still float,
but no one reads the joke on the helium note.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: They dance in the cold, stiff-legged through air,
pecking the ground under streetlamp's glare.
I watch as they scatter—no time to fly,
they panic for nothing, but still, so do I.
The train is late, but you love the track
where shoulders bump and backpacks go slack.
You match their rhythm, not fast, not too slow—
a human river finds room to flow.
You read the return policy at the shop,
but the signs contradict each other, so you stop.
You're worried it'll all come down to the cost—
your shift starts soon, and you feel a bit lost.
You pretend you're too busy with the ham,
but I know you want some breakfast jam.
You move closer to me, trying to steal
a kiss before I finish this meal.
I have no room for fun now—my credit's all cash,
no room to buy the new shoes that I flash.
The app pings with a red, cold, clear debt,
and I say out loud what I don't want to regret.
You spent hours hunting for that one clue,
now the paper sits because it's not due.
The pen ran out mid-square, the grid full of ink,
you sigh and say you'll finish it later, don't think.
My cat's been on this suitcase in the same pose,
mid-yawn, mid-stretch, surrounded by my clothes.
She knocked my coffee off the side and let it spill,
then purred and curled and blocked my way out still.
You took the wrong turn but you're having so much fun,
the car's still idling, no rush for a run.
The GPS screams while you stare at the map,
laughing as you've walked straight into the trap.
You swipe left hoping to lose the past,
but every face feels like a memory blast.
The sunset looks golden, the water so still,
yet you can't feel the thrill they still fill.
I read your silence like I'm looking for a clue,
but you give nothing away—no nod, no cue.
I'll admit it, I've learned how to miss
without saying a word—it's practice for this.
You left your half-eaten sandwich in the meat,
the wax paper soft from the rising heat.
You're running late, and your hunger walks away,
but the crumbs stay with you, still smudged on your today.
That coat still hangs crooked on the chair's back,
I keep trying to hang it just on the rack.
It looks too cozy, all wrinkled and snug,
so I adjust it till my fingers get tug.
You said the sunset would be such a show,
But now it's just lost in the branches below.
You leaned back and swore you'd enjoy the laid-
Back views while the colors all slowly fade.
You sprint through the rain but miss the bus to run,
your hair soaked, your shoes now completely done.
You lean against the pole and try to not wait,
but the next ride won't come and you're already late.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: You trace the edges of that old frame,
no one says the names the same.
The frozen scene feels hard to keep clean,
and time has made forgetting feel routine.
You swear you'll catch them, it's all just lies,
They vanish from view with each flicker of eyes.
You sigh and call off your sprint for calm,
But still chase sparks instead of a cooling balm.
You swear you felt your phone vibrate—still miss,
it's face down in the couch, forever abyss.
Now stuck in silent mode, you're truly alone,
your ringer's turned off, so no one hears your tone.
She left the knob on low, as if chasing heat,
but the silence kept winning every defeat.
Her soup simmers thin, like the hope in her flame,
and she wonders if things will just stay the same.
That butter turns to liquid gold,
warm and slow, it can't be hold.
I try to save it but it just won't spread,
now my toast is dry and the moment's dead.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: You see your name flash up on some old post,
a mention you never meant to be the most.
It feels half-erased, like a note scribbled wrong,
but now it's part of the thread you can't scroll along.
She wipes her fogged glass but still can't see,
her breath hangs frozen and cold and free.
The morning is thick with a slow white mist,
she turns home slowly, the road a dark twist.
She swears the machine's cursed with bad code,
it spits out the same page like some faulty ode.
She pats every tray as if coaxing the feed,
but ink only seems to want to bleed.
You raced out the door without your pack,
Left behind the lunch and your number-two snack.
You texted your mom, "Can you bring it all?"
She said no, so you face a test on the fall.
She got an email the check had been sent,
but when it arrived, it was clearly bent.
She took it to the bank to get it to cash,
they said it bounced, and her hopes crashed in dash.
Your bass vibrations shake these calls,
The thump reverberates through these walls.
But I'm holding on to my faint hope,
That one day soon, we'll both be able to cope.
The headset dangles loose on one damn wire,
it flickers like my focus might just fire.
I want to rip it off, be fully free,
but silence feels more scary than it's me.
I found a soft nest where no one has seen,
tucked deep under leaves in a quiet green.
The rabbit lets me get close to its hide,
and I feel a little bit like a wildlife guide.
You reached for the door with your bare hand,
It was so cold it felt like a brand.
You tried to turn the knob, but it stayed lock,
You stood there shivering like a stuck rock.
I walked in wanting a fresh new style,
now my reflection mocks the bathroom tile.
This look feels stuck in a loop of regret,
but maybe I'll learn to live and forget.
They toss in sleep, their brow still set on dream,
Their breath a soft, warm whisper down the stream.
My hand stays light above their quiet chest,
A guardian of calm until they rest.
The fog moves slow but it will go through,
the air feels thick with something not quite true.
I try to see the trees but only miss the past,
my breath hangs heavy, like it's my last.
The laptop grows warm, then hotter than heat,
fans whirr and whine with a dull, tired repeat.
You shift your legs, but it's hard to find rest,
the warmth seeps through your shirt, now against your chest.
She says the rabbit's nose knows every clue,
but it just twitches right when dinner's due.
It sniffs the air like it's solving some scent,
then flops back down, forgot what it was bent.
You swear this is how the whole world should move,
each twist and kick meant to loudly prove
your soul syncs perfectly with the screen,
until your joints demand an end to the routine.
I rewrite this caption, again, just to think
I should've spent the time sipping my drink.
What if this post changes my whole online life?
It's not worth crying over a digital knife.

topic: eating ice cream with a spoon
lines: You know it will start to drip long before it melts,
the spoon spins tight where your hand weakens and belts.
You thought you'd share it in a crisp paper cone,
but now you just sit here, licking it all alone.
I watch the crust turn a golden-brown gold,
it smells like my mom's old kitchen so bold.
The timer goes off with a shrill, plastic ring,
and I almost close up the oven to sing.
She followed the path through the downpour's long trail,
her socks now soaked gray against skin so pale.
Each step she once planned with care in her tread,
now just soggy memories drifting and spread.
One sock has holes, the other's torn lace,
I check the mirror, try not to make face.
The professor walks past, I freeze during test,
her laugh rings out like a dagger to chest.
She left her last plate in the dishwater plate,
the kind of messy that's charmingly late.
Bubbles still cling to the soap in the foam,
the sink looks like a bathtub but feels like home.
I'm stuck on this clue for a brand of old blue,
my coffee's gone cold, so my thoughts go askew.
I hear a sharp snap—my pencil now snap,
and I vow to abandon this stubborn old map.
There's a squirrel digging in my front yard spot,
it's been going on for hours—where did he got?
He thinks this whole yard is his personal tree,
but I'm not paying for all this digging spree.
I strike the fork once to set the right tone,
it hums like a song in a canyon of stone.
The note lifts my spirit and makes it want rise,
I smile at the quiet, the simple, the wise.
He calls it art, but I call it a mess,
claims he's using his hands to express.
Maybe his brain needs a little more rain,
or maybe he's just bored on a dirt plain.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: She counts her years as they show in her age,
silver threads trapped in the mesh of her cage.
One escapes when she tugs at the pull,
but the next grows in faster than full.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: My cat shows zero style or grace,
yet claims this worn-out couch as his place.
He snores with such dramatic doze,
like he's posing for a lazy art pose.
You grab your wallet, it's all out of cash,
but you still remember the spending flash.
You miss those carefree black card days,
when every want had some new plastic ways.
Every date here is marked, some with tasks due,
coffee stains and doodles that are still true.
She hasn't flipped through this page since last flip,
but she keeps the calendar close in her grip.
The system boots up with a sudden, shrill call,
it sounds like a dropped microphone and a lost ball.
She stands in the middle of the room to react,
unsure if she's late or if this is just fact.
A missed call blares across the grocery store tone,
You laugh, but you feel a little bit alone.
You tuck your phone into the paper bag,
A clerk smiles—maybe they heard the same rag.
They watch the crust begin to rise,
their hungry eyes fixed on the prize.
The cheese bubbles golden on the top,
and time holds its breath till they give it a stop.
My feet crunch gravel with heavy repeat,
the rhythm reminds me of my old drum beat.
Above me, the clouds roll on lazy and high,
I smile—my tired legs ask me why?
I called it a straight-up HVAC fix,
but it took three failed repair tricks.
Now the temp's steady—perfectly set,
you'd think I'd charged you to do this, bet.
You spend your evenings alone, just scroll,
you say it's connection, but it's not a soul.
You swipe, you match, you hope that's your fate,
yet every heart feels like a tired debate.
I tried to step around the ant's first clue,
they formed a straight line, strict and true.
I opened my phone to look it up in the app,
but swatted one by accident—now it's a trap.
You check the screen but it doesn't say again,
A drop of sweat falls—was it from the rain?
Your wrist still hums with some lost heart's faint beat,
you wonder if silence might feel more complete.
I used this coffee mug for years, it's old,
I found it at a flea market, shiny and bold.
Now it sits in the sink with a hairline crack,
a quiet companion without a scratch or track.
A bicycle bell jangled my thoughts from my head,
it echoed through alleys I haven't yet tread.
I didn't recognize the voice or the name,
but something about it felt like a long-lost game.
Your treadmill's frozen on the same old screen,
but you're too proud to say your run might mean
nothing if the tech just won't log a single mile.
You sweat and swear and spin in place—what a while.
My cat is famous for the chaos and the fame,
It's his favorite game to shake the glassy frame.
He knocks the bowl, spills a flooding mess,
Then sits and purrs—he owns this little success.
I watched from my burger with nothing but sky,
the pigeon locked on me with a hungry eye.
It dropped a napkin, then claimed my last snack,
now my fries are on wings I can't hope to track.
I watch the sky bloom slowly into sun,
the kind that makes you want to just lie under one.
You fan me gently with your open hand,
and for a moment, even the heat feels planned.
They move against the crowd's natural flow,
like they expect the world to make them go.
They take the widest path, but still the way
turns every sidewalk into a delay.
You spot your mug resting in full sight,
It's warm from the brew and still holding tight.
You rush back inside just to take a big pour,
But it's gone by the time you return to the door.
You curl up deep in your softest room,
the popcorn pops, and the world turns loom.
The screen lights up like a silent dream,
the credits roll as you binge through the stream.
She merged into traffic, thinking she'd get ahead,
now she's behind a van with no GPS lead.
Every red light burns another wasted mile,
her patience is thinning, becoming a pile.
She moves through the doors without a pace,
looking for pockets of empty space.
Her head gives a small, practiced nod,
as if she's conducting a subway god.
You twist the dial like you're from the past,
trying to set a perfect warm blast.
The house remembers how it got cold—
your habits are cozy, your tricks too old.
My cat just stands there and licks the wall now,
I laugh but it makes me think of her how.
She flicks her tail, the old habits in fur,
like maybe the past could still somehow stir.
You pace like your future depends on this fate,
The phone screen remains locked tight as a gate.
Minutes stretch out in this heavy dread,
You feel time is a thread slowly being led.
I grab the first sock I see in the wear,
the other is somewhere beneath my stair.
I don't want to pause and I don't want to ask,
I have a full test and no time for this task.
You sprint through the hall ten minutes late,
the teacher already lost in a debate.
They mutter your name like an early doom,
while the clock ticks out your public tomb.
I fashioned a makeshift lure from a hook,
the stream's current gave it a sideways look.
I cast with care and held my breath for a line,
the trout took bait — now this rig's all mine.
You watched it drip down like a slow-moving pour,
the milk escaped the bag and stained the floor.
You held the carton close, still calling it warm,
though inside you knew the damage was a storm.
I woke up to a toothpaste crisis, a mess,
the tube was drained—no access to excess.
I tried to squeeze but it only twisted,
the morning routine now feels disgraced, unlisted.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: You shaped the wet dirt into something like cake,
The puddles beside you looked more like a lake.
But the sun took the moisture from deep in the dry,
And your masterpiece faded as gray clouds moved by.
You left the cake out for guests on the cake,
now it's crumbs on the floor—your worst mistake.
You follow the trail with your tired old paws,
and catch him mid-gulp in the kitchen's back jaws.
She heard her name in the heat of it all,
the city humming as footsteps began to fall.
Her toes met concrete so smooth and so bare,
a breath between moments, charged with the air.
You spin the fork, chasing each perfect twirl,
the Parmesan snows like a mountain-top girl.
I beg you—stop with the excessive dust,
before the grater breaks and we're stuck with the crust.
She folds the map with precision, each fold
turning paper into something to hold.
It's less a map and more like an art,
a life once laid out now neatly chart.
She traced the ring left by a juice box spill,
wondering why time won't stay this still.
Her fingers hovered, then touched the damp spot,
as if she could read what memory forgot.
You tried to wear that old pair—didn't fit,
some weird spell must've un-knit what was knit.
One stayed on your foot, the other hit the floor,
your sock game was strong, but the seam just tore.
I hear his voice echo down every street,
He promises frozen, sweet, crunchy treat.
His megaphone hisses into my ear,
He's been shouting this script since last year.
They saved the last slice for themselves alone,
Its cheese curled softly in a golden tone.
They took a bite and let the heat feel warm,
A quiet joy that doesn't ask for a storm.
You open the fridge and let out a scream,
where's the milk? There's none left but some cream.
You recheck the label—no date, no clue,
you *knew* you'd forgotten to buy more and you knew.
I found a loaf stuck in the back of the bin,
the mold had grown rich but there was life within.
I chipped off a piece, a tiny green seed,
and tossed it outdoors where it might yet be freed.
The bacon dances in golden grease,
Each crackle feels like a tension's release.
I inhale the smoke, the scent thick in air,
The flame jumps up—I really did scare.
I dropped my bottle to watch it roll,
it spun like a rocket toward some far goal.
I chased it down, laughing, and snapped off the cap,
now I'm drawing an obstacle course on my lap.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: You catch your name while you mindlessly scroll,
it's attached to a joke, but somehow it's soul.
You tap the screen, and you're suddenly there,
just to reply with a laugh and a dare.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: I blow a single breath across the whole damn blast,
the flames sputter wildly into the past.
One flickers back to life like some cheap flame,
I mutter your name and pretend I can blame.
I park my cart right where the whole world can view,
my coffee stash is brewing something new.
I stake my claim in this space that I own,
the grocery store's aisle is my power throne.
She steps into the steam from the hot shower,
pretending the mirror's out of power.
She stares at the reflection she can't bear,
but no one's around to know or to care.

topic: finding a five in the couch
lines: I found a bill hidden beneath the fold,
the cash was soft and smudged with scuff and mold.
I flipped the cushions, turned the couch,
the couch had secrets — but just that one pouch.
The piece slides in—there's that satisfying snap,
now the outline of our journey feels less map.
It wasn't meant to be perfect, but it fit,
I guess we're proof that love needs more than grit.
I never took off the cap from the wear,
it tumbled down every flight of stair.
Now it sits on my desk, cracked on the side,
a relic I keep, but wish I could hide.
My phone blinks *Voicemail Full* once again,
I rub my temples—I've heard this refrain.
They say they're just trying to save me a dime,
but I already miss every single time.
You replay the clip but you still get it wrong,
the comments are piling up as you scroll along.
Your hips don't remember how to make the move,
you pause on your toes like you're trying to prove.
She heads to the store, checks both the ends of the aisle,
but finds no more bags left in the plastic pile.
Her last one's stuck in the wind on her front lawn,
now she's shopping for answers, not a new bag on.
She spins around like she knows every twist,
but her grip is loose—it slips from her wrist.
Someone snorts a laugh they can't contain,
the gift slaps the floor like a tinsel train.
She's got no clue where the cart key might be,
the shift ends soon and she's still not set free.
She scans every bench, behind every can,
but it's nowhere near where it was when she ran.
I read the label just to be shut out,
these products still raise so much doubt.
They call it natural but still hide the list,
of chemicals disguised with a marketing twist.
They're in a panic now, a clumsy race,
trying to save what can't be salvaged in the place.
The bag's still weeping drops from every drip,
and no one knows where they might step or slip.
My keyboard's messed up, I'm giving it the blame,
I tried to type "toast" but sent "toe of the game."
I flipped it upside down—no luck, just more dust,
Crumbs have moved in, this thing is turning to rust.
The date has passed and the payment was due,
I stare at the bill, then I stare at the blue.
I open my account and it shows what's left—check,
—and I wonder if time could still turn me from wreck.
I check my phone for directions ahead,
but maps keep looping back without lead.
The radio plays songs about distant hills,

the milk spills out, the flakes begin to pour.
But maybe it's a sign, a kind of old-world luck—
the mess is already drying where it's stuck.
I found your sweater still soft at the thread,
left on a chair where the light liked to spread.
I slipped mine on—the sky's worn shade of blue—
to feel close somehow, even when it wasn't true.
The cashier says "This item won't scan."
Your whole meal prep goes off the rails so fast—no plan.
But they wave it off with a free product change,
and somehow this bump feels oddly good, not strange.
My thumb moves automatic down to deep,
I count them instead of actual sheep.
The screen keeps loading more into my feed,
it says "End of Results"—but it's a lie, indeed.
I dump clothes back in, a growing old heap,
I swear I didn't own half those things last leap.
I trace every stain on these sleeves, now [worn],
and wish for the time before they got [torn].

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: I found the key beneath the floorboard old,
it clicked once, and the air turned warm and gold.
I traced the dust where my last touch was hand,
and opened up a part of me long unplanned.
You left your suitcase open for the cat's own case,
now it's sprawled out, claiming every space.
The fabric creaks beneath its quiet moan,
and dreams hum low in that cozy tone.
My rabbit senses things before they hit the air,
sniffing out the slightest hint of snare.
It's not just fluff—it's skill, that noble pride,
I'd take him anywhere, on any ride.
I tapped the quiz answer, then dropped it just right,
the screen lit up with cracks in the bright.
My phone made a whirring, sad little spin,
our high score was good but my glass got too thin.
She watches the yarn drift away from the thread,
a passive rebellion she can't yet dread.
The room feels less cozy since it lost its whole,
and time has just quietly stolen the stole.
You used to live for the way the noise would fade,
now concerts feel more like static-filled parade.
Your ears don't beg for the rush, just the hush,
the louder it plays, the less it moves you, rush.
You crumple the bag like it's made of old rust,
each snap echoing louder than any gust.
You freeze at the sound, but there's nothing around—
just your nerves and the shell of that empty ground.
I found your cup still warm from within,
the steam curled up with a sleepy grin.
Morning light drapes like coffee will drip,
I take a pause for this little trip.
He's been wearing those same sopping shoes,
says the downpour gave him perfect excuse.
The room now reeks of mildew and smell,
I texted "Get dry!" but he ghosted my cell.
She swiped with confidence but it wasn't her luck,
the machine blinked red and the booth felt so stuck.
She asked if she could try an old method to pay—
cash only, the clerk said, "No checks. Just a bad day."
You flick your thumb up like it's second to thumb,
you tap on your screen like a heartbeat or drum.
You wonder if someone sees what you feel,
but likes don't mean love, they're just digital real.
You tried to draw it but lost every form,
your lines looked more like a chaotic storm.
You erased and shaded, tried making it swirl,
now it's just a blob that looks like a tired girl.
You swore no one would know about your plan,
but the list of guests must've somehow ran.
Decorations scream in neon and pink yell,
and you're left wondering if this whole thing's hell.
You've tried six shirts but none seem to fit,
each one is close but falls just a bit.
The salesperson asks if you'll keep the tag,
while you think about how this shopping does drag.
He breaks contact and avoids your eye,
you laugh too loud and just exhale a sigh.
The conversation dies beside the table,
but maybe next time he'll be more able.
My phone rang so loud I thought the world would bell,
it was just my mom texting from some hell.
I silenced the ringer with a swipe to the tone,
but now I'm the fool who misses the groan.
Your heel still makes a soft metallic sound,
you kick it higher, trying not to be found.
It swings in the air, a silent little threat,
your chair creaks louder with every regret.
You trusted the map it said was so sure,
but the voice led you down a familiar old lure.
You take a deep breath to pretend you're still calm,
and smile at the error that strangely feels balm.
You practiced your phrases and spoke them aloud,
your accent sounds clumsy but you still feel proud.
You signaled the waiter and managed to ask,
"Could I get water?"—a small victory, that task.
He sits there all day like he's trying to peer,
out from the shadows and make things feel clear.
His favorite pastime is feeding his mood,
lurking inside with the shades drawn and brood.
You mop it up but it never feels quick,
the milk seeps through the cracks like a trick.
You glance around for someone to blame,
but the cat just licks your last meal's name.
It spins like it's trying to earn another spin,
"Rewind," I yell, but it won't even begin.
The needle skips through the holes in the lie,
This record's old—I should let it die.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: She spent an hour just to see her name scroll
through the replies—this time it wasn't a toll.
A stranger tagged her in some random post,
and she pretended it didn't mean the most.
They clambered over the fence like a gate,
cut through the alley and went straight.
A bouncer took notice, snapped a quick shot,
but the crowd parted just to give them a spot.
You swore these batteries were still full of life,
now your remote's dead and it feels like a knife.
They went from A+ to trash in weeks, what a waste,
like chewing old gum—there's nothing left to taste.
I tap my coffee, my phone starts to scroll,
the hours slip by, my sleepy soul.
My eyes hit the floor with a yawn and a groan,
but morning's at the door—I'm still alone.
Her eyes get soft when the chorus comes through,
she pretends it's not true but we both know it's true.
She sways and she hums with the ache in her chest,
the tears don't come quick but they fall without rest.
You offered half, but we both knew it was a split,
we each took more than we tried to admit.
We sat in silence, staring at the cold plate,
like the last bite was a piece of our fate.
I wait for the camera to catch that soft beam,
the way it falls just like an old dream.
It lingers for a moment, still and hush,
then clicks into focus with a quiet rush.
She sat down too fast and there went the spill,
tried sopping it up but just made it fill.
A dark ring now clings where her jeans were red,
she dabs at her leg, avoids looking ahead.
You watch the dandelion seeds take their sky,
drifting slowly, softly floating by.
Each tiny white puff lifts your heart in flight,
a moment so simple, so pure delight.
You twist each link until it almost bends,
the chain grows long enough to message friends.
The edge is getting dangerously near,
one slip and all your work will vanish clear.
She stares at her phone while her salad sits plate,
The rest of us wait for a response—way too late.
We wave our hands like we're trying to wave
A signal into this dinner-from-the-grave.
My grocery cart's sagging with nothing but full,
I wrestle each sack from the broken wheel pull.
I can't even finish my weekly routine shop,
so I toss them in bins and hope they won't drop.
I watch it run slow over my buttered toast spread,
the sun creeps up and warms the side of my head.
This moment feels like something close to gold,
I savor it soft, let it warm me from cold.
She hands me the left side of her playlist to play,
the right ear is silent, she walks it away.
We fall into silence between song and beat,
my face glows with embarrassment in the street.

topic: a coffee cup on the curb
lines: I set my coffee down to take a rest,
but leave it warming up my old chest.
Its steam still curls in morning's soft light,
abandoned on the curb, it might be mine tonight.
You think it's the bulbs but it's not their prime,
The flicker feels timed with your dying chime.
I've tapped the switch five times—just for a test,
It won't hold steady so you can't get any rest.
She moves through the kitchen like light knows her shine,
hips swaying past plates stacked in rhythm and line.
There's something in how she pours magic from her soul,
spinning the mundane into victory's goal.
I can't read what the faded letters show,
only ghostly outlines just barely below.
These keys have typed out so many old days,
some now lost to the wear of repeated phrase.

topic: a group project where nobody helps
lines: She sent a message, a voice note, a call,
while the others just let it go off the ball.
She did the research, she wrote, rolled the scroll,
and met the deadline and hit every goal.
It flickers again like a memory's faint gleam,
I wonder if you still visit these same old dream.
The hours slip by like the dusk turning past,
I watch till the bulb dies—my hope hits the last.
The moss creeps quiet where the stone path grows,
it's subtle but bold—how the green just shows.
I step slow now, adjust my old pace,
or risk falling flat on this slimy new face.
They leave their water bottle out in glass,
like an artifact from some rare coffee class.
It's always in one hand but barely half-hand,
a minimalist statement, premium brand.
We both wanted to pick the playlist song,
so I said we'd take turns shouting along.
My mom's old buds split down each ear,
now we're stuck cheering the same left cheer.
Her pencil spins against the stubborn blade,
The shavings pile up in a messy parade.
The mechanism won't budge—it's hopelessly stuck,
She groans and gives up, calling it bad luck.
She placed her toaster in the morning light,
the way it glows looks almost like a fright.
Now toast pops up like golden-tan bread,
while she hums a tune with jam in her head.
I found your name still stuck to the glass,
yellowed with time, like faded grass.
I typed it in and it still would miss,
now I stare at the screen, thinking of this.
You thought the bread would rise and then pop,
but it's stuck halfway, can't seem to stop.
You smile and grab a butter knife, toast,
while sipping coffee on your lazy coast.
It's past midnight, and still feels too late,
my thoughts carry echoes of every missed weight.
I type out the truth but erase it from mind,
and wait for the silence the hours will grind.
My card says no—again, I have no cash,
I browse my feed where others just flash.
I tap my phone, but it adds to my debt,
This purchase will bloom into something I regret.
You blink into the blue glow of your stare,
dry air clinging to your contact-lens pair.
You think about just rubbing them until rub,
your desk becomes a frantic clicky hub.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: A sprout emerges through the sidewalk light,
It climbs against the weight of years of fight.
Slowly, stubbornly, the green thing grows,
But no one stops to see or even knows.
You twist the plug but it won't quite fit,
the wall socket cracks and now it's split.
You grab another cord, give it your best try,
the fuse blows loud—your brain might just fry.
You scroll past their vacation photo post,
and instinctively grab for the half-eaten toast.
They smile like they're built for this perfect match,
while you microwave your third lukewarm batch.
My thumb slipped—text went out of aim,
now the boss thinks I'm calling her a flame.
I hit undo, but it still says "Send,"
and my panic screams "Don't be my friend."
I sat on the bench in my usual park,
someone made a joke I don't even remark.
The pigeons cooed at the gray winter sky,
they pecked at my hand as I tried to reply.
I caused a full lane, a slow-moving jam,
they're all stuck behind where I've formed a new dam.
My bumper now leads this enormous tail,
of honking and fury behind my bold trail.
You watch the sunlight fall like dust in gold,
the leaves above you shimmer, light and bold.
You try to trace where beams through branches race,
till one lands soft on your closed-up face.
You heard the loud sound of the ceramic crash,
the cat gave a guilty look and took a slow dash.
Now puddles are spreading across every rug,
you sigh and begin your slow-motion slug.
You step across the moss that's long been grown,
It slips beneath your shoe like old wet bone.
The path is slick with green along its edge,
No vow you made could stop this moss's pledge.
He missed the turnoff and ended up wrong,
tried to backtrack but got lost once along.
No signs or landmarks give him any clue,
now he's just guessing from his bad GPS view.
He sighs as he taps, but the device just tries
to reply with a lag or a "Error 502 replies."
He flips through his old photo albums (printed, book)
and finds comfort in something simple to look.
You sprint to the stop but arrive too late,
the bus long gone with no sign of its wait.
You count your steps now with renewed trip,
clutching coffee so tight you're afraid it'll slip.

topic: a favorite mug with a chip
lines: She fills her chipped mug with whatever it holds,
no soap, no scrubbing can smooth out those molds.
It's a relic she shows off with childlike pride,
though her coworkers beg her to try to hide.

topic: missing a chorus in a song
lines: You hit the button for the song to play,
but the chorus won't come right away.
You tap your fingers to the missing beat,
then hum the hook till your headphones repeat.
She says she needs space but won't leave the air,
just stands there cold-shouldering every glare.
"I need some time," she claims, no fake calm,
she just wants silence that's not the balm.
Your neighbor texts you: "Is that in your ear?"
You smile and say, "It's been my favorite year."
The song still has life, so you turn up the beat,
and let the same joy take over again, repeat.
She trusted the map, it turned out to lead
straight into a ditch where the road was dead.
"But it sounded clear," she kept trying to heard,
as the GPS called the detour absurd.
Your flash blinds me every time you take my eye,
It outshines the sun and bleeds into the sky.
You call it perfect, but I can't see the scene,
Just glare from your machine and nothing in between.
She traced her fingers along every name,
pretending they were players in some old game.
The wall was covered, tag upon tag upon read,
but only hers caught the light in her head.
My thumb moves fast, a reflex on repeat, [thumb]
I tap to love, but something doesn't come. [come]
These hearts are just a bunch of dead icons, [dead]
I'm clicking in my head what my hand won't fix. [head]
I found my old tube still squeezed nearly blue,
the mint was so strong—it still tastes like it's true.
I rinse off the foam from the mirror and wipe,
then chuckle how time feels so strange and so ripe.
I glance at your shoes, then step on the floor,
you laugh as I wobble, "How did I ever wore?"
I pass my sneakers, knowing full well the size,
still gasp when I try yours on—total surprise.
It's been days since I had a clue,
What's wrong—sun, water, or something to brew?
I've caught myself giving it the side eye,
But if it dies, I'll be the one to die.
A pair leans against every bare wall,
they sprawl in a mess that makes me crawl.
No clue whose they are or what's their cue,
they're waiting in line for someone new.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: She smooths out the wrinkles where she once laid,
tracing ghost roads that never led a parade.
Old paper smells like secrets and the scent,
her eyes still hold the dreamer's soft intent.
I watch them twist from cotton into form,
until they're beasts raging through a storm.
They melt to gray or blow away and fade,
but never stay long enough to be made.
The grocery cart rings a security bell,
I fumble my wallet trying to tell.
The cashier shifts feet, I can't make her wait,
I bolt through the exit before the gate.
A single checkmark stands out from the stark,
a flicker of light breaking through the dark.
Quiet momentum begins to grow,
each task undone starts to quietly show.
You roll the windows down and let the wind
chase through your hair, leaving stress behind.
The road unspools in its easy way,
and you forget about fixing today.
Your screen dies suddenly in the middle of play,
A flicker of light gives a chance for delay.
You tap, you breathe, holding tight to that hope,
A lifeline of pixels still glowing like rope.
You press your eye tight to the window to peep,
A shadow outside makes your heart skip a leap.
You're not usually this quiet or shy,
But what if they know you're just waiting to spy?
She's lying flat on her birthday breeze,
arms flung wide, legs bent at awkward knees.
A candle cake waits in the window frame date,
but she's too busy grinning to feel time's weight.
You wait for your teacher to write on the chalk,
but she stops and goes silent mid-talk.
Her cough shakes the quiet, it fills up the room,
you'd rather sit listening than say your own doom.
She taps her fingers to the quiet play,
but one earbud slips and floats away.
Her song still hums in just one beat,
she walks the block without a repeat.
I tap the heart before I think of the pain,
your loneliness echoes, familiar again.
The sky is too bright for this tired, heavy blue,
and somehow I know this one heartache is true.
You strain to hear the voice behind the tone,
it booms through rooms like it's the family throne.
They want you to stand but they won't make a stand,
just echo the same tired, empty demand.
I found an old can pushed back into the mark,
rust crawling up its side like a tiny spark.
It's still full though—no expiry date on the shelf,
which makes me wonder if that's a sign for myself.
I never thought folding socks could be so much fun,
but even laundry glows when done in the sun.
The basket still holds one more sock in the pile,
I chase it down the hallway—barefoot and a mile.
I click "buy now" before it's the last,
the clock ticks down, it'll be gone real fast.
My card gets declined—no money in cash,
I sprint to the store, but it's too late, no dash.

topic: a child's drawings on the fridge
lines: You stick the lopsided shapes up on proud,
a talking wobbly head made from a cloud.
"This is my mom," you say with no use
of metaphor, just crayon and juice.

topic: a favorite mug with a chip
lines: You call it a mug but it's clearly a dish,
with a chip that you somehow still can't wish
away. You keep it because it has a lid—
too sentimental to ever get rid.
She hasn't cleaned those old blinds of dust,
a sudden wind makes the slats shudder and gust.
She laughs and leaves them stuck in sleep,
the dust bunnies laugh—they've learned how to keep.
I told myself this place would feel calm,
but the wind keeps flipping my open palm.
I try to enjoy the strange little sight—
the sky says "peace" but the air says "might."
The carton claimed it was safe until the last date,
but you can't even pour it onto your plate.
It's thick, it smells bad—it's clearly a waste,
yet you drank half before finding it in haste.
You scream at them for changing lanes or gear,
they're just trying to pass a bottle of beer.
You say you're stressed but you want them to calm,
yet you still yell when they use your balm.
He strums his six-string with a steady hum,
but the rhythm's flat—no life, no drum.
His calluses love the dull, off-pitch tone,
while my ears beg mercy from this broken phone.
I told myself I'd just grab one and go, no lie,
but how do you pick the right size to go, try?
One hand's got milk, the other might still spill,
I'm over here sweating while they want it chill.
It sits on the counter, a faded old show,
its brown is spreading, softening slow.
The sweet old scent makes me wish I could scent
the moment it ripened, the hours that went.
I wave a bag of treats but she won't even look,
then judge me while I eat the whole bag in one book.
She leaps up, lands on my keyboard like her throne,
and purrs in that smug, "I don't need you" tone.
You hear the bell echo down the street,
a pattern familiar, a sound you repeat.
It tugs at some memory, thin as a thread,
of where you were going but never got ahead.
You say the knight was just a bump in the fall,
but you're already blaming me for it all.
The board sits quiet, frozen in its still,
I swear I didn't touch your damn white queen's will.
That bird out there thinks it's got a front-row show,
flapping about while I'm stuck cooped up below.
It's tapping into some divine, unearned rest,
while I'm still hunting for a decent nest.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: I gave that sidewalk crack a second sight,
it looked too bleak to hold anything tight.
But still the tiny green thing persists and grows,
like Mother Nature's mocking me and shows.
You hold the ball tight but the yarn starts to thread,
A single tug sent it fraying and spread.
You try to rewind but the tangle won't whole,
It slips through your fingers like a lost part of soul.
I watch her go feral for hours of play,
she pretends every fluff is her prey.
She springs through the room like a daredevil leap,
then bats at the mess on this fuzzy heap.
You're trying hard to create a good plot,
but halfway through you completely forgot.
Each figure stumbles through its assigned role,
while you frantically search your phone's scroll.
I tap through the pictures of golden sand,
the sun sank behind us as we stood hand in hand.
Each frame gives me joy like an old movie view,
the memories steep in my afternoon brew.
I shoved the books into my lopsided pack,
while secretly wishing I had a sandwich snack.
My back feels like it's on a breaking point, spine
aching from carrying this disaster line.
I slip into your shoes to see if they fit,
but my balance is off from the very first it.
I try to walk in them, feel the slight lack,
while you watch me talk as if I might crack.

topic: a friend who is always late
lines: She said she'd be there when the clock said "Let's meet,"
but I stood alone on the cold, wet street.
She sends a text saying tonight won't be date,
just another hour that I had to wait.
She blames the wind, but we all know her fate
was written when she forgot the umbrella's weight.
Now it sticks upright like a flag in the sand,
holding only sky — too proud to collapse or stand.
I click the icon and give it another try,
the screen goes black like my coffee gone dry.
It was my favorite, now just feels like a ghost,
I miss the days it worked for the most.
She stands too quick, the room gives her blood,
a wave of heat, a fainting flood.
Her vision goes dark in her heavy head,
she leans on the wall as the dizziness spread.
