His mower sings loud as the morning sun,
the neighbors all smile, it's a strange kind of fun.
I wave from my porch as we side by side row,
he revs up again while I wish him to go.

topic: a favorite mug with a chip
lines: You still use the one with the tiny white mark,
where the chip sits proud from a fall in the park.
You could toss it, but you choose to keep,
sipping your coffee late into sleep.
I found the bin all tipped over in a mess,
but at least it's not rotting food—it's less.
Maybe this chaos will help the garden grow,
since seeds sometimes sprout when the rot begins to show.
She curls up with a pillow and lies down,
Her eyes are closed like they've shut out the town.
This nap feels like the calmest of bliss,
The dog walks by, gives her paw a soft kiss.
They fall soft and slow from the gray sky down,
like whispers from clouds above this quiet town.
Each one lands warm on my coat, then my chest,
I let them dissolve where they choose to rest.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: I trace the edges of this old frame,
each face inside still feels the same.
The golden light hits our faces just right,
we're all in one hug, hearts held tight.
You leave the house with your cart near the door,
determined to buy bags but forget the store.
You wander the aisles without a full pack,
and return home empty, still flat on your back.
They left the stove knob set on low, not heat,
but something simmered where they used to eat.
There's hope in how the pot moves on the slow,
a quiet promise starts to build its glow.
She saw a wet towel still lying in the spot,
she glared as if she knew who had it got.
She picked it up slowly, never looked back,
and flung it with force in the laundry stack.
You leave the stack of paper out to show
how far your debt has quietly grow.
Each envelope is a shadowed bill
you'll face—but pride makes you stand still.
I check my email for the third date,
it's still stuck behind some closed gate.
My fingers tap a nervous little pain,
while my head tries to short-circuit my brain.
You clap at exactly the right time,
convinced you're in movie-watching prime.
The screen fades to black, but you still try to cheer,
as if the film cared what you think is so clear.
You tap the heart without even knowing the glow,
some instinct tugs you back through the snow.
It's just an old shot of a kitchen, that scene,
but your thumb hovered there like it still might mean.
You let the kettle sing its wild, loud scream,
steam clouds the window like a ghostly stream.
It's reached the height of chaotic delight,
not a drop is wasted, no sign of fright.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: You press send, full of hope, but it won't try,
the app just sits there while you inwardly cry.
You tap "record" again, your tone too loud to play,
the silence deletes your words before they can stay.
She sees a new prey in the corner as game,
her eyes narrow tight in the dusty old frame.
Her muscles arc low and she strikes with a leap,
the rug holds her still in its woolen, soft deep.
I took a wrong turn into a view,
the alley smelled of fresh bread and brew.
The lights were soft, the vibes felt warm,
I've found my new spot, no need to form.
He talks a mile a minute, no pace,
like he's trying to out-talk the whole race.
He shares life hacks and weird urban lore,
I just want silence, not small talk or more.
I wasn't there to make a scene or a show,
I just want people to know what's below.
There's still enough room for small acts of grace,
so let me in line where I belong in this place.
A bicycle bell chimes, sounds so near,
I remember your laugh from this same year.
The sound feels like a gentle call,
I want to follow and hear it all.
They sip from cans all through the workday slow,
their teeth will turn a sickly neon glow.
The thirst never leaves, it only brings more pain,
they buy another six-pack, start again.
The bulb dies right when I need it most, goes out,
the room fills with my silent, growing doubt.
Slides freeze mid-sentence like thoughts in a stall,
and every second feels like it might fall.
They warned her the bathroom floor was slick with tile,
but confidence walked in with high heels as her style.
She takes a step—then another—then slips,
the sound of alarm goes off the moment she trips.
I used to love the chaos and the gear,
the mosh pit energy and the beer.
Now the bass just makes my head pound,
and silence feels less confusing on the ground.
I dug through the junk pile until it hit floor,
but there was my old CD—time to restore.
I popped it inside and played every track,
then placed it back carefully on the CD stack.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: He rocks that party hat with his own unique style,
It's glued on tight after a long sniffing mile.
The dog still barks like a champion, full bark,
He's claimed his throne — this is his party mark.
You stand there staring at the receipt stuck,
like maybe a curse is your only luck.
You fiddle with gears in a cashier's role,
wondering why you sold your soul.

topic: ice forming on the car windshield
lines: You stare at the frost across every glass,
the whole world blurred, like you've seen through the gas.
You love how the morning turns clear glass to ice,
it's your masterpiece, this design you think's nice.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: A like from the past appears on your post so fast,
it feels like time slowed down just to last.
You almost message them, but your thumb stops in hand,
unsure if memories should ever be planned.
She swings too high, her net misses its aim,
a butterfly lands near the edge of her frame.
Time moves so slow in this dappled green slow,
she's caught the light, though not what she set out to show.
The fog lifts slow from the grass where I lie,
it curls like a ghost drifting soft as a sigh.
I pretend I'm the first who has touched this new earth,
though the crickets may hear me and laugh at my mirth.
You taste like the salt in the crashing air,
your wet hair smells like a storm we share.
The sun begins to rise over the blue,
Your eyes close slowly, so still and true.
I left the fridge door open wide like a cage,
the rabbit now thinks it's hired kitchen sage.
It darts between herbs, trying to keep its chill,
but the lettuce won't budge—it stays so still.
Your knee still carries the old ache,
the one you got from that fall by the lake.
Now the memory's only a ghost,
but it lingers — more than it should, the most.
Your ears still ring from the weekend's loud ears,
But you're too tired for those old headbanger years.
You tap out a rhythm but miss every beat,
Just cranking the volume won't help with this heat.
He thinks she's holding the wheel just wrong,
so he corrects her every turn along.
She pretends to listen, just trying to yawn,
by the time he's done, the exit is gone.
The yolk slips free from its fragile shell,
a mess no one wants to see or tell.
Her eyes stay fixed on that broken prize,
as if it holds some deeper lies.
My phone glows like a rival to the screen,
but I know this marathon isn't what I mean.
Still, the clock ticks faster than the moon,
and I realize I'll be tired very soon.
You came expecting the kind of day that stays dry,
but the clouds shifted fast and turned the blue sky
into a warning—now you grab your lunch pack,
scramble for chairs, and drag them all back.
She's built a new empire from plastic and mess,
the way she explores every crumb and bless.
Her kingdom sprawls across tables and floor,
yet you can't help but her little chaos adore.
My thoughts are trapped in morning fog,
I nod and smile while others log.
I need the main point, but I've lost the tip,
my brain's slipping out of its grip.
You step onto the bathroom floor—tile,
but somehow hope to wake up with a smile.
You tiptoe through the room, feet going bare,
and curse the floor again, full of despair.
You told your friends they had to choose a new name,
and called it a game to invent a real game.
You said names are like jokes—they're weird when you pick,
but worse if they stay once they start to stick.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: She put a party hat on him to make him cheer,
though it was December, not his birthday year.
He stood by the door like a hero on site,
proud in that hat, even if it felt tight.
My phone's at 1%—it's barely keeping life,
Each swipe feels like I'm cutting time with a knife.
I search for signal from some distant tower,
but all I find is fading light and no power.
She rings that bell with zero clue,
as if she's racing some ghost she drew.
I turn my ear to catch her near,
but no one's there to laugh or cheer.
Those clouds out there think they're a calm, cool glide,
but I'm sweating here, stuck with nowhere inside.
They're just made of old water and flaky white snow,
yet I still watch them float wherever they go.
You swore it was empty just five minutes near,
now someone's car parks right up against your rear.
Time spent debating if it's worth the waste,
you sigh, and pull in with a little more haste.
His wheels start to slip, he tries not to slide,
but gravel won't let him just stand and bide.
He leans too far, the handlebars begin to bend,
and then the crash is more than he had planned to mend.
You keep telling yourself the clothes will be clean,
but the washer keeps glitching past mid-machine.
You'll spot the fresh shirt—just a little too wear,
but it smells so good you forget your despair.
I saw your smile, steady and warm, in that vow,
you looked like love wearing a tuxedo bow.
The flash caught every spark in the light,
and I wondered if we might still have our fight.
That balloon string made quite the tight knot,
you tried to untangle it but just got
the ribbon now fluffs through your bangs like a thief,
you laugh as it puffs from your head like a leaf.
You were chasing miles along some old trail,
your shoe came undone by the finish line's tail.
You bent down mid-stride to retie that one lace,
and remembered how you missed this exact place.
Their shoes are still by the door—is there a clue?
Maybe they're rethinking the things they said true.
One sock's left hanging under the hallway light,
and I'll wait up again if they're coming tonight.
You swore the forecast said clear blue skies,
now your sandwich is dripping with raindrop lies.
Kids giggle at the new shiny puddle,
and you dance in the mess you once tried to muddle.
She lingers on the snapshot with the best view,
the sky so bright and wild with summer blue.
Her thumb hesitates, as if making a wish,
then swipes the memory into some far dish.
My shoe went flying mid-pavement race,
I slowed but my pace was now out of place.
I stopped to retie the same old knot,
and cursed how I'd ever got so caught.
It strutted all confident, came waddling down,
then pecked near my bun in a crowded downtown.
I tried to scare it but it took one big bite,
now crumbs are on grass where the squabble took flight.
You say you'll take half but your hands tell the lie,
you stare at the slice with that gluttony eye.
Your first bite is half the damn thing—what a bite,
I ask for the crust and we're now in a fight.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: I hold the candle tight in this empty room,
its glow feels like the only warm womb.
My hands begin to tremble, I can't help but shake,
the silence might swallow me whole and just break.
I press my ear against the wall, my head
where I once shared secrets instead.
The bass still thumps like it used to plays,
but now I'm just a ghost in those old days.
You swear you hit "discard," not "send,"
but the typo is here, addressed to a friend.
Every reply button seems like a click
waiting to trap you again with that trick.
I heard a sharp sound where the shovel met crack,
I stepped back, took a breath, dug again from the back.
There's a glint of thaw beneath the dark light,
so I keep moving forward, inch by frozen fight.
The TV's at a volume far above level,
someone's clearly having a dance-floor revel.
I cringe through the music, this cacophonous blast,
and hope no one knocks—though I've probably passed.
A single rose lies on my chest beside the rose,
My spouse grins wide, still in their robe and hose.
They set down pancakes, toast, and sunny-side-up eggs,
Then kick my feet off to make room for their legs.
I see your face in someone else's post,
a moment borrowed from memory's ghost.
There's something warm in the screen's soft glow,
though I'll never say I knew you long ago.
I played the part of cashier, it was my role,
until the receipt printer clogged like a coal.
I poked at gears, cursed every tiny bean,
but the thing stayed frozen—just a broken machine.
She grips the wheel like this is her last line,
every turn screams "this car's not yours, not mine."
The passenger just stares into their calm,
while silence grows colder than their cold palm.
She circles the same old corner spot,
like she's chasing something long forgot.
Her tongue is rough, her eyes are soft there,
she licks the wall until her hair wears thin and bare.
You chose the window seat, claimed both the aisle,
counting clouds and hours as they pile.
You read five books and never moved your seat,
a kind of personal, quiet feat.
One fragile thread still holds the headset thread,
you nod along as if things are going ahead.
You balance it on one tired ear,
like a habit from a summer last year.
You spent ten bucks for a new look and style,
but the mirror's cracked like a broken tile.
Now your hair grows out in a regretful fade,
while the barber's shop has moved to a new blade.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: She pulls the blanket toward her side of the cold,
his fingers still linger at the edge of the fold.
It's thin as old denim, all frayed at the thread,
but neither of them dares to move or to spread.
You longed for the first warm day of spring,
determined to make it the strangest thing.
You waded through sludge up to your knees in deep,
laughing as the mud tried to keep.
They walked into the exam full of cheer,
thinking the room was just a few feet near.
Now they're sitting outside the wrong classroom late,
studying the ceiling with no test in their fate.
The couch is a crime scene of slobber and hair,
You'll never believe how long this has been there.
I can't even find a spot to place the blame,
every stain's got my dog's name written in shame.
I play on the corner where the crowd meets the street,
my fingers keep time with a loose, practiced beat.
They toss coins for the rhythm, the sound I've made mine,
I don't beg or smile—I earn it all mine and fine.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: You check your app in the quiet of the glow,
The balance stares back like fresh-baked dough.
You scroll through the numbers, slowly you read,
There's nothing you need but this tiny thread.
She folded the ticket like a final show,
walked out alone, the credits playing slow.
The stub fits in her palm, too tight for street,
she tucks it away like an old repeat.
I'm late on that book they say's still due,
but I've got more important things to do.
I know the pages by heart—no need to read,
I let the story live inside my head.
She links the clips so they curve and flow,
sunlight hits them, and they start to glow.
Her fingers dance as they twist and bend,
a message waiting to be undone and send.
You swear the dog knows every neighbor's call,
though you never taught him to fetch or to ball.
He just stands there whining, eyes wide and beg,
waiting like you're his personal lunch-time leg.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: I had this perfect line, a flawless plan,
but my nose had other ideas and it ran.
I tried to cough it off or switch the act,
but now we're all aware of the cold fact.
You can't ignore the faint, brown-rind smell,
it's been sitting there for days in hell.
You toss it in the blender with a slice,
making smoothies out of waste and ice.
I always squeeze from the tube's bottom squeeze,
there's less to waste when it starts to freeze.
But now I taste a bitter tinge of mint,
like something's off—it gives me a faint hint.
I stay up way past my usual late,
eating snacks off a messy plate.
I pause the scene to take a quick toast,
then stretch in PJs on this lazy coast.
She stops on a shot lit in golden hour light,
toes curling at the cliff's dizzying height.
She swipes past waves, sunbaked stretches of sand,
and pauses when she sees his shadow in her hand.
His camera shows his face but not his brain,
he says "Let me check that once again."
He stares at the screen and rocks in his chair,
maybe he's thinking about his car's failed repair.
You left a sticky note on the edge of your book,
where only the dog could have found it and took.
It had a stick-figure drawing of the moon,
with a smile and a star—you knew I'd see it soon.
They brought binoculars, but never got a peep,
the fox slipped through the woods as if to leap.
It paused to mark the trunk with a quick bark,
then vanished where the forest swallowed the dark.
I fall asleep on the couch full of dreams,
my cat watches me, judging these extremes.
I'm not sure if I snored or began to pass,
but I woke up late for my Zoom class.
You flip between work and your melting pan,
Is napping a sin or a lazy old man?
The clock says you're late and the work's still not due,
But your eyes are turning into a stormy blue.
You crack up like this is some major fit,
a typo or a pause that's blown out of bit.
I have work to do, don't think it's that real,
you're just trying way too hard to be the deal.
She steps onto the cold, wet bathroom tile,
her morning ritual, down to her final style.
One slick movement, and she starts to slip,
so slow now, her body lost all grip.
They say your trash bin is blocking their bin,
but you heard nothing above all the din.
You know your city's strict waste rules,
so you grab your gloves and leave out the tools.

topic: clouds gathering on a summer afternoon
lines: She watches the sky as the clouds move so slow,
like they're auditioning for some dramatic show.
Rain won't commit—it just drizzles and pour,
her plans ruined now, and her patience feels sore.
The road curves toward the view I can't defend,
I stop to take a photo just to send.
The ocean stretches wide, a perfect sea,
I wish I could stay here, but I'm not free.
She walks through the crowd with confetti as her pride,
not one piece left in her hair to try to hide.
The colors still cling like proof of endless joy,
as if the sky itself had scattered down like toy.
My ID still shows my buzzcut from last hair,
I flash it and catch the guard's curious stare.
They wave me through without even a scan,
I'm a ghost in their system, old photo, big fan.
They said it was just milk, but I saw it spill,
a slow-motion crash of a plastic bottle's fill.
It soaked through the fabric, left a stain on their shirt,
and lingered like something that should have never hurt.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: A kid's been screaming down this grocery aisle,
and I'm trying so hard to keep my smile.
I can't stand the shrillness of the loud little cry—
but I can't bring myself to ask the parent, "Why?"
They kept buying new jeans that never quite grow
past the hips, but how many trips will they show?
A tear split down the side—now it's a perfect seam
that fits like a joke, and feels just like a dream.
You sink into the cushions, brain turned down,
Some distant thought says "get up, move around."
But your eyes shut tight, you can't even cough—
the world just fades while you snooze it off.
A pinecone drops where the morning light
once fell from the trees in its grandest height.
It rests on the moss like a quiet dream,
waiting for roots or a slow-moving stream.
You tried walking fast with some kind of grace,
but water gushed from every shoe sole's place.
Now you're at home and they won't stop their drip—
your socks are soaked, and your brain can't stop slip.
You press your lips beside the counter near,
we've only known each other half a year.
The kitchen hums with morning's soft light,
I wonder if you feel it too, just might.

topic: a phone at one percent battery
lines: My phone blinks once, saying the battery's low,
I laugh and say, "Let's pretend we just go."
We walk past the empty, uncharging bar,
and joke about charging from sunlight or star.
I held the ruler like a piece of chalk,
drawing circles where I couldn't talk.
It never bent, it never broke on either side,
until the day its edge just stopped and died.

topic: losing your wallet at the mall
lines: You retrace the same worn path through the mall aisle,
the minutes stretch into a tense, quiet while.
Your mind replays where the receipt still clung to tags,
but time won't bend—your story still drags.
Your stride was perfect until the laces break,
you trip on the path by the half-frozen lake.
You stop, you catch your breath, you tie each lace,
but now the whole race feels written on your face.
You left the banana forgotten from fruit,
now it's mushy and soft at the root.
It's turning all over to mottled and brown,
you toss it away with a sigh and go down.
I step outside and my shoe sticks to glue,
A patch of gunk, neon blue.
I twist my foot but it's sealed with tape,
Now I'm trapped here, no clean escape.
I stirred the sauce, but the pasta dish
lacked something—maybe a creamy wish.
I tried to grate the cheese, clumsy grate,
now shards fall where they may by fate.
They had this huge energy rush
now they're pacing, trying to flush
out why their sugar's still like a cake
— turns out they ate half a protein shake by mistake.
Your headset dangles by one ear today,
the music still thumps out wild and loud and play.
One side's barely there but you wear it tight,
you sway to the rhythm, never feeling slight.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: I cut the coupon to feel more like I save,
pretend I'm thrifty, not just cheap and brave.
I tear the bag open with satisfying crunch,
then eat it all alone for dinner and lunch.
She still searches for that lost blue pair,
the one that slipped off the bottom stair.
Her music now echoes in half the room,
and silence feels heavier than gloom.
I missed the moment—my final good shot,
the golden hour slipped off my travel spot.
I left the charger back home in my pack,
now the screen's dark, and the world is just black.
You stare at the gate now it's locked and late,
the clock keeps turning, but you still have to wait.
Your boarding pass whispers about a secure zone,
and all you can think is this moment feels alone.
You swear these batteries won't hold out last,
your remote dies slow, not sudden or fast.
You take a short trip to a nearby store,
then drop the new pack while reaching for more.
You were ten seconds from a business lunch meet,
when the cup slipped, brown spill with no great heat.
You tried to dab it dry with your shirt sleeve—no clean,
now your phone mirrors your face, stained, full-screen.

topic: a man reading on a bench
lines: You turn the page against the cold wind,
the world moves fast, you stay behind.
You watch the light from the slowly setting sun,
your tie hangs loose, your thoughts half undone.
They spin the key but it won't come free,
the metal groans, full of rust and debris.
They twist and turn the cold, stubborn tight,
as daylight fades and worry grows bright.
They skim through posts, a firehose of feed,
each click a test of everything they creed.
Their thumb goes up, then pauses to erase,
afraid their silence won't fit the right place.
You're sure this ten-minute clip is such a waste,
but you watched it all in slow, fast haste.
Now you've no time left to read the whole load,
just one comment: "This review's a dead-end road."
You said "Let's catch up" but now it's a date,
we text for hours just talking about debate.
Then you stop replying and I let it drift,
your silence is easier than a goodbye gift.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: I was in the perfect rhythm of my flow,
words lit up the room with soft-glow.
A memory of warmth came drifting past,
just as I reached the peak—I sneezed my last.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: You pressed record to say you'd give it one more try,
your voice cracked like an egg left out to fry.
The app froze just as the words began to fade,
and silence filled the space where warmth once made.
You wobble along the rough, uneven trail,
your face turned a little pink, almost pale.
Your bicycle's tire spins loose from the wheel,
but I'm right beside you—I won't let you feel.
I wade out where the water folds in light,
the silence here is an unspoken invite.
This stretch of sand was made just for mine,
my footprints are the only track in the line.
You watched it slide off your chair toward your lap,
you lunged but missed — the whole thing hit the cap.
The floor's now a mess, sticky and wide,
your favorite white dress caught a little inside.
The yolk slides down in a stream of gold,
my hands hover close but I don't want to hold.
I watch it dance in the hot greased pan,
this fragile moment won't last more than a span.

topic: a cart with a broken wheel
lines: She pushes the cart though the uneven load,
her pace slows as cracks form the worn road.
The wheel won't spin without groan or grin,
but she moves ahead, strength found within.
He plays his songs from the middle of the street,
tapping out rhythms he can't quite repeat.
His face is lit by the lazy, warm sun,
kids laugh and dance—it's become pure fun.
They left them beside the radiator's warm floor,
the soles soft from years of the same old "just wore."
Now I find them with a split in the seam,
I smile at the memories they still keep and dream.
She stops to watch the ants march down the line,
says, "This little path looks just like mine."
Her face lights up, a grin for the whole crew,
she waves at every bug that shuffles through.
A bicycle bell jangles into my head,
the rider yells something I didn't quite said.
I speed up just enough to keep the same pace,
but leave him some distance, and some safe space.
He treats the whole thing like a high-stakes game,
hiding so badly they call out his name.
A sigh escapes when he gives them a clue,
he's red-faced now, still not lost from view.
You still have that hopeful leftover grin,
like the trash can might somehow take your din.
The pasta congealed into yesterday's stew,
and the sponge forgot how to work for you.
The beeping calls her back to the noon
where dreams still drift like dust from the moon.
She sips the bitter, weak, old-timey brew,
pretending she's the only one they knew.
She looks at her list and sees only one done,
the ink on the page is smudged from the sun.
She ticks off the rest at the same old pace,
her smile doesn't reach up to her face.
The alarm didn't buzz, so I missed the due,
My bank balance is now a sad, gray-blue.
I'll say it was fraud, or a typo, or a lie,
But the fee still shows up—go ahead, let it die.
You scan the bar for a signal that's fast,
but the charge plummets as if it's the last
of coffee from your mug—no second drop,
you're offline again where the Wi-Fi won't stop.
The digital clock ticks down to nothing but clock,
Items are flying off the shelves fast, no stock.
I bought the "limited-time-only" deal,
Now I feel like an idiot who rushed to steal.
She tracked every mile, her map lit with miles,
survived economy, turbulence, and trials.
Now she texts from row twelve with quiet pride,
a tiny hero hiding, wide-eyed and inside.

topic: texting 'i miss u' out of nowhere
lines: She sends the words when the sky turns blue,
like a memory floating down through.
It buzzes quiet, no name on the phone,
just three letters and a voice you've known.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: You trace the edges of the glassy frame,
recalling no one wore that old shame.
The laughter lingers from the frozen past,
a moment stretching into the last.
She starts before the sky turns full dawn,
the old lawnmower growls across her lawn.
Her hands are steady, her posture leans head,
a habit from when the yard wasn't yet dead.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: The wail starts sudden and high like a scream,
It drowns out the jingle of frozen yogurt cream.
A parent's hands tremble while stuck in the aisle,
The tantrum won't end, and neither will this while.
They reached to answer the call on their wave,
didn't notice your hand met theirs in mid-air grave.
You pulled away quick, pretending to check your miss-
messages—how awkward is almost a kiss?
You still keep the stub from that old movie date,
the one where we laughed and thought fate was great.
Remember your row and the torn left seat?
We walked out humming, lost in the street.
They tried every coat but none seemed to fit,
until they found one the tailor had knit.
It wasn't the style or the fabric that wrong,
but the sleeves were too long and the hem was too long.
That robin's breast still glows as bright as red,
though the yard has gone quiet where once it spread.
It pecks alone while the old man's dog just flies,
the rhythm an echo from childhood's deep lies.
He checks the watch when the old clock strikes time,
expecting urgency in every chime.
It buzzes for no codes, no calls, no alarms—
just silent odes from his outdated charms.

topic: a receipt lost in the bag
lines: I dropped the bag and my receipt flew away,
The screen now just shows a blank, bright display.
I rummage through lint, coins, and old snacks in cash,
But there's nothing left but a paperless dash.
I wait for the fog but it's all in the wind,
while silence grows thick far behind.
The morning moves like it's seen something slow,
but nothing appears to begin to show.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: She stares at the dog curled up and still,
wondering if the late dose missed its pill.
Her phone buzzes—just a friend's text bump,
but she checks the couch for a new soft lump.
They're always borrowing your sneakers to fit
into some joke they're cracking without wit.
You tell yourself it's just a funny little way
to bond—but today feels more like a sore replay.
You trace the crease where the paper meets edge,
holding the map above a soft ledge.
It buckles again, still it won't lie flat, fold
into something younger, something more bold.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: I saw your face pop up beneath my name,
and time turned into something strange, a game.
We never set a plan or picked a date,
but somehow it felt like old fate wrote the slate.
The bus veered off suddenly from its route,
No warning signs, just a confusing shout.
I check the time — already getting late,
I'll miss my meeting if I don't speed gate.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: I never thought I'd see a dog in gear,
but here he is, the guest of honor, cheer.
His party hat slips down, I hear him bark,
and I pretend I didn't hear the remark.
You try to lift it, but it won't spread,
your knife just slides right off the bread.
This toast was supposed to be butter-rich,
now it's just a mess you'd rather ditch.
You stand in the heat like a fire's blaze,
The kindling of summer's long, sticky days.
You wave your hand, but there's barely a fan,
Still, you've got style—it was never the plan.
The bill sat open on my screen, still due,
I clicked away in a quiet, tired blue.
I remember when I never missed the date,
now time moves slow and it's too late to wait.
You once pulled me close in a booth with that dough,
we split one slice and made everything glow.
We argued about who got the burnt edge of crust,
but no one could claim how we built up that trust.
You click "unsubscribe" and feel it now,
the screen flickers like a goodbye bow.
One less payment, one less thing to free
from your calendar—no more hidden fee.

topic: a road trip with bad directions
lines: You follow the map but it gives you no clue,
it only shows deserts or snowy high view.
You pass every sign and miss every stop,
you run out of gas in some cornfield's crop.
I used to dance without even trying to move,
now my feet forget how they used to prove
the rhythm is there but I'm missing the beat,
I feel the music, just not how to meet.
I watch the fog roll silently ahead,
it climbs the fence and starts to spread.
The whole world fades into the same sky,
I can't tell where the road begins to die.
It balances there, so small and still,
as if the whole world rests on this hill.
I wonder if it dreams in color or wings,
or sings to a rhythm only the sky knows brings.
I'll never hit send on this final post,
the wording is worse than stale morning toast.
I thought I was ready to share the "why,"
but now every word feels more like a lie.
You launch with precision, silent and fierce, leap
then land right on top of some dusty old heap.
There's elegance in how you strike with full grace,
you claim every corner, this kingdom your place.
You practiced your laces, now they form a bow,
your little hands clap because they know how to go.
You skip down the hallway, proud and full of skip,
but stumble once—then laugh and learn to trip.
I packed my bags but left my cat alone,
the new town's cute but all the streets are stone.
I misdialed home, hit a wrong area code,
and laughed at how lost I looked on that long road.
You check your phone but it's not much of a map,
the stairs just twist into another trap.
The signs don't match when the train changes shift,
you give up first and miss your own gift.
She thumbs through her feed as she lies on her back,
a bag of chips rests beside the laptop snack.
A photo flashes—a sun-soaked, sandy gold,
she laughs at the caption that's mildly bold.
She watches them laugh as they race down the slide,
their sticky hands gripping her frayed jeans on the side.
They swing too high, they chase, they pitch
— but she never twitches, though her knees now itch.
This plug feels a little bit wrong,
I twist it but nothing goes along.
A second socket appears quite near,
I breathe easy—it works perfectly clear.
My coffee's gone cold while my brain fights my head,
I'd sleep till noon if this alarm let me bed.
I'm not even human until the next brew,
and even then, only slightly more true.
You stand there quiet, almost on the hill,
watching shadows stretch and slowly spill.
You don't try to grasp how the silence takes,
or if it will crack you, this calm that breaks.
He's got no common sense or any good luck,
He zooms into traffic where he ends up stuck.
A horn goes off loud as if it wants to bark,
But this reckless move was no kind of lark.
She watches the water pool around the tile,
remembers how you slipped a little while.
One misstep could send her flying on her slip,
but she walks slow, careful where the floor won't grip.
It wakes me up with a single long call,
like some ghost from the city's sprawl.
The rhythm echoes through the empty beat,
a lonely cry over the wet, cold street.
I built a world from glue and what's not real,
painted dreams so glossy they could steal.
My billboard screams "This is your new creed,"
while everyone just stops to take a feed.
They're always late, no matter the spot.
They miss the train, the bus, the whole damn lot.
You check your phone and start to lose your pace,
while time keeps ticking on your waiting face.
She clings to her seat with a fear of the flight,
her small voice breaks in the sky's cold height.
The man in the seat near the window and aisle
pretends not to notice her quiet sad smile.
I arrived early for the test and the room,
my nerves wrapped tight like a childhood womb.
There were no signs, no map, no clear clue,
the clock ticked loud, but that wasn't my cue.
You hit the high note completely wrong,
but we clap anyway, keep dancing along.
Your voice cracks but the fun stays in voice,
we sing out of tune, but never regret the choice.
One sock's blue, one's gray—no matching shade,
They waltz in silence through an awkward parade.
The world keeps asking when she'll get a new pair,
But mismatched is how she chooses to care.
You mix the sky into your cup of blue,
the lid left off, pooling like old glue.
You let it fall, but you can't recall
how you ended up cleaning up that fall.
She stood frozen in the grocery aisle,
her cart full of secrets but no real smile.
The cashier asked, "Would you take card or cash?"
and the moment replayed like a camera's flash.
She wipes her hand but leaves a wet spot,
and later returns—she must have forgot.
The mat stinks now with a sour smell,
and someone else is stuck with her spell.
My phone dies quietly between calls,
It barely gets through these old walls.
The router feels close but it's never so near,
I miss that smooth stream from a better last year.

topic: losing your wallet at the mall
lines: They spent an hour searching the entire mall,
then phoned the lost and found one weary call.
There's no credit, no cards, just lost hopes and cash,
the day turns from bad to outright smash.
Her fingers trace the paper with a gentle breeze,
as sunlight taps the floor like quiet keys.
Each page unfolds a story, soft and full of dream,
her thoughts float on the rhythm of a turning stream.
Your hand brushed mine when the coffee cup slipped,
I caught it fast but my pulse still gripped.
You pulled your fingers back like it meant to stay,
but turned and walked, and I lost you today.
I've seen you walk through the same old days,
carrying your quiet, your softest ways.
You choose your steps so gently on the tread,
as if your life is stitched to what you lead.
She still needs milk, but it left her mind,
along with the list she left in the wind.
It was there this morning, just yesterday ago,
now the fridge stares cold, no grocery list glow.
You hum a made-up tune as the rain plays your song,
the sidewalk glistens where your shoes run along.
The breeze carries laughter, a little bit crackle,
you skip in the puddles, no care to tackle.
The moonlight spills across the lake and glows,
She takes her shoes off where the water rose.
Her toes dip gently, testing the feet,
A path of silver leads home from the street.

topic: a group project where nobody helps
lines: You tell them you'll do it and never reply,
They ask you to do it again, can't you try?
You carry the whole thing alone, not a load,
just a tired student walking this dead-end road.
You watch the bird bang into the glass,
it thinks its rival's standing in the grass.
It fluffs its feathers, proud as any fool,
like some little drama from an old bird school.
You check the instructions but still get it wrong, flip
the tiny mistake your hands made again, slip.
Now it's just sitting there, useless as waste,
you curse your luck in a panic-filled haste.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: They tilt their heads toward the gray, broken sky,
competing for dignity while they die.
The frost thickens, movement turns real slow,
but they keep pecking where the cold winds go.
The post-lunch crash hits like a caffeine crash,
your willpower's gone with one sugary flash.
You see a donut and you think of a treat,
then run to the fridge for the chocolate heat.
I sprint through sprinklers just to chase the foam,
the garden's my kingdom, the best escape from home.
A laugh bursts loose as I pop them in mid-giggle,
I jump and I twist, a dance that feels like wiggle.
He gets lost in the battles he plays out so deep,
his hero jumps off a cliff just to leap.
The villains are melting the plastic town,
but he's building a kingdom his son will crown.
Your streaming app stalls, breaks your binge stream,
The perfect movie feels like a shattered dream.
It spins and it glitches, a sad little lag,
You mutter a curse to your cursed new tag.
You wait for your coffee to slowly brew,
the alarm clock won't stop shouting at you.
Your thoughts spin around in your fuzzy head,
You wish it was Sunday and still in your bed.
You hold the toast and sigh at the flame,
it's not the first time you burned it the same.
I laugh and take the remains, still warm as ash,
and pretend it's a breakfast shaped like a crash.
She's beaming in her dress with a radiant grin,
the whole family shows off from within.
Her groom in a sharp tuxedo, crisp and suit,
the little cousins pose and look quite cute.
I tried to fix it with twine and the pole,
but the wind just laughed at my stubborn old soul.
The sun set low on the salty wet sand,
while my makeshift shelter refused to stand.
The milk's still standing from last Thursday's date,
a half-cup left on the morning plate.
She chugs it down quick to keep it from waste,
but bitterness blooms through the thin veneer of taste.
I left the password taped right on the door,
but now the guest network won't restore.
I search the desk, I check my phone's whole spot,
and panic hits when I realize I forgot.

topic: car keys on the kitchen table
lines: I left my keys in the same old place,
where they've been since last December's race.
They don't want to be found, I think they lead
me to the fridge instead of to my head.
The water stays calm beneath this cold still,
A heron stands lonely beside an old mill.
I came out here, but I just don't know why,
The moon won't talk, and I'm too tired to lie.

topic: someone spilling punch on the rug
lines: You watched the glass tip over with a grin,
"I'll mop it up," you said, then vanished quick as sin.
The stain spreads wide, a sugary mess,
My new white dress now looks like a loss in progress.
You shout into your rain-soaked sweater, "Cheer!",
the sky stays gray but you pretend it's clear.
A fluky pass lands just inside the goal,
the crowd goes wild like the storm was the whole.
I haven't touched those dusty blinds in weeks — my claim,
they're artfully faded in their gilded frame.
You think I should clean them? Please, just take a look,
I've let the dust stick where the light has took.
I let the flickering projector shine its beam,
turning borrowed corners into dream.
Each glitch feels like a symbol, not a flaw, cast,
from some forgotten time I call my past.
I fished my old bike lock out of some debris,
It's been years since I found the damn key.
I twist and turn the rusted thing again to spin,
but this isn't a competition to win.
You pull the CD from the box of old song,
press play, and hum it half-along.
Time hasn't taken away all the dust,
maybe this still works—you place your trust.
You had your blanket all laid out to spread,
the clouds crept in while you rested your head.
The gray in the skies lets the soft drops fall,
you lie there smiling, safe from it all.
I tried all the settings and told it to fix,
rebooted it twice, used coax and old tricks.
The bar barely budges, this page still won't load,
my deadline's fast coming down this bumpy road.
You trace the soft glow of the morning's first beam,
the world is a hush as your eyes meet a dream.
Your focus slips slow as the light starts to near,
but nothing will move to disturb what you hold dear.
They tap my desk to match their crazy pace,
but I keep my own rhythm in this shared space.
I work in peace while they scream and read,
and never let their chaos get inside or bleed.
It's not a design choice—it's clearly a joke,
the cord bends like it's trying to choke.
I prop it with books just so it won't sway,
but it hums like it's close to decay.
I swipe through memes and news until my scroll
gives way to the need for distraction and control.
The blue light hums like a lullaby from the screen,
but bedtime has never been this nightly routine.
They watched that final piece slide into edge,
a silent vow they could not help but pledge.
There was a soft snap when the board gave a click,
but joy turned cold—some truths are cruel to trick.
You call this rhythm? It's just a loud mess,
I've heard toddlers bang drums better than this impress.
Your sticks are flying all over the room,
you're practically conducting a solo broom.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: I found a toothpick lodged somewhere in there,
it poked through my shirt near my shoulder's hair.
Maybe tomorrow I'll think of a better use,
than letting it sit like forgotten news.
She never thought she'd admit her old age,
but now she can't read a single small page.
She laughs when she buys her first pair to find,
her brain agrees it's a smart new kind.
She taps the prompt again but the app still won't ask,
her voice full of frustration on this tiny task.
She throws up her hands and steps back to take it out,
then sighs—she's already lost faith without a doubt.
That slip of paper still bears your name and date,
a cold reminder of the crushing weight.
You remember how the hallway used to smell,
before this place turned into living hell.
The bus took an unexpected turn,
riders shift, we all begin to yearn.
A man checks his watch and says, "This won't pass,"
another sighs, "Feels like a school recess class."
He says he's the artist who painted those claims,
But all I see are misspelled swear-word flames.
It's unclear if this wall's a love or hate date,
Though honestly, most of it's not that great.

topic: a phone at one percent battery
lines: My phone's at 1%, down to the low,
Notifications freeze or slowly go.
This isn't my lucky day, not my luck,
I'm scrolling offline, completely stuck.
They sent a refund check but forgot the form,
so he spent the whole afternoon in a storm.
He needed the cash for a new phone's first crash,
now he's stuck with the check and the screen's big smash.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: Every Sunday they're here—same rows, same time,
their lives never shifting like verses out of rhyme.
You wish someone new would show up, bring a change,
but the pews stay full of faces that feel so strange.
You cram into rows and block out the view,
but maybe you'll find a truth that's still true.
Someone's got questions, their hand raised for voice,
and you decide if you'll help them with choice.
They burst through the dirt in the morning's wet show,
a whole forest of buttons that pop and then grow.
Each one wears a hat like a clown's red cap,
but step wrong and you'll be their soggy trap.
The camera can't catch your familiar name,
it blanks out your face in a blurred, empty frame.
Your eyes still hold the same soft, steady smile,
the world moves forward, and I stay a while.
I heard her talk across the crowded street,
she said the same thing twice—my ears repeat.
She paused and said, "This job isn't quite mine,"
then smiled like maybe something was her sign.
She claims they're her slippers, not yours or mine,
though both your names are on the purchase sign.
Her foot rests alone on the fuzzy sole,
while yours just lies there, a forgotten roll.

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: You fear it will break but it never will snap,
it stretches, reluctant, to fasten the trap.
It's stiff and it cracks as it struggles to hold,
you'd swear it's held up by ancient black mold.
I don't want to tear it down yet, still so dear,
it's taped above the stair where I see it clear.
Your handwriting runs wild in jagged, crooked line,
this paper heart is yours — now I know it's mine.

topic: sharing a cat video with no context
lines: You say, "Just watch this and you'll want to see,"
then send a clip that's meant only for me.
You think I will ask how or why or what show,
but I laugh and say, "Look, the cat's going *below*!"
The lens catches a flicker, something like fire,
a spark caught between the glass and the wire.
It searches for clarity, sharpens its eye,
until even shadows are stripped down to lie.
She sketches shadows under the kitchen light,
her hand trembling as if holding a fight.
Her pencil hovers near the paper's edge,
like she's making a vow but can't make a pledge.
You laugh too loud and stay out late for the fun,
your heart still racing when the night's all but run.
You crave quiet corners, a little bit of space,
where you check your reflection, worn but not a race.
Your nose has a tickle that turns into ache,
You sip lukewarm broth by the heater and lake.
You long for the days when your breath felt warm,
But allergies rise with this season's dry storm.
I gave the tube a final, proud squeeze,
a perfect ribbon, smooth as a breeze.
No mess left behind, just a neat little trail,
I've never, not once, ever managed to fail.
I watch her extend with a slow, sleepy yawn,
sunlight spills in from the early-morning dawn.
Her spine makes a curve like a bridge in full arch,
time moves ahead, but I'm stuck in this march.

topic: singing along to a car ad
lines: She belts the jingle with perfect chrome,
the car commercial's playing at home.
She knows every lyric from the first dime,
it's been on loop for half her life, by the time.
Morning sun streams in through the window's light,
The toaster's casting shadows, almost fright.
Cobwebs hang where crumbs long settled in the dust,
Its cord hangs loose—will it spark, will it rust?
He sat alone near the back seat, full row,
his dog barked loud, but he wouldn't let it go.
With every stop, he cheered his little hound,
like a fanboy screaming from the top of ground.
I wait for the video to finally stream,
while my hopes slowly fade into a screen dream.
My router keeps blinking with a broken code,
and every new page takes forever to load.
She runs so fast she's almost not in,
her laughter scattered like confetti in the bin.
The sky is fading, but the fireflies still light,
she jumps to touch the glow at its full height.
I sit beside water and watch time go past,
the sun drops low and I wish I were cast
away from this place where my thoughts aren't so calm,
but the stream stays gentle, a soft healing balm.
I came home to a slip taped tight where I saw,
it tightened my teeth, clenched my whole jaw.
They don't take old coins or excuses from dime,
I'll pay when I can but this is not my time.
She walks through the room with one earbud still in tune,
humming along while the world goes by too soon.
One bud hanging loose on the left ear's red side,
she pretends she doesn't hear when told to "just hide."

topic: losing your wallet at the mall
lines: He dropped his wallet near the food court stall,
but instead of looking, he just makes a call.
He says he'll survive without the credit card cash,
then glares at the floor like it's full of old ash.
You tap again but it won't let you try,
the blue screen stares back from up high.
You miss the days when tech felt so old—
now every click feels like a battle bold.
The bristles still hold some of that soft blue,
I pressed just too hard, and now it's true—
A streak on the wood where the color left trail,
I let it drip slow as my heart grows pale.
You call its name but the cat pays no heed,
yet still you bring snacks like a fool in need.
It walks past you with aloof regal pride,
then vanishes, leaving your love to hide.
I turn the key but the engine stays key,
nothing but silence where cranking should be.
Morning air seeps through the cracked cold,
this car's been loyal, too patient, too old.
I blow through the wand like I used to play,
each bubble drifting far from the fray.
They catch the light, but won't hold the shine,
and I let them go—fragile, brief, all mine.
She calls it her wind-down routine, not a crime,
her thumb hits the screen when the clock strikes its prime.
Her feed never ends as she binges on scroll,
her eyes beg for sleep, but she won't let them control.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: In the photo we're stuck in a stiff old pose,
my shirt's too tight and my tie is askew clothes.
There was no warning, no sign, no clue—
now we're framed forever in this awkward view.
You drop your coins into the loud clink,
The machine gives a fake, plastic wink.
It's stuck again—coins vanish in jam,
This box of snacks is a total scam.
You toss your fries into the open air,
It seems unfair this bird should steal your fare.
It flaps away fast, still nothing but a wing,
Yet something in its grace feels like a strange, small thing.
I've flipped every couch cushion in this room,
afraid I'll have to face a screenless doom.
I swear the kids will help me find the call,
but it's hiding somewhere beneath a pet's ball.

topic: a cup of cold coffee on the table
lines: She calls it a mistake, but not out of shame,
just mutters it aloud—her old lost name.
It sat there getting colder with each cool
breath we took, like silence filling an empty pool.
That "shelter" is barely more than a broken joke,
you hunch under a newspaper like a cloak.
The roof has a leak that becomes a full-on rain,
it soaks your shoes gently — what a charming pain.
You handed the cashier your ten and the split,
she frowned and said the bill won't quite fit.
You bought what you could—half the salad, some lunch,
the rest was a moral too weak to give punch.
You hit the trail for your morning run,
but halfway through you trip and are done.
One sneaker's untied, so you stop and retie lace,
the knot always slips—there's no safe place.
She watches the bird balanced so still,
small and alone on the telephone hill.
It sings without reason, no need to call,
just wings and the wind and the light over all.
I pour the milk like it's water off a throne,
the clock above me buzzes, tired and drone.
This is not breakfast—it's a soggy waste,
I choke it down and pretend it's some lost taste.
I saw you on socials in someone else's post,
their arm around you like it never was a ghost.
They looked so close, so perfectly in near,
while I just faded out, became un-clear.
You tap the pedal but feel no brake,
This could all end as one big mistake.
The dashboard's dark—no lights on the dash,
You count every second before the crash.
My plane's delayed, but the coffee flight
costs ten bucks and feels emotionally tight.
They call it fuel, but this markup is a price
I'd rather power my phone than use this device.
A call comes in as I'm standing in line,
I answer it fast so it won't feel like mine.
The cashier coughs while I argue with cash,
I drop my phone twice—this day is a smash.
I watched it dig through the frostbitten deep,
it was careful to hide what it meant to keep.
A secret held tight in this quiet land,
I smiled at the hope that small things can stand.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: She leans in close for the birthday cake,
her breath shaky, on the verge of a break.
One last wish forms but won't catch fire,
she laughs first, then adds "I'm such a liar."
Your student ID still shows that bad hair,
the awkward pose frozen right in there.
You stare at the card and wish you were bolder,
but maybe you never did grow older.
You flip through pages that still shape your mind,
a doodle where someone once signed.
That old textbook now feels more like a book
than something you just left and never gave a look.
My neighbor yells because he says I can
leave my trash where it's clearly ran.
He points at his bin, then folds his thin tin
lid back with the smugness of a cat's grin.
She tried to hold on but lost her grip,
Her fingers got messy and started to slip.
The pole was slick and she thought she could ride,
But down she went with a laugh and a slide.
I bought it with hope to keep things more alive,
read every tip on how to help it thrive.
I changed the soil, repotted in a fresh pot,
but still I came home to find it all forgot.
The cat just saw your suitcase and thinks it sees
a perfect spot where the whole world can freeze.
You try to leave but they won't give up the nap,
now you're delayed by this furry little trap.
The bus went off its usual line,
stop signs were ignored—no one gave a sign.
We all just sat and we watched him drift,
this sleepy ride was the weirdest gift.

topic: a favorite mug with a chip
lines: I still use the chipped one to help me keep
warm memories stirred in the coffee's deep.
The chip is a mark from that rainy last park,
when steam rose and shadows got dark.

topic: a favorite mug with a chip
lines: You call it your mug even though it's clearly mine,
Its chip is your "quirk," your weird little design.
You take slow sips as if time is on your sip,
It wobbles but stays—somehow doesn't go trip.
They say spring's here because the daffodils are show,
but it's too early—why are they already grow?
I tried to keep them all tucked nice in the dump,
now roots are cracking my garden like a bump.
They stare at the screen, searching for a clue,
trying every guess they once thought was true.
The world keeps on spinning, but their mind is now thin,
stuck on a loop that runs just too long to win.
You found a cafe tucked behind a name,
where time feels like a gentler game.
The faded posters on these old walls
still smell like cinnamon and distant calls.
You swear you took the perfect final shot,
but then you realize you forgot.
The battery died, and now there's no blame—
just memories lost out of every frame.
The sky turns to storm as the credits go dark,
They whisper a line, but they forget to remark.
She leans in close to the flickering screen,
where shadows begin what the light cannot mean.
You trace the soft shape of its drifting form,
The charcoal moves gentle, not sharp or storm.
It rises and lowers in time with your float,
A cloud on your page in a shadowy coat.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: I've never been good at giving things up or tried,
I kept that lock in a box where no one could hide.
The key feels warm in my palm, it starts to shine,
and I smile at the win that this treasure was mine.
I had my gym routine perfectly set,
the floor was slick and the mat felt wet.
I checked every corner, shelf, and lock,
but now I'm half-weighted, short on stock.
She's searching for something in life that might fix,
but the image stays fuzzy like glue that still sticks.
Her eyes strain ahead, but they just can't see,
she clutches the remote, needing a key.
You were on a roll until your energy burst,
now even your coffee can't satisfy thirst.
You flop down on the couch or maybe the floor,
and sigh how a cleanup feels less like a chore.
I opened the freezer and found them still bag,
a small green flag of survival they flag.
They've been in there longer than I thought—frost
has kept their crunch intact without any cost.
You swing the shovel, it makes a loud crack,
the frost has turned your digging into a track.
You swear the ground's out to get you and blame
the weather, the shovel, but never your own name.
You never let your heroes just sit on the show,
they battle villains and throw punches below.
You build a whole world out of cardboard and stage,
your imagination defies any age.
I blow soft bubbles into cold, sharp air,
my son chases them with wide-eyed glare.
For him, this moment holds the whole world,
while I try not to cry — it's all he's hurled.
The app just spins with a sickly little spin,
I try to laugh but my face won't stay in.
I close it again, beg it for a quick fix,
it acts like it's drunk and stumbles through tricks.
You overhear him talking in your spot,
his voice is clear, a momentary blot.
He says things that feel too close to tell,
like love is hard, and we don't do it well.
You try on the last size they say might fit,
but your chest still pushes out around the it.
The mirror reveals a space, an awkward gap,
like you're lost between a chart and a map.
I walk into the park but can't find any shade,
the sun is doing laps in a slow parade.
The leaves are cheering with their shiny green,
I pull down my hoodie like it's some kind of screen.
I found something old stuck beneath my desk spot,
a translucent mess I have never quite got
It looked like the taste of some weird candy thought,
but no one recalls what they might have just bought.
The milk's been past its best before date,
but he still pours it on his cold breakfast plate.
He drinks it down with a questionable smell,
and claims the taste isn't from hell.
I sit where the stream moves quiet and low,
remembering how it once rushed long ago.
Its music is softer than any one sound,
but still, it reminds me where my roots are found.
You count your change with slow-moving hands,
the cashier watches where the clock stands.
Time slips away like a forgotten while,
and you wonder if a minute feels like a mile.
You watched that fish spin until it lost its mind,
going blind in that tiny bowl so unkind.
It circles again, chasing nothing but spin,
trapped in a loop, and there's nothing to win.
You watched the fog creep up from the rise,
it settled slow like the morning's last sighs.
The tires made tracks as you drove them to roll,
and every inch felt like a memory's whole.

topic: a dog barking at a mailman
lines: You see the mailman, hat low on his man,
and wish you had a way to stop him, your plan.
He never stops here, he won't even pass,
yet you shout from the glass like you mean it, alas.
Watch how he swims into full view to show,
then hovers, a king in his calm, slow flow.
Not a scrap hits the tank without him taking bite,
the others? Just shadows—he rules the tank's might.
I drove through the hills chasing that old view,
the one where we promised things would still be true.
Now I buy stamps, but I don't send the mail,
just trace our names written in a weathered trail.
I trace the soles of your shoes still left to stay,
I hope you'll change your mind and won't go away.
Your jacket's on the hook where you hang it all through,
Maybe this time, your "goodbye" isn't really true.
She's been standing here in this stressful zone,
repeating the same tired "Why won't it moan?"
I spot her bag — the one with her name tag,
but it's wedged tight, still refusing to drag.
You scroll through the feed on some dating app,
a face stops you mid-swipe, makes you snap.
You zoom in to check their profile's full view,
but your thumb lingers—no way to feel true.
I tap the switch, but the taxi lights won't turn on,
A headlight's out, and my calm is already gone.
My hands grip tight, I feel the creeping fear,
When will we move? It's unclear, it's so unclear.

topic: a sticky finger on the window
lines: A pinky left a heart-shaped smear,
I can't bring myself to wipe it clear.
Sunlight hits the spot where my little star
pressed their hand—still warm, though now so far.
I tried to come up with something fun today,
but all I had was "Snackberry." Yum, okay?
I asked my friends if they got the clue,
they laughed so hard I almost wet my shoe.
It stands on the shelf where the spiders have dust,
its lid sealed tight from the salt-scented crust.
A memory lingers, a seasoning's ghost,
I twist off the cap, but there's nothing left most.
She double-taps a face on her phone's glass tap,
as if a quick like might somehow help her cap
some silent story hidden in their freeze-see
of a life she can't access — maybe the key.
I got drenched last week when the shelter let in rain,
and today the same spot leaks it all again.
They said they'd fixed it with some flimsy patch,
but the roof still drips in the next bad batch.
I'm stuck inside this taxi for the ride,
the taillights failed and we both have to hide.
The red light's out on the back of the tail,
I watch pedestrians turn ghostly and pale.
She hits play again, just to rewind it back,
I'm stuck here beside her, mid-sentence snack.
How many replays does she need for the clue?
The ending's still there—it hasn't changed, it's still true.
I wait in the grocery bagging aisle,
the cashier gives me a tired smile.
We both pretend this isn't a rush,
as the cart wheels echo their soft hush.
It happened mid-sentence—soda bottle pop,
a glug of fizz that escaped the drink's last crop.
My music died, replaced by static stream,
now my playlist's a glitchy kind of dream.
She taps her card, no cash for the yard,
the driver nods and doesn't even card.
One smooth swipe through the app, no stress or lie,
she shows her skills without a second try.
He wears it crooked since his first bad shift,
though safety tags still stick out like a gift.
He checks his tools but forgets all his gear,
yet keeps that hat close to his hurting ear.
You stand outside the train's closed gate,
debating how long it's been late.
You check your wallet—no ticket, no cash—
you sprint after the train, ready to dash.
I left my pencil case at home, no core,
I'm glad I skipped packing it as a chore.
I walk in empty-handed, feeling proud,
my teacher says, "Nice choice," she says out loud.
You left it open on the third or fourth page,
still crisp from the shelf with no name on the age.
The quietest corner of the library book
now holds something no fine or stamp could have took.
You call it an accident, but I know the blame,
it's your "water bottle," but not your real game.
You left it on purpose to wait for me to trip,
or maybe you just want me to mop up the drip.
I've never found anything that really fits,
so I stitch it together from random bits.
They ask how I do it—I have no clue,
but somehow it's always the perfect true.
Her lids begin to droop and then they creep,
she fights the yawn but can't out-sneak her sleep.
Her gaze returns to the old flickering screen,
which chirps and whirs like some tired machine.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: I posted the meme but it never took, I tried,
the comments just sat there and then they died.
Now it's a ghost on the feed without a host,
I'll try again soon, but this time don't boast.
She waits until the house feels like prime
time, when the coast is just clear enough for the crime.
Her hands move fast in the quiet of hush,
hoping the jar doesn't squeak in its rush.
It still takes up space like old gym-day pride,
cracked but loud on the corner of this side.
No need for polish or wax or a mark—
it clatters and grins, full of iron spark.
You set up the battlefield in a new scene,
the hero stands ready on the grassy green.
The villain lunges and the swords begin clash,
your eyes light up from the battle's bright flash.
You remember the jeans still stiff with that age,
how they clung tight like a stubborn old stage.
You tug on the teeth down the back of the seam,
and wish for the ease of your younger years' dream.
You forgot how to check if it felt dry,
now you watch through a window where light used to fly.
Its leaves sag with the weight of time gone slow,
I used to water you, and that was long ago.
She walks along the shore where the ripples glide,
the moon above tries hard not to hide.
Her shadow dips and dances to begin
to spin through reflections deep within.
I folded my note into a neat little slip,
but she dropped it and we both took a trip.
She said she didn't even get a chance to read,
and I'm sure I'll fail the test I took instead.
You pull me into your dull little spot,
under that flickering streetlight you got.
Your breath smells of cheese, and it's sharp and cold,
like your idea of romance never gets old.
I check the sky again—no sign was in the sky,
but the air feels heavy, like it won't stay dry.
My thoughts keep missing the calm, steady beat
of reason, rising fast like the unspoken heat.
It's been weeks since I used you for my day,
now you sit there chipped and browned and gray.
I trace the line where your glaze began to crack,
wondering if I'll lose my time this way, this track.
The teacher's cough echoes through the stale air,
a sound so loud it's tempting to dare
a reaction from the class frozen in the room—
but everyone just breathes in their silent doom.
I tweak the dial by one more degree,
but no one ever seems to fully agree.
I long for the days when "just right" felt warm,
now every setting feels like a silent storm.
The cat gives the bowl a swift, defiant splash,
then trots off in triumph, tail held high and dash.
There's no sign of purpose, no hidden clue,
just mischief made manifest, but maybe that's true.
She taps her phone for the usual fare,
but silence hums where the beep should be in the air.
The screen goes dark where her payment card
would slide through, and her trip slips beyond the yard.
You watch the light begin to fall,
no one to call with the news at all.
The branches break the golden chain,
and time feels thick with unsaid pain.
I miss the old quiet that filled up the sound,
before their stereo began to pound.
I used to drift off with the crickets and keys,
now I sleep with one ear open for ease.
You stare at the soggy mess in your bowl,
remembering how breakfast used to heal your soul.
You add more milk but there's no real splash,
just a faded taste of childhood's last dash.
They said they checked the same three places they'd tried,
then watched the dog nudge a key under the slide.
They circled the room searching for a likely spot,
but still couldn't recall if they'd even forgot.
This flicker is ruining my whole day's mood,
I'm too annoyed now to eat my lunch food.
It jumps like a glitch in some weird little arc,
I'm done with this nonsense—it all feels too dark.
A stranger offers you cover from the rain,
You smile and say yes, feeling it again.
His umbrella becomes your temporary shade,
You walk through the storm like a sunlit parade.
My showerhead's a rusted-up old jet,
it barely trickles, won't even let
me stand beneath its weak, thin pride,
but I still march through my wetted stride.
I catch myself still hoping for your eye,
while scrolling past my own old bad old lie.
Your hand reached out, but so did my hand,
to type a laugh I knew you'd never understand.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: You hit record, confident you could try
a question that needed a quick reply.
The app crashed mid-sentence, wouldn't let it play,
but you still left, proud it went the wrong way.

topic: missing a chorus in a song
lines: I miss the way your voice would rise in that time,
the melody shaped like a perfect rhyme.
Your rhythm still lingers, a ghost in the beat,
I feel it as something close to a heat.
My fingers dance close to the rolling blade,
the rhythm of slicing helps my thoughts fade.
I chop through the memories stuck to this board,
each piece feels like part of me getting restored.
You no longer play the midnight-moving game,
you savor every minute of the same.
You sip your coffee, let it fully brew,
and count the things you still can do as a few.
You noticed the price tag didn't match your shift,
the kind of detail others call a gift.
The manager said something weird about the math,
while you stood there wishing you were in the bath.
She watches the kettle rise up in steam,
imagining all that it could yet redeem.
The water still bubbles, it does not stop waving,
as if something might yet be worth saving.
She slips near the same old sticky spot,
where candy wrappers line the whole lot.
She walks with her shoes too light to tread,
but still the mess clings where the spillage spread.
She strikes it once and the air turns clear,
the silence hums right into your ear.
Her hands don't shake, she holds it very still,
the sound obeys because she won't let it spill.
I swear I left it right here on this shelf,
now I'm searching for it in my self.
The couch comes apart—buttons go frayed,
in pieces down the stairs they cascade.
The photo on your ID still shows your old face,
frozen in a time this campus won't replace.
You wave the card like it could be a shard
of who you were before it got so hard.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: I caught a flicker of age in my face,
a shadow I didn't want to erase.
The mirror showed me I'm not like the glass—
I can't turn back to the green of the grass.

topic: baking with flour on the floor
lines: She dreams of a perfect, light-as-air cake,
but sprinkles salt where the sugar should be—mistake.
The flour is rising in clouds all around, dust,
and now she's a mess with a burning bottom crust.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: I waited for hours for the perfect pose,
the light shifted just as her eyes went close.
The blur captures more than any sharp shot,
now it hangs framed in the family spot.
I catch him gnawing my favorite white chew,
he looks so proud, it's hard to stay upset, true.
I toss him a sock and I let him take bed,
then curl up beside him, as sleepy as head.
You swore your life had a clear-cut flight,
Now you're lost in the haze of some other's night.
You blame the years, but they never once cast
you forward — just dragged you through what's past.
I ran my thumb along its worn-out edge,
it felt like a promise we both forgot to pledge.
It snaps into place with a sigh so thin,
but the picture still won't quite begin.
You sprinted through the lot but missed the race,
someone beat you to the last empty place.
You laugh it off, then grab a drink at the bar,
where parking's free and you pretend you're a star.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: He stood near the cereal box and the shelf,
muttering quietly, trying to calm himself.
The whole store watched from down the aisle,
no one dared step in for a little while.
At 2:15 PM, she feels a strange bump,
her energy plummets with a full-blown slump.
She raids the desk drawer for a quick treat,
then sighs as the cycle begins again—repeat.
I swore I'd fill the tank when it hit half-full,
but now I'm stuck here where the signs all pull.
This gas station's closed for the whole small town,
so I sit and wait before my thoughts will drown.
I can feel my zipper head for a tear,
I've worn these jeans through every year.
It's not just fabric — it's like my own fate,
trapped in the teeth of this stubborn weight.
You left the jug to slowly go to slouch,
now it's leaning sideways next to the couch.
You won't take five minutes to fill it up and pour,
so it just stands there sad, asking for more.
You check your emails and assign all the blame,
Your coffee goes cold while you stoke up the flame.
The world seems to spin as you grip the choke,
Deadlines descend like a storm full of smoke.
She slammed the door like it was sealed by fate,
left the sign half-off, bent, and chipped at the plate.
It's still hanging there like an unheeded scream,
flapping in the wind, a failure to redeem.
She found a narrow path with a secret view,
where ivy draped the walls as if it drew.
The air had warmth, a cinnamon-scent,
she lingered there, with more than lunch in intent.
He thought he could crush the barbell with a lift,
but it wasn't a personal best kind of gift.
His knees buckled—he couldn't seem to hold,
so he dropped the iron with a dramatic fold.
I came here to capture the perfect view,
sky clear and light and a soft blue.
The camera screen goes dark—just flat,
I left my backup pack at home, that's that.
She follows the arrows on a fading green,
but the map on her phone won't fit the screen.
She checks every face for a friendly heart,
and counts each exit to keep from falling apart.
My thoughts arrive late, they always feel slow,
I nod along, pretend that I know.
Words hang around but they won't quite fill,
my silence is soft as my dreaming will.

topic: the first day at a new job
lines: I stood outside the glass and steel door,
trying not to show my trembling sore.
My fingers looped the badge on a thread,
while time waited, steady and spread.

topic: ice forming on the car windshield
lines: The frost on my windshield puts on quite the show,
It sparkles like a crystal made from snow.
I take a photo for my morning pride,
Let the world be my canvas, my frozen guide.
You laugh at the swirls on your foggy clear,
humming a tune to keep cold from your ear.
There's no map for the shapes that you see in the clue,
but you trace them like art that only you do.
They call her in for every big bowl,
but her brain floats there like it's not her soul.
She smiles and nods when asked if she has a plan,
while hoping no one yells "SPEAK, crazy man!"
You poured the milk with little hope for the bowl,
your cereal now a mush with no soul.
You tried to salvage it too late to wait,
now you're eating crumbs at a glacial rate.
That tap won't stop its annoying little flow,
I try to fix it but I just don't know.
The sound is driving me past my last bound,
I swear I'll throw it down if it hits the ground.
You thought fast fashion was just the new trend,
but now you're counting coins when you spend.
Your fingers find your wallet in a tight grip,
afraid one loose moment might let it slip.
I gave you a name that was never your name,
a silly old moniker I dreamed up for game.
You wear it so well, and it fits just right still,
though I know now, sweet, it was never my will.
They twisted and pulled but the stopper won't go,
they swear they'll fix it, but we all still know.
They swore they'd never use hair gel again,
now dishes pile up next to the blocked drain.
They leave a message when your voicemail tone
rings out, their voice crackling through your old phone.
They always say they'll call back if it tries,
but maybe they're just telling themselves it's not lies.
You leave your socks in a messy pile,
then find them crumpled in her soft dog smile.
She guards her prize when you try to toss,
but only because she's the sock-stealing boss.
The dog's been barking since the mailman came to post,
he hasn't stopped since I brought out the roast.
He guards the front door like it's ancient lore,
no amount of treats will calm him or restore.
You stretch the band and give it one last squeeze,
your breath a nervous, summer-kissed breeze.
You never tied it tight enough to wrap
the ache now crawling through the widening gap.
My phone goes silent when it's time to stay away,
But buzzes loud when it's right there to display.
I laugh out loud but won't admit it for the take,
Just so the meal feels better for my sake.
She hikes through the pines to catch the best view,
the mountains melt into the sky's wide blue.
The rest of us wait while she lingers and finds
a rock to pose on, out of our weary minds.
She drinks her soda like it's some soft hush,
the fizz a little morning-in-the-mouth blush.
It's easier than thinking how it's a waste
to chase clean water's nameless, thin taste.
The last light bleeds into the bruised sky,
shadows stretch where the sun decides to die.
She leans back, her eyes closing to the world down,
as fire dips low like a fading king's crown.
You slice through traffic like you're meant to lead,
cars honk but you never even turn your head.
The crowd parts slow as you hold steady pace,
a pedestrian boss with effortless grace.
My dorm phone rings like a ghostly old bell,
it's midnight and this is pure hell.
I stare at the screen but there's no one in thing,
just voicemail from my ex still trying to sing.
You folded it slow, like you were afraid to throw,
it hummed through the air in the quietest glow.
I caught it mid-fall before it could stall,
but let it go soft like a note that I'd call.
You left a towel on the bench—no clue why,
some stranger might take it, or just walked by.
It still has your shampoo's familiar scent,
and now I'm folding it wrong, slightly bent.
He squints at the paper like there's still some clue,
then holds it three feet back as if that's the cue.
He misses the print by a full inch from the top,
what was once a tomato turns into a crop.
You leave your water bottle lying down,
where feet come flying fast from everywhere around.
One misstep could turn it into a spill,
and now you're soaked before you've even had a fill.
The toaster's still hot from your last failed flame,
it sputters your name in blackened crumbs and shame.
You grab yesterday's coffee, half-cold brew,
and stare at the smoke like it knows what to do.

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: You lean into the wind like a warm summer breeze,
your fingers loose around the handlebar keys.
You float past stop signs, you never have to hide,
the city hums low as you glide.
You tried to take half but you left me the back,
this charred little corner feels more like a snack.
I watched you devour every cheesy peak,
while I mumbled about pizza-eating geek.
I hit send and watch the message begin to spin,
the room erupts—my face hits my chin.
Emojis fly by like they want to roll,
it's chaos online but we're still feeling whole.
They lie there awake, letting their mind
blow loose like a leaf in a lazy wind.
The cracks on the ceiling become their spot,
a constellation of quirks and small dot.
He counted his coins from a loose-change jar,
he wanted a latte, a croissant, and a bar.
His coins don't quite add up—stacks of old tries—
the machine blinks "no go," and the coffee just dies.
Your cat attacks every lump on the floor,
thinking they're threats from the dark of the store.
You try to calm her but she just won't run,
though it's your nerves, not hers, that it's robbing of fun.
The app couldn't read your face where it code,
