it just said "unknown" again, and it showed.
You tried three more times to get past the lock,
but by then, you were stuck in your own shock.
Her cart was already packed to the brim full,
she reached again for another bag to pull.
She thought she'd just grab one more before need,
but found it was gone—there was none left, indeed.
You hear the record's familiar crack,
each track slower, like time lost its track.
The room fills with a dreamy haze,
and suddenly it's a softer, older days.
You still don't have the faintest clue
where we are, so you pull up and stew.
You draw a big "X" on the sidewalk in chalk,
then text me where you are—still no walk.

topic: someone spilling punch on the rug
lines: I watched it seep through the fibers and glow,
my phone lit up with the mess I made below.
It soaked into the rug like a sacred drug,
I don't regret the spill—no one saw me tug.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: His weekend was all about his old backup plan,
but time moves on and he's just a sad old man.
He still tries to check the news or a game log,
the screen is gone, and his mind fills with fog.
The clock ticked slow as the coffee ran brown,
it seeped through fabric, dripped all the way down.
Now there's a ghost of you on this stubborn stain,
and I pretend it's just the sky falling in rain.
You pause your meal, a smile hits your face like light,
Some distant gloom now seems worth the fight.
The words feel bold, as if they're speaking true,
And for a moment, you believe in you.
That faucet's been singing the same old song,
You hum it back, clinking glass along.
It drips in a rhythm, a slow spin,
A duet now, you two can't begin.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: You get a reminder that's just too late to call,
the screen goes black, no Netflix to watch it all.
You pace through your house like it's made of stale air,
then cook toast with your phone—no Wi-Fi, just bare.
You stare at the mess you call a pile,
the dog kicks socks around the room the while.
There's a faint stench—no, that's not your smell,
this whole scene is just a fabric-coated hell.
I got the test back with no red ink mark,
my answers so right they left the paper stark.
My mind was sharp when I wrote that first score,
and now I know—this time I earned so much more.
She lifts the lid with her small, quiet hand,
pretending the crumbs are just falling from sand.
She won't let it show when she's trying to hide,
but the guilt is already visible inside.
She folds the page with care and a throw,
then aims for the wall where it can't go.
Her eyes track the path of the doomed little flight,
as silence grows tight in the pale afternoon light.
It trembles above the still, breathless air,
a jeweled thief from some green secret lair.
I reach out, but it's gone—its fragile wing
leaves only silence where I wanted to sing.
I once believed that cereal should crunch,
but now it's a limp and soggy bunch.
It sinks like a stone, it won't even float,
my spoon rows through ruins in this cereal boat.
My laptop starts to glow with too much heat,
But I don't stop typing—this is my feat.
It's loud, it's hot, I'm not going to blame
the only device I trust with my name.
You checked it off first, and that gave you start,
a quiet thrill in your morning's first heart.
One done feels so close, like hope is so near,
you smile at the list, ready for this whole year.
I let the rain soak my shoes as proof,
I'm not stopping for shelter or roof.
Water drips down, I keep walking so,
This storm won't hide my bold, wet show.
She feeds the meter with her loose-change clink,
remembers when they gave you time to think.
She misses paper slips, the chance for no-change,
how coins feel old now, like something strange.
I left my coffee cold with a pink lip stain,
the mark still clings like it meant to remain.
It curves in the morning's familiar shape,
but not even soap could let that moment escape.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: They stare at screens instead of closing their sleep,
counting hearts that might mean something to leap.
The numbers glow too bright to leave on through the night,
a habit wrapped around the thumb, held fast and tight.
Her calendar's full of crossed-out days,
Each task pushed back by sudden delays.
But her scribbles catch my curious eye,
And I'll somehow rearrange just to try.
I swear I heard a bus horn echo the call,
waking up to a morning so grey and so tall.
The streets are quiet under a blanket of mist,
I'm making my coffee, missing you off the list.
She starts to feel brave as she tries to be cook,
Her sauce simmers softly, not quite how it should look.
The guests take one bite from the half-burnt dish,
They smile through their teeth and pretend they still wish.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: That plant keeps getting in my eye,
like it has some right to lie
there in the crack where it shouldn't grow,
messing up the sidewalk with its little green show.
The screen's soft blue glow makes your face shine low,
I know you're tired but still keep scrolling slow.
Your eye grows heavy, your brow starts to sigh,
and I wish this moment were morning or sky.
You opened the fridge to find the old bag,
of peas that your partner had left you to drag.
They've clumped into something odd and thaw,
defying the rules of food storage law.
You tilt the cup slow, you don't want to pour,
but steam clouds the air where the drops hit the floor.
You take a small sip and you burn your lip,
then dance in the mess like you meant to trip.
You got back your test without any red ink,
relief washed over you like a warm drink.
No grades, no comments—just a joyless mark,
it felt less like schoolwork and more like a lark.
My phone glows bright with a notification time,
it rings like a thief in its most annoying prime.
I fumble in bed for the screen's ghostly clue,
only to laugh when I see it's not true.
My phone glows bright against my sleep-deprived clock,
I jolt awake and feel the morning's cold shock.
I had a solid reason for this early plan,
but now I scramble eggs while cursing the pan.
Your lens searches slowly for my eye,
It follows the flash of a distant sky.
The light moves a little too far to near,
But the focus is soft, and the moment is clear.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: I posted a joke that went completely dead,
I'm still laughing but not sure if it's in my head.
I check the comments—no snickers, no voice,
so I save the post just in case it was my choice.
I made a cake but forgot my grace,
the oven burned it in its place.
The frosting weeps and starts to droop,
now it looks like a cake-shaped soup.

topic: the first day at a new job
lines: She sits there stone-faced with judging eyes,
The HR packet's full of half-truths and lies.
The office feels like a paper maze,
They call it culture, but it's just a phase.
She blasts her tunes like it's noon in the sun,
dancing laps in her yard like she's never done.
Her dog barks rhythm to every hard beat,
while the whole neighborhood marches down the street.
She knows your whole life by the time you pay the fare,
she talks like it's just second nature, fresh air.
From politics to her cat's latest bad spin,
she'll lift your spirits right up off your chin.
The billboard makes promises full of claims,
it aims to sell you the world through strange names.
It's all just a gimmick, another fake sale,
even the colors look washed out and pale.
She left the cart key somewhere in the debris,
near the snack aisle after her shopping spree.
She walks up and down every single aisle,
retracing her steps just to stall for a while.
She says something flat, but I crack at the joke,
my coffee goes flying as I try not to choke.
It's just one small comment, but it hits the wrong bit,
and now I'm wheezing, near a full-blown fit.
I baked a cake for guests and my dog's pure joy,
he saw it, barked, then raced it like his toy.
I tried to stop him, but he took one lick,
then flopped on the floor and played dead—what a trick.
The light slips through branches in bands of gold,
I try to capture it but can't seem to hold.
It slowly begins to fade from view,
while shadows climb up in a gentler hue.
You twist the cap but it won't stay on top,
A long drip stains your bag's wet inside crop.
You tried to fix it with a duct tape lid,
But the leak still drizzles—like a grumpy kid.
She's been streaming all night and it still isn't on,
The setup's a mess, and the signal is gone.
The chat is full of bored people who chat,
One even sent memes of her grumpy old cat.
You stare at the face in the neon-lit place,
a smile made for screens, not the human race.
It promises magic, a life without tie,
but you can't buy truth from a selling the sky.
You shook the branches to the sky,
determined every leaf should fly so high.
This isn't just a mess—it's your grand show,
a carpet of gold no one could ignore, below.
You held your umbrella out toward my sky,
I asked you why as rain soaked my thigh.
You said you were just being kind, not left,
I called it a gift, though I thought it was theft.
The fog rolls slow like secrets in your soul,
it wraps around your feet but you don't stroll.
You pause to smell the grass where morning dew
turns every fence post into something new.

topic: a bus stop shelter at dusk
lines: I check my phone but there's no sign of rain,
just shadows that make me too scared to remain.
The benches are cold beneath this cheap shade,
and no bus comes by for another long parade.
I typed her name once, but the screen just shows date,
I'm locked out of memories behind that old gate.
Her password was always a mix of her keys,
I can't log back in without a hint or an ease.
This helmet's been through every job site lead,
it's cracked but I still wear it on my head.
I've got the calluses and the kind of grit,
no task is too tough when you're built to fit.
I laugh when I touch the cold metal chill,
it's just another quiet morning still.
I wait until the frost starts to crack,
then twist the handle and head out track.

topic: sitting on the porch steps at twilight
lines: You watch the sky fade into that soft blue,
the wind moves slowly as it floats through.
The stars feel close but they're still so far near,
you think this calm might last all this year.
She fumbles for keys that won't turn in the key,
the dashboard hums low like a parking lot fee.
She tries the igniter but nothing will start,
the silence feels final, like winter in her heart.
She left a single towel as the only clue,
same pastel pattern from another hue.
I held it up to light, a silent test,
it matched the spot where her towel had been pressed.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: She laughed at a quiet moment, not a joke,
the kind of joy that slipped out while she spoke.
It didn't fit the film, the awkward scene,
but it became her favorite kind of routine.
You fumble around but don't find the key,
the lock's acting smug with a service fee.
You lean in to listen, the hinges stay hush,
the wind laughs at you in a cruel little rush.
Her sink won't let water escape through the drain,
It gurgles like something on tracks stuck in train.
She grips the plunger with nerves turned to raw,
Each push feels as futile as breaking the law.
You still have the headphones you bought as a set,
though years of bad habits twisted them fret to fret.
Their cords are a knotted red thread in your head,
now buried where old memories quietly spread.
I stood in the front where the heat met the room,
and let my voice bloom through the thick, silent gloom.
They sat in a wave, all eyes fixed on me,
and I craved the crowd like a deep-rooted tree.
A stranger offers shelter from the rain,
her smile feels familiar, like we've met again.
We don't talk much but we split the share,
breathing the same rhythm, better than stale air.
You opened the mailbox to find everything paid,
no surprises, no hidden charge in the shade.
It's been a long road to this simple little goal,
and you know it means more than money to your soul.
I hit the ground with a satisfying thud,
the sidewalk splattered with wet, caked-up mud.
My pants are torn, my knee's a raw red knee,
yet I'm not even hurt—just bruised and free.
You watch the morning turn branches to gold,
the leaves cradle beams that they gently hold.
A breeze stirs shadows across your light,
and lifts your spirit toward the day's soft height.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: You see another one—just a silvery spot,
but it feels like a sign on your life's little plot.
You laugh it off quick, but the thought still does age,
like time is a puzzle you're slowly un-cage.
She walks the same route down the block each pass,
sniffing every patch of damp new grass.
The neighbors step out just to hear her bark,
like her energy could light a whole backyard spark.
Since losing ten bucks last week in the room,
you eye every coffee and snack like a loom.
You clip coupons now for one lousy clip,
and count your steps to avoid any trip.
The creases in it are not from old lies,
but your attempts to read what your eyes could not size.
It folds itself back when you're done being bold,
mocking your route with a fold in its hold.
I look up at the sky to check if it's dry,
The clouds won't break, they just hang and sigh.

The umbrella opens like a strange gift.
She saw the smoke rise in a dark grey puff,

You call it a performance, almost art,
the way you hold the spoon like it's a part
of something grander than a single drop,
until it falls—and you never let it stop.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: She claims this coupon was clipped just to save,

then grabs another, still hungry, still stack.

her mind tries to recall the soft debate.

some secrets still hidden behind each link.
This pot is screaming with too much heat,

She waits until the kitchen clock
clicks past midnight, her craving in stock.

counts the warm treats between her teeth and her thumb.
You stare at the screen where your savings got read,

lines: He tries to fix the cart with a rusty tool,
but every repair makes him look more a fool.

and silence begins to take its quiet toll.

topic: a coffee cup on the curb
lines: They left the coffee half-drunk, complete with lid.

The can wobbles gently on the curb's high wave,
as if it once held something truly brave.
After lunch she makes a lazy wave,

Her head begins a slow and curious dip,
her eyes are getting heavy, almost slip.

I told him it looked fine for how little it cost,
now every mirror shows a shape I've lost.

not missing my old room or my old bed.
She sets the toaster on a level past flame,
the kitchen fills up with the scent of the same.

our hands are burned but we keep moving ahead.

horns honk like thunder on an angry stair.

topic: the smell of pancakes in the morning
lines: It drifts through the kitchen, warm and in air,

but time's ticking soft, making moments feel old.

lines: I trace the borders of a distant past,
where names have faded from the paper's cast.

and dreams of it as just a quiet lark.

topic: checking if you have enough for gas
lines: I stare at my phone's dimming lock screen,
The gas app shows barely a sliver of green.

She taps on her desk like she wants to find pace,
her eyes won't meet anyone's anxious face.
Time sinks into silence, a slow, empty void,
but no one's been fired or even gets employed.

the soup bubbles gently with barely a blast.
The kitchen feels cozier now it's this warm,
no need for a rush—just a simmering storm.
I never thought I'd grow fond of this stretch,
you see me here again with my lunch to fetch.
I try not to bend but the band won't mend,
and now I miss how we talked through each bend.
My sock pile is shrinking, it's quite the sad pile,
while my dog gives me that guilty-dog smile.

now he stares at me from the couch's view.
The plastic gave way with a quiet tear,
it's limp in your hand like a wet, heavy air.

and walk on with sorrow for something that's mend.
She stopped calling when the weekend turned late,
content to let old debts fall off her weight.
Now she walks faster where they used to thrive,
alone in her car, no one to drag her drive.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: You watch as the sky fades to blue at dawn,
a spider's web glistening, you're softly drawn.
It shivers like glass on a single thread,
and you wish you could keep it your secret bed.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: She dropped her snack at the checkout store,
she screamed for a new one and wanted some more.
Her dad stayed calm, had surprising grace,
and bought her ice cream in the same exact place.
I watch her run toward that fleeting glow,
the wind keeps shifting it left, and then right though.
She doesn't mind if they pop or they fall,
she laughs until her ribs feel about to give all.
The toaster made a loud, alarming pop,
a piece of bread that wouldn't just prop.
I tried my best with a pan and a dash,
but now my breakfast's a charred-up crash.
You still catch the sour scent when you smell,
where someone once dropped their pride and fell.
You lie there heavy, soaked, and cold as floor,
hoping time can mend but never restore.
I set my boundaries with a firm, cold tone,
I retreat to my room like I'm fleeing a throne.
I need some fresh air and more breathing room,
Not a group chat kind of mood — I won't zoom.

topic: sending a text to the wrong person
lines: I hit send with haste and got a new view,
They replied in all caps, saying it wasn't true.
I tried to pass off the mix-up as their blame,
but now we're both laughing—what a silly game.
She swears it's the rhythm, a secret new tone,
insists her dead grandma's trying to phone.

she's just baking a cake and potting some stew.
I blow out the flame that marks my new age,
my hands tremble slightly like a bird in a cage.
The table still wobbles, I feel everything shake,
one flicker of hope left—then gone from the cake.
You remember how it blocked your view of the sun,
the peak of your summer, now ruined by one.
It snapped in the breeze and collapsed in the sand,
you left it behind, but still hold it in hand.
She yells through the fence that we simply can't
dump our compost near her prize tulip plant.

but now she's just riling herself into heat.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: She tosses the bread to the birds in the frost,
but half the loaf gets dropped and is lost.

what's left in her hand and the hope in her eye.
I watched the bag flap like a torn piece of sky,
still holding whatever fruit had tried to die.

a trash-born ghost my garden gave me gift.

while he tried to pretend it was all just a dash.

is calling louder than any mouse trap.

could mistake her for a sleepy kid.

My dog gives me a look that says "got a clue?"
He waited by his leash, I should have knew.
He's already sniffed out the next best trail,
while I still stand here, turning a little pale.
You watched the leaf slowly give in and bend,
wishing someone would come along and send
a message you can't hear or even cry,
but the silence only feeds your quiet dry.

your backpack still zipped, you've got nothing but hair.

she tilts to one side with that smug look ahead.

your friends all clap like this is the show.

until you saw the sudden messy heat.

now you're stuck with a cat-shaped wet bill.

just another shift, same bland lunch deal.

The stain on her desk stays stubbornly black,
she taps out her thoughts on a silent key track.

though every new sip feels less like it's worth more.

topic: a child drawing on the table
lines: You call it a masterpiece, not just art,

my voice cracks, but I lie and say "My dear."

left her playlist still playing in her head.

Maybe you've got it all wrong since you first guessed.

You laugh, but you love it—the mess you call crust.

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: You notice the band snapped when the lever first broke,
now staples fly loose like confetti from smoke.

leaves you stuck tighter in this tiny paper trap.

all weekend dreams now buried in the mall.

but someone brought a tiny terror to hide.
That dog has been barking for twenty straight bark,
and now I just want this window to go dark.
Your toast only made a sad half-pop,
It's stuck in the toaster like a botched crop.
You laugh instead of calling it a slice,
and say your bread rebellion turned quite nice.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: You dig in the dirt where the sprinkler makes the sun,
kids laugh in the background, nobody stops the fun.

One jolt and it'll go—right out the window cash.

And asks for just a little more.
I tied the frayed line to a bent paperclip hook,
swore I'd catch something to make this trip worth took.
The tug came fast—it was a real little fight,
but the sun went down and I lost my weak light.
She claims she mows at dawn but it's midday sun,

I've never seen her face or even say hello,
yet here she is again—back to her front-yard show.

he speaks of someone who isn't there.

and all you can think is, I've felt this again.

muttering how tech treats you like a rube.

then wait like a slug for the system to bug.
She has no clue how it got there in the first place,
Toppled in the dark, now the cap's off its base.

Gravity insists on a stubborn, full will.

time seems to pause where you and it both stand.
It flaps its small wings like a fragile thing,
and dances in rhythm with the season's spring.
That acrid, bitter smoke rises up in the smell,
The kitchen's gone nuclear—it tastes like a hell.
Hot crumbs fall softly onto my shoe from the drip,

I didn't take a single perfect shot,
the camera stayed home—I just forgot.
But I knew every face in each empty frame,
reciting their names without a game.
She found them hanging in a sunlit glade,
the breeze dressed them up in a quiet parade.

she listens like this is the best part of today.
You tie a knot in the end of your cast,
the clouds drift slowly above the gray past.
You toss it far, though it's just a bent hook,

I traced your name in crayon, rough but true, [love]
your messy grin was scrawled a little above.
The colors bled through paper, smudged with ink,
now it's framed as the best memory link.
I step out back to see the morning view,
the way the light feels warm and soft and true.
They grow in rows like in a painter's bed,
I bend down low and rest my forehead there, my head.
I look up at the fading purple sky,
their song rises where the last light lies high.
I know I should go inside, ignore their call,
but I stay to hear it, this evening's small all.
You stood in the dark beside me near the aisle,
your laugh a spark from some old inside smile.
We watched the credits roll across the screen,
then clapped like fools in our old movie routine.
She watches the sunflowers follow the lead
[of the sun, their golden heads always ahead.
They lean without question or fear or delay—
she wants to grow that sure of her own way.
You swear you'll finally go through and send
those cards labeled "To My Favorite Friend."
But every one is just a bigger mess—
bad puns, wrong addresses, ink smudged or less.
I stare into the sink, a sea of gloom,
the kitchen feels like a crime scene, out of room.
I swore I'd wash them but forgot once more,
my hands are blistered, still, and feeling sore.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: She squints at the screen as her eyes start to eye,
the numbers are still the same old lie.

lines: I run my hand along the glassy frame,

and I wonder which truths we chose to disguise.
You hate the way morning pushes the light,

But you know you are stuck with the dread of this.
I was late for my meeting, but this is not fate—
a drum circle just blocked the entire block late.
I try to move past them, still stuck in my gear,

but I won't let it drown out my wife.
I'll charge slowly—there's time to save,
no need to panic like I've hit a cave.
I never thought I'd beg a sock to fold,
but this pile has been rotting in my cold.

between clean and dirty—life's such a race.
His voice cuts through the city's hot air,
he sells fresh fruit, not even a bit stale or rare.

and I miss the way his laugh used to be part.
I tried to butter the toast but got it all wrong,
now there's singed crumpets stuck charred and stiff along
the small hotel grill, which started to smoke,
and I'm here, still hungry, beginning to choke.
Her phone wakes up from a ten-hour-deep dead,
she fumbles it out of her tangled-up head.

to let it ring out in the dorm room's thin air.
They sit by the door, a pair gone alone,
their soles worn smooth like a river's cold stone.

but now they can't even fasten or hold.
You wait for the perfect moment, just your time,
the credits roll, and the crowd gives a chime.
We all raise our hands, it's not even an act,
we clap in unison, a secret pact.
She still keeps the plate from the old high school gym,
where he'd spot her deadlifts back when he was him.
Time's left a red-brown stain of sweat and old rust,
but she won't clean it off — it tastes like her crust.
I flip through postcards I never sent through,
each one faded in memory or blue.
I wonder if they'd say "hello" or "stay,"
or if they'd ask why I went away.
You left your boots near the door without a clue,
the socks were damp but it wasn't really due.
They hang by the sink, still heavy with drip,
and every step feels like a small wet trip.
I can't read the names before they scroll through,
the faces blur into "special effects who."
I want to remember each artist's own name,
but it feels like a race against time's cruel game.
You sit in the crawl where the traffic won't flow,
the dashboard screen casts a strange glow.
"Let's call it a day," you mutter and park,
then laugh as the cars never seem to spark.
You remember the moves you used to know ago,
but your feet won't follow what they used to show.
Maybe some nights you'll find the rhythm again, might,
a spark still flickers in your tired old light.
You open the fridge and you see them still green,
they've been staring at you through the freezer's screen.
You knew you'd forget them, but hoped you could know
how long they've been waiting beneath that thin snow.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: You bend down and pick up that shiny stone,
it's yours now, a treasure you proudly own.
The sun hits it just right—it still seems to gleam,
you hold it like proof of your perfect dream.
You split the slice with me out of love,
no need to talk, no need to move above.
We fold it half and bite our share,
our laughter passing through the same air.
I don't pay in installments or late fees or cash,
they lie there for weeks just to show off my flash.
They pile high in a neat little stack,
I let 'em build up just to watch them go back.
You push through the crowd to claim your empty aisle,
the cashiers all shout at the same checkout while.
You zip every bag with practiced, sharp speed,
the conveyor belts beg for more folks to feed.
You didn't plan to join, but now you're found
in the swirl of colors, the joy, the sound.
A banner declares the whole block turned bold,
and you wear the grin of a story well told.
You drift in circles like a dream you float,
you hum the softest tune without a note.
The water moves with you, so calm and slow,
your scales catch light in colors meant to glow.
I wake up twisted and stuck in this bed,
my neck locked tight like a vise on my head.
I stare around at the dusty old room,
convinced today was never meant to be doom.
That book's been officially marked due,
they said there'd be fines in bright blue.
I didn't run from the debt to repay,
I returned it proudly that very same day.
I see it there when I step out of view,
it's hard to act like it's nothing too true.
I wish you knew how much I'd rather know,
than find it taped where your keys used to go.

topic: a dog leash tangled in railings
lines: I hear my poor dog barking, whining, and cry,
the leash lies knotted around the iron tie.

and now we're both stuck out here, no way to got.
You tap the defroster, but it won't go clear,
your breath fogs the glass near each wet ear.
The road disappears into nothing ahead,
and every blink turns your patience dead.

topic: shaving a cake with a spoon
lines: I carve the top off with your favorite knife,
trying to shape it like our quiet life.

She folds the paper like it's her true art,
every crease precise, each corner a part.

she's got a new flair and no need for a brand.
I glance up and the blue sky starts to cry,
we laugh and shout, "It came out of the blue, by!"
We salvage what we can of our ruined meal,
drenched and muddy, but somehow we still feel.
There's a purple smudge on your left cheek,
how could I ever want to clean that streak?
I trace the color, this strange perfect hue,
a mess that only makes me love you.
She had nowhere to go when the downpour turned storm,
a stranger held out a blue handle, warm.
"Let's split this," she said with a grin, so they share,
and walked off like friends through the wet, gray air.
One earbud clings to your jacket's inside,
the other has vanished, now lost to some hide.

still chasing the rhythm you wish you'd hold long.
Her car is stuck in the slowest crawl,
horns honk like an angry brick wall.

trapped in asphalt like a rusted cage.

the crowd stays packed and will not remain.

I left it unopened since last week's use-by date,

The camera says "error – try again," no flash,

The wind slaps my face with salt and with grace,
it smells like the same old wild, open place.
I let the waves talk about how they grow,
and I wish I could shine like the tide starts to glow.
She sits at the back of the packed lecture room,
where shadows seem to hang low from the loom.
Her phone lights up like a small rising wave,
the only place left that feels like a cave.
I watch the fish knock against the glass to see,
if they think the outside world is free.

while I sit here breathing in quiet, curled.
She moves to a melody from the past,
the gym speakers softly cast it at last.
Her breath turns to steam in a cloud of sweat,

He honks because I switched into his lane,

The cord's still warm where I left it to lie,

Your brain forgets every single task,
you yawn when someone tries to ask.
They say you're doing it just for a dime,
but really, you're losing precious time.
You watched them slowly turn their heads to face
the sun like some old habit they can't erase.

now only you still track the sky like you.
She sets her toast to meet the morning sun,
the bread begins to burn, she knows it's all but done.

until it crumbles down—she fights the breakfast fight.
You rock your knife back and forth on the blade,
each carrot ring marches on in a parade.

the kitchen feels calm, like a summer ice.
I've spent the afternoon trying to see
what shapes hide in the sky's gray key.
A dragon, a dog, a spoon begins to form—
my imagination outdoes any storm.
They cry without a sound, just wide and worn eyes,

Your thumb still warm, you wipe the pain they hold,
And whisper something they've never been told.
I found a bag stuck where the robins fly,
it hung there flapping like a ghostly lie.
Still, I saw a kind of stubborn hope—
the plants had grown around it, learned to cope.
She watches the rain hit one lucky spot
and laughs like it's won the water's big lot.
Her eyes catch the light in a wet window gleam,
as if every drop is a wish she can dream.

turning flaws into quiet little grace.

even as time makes the plastic feel more old.
The stream keeps flowing between the rocks and flows,

She leans to listen to how the water bends,
As if it's whispering secrets only she sends.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: You tangled sheets into a warm nest,
your breath rose slow, still against my chest.

lines: That cat treats the sofa like some lazy throne,

perfectly blocking your access to clothes.
Their screen glows soft as they rub their eyes,
Words forming slow, like the truth might be lies.
My fingers hover close to the hand,
Afraid to speak, afraid to not understand.
I walk through the room with my shoes full of shame,
the world's like a judge, but not even in the game.
I say it's a look—call it avant-garde style,
while the laundry still waits on a lonely sock pile.
You watch the liquid pour off the edge and spill,
you sigh, then lift the bowl to pour it fill.
He lies there, unrepentant, still and purr,
your tears might fall but time will make them blur.
I found you tucked away from me on the shelf,
forgotten, yet still clinging to your self.
Time worked its way through you, now you're nothing but rust,
but I used to open up and place my trust.
He glares at the frozen screen and sighs too loud,
"This machine's not worth my time," he tells the cloud.
He takes a step back, breathes it all out deep,
then clicks the power button twice to force a sleep.
The weight plate slipped, I'm wedged by the bar,
my Instagram followers can't see how far
this failure went until I try to pop
out, but the steel doesn't bend for any gym shop.
I watch her stillness, this unbroken long,
as if the world outside holds some lost song.
Her eyes are locked on a bare, dead tree,
like there's a ghost she needs to be set free.
I've learned to live with the wet little shame
that drips from the cushions under his name.
It's not so bad if the scent starts to fade,
and time softens the spot I once thought was made.
I know the couch has that weird doggy smell,
but he just sat there, so how was I to tell?
He licks his chops while I stare at the mess,
and vow I'll love him just a little bit less.
They chase each other through the empty park,
someone makes a comment I don't quite remark.
A swing set creaks as they both aim to crash,
I blink and miss the moment—again, no flash.
She starts another diet with a new try,
swapping snacks for salads without the fry.
It's all going great till she cracks the plan,
then grabs a cookie and laughs at her man.
They tumbled all night in the dryer's weak spin,
the fabric got thin from the heat and the din.
She lost her last pair, no backup to spare,
now she walks barefoot through the cold living air.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: A tiny explorer set off to float,
his rainbow balloon tugged his coat.
The crowd watched as he tried to chase,
but ended up in the wrong place.
Your voice is blasting straight into my ear,
I've had enough noise for this entire year.
Turn it down now before I try to shut it off,
or I'll fake a sudden panic attack cough.
Your nose looks like something out of a blaze,
You forgot sunscreen for three straight days.
A red bump grows where your glasses will bump,
You'll regret skipping the vitamin D pump.
I stare at the notice now stuck to my door,
someone had tried to help but just tore.
It's more than the money—it all feels like me,
I'm trapped in this lie and I cannot be free.
They left their socks in the hamper again, no spot,
They swore they'd washed them yesterday—they forgot.
The laundry basket's an absolute mess,
It adds to the load that they never confess.
I watch the light blink through this changing age,
cars stall behind me, their engines cage.
I've waited here longer than anyone's song,
but the red stays steady, still holding me strong.
She stands beneath the dappled light,
where morning lifts her to new height.
The sun etches patterns in gold,
and she wears the day, both calm and bold.
I dropped my gum on the floor at my date,
now it's stuck fast to the wooden slate.
There's no getting around what's been there,
I sit and stare at my sticky despair.
You left it on the counter, bruised and spot,
the peel has softened into sweet decay and rot.
You meant to make a smoothie, you still might in mind,
but time keeps dragging onward, spinning through your wind.
She played through the storm like she owned every field,
the rain couldn't make her legs or will yield.
Her pass sealed the win and it moved the score,
the crowd cheered her name at the stadium door.
She hums along with the beep of the clock,
as if it were birds in a morning flock.
Her coffee is weak but she calls it her brew,
and sips on the calm that feels most true.
Her fingers follow the rhythm of her voice,
she reads the same chapter again for a choice.
She pauses where the margin bears her touch,
the paper's worn but never been loved so much.
She frowns as she tries but the zipper won't start,
it jams halfway up without warning or art.
The chill of the morning still clings to her cold,
and jeans that once fit now feel stubborn and old.
She draws bold arcs across the wet dirt,
her fingers stained with the pigment of hurt.
The clouds open up and the sky lets out rain,
she paints the colors in the puddles again.
You push through the crowd, claiming every last aisle,
your groceries stack high with no sign of a pile.
The clerk yells above the chaos, close to a scream,
this was supposed to be quick—never a dream.
I got lost in the details, the grammar so deep,
the phone cooled down as I fell asleep.
In the morning light, my words looked like gold,
sharp, crisp, and just how I wanted them bold.

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: You watch the old band slowly stretch and bend,
it snaps at the paper with nothing left to send.
Its purpose is done, like a string's final thread,
yet you leave it there, hoping it may hold ahead.
You still remember the hole where the roots
gave way and your hands came up clean with the shoots.
You'd figure out life without any set way,
turning the work into something you'd play.
You take a corner and the crowd makes a turn,
something in your chest begins to yearn.
A beat pulses loud, the rhythm hits drum,
strangers cheer you on—why not just come?
I left the theater still barely cried,
the story still echoing soft inside.
The credits rolled off the darkened screen,
and I whispered an "amen" to the scene.
She's miles away, her mind full of thought,
staring through windows where time gets caught.
But the coffee makes sparks in her morning breaks,
she'll map out the day over warm croissant cakes.
You meant to back up your phone, not make a snap,
but suddenly life's on your sister's clap.
Her gallery's full of your old faces, half-ghost,
while yours shows her at the beach, no such coast.
I used to answer every single call,
even screamed through a wall if it rang that tall.
Now I just let the silence wave,
but sometimes I still feel a little brave.
My sweat drops on the frosty treadmill screen,
I talk to the dust of my old routine.
I remember the pace of your footsteps in fall,
now even your echo feels too slow to recall.
I fish through my pockets for loose change, not back,
the register stares me down with a cruel lack.
The clerk waves her hand—I don't even tap,
I left my card home, now there's a cash gap.
She builds her stack to the ceiling so deep,
it wobbles but stands like a mountain of heap.
Each folder is labeled with color as art,
the whole thing looks planned like a data chart.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: She turns the old key in the rusted door,
dust dances slow as she decides to restore.
Inside glows a locket, lost and now gold,
she wears it with pride, a story told, bold.
He waves the ruler like a baton, swayed
by every noise in this chaotic parade.
It hits the desk like a loud, pointed clash,
each swing a sentence, each pause a dash.

topic: clouds gathering on a summer afternoon
lines: They stood outside and watched the gray grow sky,
whispering weather forecasts low and by.
The wind gave off a sound more like a moan,
but they laughed, pretending it was their fun tone.
I turn on the lamp to soft golden light,
the kitchen is quiet this early tonight.
I stirred the last spoonful into the pot,
just as you walked in and said, "I've got."
You promise you'll sleep when the screen goes bright,
then scroll through the dark with a dummy light.
You tell yourself coffee will somehow help you cope,
but your eyes are bloodshot, and there's still no hope.

topic: paying a fine at the window
lines: You sign your name like it decides your fate,
the clerk waves you through without a debate.
The machine beeps soft, a quiet toll,
and you wonder if money buys back your soul.
She scrolls from dawn until she's seen it all through,
but always stops to tap — no obvious clue.
Her finger hovers, expecting a grin,
though liking things is how she likes to begin.
The sky won't rise, still stuck in gray and sighs,
I trace my breath—open, blink, and close my eyes.
The world's a fog until the bus horn breaks the fog,
I wake in sweat, no memory of my dream log.
I watch the pot bubble, it sounds like a roar,
the steam from the kitchen pushes open the door.
This simmering stew holds all things I stew,
and waits for the moment when it's ready for you.
You watched the bird sit perfectly still,
head cocked, as if listening to the hill.
The world felt quiet, almost too near,
as time slowed down and the air turned clear.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: You had a perfect presentation flow,
until your nose gave a loud, proud show.
You turned it into a comedy act,
the crowd was laughing — just state the fact.
You twist the dial but it won't budge or spin,
the morning ride you were late to begin.
You're sure it's this key, but it's not even key,
the bike shop might charge you an extra small fee.
You try to twist the stub but it won't twist,
you punch the air like a kid with a clenched fist.
It's not about the lead—it's how it breaks your lead,
a quiet kind of fight where the pencil feels dead.
You fumble your pocket for one final dime,
the barista sighs while she clocks her next time.
"Exact change only," they posted for cash,
you mumble your thanks and go home to make hash.

topic: seeing your mom's new profile pic
lines: She posted a photo from long ago, so old,
it made you pause and miss her like gold.
Her smile hasn't changed since that warm July age,
while you're still trying to escape your daily cage.
You freeze when it lands on your quiet blue,
the morning is calm, not a whisper or through.
It trembles and dances, a delicate wing,
the light makes it magic, that tiny, clear thing.

topic: someone handing you a surprise gift
lines: You suddenly push into my hand
a box tied with ribbon, too neat to demand.
I wonder why now, after years of goodbye,
you're here in my kitchen, making me cry.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: She counts the years now—each wrinkle, each age,
her story once scribbled across every page.
The mirror shows silver where youth was a steel,
and she smiles at the truth it begins to reveal.
It happened so fast—the dog had the hands,
everyone laughing as he proudly stands.
But I saw the way her eyes filled with joy,
how she called him "my favorite old toy."
You walked straight into the storm without a clue,
now every step squelches, and you're soaked through.
Your shoes hiss like angry steam vents on a wall,
you text for mercy—get no response at all.
My phone buzzed once with her familiar tone,
I reached for it late—no message, just a phone.
I called her back fast, but no one would try,
my voicemail blinked silent, no one to reply.
My arms feel like they're going to snap,
this band is a cruel little trap.
It creaks and it whines like a dying scream,
yet somehow it's become my workout's theme.
The reviewer dives straight into the full roll,
claiming they've seen the entire movie-like whole.
"Let me explain a few tiny story bits,"
but I'm still trying to find a place this fits.
They bring chips and dip, they always up the game,
the host thinks they're an angel by the name.
Their laugh has this charm, it makes walls seem thin,
even the dog stops barking when they walk in.
You see the world like a pressure-filled cap,
your skull's a closed room with no exit map.
Your vision goes foggy, all color turns gray,
you wish this could end, but it won't go away.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: You promised a treat from the store down the street,
but now you're sweating in the grocery heat.
A meltdown erupts in the snack food aisle,
your fake grin slipping from your tight-knit smile.
I swear that squirrel's coming to my yard to steal,
it chitters like it thinks this is a meal.
It digs in loops with its tiny little plan—
I'm half convinced it's a genius rodent man.
You've spent weeks preparing, not just days,
The teacher already called you their main praise.
Your hands won't even shake when you check the hold,
You know your grade will be something bold.
It flickers once more, then goes dark and still,
I ask myself if it wants to or will.
That single burst was my final good-bye,
but maybe it doesn't want to die.
She spins the piece 'til she hears it snap,
her eyes trace the shape like a hidden map.
It slides in just right—how did it fit?
Some magic, she grins, and says "It's pure wit."
She's five minutes late but never seems late,
her friend sips cold brew and stares at the wait.
She calls it "traffic," which sounds like bad luck,
but we all know she's just a little stuck.
I handed the cashier my crumpled ten bill,
she smiled and said there was change left to spill.
I asked for a sandwich with extra roast meat,
the lunch rush was fading, and things felt more neat.
My pup knows how to sell the big treat,
he melts my heart with his puppy-soft heat.
He claims the whole couch as his favorite spot,
then drools right through it—what a lucky shot!
Their rhythm returns like an old familiar sound,
they hum from the grass where the fireflies are found.
I remember this hush when the world turned to dusk,
of summer, and sweat, and a faint, sweet musk.
I hit "share" too fast and tagged my old math post,
now his name pops up like some digital ghost.
The comment thread spiraled wild from that tag,
he laughed so hard the Wi-Fi had a slight lag.
The screen glows cold as it tries to see,
A shadow of wealth that's no longer me.
I watch my dreams silently start to fall,
But who do I call when the future's on stall?
The alarm rings like a funeral bell,
they call it morning, but it feels like hell.
They stare at the coffee like it might just brew,
the world looks brighter from the pillow's view.
I hopped in the taxi, expecting a ride,
but it immediately tried to hide.
It lurched forward, stalled, blinked out its beam—
I asked if this was a car or a dream?
He sat too long in the plastic chair,
while the clippers buzzed and chopped hair there.
Now every mirror shows one huge flaw—
the lop-sided cut I couldn't look at saw.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: My legs are stuck in a cold woolen clump,
I kick but only give my hip a bump.
This blanket's clearly out to wreck my fate,
it wraps like a villain and drags me down with weight.
He watched the cake with a proud little saw,
nose twitching rapidly, not a flaw.
The moment the knife hit the top he just ran,
now he's a pastry thief with a new fan.
You spot the same practiced cashier's grin,
she scans your snack while still pulling your bin.
Her eyes don't move, just stare through the glass,
a robot's face in a human-like class.
She walks slow through the checkout-free aisle,
her hunger softening the edges of the mile.
Her arms are a cradle for sugar and kale,
her cart creaks like a voice on a gravel trail.
They reached across the table with stealthy hand,
the grease was on their fingers, a guilty band.
I didn't say a word, just smiled and told,
"Help yourself. These fries are practically gold."
I woke up stuck in some weird yoga pose,
my head was tilted toward my big toes.
I tried to move and thought, "This feels like pain,"
but somehow I just locked myself in again.
You fit into me like a shape finds its form,
We weather the chaos and stay calm through storm.
Your sharpness meets mine where our quiet edge
becomes something softer than any first pledge.
I turned it on and it just wouldn't tried,
the remote was cold, the device had died.
I swapped the AAs but got no power light,
same mistake again, same old old fright.
She watches the drops run silent and still,
tracing paths down the glass to the sill.
Her thoughts fall like water, quiet and slow,
fading light turns the room to a ghostly glow.
You watched the robin tear the earth from sky,
its beak a hammer driving bugs to die.
A tiny general in this green war scene,
you felt both powerless and what it might mean.
I call this moment more perfect than art,
a breeze doesn't try to disturb the small part.
The wings unfold like a map it had planned,
and I film it slow with my phone in my hand.
The show just cut out in the middle of flow,
I rewound twice but I still don't quite know.
I scroll through old episodes, feeling a snap,
like time's a lost season with no guide to map.
I miss the old checkout lines from the mall,
where no one rushed you if your bill was tall.
We'd make small talk during the waiting while,
and cashiers still had a warm, true smile.
Your phone shows just one bar in these old bars,
but you're still trying to stream the latest stars.
You pause the show and stare at the "Wait,"
though buffering's not the worst tech trait.

topic: a group project where nobody helps
lines: You let the others fall completely slack,
while you quietly kept your progress on track.
You took the notes, did the work, set the lead,
then handed it in before they were even freed.
She's got no clue how bad the mist is in her view,
only sees through the glass as if it were brand new.
The wipers slap but leave behind more wipe,
a smudge on the dash where her face left a stripe.
She's watching fish swim upside down to show,
their bellies seem to glow in slow slow motion flow.
No one knows if there's a trick or deeper clue,
she laughs, "They're just confused—I think they flew."
My instructor barks at me about the tone,
says I'm too loose, not in my pain zone.
The band just wants to snap and fly off the snap,
while I'm still trying to figure out which trap.
A neon hand held the paint in a spray,
It left a message where pigeons could play.
The wall's now alive with some wild words in tag,
But walking past it feels less like a drag.
You flex your patience like a muscle for the post,
cutting through the crowd is never the most.
Let arms brush yours as you hold your slow sway,
you own the sidewalk where others lose the day.
Your thumb moves fast through the endless feed,
trying to fill some unspoken need.
You double-tap but it doesn't quite tap
the feeling that you're stuck in this trap.
You drop your pace as the crowd fills the street,
you make more space so they don't have to meet.
You let them move fast while you slow into flow,
it's not a race—you're just trying to show.
They stood beneath the fading summer sky,
whispering promises before goodbye.
The crickets took over with their soft play,
as shadows pulled the moment far away.
She tugs hard at the worn-out lead,
her tail wags like she's leading ahead.
She breaks into a joyous pace,
while she dances, I lose all my space.
A post-lunch crash hits me like a crash,
I reach for a snack from my fridge's flash.
I spot a chocolate bar, a sweet, quick treat,
Now I'm halfway through—I'll just eat and repeat.

topic: crackling fireplace on a winter night
lines: I toss another branch into the feed,
the flames sputter red like they're trying to bleed.
A charred old log still claims it's the main log,
while smoke curls up, turning the room to fog.
The rain keeps falling straight down from the pour,
we watch the sky weep from the window's shore.
You whisper "Let's not leave, let's just stay,"
and I forget the world ever felt this away.
I watch the board flicker from gate to gate,
Each delay just makes me feel more late.
My flight's now scheduled for endless hours,
I miss my mom's garden full of fresh flowers.
Her eyes glow blue from the screen's cold eye,
She scrolls past the dusk, ignores the gray sky.
When shadows grow thick, she fails to turn it dim,
And loses the world — and maybe even him.
I wore one sock without its matching pair,
the room felt cold, so I hugged up my chair.
I blinked through each question, tried hard on the test,
but still felt a hollowness deep in my chest.
She rolls down the window to chase out the smoke,
but the scent clings still like a stubborn cloak.
It's not just the sweat from the driver's seat—
it's something more sour, and sharp, and repeat.
The city stirs slow but I'm still awake,
A distant horn sounds like a sunrise break.
I blow it a kiss like a long-lost call,
This quiet is mine, this hour of them all.
My clever little rabbit had a wild new plan—
he dashed through socks and towels, full on ran.
He's nibbling shoe strings now, tight on the lace,
but I can't stay mad when he makes such a face.
I handed back the old apartment key,
the landlord gave a laugh and a nod to me.
There's not much I know about this new clue—
but my neighbor's dog already judges my view.
You saw the dog dart forward and grab,
now licking frosting like a sweet crab.
You try to laugh it off but you can't lie—
the dog just ate your cake and might die.
That stupid faucet won't stop running from the tap,
I tried to sleep but it wouldn't let me nap.
It drips and drags in a lazy, slow flow,
I'm tired of waiting for that water to go.
She hovers her finger above the tap,
second-guessing where she fits on your map.
Was it too casual? Too earnest or late?
The voice note feels heavier than the weight.

topic: seeing your mom's new profile pic
lines: You spot her grin—cheese-for-the-camera grin,
a little thinner than you'd last seen her in.
She's in a cozy sweater and that old felt hat,
but no one comments on the group chat.
The toaster went wild with its angry dark flame,
I reached for the spatula, the one just the same.
We laughed over coffee too bitter to brew,
and called it our ritual—burned toast and you.
She got her test back but left off the class,
she just smiled and raised up her glass.
No mark on the paper, no ink for a clue,
the grade was a guess by the color of hue.
She left the last sip in the bottommost dry,
the sun catches dust up there in the high.
Her desk still looks clean in her special old way,
but her chair's cold now, she's gone for today.

topic: a man reading on a bench
lines: He sits beneath a tree's soft shade,
unaware of the world's slow parade.
His book fills the air with a gentle voice,
and the bench feels less cold for that small choice.
She wakes up still wearing her Monday shift,
the dream gave her a raise like some strange gift.
The boss waves her over, the clients all calls,
but the office has melted into warm walls.

topic: crackling fireplace on a winter night
lines: I sit near the glow, the cold out of my fire,
warmth whispering things that it calls my desire.
The smoke curls up high where the memories smoke,
and silence begins to choke what we spoke.
You wipe the fog but it won't stay clear,
your breath curls in like steam near your ear.
That old song plays like it's made of snow,
and everything blurs but your eyes still glow.
She gives the device one last frustrated try,
her screen stays blank, she feels herself cry.
Her fingers tap, but the system just lock,
she laughs in a way that's equal parts shock.
I double-tapped your photo on my phone's post,
unsure if it was you or just a ghost.
But something about it felt like a sign,
not just a swipe, but maybe a new line.
He watches the record, stuck in its time,
dust circles the edge where the old grime
still clings to the grooves as it starts to spin,
and his fingers tremble like paper-thin skin.
My run was halfway done when I lost that mile,
the rhythm gone, no way to hold that smile.
I stopped to tie my left shoe's loose lace,
and let the wind take all the peace from that place.

topic: a quiet moment on the porch
lines: I found a stretch of peace that feels like calm,
the kind of stillness only silence can balm.
I didn't build this from a loud or wild
desire—just the quiet of a grown-up child.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: She snaps a photo of the perfect pink sky,
then spends three hours waiting for a reply.
A hundred likes later, the post still lacks views,
so she adds a filter and calls it new blues.
The words on the menu have grown more age,
I squint at the fine print, every tiny page.
My face has to get uncomfortably near,
to read without the blur I secretly fear.
I drop a coin but it just slides on spin,
the machine won't let my small wish begin.
I tap the glass, I guess I'll just miss
a snack, and maybe even myself in this.
I came here to capture the perfect wide view,
but my camera screen stays annoyingly blue.
I check the bag — no sign of the battery pack,
just my phone and keys in their lonely little black.
She shields her laptop from the leaky wall,
while her shoes soak below the puddle sprawl.
A steady rhythm marks the falling drip,
but she laughs as if it's just an honest trip.
You trace the zigzag path of the ant's first line,
watching how they map their tiny design.
They move with purpose, bold in perfect pace,
a thousand legs in time, no need for race.
The little rodent thinks it's some grand race,
spinning endlessly, no time or space.
His tiny feet move in a tireless spin,
though no one's there to hear the squeaky din.
She starts her day calm with her coffee to brew,
the quiet outside is still covered in dew.
Her steps are a steady, slow morning's pace,
she smiles at the clock—not today's big race.
They army-march across the sidewalk's edge,
one bug snatches crumbs from some poor pledge.
They've got a system, this whole little crew—
I step on one, they just line up new.
You spend hours raking your perfect little plot,
while the robin keeps pecking the same old spot.
That bird thinks your yard's some exclusive feast,
and you're just the gardener they take the least.
You say you don't know what I'm thinking, think,
but I saw your face when I ordered this drink.
There's no mystery here, you've got the whole clue—
I laugh, and you're already saying "me too."
You drive so slow through the morning's white slow,
your taillights cut a calm path, soft and low.
This isn't just driving — it's pure art,
you map the fog like it was some new chart.
You watched her pace, then start to lick the floor,
like something was dripping from every pore.
There's no pest spray, no treat or toy for clue,
she chases a secret only she holds true.
You swear it's haunted, but it's just that old chill,
the kind of quiet that could give you a thrill.
It hums in rhythm, a low steady beat,
keeping your leftovers from tasting like meat.
My screen flashes warnings the battery's low,
I sprint through the streets but my phone won't go.
I need to make one last text to her call,
I'll save up the light just to send this one all.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: I watch the dust swirl in the quiet air,
my cat sprawled out like a sleepy lair.
Her chest rises with a soft, long sigh,
and I wonder how many dreams she'll lie.
She leaned too hard and lost the whole ride,
the bike slipped out from under her side.
The gravel kicked up like a dry breeze,
and scraped her shins along both her knees.
You hum your favorite tune into the song,
the steam rises up where the melody's strong.
But when the water goes lukewarm and cold,
you still sing it loud, though your voice sounds a bit old.
I call them mine, but you always take mine,
we both left our names written on the sign.
They're warm with the ghost of your barefoot heat,
and every step is a shared little feat.
You used to say your throat never felt dry,
now you check the glass against every sky.
You fill the tap until it starts to pour,
but your body still ignores the whole store.
She didn't get a single good shot,
the camera had no power, she forgot.
The sunrise faded, the moment slipped clean,
while she stood there, just a broken machine.
She flexes again near the cracked weight's sharp edge,
she swore on her life not to skip or pledge.
Her knees shake a bit as she shifts from one lock,
the dent gives way fast—her hands take the shock.
The empty seat beside me feels like fear,
I haven't swung this high since last year.
The air gets louder, whistling through the wind,
but no one's there to catch me if I fall behind.

topic: missing a chorus in a song
lines: I was too late to hear the full catch,
the music kept playing, but it felt out of match.
I rewound and listened, still missing that part,
the silence between beats aches in my heart.
You watch the sky turn pink without a glow,
there's no one here to share the moment though.
The waves roll in like they're used to take,
but you stay still where the tide begins to break.
The water keeps moving, unbroken in flow,
it skips over pebbles the hiker steps below.
He tries to stay focused, but thoughts ruin his plan,
and soon he's just a daydreaming riverbank man.
He wears a suit but forgot the shirt to suit,
his left shoe's white and the other one's a boot.
His whole day was a disaster, no grand plan,
now he walks through crowds like a walking closet fan.
They say a warm bath will bring you calm,
but nothing soothes your legs like a balm.
You try to still them, but there's a rush,
the clock ticks on while your limbs won't hush.
I leave my headphones off so I can hear your hum,
and sometimes your voice when you're talking to me some.
I pretend to read a chapter, but I don't look—
your rhythm just now stole the silence I took.
I stand by the door, wondering if you're wait,
your shoes are still here — that's a strange little trait.
They're smudged with the mud from the path so near,
but I haven't seen you in months, not this year.
I watched the smoke rise where my toast used to sing,
you stirred your coffee, said "the fire's the thing."
I reached for the bag, but left it alone to pour
into the silence—no need for any more.
I still hear the same old creaky sound,
like the chair remembers the feet that bound.
We laughed as the sun faded into dusk,
now the silence lingers in that empty husk.
You remember the way it echoed on the floor,
how time slipped out that door and never came before.
It wasn't just coffee—was a moment that spill,
and now every stain leaves you thinking you're still.
Your sockless feet lead the march toward doom,
where a mountain of clothes blocks the whole room.
This pile seems to multiply as it grow,
and you pretend you just don't want to know.
The mailman edges past my open gate,
my dog barks loud as if to stage a debate.
Maybe today I'll get some better luck—
he drops the mail and skips the curb, stuck.

topic: a note tucked inside a card
lines: I found your note tucked in this card like a clue,
you swore we'd never break up — turns out it's not true.
You wrote "call me" in smudged ink, but it didn't cost
a dime — now I'm staring at my screen feeling lost.
The alarm goes off with a shrill little crack,
I hit snooze again just to rewind the track.
My eyes don't want to open, so I try,
but sleep still wins, and I feel like I die.
I left my sandwich open-faced and meat,
it got swarmed by flies and turned to heat.
I can't take the blame for not sealing it tight,
now the whole campus knows my lunchtime blight.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: You light the match, but the fear still feels alone,
the wind pushes smoke toward the cold stone.
Your hand begins to tremble, starts to shake,
as if the dark is waiting for the flame to break.
She types her essay by the glow of the cold,
our shared blanket patched from an old T-shirt fold.
Her breath fogs the window, she pulls out her cap,
and traces a dream on a mental escape map.
I moved through the waiting room calm and quick,
they drew my blood with a steady stick.
The results came back clean for every test,
now I walk tall, this health checks my chest.
She walked behind me, never caught my street,
just echoed the silence we failed to repeat.
Her footsteps slowed as the sky turned late,
but she carried more than the words unsaid weight.

topic: a note tucked inside a card
lines: I found a note tucked in this card with your hand,
written in cursive I can barely brand.
You said you'd call but I already read
the silence loud enough to understand your need.
You kept your head down when I missed the date,
just said you knew I'd come around to wait.
You lit the room with a calm, soft light,
and let me know I could have slipped or might.
The GPS just changed the entire route,
I was fine with the road I was already out.
I glance at the screen, my patience starts to map,
this update feels like a digital trap.
I toss these old socks in without a match,
hoping they'll still fit from a little patch.
They land in the laundry pile, soft and drift,
like memories folded into time's quiet gift.

topic: a book left open on the nightstand
lines: She read till her eyes had a dreamy look, thought,
then marked where she stopped with a ribbon she bought.
The dog licked the corner of one wrinkled page,
but it just adds charm to this well-loved old age.
Your alarm rings with the sound of a school bell,
but your sleepy brain refuses to swell.
You beg your body not to fight your soul,
yet hitting snooze still feels like a noble goal.
My screen keeps freezing in this ghostly gray room,
the faces pixelate and then they zoom.
I tap the mouse, but nothing comes from the tap—
I'm stuck inside the loop, a silent trap.
They used to live for the next big beat,
now they pay to sit where it's always neat.
Last year they screamed through every year,
this year they bought a white noise career.
I need to fill up my tank with gas,
but the machine won't accept my plastic pass.
I punch in the pin, it says wrong code,
I groan and curse this stupid road.
You move the grater with such smooth, sharp flow,
the shreds look like clouds on a cheese-white show.
This isn't just cooking—it's your art,
and every last crumb is a perfect part.

topic: a cup of cold coffee on the table
lines: You left your cold coffee as if to make claim,
it sits on the desk with your initials scrawled name.
No one dares touch it, even after the brew
has gone gray and flat, but still, it's all you.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: I pressed send and hoped you'd hear what I tried,
the words were soft, the tone I hid inside.
It fizzled out before it could even play,
my voice dissolved into pixels and gray.
I used to think it was pure joy and fun,
I'd sprint through the yard and leap through the run.
Now every puddle feels oddly deep,
and I wake stiff from my childhood sleep.
I told my doctor about the weird tooth pain,
he said I'd feel better if I drank it again.
My body's screaming, "This isn't the cost!"
but my tongue's like a kid begging for more frost.
The toast got stuck without a pop,
now smoke begins to rise from the bread's top.
They give the machine another hard try,
but crumbs are burning faster than they can spy.
You count the minutes on the long delay,
kids toss crumpled paper just to play.
A stranger offers you their warm seat,
the sun hits your face, you tap your feet.
She's stuck behind twelve people moving ahead,
her heel keeps the beat on the thin airport tread.
Her suitcase gets flagged, again, for the scan,
the guard yells, "Next!"—then stares at the plain man.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: It's that tiny toothpick still lodged down there,
I check my sleeve for stray bits of hair.
I twist and I shift trying to scratch the itch,
I'd rather just throw this whole mess in the ditch.

topic: socks left in the laundry pile
lines: You dig through the hamper, toes curling from cold,
but only one sock dares to be bold.
You toss it aside as if it were near
to someone still listening, or maybe just clear.
I need another cup, but my machine won't brew,
the clock just glows with a faint blue hue.
I stir it once with a dented old spoon,
and toast the night with the ghost of the moon.
The food still sits heavy on your down,
you shift on the couch and press your head to the crown.
A soft sigh escapes as your eyes start to sigh,
you let your tired body gently lie.
I hit "save" but it looked like "send,"
my draft went straight to a distant friend.
A quick reply comes back with a blunder:
"What is this? Is your brain struck by thunder?"
I stare at the screen like it's sacred glass,
my face is too plain for this beauty class.
I tweak every angle, adjust how I pose,
but nobody sees through these digital clothes.

topic: eating ice cream with a spoon
lines: She licks the tip, then slowly goes for a dip,
the spoon keeps sliding off her trembling lip.
The sugar melts to something soft and sweet,
while outside, thunder rumbles near her feet.
The bulb decides to act like a strobe show,
It flickers in time to the bass beat below.
I pretend I'm at a concert lighting the game,
until the switch turns it into a steady flame.

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: She reads the review on her phone's little app,
then vows not to tell the owner about the trap.
But it's all just one star and a fake sense of shame,
she thinks, "This is funny—but not much of a flame."
He's sprawled so wide he's taken up the spread,
with feet on desk and a cap askew on his head.
When asked to move, he makes a full-blown claim—
"This spot's been mine since my last coffee break, by name."
She's stretching on the blanket in a perfect pose,
her knee still stained from yesterday's red hose.
She won't let me help when the dog tries to pick
up confetti we dropped as a birthday trick.
The sky's been sprinkling like a broken pool,
You stomp through puddles like a clumsy tool.
Your shoes are now a rhythm—*drip*, *drip*, *drip*,
But you laugh when you slip and take a trip.

topic: leaving a note on the fridge
lines: I left a quick note for you to read,
just a reminder for your tired head.
It lists some snacks I put in the food,
hoping it lifts your stressed-out mood.
The teacher's loud cough echoes down the hall,
a morning greeting she turns into a call.
Her voice breaks the quiet, a rough but kind sound,
the class leans in closer, the stillness now bound.
You crack up about some stupid inside code,
like it's a big punchline and the rest are just load.
They nod and fake smile, pretend they got the bean,
but you know what you say probably didn't mean.
The players race through the muddy field,
their boots spin out where the ground won't yield.
From the stands comes a shout, a wet cheer,
it's just another chaos-filled football year.
I click on a video labeled "fast clip,"
twenty seconds in, I'm already on a trip.
They slow it down, they zoom in for some fun,
I watch the whole thing, even though there's no sun.

topic: waiting for the bus in rain
lines: I let my old sneakers sit in the shoes,
they're soaked again but not an excuse.
I used to dance in this kind of rain,
that version of me still wants to remain.
I tried to click my way back into play,
but the cursor moved not an inch or a delay.
It wouldn't budge when I tried to scroll,
so I danced through menus, hit escape, then control.
You claimed this sunny corner as your spot,
with no regard for what the others got.
I watched you stretch and sigh with your claim,
I said nothing—I made it my new game.
You stride confidently, always several ahead,
the others glance back but you never look lead.
You don't rush or groan when they call your stand,
you smile through the wait, like this is where you land.
You spend your mornings where heroes find time,
the cartoons blast in their Saturday prime.
You let the world stay in cartooned-out crown,
while every couch becomes a kingdom's town.
She stares at the mess, says nothing, no less,
than the truth that she knows she won't confess.
The wind had a laugh and gave it a spill,
another bad week in a waste bin still.
The burner hums with a sleepy glow,
I let the soup bubble slow and low.
My cat has claimed the warmest pot,
she naps where steam finds the perfect spot.
I walked all the way from my house to the gym,
I left without legs or a single free limb.
Now sweatpants are tight and my pride's drenched in shame,
I guess I'll pretend this was part of the game.
You never could find a clean sock or a pair,
they'd vanish mid-laundry without a care.
Now you laugh when you spot them neatly hide,
tucked under your bed on your dog's favorite side.
I fumble for keys but the car won't start, key
the engine just coughs and it's not happy with me.
I yell "Jump!" at the road—no cars give a jump,
the hill won't help either, stuck with a bump.
You pretend the bent paperclip could cast,
though it trembles like your grip from the past.
The lake glows still, it refuses your line,
not a ripple, not even a cosmic sign.
That purple frosting's a cute little mark,
like confetti forgot to leave a spark.
You wipe your face but keep it on your cheek—
it stays there, still bright, into the next week.
He jiggles the key but the lock stays tight,
the morning sun starts to shine so bright.
He kicks the frame, tries to twist or spin,
but the metal's stubborn—still won't begin.
You just walked in and you took what you took,
from my closet, no knock, no ask, no look.
You wore my style, but it didn't feel your way,
now my things hang in your house like a display.

topic: a coffee cup on the curb
lines: You spot your cup on the sidewalk's side,
maybe you left it there to try to hide.
Now the coffee's gone, the paper's all cold,
it looks like a relic from long ago, old.
You thought you'd need everything when you pack,
a suitcase full of shirts folded in black.
Now you stare at each item, can't quite fold,
and wonder if you'll wear this in the cold.
I watched you struggle there, the door still stuck,
I laughed but whispered that it wasn't bad luck.
You leaned your shoulder in, it didn't want to slide,
and when it gave, we both fell through the inside.
I handed my ten with a grin, no need to drop
a dime, but the cashier just raised her shop.
She counted the change and gave some cash back,
I laughed—it was lunch and a little math hack.
You swear one sock went to your dresser's top head,
but it's now tucked under the cat's warm bed.
You'd settle for a real solid black pair,
but all that remains is a ghost on the stair.
She lowered the sign by the slashed final price,
while shoppers like eager young mice
all rushed her at once, but she kept it last,
and smiled as they hurried back faster than fast.
You checked the loaf and you saw the green spot,
it spread across crust and it spoiled the whole lot.
It's growing, you swear, with a will to grow,
you toss the bread now, but not far below.
You wish this car would just crash into the side,
but you keep quiet and try not to hide.
You count down the seconds till things get calm,
your whole body tense in your sweating palm.
The taxi driver's got another long tale,
a story so bad it won't even fail.
He talks so much there's no quiet or way,
I'd sell my soul for some silence in clay.
They used to text late at night with endless calls,
then stopped replying, went behind their walls.
You check your screen like always, but they're gone now,
and you still wonder why they chose to leave you how.
The pan whispers secrets, no sizzle or flame,
The kettle just sighs—no whistle, no game.
I stir up the past with a spoon and some glaze,
This low heat is perfect for warm, lazy days.

topic: a dog barking at a mailman
lines: The dog sees the shadow, he knows it's the sight
of the man who comes dashing through his own night.
He hears the mailbox open, the little bell
rings like a siren — this is his personal hell.
She slides her card slow, like it's her last card,
the screen just stares back, flashing red and hard.
She tries cash next, but the machine won't check,
some "security issue" from corporate tech.
You drove through ten towns for this scenic view,
The brochure promised it was more than true.
You take a hundred photos—each looks the same shot,
The horizon's blurred, and your patience is a knot.
The rain comes down and erases the dust,
it cracks the heat-sealed soil, soft as a crust.
She watches the clouds in the wide blue sky,
and feels the first sign of a yes in her reply.
I never could find the right pair,
one sock left lonely up there.
They lie on the hardwood floor,
mismatched but still I adore.
The strap gave a soft but definitive snap,
it slithered down into a chair leg's trap.
One bag stays now on my poor left side,
while the other waits out of sight to hide.
I've stopped pretending I heard every age,
the years have locked my ears behind a cage.
But if you shout your words, I might just pick
up your message — it's a funny little trick.
She moves the tiny limbs into a new pose,
a hero's tale blooming from plastic and rose.
The characters speak in their little role,
but now her laugh sounds less like a child's whole.
The radiator coughs out cold, stale air,
my breath hangs thick with windowpane glare.
I trace a heart on the frosty snow,
imagining spring and the sun's slow glow.
I found the right place for this jagged spot,
the edges matched where it didn't look got.
There was that satisfying soft click,
the picture feels whole like some hidden trick.
She blames the landlord, the school, the old frame,
she stokes a candle like some small flame.
Her breath fogs up the window's thin crack,
her fingers trace the chill along the baseboard track.
The group chat's alive but my screen is flat,
I laugh through the silence, no one knows that.
It replays the same stuck message in loop,
while everyone thinks I'm still in their troop.
She swore she'd stick to a budget, but vow
gave way when the "sale" tag popped up just now.
The cart got too heavy to carry without slip,
and though she loved it all, her joy's losing grip.
Your phone blinks once—battery, so low,
but you keep scrolling, you won't let it go.
You spot a socket at the café's spot,
and rush there fast while your screen turns hot.
You still feel the sting that gave your nose its glow,
it happened months ago, but not long ago.
You remember the laughter, the ache, the pain,
and wish you'd worn a hat in that old July rain.
You stretch the band like a slinky gone spring,
It bounces back with this weird rubbery thing.
Your arms feel strong, your shoulders go tight,
But you laugh anyway—it could hurt, but you might.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: She scans every landmark for some hidden clue,
the deadline is looming, the task is overdue.
Her fingers trace roads that are faded and fold,
she whispers of secrets buried beneath the old.
I walk in and there she goes again, sees
my jacket draped where she might borrow keys.
I hoped this look would send a silent thought,
but she's wearing it now—just my luck, I'm caught.
You hit "send" before you saw the post,
your comments were harsh and said the most.
Your teacher replied with a sarcastic read,
and now you regret it from the top of your head.

topic: a road trip with bad directions
lines: We followed the "easy" route on my phone's map,
but we've been driving straight into a trap.
The GPS says "Turn left in ten miles—just go,"
while the road ends at a cliff no one wants to know.
You text them fast to keep up your morning run,
they're still in bed but agree it's already done.
You ask for their order, just vanilla and pick,
they say anything's fine—don't bother to stick.
She meant to tag a friend but tagged her post,
The teacher replied like she'd seen a ghost.
Class laughed as she tried not to clap,
Her face was red—she'd walked right into a trap.
My water bowl tipped over in a spill,
I tried to clean it up before you'd kill.
You followed me through every room, the track
of footsteps close behind felt like an attack.
They watched the wind whip the canvas to shreds,
while waves whispered warnings from out of their heads.
Now the broken frame lies flat where they lay,
salted wood already showing signs of decay.
She tried my boots and swore she wouldn't wear
them again, but forgot they're still in her hair.
I asked if she'd moved the hoodie I try to hide—
now it's on a hook in plain sight on her side.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: I could stay here watching your soft fur,
waiting for the moment you decide to stir.
Your breath moves slow like you're in a dream,
while sunlight spills across the room's gold beam.
I left my cereal in the bowl too long,
it softened like a song off-key and wrong.
Where's the crispness that makes breakfast crunch?
Now I chew on what I thought would be lunch.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: The map's got a tear right across the flat,
She's been staring at it since she first sat.
