"There's gotta be treasure," she mutters the clue,
then spends all her cash buying more glue.
Her thumb moves fast across the glowing blue,
remembering every color and hue.
She taps on the image of the bright sun,
and the moment feels half-undone.
Her books hold her shoulders in a frame,
Each spine marked with a scrawled-out name.
She carries the weight with quiet wear,
Up every flight without a stair.
You slide into the passenger seat,
a cloud of cologne follows your heat.
I crack the window, but it's still a bad deal,
I grip the wheel as I try not to squeal.
Her shade is still stuck where the wind had caught,
she pulls but it won't budge, a stormy little plot.
Her shoulders are tense with all this stress,
she's praying for calm or something less.
His screen shows one lonely pixel-shaped bar,
he texts back "be there" with a wink and a star.
He scrambles to find the right charging plug,
and trips over shoes, then his coffee, then rug.
You say you love me but it gives me no clue,
I've heard that line before, I already knew.
You call it fate, I call it poor old deal,
Your thoughts are loud but still, I don't feel.
She knows the barista by his last name, bean,
watches the drink board flash too fast for her screen.
I slide the latte over, already paid,
she shifts from guilty to thrilled in one shade.
Your voice blasts into my poor ear,
you think this is how to give a cheer.
The off-key notes hit every wrong tone,
I wish I had somewhere else to moan.
You leave your fingerprints as fresh as dirt,
smudged across the glass like an old man's shirt.
They're not a flaw but your silent proof,
marking every space you built from the roof.
The coffee slipped and stained your final page,
The ink now swirls like something from a cage.
A brown-stained panic starts to feel like storm,
But drying is the only possible norm.
She claims she's mad at the oak out back, the tree,
but I know this is just her sock-theft spree.
I leave them stacked, she snatches each one to chew,
now my laundry is full of dog-slobbered blue.

topic: someone spilling punch on the rug
lines: I raise my hand too fast, the cup slips from my hand,
Crimson swirls spread out across this favorite brand.
The punch keeps soaking in, it's more than just a spill,
The rug's been ruined now, and it won't clean it still.
You thought this was your favorite old song,
but they played it half-speed just to go along.
Someone made it clear there are strict rules,
and anyone who disagrees gets called fools.
Your face freezes mid-sentence in the feed,
the Wi-Fi crawls with the slowest of speed.
You wave at the screen but they can't hear you talk,
like a kid with a board, you draw thoughts in chalk.
The milk came loose when your bag gave way and spill,
now your last antibiotic is late to kill.
You check the stain, hope it won't smear the ink,
but the carton's just a broken grocery link.
She turns the knob for a steady stream,
but remembers the old one she used to dream.
Now it drips and drizzles, its nozzles all rust,
she longs for the spray that once stirred her lust.
I lie awake and map the cracks up there,
the silence heavy, but I choose not to care.
I trace the shadows where my thoughts might trace
new paths ahead in this quiet space.
You call this peace? Just sand and waves alone,
some seagull dropped a clam on your warm stone.
The shore's a mess of shells and plastic trash,
I guess that counts as nature's perfect hash.
They claim the air reeks of some vague old mint,
but the scent is a mystery left without print.
There's no clue whether it's mold or a prank,
just one weird hue of something they can't rank.
You double-tap to like the photo-post,
but never comment—just fade into ghost.
Your thumb's a pro at that swift little tap,
the perfect way to keep it casual and cap.
I spill coffee into my keyboard mess,
the delete key sticks like a glitched-out bless.
I tap it again, but it won't go away,
I fear I'm doomed to type wrong today.
You thought it was just a closed-off city block,
but then the brass band came rolling in like a rock.
A taco truck screamed, "We have five kinds of food!"
You were out of shape, but your feet found the mood.
You fumbled through your bag and the milk ran,
the kid across the bus gave you a funny man.
You tried to dry the stain, but it left a spot,
and now you miss that lunch you never got.
My bag's been missing since the baggage claim,
and now it's chasing me through airport shame.
I check the carousel again, same old belt—
someone's got my suitcase and they haven't dealt.
She lies there awake, not wanting the bed,
her thoughts buzz around in her active head.
Her toes start to tap, her knees begin to wiggle,
she laughs at herself and the fun it all giggle.
He stops to check out a billboard's bold view,
a dragonfly wearing jeans who just flew.
It promises magic that can't help him sell,
but he laughs and texts friends to come and tell.
The distant bus horn starts before the call,
she wakes up slow, lets the morning crawl.
Her coffee brews black, no hint of a flame,
another day beginning the exact same.
She stepped into the downpour without her rain,
her shoulders soaked while mine chose to remain
dry under the curve of this borrowed shade,
we walked through the storm like it was a parade.
I tapped "save" but the draft went out to send,
my clumsy fingers, always sure to bend
the meaning of my words into the truth—
you deserve more than my tired, draft-lit youth.
I felt the softest little tear
while zipping up my travel gear.
Now the strap keeps slipping down the slide,
and everything's falling out the side.
You wish you could speak just a little more clear,
but maybe it's others who can't catch your ear.
They nod when they hear you, then ask to go slow,
and now you feel seen in a way you didn't know.
They left a mountain of dishes in the bowl,
It's more than a mess—it's a draining of soul.
They might as well live in a crusty dish cave,
No sign they've heard the dishwasher's white wave.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: You crouch by the water, spot a silver glint,
it's a stone that catches the light like a mint.
You pocket it carefully, vow you will keep
this secret from the world while it helps you sleep.
I've filled each card in pen, in blue and black ink,
but never hit send or attached the e-link.
I wonder why I bother writing them why
when silence is all they ever seem to reply.
She had no idea when the bill was due,
it sat in her inbox, ignored as a clue.
Her account's empty—no time for cash,
she sighs at the fee, her face turning to ash.
You walk with your phone pressed against one side,
the missing earbud has nowhere to hide.
You sing every lyric with just one ear,
and somehow, it sounds unusually clear.
The river mirrors the sky so clear,
A passerby stops to give an ear.
Her phone's camera tries to catch that sheen,
But she says, "It doesn't do the light any mean."
You watch the river go where it flows,
it once held the stars and now only knows.
A cloud passes by and paints your shadow,
but the sky's still blue—like yesterday's tomorrow.
You trace the jagged shape of the edge,
your fingers give a quiet pledge.
It slides into place where you see
the moment like a sudden key.
I need my cash but the machine's on dash,
it's blinking red with no hope of a flash.
The queue grows thick with each added delay,
while customer service does a frantic ballet.
He pays for his lunch with old wrinkled cash,
The register rings with a soft little splash.
It's a sandwich he'll call his best bet the meal,
But he eats fast—it was too pricey a deal.
She still has the key from where we used to play,
though years have passed and the lock's worn away.
The door hangs loose, the hinges full of rust,
and time has taken more than it could trust.
It used to hum where it hung overhead and glows,
now there's just silence where the light should shows.
I climb the stairs by the flashlight's weak path,
but fix it tomorrow feels like doing the math.
My dog won't stop barking, it's getting to my mind,
the breeze does nothing, just teases with the wind.
He stares at the leash like it's some cursed chain,
and I can feel his hope in the handle's tight strain.
She sighs like she knows every single clue,
but my face betrays not one tiny hue.
"What are you thinking?" she asks me to say,
I roll my eyes—same old empty reply play.
I watch the dawn turn everything to glass,
the yard looks perfect, but it won't last.
Each step will crush what can't be held or melt,
the sun has plans for every frosty welt.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: She bends to pick up the rock's brief gleam,
convinced the creek hides what she can't seem.
"I'll sell this," she tells herself to keep
from thinking how far that dream runs deep.

topic: a quiet moment on the porch
lines: You made the whole world disappear with sound,
feet still on the ground, mind now unbound.
You claimed this corner, this rusty old seat,
and silence became your small, perfect feat.
She knew every shortcut but missed the new route,
the driver barked directions, loud and a shout.
With calm hands, she took notes and vowed to lead,
not letting the chaos change her proud head.
You punch the buttons but the screen won't dash,
your progress stuck in some tech glitch crash.
You keep on walking while the belt just spin,
pretending you're somewhere more fun to begin.
She still keeps her peas in the same old batch,
bag crumpled and dated in the freezer's cold patch.
Her hands hesitate when they're meant to thaw
the icy tradition from long-ago law.
You time your clap with the final scene,
there's silence only seconds long 'between.
A ripple starts in the row, gains a wave,
and you're the last one still too brave.
They drew this with love using only a pen,
The words are crossed out and written again.
Faded colors still hint at their favorite hue,
I wonder if they're thinking of me, too.
I water, I prune, I have given it try,
yet leaves curl and droop, turning all dry.
I swear it's resisting any will to grow,
but maybe next week, it'll surprise and show.

topic: clouds gathering on a summer afternoon
lines: You watch the gray mass roll in ever so near,
A storm might wash clean all that's unclear.
The sky holds a promise no thunder could glow,
So you wait with a smile, just a little though.
You watch the rain make tracks down the glassy show,
your reflection staring cold as the snow.
You won't wipe it off, you let the drops press
against the pane like they're sent from heaven to bless.
She watches the ant parade as it lead,
marching bits of crumb from a lost bread.
They form tight little lines like soldiers in rows,
never breaking their rhythm, staying so close.
You lie back and trace the shapes in the sky,
laughing at how the clouds go by and by.
A dragon, a cat, a fox—it all takes form,
until one breaks apart and becomes a storm.
You bring a strange kind of calm to her light,
the kind that softens a tense little fight.
She'll share her whole day with you in her head,
and you listen like you're handing her bread.
You punch through the page with a crayon-shaped hole,
Each swirl tries to capture a child's sunlit soul.
You twist every color you had left to spin,
The paper now holds what the lines could not begin.
You think the cloud looks like a perfect pose,
until your hand makes a huge smudge with the hose.
You try to fix it but lose every shape,
and finally laugh when the sketch starts to escape.
He arranges the toys for another big scene,
every move rehearsed to seem not too mean.
One figure tumbles and knocks the whole falls,
the chaos spreads—his script hits the walls.
His eyes stay glued to the cracked screen's narrow view,
he swears his message holds some life-or-death true.
A truck slams brakes—I brace for sure delay,
but time just ticks while he ignores the betray.
You made a chocolate cake meant for a birthday treat,
but your pup already knows the tricks to repeat.
She darts through the door before you can dash,
and the frosting is gone, along with any crash.

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: I skim the review of my usual read,
It says the flatbread is nothing but bread.
But the barista got a glowing new score,
I'll stick with my seat and my favorite lore.
Their head starts to spin when they stand from the chair,
a sudden loud din ringing here and there.
They clutch at the wall for some faint bit of light,
but dizziness takes them before they can fight.
You thought it was just resting, this tiny, soft rest,
but no—its mission's far too vast for such a quest.
It dips one iridescent wing,
and leaves you speechless for no real thing.

topic: a taxi driver yelling on phone
lines: His car's been stopped since we asked for a ride,
he sweats in the heat, complains from the inside.
"I'M A PROFESSIONAL!" he yells out so loud,
the whole block hears him and stares from the cloud.
I looked all night but found no keys on the floor,
my room felt bigger than it should have been before.
I told my dog the same old tale—
now maybe the keys are stuck in my mail.
They left the dirty dishes stacked in plates,
Some forks still had food from last week's dates.
The soap scum has hardened into foam,
It smells like the ghost of a family's home.

topic: sharing a cat video with no context
lines: You send a cat video without a chat,
like a dream someone thought out of a hat.
They stare at the screen, no clue or cue—
it's chaos, but this time it felt kind of true.
She slams it down on the floor near the wall,
as if it were something she'd kicked like a ball.
But the scent of her effort still lingers like smell,
and the room breaks into a little heat spell.
A frog does a dramatic leap into splash,
like it paid for the pond with a check from the cash.
It sits there, unbothered, doing the float,
while I drown in this metaphor I wrote.
I checked the coupon's date with a frown,
Now I'm stuck debating if I should drown
my sorrows or cheer up and let go—
Maybe next year it will come back, though.
I tap the message and pretend to send,
my thumb hovers, "Should I? Should I friend?"
You'll never believe how long it took to be
this confident ghost in your midnight feed, me.
They left the kettle on high and forgot the pot,
Now steam is hissing through cracks they have got.
It bubbles and jumps, starts to spill over foam,
But somehow, they laugh—this chaos feels like home.
You hear it first when you're near the wrong age,
a breathy stammer mid-sentence or mid-stage.
It slips out when you try to hold back the break,
but you're not sure if it's sound or a mistake.
You push the door open, still smell like the gym,
the light overhead flickers and goes dim.
You trace every mark left behind by the dent,
a shape in the metal that memory bent.
Your world spins twice when you lift your head,
the morning clings to where you left your bed.
You try to steady time in a sudden rush,
but the past still shows through a pale blush.
That buzzing sound isn't your ideal tone,
It's not a gig—it's just your silent phone.
You knew you'd forget to tune it this long ago,
Now it just hums, but won't bother to show.
I still remember how it looked at the event,
a smile stretched wide, my hands slightly bent.
Now confetti lingers in these dry strands,
a moment so bright that still somehow stands.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: She hit record with a smile and the right tone,
but the app said "failed" when she pressed the phone.
She tried again, but it still wouldn't play,
so she laughed and walked off, taking the mic away.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: She hasn't checked her account since last year past,
but now her phone lights up with a random like blast.
A message takes time—it all goes so slow,
yet hope finds a way to make the screen glow.
It snapped in half during the first cold snap,
Now every storm looks like the same old trap.
We never talk about the bad weather,
But we remember how we stood together.

topic: a phone at one percent battery
lines: Their phone dimmed low, the last of the screen,
a fragile old thing, a tired machine.
They try to send out a faint plea in calls,
but silence is all that the concrete walls.
She adjusts her stance but can't hold the grip,
the band flies out and grazes her hip.
Her muscles scream with every small pain,
her brain keeps telling her she's in vain.
You swore your watch was set to the right zone,
but it's hours off from your actual phone.
You check the clock on your desk—it didn't lead,
just showed the same wrong time, totally dead.
You said the fog would lift by now—how slow,
it's been three days, and you still can't go.
You act like it's a fairytale, this weather act,
but even magic has a shelf life, dear fact.
You stare at the rules in the return form,
unsure if your purchase is still in the storm.
"Final sale" says the tag, but you'll still try to take,
the product feels flawed—like it's meant to break.
I watch the same faces pass down the street,
their routines and stories, sad and repeat.
My wallet feels heavier, like some old thread,
pulling me back through time, stuck in my head.
You carried the textbook back from the tome,
but forgot it was still checked out from home.
The date on the spine says it's overdue,
and the barcode's half-melted in glue.
I still feel the same when I see that old tear,
where my backpack's worn strap dragged on the gear.
It broke with a soft, almost musical snap,
on the trail where I lost my childhood's last map.
You tamed a balloon into a twisting snake,
no one could guess how you made it not break.
It's not just craft—it's full-out art,
I'll keep this memory as a cherished part.
We used to joke about our hangout call,
how we'd debate just who would throw the ball.
But now it's just two of us, both feeling left,
stuck in a project we're already bereft.

topic: a bike locked to a pole
lines: I left my bike here the morning it was gone,
and now the chain hangs still like a cold dawn.
Its tire marks are faint, already off the track,
I whisper goodbye by the weathered fence crack.
I pile the pasta high so it touches the top,
but the Parmesan won't pour from its stop.
I tap it and shake it until it turns to dust,
but I can't find any joy in this grated lust.
You watch the butterfly land so near,
it's the first one you've seen this whole year.
It flaps its small wings in a slow, soft wing,
but soon it's gone—just a memory of spring.
She raises an eyebrow, gets me every clue,
I finish her sentence like we're only two.
We read each thought as they start to flap,
We've outgrown needing words or a plan or a cap.
You never know how weird it feels to wear
the sneakers I saw you kick off the stair.
We measure feet but never check the size
of dreams we step into without a surprise.
You promise me forever we'll stay and play,
then disappear into some new toy or clay.
I trace rainbows in the sidewalk's dry bend,
waiting for a text you never intend to send.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: She still wears that same old crooked grin,
the edges of joy seem to fade a bit thin.
We hang her portrait in that empty frame,
we whisper her [name], but only her name.
He keeps his dented bottle in perfect shape,
though every sip feels like an old escape.
It's from a trip he still can't quite put past,
a reusable relic, not really a blast.
The last one sputters out in a sudden flame,
Someone yells my name—let's not blame the game.
I strike a pose with my wide, birthday grin,
I made it through ten wishes, so I begin.
You turn the knob, but there's no water flow,
You swear it worked here yesterday you know.
You bang your fist against the tiled head,
The shower's gone silent, it seems completely dead.
He always interrupts before you can say,
"Wait—what about my calendar today?"
She claims she gets every joke and each clue,
but just gives you side-eye and walks into a stew.
She posted the meme just a little too late,
but it felt like she'd seen her own fate.
The comments rolled in on that old worn thread,
where every post ends up going to dead.
The handle stays frozen, my breath turns to cold,
It's been this way since that snowstorm from old.
I twist and I yank but the thing won't spin,
The chill starts to bite through the glove on my skin.
One laces loose, they tie it tight again, string,
but it won't stay tied—it's some strange thing.
A heel starts caving, then a sole begins to snap,
he slows down just enough to feel the pavement trap.
We had no plan—just improvise and plot,
The bouncer almost saw us, but he did not.
We squeezed three into a section meant for seat,
Security's watching. Don't try to repeat.
The treadmill screen is stuck on same old date,
my stats haven't moved from yesterday's weight.
But I'm still moving—this is turning into joy!
My neighbor yells through the wall, "You're such a weird boy."
You turn the corner and you get the sight,
music lifts your feet without a flight.
Everyone's queuing for food to eat,
you taste the air—it's one big sweet.

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: I stuck it there one day with a sigh, half tried,
hoping to tuck time neatly to the side.
It's frayed and won't hold, barely can bend,
but somehow I still don't let it mend.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: I trace the faces frozen in this frame,
their names are etched but I don't know the name.
They all look so happy and they once wore
the clothes I now hang up behind my bedroom door.
They'll paint it over or tear it all run,
the city says art has its time and is done.
She traces each tag with her careful, tired eye,
afraid soon there's nothing left but to cry.
The "no receipt" machine won't give me my check,
some robot voice says "See a store tech."
I just want to say I've had enough and paid,
not act like a scene from a discount parade.
She plops down with snacks on the sun-warmed sill,
her laughter the highlight of every thrill.
The remote stays glued while she mashes eat,
until the old TV starts to emit heat.
You check your watch—no time to spare or hide,
The bus is full, you try to climb inside.
People just stare as the packed seats sway,
You stand like a ghost and drift away.

topic: singing along to a car ad
lines: A commercial starts with the same old song,
you hum too loud while you drive along.
Your voice shakes a little with some strange fear,
you feel like someone's walking up real near.

topic: a plate with two leftover bites
lines: The plate's still warm, I hear my stomach's tone,
maybe someone left it here just for my own.
It's not much, but two bites could still be might,
I'd rather eat alone than waste this last bite.
She keeps tossing clothes into the same old toss,
the pile grows soft with time and damp and moss.
But she's near the edge, she knows it, makes a pledge—
this weekend, every sock will find its ledge.
She kicks her shoes beneath the table's rest,
confident and carefree as her chest.
There's something in the way she moves today—
like every shadow fades when she walks away.
You watch every frame for the big clues,
the hero frowns, but nothing bad is news.
The music swells like certain doom,
you check your popcorn — and the next room.
I missed my usual stop again, this train
had left me soaked in the sudden rain.
I show my face instead of the lost fare card,
and watch the city blur past the subway yard.
One checkmark says "it's mostly all done,"
but the clock reads noon and the light's still from the sun.
She crosses it off with a sigh and a yet,
knowing she'll never quite catch what she wants to get.
Your progress bar just got stuck near the bar,
I watched it flicker like a digital scar.
You click refresh and you tap it to try,
but the update won't budge—it might as well die.
She checks the clock with tired eyes,
her phone buzzes softly with half-truth lies.
Her chair creaks louder with each restless edge,
yet she still believes this team will make a pledge.
I stood too close and the crowd pushed me near,
the lights blinked red and the doors slid clear.
I gripped my bag like it might still be hold,
but missed the train I once thought was my old.
I stare into the fog until it sees me,
my breath a ghost, the glass full of debris.
There's nothing left but time and a dry cry,
and the echo of who I used to be, so high.
I used to dread the hours spent in time,
beside a neighbor who talked like a mime.
But lately, the noise just fades into flow,
and their energy helps my work begin to glow.
I push a cart in the store's snack aisle,
my mouth already begins to smile.
I pretend I'm on track, stick to a diet,
but my cart screams chaos, a sugar riot.
I read the sign pinned to his cardboard and read:
"Drop a dime if this guy your moral lead."
He asks for loose coins in a paper coffee change,
yet somehow it's me who feels oddly strange.
You schedule an appointment, then another time,
the nurse texts back a reminder—thanks, chime.
They take your blood, then your story for the chart,
and you forget why you thought this was your part.
Your alarm rings again with that shrill, false call,
you hit snooze and just stretch out in a sprawl.
Another class will be marked down as you miss,
but for now, this sleepy chaos feels like bliss.
Your shoes sit soaked from some long-ago storm,
you left them there, as if that were the norm.
One sole is peeling, begging for a beg,
but you won't bend to save this broken leg.
I hit the floor hard, not a graceful drop,
my jeans and ego both tore at the stop.
My knee is bruised but I'll walk on it soon,
at least I'm still upright—mostly me, not the moon.
They used marker and crayon, all that ink,
probably forgot that birthdays can still wink.
It's clear they tried—hello, off-center tried—
but now it's framed where the flaws can't hide.
He cuts through the crowd like he owns this aisle,
pretending the baggers are all on his smile.
"No need for a bag," he says, takes out his cash,
then flaunts it at everyone with a guilty flash.
That snarling dog approaches fast and near,
We've been through this dance at least this year.
I freeze mid-step, anticipating bark,
Its eyes are wild, the evening turning dark.
You open the old voice memo app,
hoping to catch your thoughts in a trap.
The past feels closer when the quiet days
are spoken softly through the speaker's plays.
A stranger's bag is caught on my shoelace hook,
I side-eye him but he just gives a slow look.
This is not how I pictured the morning rush,
the train car hushes like we all share a hush.
She counts each coin in her warm, tired hand,
muttering how they aren't her favorite brand.
But she keeps the change, still holds it like a dream,
as if her future flows from this small stream.
She tucks the kids in and walks through the cold,
the landlord's red notice stuck firmly, bold.
Her voice soft as wool, she reads every tone,
then folds it and hides it to keep her own.
She remembers the joy of the springtime rain,
how she'd wait for the storm to come again.
Her boots splash loud, her laughter lifts her feet,
while the world outside still stays on the street.
You stare at the page but you can't seem to see,
the letters are dancing like tea leaves in tea.
You hold the book closer, trying to read,
but maybe it's time for some glasses you need.
My phone blinks red—this can't be true now,
I ask myself how to act or how.
I fumble for a plug, my hands feel numb,
I'd rather unplug than face what's come.
Your bare feet hit the tile and it makes you cry,
You beg the heater to do more than dry.
That chill down your spine feels like old fear,
as if every mistake comes back in a year.
You groan as the sun climbs through your light,
Your eyes still want sleep, but you're forced to fight.
The morning feels cold, like the world isn't fair,
Not even your coffee could make you not care.
I lie here counting cracks in the sky,
wondering if it's ever going to dry.
My thoughts just float along without drift,
this boredom is a weird but free gift.
He built his domain where the umbrellas don't stand,
bent ribs still sticking up from the land.
He says it's his kingdom, no sign to his claim,
but the wind whispers loud his defiant name.

topic: missing a chorus in a song
lines: The song skips the chorus again when it should play,
I slam the repeat button, but there's a delay.
It auto-skips the best part — I'm ready to skip
this whole playlist, I can't even begin to trip.
You keep waiting for someone to fill
your bottle, but no one's got the will.
You add ice from the cooler's melting light,
and raise it high—like hope's full height.
You bolt upright without giving it a rush,
your vision goes dark and you feel it flush.
Your hands hit the tile and you grab for the floor,
the dizziness lingers—there's nothing left but sore.
You watched the butter run out of control, spread
and wondered if warmth was worth the mess in your head.
Now every bite tastes like time on the toast,
slipping away soft, without much of a coast.
They curl up under blankets, nice and deep,
the plot could fall apart and they'd still keep
munching from the bag, a steady snack,
as scenes repeat because they missed the track.
I traced my thumb where the salt washed it then,
they laughed through sobs, these tough old men.
Their eyes held echoes from long-buried dust,
and time kept ticking beneath our trust.
You try to chase your shadow but lose its tail,
the sun laughs hard as you turn quite pale.
You strike a stance like a yoga studio pose,
your shadow's already in better clothes.
We turned our block into this week's town,
Lined sidewalks with flags and home-made crown.
Laughter and music rise loud in the cheer,
Look what we built with no warning or fear.
They slump face-first into a pillow down,
One arm dangling off the couch like downtown.
A sneaker escapes and lands on a cap,
The cat leaps in slow-mo, sets the trap.
He digs through his pockets for loose cash,
the barista rolls her eyes with a flash.
He fumbles a dime, a nickel, a dime,
she mutters about how it's taking too time.
I waited through buffering every time,
the stream would lag even during prime.
A pixelated screen fills with blue,
my show fades out of sudden view.
She can't stop her thumb from a lazy scroll,
the hours melt into a blurry toll.
Her contacts burn with a desert-like dry,
but she won't pause—there's too much to cry.
She lunges through the hallway with one fierce leap,
knocking over a candle, a cup, and a heap.
To her, that dusty mess is a royal treat,
pouncing until her paws smoke from the heat.
You flip the package over to scan,
hoping there's something healthy in your plan.
You squint at the list—most of it you see,
but wonder if it's really gluten-free.
They've added three new specialists to his days,
each convinced their treatment is the final phase.
He needs a calendar to track every need,
but now they're asking if he feels like he bleed.
I fit into this seat like it's made for a small,
my belt clicks twice tight, I don't even need a call.
My leg won't move an inch, but I won't beg,
I'll turn into a prop if it means no jet leg.
You wipe your eyes, but they won't stay dry,
The credits roll in a hazy, watery sky.
The silence hums and you just want to feel,
The fiction fades—but the ache still feels real.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: I tap on my phone full of quiet hope,
the screen shows my savings have grown in scope.
A number that feels like a steady calm,
it whispers there's time to build your own balm.
I feel it creeping in, this quiet age,
my thoughts are caught behind their usual cage.
My hands move late and sometimes they slip,
I miss what I touch before I can grip.
You organize your shoes like they're part of a team,
each pair lined up neatly, all in their stream.
There's pride in your posture, you take such good care,
not one scuffed sole by the front room's main stair.
She flips through the mail with a wide grin,
ignoring the stack where her savings run thin.
Her eye lands on dates—most are already due,
but she sorts them by color, adds a little hue.
You pull out the crumpled bill as your cash,
knowing the clock and your hunger will clash.
You hope the hot soup still counts as a meal,
and not just a wish from a coin you can't steal.
She sings every lyric at full volume shout,
the radio plays a song she knows about.
Her hair flies wild in the chaotic breeze,
she drops her phone twice between the car keys.
A dry sidewalk lets rain make a crack,
Each drop jumps in its new puddle-track.
You stomp where the water sounds splash,
And send tiny waves through the gray ash.
She ties her shoes too tight around her heels,
the bus has left the stop, she misses its wheels.
Her hair comes loose from a fraying black thread,
she hides behind the collar, pulls down her head.
You watch the clouds change from vague to form,
a dragon or bear, then fade to storm.
You wish you could keep what your eyes have seen,
but the sky is free, and nothing's been kept clean.
You dug out a CD from way back in time,
still in the case and in perfect prime.
You remember holding the disc in your hand,
a mix you burned yourself—your very own brand.
She blows on her hands but the cold won't give chill,
the handle remains stuck, motionless still.
She rubs it with gloves, she gives it more wait,
the ice cracks a bit—her key finds the gate.
She's been stuck on the same crossword clue,
tapping her pen like it was old-school glue.
Her frustrated face is starting to erase
any hope that she'll fill this empty place.
You haven't heard the old bell chime a single rung,
but you don't need it — your guests know your tongue.
You wave from the porch with a confident hand,
it's part of your style, this small DIY brand.

topic: crackling fireplace on a winter night
lines: I watch the fire's flicker dance on flame,
This room feels peaceful, just the same.
The embers hum a soft and steady glow,
Like memories from a long, long ago.
You stare at your phone, the moves flash on the screen,
each step feels more awkward than the last one you mean.
Your heart beats too fast, you can't keep the pace,
the comments will come when they zoom in on your face.
His brain's still buzzing from a meme-spree train,
He sends another link — it's late, but he can't chain
the urge to share his latest wild post,
until the screen goes dark like an old-night-club ghost.
She found a single green spot on the loaf's soft top,
but the smell of the rot told her not to stop.
She left it in bins where it happily took,
"It's compost," she joked, gave the bag a good shook.
I push my plate away, my empty tray,
but maybe tomorrow will be a better day.
A cook smiles and says, "Hang in there, good luck,"
while I'm still here, hungry, and feeling stuck.
You tap out the message as if in the air,
the screen reflects your sleepless, side-eye glare.
You think the meme hides the true underlying truth,
but it just screams "desperate old Gen-Y youth."
You watch the bird sit balanced and still,
its shadow trembling on the far hill.
You hope it finds the calm you want to find,
riding the whispers that rise from the wind.
I need my shoes to be clean and dry,
But the clouds won't stop pouring from the sky.
Water squelches each step, I begin to slip,
My shoe soles are useless, no traction, no grip.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: I found a toothpick lodged in my sleeve, just there,
I sat down slowly in case it reached the chair.
It felt like something sharp was in my meat,
but maybe I'd finally lost my lunchtime beat.
She walked right in like she had no slip,
her socks too thin for the lack of grip.
Her body hit every slick tile,
the dog just laughed the whole while.
You still smile at me from behind the flame,
We both laugh as the toaster plays the game.
I think you remember how it all got burned,
but never let on that the past's returned.
I check the box where the morning mail
of envelopes lands without fail.
A stack of bills with their numbers all due
still somehow feel like a problem untrue.
She holds the fork steady in her left hand,
it sings a soft note without a demand.
The air feels a little more still and calm,
like music can mend every ache and balm.
She stops mid-step, she sees the long ant row,
they march as if war is about to go.
There's purpose in every tight-laced little sign,
their shadows march straight down the brick line.
My desk is narrow, but my focus has space,
I carve out a zone where the chaos can't chase.
He bores through walls with his power saw drill,
I code through the noise with a stubborn full will.
They're pacing around with their hands in their stress,
muttering swears at the same old address.
A blank Word doc stares back at each page,
while deadlines loom like a paper cage.
You said you'd be home but were twenty minutes late,
now the stew is cold on the chipped plate.
The chicken was dry, and the veggies were roast,
but at least the bread turned out decently toast.
You ordered oat milk, but your latte won't blend,
We laugh as the barista tries to fix the bend.
You call it a sign, some cosmic weird thing,
I want to vanish, but I feel I should cling.
You stumble through words but you keep giving it try,
the cashier smiles when you force out a reply.
Mistakes don't deter you, you want to grow,
so even if clumsy, you're bold enough to show.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: You trace the frayed edge, follow it back to the thread,
where we pulled it across the bed in a spread.
Time folds itself into corners and bends,
but the past stays stitched in this tangle of ends.
She jolts awake, still half in her head,
the dorm phone shrills till it runs dead.
She answers low, voice worn thin through,
but no one's there, and it isn't true.
You think the dust bunny is the perfect prey,
so you practice your evil-cat stare display.
You launch with the drama of a full-blown leap,
then retreat when it rolls into a heap.
You tear down the wall and you dig out the hole,
A broomstick becomes your fort's central pole.
Dust bunnies are bricks, you stack every dust,
The floor is uneven but your joy won't crust.
You pause to watch how the light starts to break,
it flickers and dances and never will shake.
It spills through the branches in patches of gold,
and reminds you your dreams are not getting old.
She makes a perfect spiral, never a blob,
this morning ritual is her top job.
The sink reflects the smoothness of her art,
while I stare stunned—how is she that smart?
I pull and push but the handle won't turn,
my phone buzzes with a friend's text of concern.
I try again and the door lets out a bang,
lucky me—it was just off its hang.
The field's a muddy blur beneath the pitch,
we're all soaked and no one wants to ditch.
My fingers tap the seat—this game feels tense,
but logic says there's nothing left to sense.
You track the hawk with your sharp, curious eye,
it rides the wind where the clouds pass the sky.
It carves the air in a wide lazy loop,
like a solo show for an empty troop.
That office printer's always getting jam,
It clogs and whirs like some old rusted dam.
It spits out pages, half-toned and a mess,
But no one dares to touch that red press.
She checks her watch, the train left ten minutes past,
the overhead speakers give a delayed blast.
She'll miss the connection she had planned to take,
but maybe the day isn't totally to break.
She throws on the coat like she's taking the stage,
spins in the mirror her private cage.
She slips on the hat, it becomes her new mask,
transforming the chore into grand performance task.
Your usual coffee's lost its daily brew,
even the buzz you need doesn't feel like it grew.
You grab the beans and make a bolder fix,
the spoon trembles—your courage still sticks.
He always forgets to turn down the set,
neighbors once called to remind him, they bet.
He says it's the way things were back in that time,
when joy would just climb out of static and chime.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: You spot a glint beneath the water's gleam,
It catches the light as you crouch by the stream.
Your fingers close tight, but slip from the hold,
And the moment is gone, like hope in the cold.
One slip and the whole thing tumbles off the edge,
I made a weird vow to finish this odd pledge.
A single link pops and the whole mess just snaps,
now I have to redraw all my plan's weird maps.
I count every beat of your echo, drop,
it fades at the wall where the pipe has to stop.
That soft rhythm's the only sound I know,
and it shakes like a secret I can't let go.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: She builds her kingdom out of mud and mess,
each tiny detail becomes a true success.
Her hands are covered, thick with red dirt,
but she's too proud to think of washing her shirt.
I stare at the handle, stiff and real cold,
my breath stuck between stay or go bold.
I try to twist but the metal won't twist,
my face fogging up like I'm caught in a mist.

topic: a plate with two leftover bites
lines: She left two tiny bites, called it her perfect meal,
but I helped myself—what's a little cheese steal?
There's no room for guilt or a whisper of shame,
we both knew the deal and we played it the same.
You read the label like a window to the past,
trying to trace where the flavor was cast.
It's been years since you knew every shelf,
but the words still feel like old advice from yourself.
You stare at the screen where it won't scan,
your grocery list now turned to panic plan.
You don't want to ask how much you owe,
but the clock is moving, and you should go.
They left the old bread rotting in the bin,
As if it were somehow less of a sin.
Now the whole fridge smells like it's gone and stank,
And I'm picking bits off the kitchen plank.
You call it a walk but it's more like a bake,
the sidewalk glistens, the air's a dry lake.
They sell you drinks from a cart that doesn't pour,
your throat turns to gravel, your temples wear sore.

topic: laughing too hard at a joke
lines: You tried to stop but the laugh wouldn't fit,
your eyes watered, your sides ached at it.
Back then you knew what joy could still do—
now you barely laugh like you once laughed for you.
She gave the jar a good shake to get it to spin,
but the honey clung thick to her wrist's soft skin.
A golden trail of the sweetest mess,
she licked it clean and declared it a bless.
You tapped your card but the screen said no cash,
You slammed it twice just to have it smash.
You pull out your phone to do a quick check,
But even the apps are down—what bad tech!
You slip behind me just to be away
from rules or timing or anything today.
We catch ourselves smiling in the jam
of breakfast hour—like lovers playing ham.
You didn't plan to join the parade,
but now you're dancing in the shade.
Laughter mixes with someone's scream,
the night feels close to every dream.
Her feet never hit the ground before the door,
the hallway buzzes with gossip and lore.
She runs through the courtyard in full-blown rush,
her face still pink from sprinting or flush.
I lost my favorite sock again—no pair,
it's dancing on a clothesline out there.
The dryer hums as it tries to spin,
but I'm smiling now—I'll find them in.
This man's been slouching through his whole damn shift,
eyes barely open, can't even keep this lift.
Every stop sign comes, he jerks us way ahead,
and I'm ready to scream if he's not fully dead.
You lift the plate from the gym's dusty past,
and trace the initials carved deep into the cast.
It gleams now with sweat and a coat of old rust,
but still you believe in the strength of that trust.
They say the message was just a quick call,
but they're still typing fast into their sprawl.
They've read every word and reacted with read,
but never once typed back at full speed.
These shoes still echo with where I have wear,
They saw me tiptoe past midnight's stair.
Their soles know the path of a few lonely years,
And spots from old spills and silent, wet tears.
Each swing lands with a dull, defiant thud,
the shovel spins back out of the mud.
You pause and laugh—this isn't your dig,
the earth's being stubborn as a stuck pig.
I sat by the stream where the water runs deep,
it whispered secrets it had always keep.
The sunlight danced on the surface so light,
and hope began to feel like it still might.

topic: a phone at one percent battery
lines: Her screen turns flat with a warning so slight,
She swipes through old chats, her only light.
She begs for just more, but the power won't pour,
She slumps by the desk where she swore, swore, swore.
She spent her lunch break just clicking and scroll,
convinced she needed it all to enroll.
The box arrives—this was such a waste,
but she ordered it fast in her usual haste.
She twists the throttle for more reckless speed,
the wind grabs her lunch bag and scatters the feed.
A dog chases shadows it mistakes for a bike,
she laughs with the city, all sharp and light-like.
He plays as if the whole world is his stage,
his music breaks free from the metal cage.
He wins the crowd with a wry little charm,
and waves his six-string like a conductor's arm.
You sort through the pile of old postcard mail,
each one left mid-sentence, a story's trail.
You won't send them now, but you still like to read,
the way the ink loops around what's stuck in your head.
I stack my bags there, keeping the space tight,
from every corner, it's clearly in sight.
You try to move past but you come to a stop,
my shopping cart's throne is no temporary prop.
My socks are now just a pile of old chew,
the dog did it again with my favorite blue.
I shout at her as if she'd do it for leg,
but she's at the door, whining to go out and beg.
You pedal through gravel, the wheels refuse to spin,
your grip's getting thinner as tension moves in.
The frame lets out a warning — it sounds like a creak,
you hope it survives until the end of the week.
The dashboard shows only an empty glare,
I drive without lights though I try to take care.
My phone's flashlight does all that it can dash,
but shadows get closer, I feel a crash.
I twist the knob, but it won't really start,
the burner hums faint, like a cold heart.
There's warmth that used to come from the glow,
now even the heat feels like it's moved though.
My neighbor's typing like it's the keys
to something only they understand in a breeze.
They never pause to match my own pace,
but somehow I've learned to love this shared space.
She stared at the screen where her savings used gas,
then fished for her card in a fraying leather pass.
The machine blinked once, like it took a deep toll,
and left her alone with her quiet, bare soul.

topic: a dog leash tangled in railings
lines: The park is chaos, we are the whole scene.
My dog's leash is now a twisted machine.
I tried to sneak out but got stuck in the spot,
it's not a love knot, it's an exclamation knot.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: I spot the first one in an old gray shade,
it's not so bad if it's on Team Parade.
It catches the light in a mischievous glint,
I leave it be—like a badge, a silver tint.
The toast turned black, the kitchen filled with smoke,
he coughs into his coffee, trying not to choke.
He grabs a plate and makes a fresh one drop,
the first one's still a charred, brown crop.

topic: reading under the covers with a flashlight
lines: They sneak a flashlight under the bedsheet light,
turning bedtime into a midnight rite.
They pause to yawn but keep the story rest,
hiding the glow pressed tight against their chest.
She walks the neighborhood with steady lead,
chasing squirrels or sniffing old bread.
People smile, they say she helps them grow
in small ways—like a dog who just wants to glow.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: You're in bed but you still do that final scroll,
like numbers are somehow your secret life goal.
Now you dream in graphs, stats, and blue light gleam,
your validation fix feels way too extreme.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: She taps through her feed as she winds down to scroll,
the minutes she thought love had never quite stole.
The screen still glows soft with a number too low,
but dreams don't have likes, they just quietly show.
You kick off the ground and let your feet rise,
arms stretched wide like you could touch the skies.
The wind whistles past and seems to call,
a version of you who's growing tall.
She expects calm reflections in the moonlit still,
but the lake won't give her peace to fill.
She kicks at pebbles, shouts at the shore,
wishing for silence, getting some more.
She watches the steam curl upward, tight and thin,
the way she believes the day should truly begin.
With slow deliberate hands she starts to pour,
her tea is never just a cup—it's always more.
It trembles above the water's thin air,
wings flashing like daggers in sunlight's glare.
I step closer, my shadow hits its wing,
and still it stays still—yet my fear begins to sting.
She turns it up high to outsmart every chill,
but her cold feet know better than any will.
The heater kicks in with a loud, warm blast,
she jumps back and yells, "Not that quick, so fast."
The shoes by the door hold more than a clue,
their soles whisper secrets she can't undo.
One has a smear of paint, a faded stain,
like evidence of a life left remain.
You watch the rhythm of its tiny feet,
how it ignores the traffic and the street.
Its world is small, but the sky feels wide,
and you miss how free you once felt inside.
I watch the fog roll in like morning is slow,
it drapes the fence where the birds used to go.
It swallows the trees, it hides every hide,
and I laugh as my boots sink up to my side.
She watches the yarn fall with a casual throw,
the tangle now reaching out to her toe.
She tried once to wrap it but missed every wrap,
the ball's now a rat's nest, and she's stuck in that trap.
I watch them chase each other through the grass,
laughing loud enough to shake the pass.
Time slips away as they start to grow,
yesterday feels like a lifetime ago.
I could tell you every thought I know,
but you'd still say I don't understand how you grow.
We both think we get where the other one ends—
and neither of us mentions how it all just bends.
The squirrel digs a hole for every nut,
leaping midair without a single cut.
It marks each spot where it hides the ground,
then dances in circles—so full and round.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: You inch closer as the storm blows you near,
this is how it always goes by the year.
Your hand brushes mine, a moment's slip,
and suddenly the couch feels too tight to grip.
You call it a crisis, not just a mess,
and maybe you should all just confess.
The dinner was great but who paid the bill?
No one's admitting it—no one's still.
I raise my phone up, but I know I'll miss,
the screen says "low light—wait a bit for this."
It's not my skill set, I don't want to know,
the moment slips by and the shot won't go.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: I try to guess the story behind the pose,
but no one looks at home in those old clothes.
We've tried to take one better since that frame,
yet still the best one never got our name.
He said this trinket was handcrafted and sold,
but the price tag was written in all caps, so bold.
It felt like a scam, a plain old rip,
and yet he bought it—what a silly trip.
She watches the sky turn from gray to a glow,
the thin crust of ice lit gold on the snow.
The geese haven't woken, they won't be awake,
until the sun lifts their wings off the lake.

topic: a long queue at the coffee shop
lines: The barista yells, "Don't push—just take your stop!"
Some guy in cargo shorts won't let the line crop.
I check my smartwatch, still no green light [sign],
I whisper "delay" into my coffee [line].
I tap the icon where my hopes were hope,
but nothing loads—just my old ways to cope.
A white page stares with no way off the screen,
while dreams feel close, but no one ever seen.
She counts her coins twice before she goes shop,
afraid to let go, too quick to drop.
Her fingers curl tight into the grip,
but fear still whispers it might just slip.
You hit "save" but it read it as send,
the message went out without any mend.
Your phone rings with that cold, familiar shock,
you freeze like your fingers are glued to a lock.
Your smile slips through the glare of my eye,
The flash painted us both in the same sky.
I should've whispered, "Wait for a moment of love,"
Instead I said, "Let's try one shot from up above."
She swears she's done it right every single time,
but the plates still come out spattered with grime.
She says it's a curse, bad kitchen appliance luck,
though deep down she knows it's just her plate stuck.
I can't resist the pull to scroll,
it's habit now—my thumb has total control.
The blue light tries to mimic some fire,
but my eyes call the screen a tired old liar.
You eye the line with a groan in your sight,
your patience is wearing thin, feeling tight.
The belt moves slower than you want it to slow,
your frown just deepens as the minutes grow.
She walks through the puddles as if they were so
easy to cross, but the rain won't let her go.
Water climbs up her socks, cold and deep,
she keeps walking, though her feet are asleep.
Your dog waits by the door like it's always been prime
time to beg for leftovers from your dinner crime.
They tilt their head like they believe you'll take the lead,
while you're still dreaming of that slice of warm bread.

topic: a sticky finger on the window
lines: You leave a greasy fingerprint on the mark,
your mischief still buzzing with a spark.
You could wipe it clean with just one hand,
but why would you when it's so absurdly grand?
You stomp through the pavement as if chasing the sun,
calling this "therapy," not some kind of fun.
Each blister you get is a red-hot pain,
and yet you do it—same spot, same again.
We always split the bill after the meal,
but never discussed whose love would heal.
Now numbers confuse me, debts feel like a sort,
I hope you're still my friend, but not my support.
I clicked "Buy Now" because it seemed a deal,
but now the guilt is hard to bear or heal.
What if this thing was never what I bought?
Just something I wanted when sleepless and thought.
You adjust the dial to keep out the cold,
your hands trembling still from the way it hold.
The heater hums until the room feels warm,
and silence blooms in the shape of your form.
You leave your towel on the cold, hard floor,
your sweat now part of the gym's dark lore.
It hangs there heavy, still wet and drip,
as if warning newbies to never slip.
I listen for the wrapper's final crunch,
still half the film left to get through my lunch.
My fingers brush the folds, I feel each tear,
like secrets spilling out if I hold too near.
They cut the best part right before the scene,
some ominous music starts to fill the machine.
A close-up lingers — nothing happens, still,
but I'm hooked anyway for that cheap thrill.
There was not one sign this would happen with clue,
they blocked both directions in garish new hue.
I try to re-route but they block every pass,
I park on the lawn and stomp back through the grass.
She watches the sky as the morning light break,
A sound pulls her from the fog of her wake.
A distant bus horn hums low from so far,
Her old town is gone, but the echoes still are.
A neon sign climbs the top of the hill,
promising thrills that never quite fill.
It shouts, "Try our new flavor—pure mint!"
But I spot a typo as my smile gives a hint.
I watch the light flicker and almost fall,
a breeze whispers secrets it can't recall.
The branches are growing too thin to bear,
I hold my breath in this heavy air.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: You were mid-sentence, halfway through the flow,
your nose betrayed you and it had to go.
The room stared silent, expecting a disgrace,
but you laughed it off, still in your rightful place.
I watched the dandelion seeds float through the sky,
each tiny puff a wish that I could sigh.
They twirled and spun but never stayed to fall,
like dreams I whisper to but never can recall.
She taps the machine for the correct fare,
but nothing happens—no beep in the air.
Her hands hover, almost like a plea,
while I watch her and wish it could be me.
I slipped through the fence before the gate,
but the bouncers caught me and said "Too late."
I watched from the side of the empty aisle,
my friends partied loud for the rest of the while.
You tilt your chair back, still caught in the smell
of chocolate, maybe a dropped jelly bean shell.
The teacher calls you out for being so late,
but you pray your delays won't seal your fate.
She sees a dark lump that she's sure is a play,
her tail flicks once, then she runs it away.
With fur bristling out, she explodes into leap,
then trots back proud to sit tall on the heap.
A tiny world spins as he races the zoom,
his shadow spins fast in this little room.
He's chasing some dream on his endless dash,
but the wheel keeps turning — no sleep, no crash.
She gives up fashion to walk in her style,
the others stumble and wobble a while.
She says her comfort is more than just worth,
the ground feels kinder when kind to the earth.
He used to crave the raw, electric sound,
bass that would shake every wall and pound.
Now he craves silence as songs begin to fade,
a quiet so deep it feels like a blade.
She rubs the fog from the screen to make it clear,
muttering to herself what she's heard in her ear.
A beam hits the seat and reveals a faint light,
like hope trying to break through the dark of the fight.
You stare at the text but still can't make out a clue,
the article is due and you're stuck in a stew.
You squint through the screen, it burns like a pain,
you'll need to ask someone to read it again.
I saw your old towel still damp on that spot,
you must've left it when you forgot.
I kept it in my room all that summer's heat,
just in case you'd come back to meet.
You stare at the screen but can't remember the pass,
you kick at the lawn like a toddler kicks grass.
You guess old codes, shout "password" just to try,
the router glows blue—it's not going to die.
She squirts it all down the sink without pause,
a wasteful move for a small-town cause.
She leaves half the tube still full of paste,
while science screams about this daily waste.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: She always makes the bed without a single fold,
but the blanket still finds some excuse to hold.
I miss the way she stitched my dreams with thread,
soft and warm, a story she used to spread.
This mat reeks of old sweat and stick,
A film coats the floor that's just too thick.
I signed up for gains, not germs to pay,
I wipe down the space and walk it away.

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: You pose for the shot, alone in the frame,
the tag bar empty—no friends to your name.
You'd hoped for a comment from someone, a crowd,
but now you just post it and feel oddly proud.
This old light bulb won't quite stay in its fit,
it wobbles loose, making me question it.
Its dying glow fills the whole empty room,
a silent flicker, like an oncoming doom.
You pile your plate with the same old toast,
all butter and salt from some distant coast.
You watch the sunrise through the glassed-in view,
and smile at how time feels like breakfast glue.

topic: a dog leash tangled in railings
lines: You twisted the leash in some complicated loop,
you and your dog, a mismatched old troop.
I watched how you clung to that fading string,
like holding the past by its strangest thing.
You took a wrong turn down a narrow stone lane,
ignored the sign that said "Don't Enter—No Gain."
A bench out front read "Open—Your Fate,"
and sure enough, your sandwich came on a plate.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: You haven't seen a new face all week,
and everyone knows how you used to speak.
You keep to yourself, but they still throw some shade,
smiling in their pews like a Sunday parade.
You blow out the candles on a stale cake,
A silent room stares like a drowsy wake.
The only card came from a long-lost mail,
You laugh as your face turns slightly pale.
I stand outside now, three hours too late,
while the last flight closes behind the gate.
The passport was here, just a room and a key,
and now this whole trip might not be for me.
You watched the clouds pass through the dusty sky,
your breath fogging where the glass had gone dry.
You wiped a palm wide to peer more clearly through,
and saw a world waiting to look brand-new.
I feel winter in every cold wind's bite,
my gloves are wet, my fingers feel tight.
I pause, and I look at the gray blank snow,
but the work still stays, and I can't just go.
It sits so quiet, not moving a still,
high above the world balanced on a hill.
The sun hits its feathers, it flicks one wing,
and time seems to pause for this fragile thing.
They fumbled with the handle, lost their key,
a repairman would cost them twenty-three.
They kicked the wall, they twisted, they tried,
the lock refused to budge — now they just cried.
I bought these shoes because they looked so
serious, like they'd never skip or go
but now I'm sliding on the tile floor,
why did I want *more* than cute and sore?
The zipper digs in where my skin feels cold,
these jeans are threadbare, stiff, and old.
I try to lift it up but still can't pull,
and now my heart feels kind of full.
I tap my card but it won't take my fare,
the machine's offline from head down to stair.
A red message blinks on its frozen screen,
and I miss my train, stuck in this bleak little scene.
He treats the whole trip as a chance for a ride,
tells jokes, gives advice, talks very inside.
He points out landmarks from memory's map,
but I'm stuck in this chat — poor conversation trap.
You run fast but your left shoe's lace
won't stay tied through this final race.
You try skipping, but it only leads to flip,
and down you go—grass laughs as you trip.
She scaled the fence without a care for the gate,
she missed her ride but not her favorite date.
A friend found her a seat in the front row spot,
they didn't check IDs—how'd she get this shot?
You left your towel in a neat white fold,
still warm from where your back used to hold.
I found it here, still trying to stay dry,
curled like a question it never could ask me why.
She typed "by" but the screen said "meant,"
Her message now reads like she's spooked or bent.
She tries again, but the app still wants to say
"Butterfly ballet," not "buy this cray."
I left the tube open without the cap,
now the sink looks like a gelatin trap.
White bubbles spread all across the foam,
my toothbrush sighs—this feels like its home.
The flicker feels familiar, almost too old,
like moments once caught in a soft-glowed gold.
She reaches to fix it, her hand starts to shake,
the bulb never breaks, but the silence does take.
You twist the pencil, it's all splintered wood,
the sharpener just grinned where it once stood.
It promised a point, but got stuck on the blade,
now you walk to class with a stub in a parade.
It was the perfect kind of quiet at noon,
the kind that screams disaster is coming soon.
One tiny breath from a kid turned into a puff,
now the party's just a mess and bad stuff.
You watch them lift into the wide blue sky,
one by one they vanish, slowly die.
You whisper hopes you'll never live to blame,
each tiny parachute carries your name.
You check your phone, it's down to three bars,
desperate for any kind of Wi-Fi stars.
You gesture like Gandalf, waving your wave,
hoping this magic makes your screen feel brave.
She spends hours chasing a sunset's sharp view,
the light shifts too fast, and she loses it too.
She takes fifty bad shots—no good ones will click,
now the café wall's her new favorite old brick.
You open the fridge and it hits you with smell,
the air is still thick from the bacon from hell.
You try to flip slices but they stick, so you flip,
your grip lets the tongs take a slide off the lip.

topic: steaming coffee in a blue mug
lines: The morning light hits my steaming brew,
the way it curls feels more than a view.
I sip the warmth, but the day won't stay,
it slips like steam from my empty hands away.
You found a new kind of art on your yard,
it's splashed where your rug hits the floor, hard.
The dog ran through puddles and left a small trail,
you laugh until you see socks that are pale.
He watches the fish eat with quiet grace,
their mouths popping fast at the tank's wide face.
He's been here for hours, no one ever told
how something so simple could feel so bold.
She always showed up late, still caught my door,
her laugh was warm even if she ran sore.
We'd plan the next thing we would do, so then,
I couldn't remember where or when.
Her smile stretches wider than the sky,
the kids chase shadows as they slide by.
She watches them run, her face begins to grow
with a light no sunset could outdo or know.
They leave their phone alone, let the ringer stay off,
and listen to silence instead of a cough.
The screen glows dim, too far to be near,
but they wait for a message from last year.

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: I tried to stretch it past its final snap,
now the stapler's stuck, no longer on the map.
I yank and twist to free the tangled twist,
but end up with a paper cut on my wrist.
She hasn't checked her phone all morning—smart head,
She memorized the code years ago, she said.
No fraying router cords, no searching screen scroll,
Her confidence stays strong—password is her goal.
You have a detailed and carefully planned plot,
but your action figure just stares at the spot.
The villain's sword misses by far and by clash,
yet you cheer for the fight with an inner child's flash.
You press your palm to the windowpane's glass,
the sun warms your skin where you touch it, grass.
Jelly clings to you, a fading scent,
the lunch bell rings, and the moment is spent.
My phone froze twice this morning—how could it fail?
I stared at the screen, my hopes growing pale.
I took off the case, checked the ports, lost my cap,
and screamed into the void it had become a trap.
You swear the sniffles are some magical cure,
like winter's cold air is a sneeze-filled lure.
You let the heat blast all the moisture so dry,
then sneeze in meetings without even a reply.
I haven't mailed them, but I still like to write,
my desk glows soft with the morning's faint light.
Each card shows a view from a distant, blue sea,
and I wonder if you'd write one just for me.
You remember the party that left you a blast,
how the colors flew out far and real fast.
Now confetti's still tangled in your hair,
you try not to flinch when brushing with care.
My app says "Updating!" but the progress bar
hasn't moved since I said "Okay, let's get this mar."
The wheel keeps spinning, acting like I'd spin
a prize if I waited long enough to win.
She kicks off her shoes and leaves her boots,
the earth drinks her rage down to the roots.
Each step makes a loud and guilty splash,
the mud turns her white jeans stained and ash.
You thought the cliffs had the best possible view,
the sky was perfect, a flawless pale blue.
You took a hundred great photos of that shot,
only to realize all look just like the lot.
They've been left here through every storm and rain,
dust has settled where the soles still remain.
Some are mismatched, one lone shoe per pair,
others rest neatly up by the stair.
She found a dry leaf near the fading sun,
and whispered to it, "We're not quite done."
She moved the pot where the light will bend,
and waited for signs it might still mend.
She left the cart keys somewhere far apart,
it's not worth a panic, but breaks her heart.
She walks down each aisle with a tired smile,
the store plays old songs as the minutes pile.
His face is locked on the spinning loading screen,
He mutters something that he does not mean.
He pries his eyes away but can't seem to hold,
The app just sits there, stuck where he was told.
You wake up to the ghost of the boss's old call,
your dreams still wired to punch a clock at the mall.
Your brain auto-loads every Monday task,
but you lie there and dream, pretending to ask.
You watch the flutter where it makes a pause,
it lands like a dream with no real cause.
Your eyes follow the soft arc of its wing,
as if summer itself took a new spring.
You find it by accident, with mounting dread,
it's a rabbit curled up hiding in your head.
It thumps and whimpers, claiming it's so snug,
you forgot it was there when you first dug.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: You tuck the blanket's edge into a fold,
your fingers linger where my cold ones hold.
The TV hums soft, and you feel so near,
like this moment could stretch through the entire year.
Your phone just buzzed, but it's not a call,
It vibrated once like a lost little ball.
You check the screen — no name, no "text," no "miss,"
Just silence holding its breath for your bliss.
I don't have change, the machine won't take cash,
I bang my fist in frustration, trying to smash.
Now guards are asking for proof of my fare,
I whisper "out of order" into my despair.
You catch her mid-pounce before it goes spill,
she bats at the rim, the bowl never does fill.
The droplets land softly, then spread on the rug,
you laugh as she purrs and your sleeve starts to tug.
The clouds let loose with a cold, steady rain,
The bus is late for the tenth time again.
Her clothes are now dripping and fully soak,
She mutters a joke only misery spoke.

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: July hits me like a hot new glow,
my forehead's slick as raw pizza dough.
I wipe my brow but it just won't stop,
it's a full-on sweatshirt fabric crop.
I never believed that this year would be spring,
now color and scent are my favorite thing.
The morning is soft and the petals are light,
the tulips all stretch to their fullest height.
You take off your shoes and you press your bare feet,
the morning is quiet, the floor holds no heat.
You trace where the sun never comes near the stone,
yet still you stand there, warm only in bone.
You toss the spatula into the air,
the perfect arc, it lands with flair.
One hand, two flips — it's smooth as flip,
I swear you could juggle eggs and not trip.
She dreams of silence in borrowed hours,
but the beat from next door rules her showers.
Her hands press against the thinning bass,
as if she could hush the music through glass.
I thought I'd rinse it but somehow it went
on the wall in a spiral, half-tube still spent.
Now it's clogged up the drain and looks like a tub
of regret I can't scrub or wash out with rub.
I watched you move it like it was all in play,
now it's lying crooked, far from the fray.
That knight sure took a tumble when it fell,
but please don't act like this is heaven or hell.
We tried on each other's shoes to find our size,
glancing at reflections in shop-store eyes.
You said nothing but your laugh felt like you took
me somewhere familiar—like a memory hook.
My fish stares at me like he finally sees,
I hold my breath — he's judging if I freeze.
He swims in circles, shimmering with gold,
then swallows a flake twice too big and bold.
You dig with flair but keep falling into dirt,
your favorite flannel now soaked through your shirt.
You think this yard is the only safe place,
but come back tomorrow—it's a new acorn race.
You stare at the photo that still makes you look
like someone who studied in college's old book.
Your bangs were that way, your clothes styled so hair,
but time moved along, and that person is there.

topic: someone handing you a surprise gift
lines: They place the box in your open hand,
you recognize the paper, but not the brand.
Their eyes light up with a silent smile,
you unwrap the moment for just a while.
I miss the quiet that settled us calm,
your head on my chest and my fingers in palm.
I miss the soft cadence of stories we read,
the way you'd fall asleep curled close at my need.
I nearly lost my cool when they jumped the row,
claiming they were late and needed to show.
I stepped back twice to let them make their move,
but now I'm just waiting for my patience to prove.
You're squeezing the tube from the wrong end, paste,
it's all just minty, useless waste.
Half the tube's still full, you'll soon feel the bump,
and face this sad, un-spent toothpaste slump.
You grip the ruler as if it were a thought,
a tool to shape the ideas you've been taught.
It taps a path you're sure will lead the way,
and marks each lesson for the days ahead, they say.

topic: checking if you have enough for gas
lines: You pull up to the pump praying your tank won't fail,
then count your cash and swear your bank is a jail.
The gas app says "cheap today—$3.88 per app,"
but when you pay, you're just short by a trap.
You see a feather drift through the sky,
it floats where the clouds are so high.
It twirls around the old willow trees,
until the wind carries it in a gentle breeze.
I missed the date the bill was due,
my screen turned red, not even slightly blue.
Now every clock just ticks me late,
and guilt sits heavy, a silent weight.
The shovel hits something hard beneath the cold,
you dig again with a hand growing bold.
A crack spreads wide, the ice feels so near,
your breath hangs still in the gray white fear.
I stop to read the claim on the roadside view,
it says this product cures everything not true.
They promise joy, discounts, a reason to buy,
while snowflakes fall and paint the screen with sky.
At two a.m., they're still in their lane,
spilling jokes from some weird other brain.
They send a meme with timing so live,
the group chat knows they're meant to thrive.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: They hit "share" again, unsure of the post,
the joke's gone stale since the last time they toast.
Their face lights up, but it's fear that it shows,
deep down they know, but no one else knows.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: I saw my name pop up beneath a post,
the kind of comment you read from the most
oblivious stranger—could this be mine?
A cosmic wink or just the internet's sign.

topic: checking if you have enough for gas
lines: She checks the gauge—empty as a dry tank,
then counts her cash against the cost at the bank.
The pump reads "$45.99" and gets quite a bit near,
she mutters, "This can't be real—it's way too dear."
A flake lands and winks like a tiny test,
then melts on my shoulder and starts to rest.
It trickles down slowly along the seam,
like a cold, quiet tear turned into cream.
You paid five bucks for this sad little deal,
But you thought it would taste like a Parisian meal.
The beans probably cost a dime at most,
Now you sip and you silently roast.
You endlessly scroll through the hungry app scroll,
selecting dishes you think you have control
Each item was meant to be your comfort and hope,
but nothing satisfies how bad you want to cope.
She fills the empty jug from morning till dry,
humming a tune only she can imply.
No shadow of worry crosses her head,
she dances through chores, feeling like warm bread.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: It settles between us soft as a fold,
warm and heavy in your quiet hold.
Your breathing slows, your shoulders start to drift,
and I don't move in case I might lift.
The photo on my card shows a younger face,
a time and a place I don't quite embrace.
I swipe through classes, feeling the slight
of being stuck between past and present night.
You say it's fine if I don't match my wear,
one sock blue, the other full of air.
You laugh when I ask if this feels strange to you,
then call me your kind of quirky and true.
I walk through the room with a steady foot's pride,
comfort tucked neatly behind every stride.
I don't chase trends — I wear what I choose,
no stilettos, no pain that I refuse.
You open your laptop but dread the start,
the weight of it all still sits heavy in your heart.
A deep breath helps you begin to clear,
the clock says midnight but hope is still near.
I trace the creases from my last known hand,
each wrinkle maps a path this paper once planned.
The edges curl inward, resisting the fold,
as if it's holding on to something too old.
That dent on the top is more than just a dent,
the whole lid's warped now, completely bent.
I tried to pop open what was left of the lid,
but the beans stayed sealed tight, well out of my hid.

topic: someone spilling punch on the rug
lines: The bowl slipped just as they turned around with a crash,
sending ruby punch across the floor with a smash.
It blended with the rug in a wild new hue,
and now it's your job to clean it up, you.
You wake to sunlight as Monday fades to dawn,
The weekend's laughter still feels freshly gone.
You leap into your day with a smile and a jump,
The coffee hits you—no more midnight bump.
You gave not a single hint or clue,
Yet every detail was sharp and true.
From snacks to the playlist, your secret plan,
Was genius in motion — you are a party man.
She cuts in front of the guy buying meat,
as if she's late for some emergency treat.
She doesn't know how the grocery store zone
works—everyone starts to politely moan.
A plastic bag still clings where it drift,
fluttering like a ghost of some old gift.
It probably flew here from some day ago,
when life felt lighter, soft, and slow to show.
You pile the pasta high on your dinner plate,
the cheese lands dusted, but it's never too late.
You laugh off the mess like a summer shower,
that small cheese grater has pure flavor power.
I tied my last shoelace to be a makeshift hook,
the kid laughed as we walked where the park had took.
We sat by the fountain, called it "the sea,"
and caught plastic bags that looked wild and free.
The bark cuts through the hush of the night loud,
It sounds so fierce, so lonely, and proud.
I wish I could walk down that street once more through,
but silence is safest when memories are true.
She sways in the backyard where it's meant for a rest,
a bird tries to build there beside her small nest.
The chain starts to whine like it's groaning with rust,
but she laughs, says the swing knows the secret of trust.
They said this was the future, all smart and stream,
now they call it a "buffering" dream.
The screen just spins in a fake, calm load,
while silence screams in silent, frozen mode.
She stirs her drink, a bitter black,
the clock counts hours with nothing to lack.
Her thoughts won't slow—her mind is unkind,
she sips alone, the silence so behind.
She sips her latte while watching the flight,
the neon glow flickers too harsh for the light.
She wonders if this small joy is worth pay,
and counts how far the money went away.
You scatter the seed in the morning's green light,
the robin wants snacks and it knows how to fight.
It bobs on one leg, flaps fast with each wing,
a tiny thief bossing the whole spring thing.
You didn't hesitate when you made the pick,
this film's your old friend, not just a quick trick.
You watched every scene again, still you two
would hit all the notes that you both knew.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: You posted a shot of the sky turned to gold,
no caption, no story, no reason why told.
The colors were sharp, but your eyes left the light,
and now every scroll feels a little less bright.
She wags her whole body if she sees your tail,
she follows your steps along the same trail.
Her joy is a constant, upbeat, cheerful bark,
she greets the whole world even when it's dark.

topic: a forgotten lunchbox on the floor
lines: You spot your lunchbox where you left it to find,
it's messy but there, so you leave it behind.
The sandwich is soggy, but still worth the eat,
the sun warms it gently, adds a soft heat.
You left the shelter too soon for the rain,
Sodden from walking, it all happens again.
Now you wring your socks out in the cold air,
Hoping there's somewhere nearby they'll dry where.
I left the slow cooker to turn my stew,
while I doodled something weird nobody drew.
The carrots look better than the meat,
but it's all so warm, even the air feels sweet.
I watched your knight go down without a fall,
no shout, no challenge—just the way it all
went quiet after, how the board turned still,
and left me wondering if my move was ill.
You're flipping through every crumpled page,
trying to rebuild your memory cage.
There's order in chaos, you'll soon find your space,
you're not behind—just not in a race.
He watches the clock but never moves as slow,
still thinking he's thirty years or so ago.
His coffee cools while he raises his hand,
