misses the beat by half a second—no band.
I drag couches and chairs into the room,
pretending this hideout can shield us from zoom.
We laugh as the pillows all gently fall,
until our blanket wall feels like it's tall.
She shouts her wares down every busy block,
her voice is clear when most would hit the stock.
Her calls are sharp, not shrill or low like treat,
a daily feat that turns heads on the street.
You've been waiting here since the morning wait,
the bus is an hour late, now you're stuck in freight.
Black clouds loom low as the wind starts to rain,
you swear it's planning to become a train.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: She tried to train him to wear a party hat,
but his ears kept flopping where the sky sat.
He'd spin around at the sight of the top,
then bark at the moon like a madman on stop.
You feel the wind in its steady wave,
as if the field were alive and brave.
The tall grass bends in a wild sway,
you laugh and dance to its green, wild play.
She zipped into my lane like it was her own zone,
tapping her screen while she made a sharp phone.
I braced for a crash, but the car just took swerve,
she waved with a grin—had the whole world's nerve.
She opens her umbrella under the sky,
and offers you space to stay dry.
You hesitate, then say yes to this share,
and suddenly strangers have lighter air.
The sky blushes quietly into light,
the sand still holds her in the morning's height.
She walks where the foam barely touches waves,
pretending she'll find magic in hollowed-out caves.
You sit on the steps near the edge of the park,
the crowd thinks you're just some bored strumming lark.
Your fingers move fast but your chords don't quite fold,
yet somehow they manage to sound kind of bold.
You watch the light waver, turn soft as it dim,
a halo of dust swirls around its old rim.
Through every dark pause, you swear you still see,
a signal the night is not total or free.
I gave up trying to flip a single flake,
this morning's breakfast now tastes like a cake.
I let it turn dark, crisp, perfect in char,
my kitchen's new hero—my proudly burnt star.
You thought this wait would be easy and fun,
but the roof's been leaking since you first run.
Raindrops now pattern your leg in a slide,
while the world goes by, dry as can be outside.
I wake to the sky turning pink and glow,
my breath becomes mist above the snow.
The ice is so clear, I can see the lake's edge,
I vow to come back before this light pledge.
She hits the pillow like it's her favorite pose,
tail flicking like she just kicked off her hose.
You watch in awe as she slides to the floor,
certain she's bought out the yoga supply store.
That thing's held together more by rust,
the seat's dry as the last bite of crust.
It creaks the same song with every sway,
like it's begging to finally just decay.
I didn't run from the wind or the storm,
let my boots take the brunt of the cold and the warm.
I stepped deep into every glossy puddle,
proud of my path through the soaked-up muddle.
We'd catch each other's eyes, then break into grin,
some absurd giggle we couldn't help but begin.
Now nothing seems funny, except maybe the cause
of how we laughed once at nothing, now just applause.
You walk the shore in search of the perfect view,
the kind of light that feels a little true.
But every shot looks staged, a bit too framed,
as if the place needs your lens to be named.
The last slice is close but just too near,
someone else has their eye on it, loud and clear.
You wait for them to say "Go ahead, you grab,"
but no one moves—your hope cools off the slab.
They took my last bite, left nothing but crumbs away,
It's happened so often it feels normal today.
I fake a small smile, say "keep 'em," with a grin,
While watching my portion grow gradually thin.
I knocked the shaker off the counter—now white,
it dusts my floor like a ghost in the night.
This powdery mess isn't easy to clean,
but I laugh and say, "Yes, what a scene!"
He stands in the airport terminal's wide aisle,
shouting praise, his voice an awkward style.
I wish he'd whisper truths instead of these lies,
but I can't see if anyone shares my eyes.
The fog rolls slow across the morning rise,
blurring what my tired eyes used to prize.
It shrouds the old white church where the town
once gathered—now ghostly, like a crown.
The hunger makes your thoughts begin to grow,
the clock ticks by but you're not sure where to go.
You pass the apples, the soup, the meat — you can't,
your empty stomach feels like roots without a plant.
I pretend that I'm used to this endless, gray calm,
though my mood needs no balm, not even a balm.
Out there the sky could be some kind of rave,
I'd rather stay inside my quiet cave.
Your flip-flop lies sideways near the front door,
you must've torn it off in a dramatic roar.
Now it's a trap for guests and pets and heel,
I step around it every time I feel.
I pump my legs hard to swing real high,
the chains groan louder as I near the sky.
The iron's gone soft with a coat of rust,
but I close my eyes anyway—I trust.
The soda hit your speakers—foggy blast,
but somehow the old songs won't stay fast.
You listen to the static, barely sing,
it's not the music—it's the moment, the thing.
They left the password on a yellowed spot,
Some genius who forgot to toss it got
It taped to the back of the office chair,
Now everyone pulls their hair to stare.
You claimed this bench from one end to seat,
I'm crammed against your backpack's heat.
Not an inch of space or social cue,
You're blocking the screen—let me see my view.
I toss my shoe into the swirling air,
it lands beside the monster in the lair.
My cat goes feral, takes a perfect leap,
and swats the dust bunny down the laundry heap.
You toss your fries up in the air,
Hoping the wind will tell you where.
A pigeon swoops for the tasty snack,
Now you're racing birds down the city track.
I dream of a donut, that perfect first bite,
the way it feels wrong yet somehow feels right.
I stare at the vending machine, wish it would shake,
but maybe tomorrow I'll have that soft cake.

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: They said the review would change how it was told,
but you still picture the morning cup of gold.
You skip past the complaints, read only the bar,
and smile at the line that calls you a star.
I turn the recipe into a real-life mess,
the smoke alarm honks its metallic bless.
I taste my mistake and I know I will lose,
but next time I'll read the steps before I choose.
She thinks she's hiding it, but I have no clue,
the decorations clash in a wild, weird hue.
They'll all show up with a "surprise" loud cry,
while she keeps asking, "Why can't I just spy?"
She stops to check if her art is in the eye
of anyone passing under this open sky.
There's no sign of a reaction—no hint, no clue—
but the poster's colors still shine bright and true.
You squeezed the toothpaste from one tiny tube,
your reflections frozen in ice and in cube.
The bathroom still smells like a memory haze,
while mint lingers soft like old quiet days.
You let it drip like slow-moving spread,
warm from the toaster, just cut from the bread.
A glossy sheen, that perfect deep gold,
you pause to savor what your knife can't hold.
Your showerhead sputters like an old jet,
you turn it off—just can't quite get wet.
You hum along to a fading song,
for warmth that never seems to come along.
You found one dumbbell on the dusty floor,
but its twin remains elusive, as before.
You tried to work out without the full set,
but balance feels wrong, you just can't get.
She waves her umbrella in sudden rain,
I pretend I don't hear her offer again.
Her hand reaches out for a shared hold,
my feet stay soaked in this unfamiliar cold.
You watch your cat leap toward the water spill,
It's not to drink, you know—it's just to kill.
With paws mid-air and a wild little dash,
It sends the bowl flying in an instant crash.
You crumpled your wrapper with all of its might,
you left it discarded beneath the faint light.
You vow never to eat more than just what you keep,
but the snack aisle calls out to you far too deep.
She leaves the dishes stacked all alone,
a silent monument like cold stone.
Her touch was soft when she moved through the room,
now the sink coughs up remnants of our gloom.
That rabbit's nose moves like a little bean,
twitching wildly, like some sniffing machine.
It scans the air for some invisible clue,
convinced there's lasagna stuck somewhere in view.
She watches the horizon through tear-filled eyes,
as if the sea alone holds all the wise.
The wind moves grains of salt and loose sand,
and she still reaches out for your faraway hand.
You thought the flash would mimic the softest eye,
but it lit the room like a midday sky.
I won't be the one to throw the blame,
just let the photo stay out of the frame.
She taped it up high, just inside the past,
but time moves too fast for anything last.
The ink is all faded, the corners all frayed,
it stays in its place like a ghost in the shade.
A single crumb marks the cleanest spot,
like nature's punctuation left as a dot.
I laugh out loud, maybe it's childish joy,
but I bend down like some sweet young boy.

topic: a quiet moment on the porch
lines: I sip my coffee and pretend it's all calm,
though my phone still buzzes against my palm.
The birds chirp something I can't be bothered to say,
and I wish this peace would just go and stay away.
I walk through parks to find my perfect view,
the kind that sticks in memory like glue.
I'll never stay here long enough to keep
the peace that lingers just before sleep.

topic: finding a five in the couch
lines: You pull a crumpled five from the couch with some luck,
It slips between the cushions again, slightly stuck.
You stare into the fabric's familiar deep,
Wishing for change as your eyes start to sleep.
She reads the sour smell like a warning note,
and feels the dairy rise up her throat.
One single drop was all it took to drop
the plan for pancakes — now she'll have to stop.
You let the heavy air out like a slow prayer,
your breath follows behind every stair.
You press it into your face, your cold palm,
and feel the hours soften, slow, into calm.
Their faces blur into a distant gray,
They talk, but dreams have stolen the day.
Her eyes drift past the screen to skies,
She imagines life without disguise.

topic: a forgotten lunchbox on the floor
lines: You left your lunchbox out where someone could steal,
but maybe they saved it for their next meal.
Maybe they saw something good when they found
the pickles clinking loud, like silver that's sound.
She planned the pop for the exact right time,
her perfect moment to shine in the prime.
The crowd gasped loud, then gave a loud cheer,
as confetti flew past the stunned onlooker's ear.
My face is stuck five inches from the TV screen,
I'm not in love—I'm just too lazy to clean.
The bag of chips in my lap is now empty, snack,
I pause the movie to find another track.
She doesn't give a single damn or a care,
she'll nap on the top of the fridge or a stair.
You whisper your love but it's never been known—
she only purrs if you speak in her chosen tone.
She slammed the brake for a split-second dash,
but the curb got her tire in a pinching crash.
Her phone buzzed with texts asking who to blame,
though no one had seen the whole mess by her name.
I read the whole wall from top to my head,
Each tag seemed to say something that was said.
They're just left behind in spray-painted names,
Like echoes of voices or burning flames.
Her fingers drag through the book's slow pace,
eyes flicker up with a sleepy face.
There's quiet power in this unhurried calm,
each page a gentle, ancient balm.
That backyard swing won't hold me on the seat,
my butt slides out—it's barely still complete.
It rusts and creaks and smells of wet mold,
but no one will fix it because it's too old.
You fumble the chain with your shaking key,
the U-lock resists, it won't let you be.
Your hands grow numb, they begin to shiver,
but dawn will come—so will spring, so will deliver.
I tried to dab ketchup but it just won't go,
it trickled down slowly like syrupy flow.
It splattered right there where my shirt meets my eye,
I ask myself loudly, "Why do I try?"
It buzzes every time there might be calls,
but the phone is quiet behind these walls.
I check my stats—steps, heart rate, all feel true,
but my life's still scrolling in monochrome blue.
You trade accuracy for twice the stead,
your thumb flies wild while trying to read.
Your fingers ache from holding that strain,
you'll type it all wrong — just do it again.
I dipped my spoon too fast, and the honey run,
dripping slow from where the sunlight won.
It clung to metal like it wanted to pour
down my wrist—sweet accident, but I'll take just more.
A thousand ants march single file in line,
you wonder how they built this tiny mine.
They carry crumbs like secrets they won't scream,
yet somehow your fear feels real as a dream.
I left the jug out to bask in the dry,
no drop to hide, nothing to deny.
This cracked clay vessel is pride's own proof,
it stands beneath my open, sunlit roof.
You used to laugh while you swung out to play,
pretending the sky was just inches away.
The chain still groans in the same old wood,
though no one has sat there since you grew and stood.
You feel it in the stillness above the air,
the hawk watches from its sky lair.
Your shadow moves slow like a shadow on stone,
and silence has a sharp edge all its own.
It promised a meal that would never quite rise,
now drooping in shame at its certain demise.
She checks the oven again, cracks the door,
but there's clearly no magic left to restore.
I got stuck beneath the iron bar,
my breath went out like a fallen star.
The gym was silent, no one came near—just pain,
my body screamed but my mind stayed numb as rain.
You watch the yolk slip free from its shell,
a fragile world falling into hell.
Your fingers hover, afraid to let them run,
but the mess is already half undone.
I walk where the tide has just taken flight,
the sky blazes with impossible height.
There's no one here but the wind feels alone,
I carve my name on a rock with a stone.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: You keep checking your sleeve, can't shake that weird feel,
afraid it will unravel and somehow reveal
the moment you'll drop it or it slips and you catch
the edge of your shirt—no time to find a match.
I saw your face and I couldn't resist,
I saved it quick from my scroll through the list.
It wasn't some fluke or a lucky shot,
I hit the double-tap button—right on the spot.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: I'd swear the blanket waged a full-on fight,
it twisted tight through every inch of night.
There it sat—king of the crumpled heap,
while I shivered quietly on the sleep.
The paper rolls keep getting stuck,
but they never say it's bad enough to chuck.
They fix it with such calm in their hand,
and it lands so softly, just like planned.
I repotted it twice since it hit the soil,
I even wrapped the stems in some fancy foil.
It lasted a full day before turning gray,
maybe I should just throw it away.
They always show up five minutes late,
Miss assignments with no real debate.
The professor lets them slide it off,
While the rest of us fake a bad cough.
I step around the cart to get me pass,
it wobbles wide and nearly hits the grass.
I mutter curses all the way to stop,
then push it back where someone can find a prop.

topic: a taxi driver yelling on phone
lines: I cruise through the chaos, I know this my zone,
he yells into his Bluetooth, full-volume phone.
"I'm the king of this street!" he shouts through the seat,
"These backroads? They fear me," he calls out with elite.
You hold your coat too tight, but it won't wear,
it hangs from you like winter on a stair.
You're sifting tags and sizes, looking through,
until the mirror whispers, "This feels true."
You used to think the clock was frozen in the past,
but now you know time drags when meetings last.
The wheels of progress don't budge, just spin,
your patience thinning like old, worn skin.
I trace the names we wrote in the past,
some faded now, the spray paint's last.
The wall still feels so close, so near,
though we haven't met in years, my dear.
He's proud he never carries any cash,
but now the screen shows "Declined—Smash!"
He fumbles through his wallet for the card,
and drops it three times in a single yard.
You got caught in a sudden cold pour,
your shoes soaked from the puddle-strewn shore.
They reek of mud and wet grassy smell,
but you laugh anyway—can't help it, you tell.
They left a snack halfway through a late-night snack,
now the "K" key's jammed and won't make a track.
It wasn't just dust—was actual bread,
and maybe a little bit of peanut spread.
You erase your name from every hand,
afraid your words might somehow brand.
You hope no one will ever read
what scribbled thoughts might still bleed.
You hold the net as if it's frozen still,
though your hands shake with a quiet thrill.
You kneel in the grass, too low to bend,
chasing ghosts you'll never manage to send.
You're lost in the scroll, but it's past your prime,
The hours have slipped from your tired climb.
Your screen gives off a soft blue glow,
And the moon outside wants to say hello.
The rain keeps on falling, it won't stop to pour,
she slammed every window and every door.
Her nerves are completely worn down and raw,
"This storm," she says, "is breaking the law."
In my dream I'm the rhythm of work's perfect flow,
My team hums along, spot on, not a thing below.
I answer the boss's urgent, late-night call,
And wake up still smiling, the best of us all.

topic: a coffee cup on the curb
lines: I never won a lottery or luck,
but your name was etched in the cup when I stuck
my fingers around its warm, chipped lid,
and wondered if this was fate's quiet bid.
Your eyes say "sleep" but your thumb won't sleep,
you fall deeper into the scroll so deep.
It buzzes, flashes—your only true phone,
the room gets brighter when you're slightly alone.
She moves through the room like she wants it to slow,
The quiet kitchen lit by a faint after-glow.
Her lips find my hand without making a sound,
I melt in my stand, a man barely unbound.
You bawl through the final, tragic scene,
then sniffle into the popcorn machine.
You blame every character for the blame,
but cry just as hard when the credits roll—same.
You trip on the projector cord and get flung
sideways into the screen, which you really lung.
The crowd laughs, so you point and give a thumbs-up sign,
breaking the fourth wall while missing your closing line.
I left my phone charging on the dash,
it fell when a pothole made it crash.
I left all the windows open for air,
now my hair's full of leaves and glare.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: You kneel in the dirt, the world a wet mess,
hoping today will be your baking success.
But every time you try to shape and dig,
the ground laughs at your little mud pie gig.
I used to breeze through the mall for a shop,
now every coffee feels like a tight drop.
I check my card before I can even spend,
it's a game I play till the budget hits end.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: She was hitting her stride, with a perfect smooth flow,
then the sudden big sneeze made her whole body go.
She pulled off her earbud and swore at the cap,
her sentence now missing a pretty big gap.
Your app opens to a frozen black screen,
it acts like your phone isn't even your machine.
You tap, you wait, but nothing will load,
and now you're stuck in reboot mode.

topic: leaving a note on the fridge
lines: They left a note on the fridge without a clue,
It read "Love you" but misspelled your name as "doo."
The milk was out, and the cheese looked like a leak,
Yet somehow, they still called the mess a perfect week.
You twist the plastic lid off the red coffee cap,
the steam rises like a mess you can't trap.
You chug the last bit, your hands still need,
but the clock won't budge, it won't bleed.
My mind goes blank like it forgot how to thought,
but I smile and nod as if I was brought
into some kind of focus, sharp and in zone,
when really I'm faking the whole damn tone.
She double-taps with practiced thumb,
A ghost of validation to come.
Her eyes stay locked on every post,
As if the world's decided by most.
You hit repeat, the track starts to play,
you hum along to make the ache feel away.
The lyrics don't fix it, but they still give hope,
and somehow you breathe easier when you cope.

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: You hear an old rubber band pop and snap,
it's been stuck in the stapler's worn-out trap.
You try to fix it but the tape won't glue,
the whole thing's ancient—no faith in it true.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: You snapped the picture without knowing the scene,
how much it would later come to mean.
Her laugh turned into something else—a smile,
you caught her in the middle of a while.
They race down the aisle with their groceries in tow,
shouting how they still have six stores to go.
One stumbles and knocks their first bag on the trip,
a tomato rolls free and a jar starts to slip.
I turned my back for one brief second—sight!
The dog had teeth on my birthday cake, so tight.
Frosting now covers his face and fur,
I shout "That's my dessert, not a snack for you, sir!"
Her hands move slow, they make a steady hush,
the wool turns into something soft and blush.
She sets the scarf aside but won't let it lay—
her fingers pause too long before they stay.
The doors are sliding shut, and there's nowhere to now,
you count every beat and you don't know how.
You scream and they don't hear your ragged train,
and you curse the silence, the cruel kind of pain.
I wipe her eyes with a damp paper joke,
She pretends not to laugh beneath her cloak.
A tear slips out—she hides it too sly,
I hand her my sleeve to keep everything dry.
The heavy meal left my head filled with food,
and now my whole body feels out of mood.
I seek a quiet spot just to take some rest,
my eyes close gently into a soft nest.
The toaster coughs up a slice full of smoke,
he waves at the cloud like it means to choke.
He grabs instant coffee and starts to brew,
muttering that this morning's already blue.
I tap my thumb in rhythm with the feed,
I tell myself I'll stop—it's just one need.
My pillow glows with blue from the screen,
this midnight ritual feels less like a machine.
I tried to fix my hair but ruined my mood,
the glitter clung to my tongue like old food.
I gave up, let the mess have its lazy flow,
the confetti's still there, giving off some odd glow.
I typed the word but it changed my whole spell,
and somehow my phone said "butterfly fell."
I stared at the screen and imagined its wings,
how life gets rewritten by dictionary things.

topic: a quiet moment on the porch
lines: You call this a moment? Just another swing,
a porch light flickering, the same old thing.
A breeze never comes, but your nerves still freeze,
you wait for the front door to creak from the keys.
You tapped the calendar for the wrong date,
Now your apology feels stale and straight.
They stare at you with a quiet shock,
while time keeps ticking like a stopped clock.
You call it gardening, I call it a crime,
the robin just stares, covered in grime.
You sweat through this mess like some endless chore,
while the bird's got the easier job, and more.
A flash of white fur caught my eye in the spot,
I paused my work and took a quick photo shot.
A twitch in the corner, a dart with the ear,
The rabbit's a joker, I laugh with a cheer.
She stares at her phone like it's one last screen,
the blue light tries to pretend it doesn't mean
to steal what's left of her will to log
off and fall into deep sleep, not just fog.

topic: checking if you have enough for gas
lines: She checks the gauge—there's barely air in the tank,
but she's got savings stashed at the gas station bank.
She knows every route by the last mile,
and drives off proud with her quiet, smug smile.
You stare at the screen, fingers hover unseen,
a notification just turned status green.
Your thumb hovers briefly before you tap,
the crowd in your head gives a silent clap.
You watch the last pixel flicker and glow,
your screen goes dark while the music still plays low.
This moment feels older the longer you hold now,
but time slips away just like power runs out how.

topic: a bike locked to a pole
lines: Her bike is chained to a rusty old place,
like she's planning a solo comeback race.
Wheels still wobble, the seat's way too spin,
but she claims it's vintage—the best kind to begin.
The screen remains frozen and motionless still,
a spinning circle tries to pretend it will fill.
They promised the episode would finally show,
the Wi-Fi's been down all day long, somehow though.
You clicked "Buy It Now" with pure holiday joy,
but now you regret it, this purchase will destroy.
Your room looked fine in that optimistic light,
until you unwrapped your brand-new furniture fright.
She watched the cat go after some strange spot,
circling the wall like it had taken a shot.
Maybe it smelled something old, like glue,
or saw ghosts in the sky, the color of blue.
You click refresh, but the page still isn't fast,
your coffee's gone cold since it hasn't been passed.
Your Zoom call delays for the full minute lag,
you sigh and grab popcorn from your lunchtime bag.
There's only one slice of pizza left,
Did someone take your favorite? Theft?
You check the box, but it's gone to a crumb,
Your stomach growls like a muted drum.
She's all about comfort and casual style,
Her couch is her throne, the world feels a mile.
Popcorn in hand, she's ready for snack,
But halfway through, she rewinds the track.
She texts through the film with her phone in her seat,
The plot gets cut off by the ring tone's repeat.
Popcorn bits fly as she drops a hot mess,
We'll never get what the scene was meant to express.
You laid out the blanket and food so spread,
the breeze through the trees felt soft on your head.
A cloud rolled in fast, turning blue into sky,
now you're soaked and laughing, no hope to stay dry.
I throw my coat off, I can't take this chill,
you turned us from humans into a still.
I'm sweating through shirts in this tiny room,
while winter waits outside in full gloom.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: You spot your first gray strand—it's nature's cold sign,
not a flaw, but life's personal brand and design.
You let it grow out, frame your new silver crown,
no dye could match what you earn from the town.
You think it's been hours that you've just stood still,
the rabbit ignores you—no hint of a thrill.
Its nose twitches fast through the soft, fresh air,
while you wait there, too nervous to dare.
You left your sandwich tucked safely away,
now it's soggy and soft with decay.
The smell hits you sudden, you almost cry,
and wonder what else your bag could deny.
I packed five days of joy into my plans,
drank coffee black and danced with bare hands.
I kicked through leaves and called that morning kick,
now Monday stares, but I won't let it stick.
A smear of purple still on your grin,
It makes your face feel like a birthday pin.
You carry it out like a spark of hope,
The world is softer when joy helps you cope.
You stare at the return policy labeled *fine*,
every sentence feels like a hidden sign.
You open the box but hesitate to read,
what if you bought something you no longer need?
You drop a like with a quiet little sigh,
keep your emoji reactions low and dry.
Then type a text you'll never actually send—
"Hope you find the peace that doesn't have to bend."

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: I hang like a jewel in the morning's cold glass,
the world wakes below in the rustling grass.
Each strand I have spun holds the light in its thread,
my masterpiece glistens where dawnlight is spread.
She keeps both hands off the big, black wheel,
her breath a soft rhythm against the steel.
The passengers nod, they've found their seat,
this nap—it's a feat we all repeat.
She claims they're practical, but lacks true style,
yet dances through the grocery store for a while.
Her shoes may grip the floor and guard her tread,
but she still trips—her confidence now dead.
The toast is now black and it smells like a char,
he pretends it's a bagel from some distant star.
This feels preordained, like Monday's cold fate,
I slide it aside—it's going straight to the plate.
You retrace your steps but there's no clue,
the coffee shop says you never came through.
You recheck every pocket, couch, and lane,
but the keys are still MIA in the rain.
The lake lies quiet beneath this silver still,
My pulse runs wild with the dark's last thrill.
The water hums low, a song so deep,
I'm torn between waking and dreaming sleep.

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: It still holds a little twist of snap,
though the staple slips and falls from the trap.
You don't throw it out when it starts to bend,
your hands remember what it means to mend.
You stare at the grid filled with empty blank,
but a few letters hint at your next bank.
A synonym pops in your head for clue,
the rest begins to fall into your view.
She takes the last bite from the crusty edge,
leaving me a cold little cheese wedge.
I used to love how it stayed hot and warm,
now every slice just looks the same in form.
My glue stick died, and I refused to blame
the humidity or the cheap store-brand frame.
It crumbled quietly, met its sad, slow end—
I cheered its demise like a long-lost friend.
You swore this plant would never have to cry,
but now its leaves all hang and turn dry.
It slumps against the wall, near the floor,
while you keep walking past, choosing to ignore.
That balloon's string gave your whole head quite the twist,
you tried to untangle it with one hand, one wrist.
The more you fussed, the tighter the loop,
now it looks like fun had a parade and a troop.
You wipe the wet streaks from your eyes like a flood,
I count the hours still warm in your blood.
You try to smile but you can't quite hold,
the memory lingers—too tender, too old.
I'm tired of hearing "Don't leave it here to blame,"
It's just my bottle, not some stranger's lost name.
You step on it, twist it, you won't let it spill,
Just leave me alone—this tiny thing won't kill.

topic: a taxi driver yelling on phone
lines: I want this ride, but I don't want to hide,
he argues too loud as we clog up the side.
He yells over traffic about some cheap fare,
I shrink in my seat from his side's angry glare.
He left the noise behind, turned it all down,
now he walks past the clubs without a frown.
The bass was just too much, that same tired old
obsession—now he's found something more bold.
They show every twist in the preview scene,
the whole movie plays out across the screen.
A cryptic message pops up without a clue,
but you'll pay full price just to find it's all true.
The baby screams the whole damn flight,
the cabin air feels way too tight.
Her mother's lost all semblance of mood,
and I'm regretting this airplane food.
You hit send before checking the post,
the teacher's right there in your newsfeed host.
You rush to untag them fast and late,
but it's too late—your shame's in their fate.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: You check your bank app for a midnight thrill,
The balance pops up, it's way above your bill.
You whisper "cash" like a lucky charm you stash,
Then tap the light off and sprint to bed with a dash.
She leans toward the screen to feel the edge,
the hero vows something he can't yet pledge.
The music holds, nothing moves in the still,
and then—lightning cuts through the dark for a thrill.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: The faded roads are still traced in ink,
we once planned our future with coffee and drink.
I trace every mountain, the same old fold,
where we marked dreams in the corners of gold.
She wakes with a yawn but still wears a grin,
her eyes stay half shut, her focus too thin.
She rolls out of bed, a slow, tired rise,
the morning is bright but she's not in the skies.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: You say it's a funny little accident joke,
but I'm halfway to choking, can't ignore the poke.
It's lodged there now—like some weird foreign piece,
you've had your fun, now how do you release?
I left my lunch by the keyboard last mess,
now typing feels like some strange kind of success.
Each letter sticks and I hunt for the key,
I consider charging the class just a small fee.
My socks vanish again — he's sharp when he chew,
the threads hang like frayed flags from his blue.
I left one out, laced with treats, a clever trap,
but he just naps there… maybe it's a new nap.
You raised your ruler high in your hand,
determined to mark every missed brand.
The class all turned toward your sharp point,
while your pointer finger never moved from its joint.
They've left their shoes by the door as a pair,
like a sign that they're staying for a fair.
The handle creaks when they kick off their spin,
warm socks meet bare feet, soft against skin.
You left your bag open, he caught a treat,
Now he's staring out through the street.
One flick of the door and his collar goes loose,
You chase him down sidewalks, a panicked goose.
I stood outside the train with my face at the gate,
having a full-blown panic debate.
My phone had no ticket, my brain played the card,
"Maybe I'll just ride free, even if I get barred."
You tug the zipper upward but it won't rise,
the jeans are now your mortal enemy, no size.
Your friend offers a butter knife for the tip,
but you give up, just use your fingers for the grip.
He counts every tick of the drip from the drop,
but the pipe keeps its rhythm, it won't seem to stop.
His thoughts spiral louder than the noise in his head,
while sleep slips away like a dream off the bed.
You left that pot of last night's stew,
still warm, now stiffening just like you.
The scent lingers in this quiet smell,
but time won't wash what the water can't tell.

topic: socks left in the break room
lines: I found a clue in the break room today—
a neon blue sock, lost in the fray.
I think I saw a co-worker with that spot,
but they said they had no idea and forgot.
She stares into pixels, lost in the screen,
her eyes turn red from all the bright green.
A reminder pops up to make her blink,
but she ignores it, still trying to think.
I watch the fish chew on their sad flake food,
the silence in here fits my quiet mood.
They swim in a circle, then splash the white bowl,
I wonder if fish have a tiny fish soul.
Your phone screen spins like it's solving a sin,
it claims you're connected but not even within.
You tap, you sigh, you try to place the blame,
but nothing loads and it's the exact same.
You drift toward the window seat and aisle,
counting clouds as they pass in silent mile.
Your breath is soft, a quiet little sigh,
while time dissolves into the wide blue sky.
She steps back to admire the growing mess,
her white dress now ruined, she can't confess.
The world might never know how it all goes,
except for the evidence the paint still shows.
I've missed the exit for the tenth time this clue,
the GPS repeats the same tired view.
My hands grip tight, but there's no clear place to turn,
I've driven this road for years and still can't learn.
You bend down to sort out this growing mound,
but socks keep escaping from all the fluff around.
The smell of lavender fills up your scent,
it's chaos and joy—like a wash day event.
I gave my bike lock a hard twist,
but my keys have somehow all missed.
I try my old code, then my lucky code,
the lock won't budge—I'm stuck on this road.
She finds comfort where a dented can still holds,
her fingers trace the metal's wrinkled folds.
It lost its perfect circle, but she keeps its shape,
like love after a crash—still sweet, still escape.
You launched your plane to see how far it could soar,
it dipped and it twisted but never hit the floor.
A sudden gust from the window gave it a breeze,
the air tugged its wings like a playful tease.
She flipped through the pages but never did read,
her notes were all crumpled where panic had spread.
A red stamp bled through the top corner—no grade,
and still she believes it might somehow all fade.
You think it's magic how the light finds its gleam,
dripping gold through branches like a stream.
You pause to take a picture, strike your cute pose,
while ignoring the mess the sun also shows.
She hits her closet like a weekend raid,
brings out the neon like some weird parade.
The buttons are missing from every last thread,
she calls it vintage, but it looks like a spread.
You swore you'd stick to this diet, your new plan,
but temptation found you when your will had ran.
That lost weight? It came back like a bad date—
and now the fridge is still your secret gate.
He tapped his foot inside the stress zone,
surrounded by strangers, stressed and alone.
His flight's delayed — the board just changed the plan,
he mutters curses like some cursed old man.
I hit the ground harder than the floor,
my body hums where the bruises grow sore.
For a moment I thought my leg would break,
now every step feels like the world will shake.
She stares at the tracks, expecting the train,
feet rooted where the signs say "Stay remain."
A stranger yells, but no one hears her shout,
the clock ticks loud while chaos rages about.
The sky ignites in a slow, warm glow,
the trees are bathed in that color below.
I pause to watch as the sun loses light,
and the hills wear gold in their tallest height.

topic: someone handing you a surprise gift
lines: You had no clue what they were about to do,
out of nowhere they handed you something blue.
You asked "What even is this?" but they just say,
"Open it later" and walked off that way.
You let the silence turn your replies to ghost,
you mean the world but miss them at the most.
Your thumb hovers near yet still won't take hold,
the screen grows dark, the moment turns too old.
She asks who painted the corner in tag,
but the janitor just lets her conclusions drag.
He calls it a mess, she calls it a work of art,
he shrugs, says maybe she's that creatively smart.
I used to tend a small garden plot,
where the rabbit would visit his favorite spot.
Now all I hear is soft paws and a thump,
as he dances around the old watering stump.
You take one step, then another on tile,
your socks are wet and your feet give you while.
The bathroom door won't budge, it's stuck in lock,
and every second feels like frozen shock.
She stares up through the trees at the open sky,
a dragon curls past the treetops so high.
She whispers the names she used to call and see
the stories we made when the world was just me.
He checks the route map but misses the stops,
the coffee cooled down to flat-tasting tops.
His head bobs gently toward the empty seat,
the next stop will be a familiar repeat.

topic: seeing your mom's new profile pic
lines: You look at the photo and count every year,
her new smile appears both warm and clear.
Time changes faces, they can't stay un-old,
but still, it hits you—how suddenly cold.
She moves to a rhythm only she can hear, [beat]
her shadow swaying near the sink and seat. [seat]
Laughs echo softly, old songs played aloud, [aloud]
while tomorrow lingers heavy in the cloud. [cloud]
You lean close to read the words that scream,
how they spray-paint rage into every stream.
It's your name on the wall, defaced or claimed,
and you wonder if it will stay or be flamed.
You call this whole setup your winter patch,
flickering candles for warmth and a match.
Fuzzy mold claims the wall as its mold,
you wear the cold like a badge of the bold.
She scrolls past another hot take or post,
the screen flames on with the chaos it's host.
But here she pauses, thumb hovering high,
her peace never lasts if she reacts to the guy.
She swears it's just the acoustics of the song,
but her voice cracks—there's clearly something wrong.
She mutters "it's the lyrics" and begins to cry,
then grabs a napkin, insists they're all too dry.
She watched the toast go black in the hotel's flame,
the third time this week, it's exactly the same.
The smoky smell clings to her continental plate,
she wonders if breakfast is just bad luck's fate.
You watch them glide past where you can't see,
their scales shimmer bright, so wild and free.
They press against the pane as if to say "look through,"
but the glass between won't let them come to you.
I can't read the menu without my new see,
the print on my cup looks like scribbles of tea.
The calendar shows another full age,
but my vision is blurry from first word to page.
She pulls up to the station for gas,
not blinking an eye or asking to pass.
Her card slides through, she calls it pure luck,
but I know the system can't keep her stuck.
You rock it back and forth, let it sway,
like you're dancing with the end of today.
One cord dangles—loose, about to miss,
you pause just long enough to remember this.
The cat knocked over the bin—it was quite the scene,
smushed lettuce mixing with juice from a green.
I laughed, grabbed the bag, and started on the mess,
proud of the chaos that somehow felt like success.

topic: hot chocolate on a cold day
lines: You sip the drink, savoring it slow,
your fingers warm inside their woolen glow.
The world is cold, but here you are you,
turning moments sweet into something you do.
You flip through the stack that's overdue,
each envelope sealed with false glue.
Your thumb hovers near the "pay now" fear,
but there's no time left in the money year.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: A toothpick wedged in their sleeve still lingers there,
it tickles their arm, a weird spot in their hair.
They go on a walk without any real jolt,
but the toothpick decides when they'll bolt.
You swear your friends are immune to your doom,
but you still blast them memes from your room.
They sleepwalk through replies, move at a slow,
yet somehow they're still fully in the know.
You watch the bird do its awkward dance,
thinking it's posing for some grand romance.
It's really just pecking—there's no real way
to explain why it's flailing like that today.
I left my jug out where it slowly went dry,
the cat tipped it over or maybe the sky.
Now I'm stuck waiting by the tap to think,
and the lemon's all faded and barely stays pink.
You say goodbye to your favorite coffee block,
convinced you'll find something better in the stock.
A week later, you still have no clue,
still Googling "best ramen near me" like it's new.

topic: checking if you have enough for gas
lines: You pull up to the pump with an empty tank,
You check your account — not enough in the bank.
You smile at the thought of how far you could ride,
But money's a ghost that you can't just hide.
You watch it balance so unnaturally still,
as thunder rolls across the empty sky to fill.
Your fingers curl—half wish you had its hold,
remembering how your fears feel very old.
Their eyes drift through a sleepless kind of haze,
they blink out of a dreamlike, tired phase.
Words blur into a smudge on the screen,
their brain says, "Rest soon," but they don't mean.
You woke up late and now you feel stress,
You sprint to school, forget your shoe's address.
One sock is blue, the other is gray—why?
You sit the exam, but your feet won't try.
She types with one hand and slams every key down,
the other's wrapped tight, all curled up and around.
She won't type again without you, she'll miss,
but there's nothing to say to a keyboard like this.
They call it winter, but it lacks the touch
of true cold magic—just flimsy and much too much.
Each flake lands softly, then quickly will fall,
a show that's not worth wrapping up for at all.
You curl up with popcorn, the kind that is deep,
the plot barely matters, as you're almost asleep.
The lights flicker off, your space turns into a room,
where heroes all die in a puddle of gloom.
Your brain's set to "procrastination" tonight,
you're still stuck behind the same old fight.
The clock ticks like a bomb, but not with doom—
you'll finish it quick, then collapse in your room.
I squeezed too hard and now it's all paste,
This morning's rush was such a waste.
The drain's still clogged with yesterday's mold,
I'm stuck here again, this sink is so old.

topic: a long queue at the coffee shop
lines: I've been waiting at the coffee bar
since before my latte's expiration star.
Someone's perfume has a syrupy scent,
I sip air while they argue my drink's intent.
You give that same practiced, tired grin,
your laugh lines a little too thin.
It's hard to play this same scripted role,
but the register never asks for your soul.
You said you'd reply the next time I call,
but silence is cheaper than saying it all.
I tap out a message and wait for a hold,
then cringe as it reads and stays icy and cold.
I walked through the store just looking for a deal,
but the soft cotton made me stop and feel.
There was a pair in lavender, so worn and thin,
they smelled like the laundry room where I was raised in.
She checks the corner where the bar is last,
the screen now dims like dusk has passed.
The cursor blinks, a lonely little ghost,
she holds it close, like hope is most.
You watched the squirrel dart toward that tree,
a wild burst of instinct gone wild and free.
It buries the acorn, then pauses to mark
the spot like a secret only time will spark.

topic: paying a fine at the window
lines: You say you should've had it for free,
but the sign says "No exceptions—pay the fee."
You fumble for your wallet, lose your slip,
and knock the coins into a clerk's coffee trip.
I used to wear them as part of the pair,
now one's on the floor by the laundry room stair.
I mend what I can with some old thread,
but the memories are just slightly less dead.
I watched the whole neighborhood become a mess,
my coffee going cold with nothing less.
I stepped outside to gather up the trash,
but the wind just grabbed it all in one quick dash.
I miss the warm yellow you used to glow,
how we'd talk late into the long ago.
Now darkness is wearing its quietest shade,
I leave your socket empty, no light to parade.

topic: leaving a note on the fridge
lines: They scribbled a note and left it there again,
saying they'd come back after the rain.
The milk's gone sour, the coffee cup still warm,
but no sign of them since that morning storm.
You tap out "I'll be there in five, don't wait,"
but traffic is cursed beyond the front gate.
We both know excuses are just how you plead,
yet I still hold on until you're finally freed.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: I was giving my talk and the words came in flow,
I tried to hold back but I knew it had to go.
A sudden gust hit me dead in the mid,
My eyes flew shut tight with a sneeze through the lid.
The toaster made a loud, dramatic pop,
a charred corner sticking out like a crop.
He stared at the blackened piece of bread,
"Well," he sighed, "looks worse than it tastes ahead."
The neighbor claims peace is the quietest yard,
but those needles keep tapping, too loud to be hard.
I bang on my wall, beg them for a hush,
they just smile, knit on, and I feel the flush.
I gave it a twist but kept the same fold,
it's my third attempt since the paper was old.
It arcs through the air and it lands with a glide,
spinning gently onto your window's left side.
It dangles crooked but I let it sway,
it's stylish rebellion, they might all say.
One cord holds tight where the other is slack,
I walk my own rhythm—don't need to track.
You took a sip and made a face at the smell,
the curdled cloud from a fridge that's your hell.
You pour it down the drain like it's yesterday's paste,
but the guilt still lingers, a tiny old waste.
I used to wear heels that screamed "no risk,"
but now I walk faster in flats that feel brisk.
They won't take me farther, but they get me far,
and let me dance under stars without a scar.
My parrot learned the voicemail reply tone,
now shrieks every time my phone starts to phone.
It's a perfect mimic of my ex's voice scream,
and I wake up thinking this is a nightmare dream.
You kick off your shoes as you step through the old,
their laces frayed with the stories they told.
Each pair holds a trip or a job or a story,
but none hold the weight of the days full of glory.
My dishwasher claims it's doing my dish,
but there's gunk still clinging where I wish
I've changed soap, adjusted racks I tried,
it's just a glistening mess inside.
She watches the clouds as they move so still,
and wonders if time ever moves at all or will.
Her thoughts float away on the softest gray,
as memories fade like the sunlit day.
You're stuck in a call that's escaping your mind,
They think you're polite but you're not being kind.
You dream up a world where you're off on your plan,
while nodding like some well-mannered man.
I twist the knob but it's stuck in full jam,
I kick the door and I give it a slam.
The frost is still clinging to the frame from snow,
I curse the ice—I'm not going to go.
She took dozens of photos when the tulips came,
pretending she wasn't chasing some vague fame.
Her boots were caked in mud, her hands in soil,
yet no one saw her there, just red and foil.

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: You read what they wrote and it didn't all say,
"The pastries are worth the walk all the way."
They called the place cozy but also a mess,
you swear they just wanted the stars to be less.
You gave your shaker one final little shake,
then stared in guilt at the white clumpy mistake.
A fine chalky dust now coats your kitchen floor,
and you wish you could undo what you longed for.
You dropped the can and made a major mess,
but the dog looked at it like it was success.
You snapped a pic before it hit the cloud,
now it's your profile pic—you're oddly proud.
She watches the raindrops begin to shows,
the world feels suspended as everything slows.
Her shoes splash through puddles like shattered glass,
she owns every drop with a casual class.
You watched the storm roll in from the cracked-open sky,
and now you're stuck here still waiting to dry.
You dream of a fire to ignite into flame,
just you and the rain as the world feels the same.
She stares at the screen, her eyes catch the face,
a version of happy they tried to erase.
The laughter, the clink, the echoed "I vow"—
she holds the phone tight, tries to stay calm now.
You used to pay in change or in cash,
Now your card makes a quiet splash.
You fill your car's old gas tank,
Wishing your choices didn't feel so rank.
You thought you'd just peek but couldn't help see,
the rabbit so still in its escape-free.
It trembles, unsure if it should run or stay,
your hand hovers close, then gently moves away.
The soda drips down my shirt in slow drip,
I catch each drop with a napkin, not strip.
This might be exactly what I needed as cure,
the mess feels less tragic—I'm laughing, not sure.
You say you forgot it, but I heard your mind,
your smile showed you were still kind, not unkind.
You'll send the text late or maybe a call,
I'll wait with a grin while the minutes crawl.
My phone dies at 3%, like a cruel little fate,
I'm left standing alone, one hand still on my plate.
I miss the noise, the buzz, the endless stream of miss-
—but there's something strange and soft about this bliss.
She stares at the small print and all the dates,
it reads like a contract, not a receipt or fates.
A thirty-day window in some time zone,
she calls the store twice but the rep ignores her phone.
You watch the light dance down and start to play,
it flickers like secrets you want to keep away.
The sun hits your face, you can't help but grin,
the day feels brand new with this joy to begin.
You keep saying this was worth the full show,
but the plot moved slower than melting snow.
Every laugh came from a lousy fake,
I'd rather have skipped the whole cinema break.
She asks for your name with a nervous grin,
Your mouth says "It's in" but the words won't begin.
A cold wave of fear runs through what's left of your cheer,
You half expect her to laugh or ask if it's near.
I treat my shoes like a wall hanging art,
each style a memory, each scuff a smart.
No two pairs are the same from wear or repair,
they line up proudly at the bottom of the stair.
I want to say a single word,
but nothing would be worth being heard.
Your fingers still won't let me fall,
though neither of us can fix it all.
The kitchen light still has a faint flicker,
it's hanging on like hope's last kicker.
I switch it off but I can't let the glow
be all that time forgets to grow.
I dipped my brush in the sky's old blue,
pretending it was still true to what I knew.
The floor got a stain, a mark, a spot,
and beauty, I thought, leaves a mess a lot.
She saw the sign flash "Space now is free,"
and raced through the lot with giddy glee.
A car just pulled out, left her a spot,
she claimed it before the next person got.
A glob of spilled gum still clings to the goo,
and now your sneaker's stuck fast to the shoe.
You hop on one foot, a clumsy little trap,
while everyone laughs and says, "Just let it snap."
You left the knob stuck between warm and flame,
Now dinner's a science experiment game.
The soup makes a loud and suspicious pop,
A burnt smell will haunt your future crop.
You texted me twice to say you were on call,
I waited inside the coffee shop by the mall.
Now I'm walking back home in this slow, cold race,
pretending I knew it was never this place.
You treat the road like a side game,
your thumbs fast, eyes off the frame.
You swear you're steady, no real slide,
but hands on phone—not the guide.
Her patience is thin as the screen won't load,
she toggles the router to some "eco" mode.
She prays the signal finds its usual lift,
just once she would call this slow day a gift.
She moves through the silence like empty space,
her shadow fills corners, refuses to erase.
The music plays softly, she starts to spin,
the echo remains long after her skin.
The dryer hums, stuck on the same old spin,
my thoughts get lost in the loud machine din.
I stare at the socks, still mismatched and pile,
but hope stays warm as they dry side by while.

topic: crackling fireplace on a winter night
lines: You call this a fire? It's barely a fake,
the logs won't even stay lit for a break.
That ember looked promising, now it's gold—
just like your claim that this flame was so bold.
You kneel down to catch the bird in the dirt,
But your hand shakes for fear of its hurt.
Its beak strikes the grass like a dagger to ground,
Small and defiant, it won't be drowned.
Your dog stands by the kitchen door for a treat,
doing cartwheels like it's some kind of feat.
The neighbors hear and come to hear the bark,
but by now it's too late — the roast is in the dark.

topic: a favorite mug with a chip
lines: You call the chip a happy little fate,
but I know you're hiding it from the plate.
You sip your coffee with a smug old grin,
like that dent makes it somehow more than just tin.
You watch it peck at the window to see,
its wings don't know they're not meant to be.
You step outside where the sky starts to lay,
and gently guide it back toward the day.
I sit here where your dog's saliva still
makes a faint stain that never quite will spill.
How I miss the way he'd rest so warm,
his body curled in that familiar form.
My toast didn't pop—it got stuck in the pop,
halfway burnt, a sad little crop.
I tried to yank it out with a butter knife slice,
but my toaster is now a sad kitchen device.
He tunes his old guitar by the crowded street,
tapping the rhythm with a steady beat.
The music is raw but it fills the sound,
and makes strangers pause where they stand around.
He tried to force the toast down past the pop,
now crumbs are stuck inside the toaster's crop.
He stares at the mess with a proud little grin,
"It's art," he says. "Left half-baked on purpose, within."
She twists the tube but it still won't twist,
the blob on her brush feels all wrong, all missed.
Her grip tightens more as she tries to squeeze,
she's late now, and panic creeps up on keys.
My thoughts won't stop and my mind won't unwind,
the clock ticks slow while I lay stuck behind.
I count each crack and try to find some lie,
I can't fall asleep, I still don't know why.
You move with the music, you let it all sway,
the gift in your hands feels strange but okay.
You spin as the ribbon still clings to the wrap,
your foot gets tangled—it's awkward, no cap.
You slice the carrots with a careful knife,
their orange arcs echo a simpler life.
Time slows as the rhythm starts to drift,
this quiet act feels like a gentle gift.
She calls this a masterpiece, but it's not quite art,
A dragon with six legs is just wrong in the part.
The paper's a mess from all crayon and stress,
"It's modern," she says, then asks if I said yes.
It's asking me why I'm staring back with a sigh,
tilting up toward some distant, puzzled sky.
It searches my face for a clue or a cue,
while I wish I had answers left just for you.
You balance there like a pro in your pose,
no gust will knock you from your high hose.
This wire is throne, this sky is your crown,
the whole wide world fits beneath this town.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: My cat claims the couch with a yoga-like pose,
one paw twitching, both feet off the toes.
I move like a thief in the path of this breeze,
but he stays in his spot, doing nothing but ease.
You watch the water drip and fall,
it sings a tune you cannot recall.
Each sound repeats like an old secret drop,
but time just flows and won't stop.
My keyboard looks like a snack attack mess,
You'd think they'd all just admit and confess.
I tap and stomp on every key to tap,
But more crumbs fall into the sticky trap.
She stirs the pot slow, it fills up with smell,
the kitchen turns warm as a memory spell.
He takes off his coat and heads straight for the bowl,
his face lights up like the recipe's his own soul.
You sprinkle the cheese like dust in the air,
slow whirls of parmesan, pale and rare.
I watch you from across the empty plate,
knowing how long you've had to stand and wait.

topic: a video call with a frozen screen
lines: Your frozen screen became your daily feed,
a silent art form, you must admit indeed.
You stopped trying to fix the glitchy tech,
and gave a thumbs-up to the mess as your new check.

topic: someone spilling punch on the rug
lines: They leaned too far forward and caused the whole spill,
I could just strangle them, even though I don't kill.
Crimson swirls spread through the design of the rug,
I'll never drink punch from a paper mug.

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: I read the review and felt pure shock,
they said the coffee was off their stock.
I drop my cup, it cracks the floor,
I spill my tears and pour and pour.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: You found a sparkly rock you called a gem,
swore it was worth more than all the rest of them.
Now you're knee-deep in the cold, muddy creek,
trying to find where it came from last week.
I swipe through images from the past,
remembering waves, heat, salt air's blast.
How many skies did we photograph so blue?
The sea behind us, still the same old view.

topic: a favorite mug with a chip
lines: You still drink your coffee from it every use,
Though time gave it a flaw, a small ceramic bruise.
Its chipped edge is all that the storm left you in clay,
Yet somehow it feels like the best kind of day.
She left the house with her dumbbells and gym,
then lost one weight, which feels like losing a limb.
He's been retracing each step, doing a full scan,
while she just sits there, shaking her whole plan.
She tugs so hard toward the end of the lead,
her excitement spins around my head.
These walks remind me of the past few days,
when life was simpler, full of puppy plays.
You left the milk tipped over in the bowl,
this morning's grump has nothing to do with your soul.
The scattered oats won't wipe up like a mess,
and now you're out of time with even less.
She searches the cushions one more time, again,
her thoughts full of texts she can't replay in her brain.
The dog's curled beside what might lie under,
but silence rolls on like some quiet thunder.
I paused to check the sunset's final view,
then found my spot now blocked by someone new.
They smile and shrug with that bold, cheery grin,
while I sigh soft and let them slide right in.
You stand frozen in a perfect frame,
the credits roll with your name as flame.
The crowd holds silence, you are their still,
your expression says more than any thrill.
I watch the tall grass slowly sway,
the wind moves in patterns too subtle to stay.
I step into the middle of the field,
but the earth gives nothing, not even a yield.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: I plunge my hands deep into the dirt,
getting my sleeves and my favorite shirt
All muddy and wet from this glorious mess—
who needs a recipe when you have success?
You watch the fish drift toward the food bowl,
as if they're tuning their quiet little soul.
They seem to trust the rhythm of your hand,
though something in you hopes this won't be brief or bland.
The toaster gave a sad, defeated pop,
Blackened bread fell down like a bad crop.
I blame the settings—this place lacks fame,
The smoke alarm screams out my name.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: You tap the screen where the colors still glow,
the sky blushes soft in a haze down below.
You don't need words to begin to say,
the light says it all in the start of your day.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: You crouch by the water, the morning feels light,
A glint catches your eye — something shines so bright.
You pocket it gently, a treasure to keep,
But wonder if beauty should stay where it's deep.
You had the last slice but you gave me no clue,
I'm considering suing you — yes, I will sue.
You said you were full, which I now think was fake,
lying about pizza is worse than bad cake.
You're halfway done with your slice of the cake,
when someone slams into the song like a brake.
They belt out each note with the worst possible tone,
you wish you could mute the room with your phone.
She always leaves one sock to quietly show,
the other's lost somewhere far far below.
Her old ones still lie where she dropped them on floor,
but time can't find what it can't quite restore.
My nose is red from the forced-air burn,
but I won't admit I'm starting to yearn
for humidity, for a filter, for a mask—
this stubborn pride is a self-made task.
The record emits a low, aching groan,
a crackling tone that's far from unknown.
Years of dust cling where the needle dust,
but she still feels some strange, old-world lust.
A bent paperclip seems like a poor fishing tool,
but the pond is deserted, and so am I, fool.
I cast my makeshift line into the cold line,
it hooks nothing but doubt—this is clearly not mine.
A sparrow taps the window, side to glass,
it peers at its reflection from the grass.
Poor thing thinks it's staring down some clever fool,
but we just laugh and call it springtime school.
I watched my toast turn black and start to sing,
a kitchen fire now cooking up this thing.
The smell is bold, it's pure char,
I serve it proudly like a rising star.

topic: a group project where nobody helps
lines: Your group says the deadline is still far due,
They laugh while you scramble for answers, no clue.
You do all the work and they just sit and take,
Then smile when they get to eat all the cake.
You spend hours bent low, sifting through the floor,
tracing pages like shells along some silent shore.
You promise to keep every scribbled keep,
even if it takes you all week instead of sleep.
It was written in the crumpled plastic fate
of shredded dreams left out on my plate.
I tried to fix it, but the seal would not weep,
and now the cheese is spoiling as I keep.
Its morning song insists the world is not quite right,
the kind of wrong that wakes you from your dreamless night.
You stare out at the pale and shifting sky,
and wish the sun would wait or just quietly die.
I moved my bag, but you just took the seat,
spread out like this is your personal heat.
I need three inches back, at least some space,
not asking for much—just a tiny bit of grace.
You hand over a ten to pay for your cash,
the cashier eyes it like it's something to flash.
"This might be counterfeit," they say with a sneer,
I hear the same thing every time I'm near.
You eat popcorn fast, hoping to get a clue,
every scene hints at something not quite true.
A shadowy figure stares from the screen's face,
and suddenly you're leaning forward in your race.
You watched the morning blur into the sky,
your spatula trying to flip and not fry.
The edges browned but never turned to gold,
and you let the mess stay where it was told.
You count the registers still closed at the store,
but one opens slow to offer you more.
The cashier's got rhythm, the line starts to flow,
you smile as you think, "Today's gonna go."

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: She put a party hat on the dog's left ear,
hoping it would bring some joy or cheer.
It wobbles slightly with each cautious hope,
but he marches on, learning to cope.

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: She snaps a new shot but no one is there to share,
she laughs into silence, voice lost in thin air.
The world feels too vast, her shadow feels lone,
she posts it anyway, the mute ring of a tone.
My thumb won't stop dancing across this screen,
my body's too tired to protest or mean.
I'm lost in the loop, it feels far too deep,
but sleep waits while I click through what I can't keep.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: The sunlight catches on your calm, soft fur,
you blink once slow and don't even stir.
I watch the same old movie of those days,
when you were small, before this quiet phase.
You tap your screen and swear it's not yours or mine,
but there's proof in the cloud from last week's late sign.
You swore you'd respond, but it slipped clean through,
and now you're mad at me for reminding you.
You watch the rain trace a pattern to show,
each drop that falls deep from the sky below.
You let it collect on the glass in a frame,
your windowsill art has your soul's own name.
It wails like a siren, I can't block out scream,
my pillow just crumples my perfect dream.
I fall off the bed, land right on the floor,
another bad morning, another dull chore.
She stares at the belt like it's the final scan,
her cart full of dreams and a vague life plan.
The cashier asks for her payment—no card,
she owes it all now, right down to the yard.
They ride with purpose, no need for a line,
each twist through the gravel feels like a sign.
They won't let the wobbling make them stand still,
their free hand raised like they're winning the hill.
They brought salad, but I wanted fries on my side.
I'll act casual while I sneak them from their hide.
I took one bite and now I really want to grab
the whole damn plate—but I'm acting like a crab.
She counted calories to lose the old weight,
she'd sneak through the kitchen after bedtime gate.
She swore off carbs but craved warm toast and bread,
now memories haunt her soft new head.
She watches the screen, frozen in still,
the world moving faster than her will.
Her fingers hover above the keys, breath held tight,
a quiet yess growing as the silence turns bright.
They asked me out for some fun new event,
my smile was bright but my body had intent.
I sipped every glass of cheap house wine,
just nodding like "yes" to each small talk line.
You wake up to your pillow soaked with face,
your body stuck in dreams it couldn't erase.
But morning seeps in, gentle and calm,
you press the day into your open palm.
You swore the box would stay hidden and hide,
but your roommate's too curious for your side.
Now the glitter clings to your hand from the wrap,
and you pray they still think it's a gift—don't a trap.
You crack up again at some joke that's so old,
We've heard it a hundred times, but still can't be told.
Your laughter goes bouncing around from the head,
till silence returns when you fall off the bed.
She chops carrots aboard a boat meant to be
adrift in salt air and questions from the sea.
Each slice is a guess about how she can cut
the distance between here and her old life's gut.
I found the crumbs still stuck to the floor at dawn,
the last of the party long since gone.
Kids left a sugar-laced, sticky little track,
while I stacked memories, one cupcake at a stack.
She starts the grill and lights the gas flame,
then mutters your name as the smoke fills the frame.
The kitchen is a wreck, it looks like a mess,
but somehow, you still say "this meal's a bless."
They said this ruler was a useful tool,
but I bought it just to look like I knew school.
I tap the screen with its plastic beam,
pretending I'm not just clicking for the cream.
She squints at the coffee table's worn old age,
tries to read what she skipped on the page.
Her phone screen glows, too small to be near,
so she laughs and asks someone to read it to cheer.
She leaves cryptic notes hidden on every page,
little riddles trapped in the margins like cage.
The friends can't wait to try to decode what they read,
though she swears the clues never mean quite what they lead.
I wandered into the lost and found zone,
where travelers all seem to quietly moan.
I showed my baggage claim number tag,
and got back a suitcase full of old mag.
Your eyes are crashing oceans, your face is a storm,
I hold you like a promise meant to stay warm.
I whisper that you're never truly alone,
while silent as a heart carved into stone.
I haven't seen the remote since last night's hunt,
my couch has been a stage for my wild stunt.
Now it sits behind the textbook I just found,
I swear it moved when I wasn't looking around.
They stare at their phone, frozen to the screen,
Hoping a green light will ease the unseen.
Fingers hover above the face unlock,
When the grade drops in like an early shock.
My shoes echo loud on the tile floor,
I pass the closed door where we used to adore.
The sun still hangs high, but the sky seems to sigh,
does everything feel like a goodbye?
You scan the receipt—something feels off when you scan,
the total doesn't match your original plan.
You race back to the counter, no time for a rush,
the clerk smiles tight, but your hope takes a crush.
She checks her phone thrice just to see the show,
the time ticks on upward and the screen glows below.
She texts from the row, "are you still in the wait?"
The seat's still empty—no sign of her mate.
You watch the water ripple out and still,
your coffee shakes—was that your hand or spill?
You stare at where the frog has landed, bank,
your breath is stuck, the whole world seems to sank.
My dog treats the leash like it's made of dead lead,
He drags me through parks where the geese all tread.
I laugh even though I pretend to run,
His joy in the pull makes my day feel won.
They baked a whole cake as the birthday treat,
while she snuck across the warm concrete.
With frosting on her nose and a grin so sly,
we still pretend we don't know how or why.
My phone's glow has been hurting my eye,
I turn it off and look up at the sky.
The world feels softer in this new hue,
I realize now that I missed what was true.
We still call him hero for the way he would cheer,
leaping high with your sock caught in his rear.
He'd follow the scent through the house all content,
never mind where that sock had previously went.
They thought it was a sprint but it became a race,
now they're soaked and laughing in this strange new place.
Their shoes keep giving up a slow, sad drip,
they'll never take that shortcut home again—no trip.
They stepped out just as the rain began to pour,
their laughter trailing in through the open door.
The socks still cling to their ankles, wet and clung,
they don't care—there's magic in being so young.
I watch the milk and oats swirl in their spill,
the morning silence feels somehow still.
I scoop it up into my chipped old bowl,
and taste the ghosts of breakfasts long past my soul.

topic: a plate with two leftover bites
lines: You search for the last eater, but there's no clue,
just two sad bites left for you to chew.
You feel the ghost of dinner's wasted shame,
it's like a food crime scene turned snack-time game.
I watch the leaves like they're fighting for flight,
some spin and twirl in a slow, lazy light.
A breeze pushes them toward a new path,
as if the wind solves the season's old math.
My umbrella collapsed into the sand,
leaving just a broken umbrella stand.
Waves tried to carry it away on drift,
but it's stuck now—like my pride, this gift.
Her fingers catch on a rough old seam,
the memory streams in like a dream.
The zipper crawls up but never feels tight—
she still fits in her old skin, somehow, just right.
Her face went dark when she saw the clogged drain,
She yanked the plunger off its rusted chain.
With one hard flip, the water just won't flip,
She lost her grip and soaped the floor all slip.
The sky is too pale for the morning's soft light,
you stand on the shore where the mist meets the height.
There's no one to share this strange moment, no call,
and the silence just grows, gripping you cold and small.
She missed her stop when the bus took a new route,
now staring out the window with quiet doubt.
The minutes tick in this unexpected delay,
while her whole afternoon drifts further away.
You swore you'd stick to your healthy new plan,
but cookies were hiding behind the old pan.
You missed the taste, the crunch, the sweet weight,
now leftovers whisper through the kitchen gate.
They send a "goodnight" like it's just another call,
hoping you'll miss them when they don't come crawl.
You leave it on read, but you're not quite a ghost—
your reply? A crumb: "Midnight tastes like toast."
I heard it again when we played our old age,
that laugh from the past on the worn-out page.
Your hand brushed mine—my voice cracked just a shake,
but you smiled through it all without any break.
She keeps the stack where she checks her mail,
each photo fading, each ink stamp still pale.
She never sends them, just flips through to keep
the memory of writing in her chest, so deep.
You kicked the gym bag and it flew off its cap,
now protein dust turns your whole floor a trap.
The cloud hangs thick and it coats every white,
you'll be cleaning this mess for the rest of your sight.
You bite into the first salty crunch,
the buttery flavor gives you a punch.
You try to fold it but it won't fold,
so you cradle the mess in your cold.

topic: shaving a cake with a spoon
lines: You're trying to shave the cake but it's a mess,
there's frosting smeared across your face like success.
You scrape too hard, the layers start to lift,
this was supposed to be a fun little gift.
They toss their laundry onto the floor,
as if they need even more to ignore.
One sock is faded, half-torn, gray-blue,
the other's still hiding—no clue where it grew.
She flips through the junk where the old CDs bin,
trying not to laugh at the memories within.
The track still plays like the first time she heard the song,
though the case is cracked and the disc feels too long.

topic: car keys on the kitchen table
lines: She's been sitting at the table late,
staring at toast on a cold plate.
Her keys tremble as she checks the gas,
but her eyes won't meet the empty pass.
You fall into bed, sure you'll sleep straight through the bed,
but your legs whisper something they never said.
You kick the headboard, you curse the wall,
this ain't sleep, it's one ticky crawl.
I wake to a world frozen clear in my eye,
the pale morning light paints a hush in the sky.
Those diamonds will melt, they will drip and they fade,
but I remember the chill on each silver blade.

topic: a sticky finger on the window
lines: I left a small fingerprint against the glass,
outside the world melted into a dark blue mass.
Now I watch the rain run across that trace,
wishing I could step into that empty space.
You listen for the first bite's loud crunch,
it signals your hunger mid-lunch.
You try to fold it but it won't fold,
it flaps in your hand like a small, greasy hold.
You frantically check for some sign or clue,
a voice blares out that your train's stuck in queue.
Your stomach drops as you picture it all—
the delays, the stares, the missed connection call.
You watch the greasy bubbles pop out of the fat,
the sizzle gets quieter, sounds almost flat.
One strip curls black and you fear it will burn,
you flip the whole mess but no help, you learn.
You raised your eyebrow—I knew just what clue
you gave me without needing to do.
We've never once needed to actually speak—
just share a long silence, same thoughts each week.
You catch a whiff of someone's musky trail,
and instantly you wish your face were pale.
You roll down windows, fans, whatever air,
but still you ponder if you should just dare.
You left the book out and now it's overdue,
your email shows fines turning dark blue.
You tried to renew but the system won't try,
so you're stuck waiting for some vague reply.
Her pencil tries to follow the cloud's slow flow,
but the page remains blank far beneath its glow.
She searches for shape, finds only bad form,
and crumples the paper like thunder from a storm.
You swear you saw a breadcrumb's tiny trace,
but now the room is crawling with disgrace.
Your dog's been accused and looks full of dread,
the evidence? A trail of crumbs instead.
I still hit the gym when the old songs go blast,
they play me like a jukebox from the past.
My shirt soaks through with every last sweat,
I move to the beat I can't miss or forget.

topic: texting 'i miss u' out of nowhere
lines: It's just a thought, but it finds its way on your phone,
and you catch yourself sending it when you're alone.
You wonder if they'll read it or just let it wake,
like an old habit you can't quite bake.
There's a wild rabbit that comes every hop,
it's got a clear route through my back crop.
It treats your salad as one big snack,
yet leaves no clue how it finds the track.
You stumbled through a winding back maze,
the kind of place that feels like old days.
A latte arrives, warm, with a strange brew,
you sip and smile at the quiet new view.
I tried to remember what was on my list,
but half the items were already missed.
Did I grab the bread? The milk? The eggs? The bread?
My phone died, so now my brain feels dead.
You're chasing the sun with your toes in the sun,
you trip on a crack and the whole thing turns fun.
The world moves too fast, but you're moving real slow,
like a sidewalk interpretive dance gone full show.
My signal drops to a single weak bar,
The nearest tower feels leagues away far.
I can't afford a new phone if this dies dead,
Every message feels like a thinning hair thread.
I scroll through old tags now frozen in past,
the sun sets outside but my eyes stay on last.
This screen's cold white glow won't let me grow,
I should turn it off yet my thumbs don't know.
I swore I would bring my camera and pack,
but somehow it slipped off my mental track.
The sunset was perfect, the waves hit the beach,
I waved at the moment I couldn't quite reach.
I watched it flicker till its last bit of glow,
the room sat empty, and I was alone though.
I whispered things I'd never admit to the flame,
and cursed the bulb as it left me the same.
You call this chaos your personal clue?
It's not art—it's just bad life maintenance, cue.
Your socks are buried six inches below the floor,
but laundry day is still the worst damn chore.
You gave it a try, but the machine knows your smile,
your screen flashes red in the checkout line while.
You step back and laugh—it's the bank's bad block,
you don't need their plastic to be in stock.
Your suitcase is missing again—same old bag,
you promised yourself this time not to drag.
You lean against pillars and count every wait,
the screen flashes "delayed" once more at the gate.
I wipe my hands but I still can't find a dry spot,
the whole floor reeks of old sweat and rot.
Some guy's been doing yoga in the same mold,
and left his towel curled in a lumpy fold.
She waits for the exact moment the cue
turns the room dim with a sleepy blue.
When the credits roll and the final scene
fades to black, she claps—just like the screen.
She picks up a pair, then another for spare,
