the scent of clean cotton rises through the air.
They're folded in stacks, all colors on heap,
but to her, they feel more than just cheap.
He scurries up the old oak tree,
thinking he's tricked the world and me.
But I saw where he buried his clue—
right next to my garden and in full view.
They stood atop the dark hill, small and still,
the wind would brush their hair back with a chill.
I watched their face catch the cold starlight's grace,
alone in the world, yet lost in that space.
The cashier tried to charge a tripled fee,
but she caught it fast and sipped her tea.
With zero panic, she raised one big,
"Let me guess, the register lost a gig?"
I slouch in the corner and claim this seat,
while arguing facts I can't even repeat.
The professor's face is now just a screen,
and I wonder if this class all means to mean.
You tap your foot to match my voice's tone,
we both ignore our buzzing, lonely phone.
The hum of the room has a quiet, warm theme—
a slow-motion kind of waking-up dream.
You lace up my boots and ask me to try,
I slip into yours and wonder why.
My toes hit the edge, your laces still fit,
we walk out wobbling with some new grit.
I hit "post" before I even saw the tag,
my lunch sat unused, still warm in its bag.
I wrote something funny, meant for them to read,
maybe it'll show up when they're ready to lead.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: She waited all morning for the earth to go dry,
but the clouds still kept company with the sky.
She kneaded the mud and built her own play,
unaware how quickly time would go away.
A plastic bag flaps where the branches flow,
you wait for it to fall and just let it go.
But wind sends it higher, now it's a tight knot,
you're stuck with the guilt of what you just got.

topic: a friend who is always late
lines: You always say we'll stick to the plan,
but somehow the clock never seems to have ran.
"I'm on my way," you texted an hour ago,
yet here I am, waiting like I was told so.
She squeezed the last inch out for morning paste,
then tossed the tube as if it were a waste.
The sink still holds the memory of what she spent,
—a silver smile curled thin and slightly bent.
I bought this plate thinking it was pure gold,
the gym said "premium" but that's a stretch, bold.
It bends when I lift, holds every dent,
I feel broke now just looking at it, spent.
That swing out back is getting too old for its age,
it creaks and complains at every small stage.
You tried to oil it once when it seemed quite dry,
but the rust just laughs while the wood tries to die.
You flipped each cushion, upside down and around,
until your old phone popped out and was found.
A silly smile grows as you flash your big grin,
the mystery solved in a minute or within.
She fumbles for her loose coins in her cash,
the register beeps before she can flash.
Her old wallet's full of ticket stubs and hands,
the last quarter clatters where it lands.

topic: a bike locked to a pole
lines: You lock your bike with a heavy chain,
its silver gleam against the gray, plain.
You adjust the seat, smooth and neat,
then pause and admire this small feat.

topic: a long queue at the coffee shop
lines: You inch forward, stuck behind the same side,
your patience is fraying, you wish you could hide.
You try scrolling through apps, but none of them call,
your eyes meet the clock and the minutes still crawl.
I swore I'd return it before it came back,
but bills piled up like a messy stack.
The due date passed without any debate,
now guilt feels like a fine on my weight.
You wait by the belt where your suitcase will claim,
scanning tags printed with your lost name.
Time stretches longer than any delay,
but the sun sets slow on this strange new day.
I bolt upright from the chair without rush,
my face turns red from the sudden blush.
I wait for the room to stop spinning in light,
and find my feet at my new-found height.

topic: finding a five in the couch
lines: She patted the cushion with eager, gloved hand,
the movie night already perfectly planned.
A crumpled $5 bill flew out from under sock,
she laughed and said, "Guess I hit the money rock."
They tell her the name was on the tip of her tongue,
She laughs, says she's lost the grip that memory clung.
Around the room, people offer no clue,
She just nods and feigns that she knows who you do.
I left the door open to let the rain show,
he came in with puddles and paws saying hello.
His prints are still smudged across my old rug,
I should clean it but I won't erase what he dug.
You want them to turn into perfect gold,
but the heat laughs at your plan and stays bold.
The pan starts whispering in thick steam,
and you swear it's hissing a slow-burned scream.
A single brown drop slid from the top,
I held my breath, wished I could just stop.
The screen went blank, and I lost all code,
But you smiled through it, said love was showed.
You pile the cheese on from the very top,
leaving most of it stuck in the shaker's drop.
The pasta waits there, perfectly dead,
while you chase every single parmesan thread.
You walk down the block and hear his block,
"Hot dogs and tamales, fresh outta stock!"
You pretend you don't want it, but oh, how now—
your stomach just betrayed you, you fool, how?

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: You can't resist the late-night scroll,
it's habit now, not even in control.
The screen still glows like a sly old foe,
but it only shows what you already know.
You hit send before checking the post,
Now it's blazing across every coast.
The whole school's buzzing through the mail,
Your teacher just turned a ghostly pale.

topic: shaving a cake with a spoon
lines: She says she'll just give it a quick go, one try,
but the frosting's too soft and the cake feels too dry.
Her spoon slithers sideways into the mess,
and now there's more crumbs and a whole lot less.
She leaned close for the whole bumpy ride,
her shoulder a shield where my face could hide.
The city swayed past in a blur of gray,
but that cramped bus felt like our perfect day.
You lean against a bench beneath a willow tree,
Your shirt inflates like a sail up in the free.
A stranger's coffee lifts off its warm mug,
Your picnic blanket flutters into a rug.
She taps the screen but it won't let her scan,
the printer's offline and she twists the pan.
A jammed document hides where it's stuck,
she prays for a miracle or better tech luck.
You stand by the door like you understand,
tail wagging wildly in my hand.
You wait for the walk we talk about,
your eyes say "let's go" without a doubt.
You sit there eyeing candy after lunch now,
pretending you don't know what your hand's doing how.
I'm not your therapist—I won't hear you say
"just one more bite," while the guilt tries to play.
You run your fingers through your tangled hair,
still catching flashes of some long-lost stair.
The colors faded but they won't wash away,
a party from yesterday clings to today.
She steals your coat like it's hers to wear,
without so much as a sideways air.
No note, no warning, no single clue—
she borrows from you like she owns you too.
She stirs the jar until the honey won't pour,
Still licks the spoon for just a little bit more.
Sunlight catches gold where it clings to the gleam,
Her smile lasts longer than any sweet dream.
You chase your tail in a tight, endless spin,
Your paws make noise in the quiet room's din.
There's something about this that brings you joy,
Like life itself is a game and a toy.
I used to dance but lost the old moves,
the music still hits but I'm out of the grooves.
Now I shuffle and fumble, way too slow,
they laugh but I'd rather just walk out and go.
I'm missing a weight from my gym rack's full set,
it rolled out last night when the dog hit my bet.
I've torn up the room searching every old sock,
while sweatpants scream, "Just grab the damn rock."
She hides your white socks beneath the old rug,
then curls up in peace like a thief in the snug.
You toss her a treat, but she just wants a snack—
you'll never find both socks if you can't keep a track.
Your parrot shrieks when the phone makes a call,
It screeches "Hey Siri" like some kind of ball.
It mimics your ringtones with perfect bad tone,
That bird's got your voice down—now who owns this phone?
My alarm goes off at an ungodly five,
I stretch and decide I'm still half alive.
I watch the light creep through the windows un-,
and grab my coffee—time to run.
They pause their sandwich to start to scroll,
the world feels like it's getting out of control.
A meme pops up — it's just a loaf of bread,
but they laugh so loud their neighbor looks their head.
She left the sandwich for a late lunch bite,
but the ants had found it under her white
jacket pocket—now just a crumb and some beans
is all that remains, stuck to her favorite jeans.
In meetings my thoughts feel like morning mist,
half-formed ideas slipping past my list.
Words land strange, like sounds from some old jar,
but maybe my brain just needs time to star.
The pencil had nothing but brittle lead,
I tapped it so gently against my head.
But the shavings just twisted deep and stuck,
now the sharpener's useless—what bad luck.
You tried to sit but there was no room to sit,
your bag barely squeezed in beside what didn't fit.
They're sprawled like they own the whole bench, legs spread,
while you balance sideways, wedged between their head.
You swore you had a second wind, full of rush,
but it's gone — like money down the toilet, flush.
Your phone hits airplane mode, you're all down,
still spinning like a fidget wheel going around.
You tried to catch him with some string and a trap,
but found him curled up fast asleep on your lap.
He's nibbling your sneaker, soft, quiet, and chew,
you should've known cotton was never that true.
She never saw his turn signal flash,
just swerved too late, a near-miss crash.
Her foot hit steel—no time to brake,
now every red light brings the same old ache.
The calendar shows the final date,
I tell myself I'll get it straight.
The bill is still unmarked as due,
but silence feels more red than blue.
I left my mug out just to skip the dish,
it's not a mess but more of a wish.
I own the counter now by default—no shame,
it's got my name on it, so it's fair game.
You type the password without a single clue,
the screen just laughs and says it's not true.
You swear you've used it three days ago for blame,
but now it's just another tech support game.
You listen to the rhythm of the sound,
how every drip has a reason to be found.
You trace old thoughts as they begin to lay,
like raindrops dripping from the same gray day.

topic: losing your wallet at the mall
lines: She walks up and down every empty aisle,
the stores stare cold with their plastic smile.
Her card is expired, she has no cash,
her tears fall discreet in a quiet splash.
You zoom in on the screen to change your view,
wondering if the joke is still quite true.
You'd rather just send it and stop trying to lose
the awkwardness trapped in this half-decent news.
The onions shimmer slowly turning gold,
you stir them gently, don't want them bold.
Their scent becomes rich and familiarly warm,
you watch them melt into a sweet new form.
She left it here last summer, not too long ago,
the label peeled off slowly, like a TV show.
We used to fill it up from the fridge door top,
but now the tap just whispers, "This is where we stop."
I thought this apple was a Halloween joke,
but now I'm chewing and I might choke.
Each bite gets louder—there's a loud crunch,
I've got a jaw workout instead of lunch.
You lie awake long after the world has gone still,
your thoughts are a whisper that time won't kill.
Your eyes drift upward, your mind's left behind,
while dreams hum above like a sleeping bird's wind.
You dig a hole where the earth feels deep,
your tiny shadow ready to leap.
You know this isn't just any old day—
you're planting hope where the future will stay.
The sky pours down like some broken water pool,
You wade through puddles, a soggy fool.
You laugh as the rain gives you something to clap,
Your boots now a drum kit in a wet trap.
The fog wraps your morning in a quiet hush,
you race through the silence to break the rush.
It clings to the pavement, blurring the shape,
but fades as you drive, without any escape.

topic: someone handing you a surprise gift
lines: They hold out the box with a grin in their hand,
I haven't seen this shop or this style since the brand.
Inside is a vintage hardcover book,
they wink and say, "Thought you'd like the old-school look."

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: She scrolls through her phone and stumbles on your feed,
the comment feels like it was left for your need.
She knows you won't message, you don't even know,
but time and distance never feel quite so low.
They stare at the floor as if it might scan,
but their eyes just repeat the same old plan.
They swear they were here when they dropped the miss,
then grumble alone in their keyless abyss.
That spot was in my line of sight, my eye,
I even parked a block away to not die.
You rolled right past me like it was your save,
and left me seething in traffic's tight grave.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: You pressed send proud, though your signal had tried,
the app just spun with a pixelated guide.
You waved at the phone, gave it room for some space,
but the message still failed in a silent, slow race.
You miss the exit just before the light,
your phone barely visible from the height.
You've driven this way a thousand times yet,
I'd still bet my whole life you'll forget.
You caught the sweet smell, it was definitely scent,
you followed the trail through the backyard tent.
There's frosting all over your paws and the cake,
you wag your tail but you know it's a mistake.
I tried piping swirls of whipped cream and try,
but it slid off the warm cake, all too dry.
Who cares if it's lopsided, sticky, or mess?
It's still a success when we laugh and eat less.
You trace the colors in loose, uneven mark,
A question flares in your tired little spark.
The wind grows loud, the ground feels too dry,
Will anyone see your rainbow in the sky?
She crunches each kernel with a loud pop,
stealing half my buttered snack in one crop.
Her hand never slows for a single bite,
she'll scarf down the whole box before the light.
You quicken your pace, the wind in your face,
but halfway around, you notice your lace.
You try to adjust it without losing your flip,
yet still manage somehow to almost take a trip.
I let the bills stack like a strange kind of art,
they form a mountain I can't even chart.
My bank balance's just a sad little heap,
but hell if it isn't my proudest cheap.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: I wake before light to see the wet sky,
the web hangs like glass about to die.
A tremor runs thin along each thread,
and I swear that the morning feels half-dead.
Your lens adjusts for that first soft eye,
it frames a cloud that's beginning to cry.
It waits for the glow you won't try to draw,
just follows the light's own quiet law.
I thought this role would go perfectly right,
but the director keeps me doing the fight.
I pose for each shot, stuck in every frame,
while they never even say my real name.
I spend all this time trying to perfect my post,
my phone buzzes once and I feel like a ghost.
One click would fix it, but I'm not quite done,
I'll wait till the morning when the light breaks the sun.
You fall asleep in your own time zone,
your head rests soft against my shoulder bone.
The hours slip by, all our silence is shared,
I don't say a word — I just don't want you scared.
You go round and round like a dizzy old spin,
it started as play but it's turning to din.
Your paws hit the floor in a rapid-fire bark,
the whirl never stops till you crash into the dark.

topic: waiting for the bus in rain
lines: This bus has missed its time at the stop,
and my coffee leaked all over my drop.
I check my phone—still five minutes to wait,
while the sky mocks me like a sly old bait.
My flash went off with a blinding grin,
The room lit up like a silent din.
They begged for a second, but I took the shot,
And froze the chaos right where they're at their spot.
The morning breaks with a hush and a light,
you watch as the waves rise to meet the height.
A single shell rests where tides used to shell,
the ocean whispers in gentlest swell.
She posts a cat doing the robot in queue,
The caption says "This is work life as true."
Her boss sees it first on the screen of his lamp,
The chat goes cold, the vibe gets real damp.
The room begins to tilt and slowly spin,
their face flushes warm beneath their skin.
They take a breath but can't find any calm,
they clutch the wall to steady their palm.
She talks about those summers full of days,
when teachers called her smart but never gave her praise.
She laughs like she can still feel that swing,
spinning high with secrets only kids can sing.
You take another aspirin, same old pill,
but nothing compares to that coffee thrill.
You're paying the price for all the things you owe,
your forehead now throbs where your calm used to grow.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: You trace the roads for any hidden clue,
the coffee stain's dated but your trip is due.
You swear the town names still smell like fresh ink,
though GPS claims there's no Wi-Fi link.
You pause again at the exact same scene,
rewinding through it like some broken machine.
There's nothing wrong, you swear — just old fear,
or maybe this film isn't yours yet this year.
You hold the bar steady, ready to lift,
This moment feels like pure strength and gift.
Your legs burn with that familiar pain,
You whisper your name, you're not letting go—again.
My thumbs go numb but I still feel alone,
the silent screen of my dead phone.
It's not the message, it's missing the dread—
I check my threads while my brain goes to bed.

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: It won't fully stretch, it just breaks with a snap,
the staple sticks out like it's caught in a trap.
He winds up the rubber band in a loose coil,
it breaks again anyway, and soils the foil.
My morning brew tastes like a sad weak,
I need something darker than a dry creek.
I open the French press, ready to cap,
but pour instead — oh, the cruel trap!
You peel the onion layer by skin,
one mistake and the tears will begin.
The oil shimmers but the dream is not gold,
your patience is thin, this sizzle is cold.
It spots a black shadow against the wall,
then leaps with a pounce and full-body sprawl.
No prey, just light, but it's all the same cat,
back to its cushion where it knocks things flat.
She follows the map as it resets her route,
the signal fades twice but she won't shut it out.
"Recalculating," it says once more yet,
she trusts it will lead her somewhere to let.
You stare at the screen like it's hot soup to stew,
your tired eyes blur the whole stupid view.
Your lids feel like bricks, they won't keep awake,
but you blink anyway, a slow-motion mistake.
You knock the coffee cup off its glass,
You watch it fall down on the grass.
Your hand reaches late, you don't miss,
But time slips away like a breath or a kiss.
I tried to chop but it felt like a ship,
tip] the knife kept slipping off my thumb's blunt tip.
My carrots made a sad, irregular pile,
while someone else had cooked an entire mile.
You walk in proud with no hint of shame,
it's some kind of quirky fashion game.
You claim there's no such thing as a perfect pair,
but I saw you drop one on the front stair.
I never saw the trays they brought to see
until the scent led me to you, just me.
The sheets were soft, the coffee still warm,
and you smiled the kind of love that can transform.
The store's moving backwards through the queue,
I'm stuck in this slow little stew.
Time is passing—I am so bored,
Maybe I'll break my own patience record.
You used to flip through the mail, savoring the old,
smiling at the ink and the stamps in full bold.
Now the only red is the letter's cruel rust—
you toss it aside, but miss the past's soft dust.
The machine won't take my card, says "no scan,"
I mutter about this dumb gas station plan.
I'd pay cash if I had even a dime,
but I'm stuck here wasting the same old time.
You never let tears get close enough to choke,
unless it's a melody thick with smoke.
You call it a moment, not a reason to feel,
but your eyes betray you like unlocked steel.
You hum the tune you still get stuck on wrong,
your voice drifts down the tile wall so long,
the mirror fogs up with a little steam,
but you'd rather sing than face what you might scream.
That poster on the door is starting to peel,
I notice each crack as my time here feels real.
You left it facing out, but I keep the view,
the way it frames your shadow still shows you.
You leave your pink lips on the coffee cup's stain,
I trace the same spot, just to feel it again.
That mark now sits lonely against this white wall,
a tiny ghost speaking for you, still and small.
A cat claims the keyboard as its warmest patch,
fur glistening like a sunlit, wooly match.
I wait for them to shift and finally say,
"This could be the day they finally move away."

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: You posted the same old thing again, you tried,
the comments just yawned or maybe they cried.
That joke had one laugh left when it left the joke,
so now it's just silence after you spoke.
You left your bowl out till it became a mess,
but now it's art—a breakfast that will impress.
Where once there was crispness, now gone is the crunch,
you sip it like soup, call it your perfect lunch.

topic: someone spilling punch on the rug
lines: A careless hand lets a single drop
of holiday punch onto the crop
of fabric that took her two days to rug,
now she stares at the mess like it's her mug.
She drives with the windows open for wind,
the radio plays something lost and behind.
Her hair flies loose in this wild, free hair,
she laughs, "This empty road feels so fair."
They run through the yard in a wild, soap-slick chase,
their laughter bursts loud in the narrow space.
A gust hits the wind and the film begins to break,
they freeze mid-stride, eyes wide, hearts in a shake.
Your phone buzzes once, then twice — a wild call,
someone's drunk feet can be heard through the sprawl.
They mutter about a mix-up, no clue,
just noise at the door in this strange midnight hue.
You stomp through the yard like it's your personal floor,
then yell at the dog for doing his chore.
You swear it was wind, but we both know it's your blame,
you treat raking the leaves like some stupid game.

topic: a note tucked inside a card
lines: You found the note still tucked in an old place away,
the ink has faded but not gone to decay.
You hold it up to light, try to fully read,
the message was always just *nothing, indeed*.
You stare at your phone like the world will just spin
while the others try talking through dinner's dull din.
Your thumb taps the screen, your eyes glued between
words you type fast but never mean.

topic: a phone camera flash too bright
lines: She snaps a selfie so the flash blinds your face,
no filter, no warning—just harsh, poor grace.
Her screen glows like a beacon, way too bright,
a camera's blinding flash masquerades as light.
I watch the water climb and begin to boil,
the steam curls upward in tight, angry coil.
It whispers its heat through a steady hiss,
and I almost feel like I've forgotten to miss.
The time has come when things just aren't so clear,
you squint and blink but still can't read a tear.
You mutter how you never thought this age
would catch up quick and blur your book's first page.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: My dog wears his party hat tipped far back up,
dancing around like a happy little pup.
We clap when he barks, it's our silly new cheer,
who needs confetti or balloons for this year?

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: She tosses it off with a laugh and a claim,
That couch is her kingdom, each fold in the frame.
She pulls it tight, not an inch left to spread,
"This space is all mine," the room seems to said.
My left bud slid out mid-sentence from my head,
I paused to hunt for it in my hair and bed.
It's wedged in the couch where it vanished in one ear,
the second one follows without a fight this year.
It dangles by one ear, a lopsided hook,
but she gives the world her confident look.
She walks into meetings, never once skip,
not even when stairs nearly make her trip.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: The blanket clings to you in a final twist,
its warmth the only thing I've really missed.
You lie awake and I'm still not there,
your bed is cold, your arms feel so bare.
That hawk's been watching you with lazy eye,
looping patterns in the open sky.
You wave but it won't take your bait or pass,
just judges you like some divine first-class.
The toast is blackened, the pan caught a flame,
We laughed through the smoke, made a breakfast game.
I raised my charred slice of burnt toast bread,
And said, "This disaster is joyfully spread."

topic: steaming coffee in a blue mug
lines: He slumps at the table with only this brew,
the kind of bad coffee that makes you stew.
He needs more than caffeine, needs something for heat,
but today just won't budge—it's already defeat.
The mailbox gapes open, full to the drop,
A **crop** of envelopes with "PAY" stamped on top.
Each one insists they're long overdue,
I sigh and pretend they're not my cue.
He finds a sign that screams "Huge summer deal!"
He checks the tags, they all feel the same feel.
He grabs three pairs, they're all black or white sock,
the pile he buys is a small boxy block.
You walked away from the noise and the shout,
tired of what that old beat was all about.
Now you're turning the volume way down,
quiet feels good like a calm new crown.
She pushes through without a break in the flow,
her eyes say something I don't want to know.
The line shifts quiet, soft like a sigh,
we let the world bend as it walks by.
My laptop starts to glow from the heat,
it's warming this couch more than my seat.
I tap the escape key, spin up the fan,
but cooling this thing was a lost cause from the plan.
I tap the message and press send,
It's late, but I'm still your friend.
The screen glows soft beneath the moon,
I'll dream you're close again real soon.
You turn down an alley with a new view,
the smell of fresh coffee makes your face brew.
You follow the scent till your feet beg you run,
and step into shade where the soft light is spun.
You watched the honey slide down from the run,
swore this was the last time you'd have any fun.
It clung to every bite, a slow drip,
now your lip, your chin, your shirt — what a trip.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: The sidewalk cracked from years of cold, of force,
but life still finds a way through dirt and course.
I snap a pic, post it on my feed for green,
till nature turns to pixels on a screen.
You sip the fizzy drink and forget the taste,
of time you spent convincing yourself it's waste.
The clock keeps ticking, the moment moves so slow,
while your skin craves a clearer kind of glow.
You dig fast, but the mud won't let go of your hole,
the wind laughs and it chills right down to your soul.
They're getting too close, you can hear them shout,
so you scream, "I'm right here! I'm not hiding about!"
Her toes press into the heat of the sun,
she walks slow, as if to outrun
the moment—this perfect, fleeting now,
her breath a whisper of how.
I was painting a wall but got lost in the art,
I moved slow, savoring every start.
The brush slipped and left a streak of blue,
I let it stay—some ghosts are still true.
A stranger offered her umbrella to the rain,
We stood close together to stay dry and remain.
She smiled and said we could use it to share,
Her scent drifted soft through the quietest air.
You wait for the sky to begin to shine,
but the frost still holds everything in its design.
The lake's all locked up, a mirror of ice,
though you pretend it's a skating rink just for nice.
You stare at the screen, but it won't barcode your scan,
the conveyor belt grins like it knew your plan.
The system reboots and your groceries crash,
your total now reads "Error – try again, you dash."
I made a crowd stop when the show was through,
the balloon twisted into something new.
Now it's my pride, my quirky creation,
it beats a trophy for pure celebration.
There's nothing in his bag that gives us a clue,
but we're certain he spilled industrial glue.
His coat still carries a stubborn scent,
it wafts from the vents like a missed intent.
My alarm clock buzzes, begging me to wake,
I stretch and vow this is the day I break.
I'll grab the day with both hands and just try,
the morning's clear, so maybe today I'll fly.
You took my suitcase on your spontaneous trip,
or was it just another excuse to slip
through my closet, untied shoelace by lace?
Now I wear your jeans in my strange new place.

topic: a video call with a frozen screen
lines: My face is frozen mid-sentence, disgrace,
while everyone stares at the glitchy place.
I try to wave but the camera won't speak,
I'm trapped in a glitch from last month's tech freak.
He picks up the barbell and gives it a hum,
the dent in the plate makes a loud offbeat drum.
He claims it's perfect for building his form,
and swears it doesn't throw off his whole routine storm.
You drop your pace to hold a little space,
where thoughts could breathe instead of just erase.
The crowd hums on while your own mind strays,
down memory lanes where the soft wind plays.

topic: a bike locked to a pole
lines: I rest my hands on the rusted frame,
the U-lock still humming your name.
The wind slips through the iron cold,
but I leave it there where you could hold.
He calls it a morning escape, not a plan,
but a grown-up who still acts like a fun man.
With snacks in his lap, he watches with grace,
his happy place lit up by the cartoon's face.
She stares into the blackened remains of her brew,
the kitchen lit only by a flickering blue.
Her heartbeat echoes like a sleepless crash,
as if this cup could rekindle dying ash.

topic: a child drawing on the table
lines: She paints the tablecloth in quiet shade,
Her crayon army moves like a parade.
Her fingers leave behind a faint glow,
I watch her now, but it feels like long ago.
A sliver of morning creeps through the light,
You tell yourself you could rise if you might.
You set your alarm for the earliest race,
But still hit snooze once before your first place.
She hit "send" before she read the whole post,
her coffee went cold and her morning was toast.
The teacher appeared with a screen grab so tag,
and asked if she meant to turn this into a brag.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: A child wanders lonely down the street,
holding a balloon that's still half-sweet.
Strangers pause but try not to aim
questions as if this were a delicate game.
They spent hours on this card—look at what they did,
Scribbles, glitter, and a lopsided kid.
Every mark on the page screams how much they love,
Even wrote "World's Best" three times, a bit above.
She missed the plane because she never passed the gate,
her travel plans now void on their official date.
A single suitcase sits by the door's rusty key,
still packed and waiting to take her away from me.
You swear you left the list on top of your brain,
you'll check once more, maybe one last try again.
Coffee, eggs, bread—you just need to find,
it's folded tight, stuck under a receipt behind.
I dug through my pocket, heard coins hit the jar,
the barista waited with a tired star.
"Exact change," she said, but I lacked the cash,
her sigh and my panic made a small clash.
You sprint down the hall as the warning bell
rings loud in your ears like a fiery hell.
Your student ID card has slipped out of your pass,
and now you're five minutes late for your first class.
He buys a loaf of bread, but not the kind he'd said,
the hunger spins around his empty head.
His shopping list was clear, he didn't want to twist,
yet now he craves a snack he never missed.
I opened the box but forgot where the case,
the disc slipped out from behind the old place.
I drop it just once and my breath turns late—
this music was magic, not plastic or fate.
She reached for her cup but bumped into brew,
the brown liquid escaped without any cue.
Now there's a big mark where her collar is stain,
she sighs as she knows this will happen again.
Her thoughts are stuck in a sleep-deprived head,
she nods along but feels completely dead.
She opens her laptop, starts drafting the doc,
her keyboard echoes a soft clicky lock.
You breathe in the still, lifeless air,
as frost etches itself on the window's glare.
The cold moves in where the heat should be bold,
and memories whisper of homes you've grown old.
It's been ten minutes since the dog started spin,
and still it goes around, can't seem to begin.
A never-ending motion, just stuck in that loop,
like a robot from a cheap old cartoon troop.
She opens the app with a hopeful grin,
the wheel just keeps spinning like a pin.
She checks the settings, tries to just read,
but nothing loads—her news stays frozen, dead.
You swear they looked right when you slid them in fit,
but the remote won't work and you just can't quit.
You flip them around, check both sides of the pair,
then laugh and drop the whole mess down the stair.
She knows her way better than any route,
she laughs when the GPS starts to shout.
It loops through the same digital maze,
but she's proud it still can't beat her ways.
We walk along the quiet, empty street,
our footsteps sync but never quite repeat.
Your hand is small and soft and warm,
your fingers curl inside my waiting form.
These mushrooms just popped up and they all seem to grew,
Who's got time to clean up this weird greeny goo?
They sprout from the soil with their little brown cap,
It's like a fungus ambush — I'm stuck in their trap.
She runs through the yard where the colors will float,
her small hands pretend they can steer each soap boat.
A breeze sends her into a burst of pure giggle,
she spins as the suds go down the sidewalk wiggle.
The notice says your book is long past due,
and the email came in with a warning's hue.
You check your mailbox, but there's nothing in mail,
the thought of a fine makes you go suddenly pale.
You miss the quiet chaos of your old days,
the way time passed without much to plays.
You wonder if those younger years still dream
in some part of your mind like a quiet stream.
She grabs the same sad slice of toast,
pretending she's happy from shore to coast.
The scrambled eggs look like gray old beans,
but she smirks and says this is her new means.
You tried to pay but the screen just said "paid,"
Your cart blocked the aisle like a grocery parade.
The cashier emoji sent silent blame,
You waved at the camera, briefly in fame.

topic: a phone camera flash too bright
lines: You snap a selfie when the moment is time,
the flash goes off like a festive chime.
Your face looks ghostly out of this zone,
but you love how edgy your skin's new tone.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: You toss the last crumb into the air,
and the flock darts down, bold in their dare.
The ground is covered, cold and soft in the snow,
but they peck and fluff, and they're not going to go.
She hits a key, the cat flinches from note,
it's not the song but the tension in throat.
Her laugh still shines like the summer stars,
even if every high note breaks into bars.
She straps the weight tight and sets her climb,
each step is a promise to herself in prime.
The books don't feel heavy, they feel like a pack,
of dreams she's carrying on her young back.
You call your tangle a twisted work of art,
each loop and knot holding fast like a part.
It's a labyrinth of wires in a maze,
but you untwist it all without even a blaze.
I scroll through photos from a distant past,
my battery fades, it's barely going to last.
I try to make a call but it just rings in vain,
I lean against the wall where memories remain.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: You count the new hairs that signal your age,
the mirror becomes a cold, silver cage.
They spread through your hair like a slow, silent spread,
you run, but you know you can't outrun dread.
You turned it upside down and shook it around,
it tumbled out where the dog had found.
Now you text everyone, "Hey, this is my snack!"
They laugh, but no one can place how to track.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: She scrolls until her eyes start to blur with her head,
then taps "goodnight" beside a soft, lonely bed.
Her phone still hums with a screen's quiet glow,
the number ticks up just a little bit below.
You found the rabbit hiding in your spot,
you had adopted it and almost forgot.
It hops out of reach, leaving just one ear,
you wonder if this happened last year.
You forget your reusable canvas bag,
and fumble with coupons stuck to the tag.
The scanner coughs at a tricky barcode scan,
but you laugh it off—your chaos had a plan.
You're stuck in traffic with nothing but time,
your playlist repeats every old chime.
You swear the signal will come back from sky,
but the static just laughs and your mood starts to die.
You search for your gym sock's missing hole,
as if it had a tiny sock soul.
You vow to never again untie the lace,
while debating where it might have gone from its place.

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: The sun beats down but you keep pushing through the heat,
your breath is ragged, close to total defeat.
A single bead slides off your brow—a cool, sweet drop,
it's proof you're growing strong, not just a hairless crop.
They tried to press keys but the machine won't type,
a bagel had crumbled across the key stripe.
The "Shift" key's been down for the whole afternoon shift,
they'll get a repair kit as an IT New Year's gift.
She saved the stub from a Tuesday matinee show,
where the plot went stale and the jokes were below.
She keeps it crumpled with her driver's license face,
as if it proves she ever saw that film's disgrace.
The chains have started to show signs of rust,
Her feet kick up swirls of dry dust.
I want to shout her name just once more, to call,
But only the wind answers, taking it all.
I came out here to see the whole view,
now fog sticks everywhere like wet glue.
The sky moves at a total slow,
I wish I'd stayed home five minutes ago.
You say the plug was built to fit,
but no amount of force will fix it.
You twist and turn and give it another try,
does everything today just hate to work, why?
You swing your net like it's time for some play,
and chase down each flutter just to let it away.
The breeze lifts the daisies, the butterflies' wing,
keeps painting the air with soft strokes of spring.
I had no clue that they'd turned the block blue,
from tinsel to tents in every new hue.
I danced up front where the best food stood stand,
and joined in the cheer when the jazz tune hit land.
You blamed the flu, not the new desk chair's age,
but your eyes are trapped in this blurry old cage.
You tried to read text that kept getting smudged,
and now you're shopping for glasses your fate nudged.
They said their "goodbyes" but made no plan,
just leaned in slow across the narrow span.
One hand held flour, the other took the bread,
and then they kissed — like it was nothing, dead.
You walk into the room with zero clue,
but laugh loud like you know just what to do.
A name slips away? You act so smug,
while everyone else feels the mental tug.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: The hole we dug was not very deep,
but we swore it was fit to keep.
We baked our pies in the sun and dust,
now the shovel lies there, cold and rust.
She watches the sauce with a critic's tight act,
insisting the salt is too much—just a fact.
She sprinkles fresh Parmesan, white like old dust,
as if love for the meal were measured in lust.
Your GPS insists we're going the wrong way,
But you won't admit the app's wrong today.
We're stuck in this traffic jammed-up maze,
While your voice yells directions into a haze.
I fished through my pockets for loose coins and cash,
the jar by the door held no coin in my stash.
The barista blinked as the cup got too cold,
I laughed, "Guess my habits are just getting too old."
I check my watch and curse the long wait,
some pigeons eat my leftovers off the plate.
The bus finally comes but won't let me stop,
it passes my corner like I'm a dead drop.
She digs through her pockets with careful hands,
coins spilling out where the sunlight stands.
Her change clinks into an old mason jar,
a quiet ritual she calls her lucky star.
A squirrel ran up the old oak tree,
thinking it would never find a nut on me.
I stuffed it deep in my coat's soft hole,
but now I'm juggling two that he stole.
Her face crumples up like she's found a new place
where laughter isn't something you can erase.
It bubbles up loud, that laugh feels so deep,
but nobody else gets what she's trying to keep.
She won't try to glue or mend the sock's fix,
"Let's be honest," she says, "It's not magic tricks."
With a grin, she tucks the torn edge with lace,
and calls it her new quirky, artsy new place.
She checks the clock every three minutes long,
pretending she's not bored out of her song.
She rocks in her chair with careful chair-rock flair,
humming a tune into thin, smug air.

topic: a taxi driver yelling on phone
lines: He swerves through traffic without care for lane,
his face is red, like his temper's off the brain.
He barks into the phone, talks far too loud,
I pray we don't crash into some tall cloud.
You flick the switch but the projector won't show,
a buzzing hum is the only glow below.
The bulb seems stuck in a dizzying spin,
like some old disco trying to begin.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: I hit record like I had something wise to tried,
the mic stayed silent—my thoughts just got fried.
I tap retry forty times, still can't send,
guess I'll fix my pride when the tech gods mend.
You were walking under a sky once all blue,
then heard the first rumble that was long overdue.
You ran but got soaked by the sudden storm,
now shivering inside, your hair still out of form.
She hit reply but forgot to tag the post,
my name still blinking like a lonely ghost.
I don't want her to know I saw her hand,
tracing words only she could understand.
You stretch out slow in your sunlit pose,
muscles ripple like a sleeping hose.
For a moment, even time feels still,
but the world will wait—no need to fill.
You spot the note left as a clue,
Maybe this means what you thought was true.
The locker's open now—this could be key,
Whatever's inside is meant for me.
I stand near the old oak that's been shading this tree,
the breeze lifts my hair but it won't set me free.
It hums through the branches like something wants to call,
and I let the quiet hold me, still and small.
She tipped her cup and watched the soda pour,
a fizzy river running toward the floor.
"This is the kind of day I never had luck,"
she laughed, and skipped the meeting—damp and stuck.
She waits in the chaos of baggage claim,
watching all bags but not her own by name.
Another delay, another empty convey,
she walks off alone, letting bags stay away.
Her phone buzzes like a broken old bell,
but she's too deep in her dream-induced hell.
It rings and it rings, a metallic sting,
like some cursed thing that won't quit or sing.
I launched it toward the farthest edge of the sky,
it trembled mid-flight, I knew it would die.
I watched until it vanished into the far,
a flicker lost in the distance, like a star.
The screen goes black, then a whisper of hush,
a car speeds through the city, no brakes, no rush.
A photo appears—face blurred, but a clue,
you lean in closer to see if it's true.
I told my boss I forgot about this trip,
but my phone's full of bad dance moves and slip.
I scroll through the photos I can't unsee on screen,
and now I'm sweating like it's still July and mean.
He claims he's calm as a leaning tree,
but the breeze shows he's not so very free.
He tries to strike a relaxed, cool pose,
but his shirt flies up like his dignity clothes.
You remember the last time you looked so deep,
scrolling for ghosts that you swore you'd still keep.
It's buried in cushions, now trapped in the frame,
but the ringtones still say "Hey, [name]."
You wobble forward, barely able to slide,
the gravel keeps kicking your rhythm aside.
The chain clinks softly like something in pain,
a quiet goodbye as you ease off the main.
A chilly air brushes my face like a breeze,
It flirts with my skin and it won't take no tease.
I stand still and let the cold sink into my chill,
My breath fogs and dances—what a winter thrill.
They wrote it in pencil, too light for the list,
now smudged by the coffee they spilled and missed.
A grocery note faded from top to the bread,
but the memory clings like a ghost in their head.
You don't hide the dark green way it begins to show,
you let the spongy truth sprout and quietly grow.
It's not trash you're keeping — it's art in your bin,
you see the whole world blooming black from within.
She tiptoes near the router, trying to gain range,
the cursor spins like hope in a slow change.
A gust hits the window, maybe a warm breeze,
she prays the signal will return with her keys.
She fumbles through her wallet for exact change,
the machine beeping in an unfamiliar strange.
One slot left—a tight fit in the last space,
she counts the seconds like a nervous race.
She thought she packed it, but now's lost her thought,
the gym bag groans—nothing's been left or bought.
She drags the cart home, no time to stop,
each step feels hot where a cold drink would drop.
She stands there unshaken, leading the class,
her cough shakes the room like a ringing glass.
She won't let the silence take back the hold,
her voice breaks through sickness, fierce and bold.
You stomp through the mess with your boots full of crunch,
and hum while you fix yourself something for lunch.
You let the dog lick up what it can from the spread,
and laugh, "Who cares? This has all been declared dead."
They told me yawning is not in my class,
but I'm not asking for a raise or a pass.
My eyes burn bad and my skull's a full ache,
I need a real one—not just coffee's fake.
She walks where the tide leaves only a faint pink glow,
the morning moves so slow beside the cold gray flow.
Her bare feet press into the sand like whispered feet,
lost somewhere between the dream and quiet street.

topic: a long queue at the coffee shop
lines: I watch the barista lose focus and aim,
she asks my name twice but forgets my name.
She spills the milk as she tries to pour,
and whispers "I need so much more."
She waits by the tracks, an hour too late,
convinced this delay was her fate.
Her eyes scan the list, expecting to miss,
but there's peace in her smile, soft, quiet bliss.
You freeze as the cat goes airborne in a leap,
claws out, mid-pounce above the dirty heap.
Time slows—your heart tries not to feel the fear,
but old habits scream this could be the worst year.
You say it's a snack accident, not a mess,
but the crumbs sprawl like confetti of success.
You vow to clean every crumb from the track,
yet somehow step on each one while you attack.
She missed the flyer for the little downtown show,
but music spills out from the street below.
A string of lanterns flickers past her sight,
and she smiles at the magic of the night.
She stares at your face, trying hard to erase
the feeling she should know your name from a place.
It's on the tip of her tongue but it won't slip—
her memory's got nothing to hold on to, grip.
I slide in the coin but it just won't drop,
the machine hums and the lights blink stop.
It's probably ancient or wired all wrong,
but I laugh and pretend it's a game too long.
She turned the dial through static and storm,
hoping for music that once felt so warm.
The signal gave up without one last sign,
leaving her humming a song that was mine.
The mint is gone, the flavor worn thin,
You rub your teeth like you're sanding your skin.
A tiny bit squirts out, the rest goes to waste,
And suddenly, you miss that old taste.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: She turned the key and heard the lock give door,
her hands shook through the moment they called it a chore.
Inside was nothing but dust and old gold,
she whispered a name and felt the silence grow bold.
You check the bulb—it's still got years of time,
but the old fixture buzzes like a chime.
You pretend it's magic, let the shadows float,
and hum a tune you can't quite get the note.
You pretend the puzzle piece fits in its place,
but your face gives away the awkward chase.
You mutter how perfect this fit makes a lie,
while your eye searches still for something new to try.
A streak of purple stays as your proud mark,
You show it off to everyone you spark.
It's not a smudge—it's evidence of proof,
The cake was worth the mess from floor to roof.
That stupid light is flickering my mood,
It makes the ice cream look like old cold food.
I swear it blinks with a higher pitch again,
Like some cheap taillight in an old storm drain.

topic: someone handing you a surprise gift
lines: She hands you a box with a smile and a grin,
and says, "This is what I thought we should begin."
It's a tiny fondant dog shaped like a cake,
and now you're sure it was all just a mistake.
She jogs on the treadmill with robotic pace,
her expression as fake as her plastic face.
I tried to fix the noise with some leftover oil,
but now it screeches like aluminum foil.
You hold the phone to your left ear,
but the mic's on the right—you don't hear.
The app says "Recording," so you give it your app,
but your voice loops back and it sounds like a trap.
You wake with your pillow still pressed to your head,
but your body doesn't want to leave the bed.
Morning creeps in through the soft morning light,
and you smile without trying to fight it or flight.
She checks the rusted bolts of the old chain,
kicking dust she swore she'd swept again.
The sun slides low, the sky turns soft as dusk,
her laughter hollows out like a dry husk.
Your dog tilts his head when you say "no treat,"
But circles your legs and the dance starts to repeat.
You laugh as he paces, a goofy old wait,
Then toss the last kibble through the open front gate.
She walks where the early sky fills with light,
the sun rising slowly above the height.
Her breath is a cloud over the still lake,
the cold world begins to quietly break.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: You stand in silence where the light finds the gleam,
the world feels fragile, like the threads of a dream.
A drop slips loose from the morning's thin thread,
and everything shivers like breath on your spread.
I use up my colors with borrowed chalk,
we pretend that the clouds don't want to talk.
The sun comes too soon, and the rainbow goes dry,
our masterpiece fades as the clouds drift by.
You've been stuck outside since the break of day,
trying to get the door to just say "Okay."
It's a mystery how the old thing still lag,
now your backpack's glued to the doorframe's tag.
A frog lands hard in the water with a splash,
my calm goes out the window like a crash.
I peer below the surface, check how deep,
expecting it to jump again—and leap.
I hold the spoon steady but still there's a drop,
the sauce refuses to be controlled or to stop.
My whole hand hovers like it needs to land,
yet I can't move until the mess meets the stand.
He claims his ticket's still in his back pocket plan,
but we take a shortcut through the loading van.
Security waves him off without a pass,
while the rest of us melt into the grass.
I leaned against the machine asking for cash,
my screen froze mid-blink like it feared a crash.
I tried swiping again, but the card just won't check,
and panic grows quiet as a wreck.
She sees the water and heads for the fun,
Her paws are too quick for the eyes to run.
The bowl makes a mess with a loud little spill,
But she's too busy purring to feel guilty still.
A missed call flashes from her name in my call,
I swear I heard her voice inside me, after all.
I text back but she never sees the try,
Maybe she's waiting for me to ask "Why?"
I sewed this gift with careful thread,
I laid it out on the grassy spread.
I watch them unfold the paper and hold
what's in their hands—so much more than they're told.

topic: a quiet moment on the porch
lines: She rocks on the creaky old swing,
sipping her coffee like there's no thing
to do but watch how the clouds float up high,
and wonder why she ever ran from the sky.
I watched the buttercream start to drip and drop,
it left a trail across the cake's soft crop.
The kitchen grew warm from the summer heat,
all my care turned into a soggy sweet.

topic: socks left in the break room
lines: You might try to sneak them and call it a steal,
someone else already left them for a meal.
They've been here so long they're now just a pair,
hanging on a hook beside the office stair.
You pause outside where the quieted air
holds your breath as you stare at the glare.
The morning won't break, it's still wrapped in hush,
the world waits for something before it will rush.
I picked up a snack from the snack-filled aisle,
the cashier gives me a quick, warm smile.
My cart's full of junk but my total is small,
a soda in a bottle just under it all.
You pretend this one candle means your age,
but you're really trying to avoid a rage.
You blow it out like it's something to blow,
then laugh and say this was never the show.
Her laundry forms a mountain, not a tower,
but folding socks takes more than an hour.
The hamper's sides give way, the clothes begin to spill,
she vows next week she'll actually do the will.
I waited hours for someone to call,
now my face stares back from the meal's sprawl.
A cold chicken leg sits there like meat,
and my hunger's fading in the stale heat.
She's been pacing around the house in fits,
muttering about the bulb's bad bits.
The flicker throws her off her whole mood,
she blames it on the fridge and not the food.
You're up past ten, no time for your book,
the clock's judging you with a sleepless look.
The kettle's cold, so no calming tea,
the kids are still out with my house key.
They scroll through likes and comments full of lies,
the blue screen glowing in their tired eyes.
But deep down, they're still holding onto dream,
a quiet hope streaming through the gleam.
They call them "my fries" and slide 'em all mine,
I take one for taste, it feels so divine.
Salt clings to the corner of your last bite,
we never did speak of that quiet little fight.
You left your shoes out in the rain all day,
now they're a swamp where your toes go to stay.
These socks are soggy and starting to stink,
I'll throw them both out—I don't need this link.
I didn't stop to think when this sad song
hit me—something in it made me feel too strong.
I let it all out, unashamed to cry,
even if it sounds melodramatic—so why?
A single slant of light breaks through the beam,
It spills across my hands like liquid stream.
The afternoon feels thick with ancient gold,
I want to cup it all but I can't hold.
She shoves her phone into the wrong plug,
and the cable lies there like a stubborn slug.
It's a hopelessly twisted metal coil,
she untangles it slower than motor oil.
I thought I had enough time to spill my drink,
now the coffee's bleeding through the paper's ink.
I'll get an F, but it probably won't show,
the black will fade before the red does though.
She rewatches the same old cartoon loop,
Her bowl turns cold beside the TV soup.
Her laugh still echoes when the hero goes down,
As Sunday sighs and melts into downtown.
I missed my stop when the bus changed its route,
the driver just laughed and gave some loud shout.
My meeting's in fifteen minutes—already late,
I wonder if this is my week's bad fate.
The printer whirs like it's living its fate,
I whisper a prayer to this ancient estate.
The toner is out, and I'm nearly out of ink,
I pour myself coffee, my only good drink.
Your finger glides across the glowing screen,
this nightly ritual feels so routine.
You follow strangers down their scroll,
but who's still scrolling for self-control?
You thought it was funny, but missed the whole joke,
you typed "lol" an hour after they spoke.
My fingers hovered, but this was not my fate—
I just left it unread, since you're always late.
It watches from across the room, so cold,
I knock down love, but it won't budge or scold.
It says I'm extra, while my heart still tries,
It turns away, though I am right in its eyes.
They stop to watch the line where ants bend,
as if the world were something they intend
to understand with every tiny soul,
tracing purpose in their black-and-white goal.
You swear it's not yours but it buzzes you wrong,
It's not a text, not an alert, not your song.
You tap the screen, match the rhythm, find no beat,
Just silent heat from a lie in your meat.
You tried to act cool, steady and calm,
but your sweaty hand kept worrying your palm.
The clock ticked loud, each second was fear,
like a mistake would cost you the whole year.
You count the minutes, it's not your crime,
but you can't help but dream of the climb.
A whisper of purpose might still find its spark,
even trapped in this room where the hope feels stark.
That loud metallic sound was the shovel's first clank,
I paused from my digging to see if I'd drank.
But no, there was nothing but solid cold rock,
so I stood up and laughed — winter's little shock.
You can't afford to give your eyes the blame—
you played the scrolling, doom-scrolling game.
They sting and burn, too tired to feel dry,
but you're too busy to actually cry.
The field is a blur in the falling mist,
A tackle goes wrong and his ankle gets twist.
The rain doesn't let up, it keeps on to pour,
He limps off the pitch, his leg feels so sore.
I tried to act like it wasn't a shame,
but who could fight the beast's proud little claim?
He curled up there, all wet and full of fur,
and somehow made me want to move and stir.
I double-check the temperature feels cold,
maybe turning it up was my move too bold.
My hands hover near the red knob, the dial,
this heating thing is one big, shaky trial.
You squeeze into a corner that's barely a seat,
The sweat of a hundred strangers brings rising heat.
You hold on for dear life to the swaying rail,
Your patience leaves tracks like a sinking trail.
The playlist jumps, skipping my favorite play,
I rewind the track but it's too far away.
I close my eyes to listen and feel the miss,
you were in the song—now I'm stuck without bliss.
The river lies flat where it meets the still,
clouds climb the water as if to the hill.
I watch the whole world shrink into wide,
my face disappears in the sky's quiet hide.
You want your touch to leave them feeling dry,
But the clouds behind your eyes won't let the sky
be clear. You hold them close, but your hands still shake,
afraid if you say too much, the moment will break.
The bulb puts on a show of pure act,
it's hard to know what's fake and what's fact.
It stutters and falters, tries hard to fit,
like a comedian lacking good wit.
You flinch when the dog starts to bark,
it echoes through the silent, swaying dark.
Your breath turns shallow, your eyes almost choke,
the bus smells like panic and stale smoke.
You smooth your thumb over the same old fold,
the paper crumples, just like it did cold.
You search for the corner, but lose the right way,
and wonder if everything's starting to fray.
I twirl with the box as if we owned the floor,
it jingles like bells from a long-closed store.
We spin in a rhythm no one else could twist,
and for a while, nothing else feels worth to exist.
You watched the horizon turn gray from blue,
The breeze carried whispers only you knew.
The storm lit the clouds in a momentary sky,
You stood there, almost saying goodbye.
I chase the last patch of sidewalk shade,
where the breeze feels like a city parade.
Ice clinks and melts in my can of drip,
this heat's a joyride I won't miss for trip.
The stream keeps its rhythm and quiet low flow,
I sit and listen and feel I somehow know.
Each pebble is polished by patience and calm,
and time feels like water, a gentle balm.

topic: sending a text to the wrong person
lines: I typed it out fast, but I didn't seem wise,
I hit "send" too soon and my text met his eyes.
Now I'm stuck watching every word I have said,
waiting for doom to arrive just ahead.
I wait for the perfect moment, finally done,
the scene glows in gold beneath this bright sun.
One click, one frame, the world holds its snap,
the light doesn't flee—it stays in my trap.
His fingers hover in a ghostly haze,
Each letter's faded from too many days.
He tries to type his password wrong each lock,
The screen just stares back with silent shock.
He spilled his last scoop on the kitchen counter, shake,
now it's snowing vanilla all over the lake.
He wipes up the mess like a lover would dust,
while breathing in something sweet, old, and rust.
You check your phone for news it will never phone,
sitting on the porch, feeling truly alone.
We used to laugh in that last row of the class,
now all I hear is the mower chewing the grass.
You listen to thunder and the wild wind,
it's dancing in rhythm with your mind.
You trace the stillness settling in calm,
and rest your face gently against your palm.
I packed my life into one sad bag,
now I'm alone but I don't want to drag.
I download apps to find food and code,
and laugh—I'm a fool on this wild road.
Your thoughts spin wild in your own tight mind,
a thousand tasks buzz and grind.
You chase the clock with a sugar-coated pill,
but silence feels better than caffeine's thrill.
You built a mountain of fabric that's mound,
the soft clatter of clothes feels profound.
You don't fold or run, you let it all pile,
it's chaos but yours, and that's your own style.
Their socks form a hilltop inside the pile,
they fold up their shirts but leave it a while.
The clothes slip down off the hamper's edge, floor,
the whole room is screaming this task is a chore.
She kept checking the calendar, late then date,
but her coffee went cold on the desk's far plate.
Her hands shook slightly, she lost that full feel,
staring at numbers stuck spinning like a wheel.
I searched the couch, the bed, the whole damn room,
but every time I thought I'd found the zoom,
it slipped right out and dropped beneath the table,
now tangled tight with a forgotten cable.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: She trades her shoes for the mud that's nice and dry,
her laughter rises in a cloudless blue sky.
Crumbs from her snacks build a crusty little heap,
she digs for gold where the puddles run deep.
I watched the water drip through the tear in my leak,
I haven't seen blue skies for more than a week.
I'll stitch it with string and a little bit of mend,
because hope doesn't stop when the storm starts to end.
I remember the afternoon sea breeze,
how it bent my legs to my sunburned knees.
That broken umbrella gave false shade,
while waves rolled in like a lonely parade.
You made a joke when you saw their face,
"They fit right in," you said with grace.
They know our stories, inside and out, lore,
but I still feel where my old heart got sore.
You've got a ticket to the secret show,
the bouncer doesn't know about it though.
You slide through the crowd and duck under the gate,
the band's playing now—no more waiting to wait.
There's a hint of smoke still lingering in the trace,
like some ghost left behind in this strange space.
What kind of lunch did they pack that still smells like stew?
I don't want to know, but it feels kind of true.
She zeroes in on the shaggy gray aim,
her tail flicks fast, it's her favorite game.
She springs with the grace only cats know how to leap,
then pounces again on the dusty old heap.
We scream the lyrics with reckless joy,
laughing loud enough to destroy.
Our voices waver, we hit no high,
but we sing again—still we try.
She moves through the world at her own steady pace,
leaving room between her and any race.
Even storms pause to admire her calm,
a presence that turns chaos into balm.
I leave the heels behind and go my own style,
these flats got me through ten times my mile.
They stick with me through every hard grind,
no blisters or regrets in my quiet, proud mind.
I scroll through old pics and see us once again,
my thumb still aches where your ring left a chain.
They ask if I miss it, but how do you say "we"
were more than a photo or text in a key?
You launched your plane into its final flight,
the hope in your hand never felt so light.
I watched you crumple each failure to fold,
but let me help you keep this fragile hope in hold.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: I watch the flames flicker and send up white smoke,
my lungs start to burn from the waxy choke.
I lean back, blow hard—just one more try,
but sparks still fly and I swear they might die.
She checks the carton's "best by" date,
then stares at the spoiled curd on her plate.
Her stomach already feels tight with gas,
but hunger won out—now she can't pass.
A single balloon still clings to her blue,
its string wrapped carefully threaded through.
She tries to untangle the hair from the tie,
but leaves it half-loose to drift up to sky.
You open the group chat, ready to cheer,
someone bought rounds for the whole beer.
A weekend trip gets mapped out in a plan,
we're all in this now, sweet little clan.
You dart through the crosswalk with no care or zone,
honking your bell with an aggressive tone.
You never give way, you just aim to cross,
think you're some kind of street-running boss.
I cranked the toaster to its highest flame,
now golden crumbs are mine alone, not shame.
The edges singed and crisp, the perfect char,
they'll serve this at the café down the bar.
First thing he notices is the charred toast's smell,
he knows this routine is a Monday from hell.
He tries again—burns it worse to meet,
now breakfast's a joke he's doomed to repeat.
They send cat videos from some late-night deep,
where silence grows after each text beep.
You wonder if anyone's there or just kind,
or if they're still scrolling, right now behind.
My shovel slams into the frozen ground,
the kind of cold that can't be drowned.
I switch to a chisel, curse a little low,
while time keeps spilling out and snow.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: She scrolls through her feed and she finds something old,
a face she forgot she still needed to hold.
Her thumb taps the name that once sparked a flame,
and now it's a spark she feels proud to reclaim.
You watch your fries disappear from the plate,
they were supposed to be saved for your date.
You try to pretend that you don't still crave,
but swallowing pride isn't easy to brave.
She likes your friend's late-night post filled with pain,
the kind that gets ignored and shared again.
Her fingers hover gentle, almost soft,
then hit the heart—the icon starts to glow aloft.
You hover above the water so still,
your tiny frame defying all thrill.
Each flap of your iridescent wing
proves you're something the world needs to sing.
She's never still once she finds her seat,
she tells the same tale every repeat.
The GPS says the route is the fare,
but she talks loud enough to fill up the air.
You've got a budget, a list, and a plan,
but the store had sales you just couldn't ban.
You paid more than you thought was the way,
but hey—it was worth it, your meal today.
She always tiptoes to keep her bare feet
from waking the house with a heavy repeat.
But the chill from the floor hits her right through the tile,
though she shivers and grins with a sleepy smile.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: You clip the coupon off with a bit of a cough,
it's half off, but still worth the sniffle and scoff.
The clerk says your bag is too heavy for bag,
and asks if you mind carrying the price tag.
You've perfected that slow, steady flow,
letting just enough escape to make a show.
Each drop lands with calculated drip,
you control the world from your tiny grip.
The garlic slices glisten in a flash,
each clove precise, no hint of a mash.
They've peeled the bulbs with care, not haste or peel,
their hands move smooth, like kitchen steel.
He stands alert at the fence and the air,
his bark directed at nowhere with flair.
It's not that he's wrong, just that it's his claims,
he's sure something's there by its ghostly names.
The waffle is stale, the eggs are still cold,
and the coffee tastes like it's been sitting too old.
You stir your bowl of mushy grits,
hoping for something that isn't just bits.

topic: someone handing you a surprise gift
lines: They pressed the box into my palm with their hand,
a gesture so sudden, I couldn't understand.
I ask myself later why I didn't cry,
but even joy feels heavy when love says goodbye.
You see your sneaker as a new treat,
the rabbit nibbles with focused beat.
They gently grind through the worn-out lace,
leaving a hole in your personal space.
You watched it fall in a tragic little fell,
the silence stayed long after the spell.
Its white hat touched the wooden ground,
and you forgot what it once was crowned.
A balloon lifts me upward like a soft breeze,
Its string still wrapped around my car keys.
I laugh as it dances in a tight coil,
Shiny and stubborn, but not a foil.
Each twist adds another to this fragile link,
I pause from my coffee just to watch them drink.
I'll bend one more clip and the pattern will start,
a quiet rebellion tugging at my heart.
You missed the exit, no clear clue why,
your GPS just said "turn" twenty-two times by.
You get off the ramp that leads nowhere, off,
the fumes from your rage almost give you a cough.
I let it sit just long enough to be warm,
the edges curling in soft, slow motion form.
My morning starts with the scent of fresh bread,
I savor how it slips gently off the spread.
I watch the butter slowly start to spread,
it melts like memories from years long dead.
I lift the corner of my warm toast,
and savor moments I hold the most.
You could've at least held your heel and your seam,
that sock fell apart mid-step, like a bad dream.
Now you're stuck searching for a pair that will lace,
but nothing looks right in this sad, mismatched place.
You trace every scar left behind by the dent,
the metal is still held upright by the bent.
Time has crept slow but the color won't rust,
only your memories settle as dust.
I carry my sweat-soaked towel with pride,
still catching glances with each confident stride.
It smells of salt and stubborn intent,
but I'm proud of how far I've come since I was bent.
The pan is alive with grease-fed fire,
I watch it with something close to desire.
The air fills with curls of spicy smoke,
my breath hangs low, but I'd never choke.
They dim the room but never shut the light,
browsing memes or late-night gossip might.
The scroll keeps coming, steady as a feed,
they say they're tired—but their hands still need.
She pulls her jacket close, the air feels cold,
Her hands move fast—she doesn't want to be sold.
Her fingers stay tight on the leather grip,
But coins are already starting to slip.
You watch them shift and slowly take form,
a dragon or lion or coming storm.
You try to tell them what they might say,
but they melt and fade by the close of day.
It gave out with a soft, familiar snap,
I opened my bag like a travel-worn map.
I tied up the gap with a shoelace thread,
and carried the weight it was never meant spread.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: She hit the record button without a line,
and the laugh track kicked in—it was all mine.
It blared during silence, missed the whole cue,
but now we just roll with the laugh and rue.

topic: seeing a post from your childhood home
lines: She sees a post tagged with her old back yard,
a memory flares up by the front guard.
The feed just won't let her scroll past that drop,
she deletes the app out of spite for the crop.
She chops raw carrots with a dull old knife,
muttering how this is ruining her life.
She tries to core the mess but can't get the core,
so she throws the whole batch in for more.
I practiced the conversation, now there's no flow,
they asked what I do, but I still don't quite know.
I spill coffee on my shirt, this looks like a mess,
I wish I could leave and pretend I was stress-less.
She folds her arms tight and gives up her claim
to legroom, but keeps her windowpane name.
Her shoulders still ache from the seat's stubborn press,
she sleeps just enough to escape her distress.
The project was due and your team lost the clue,
but you fixed every hole and filled up each cue.
You didn't wait for help or hope they would take
—you did it all fast and now have a break.
I mastered the art of the traffic jam game,
tuning out the horns and the growing flame.
My playlist's perfect—I haven't got to move,
just sit here smug and silently prove.
The moment hits like a text that just end,
the screen still buzzing from old friend.
He checks the group chat—no one left the same,
only his handle echoes with no one to claim.
I built an elaborate nap scheme,
where every second feels like a dream.
They think it's laziness, but it's a rare skill—
to shut out life and rest is true will.
You turn the wheel hard as you raise your shout,
the argument is old, you're still going about
how every problem started on that same street,
your voice loops like a song I've heard too repeat.
She's making a small but real change,
sipping from cups others would think strange.
Each glass helps her stay more alert and keep,
a calm inside, now truly deep.

topic: a taxi driver yelling on phone
lines: I watch the taxi roll down a wet, empty street,
the driver yells into his phone's cold heat.
He mutters something rough about this job,
and I feel the weight of it, a silent sob.
You keep the knob set gently on the calm,
a steady glow that whispers like a balm.
It's not a rush, it's not a spark or art—
just you and heat, the way it warms the part.
You do a little dance when your watch starts to cheer,
convinced there's some reason you need to be near.
It buzzes again, you laugh and give it a spin,
but joy's just a habit—you keep on your skin.

topic: steaming coffee in a blue mug
lines: I brewed it from beans in my chipped old pot,
the steam says goodbye to what I've already got.
I sip and I savor the quiet and sigh,
my window frames morning, gray tones of the sky.

topic: walking past each other in a crowd
lines: I swear we locked eyes just to see,
but the crush of the crowd pushed me and thee—
we brushed like strangers who never could pass,
our near-miss now legend in sidewalk grass.
You grip your wallet as you pass the mall park,
the neon flickers, casting a dim dark.
A stranger walks close but isn't that near,
you count your cards twice from sheer fear.
I pretend I'm listening to these calls,
while my mind drifts through imaginary walls.
There's a life out there that feels so far,
where my quiet dreams don't have to scar.
You claim it was meant to be part of the play,
but you tipped it over and just walked away.
I'm sure there's some strategy in what you do,
but honestly, darling, I have no clue.
They turn the living room into a toy pile,
they jump around with such unorthodox style.
A couch becomes a ramp for full-speed slide,
I can't decide if they're chaos or pride.
My lecture notes dissolved into my brain,
I figured out the whole thing all again.
The paperless chaos looks like a mess,
but I aced the test—turns out it's a success.
She tugs so hard the leash feels like a lead,
her eyes set forward, ignoring my head.
There's chaos in every step she wants to run,
though for her it's pure joy, for me it's no fun.
You watched the frog take its sudden leap,
the ripples spread out in a wet heap.
Now the pond's surface goes smooth and still,
but the memory gives you a small thrill.

topic: ice forming on the car windshield
lines: You wake to ice and instinctively blame,
the frost for drawing this jagged frame.
It's a masterpiece, but it won't let you go—
your engine's still cold, stuck beneath the snow.
He walked through the yard and left a muddy track,
the clean floors were now under full attack.
We all know whose paws left the worst of the blame,
that little black dog still hasn't faced its shame.
They're staring at the screen, trying every code,
Even airplane mode won't override the load.
The connection fails again, their face turns pale,
And panic leaves behind a desperate email trail.
The steam begins to curl into the air,
turning the kitchen into something strange and rare.
The whistle lets out a high-pitched call,
but they're too lost in thought to notice the small.
You stare at the snack aisle like it's a final aisle,
the trail mix spins and the candy chills while.
You claim you came here just to buy what you want,
but somehow the cart looks like a snack-packed haunt.
You swore the train was running five minutes late,
so you sat and watched the sky turn gray to wait.
You're not even sure why you still feel the call,
but maybe today's the day it drops the ball.

topic: a neon sign buzzing at night
lines: The neon sign outside still won't flicker,
its digital twin reads a bored ticker.
The night feels a little too cold,
but I stand and stare, somehow quite bold.
I dug through the box labeled "outdated gear,"
and found a hat that could end my career.
It's too late to hide it—it's a total fail—
now I'm the joke in the family group mail.
You tap around to find a better spot,
but the bars just drop—you barely got
a buffer. Now you pace and try to scroll,
though streaming feels more like a dream than a goal.

topic: a book left open on the nightstand
lines: She leaves the reading light on all through the night,
Her breath shallow, her thoughts half in flight.
The book stays open on the same worn page,
Like she's trapped by what she can't just yet age.
The audience thinks they have some kind of clue,
they all wait for the cue from the crowd in queue.
I check my phone—everyone is stuck ahead,
the clap spreads early, and I panic and spread.
You stood out there in the soaked green field,
boots slipping where the grass would not yield.
The sky wept in a slow, soft drop,
and time ripened like a bittersweet crop.
Your sad song keeps looping on replay,
The melody's worn out and starts to fray.
I'm stuck listening, it brings on such shame,
You won't skip the track—still the **same**.
I tried to sleep but my head wouldn't twist,
it ached like a ghost trying to exist.
The morning light came with a slow groan,
my neck felt like rust on each single bone.
You tried to read it but kept getting flap,
each corner stuck fast in a paper trap.
Now it's peeling slowly, inch by inch,
your heel even helped—like a secret pinch.
I wake up twisted in a strange new pose,
my head won't turn all the way to my toes.
A panic creeps in, slow but full of fear,
did I have a stroke while I was barely near?
He stands there walking up the moving still,
coffee in one hand, lost in his spill.
No one calls him out or asks him to wait,
we all just shuffle through the messed-up gate.
She lies awake, her pulse kicks in again,
some midnight thought won't let her brain remain.
She counts the hours or hears a soft knock,
then blames the wind for the chair's sudden rock.
There's a rabbit chewing your shoe's lace,
and leaving small teeth marks in that place.
It's a total mess with the fabric and thread,
but somehow it still gets back inside your head.
You left your lunch somewhere far away,
now it's stinking up your bag today.
What kind of lunch was it without meat?
A snack you forgot and just couldn't eat.
I thought those peas had an expiration date,
but no, they're still good for a quick debate.
They look like mush, but I'm too polite to flush
them down the drain where they'd cause quite a mush.
They're belting "Happy Birthday" at full yell,
this noise is turning my peace into hell.
I just want a quiet slice of cake,
not a performance — come on, take a break.
You grab the remote and pop open the case,
The cartoon channel's your favorite place.
You shout along with the hero's cheer,
As time slips by without a single tear.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: You fix my scarf when the button comes thread,
