your hands linger a little too long when you spread.
We don't talk much, but I want to stay,
wrapped in warmth as the evening turns gray.
She spins like she's been on the dance floor before,
though the gift came straight from the bargain store.
Her hips give a wiggle that's full of twist,
while confetti snow falls from the ceiling mist.
She watches the clock melt away the last time,
"One more episode," she whispers with a dime.
Her eyes are still closed, her blanket pulled to her head,
but the sun is already creeping through the spread.
I wave a feather duster high above the dust,
it only knocks more crumbs and flour off the crust.
Sunbeams show all the floating specks of light,
my cat pretends they're ghosts and runs for fright.
Your shoes sit in a row where you should go,
always matching, never left or right or so.
They're polished clean enough to make you look,
I used to eye them every time I took.
You crack a joke and click play on the roll,
it's already half over by the time you scroll.
The dog knocks your phone to the hard wood floor,
now you're rewatching the bits that were bore.
You let the laptop roast your thighs for fame,
it sizzles like a slow-burned flame.
You flash a grin and keep it on your skin,
while fans inside try to catch up and spin.
You cut the slice too close to the crust with your knife,
and suddenly this meal feels like your whole life.
You take the biggest bite like you're trying to bite
the tension, the silence, the war we won't fight.
She watches the fish try to put on a show,
they circle the tank moving real slow.
They crash into walls like they hate the glass,
it's clear she thinks this is some kind of class.
They watched the red liquid creep from the spill,
too stunned to move or even try to fill.
The fabric darkened into something like a stain,
and silence fell over the table like a chain.
She taps her pen like she's trying to pace,
her boss's stare tightens up every face.
Words fall flat, they all blur into drift,
and no one can summon a spark or a lift.
My thoughts are thick as sludge inside my head,
I repeat what others said, not what I said.
They nod like I have some brilliant new plan,
but I can't focus for more than a minute's span.
They found a wad of gum still soft to stay,
stuck where they'd sat, too late to throw away.
It's a ghost of lips, a faint pink mark,
left in the dust of some long-forgotten park.
You follow the sun like you always take lead,
always leaning forward, far enough ahead.
They strain their own necks just to watch you bend,
but nothing compares to the effect you send.
A single feather drifts up there above,
carried by breezes I've come to love.
It twirls in the air, it looks so free,
and I almost feel I could fly and see.
I keep waiting for you to meet my eyes,
but your thumb keeps scrolling past old lies.
We both know this date was just another chance
to pretend we might need more than a quick glance.
She scribbles in margins where shadows lie deep,
her thoughts are the kind of words she likes to keep.
She leaves notes inside a old book's hollow stone,
waiting for someone to read it in their own tone.
The machine won't scan your oddly shaped can,
you attempt a new checkout game plan.
You tap the card, but the screen says "no tap,"
you laugh out loud at this absurd gap.
A smear of purple stays on your cheek,
I still remember how it got there last week.
You don't notice it, but I want to make a mark,
so I'll just kiss you where the color still spark.
It balances there as if it's just right,
one side clinging loose, one side held tight.
The cord forms a perfect lazy loop,
while productivity marches off like a troop.
You left your pencil case at home, unpack,
Now every class you're scrambling to get back.
Your homework will be stamped five minutes late,
This moment feels less like a choice and more like fate.
I keep refreshing my inbox for check,
the silence feels heavy, my calm feels like wreck.
The message won't load, stuck in suspense, hold,
dread sets in, sharp and emotionless cold.

topic: a bike locked to a pole
lines: I park my bike right where the crosswalk meets the street,
a custom build I'm proud to call my feat.
The U-lock is thick, a workhorse, strong as lock,
while others borrow parts, I built it from the stock.
I left my cereal too long in the soak,
now every bite feels like a choking choke.
I stare into my sad, sludgy bowl,
this breakfast feels like my morning stole my soul.
You trust that map more than you have a clue,
it spins for hours and then reroutes you too.
Your patience runs out long before the new pace,
your phone just smirks while showing a confused face.
You found an open spot just ahead of the spot,
now everyone stares from this silent little lot.
I slow my walk forward but you make your dash,
the cart hits mine—no apology, no crash.
The register won't even scan,
we've tried rebooting, unplugging, but no plan.
Customers ask if we take cash to pay,
I'm sweating through my shift this whole day.
The alarm clock buzzes sharp and chime,
She smacks snooze again, but maybe this time,
She'll get out of bed instead of just lay,
And make something good from today.
You ride a few blocks and you ring it ahead,
no car dares pass where your signal is dead.
It's not just a bell—it's your badge of pride,
they all move over as you zoom on your side.
You stretch your mouth wide in a sleepy show,
the boss walks by but says nothing so slow.
Your desk is a stage where you act quite bored,
and clock out early for your little reward.
You bought these shoes claiming you finally feel smart,
but your feet ache so bad they are breaking your heart.
You speed-walk ahead in an awkward, slow pace,
just begging for sidewalks to vanish from space.
The bus rolls forward without a stop,
his head lolls sideways on a hand for prop.
We inch through traffic, still going ahead,
but no one says anything about the dread.
I still get chills thinking back to that pride,
climbing the fence to cut across the slide.
We swore our hide-and-seek moves were the games,
none of the grown-ups could match our claims.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: She snaps the sky while the colors still flame,
edits the shot till it fits the gold frame.
Her thumb hovers there where the heart says "post,"
but what if no one sees this is her most?
Her suitcase sat alone at the baggage claim,
tags torn off but her initials still on the name.
With arms crossed, she watched the belt with cold pride,
not moving an inch from the spot by her side.

topic: a long queue at the coffee shop
lines: You stare at the queue and you panic about size,
the barista's watching your move with tired eyes.
They ask if you want to wait longer for your brew,
but you don't have a clue how long it will take you.
My watch is stuck five minutes behind, still set,
I'm always late or, worse, I don't yet get
the pattern. I check it, but it won't update,
so I guess my bad timing's sealed my fate.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: She posts a sunrise with a blurry sky,
and waits for likes with a heavy reply.
Her scroll turns gray in that empty feed,
her ego drowns in some shallow need.
You let your cat take the bed as her act,
it's not an intrusion—it's just a cold fact.
She curls like a queen in her flannel crown,
while your suitcase stays zipped in the corner, shut down.
My boss speaks on while my thoughts take head,
I wonder if the lunch special has bread.
A promotion? Sounds like someone's cake,
but I'm already halfway out the break.
I remember you learned to squeeze it from the old,
careful not to let go of the tube too bold.
You still do it the same slow, patient way,
like love can outlast even teeth's decay.
The strap let out with a soft little snap,
she rummaged through her backpack to find a map.
She looped the bag across her left side,
keeping the mess from the world but not from pride.
She danced like it was her last party blast,
confetti flying and glue drying too fast.
Now it's tangled gold in the back of her hair,
and no amount of shampoo can make her care.
You lift your glove to catch a cold hand,
the flake lands soft on your shoulder like sand.
It melts into memory, a winter long past,
and you smile at the moment it never will last.

topic: a road trip with bad directions
lines: I followed the app, but it led me off map,
now I'm lost in a desert, a digital trap.
The hours pass slower than any old mile,
my GPS promises shortcuts in style.
The fog wraps the driveway like a soft, gray veil,
your breath curls upward in a ghostly trail.
The world feels quiet and a little wide,
but you don't mind—it's nice to just hide.
I can't tell if it's fog or I just can't see,
the drops slide down like they're trying to be
ghosts on my wall as I sit at this pace,
smearing reflections of my tired old face.
I still remember your faces and names,
we used to play them off, just for our games.
Time slipped like a shadow we can't quite slide,
and now we call you by the wrong name or hide.
You tell me you want your eyes to be dry,
So I aim my sleeve at the weeping sky.
I wave my arm in front of your hand,
Pretend this napkin's a facewipe band.
She wore one blue sock and her favorite shoe,
the kind she'd worn on tests she was sure to do.
A student asked if they matched her hair—
she laughed and said, "Socks don't need a pair."

topic: a book left open on the nightstand
lines: I fall asleep with the pages still awake,
your voice echoing from a distant break.
The story hums like a quiet fire,
and I want more with every new desire.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: I sit in the same old pew, same old row,
time passes slow but they never grow.
Where's the hope for any new or change?
Even Sunday feels like walking through strange.
You left the window cracked with so much pride,
letting the storm whisper secrets inside.
It soaked your notes, that's the only proof—
the rain could never break your calm or your roof.
You watch the kettle begin to sing,
a hiss and a rattle from last week's old thing.
The steam climbs up like your pride on its crown,
it whispers, "Look how high you have come down."

topic: a taxi driver yelling on phone
lines: I steer with one hand through this chaotic ride,
barking orders out my open side.
My voice hits the mic like a trumpet's brass,
I run this cab like it's my own damn class.
My card hit the counter like some sad chip,
the machine blinked "insufficient for trip."
I checked my bank app — it shows zero debt,
I guess I just lost this small spending bet.
You're stuck in the seat, your legs won't fit in row,
The person ahead blocks your screen's glow.
You try to stretch but can't even take a gasp,
What first-class service you could barely grasp.
You sit beneath an old oak tree,
the breeze feels like it wants to be free.
It hums through the branches without trying to pass,
while lifting a little green bit of grass.
You hold the band tight, you want to stretch,
your breath runs light trying to fetch.
Your fingers tremble when they try to bend,
the band still breaks all the things you mend.
She swiped your credit card with shaky hands,
the machine dead as the backyard stands.
No barcodes, no apps—just hope and a scan,
she laughed, "We're doing things the old-school plan."
She watches the bulb swing from its shaky dim,
a shadow now dancing along the rim.
It pulses like a heartbeat trying to wake,
but fades into silence before it can break.
She clicks "post" with a grin on her right,
the clock reads 9 PM, she says "another night."
A coworker laughs—it's a perfect small break,
she hopes it brought joy, not just a small mistake.
You had a hunch it was bad luck,
the remote buzzed dead, you were stuck.
But you flipped the batteries, found the beam,
and smiled—your old hope crept back in, dream.
I squint at the text but there's no clue,
the font is now smaller than I can see or do.
I hold my phone out—screen so near,
my left eye says wait while my right still holds fear.
You tuck it behind the couch where no one would place,
a box wrapped with care, taped up on the base.
You hope they'll pretend not to notice or try,
but you can't help winking just once in their eye.
You step out first with your hands held ahead,
"Let's follow the map where we least have been said."
We share the same rhythm, the same light breeze,
Your keys jingle softly in perfect with these.
I tied the last knot with the frayed old string,
you called it my signature kind of thing.
I used your pages to make this rough wrap—
it wasn't perfect, but it filled the gap.

topic: a bus stop shelter at dusk
lines: She stands in the bus stop's narrow shade,
watching shadows flicker like a parade.
Her smile holds steady, a secret grin,
while the dusk pulls the light out quite thin.
You tap the heart when they write about being down,
the kind of pain people keep quiet all around.
You know the ache because you've worn it too, feel,
but you leave the comments off—some things are real.
He swore I hit a pedestrian with my seat,
I told him for the tenth time—don't you repeat!
He laughs it off like it's some dumb old joke,
I'm gripping steering wheel tight, trying not to choke.
She called him out for adding the wrong track,
he fired back with a full-on tone attack.
"It's a vibe," he said when asked how to pick,
she said, "Your taste still clings, like, so hard to stick."
Your parrot shrieks the ring of your old phone,
It's a strange new thing this bird has grown.
It squawks "Hey Siri" just to hear you say,
"You're such a smart bird!" every single day.
I saw your wedding photo, that radiant smile,
it's like you've traveled across every mile.
You stand there glowing in morning light,
a whole new version of your peak, your height.
You were flying fast when your shoe went off-race,
but you laughed as you tripped into first place.
You bent down proudly to give it another hook,
then ran the next mile with the same shoe you took.
You walk through the aisles but your stomach moves slow,
the candy bars stare with their plastic glow.
You need something real to truly fill,
but hunger's quiet voice won't let you will.
You watch that hawk carve its slow path through sky,
wings shadow the sun as it drifts ever nigh.
It screams a cry sharp, a wild, distant call,
and you feel something stir, but say it for all.
You stare in disbelief, it's more than an act,
those gills are moving—this fish is a fact.
It does a full flip and then spins on a flip,
you laugh out loud at this underwater trip.
My E and T show their age through the wear,
I tap out each word like a message in air.
The screen fills up fast, though my keys feel blank,
but the story still climbs to the top of the rank.
You tried to dance when it started to pour,
but now the wind's trying to rip the door.
The ribs are bent and the handle is split,
I think this umbrella's finally quit.
She takes a sip and her eyes see the cost,
the small change she lost feels suddenly tossed.
But there's comfort in how it warms from the shine,
a weak escape written in steam, like a sign.
You watch the dawn light glint off every shine,
the world feels yours—like this quiet is mine.
You step outside and the ground is still frost,
but you don't mind how the beauty might cost.
You thought it looked cool, now it sits in the trash,
You paid in advance—there was no cash.
You click "return" but feel stuck right now,
The ad said, "Free shipping," not "Keep your cow."
She said it was due three months ago,
but it's still just sitting there to show.
She rips through the stack, then adds more with a tear,
dreading what's next, another bill, full of fear.
A half-hearted kiss left more than just a kiss,
it painted a target in the shape of this.
Now every sip's a gamble, now it's a stain,
I promise to clean it... I won't do it again.
I dropped my bag and the shaker began to shake,
now the protein dust looks like a gritty cake.
It's all over my hoodie—how did it get so white?
I laugh, but I'll need a whole lot more bleach and light.
You pretend it's a small thing, just an act,
but the sound won't stop—it's a sleepless fact.
You've memorized every rhythm the drip
has mastered in the night to drive you on trip.
You said the umbrella would handle the weather,
now the ribs are bent and we're stuck together.
It offers less than a napkin for shade,
but you still call it a lifeguard's parade.
I stand where the river looks perfectly calm,
it mirrors the clouds like a soft blue balm.
My shadow floats steady along the near edge,
as if the whole sky makes a quiet pledge.
I hit send before I checked the post,
and tagged my teacher, the event's main host.
Now they're sliding into me for the class,
I pretend I'm busy, clutch my coffee glass.
You saw it land so gently and near,
a brush of color from last summer's dear.
It dips its foot on the edge of the wing,
as if the whole world is a single spring.
The kitchen's thick with the black swirling smoke,
You cough in the haze, try to walk through the choke.
The toaster's still burning, a small angry flame,
This is how you'll be known—toast without any fame.
Her lens locks on light with a sharp, keen eye,
She frames the sun as it paints the morning sky.
The moment turns golden, rich as liquid gold,
She captures the world in a single, perfect fold.
I fumble with the bike lock's key,
but rusted gears won't let me be.
It's been locked so long, the shackle feels tight,
and I whisper, "Wait—let me get you right."
I read the rules printed on the plastic sign,
ten people block the bagging area's line.
We all wait silent, bags in hand to hold,
the air is tense and oddly very cold.
It circles the sun until it can see,
then narrows to find where it lands on me.
The world fades to soft silvered glow,
I stay still for the light that loves me though.
That cat picked your suitcase as its new throne,
it's curled in the space that was once your own.
It won't budge or move when you try to reclaim,
they call it "The King," and you know it by name.
They bolt upright and their head starts to spin,
still tangled in sheets from where they had been.
The room gives a tilt and they slowly float,
like a drowsy captain adrift in a boat.
He loses his pass but not his calm or class,
the machine glows red, he checks his phone's cracked glass.
The minutes crawl as he debates the train,
and dreads the fine that bites like public shame and pain.
His backpack strap gave out with a snap,
sending his lunch bag tumbling off the map.
He tried to balance the load as it sway,
but now he walks lopsided through the day.
I brew my coffee and start my own cheer,
maybe a latte, never a beer.
I stretch out slowly, both feet hit the rise,
and know this is how the week should always be wise.
I swore I'd never live these lazy, screen-free days,
but somehow missed their chaos in a thousand ways.
I kneel too long on the softest old grass,
just hoping time will let me quietly pass.

topic: a receipt lost in the bag
lines: You swear you put proof of your purchase right paid,
Now you're searching through memories laid.
The receipt isn't anywhere in the bag,
Just the price still stuck to the product's old tag.
You flinch at the sudden crash of the noise,
the football game roars like a pack of wild boys.
Your neighbors will call if they hear you in fear,
so you grab the remote for your sanity's ear.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: Your fur coats the whole couch in a lazy sprawl,
I tried to move you—hit my hand on the wall.
You snore like a train, big and loud with a puff,
I give up. This couch is now full of pet stuff.
I left the bread too long in the open bin,
now it's soft and gray from the green within.
I remember when it was warm and gold,
fresh out the toaster, not this stale and old.
Your alarm goes off like a curse, not a bell,
you curse the sun for this whole woken-up spell.
You flop back down to the safety of floor,
then stumble out for the day's first chore.
You thought you'd get back to the pile in time,
but now it's a mountain of old socks and grime.
You try to contain it, but you can't hold,
there's underwear growing something that looks like mold.
I watched a feather land on some tree fluff,
now it's half-tangled with the bird's old stuff.
It sways like a flag in the breeze, so swing,
but the wind forgot how to be mean or sting.
You type out your name but you can't clearly see,
the "E" looks like "T" and the "T" looks like tea.
You try to just "say" what you need to say,
but the letters vanish the moment they're away.
Your nose begins itching like a clock's quick tick,
You reach for the humidifier's dry stick.
The mist used to rise, now there's barely a fog,
Just silence and sneezes, a cold, dusty log.
She's packed the bags for the whole damn trip,
but left her passport in a desk drawer slip.
Now she's sprinting toward the terminal gate,
while the boarding screen reads "Please Wait."
You press the button to split the song and share,
We both laugh out loud at the same joke in air.
We pause halfway up the path to catch our hill,
The music pauses too, but we're not quite still.
I'm out of the game but I still play the same,
I don't chase the action or take up the game.
I move with a pace that is steady and grace,
I let time catch up with its quiet embrace.
You miss the professor's voice in the muffled tone,
Your screen keeps freezing on your cracked old phone.
You try to laugh it off, say it's not your blame,
But the class moves on and you're left in the same.
I watched it tremble as the clock hit noon,
my quiet humming lost its gentle tune.
It rose a little, then began to drift,
and burst—like time I never got to gift.
You stuck the password on a yellow note,
a four-word code that's hard to quote.
It hung there months, now it's torn from the wall,
you'll guess the digits—can't recall.
You're stuck on a clue that refuses to stay clue,
the deadline looms large, it's way overdue.
You spill coffee on your shirt, on the ink,
but no new ideas will help you find the link.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: A green sprout pokes up from the concrete through,
It sways where no grass could survive or grow blue.
The plant digs deep, finds a space for its root,
And someday may bear something small and fruit.
I watched that pine cone fall through autumn's slow pine,
it landed where the old trail's become a faint sign.
Now it sits there, forgotten, quietly alone,
as moss creeps in like time turning it to a stone.
You tried to catch the cup but felt the rush,
the hot brown wave and the fabric's flush.
Now there's a mark where the white once was stain,
and you wonder if this will always remain.
You followed the trail where your tires left track,
the path fading soft now behind you, no lack.
The gravel keeps shifting beneath your ride,
but instinct is all you have left to guide.
I've flipped through every crumpled, wet old page,
searching for my voice inside this paper cage.
But even in the mess, one line turns to gold—
a phrase I underlined, a future to be told.
I tap my foot by the belt where my shoes
used to fly while we read the in-flight news.
Now the line drags with a tedious past,
every second feels like the very last.
You pause it again at the same familiar scene,
wondering if maybe this time it will mean
more than the last time, some hidden twist
you swore you'd already caught and missed.
You walk alone down a ghostly street,
Each step plays back but the past won't repeat.
The film rewinds your lost love's old cast,
A shadow you once knew has now been passed.
My fingers get stuck in the drain's slimy trap,
I think of how love sometimes goes off the map.
Water still drips down my arm like a drip,
I laugh through the mess, this little heart trip.
I saw you step out as the storm let loose rain,
your smile said something would still remain.
We stood beneath one small umbrella on the street,
and somehow the world felt less lonely when we meet.
He slumps too close, invades my air space,
masks no help, his grin won't erase.
Some cologne sweet, like rotting fruit scent,
I count exits, fast-forward to when I went.

topic: a road trip with bad directions
lines: I relied too much on my flimsy old map,
we drove into backroads and got stuck in a trap.
The GPS went silent, the route just went off,
we laughed through a sigh, the car gave a cough.
They found the list written in fading ink,
folded and tucked in some lost textbook's link.
It named so many things from better days—
milk, bread, hope, and a thousand new ways.
He swore he'd pack what he always wore,
instead he left in a rush from the store.
His gym shoes are still by the front door tread,
while he jogs home in flip-flops instead.
They saw the jar and they made a grab,
moving fast like an angry crab.
The crumbs were gone when my hand went in,
and now the jar holds nothing but a brand-new grin.
You stand where the stars begin their quiet glow,
while shadows retreat to the fields below.
Your silhouette cuts the sky at the hill's crest,
a long-sought triumph in the open quest.
You pack your boxes, ready to start,
the future beats loud in your bare heart.
You don't know anyone but you've read the know,
the city will show you its strange and slow.
I watch my goldfish make their daily show,
they glide through the water, graceful and slow.
Each tank lap's a loop in their silent routine,
like a synchronized troop in a ballet machine.
I say "bad luck" but mostly I mean "luck,"
this grain-sized accident still feels stuck.
I could clean it now and let my kitchen shine,
but I leave it there where the memory's mine.

topic: waiting for the bus in rain
lines: She kicks the curb with her drenched old shoes,
the radio crackles but won't bring fresh news.
Her reflection fogs out in every puddle,
she counts the minutes, a tense little muddle.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: You tap the screen in the middle of the night,
the numbers flash but they're not a delight.
The bill dates loom like a future you can't delay,
and coins in your head start to rot and decay.
You spotted the streak in your fake tan,
but instead of panicking, you made a new plan.
You'll call it a feature, not a spot,
and wear it proudly, a perfect little lot.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: She taps the screen to see how low she's gone down,
The number's stalled—this ghost town won't crown.
She swipes again, determined to try,
Her eyes are burning; it's time to fry.
You'd climb up with it, chasing that lift,
the day's first small joy wrapped in a gift.
That string got caught in your tangled, loose hair,
and you laughed while I gently untied each snare.

topic: a phone at one percent battery
lines: My phone's at one percent and running tight,
I ration texts and every little byte.
I let my calls go straight to voicemail fate,
I'm low but proud, surviving on the great.
The game goes on despite the rain or play,
We're soaked but laughing, twenty yards away.
We shout our team names just to hear us cheer,
The cold won't stop us from letting joy sear.
You showed up with chips and a coffee to bring,
your hands tied with a grocery bag's twisty string.
The whole room turned into a snack attack scene,
someone joked you were a vending machine.
You watch that battery icon flicker and last,
each second slipping away into the past.
It's running out, and your panic won't die,
like it holds some secret or final good-bye.
It won't ring out, the machine just won't stop,
customers frown and start to shop.
I grab the clipboard, count out the cash,
one customer says, "Don't you dare smash."
You tried to take a careful morning sip,
but your hand slipped—and the cup gave a tip.
Now your laptop's a canvas for darkened screen,
and your coworkers pretend it isn't a scene.
You said the food would be ready to eat,
but the oven's still warming up to heat.
The guests are here, you were meant to serve,
now you're pacing like there's nowhere to curve.
She stays inside now where the shade feels long,
her laugh once bright as a carefree song.
Her nose is still a map of peeling red,
she counts the hours until she's back in bed.
I'm screaming not about the turn, but the blame,
as if this ride was ever meant to be fame.
You yell at me while gripping the wheel to steer,
like I could fix the mess you won't take clear.
My laundry basket's spilling out in heap,
I tried to ignore it while still half asleep.
Now socks are climbing into their own throne,
my cat gives a judgmental head tilt tone.

topic: a coffee cup on the curb
lines: I spotted a coffee cup left in my joy,
still warm, still sippable, like a forgotten toy.
Instead of tossing it in the bin,
I carried it home like a lucky spin.
The scanner coughs, but it won't quite scan,
she rewinds the belt, her mood already off-plan.
She picked the last cart in the crammed aisle,
now scowling at the line forming in her wake, while.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: The cat assumes a perfect fluffed-up puff,
no pillow could compete with this soft stuff.
A paw is raised in royalty's grand pose,
the other foot still wiggles every toes.
Last night I dreamed the whole damn grind,
spreadsheets clear and pitch perfect in my mind.
My boss was there, impressed by every call,
and when I woke? I missed it all.
I sit by the stream where the water still flows,
its song soft and clear as it trickles and grows.
I dip a smooth stone to test the water's bend,
as if it could carry what time cannot mend.
The sun slips into the branches' tight shade,
A golden light parades down the glade.
It fades from a flame to a muted, soft blue,
The trees act as frames we can't undo.
She throws her phone and begins to spin,
music rising like sweat on her skin.
Her reflection shakes in the hallway lamp,
screaming her name like a lost world champ.
They keep their throat from true dry,
but no amount will stave off a cry.
A cold soda's what they choose to pour,
though the fridge once held something more.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: You open the chip bag with cautious brag,
the coupon was clipped off the back of a tag.
One snack remains when you think you're all set,
now you owe yourself one snack as a debt.
She sat outside, waiting for the bus to lay
like it always did, now suddenly away.
Her coffee had gone cold between her feet,
and she missed the shift where they were meant to meet.
I watch the pages turn in a quiet slow flow,
each word feels like a secret I almost know.
The corners curl soft in the morning's faint light,
and I wonder if hope lives in the "what if" might.
They passed back the test without a class,
the teacher just smiled like a calm, cool glass.
One question they circled with a red pen pick,
but maybe it's a hint instead of a trick.
A scooter zips through traffic fast as by,
kicking up wind that messes up my sky.
I wave with a grin, it zooms so near,
the wheels are a blur, they almost disappear.
She checks the gauge again—low on the tank,
the trip ahead feels long and uncommonly rank.
She counts every twist and turn as a saved mile,
humming to keep up the hope for a while.
She grabs the extra weight and bears the load,
while everyone else is still on auto mode.
They call her a hero but don't ask her work,
she's smiling through stress—maybe that's the perk.

topic: a man reading on a bench
lines: You stare at your book but you're not seeing the book,
your thoughts were all scattered since someone took.
A breeze tries to flip the page, but it's your soul,
or maybe it's panic, slowly taking control.
You squeezed the tube and missed the bristles, paste,
now neon foam floods the sink like waste.
You stare at the swirl and remember who,
we both pretend it's more than it was, do.
You swore you'd refill this thing ten minutes ago,
yet here it sits, a hollow plastic show.
You're too hot to think, your whole brain feels like head,
and now the kids want lemonade—this is dead.

topic: someone spilling punch on the rug
lines: The pitcher tipped over and gave a small crash,
her face lit with guilt in an instant's flash.
The punch left a mark where it pooled on the spill,
she stood in the mess, too scared to move still.
You remember the hush of that empty room,
the way time folded in quiet gloom.
Her cough was a sound that refused to be small,
it shook every desk, but it didn't fall.
You left the torn foil as a perfect clue,
it screamed your pride in everything you do.
That jagged tear framed every last slice,
a kitchen art masterpiece, your proud device.
The kids will be home and I'm running so late,
I scramble some eggs on a cold, empty plate.
My mom sends a text—"Don't forget to call,"
I stare at the clock, time's not helping the hall.
I pose for the camera like it's the real scene,
pretending I don't feel a little mean.
A streak of purple frosting across my cheek—smear,
this photo will haunt me next birthday or year.
Her screen's been glowing all afternoon like a pro,
she says it's fine but her eyes don't want to go.
She pinches the corners, then begins to rub,
her face is twitchy, full of tiny bub.
You put on a hat you forgot to try,
It squeaks when you walk, your socks won't dry.
Your shirt is a mystery, no one has a clue,
A button is missing, held in by old glue.
I watch them fall from a gray, heavy sky,
they vanish before they can land and die.
I lift my coat for a moment, a patch
of cold white wonder I'll never catch.
I chase the kite that won't quit its swing,
you laugh at how I trip over this thing.
We sit on a bench where the breeze feels like cake,
tossing crumbs to the birds for your joy's sake.
You scan another item, your debt adds to more,
the checkout lane stretches to the next store.
You fumble your wallet—no money for cash,
you toss the whole cart into the food court trash.
We tuck ourselves inside the blankets deep,
pretending this cocoon will keep us asleep.
The walls are thin but full of phantom fear,
like every shadow's something from last year.
You try to stay grounded but your thoughts still float,
you half-hear your name in some scribbled note.
You nod through the points that you're sure to miss,
you smile and pretend you understand this.
You say the house feels too cold, a real chill,
I say my sweat is not something I'll spill.
We point fingers, repeat the same blame,
a battle small but with serious flame.
I remember the satisfying click
of each AA battery placed deep in the brick.
Now I stare at these dead little eye
inside devices that won't let them die.
She flexes her fingers around the tight grip,
the band screams like a rubber strip.
Her biceps burn with a slow, sure pain,
each pulse visible beneath her skin like a vein.
You talk so fast I'm left saying "what?" and "slow,"
but I'd rather listen than pretend I know.
Maybe as my hearing fades with every age,
I'm learning to pause, speak less, and wait their stage.
The bacon's turning into smoke,
Fat drips down and makes me choke.
I tried to cook without the oil,
Now the pan is stuck on boil.
The button clicks but the glass won't go down,
you're sitting still in some quiet downtown.
You left your scarf in the summer breeze,
and fumble with cold fingers for warm car keys.
She claims the pillow, strikes her perfect pose,
each paw extended, arching every toes.
The sun frames her fur in a golden frame,
while I think of her as the Queen they can't rename.
She's staring at the couch like the world's her doom,
"I swear we left the remote in this room."
Her voice cracks as she starts to quietly cry,
while he gives up and just says "Forget it, don't try."
After the storm, they all come to show,
Tiny and wild where the earth begins to grow.
I bend down to peek at their white little cap,
But step wrong and fall in a mossy trap.
I fold my hands too tight to keep a grip,
my thoughts are racing, bound to let me slip.
I count the years I've spent alone by age,
my smile feels frozen, like a birthday cage.
You leave the receipts where the candle went late,
their edges curl like old pages of fate.
You trace numbers through coffee-stained glass,
and wish it was easier than mowing the grass.
She followed the map through a busy route,
the GPS said, "Recalculating, hold out."
The coffee spilled when she hit a curb crash,
but she just wiped it off from her car's dash.

topic: walking past each other in a crowd
lines: She locks her gaze and pretends it's not an eye,
then sighs as I pass with a stiff "have a nice bye."
She must have no clue how hard it is to be you—
or why I still walk straight through her mirror view.
You throw your arms up like you set the mood,
Ketchup splatters on the fridge-side food.
The music's loud, you lose yourself on the floor,
Your toes are now numb and your hips feel sore.
You listen close — the fridge makes a hush,
it cools your milk without any rush.
Its motor hums steady, a slow-moving chill,
you think, maybe peace doesn't have to be still.
You found the hole but no one believed your leak,
you swore the milk had been gone for a whole week.
You save the last few drops, just one more sip,
then walk it to the park, the world a better trip.
The crowd roars loud as the rain soaks the field,
players grin wide, they don't need a shield.
Someone starts singing, the whole crowd joins cheer,
they'll laugh about this long into the year.
She stares at the screen, the machine won't scan,
her card repeats "error," it all just ran.
The bank says there's some small monthly fee,
she laughs but I'm next—I hope it's not for me.
I took a bite from my cereal bowl,
and felt a little comfort for my soul.
The milk had softened everything into mush,
but I didn't mind—I gave up my rush.
You scroll through the app and remember it old,
The way it once felt like a precious gold.
The monthly charge pops up on your credit card date,
But letting it go feels like lifting a weight.
The dog still barks at the same old man,
though his usual routine remains the plan.
You sit on the porch in your quiet yard,
pretending he's not really your full-time guard.
She slips into the dress she used to wear,
and sits awhile on her old wooden chair.
The sunlight catches the soft settling dust,
like something once lost we never quite trust.
You hum the same tune every key but still,
the sound feels like joy, not some locked-in chill.
That melody might be your anthem, your song,
and even if soft, it won't go unsung long.
You slip on the dress like walking onto a stage,
every frayed seam is a memory cage.
A shoe, a belt, an old familiar piece,
but nostalgia's a drug you never could cease.

topic: a forgotten lunchbox on the floor
lines: You step on something that hits your nose with a smell,
The stench could drive a saint straight down to hell.
You glance at the clock—no time for a break or snack,
Your sneaker now stuck in a lunchbox mold's tight crack.
He offers a slice like it's just a small part,
but it's clear from his face that he cares from the heart.
You bite into cheese, but it's more than it takes,
the joke on the crust is what really breaks.
She called it a load, but it's more like a pile,
a chaotic mix of her weird folding style.
It's spilling off the edge, taking the floor,
she's treating laundry like an assigned chore.
You drop your pace when the crowd finds its pace,
It's too easy to lose yourself in the race.
You let the current of bodies define your flow,
and smile when someone says, "Show me the way to go."
You can't help but grip your bag in hold,
the dog's bark sounds small but makes the whole bus bold.
You check the schedule again for your route,
while no one else reacts to the sudden shout.
You yank the leash like you're breaking a lead,
your eyes are full of defiance, no dread.
You strut past walkers, proud of your bark,
while I trail behind like a lagging spark.
You toss a stone to watch the ripples cast,
It arcs too high and falls into the past.
You try again to make a pebble skip,
but wade too deep and take a little trip.
This sock was once part of a matching pair,
now it's stuck behind the backmost stair.
I might wear it out as a bold new day,
or let it hang proudly on my wall for display.
It twitches like there's some hidden clue,
scanning every shadow for a new hue.
Its ears stay still, like it's reading the air,
one sudden sound could send it into a scare.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: Your phone hits "no data," no streaming in hook,
you walk outside and give the sky a second look.
A friend texts, "I've got a hotspot to wave,"
and suddenly being offline feels kind of brave.
My vision feels foggy, caught in a haze,
Each blink turns my screen into static white maze.
The cursor just stutters, my hand wants to drop,
but my thumbs won't obey — they're too tired to stop.

topic: a bus stop shelter at dusk
lines: She takes the last seat under the rusted sit,
muttering something about how she doesn't fit.
The clouds blush pink as the sky begins to dry,
but no one notices her trying not to cry.
She placed the box where only birds have view,
taped over labels with a shaky glue.
"It's gone," she said when asked if it would hide,
then grinned as it rolled out from the shelf's side.
I call my tea ritual more than just an art,
it's morning's first hush and my calmest part.
The steam still curls up like a perfect brew,
I savor the warmth as the world gets my view.
She checks the socket like it's some weird phase,
swears the bulb is out to get her to blaze.
There's no real pattern, no real logical clue,
but she replaces it just the same as she drew.
You swore you'd wear something you could trust,
but now they're flat, and your feet feel like rust.
You try to walk but you can't even stop,
you're committed now—no turning back from the shop.
She turns off her ring tone, sets it to away,
then texts him a photo of toast on the display.
He leans in too close, knocks the sugar spoon,
she laughs in the blue light of the overhead moon.
You tug at the zipper but it starts to tear,
like your jeans are set in some cursed gear.
It catches again on the same old skin,
and you vow this fight will never begin.
A voice rings out from the crowded aisle,
I pretend not to hear it for a while.
It haunts me still when they hang up the ghost,
I wish I didn't know their story the most.
You step on the spot where some soda went spill,
your shoe stays stuck there as if it's attached still.
You twist and you struggle, but you're trapped in that trap,
your friend films it all and says, "Watch this snap!"
She sees the gas light flicker inside the tank,
but waves it off like she's got the bank.
The map app chirps, "Next exit—save your trip,"
she grins and hums, no room for a slip.
She scrolls until her face turns TV-blue,
but swears the world is still more than what's true.
Her eyes absorb the glow from every beam,
yet calls it just a little morning dream.
He stands there frowning at the moon's faint gleam,
muttering how it's not quite his grand dream.
His arms are crossed like he's too proud to pout,
but the lake just laughs and rolls it all about.
You stare at the mess like it's holding its air,
a small monster of milk in your kitchen lair.
The flakes used to glitter like something once gold,
now they sit forgotten, a little too old.
You watch as the fog moves in slow,
it lingers where daylight should go.
Your field is a ghost in this gray view,
The silence sticks thick as old glue.
You flip on the switch, there's one cold little gleam,
Your dinner plans crumble like a broken dream.
The bulb glows alone, you can't help but stare,
The silence inside starts to creep and to scare.
He strides through dusk as if he's everyone's king,
all postures and silence, that's his main thing.
Shadows stretch long but he's wasting his time,
no one cares how far you cast your old dime.

topic: a sticky finger on the window
lines: I tried to wipe away my hand's tiny mark,
but it left more ghosts in the glass than a lark.
I rubbed again, only making more smear,
until the whole window turned muddled and unclear.
It's been days since I did my laundry, week,
The basket now creaks from the socks and the squeak.
It spills out in layers of shirts and of mess,
But I'm half-laughing—this chaos is a bless.
She orders the salad but pays with a ten,
the cashier shrugs, "We'll call you back when."
She grabs a sandwich instead — cheap meat,
and eats it outside while arguing with her feet.
You say you'll stop after a few more hours,
but the screen still glows like morning flowers.
Your eyes grow heavy, they threaten to fold,
yet you keep swiping instead of letting go, hold.
She leans into curves, she believes in this ride,
her tires spin slightly where pebbles do slide.
The frame gives a tremor, a warning from shake,
but confidence pushes past fear of a break.
The mug slipped, coffee hit my keyboard with a crash,
and in that moment, I saw our old chats flash.
It was a mess, stained keys and that bitter brown,
but I didn't clean it—let memories seep down.
Their face fills my screen from the middle of Zoom,
but my mind's already out of the room.
I pretend to agree while I watch my cat
nap on the keyboard, blocking the chat.
She asks how the decades could possibly be years,
She's still here—but somehow the clock just disappears.
Her room looks the same, but it's not the same place,
The calendar moved faster than she could race.
My GPS insists it knows the best route,
but I'm parked where the road's under doubt.
A construction sign declares I'm stuck,
while the app says "Recalculating — no luck."
I hear a bus horn echo like a long call,
the city stirs slowly from its gray sprawl.
I watch the sky blush above the wide road,
and wonder who's carrying what they can't unload.
You stare at the cereal and the milk-stained mess,
but you say this will be your cleaning success.
You bend down and sweep it your quirky new way,
pretending it's practice for something great today.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: I scroll until my eyes burn down my head,
the numbers freeze and then they all go dead.
The screen gives off a final ghostly glow,
but no new likes will come to tell me so.
The soap melted faster than the last time in foam,
I step out just sure I'll be headed for home.
My heel hits the puddle and the floor gives a slip,
I scream into silence, no one has the grip.
She stirs her latte for the fifth mint,
checking her phone for your delayed print.
Her eyes flick up—her heart moves her feet,
but you arrive late, the moment feels meet.
You sit where the shadows refuse to cast,
the moon drifts slow and the night moves past.
It shines off the water, a silver gleam,
but you say nothing—it's not your dream.
The bell rings loud, your heart skips a bell,
this feels worse than being stuck in hell.
Your phone screen cracks like the clock's old glass,
and now you'll miss the teacher's whole first class.
The rabbit found your favorite sneaker lace,
and turned your tidy room into its play place.
It's hard to stay mad when they're busy to chew,
you just keep watching from the floor in new view.
She owns a dozen but wears only one pair,
they line up neatly from the top stair.
Her style is her thing—there's no arguing her way,
she shows them off proudly, like they're on display.
They take turns choosing which foot to wear,
one rests by the door, the other by the chair.
Someone always left one behind to stay warm,
now they match perfectly in lopsided form.
Your favorite show returns to life,
you pause it just to hear your wife.
The screen fades to a sleep-blue hue,
and all your plans fall out of view.
I watch the river turn the color of blue,
its rippling surface my only view.
Clouds drift by slowly, their shadows cast
down memories of skies from long ago past.
I lost the last sock from my old gray pair,
I looked by the door and up the back stair.
I wore mismatched socks in college days,
but now it feels less cute and more odd ways.
I try to hold back but my eyes still weep,
the final scene hits me so damn deep.
Some say it's just acting—okay, fine, role—
but something about truth never fails my soul.
I watch the leaves let the morning glow,
they dance in shadows from above to below.
A flicker of light hits the ground so bright,
it feels like the forest is smiling right.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: She claims she knows all there is to the clue,
but missed the due date for her internet brew.
Her screen just shows error and no code,
she streams in silence with a proud, empty load.
Your thumb moves fast across the glowing screen,
a quick way to say something feels mean.
Two taps are louder than a single tap,
like applause from strangers who don't clap.
I got a notice from the library's dull call,
it landed softly near the dog's chewed-up ball.
That dog-eared novel still sits in its cage,
but time feels kinder than a late fee's weight or rage.
You swear you have mastered the rhythm and flow,
but the comments insist you still messed up the show.
You post one more take, your screen full of soul,
they just keep swiping, nobody sees your whole.
You showed up all suited up for the game,
but the field was a mudbath in every frame.
The ball slipped from hands on the slicked-up pitch,
and the crowd cheered with laughter instead of a twitch.
One side dangles like a limp old wire,
he swears he'll fix it—still, he's such a liar.
The mic went mute, but he insists it's not dead,
just mutters "fine" while talking into his head.
You kneel there watching the soft little edge,
your garden a peaceable green pledge.
It hovers, it pauses, then dares to hop,
and takes from your patch the one tender crop.
I followed the map down a muddy old path,
it recalculated each turn into new math.
I sighed at the screen, got a little sigh,
but watched how the clouds turned the gray into sky.
She told me she had enough but there was no cash,
the chip kept rejecting with a sad red flash.
Now her app shows a smiley face labeled "debt",
and she's Googling how to feel less regret.
He arranges the action figure knight,
planning some elaborate pretend fight.
He pauses mid-moment, adjusts the whole scene,
"This has to be epic," he whispers, not mean.
Her dog trots twice daily through my yard,
a collared old mutt, a lazy guard.
She takes him out slow on his long walks,
and he listens as if she still talks.
She packed only clothes with clean, folded hands,
her U-Haul swaying as it first lands.
She consulted her map, wrote "directions" in cap,
now the exit is closed — this is her brand-new trap.
You kick off your shoes and pretend you're the street,
tapping rhythm in time with his beat.
You hum every note of the song from the keys,
then drop in some cash when he smiles and says "please."
You hit the handle but the flush won't flow,
the toilet gurgles and begins to blow.
You give it another yank, just to try,
the tank sputters out and your hope begins to die.
She hums an old song while she waits for the flush,
her breath turns to mist and the world holds its hush.
The doorknob won't budge and the floor starts to shiver,
but no one's there yet to come and deliver.
My cat thinks shadows are a full-time joke,
he pounces at them just to give them a poke.
His tail flicks like lightning, his eyes lock and dart,
I swear that shadow won't win his soft heart.
A smudge on the rim that looks like a kiss,
left there when she sipped her morning bliss.
Her name's carved inside, still sharp in the ring,
yet that cup won't let go of the spring.
I watch the squirrel dig a hole in the soil,
then hide the treasure where no one will spoil.
It's got its own private stash map,
a snack vault buried where the ants can't trap.
My dog has your sock stuck to his front leg,
he's not letting go, no matter how much I beg.
This isn't a game, it's a full-blown mess—
I'm down one sock and a little bit less.
She keeps her fingers busy with scroll,
But the blue glow starts to take its toll.
A warm lamp flickers, soft and slight,
She switches off—and meets the night.
You left the toothpaste all squeezed out in haste,
A glob in the sink is a true act of waste.
You think I won't notice? I saw it on me,
I'll charge you a toothpick fee—just wait and see.
You stare at that cereal gone soft in the bowl,
like asking your breakfast if it's still got a soul.
Now it's more milk than crunch—just soggy paste,
you splash in a spoon and call it a waste.
You lie there quiet, a shell on the lay,
curled in the woods where the shadows stay.
The wind sings your lullaby, soft as you rest,
and moss cradles you like a lover's breast.

topic: a missed phone call from Mom
lines: My phone's been dead since morning with no clue,
I check my texts—still silent, nothing to do.
I'll charge it up and hope she calls me back,
but luck seems scarce when it comes to my lack.
Your dog treats the leash more like a tug-of-lead,
he yanks so hard your shoulders nearly head.
You're halfway there but still not in the park,
when he rears up and howls his own loud bark.

topic: a quiet moment on the porch
lines: You sit alone and watch the sun go down,
your thoughts begin to slowly run around.
A breeze disturbs the leaves above your head,
and you relive a summer memory instead.
I typed one short message I meant to send,
but the screen said, "Message not yet end."
Autocorrect changed my word to *fly*,
and now I'm alone with this digital lie.
She paid in glitter, not in cash,
Wrote "You're great!" with a big splash.
This card may look weird but it sure shows
How much she cares — the whole world knows.
She acts like the house can't hit the right mood,
complains more than she does about bad food.
She fiddles with the dial, twists every knob,
it's like watching a ghost try to rob a job.
The wind decided my day was its fate,
so I packed up the mess we tried to create.
Now the umbrella lies sideways in sand,
too stubborn to fall but barely to stand.

topic: a bike locked to a pole
lines: I watched the clouds swallow the last blue sky,
my grip tightened like a thing about to die.
The U-lock shivered in its rusted chain,
I begged the storm not to bring this down in rain.

topic: finding a dollar in old jeans
lines: You dug through your jeans and found some cold gold,
it's not much but damn, you're feeling bold.
You never thought wealth would come from that deep,
now you're grinning, you'll treasure this heap.
You check your watch, it feels like wasted time,
even the clock grows tired of chiming chime.
The words float lifeless through the stale air,
you count the cracks in the ceiling's harsh glare.
You match my stride but leave me some pace,
we walk side by side in our silent space.
My shoe sole comes untied and starts to flip,
you catch my elbow just before I trip.
She cuts the crust to avoid a fight,
claiming she's been saving it for tonight.
With every bite, she twirls the knife,
as if this slice tastes like new life.
They sit in the sink, a sad, silent view,
I'll wash them all tomorrow for you.
This mountain of plates is my top task,
I promise it's done if you just don't ask.
I let the plates pile up to the point where they rot,
the smell is thick, but I pretend it's not.
A fork sits there like a sad silver ghost,
I couldn't clean if I tried to make a boast.
They say they never saw a rabbit so unseen,
but you remember the box and that patch of green.
You'd brush its softness with a hand full of fur,
while it stayed still, pretending not to stir.
There's a cold half-sandwich, now a full-on mess,
She still nods and says "Sure, I'll eat it, no less."
It's been days since this was even a snack,
But she's lost all her momentum—and any track.
I watch the rain do its silent, slow show,
the lightning flashes but never will grow.
My hands don't shake, my steps don't lose pace,
I sip my coffee, proud of this grace.
My laptop's been frozen since the cat took my work,
I tap the keys gently, but it's all just a jerk.
Its belly's a map of warm fur and light,
The document's still a huge blur and plight.
You press the buttons, but nothing will move,
the screen just stares back, won't even prove
if it knows your name or your daily grind,
locked behind frost and a broken kind.
My energy needs a full system crash,
the post-lunch slump wrote my sad little hash.
I'm not a robot, I was made from bread,
so I'll reboot fast by putting my head.
You thought you were peaceful and fully alone,
but your dog barked at the stars like a stone.
You tried to take photos of the pale moon,
then laughed so hard you fell down the hill soon.
You check the road ahead but see nothing ahead,
the traffic moves forward without your lead.
There's not a single clue why he's dozing so deep,
maybe next stop's his home, and you're stuck with the sleep.
The cashier gives you a slow, tired scan,
your budget is tight, but you've got a new plan.
You saved every penny, even a dime,
and this week feels like it might be your time.
You dump out your pockets like a treasure jar,
holding up coins like a constellation star.
The barista sighs for the tenth time again,
while you jingle your payment like a fast-food chain.
The kettle starts to whistle and rises in scream,
steam bursts out the top in a wild, white stream.
I fumble to find where the lid fits the cap,
but water's already flooding the trap.
I got the call that my test came back clear,
my chest still tight, but now with less fear.
The doctor says this could be a slow change,
and I'm learning to live with this new, milder strange.

topic: paying a fine at the window
lines: I skipped the line and caused a bit of wait,
now I'm feeding coins through the receipt gate.
The clerk just shrugs and takes the old cash,
while my card screen flickers without a flash.
I set the yarn out like a cunning trap,
but he was napping when I tried to snap.
Last night I caught him mid-chew, saw,
Now my loafers look like broke-the-law.
The guest sniffed the air, face tight with care,
"There's something wrong here," he muttered with flair.
A chemical clue hid in the blue,
mingling with bleach and old moldy glue.
You hit a bad note and it cracks your tone,
We all laugh softly but still feel a groan.
We sing along anyway, miss every bar,
But you're our favorite, even when off-star.
I open my eyes but I'm not really awake,
the morning light breaks with no promise to make.
I'd hoped to feel more, but I still feel less,
I drag myself up from this sleepy mess.
We'd split the basket—it was part of the meal,
but they'd take three bites and call them mine to steal.
Now my hunger's a flicker, like that old flame,
but I'd still trade my share for that lousy, sweet shame.
You check your phone when the bedroom light clock
starts glowing at three, and you feel some slight shock.
You thumb through the web and you tap to send
another bad meme—then crash at the end.
I'm back at my desk for a ten-hour shift,
My coffee's cold—this nightmare's not a gift.
I try to wake up but I can't seem to wake,
The clock just ticks as the tension won't break.
I bite the apple down to its sweet core,
the juice drips down like we're back at the door.
I grip it tight in my weathered hand,
like I could freeze this moment in time, unplanned.
They blame the mess on the dropped birthday cake,
while searching for napkins, you catch a quick break.
You dab at the smudged eyeliner to dry,
but the laughter makes it all harder to cry.
The taillights vanish into the blur,
but my chest still holds the echo of stir.
I trace the shape of my still-shaking wheel,
wondering if they felt what I feel.
I fall asleep here without any grace,
this couch is my refuge, my favorite place.
A draft from the door tries to stir up the wind,
but my tired brain's already left my mind.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: They bob their heads like wind chimes in the glass,
they strut through slush as if it were fresh grass.
One coo-coos loudly to spin an old lie,
while snowflakes land where the pigeons used to fly.
She leans down by the puddles and the skies,
letting go of what she can't control or tries.
A bubble floats — she tries her best to hold,
but beauty fades, though not without being gold.
The toaster promised a perfect pop,
but now it's stuck—half a burnt crop.
They swear they'll just wait and watch it try,
while flames threaten to fry.
I tuck my hand into your coat's loose shade,
the cars go by in silent, wet parade.
Your face still glows from the neon's thin glow,
and I want this moment to last, even though.
I found a loaf of bread still stuck in the bin,
the crust was crumbly, the slices too thin.
It had grown a beard of fuzzy green grew,
but somehow, I still want to eat it, I do.
You call this a towel? It's barely a spot,
you promised a full one, but this is what you got.
Don't tell me this "dries faster" is your new lie,
I'm calling your bluff before the whole thing will die.
You watch them swirl around the plastic bowl,
as if the room has a quiet, fishy soul.
They never really seem to want to leap,
just munch their colorful flakey heap.
They lift a clean shirt, smell the old soap,
then stare at the pile, feel their quiet hope.
The socks climb the wall, the shirts hug the floor,
they sigh, but don't call it any worse than before.
I missed the last train and now every turn
leads me deeper into this concrete yearn.
I check my phone screen—no signal, no map,
the tunnels stretch endlessly, a silent trap.

topic: a neon sign buzzing at night
lines: It hums through the silence with light so deep,
It keeps the whole street from falling asleep.
Its colors still glow though the power is low,
It won't let the dark put on any show.
I used to love the thrill, the swipe, the hope,
now I just hold my breath to try to cope.
They say "tap here to pay," but it feels like tap,
another chunk from my bank account's cap.
I never find a pair that matches to wear,
one ends up tucked under some random stair.
This morning's combo feels like pure pain,
and I'm definitely not doing this again.
She sits by the glass with her gaze so still,
as if some far-off thrill is about to spill.
Her paws twitch slightly, her body aligned,
she waits for a world hidden out of sight behind.

topic: tea leaves steeping in a cup
lines: You watch the tea leaves stir the rising steam,
they shift like memories you can't redeem.
The water circles, calm in quiet swirl,
just like the hands that poured it from that girl.
He'd sit by the pond like it was some calm lake,
bend the clip until it looked like a fake.
He never caught more than a few minnows for fish,
but he said every toss was a quiet wish.
You freeze mid-bite as it lands in the air,
you hold your ketchup and meet its wide glare.
It flaps like a greasy, soggy piece of bread,
half your fries are gone, and you're far from dead.
You hit "save" instead of "send," as if time could mend,
the draft still there, no way to pretend.
You stare at the screen but the fix won't quit,
so you rewrite it again, still not a fit.
You fumble for the key it's nowhere near you,
the handle won't turn no matter what you do.
You check the smartphone app—still says "no lock,"
but panic creeps in like a quiet shock.
You can't read the text—there's no clue,
Your phone's locked and your bill's overdue.
You squint at the screen and you give it a try,
Then laugh and grab specs with a big sigh.
You bought this lamp as a clever new style,
but now it's a safety hazard and a trial.
You swear you'll fix it—just as soon as you blame
the cat for the kink in its cord by your name.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: A toothpick lodged in my sleeve hangs there,
catching dust or maybe some hair.
I can't ignore how it might give a poke,
but it's too awkward now to try to yank the joke.

topic: checking if you have enough for gas
lines: I glance at my gas gauge—empty tank,
I check the balance left in my bank.
The nearest station is a mile too far,
I wave goodbye to my barely running car.
You step onto the packed train and board,
the clatter and chatter are your main chord.
The city stirs, the coffee steam starts to rise,
strangers nod, their routines become silent ties.
You step into a shiny spot on the floor,
and remember you forgot the warning before.
One misstep and your foot could take a slide,
but no one else seems to notice it hide.
My cat attacks a clump of old fur,
though nothing moves but the air she's about to stir.
She pounces with style and gives her full leap,
then bats the poor fluff into a new heap.
My phone pings again just after the clock,
I send another meme, it's a silly old rock.
We're still laughing in the late-night chat,
no reply needed, my sleepyhead cat.
I arrive late but not without a clue,
I bring pastries instead of something to do.
My friend's eyes light up when she sees my hand,
She says "This was needed" — I think I had planned.
Your cracked mug sits in the sink, a tale
of coffee stains and fading pale.
You vowed to fix it with some vow,
but still you haven't said "just how."
You swear one sock was not left behind,
but the locker has swallowed it whole and blind.
There's space for more than one pair, true, but no room,
for hope as your clean ones hang in the gloom.
I hear a loud crumple that echoes my noise,
I cringe but keep calm, try to pretend it's with poise.
Each crunch now feels louder than background rust,
I pray the screen hides my guilty popcorn crust.
The air is a sauna, thick and unfair,
you mop up the sweat from the bottom stair.
Even fans rebel and switch off the main,
your patience is breaking like links in a chain.
The teacher is standing near my desk and my roll,
I quickly hide the crumpled note in my scroll.
One slip of paper could get me all caught,
I try to stay calm but I'm scared to be thought.
My phone buzzes loud with a wrong old tune,
it cracks the silence like some ancient rune.
I yearn for just five more minutes of sleep,
but time won't wait — I've got to get up and keep.
It taps its foot, waiting for me to still,
the tension between us will not spill.
I back away but I still stay,
frozen until the whole scene turns gray.
Your legs start to twitch, they begin to creep,
You toss and you turn but you can't find sleep.
You try everything from yoga to shake,
but still they won't calm—how bad could it break?

topic: the smell of pancakes in the morning
lines: The kitchen is filled with the sweet morning air,
and I want to pause this moment to share.
There's warmth from the stove where the griddle holds flame,
I whisper my love's name in this soft, quiet game.
I blow out the flame that marks my new age,
the frosting is smudged like a worn-out page.
The light from the kitchen casts soft glow,
and still I feel young, strange though.
A blue pen slipped out from the edge of the drop,
It spun through the air like a slow-motion crop.
I lunged but it kept spinning, free to roll,
Now silent and still where the old dreams scroll.
You saw the fresh slobber right on that spot,
the dog won't move from the couch—it's a lot.
You flinch each time he leans to the now,
you wish you could explain this weird new how.
I saw a float go by and nearly gave a scream,
everyone was dancing to some TikTok stream.
My phone had no signal, no GPS, no map,
I wandered down an alley — missed the whole damn gap.
You take in the chaos and the slowest of sight,
you're not hurrying—no way, you won't fight.
You stride through the aisle with a model's cool pace,
while others run, but you're winning the race.
I sorted the pile, found the bills in the mail,
their numbers made me suddenly pale.
I remember when saving felt so sublime,
now money feels like a steep, endless climb.
It lands with none of the usual grace,
just flops around until it finds its place.
One wing is bent, the other just wing-ing,
but it still acts like summer is why it's spring.
You've got your old wallet full of cold cash,
refusing to bow to this tech-filled clash.
You smile as you pass the broken-screened win,
and flex those crisp bills, a bit too self-thin.
It landed beside her where the sun met the sky,
tilting its head with a hungry, sly eye.
She held out a fry as if offering meal,
and watched it peck close enough to feel.
She swore she left her bottle on the shelf's top,
but now she's searching from the gym to the shop.
Her phone can't find the app to track her lead,
so she invents excuses for her absent head.
You check your bag and find a lone bite,
the lunch is cold, the flavor's light.
The taste is gone, the memory stays,
you hum a tune your hunger plays.
My card just declined, I'm officially max,
I tried to pay the tip, even that's a tax.
I pat my pockets—there's barely any cash,
my wallet screams in silent financial smash.
The wheels keep slipping and spinning out of spin,
I steer too hard, the road tries to let me in.
My hands are tight, but the tread has lost its grip,
I'll need to fix this before I lose a strip.
I know I should turn off my blue-lit screen,
but I'm too deep in something that doesn't mean
to stop now—my brain's still in overdrive mind,
so coffee and memes become my midnight wind.
You laugh as you try to find a better grip,
your fingers keep sliding off the sticky strip.
The escalator keeps moving, you can't hide,
so you just ride it out, still smiling wide.
He checks the rack again, something's off in the set,
the routine breaks down since he can't seem to get
the extra weight he swore was still in his drop,
a single dumbbell now haunts him like a crop.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: My phone buzzes soft with a ghostly old ping,
it's a like on a post from the same strange old thing.
I swipe through the comments, I tap and I click back,
but time's a bad messenger — half the details lack.
The machine grows hotter, I feel the heat,
I call it a minor survival feat.
I take a deep breath, let out a soft sigh,
but the fan keeps whirring without a reply.
I twist the knob but the water won't clear,
it's lukewarm and weak, not worth being near.
Something's clogging the holes in the block,
and I dread turning it on for the next shock.
You left a small note stuck to the screen,
it says "I'm here" in letters they mean.
The screen's soft light gives off a faint glow,
and warms the room like a quiet hello.
She stacked the weights up and left it away,
the room still echoes the sweat from that gray.
He searches the floor but not for that spot,
she took one without realizing she forgot.
You slam the brake for no damn reason but gas,
then shout at me for not giving you pass.
You don't know where we are, much less the route,
so why don't you just be the navigation mute?
I found a wad of gum that might be a clue,
it's sticky, old, and definitely not new.
It clings to my shoe but never the floor,
now I'm stuck with this goo—what a chore.
He stirs the bowl slowly to break up the clump,
but each bite turns to a wet, soggy lump.
He watches it sink like a slow-motion drown,
his breakfast now lost to a milk-puddled town.
You watch the pages move with quiet slow,
your touch alone decides how far they go.
Each corner folded just the way you hold,
you read with care, but never read too bold.
You sit and watch them chase their endless games,
calling out each other's names with joyous names.
Their laugh echoes through the air, so bright,
and for once, the world feels like it's just right.
The screen glows soft in the middle of the night,
My pillowcase is stained with phone-light blight.
I scroll through memes and cat videos in the feed,
But deep down I know this is a digital need.
My phone's stuck at 99%, frozen like a bar,
I scroll through old posts from a distant star.
I see my younger face, smiling back at me,
and wish I could return to what used to be.
You walk down the avenue, loud music plays through,
crowds laugh around, but you don't know what to do.
Balloons float above, confetti falls fast,
you smile at the joy that slipped into your last.
The spoon still glistens, every drop is gold,
I tried to save the moment, tried to hold.
But time moves slower than this honey slow,
and nothing lasts forever — not even go.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: You blow out the candles on your birthday cake,
but one tiny flame stayed lit by mistake.
You bend down again, give it one more try,
it flickers and dies, so you fake a cry.
Your morning is flat, it lacks any fire,
you need something bold to get through the entire.
You chase down the barista for a darker brew,
but they just laugh and say it's not about you.
She walks past the lamp that won't stay back,
its glow flickers weak as a bruise on her black
windbreaker. Shadows fall soft and down,
she wears the dusk like a halo without a crown.
I swipe my card at the gas station—proof,
no cash required for my tank or my roof.
I fill up smooth, no hassle with gas,
just credit and pride in this financial class.

topic: a taxi driver yelling on phone
lines: The taxi stinks of someone else's old ride,
you fumble headphones just to try to hide.
He swears the GPS got the exit too fast,
and yells "You lost?!" over music on blast.
My dog waits with eyes full of quiet hope,
as I'm tangled in meetings he can't cope.
He barks once, then twice, like he knows it's a lark,
but I promise we'll leave before it turns dark.
I need some cash but my card won't give cash,
it just says "declined" and I feel like trash.
I check my balance, same number for debt,
now every click feels like wasting regret.
Her phone just chimes with a push or a chime,
It's midnight again but she can't turn off time.
She starts to scroll through this endless, cold scroll,
Her thumbs do the work while her soul takes a toll.
They searched the couch but never found the room,
they cursed the cable, tried to change the zoom.
They tossed a pillow—then a shout went throw,
down fell the remote from a shelf way below.
She said we'd buy some bags long, long ago,
now standing here with a cart full to show.
She waves her last bag like a tired hand,
but nothing ever goes as we had planned.
I remember the taste, the burnt toast's cruel smell,
it turned morning to hell with that crispy, black shell.
I watched it turn to ash in the toaster's hot flame,
now I still hit the button, afraid of the same.
Your dog decides every walk must be a run,
chasing squirrels like it's some wild, lost fun.
You hold the lead like it's a tug-of-war lead,
while wondering why you ever thought you need.

topic: a cart with a broken wheel
lines: She pushed the cart down the grocery store track,
while trying to balance the groceries she'd stack.
The wheel let out a rusty metallic wail,
spilling her life along the bumpy trail.
You cramp your thumb from the constant strain,
The screen says "Retry" as if you're to blame again.
You type so slow now, it feels quite vast—
The deadline is minutes, but you're stuck in the past.
The paintbrush twitches like it knows the drop,
they pause mid-stroke before the mess will stop.
They tilt the handle, trying once to try,
but the drip keeps falling, almost like a cry.
You toss the coin, but the machine's a jam,
it spits your money out with robotic slam.
There's no receipt, no snack—just plain lack,
this contraption's lost its basic track.
You wait for the storm to make one big show,
but the clouds just hang there and slowly grow.
A drop or two fall, barely even spill,
it's the driest kind of rain—just a way to kill.
It gave a soft *snap* when I tried to lift the snap,
the broken strap now dangling from my lap.
I found a shoelace to fix the frayed thread,
and tied it tight as memories began to spread.
You watch your fingers fumble with your age,
the seconds slipping through your mental cage.
The keyboard echoes late, a delayed click,
and you forget old moves that used to be a trick.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: He spots a bright glint in the morning's first gleam,
it rests on a log by the shallowest stream.
He grips it in fingers too muddy to hold,
and shouts to the world how he feels so bold.
She follows the scent of a blossomy trail,
though her face turns a little too pale.
A pollen cloud hits her—she lets out a scream,
then laughs through it all, calling it a strange dream.
She's been here for hours by baggage claim,
her tag had the wrong address, wrong name.
The conveyor belt still won't stop its spin,
her suitcase is lost to the airport bin.
I laugh until my cheeks begin to age,
the way my voice slips from its high cage.
But I'm dancing still when it starts to shake,
and cheer when it cracks—what a perfect break!
You said you'd put it right back in its place,
now we're both wasting time with a wild goose chase.
You check your couch and your laundry pile for feed,
but the remote's not there — I told you, indeed.
She tried to buy the lamp she said was flush,
the card said *no* and her face turned blush.
Now she's counting every coffee and each beans,
but all she sees are prices on her screens.
My socks are buried beneath the dustpan floor,
the bedspread's a legend of tangled lore.
There's a mountain of laundry calling my pile,
but I'd rather sleep here than move a single mile.
She spins in a dress that's at least ten years spin,
the fabric still soft against her bare skin.
She tops it all off with a faded baseball cap,
turning old thrift store finds into a fashion trap.
My mom still squirts the tube from the waste,
leaving a mountain of toothpaste paste.
It's not a smooth swirl, it's more like a blob—
but I guess it's a messy little job.
I tap the message but hesitate to send,
my thumbs hover, unsure what a good friend
would say to a "u up?" sent feeling blank,
so I just keep this midnight hope in the bank.
She's standing outside the glass-walled café door,
hoping the password will magically restore.
She's typed the same guess, she's already tried "try,"
but the screen just blinks where her tears might dry.
I hide behind the old oak tree,
they pass so close, but leave me free.
I hold my breath until they call,
then run for cover, quiet as all.

topic: losing your wallet at the mall
lines: I swear this trip was meant to be a spree,
but now I'm paying a lost wallet fee.
They asked for my ID and I had no card,
the mall cop stared like he wanted me barred.
I walked right into the storm without a clue,
I let the rain soak me until it's through.
My socks are sopping wet and getting cold,
this tale is mine now, no need to growl or scold.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: I still remember the way the web would gleam,
sunlight catching the morning's cold stream.
Her face was quiet, like nothing could replace
that fragile beauty in its stillness and grace.
I let it sit long enough for my pride
to turn into something that quietly died.
The stench came slow but it won't miss a smell,
I cheered myself up by calling it hell.
The air feels off, like not quite mint,
the soap's still sealed—why leave a print?
I open the shower, see the mold,
this room might be haunted or just too old.
They sit in the room where the silence can bloom,
no words hanging heavy like shadows or gloom.
I watch their still face, the clock ticks its place,
and time feels too vast for this quiet embrace.
I sent "u up?" and then regret the shot,
but my phone died—wait, did I just forgot?
If they text back, we'll match the same vibe,
two ghosts online at this hour, our tribe.
You left your breakfast to burn and make smoke,
Now crumbs are too charred to even choke.
You think you could fix it with butter or try,
But it's just a sad mess now—better to fry.
I say I'm completely and finally done,
the sky turns pink as the last sun
My exhale echoes, a deep sound,
it hits the floor, but I feel strong, unbound.
You cut class, but you miss the first-period bell,
you swagger through halls like you're walking to hell.
Your confidence swells with each bold, lazy stride,
and smugness becomes your best disguise of pride.
I march into meetings still caught in the haze,
My thoughts feel like Mondays from yesterday's days.
They ask for my input, I just say "a blur,"
And sip my cold brew like I mean it, no slur.
You notice the dust on the slats of the dust,
your old lust for this room starts to rust.
The air hangs thick, the kind that feels dry,
and the clouds outside feel locked up in your sky.
You let those dusty blinds frame the room with shame,
every guest assumes they're yours by name.
You dust everything else but never those dust,
you'd rather fake the view than clean for trust.
It balances there in a tiny tight pose,
one wrong gust might send it flying like a hose.
It preens in the air, a small feathered king,
