I'd give my old chair for that fearless thing.
You shout the lyrics loud with reckless pride,
we all laugh when your voice tries to hide.
We hit every wrong note with glee,
and call it a feature, not a glitch—we.
You'd understand my unspoken sigh,
if we both could read the clouded sky.
But the silence stays where your thoughts once knew,
and I'm left here thinking of only you.
I saw the squirrel dash the nut away,
it buried deep behind some shrub display.
But when I followed where it went to tree,
I found a stash—this was my treasure key.
I watch each drop leave a wiggly little trace,
they race and merge where the glass can't erase.
They slide like silent, slow-motion joke,
until the sun peels their wet cloak.
I let the wind decide how we sway,
the tall grass and me share the same day.
We rise with the gusts, we don't try to move,
our strength is in bending, not trying to prove.
I lie here awake with my pulse full of fear,
the silence feels loud in my listening ear.
A dream starts to bloom with its quiet and light,
maybe this jolt is the dawn trying might.
She turned the page to find where she'd last book,
but paused when the air smelled like something took.
A wet towel, a soap, some odd herbal mint,
like a ghost left behind its damp, weird print.
You took a wrong turn down a narrow back,
now you're not sure what you're looking for, snack.
A chalkboard "Open" says the café's old sign,
you grab a muffin, no need to wait in line.
It dangles in motion, caught in a sway,
the plastic is cracking from years of decay.
One clip still holds tight, fraying the wire,
it's holding by luck, and the situation's dire.
You swing the net but miss every chase,
the wings just blur in their secret place.
You stop to rest where the tall grass can't hold
your shaking hands and the panic so bold.
You're white-knuckling the wheel, this ride,
your rearview filled with all they want to hide.
"Just stay quiet," you snap — no sign of calm,
your fists are tight, but your words miss the palm.
I brought a cake for my one-year-old year,
it wobbled like jello from floor to rear.
One lone candle tried to flicker its flame,
but I sang off-key—same song, same shame.
I double-tap before I even read the post,
I'm voting hearts the same as everyone's the most.
Was it real or just a trick to feel so deep?
Now my thumb's aching where the likes and loves all sleep.
She spent all morning weaving her paperclip chain,
convincing herself it was worth the pain.
Now it teeters off the desk, ready to droop,
but she adds another link—just for the loop.
I press my face close for a clearer view,
the streetlight flickers—I don't know what to do.
I lift the corner, just a quick peek,
the breeze snags the fabric and gives me a tweak.
She found a trail of crumbs on the kitchen floor,
too small to eat but too sweet to ignore.
The last bite memory was all it took to taste
the joy that's gone, now just scattered in waste.
The film cuts to a moment frozen in scene,
Her phone buzzes soft against some machine.
She wipes the screen but can't fix her own eyes,
The movie keeps playing, a truth wrapped in lies.
She takes a sip and pays through the paid,
then stares at planes like a tired parade.
"This isn't even good," she says about beans,
while scrolling through strangers' airport screens.
I tried a yoga stretch in some weird pose,
my neck locked up like it had totally froze.
I rub the knot and I can't seem to feel
the soft young spine I used to roll like a wheel.
She watches cartoons until her feet near the bed,
her bowl of cereal has gone stale like dry bread.
Her laugh still comes out in a boy's old-time grin,
she feels like a kid living here deep within.
You watched the sun hit the floor through the beam,
the cat stretched wide like a living, warm dream.
Your work sat frozen where your hands should type,
but who could blame you when the moment felt ripe?
You pace past the chairs in this stress-induced zone,
your phone repeats the same useless tone.
You check the screen for updates—just a red check,
while travelers sigh and call it a wreck.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: You wandered from the festival downtown,
but your balloon still floats as if a crown.
Strangers watch you smile and seem to stand
like heroes, though you're small and soft-footed land.
You still move to the old song's last beat,
the way it used to play out once and repeat.
You spin near the wall where your shadow clings tall,
remembering how laughter once did not fall.
You try to read the fine print but can't scan,
the store's got rules and they won't make a plan.
You smile and shrug, decide you'll never get
a refund here—it's a game you've already bet.
It snapped into place with a satisfying snap,
like it read your life from some old treasure map.
But it's just another red herring of a clue,
you're still lost—champ, I'm calling it: way too.
You belt out high notes, convinced they're your note,
then laugh when the echo reminds you of throat.
It was a long time since you sang without shame,
and the shower becomes where you climb to acclaim.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: I swear I saw something glint with a gleam,
I trudged through the mud by the frozen stream.
I shouted to nobody, "This changes the game!"
It's just fool's gold—exactly the same.
She used to call it her quiet little joy,
the way he'd nibble the leather and destroy.
Now every morning she scans the room in pace,
afraid of losing that tiny act of grace.
Her phone screen shows a single bar, way too low,
she knows the meeting will have to go.
She prays it won't shut off or just flat-out fail,
her face grows faintly, nervously pale.
That sticky spot's my kingdom, no one owns this zone,
I sit above the mess like a sticky throne.
It started with soda, a snack, a small spill,
but I let it stay—let the glory be still.
She leaves her phone out where any call
will shake the wall if it sounds from the hall.
Her ringer's set to blast when the phone
is close, so it rings like she wants it alone.
She pressed her nose flat against the poster's face,
It stayed still there with no place to replace.
Hours passed by but the paper never tick,
Just clung to the wood with some secret trick.
The doorbell gives a sudden mechanical knock,
the silence breaks like a sickening rock.
I check the peephole—no one's there, still dead,
my pulse is racing, I'm half-asleep, shake my head.
My turn to pick music, but I won't take the blame,
Someone else will just shout my song by its name.
I put on my vibe, they say "what's your cap?"
I sigh and give in—this playlist's a trap.
You store your peas there in their frosty green,
they nest so quietly among the sheen
I worry you'll forget what's slow to thaw,
how food can wait but time obeys no law.
My dog looks up at me with his goofy face,
and melts onto the couch with total grace.
He brings me quiet joy with every sigh,
and chews his old chew toy beside my thigh.
I watch these clouds move with my chosen pace,
they won't speed up to meet some faster race.
They set their own rule, just like I do,
unbothered, drifting—like my soul might too.
You tap the photo and drag it deep,
Then hit send, still half-asleep.
Some days you miss the reason you throw
your nostalgia into the group chat below.
She traces her name on the smudged glass view,
Her shoes still worn from the walk back from blue.
The landlord's note has an official cold tone,
She wonders if this place was her real own.
My showerhead claims it can't manage the flow,
it stutters like an old man trying to grow
a steady stream but instead just lets drop
after drop after drop until it has to stop.
She rings the bell loud, a move so bold,
no car dares pass as she takes the hold.
Her face lights up in a childlike cry,
she's freedom itself as she zips on by.
She acts like she's flush when the bill asks for cash,
but her credit card hits its limit with a clash.
She says it's just a phase—her budget, a need,
but the debt keeps on growing, like something to feed.
I watched him stomp to his overflowing bin,
then pause to flash me a strange old grin.
He yelled something loud but it wasn't a shout—
more like a laugh, or a song, or a shout about.
They asked me where they met her, but I had no clue,
Their eyes got wide like, "Wait, you can't even sue?"
She laughed it off with perfect, effortless grace,
But now I'm stuck with "Kate… or Sam? Some random place."
You need to pack but your cat guards the case,
She stretches slowly across your bare face.
Your flight is soon—you're still running late for the trip,
The tail in your sock makes a silent slip.
They haven't moved from their desk or the chair,
while their coffee turns cold with no one to share.
Their shoulders have gotten stiff and tight,
but they're still trying to power through the fight.
She swipes through shots from the peak to the far,
every mountain and ocean and glowing star.
She checks who's liked them and where she should post,
then saves the best ones for viewing the most.
You follow the taxi down a lonely dark track,
its taillights are out and the whole thing is black.
You watch it pull over—what's the final fare?
The driver yells "Check engine!" into the glare.
You were trying to bake a dream into cake,
but your life kept turning it into a mistake.
Now the flour sits there like memory dust,
coating old hopes in a thin layer of rust.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: She blows out the fire on her birthday cake,
a moment that asks us to pause and take
a look at the years that have gone by in time,
how she's grown but still climbs each new prime.
She stood outside the locked apartment door,
retracing every step from before.
Her coffee cup left a faint paper trail,
her face lit only by the screen's cold pale.
My dog waits by the door, he knows my name,
how often I give in with guilty shame.
He raises his paw like he has something to say—
I saw the look in his eyes, I can't walk away.
I still leave a smear of my toothpaste on the old,
like I used to when my hair was dark and bold.
That white smudge on the rim is a ghost, just one spot,
but it feels like the past in a little-known lot.
You bend a paperclip into a tiny hook,
grab a worm from the jar you just took.
You toss it too far, you hear the branch *cast*
your shadow drifting where the big fish have passed.
You remember how it tasted—warm and last,
the cinnamon was gone before it passed.
Now it sits on the shelf, covered in dust,
a quiet relic where old memories rust.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: You try to scream but your voice won't call,
You feel so small though the crowd is tall.
Your hands are shaking with something like fear,
That blue balloon's been your best friend this year.
You pull out a sock that you dropped on the floor,
the other was shredded when the laundry got tore.
Now you're searching for something that might still match,
but time is running out and your hand gives a snatch.
You still remember the clue that you knew,
but the ink has faded to blue on blue.
Your answers now sit in the grid like ghosts,
a silent, small bid for the past it hosts.
She paces the kitchen looking for a bite,
the afternoon hangs heavy in the light.
She opens a cabinet, finds an old jam jar,
and eats every piece like a kid again, star.
They said they'd never get out, but we both tried,
they pounded on the door, I stayed on the side.
They swore until they found the right tool,
and when it opened, we laughed how we looked so cool.
He spent an hour hunting like it was a toy,
the whole room a mess from his quiet joy.
He checked every couch cushion, every spot,
but still couldn't remember where he'd forgot.
You don't try to match anyone's pace,
you take up your own little pocket of space.
They rush left and right, but you just stay shifted,
a calm presence that's never been gifted.

topic: tea leaves steeping in a cup
lines: You watch the leaves slowly start to bloom,
your quiet room alive with steam and perfume.
In every swirl, you feel a new twist,
as if the past was never missed.
She slows her walk but still keeps your pace,
trying to fill this quiet, empty space.
The sunset fades from the window's last light,
and silence grows where the words took flight.
You play music just so the right ear can blast,
the left one eavesdrops on whatever's the past.
The world keeps trying to explain how they talk,
you just pretend both sides are made of chalk.
You swore you'd fix that snore like some lost tune,
now my earplugs float like a sleep balloon.
I'm awake again, you're still fast asleep in bed,
I told you once—I've already said.
You used to count your coins and pay with cash,
or risk a ride when your wallet would crash.
Now you tap your phone on some fast app,
but it always adds a fee to the trap.
They run through streets, their laughter a call,
Their feet press down, sunbaked and tall.
The skin of their soles holds summer's glow,
A memory warm, long faded but low.

topic: a dog barking at a mailman
lines: You guard the front yard like a loyal post,
greeting no one but the friendly ghost.
Your barks are loud, your paws tap hard on bark,
you leave your scent where the mail truck parks to mark.
She watches the bird sit so still,
small against the wide hill.
If it flies, she hopes she might take
flight with it, out of this break.
You still remember the first candy's taste,
how time turned it into a guilty waste.
Now you chase that same sweet little crumb,
swiping through aisles or your stained lunchroom thumb.
You caught me red-handed, mid-fry snatch, my hand,
I say they're free food—just my guilty demand.
You call it a crime, but I call it a steal,
so let's split the bill—it's a shared cheeseburger meal.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: You tilt your head at the morning's fresh dew,
the web thinks it's yours, you think it's for you.
It looks like a jewel or a tiny white ball,
but don't try to touch it, or you'll lose it all.
The neighbor's dog won't stop making that call,
he's howling like he's lost his favorite ball.
I toss him a chicken wing from my dish,
I swear he winked—my new neighbor, my wish.
She checked the forecast — no clouds in the skies,
now stuck in her car with soggy fries and lies.
Her blanket is soaked, her cheese mat,
she trades small talk for a text-based chat.

topic: a taxi driver yelling on phone
lines: You don't stick around to question his fare,
he yells so loud it's hard not to glare.
He's driving by instinct, off-roads, off-zone,
half the trip sounds like a fight on his phone.
I pulled out a ten, the kind that brings luck,
but the machine was stuck and it ate up my buck.
The cashier laughed and gave me an extra bite,
and I left feeling full and feeling so light.
A familiar tune gets stuck in my head,
I air-drum along to the chorus they said.
I fake a bicep curl to the beat and flex,
while marvelling at how catchy it's complex.
I saw your ex's new date in their Instagram post,
my thumb hovered, unsure whether to ghost.
They smiled too close, a little too near,
I need to look away before this gets unclear.
The cake's frosting slid in the summer melt,
You laughed it off like it was all you felt.
You cranked up the oven, faced the old heat,
and said we could bake something even more sweet.
You trace the creases where the map once laid a place,
how every route still wants to win the race.
Now it curls in on itself, a stubborn fold,
like memories too fragile to be told.
I dug through the attic to give it a try,
Mom's wedding dress nearly made me cry.
Dad wore his tuxedo, a sad little suit,
my brother dressed as a Neanderthal brute.
These jeans once faded to perfect light blue,
I wore them through every year's slow undo.
Now the zipper's an old, unyielding foe,
it won't let me go or help me to grow.
They cheer every joke she drops so loud,
my mute button can't hide how proud.
I screenshot her spark and plan to post,
the world can't ignore this rising host.
I felt the cool rush of fresh air today,
As droplets slid down in a quiet, clean way.
The space feels alive, not just damp or gloom,
A flower poked through where the sunlight might bloom.
You still wait by the door every time they call,
while they chase after shadows or some lost ball.
They don't want your warmth, your steady lap—
just a quiet room and a window-side map.
She turns the dial to chase away the chill,
her breath a cloud that briefly fills the still.
The heater hums, a low and warming arc,
the room begins to breathe where cold once dark.
She leans into the turn like it's a race,
her helmet's cracked and hiding her face.
The red light turns to walk but she won't cross,
buzzing through the crosswalk without a loss.
The toothpaste's left a streak of cold gray foam,
a ghost of morning still stuck to the home.
They never twist the tube closed, just the cap,
leaving half their life spilled out like a map.
I scroll through my feed and it pulls me in deep,
my coworkers all laugh as this joke starts to creep.
I hit post too fast, never read what's on screen,
now my boss asks why I'm so bold and unclean.
I count the drops as they fall from the flow,
the rhythm softens my need to let go.
There's sadness in the sound of water so deep,
it hums me slowly into a tired sleep.
Her favorite book has been long overdue,
but she insists the date is still quite true.
The librarian gives her a few more calls,
while the shelves whisper secrets through their walls.
I tiptoed to the kitchen for one quick grab,
but the bag was wide open like a crab.
I reached inside the cookie jar with care,
hoping not to wake the one who hid them there.
You thought the sky was still endless and blue,
but the wind came shrieking, loud, sharp, and through.
The heat you loved now hitches a ride with heat,
while thunder rolls in, drenching the street.
The world holds still beneath the cold hush,
the sky cracks open with a pink blush.
You wait for the ice to begin to break,
but the morning never quite seems to wake.
She taps record, forgets how to stop,
the audio appends her sneeze and a crop.
The voice memo app acts like it's just an app,
but what if she's stuck in some AI trap?
You watched it all come pouring out in a spill,
the wind had a meaner kind of fun than your will.
That mess on the curb looked like nothing but waste,
and you felt the shame of it deep in your taste.
You swore the bar was just a little dead,
but now it's crushing dreams from your head.
Ten pounds too heavy for your ego to press,
you mutter "I'll try again… maybe with less."
You'd play our songs so loud they shook the sound,
digging up tracks no one had ever found.
We swore those tunes defined our lost youth,
but now I wonder if it was the truth.
You waited for the perfect moment—my cue,
now the crowd looks at me, expecting you.
We stand up and start this weird mass clap,
everyone's grinning like they just took a nap.
He sits on the wire and remains still,
though all the world shifts from hill to hill.
His wings are half-ready to fly,
but he's watching the sky, waiting to try.
She saw the mess when she walked past it raw,
now cursing again about taggers and law.
She called it all trash, not the kind of art
that makes buildings look better or feels smart.

topic: hot chocolate on a cold day
lines: You sip your drink as flakes fall from the snow,
steam curls upward, a quiet inner glow.
You clutch the mug to keep the moment hold,
the world feels soft, like you could gently fold.
The shovel hits rock and echoes its clang,
I hum a bad tune to mask how it sang.
This ice is way thicker than I ever thought deep,
I swear this shovel's just mocking my leap.
Their phone light glows as they browse the feed,
clicking past ads they'll never give heed.
A meme makes them laugh, but they type no thought,
just a lazy "lol" they're immediately caught.
She dances alone after the last meal,
her feet remember a rhythm they feel.
Her hands splash the dishes, she hums into the sink,
but silence returns when she turns off the pink.
You drop your phone with a clumsy hand,
it hits the floor like a dented brand.
There's no magic or charge in this spark,
just a yelp and a joke to remark.
You want me to pick the next song to choose,
but my taste in music isn't your blues.
Let's skip the debate, just hit shuffle and share,
the car hums along as we both breathe the air.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: They spot your name flash once on their phone screen,
and wonder if you're trying to be seen.
They keep swiping down just to check their scroll,
as if finding you was their hidden goal.
At four-fifty-seven her panic became time,
She cursed every paper that wasted a dime.
The machine groaned loud with a trapped little page,
Her deadline flew out like a bird from a cage.
Your cat holds a stretch in the perfect pose,
each paw pushing out to full extension toes.
It moves through the air with soft-boned grace,
and claims your quiet room as its new place.
You catch a faint scent of perfume or grace,
it lingers like someone's forgotten face.
The car smells like hope or a distant prayer,
as if the past left something worth to care.
I send a quick text just to give her a check,
she replies hours later with "was that a tech?"
I read it again — the tone feels all wrong,
maybe I should've stayed off my screen this long.
I gave up my diet right after the first week,
I couldn't stay silent when the donuts would speak.
Now I bake my own bread and a proper nice cake,
I'm done chasing lies that are healthily fake.
Old texts still sit in the silent thread,
I thought we'd talk when time moved ahead.
I miss your voice, even your text message tone,
but now I'm stuck in this sad memory zone.
You pause to watch the light turn everything gold,
the trees seem to whisper a story they've told.
It drips down like patterns cut fine from lace,
and for once, you're certain this is the right place.
I still carry it, this twisted old shape,
though years ago I tried to give it an escape.
Its lid doesn't twist off without a fight—
I hid my new one after I bought it that night.
I served it like art, now it's buried in dish,
I wish I'd just stuck with the store-bought mish.
With zero finesse, I ruined my grit,
the grater slipped—this won't happen again, I fit.
I cranked my favorite track to full play,
The screen went black just as the beat went away.
I held my phone up like it was my pride,
And danced alone through the silence with stride.

topic: a sticky finger on the window
lines: A smudge appears on the clean window mark,
I rub it away, revealing something spark.
Sun slants through, and I see it in light,
the sky feels a little bit brighter tonight.
Morning sunlight glances off the toaster's light,
It hums low, maybe it'll toast again some might.
I don't know why I kept this machine so old,
It's part of the kitchen I can't bear to scold.
The pan begins to breathe a thin, gray smoke,
the air turns rich enough to almost choke.
You watch the bacon curl into its meat,
remembering how much you once missed the heat.
His coupon was good for one dinner date,
but now it's expired and he's stuck with his plate.
He tried to argue with the cashier about soup,
but she laughed and said, "No deals for your group."
I cradle the box where the warmth still holds heat,
It's just me and the grease and the leftover meat.
That last slice was magic—it's vanished, all gone,
I stare at the crust, story playing me on.
I found a forgotten loaf taking on mold,
it's been there since before this year got too old.
Now the pantry feels like a museum bin,
but throwing it out feels like a waste to begin.
You find the seat still damp from yesterday's spill,
but sunlight hits the spot like some strange thrill.
You sit down gently, praying it will stay dry,
the mess may fade before your eyes like morning sky.

topic: socks left in the break room
lines: I found your sock tucked under the stair,
still warm from the shadow it dared to share.
You must have rushed through the day with such grace,
leaving only this soft, mismatched trace.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: I saw my name pop up below a random post,
the internet had called me their favorite host.
I read it again just to make sure it was name,
this moment felt close to something like fame.
I drink less now—my pride is in that claim,
I hold it up in front of the mirror's frame.
It's not a gimmick or a health routine sign,
it's my daily proof I'm walking the tightrope line.

topic: reading under the covers with a flashlight
lines: You dim the room with your flashlight's beam,
lost in stories where you'd rather dream.
The pages turn, the hours fly with the book,
and time forgot how lonely it took.
They argue over the songs and the keys,
each note a memory, a slight or a tease.
The music begins but it all starts to blur,
the past and the present begin to stir.
I hear a half-baked comment or a bad joke,
it's not funny but somehow I start to choke.
My coffee stays untouched, but my laugh starts to spill,
I can't explain why my chest still wants to fill.
They are scattered in a haphazard row,
I'm too tired to pick them up and go.
My roommates won't admit it's their own blame,
we argue over who could've had the shame.
I watched them slip into your shoes and tried,
to tell if it was love or the high tide.
They walked the room, never once did they weep,
but paused at my photos and stared down so deep.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: I remember the cry echoing through the mall,
she waved up at me with a wobbly small call.
We pass those same aisles with more miles and years,
and sometimes she still hides behind her own tears.
She lies flat out in the warm afternoon breeze,
arms flung wide, her legs bent at the knees.
The sky's so blue it almost seems the world
is nothing but light that's lazily unfurled.
She spots a café and gives me a sign,
"Go ahead," I say, "this one's mine."
I tap my card, the receipt reads *paid*,
She grins like I just led a parade.
The machine won't scan your slightly bent can,
a passing stranger cheers you like a fan.
You wave at the camera, joke about the bar,
they clap you through checkout like a small-time star.
She hit "send" without thinking it through, just a call,
a voice from the past where old ghosts used to sprawl.
The words still echo loud and strange in their sound,
while silence breaks hearts like a fault line unbound.
You listen to the wind's soft, wild song,
it dances out where the fields run long.
Your body moves as you let it sway,
the tall grass waves off your worries away.
She gives the cashier a look from her eye,
"Not this again," she thinks, not to buy.
She clutches her bag and sways it for swing,
now every small purchase feels like such a thing.
She laughs as she waves off the broken scan,
"We'll wing it—no receipts, just a dream of a plan."
The total is guesswork, all off-the-cuff math,
and everyone leaves on some weird new path.
She claimed the whole row from the window to aisle,
I watched her stretch out with a contented smile.
She opened five bags and tossed crumbs for snack,
now she's snoring loud and I'm missing my track.
She laughed through her coffee and morning rush,
the sugar high bloomed a brief moment lush.
Her legs hit the floor like two heavy door-
slams, and she flops back down with nothing but sore.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: A kid is wailing in the middle of the aisle,
her doll clutched tight, her bottom lip a mile.
I used to melt when kids would break and scream,
now I just count my own lost afternoon dream.
It's been a whole day since I got any paste,
I squeeze and I shout, but there's nothing to waste.
I almost want tears to flow fast and un-cry,
This tube is completely and totally dry.
I found it tucked behind a dusty old shelf,
the kind of thing I swore I'd lost myself.
I pop it in—still skips when it tries to play,
but nostalgia's stubborn, like mildew or decay.
You open the mailbox and see the pile,
The stack never thins, but you try to smile.
You log in late, and you feel the dread,
The clock ticks louder, your calm goes dead.
You checked the bin but it's definitely mold,
It's been there weeks in this kitchen so cold.
The stench is now part of your daily smell,
You're cooking again in this landfill hell.
They squeeze the toothpaste tube from end to end,
pretending they're saving the world for a friend.
But when the paste escapes the tube's cap,
it becomes a mess that no one can trap.
She checks the gas gauge—empty again, that's the tank,
some cosmic joke she swore wasn't a prank.
Her phone has zero bars and no GPS aim,
this trip was supposed to be epic, not lame.
I used to fly up here and find my rest,
now I sit on the seat, wind in my chest.
The wood groans with the sound of every age,
and I feel like a bird trapped in a cage.
She keeps the old watch still stuck in her time zone,
ignores the updates, clings to the old stone.
She checks the glow when the new one's too bright,
and misses the sun every single night.
A single drop lands, then a flood on the floor,
the ice cracks and the soda begins to pour.
You grab napkins like a warrior in shell,
it's too late—you're already halfway to hell.
She stares at the water, it's so very still,
a breeze won't come up from that distant hill.
Her phone doesn't buzz, it doesn't even shake,
and silence just grows where the dark will break.
The moment their hands brushed, there went the spark,
a flicker in the crowd at the coffee park.
You tried to laugh it off with clumsy grace,
but your cheeks betrayed you—flushed your whole face.
She stands beneath the lamp that won't hold,
letting the flicker make her look bold.
The glow bounces off her steady light,
turning each waver into quiet height.
You check the registers and see the long, long sight,
a silent battle not to lose your mind outright.
Your coffee's cooling now—this feels like a delay,
like time itself has slowed into decay.
She walks, eyes fixed on the path just ahead,
repeating silently what she needs to have said.
Her thoughts spin out like the leaves in her mind,
chased away by the sharp, cold, leaf-strewn wind.
You flip through them slowly, one by one, through,
each postcard a memory now faded blue.
You wrote them in hopes you'd send them, but why?
Not one voice has answered your delayed reply.
She checks the schedule—wrong classroom, same doom,
The clock ticks louder with each passing gloom.
She scans the test board but can't seem to read,
Her brain spins wild in her panic-stricken head.
You carve the corner with reckless spin,
your knuckles white against the handle's skin.
This city's yours—you don't just ride,
you move through traffic with a bold new stride.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: They flutter through the cold like falling air,
a wobbly pair in silhouette and glare.
Their beaks dip low where the crusty snow
hides the last remains of the bread we throw.
They said they'd do it last week, now it's doom,
they're sitting in their messy, uncleaned room.
They want to watch one more episode, mess,
while Google Docs still shows a red "0%" of progress.

topic: a taxi driver yelling on phone
lines: The cabbie swerves into the wrong lane,
shouting on his phone about some gain.
He mutters something about unpaid debt,
his grip white-knuckled, face slick with sweat.
I watch the sunflowers all turn their face,
chasing daylight through dry summer race.
Their heads grow heavy with the morning's gold,
and bow a little when the light begins to fold.
He checks his phone, a nightly scroll,
The blue glow fights the dark for control.
It dies at last—screen now blank,
His dreams begin in a data bank.
I savor each crumb, each olive's sharp taste,
I'd hate for this golden moment to waste.
We take turns with the slice, each careful bite,
the crust crumbles, we gently avoid a fight.
He never deletes a single missed call,
they stack up like dust in a digital sprawl.
His phone's a trophy case, not a smart tech,
the voice mem'ries play on his crowded deck.
I found your notes scrawled across every page,
your tiny arrows pointing from the cage.
Now I'm back home, still I can't help but miss,
the weight of that book, the ache of this.
My smartwatch beeps—it's not on the work,
it buzzes random and makes me jerk.
There's no text, no alert, no incoming call,
I'm fine in my sweatpants, just sitting and sprawl.
I wake up to garbage spilled out in the morn,
a bag split open, half the mess now torn.
I grab my gloves and I step up to cheer,
maybe today we're all finally clean and clear.
She drove through five towns just to see this view,
and paused where the light felt old and true.
The camera gave a low sad digital click,
but framing the shot was nature's own trick.
She's been standing near the same old gate,
her carry-on feels like it holds all her weight.
The line crawls ahead at a shaky pace,
she checks her phone for the tenth time today, her face.
You tap your card in the ride-share app,
but it deducts the wrong amount—some sort of trap.
You never knew how much joy one missing dime
could waste, now stuck in this car with no new time.
I stare through the window into the space,
this journey feels swift yet I'm barely in race.
They handed me peanuts and plastic-wrap map,
I raised my reading light, tipped back my seat, cap.
You scan the label, lost in the past,
remembering how your mother read it last.
The list is long, but you don't want to shout—
you check again, still full of doubt.
You stand there watching the leaves how they fall,
the wind has no name but it lifts them all.
Time slips through fingers like colors too fast,
and the trees let go of their final, soft last.
You claimed that space faster than a car near,
like a hawk in December, all grit and no fear.
You signaled, you braked, you swooped in and took,
leaving others jaw-dropped, just a sideways look.
You open the food delivery app,
but endless options feel like a trap.
Still, something here will surely let you eat,
and warm your hands while you wait to meet.

topic: chair squeaks when you lean back
lines: You lean into your chair but the back gives no slack,
It screeches like tires on a gravel road track.
Your coworkers all cringe as they fill up the room,
You mute fast and pretend it never did zoom.
You guard your kingdom like a noble post,
barking at ghosts you claim deserve a toast.
No one sees the menace in your bark,
but you treat every shadow like a lark.
You said we should fix the snoring this time,
I offered a white noise app as a chime.
It only plays loudly on repeat mode—loop,
so now my dreams feature marching snore troop.
Your name plays loud across the empty call,
it echoes off the office walls so tall.
I hear you now, clear as the noise cuts through,
maybe this time, my hope feels honest, true.
You keep your wallet safe in your hand,
and pass up any discount or brand.
The numbers add up, you've got this math,
your money stays strong on its own path.
They lean against the door like the whole world's weight,
a day that feels too long for their own estate.
A sigh slips out, thin as a broken thread,
the kind that only comes when the day is dead.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: You clipped a coupon with some hope it would come off,
now you chew the stale stuff, it tastes like a cough.
You thought you were saving, but still had to pay,
and your teeth already feel a little decay.
There it hangs—a ghostly white plastic sight,
torn from some grocery bag's flimsy flight.
It flaps like a fake bird, pretend wing,
an eco disaster with a sneaky sting.
They left the baking sheet out, still hot on the tray,
convinced something good would happen by day.
The air smelled like hope and sugar still warm,
waiting for life to slowly begin to transform.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: A green shoot pushed upward where the concrete grew,
It wriggled from darkness and split it right through.
The sun hit its leaves with a warm, golden light,
Such power in something so small and slight.
You pull out your card and the machine says "no cash,"
the screen lights up red like a warning splash.
You check the balance, no real game or aim—
the card's just a charm that went out like a flame.
My pencil felt fine until it ran out of lead,
the sharpener just laughed and said "go ahead."
I gave the crank a twist, then another, click—
turns out, the jam was hiding its own little trick.
You swing the shovel's rusted blade in vain,
each strike made dull by the frozen plain.
A rock could pass for ice and lie like stone,
the silence thickens, work never done, you're alone.
That dented plate hangs on your wall with pride,
every dent a memory you keep inside.
It's more than iron—it's a part you lift,
a rusted trophy you gave yourself as gift.
She set strict rules for the week, her new goal,
but her cravings kept whispering to her soul.
Now she counts calories only by rough measure,
and eats whatever brings her real pleasure.
You say it's hormones, not a single thing to blame,
You act like cracking's some awkward new game.
Your voice didn't just change overnight while you grew,
this isn't middle school—try again, that's you.
I fall into the feed and scroll so deep,
the morning comes with zero chance for sleep.
A thousand smiles float by my tired face,
each one from a world I can't replace.
You hold the phone high in the checkout line,
letting your voice shine without a single sign
of shame. The cashier nods, swipes your card,
while you take a quiet, earned step off the yard.
The sky pours down sludge that they call sleet,
the game's already lost since the first defeat.
We watch the whole mess of muddy pitch,
where players slide helplessly toward ditch.
She tugs the leash like she's racing to run,
chasing squirrels and calling it all the fun.
Her handler still clings tight to the lead,
though the dog's already past her dinner feed.
You elbow your way through the packed train door,
your shoulder is sore from the commuter before.
You pretend to be busy with scrolling and read,
while jammed in place like a crushed tomato head.
They hang on the hook, faded and worn,
a pair with the heel threadbare and torn.
He never found the match, left to stay,
a quiet comfort against the cold and the gray.
Her calendar holds the quietest date,
she didn't expect anyone to wait.
A playlist plays on without its song,
and hours stretch thin where love should be long.
My morning alarm still says half-past clock,
but my brain hasn't woken up from the block.
The coffee machine beeps, it thinks I want brew,
I stare at the window instead of its view.
There's a 50% off sign, what a deal!
I try them on just to see how they feel.
I take ten pairs but only pay for three.
The cashier says, "Enjoy your happy free!"
He spends hours on this bubble-blowing time,
Swears it's cheaper fun, though he used up a dime.
He calls it performance art, or something like art,
But no one else thinks it's that clever or smart.

topic: a quiet moment on the porch
lines: A breeze slips through the door with a slight chill,
you sit on the step, steady and still.
You watch how the dusk climbs the old tree,
and wonder what's left out there for me.
I listen to the crisp and brittle sound,
the kind that makes you miss where summer's found.
They never stay up long—they always fall,
like the wind is whispering something to recall.
You found a wad stuck beneath your chair, truth,
it smells of cinnamon from someone's youth.
You leave it there without a second take,
it feels too close to memory to break.

topic: a child drawing on the table
lines: The table's a canvas of color and art,
crayon paths cross where old recipes chart.
I see my own hands in the little ones' past,
they'll clean it all away with their work from the last.
You've been stuck here since the morning gate,
but you're laughing now—it's a fun kind of date.
Strangers smile at you, they all seem to grin,
someone tossed a snack in your empty bin.
You watch the cheese fall like snowflakes that fell,
each granule lands soft in the pasta shell.
You lift the grater to catch what's at top,
but time slips away when you savor each stop.
I left my bag behind when I ran out for school,
now I'm in class with no eraser or tool.
My pen leaks, my highlighter lost its cap,
and every desk looks like it has a gap.

topic: walking past each other in a crowd
lines: I push through people just to get my space,
but they fill it instantly to replace.
My shoulders are tense, I may hit someone right,
the sidewalk's too small, and the air feels tight.
You count the coins you can't afford to love,
they clink like echoes of a mourning dove.
The machine whirs, accepts your meager cash,
your warmth turns to coffee, joy to ash.
It's old but it shows in the wood's steady age,
She pushes herself back to her childhood stage.
Her feet leave the ground as she builds up her sway,
she laughs like she'll never want to go away.
I watch the stream keep its quiet, steady flow,
wind bends the trees but it can't stop the show.
It carves through the stone with a patient, sharp shape,
and whispers how time turns the rock into escape.
They serve the lunch but forget the coffee, bread,
my eyes are drooping, making my head dead.
I say I'll work just five more minutes, lie,
then stare at my desk and sigh and try.
I still watch old cartoons on my morning shows,
the coffee brews as the world out loud grows.
I pause for a moment, take a quiet slice
of childhood tucked inside each bouncing mice.
I watched my toast go from brown to gold,
then waited for it to burn or fold.
The butter's a puddle, can't even pretend,
I ate it slowly, like I still intend.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: I hit record hoping you'll finally try,
my voice says "call me" but you never reply.
I tap send again and the app won't let me send,
it's stuck in a loop with no clear way to mend.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: A child kneels on the floor in the aisle,
her candy bar torn with a tearful smile.
The cartwheels spin fast in her little cry—
can't she have both flavors of yogurt, why?
The toast is stale, the coffee tastes too cold,
They charge you extra for the jam in bold.
The scrambled eggs look suspiciously like meat,
The syrup's half a gallon, barely sweet.
You pick up your phone and begin to scroll,
your sandwich goes cold as your mind takes control.
A passive-aggressive thread starts to stew,
you read through your lunch, but it's really about you.
She's been standing since the first stop after seat,
her face red from the air that won't beat the heat.
Everyone watches but no one meets her eyes,
we all know the car's full of quiet lies.
I find a slice left over from your love,
tucked away beneath the cookies above.
It's covered in flour and time's fine dust,
but I'd still eat it, just like your crust.
You watch the fish drift in your tired mind,
they swim the same path like a daily grind.
They loop around the bowl, never going through,
their tiny world feels so sadly true.
I hit the unsubscribe button with a click,
it's the first smart move this month, old trick.
No more payments, no monthly parade
of useless emails saying "you were paid."
I wave my mouse like I'm making a call,
the cursor spins, a pixelated ball.
We laugh through the glitch, still trying to share,
we trace the same steps in the same stale air.

topic: sitting on the porch steps at twilight
lines: You sit on the steps where the last light clings tight,
the air smells of dusk and the coming of night.
You think you could stay where the shadows still play,
but the wind calls your name and pulls you away.

topic: a long queue at the coffee shop
lines: I count the bodies stacked ten deep ahead,
my phone buzzes with work emails I should dread.
The line moves slower than a snail's crawl,
I watch the clock, my patience close to sprawl.
She drops a ten-dollar bill for more than a dime,
she savors each bite, chasing lost old time.
This meal costs less than what she used to feel,
but comfort is cheap when your hunger is real.
Your phone glows like a tiny, tired eye,
the real one above fades into the sky.
The screen keeps its electric lullaby hum,
while your thumbs tap out a sleepless drum.
I watched her drift across the painted line,
her eyes fixed on the glowing phone's small sign.
The crash came loud, a silent sort of scream,
now my quiet road feels like a shattered dream.
The moment was brief but it felt like fate—
a spill on the desk, minutes too late.
Hot brown waves crept across the glass to melt
the screen into static, a sizzled welt.
The coffee spills because he missed the drop,
a slow motion fail his body can't crop.
He catches the next cup just as it starts to wait,
but misses the toast that lands face down on the plate.
He never asked for a single fry,
just stood there cooing toward the greasy sky.
You thought he'd settle for a cool little act,
but he took the whole bag—cold, bare, and fact.
I smooth the blemishes off my tired face,
then choose a background I'd rather erase.
I tweak the light till my skin looks too glow,
but no one sees how I feel from below.
A pigeon lands with a squawk and some flair,
it eyes my French fries with only one care.
I try to scare it but lose the first bite,
now crumbs are gone and it's off in full flight.
You watch every drop as it falls from the flow,
it's your masterpiece now—let's call it a show.
You timed each small plink to a perfect drip,
you'd never let go for a single skip.
She taps through the feed without a skip,
a hot take appears, but she just lets it trip.
There's passion in pixels, but no real fire,
so she swipes on in calm, quiet desire.
She built it high, a precarious pile,
she thought she'd have time, but the minutes ran while.
Now she can't bend without losing her reach,
though she still tries to learn what the chaos might teach.
I tap the screen but decide not to scroll,
my fingers freeze like a paused movie control.
I leave it unread, a digital stone,
pretending I'm out of cell signal tone.
You toss your plane and watch it take start,
it loops through air like something from your heart.
It dips and turns but keeps the perfect glide,
I swear it's plotting ways to stay and bide.
This hotel room reeks of stale, old air,
The soap's a weird orange in the shower's glare.
I close my eyes, but I still don't see
What this place smells like home to anyone but me.
My playlist was set for the perfect replay,
a vibe from last summer, same lingo, same day.
But the track just skipped and my coolness went fail,
now I'm stuck humming the chorus down the trail.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: They're skimming through posts and they spot your name scroll,
it catches their eye, makes their face light up whole.
They double-tap fast, then their cheeks begin blush,
they wonder if maybe it's fate holding a crush.
Your name gets stuck against my mental wall,
I meant to call you, but I just forgot all.
We met last week, or was it months? I meet
panic in my brain every time we greet.
My eyes feel heavy, they're moving in slow flow,
the screen's bright glow won't let me go.
I yawn and check if there's a shut-down sign,
but my thumb just hits "read" and skips the line.
She tapped and she typed, then hit send too soon,
and the group chat all laughed at her tune.
Her face drains of color, she's clearly a miss,
the wrong ex gets called up with a "Don't you still kiss?"
You think it's a clue from the janitor crew—
some message about a new brand of glue.
You take careful steps, just a little ahead,
and slip where they warned you not to have spread.
I trace the flour like a map of old days,
we laughed at mistakes in the same weird ways.
Now it sits on the counter, thin layer of dust,
but maybe tomorrow I'll bake into crust.

topic: a favorite mug with a chip
lines: I bought this mug 'cause it had one small flaw,
now every guest breaks some odd household law.
They all reach out to give it a show,
as if it's fine china, not chipped coffee dough.
You hold it up like a medal, that perfect char,
golden around the edges, a kitchen star.
The whole room smells of failure, but don't you scent?
You're just here to celebrate your twisted intent.
Your GPS insists this is still the way,
but traffic piles up in some strange delay.
You question if it knows the correct path,
(math) yet it claims the numbers are perfect math.
I bought six bags but they didn't last for more,
I filled them all, now the handles just tore.
I'm proud of my haul and the mess in this state,
let the next bags come — I'm ready for fate.
I always squeeze the tube from the squeeze,
the minty mess nearly makes me freeze.
A river of foam at the sink's edge grows foam,
and for a second I feel like I'm home.
You blame the wind when your porch light goes spell,
But you know it's the bulb that just quit and fell.
You fumble for switches, for wires, the key,
I laugh from my car while you glare at it, me.
She never thought twice about who would dare
to leap into that mucky puddle with flair.
Her boots splashed loud in their careless, fast pace,
while her grin got dirtier than her mud-smeared face.
Your phone buzzes out of nowhere in the call,
you lift it in a half-awake sprawl.
You stare at the screen in that silent deep,
no name just a number that won't stop beep.
I count my change now like it's buried treasure cash,
no more splurging when the cards start to flash.
I skip the candy bar from the checkout aisle,
but save my spending for the things that make me smile.
A bus horn blares through the sleepy suburb's call,
It cuts across the morning's slow sprawl.
She stirs slightly but doesn't quite wake,
Her dreams are too perfect to break.
She typed too fast and lost her aim,
the message went to the wrong name.
Her thumb hovered, unsure of where to land,
but she didn't delete—just stared at the brand.
You wish this meeting would somehow just call,
but time drags on with a restless sprawl.
You tap your pen, itch through the air,
at the clock, wishing someone would just dare.
You chose a second opinion with care,
not fearing to question what others would share.
You take your health at a steady pace,
and let no one push you into a race.
It plowed into the window like it was a wall,
then screeched a warning call no one could recall.
You tapped the glass with your finger and wing,
annoyed by the bird's clumsy little thing.
He watches fields and roads from the air,
the only one who could get away with that dare.
The hawk circles high, he owns the height,
like everything else, he makes it look like his might.
I hand over my ten with a hopeful change,
the cashier sorts coins into a quick arrange.
I savor the moment, this warm little bite,
the promise inside feels like something bright.
I used to have rhythm, I had such grace,
now my feet stumble into each space.
They don't listen to music they just can't move,
I pretend I'm fine but my hips never prove.
You check your phone for a digital map,
but the signal drops—now this whole place is a trap.
The signs are unclear, the language feels read,
and every turn here looks like it could mislead.

topic: reading under the covers with a flashlight
lines: She'd hide the book beneath the blanket's glow,
the world outside could never read her so.
The stories lived inside those yellowed pages,
while moms raged downstairs about bedtime's ages.
She planned the party three weeks ahead,
but forgot the cake and the candles she'd said.
We all pretend we're caught off our cheer,
while she swears this is how good years appear.
Your dog sits at the door all day, won't go away,
He barks in your ear till you finally say.
You toss him a treat for being such a treat,
But he just looks at the door, ready to meet.

topic: a bike locked to a pole
lines: He left his bike locked to a pole with no clue
where he'd gone—keys vanished, rider too.
The U-lock stuck tight like a stubborn old shame,
a puzzle he left that no one could claim.
She pushes through miles on the same old machine,
each motion a clockwork, stubborn routine.
Her hair whips around like it wants to fly,
but she can't stop to ask herself why.
She loves that old tradition, the curtain call scene,
the whole block applauds when the credits hit screen.
She wipes her eyes while she walks down the aisle,
remembering how they used to clap and smile.

topic: a friend who is always late
lines: She's never on time but she's never a crime,
she rolls in like music with a lazy chime.
Her rhythm's her pace, no need for a race,
she shows up just when you think she won't face.
You wear your grandpa's faded polka-dot suit,
and mismatched socks with one scuffed-up boot.
Your hair's a disaster, but you love the flair,
you twirl in the mirror with wild, dramatic air.
She sends "u up?" like it's just a quick dime,
no thought, no plan, just a random climb.
It's past two a.m., the kind of too late
where answers don't come and silence will wait.
You pull out your ten like it's old school cash,
but the menu prices all look like a slash.
You settle for toast and a weak hot dog bill,
still calling it "lunch" for that faux thrill.
You stare at the screen that won't let you feed
your thoughts as the chorus repeats to bleed.
The dancers twist in the same old scene,
their moves too perfect, like some sick machine.
I've been waiting here since the baggage claim,
watching tags flake off with my last name.
A cart slides by, but my bag isn't light—
maybe it's still stuck, or someone took it by might.
She watches the pawn fall slowly to the floor,
its white face down like a soldier from a war.
Her hand hovers, unsure if she should make the move,
or let it lie there as her doubt begins to prove.
You left your things behind in the sand,
the wind took the top off your old red stand.
Now it leans just a little bit more your way,
like a memory, starting to decay.
You still keep them by the bedroom door,
where we once laughed while we both wore
them in together—now they look too old,
but your hands still find what they want to hold.
They claim they're not giving in to another treat,
but the dog is leaning in with hopeful feet.
They mutter about how it's time for the meal,
then cave with a grin—can't resist that appeal.
I saw a dark stain where the floor was one spot,
I stepped right through it and now my shoe's got hot.
I asked for a warning but got no clue,
the mess feels like something spilled and dried to glue.
You tried to log in, but the screen still won't view,
your password is right—somehow it's not true.
You tap the button, hoping maybe you'll tap
into something real, not just a ghostly trap.
This stupid band is about to snap,
I reference no fitness guru's map.
Just pretend I've had enough and want to stop,
or maybe I'll yell something like "band, you drop!"
The rain soaks through my jacket and the field,
but no one's leaving — this game is sealed.
We chant and clap, we raise our cheer,
while my socks drip and freeze in wetter gear.
He scans the spread for something more than eggs,
but the toast is sad, and the meat has no legs.
There's mystery sauce and the same old cold ham,
and he leaves with a ache where his appetite jam.
You stare at their vacation photos in the post,
every smile feels like a past-life ghost.
You pour yourself a glass, too full of wine,
but the silence still hums way below your line.
You know every lyric to the gym's old beat,
They loop the same track just to keep you repeat.
You lift with the rhythm, you move with the lift,
The weights feel lighter when the music gives shift.
The tray goes flying with a sickening clatter,
Soup soaks the floor where the whole world might matter.
A pickle splutters in a pool of lime,
The clock ticks slow — this is the worst time.
You watch the stream as the water flows,
it moves like thoughts you never compose.
It carries something from your own soul,
you try to stop it but lose all control.
I tap the icon, the logo fills screen,
a spinning circle turns bright green.
I force-quit, restart, but it still won't try,
the app just crashes—what's there left to why?
They say they hear the same old lonely sound,
how each drop falls, the echo stays around.
Their eyes drift upward toward that gray sky,
wondering why the clouds won't just let dry.
She watches the bird as it teeters and sway,
the whole world reduced to this quiet, small day.
A breeze lifts its feather, one tiny wing,
and suddenly she feels like she could just sing.
I step back to take in the perfect view,
A sky fades from dawn into soft blue.
My phone hits the wall as I try to frame it all,
The moment escapes me, though I try to call.
You drizzle store-bought sauce all over your plate,
as if it could ever replace what was great.
That pre-shredded cheese tastes so fake,
why not just toss the whole dish and take a break?
I gave it a twist and another try,
but the plug stayed stuck, I couldn't let it fly.
It's the wrong size again, it won't quite fit,
maybe I'll just use this as an excuse to quit.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: I snap the sky turning gold and light,
the sun bursts up, so warm and bright.
I upload the photo, just the scene in post,
I let the silence say it's beauty's most.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: You spoke clearly, so they should've heard you through,
but the app said "sending" in silence for you.
You recheck the signal, maybe it could not mean
something wrong inside the phone or the screen.
The silence in the house sets in with fear,
you check the couch with both hands near your ear.
Your voice breaks the quiet — "Phone? Hello? Call?"
You stare at the wall where it's stuck, small and tall.
I've seen your message pop up on my read,
but this whole conversation feels dead in the thread.
You'll just assign it, as always, to blame,
while I'm left doing something more fun than your game.

topic: crackling fireplace on a winter night
lines: It's supposed to be warm but my bones are still cold,
I was told this fire would light up the old.
I toss in another damp log or two,
the dog yawns and shifts where the heat won't come through.
You trace every dent like a scar or a mark,
it gathered them all in the gym bag and park.
You still use it though the lid won't keep,
and drink from it late when you lie awake, sleep.
You thought this was going to be your gourmet feast,
but clicked "Buy Now" at the very *least*.
Now you're staring down the bowl, full of regret,
wondering how you paid so much to just not get.
I pulled out my crumpled, damp ten-dollar cash,
the cashier smiled as her screen gave a flash.
I ordered a sandwich, fries, soup for the meal,
and left with a grin and a lighter feel.
You feel the stillness as the morning turns calm,
the ocean waves whisper between your palm.
Breezes rise sweet from the salt-heavy air,
you stand alone, not sure how far or where.
That squirrel's acting like a total thief,
burying acorns under every leaf.
It digs so fast, you know it's done it deep,
then naps like it's earned a solid week's sleep.
I never needed that plastic for cash,
I've built my life without owing a stash.
The screen may say I have nothing but zero,
I'm rich in choices—no debt means I'm hero.
It stands there drooping, quiet and alone,
while she's too busy scrolling down her phone.
She used to water it, she said she still knew
how tenderly to watch it bloom in view.
I saw a small robin land in that spot,
it wasn't there when I mowed the back lot.
It pecks the cool earth for the first seed,
maybe spring's here to stay, after all, indeed.
She grabs her fork, takes a bite from the edge,
but hesitates before she makes a pledge.
Her eyes keep darting back toward the fold
where your half remains, too hot to hold.
I set the last dish down on the plate,
just in time for our pretend dinner date.
The kids come barging through the door to run,
they ruin the mood but we call it fun.
You got your test back but there's no grade in class,
I'll pretend to care while I stare at the grass.
You swore you studied it all night, don't fib by,
it shows—your name's missing from the topmost lie.
You walk through the orchard, cool as a tree,
the breeze whispers only "eat one for me."
You crunch through the flesh until there's just core,
and wish that the moment could somehow be more.
It won't come down from the very top off,
I've tried a stick and even given it a cough.
It still blocks my window, spoiling the view,
pretending it's some ancient art display new.
I felt the world shrink when I stood so near,
the crowd faded into some distant cheer.
Your face lit up in the warm streetlight glow,
and for once, I didn't want to just say hello.
I didn't check the gas when I took my clue,
now I'm stuck on this road with a bleak point of view.
The GPS is offline, my phone doesn't map,
and this rental's a joke — what a lovely trap.
She waits until he's close enough to door,
then grabs the butter from the fridge to store.
Her fingers brush his, the sugar starts to spill,
but she just laughs and says she'll clean it with a will.
I trace the cracks—pretend they're old and full of fun,
the clock ticks slow, but time still wants to run.
My mind floats upward, joins a passing cloud,
while silence hums a tune too soft to be loud.

topic: crackling fireplace on a winter night
lines: The flames die down but the warmth is still,
outside the wind carries a sharp chill.
Logs turn to ash in the hearth so slow,
time slips by as the fire winds down to go.
I can't escape the scent of that familiar past,
it hits me like a memory-infused blast.
The pasta lies still on the lukewarm dish,
I want to go back to that kitchen with my wish.
I'm in a rush and it's costing me time,
my cart waits patiently, not even a dime.
They wave me off, but I block the aisle,
they fake the nicest, tightest fake smile.
I turned my ruler into a wand for the class,
I tapped it with purpose, not even like grass.
We followed the line while I tried to draw,
but it slipped from my grip and hit my jaw.

topic: a taxi driver yelling on phone
lines: You swear he doesn't know the rules of the lane,
his loud phone rant feels more like a pain.
He slams the brakes for a text message ride,
like this could be worse than a sinking ship's tide.
You count the rhythm of the rain's soft beat,
while laughter echoes off the wet street.
The storm feels close, but skies are growing near,
and sunlight's peeking through—so it's all clear.
The lake lies flat beneath this silver still,
the silence thick enough to cut and fill.
A ripple breaks but never changes form,
yet something in my chest begins to storm.
She finds another sock, a cold twist of shock,
the laundry room timer ticks down off the clock.
Her feet feel so cold, now one foot is bare,
the dog chews in peace, with no hint of care.
You took your last sip and set the mug to drink,
the warmth still clinging where your lips would think.
A pinky smudge now marks the rim as stain,
like memory—faint but meant to remain.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: They spotted a rock that caught the sun's gleam,
it sat alone in the soft-pebbled stream.
They held it close, like finding their fate,
until it slipped through their trembling weight.
Her fingers fly across the glowing screen,
crafting a reply that sharp and mean.
She pauses only once to hit the key,
then texts go silent, like digital debris.
They used to whisper secrets in their prime,
how the nights would blur into the climb.
Now they lie awake, heart racing late,
tracing ghosts of love that shaped their fate.
I left my lunch here and now it's a snack,
the keys won't release—my cursor goes track.
I spray some air hard to get them to pop,
but maybe next time I'll eat at the shop.
You said it was the only thing that felt true,
the crayon hearts and shaky writing in glue.
I haven't had that kind of joy in a while—
just cardboard, but I wish it could still make you smile.
A melody hits me, I can't ignore the tune,
my eyes get heavy with tears so soon.
I wipe them off but they just won't erase,
this song is magic—it brings me to this place.
My dog tugs the leash like it owes him his tugs,
he's trying to sprint where the neighborhood bugs.
I pretend I'm in charge but he shows me the way,
we end up at the park for our daily play.
He strums the same few love songs, old and tunes,
the crowd nods like they're listening through moons.
His calloused fingers never miss the strings,
but I'm distracted by the weirdest things.
You let the paintbrush leave a quiet trail,
the blue streaks across the floor so pale.
You crouch there carefully, as if to bend,
your shadow tracing what you meant to send.
I flip through the calendar page by date,
recalling the scribbles I once wrote to debate.
Some days are crossed out with no further room,
while others still smell faintly of old perfume.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: I feel a small nudge from a toothpick there,
I check my sleeve for the stupidest hair.
It's lodged deep enough to still look like a stick,
I hope no one asks me to explain it real quick.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: The TV roared with laughter at my joke,
I coughed out words I never meant to choke.
There's no real audience, no hidden clue,
but maybe this means someday you'll laugh too.
You smudged the pages from front to back through,

but silence feels louder than any applause.
