their fingers fumble, unsure how to know.
The laces always seem set to fall,
but you never say, "Let me take over, doll."
You tap your foot as if it's your last brake,
radio static hums like a burnt cake.
You count every inch, every stalled mile,
but miss the open road on this lost trial.
They stack like relics from a life already due,
each one a reminder of the debt in plain view.
I watch the dust settle like snow on their glow,
and wonder when my soul will stop trying to grow.
She's got a knife and a cutting board,
it's less a task and more like a sword.
She keeps a rhythm with every chop,
until the veggies make her want to stop.
Her finger brushed mine without a care,
like a ghost mid-step on the stair.
She looked away, but her face gave more,
than all the empty space we ignore.
My coffee slips between my fingers and drops,
I miss the time I caught each cup before it crops.
I fumble now with the remote or my key,
paying late fines like some sad membership fee.
You read the sign again, searching for the rest,
but the rules are vague, like some retail quest.
The employee shrugs and says they can't say,
so you leave the box still sitting out away.
You wait and wait but the buffer won't time,
your patience is gone long before the chime.
You click "refresh" and pretend it will play,
but the loading bar always wins the delay.
You say this song doesn't belong on the track,
but I'm just defending my mix with an attack.
We have no rules when it comes to these rules,
so why are we acting like the other side's fools?
You drop the first dish you made on the plate,
it's lopsided and comes out way too late.
You grab more than a pinch of the salt,
the meal is ruined, but you take it in fault.
You toss a crumb but it slips straight down,
the robin circles with eyes all around.
It pecks at the earth for some hidden seed,
but you're the only one who can claim the deed.
She cracks the egg and it spills into shell,
too fragile to cook, she can't seem to tell.
She watches the yolk turn a sickly gold,
unsure if she should stir or let it just hold.
She leaves the kitchen light on all through the beam,
as if it could catch every stray thought or dream.
Her coffee brews in an old chipped pot,
and warmth spreads out where the bulb gives a lot.
I left it too long when it started to dry,
I panic now, watching it slowly die.
I'm miles from a store or a garden or far,
it's just me and this wilting green star.
You've tried so many times to get this tied,
your laces still hang out and won't abide.
You kick off your shoes and mutter about the lace,
when suddenly both loops fall into their place.

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: The handlebars tilt as the afternoon breeze
brushes my legs, warm against my knees.
I lean left to let the sidewalk glide
under me, slow and steady on this quiet side.

topic: a receipt lost in the bag
lines: She rips through the bag looking for the tear,
receipts crumple and fall but the refund is near.
Her phone scans the mess, finds nothing but scan,
the cashier's closing in and she has no plan.
You spend hours watching the rabbit sniff the air,
it twitches through dust like it's dodging a snare.
It freezes at noise, but ignores your offered food,
then hops off mid-stare, never explaining its mood.
I can't remember if I reached my stretch,
the band snapped loose when I was halfway fetch.
My thoughts keep drifting from the task in mind,
and all the effort feels like wasted wind.
I stare at your frozen face on my screen,
it's paused mid-laugh in a pixelated scene.
I try to keep things light, I tap the touch,
but silence stays heavy—I miss you so much.
He sighs at the sunset, it's such a fake,
pretending to enjoy this perfect break.
Every photo's a calculated pose,
lit by a dying sun and not a single rose.
Your toast never got the signal to pop,
it's lodged like a tragic, burnt-out crop.
You're certain this toaster will trigger your scream,
a morning so basic turns nightmare-dream.
You left your keys with not a single clue,
I had to follow you the whole way through.
I let you search, I didn't even dare
to laugh when you swore they weren't in the air.
I found my sock—just the left heel,
and now my foot feels like it's missing a wheel.
I tried to tie my sneaker with the lace,
but neither shoe can agree on its place.
She left her shoes out beneath the open sky,
hoping the sun would work magic and dry.
The clouds didn't listen, the dampness still lay,
so she wore rain boots all the way home today.
You watched the ferry glide where your plans had failed,
the last one gone before your ticket was mailed.
The dock's still warm with footprints made by you,
out across the water's slow, gray view.
She taps the same keys as she did all her time,
but now they're faded, not quite in their prime.
Her fingers move fast, though the screen shows it slow,
but she still hears the sound of old habits grow.
You leave your shoes out like they own the floor,
no time to clean up, no thought to the chore.
You swear there's a system—some secret type,
but they look more like a wild, lazy stripe.
My face hits the glass as the train tries to race,
The door slams in my personal space.
I mutter some curses, maybe too near,
The guy next to me hears every word clear.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: You saw the coupon and claimed the deal,
now you're munching chips for lunch instead of meal.
The savings were good, but the flavor's a cap,
next time, maybe skip the snack trap.
I bought this fancy cheese for one main dish,
I wish I'd just ordered a quick takeout fish.
The pasta is cold, my efforts feel flat,
I toss the unused Parmesan into the hat.
She gave the light switch one last firm *tone*,
the bulb replied with a nervous little *moan*.
She yanked the outlet, tried to twist the *plug*,
and tripped over the cord, right onto the *rug*.

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: You pose beside an empty chair and feel alone,
then notice the sky has lost its gray stone.
A breeze flips through the pages, soft and light,
and somewhere, someone sees this post and smiles, just might.

topic: crackling fireplace on a winter night
lines: The fire crackles soft, low now but still it blaze,
Your old flannel sleeves smell like these quiet days.
You trace the shapes in how the shadows glow,
and let the warmth collect inside you so.

topic: car keys on the kitchen table
lines: You left your keys where the light begins to fail,
by the dishes and the dog's wet old tail.
They're sitting proud on a milk carton slab,
you groan and toss but you won't even grab.
She counts the times it flickers in quick fits,
each pop and flash like memory's loose bits.
Her fingers hover, trying to fix her mind,
but old regrets still whisper through the wind.
You say it's still early, but Monday comes yet,
you try to hold time by pretending to let.
You scroll through old photos from Friday ago,
and wish you were someone who never needs to grow.
I let the confetti stay for my pride,
It's glitter and luck from that wild ride.
A few bits are tangled in loose hair,
I leave them—proof of where I was there.
You move at your own gentle pace,
giving others room to pass with space.
The crowd shifts around you, soft and slow,
they somehow feel it's better just to know.
You thrash in sleep but don't seem to wake,
your boss is yelling that your lunch break
is up and you're late, so you bolt out of chair,
only to open eyes and still see the stare.
I've paid for silence, but this won't be my ride,
he talks so loud I wish I could just hide.
His stories spill from back to front seat,
I turn off the air—this man runs on heat.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: A crack runs through the sidewalk, not too wide,
some green has peeked out carefully inside.
She kneels each morning, just to give it a lift,
though she says it's not a plant—more like a gift.
You peek through the curtain for a better view,
but doubt if what's there is really true.
A figure passes, your breath turns to shadow,
you wonder if running is worth the tomorrow.
I took one look at it and let out a sigh,
the cheese sat there dull, its wrapper gone dry.
It's written in ripples of plastic and fate,
we both are too late for this perfect, fresh slate.
She climbs the hill for the best possible view,
the sky turns soft in a painter's last hue.
She doesn't move when the shadows begin to stand,
she claims the light as her quietest land.
She scrolls until dawn just to hide the screen,
the blue light still whispers what it doesn't mean.
Her eyes get so heavy, her head starts to fall,
but she waits for a text that never comes at all.
The plug just won't twist into its fit,
you fumble a bit, then laugh at your wit.
It goes in sideways—what a weird old way,
but you lean into it and call it today's play.
The paper's still blank, the deadline's due,
your pencil skips with a nervous blue.
Each line you write feels stuck in the page,
but maybe this ache is a kind of cage.
I was halfway through the next row of songs I know,
but the track just jumped and refused to go.
I tapped the screen, flipped my phone's lid,
and laughed when it played the one I had hid.
I choose the most practical, sensible smart,
I never run late since I laced up to start.
My foot doesn't ache from some flimsy heel,
I walk with confidence, built like steel.
You step in a puddle that looks like the floor,
the kind that appears outside every store.
You check how much water is soaking them deep—
your shoes are a sponge, you look like a sheep.

topic: a taxi driver yelling on phone
lines: You grin through the chaos of his loud ride,
he argues with someone on his cell side.
He waves off the question about your fare,
and laughs into traffic, loose as the air.
You twist the dial until it reaches your ears,
the same songs play like they did for all those years.
The music still feels like a warm summer blast,
though every chord screams of a time long gone past.
They walked straight into the storm without a look through,
the map was folded, but the path was never true.
One sock is soaked, the other's just a sock,
but both feet hum a tune of slow, cold shock.
My vision blurs like the morning haze,
It's been weeks since my eyes felt fresh new days.
I rub my lids to try to finally see,
A light switches on—this could be the key.
You offered half but I wanted to take
the whole cheesy cake and be blamed for the break.
We laughed at the mess, shared every last char,
and finished the slice like a perfect small star.
I thought I saw the king make his move,
but it was just the breeze trying to prove
a point about how even kings can fall—
now I pick him up and call it all.
Your dog tilts his head, he's searching for a clue,
He seems to think you might tell him what to do.
"Why are you talking?" he asks with a sigh,
He'd rather chase squirrels than study the sky.

topic: losing your wallet at the mall
lines: I lost my wallet mid-shopping spree,
now everyone's asking if it's still on me.
I walked from kiosk to kiosk, every tile,
but the security guard had a hopeful smile.
The chorus hits and my throat begins to swell,
I blame the pollen or something else to tell.
I could turn it off but I don't think I might,
this ballad's magic is too strong for the night.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: She walks the block the same old way,
as if each concrete day won't change or decay.
But there's a green thing pushing through where it grows,
a quiet life the cracks have allowed to shows.
Its golden eye tracks me from up high,
it soars above where clouds won't fly.
I think about those talons built for claw,
and wonder if the wind obeys the law.
You can't think straight, your head won't feel clear,
the slides blur past like smoke from a rear.
You miss the whole thing, lose the main thread,
and nod like you knew it was already dead.
You felt a silent electric spark,
when our hands brushed by the park.
You tried to catch my eye that wave,
but never worked up the nerve to be brave.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: You see a gray strand while brushing your face,
It's not just one—there's a whole gray race.
You grab the scissors, your trusty old tool,
But more pop up like targets in a pool.
Your thumb bears the strain of this quiet ache,
You text me a joke—*I miss you, no cake*.
Words form so slow, but they're full of glow,
Each letter a flicker from your steady flow.
I give this recipe another try,
the smoke alarm thinks I'm out to fry.
But I taste the risk and let it grow,
one day I'll master what I need to know.
I was so sure I'd master this whole thing with paint,
but now it's all chaos, and hope feels too faint.
The floor will keep that blue mess as a scar,
and I'll never hold that brush in the same jar.
You grab the spatula and pretend your shift
is serving breakfast when I whisper "gift."
We lean too close, almost for the sake
of holding heat before we make a mistake.
She cranks up the music and calls it a blast,
neighbors text to ask if we've all been passed.
I clap my hands over my poor, abused ear,
she sips her cold drink and shouts "Cheers, good beer!"
She rides the swing to the highest height,
her laughter spins like birds in flight.
Her knees press in where the metal ache
holds time still, as if memory might take.

topic: waiting for the bus in rain
lines: I pull up my jacket but still get my hood,
a joke about weather might be pretty good.
A bus pulls up slowly, looks like it's been near,
the clouds part slightly—it's starting to clear.
Your fingers move steady around the knife,
slicing slices of red into your life.
The boat rocks gently, wide open sea—
you feel wild, purposeful, endlessly free.
Her socks never quite seem to find their match,
one heel has a split and a frayed-out patch.
She leaves her one shoe by the coat and shoe,
and claims she's not sure if it still will glue.
You pick the lane that goes way too slow,
the cashier's just learning how registers flow.
You watch everyone else finish their cart,
while yours sits heavy at the very back start.
The sky begins slowly to glow,
mirroring ice on the quiet snow.
The sun lifts up, calm and slow to rise,
I blink twice, stunned by how bright it flies.
I was certain the weather forecast said calm,
now my phone drips water from every palm.
We left our umbrellas back home in the park,
the sky turned to a mood without any dark.
They crumpled hard against the wooden floor,
their jeans were ruined from the gash they tore.
Blood dripped slow into one swollen eye,
but still they stood—refusing to die.
You trace the jagged shape it won't let go, [edge]
the quiet vow it felt but couldn't pledge. [pledge]
For a moment the picture looks complete, [whole]
but the thing that fits never feels like your soul. [soul]
I always squeeze the toothpaste from the bottom squeeze,
the coldest minty rush to make my mouth freeze.
A tiny white mountain forms on my toothbrush hill,
it tastes like medicine but feels like a thrill.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: She sobs into silence but hears the wrong tone,
Her grief's met with laughter from somewhere unknown.
The scene's cut abruptly—some error, now dead—
She drops hers in her hands, "Is this my own head?"
She stands by the river where the water runs blue,
the clouds above ripple like they're all too true.
Her shadow and sunlight begin to dance,
it feels like a moment she's meant to enhance.
I wait by the belt with my bag in the claim,
the tag has your number, but not your full name.
A worker pushes the broken, mismatched cart,
but hope beats steady in this uncertain heart.
My hair trails out like a slow motion flow,
I pedal in rhythm but no one can know.
The machine hums on, just me and this spin,
while time fades to static inside this white din.
He checks his map but has no real clue,
the subway signs look all the same to him, too.
He leans against the platform's dull wall,
and seriously considers calling it all.
You press your palm flat against the cold clear,
trying to calm it with just one more ear.
It taps on the pane with a little wing,
mistaking this world for a space to sing.
This place says "Made Here" — yeah, right, that's a lie,
I'll toss this junk before my patience will die.
I already paid for this stupid tourist-paid
plastic keychain, now my nerves are totally frayed.
They never heard the milk begin to cry,
just left it out too long and let it dry.
Now it's a lumpy, sour kind of waste,
curdling into something thick and paste.
The sky begins to weep like it wants to pour,
You laugh as puddles form by the front door.
Who needs an umbrella when you have no plan?
You spin in the rain, joy in your stride's span.
That party had confetti thrown like a blast,
Now every time I move, it falls out fast.
I check my reflection and see the bright hair,
I really should have paid more attention there.

topic: finding a dollar in old jeans
lines: You turn the jeans inside out looking to find,
some loose change or a bill left behind.
It's strange how a dollar can lift your whole cheer,
like it's money from the past coming back this year.
I heard the old kettle begin to scream,
steam poured out like an angry stream.
Water climbed up the kitchen wall,
I called for help, but no one was there at all.
Her morning's broken by the sudden tone,
you can see her pop out of her calm zone.
She marches straight to the machine to brew,
even if there's ten others in the queue.
It was your old bag, the one with a torn seam,
we'd packed for hikes and school sports team.
Now the strap has snapped, it's a clumsy kind of trap,
but you still smile—there's history in that snap.
He says it's the way my voice shifts in tone,
but I think there's something off in his own.
He tilts his head like it answers the why,
but I still can't meet his stare in the eye.
She swore the GPS had the perfect route,
but now it beeps and says she's completely out.
The screen keeps spinning, trying to re-spin,
while she mutters curses into her din.
She thinks she left it at the bus stop or card,
but now she's stuck between the tracks and the yard.
Her phone says "tap here," but the app won't train,
and she's late again, all because of this rain.
They call it breakfast, but it's more like crime time,
Black crumbs on their plate form a perfect grime.
They stare at their coffee and wish it would crawl,
While Monday just leans against the kitchen wall.
I noticed a shiny sticky spot,
someone left soda there they got.
It's like walking through a hidden glue,
but I'm dancing anyway—what can I do?

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: It won't smooth into a single fold,
it clings to your bones like it's trying to hold.
You untangle the knots, each a stubborn thread,
but the mess returns every time you spread.
I tried to fix it but just made a mess,
the remote's still silent without success.
They're in but flipped—no amount will flip
the tiny ridge I always fail to slip.
She counts the drops but can't keep them in her mind,
the rhythmic plink won't let the thoughts unwind.
Her fingers tap a nervous, shaky pace,
like time is crawling but she can't escape the race.
He taps the mic, then asks for just a time,
like we're a jury here to give him a dime.
He announces the fire alarm's just to say,
we need to practice one more drill today.
You stand there smiling at the growing pile,
I watch you work without complaint or while.
Your hands know every fold, every tear,
and every shirt from every year.
I watch them fall in a quiet, slow flow,
my thoughts drift silent, the world far below.
They tap soft rhythms against this cold mind,
and whisper life could still be kind.
The kitchen fills with smoke and a burnt smell,
this morning's ritual turns into hell.
I pat the dark crumbs, not the golden gold,
but maybe next time I'll remember to hold.
They stir the onions in a silent air,
the flame below gives off a golden flare.
They watch the edges curl inside the pot,
and think about the thing they haven't got.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: You pull the blanket tight to the fold,
your toes were numb but they're not cold.
I nudge your shoulder, a grin in my tease,
you flick my hand with your phone's lost keys.
He opened the can of pinto beans,
spilled chili powder on his phone screens.
As he tried to wipe the mess, he caused a spill,
then tripped on it—now we all watch him, grinning still.
You move your legs with practiced strut,
each step precise, cutting through the rut.
You tilt your head, strike a tiny pose,
as if you're modeling for the whole world's those.
He stood there frozen in the chaos scene,
hands hovering over his ringing screen.
The train had left without him, seconds past,
a notification goes off—just a blast.
You stand too quick and your whole world turns head,
like stars and static in a dizziness spread.
But then you steady your breath and plant your feet,
and do it again, this time without repeat.
Your dog curls up in the corner with joy,
slobbering love on your favorite old toy.
He claims this couch—his kingdom, his spot,
you almost forgot how easy it got.
She steps into the crosswalk like a race,
but traffic doesn't care about her place.
You think she's got the world all figured in mind,
till she freezes mid-stride, completely cross-blind.
I type "u up?" and hit send,
my thumbs ache from this old friend.
I wait for a reply to appear,
but silence is all that is clear.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: You hadn't touched it in so many years,
the dust lifted slowly as it appears.
Your fingers tremble as you turn the lock,
the smell hits you first—a scent of shock.
You watched the paint drip, making strange art,
it wasn't your plan but it was a fine start.
That blue on the tile felt familiar, so blue,
like summer days when the colors felt true.
They saw her walking with feathers that drift,
the wind tried to help but they never did lift.
Some were tangled now, stuck where they caught,
like memories tangled around what she thought.
The butter oozes down the toast in spread,
I tilt my plate to save my buttered head.
It moves too fast for any salvage slide,
I toss the mess and grab a fresh slice aside.
The drizzle starts, but I walk on too slow,
the clouds won't wait—they decide it should go.
My shoes were dry until I took that tread,
now puddles bloom where my footprints spread.
She left the glue stick out for way too long, time
now crusted and useless, but still in her prime.
Her messy desk screams, "Look at my bad art,"
yet she calls it a project and keeps it as part.
You step outside in your flannel and coat,
the fog curls around your bare ankles and float.
The road looks so close but it's smudged out and near,
you wave at the mailbox — it doesn't get clear.
She swore she had matched every single pair,
but now they're all tangled down the old stair.
Her hands shake as she begins the big test,
her panic rising fast, her heart tight in her chest.
I watch the single bright color drop
and splatter across the white linoleum crop.
This tiny mess feels huge, I confess—
I drop my keys and freeze on the spot, mess.
They loaded the dishwasher wrong again by plate,
It's like they're tempting the machine's cold fate.
You'd think they'd read the manual or just say,
"Hey, this is how you wash a cup, not a day."
You didn't panic when you left your hope,
just said it's fine, you'll somehow manage to cope.
You'll borrow pens from the kid beside the chair,
and turn this mishap into something quite fair.
I left the kettle on high once again today,
and now I've got steam all over my way.
The water is escaping through every spout,
I think I may scream if this mess drags on about.
The music swells and the sky begins to drop,
a figure runs through the field too fast to crop.
A beam cuts in—everything turns so light,
then silence hits just before the big fright.
There's a white blob on the edge of the spot,
I must have left it there, I totally forgot.
But maybe from this mess something good will grow—
a reminder that even mistakes can glow.

topic: seeing your mom's new profile pic
lines: She changed her profile pic to a cleaner dress,
maybe she's still here if we talk less stress.
Her bangs aren't frizzy, her roots aren't in hair,
could be a sign that she's learning more care.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: She caught a single gray hair in her spot,
ran her fingers through tresses, still quite hot.
She laughed out loud at the idea of age—
it's just another role, she's claimed her stage.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: You step on the crack like it's trying to be mean,
but your shoe won't win against this green machine.
That sprout's not asking how the sidewalk feels,
it's out here making moves through the concrete deals.
You still have that balloon dog full of pride,
it's held together by string and your guide.
It looks like a mess, but you call it a fail,
now it's leaning sideways and missing a tail.
I look at my clock and realize it's now,
I haven't begun and I don't know how.
It's way past midnight, I'm still too late,
but maybe I'll stay up and try to wait.
I check the pantry — there's no bag in sight,
my grocery hand is cramped and feels too tight.
One punctured hole could make me want to lose
my mind if I don't find a single bag to use.

topic: walking past each other in a crowd
lines: You feel the brush of a stranger so near,
their scent like summers from long ago, dear.
The moment is gone, but it still rings true,
a flash of warmth in a city full of you.
I match my breathing to the needles' soft pace,
they dance through the yarn in a quiet space.
It sounds like a lullaby they hum as a song,
I'd sit here forever if this moment were long.
Your favorite umbrella took a bad split,
when the wind knocked it sideways and hit.
But you're laughing through puddles and rain,
knowing joy still wants to remain.
A cloud of flour rose like morning dust,
Her hands moved steady, though the plan was trust.
The counter was messy, but she kept it yet,
afraid to clean away the proof that she'd let.
You wash it gently but leave one small spot,
a chip from last winter when mugs took a lot.
You still like the way it feels in your hold,
some memories taste better once things are old.
You step onto the bathroom floor's wet tile,
your balance shaky in your clumsy style.
A patch of soap appears beneath your spin,
you barely catch yourself before you skin.
She watches the yolk fall from the shell's tight drop,
the silence of breakfast now just hit a stop.
She thinks of how fragile things used to bloom,
before time turned the kitchen into a tomb.
You tap through the shots from the perfect view,
the ocean in every frame still feels so new.
There's grain in your phone from that last day's sand,
and you swear you can smell that salty land.
She stands by the water so still and above,
her gaze caught between the ripples and love.
The clouds drift like thoughts she won't let move,
and the river just mirrors what heaven won't prove.
Your morning peace gets cut by his loud dawn,
he treats the neighborhood like a noisy pawn.
You type a complaint, hit send—quick blame,
but it just bounces back with your own name.
The alarm clock rings like a curse from the bell,
and I curse it back, this cruel morning hell.
I stare at the ceiling, not ready for floor,
so I hit snooze once—then silently ignore.
You need some time for the room to feel clear,
and silence your mind from every loud ear.
You'll come back when the distance begins to grow,
ready to talk and let understanding show.
She's been staring at the ceiling telling tales,
her eyes get heavy but her focus fails.
Patterns in the plaster twist and swirl,
she says, "This could be art," then yawns, bored girl.
The morning sun finds the cobwebs and dust,
it rolls through the silence like a soft gust.
A golden streak of pure winter light
is all it takes for me to turn things might.
I'd rather stay inside and avoid the gray,
the forecast calls for thunder all day.
A storm moves in, but I switch on the light,
this quiet morning could be so bright.

topic: socks left in the break room
lines: No one knows which employee left this clue,
They're still on rotation, but their shoes are due.
The janitor found them, asked the staff,
No one spoke, but everyone gave a laugh.
She trusts the map when it picks a new path,
even if basic geometry breaks the math.
I ask how we got lost — she's full of no clue,
the app said turn left, so she turned left and flew.
Your keyboard shows the years it has to bear,
the Q and W faded into air.
You tap where letters once were—now just ghost,
you wonder who will be the next to boast.
She claims her shoes are good because they're flat,
but can't she hear her heels thudding like a bat?
We warned her not to run in them to meet
the bus. Now both her knees ache—and her feet.

topic: tea leaves steeping in a cup
lines: She watches her tea leaves get properly brew,
muttering spells like a witch's secret too.
They spin in a circle, a lazy swirl,
and she imagines they're fortune-tellin' girl.
That pink smudge on your cup isn't just a kiss,
it's a full statement you can't ever miss.
A lipstick stain clings to your usual stain,
you swore this would stop—but here it is again.
I didn't look for any perfect pair,
just stepped on the ones by the door's stair.
They're frayed and old—no need to mend,
they've been good company, my odd friend.
He swings the shovel at the stubborn ice,
the blade just slides off like it's made of nice.
He shakes out his gloves and rubs his sore head,
the snow won't budge, it won't be tamed or spread.
You breathe it in—salty, wild, and air,
the wind braids your hair with the sea's own flair.
The tide keeps its rhythm, never runs out of tide,
while you take the salt and keep it deep inside.
My GPS just told me to make a sharp lead,
now I'm stuck in a field with a dead car ahead.

maybe tech knows best, but my patience isn't true.
A slant of sunlight slips through the beam,
I lie here pretending this moment will dream.
I follow the shadows, I try to trace
how the light fills each gap in this golden space.
I tap the icon hoping it will start,
but dread seeps in and begins to tear my heart.
A crash report pops up with just a log,
I'm trapped now in confusion like thick fog.

lines: I keep checking the group chat for your calls,
but my screen just shows red and "all hell's balls."

then hand in our name like it was a bad gift.

of knowing your old jokes never came.

half-wishing I could erase this awkward form.
She holds out her wish for the breeze and the sky,
the clock ticks too loud but it drifts on and by.
She laughs as they lift and they dance and they spin,
the world gets so light in between what's been.
The fog moves in like a quiet, cold ghost,
it clings to the fence and the weathered post.

turning the hills into something quite pale.
You count the change like it's your last dime,
the cashier sighs at the slowest time.

and maybe part of your lunch and your soul.
I looked at my list—just one task crossed ahead,
while three dozen loom like bad old bad bread.
I'm proud but I'm sad, feeling stuck and alone,
like I moved one small stone off a mountain of stone.
You tap your phone as the comments scroll feed,
their drama dripping like something to bleed.
A laugh echoes—cut to her empty room,
you pause, unsure if this stream's your new doom.

but now concerts just feel like bad stands.

The crowd's loud joy means nothing to your cheers.
I trace the slow growth of a fuzzy old mold,
The cracks in the plaster look wiser and bold.
I watch dust float up where the ceiling meets beam,
And map out new stories that lift me from dream.
They speed through the credits in a mad, dull pace,
it's all so rushed it robs you of the grace.
I pause and zoom in just to try to find
every name that my brain insists I'm blind.

topic: a taxi driver yelling on phone
lines: The taxi driver yells at the phone in his mood,
threatening to quit over bad takeaway food.
He shifts into gear with a grin in his ear,
shouting, "That's it—I'm taking this job right here!"
I've searched every inch, but the key isn't found.
I retraced my steps, checked the fridge, looked all around.
I paused and sighed, maybe fate wants me to stop.
The neighbor's dog just brought it back in its crop.
These shoes claim they're built for all-day fit,
But every step feels like a stone I hit.
I thought "comfort" meant more than my grand plan,
This walk could not have stretched out this long-span.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: You hit play and the laugh track cues the scene,
a sitcom moment feels too much like your routine.
The humor falls flat while you try to hum,
your laughter echoes, but it doesn't numb.
She tries to pay with a wave and a tap,
the screen says "no chip in your cap."
She enters her PIN, the machine asks for code,
she laughs—then walks off as the gas pumped showed.
We don't say a word or break our vow,
the air feels warm without us knowing how.
I memorize every small trace,
your face against mine, almost like grace.
You set the timer for the soup and the clock,
the bread is still warm from the oven's back block.
The room fills up with the roast's rich scent,
and you smile—no shortcuts were spent.
You hand over a ten for a sandwich and crumb,
the cashier checks the screen with a thumb.
"Your change is complicated," she shrugs at your lunch,
you nod and escape with a coffee and bunch.
Your shoe went flying on the winding trail,
your face turned briefly—then you went all pale.
You slowed down, bent low for the loose loop,
now everyone's watching where you used to troop.
She lingers by the trash can, holding the core,
like it's a secret she should keep locked in the door.
Each step crunches with the last day's cold, hard bite,
her jaw still clenched from chewing something too tight.
I twist the wire to create a new arc,
it flickers once, then leaves the dark mark.
Its light now bends in a strange new shape,
I won't try to fix—let its beauty escape.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: The kid lets out a wail that echoes through the mall,
I check my phone—no signal, there's no call.
I wave a snack at them, like some strange bread,
they scream louder still, I'm officially dead.
I left my cake in the fridge all day,
we had a fire but forgot to say.
I didn't get texts or calls to send,
just silence from every old friend.
You left the bread out till it turned to gold,
A hardened reminder of yesterday's mold.
You take a photo—your frugal pride,
That old loaf means more than it looks inside.
It's not the dark—it's something else that brings fear,
this feeling I get only once every year.
My pulse is loud, like a siren or gun,
but there's no one here to run to or run.
The final shot fades to black and stays frame,
A flicker of hope feels like a wild flame.
The credits roll, but the story still weighs fate,
Your heart holds the build-up's familiar weight.
You pivot with care, keep the box on your hip,
one false move and the gift will slip.
The ribbon stays tight, still tied in a bow,
but you're not dancing—you're just trying not to go.
They asked how long you wanted on each side,
You said "just enough so it won't collide."
Now the color's starting to fade away,
but your laugh still makes this look okay.
The shovel bites deep into winter's hard edge,
I give my old back a new labor pledge.
Each motion is slow, a defiant scrape,
the snow and the ice yield to grit and new shape.
She weaves through traffic like she left a trail,
some call it luck, but I know they'll all fail.
Her hands don't shake, her stare is so cool,
she cuts me off just for the rush and the fuel.
The screen went black while the credits were on,
a frozen last frame where the story was gone.
She lets out a quiet, defeated sigh,
but no prompt comes back when she tries to reply.
You used to hold your phone in your hand,
now you curse as it freezes mid-command.
There's something sweet about a world without lack,
except when your phone can't keep its place on the track.

topic: socks left in the laundry pile
lines: She swears that she found the missing sock's match,
but the dryer may have just stolen its snatch.
There's no clue where the other one flew—
maybe the cat has it, and it's hiding from you.
You see a stranger standing in the rain,
their coat soaked through, but they choose to remain.
They offer you half of their umbrella share,
as if this were normal and not strange or rare.
My fingers set a rhythm on the beat,
the pattern clicks with perfect repeat.
This isn't noise—it's something more than art,
I feel a crowd would beg me just to start.
It's not just a little chill—it's borderline cold,
This heater's been coughing since the Ice Age got bold.
I turn the dial gently, I really just tweak,
And it roars like a dragon, it doesn't just speak.
You tapped the screen, lost in the past,
the date was faded but not the blast.
That version of you still has a smile,
and now you believe it for a while.

topic: a taxi driver yelling on phone
lines: You shout into your phone about some lost ride,
I cringe as you curse where you wish they would hide.
You blame it all on the app or the fare,
but your grip tightens like your last hope's in air.
You check the mailbox for something fun to mail,
but find only letters waiting in the trail.
They shout about dates they say are coming due,
yet somehow you still can't believe it's true.
We dance around the same old fight to chill,
I swear this place could freeze a goose to kill.
You say I'm out of line, take it as blame,
but I just want this thermostat to flame.
I hit my horn, then I slam on the brake,
the driver never even saw the mistake.
I laugh out loud—this is not a cheer,
but the road's too full to let me be clear.
Their shouting all started about who used the bin,
A loud and unending backyard din.
I sipped my cold coffee and let the old man rise,
He'd yell until calm, but never feel wise.
You're driving so fast you forgot the pace,
your passenger screams and contorts their face.
"Don't touch the wheel!" you shout as they try to steer,
then spill your cold drink on my brand-new beer.
The office clock just hit 4:57 bell,
the printer's screaming like it's in hell.
I rip out the paper jam in your mail,
leaving a mess in my hectic little trail.
You bend a paperclip into a flimsy hook,
it trembles when you cast your hopeful look.
The bobber bobs slightly, but the fish all drift,
you yank too hard, and lose what little you lift.
I missed my stop because I lost the train,
not the first time I've been late again.
My ticket's gone, I can't find my card,
so I tipped the train guard just to get off the yard.
She re-traces her steps down every known trail,
her face turning pale as the minutes mount pale.
She replays the morning, checking it again,
she thinks she left them somewhere near the train.
I step out of the shower, my bare toes meet,
the floor insists it knows nothing about heat.
My socks are wet, so I tiptoe on tile,
this morning's routine feels like punishment trial.
I almost forget my card when I see
the total flash bright on the screen with a fee.
The groceries feel heavy, my savings feel low,
but I smile anyway, let the groceries go.
I watch the sky turn warm with orange glow,
while shadows stretch across the ground below.
The trees are playing hide-and-seek, they cast
quick glances at the sun before its last.
The fog moves in like time itself goes slow,
it blurs the hedges in a ghostly glow.
I remember walking these fields in old days,
chasing lost thoughts down the same old ways.
Those papers have grown into quite a stack,
a financial avalanche waiting to attack.
You miss a late fee, you owe them a dime,
and now you're trapped paying interest all the time.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: She pats the spot where the cat lies in fur,
but the animal won't so much as stir.

she's sure it's not sleeping, it's something more ill.
She stares at her latte and not his face,
the booth feels smaller than this whole disgrace.

but now it's too late to call it a mistake.
You tiptoe around that electrical hump,
the lamp still slumps with a lopsided slump.

but gravity laughs as it slowly goes.
They split the headphones and blast the tunes,

A breeze kicks up as they match their side,
Of steps, laughing loose like the tide.
You found the old gum, still sticky with truth,
left there from some fleeting moment of youth.
It's just a small thing, but it makes a trace,
like proof of a life that once filled this space.
You bought them because they have no heel,
but now your bad feet still don't feel real.

and wondered how "sensible" helps you stand.
I woke up missing my favorite pair,
now every room smells like wet dog hair.
I found one sock near the laundry hole,
the other's likely lost deep in his soul.
She turns up the music and claims the floor,
she bought the beat just to teach the store.

the neighbors bang on the wall from the din.

but your dog's already in full alarm prime.

his fur on end like lightning struck a stump.

the sun whispers praise as you grow your shout.

through photos, but now I just reel
my fingers on glass—double-tap,

now every shadow feels like it just might rust.

but part of you wants it to stay that way for all.
His favorite band once blew both his ears,
but time and tinnitus took those loud years.
Now he yells "Turn it down!" at the band,
and waves his phone in their angry hand.
I picked the wrong day to forget how to wear
my socks up either stair of the pair.
The proctor just stared as I took the [test],
I passed but it nearly tore out my chest.
The tulips rise in a burst of bright red,
their color too loud for your quiet head.
You kneel and you touch where they grew from the soil,
like blood in the earth, this springtime's dark oil.
You kick off the ground and touch the sky,
the air hums beneath your outstretched high.
For a moment, you forget how to feel
the rules of the world—just a breeze, a real.
I used to drink water, said it was better, clear,
but now I chase the fizz in my lemonade beer.
It's not for lack of will—there's no good reason,
just that this summer tastes like this golden season.
You blame it all on the weather's cruel heat,
not the fact that you slept in a sauna-sheet.
You toss, you turn, you take one long puff,
and vow that this sleepless night is enough.
My parrot repeats every voice on the call,
squawking the ring like a squeaky red ball.
He picks up the rhythm, the pitch, the full tone,
and now my old kitchen clock sounds like a phone.
This place is full of junk and bald-faced lie,
I almost bought a keychain that will surely die.
Everything's mass-produced and stamped as "fake,"
my wallet feels the sting—oh, what a ache.
We dug through the couch until we reached a hole,
where shadows and dreams came out to stroll.
No grown-ups allowed, no time, no rule,
this blanket was better than any school.
The birthday song plays, you laugh and sing along,
your voice rings out, holding the tune so strong.
You blow hard, the candles' flame dies in a rush,
your grin stays bright — it's the same joy, success, and flush.
I watch the socks go wild in their spin,
they tumble so loud like a happy little sin.
One sock finds a home but the other lacks pair,
they flap in the air like soft wings without care.
You tried to look natural but didn't quite blend,
cheeks puffed like you're greeting an old best friend.
Everyone else struck their classic "just say pose,"
while you leaned in like the bouquet was a rose.

lines: They steal half the blanket without a claim,
curling up like it's in the frame.

so I pretend this was never a gift.

The fog lies thick where your tires would lay,

the road becomes something the mind can't twist.
She hasn't cleaned the office window in a week,
just stares through smudges to give things a tweak.

like this is the worst crime she's ever seen.

we snorted our drinks and began to choke.

we're laughing so hard we can barely sing.
That's not a sink—it's a food-related crime,

The lyrics get thick and I start to choke,
the melody burns like old cigarette smoke.
Tears fall in rhythm, one silent drip,

She checked the carton again for the date,
but the scribbled numbers were smudged on the plate.

so the milk sat cold near the open fridge door.
I'm stuck on this clue that's been giving me grief,
it's due tomorrow and I can't get relief.

I slam my pencil down in frustration and stares.

topic: checking if you have enough for gas
lines: You check the gauge when there's nothing but mile,
the app says "OK" but your face loses smile.

but the light stays yellow—you might not make pass.
My nose gives the game away, there's no clue,

I'm not trying to win some big race,
I just love the world and my favorite place.
The keys are a sticky, chaotic mess,
but they call it their cleverest success.

and pretend it's their style—not a laziness sin.
You've traced the cracks where the ceiling grew mold,
Your fingers imagine the love you could hold.
The patterns catch your tired, unblinking eyes,
and time turns gentle, and life feels more wise.
You grip the handlebars but still they shake,
the tires skid across the pebbled lake.
One more turn and you'll surely fall off,
your heart tries to escape through a panic cough.
She watches the fish go around the same bowl,
their rhythm reflects something deeper in her soul.

she says they know where they belong in this strange place.
I watched the clouds drift through airplane skies,
while a baby cried with nowhere to hide her eyes.

me back to my first flight—smaller, but no less break.
He wipes his shoes but still tramples the pride,
convinced the germs are all locked far inside.

though he pretends he can't even smell it or tell.
The first bite of breakfast brings back the smell,
of blackened carbs and the kitchen from hell.
You sip coffee and call out the day,
while time feels like sugar left out in decay.
That rabbit found a quiet corner, that's the hole,
it burrows through the office and steals my stole.
It makes a nest inside my shipping box,
and chews all four of my gym socks.
She tugs so hard the leash turns into a lead,

Sidewalks are ignored—she just wants to run,
But the owner thinks this is no kind of fun.
I can't stop myself from rubbing my stare,
dry air settling deep inside my glare.
The light glows brighter with each time it burns,
but turning off the screen feels like a world of yearns.
He clocks every mile but talks like he flies,
a crooked smile softening his lies.
His stories will fade once the fare is paid,
another stranger left behind the parade.
You stayed dry beneath the broken rain,
while others huddled or tried to remain.
A puddle formed, and the water kept drip,
but you stood tall and refused to trip.
My steps keep going but the pace won't show,
the screen's stuck on "0.0" like a ghost from long ago.
I wonder if this machine was built to fail,
or if I'm just left running down memory's trail.
My sock is gone—again he found the chew,
I tried to hide them but he always knew.
I need a new plan, some cleverer stash,
than leaving mine out for a chewy rash.
She taps her foot and mutters things about me,
"Why isn't there a faster lane? This is not free!"
She waves her loyalty card just to try,
If this line doesn't end soon, she might just die.
I left my list at home, my head in the wind,
now wandering aisles with nothing but my mind.
I try to recall each item I should grab,
but memory's a mess, a science gone crab.
You watch the insect hover, pause, and leap,
swinging through the daisies on a flimsy heap.
It lands again, still light upon its wing,
while you hold your breath and try not to sing.
She pulls up slow, then pays for her gas,
checking if the bank account still has pass.
A receipt drops out—it triggers a smile,
while the future whispers, "Hold on a while."
I found a wild rabbit inside an old crate,
it hasn't moved since my last shift's end date.
It's twitching in silence, no sign of a hair,
yet somehow it's clearly still sitting right there.

topic: a taxi driver yelling on phone
lines: He yells in traffic, waving his hands in a row,

we both hum the song—two voices, one cheer.

it creaks the same song if you dare to repeat.

but time has unmade every promise you trust.

my mind drifts somewhere far away.

the future feels within my grasp, caught.

each hero clashing on the bedroom floor.

but time's the villain no script can out-cause.

the point when you wave that cheap ruler at this.

topic: a group project where nobody helps
lines: You post another reminder, same old call,
while everyone's off chasing their own ball.

the only noise is the happy little din.

just runs in tight circles right back to me.

the whole class smells like burnt stale bread.
The sharpener spits out a paper cone,
and the teacher gives her a judging tone.

topic: restaurant with no menu in English
lines: She smiles when we ask, so we're left to guess,
the waiter shrugs but serves it to us.
We point at whatever lands on our plate,
and call it the flavor of our fate.

topic: a book left open on the nightstand
lines: The pages still hold the warm lamp's glow,
you stopped reading where the tension would grow.
Your mind was somewhere the silence couldn't find,
your thoughts were locked tight, what was left behind?
The sun slips low, casting a soft new hue,
they sat here sipping juice with just you.

my voice stuck in my throat, too nervous to float.

your favorite was drawn in a clumsy, soft blue.

now messages flood from the sunny coast.

we dropped plans we swore we'd never undo.

we raced out to get drenched instead of inside.

this feels like a project, not just a quick job.

it zips past the teacher who's standing at door.

now your flight path's on the whole class's dash.

Your plans fall apart like a chaotic wreck.

Pretend you're still in control of this place.
She lunges across the couch with full claim,
calling it hers since before your shift came.
You fake a yawn and suggest we just split,
but she's got the chip and you're stuck with the pit.
They're still typing at 2 a.m., so late,
every thought feels too heavy for weight.
Their fingers dance loud across the keys,
perfecting words they'll never read with ease.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: You lie there as if life is some grand pose,
one paw up, your belly, your crooked toes.

snore through the thunder—I'm left wondering why.
I watch the morning turn everything gold,
the way the light falls is a story yet told.

a VHS player wheezing like an old machine.

my friends laugh when I forget their names fails.

the clock ticks loud but it won't chime.

like time or love, small, invisible, waste.

when a frog hopped in—what rotten luck.

it startled me out of my morning shock.

while others sleep in, I have a screaming view.

Like a message in a bottle left to fish.
I tried to re-seal the bag but it wouldn't seal,
the snack I bought was supposed to be my last meal.
Now the cheese is unwrapped and I'm staring at foil,
this wrapper's worse than a stubborn extension coil.
The butter slides slow, just enough to be spread,
softening like secrets a spoon can't yet thread.
Morning leaks in with the kind of light
that makes her face look like the future feels bright.
I hung my towel on the locker room wall,
now everyone thinks it's a stress ball.

I should've aired it out before I lent.
You pretend you're just doodling and draw,
but your note says "Let's break all the law."

then grin when the teacher asks you to replace.

no beep, no total—just silence and guitar.

while they all watched me shine down this new path.
She still has the tag from her last long flight,
crumpled clothes and a laugh still a bit tight.
They scan her passport again by the zone,
asking where's her suitcase, but not in a harsh tone.
Her hand hovers near her mouth, so still,
she walks alone up that quiet hill.
A shadow appears from behind the dread,
and silence tightens across her face like a spread.
My eyes are tired but I haven't hit my cap,
the screen's too bright, I fall right into the trap.
The clock says midnight, but I'm way too late,
my bed still calls me—yet I stay in this state.
I opened the fridge and gave a quiet grin,
some peas had escaped from the veggie bin.
They rolled like little balls of frozen snow,
I couldn't leave them—this was too good a show.
My umbrella collapsed into a sad frame,
no longer a shield but a source of shame.
Now every step ends with a steady drip,
and I'm wobbling home like a clumsy trip.
She swears she's not emotional, just the tune,
but sobs already rattle her voice by noon.
Her mascara's smudged where the tears have gone by,
she says I'm overreacting—just why?
She paid for the room with a premium view,
but the food's all beige, same shade and hue.
Her teeth still ache from that overly sweet cake,
and now she swears the whole meal was a mistake.
I balance the headset on a single wire,
letting one side dangle, half-melted, on fire.
This is my signature look, my chosen way,
not broken—I'm just making it a display.

topic: reading under the covers with a flashlight
lines: I flick on my flashlight with quiet delight,
the dark cannot touch me this late at night.
It's bedtime, I know, but I break every rule,
this secret escape is more fun than school.

topic: laughing too hard at a joke
lines: She laughs so loud like she's running away,
her eyes still hold pain from some other today.
She won't let it show, won't let it hide,
the humor is sharp, but the joy is inside.
One side still caught in its cord's tight loop,
you march through life like a sad headphone troop.
It sags like a flag without a cause to sag,
your shirt now holds its lonely little tag.
The sky flipped from blue to bruised and black,
Wind howled through trees, ripped leaves through the track.
I watch the storm with hope for bloom,
My garden's waiting, soaked by gloom.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: You ignored the notice, it was well overdue,
Old websites vanished into a ghostly blue.
You miss the streaming shows you used to chase,
They're gone like that voice from your favorite place.
The dog stands still but it won't stop barking,
it's clear this spot means more than just a marking.
Its eyes are locked on something down the lead,
and you wonder what it needs so deeply, indeed.
You told me twice already, not the same,
but your name keeps slipping out the frame.
There's a ring to it, something like a bell,
but I'll call you "hell" again if I can't tell.
A single drop falls where a stream should drop,
the showerhead's turned into a faulty crop.
They twist the knob, but the spray won't aim,
they scream into the trickle, dry as flame.
She says it's no big deal but wants a clue,
her outfit matches mine down to the hue.
I check my phone for some kind of link,
afraid she knows I didn't even think.
She watches the ants march slowly along the path,
muttering something about their tiny math.
A shoe comes down, and she says "Not now,"
but swears she won't step on them—not even by vow.
She walks through the air where the branches were bare,
pretending this weather's no personal affair.
The leaves fall on ground with a muted sound,
like secrets discarded, but nothing is found.
You swear you'll put down your phone and go away,
but it pings and you scroll with the same old obey.
You send another dumb meme out into the post,
and wonder why morning finds you feeling the most.
You turn the heat down for your sleepless room,
but I stay awake in this quiet gloom.
Your shivering is enough to strip me bare,
I'll adjust the air—I know you care.
You lie in bed till your phone gives a morning,
the coffee's gone cold—no sign of a warning.
The old shows run in a lazy loop,
while you pretend that you're still part of the troop.
She checks her phone again for the class map,
but the building is huge and a confusing trap.
She rushes up the stairs and finds no empty seat,
her panic rising fast in the classroom's tight heat.
I showed up late but I came with something to bring,
they raised an eyebrow, then laughed at the strange thing.
We took a big break when we craved a good bite,
the room filled with crumbs and with soft afternoon light.

topic: missing a chorus in a song
lines: The music skips ahead but you haven't played,
you pause it, rewind—just in case you stayed.
You hum the missing part, feel it in your start,
the silence fills your chest, a chord for your heart.

topic: car keys on the kitchen table
lines: He always leaves his keys on the same old spot,
or claims he's sure he left them somewhere forgot.
They don't belong—they just sit there to sit,
like he can't be bothered if they don't fit.
Your bare feet hit the floor like sad feet,
Each morning, same routine, just repeat.
The tiles are colder than a winter stone,
But you still pause there, in your quiet tone.
You watch the line creep forward, slow and sight,
a clock ticks louder than your planned flight.
Around you, sighs and credit-card machine groan,
you feel the weight of being stuck and alone.
Your battery bleeds a pixel-perfect save,
it glows like a dying headlamp in a cave.
You hunt for a cable, not a single plug,
you even unplug the toaster near your rug.
She stands by her locker but forgot where's the key,
she pats down her bag, asking no one but me.
Her face says the answer is close but not near,
The bell will ring soon and she won't have a cheer.
You said we'd meet but never showed up on time,
now my latte's cold and wasting my dime.
You'll take the bill as your "apology take,"
while I count the hours this date didn't make.
The bulb has blinked out twice and that's again,
I grab a screwdriver to fix the chain.
I buy a new LED with perfect size,
it just makes the flickers worse—what a surprise.
I tap my wheel — the light won't help me move,
pedestrians laugh and wave, trying to prove
I'm trapped in gridlock, not a single car
in sight but one at the next stoplight's bar.
I can't seem to shake this stubborn awake,
my body still waits for a forced break.
The screen glows with numbers bold and red,
but my mind won't move from where it's dead.
My dog goes walks through the mud every day,
and I end up talking to neighbors and say—
Those paw prints sit there on the living room rug,
I should clean it, but who has time to bug?
She pats the U-lock, now stiff and old-cold,
where rust has turned her blue plans into bold.
She gives it one last yank, a desperate shake,
then laughs at how she forgot it was a mistake.

topic: a long queue at the coffee shop
lines: I've been standing here forever, just wait,
they promised the service would be fast as bait.
I inch forward, still no movement at the bar,
my caffeine craving starts to burn like a star.
She hates how daffodils insist on show,
bursting up where she said they should not grow.
Her boots are caked with mud and tears and yell,
while spring keeps coming, ignoring her swell.
She watches the clouds as they float like a sail,
their shapes shift and wisp through a summer sky pale.
The sun breaks through holes, casting gold on her gleam,
she whispers a wish into wind of her dream.
You clicked "Save" but it vanished down the send,
your fingers freeze mid-thought—no way to mend.
You left the tab open, hoping it might stay,
but minutes blurred on your blank display.
You've been standing forever, still no empty seat,
the air's so thick you could fry an egg on the heat.
Everyone's late, but no one wants to take the blame,
it's a commuter survival game.
The popcorn hits the floor as the credits roll,
They pause just long enough to check their scroll.
"This was worth the time," they say with a treat,
Then queue it up again to watch once more, complete.
A crack split the fabric, then formed into hole,
but she carried it still as if giving her soul.
She walked home through puddles, soaked all the way down,
and mended the breaks when she got back downtown.
My boss says "yawning isn't your class,
you're paid to do work, not stare at the grass."
I yawn again just to mess with my task,
he sighs and says, "Can I help you re-ask?"
The oven hisses with hot, empty steam,
a frozen dream you forgot to redeem.
Cheese stretches slow, it won't really melt,
and you hum an old tune you used to belt.
She keeps the stack like a museum of mail,
a whole life left on the sending-line trail.
"Maybe someday," she tells the waste,
as if love letters were vintage or taste.
You watch the leaves come down from the gray sky,
They spiral gently, no fight to stay or die.
Each one lets go, no need for them to fall,
Just nature's way of saying goodbye to it all.

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: I snap the world into a perfect frame,
the faces missing, everything the same.
I post it online but still feel alone,
a silent reply from the cold, gray stone.
You feel the cold wind as a bold breeze,
not shivering but instead with ease.
You leave no sign of how the chill might mark,
it only fuels the fire you want to spark.
I've been waiting here for far too long to stay,
cars inch forward but they won't go away.
When is this thing going to turn green?
It looks like it's broken — maybe the screen?
They stack up like snowfall—another small debt,
You swore you'd pay this one but now you forget.
The dates blur together, the notices due,
Each one arrives late, and you know you'll have to rue.
I smooth it out but it won't quite glide,
I pose in mirrors to try to hide.
The color fades on my collarbone's edge,
I laugh and say this is my new pledge.
They watched the clouds shift and take new form,
pretending each shape was something from a storm.
They pointed out creatures they claimed to see,
like the sky was a puzzle only they could key.
I step outside and twist it open for me,
the rain bends down like it wants to be free.
My伞 starts to spin with a rhythm so clean,
the drops hit my skin like applause for a queen.
The app says there's a service charge on the fee,
I squint at my phone but I still don't see.
The meter ticks up, my payment's already due—
My face turns a shade only emojis can hue.

topic: seeing your mom's new profile pic
lines: She posted a shot of her shoulder-length hair,
a style he swore she'd retired right there.
That shade isn't even her natural brown—
it screams "I'm moving out, let it all come down."
You love how it breaks through the quietest sound,
a small chime that dances all around.
A flicker appears in your phone's little light,
and you smile because joy finds you in spite.
You tried to hit new weights with one last press,
your breath a ragged, hasty kind of mess.
The barbell dropped — another quiet fail,
but pride stays in the iron's crooked trail.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: I trace the faded roads with my finger's ink,
each town still holds a secret or a link.
I dream of roads heading toward the north,
I pack my bag and I set off forth.
The frost looks like glitter, a winter-time spark,
I laugh at the grass, pretending it's a lark.
I step outside hoping that it will melt,
but my shoes are now stuck in an icy belt.
The clock ticks louder every single time,
it's dinner hour but I'm not yet in prime.
I pace the kitchen, afraid they'll have to wait,
and burn the rice I meant to set on the plate.
My cat sits still with that same distant gaze,
eyes lost in the morning sunlit haze.
She watches the branches sway toward that old tree,
like maybe they're calling her back to be.
Your stomach growls loud in the checkout ache,
You pause by the chips near the peanut lake.
The cashier smiles slow, her voice stays soft,
You lift a banana, your hunger aloft.
I hear the old swing creak just the same as it still,
but no one's there to push me up or down the hill.
The wind rustles leaves where my hands used to be,
I wish I could soar like I was meant to be free.
I fished around my pocket for loose change,
the machine blinked "invalid" in a strange range.
My coin purse stayed at home on a clip,
so I walked right past and made a fresh trip.

topic: sending a text to the wrong person
lines: You sent the message to the wrong address,
A typo blurred what you tried to express.
You delete the thread but it won't feel true,
and now your silence feels meant for you.
I tried to stack them but my hands lost the place,
they slid off the table in a paper race.
I paused to check what I had actually read,
then sighed and let them pile up at my head.
Your body hums for a post-lunch crash,
you press against the couch like mashed potatoes bash.
The quiet room won't help you stay awake—
your eyes have a tiny rest they beg to take.
You turn down an alley where no one would back,
the sign reads "Daily Sandwich" and "Hot Pretzel Snack."
A barista leans out and smiles as she pour,
"Welcome," she says, "we open for you at this door."
You stuck a note there to remind you how bright
your screen should be, then left the light on all night.
Now it glows with a message you can't seem to read,
but at least it won't let your eyes start to bleed.
Your new partner's smile pops on my newsfeed post,
I'm not sure if I'm glad or a little ghost.
Maybe you've finally found some calm and ease,
and your hands don't need mine to unlock the keys.

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: I found an old rubber band still stuck in the snap,
coiled tight like it had somewhere to map.
The stapler's dry, but I can't deny the glue
it forms with me—it's charmingly true.
I thought I'd give this plant another try,
but my so-called green thumb's still too dry.
I keep forgetting it can't live on blame,
its droop is less a sign, more like my name.
You can't stop thinking about that red stain,
your mind rewinds the whole scene in your brain.
Was it a slip, or did they just take a sip?
Now every glance feels like an awkward trip.
They swipe through the photos, every one
of them grinning like they had just run.
A sunset, a dive, a perfect seaside view,
then a blurry shot of feet in blue.
Your fingers are trembling, you say it's not cold,
but your pulse is too loud, and your voice sounds too bold.
You check if the time on the screen matches your clock,
then swear it's your heartbeat you hear at the knock.
You stand alone where the waves are still,
waiting for something the tides won't fulfill.
The sand holds echoes of footsteps that cry,
and the pale morning sky feels too close to lie.
They sleep with the window wide open for heat,
the AC fights them, drenching each sheet.
By dawn the whole room smells like old mold,
and they're still hot, but stuck in a cold.
You read my tweet mid-lunch, just a short post,
about how I missed you and thought of you most.
You pause your sandwich, let the moment feel,
and wish I were sitting here, close and real.
You look at the list and pretend you're all done,
but the only thing checked is your walk in the sun.
You wonder where the time has gone and where,
it's lost in the stillness of tasks left in air.
You see the brake lights begin to blur with the car,
your eyes still scroll down for just one more star.
The road is quiet but chaos lies ahead,
you hold your breath, anticipating dread.
You try to rewind the old cassette tape,
but your finger keeps getting stuck on the escape.
It whirs and it clicks, the song starts to skip,
you swear it's designed to make you all trip.
They show a tear slowly falling from her drop,
the hero's shadow looms large in the crop.
The music swells, you can't ignore the score,
and suddenly someone slams into the door.
My keyboard's a mess, the keys are all jam,
I type "I love ham" when I meant to say "ram."
I tried cleaning out every single key,
but the crumbs just won't leave, they're debris.
I watched the frog do its sudden leap,
landing so splashy and wet and deep.
It hopped from the edge of the mossy bank,
where I was sitting, relaxed, on my plank.
There's a full bench but she takes the whole seat,
like claiming this space is her daily feat.
No hint of apology, no social cue,
just relax, the world's better when shared with you.
You stand beneath the broken showerhead beam,
pretending it's a luxury spa dream.
But the water just keeps falling in a drip,
and you lose your patience—now you've lost your grip.
I cranked up the heat but it's all in my seat,
the fan on full blast won't let me retreat.
I yank the window down but it won't budge or slide,
I'll stew in this mess if I don't somehow bide.
You pass the bowl of warm garlic and plate,
the dinner's been waiting forever too late.
I can't help but watch the cheese fall like dust,
it lands on the noodles just right on the crust.
She searches her brain for the name again,
the silence between them feels like a pain.
He stumbles, his voice catches like a ring,
"Maria," he says—it's close to a sing.
I keep my phone close while scrolling the chat,
we talk through the hours until one o'clock at.
I tap out a message and hit send,
it reads "goodnight" but it feels like the end.
I watched the starlight fall across the midnight sky,
too bright to miss but far beyond my high.
The dark hills held a quiet, heavy kind of pain,
and I wanted to stay but knew I'd try again.
You step right into that shiny new trap,
it clings to your sock with a sugary slap.
You laugh, not minding the mess or the clue,
it's just one more reason to clean up with glue.
You watched them stir with a steady flame,
you mimicked their moves but it never felt the same.
Now you take a bite and you test the taste,
the meal's not perfect—but you won't call it a waste.
She chops the carrots steady on the deck,
her mind trying not to be a wreck.
The knife finds rhythm, the peels begin to flow,
and hope starts rising like the steam's soft glow.
You count the coins with your free hand,
while trying to look like you don't need a brand.
There's a quarter, a dime, and maybe a dime—
why does math suddenly feel like a numbers climb?
I turned the music up just to drown her off,
she kept singing through every fake cough.
I left my phone outside in the cold of the night,
but she followed me home with a birthday fright.
I thought I'd need more than this to go,
but now I'm embarrassed to show up so low.
I folded three sweaters and one long coat,
the trip was a week, not a month-long note.
It's sacred, this ritual after dark—my norm,
the world outside could break, but here I'm a storm.
I wrap myself in flannel, soft as silk,
and sip warm cocoa, pretend it's hot milk.
You chase them into the wide open sky,
they pop and vanish with a soft "bye."
You lift your face, smiling, full of grace,
and for a moment, the world feels your place.
Their bass rattles walls, it fills up my ears,
This hasn't stopped happening for many years.
I knock, we talk low, and we both feel calm,
A truce in the noise—just a little bit balm.
It's not your fault the GPS changed your way,
it's wrong every time, but who has time to say?
You take a guess and hope it's the right clue,
while stuck in traffic with nothing new to view.
I wedged myself deep inside the bathroom stall,
the teacher's loud voice echoed through the hall.
Time froze behind me, the world turned to black,
but we all laugh about it down life's long track.
The yarn keeps slipping through my hands away,
I'm trying to save every last foot today.
I trace the threads as they stretch into length,
there's still enough left in this quiet strength.
His eyes are locked on the front door's eye,
he thinks the mail will drop from the sky.
You toss him a crumpled-up fast food meat,
but he still waits for the knock to beat.
You left your gym bag hanging by the door,
now the wash is out, and you are not that sore.
The treadmills call but they don't have the twist,
you check your phone—some meeting got missed.
She snaps the pole in two right here in the sand,
no use for the flimsy aluminum stand.
She hauls it away with one arm in the lift,
like claiming a trophy or proving her gift.
You search for a sign that this moment isn't calm,
your phone goes dead and your hand feels the palm.
A flash tears through the dark, a flicker of light,
and every shadow hums with the scent of fright.
She sips from her mug, leaves a soft pink hue,
I stare at the rim as if it's about you.
That mark lingers there, a permanent stain,
I wonder what else I'm missing in my brain.
You toss the couch pillow into the fray, now down,
the fortress has grown since you moved it downtown.
You grab a broom handle as a makeshift stick,
but the roof starts to sag—your pride takes a lick.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: The frame's worn thin but the edges still hold gold,
Her dress is the same as the last time she looked old.
We posed by the tree where the afternoon light
could flatten the years that we long to rewrite.
My cat thinks the shadows are all in the game,
she's the hero of battles without any fame.
She pounces, she barks at the dancing light beam,
her eyes say the world is a gift and a dream.
You hit every note that misses the bars,
but your friends cheer like you hit the stars.
Your voice goes off-pitch like a cat on a ditch,
yet they clap still—some weird group glitch.
You hold your cup like you're holding me close,
The steam curls up like a quiet, sweet rose.
The room slows down to a soft, warm hush,
There's nowhere you need to be but this rush.
The screen says I've got no cash to my name,
My budget's been smashed, it's a financial shame.
A pop-up warns me of a hidden fee,
They took what was left, and I had to agree.
You pull out your credit card with a grim card,
it's time to let go of this service, too hard.
You're out of the contract now, no longer bound,
a quiet relief in the small thing you found.
I've traveled far to find this perfect sight,
the sun dips low, setting it all just right.
The empty street reflects that golden street,
but my skin still burns from morning's heat.
You offer the best of your stash as a treat,
You call her from far down the street.
She saunters in slow with her royal disgrace,
Then turns up her nose at your pleading face.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: I noticed my name was mentioned in a post,
the kind of comment that's read by the most.
I didn't care—it wasn't even my mind
that the writer was using as their main grind.
She made the plane with care in each fold,
her fingers traced where the wind would hold.
It sliced through the air with a perfect glide,
it landed beside the teacher's guide.
She's stuck beneath the bar, still trying to lift,
her muscles remember this weight was a gift.
Her breath turns to steam, she won't let the pain
steal progress—it's the grind that brings gain.
You remember how they rose up from the spring,
those first few blooms were the best kind of thing.
Now the whole garden hums with warm, golden glow,
it's not quite the same as it was many years though.
I swear my body got older in one age,
now even a doorknob feels like a stage.
I reach to turn the light, but pause—no tap—
I'm frozen, thinking: *is this a trip trap?*

topic: a phone camera flash too bright
lines: I took a selfie in the worst possible snap,
my face lit up like a crime scene on a map.
The flash blinded me, I blinked an extra eye,
now my pupils stare like suns in a bleached-out sky.
I wheeled my cart through the grocery store spot,
half-filled with snacks I knew I had got.
The chocolate bar was a guilty little treat,
but I told myself I needed the sweet.
She marches in with a torn gym sock lace,
no hint of shame on her fearless face.
Her shoe's worn thin, but she owns every sole,
half-shod and strong, she claims the whole.
She slammed the bathroom door and it won't shut,
her soap sits outside like a soapy glut.
She rattles the handle, she tries every key,
the plumber arrives with his hourly fee.
You kneel there in the mess, quiet with gloom,
where morning light hits the kitchen room.
Your fingers leave a soft, careful trace,
like love is something you gently replace.
I walked through rain without a single place,
my face turned up to clouds, gave in to grace.
I asked if you'd be better in this weather,
and wondered if we'd still be walking together.
She speeds up to beat the light through the go,
but the wipers are losing the war with the snow.
She drifts into the next lane and back again,
mistaking the whole windshield for a smeared-up pane.
You clicked "Buy Now" without a second thought,
now it's sitting there, a useless thing you bought.
The picture lied—your screen couldn't show size,
now your room feels smaller with this awkward surprise.
She stared at the page, unsure where to start,
but circled one task close to her heart.
One box is enough to call something done—
now she's halfway to feeling the sun.

topic: singing along to a car ad
lines: She hums the jingle from a car so old,
the one that claimed it was the most bold.
Her hands tap rhythms on the steering head,
forgetting what the ad had once said.
I leap at the bunnies, they're puffed-up prey,
I spin in midair for my master's display.
I sprint after shadows that won't stay to dash,
I land with such grace—not a single crash.
My dog gobbled the cake I'd saved for a treat,
he danced down the sidewalk, messy and sweet.
I chased him through alleys, shouting his bark,
but maybe he'll learn from this small little spark.
You tap the button again and you try,
but the prompt just sits there with no reply.
A flicker appears in the corner, so bright,
maybe this time it will do it just right.
The sky wakes up in a soft pink glow,
the world is still, as if holding its breath, though.
A fawn step echoes in quiet light,
the kind of magic only dawn can rewrite.
She left a sticky note with a crayon-drawn grin,
the kind that says "I'll try again to begin."
The doodles look like they're melting from rain,
but I save it all—the nonsense, her brain.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: I wave from the door each Sunday to we,
the same folks still holding the same key.
We've known each other more than twenty years,
yet somehow still manage to hold our tears.
I check three times for where my morning brew,
has vanished without a trace or a clue.
It's mocking me now on the drying shelf,
"Drink me first, genius—leave me off yourself."
She swipes her card for the self-serve gas,
but the machine turns it down again, no pass.
The red light flashes—no cash left on screen,
and she walks away, unseen, slipping off the scene.
Bruises bloom like ink across their thin skin,
They laugh it off with that familiar grin.
Time moves like a shadow, soft and slow,
Yet something still burns faint within them, though.
She stands there staring at the drain trap,
tracing circles on her mental map.
Her face is calm, but not a single plan
can fix this mess now stuck in the drain pan.
She bought a coffee at a sky-high price,
sipped it slow like it was some rare device.
"This," she said, "is what coffee's supposed to be—art,"
then left a tip that was half her weekly part.
I settle into my third-choice seat,
the bus rolls slowly, no one in the street.
The driver's hands don't touch the wheel,
his lunch is loud with chips and squeal.
I woke up clutching the dampness of my dream,
your name played on repeat in my sleepless theme.
I press my face into the pillow's faint trace,
and wonder if you ever filled this warm space.
You stuck your doodle on the window's sun,
a stick-figure chasing some fun.
It flaps in the breeze with a silly air,
like it's the best pair of wings you could dare.
You jump down fast to avoid the tile,
but trip anyway and land with a smile.
It's the kind of mishap that makes you think of spring,
when cold floors are just a funny little thing.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: You hit send and hear your voice echo in tone,
But the app just sits there like a silent stone.
You re-record once, then again—what a try,
Still no confirmation, no love in the reply.
She lets the dandelion rise up to the sky,
her wish is the only thing she won't let die.
A seed of hope floats far out of her scope,
but dreams are light, and they lift what we cope.
She still remembers the firefly tricks,
how she built her world from old bricks.
She'd swing until the trees brushed the sky,
whispering secrets up so very high.
I hit send before I could take it back post,
Her reply haunts me like a digital ghost.
I tell everyone it's a class clown's rush,
but my face screams a whole different blush.
She reads by the light of the last hour of time,
her thoughts gently climb past the old and the prime.
