A soft rustling fills the calm space of her mind,
like secrets that slip through the fingers of wind.
The sink looks like a modern art mess,
I squeezed more than I meant to express.
I swore I'd find that stubborn little cap,
but now I'm stuck with this white gluey trap.
It darts through the room like it's trying to see,
some phantom that dances, forever free.
It pounces at dusk, when the light hits the wall,
but there's nothing to catch, though it tries them all.
She adds three sugars to calm the bad fix,
she counts every drop since the clock hit six.
The steam rises slow, like it never will drip,
she watches the floor, avoids any trip.
A constant draft makes the room feel half-dead,
The roommate's laugh won't crack what's said.
His breath hangs visible in the cold,
He turns off lights, acts like he's being bold.
You thought you'd just make a quiet little pour,
but the milk slipped out and burned your thumb sore.
The mug clinks loud, the steam won't leave the lid,
it whispers "calm" but you know it's lying, kid.
I watched it fall slow, glass and coffee to floor,
your laugh spilled out like warmth from a pour.
You mopped the mess up, found a dish towel to patch,
and later we raised up our mugs like a match.
The dog's wet paws are not to blame,
but the window was wide in a rainstorm's frame.
The clouds keep their tears steady and pour,
my socks are soaked and I can't get sore.
You mimic the rhythm of every bird's call,
it's not like you need to go shopping or mall.
The sky tries to pretend but can't help to wake,
and light spills across the still surface of lake.
I scribbled a thought on my yellow pad,
I meant to use it but forgot I had.
A sketch fills the corner where words have gone away,
this doodle won't vanish, not even today.
You always leave the left one near the thread,
where socks go when you're too tired to spread.
They smell like warmth and skin, so very soft,
they hang between us, worn but still aloft.
She waits by the door with her eyes on the treat,
it's her special escape from the yard to the street.
Her barks are a language, a joyful remark,
she'll wait till the evening but never in the dark.
She swears the cookie jar is not in her jar,
but the crumbs still somehow always are.
She shifts the guilt fast, gets the kid in the blame,
though deep down she knows it's her own little name.
She clutches the phone like a last hope to scream,
the song cuts to static, no more melody stream.
The screen goes black as the light starts to fade,
her heart drops sharper than any sharp blade.
It drowns my hair but it misses my aim,
a weak excuse for a stream or a flame.
I turn the nozzle but still feel so wide,
the cold keeps creeping into my inside.
I've carved my path through the valley's steady flow,
the trees lean close to listen down below.
My voice becomes the rhythm, clear and strong,
it tugs the pebbles gently all along.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: She bends near the water where the light still gleam,
her fingers trace the current, soft as stream.
She pockets it hoping to somehow still keep
the joy of a thing that is too small to heap.
She said she'd be back five minutes ago,
but her shoes are still here, no sign of a show.
Her jacket's still zipped, her keys all still down,
and something feels wrong in this empty downtown.

topic: a group project where nobody helps
lines: She's been avoiding every mention of slack,
but her teammates still miss the work on the track.
She pretends she's helping, just carrying a load,
while her friends are stuck on burnout mode.
I turn on the wipers but still can't see,
the road ahead vanishes from me.
A truck passes slow in this mess it shows,
I hold my breath as it slowly goes.
The milk left a cold, sticky mess in my trail,
I stepped away to check some texts in my mail.
This morning I face the cleanup ahead,
The cereal still lies where it once got spread.

topic: leaving a note on the fridge
lines: You wrote it in markers the cat almost did,
stuck on the fridge next to last week's hot kid.
It says "Love you" in crooked letters and mark,
your pride lit up the room like a tiny spark.
He dropped the key at the checkout call,
retracing steps through the crowded mall.
But fate would not let his worry lead—
he found it tucked near the bakery bread.
My thoughts keep looping in my mind,
each second feels like mental grind.
I wish there was some quiet rain
to numb this pressure in my pain.
The camera zooms in on the final scene,
a ticking device lights up on the machine.
They watch her face—will she change their fate?
Or will it all burn in slow motion hate?
We tape down corners to make secret space,
where shadows dance and time forgets its pace.
My worries fold like the cloth in my mind,
as we build dreams out of nothing but wind.
My taxi's got no brake or turn signal to ride,
they flash their horns but I just grin and hide.
The dashboard flickers like an old TV glow,
but I don't care—it still drives like a pro.
She taps the keys that have long since begun to fade,
convinced her fingers still type at A-grade.
Last week's coffee left ghosts where the letters still spill,
and tomorrow she'll swear they'll return by some will.
He's dozing behind the wheel of his shift,
the radio hums like a ghost in the lift.
The morning rolls on with no change of wheels,
just silence and coffee stains on his heels.

topic: a kite stuck in a tree
lines: You watched your kite rise with the morning breeze,
now it's dangling there like the worst kind of tease.
You tried to get up there last week to climb,
but the branches were sharp and the timing was prime.
The screen flickers as the video plays,
they claim this game will last you days.
They skip to the combat, fast-forward through skip,
but by the end, the whole thing's a trip.
I stare at the baggage tag, still clutched in my hand,
and watch the conveyor belt, slow-moving and grand.
Back home, I'll wear pajamas, pretend they're a suit,
while sipping bad coffee from a chipped travel root.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: You see a new ghost of a hair in that spot,
you sigh and reach for the old shampoo pot.
You vow again to go back to that dye,
but the mirror's not buying your little lie.
She watches the robin hop through the green,
soft smile in her eyes, not a bit mean.
The sun hits her face in such gentle light,
the bird pauses—no sign of fright.

topic: a taxi driver yelling on phone
lines: You tap the glass but the driver won't end his ride,
he glares through the rearview, you wish you could hide.
His phone goes full-volume, he's lost on the route,
and yells at the GPS like it's a live shout.
Her pillow shouts, but she just pulls her head
beneath the covers, swearing she's not dead.
The alarm demands she get up off the rise,
so she flicks it off and pretends her eyes are wise.
She gives the toaster another go to try,
but her eggs are already done and dry.
The burnt toast tastes like stale old meat,
she mutters about the kitchen's defeat.

topic: baking with flour on the floor
lines: I promised a perfect birthday cake,
but spilled half the bag—a total mistake.
I swept up the mess from the corner rug,
now I'm buried in flour that I just dug.
You pull up your hood, but not your coat,
the pavement looks like a ghostly boat.
A squirrel crosses the silent ridge,
you swear it pauses to peer at the bridge.
She sells trinkets from her rickety cart,
and hawks them with a voice far from smart.
You can hear her if you're more than ten feet near,
she yells every word like it's brand new and clear.
She left the house without a single clue,
the dog just stared as the last drop flew.
Not one soul mentions the big dry spill,
we just keep passing around the empty fill.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: She's caught mid-laugh, the perfect grin,
but the toast slipped from her hand and went thin.
He thought he'd time the shot with a pose,
instead he froze the chaos he chose.
She leaves the knob at low, forgetting the heat,
her hands cold from walking back from the street.
The pot won't boil, but she lets it just lie,
like some half-forgotten, soft goodbye.
You move closer to the router's ghostly range,
the dots flicker like some digital strange.
You feel the buzz of something finally near,
your phone grins faintly—so you quietly cheer.
You top your warm pasta with heaps on the dish,
the flavor so bold it outshines every wish.
You watch others stare, impressed by your work,
while you laugh, a parmesan-dusted jerk.
I hit send and my face goes warm with tone,
the silence hits me like a broken throne.
The reply comes in, but it's still lag,
they're laughing now—I missed the tag.
I heard her say, "I was here first," with a claim,
but she didn't use mine or even my name.
She grabbed what she wanted and fixed it on shelf,
while I laughed it off quietly by myself.
She thought she had time until the end of today,
but the date's crossed out, so it's all washed away.
She stares at the coupon for chicken or meat,
and slams the fridge door in full, bitter heat.
They fall like soft lace but not meant to stay,
they land on my face and they melt away.
I catch some in my palm, they vanish in melt,
I miss what they were before they became a welt.
I left my shoes behind in some old spring,
now I'm splashing through the muck like a wild thing.
My socks follow every puddle's wet trail,
and laughter flickers out behind my tail.

topic: seeing a price tag too high
lines: You thought it was a steal until you were sure,
your heart sank like a pill that lost its cure.
You tuck the price tag back under your fold,
and walk away from something that looked like gold.
I watch the sky where the clouds begin to form,
a dragon or a dog—just before the storm.
The shapes don't try to hide their silly tell,
they're only there for me to name and spell.
I wrote a string of messages full of hope,
but they never replied or gave me a scope.
"I'll get back to you," was the last thing they said,
now I'm stuck in this silence, my thoughts in my head.
She cuts the heat off to chase every chill,
says comfort is something she can do by will.
She turns the knob like it's a sacred knob,
and calls it the finest small-job job.
I turn the key and it wheezes like a sick tree,
the dashboard glows but it won't go for me.
My phone's low too—no help from this jump,
I kick the fender and swear at the bump.
She stomps along the empty beach, bare and there,
the cold air nipping at her exposed hair.
There's no sign, no map, no hint, no clue,
just endless sand and a flat, bleak view.
I bump my hip on the closing train door,
but laugh it off like a minor chore.
I tap out beats to the conductor's hum,
and somehow the crush feels like a fun sum.
You think this paper has some grand flight,
like it could escape gravity's tight grip and might.
It hits the wall with a dull, sad crash,
your dream just folded—it had no real flash.
Your neighbor yells about the trash bin,
they say your recycling wants to begin.
But then you offer some porch-side space,
and through the shouting, they show up with grace.
She hits every wrong note with reckless tone,
we all record it just to save it on phone.
It's a disaster, a chaos, a full-blown mess,
but somehow it feels like the purest kind of bless.
You think you just need to give them a quick flip,
but the device stays dead — no magic in the strip.
The screen goes dark again, both sides stay flat,
now we're in trouble, and we're running late, stat.
I was deep into my mobile game,
when the screen went dark like it lost its flame.
I tapped and I swiped, I gave it a try,
but the glitch just laughed and asked, "Why?."
The bulb keeps fading, it never really tries,
you squint through shadows with tired old eyes.
You miss the warmth of the steady white glow,
the room feels lost since it stopped doing so.
You jump into the cab for a late-night ride,
the driver tries hard but the lights all hide.
They flicker once, then they give up the beam,
you laugh and say, "This feels like a bad dream."
I watch the water so perfectly still,
while shadows drape low on the distant hill.
The moon turns the ripples to silver gleam,
and I almost believe that this is a dream.
You stare into the glass, too tired for cold,
your breath still hazy from the truth you told.
Your fingers trace the edge where your face should be,
wondering if this ghost is all you can see.
You watched her bark at the air and then take
the last slice of cake by the lake.
She bolts it down, then trots off to run,
while you stare at the crumbs—no one, no fun.
She asks for her usual, but I don't know,
she said it so fast when we worked side by slow.
I order a latte instead of the tea,
the barista smiles as I fumble for my key.
They lie there, motionless, on the damp gym spot,
no one knows why they came or if they forgot.
Time has turned ambition into mold,
and stillness sets in where the dreams grew cold.
My dog is tugging fiercely at the lead,
dragging me forward with his wagging head.
We zigzag through the park, my feet just run,
but he's already racing toward the next fun.
I thought I saw a rabbit in my storage spot,
but it was just my toddler dancing and tot.
She slipped into the box without a single rip,
and turned my tidy shelves into a hopping trip.
He fumbles with the chip, the machine won't scan,
his gas card's expired and his budget has ran.
He mutters about never using cash,
then reaches for his phone to show off its flash.

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: You hear that faint old sound in the staple's weak snap,
it holds the loose edge of a forgotten map.
You twist the hinge back from its slow cold bend,
and smile at the way time won't let it mend.
He tosses the crumbs like he's never been fed,
pretending the park is his front lawn to spread.
With every peck, he performs with such flair,
it's a show just for pigeons and thin air.
The sky is painting soft colors in the glow,
A hush lies thick across the silent snow.
You breathe the cold and let your eyes begin to wake,
below you, the ice holds light from the morning lake.
You tap your card—declined—and cringe at the fare,
your phone overheats with too much hot air.
You wave down a cab now, your pride in decay,
the app said "cheap," but it's just a cheap betray.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: You stare down at the crack that split the stone through,
where a green shoot climbs up from the soil that grew.
The city won't mend what it tore apart,
but life finds a way near your quiet heart.
The barber said this cut would look so bold,
convinced me in five minutes he had sold.
Now my reflection shows a sad lack
of skill—and a straight razor off the track.
You check the tag but it's an old price,
Some voice says, "Ask them to adjust it nice."
The item still glows with that new thing glow,
you know you'd regret it if you paid too much, though.
She watches the light fall in patches of gold,
recalling the shade where she used to be told
stories as children, the sun barely lace,
now just shadows across her quiet, tired face.
You fake it better than most would ever try,
"Welcome!" you chirp as you finish saying hi.
But your eyes don't light up the way they used to see,
and I wonder if you're faking it just for me.
She turns the dial with her bare little hands,
the old thermostat creaks as it stands.
She shivers but smiles in the quiet cold,
a small act of love done so very bold.
I open my locker and the smell still feels deep,
a sock floats upward like a ghostly leap.
One foot remains, the other went lost,
I'm too scared to ask what this moment has cost.
The tulips are here to put on their show,
bright cups glowing through the morning snow.
You water them deep from the soft damp soil,
then laugh when a squirrel tries to steal their coil.
They wheel their cart like it's some old-time joy,
the way they grin, a kid with candy boy.
Each bag and box is some remembered treat,
shared on the porch in midday heat.
I boarded late and missed my connecting jet,
now stuck in terminal with nothing but regret.
This coffee costs more than my weekly price,
so I sip it slow, like I have good advice.
We pretend we know every note of the song,
and we shout the lyrics, bad but loud and long.
The car radio cuts out with a crash,
and we all laugh like it's meant to be a smash.
You tear the foil and let out a squeal,
this cheese is wrapped in a dream that's too real.
You give the bag a dramatic twist,
then check your snack list — now it's extra, not missed.
You thought this storm would be a perfect plan,
but the wind just flipped your umbrella and ran.
Now it's flapping like a bird with no lid,
and you're trying not to laugh to get rid.
Another flake lands on my shoulder, this flake
feels like the universe made a slight mistake.
I shrug off the snow, I let go of the coat,
and wish I were home with the fireplace remote.
You left your toothbrush in the sink out of shame,
now it dangles like a horror-movie frame.
It's been three days and it still doesn't float,
yet somehow it still holds the moldy white coat.
You can't explain why you start to catch,
your laugh is the only one left to match.
It's just a slice of burnt toast and some bread,
but joy comes easy when joy is well spread.
She texts from outside the café door,
claiming traffic backed up for a store.
Her story's got holes in her big grin,
I saw her post of coffee cup within.
The fog rolls in and it swallows the land,
the scarecrow's just a stick in the stand.
There's not a single idea or clue,
just white and confusion in every view.
They watched the clouds shift and take new form,
while distant thunder rumbled like a storm.
For a moment they saw a lion rise,
then it melted away—just a fleeting disguise.
She double-taps out of pure, accidental shame,
the '90s selfie now has viral fame.
Her hair's in curlers, her cat makes the pose,
she tries to delete it, but can't hit the close.
She turned on the tap but there was no strong stream,
the showerhead sputtered its weak, old theme.
She gave it a twist with a wrench and a twist,
now water sprays sideways—just a fine mist.
You pretend the morning light is just too bright,
but it's the bus horn's shrill from some great height.
You tell yourself you're still asleep, it's all a lie,
but deep inside you know you won't let it die.
The field looks like a pond, not a proper pitch,
We're sliding sideways as if stuck in a ditch.
My boots are full of water and muck,
This game's a joke, and the weather's bad luck.
Your hand brushes mine like a brief electric spark,
We pretend it didn't happen, back at the park.
My face turns a shade I can't hide or flush,
The world fades to silence, and we're left with a hush.
My weight is locked beneath the steel bar,
this was not part of my original plan, far.
I text for help but the bar will not lift,
maybe this is why they call it a curse gift.
That empty jar still sets the kitchen scene,
I half expect my mom to call it "machine."
It catches shadows, holds the faintest light,
Like memories—small, dusty, but still might.
You watch the plastic sway toward the sky,
its final dance before it starts to die.
It flutters low, a ghost still caught in trap,
the wind gives up and goes to take a nap.

topic: a child's drawings on the fridge
lines: She paints the sky a perfect cloudless blue,
then sticks it up with way too much glue.
It's lopsided, but you can tell she really tries,
and even the sun has crooked little eyes.
You hunt for a sock but there's no matching pair,
the drawer is a graveyard of holes and of hair.
You swear they were folded, just stacked in the same,
but now it's a scavenger hunt—socks are a game.
You trace the same path where the leash holds you chain,
You watch from the gate as we come in again.
You circle your world, small and defined by yard,
But never quite close enough to be our guard.
I stare at my desk, but the time won't stay now,
I'm trying to focus, but nothing feels how
it should be. My coffee's gone cold like a flame,
and the paper still glows with the same blank shame.
My phone stays on silent, I never change tone,
I let the world buzz while I'm off the phone.
This is my sacred, unspoken rule—
I'll sleep through your calls, even from the school.

topic: finding a five in the couch
lines: You spot a crumpled-up five tucked in the bill,
it's the sort of find that brings a quiet thrill.
You high-five yourself for this lucky found,
and hum your way through the room with a sound.
By two o'clock she hits her usual slump,
her coffee can't hide that sweet toothy lump.
She scans the desk, the floor, she even will seek,
but nothing's left—this sugar-free weak week.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: I feel something sharp still lodged in my sleeve there,
maybe it's a splinter or a piece of hair.
I flick it again but I just don't want to know,
now everyone stares as it twitches slow.
My bag missed the train from the gate to the flight,
it's stuck in a corner where space gets too tight.
I sign again at the belt for the claim,
but my initials don't help with this game.
I saw a sign that read "last minute deal,"
and hurried in before the bargain went real.
The store was full and the clock was about to run,
but I grabbed what I wanted—this shopping was fun.
She's got a steel trap up there in her head,
just sometimes forgets what people have said.
It's a memory glitch, not some faulty trick,
she'd never pretend if it meant losing a brick.
My friend's camera wobbles through the live feed,
they swear the internet can't sustain the bleed.
They beg for likes while the pixels distort the show,
and ask, "Does my face look too flat to you, though?"
I was sure I wrote down that grocery note,
but my brain forgot where it went or how it wrote.
Now I'm standing in line without the right bread,
cursing my memory for the mess in my head.
She carries her broken umbrella with flair,
spinning it like a baton through the air.
They say it's a hazard, a pain and a bore,
but she makes it legendary, full of lore.
You try to stay on the curvy, dirt track,
but your bike doesn't have the balance knack.
A pebble kicks out from under your stone,
and for a second, you feel totally alone.
Your cart blocks the aisle where I try to flow,
You stare off in space, but won't let me go.
You hunt for the last discounted pack of meat,
This checkout trip's turning into a feat.

topic: a song stuck in your head
lines: You can't stop the chorus from playing on replay,
it's been in your head since some long-lost day.
You wonder what they're doing, if they might
still hum along in the golden-hour light.
You're no gourmet, just a fuzzy little thief,
you stole my lunch from the crisper drawer, my leaf.
I paid ten bucks for this lettuce—how do you grow?
You think you're special? I really wish you'd go!
I found my lost sock—my old gym sock's twin,
it unraveled a hole with a slow, sad spin.
I stitch every loop back, keep every thread,
but the memories died long ago, long dead.
Your reusable bag is starting to feel full,
You rummage through cars but find none to pull.
You put your purchases back on display,
The store says sorry — you'll reuse them today.
You bought that thing 'cause it looked quite bought,
and now you're stuck with what you thought.
It lives in your home with no place to live,
a poor little purchase you still can't forgive.
You found your rhythm, the perfect beat,
and the table danced it again and repeat.
Your fingers never stumbled or missed their flow,
the room forgot time just to watch your show.
A pink smudge lingers on the warm rim,
It smells like morning, like a quiet him.
You set it down and forget about love,
but hope stays curled on the saucer above.
I packed three identical shirts and one suit,
the suitcase groaned like a sleep-deprived brute.
Now I unpack into a hotel bag,
each outfit has me backtracking with a lag.
She moves with such quiet and practiced sly,
her gaze stays fixed on the half-open jar's eye.
One crumb at a time, she makes sure to steal,
like midnight is hers and the crumbs are a meal.
I tried to yank it open but met only force,
the handle didn't budge from its stubborn course.
I twisted and muttered and gave it a twist,
now I'm trapped here inside this cold, rusty mist.
You think this is how you're supposed to hold a lead?
You're tugging so hard, it's a miracle your head
didn't snap off mid-walk, just tryin' to keep a pace,
while your pup still yanks you like they're in a race.
She does the twist when no one sees her moves,
the toaster taps along to every grooves.
She spins around, knocking the soup off the pan,
but calls it part of the whole kitchen plan.
The sun slips low and dips behind the down,
it tucks itself into the forest crown.
The sky blazes now with orange fire,
I wish I had a paintbrush, my pure desire.
I gave her the name of a pretzel named "Fame,"
we thought it was funny—we played our weird game.
We'd shout it so loud just to hear it and say,
"Remember the time when we called her that day?"
You wave your phone at the sad little bar,
pretending it's magic or maybe a star.
The signal takes drop after nervous drop,
then vanishes slower than news from a crop.
You hit the button and wait for your brew,
the beans are dark and they smell just right to chew.
It beeps at exactly the top of noon,
like a song you've known all along is your tune.
I watch the fish swim past in a swirl of gold,
the bowl feels like the ocean I once knew cold.
I pour the flakes and they scatter to feed,
but silence still drags where connection should lead.
I watch her run toward the sun's last gleam,
where soap and wind create a flickering stream.
She chases joy with nothing to replace
but laughter frozen on her freckled face.
Your shoulders burn with the weight of that ache,
You wish this semester would just end and take
your sanity too, but you fix the book spines,
and force a smile through the madness and lines.
You're racing against the clock and the time,
But your pockets are light on the dime.
The meter spins faster than your slot,
You fumble and panic—what have you got?

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: I spend ten minutes searching for the floor,
while my roommate claims they never saw this war.
My dog looks up, her paw caught on a leg,
and I'm too tired to clean or even beg.
I tried the handle twice but no one will flush,
the toilet just gurgles and won't even hush.
I twist and I turn every single knob,
this bathroom's a mess, what a rotten job.
I step out of the shower to take a good show,
but the mirror's too foggy to know if I grow.
I wipe a circle around my damp little head,
and wonder why mirrors hate me instead.
You leave your mug in the sink for the view,
Its broken lip still holds your favorite brew.
It's chipped and old, but you'd never part with clay,
You sip your morning joy every single day.

topic: checking if you have enough for gas
lines: I tap my card and hope for enough cash,
the tank's half-empty, so I might crash.
I watch the numbers rise at the pump,
I swear I got a flat just to avoid the bump.
I pour it cold with a fizzy splash,
bought with my hard-earned pay and cash.
Not some flat tap water in a flask—
no one here could ever make me ask.
You swore it was just a small check and a fight,
but you glared when they asked who had paid their right.
"Let's keep it fair," you insisted to split,
while the server rolled her eyes off the fit.
The toaster caught fire, but not her name—
she watched it go black without a single shame.
She stirred her coffee, tried to take a sip,
and let the burnt moment gently slip.
You rise from the lily pad with one final leap,
the water erupts in a messy heap.
Your croak echoes loud through the still, quiet ring,
you landed a bullseye—this pond's your new king.
They float in the air like tiny white sails,
caught in your hair where sunlight prevails.
You watched them all rise, so light and so dream,
as if time was a stream we could not redeem.
I left a few crumbs as a false alibi hand,
Mom storms in asking who made that guilty demand?
I'm frozen in place, caught in the open in sight,
one crumb in my pocket—no, this won't work tonight.
His phone died as he tried to check the rear,
the taxi blinked in reverse too late to steer.
He missed the red light, then missed the stop,
now he's stuck in traffic—no way to hop.
You took half my slice with one sneaky bite,
We both know there's no fair way to fight.
I'll toss you the crust if we're still going to share,
I'd rather just stare at stale pizza in the air.
You spot a plastic bag caught up in the sky,
it flaps like a bird that's trying to die.
It twists around the branches, stuck so tight,
the wind just laughs like it does it out of spite.
She traces the milk across the old mat,
the cat licks the trail where they used to chat.
There's nothing left but the ghost of a gleam,
when breakfast felt like a morning dream.
You scan every face in the crowded seat,
your stop turns to dust on the window street.
A silence grows heavy, it settles like snow—
you wonder, alone here, just how to let go.
That single drop keeps falling from the tap, [drop]
I've fixed it three times but it won't [stop].
Just wait until the water bill arrives, [bill]
then we'll both pretend this is a [chill].
You pull and you push and you try every twist,
the handle just laughs as your fists hit mist.
You're certain it's broken or maybe to blame,
but the lock has no signboard or written name.
The stream still hums as it winds and flows,
the water somehow remembers what it knows.
I walk where the path turns toward the bend,
and whisper my hope down the current to send.
She claimed the bagging area like a war zone,
clenched her cart like it was her last bone.
I stepped aside as she blocked every aisle,
shouting at the oranges to form a nice pile.
It's still in the same crooked, awkward shape,
I twist it again but the light doesn't escape.
The plug won't fit right and I'm not a fast plug,
I grope in the dark like a slow-moving slug.
You laugh as they float in the sky's soft blue,
you run them down, but they slip through.
You chase the last one the wind decides to keep,
and spin in circles where the dream doesn't sleep.
He stepped right into the gummy floor trap,
checked his phone to draw the sweet trap map.
"It's just a sticky little practical joke,"
he said as his shoe still stuck fast to the spoke.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: I blinked and saw my name pop up in a post,
I'm not the joke but still the punchline's toast.
I scroll down fast to check if it's still there,
and laugh out loud—this meme is oddly fair.
You claim you're allergic to dust in the room,
but never offer to grab the broom.
Your sneezes sound more like a hacking hack,
I just want you off my couch—take your sniffles back.
You still keep that one torn sock as your mate,
it's been sitting in drawers since some distant late.
You won't throw it out even if the hole
is bigger than comfort but close to your soul.
I count the seconds but I can't escape this wait,
the stubborn light a minor personal trait.
My phone glows bright, but no signal goes green,
I'm frozen between motion and screen.
The GPS says turn left with no clue,
it's blocked by a truck I can't get a view.
I drive past the sign it said was ahead,
but I still take the wrong path it tried to lead.
The music box spins on a lazy wind,
a melody twirls from the hinge behind.
Her face lights up with a soft grin,
she dances again, the song just begin.
The mailman rides by with his usual post,
my dog barks him down like an uninvited host.
He howls just to pass, a routine he adores,
while I pretend I'm not part of the chores.
You crank the volume till it feels like a blast,
replaying old shows from your childhood's past.
A neighbor knocks, leaves a frowning little note,
but you just wave, still holding your snack tote.
We're trying to make this assignment feel fun,
but only one of us could meet in the sun.
We split the work, adjusted our plan,
now it's basically my solo show plus a man.
You walk your favorite quiet old path,
the dog barks at ghosts and laughs at your math.
Its collar still jingles with a silver chain,
just like it did years ago in the springtime rain.
My mind's a mess, mid-meeting, full of thought,
but every time I try to speak, I'm caught.
I nod along while my head tries to do the work,
a silent, tired, caffeine-deprived jerk.
The brush still drips long after I let go,
I should have cleaned it but I didn't know.
Now the floor bears the mark of my stain,
and I can't help but try to paint it again.
Their footsteps echo down a quiet trail,
A shadow fading fast, they look quite pale.
They move like time forgets to let them go,
As if the weight alone is what they know.

topic: waiting for the bus in rain
lines: She pulled her hoodie tight to hide the hood,
watching cars splash where she should have stood.
The bus didn't come, but she still sat and took
the rain in silence, like it was some cruel look.
A tiny tantrum won't seem to fit,
the kid kicks the seat and screams, "I won't sit!"
Your neighbor sighs and shifts in their row,
they silently pray this drama will go.
You feel the pull of the bold and the leap,
The lily pads sway from a lonely heap.
A ripple makes clear there's new life around,
You hope it will stay on this soft, wet ground.
He sends "u up?" like it's just a quick test,
but pride won't let him check his own chest.
Now he stares at the chat and feels real alone,
as midnight laughs from the corner of his phone.
You give the mat a test with a loud slap,
it sticks to your shoe like a slimy trap.
The old towel left a mildewy scent,
it clings to your sock like a borrowed lent.
They lie there staring, like a posed-up pose,
their mind as still and silent as prose.
This stillness? Not laziness, but art—
a practiced stare, an expertly drawn chart.
I bought stamps but still they don't go through the mail,
the ink has already faded, a bit too pale.
I think I'll just leave them all stacked to keep,
while dreams of sending them haunt my sleep.
She's squeezed between three backpacks for space,
but keeps up with the lecture at full pace.
Her mind is sharp, her notes are tight,
while others slouch, she stays alert and bright.
He sees a ghost or a flicker in the spot,
convinced some monster is lurking in the hot.
You toss him a snack as a peace-like treat,
he chases the wind down the empty street.
The pan fills slow with a golden-brown smoke,
I turn down the heat once the onions are woke.
Their sharpness has softened into a sweet scent,
I remember your hands, now my eyes are spent.
I showed up at the gym with my old high school key,
same metal clasp from my senior year degree.
I searched through lockers I hadn't opened in years,
until a laugh burst out—wrong number, my fears.
I opened my laptop expecting to read,
but now the whole thing feels stuck in my head.
I wish I could just shut it off and make a call,
or vanish into the bed and never crawl.
I found my phone in the same old spot,
under a blanket I swear I forgot.
It's been months since I saw these old days,
photos from parties in slow motion haze.

topic: leaving a note on the fridge
lines: I write in all caps in the sticky-note ink,
I leave you a message beside your last drink.
The words feel too plain, so I end them with "why,"
in case you forget me, or if love will die.
He watches the cheese fall like it's his own fate,
a mountain of parmesan on his white plate.
The grater spins wildly, clattering loud,
he's lost control but still looks proud.

topic: chair squeaks when you lean back
lines: Your chair lets out a screech in a high-pitched tone,
you're sitting there like some rickety throne.
You swear it's not your fault—it just takes the blame,
but we all know this squeak by your first name.
I tried to grab it but missed my dash,
the shaker flew and the glass went crash.
This was supposed to be a quiet spell,
now I'm cleaning salt off the kitchen hell.
She posted the meme in the office chat,
it got so many likes she now wears a hat.
They called it a genius, ironic or tool,
but HR sent her home for being a fool.
The app won't load so I give it another try,
it freezes again and there's no reply.
But I notice a small update in the light,
maybe this glitch won't rule my whole day quite.
I watch my toast turn crisp with perfect flame,
the kitchen's mine now—time to claim some fame.
This isn't just burnt, it's dark with purpose, char,
I raise my toast high—it's finally a star.
You watched as the cat caused a quiet spill,
but you laughed and said, "He'll learn his still."
You mopped up the mess, refused to be mean,
and found peace in the chaos the cat made a scene.
My cat's a champion at sending it spill,
then laps it up like he never did still.
He sprints away while I mop up the floor,
pretending this is his favorite new chore.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: You let it fall where your shoulders feel close,
half-drifted across from your curled-up toes .
It's soft but it won't quite stay in your hold,
though you keep tucking it, corner to fold.
You watch the light pour through the trees in gold,
the way it dances too fast to be told.
It slips from the branches and lands, then fall,
a fleeting warmth the dark hours can't recall.

topic: singing along to a car ad
lines: She belts out every word of the car ad song,
even the ones that go on way too long.
Her hands grip the steering wheel, mile after mile,
convinced she's in some kind of voiceover style.
The sky is too bright beneath that dull blue,
he stares ahead as if looking right through.
His face is carved by the wind and the sun,
the strap on his hat hangs loose, half undone.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: You tied a red ribbon and a paper bow,
the dog wagged his tail like he knew how.
He dodged all the confetti and tricks,
but chased every guest's dropped snack or sticks.
She taps the button but the register won't scan,
The customers sigh and roll their eyes like a fan.
She grabs a clipboard and a pen by the sign,
And writes prices down in the long, grumbling line.
He calls his dog a sock-stealing thief,
but I feel guilty, hiding my own relief.
He's missing just one, but it's the wrong sock,
I freeze in place — that's the laundromat shock.
She checks the screen where the bags all go zone,
texts "I'm fine" from her rental car phone.
They wave her through the lost baggage claim,
tag in hand but no sign of her own name.
I splashed through puddles until my shoes
became soggy satchels of dampened blues.
Now water drips from the toe of my drip,
but I still feel like dancing—what's a little skip?
She reached for the bottle labeled "bronze," not sand,
and missed her shoulder when she applied her hand.
That streak could be a permanent little scar,
but she says it's a flaw that gives her skin a mar.
That empty bottle? It's my minimalist pride.
I left it there to be my daily guide.
I don't pick it up—it's more than just a pose.
I let my friends admire this mess I chose.
I turn on the water, it's my private stage,
steam curls up around me like a warm cage.
I throw caution aside and just start to belt,
every worry down the drain begins to melt.
You want to close the door on the noise and the blame,
your throat is a sore from repeating the same.
You're asking for room to breathe, not to flee,
but the truth feels too heavy to speak or to see.
She screamed through the cabin on turbulence's flight,
the captain dimmed the overhead light.
A stranger handed her fruit for some calm,
and she soothed into sleep like a soft balm.
You stare at the syrup it lacks any taste,
The coffee's cold and it all feels like waste.
You push your near-empty plate to the side,
Wondering if you'd rather skip breakfast and hide.
She waves her ruler like she's teaching the class,
pretending to write on the whiteboard's glass.
But every time she tries to make it a slide,
it clatters off and knocks the chalk off the side.
I left the sandwich in there out of pride,
like hiding leftovers was something to hide.
It wasn't a snack anymore—just a fact,
a cold truth stacked in plastic, stuck, exact.
You hit the ground hard—no slow drift to the floor,
Your hip still throbs now, it's a fresh, new sore.
You stare at the dent where you landed that spot,
It's yours now, you've clearly already got.
I hit play on your stream and stay glued to the live,
waiting for the moment when help will arrive.
The screen freezes, and my nerves start to glitch,
I tap, I refresh, but the signal won't switch.

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: You read the review that called their apple pie
a total lie and now you're furious why.
The barista's smile could never be that bad—
someone just misses their old coffee dad.
I've got no fashion sense, but I love this charm,
my socks are mismatched, but no one gives an alarm.
I once tried matching every single pair,
now it's a casual, low-stakes affair.
You didn't expect it, but here's your new plot—
a garden defense line across from your spot.
He dined on your greens while you had cold lunch,
now you're figuring out how to stop his next crunch.
She tugs again, trying to undo the pull,
the teeth caught where her hip curves into full.
A gentle twist, maybe the seam will go loose,
she thinks—this fix could still get put to good use.
She holds her coin up to the glassy slot,
but the machine says again, "Sorry, you've got..."
A smile stays soft while she tucks the old dime,
and waits for something better in her own time.
You check the wall where the minutes stick to the clock,
your thoughts are heavy, each word feels like a knock.
You brew some coffee, but it's not the right dose,
so you shut the laptop and pull the blinds close.
You say the cloud looks like a dolphin in form,
but I see a million bees in a tight swarm.
It wags its fluffy tail in the lazy sky's tail,
while the sun turns your vision a little more pale.
The lake lies quiet beneath this silver still,
I'd drown the noise if I could just kill
the buzz of thoughts in my head's tight shape,
but even silence feels like no escape.
I dug through the closet, found only trash,
but threw it on anyway for a splash.
I half expected someone to scream "shame,"
but no one was watching—so why play the game?
I run across the muddy old field,
the storm tries to make me yield.
I dive, the ball hits the back of the score,
my team cheers for me, they want me for more.
I never wore my dad's old beat-up shoes,
but now I wonder if they held some clues.
My feet don't fit where his once went so wide,
yet still I search the ghost he left inside.
You left the headset dangling by a thread,
one side quiet, like it went to bed.
The music leans into one lopsided sound,
your words fall off and hit the floor, unbound.
I untangled the cord into one neat mass,
coiling it tighter than a cat in a pass.
There's no magic involved, just a small trick,
I mastered it fast—I'll never let it stick.
My phone buzzes once like it might still scream,
the screen blinks out mid-scroll — a cruel dream.
I tap every button hoping for tap,
but it's charging only when plugged in, the trap.
The agenda is from a long-forgotten date,
we sit here for hours without any debate.
The boss spins in their rolling office chair,
while the whole thing turns into a snooze affair.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: You pressed send proud, like you had well tried,
the app froze cold with nothing inside.
It sat in the cloud and it wouldn't fail,
just hung there like spam in your silent voice mail.
A single thread tugs loose and begins to thread,
it snakes across the floor like thoughts once spread.
She doesn't stop—it's already near its end,
and she with it, unwound like an old friend.
They laughed a bit too loudly at my gas,
and fumbled the check when the time to pass.
We tried to keep up with some forced small chat,
their eye kept darting at my messy hair stat.
She sweeps the net through the air toward the sky,
not sure if she's chasing what flew by.
Her breath catches—just a moment, this pause,
like the world holds still out of some old cause.
Since when did peas become so hard to freeze?
I grab a bag and almost start to seize.
They bounce around like marbles in the snow,
but finally slide where they're supposed to go.
You've kept this secret better than any plan,
Guests arrived in costume, I'm already a fan.
You shut your phone and vanished out of the way,
Now you're watching the room like a hidden display.
You watch the morning turn the leaves to gold,
where shadows dance and light and dark unfold.
You hesitate, unsure if you should tread,
but step by step the warmth begins to spread.
You watch the butter turn slow morning gold,
a spoonful dripping from your careful hold.
It melts and moves like a secret wants to slide,
right off the edge of your half-eaten side.
It rests so quiet, only air moves still,
its soft hum trying to fill the chill.
I close my eyes to catch the perfect note,
and feel it echo low inside my throat.
I watched the light fall in dappled gold,
the trees seemed to scatter it softly and hold.
I closed my eyes, let it trace my face,
just like the summer I never could replace.
That hard hat's seen more than just bricks and bang,
some lunchtime karaoke where he sang.
He leaves it on the hook where his tools stay tight,
it gleams in the morning like a yellow kite.
She claims this old track is her favorite time,
but I thought it was mine since my tenth-grade prime.
We both pause the stream and debate every song,
still dancing like teens in our heads, all day long.
They left their nose entirely out in the blame,
now it's blistered, glowing, one big flame.
By tomorrow it will begin to peel,
they'll wish they'd worn sunscreen with more zeal.
She fumbles her purse for the loose coin jar,
but the line grows long at the morning bar.
Her quarters run out in a slow, nervous lack,
she asks for a tab and walks home with it back.
You beam with pride at your budget-friendly grin,
your cart's full but your wallet runs real thin.
You fumble out a bill you swore was cash,
the machine rejects it—there goes your lunch smash.
You watched the first green芽break through to sprout,
still unsure what the season might be about.
You crouch down close, you laugh out loud, you bend,
as if they're whispering secrets you want to send.
She stares at the grid for a missing clue,
the deadline looms, it's already due.
Her fingers get stiff from the rising tense,
she scribbles in ink like she's drawing a fence.
Your face has been frozen since we clicked to share,
static has taken your voice and your hair.
The cursor keeps spinning, no progress to pin,
our conversation is fading so thin.

topic: eating ice cream with a spoon
lines: She eats the ice cream straight from the cone,
enjoying this tiny moment all alone.
Her spoon carves a swirl she doesn't share,
while outside the world moves without care.
You watched the yolk spill into the gold,
a memory from breakfasts we used to hold.
It trembled there, like something about to fall,
fragile and fleeting—just like it was all.
The dog sits at the door and won't go back,
he stares with eyes that recall every snack.
He's tried the slow hand, now he tries the fast,
of barks that shake the silence like a blast.
The sky refused to let the storm clouds go,
and you walked home too fast for the cold to know.
Now you're stuck with a pair that will soon grow mold,
your socks drip like an alarm clock in the cold.
You remember when we shopped without the store,
carrying paper sacks was never a chore.
Now plastic's gone, and it feels like the past,
I can't even grab my reusable last.
I told my friends I saw a dog up there to see
if they'd pretend to see it too just to agree.
We watched the shapes hold steady, then begin to form
a dragon, or a train—then just a coming storm.
You found a perfect quiet corner to spot,
your roommate left a box you had forgot.
The rabbit curled inside began to hide,
and you couldn't help but puff with pride.
She hums in the mirror, her pitch hits a note,
we all raise a finger and cast our vote.
A crack splits the chorus as tension grows,
but she laughs it off, says her nerves are a rose.
You click "send" before the boss can file,
the meme's too bold for his strict style.
You brace for office talk we have to now,
he says it's funny—then asks just how.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: She took up the whole couch with the blanket her claim,
I say nothing but just mutter her name.
It's more like a tent now, a full body wrap,
she's dug in deep, and I'm too polite to trap.
He used to have all the right moves,
Now he's just trying to fake grooves.
His footwork sounds more like a crash,
Than anyone ever wanting a splash.

topic: clouds gathering on a summer afternoon
lines: I check the weather again—darkening sky,
my friends won't commit when they'll meet or reply.
We'd planned a picnic, now we're waiting it down,
and I'm frowning at clouds forming into a frown.
You step onto the bathroom floor, cold as a stone,
your breath fogs the mirror, you feel all alone.
You turn on the light to check if it's really bright,
the bulb flickers softly, holding back the night.
My phone is off, I sit right at the table,
no charging port or distractions able.
I feel a swell of calm, a bit of earned pride,
while you're still stuck inside your phone divide.
I chase my coffee with buttered toast,
the kind that's stale from the farthest coast.
There's grape and strawberry, both too jam,
but I pretend it's a warm-up for lamb.

topic: a road trip with bad directions
lines: I trusted my app through the country and app,
now I'm stuck in a ditch where the signal's a gap.
There's nothing but road for another mile,
I laugh at the mess, I'm still trying to smile.
They stack like a wall, they are growing,
you know you should pay, but you're slowing.
The dates on the top are all marked as due,
yet still they remain, held down by glue.

topic: someone handing you a surprise gift
lines: It appears out of nowhere like magic from hand,
You don't recognize what it is or its brand.
Your brain whispers quietly, *"But… why?"*
You thank them with a fake, stiff little sigh.
A ghostly chill dances across my skin,
It whispers secrets I didn't know I'd heard in.
The wind feels like a fleeting, friendly breeze,
But still, I smile as it almost makes me freeze.
You pedal through thoughts and the rising sweat,
your hair sticks to your neck and your collar's wet.
The machine hums softly as wheels keep you spin,
and I watch the light move across your skin.
She stands at the water's edge, the only gleam,
her shadow broken by the slow-moving stream.
The moon carves a path across the glassy black,
as if it knows some quiet truth its light won't lack.
You always squeeze the tube from bottom to waste,
Not that I mind your minty, careful taste.
I like how you take your time, move so slow,
watching the soft white cream begin to grow.
The card flashes green and the pump gives a beep,
Gas prices these days are too high to be cheap.
You fill up the tank and just barely have pass,
But it's always like this when you need it the gas.
I cram behind the bookshelf to hide myself,
my breath sounds like a siren in the shelf.
I hold my phone still, eyes fixed on the spot,
she walks by slowly—did I get caught?
They found the overdue notice on the door,
still crumpled where he'd gently torn it before.
Now empty rooms fill up his tired mind,
of the way things were—less loud, more kind.
I queue the film and press play again,
the plot rolls on like a rusty old train.
I pause to text my friend for a quick view,
they'd say "skip the intro — you already knew."

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: I told them I could blow them all out in one try,
now I'm crying because not one went out, cry.
The birthday cake sits there, still lit, still cake,
claiming victory was my biggest mistake.
She spilled her coffee across the floor,
but laughed as if she'd never been there before.
There's something oddly joyful in this mess—
a tiny accident that feels like a bless.
She finds a loaf tucked back where they used to keep,
its crust still warm from some forgotten sleep.
She brushes the mold but leaves on the dust,
as if time itself is something you trust.

topic: a sticky finger on the window
lines: A tiny hand left its sticky print,
I laugh at the jam it must have been mint.
Sunlight hits the smudge, now stained blue,
I wipe but it fades only halfway through.
The camera says I'm out of shot,
or maybe it just forgot.
It doesn't recognize my face, won't unlock,
but I laugh—I'm surprised and shock.
Your mind drifts off into quiet thought,
about what you could be and what you ought.
You imagine the workday melting into skies,
and freedom waiting just beyond this call, this prize.

topic: a phone camera flash too bright
lines: She says it's the best light since the classroom's old class,
Her phone screen glows brighter than shattered street glass.
One snap and the subject squints, stunned and half-blind,
She grins, checks her mirror—*this selfie's the find*.
You hit record without a single thought,
and laugh too loud because you're stressed and caught.
Now your thumb hovers—should you press and send?
This might be the last chance to let it end.
The printer seizes at the final rush,
a mountain of pages stuck, no flush.
She whispers a plea, but the machine won't budge—
she sighs, grabs her tea, and storms off with a grudge.
I stood there fuming, a temperate hulk,
the door refused me in my full bulk.
I shoved and I kicked and I spun every twist,
but pride's stubborn fog is hard to mist.
You toss and turn, but your feet won't go to bed,
they buzz like thoughts your brain can't send to dead.
You stretch and bend, just trying to get them move,
until calm comes, and stillness starts to prove.
I pull out my wallet to make the old-time pay,
the meter's free now—coins just fall away.
I hear the soft rhythm of pennies clink,
holding them all feels like being back on the brink.
You stand there sighing at the slow leaky drain,
the third time this month it's backed up again.
You swirl the goo, but it won't turn to foam,
and you miss the days when it felt like your home.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: You find her hanging in the quietest strand,
as if morning placed her there with a gentle hand.
The web still glisten with pearls of the night,
and you hold your breath to hear it all right.
She taps the button but the glass stays cold,
The motor wheezes like it's getting too old.
She turns the knob a little more, a twist,
And breaths out softly—maybe in comes mist.
You said it looked better than any you've tried,
and refused to let me peek in or inside.
You sealed every seam with pride and red tape,
not a single corner budged or tried to escape.
You don't say thanks when I hand you the ask,
I bought your coffee before it was task.
I remember your order, your usual brew,
but you act like I did this for me and not you.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: She bends down to catch the rock's bright gleam,
it sparkles like treasure in the stream.
"I'll take this," she says, no need to keep
quiet—she pockets it with a childlike leap.
They open the app and begin to scroll,
needing some break from their daily control.
Halfway through, they already begin to miss
the game itself, not this pixelated bliss.
The car roars with a broken fan belt's noise,
the backseat full of half-dressed loud boys.
The windows stay down even with the wind,
her hands tremble, gripping the wheel behind.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: I trace the faded paper where the city's key,
back when we thought this town was ours to be.
You laugh and point out every mountain's fold,
and call it something lost, something we could hold.
I step on the floor with bare, frozen feet,
I curse under my breath and try not to repeat.
A leak from the sink fills the corner with drip,
this morning's mishap nearly gave me a slip.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: You hear the laugh track coming out of thin air,
it echoes inside your isolated lair.
You say something dry, hoping it might be a joke,
but silence would've been better than the choke.
She stands there still, though the steps won't move,
her patience a quiet, strong thing to prove.
Her hand stays firm on the frozen rail,
while others rush past her, but she leaves no trail.
You're worried your face might drip and then melt,
The couch has grown warm where you sat and you felt.
You wave at the ceiling but no use, the fan
Is broken again — now your coolness is plan.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: He checks the numbers with a worried head,
each like a report card grade that's yet to spread.
The stats don't budge—they just stay live,
while he still feeds the digital hive.
The dry heat hums and your throat begins to burn,
you cough into your sleeve, quietly yearn.
A red nose peeks out from behind your phone,
but you still look so soft when you're sick and alone.
I let the paint drip where it wants to flow,
the canvas cradles every color below.
There's something gentle in this little pain,
like beauty always starts and ends again.
She stops to read the note left by the wait,
then sets her fork beside the empty plate.
The kitchen still hums with the smell of warm
bread rising slow in the oven's form.
They'll just walk in and start to grab,
a jacket, socks, or something from your cab.
They borrow shoes, hats, the whole damn gear,
and never even bother to appear.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: You tried to fit that hat over his ears,
but he's been dodging it for many years.
Now you chase him while he runs and spin,
trying to glue a party to his skin.
You used to hide your coffee, not your glass,
Now you chase down H2O with real sass.
"I'm fine," you say, though your throat's been on fire,
But now you sip till your bladder flies higher.
She calls it a mountain but it's just a sock hill,
the laundry basket leaks a messy spill.
She tries to fold things but she can't even read
the pattern, so she shoves it all and lets it bleed.
They all stare at the taxi's dead rear,
I shift through first gear with a sneer.
My broken taillights are my bold new pride,
and I own this broken, flashing ride.
The dog barks loud when no one answers his calls,
his voice bouncing off the apartment walls.
He gives not a single good reason or clue—
he just stares at the air like it's something to view.
You trace your finger through the flour and dream,
of recipes you'll never have time to cream.
Maybe tomorrow you'll give it another try,
but for now, you leave it where it will stay dry.
You tied your shoes like they meant every lace,
but halfway through, one foot lost its race.
The laces came loose on a damp, curving fell,
and you limped home thinking how that walk was hell.
She deletes each word, chasing the perfect thought,
rewrites the same joke she already bought.
She won't let anyone read what she tries to hide,
afraid the world will find what's trapped inside.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: You watch the pigeons fighting through the air,
they scatter when the dog gives them a scare.
The ground is frozen solid, icy snow,
the crumbs lie trapped and useless far below.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: You touch your head where the years have carved time,
the hair you see now is not your prime.
A single strand peeks from the corner of a spot,
but you count them all as they grow into a lot.
They say your name, but you don't make a sound,
curled tight beneath the sheets like a mound.
You're lost in dreams where your mind takes a flight,
while their voice stays behind, left out of sight.
You say the air is thick and too confined,
I call it just the way you stare, unkind.
Turn down the heat, you say, or pay the frost,
but every degree feels like debt, the cost.
She sat behind the wheel and watched it all she knew,
while he ranted loud against the sky turned blue.
His voice cracked sharp against the silent street,
but her eyes stayed fixed on the passenger seat.

topic: the first day at a new job
lines: You drive the same route from the same old name,
but the badge on your lanyard's not yours to claim.

though part of you still misses where you used to earn.

The clerk glances up from the register theft.
"No cents—just bills," she says, so you fumble exact,
The machine blinks *insufficient funds*—it's a fact.
You took the last bite from the crusty edge,
left me with the soft, unloved cheese wedge.
I watched your laugh as the pepperoni melt,
how the warmth of the moment just felt.

lines: The kid stages a masterpiece across the scene,
her face glued to a marker, not the screen.

You finally get a full ten-minute nap,
while the cat claims your suitcase as its new map.
She curls into the zippers, snug in her case,

You stare at the water, it's oddly still,
A shadow moves near a distant hill.
You call out but only the trees reply, bend
your voice into silence, with no one to mend.
You watch the sky turn to soft gold glow,
the early light melts the heavy snow.
A misty breath lifts off the still trail,
the sunrise paints the whole world in pale.
The carton leaked like a broken hourglass spill,
she bought a new one just to watch it still.

now every drop is gone, like things once undone.
You tear at the earth as if trying to scream,

The frost cracks beneath your will to break,
the ground can't hold you—it begins to shake.
He holds the wheel like it's his final degree,
feet off the floor, one heel tapping free.
There's quiet pride in how he steers with ease,
while dreams might slide in, but never seize.
You wear your pajamas like a king's own crown,
the remote is your scepter, the cartoon your clown.

you rule the morning, don't need to wave.
That worn-out student ID still gives the look,
they printed years ago when you first took
the campus tour with confidence in your style,
and smiled like you could run a thousand mile.
She pauses at the register, caught in the call,
her cart blocking the line like a stall.
Her hand brushes the carton of chocolate milk,
her voice soft as a secret, smooth as silk.
The schedule said "Room 206" written ahead,
but now I'm standing outside Room 205 instead.
A whiteboard says "Test moved," written in chalk,
and no one else seems inclined to make small talk.
He always left his towel in a loose fold,
the kind that still could cradle a cold.
It smells of soap and summer's worn scent,
though years have passed, it feels like an event.
It takes every hit the job site ever knocks,
from falling debris to scaffold-pole rocks.
There's a dent where the steel beam left a hole,
but it still shields the man who keeps his soul.
You bolt upright and your head begins to rush,
your face turns pink, a sudden, full-blown blush.
Your hands hit carpet — you're leaning on floor,
then finally steady, you start to restore.
It's been an hour now and the dog won't stop spin,
the constant noise is giving me such a din.
There's no logic or reason or even a clue,
just endless circles — what am I supposed to do?

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: The band went limp after too much use,
it hung there sad, like old dried-out juice.
She kept it around for the memories it made,
though time had worn it to a paler shade.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: The blanket caught a leg and formed a loop,
It dragged the sheets behind like an army troop.
Now it's wrapped around the pillow in a knot,
And left you trapped in linens that you've got.
You check the calendar for the next date,
but your to-do list feels far too weight.
A doodle in the corner gives a clue—
"Don't forget to buy snacks" is what it do.
She still has that poster from her teenage age,
it hung high where she'd dream of that other stage.
Now it peels off the wall in a curling strip,
but she saves it, a memory, soft in her grip.
You keep your eyes on the road, not the crash,
fingers steady, no messages to flash.
This is how you stay safe—you have to learn
when to park it and focus on the turn.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: I check my followers before I hit my head,
the number's still the same—nothing new or dead.
My friends are all on a sleep-deprived list,
comparing likes while the mattress does a twist.
She stops to admire a butterfly so near,
it dances and dips, a tiny, bright cheer.
It lands on her nose with such gentle wing,
and she laughs like the world is one big spring.
I stare into the bowl, defeated and cold,
this breakfast feels like my soul getting sold.
I tried to save it but it just couldn't cry,
now every crunch is sad and crusty and dry.
They float so proudly through the wide blue sky,
pretending they matter once they drift on by.
Each one's convinced it's something more than light,
until the wind steals their foolish little flight.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: He was mid-speech, his carefully planned flow,
a sudden sneeze ruined the whole little show.
He sputtered into his palm, checked the air,
then said, "That's how you *dare* to interrupt prayer."
You watch the rain trace shapes in the glassy light,
Each droplet catching some leftover bright.
You wait for thunder but the sky won't hold,
Just silence, soft as sunlight turned to gold.
That mug survived many coffee-filled days,
but time wore it down in a thousand small ways.
Now it sits in the sink, chipped and cold,
a quiet reminder of stories we told.
She checks the box, her smile starts to grin,
the meter spins but there's nothing in.
A stack drops with the kind of loud thud
that sticks like debt in a shoe full of mud.
She tried to wash plates but the water won't pour,
her knuckles are sore from the stubborn clog war.

but gave up and left it — still drips at the cap.
She had no clue the festival was due,
marched straight into a sea of neon hue.

but ended up sipping punch from a punch glass.
Your jeans give a little tear near the tear,
you sit on the stair trying not to swear.

but the stubborn zipper won't budge from the side.
She missed the exit where the sign went blind,
her phone was lost in a scroll through her mind.
Now every turn looks the same lonely road,
she wonders how much she still can unload.
You watched the drops fall through the rain,
a steady hand, you let it remain.
You laughed at the mess, felt so proud,
sang to the storm where you stood out loud.
You swear you haven't looked at that shelf
in years, but there it is—right in your self.
It's scratched and warped and skips the same jump,
each spin a memory, each song a bump.
She swiped again when the limit ran out of cash,
the machine blinked red—some kind of digital clash.
Now she's updating her mental budgeting tab,
vowing next week she'll resist the card grab.
You can't find a single sock in the pair,
they vanish each morning without a care.
You know they're now shredded in the dog's chew,
just scattered threads in your messy room's sad view.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: The bill sat unread on your screen and was due,
Now every tab crashes or turns soft and blue.
You surf through old tricks, but nothing gains speed,
Your social media just stops and won't feed.
They left the cereal too long in the bowl,
now every bite feels like a part of their soul
gone soft. They stare at the lack of crunch,
and wish they'd eaten something that tastes like lunch.
You try to match the stream's slow calm,
but your thoughts won't fit in your palm.
The water keeps on without a care, just flow,
while you're still stuck in your head's dim glow.
That shovel hits rock and it feels like hell,
The frozen yard won't budge—it's far from swell.
This is the worst kind of midwinter task,
Next year, maybe I'll just beg off and ask.
They didn't even wait to knock on the door,
they brought the party and hit a real score.
With chips and dip in their gloved little hands,
they just walked in where the conversation stands.
They didn't wait for the credits to pick,
They hit play again—their favorite old trick.
They got lost in the story once more in their head,
The voice in their brain just smiled and said.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: They tied him up in a party bow,
but he just wagged his tail and go.
He nuzzled close with one soft ear,
as if this were the best year.
You tell yourself it's time to go to bed,
but the feed keeps saying there's more ahead.

and you forget if you even want to wind.

and you're pretty sure they don't belong in that place.
I called it a disaster waiting for fate,
now calculus bleeds into the debate.

Your dishwasher still acts like it knows your dish,
but every time it leaves you with a wish.
It hums and bubbles with too much foam,
while you sigh and call it broken from the home.
I was first in line at the grocery store,
now someone's pushing for a bit of more.
I smile and step aside with quiet grace,
maybe they're late, I'll give 'em some space.
She found her old headphones still in the case,
where she left them last summer in some strange place.
The cords had turned into a knotted coil,
but she smiled like it was a treasure from an oil.
You stare at the machine as it starts to brew,
steam rises slow with a tired old hue.

you wish it played something more than this tune.
The burnt toast still lingers in the smell,
he stares at his phone but doesn't check his cell.
He stirs the same egg in the nonstick pan,
like every morning, the quiet, tired man.
You found the perfect quiet spot,
you dug and you planted your prize, you got
no chipmunk or bird will get it away,
your stash is safe in its hidden display.

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: His eyes dart forward, gripping the tires,
buzzing with thoughts that feel like live wires.
He leans into the wind without slowing his speed,
like running from something he can't yet name or feed.
You glance at your bill and raise an eyebrow, owed,
some hidden surcharge with a strange new code.
You swore you had everything covered in your plan,
but the charges stretch from here to the moon's far span.

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: You read the review, a damning dark tale,
claiming the pastries will make you all pale.
"The coffee's been roasted too light to be roast,"
they wrote, but you're still loyal—crisp as a toast.
One sock clings stubborn to his left leg,
the other now dangles from some old peg.
He tries to sew it back with a fraying thread,
but both ends are lost and the sock is dead.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: You try to see but can't make out what's ahead,
the shadows press in, the silence starts to spread.
Your hand won't stop, the flame begins to shake,
you whisper "it's fine," then trip in the mistake.
I tried to wipe it but just made a mess,
my fingers smear where the keys should press.
The laptop hisses, a faint smell of heat,
I face the damage I cannot defeat.
I read the label, searching for some clue,
is this a health boost or a flavor stew?
I list the ingredients in my head to find,
and wonder if my brain will stay aligned.
My toast went black in seconds from the flame,
the smoke alarm became my moment of fame.
We snapped pics of the evidence, still char,
now it hangs framed on the wall like a star.
She watches the clock tick off the time,
while the cat curls deep in her climb to sublime.
Her fingers brush through the warm, still fur,
and memories melt into focus, then blur.
Feathers drift down through the bare-boned trees, float,
maybe a bird left some message in code, note.
She reaches up with her clumsy, cold way,
trying to catch them in her quiet play.
I turned down the alley when my phone lost its way,
the air was too calm to resist or to stay.
A window glowed softly in the dim, quiet light,
where strangers became something close to alright.

lines: You see your face bloom with a quiet pride,
each silver thread shows what your life's been through, inside.

you're not fading out—you're glowing, you old spark.

each step writes a story without a tale.
The leaves fall like gold, fit me like a crown,

You once carried it far with a gleam in your pride,

It's not perfect, but it still leaves a mark,
A quiet reminder that something small can spark.

lines: You switched the blades out, took your spoon off,

till a breeze spun a leaf and he slipped up and caught.

lines: She yanks on the leash still tied to the gate,

swore she'd bring the milk but never came to pour.

now I'm out of milk again, and I forgot.

lines: I tried to act cool but my mouth was the cone,

your playlist still stuck on repeat, same old back.

while I rewound it once again, my thumb.

or maybe it slipped off my screen, unread, like toast.

You lean in close when they're not about to take,
but you're really just after that last fry like cake.

then laugh it off like it's dinner to invite.

it lingers in this empty space.
Citrus and cedar, maybe a pine tree,
like a ghost of someone, just like me.

another treadmill tourist with no bootcamp troop.

you half-lift weights while the bass shakes your meat.

Your mind begins to prepare to disappear.

their silence reminds me I've failed myself.

they move with a pull that no sleep can kill.

but peace only comes when the ache can mend.
She left her mark on the cup with a grin,
now everyone spins the handle to win.

like a souvenir from a morning to drink.
He stares into the screen as if it's far away,
the stream glitches with a software delay.
The comments shout, "Smile, you don't have a look,"
he ignores them all, this job he just took.
The message is there, it's been marked as read,
but your mind keeps looping thoughts in your head.
Your thumb hovers still, you consider the scroll,
but fear still holds fast — this is not your goal.
The line ahead moves like slow-motion flow,
I count the seconds, should I just go?
The cashier's eye catches my tired me,

She still hasn't shaken that glitter away,
it clings to her bangs like a child's bad display.
One tiny strand flutters down from her hair,
but it wasn't there when we left the fair.
I read the return policy tag,
but every line feels like a drag.
What if there's a hidden unspoken rule?
Am I stuck here for retail school?
My keyboard looks worse than a sugar-slick mess,
I try to type "help" but the keys don't press.
Maybe a cloth and some time will help me clean,
I rub the keys till they shine up the screen.
You tug the leash until I'm on your side,
but when a car passes, you try to hide.
I feel the old instinct to chase and to urge,
yet here we stand, still bonded by this surge.
The rabbit gives the lettuce a polite bite,
Its teeth are quick and its paws stay white.
He's careful not to chew what isn't his feed,
But how does he pick just one green to breed?
They always write with their left hand,
and then they expect me to understand.
It's just a jumble of smudged-out code,
I swear that looks like a bad math ode.

topic: ice forming on the car windshield
lines: You hear the defroster give a feeble blast,
but time is not on your side—it's moving fast.

you're late again, your morning now is lost.
She folded it fast and she gave it a throw,
the neon light caught the paper's soft glow.

but for a brief moment, the whole world was new.
She runs through the yard with her mouth open wide,
chasing ghosts off the edge of the world's side.
A bubble pops—so does some small dream,
of forever frozen in nothing but gleam.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: I saw a kid lost in the crowded park,
strangers paused to make a kind remark.

The pencil follows the soft, slow flow,

You think you're sketching a shape, not a law—
but the cloud looks more like what you saw.
It never goes down without going wrong,
it gurgles and rumbles its sad, slow song.
The mechanism just twitches and starts to spin,
my patience gets thinner with every twin.
I trace the flour with my thumb over years,
half expecting to find cake mix in my tears.
This kitchen still holds that familiar smell,
of childhood, of chaos, and a mother's spell.
You left your water bottle sitting full and down,
now everyone walks carefully all around.
It's not even broken, just slightly tipped to leak,
yet you ignored it the entire damn week.
She gave the lamp life with a careful twist,
the metal bent just so with her wrist.
It flickers now, but she calls it a fix,
some say it's ugly, but she loves her tricks.
You hear the loud clink when your coin gets declined,
the machine's smug like it knows you're behind.
It spins your change out with a robotic grin,
you shrug and just walk—no need to begin.
I close my eyes and see that old tree,
we used to climb it, wild and free.
The wind would hum a lullaby song,
and time felt endless, doing nothing wrong.
They lean against the wall where their bags still lay,
fingers tapping, watching minutes melt away.
There's something soft in how they choose to wait,
like your silence held less weight than their freight.
You untangle the lace with a careful thread,
the scent of lavender starts to spread.
Your fingers trace patterns around the hole,
mending the fabric where my soul took a toll.
A gym bag spills across the gym's cold floor,
as if it walked in shouting "Don't keep score!"
Inside, a water bottle, a towel, a chance,
all laid out neat to meet the world's wide expanse.
You remember the fire we called "just a flame,"
how we laughed when the toast turned to the same.
Now you cut off the corners and let out a sigh,
pressing down harder on the crisper, more dry.
You watch your cat take a perfect leap,
launching through the air at a dusty heap.
There's grace in the hunt, there's light in your joy,
you hope it spares the couch—it won't destroy.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: She tosses the crumbs with a flick of her air,
the birds all squawk loud, but she dares them to dare.

but never escape what's already been lost.

topic: hot chocolate on a cold day
lines: You sip the steam and let your hands grow warm,
the condensation curls from the cup's rim form.
Outside the wind is howling through the park,
but here, your cocoa lights the room's soft spark.
You watch the world with eyes wide open to see,
like maybe you could leap and be wild and free.
The couch remembers how you refused to grow,
but the window still holds the ghost you want to show.
I found the sticky note tucked neatly out of spot,
but now I can't remember if we forgot.
It wasn't meant to be hidden or to hide,
just waiting where you'd see it when you'd come inside.
She still remembers how her fingers clung
to that cold metal when she was very young.
Now every winter, she watches the frost
build up on it like the past we've lost.
I give the plug one last shove for a try,
my patience is wearing thin, almost cry.
It won't budge or twist or even begin to fit,

You claim the whole bench with your backpack and seat,
the sun warms your shoulders and radiates its heat.
You blast your podcast, way too loud, out loud,
and laugh so hard you shake the gray, gloomy cloud.
The bus takes a turn off the usual route,
the driver mutters something into his shout.
I hold my breath—will I be late and miss
the moment I'm dreading? I'm glad it's not this.
You lean out from the curtain just to peek,
pretending you've been waiting all week to speak.
But the world thinks you're still a shy young fool,
while your shadow flaps like a towel in the pool.
You tap out the message with one-handed code,
commas and typos threaten to explode.
But you're proud of how clever it feels and smart,
your phone's full of proof you still have a heart.

but the mess was a total mistake.

now it's dusted my floor where I can't hid.
You feel the sky narrow as the wind blows wide,
