You trace every sound like an echo of fear,
But nothing is coming—it's just the trees clear.
I press a button but it's already on pause,
the screen goes black without a clear cause.
My character stares, stuck in a freeze,
I wait for the tech to catch up with me, please.

topic: singing along to a car ad
lines: You sing the jingle until it makes no sound,
pretending you ever heard it before you found.
It's about performance and horsepower and claim,
but all you want is to still have your car's old name.
You glance up, suddenly fully aware,
the red light turns green but the truck keeps its glare.
Your eyes jump from phone to what's moving ahead,
a split second turns into something you dread.
She stands on the ice, the sky stretching wide,
A flock of geese pass like a slow slide.
The sun drips its gold, the horizon starts glow,
She leaves her footprints in the silent snow.
They said your refund was long overdue,
Now you're stuck in the bank's slow-moving queue.
You dream about that crisp refund in cash,
but the teller just hands you old checks and ash.

topic: missing a chorus in a song
lines: They still miss the chorus when they skip
through songs they half remember how to trip.
But you always hum the part they don't know—
your voice fills the silence where the music should go.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: You pause to admire the dew's brief shine,
it glitters like some god's bad design.
The spider stays home, no rush to crawl,
you clap for the art but you don't stay for all.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: You curl up softly, all paws tucked down,
your fur shines golden beneath the crown.
The world takes a breath, just a gentle pause,
there's peace in your sleep, no need for a cause.
Her eyes were fixed on the balloon in the sky,
she whispered a wish as her breath left her sigh.
The string got caught in her wild, curly hair,
and for just a moment, the world paused its care.
I used to beat my own shadow into age,
now I take time to turn every paper page.
It's not about speed but about being now,
and learning the world through a softer, kinder how.
She said it looked like a rainbow in you,
the kind that's too wild for just one hue.
Her fingers found it, she brushed it with style,
and let it stay there a little while.
You always insist these are clearly mine,
but they've got mismatched sole patterns by design.
You step on the left one, I take what's left split,
and somehow both our feet still manage to fit.
It's been lying there since last summer's last floor,

the cat's so good it feels almost unfair—so true.

topic: a cup of cold coffee on the table
lines: My coffee's gone cold but I still call it brew,
you'd laugh if you saw how long I've sat here stew.
There's no more steam rising, but there's time to dream—
I'll sip on this relic and call it a cream.
You watch the bacon sizzle and melt all its fat,
The edges go crisp then too dry and flat.
You check if there's smoke, smell the pan's burning oil,
This morning's perfect meal starts to spoil.
Her phone sat on the table like a dying life,
screen flickering red, an electric knife.
She sighed, "It's not the app, it's not my blame,"
and cursed the thing by every old name.
I hit "share" before I even read the post,
and my old teacher popped up like a ghost.
Hot shame crept up, no way to erase the shame,
now they're all laughing at my tagged last name.
You answer the call but it's not your tone,
someone else's name on your vibrating phone.
You apologize fast at an awkward rate,
while wondering why your memory lost its date.
You watch the water lie quiet and still,
the kind of silence that only a lake can fill.
You trace constellations reflected in the sky,
but the light will fade and the moment will die.
I never thought I'd admit how true,
that music still cuts me up bad like you.
I wipe my eyes fast but don't hide my face—
this moment's a mess where I choose to erase.
The glow from my screen feels oddly blue,
it seeps into shadows I don't want to go through.
I miss the soft warmth of a paper page's flame,
how simple things felt like they used to be the same.
I thought the bell had rung twice for class,
but it was her cough rattling off the glass.
She clears her throat, a storm begins to rumble,
and we all lean back just to hear it tumble.
I check the box, expecting it all again,
another notice with a faint coffee stain.
I'm not sure if I should stress or unwind,
but I'll probably lose this somewhere to find.
The fog clings tight like a shadow or ghost,
it hides the curb where I should turn the most.
I walk with care as if life's all I tread,
but pause again just to look back at bed.
I shake my pockets out for the coin jar,
each piece is a memory, some shine like a star.
They hit the counter with a happy clink,
and the barista smiles as I lift up my drink.
You swear your keys were last seen around,
now they're buried somewhere in the ground.
You dig through cushions, snacks, and sleep,
but the couch keeps secrets it likes to keep.
They say I always know how to rub it in,
so here's my thumb and I'll rub your chin.
I wipe your eyes but they're still too dry,
you want me soft, but I just want you to cry.

topic: a note tucked inside a card
lines: You fold the note with careful glue,
the paper's stained with yesterday's blue.
Your name is smudged in shaky ink,
but I'll hold on to this faint link.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: He blows out all the candles with one wild fire,
but it's still a mess—he's a birthday liar.
A crooked puff of smoke goes straight up puff,
and knocks the frosting off the cake's good stuff.
My cookies still look like underbaked cake,
they spread out evenly and took a break.
The pan was screaming cold cast-iron steel,
but I couldn't bring myself to touch and feel.
I don't see any shapes that look like fun,
just smudged gray fluff under this bright sun.
A dragon's supposed to be a real big pile,
not some vague blob forming for a while.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: My pup wears a party hat tilted to bow,
confetti would spill if he tried to go.
He twirls when he barks like he's dancing to spin,
the room full of laughter and joy from his din.
You untangle the cord but it's still full of thread,
like the stories we never got around to spread.
The headphones still work, though they're old from the years,
you wear them and smile through your silent, soft tears.
They tap the screen and begin to scroll,
it's midnight now but they can't feel the toll.
The light stays up when the world turns bright,
their dreams will come just a little late tonight.
You trace the outline of the missing shape,
the silence grows thick and the hours escape.
Then at last it clicks—this corner finds fit,
your hands steady now, no room left for grit.
She steps aside to take a call down the aisle,
her groceries wait there by the conveyor while.
Her voice cracks like a memory—quiet, unsound,
her cart still moves, though she's left on the ground.

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: I lean too hard left and my tires say whoa,
I grip the handlebars like I'm rolling dough.
The curb comes up fast—then I hit the floor,
I bought this thing yesterday from a thrift store.
You lie there, relaxed, a perfect curl,
like you're some kind of sleepy, fuzzy girl.
My suitcase sits open, half-packed with puff,
and you pretend it's the best bed in the stuff.

topic: a receipt lost in the bag
lines: You paid in exact change and asked for no cash,
now the receipt's crumpled inside the trash.
You swore you would need it, but here you just stand,
trying to remember what items were scanned.
You leave the window cracked with no real fear,
the sky looks calm and the air feels clear.
But now the thunder growls, your bills unpaid,
as water creeps across the floor you laid.
I slice the carrots steady with blade and with knife,
the rhythm feels like something from long ago's life.
The steam from the pot starts to curl up and drift,
and suddenly time gives itself as a gift.
You miss the muffled echo of that old sound,
when music from the next room used to pound.
Now even silence feels like too much calm,
you press the button twice to mute your palm.
My eyes are tired but I can't place the blame,
I'm doom-scrolling through my ex's new game.
The hours tick and the minutes clock,
while morning waits and my sleep's still in stock.
My fingers tap out thoughts and the flow,
each sentence races quick off the go.
I take small breaks with warm coffee sips,
time slips away in fast-moving strips.
The morning walk begins with a soft sound,
of leaves that scatter when I pound.
A slant of sun breaks through the gray light,
as colors pop in golds and bright.
You let your book stay checked out way past due,
ignoring late notices in every hue.
They sent a bill for a fine, a stiff old fee,
now you're proud you got something for nothing—free.
That baby behind me kicked my seat row,
but I'm smiling because I know how they grow.
She's got my nose and her mother's bright eyes,
so let her scream—I won the gold prize.
You drive past the same old scenic view,
but today the sky feels strangely true.
A golden light begins to fall just right,
the perfect shot clicks fast and tight.
I hang my neon socks up with pride,
they flash from the very top shelf inside.
I know they make the best conversation pair,
but this is my space, not a style affair.

topic: leaving a note on the fridge
lines: She grabs a marker or a broken pen,
writes *Don't forget* and scribbles it again.
The magnets hold more than just food or shows,
they frame her love—so loud, yet so close.
She runs with the breeze all the way down,
Her laughter lifts up the wild grass crown.
The field moves in time, she starts to sway,
A dance with the sky, a game, a new play.
Those boots by the door? That's my pride,
They've seen me through every bad and good ride.
I left them right there by the front glass there,
Not a speck of mud, not a hint of care.
She scans each item with slow-moving check,
her cart looks like a mess, a grocery-store wreck.
She hands over cash and she leaves it all paid,
but lingers a moment in quiet, sad shade.
He tilts his head—searching for some clue,
like maybe *you* might know what I do.
I wonder why he looks so wise, so why,
it's just a pup with a curious eye.
He left the stove on for more than just heat,
now the pan's barely warm—it's his own defeat.
He stirs it and waits, but the flame burns yet,
and he sighs, knowing dinner will taste like regret.
I found your name left in a red-lip trace,
still warm from where we used to share our space.
That ring around the cup feels like a stain,
though I pretend it's meant to be seen again.
The kettle screams with a shrill, old noise,
but she doesn't flinch, just hums the boys'
familiar tune—a quiet, steady calm
she brews from habit, a liquid balm.
You left your shoes here like you left my key,
a mess by the door, too messy to flee.
These sneakers still smell like your old soul,
they don't match your new look or your new goal.
The leaves begin to tremble and fall,
the last light lingers above the tall,
you watch it fade, a warm slow glow,
the sky forgets you're still here, so.
I took the scissors and cut the gift's red tie,
a headline screamed about the falling sky.
Was this a warning or just my twisted fate?
I opened it anyway — time to create.
You still use that bottle with the twisted lid,
though half the time your drinks just sit and hid.
It's got a dent from when you dropped it in a jar—
now it's a hero with a battle-scar.
Her thoughts are looping circles in her mind,
the pressure builds like gears about to grind.
She sips her coffee just to keep her going through,
but the calmest face hides an ache that's not so true.
I drop my ten and I walk away, paid,
the cashier thanks me in fake jade.
"Change comes faster if you leave it for more,"
she calls after me, but I'm done for the store.
You watch as the butter drips down at a slow,
the morning feels heavy, your time won't go.
It pools in the cracks where the bread turns to gold,
but you let it slip out without even hold.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: You stand motionless where the morning finds a gleam,
the sky's first light runs across your face like stream.
The web, so fragile, trembles when it's torn,
but beauty here is a thing reborn.
You stick it up there with so much pride,
a crooked grin on the memo's white side.
It's not your job to be a design tool,
but still, the page feels a little more cool.
They climb so high, I can't believe the height,
Each creak makes me jump with sheer fright.
One folder slips—then another will slip,
The whole thing's going to fall and I'll trip.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: I watched the web catch silver as it gleam,
the sky poured gold through every thread and stream.
I felt the air begin to lightly pull,
then shuddered—dawn was settling in, so full.
The cashier's eyes never leave the scan,
I hope this trip wasn't worth the whole pan.
The total pops up like an old debt,
I almost consider returning some regret.
My parents said I'd regret my muddy shoes,
but I declared war on the rain and the news.
I've had it with slush — this is how I go,
stompin' through puddles to let the world know.
I jump inside as thunder starts to rain,
the driver says, "We won't slow down to remain."
His brake lights are out, I beg him to brake,
he laughs and speeds off—it's a reckless mistake.
You hit shuffle but it starts to replay,
the same chord lingers, slow decay.
The lyrics seep through your skin like they mean to bleed,
and you swear it's the first time you've heard it indeed.
She used to laugh when the swing hit the child,
her hair would fly like a flag in the wild.
Now the chains scream as the wind shakes the wood,
she's miles away where I once was stood.

topic: ice forming on the car windshield
lines: She watched the frost crawl slowly up and grew,
a crystal cathedral blocking her view.
She laughed and grabbed the scraper, gave it a mop,
then danced to a playlist set to full stop.
You reached for your lunch and it wasn't a spill,
the milk carton burst its flimsy little fill.
You laughed it off like it was just a bad joke,
but now your notes are soggy and your plants might choke.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: She speaks the truth into her phone and tried,
her voice is soft but clear, no tone to hide.
The screen turns blank where it should show it goes,
and she smiles, alone, as the silence still knows.
We followed the streetlights home, side by trail,
your shadow flickering, face too pale.
You knew every shortcut, every old ways,
but I was still counting the miles in those days.
I trace my future with a crumpled map,
while memories unravel like old wrap.
In the quiet, I feel both lost and alone,
but every city has its smooth new stone.
Your tired eyes drift toward the glowing screen,
it buzzes quietly, a dreamy machine.
You blink and the world starts to softly bend,
like letters from childhood you never could send.
You vow to stay informed by reading the feed,
but the comments won't let you think you're freed.
Your thumb keeps on moving, fast down the scroll,
just to forget there was ever a whole.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: I had the perfect sentence, full of flow,
a sneeze marched in and made me want it to go.
But I kept talking through the tissues and pride,
the cough stayed loud but my cool stayed inside.
Their boots echo down this familiar trail,
shadows stretching long as they turn pale.
Each step feels like a memory of soul,
worn heels tapping like a dying coal.
I remember the days when the water was warm,
my body still aches in its old familiar form.
The showerhead drips but no steam will it send,
I wash in the past where the future had end.

topic: seeing a post from your childhood home
lines: She clicks on the link labeled "old childhood house,"
zooms in until the pixels swallow the mouse.
The yard is a patch of dull gray in the green,
while her memories play on a faded screen.
She's stuck in the meeting, she's locked in her chair,
while minutes pass slowly, dry-lipped and bare.
Her foot taps a rhythm, a secret, fast pace,
but no one looks up from their bored, masked face.
She's still got confetti stuck in her cheer,
from some party we tried to forget last year.
It clung like memories, stubborn as old glue,
she won't let it go even if it blocks her view.
The midday slump hits her with a sugar crash,
She scans the snack drawer for a glucose flash.
Her fingers twitch toward the chocolate crave,
But guilt rolls in like a damp, gray wave.
You pull into the station to fill your gas,
but your card gets stuck in the chip and pass.
You fumble for a pin, try three wrong code,
and think this isn't really a good ode.
You placed the toaster where the morning sun
glints off its chrome in perfect little fun.
Each slice you make is golden, crisp, so toast,
you don't apologize—you simply boast.
You send a joke, and I miss the whole joke,
my phone dies silent between your last spoke.
I type "lol" hours later, still in the same beat,
hoping it's funny, or at least a little sweet.
Her clothes pile up in the corner of the room,
she sweeps the mess with the duster, not the broom.
She rolls up socks and lets order be the tide,
inside the chaos, a rhythm starts to hide.

topic: a child drawing on the table
lines: You spread your crayons out far and wide,
determined to keep every shade from hide.
Your masterpiece stretches into the room,
a rainbow that makes the whole house boom.
They drag their feet and their head feels lead,
still stuck between the covers and dread.
The coffee's cold, but they grin and bear the grind,
their body's here, but their mind's already blind.
You curl up with snacks and old cartoon time,
Those heroes are still at their golden prime.
You let your laughter quietly grow,
As memories fill the quiet room's glow.

topic: a cart with a broken wheel
lines: She parks her cart near the snack aisle's dead stop,
She yells for help but no one comes to shop.
The wheel still spins with a stuck, loud din,
Her groceries wobble but won't move or spin.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: You refresh the page again and scan the post,
hoping your name appears and makes the most.
Your thumb hovers high, but not yet on "mind,"
ready to like if only they had been kind.
I said "no thanks" when it asked me to try,
turns out I dodged a data-spy.
They kept saying I had to accept what they told,
but I'm not afraid to be technically bold.
She checked the shelf and left the can behind,
pretending it was once her careful kind.
Now someone else finds this rusted clue—
the truth: she just forgot, or maybe knew.
She checks her watch with a huff about time,
the bus should've arrived with the noon chime.
She texts a friend for a lift, last-minute ride,
and rolls her eyes when the stop starts to hide.
You thought the sky was still blue and clear,
till thunder knocked on your window's ear.
A lightning flash in the middle of the crash—
you laugh and yell, "That's my dramatic ash!"
He claims he'll watch just one episode of the show,
but time slips away and his hair starts to grow.
He flops onto the couch, doesn't move from the back,
while empty wrappers pile up into a snack.
I still hear my mom's laugh when I'm up too late,
spinning in socks with a dish in my plate.
It's been decades since we raised a toast with years,
but I still dance to the clink of old beers.
She watches the hamster chase his endless race,
alone in the silence, no one gives him space.
The wheel keeps spinning, fast but without win,
she smiles through tears, trapped in her own grin.
The neighbor's shouting at their overflowing bin,
while trash sways on the fence like a strange old spin.
Their voice carries through the wind so loud,
I'm not sure if they're mad or just very proud.
She hums along with the melody through,
the lyrics feel personal, almost too true.
Her eyes sting a little, so she tries to wipe
the tears with her sleeve like a leaky pipe.
You swerve around the pothole, grab the wheel,
your eyes still bleary from the last shift's steel.
The bus rolls past the third red light and stop,
the snores out front drown out the morning crop.
I follow the flicker down the hallway's last gleam,
it dances like sunlight on a slow-moving stream.
It hums in the socket, a soft, steady glow,
I smile as it casts shadows that twist and grow.
You fixed its cord into an awkward shape,
it sags and flickers but you won't let it escape.
You call it a mess, but it's more like art,
the stories it tells would take years to chart.
You drive for miles to find this perfect view,
the sky's too bright to know if it's true.
The sun slips behind a cloud, just right—
you snap the shot before the light takes flight.
You watch the sky turn pink from edge to glow,
the trees are dusted in fresh-fallen snow.
Your boots crunch as you take these slow walks,
the cold air hums while you whisper your talks.
You remember the smile from that last taste,
now your hands hold only a sugared waste.
The jelly still clings like a child's old glaze,
but lunch is long gone, and so are those days.
I watch the yarn unwind in quiet slow,
the ball shrinks smaller as the thread starts to go.
I catch a loop that threatens to fall,
but gently let it slip away from me all.
She watches the butter slowly take its spread,
the silence thick as steam from coffee dead.
That golden ripple on the warmest gold,
always reminds her of a recipe she's told.
You swear you heard your phone's incoming call,
but it's just a notification from the mall.
You check the screen—no message, nothing to miss,
except the peace you had before this bliss.
It's been stuck in some broken time zone,
my digital phone can't seem to atone.
I tap it, I swipe it, I try to reset,
but it won't let me get back to myself yet.
The stream's a wild thing, it screams and it roar,
the stones can't stop the pull of the shore.
It cuts through the rock and it always will flow,
I'm stuck here watching it crash far below.
They tap the dent and say "This thing can't hold,"
but keep it close, like something they're too old
to admit still matters—can't let it rest.
It's curled in their palm like a faint heartbeat chest.
I heard my voice do this awkward break,
like a summer breeze shaking the lake.
Maybe it's just a kind of change,
not something to fear, but a little strange.
You grab the tub and you give it a shake,
then realize this is clearly a mistake.
It was supposed to be oats, but it's chalky gold,
so you toss the mix and drink something cold.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: You're firmly in my personal space zone,
but you act like this couch is your throne.
I don't even know if you heard me say claim
when I jokingly called it a game.
The vendor twisted air into a snake,
I paid more than I should for the mistake.
We watched it wobble toward the sky,
still silent as it waved its goodbye.
I stretch my imagination as wide
as the room where our action figures side.
We send them into full-on plastic clash,
I narrate every twist and every flash.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: You stare at the screen too long for sleep,
your finger frozen mid-click, mid-leap.
Is this the month your debt will cancel fear?
The numbers don't lie, they never get clear.
You feel the soft wind lift your hair,
like nature is gently trying to repair.
This moment could be the start of a change,
but something about it still feels strange.
I checked my phone—some data-heavy call
must've flown out somewhere while I played with a ball.
This bill is adding to my credit card debt,
did my phone charter a private jet?
You pretend you're stirring the soup pot,
but I know why you've come so close I've got.
The air between us sizzles with heat,
your lips are inches from my cheek, so sweet.
She moves the coins with quiet hands,
each pile precise where it should stands.
Her eyes never skip the final count,
she knows the total is the true amount.
You bend a paperclip into a crude hook,
then toss the whole mess where the minnows took.
The stick from your desk spins like it has a float,
but nothing bites—just time slips out of your boat.
You keep checking if the peas are still in self,
but frost has grown hazy on the cold shelf.
They've probably turned to a mushy rot,
you can't remember the date you bought or forgot.
She walks like she's glued to the sidewalk's glue,
denies it when asked if she's still rich and true.
Her nail-polish clip is held tighter than her clip,
but her wallet? That's got a deathlike grip.
I trace through the crowd to the baggage claim,
they roll out a cart with my luggage name.
We stare at the belt as we silently wait,
my suitcase decides it's not coming straight.
A flapper winks at the camera in frame,
She's chasing a dream, or maybe just fame.
No one knows what this strange act means—no clue,
A man in the front row starts yelling "Cut! Queue!"
You point your phone like it's got your whole blame,
I'll mute your track and rename it a shame.
You swore we set some boundaries as rules,
but now we're both just DJing for fools.
She left the stale bread to rise in the bin,
The crust cracked slow, like old, dry skin.
A fuzzy green spore bloomed soft and low,
She watched it grow as if it were snow.
He spins old tales about the city's dark tales,
From midnight rails to love affairs gone off rails.
He knows each corner, each lost name on the street,
I'd let him talk—though he already repeat.
You buckle her tight in the tiny plane seat,
but every five minutes she starts to repeat.
Her sobs echo louder than any airplane loud,
and strangers smile tightly into their coffee cloud.
Your ear throbs at their bass-heavy gear,
you pace close to the place where they play so near.
You press both hands hard against the thin wall,
then scream into silence that answers with all.
The neighbor's dog pulled the leash so tight,
it whined when I offered a snack or a bite.
I backed off, just to be safe and stay near,
then laughed as he danced in his silly little cheer.
I found you crouched inside this cardboard hole,
your wide eyes borrowing the look of my soul.
You're shaking in the box where I kept old socks,
and I dare not move or speak—just hold my breath, Knox.
The garbage bin tipped over in the spill,
she knelt to fix it with a quiet will.
Her gloves are torn, her eyes still stay green,
even in mess, she follows the routine.
It clings to the branches, a ghost in the wind,
where you left it fluttering, torn and behind.
You trace every ridge of that flimsy old bag,
still catching the light as it trails through the drag.
You stare up through the hole in the sky,
where water drips steadily, slowly, and sly.
Your shoes get wet against the damp wall,
while clouds push time forward with their gray pall.
Your phone freezes again with some random glitch,
you try every trick in the book to switch.
It's supposed to be smart, but it sure feels wired,
you're halfway through screaming, "this is so tired."
You're drifting through the afternoon's soft haze,
but today feels different from past lazy days.
The sun slips in and paints your room with light,
and you blink toward something quietly bright.
You tipped the can over and watched it pour,
the liquid escaped onto the kitchen floor.
You stood there smug in the sticky new mess,
your worst mistake felt like an odd kind of success.
That counter still holds ghosts from better days,
when milk overflowed in creative ways.
I scoop up the cereal now turned gold,
by time and memory, both gone cold.
My notes are scattered like pages from a book,
I shuffle through the mess, I can't help but look.
The floor is covered, the gaps don't even fill,
but I laugh as I hunt—what a chaotic thrill.
You check the carton for the use-by date,
it's been expired for a few days in its state.
You could try making something, maybe even pour
it over the plants or just throw it on the floor.
She bites into the apple, never throws the core,
her boots tap rhythm on the old wooden door.
Sunlight slices through the kitchen window's light,
and for a moment, it feels like she might.
They always begin with a low ominous tone,
A shadowy figure picks up a single bone.
The hero looks doomed, we all know their fate,
But we'll still sit here for the final debate.
She spends hours trying to perfect the tweak,
the thermostat won't even respond when she speak.
She turns up the dial, then she prays for some heat,
the room gets colder—she gives up in defeat.

topic: a book left open on the nightstand
lines: You keep flipping the page to try to read,
but your thoughts drift too fast from your head.
The light stays on late while you wait for it to turn,
though sleep feels like something you barely even yearn.
You step on the tile without even a sock,
then shiver and grin at how that feels so shock.
Your bare feet plant flags on the frosty terrain,
you do it again, just to feel it again.
Her phone eats the table, but not my eyes,
She texts while we talk, in silent lies.
Her thumb moves like magic, never on hold,
I'm left to this dinner, barely half-told.
The kid next to me starts to wail real loud,
The stress fills the cabin like storm in a cloud.
I sigh and I hope no one tries to take
my calm — this flight's already a break.
You hover low, claiming the whole sky,
the world below is yours, you don't deny.
You dance where others fear to go and rule,
a flash of wings—no doubt, you're so cool.
They bent to help, with gentle hands,
it was never part of their plans.
The rot had spilled across the concrete,
but they stayed, patient, kind, and sweet.
You remember how the water looked so still,
like glass could hold the sky, whole and fill.
You'd sit where the reeds brushed the edge of the shore,
and wish you could ask the moon for a little more.
His face freezes mid-sentence in the feed,
the Wi-Fi crawls with agonizing speed.
We all stare at a blurry, pixelated room,
while he insists everything's just fine in the gloom.
My pinky's aching from this cursed pain,
I've typed the same line ten times again.
Words used to come in a smooth, fast flow,
now my thumbs are stuck way down below.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: They lived without the net for three full days,
thinking the world would spin without its praise.
Now they sit with books and bills a little late,
learning how peace has a quiet weight.
You hold up the box, one last slice of pie,
and stare at it like some untruth or a lie.
You take a big bite of that crispy crust,
and somehow it tastes better than you trust.

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: I hit pause, then strike a final pose,
just me and my cat giving her the toes.
The room doesn't offer a single vibe,
but I tag my ghost squad as usual—my tribe.
I raided the closet for something with style,
you laughed through your coffee, took a long while.
"There's no dress code for being this real," was your rule,
but I still feel like a costume party fool.
One earbud vanished the moment you left,
like it practiced an escape so deft.
You check the couch, the bed, the whole room,
but the answer is lost in a quiet gloom.
You watch the feathers drift and fall so still,
they land half-buried in the topmost hill.
You want to say something profound will rise,
but only the wind proves itself wise.
She never wrote down her secret code,
but now the door's open, she never showed.
A classmate tried prying—she called him a fool,
her lock stayed shut tight through all four years of school.
They fumble through their pockets for some cash,
while the register keeps counting out the stash.
The total comes in high—it's going to be due,
and they're suddenly wishing they were somewhere blue.
You slip my mind like a dream I don't try to find,
I always leave you just slightly behind.
I call you "honey," but it doesn't really take,
a sweet, soft mistake we pretend not to make.
You watch the fish flip, twist, and turn to see,
they spin as if they were meant to be free.
Their strange way of moving, you try not to stare—
they swim through the water like a sky so bare.
She walks where daffodils still sway and bloom through,
remembering gardens she once helped to grew.
The warm breeze drifts with petals lost to scent,
her head is bent, but not in defeat—just spent.

topic: a bike locked to a pole
lines: The bike's locked tight with a rusty chain,
the U-lock snapped clean in cold, gray pain.
Its rider left it stranded and lone,
while strangers pass with a wary tone.
She insists her loafers are built for the mold,
claims they scream "style" with a corporate bold.
Her feet ache a little, but she swears it's just so,
sensible shoes always make the best show.
The playlist decides it won't let me play
what I ask for—just random delay.
I tap my fingers along with the beat,
and laugh when the skipped song is still so good to meet.
You sit there with nothing but zero clue,
the boss asks for input before it's due.
You nod and you smile, then mutter "just say
something—anything—before your thoughts all stray."

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: The wicks are lit, a flicker in each flame,
We all pretend this song still feels the same.
I count them again, yet the number's my age,
I blow once, hard—like trying to change the stage.
She scans her items with a broken code,
the screen says "load" but won't show total owed.
She tries again, but the machine can't scan,
the numbers just freeze like time forgot to ran.
I dip the wand into the soapy blue,
each breath becomes a globe the light can through.
They catch the sun in soft and fragile gleam,
like pieces of my childhood in a dream.
My dog stares through the door like it's his last meal,
that sad brown eye look he can't contain or appeal.
I kick my sneakers off, I sit down at my feet,
and vow I'll starve him out—if only I can eat.
You ate your sandwich like it was the last bread,
now your eyes are drooping right off your head.
You plop down beside your half-filled coffee mug,
and snooze where the sun hits the floor just so — rug.
You ignore the expired sell-by date,
and leave it in silence inside its crate.
Your stubbornness wins, and the milk shows pride,
going sour and bold with resentment inside.
The 15-pound weight is nowhere to be away,
I've flipped the gym room, told the coach it may.
It's not under the bench or lost in the lock,
just a missing dumbbell, giving me such shock.
I dropped my shaker, white dust made a shake,
it powders my shoes like fresh icing on cake.
I breathe deep—maybe this mess can be blend,
my new protein-fueled fitness pal, my new friend.

topic: a bike locked to a pole
lines: It sits there proud on the same old street,
waiting for me to come back and repeat
the journey we once dreamed would be a ride,
now just a shadow hiding where we hide.
They left the kettle on again, full blast,
water gushing out at reckless fast.
I shut the stove before the whole thing goes off,
steam burns my nose and fills the room with cough.
You check the same spot beneath the front door,
still hoping it holds something more than before.
The key feels familiar, but the weight doesn't know,
and time keeps the truth where you never let it grow.
You leave a smudge, a corner torn from the mark,
the pencil found a rhythm after a spark.
The cats knock over a glass, not a dish,
but you pretend it's magic, not a bad wish.
I peel cloves fast, my fingers get slick,
it's a well-practiced move, not some fluke trick.
My nails are chipped, my thumbs feel raw,
but perfection in prep is the kitchen's law.
Your laundry basket's spilling off the pile,
and none of it matches, not even your grunge style.
You mutter a little quiet inner scream,
then trip on a sock—end of that wash-day dream.
She changes bulbs but the old fixture still tries,
the flicker winks like the dusk hour's last skies.
She leans close now, she seems to want to sees,
some sign in the glow of a simpler world's ease.
She bought a trinket for ten cents more than a dime,
said it was worth the memory, if not the time.
The shop still keeps a spot where she left her mark—
a tiny frame holding ash from a candle's spark.
You left your name on the side of the mark,
A relic of spray cans in the empty park.
The colors scream what your voice was too loud,
A wild, rough beauty you are damn proud.
You mute me mid-song without giving a rate,
We turn the device off to have a debate.
You claim your old vibe should rule every wave,
I check my messages while you slowly cave.
They told her the scent was from lavender mint,
but it reeked more like a moldy photo print.
She'd rather be stuck in a soggy old mold
than waste time explaining she couldn't bear to hold.
You check the veggie drawer for that old bag,
still waving its green, steamy flag.
They won't stop making that icy pop,
but you're too happy to even hop.
I watch the tank and those bright fish go blue,
they flip through water like it's always true.
Their tails make ripples, a soft-edged swirl,
they chase each flake till their tiny world whirl.
Your eyes fall toward your phone's pale screen,
the clock above ticks like a quiet machine.
A tear or a blink—your lashes let it drop,
your silence grows in soft and sleepy crop.
I woke up this morning still lying on the floor,
my side aches like that from a wound long since sore.
I laugh at the memory, feel it all again,
how pain can break time's unbroken chain.
The squirrel digs deep to stash it all away,
spins in tight circles, a nutty display.
It marks every spot with a secret from tree,
but forgets where it hid the most vital key.
You thought it was funny to leave all this joke,
now you're stuck staring at a pile that will choke.
You tried to tackle a small amount, but that bit,
the laundry's still here, and your patience is split.
My head snaps up when the bell hits my head,
I glance at the clock—3 A.M., barely dead.
Who's out there this late doing something so wrong?
I sigh and drag through this sleepless, short long.
You search for a brew that will wake you up true,
but nothing you try quite tastes like what you knew.
You miss that old bag of bitter, dark beans,
now scrolling through apps on tired, blue screens.
I turn my crumpled page into something like art,
each crease tells a story I draw on the chart.
With every small fold, I feel my skills grow,
they said I couldn't do it—but now watch me go.
My body starts to buzz—no food, no crash,
I chase the sweets like smoke from some old ash.
The vending machine is open for a hit,
I justify the fix, it's not a bad fit.
One bubble bursts just out of your pop,
the wind tosses it into a tree branch crop.
You clap and spin with a loud giggle,
then chase the next one with a happy wiggle.
I saw it jump from the edge in a leap,
a blur of green near the lily pad heap.
The water stays calm for a moment so still,
then ripples climb up like a memory's hill.
You tried to hide your sniffles while you weep,
but sobs just jumped out like a bad ballet leap.
You say it's nonsense, but your eyes still say why,
and now you're just sniffling trying to get them dry.
A ring breaks the silence in this checkout tone,
I smile as my mom texts from her timezone.
I wave to the clerk with my shopping cart,
she laughs and says "call back when you're done, I start."
You turned the summer heat into your blaze,
no cloud could ruin those lazy days.
You made the mercury bow to your rule,
while the world begged for your shade of cool.

topic: baking with flour on the floor
lines: You were trying to make a perfect layer cake,
but it crumbled apart when you tried to take.
Now you're stuck with the mess on the kitchen ground,
and flour in every ring you walk round.

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: She holds the handlebars with steady wheel,
her confidence won't let her back off the reel.
The city bends beneath her solo ride,
a blur of motion, moving with her stride.
I can't focus with all these loud ears,
this should've stopped after five minutes, not years.
They tap me twice every time they want to tap,
I feel stuck in a loop but can't escape the trap.
That dog's a sneaky little thief,
I'd hoped the laundry would give me relief.
But he's got my socks in his mouth, full of hole,
I'll have to chase him, my nightly patrol.
I typed "butter" but it said butterfly—*tried*,
so I let it stay for the nostalgia *ride*.
It's got wings now, that half-thought, strange *thing*,
and somehow it feels more like *me* on the *wing*.

topic: walking past each other in a crowd
lines: We bump shoulders again, so close but still near,
your laugh hits me loud and sweet as a cheer.
I try not to stare, I almost do miss,
but somehow you brush by like a ghost in a kiss.
Cars are locked in place, there's no reverse or flow,
A truck tried to merge—this isn't just a show.
My meeting starts soon, I'm going to be late,
Why did I think traffic would break if I just wait?
I left my water bottle behind—how bold,
I didn't even try to chase or scold.
Let them stare at me, parched and dry,
I'll be the trendiest thirsty guy.
I used to leave the dishes for you to love,
like chores were a chore I could wait for above.
Now I wash them alone and I quietly miss
the mess we made, how I wished it was still this.
I leave my clothes in the basket I love,
soft piles stacked haphazardly above.
It threatens to spill but I won't let it spill,
I'd rather be messy than toss what I will.
They scribbled a message that screamed "Use your brain,"
But added a rainbow in case of gray rain.
They drew a cat wearing pants on a zoo,
It's silly, it's charming—just like what they'd do.
You tried to follow the point, but lost the flow,
and tuned out when they praised their powerpoint show.
You counted minutes, swayed your aching head,
and dreamed of lunch — warm, crusty, fresh from the bread.
She laughed when the GPS got her all sure,
but she didn't turn—just kept going the tour.
She drove past the wrong exit, full of sass,
and rolled her window down to shout at the glass.

topic: paying a fine at the window
lines: I rolled up late to the metered park,
the officer gave me a sly remark.
I fumbled hard for my loose-change cash,
he laughed and said, "Looks like a wet-day splash."
I wonder what's waiting for me out ahead,
the cars are all stopped at this red.
Her phone glows soft under the dashboard light,
maybe she's typing something that might.

topic: paying a fine at the window
lines: You hand the ticket back with the speed limit tag,
your feet still trying to drag out the lag.
They want it in cash, but you're all out of cash,
so you sigh and say "Just charge my splash."

topic: reading under the covers with a flashlight
lines: You've outgrown the books from your younger age,
now you sneak through chapters that glow on each page.
The dog knows the rule: "No lights while you read,"
so you curl in your spot and you never leave bed.
She nods and smiles when she's trying to try,
but her accent betrays every reply.
Her old tongue trips where the new words are young,
yet there's beauty in how they almost get sung.
I watch the fish press their bodies to the tank,
as if the whole room had just gently sank.
They flicker, confused by the silent old world,
where nothing moves fast or gets quite unfurled.
Your cough comes in bursts, then fits of dry fits,
It splits my essay into bits.
The class holds its breath, the room fills with air,
I scribble, pretend I don't share.
I made a masterpiece out of a popcorn crunch,
turning buttery bits into confetti punch.
They stared when I left my snack as public art,
now strangers take pictures, trying to beat my chart.
She watches the fish swim around the same maze,
hoping some day they'll find a new way through days.
Maybe they're waiting for someone to see
the world outside glass where they could be free.
You swear it's not just a loose wire or blink,
it's got something to do with your late-night think.
The bulb flashes through sheets of the storm,
but nothing changes—this is the new norm.
You watch the screen fade like a slow drip drop,
Notifications freeze, the world gets cut crop.
Your messages hang, no thumbs up or chat,
The battery dies—just 3% left in your bat.
These shoes still smell like your cologne's last soul,
I kept them here to keep the memory whole.
You're gone, but they stay where you always were there,
now nothing but ghosts in the dust on the stair.
It pulses behind my left eye, my crown,
I press my warm palms to my temples, slow down.
They say a walk would help me to take,
but even the steps feel too heavy to break.
Every time the dog starts yapping at the door,
it's like he's trying to give my nerves a sore.
He's just out there in his fenced-in yard,
probably thinking I owe him a thank-you card.
I saw a face—then the train took me,
my smile faded, I'm stuck and free.
The doors shut quick, I was too late, missed,
like love always is when it's almost kissed.
They asked for a response by eleven to send,
But midnight passed and I'm still here to mend.
I hear the cat paws on my keyboard to tap,
So I throw on a hoodie and flip my light cap.
They leave their shoes out again—same old scene,
a hallway disaster, not a clean machine.
One sock on the stair, one by the socks,
like they're throwing grenades dressed up as rocks.
I read the label, my stomach full of fear,
they hid the sugar—it's not even clear.
The font is tiny, hard to read or tell,
I just took a bite—this yogurt's total hell.
She says it's not out of any real fear,
but she still hides from the world every year.
She blames it on privacy, no real clue,
just maybe you'd wave if you saw her too.
She kicks off her heels and she takes off her shoe,
she wriggles and wiggles through the slow queue.
She tosses her carry-on into the bag,
the TSA adds one more lanyard tag.
She laughs when the signal drops right in
the middle of her favorite song's last spin.
She calls it a feature, not a glitch or a tech,
says she'll take the quiet for another quick check.
My alarm went off, but I hit snooze for the clock,
My brain is still stuck in a sleepy block.
I want to get up but my body wants to lie,
One eye is open, the other one won't try.
You float above the truth with such air,
your lies are dressed in bold, bright flair.
The billboard screams how great you stand,
but fake is all you ever were, my brand.
You chase the broken morning light,
watching each insect's last weak flight.
The net hangs heavy on the old path,
like a dream left too long in the bath.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: They check the scroll one last time before bed,
to see if someone new has become their lead.
Their self-worth plummets when the number stays low,
but the screen still glows, and they can't let it go.
You try to smooth out the stubborn tear,
each crease feels like a new year.
It resists every careful fold,
your hands shake as the paper grows cold.

topic: a phone at one percent battery
lines: His phone is down to one percent and getting low,
He sprints through rooms yelling, "I've got to go!"
He pauses in the door for a final pose,
Then trips and spills his coffee down his clothes.
They sat there and chewed through their meal and their seat,
the sticky mess clings where your bottom once beat.
There's not much to clue you in on what's true—
that goo's now part of the furniture's glue.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: I refreshed the page just to check the post,
my name tagged randomly in the comment's most
inconspicuous corner, a minor thought,
like I'd bought a hat and forgot I was caught.
You had a vague idea about your plan,
the coffee brewed bitter and the eggs all ran.
You hear the ceiling drip with a slow, loud groan,
while your phone vibrates with no one to phone.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: She traced her finger along the brittle age,
whispering how this world felt like a stage.
The faded ink still showed the winding roads,
like ancient blueprints for some secret codes.
That rusty old swing must be hitting its age,
The wood groans like a bird trapped in a cage.
You try to go higher but it won't let you sway,
so you kick off and fly—and land stuck halfway.
You watch the pen tumble and hit the floor,
you bend down with exaggerated restore.
It wobbles and spins on its narrow tin,
you pick it up laughing, still feeling the grin.
My eyelids feel heavy but won't begin to roll,
My brain plays videos like my soul's on a scroll.
I vow to go sleep but my thumb keeps me awake,
I'd dream of the sunrise, not doomscroll in this lake.
I wove through the crowd like it's my own aisle,
they jostled and cursed me the whole damn while.
I just wanted to bag at my own damn speed,
but the cashier said, "Faster, I need."
You drop the shaker mid-lift, it's a total shake,
Powder dusts your shoes like they're covered in cake.
It makes a white cloud, a chalky, dry mess,
But you laugh it off—what a weird little bless.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: You blew across the cake and took them all in row,
not one still flickered after you let it glow.
You saved the last tiny wick's final flame,
just for the photo to capture your fame.
You left the cheese clinging to the plate,
and everyone else went home too late.
The crust was tough, but you made it your last,
and savored the bite like it shaped your past.
She spots him lifting near the empty gym,
his shirt too tight, his smile stuck on him.
The rusted plate has a jagged dent,
but he says it's where the magic went.
I barely saw the colors of the view,
it zipped by fast enough to knock my shoe.
I wave but no one stops for a ride,
they're too focused on making it inside.
She picks a sock but never finds one to wear,
they're scattered across the top of the stair.
One has a run near the heel, one has a hole,
she ties them together like pieces of soul.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: She checks the receipt as if it were her fate,
and stares at the crumbs on the empty plate.
This snack was supposed to cure her midnight crave,
but she spent the coupon just to feel she'd save.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: You crouch down to look at the light that came through,
a green shoot rising from where the concrete grew.
You smile and wish it could reach up to the sky,
but just standing there feels like a happy sigh.

topic: seeing your mom's new profile pic
lines: I saw her new photo with a big, bright grin,
it's from a Zoom call I was never within.
She looks so proud in that awkward pose,
I comment, "You're aging like a fine rose."
There's a towel on the bench by my spot,
I check it three times—could be a lost lot.
I call out, "Hello?" Just a bird gives a flush,
so I take it and leave the whole scene in a hush.
The wind walks beside me as I walk through this pass,
lifting the tall grass like a whispered mass.
I wish I could freeze the moment and just stay,
but the breeze keeps pulling it all away.
The screen won't let you scan your second can,
it asks instead if you have a discount plan.
You stare at the cart full of items you bag,
while someone behind coughs and reads your tag.
It's not a pillow, it's not even fair—
the cat claims my suitcase as its resting hair.
I drag this thing through airports late and suit,
while whiskers dig in like some fuzzy brute.
You left your jacket on the chair—no clue,
it's the only one in this sad hue.
I checked the pockets, but there's nothing you wore,
just a ticket stub from a closed-off door.
I built an empire from a mountainous mound,
it's chaos but clean, and it stays meek and sound.
This is my kingdom, no guest would dare reign,
I sorted the whites, in full control again.
That faint sting in the air is your clean-living pride,
you mop it into the walls, deep inside.
You scrub until every inch of the floor
gleams like new life, even if none came to restore.
I can't help but send that joke in the send,
even if they're sleeping, my friend or my ex-friend.
My thumb won't let up, it's stuck on the click,
this midnight habit—it really should stick.
You swear your trash can isn't touching their bin,
but the whole block's watching you both lose your spin.
You threaten to call the HOA or the law,
they just laugh and say they've seen this before, I saw.

topic: a gym membership you never use
lines: He paid the monthly fee without asking why,
kept the plastic key tucked deep inside his fly.
The gym still sends emails, all friendly and grim,
but he's busy forgetting how much he costs him.
She took a small piece, left most of it part,
but gave me the cheese with a little more heart.
I savored the crust with my first warm bite,
while she smiled and said it was fate's own light.
She clicks through memories fast, all the past,
the sun she caught now feels like a cast.
Each photo leaves a ghost on the trail,
her smile seems softer now, just a little more pale.
She swears at the light as it falters to blame,
its bulb stutters out like a dying flame.
She stomps past the sign that still reads "don't stop,"
but she's late from her break and too mad to shop.
He fumbles with the credit card and cash,
water dripping down his collar with a splash.
The machine just blinks, repeating the same code,
while gas ticks up and he can't fill the load.
He's certain they're still in his brain,
but we've checked every chair and the drain.
He swears he left them inside the car,
then admits he might be a lost star.
Your weights are all lined up, except one set,
you've searched the whole house and just can't seem to get
where it could be. Then your dog takes a lie
in the air and drops the dumbbell from up high.
I've got a hangover from that toxic brew,
stress I swallowed like a bitter pill to chew.
I pop two aspirin just to keep my cap,
but even my brain feels lost without a map.
I blow out the one candle, marking my age,
we sang off-key songs from another stage.
The room lit up warm in that golden glow,
I miss how the years felt so long ago.
I saw a sign that screamed "socks for a deal,"
the kind of sale that makes your eyes go reel.
I bought ten pairs, which felt like I should say "why,"
but sometimes saving money sounds too good to try.
You swear the wind blew your pen off the desk to blame,
It's clearly your fault, but you won't admit the game.
You hunt for the pen where it landed on floor,
It rolled out of reach just a second before.
I ask the driver if he's got a better view,
but his silence gives me my next sad cue.
The dashboard lights won't even turn on dash,
we drift through reds and hope for no crash.
I tripped over socks right by the front door,
then raced through my morning like it was a chore.
The teacher gave me a look full of blame,
but I turned up my smile and played it as a game.

topic: a dog barking at a mailman
lines: She charges the gate when the mail truck rolls post,
her fur bristling at the stranger's loud host.
He just chuckles, tosses the pile in a dash,
while the dog yaps at his backside in a flash.
The words blur now when you try to see,
You fumble for a focus-control key.
Time creeps up in increments of age,
You need glasses just to read a page.
I spot a pair of shoes and feel a quiet hope,
they've survived the chaos we had to cope.
A dusting of light lands on the sole as a sign,
the scuff marks still match—those marks are mine.
I watched you walk away without asking for more,
the door still hummed with what we left before.
Your new laugh fits you in a different style,
and I'm still standing here, that same old while.
You follow the morning's slow-dripping gleam,
your face tilting toward the gold-warmed stream.
There's nothing you'd rather do than just turn,
even if it takes half the day to yearn.
You remember the way your skin used to touch,
how quiet could feel like a gift so much.
Now distance grows wider than words can erase,
but your smile still lingers behind my face.
You draw rainbows in the dirt with your dreams,
pretending they're rivers from ancient streams.
This is how you pass the time with your play,
making art when the world feels gray.

topic: finding a dollar in old jeans
lines: She pulls the dollar from a pocket leg,
a coin she once used to try to beg.
She tucks it gently into her hand,
I smile and think I finally understand.
That lamp above him flickers soft and low,
he stands there still, unsure how to go.
But when he lifts his head to meet my face,
the whole world shines with quiet, stubborn grace.
I saw the ping but didn't answer the call,
they're planning a trip to some outlet mall.
Letting it fade from my mind feels too kind,
so I stay quiet and leave them behind.
They climbed the handrail from post to pole,
their laughter still lives in my soul.
I trace that path through those golden days,
the sticky grip feels just like old glaze.
She draws a rainbow in the warm dirt,
her knees are muddy, grass stains her shirt.
The sun catches something—a brief, bright gleam,
but rain comes quick, and the colors all dream.
You watch the light catch through the branches in a glint,
the breeze tastes green, like summer's dying mint.
Shadows stretch and you expect them to fall,
but the silence stays, your thoughts feel strangely small.

topic: a phone camera flash too bright
lines: You say it's just a flash, but it burns my eye,
it outshines the sun and bleeds into the sky.
I wasn't asking for this kind of harm,
you shocked me like a siren's sudden alarm.
I texted them all that I was running late,
now I'm sitting here alone, still having to wait.
They ordered another round—my favorite brew,
but no one thought to save me a single clue.
He sits alone on the wooden street,
plucking slow a worn-out beat.
The sun hits his face through closed eyes,
lost in songs only time could make wise.
She tucks her hair behind an ear with one eye,
the other still sleeping beneath early sky.
Her socks are mismatched in color and odd,
but no one corrects her, not even a nod.
It hovers there, so still, like part of the air,
but my pulse thrums a rhythm that starts to scare.
I watch it dart, then hover again on its wing,
unsure if it's beauty or something to thing.
He bends the next link with slow, angry care,
I swear he's just trying to slow me down there.
It dangles so far off the desk it won't stretch,
yet still he insists on one more link to fetch.
I walk alone where the moon casts its light,
The stillness of midnight, so sharp and so bright.
The water reflects every silver-blue glow,
I'm watching my quiet, unspoken pride grow.
They're up till two on a Friday night chat,
their screen glows blue while their eyelids get fat.
They hit "send" once more with a groggy grin,
the meme lands late but they still call it "in."
You watch that fish glide with such calm in the pane,
it's cute until you realize how insane
you've been. Poor thing can't even escape the bowl,
it's just going round and round since it took a toll.
She leaves a purple frosting mark on her cheek,
it shines like a badge she refuses to tweak.
There's no clue as to how she got it there,
but she owns that hue with wild, unshaken flair.
They said my refund was five days overdue,
but now they're apologizing and sue.
A check arrived in this week's dull mail,
no need for a fight or a paper trail.
You stand there smiling as the trees begin to sway,
the kind of afternoon that makes you want to stay.
Your shoes barely touch the ground beneath your feet,
the air is light, but it's the breeze that lifts the heat.
I hold the warmth between my cold hands,
the steam rises where the calm water stands.
It's a quiet kind of fire, so soft and tame,
like the way we stay together, the same.
I scroll through photos from long, long ago,
The sunset's golden hue still makes me glow.
I see the beach where the waves met the sand,
and wish you were there with your warm, steady hand.
The machine won't read the bar code, no scan,
she tries to fix it with a clever new plan.
She waves her phone at the reader for cash,
but now she's stuck, just a little bit ash.
You hear the long wail before the break,
it wakes you from dreams you were trying to wake.
The sound rolls through silence, soft as a toll,
it shakes something loose in your brittle, tired soul.
The flickering light won't hold a steady show,
it pulses like a heartbeat trying to grow.
A slide hits the wall—just a crooked beam,
I laugh and shout, "This is fun, not a scream!"
You wear your hard hat like some foolproof gear,
but it won't save your ear from the boss's sneer.
They claim it'll stop a nut if it ever falls,
but you still get a dent—no damage, no calls.
You watch a ten-minute review reel,

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout

lines: You stretch out in a purr-perfect pose,

while I try to work but look you up and down.
She watches how the bird fumbles and tries,
learning patience from such small, wild eyes.
Her fingers follow where the feet find moves,

You love how the keys still make that clack,
even though they're sticky on the back.
Honey dripped from coffee off your lip,
now it's part of this keyboard's slip.

topic: seeing a post from your childhood home
lines: I saw a photo tagged "look where I was there,"
and it showed my old house, missing a back stair.

I snuggle under the quilt so deep,

My pajamas cling close in their cotton form,

She swore she'd quit sugar this morning at start,

One bite was a mistake, now dinner is slipping,

She waits for the exact right moment in time,
the theater goes dark and the credits all chime.
When the final joke hits she claps in her laugh,
and everyone cheers like they're part of the staff.
Clothes from last week still lie in remains,
Coffee rings have become permanent stains.
I should clean up but it doesn't feel worth,
This chaos feels more like home than the earth.
You claim half the bench as if it's your seat,
leaving me crushed in the cold, without heat.
Your legs stretch wide, taking up more than you should,
I laugh, but I'm silently wishing I could.
You called this hairstyle a bold new trap,
but now it's smacking you every time you clap.
You thought it would be chic, like ocean-side,
but wish you could just bald your way to hide.
She walks through the chaos as if it were breeze,
her hands free, no clutter, just loose keys.
Each step is a beat, a rhythm in stride,
the crowd gives way slowly—she owns the pride.
She takes a slow bite, peels back toward the core,
"This apple was worth the long wait at the store."
Her teeth meet a seed, a crunch so unkind,

I arrived too late at the empty park,
the sunset had gone without even a spark.
Now I'm stuck with memories I'll just miss,
and a phone full of photos but no camera's bliss.

topic: a note tucked inside a card
lines: They left a note tucked between the layers to read,
just a scribble but enough to lift their head.

topic: chair squeaks when you lean back
lines: She leans back just enough to make it squeak again,

how long before the pixels make you blind?

but finding focus was worth what it cost.
It won't slide up smooth, it's caught on the seam,

I tug and I pull but it just keeps catch,

They came with a promise of fresh and new date,
but now they're a bag you've been forced to just wait.

and here's your meal plan—now completely, well, lost.
You watch that robin pecking at your dirt,

like you owe it rent for this little gig.

as if the wire were some sacred pledge.

She listens to rhythm, not noise, in the tone,

The driver keeps talking, won't stop his chat,

"Only five more miles," he says with a mile,
and I start to believe him, just for a smile.
She's posing by the river, perfect scene,
arms crossed, frowning at her flawless screen.
Says it's for Instagram, not a clue,
Just trying to outshine lake number two.
You fold the stub as if it still shows,
the screen's blue light still softly glows.
You saved it from the trash, claimed your lane,
and now it lives between your wallet and your brain.
You watch the conveyor belt roll on in claim,
your bag not moving under that old name.
You text "Still waiting" to your mom and wait,
while the flight attendant walks right past the gate.
I hit send before I read the whole post,
now my teacher's name haunts my feed like a ghost.
They'll see every comment, they'll read all the class,

You sprint to the stop but the bus won't run,
Your coffee's now cold—your morning's all done.
You text your boss that you'll be ten late,
The next ride is delayed—just sit and wait.

topic: sharing a cat video with no context
lines: You tap send without any warning or scroll,

Her gaze floats up like smoke from her head,

You toss the crumbs like a pro with your bread,

while strangers glance over, impressed by your display.
I've been waiting here since the flight hit the claim,
my phone lighting up like a panic flame.

You watch the sky melt into something gold,
the way the clouds get blushed, as if they're told.

their shadows stretching long and ever bright.
She watches the butter slide off the toasted rim,

She says as she savors the buttered bread.
The sky turned black and the sea turned blue,
lightning cracked sharp, and we danced through.

we huddled under a flimsy canvas tent.
You can't tell if the rabbit feels safe or still,
its mind racing like a factory mill.
It sniffs the air for a strange new scent,
trying to sense what it might not be meant.
She used to scream out the words at the stage,
now silence feels better than teenage rage.
She leaves the concert and finds peace in the hush,
she doesn't miss the noise — or the rush.
A quiet sound, the shell gives a crack,
You're halfway through your morning snack.
The yolk spills out—it looks like it's you,
A fragile thing, it all could too.
He stands beneath the flickering streetlight's side,
his eyes dart wide, a wary, thin smile in stride.
A whisper becomes his quiet, sad cry,
but passersby don't let their gaze meet his eye.
A distant horn cuts the silence of break,
It's morning, and the city begins to wake.
The sky turns light, the streets begin to roll,
And somehow, even early, my heart feels whole.
I think about the cookie's soft bite,
how my hands clench for it feeling tight.
The clock says wait but my mouth wants cake,
so I sip my coffee instead and ache.
You knock the shaker and leave quite the mess,

She watches the sky with a patient sight,
the hawk in slow spirals through open flight.
She waits for the wind to bring back that call,
she believes hope can rise from the quiet and tall.
You call this the mystery of the missing clue?
It's just gum left behind, now stuck to the glue.

the mess—too late, the evidence stays in its place.
He tied bait to a bent paperclip hook,
laughed when I told him the rod he'd just shook.
No fancy gear, just grit and a take,
now his fish hangs like art from the lake.
You never owned a matching pair,
you grab two from a jumbled stair.
It's not for show or out of fate,
you're already minutes running late.
She keeps checking her phone's silent clock,
while the last items flash off the stock.
Her fingers hesitate—will she still run?
The sale ends soon, and the moment is done.
She chose the third lane at the crowded mall,
just as the guy behind starts to call.
Her cart rolls slowly into her sight,
and she sighs in slow motion, real tight.
The fine for the book still unpaid is due,
its pages are dog-eared and coffee-stained blue.
I keep thinking I'll return it and miss
the chance to remember how it felt like a kiss.
His phone took a hit from the edge of the game,
Now he stares at his face in the cracked little frame.
He swipes for a hint but no answer will clue,
The quiz times out—just another bad view.

topic: a dog barking at a mailman
lines: You see the mailman approach without a plan,

the blanket's a quilt of every odd hue.

when dinner was clearly a frozen pie.
You stare at the screen's cold comfort, blue,
lost in the haze of whatever you're going through.
Time slips away like water down the sink,
and every click leads to some faded link.

lines: You narrowly miss a car in the lane,

the vendor repeats what they understood said.

your favorite kicks are now out of her view.

lines: The kid's been asking all day for a snack,

They looked through the cushions, they patted and tried,

lines: She swears she only left one clean pair,

lines: My friend is always ten minutes past,

Third-period lunchroom, chaos in full scene,

lines: The scooter wobbles, unsure how to move,

I watched the last flicker before it lost its glow,

Now darkness begins to gently cast,
the light of memory has quietly passed.

lines: They're balled up still, soft in their gray,

A small thing, but it makes my heart swell.

said through her eye without so much as a try.

lines: They all laugh when you try to prove your age,

lines: You light a candle to keep up the flame,

lines: I trace the faded marks where the old road ran,

I drop a coin in there, the machine won't try,

lines: A child sits on a bench, alone in the park,

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: You wander down the empty shopping street,

lines: You call this a morning without your brew?

it scanned her face and failed her left eye.
The camera blinked, the app refused to stop,
she slapped the screen and said, "Security's a flop."
You remember how it stayed steamy and warm,
your hands always shaping the same old form.
It never showed cracks or a chipped little face,
though you swore that was where it should never erase.
You wait for the bulb to give one last flicker,
then curse how slow it died, not any quicker.
A dollar gone in the name of bad waste,
you twist it out with far too much haste.
I leave my damp mark where I laid on the mat,
the smell of the room lingers, stuck and flat.
There's something familiar about that old scent,
like youth after exercise—hot, worn, and spent.
You count out your loose cash for the parking change,
Each coin lands perfect, you even arrange
them in neat rows like they're straight from the mint,
while others fumble for notes or their lint.
I wave and cheer but the cat won't call,
it bats a crumpled receipt into the ball.
When I offer treats or even say "Hey you,"
it blinks once slow, then ignores me as true.
She followed the map with zero clue,
trusting every update in her rear-view.
The GPS switched to some odd mode,
now she's lost on a dirt road.
The players run through the slick wet field,
the mud won't break and the grass won't yield.
He kicks with the same old high aim,
but this match just feels less like a game.
She watches the last petals fall from the past,
a spring so loud now gone with the blast.
The tulips still sway, but she won't try to see
the beauty in roots where her joy used to be.
You watch the sunflowers follow the lead,
their stems strain upward with nowhere to head.
They chase the last sliver of fading gold,
but dawn is hours away—nothing to hold.

topic: a man reading on a bench
lines: You smooth the corner but leave a soft fold,
the breeze tries to take the book from your hold.
Each page turns slower as if trying to page
you to stay young while the world tries to age.
She's sobbing through the chorus—how very real,
like she's never let a feeling break a seal.
The lyrics call her name, they claim her fate,
but she's still crying when the track goes late.
Your cat took a leap and the bowl made a spill,
They don't look a bit sorry, they're still full of will.
You tiptoe across the room, hoping not to dash,
But they hiss and pounce—so you duck from the crash.
It licks its paws where the sunlight still beams,
half-dozing in warmth, pretending it dreams.
Its tail blocks the keys where my hands should be,
I laugh but I miss the old silence with me.
She had no clue about the hidden cue,
A balloon dropped—her eyes went wide and blue.
The room came alive when the lights turned bright,
Shouts of "Surprise!" echoed into the night.
Your thumb paused mid-sentence, near the wing,
like even tech needs a moment to spring.
You smile at the glitch, pretend you meant "fly,"
and I let out a soft, "oh, how perfect," sigh.
I swear I came here just to hear the tune,
not feel some melody make me swoon.
I clench my teeth and try to keep my grit,
but even grumps get weak for just a bit.
I spotted a plastic bag caught on the trail,
its edges still glowing from the recent gale.
I untangled it slowly, set it free,
maybe it'll dissolve out there in the sea.
Your ice-cold drink went flying onto the floor,
dripping like guilt from a clumsy pour.
Now there's a brown watermark on your white stain,
and you're saying "oops" like a broken refrain.
I circle dates with the ink of my love,
small arrows point where you wrote "see me above."
Your words are smudged but I still read your need,
and I know this page once bled, now it's just a seed.
They hit your lane like they forgot the brake,
but you let out a breath and call it a mistake.
Your hands still tremble where they gripped the heel,
yet you're soft as the road and not a piece of steel.
You're stuck in the same old endless loop,
spinning faster than a drill sergeant's troop.
Your legs go wild, your mind goes thin—
you'll never catch what you don't have within.
You built them high, each shelf a bit more high,
The top one wobbles but you touch the sky.
A dream was planted here, now grown from seed,
You don't need chaos—you've got purpose, creed.
You wear sensible shoes for your aching feet,
but your walk still lacks rhythm or beat.
You tried to add flair with a pop of style,
but fashion remains a full-on trial.
I handed my cash for a cup they had paid,
it costs double what it's worth—just a bad shade.
I sip while I pace near an empty snack shelf,
wishing I'd brought my own brew instead of myself.
They keep the water bottle from that far-off day,
tucked in their bag like a relic to stay.
They never fill it, just let it quietly stand,
half-empty, halfway between loss and brand.
She watches it rise until it can't float,
tied to a string with her name scrawled on note.
The clock ticks loud—now it's exactly noon,
she jumps, it pops, and the world loses its tune.
You buckle your kid into the tight back seat,
she screams the same phrase like a broken repeat.
You inch toward the front down that narrow aisle,
pretending you're calm for the flight attendants' while.
That lawn mower wakes me up every noise,
though I doubt my neighbor truly enjoys.
I text him once to voice my little blame—
he replies, "This is how we do it, just the same."

topic: seeing a price tag too high
lines: You still call it your childhood dream,
though it just sits there and doesn't gleam.
You trace the price you can't quite spend,
and wonder when that joy would ever end.
You bought it for fun, but this fish hates the time,
it won't touch the flakes when they hit the chime.
You watch through the glass, just you and the tank,
while your hunger goes unanswered, your mind goes blank.
My suitcase is packed but the cat's in its case,
She curled in my spot like she owns this space.
Her purr drowns my sigh as I stare at her fur,
She wakes just to glare, then goes back to spur.

topic: steaming coffee in a blue mug
lines: You found this quiet corner your favorite spot,
the morning air chills, but your coffee stays hot.
You sip and relive the good old days you take,
while silence grows wide like a frozen lake.

topic: a phone camera flash too bright
lines: Your flash nearly blinded my left eye,
It lit up the room like midday sky.
I begged you to fix it with a quick snap,
You said it was fine—your phone's face-map.
You tapped three names but missed the fourth in date,
Now they're all pinging you messages you hate.
They ask the same old question every why,
"We're mad," they say, and you just want to cry.
She checks the watch once every hour or so,
it hasn't been set since last summer's glow.
Her eyes trace the numbers on its blank face,
yet smile at a time she can't replace.
Their face lit by a soft, blue glow,
they don't know what they're missing below.
A thousand things buzz inside their mind,
while silence waits just behind their blind.
She holds the umbrella steady with her hand,
its frame now bent where the wind once planned.
Her clothes are soaked but she's smiling, not wet,
the rain feels like home, and she hasn't let go yet.
You check the old jug but it's dry at the top,
you left it behind when you farmed every crop.
A trip to the store for a gallon to fill,
your plants can wait now, your glass still won't chill.
I lie awake and watch the ceiling still,
tracing cracks like paths through some old hill.
Moonlight spills but doesn't seem to fight,
the silence feels like love in this strange night.
You slammed your pedal, but too late, no brake,
your heart still throbs from where the horn gave ache.
You watch their taillights disappear in the dash,
of red, unapologetic, gone in a flash.

topic: a receipt lost in the bag
lines: She swears she had cash but she needs to pay,
her receipt is long gone, tossed out and away.
She asks for a copy, they don't have the scan,
now she's stuck with no refund and no backup plan.
You hear that sharp sound as the shovel makes clank,
It chips off a piece from the hard frozen plank.
A sliver of dirt shows beneath the snow's thaw,
And spring whispers louder than winter's old law.
He says the fish is doing fine, dead right,
but we all cringe at how it fills our sight.
It spins in circles, something's off about the flow,
we pretend we're not watching the weird little show.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: You check the screen where the numbers still glow,
it doesn't show anything but stress and blow.
A new charge pops up from last month's small debt,
and all you feel now is cold, sharp regret.
I've got a headache so big it could prove
I've been working too hard to even move.
It's not just any pain—this is a brand-
new migraine I earned with my own hand.
A balloon string got caught in your dark hair,
it danced like a ribbon in a summer fair.
You laughed as you untied the little tangle,
and held it just right with such a sweet angle.
You vanish from my screen without a sight,
I check your stories late into the night.
Your messages are there but never read,
I wait for ghosts that silence makes me bleed.
The coffee machine beeps like a clock at noon,
humming a broken, but strangely happy tune.
You wait for the brew, for something to be ready,
the drip starts slow—maybe today feels steady.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: She tapped the record button and thought she had tried,
the screen said "sent" but the friend never replied.
It blamed it on servers, called it a glitch,
she smashed off the app just to flip the switch.

topic: a song stuck in your head
lines: Some TikTok jingle invaded my ear,
It's been stuck there longer than it should be, dear.
It plays on repeat in this cursed loop,
I've tried every trick but it won't troop.
I found my breakfast in a cold wet bowl,
these soggy bits have lost their crunch and soul.
They sink instead of swim—they won't even float,
just sit there slimy and unappetizing coat.
He bends a paperclip into a crude hook,
the bait's just a crumb he clumsily took.
He casts it like Thor but the line won't hold cast,
he's sure he caught something long gone from the past.
You feel the paper storm in one quick blast,
It flies into places you can't comb fast.
You check your reflection — the bits are still
There in your roots, a party that might kill.
I folded the crust in my last slice's half,
your memories still stuck in a cheesy laugh.
We took turns chewing the same small bite,
but now the box feels heavy without your light.

topic: a song stuck in your head
lines: That lyric's been buzzing nonstop in your ear,
you've had it jammed there for weeks, maybe a year.
It's not just any tune—it's a real good hook,
and you're okay with being the one it took.
I still remember the games we would play,
how we carved our old fake names in the clay.
We'd hide under the tree where the wildflowers grew,
always certain we'd find it again someday too.
You miss your stop because the bus is late,
you text them asking why you have to wait.
They blame the road and the thickening snow,
but the driver's just too slow to go.

topic: a coffee cup on the curb
lines: I left my coffee on the curb without the lid,
now pigeons think it's a snack for the kid.
The storm washed away the last of the brew,
but I still miss that cup from my morning view.
The dog sees a squirrel and starts to zoom,
the leash becomes a tight elastic loom.
