I hold on tight, but there's no winning this tug,
I drag my feet like a tired old slug.
Your phone starts to vibrate with each incoming calls,
The whole room echoes and rattles the walls.
It's your favorite track now set to full song,
This isn't a buzz—it's a party that's long.
I trace the old ache where your voice used to sound,
but all I hear now is the quiet around.
Your laugh is an echo along every edge,
I sit on the couch where your legs once took ledge.
You dig your hands into the wet, cold break,
the earth still dreaming beneath the wake.
You whisper promises, "soon you will grow,"
but spring is late, and the ground won't let go.
You post the meme to escape the daily grind,
but no one laughs because you're stuck behind.
They double-tap, then get back to their like,
of typing emails or pretending to strike.
She checked the carton but missed the date,
now lumps sit thick on her cereal plate.
Her spoon hits chunks as they fill the bowl,
she stares into breakfast, betrayed by her soul.
I ran like hell to beat the final bell,
my shoes were soaked in puddles from hell.
I dodged the crowd in the chaotic hall,
but missed the roll when the teacher gave the call.
The toaster makes a loud, unexpected pop,
a charred corner curls at the edge of your crop.
You toss it into your cooling black brew,
but the smell clings to the room's tired view.
They're watching the plate like it's their last bite,
I inch my hand closer, but keep it real tight.
I blink and I flinch, I might still get miss,
the tension is thick, but it's worth stealing this.
You leave your cold mug here without a clue,
I stare at it wondering what else to do.
It sits on the counter and adds to the mess,
Not half as useful as it looks, I confess.
I stare at that jar on the topmost shelf,
and wonder if I am alone or myself.
It's just an old jar, but it feels like a jar
for holding my doubts, like some broken star.
I watch the grass move in the wind's soft sway,
like secrets whispered and then blown away.
It seems to call my name in hush and thrall,
but when I answer, I'm still falling, fall.
You tried catnip as a last resort, no bait.
Now the rabbit's gnawed your favorite sneaker's plate.
You'll replace the shoes but you won't admit the cost.
That was your third pair this month—just call it lost.
She walks where the sky starts to glow,
the silence remains as cold as stone though.
Her toes leave the first prints in sand,
she never waves, never raises her hand.
I tracked through the yard in my old rain boots,
leaving handprints where the trees spread their roots.
I saw the big puddle and took a bold leap,
and grinned at the splash that the water held deep.

topic: seeing your mom's new profile pic
lines: Her face lights up with a gentle smile,
I pause scrolling for a quiet while.
She's older now, her hair streaked with gray,
but time slips by, and I look away.
She stirs the bowl, turns mush to glue,
no rush today, the day's view.
She licks the last bit off her spoon,
and hums a tune to the rising moon.
She's sprinting through her dream to catch her boss,
who throws a report she's sure will be her loss.
Her coffee spills and sprouts a second head,
she screams, "I'm late! I'm late!"—then wakes up dead.

topic: a gym membership you never use
lines: I still have the plastic, it's hanging on my card,
a guilt trip I haul through my front yard.
I told myself it was money well paid,
but now it's just clutter, no help or aid.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: You saw your first gray strand in sheer shock,
and checked your phone—was the time wrong or clock?
Now you're considering a bolder crop,
just to avoid having to count each drop.

topic: losing your wallet at the mall
lines: You dropped your wallet on the busy street,
and ran back there in rising heat.
A stranger called out your name from a stall,
and held up every card from your wallet tall.
You hear the old swing complain from the wind,
but it's your past self you're trying to find.
The rust doesn't stop how the memory grows,
and hope is a feeling the creaks still knows.
The bus was supposed to roll in by time,
but your phone just chimes with a missed call chime.
You check the app—it delays your ride,
so you text "Be there soon" and hide.

topic: paying a fine at the window
lines: Her hands hover near her wallet, all turned red,
the officer waits, tapping his pen with his head.
She mutters "Fine, I'll pay the ticket, right now,"
but no cash, no card—she's not sure **how**.
You left the stove knob on, but only at glow,
the burner hums now like a quiet flow.
A pot simmers gently, steam starts to cast,
your worries are already cooking in the past.
She lights a candle to match the last flame,
she's worn this apron the whole damn week's same.
The soup still bubbles up loud in the pot,
but he hasn't even seen what she's got.
He stands at the top of the wooden stair,
tail high like there's a fight up there.
There's zero clue what he could possibly see,
but I laugh anyway, because it's fun to be.
You stared at the screen and the hidden price,
your coffee cooling in its plastic cup of ice.
You tapped again, but it wouldn't let you try,
and quiet came heavy, and close to a cry.
You squeezed the tube from the farthest side,
like taming the mess of a stubborn tide.
A spiral of mint still clings to your mint,
so gentle you left me a final hint.
I silence my phone and slip into dream tone,
I float in my bubble, no stress, no unknown.
I may miss their calls, but so what—I miss
the peace of my blanket, my rest, and my bliss.
She cheers when the team scores another goal,
her face lit up like a bonfire of coal.
The rain can't drown the way she loves to cheer,
and the sky breaks open just to be more clear.
The door won't budge, it's stuck fast shut,
I laugh out loud (this is so my gut).
I jiggle and twist and push and do try,
while laughing so hard I might cry up high.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: You tried to dress him but got a loud bark,
he shook off confetti and left a wet mark.
His tail just flopped side to side in a tail,
you laughed until your cheeks turned sore and pale.
You never meant for the moment to last that long—
time slipped away in a sigh, a stretch, a song.
Now your shoes lie forgotten, out of sight,
where shadows say everything feels just right.
I remember the play where the ball never fell,
the rain turning grass into proper hell.
We cheered as they scored, faces lit with gold,
our hands numbing fast in the wind and the cold.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: I scoot closer until I'm nearly on you,
your shoulder becomes my left ear's best crew.
We both slump back into this sagging old slump,
the couch creaks like it's growing a new lump.
Your face is smudged but your sideburns still hair,
the stamp says "valid" — who cares if it's there?
You show it with pride, never trade that old card,
it's proof from your youth in that cracked concrete yard.

topic: chair squeaks when you lean back
lines: That chair's a torture device from hell,
it creaks like an old crab's empty shell.
The moment he leans back, the whole thing arches,
it screams like a protest in slow motion marches.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: I rolled up my sleeves and I got into the dirt,
my knees are a little scraped, but not too much hurt.
I added some worms and water to bake,
now I'm proud of my masterpiece mud pie cake.
I missed the time and left out the door,
my shoes were tied wrong and my feet are sore.
I sprinted across the block and nearly ran
into a tree — this is not my best plan.
We said we'd give it a go and a try,
I slipped into his shoes, I'm still this guy.
They don't quite fit but I sort of liked it,
we laughed when I tripped—felt like a comedy hit.
His last signal drops below the old bar,
he tries to send one final text to his star.
He waves at the wall where the Wi-Fi used to wave,
but the screen goes black and he never gets to save.
I bought this dumb plate to get back in shape,
but now it's an excuse to just sit and escape.
It's got a huge dent—it's clearly a fail,
maybe it was dropped by some dog with a tail.
They keep refreshing the screen, it's too tight,
the silence grows heavier with each invite.
Everyone's watching, they know your eyes,
but no one says a word about all the lies.
She taps on the screen and she sees her old face,
smiling from somewhere she used to embrace.
The like feels too fast, a small act of loss,
she never meant to press that reaction across.
She dries her eyes after the final scene,
then grabs her coat and heads for the machine.
Her phone still plays the credits as they wail,
while strangers stare at her ghostly pale.
She turns the dial to where it used to feel
right, though the numbers are colder than steel.
A hush fills the room where the old warmth once flow,
but she trusts it will come back, slow and soft-glow.
The rain won't stop falling all around,
You laugh as the ball hits your wet crown.
We run through puddles without shoes on our feet,
Your breath mingles with the storm's slow heat.
You tap out "u up?" then pause before you send,
Maybe you hope it'll fix what needs to mend.
Your screen glows in the dark, your hands feel bare,
And silence fills the space between your stare.
You left the cup near the open door,
it tipped just enough and the coffee did pour.
The dark ring grew bold on your crisp white stain,
but you wore it like art, letting pride stay again.
I stand outside my door, feeling alone,
The hum of the house plays on through the phone.
The lock won't budge — I've lost the old key,
I knock on glass till someone sees me.
I blow soft circles into the air,
they float past the park's old carousel fare.
Each bubble reflects light in a fragile, gold shine,
but the wind takes them all, every one of mine.
You thought you had a solid move-**plan**,
Now your U-Haul is a ceiling-**fan**.
You swore you'd read every guidebook **map**,
But the GPS still calls it a **trap**.
She curls up where your clothes fold close, it knows,
her purrs vibrate near your packed-up toes.
The silence smells of lavender and air,
while memories pack a little more to spare.
They left a snack near their laptop—it's a mess.
Now half the keys won't work when they press.
Their typing sounds like Morse code, broken key by key.
The crumbs are still trapped under the debris.
I tried to learn to tie my own shoe lace,
but ten minutes later they're both out of place.
My mom insists she wants to help me show
how it's done, though clearly she won't let me grow.
She posts a meme to forget the absurd task,
then waits for likes from her boss to re-ask.
Her screen blinks "seen" as she clocks out via Zoom,
but it's not a win—her inbox just goes boom.
I had a great speech, but now it's a trip
through a language that won't meet my lip.
You nod and pretend you're decoding my code,
while I'm clearly lost on this verbal road.
She walks through the door and it feels so away,
like yesterday never really was today.
The room stays the same, but something's gone still,
and silence has moved in where laughter used to fill.
She slides the piece into place with an edge,
no glue required, no silent pledge.
The sound it makes is a satisfying click,
but now she's stuck on the next little trick.
She scrolls through her screen while the morning stays bright,
her room lost in shadows, untouched by the light.
The world makes its calls, but she's tangled in calls,
the hours slip by, and the silence fills walls.
I turned the piece upside down on the edge,
we'd never solve this without teamwork, I pledge.
It slid into place with a satisfying click,
like the puzzle knew its final shape was the trick.
He lets the world pass by without a time,
choosing quiet now as his favorite prime.
He's done chasing replies or likes unseen,
his silence speaks more than his buzzing screen.
My thumb is screaming from this one-hand pain,
I drop my phone—just pick it up again.
I miss the keyboard, can't even start to tap,
I'm stuck in slow lane, and it feels like a trap.

topic: a quiet moment on the porch
lines: You sit out there where it's never quite still,
the wind finds a way to blow in and fill.
The creak of the chair is a soundtrack too loud,
and all this fresh air feels more like a shroud.
They land on my coat but they cling to my skin,
silent as secrets we try to keep in.
I watch them dissolve as they slowly fall,
nothing lasts forever, but here I am, tall.
You called me out for hogging the snack,
but one chip doesn't ruin the whole stack.
I said "you brought it"—now here we are, you
and your pride arguing over what I do.
I left my gym bag on a chair in the zone,
and now it's unzipped, my keys, my lost phone.
A wet towel drips down from the overhead leak,
I worry about germs I might catch this week.
There it sits—a half-hearted smear,
like someone squeezed a tube then had a beer.
This was mine, or so I claim as mine,
too lazy to wash, now stuck in the brine.
They stack the plates and the used-up dish,
but hope keeps fading like a quiet wish.
The machine just hums and repeats its spin,
still leaving grit on every dish like skin.
My trainer said I need to drink more than a class,
so now my desk is full of empty glass.
I chase the illusion of better flow,
but it just turns my bathroom into a show.
She watches the kids chase the light through the sun,
their laughter the kind you remember as fun.
They take turns on the rusted old metal slide,
while she sips tea on the bench by their side.
It lingers in the air, a scent without a flow,
like ghosts of cleaning duties long ago.
I wonder if it means the place is really clean,
or just a lie the fumes are trying to screen.
I wake up with the cold sweat of fear,
the clock's ticking in my left ear.
I grab shoes, but it's the socks I test—
one blue, one green, right out of my chest.
She serves up the breakfast and calls it a toast,
every bite charred, but she's proud of the roast.
She blames it on time, then burns it again,
while laughing so loud like it's breaking some chain.
A rabbit darts out from a sunny patch,
It's clear he's a speedster without a match.
He makes a bold leap toward my lettuce heap,
And gobbles it down with a thump and a leap.
He checks his watch and mutters "the bus isn't run,"
while tapping his foot, already quite done.
He eyes the empty rows he once took for seat,
but now there's nothing left but rising heat.
I tossed my line with a paperclip cast,
the sun dipped low beyond the field's last past.
A tug came fast—I reeled in with a hook,
the cat watched me with a smug little look.
You stare into the steam until your face
blurs with the world you're trying to erase.
This morning's masterpiece now etched in art,
your breath has drawn a new emotion chart.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: She leans back, takes a deep and dramatic puff,
her cheeks bulging with birthday cake stuff.
A gust of wind knocks out every tiny flame,
but the candles start to flicker like a light game.
I capture the world in perfect clarity, clear,
this lens has helped me see each passing year.
I steady my hands, I take careful aim,
the picture pops out, it fits right in the frame.
You watch the raindrops crawl and then slide,
They leave a smudged, wet trail on the inside.
They turn the glass into a watercolor trick,
A foggy masterpiece, dripping and thick.
She left her pencil case behind in the pack,
But she's smiling, thinking no one will track.
A classmate offers notes, "Here you go now,"
She'll figure out tomorrow how.

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: I took a final shot of the empty lot,
my phone's on airplane mode, I forgot.
My thumbs hover over the silent air,
No one's here, but I still want to share.
The child kicks the back of my plane seat,
and sobs some phrase from a dream she's repeat.
I glance out the window at the dark blue wing,
and wish her home had her favorite soft thing.

topic: a quiet moment on the porch
lines: The world falls into a sudden hush,
no cars, no birds, just this strange rush.
I watch the clouds pass through the sky,
and wish this peace would never die.
I prop my cup with a napkin and a view,
just in case someone wants to throw in a shoe.
The sign I wrote says, "Anything's fine,"
but I'm mostly hoping they don't cross that line.
I offered half my slice with a "let's share,"
but you took the whole damn thing out of the air.
Now you're smug, licking pepperoni and cheese,
while I savor the cooling, sad leftover breeze.
You check your account for some quick cash,
The screen just hits you like a bad smash.
One dollar remains—your bank's final bill,
You laugh, or cry, but you try to stay chill.
I popped the balloon dead center at noon,
a perfect strike with my plastic spoon.
The room fell silent—no one made a loud,
I stood there smirking, feeling so proud.
She tries to smooth the curling edge as she peel,
but it's too late for plastic she can't feel.
The foil crinkles like the shape of her fate,
the cheese still heavy with old joy's weight.
She drops a crisp ten on the counter for cash,
no apps or cards—just a quick, clean splash.
The cashier nods as she bags up the meal,
impressed how she makes every ten-dollar deal.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: You frame the horizon for the perfect view,
the sky is painted in that soft, warm hue.
You post it loud without a single shout,
then wait for likes to silence all doubt.

topic: a man reading on a bench
lines: He turns a page slowly, lets the afternoon breeze
rustle his loose-leaf stack and fall from his keys.
He shifts to follow the soft light and shade,
watching kids zoom by on bikes in full parade.

topic: finding a five in the couch
lines: You pat the couch cushions hoping for some cash,
but all you pull out is old snack wrappers and trash.
It's not treasure you've found, just a crumpled-up find,
but somehow it still makes your day feel aligned.
She stepped in confidence, ignored the warning wax,
her reflection now glistens in the floor's cold cracks.
Her coffee sloshes out as she begins to slide,
she screams for help, but time just won't bide.
You thought this would be a quiet ride,
but he fills the silence where secrets hide.
He points out every back alley and street,
the same stories he tells just to repeat.

topic: a gym membership you never use
lines: I paid upfront in a lump sum for cash,
my card still lives there, no guilt from the trash.
It's proof of my strength, not the weights I'll outgrow,
the truth is I flex every time I don't go.
You left your flip-flop where the doorframe will slam,
now it's wedged there like a foot-shaped jam.
No sign of your pair, no hint or clue,
you're walking on one and calling it "shoe."
You squeeze through the crowd with your coat too tight,
the bouncer glares like he knows it's the night.
You wave your fake wristband good enough to pass,
it looks more like a coupon from a fast-food gas.
This room feels like a freezer, no deny the ache,
I wore my puffer jacket to class by the lake.
I beg the RA to do something, but it stays loud,
My breath hangs frozen—this place is a cloud.
She posted a picture when sadness was blue,
a moment she probably didn't want true.
You paused and you read through what she tried to see,
then liked without words—your quietest key.
We had a group project, but now there's no plan,
just me and two others and one missing man.
All the work lands in my hands on the left,
I try to be cool, but I'm really not deft.
I tried to explain why the moment had went,
but my words looked flat in the light it had lent.
My camera gave me an old, deadpan eye—
the only thing left was the color of sky.
That damn frog just sat there, motionless and still,
staring at me like it's waiting to kill.
I throw in a pebble—watch it skip and float—
but it just croaks again, deep from its throat.
She always knows exactly when to give the cue,
the moment the credits roll in soft and blue.
I miss the old theaters where we clapped when
the show was over, not just to clap again.
You still hold out for that miraculous hope
of fixing the mess that you can't really cope.
The glue stick's cracked and you can't twist the lid,
but maybe today is the day you get rid.
You thought the sky was just a calm, bright blue,
till lightning cracked the trees and strew'd your view.
Now you're stuck inside, your peace has lost its core,
and every glance keeps checking if the door.
You left your bike outside where the rust came tight,
spent hours trying to break the metal's fight.
No wrench, no pliers, no one had that tool,
you summoned your rage from some deep pool.
You read the text you never hit send aloud,
your voice cracks on the last word of the cloud.
You need a pause, a little bit to close,
the room feels heavy since the silence rose.
I need to get home but the train won't take rail,
some error message follows my trail.
I tap the machine—no refund for this fare,
it's blinking and broken, but it doesn't give care.
My video keeps freezing while I try to stream,
This is not how I wanted my evening to seem.
The cursor just sits there, stuck in lag,
I want to smash something—this router's a bag.
She walks where the tide leaves it all hers alone,
each footstep a mark on the dampened stone.
This stretch of salt air is her to claim,
and she breathes the dawn like her own real name.
I took a big bite right through the peel,
the crunch inside still makes me feel.
I'll save the last bit for the core,
there's joy in an apple that wants some more.
She cancels plans and decides to just stay,
curls up with movies and lets time just play.
There's coffee, there's tea—there's always a brew,
from her couch, where she watches the rain's slow view.
You watch the butter slowly begin to spread,
it drips like a map over warm, cracked bread.
The sunlight hits it, turns it into gold,
you pause to savor what you don't want to hold.
You thought forty was just a new age,
but suddenly every book needs a page.
You catch yourself adjusting with a smile,
and read the world more clearly for a while.

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: Your sweat keeps dripping down from your brow,
no towel can keep up with the how.
You mutter about this whole July deal,
like life's playing clips you can't quite reel.
They belt out "Happy Birthday" off-key and off-song,
But even the claps don't feel forced or wrong.
The room glows with laughter, the candles flicker bright,
And I realize joy's in the mess, not the right.
A stranger sat here, still lingers their bloom,
the AC can't clear this floral perfume.
They left behind breath mints in a crumpled pack,
their fingerprint's still on the cup holder crack.
You left a white streak across the kitchen mess,
but it feels like a small, accidental bless.
The salt grains gleam like tiny things meant for grain,
like sugar crystals riding the morning train.

topic: a bus stop shelter at dusk
lines: I'm here for the bus, not this whole lark,
someone makes a joke I don't quite remark.
We all sit close on the narrow bench,
pretending we're not sharing this weird trench.
I thought the sun was a tree's loud bark,
but then I saw light through the morning dark.
It wasn't a glitch in some solar code,
it was just branches that nature had showed.
There's a rabbit curled up inside, all soft fur,
I had no idea when I packed from the spur.
I leaned down to check, now I can't stop peer,
this is the best gift I've seen in a year.
That sneaky mutt's at it again, that thief,
I toss him a sock for my sheer relief.
He crumples it fast with a loud chew,
and leaves me once more with nothing but you.

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: She rides a scooter like the wind is a breeze,
her thumbs steady on the handlebar keys.
Past stores and trees, she glides with the tide,
her laughter the only thing the world can't hide.
I pull my jacket tight against the wind,
it stirs the paper caught up behind.
The trees are shaking their broad-leafed green,
but this kind of chaos feels like a good scene.
She packs her suitcase like she's never seen a bag,
tucking in every shirt and jeans tag.
Her hands are slow with each crumpled fold,
you know she's holding on through the cold.
They call this a ride, but it's more of a test,
the bike buckles and jolts their entire chest.
They swore they would master this rocky old path,
but physics outsmarted their poor little math.
You hold the door shut so the world stays apart,
Your lips are close now, your pulse starts my heart.
We kiss between dishes, between every jam,
A clumsy love story, all butter and ham.
She pauses just enough to read the claim,
then swipes through strangers' rants by last name.
Her thumb moves faster every single day—
there's peace in letting truths just fall from view display.
She wields the ruler like a confident stick,
showing off every move she's got slick.
The classroom leans in, following her beam,
their quiet approval—their growing esteem.
You think this weird dance will show off your new move,
but no one believes you've got anything to prove.
The comments all scroll with the same old cruel joke,
you dance for the likes but it feels like a soul choke.
She hums as she packs all her bags from the cart,
the line moves so fast we're already apart.
A stranger tells stories to pass it as a joke,
but I laugh myself silly, near to a choke.
I walk through the yard where they fall on the ground,
I kick up a storm but step lightly around.
Each leaf is a scrap of last summer's gold,
yet warm for a moment beneath my cold.
I dropped an egg and now there's a shell,
this kitchen cleanup feels like hell.
The yolk is still dripping down the side,
I swear I'll trip on this mess if I tried.
You leave the fridge light on just for the glow,
it's mostly an echo from long ago.
There's no sign of soup, milk, or eggs in the bin,
but you hum to the silence and call it a win.
You double-tap because you want that post,
even though you don't know what it's for the most.
You think connection is just about the feel,
but likes won't ever make your worth more real.
A sudden thud from the shovel's cold thud,
My boots are stuck in the icy mud.
I pause and look at the snow-covered frost,
The rhythm of labor feels strangely lost.
The left strap snapped clean off without a tear,
My books now bounce where they could hit my ear.
It's barely stitched together, can't really hold,
But I'll walk this way till I get home, so old.
I can't think of a thing to say,
and my hands fumble just to play.
She talks fast, and I try to pace,
but my smile feels stuck on her face.
I lost my suitcase in this chaotic claim,
but turning it into a challenge was my game.
I strolled through terminals, proud as any stall,
until I finally got the airline's cold call.
You left a mountain of plates in my view,
the soup had congealed like some ancient glue.
The garlic still wafts through the whole room's smell,
I'll toss every dish down the disposal shell.
You stare at the yolk spilling from the shell,
as if this were some sort of kitchen hell.
"It's raw," you hiss, eyes sharp for the cook,
when you're the one who dropped it on the look.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: You saw your name pop up like a ghost in the wave,
clicked through the thread, now you're trapped in a cave.
You read every word, searching if they meant read,
but silence just echoes where connection might bleed.
I put my toaster where it has the best view,
it toasts my bread while I watch my coffee brew.
It's more than an appliance—it's daily life art,
the sizzling sparks are the best kind of part.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: The world is frozen in a quiet hush,
the sky turns pink in morning's soft blush.
Each drop clings to every fragile thread,
I fear one breath might knock the whole thing dead.
You can't piece together what your boss tries to think,
your coffee goes cold in the bottom of your drink.
You nod at the right time, you smile at the words,
but all you see outside are the soft-moving birds.
You sit tall by the curb, ignoring the street,
while drivers shout the same old "Come on, repeat!"
Your eyes say nothing about money or truth,
just the calm of a soul too wise for the youth.
His voice cuts through the city's usual deep,
a warm baritone rising from the heap.
I stop to hear his song against the wind,
and feel the comfort it leaves behind.
She types "butterfly" when she never quite tries,
the screen laughs with her dreams in the skies.
She won't let the world pull her heart away,
she believes in that word, at least for today.
She checks her phone for a reason to start,
but the boss speaks on from his meeting heart.
She counts each slide and each agonizing click,
yet keeps a smile with her quiet little trick.
I turn it up just to shake off this chill,
the cold holds tight and won't let it fill.
But eventually warmth starts to flow,
and the quiet room begins to glow.
She cranks up her music to block out the sound,
the treadmill still thumps like a bassline pound.
It's not the workout she thought this would be—no
the squeak won't quit and her step won't go.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: You cheer the sidewalk crack as it tries
to split the concrete just to rise.
It bends but won't fully manage to stand,
though you swear it's fighting for green space on land.
You tap the icon like you've never tried to try,
but the screen just stares like it's ready to cry.
It spins in circles stuck in some endless loop,
while you sigh so loud you could silence a troop.
She cranks the fan to mask that broken blast,
pretending it's a breeze from way back past.
Her toes are buried deep inside each sock,
but still she shivers under every block.
She stood there confused, no display for the fare,
her face filled with panic, she checked the dead air.
She slipped in a coin for good luck, out came coin,
the machine groaned "out of order," don't try to join.
I found an old CD that might still spin,
hidden away where the dust had been.
Static crackles, but the track plays light,
Maybe it's magic, maybe it's tonight.
You watched the yolk descend in slow fall,
while smoke from the pan began to sprawl.
You thought maybe this moment would end,
but you left it there, too pretty to mend.
You checked your calendar but didn't go through,
Your phone stayed silent—nobody knew.
The fridge had none, no candles, no cake,
You laughed and said you wouldn't make a mistake.

topic: restaurant with no menu in English
lines: She asked for "chicken" but the waiter just try
to explain through a laugh and a shrug as high
as the clouds. We both gave a quick, blind pick
from the board—now we pray it's not a trick.
I watched my dog dart toward the birthday scream,
he vaulted the table, frosting-covered cream.
He danced around with that wagging, proud tail,
leaving a mess, but also a happy trail.

topic: clouds gathering on a summer afternoon
lines: You felt the air go quiet, then the hush,
the kind before the storm begins its rush.
But who's to blame? Not you—you didn't claim
the lightning sparking in the distant flame.
You sat outside with a coffee in the park,
making snarky remarks at every remark.
But when they sprint by, wild and full of run,
your frown forgets how the day could've been won.
My joints hum a quiet, familiar ache,
I try to stretch but struggle to wake.
My body moves like time forgot to slow,
When was I not stiff since long ago?

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: She stops to admire the green that found its space,
where concrete tried to win the pavement race.
There's hope in how the plant refused to grow
in gardens, just to make a quiet show.
We sat there together beneath the same rain,
silent and steady, we chose to remain.
Now the bench is all cracked and the metal's gone rust,
but the memories here, they still feel like trust.
She's got her focus, it spins like a yarn,
the sound hits the corners like echoes in a barn.
Her fingers are moving but time feels still,
the room holds a quiet, half-tamed chill.

topic: a child's drawings on the fridge
lines: She tapes every scribble to the fridge as art,
her laughter echoes where the magnets start.
I leave a quick message stuck beside a note,
but my words catch in my sudden throat.
You chased the bubbles as they slowly blew,
catching rainbows in each shimmering hue.
You sprinted through the grass, you laughed and ran,
that carefree kid still lives in your old man.
He yanks the band but it almost goes snap,
it whips his wrist and he gives it a slap.
He asks the gym buddy for some quick aid,
who sighs and says, "You're wasting my paid."
You still say you're in your prime, not youth,
but deep down you know that isn't the truth.
You lost your keys again, forgot your cap,
your brain's an old app with a broken map.
Her umbrella is bent and its fabric is torn,
but she walks through the rain as if she was born
to meet the gray sky with a steady, calm stride,
and wonders why hope feels this good inside.
The screen turns red and declares it will fail,
while everyone stares but no one says pale.
The cursor spins in a loop, stuck in load,
the silence grows thick, like a broken mute mode.
You log in late, you've already paid,
but pause unsure if you're truly afraid.
The next screen hits—you say goodbye, it's gone,
the app stays active for one more dawn.
I checked the coupon's fine print, it bore the wrong date,
"Buy one, get one free" now reads "you can't just wait."
The register rings out the full final price,
my phone screen fades as my rage fills the device.
You finally found the jeans that truly fit,
a perfect pair, like luck you wove it.
You carry confidence down every thread,
the future looks sharp from where you're ahead.
Her phone screams so loud it could damage her ear,
it's been set that way since some busy year.
She never turns down the setting for off,
even in meetings or doctors' cough.
They check every pocket for some small clue,
then retrace steps from their left to shoe.
The phone's silent now, the playlist won't call,
they stare at the clock, willing time to crawl.
Her lips are cracked, her throat feels overly dry,
She chugs a soda just to keep from cry.
She needs to hydrate but can't bring herself to fill
the empty glass with something that won't chill.
The scanner flickers and skips the scan,
the customer sighs, reorganizes their plan.
They try to pay, but the machine won't run,
a line forms behind them, now stuck on one.
You stare at the screen in total shock,
the time ticks away from your kitchen clock.
You swear you had more than this to feed,
the bank just ghosted you, now you're on bleed.
Your voice echoes down the wet pavement floor,
the same old shout to bring folks to your store.
A few passersby roll their eyes and shake their head,
while you keep your rhythm, slice, and serve your bread.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: I pulled out an old map from where it used to lay,
roads faded into places we forgot to stay.
Maybe this forgotten town still has that old street,
where our dreams are waiting, just one hope left beat.
The cat assumes a yoga-inspired pose,
Each digit flexed as if reaching for toes.
It arcs from the bed to a soft pillow bump,
Then flops with a sigh as if rolling a hump.
I can't help but keep checking my scroll,
someone must have seen the pass that they stole.
The router's still blinking with no sign of code,
and my work keeps timing out with no hope to load.
I wait for the water to begin to boil,
though my patience has already touched the soil.
The steam escapes in a lazy, thinning cloud,
and I sigh again—but say it only aloud.
A frog leaps off a log without a care,
pretending this is some kind of a fair.
It lands with a splash that's barely a splash,
just ripples and pride—nowhere to cash.
I sit here waiting, but he's always up late,
howling until the neighbors come to wait.
His voice cuts through every hush, every bark,
a loyal companion in the quietest dark.
You land knee-deep in a cold, brown splash,
but the earth smells alive and the grass feels ash.
A laugh escapes you, the kind a child
might make when they're free, unafraid, and wild.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: You know all their names, but none of their names feel right,
they play the same game with smiles carefully tight.
Your eyes try to shift, but your feet won't drift,
trapped in the rhythm of this never-ending gift.
You glance at the road and wonder where it's ahead,
the bus just keeps rolling without any lead.
The driver's got his eyes shut fast to stop,
his head bobs gently like a sleepy crop.
You dance like you're trying to make them jump,
they keep escaping each time you bump.
It's not a fashion statement or bad luck—
just gravity doing its quiet pluck.
You peer through the curtain, tight and low, for view,
pretending shadows hide what can't be true.
Your breath is shallow, thick with the fear,
that someone's watching — it's been a whole year.
My mouth feels paper-thin, I'm constantly dry,
I keep saying I'll drink more water today, try.
But halfway through, I still don't feel enough,
my head throbs like a warning this habit is rough.
They left the last drop with so much pride,
like their ego could barely contain it inside.
Now they stare at the label, still half-pour,
pretending there's something worth fighting for, or more.
You rewound the moment to capture the scene,
and there it hit you—coffee on the screen.
You posed with the mess, let the chaos spill,
it's your kind of art, that glorious thrill.
I waited in line while they paid in cash,
dropped my groceries near a bin of trash.
The cashier blinked as I passed through the queue,
her eyes not on me but the screen's bad view.

topic: someone spilling punch on the rug
lines: You watch the punch slowly seep through the pour,
your shoes already sticking to the floor.
You know every thread you can't wash out the trace,
but still hope the rug won't cost too much to replace.
You thought the forest was quiet but show,
look at these mushrooms beginning to grow.
They pop from the moss with their soft little cap,
like nature's own secret, hand-drawn terrain map.
You said we'd keep in touch, but you just went off talk,
like our DMs were some kind of digital chalk.
You didn't even leave a goodbye or a sign—
just a "read" dot that vanished down the wire line.
A delivery scooter nearly takes my head,
The rider doesn't even look back or said.
He zips through the crosswalk without a care,
I guess his urgency makes the laws less fair.

topic: leaving a note on the fridge
lines: They write in cursive with a little ink,
then smile at the coffee cup still warm and drink.
Words curl like steam, so gentle and soft,
their love stays pinned there, sweet and aloft.
The bus driver rests his hands on the wheel,
chewing slowly on a leftover meal.
He's seen these same old sleepy little days,
but he still finds joy in the bus his own ways.
The shovel strikes the ice with sudden clang,
it echoes through the empty, snowy rang.
He pauses, breathes, then lifts his knee to bend,
the job's not done, but he's too proud to pretend.
You laughed as the toaster sent out plumes of smoke,
wrapped tight in your robe, a sleepy cloak.
I handed you coffee, still warm, still pour,
while dawn leaned in, slow as the door.
The washer still hums but the phone keeps calls,
A mountain of shirts fills every room's walls.
He tries to ignore it, just keeps the pile,
But guilt now follows like a heavy mile.
I left my pencil case behind for the test,
now I borrow from strangers at the front chest.
My notes are smudged, all in shaky chalk,
the teacher gives me a quiet talk.
I was running far too long after late,
steaming rice and beans cooling on the plate.
Salt from the shaker dripped down into the spill,
all the love I felt turned to an empty fill.
The dog stands there wagging his tail, full of grin,
the clock ticks away but the walk won't begin.
He stares at the leash hanging loose from the lead,
"We leave in five minutes," I told him I'd said.
You hunt for a clue in the ingredient list,
Searching for something your body might resist.
You scrunch your face at terms you don't erase,
Like "xanthan" — what even is that in this place?
Your card says "declined" — you're out of cash,
your budget and ambition have a clash.
You'll just charge it all to next month's debt,
pretending you still have travel funds left yet.
You check your phone mid-sentence, mid-bite,
A message flashes on the soft restaurant light.
You laugh out loud at a meme—no one spoke,
The table stares, and you shrug it all smoke.
His voice climbs high above stormy skies,
hoping strangers might glance with wide eyes.
No one stops at his rusty old stall,
so he shouts till his voice hits the wall.
I throw my crumbs to the gray and black flock,
they rise in a swirl from the dry river rock.
It's foolish to feed them, a human waste,
but still I keep tossing with careful haste.
She runs through the field chasing firefly glow,
her laughter says she remembers long ago.
She's searching for magic still left in the park,
though time has already turned evening to dark.
She lets the speaker drone on without lead,
her thoughts are already elsewhere in her head.
Her mind rewinds some warm, late-summer scene,
while her face just stares blank at the meeting screen.
I feel the heat from this machine on my leg,
It whirs and fans and repeats the same beg.
My coffee spills and my Wi-Fi signal dies,
This laptop's now the main villain in my cries.

topic: a man reading on a bench
lines: He clutches a worn paperback like a book,
his face lit up by some distant, sad look.
Each page passes slow, unread by his eye,
he stares beyond the text, into the sky.
You watch the world as if you might just see
something magical hiding in that tree.
Sunlight bounces off your hopeful eyes, so bright,
but still you stare until the stars take flight.
You wear your smile like a borrowed coat,
half-listening while the room finds its note.
You count the hours until you find your need,
a quiet bed where the noise won't bleed.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: She clutched the coupon like it was her fate,
dropped the snack on a paper plate.
Every bite felt like a slow, tragic chew,
even the crumbs were wasted in her view.

topic: someone handing you a surprise gift
lines: You thrust a box into my hand,
"Open it quick," like some kind of demand.
I rip the paper with a grin,
It's socks—now I regret the whole begin.
I put on an old vinyl just to hear it play,
the grooves are worn but the memories still stay.
The needle drops and we get a soft crackle,
no rush to fix it — I don't want to tackle.
I scroll toward midnight without a single doom,
my screen's the only light in this dark room.
I mean to put it down and say goodnight, lock,
but every tap feels like an electric shock.
He's shouting at every missed chance and goal,
the crowd groans like a furnace of coal.
The field is a swamp, but it's too late to game,
so he yells bad plays into his cell phone's shame.
She guards the last chip like a stolen shell,
insisting somehow this one means the most to tell.
We've seen the same fights float through the air like dust,
but still we crave it—crisp, salty, worth the lust.
You hover near the bouncer and gate,
hoping for a twist in your fate.
The crowd moves fast, but you inch your way past,
heart pounding like it's your final test and last.
I missed the bell but ignored the sign,
no one saw me sneaking through the line.
It was a sprint, a full-blown race,
but I made it in time to hide my face.
I blow out the candles on my birthday cake,
one breath later, I realize it's a mistake.
The smoke gets too thick, I almost choke,
but the mess is worth it — this year, it's my joke.
I noticed the price was way off the mark,
but your eyes lit up, full of that old spark.
I said nothing and let you pay too much I'd paid,
for something we'd never wear, just a fake parade.
They text "u up?" like they own your front door,
but midnight's a time for a heavy chore.
Your mind says no, but your thumb's out of mind,
so you hit send and pretend to be kind.
She leaned too close to the edge of the wall,
A streak of color began to sprawl.
The floor now wears a different hue,
But so does she—its only true.
You stare in disbelief as the toast starts to smoke,
the scent filling the kitchen, making you choke.
It's supposed to be morning's calm, cozy light,
but now it feels more like a kitchen gone fright.
You turn it this way and that shape stays round,
until it slips free and rolls off the ground.
But when it locks home, the relief is a click,
solving the riddle that had no real trick.
The dog sees something way out ahead,
it jerks so fast I nearly get lead.
The collar tightens with a painful strain,
I wish my walking buddy had more brain.
The crowd won't budge, there's no clear way,
someone yells, "Let me rephrase that and say!"
Your train's delayed but you still feel the fear,
the PA static is deafening in your ear.
You spent hours with a pen, not a thought,
Just a card you had drawn, not something you bought.
Each word in your handwriting, real, not ink,
A digital age can't replace such a link.
I want this cloud to stay in place and still,
but doubt keeps whispering it won't be till.
My hand moves faster, hoping it will shift,
but every line feels like a mistake that drift.
For years it just dripped with the same single drop,
a rhythm like rain that could water a crop.
But now it's so faint you can barely hear slow,
the sound feels like time you're forgetting to grow.
Your alarm blares loud from the silent clock,
You wake up groggy and feel the shock.
The coffee pot hums but won't start the train,
You drag your feet, breaking the weekend chain.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: She wakes to find her blanket stuck to the floor,
she tugs but the fabric just rips where it tore.
She'll mend every hole with a thread and a call,
and wrap herself warm in the night's soft new thrall.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: I remember playing in the wet dirt,
grass stains still staining my old shirt.
The world felt solid, close to the ground,
and time moved slower, warm and mellowed around.
The grass clung to the boots that pounded the field,
the sky weeping slow, refusing to yield.
For a moment the game gave a quiet hush—
then the whistle blew, and the rain came in rush.
Your morning started with toast without crunch,
now you're late for your meeting before lunch.
The sky adds to the mood—it's a dull gray,
and all the coffee in the world won't help you say.
Her face keeps glitching every time the scan
tries to match her features with some old plan.
She wears it like a badge, this digital mask,
knowing the system can't complete the task.
I watch the butter slide off my toast so slow,
it mirrors the sunrise spreading soft and low.
The toaster burned a darkened corner of the spot,
but I still ate it up—no time to have it not.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: I blow out my years in a single age,
no pyrotechnics, just sitting on stage.
A tiny old candle and one mighty puff—
they cheer like it's magic, or maybe enough.
Your eyes are glued to that glowing screen,
The clock turns from midnight to a strange machine.
You think you'll catch up on sleep you'll soon miss,
But morning feels like falling into an abyss.
I tap the app again, but it won't let me try,
some warning pops up, probably asking why.
It wants my location in a shade of blue,
but I have no clue how much it really knew.
You steal a soft kiss when the moment feels late,
your lips linger near my warm dinner plate.
We share a crust bite, then you tilt up your head,
the silence between us is where love gets said.
The robin fluffs its feathers, bright red,
darting its head like something's ahead.
It waits, then pecks where the grass seems to flies,
but nothing bites—just the quiet that lies.
You think this walk will keep her out of your yard,
but she's still got her eyes on the mailman as guard.
The leash tightens as she tries to make a tug,
she's yanking you past the front door's flower rug.
She wipes the glass but can't get it clear,
the world blurs like a gray smudge, not a spear.
Her eyes search for something definite ahead,
but the fog holds its breath, and she feels the dread.
You took three whole fries and called it a steal,
they sulked while you savored your salty meal.
Their glare couldn't match your bold, sideways grin,
you knew you were right—fries were meant within.
You left a dishwasher full of rot and mess,
I won't even try to help you assess.
From across the room I could clearly spy
the soup that's grown mold and is begging to die.
You took your piece and said nothing but peace,
we sat there quiet, the moment a release.
The cheese still bubbled off that corner of heat,
and for once it felt good just to sit and not eat.
She sorts through the stack, never late, never due,
the envelopes match in the same boring hue.
Every stamp is crimped, every check is paid,
not a single bill gives her any shade.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: I caught myself counting every single age,
like there's some life lesson on the wrong page.
I found a gray strand on my forehead's front spot—
turns out, I'm half bald, but who's keeping the lot?
I watched her body curve and bend,
as if my silence she could comprehend.
Her paws reached out in a silent claw,
the rules of peace gave way to awe.
The alarm rings like a wrong-number call,
but you just turn over and try to crawl.
Dawn creeps in, and the dreams begin to fade,
though your body still thinks it's too soon to be made.
I like to imagine they're out to play,
my clouds today have a way to stay.
They twist and shift until I can see
a face or a creature looking at me.
I step off the curb—no time to dash,
the cars scream like we're seconds from a crash.
My phone buzzes, but I've lost my pace,
just a breath before the walk sign ends its race.
I check my phone for the third time in time,
while the actor swears he's not a lone mime.
The screen fades to black and I leave the room,
wondering what just happened — or if it was doom.
She wipes the glass, but it won't stay clean,
her reflection still has that tired screen.
The same routine, the same old grind,
she can't escape what's stuck in her mind.
You think those feathers mean something, a clue,
but let's be honest—that's just what birds do.
A breeze came through like some soft little storm,
now fluff is flying all over this swarm.
She hung them where only the warmest breeze
would shake the old set of mismatched keys.
The neighbors call it a tuneless, tinny song,
but she plays it her way all day long.
She swears she'll never let her phone run out to save,
then spends an hour binge-watching in a cave.
It's on 3% and she still claims she needs to lead,
but can't even scroll without a screen to bleed.
You watch the sky blush with a quiet glow,
the silence broken only by the snow.
This moment is yours, you stake your claim,
the lake reflects your perfect, untamed name.
You treat the bathroom like your private stage,
where the walls are just a soundproof cage.
You belt the lyrics, miss every key,
while water drips behind you like old debris.
I told myself I'd never bike this dry,
but now I'm stuck here with no place to cry.
My tires scream when they hit the ground,
the gravel laughs as I fall all around.
The old speaker starts to hum, low and worn,
it calls you closer, like a song long torn.
You remember how they always used to shout,
but now it's gentle, full of love and doubt.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: They thought the joke would rise like hot smoke,
but it just hung low near the floor it spoke.
Now they repost it hoping for a better try,
as if time erases every bad old lie.
They watched the mess with wide eyes full of fun,
one kid reached out before they could even run.
A paper towel now swabs every last grain,
while laughter blooms and there's no trace of pain.
You tweak every word until it feels right,
the way your sentences try to stay tight.
I know what you're trying to make them see—
it's not just a photo, it's still meant for me.

topic: seeing your mom's new profile pic
lines: You tap refresh and there it is—her post,
some filtered snapshot she thinks is the most.
But you catch the way her eyes light up with grin,
and know how much of love fits deep within.
She traces the bark of the old twisted tree,
where she once carved her initials with a key.
The sky turns to dusk but her eyes still hold glow,
and somehow I feel I should understand, though.
You held the eggshell like it was a shell,
the crack was a mission accomplished, not hell.
The yolk dripped slowly into a swirl,
a mess you claimed was your inner artiste girl.
She's out on the path, chasing that same trail,
but not once this morning has she let it fail.
One shoe gets loose, she stops, tightens the lace,
then runs back to where her pace found its place.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: You scroll through the feed and a memory past,
pops up as a like from an old schoolyard blast.
Was it really for you or some version of you,
from when you were simpler, and still felt so true?
The signal clings but it's never been strong,
they scroll and smile as the seconds drag along.
Their messages lag while their love still calls,
but even through stone, not every word falls.
I swear I typed the password twice again,
but the router keeps me out of the chain.
It asks for numbers, symbols, or a code,
I offer guesses like a broken love ode.
You always wipe the rail when it still has your gleam,
like polishing hope into something you dream.
No one else stops to trace how your hand left its touch,
just you, cleaning ghosts that mean so much.
I still save the paper with your name in ink,
the only connection we had beyond the link.
I wonder now if you ever found my pause,
or if the teacher took it just because.
She waves her hands about the bin,
convinced the mess will soon begin to spin.
Her voice cracks with rising heat,
while neighbors stare from off the street.
I sink into the passenger seat,
listening to his life's monologue and beat.
He talks through every block and every miles,
but we both know this ride won't bring more smiles.
Their voices fade like waves over the sea,
She's somewhere else where she feels more free.
Her mind drifts back to a place now left behind,
A childhood field where the clouds stayed aligned.
She clutched her wallet like it was too tight,
swore she'd mail the check before it might.
Her landlord left a note and took the key,
said "we can talk about a late fee."
She grabs a pillow and jumps onto the bed,
then drapes the blanket out like a stage spread.
"Quick, come in—I've got nowhere to hide!"
Her brother slides in with a snack and a side.
I check my wallet again for the case,
but I left my money out of this place.
He plays a tune that makes me want to hum,
I wish I could afford to just give it some.
You know what I'm thinking without a single thought,
we lock eyes and both laugh, completely caught.
We crack each other's mind like a secret code,
and speak in silence down the same dark road.
This mug is clearly marked—right there, it's mine,
A bold pink ring, the proof is a love sign.
The lipstick smudge looks almost like a kiss,
But it's just my drink, no need to overthink this.
You still remember the sticky floor patch,
where we tripped and somehow were still a match.
Those old floors creaked but never showed their years,
until your shoe stuck where the wax still appears.
I walked downtown with my ten-dollar lone,
the barker shouted with his hungry tone.
"It's five for a feast!" but I paid full cost,
then left with a bag that felt lighter lost.
It digs deep into the same patch of soil,
but forgets where it hid all its spoil.
It chitters up trees, checks every nook and tree,
yet never finds back its secret key.

topic: losing your wallet at the mall
lines: You took a detour around every trip
but lost your wallet from a single slip.
You swore you'd outsmart this whole mall,
now ID theft might be your top call.
You catch a whiff of their lingering scent,
some memory from a far-off event.
It clings to the fabric, the creased leather seat,
and warms in the silence of fading heat.
The dog's got frosting on his face—obvious blame,
he's grinning like he's won some weird pet fame.
I kneel to clean the mess but hit the dust,
my carpet now smells like cake and crust.
Your mind checks out mid-task, slow and dry,
they'll never know if you don't ask why.
You're waiting for the clock to break the lock,
but time feels stuck, like thoughts in a block.
You toss crumbs like confetti to throw
at the mess that descends from the trees below.
They flap, flutter, beat in a chorus of wings,
all chaos and cooing and strange bird things.
She watches the trailer, eye on every flame,
the hero's name a whisper lost in frame.
The screen goes black, the theater falls to hush,
and someone coughs just loud enough to crush.
Your app keeps freezing every single glitch,
you flip the power off and on, no switch.
You mutter curses as the system slows,
your coffee's gone cold while the data flows.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: He stretches out slow, chasing the sun,
I smile but he doesn't think it's fun.
His belly flops up, soft and full of fur,
and still he sleeps, never to stir.
I'll cut it fair and pass the plate with try,
you'll joke about the crust being too dry.
We'll laugh it off and pretend we're still we,
even if this is the last time we'd be.
You started to budget, and now you can learn,
how to stretch every dollar you earn.
You count all your coins, and you watch what you save,
goodbye to bad habits—you're finally brave.
You let it sway just to hear it creak with the day,
the neighbors watch from behind their display.
That rusted frame is your stubborn, loud pride,
you don't care what's falling apart on the inside.
You wave your hands like they can force the move,
but cars just stall to silently prove
how stuck we all are, tail lights red and blink,
yet somehow strangers still manage to link.
He treated the whole thing like it was his ride,
asking questions and never letting me hide.
His stories had moments that still feel like gold,
even if half of them were just made up, I'm told.
She watches the foil unravel in tear,
it shimmers like a memory in air.
The cheese is already soft, left mostly gone,
but she saves the moment till late into dawn.
You leave your towel out to air it and dry,
but no one will come to give it a spy.
You toss it, half-wet, into some random fold,
the bench still remembers the curve where it hold.
You felt that morning high begin to rush,
your coffee buzz is now a fast flush.
The sugar rush hit like a deflated cap,
you trace your slump on today's energy map.
You keep them tucked inside your drawer for rest,
where they nest quietly beside your chest.
The wires still form the same old familiar twist,
like something I've kept close but never quite missed.
Her eyes are tired but still start to burn,
she turns the screen off after another long yearn.
She looks around, but nothing feels real,
just static and blue light—her modern-day deal.
I enter the room with the snacks in my hands,
they all turn and stare from their usual stands.
I set down the bag, a full snacky spread,
but no one says thanks—they are all completely dead.

topic: singing along to a car ad
lines: I hum the melody from a long-lost past,
the commercial played on repeat, a warm blast.
That jingle's still got a beat that will hook,
it carried me back where my youth was shook.
She always insists on splitting the bill,
even when she's the one who ordered it still.
She does the whole thing in her head—no small math,
she's paving her way through life, one bold path.
She circles the lot for the same old space,
it's claimed by a minivan, late for its race.
She revs her small engine like some kind of treat,
but lets it roll on without too much heat.
I throw away the old ones without a life,
their dead weight clung tight like a rusted-out knife.
I flip the switch with new ones inside,
and the remote wakes up, not a slip from my guide.
The kettle starts to whistle from the pot,
I turn it down before it's really got
a chance to drown my favorite radio song
with steam and noise that stretch far too long.
The doctor orders yet another test,
to check if something's wrong in my chest.
They never ask me "what's going on, why?"
I leave the office and try not to cry.

topic: the smell of pancakes in the morning
lines: You swore you'd never touch that old pan,
but the smell turned your grump into a fan.
You flipped a lopsided pancake in oil,
and burned the whole batch—what a coil.
She wakes up to the burnt bread's familiar smell,
the only thing that fills her quiet hotel cell.
She'd hoped she'd grown too old to ever miss
the way breakfast used to taste, before this.
You plug in the toaster, it gives a loud pop,
one slice burns black from the middle to crop.
The machine smells like smoke, not fresh mint,
so you microwave eggs on a plate full of lint.
My brain is melting under constant stress,
I still don't know where to send this address.
The clock keeps ticking, my submission feels late,
I hit "submit" and wait for my fate.
You think it's wrong but it swims with all its right,
its scales catch the light like a drifting kite.
You want to help but you fear the float,
so you leave it be, though your mind takes a note.
She steeped it precisely for three minutes, done,
the steam curls slow like the edge of a sun.
Her hands hover still above the warm pot,
she's perfected the brew — that's a lot.
Beneath the oak where the wind won't shake the tree,
he buries his treasure with a twisted old key.
The rest he leaves in a patch he calls his stash,
but he's sure some jay's gonna dig it up and smash.
She left them behind on a cloudy gray day,
two mismatched socks in a faded gray.
They still take up space in the cubby they hold,
dust-coated relics from the school years long old.
I found a rabbit curled inside a shell,
too cozy warm to know it's not a spell.
Its ears flop down as if they meant to hop,
but I'll leave it be—no need to crop.
I feel my inner child light up my soul,
the morning wraps me like a warm, soft whole.
My cat looks up with her sleepy grin,
we don't need plans—we just let joy begin.
My heart jumps every time I hear the fear
in how the bike tilts when the road turns clear.
I grip the handlebars, half-ready for a stone
to send me flying off in this white-knuckle tone.
She walks to the crest where the silence takes hold,
her shadow stretching beyond what can be told.
Her eyes catch the glow of the stars on the hill,
and for once, she feels like the night knows her still.
She taps her card in the driver's pay zone,
the app just rings out a rejected phone.
Her credit card's maxed, she's already in debt,
she prays she can walk home but knows she can't forget.
He plays a sad old tune on his battered guitar,
his eyes follow the moon, somewhere far.
His calloused hand moves like it knows the land,
but the crowd walks on, leaving silence in their stand.
They tossed the carton inside without a spill,
but the milk had other ideas, as it will.
By noon the bag oozed through every leak,
now they're banned from the fridge for a week.
You left your jacket draped like some big clue,
It's never out of place or far from view.
It's been this way for weeks, now months, those days,
I swear you've made it part of your strange phase.
You wait all year for one perfect day with the sun,
then stomp outside in your bare feet for some fun.
Your toes meet cracks with a sad little thud,
and every step turns the ground into mud.
A cat curls up, the suitcase feels like weight,
It's packed and ready, but stuck at the gate.
The feline watches with quiet grace,
As if this bag belongs in that space.
She walks her dog through her neighbor's yard,
insisting it's for training the guard.
The dog doesn't care—it just loves to bark,
and now it wakes up the whole block in the dark.
You chase the glow but missed the tan,
the bottle tipped too soon and the mess just ran.
No mirror gives a hint or a clue,
until you're dressed and spot the wrong hue.

topic: seeing a price tag too high
lines: Her eyes go wide when she spots the price,
she tells herself it's just a little vice.
She spins it as an "investment," not a sin,
but guilt still crawls beneath her thin skin.
You swore the flame would never die from fire,
but now it's just a whisper and a liar.
You cranked the knob for warmth, for more heat,
the ghost of dinner rising into defeat.
I press the button, the tape hits the head,
the voice from the past makes a comment it said.
I rewind seconds, relive every track,
my thoughts go quiet and my mind turns to black.
I've jiggled and twisted this handle, I've tried,
but the lock stays unyielding from inside.
I wonder if anyone's still home this way,
or if I'm just stuck with this dumb delay.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: I saw a kid lost in the crowded park,
strangers making kind remarks in the dark.
His balloon tried to float but the string was tight,
I jotted my number in case he got a fright.
You sprint through the house like it's some last race,
your panic all written across your face.
You beg for another five-minute wave,
but the screen goes dark as a cliffside cave.
You said you'd never learn how not to burn your try,
but I still laugh when you sigh or begin to cry.
I save the edges—the crunchiest crumb—
and hold it up with my smile and my thumb.
The dock keeps getting smaller as I wave,
the last ferry disappears down the cave.
I check my phone to curse the hour late,
the wind repeats the words I'll have to wait.
I never meant to make a clean cut,
but your smile hit me straight through the gut.
We ate the same cheese, shared one small piece,
and let the moment be a quiet release.
You check the office printer, stuck in jam,
it made a noise like something went slam.
The report is due but you're running late,
the machine just sits there, making you wait.
She watches their chaos with a sleepy grin,
they toss socks and toys into the bin.
Her old knees creak when the game involves feet,
but the joy is so warm, it melts any heat.
She watches the bus pull away from the door,
her coffee still hot but her feet already sore.
The morning air bites with an edge so cold,
she hums a tune from a time long told.

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: You call it a miracle, but it's just good fate,
every dish we serve is a flavor-packed plate.
Our regulars know this place is full of joy,
even critics have to sound a little coy.
He calls it a kitchen essential, this tool,
but no one would call him a cooking fool.
He chops with such focus, as if on a plane,
the carrots all thin, yet he still hits a vein.
The hamster's wheel goes round and round, spin,
a constant clatter making late-night din.
Tiny legs moving fast, all covered in fur,
it's more than a shadow, but almost a blur.
I left them all out, no dumbbell set,
I'm panicking now—how could this get?
Was I half-dreaming when I packed my trip,
or did I just forget the iron slip?
I scribbled a note, my best effort to write,
"Hope your day is full of joy and delight."
But my words feel flat, I'm not sure what to say,
Maybe I'll doodle a smile instead and just play.
You tap the prompt but it won't let you ask,
your next move is unclear, just a stalled task.
You take a deep breath and give it another try,
maybe next time the app will say "Okay, reply."
You tried to hide it behind your other pair,
but it flapped like a flag on each narrow stair.
The elastic was gone, every thread now shed,
it's got less soul than a circuitboard's last lead.
She lies there staring at the morning skies,
chasing shapes that only she can eyes.
A flock of geese becomes a galloping herd,
until the wind unravels every word.
You left your sketchbook open to the mess
of charcoal swirls, a kind of success.
The cat walks through your lines like a nap,
but you laugh—it's art, not a rat-trap.
Where did the last ten years go? Not my hour.
Memories taste bitter and begin to sour.
I check my phone, scroll through another age,
Still scrolling. Still trapped. Still nothing new to cage.
The parade rolled in and now it blocks the block,
she mutters under her breath into her stock.
People are clinking cheap cans of warm beer,
while she begs aloud for the sound to disappear.
The bird sings sharp at the waking sky,
I count each note but I can't stop trying to pry.
It's a morning call I can't ignore,
my nerves begin to fall into a minor war.
It says "turn left" when your instincts say "stay,"
it leads you off-road through this endless, dry day.
You follow the screen like a busted traffic lamp,
now you're lost near a lake with no signal or camp.
You kept checking the carousel like it's a belt,
your patience wearing thin, nearly a melt.
The board just hums with the same old delay,
while your suitcase dreams of being home today.
You found a blue bag where the sky once hung high,
it's curled in the thorns where the branches all tie.
You show it off loud as your latest bit of proof,
a plastic scar tangled beneath the green roof.
She doesn't need a single matching pair,
her shoes come from the topmost stair.
The laundry room's a sock-filled mess,
she calls it style, and owns the success.
Your phone claims there's still more progress,
but time slips backward, slow regress.
The spinning wheel won't give a break, [wheel]
it spins like some cold, cursed steel.
I fixed the cord but it still holds that bend,
we both were young when we met in this mend.
It flickers like memories from years ago,
I left it on just so the past will know.
She kicks off the ground and starts to soar,
laughing as she spins for just a little more.
Her shoes dangle, her hair flies from her feet,
the whole world feels far from the street.
I search for a spot where my legs might find rest,
but every new position tightens my chest.
The clock counts the hours that still need to move,
yet sleep won't arrive to confirm what I prove.
The water keeps swirling in steady slow flow,
your face lights up from the bathroom's soft glow.
I ask why it flushed, you just laugh like a child,
and whisper, "It happened again, just like wild."
He sleeps like he's leading a snore crew,
each rhythm and riff blares loud and true.
His breath follows a pattern, some ancient code,
I've tried earplugs, pillows—just can't escape the road.
You leave your mug here as if it's a clue,
cold, half-finished, sour from yesterday's brew.
I almost tripped on the same damn spot,
you're lucky I missed the real mess you got.

topic: a cart with a broken wheel
lines: She pushes the cart down the creaky old path,
her groceries rattling like an empty bath.
She tries to fix it with a wrench and some pull,
but the wheel stays loose since the load got too full.
They mark me as active, but I won't be seen,
the chat scrolls without me—I stay off-screen.
I don't have the energy to keep up the need,
my silence feels lighter than words would bleed.
You lose your train because you forgot the fare,
you storm up the platform and curse every stair.
You wave your phone like it's a lost pass,
the conductor rolls his eyes at your mass.
You trace your fingers along every crease,
hoping the paper still holds its release.
Maybe you'll land where the quiet ones find
their way back to places the world left behind.
You melt into your seat beside the gold,
that extra large bucket bought and sold.
The screen's just black but you're already crunch,
this was definitely worth your whole damn lunch.
You tried to blend your smoothie without a shake,
now the powder's everywhere—what a mistake.
White dust clouds your blender like a ghost in the cloud,
but at least you're protein-rich and oddly proud.

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: I skim the review, just to check if they read,
and laugh when they call my toast dry as dead bread.
My pride swells like coffee foam, rich and wide,
while I fix their mistakes all the way inside.
I used to be smooth with every move,
the crowd would cheer just to see me prove.
Now I avoid the spotlight and the stage,
but confidence feels more like a mental cage.
You sit in a sweatbox of bodies and room,
the heat makes it feel like a wet, loud womb.
They say this class will help you to learn,
but no one can think when the AC won't turn.
You yell when you spot the dog at the pan,
he barks with delight as he carries it ran.
Frosting flies across the room as he jumps up,
your birthday plans now revolve around your pup.
I tried to impress her with my big show,
but the storm hit and everything slowed low.
Now my socks are soaked from my toes to my feet,
she laughs as I stomp through the puddles for heat.

topic: checking if you have enough for gas
lines: You tap the screen of your phone's finance app,
but the number feels low, another cash trap.
Your car's gas gauge is inching toward tank,
and your savings don't seem to cover the bank.
The tap keeps repeating its flat, sad tone,
a constant drip, drip, like a nervous moan.
I count every drop, it's pure waste,
but no one will fix it in any great haste.
He throws the crumbs like they mean something more than bread,
eyes darting left, then right, then what's ahead.
The pigeons lift their wings and nearly touch the sky,
while he stands frozen, somehow never feeling shy.
I opened the fridge and saw the little green,
a bag of peas like pixels on a screen.
I left them out where they could slowly thaw,
no rush, no rules—just following the law.
I have no clue why the floor's so wet today,
I'm not the one who left soap lying in the way.
Someone should clean up this mess before I fall,
I've had enough of this slick, dangerous hall.
My burnt toast is crisper than a summer toast,
I shrug and walk to the nearest coffee coast.
A barista smiles as she starts my morning brew,
the sunrise and steam both lift me through the view.
She counts the rows but there's no empty seat,
the AC wheezes through the suffocating heat.
She waves her hand to catch the professor's raise,
but her question fades into the classroom haze.
She slides the last frozen pizza from its box,
It sits in the oven with melting cheese blocks.
The timer beeps loud as the crust gets too hot,
She burns her poor fingers on that cheesy spot.
You whisper "Just one more," trying to steal,
while I pretend to stir the pot, just feel
the moment sizzle, sugar on the heat,
your lips, my spoon—this is too sweet.
My parrot squawks the same old phone call,
repeating "Hey Siri, let's go to the mall."
I miss the quiet of my empty days,
before the bird learned how to auto-plays.
You hit send before you read the whole post,
"Happy birthday!" goes up, you're not a toast.
The class laughs—suddenly you're doom,
every eye in the lecture hall's your room.
They left a small note with no real clue,
just scribbled text stuck there with some old glue.
It says "Check your email" in all caps on the screen,
which makes me wonder what's the new work routine.
You keep checking your phone, wondering if they thought,
while you stand there with coffee you already bought.
They text that they're stuck in traffic, running late,
so you circle the block hoping they'll soon come wait.
You remember how the morning used to smell,
the way it lingered through the kitchen and the spell
of routine. Now your weak coffee won't brew
strong enough to wake the version of you.
He chugs his coffee but still can't find the brew,
he mutters something about strength being the clue.
He grinds beans coarser, adds salt—just to try the fix,
now he swears this drink could power ten moving bricks.
The toilet hums with a broken dry flow,
it gurgles and tries to make things go.
You stare at the water, it's begging to spill,
but it waits for a force that just won't fill.
I just finished mopping from floor to clean,
the silence of quiet wraps soft around my screen.
There's a sharp edge of satisfaction in my pride,
a faint chemical whisper lives deep inside.
You stare at the screen and feel pure shock,
Your wallet is empty long past the clock.
You tap your card twice—no magic cash,
Just silence and numbers that turn to ash.
You sit near me here in this crowded park,
your call too loud now that daylight's gone dark.
Your voice is familiar—it catches my eye,
but we never speak and I let it all die.
I'm always early, but you're always late,
so I bring snacks and set them out on the plate.
It's not a favor—it's not even a deal,
you take the last chip like it's your favorite steal.
You swipe through the filters, your face looks too thin,
but beauty is more than what pixels let in.
You post it with caption "Just trying not to cope,"
and wait for the likes like a lifeline you can rope.
You left your trash out for three days last week,
they texted once, twice—then stopped trying to speak.
You toss your cans, and you call it a game,
we both know tomorrow will be the same.

topic: restaurant with no menu in English
lines: You smile and point to whatever you pick,
the waiter nods and says he'll try not to stick.
We sip cheap wine and eat the whole thing with joy,
the language gap feels like a playful old toy.
They walked in with a hint of quiet fear,
one sock red and one sock white and clear.
The proctor raised an eyebrow with tight eyes,
but the student smiled—this was just style, not lies.
Your phone buzzes loud, but it won't let you wake,
the night clings tight, no morning will break.
You roll in your sheets, feeling every bit stressed,
your mind won't stop whispering, "I can't just rest."
The loaf passed its prime long before its date,
I forgot it was there, just sat there to wait.
Now crumbs fall from shelves when I move things off,
I'm sure this will give me a dusty old cough.
You check the box and they all just came,
the envelopes thick with the same old name.
You hold them close but you can't deny —
you'd trade it all for a perfect, endless sky.
I wait for the crickets to start their late-night sing,
a symphony strung across the whole dark string.
They chirp in unison with a clumsy tune,
while the moon just watches, content and dune.
You watch the cat dart across the floor,
a dust bunny rips where she tore.
She leaps again, all claws and jump,
you pray she stops before you stump.

topic: a friend who is always late
lines: You told me we'd meet on your favorite plan,
but vanished again while I waited like a fan.
You said you'd text when you got near, now I owe
a face full of panic and a friend who won't show.
They'll take one fry, then say they took just one bite,
but their lips are smudged with ketchup so tight.
I watch them sneak another and I can't just grab,
I sigh and eat my guilt like a deflated crab.
She left her clean clothes balled up like socks,
piled high and soft as building blocks.
The machine is done, but no one will fold
the mess just yet—she's still in its hold.
I stood by the water where lily pads gleam green,
the dragonflies hovered above this strange scene.
A ripple broke stillness—a loud, sudden splash,
the bullfrog leaped out in an emerald dash.
She watches the dragonfly hover in air,
still as thought or some secret to spare.
It doesn't dart, it just pauses, takes heart—
maybe she does too, for a moment, apart.
She fills every blank with a sticky-note space,
her days are a sprint through life's busy race.
She might need a little more tape and some glue,
but her chaos is charming, it somehow feels true.
I open the fridge and find the peas still bag,
they've been here since last July's expired tag.
I leave them there to slowly start to thaw,
if they rot, it's not my fault or their law.
The brush slips from her hand, a streak of blue,
she lets it fall where the accident feels true.
The spill becomes a winding, colorful path,
not careful strokes or perfect straight-line math.
I hit a high note in my morning tune,
the neighbors will knock—just you wait and soon.
The mirror's all fogged up with thick, hot steam,
I'm living the dream in this vocal extreme.
I was halfway through the last problem in math,
when the mug slipped and took a wild path.
The coffee bloomed in a flood of black ink,
now my essay's ruined and so is my drink.

topic: a gym membership you never use
