lines: The monthly fee shows up again as due,
I vow this time to get some good and new.
But every week I leave it still a waste,
and let my fear of change outpace my haste.

topic: checking if you have enough for gas
lines: She stares at the gauge creeping toward empty tank,
counts coins in her pocket, won't touch the bank.
A whole forty miles left on this winding mile,
she drives slow and low in a quiet, careful style.
I tap my phone but the track won't replay,
it jumps to the next one and runs it away.
My fingers drum time on the dashboard beat,
while silence builds up like steam in my seat.
You watch the drop like it's your grand claim,
calling it persistence or your own name.
You won't turn off the tap, no great sin,
you're showing off how the leak stays within.
His phone screen glows with a sliver of bar,
he texts "I'm dying" to every known star.
He races for the wall to jam in the plug,
then trips on his dog and lands flat on the rug.
I wait all year for this strange kind of weather,
the gray skies that call me out to play together.
I stomp through the mud and I leap with a splash,
the storm may be ending, but joy gives me a flash.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: You spot another gray strand on your age,
the mirror feels like a cruel little cage.
You try to hide them with more dye and hide,
but worry grows darker than color inside.

topic: baking with flour on the floor
lines: You dropped a floury mess on the tile,
but it tastes like your best creative while.
The oven hums low, the cake starts to rise,
and you take pride in the recipe's disguise.
He hasn't touched those dusty blinds still,
sunlight has crept in through the gaps to fill.
He claims he meant to clean them off the log,
but silence settled there like morning fog.
She still checks the couch for a ghostly clue,
halfway hoping they'll pop in for a brew.
She swipes through old pics, trying to see
if anyone missed the sign—it was the key.
She steals a cookie with a guilty grin,
the jar is almost empty now, so thin.
I swear I saw her do it, but I'll just try
to pretend I don't know where they went by.
You hit reply but it was way too send,
the conversation's gone, your old friend.
Your fingers hover, lost on the key,
your message floats there, digital debris.
The sky is slowly bleeding into a soft glow,
but I don't stay to watch the morning grow.
My feet remember every step from the tide,
yet I leave no trace where the waves might hide.
You think you've struck gold with that postcard view,
but the stand's too wobbly and you'll tip it too.
Keep shifting your weight till you finally find
a stance that outlasts the breeze from behind.
I wait by the door, expecting your call,
the silence feels heavy, my anxiety tall.
I hear a soft knock or maybe a tap,
but nothing rings through—this house is a trap.
The sudden burst startled me from the noise,
a flash of color and laughing boys.
Balloons drift like memories, soft as gold,
and for a moment, I'm that boy of old.
That streetlight has been flickering all night,
it's the blight of the block, a civic blight.
They said they'd send someone out to fix,
but I know by now, it's just their tricks.
I dropped a few coins—what a satisfying clink,
the meter guy winked like he knew how I think.
My wallet's got dents from the plastic I bent,
I paid cash again just to feel I was spent.
You left a whiteboard full of coffee and mess,
the team knows you're the one they all want to confess.
No one touches your desk, let alone your old code,
you screamed "It works!" but forgot who it showed.
You were Zooming through tasks with a kind of zoom,
until your desk chair felt more like a tomb.
Your coffee goes cold as you silently slump,
a tired lull descending like a warm lump.

topic: ice forming on the car windshield
lines: You watch the frost bloom just before the dawn,
like crystal lace someone forgot to pawn.
The sun comes up, starts melting it all thin,
the car wakes up, and you're right there within.
He sets his little pace through midnight's hush,
His tiny face lit only by soft flush.
The wheel keeps spinning, tireless and thin,
You wonder what he dreams of deep within.
He spends three minutes just to make the move,
trying hard to seem strategic and prove.
It was a pawn—there's nothing noble in the lie,
it slipped off the board and just happened to die.
Its eyes are all judgment, it stares me down bark,
it drags me outside into the dark.
I hold the leash tight, but I feel it still lead,
I never should've taken this dog I don't need.
You know the moment when your tears will spill,
the credits roll but your eyes won't let it kill.
Your throat goes tight, your hands begin to lock,
as sobs sneak out in waves you can't block.
I watch the screen, it's all black and white still,
a boy walks slowly down the lonely hill.
His smile is warm but his eyes show the face
of longing and love I can never replace.
My cat thinks shadows are the real deal,
like they're something to chase or a full-course meal.
He pounces, yowls, and lets out a shriek,
I swear he's some feral movie geek.
His wagging tail gave him away by the tail,
he left crumbs behind on his sweet little trail.
He knew where the birthday cake hid for a treat,
my oven was warm, but so was his deceit.
I tried to dash across the crosswalk race,
but bodies blocked every possible place.
The "Walk" signal blinked with a broken sign,
we all stood confused, crammed into this line.
A smudge of purple's the best kind of proof,
a memory stuck to my cheek like glue or roof.
It's not just color—it's hope in full hue,
a little accident that feels like it's true.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: I was caught up in the rhythm, ready to flow,
when a sneeze cut through my carefully built-up go.
Now there's silence, a strange kind of sacred space,
where they stare at me with polite, awkward grace.
They slice the green tops with a steady knife,
the carrots fall spinning into new life.
Their hands move like dancers, they never sway,
it's veggie prep therapy to brighten their day.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: I trace the edges of this faded town,
a place where my name once meant a crown.
My finger slips on every fold,
the ink feels like memory, worn and cold.
You left your lipstick on the coffee cup's rim,
hoping he'd notice how it matched his skin him.
But now it's just a stubborn little stain,
and you're washing it away—again and again.
You check your phone to kill another hour,
but time tastes bitter, the calm feels sour.
You wish they'd pass, this stress can't last,
the neighbors' dog barks through the living room glass.

topic: seeing a price tag too high
lines: She still recalls the item in her dream,
how it once felt like a perfect theme.
But the price stuck out and it made her let
go gently, though she still feels slight regret.
The rain soaks the players but not the whole field,
They run through the storm like they've got a shield.
A kick in the corner bends toward the goal,
The crowd roars like flames from a furnace's coal.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: I found a toothpick stuck right in there,
it's wedged between fabric and shoulder hair.
I can't ignore the annoyance of that itch,
but who has time to deal with this? Just ditch.

topic: a kite stuck in a tree
lines: My kite still dances with a crooked tail,
but every tug ends up a downward fail.
It perches proudly where the branches tee,
like some bird's toll for a crash landing fee.
I watch them spiral where the sky meets the ground,
no path to follow, no place they're bound.
They twist through the air like a memory's drift,
and I'm left with their silence—no easy gift.
You chase the thought down a lost conversation thread,
the silence grows thick and the clock ticks dead.
Your coffee has turned to bitter anger stew,
but hitting send now would just annoy you.
I tap the wheel, still waiting for a green,
my phone blinks messages from the screen.
The cars don't budge; there's nothing ahead,
but hope in my pocket, warm and spread.
She types with one hand and moves just as fast,
her cursor zips effortlessly past the last.
Her rhythm is smooth, she finds a new flow,
and proves no one needs both hands to go.
She watches the tulips rise from the past,
each petal a color, a memory blast.
Her hands tremble, her eyes fill with a tear,
she planted these bulbs just one lonely year.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: You tried to tell a joke that didn't kill,
but maybe your humor's not your top skill.
A deep sigh came out from the crowd's groan,
now you're stuck laughing at your post's sad tone.
We never agreed on what degree was cold,
but you'd always laugh when I got it wrong and told.
You loved how the vents would hum their old-time heat,
said it smelled like the winters we knew from the street.
You gave it just the right twist and fold,
A quiet thrill in your palms so cold.
It leaves your hand with a wobbly flight,
Cutting through air like a glimmering light.

topic: a long queue at the coffee shop
lines: She hops from counter to counter at the bar,
convinced she's next in line after the star.
The latte art goes cold while she debates the brew,
but time moves fast when you're last in the queue.
They run another test I didn't request,
I'm x-rayed again from my head down to chest.
They say they don't know what it is I need,
but I'm paying for "more research," so indeed.
He walks through the mist like time's moved slow,
the fog clings to him where the others go.
No one stops to ask his name or past,
just shadows shift as he begins to cast.
She tapped "send" before she checked what she'd send,
It was meant for a file, but it went to a friend.
Her boss replies fast, says "Please just quit,"
and now she's one typo away from a fit.
You check the group chat, it's been dead since last night,
no one is talking, no one is right.
You type out a joke but your thumb hits "mute" instead,
and watch as the silence swallows the thread.
You spot a winged thing in the morning's last gleam,
the sun spills like honey down the dry stream.
The net arcs high as you aim to give lift,
and miss by a inch—what a strange little gift.
You watch your goldfish spin in the bowl,
tracing paths like you take a quiet stroll.
They keep their tiny, endless lane,
turning tight and starting again.
She stops to listen when the whole world turns to sky,
like maybe the wind will help her learn to spy.
The crickets start their chorus, low and hum,
she dances barefoot in the rhythm of the drum.
Sunlight catches specks of old dust,
they dance like dreams I used to lust.
A single beam slips through the slats, a ray,
I watch it fade as daylight moves away.
She heard the doorbell ring just after a call,
said it was just her cat from the mall.
No signs of a break-in, no clue to pursue,
she laughed and said, "It's all for you."
A bird thinks it can fly through the window and see,
mistaking the glass for the empty tree.
It keeps trying to go where it clearly went wrong,
squawking loud until someone hears the whole song.
You march right past the line that cuts you ahead,
the music swells and the crowd is already spread.
You kick off your heels and toss them to the shoes,
dancing hard now, no time for yesterday's blues.
She holds up the slice like it's fresh from the air,
the cheese curled and browned in its golden rare.
Her teeth close around it—then she leaves out a bite,
and smiles as the box fills up deep into night.
I stepped outside—everything's all shine,
This quiet perfection, it looks like mine.
The grass is still wet with the cold dew,
And overnight, beauty just grew.
You tap record to hear your voice from the past,
A memory machine you hope won't be last.
The phone's just an app but it holds all you've said,
Yet words fill the air where silence once tread.
You drove ten miles to see this perfect view,
the sky's too gray and the light lacks true hue.
You've taken a thousand and not one looks shot,
but you left your camera at home and forgot.
You laugh when the GPS calls this a trip,
though you're stuck behind a bus trying to skip
a red light, and waves crash out of the sea—
you hum along, pretending you're already free.
You drag the couch to the center of the room,
the cat just stares as our shadows zoom.
We laugh until the old ladder starts to fall,
but keep going anyway, pretending it's all.
You nod along, pretending you're in zone,
but half your brain is on your to-do own.
The others talk like they've got every clue,
while you stare blank, pretending you once knew.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: You stare at the screen's cold, blue glow,
the balance reads less than your hourly dough.
You tap refresh, just to be sure it's not a tap,
but the number stays put, like a thief in the map.

topic: walking past each other in a crowd
lines: She moves through the crowd like she owns the whole clash,
each step is a statement, not just a dash.
I catch her in profile, a face out of sight,
her posture alone could outshine any height.
She says she's good with plants, but that one still tries
[to thrive while clearly on its slow demise.
It's rooted in the same old cracked clay pot,
and gets no light—what did she think it would not?
You're pinned beneath the cold iron bar,
the ceiling blinks like dying fluorescent star.
Your legs burn with a deep and certain pain,
your brain screams, *just unlock the damn chain.*
You'd counted to ten, searching every last sight,
behind bushes, trees, anywhere held real tight.
The grass whispered secrets where you hid so tall,
till the sky split open with laughter and a call.
Your head turns toward their voice in your ear,
it's a tone you haven't heard in a year.
They swear it's not their day to be wrong,
but your peace walks out the door with their song.
I saw your post when the day felt too blue,
I didn't say much but I think I knew.
There's power in a like when it shines just a light,
a quiet "I'm here" that says, "It's alright."

topic: socks left in the laundry pile
lines: You spot a sock on the laundry room floor,
you wonder if you should go to war.
Your cleaner's probably judging your soul,
but matching pairs was never your goal.
My coffee goes cold while my fingers lag, age,
I chase the cursor but it stays in its cage.
I try to tap fast but it registers tap,
the phone says "retry" — I'm trapped in this trap.
I reached for my headphones, still full of wire,
they promised they'd fold flat, but that was a liar.
A tangle of cord is a mess I confess—
I need a new drawer labeled "not this address."

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: You trace the crack where the sidewalk runs wide,
something stubborn pushing up from inside.
You wonder if it wants to break through and grow,
or just remind you how far roots can go.
You pull up to the pump and your hands nearly gas,
the card gets declined for the third time that pass.
Your phone buzzes with a message it can't quite shake,
but you're too nervous to let your calm ever break.
You didn't yell or argue your place,
you smiled when they asked you to retrace.
They said it was fine but you gave them your take,
and let the small fight turn into a break.
You've seen the whole film but you missed the plot,
now you're weeping into your popcorn lot.
You walk out alone through the quiet hall,
your reflection blurs on the dampened glass wall.
She saw the first lightning strike give a flash,
her bare feet hit the ground and she gave a dash.
She didn't care if the rain left her soak,
this storm was just one big, wild joke.

topic: reading a review about your favorite café
lines: I skim the post where they claim I should read,
but their sour tone hurts more than stale bread.
They missed the barista's quiet charm,
the beans from a small local farm.
The rice still steams from the pan in the heat,
You dreamed up this meal while you walked through the street.
I served it all warm in a chipped old bowl,
This dinner tastes like my heart's whole soul.
The machine just showed me "Payment failed—fees,"
I jingle my wallet full of loose keys.
I try my old twenty, it's stuck in the cash,
this isn't worth getting all stressed and rash.
I grabbed the marker and the yellow pad,
left a message for my past self, *Don't be bad.*
A stick-figure sun blinked up from the eye,
so I added clouds and made it a sky.
You left the can of pinto beans,
but didn't label which ones are greens.
The salsa's warm, the cornbread is hot,
I'm trying not to ask what you got.
Your left shoe begins to untie its lace,
you slow down just enough to re-tie that place.
It happens again when your step starts to fall,
but you smile through the trip—this moment feels small.
The jelly drips down my hands in a mess,
I'm stuck out here in this sugared-up bless.
My palms feel like they're glued with old glue,
but I wouldn't trade these sticky days for true.
You step right into every single puddle,
your socks are now drenched in a soggy muddle.
Each stride releases a slow drip,
you spin and slip, then laugh while you trip.
You remember the days when we used to love,
now it's just his breath hanging warm above.
He dreams on the couch where you used to sit,
saliva streams down from his jowls to fit.
They don't know what to say or even the air,
just stare at their laps to avoid the scare.
Her fingers tap once, then clasp both her hands,
while the clock ticks on how the moment stands.
You wave your card, but they ask for cash,
you toss the receipt into the trash.
The total still haunts the amount you owe,
next week's budget will have to grow.
I'm used to my coffee being strong and hot,
but this weak stuff feels plain and flat and got.
Maybe I'll find a better grind to brew,
from the local shop that smells like fresh and new.
They book you for an MRI and a scan,
you haven't done cardio since you last ran.
Now you carry a wallet full of your pill,
but nothing yet wills the health you still will.
She sits beneath that old oak tree,
the wind sets her hair completely free.
It dances around her, wild and through,
that girl used to play where the willows grew.
It curled up inside the cardboard hole,
soft as a whisper, fragile as a soul.
Moonlight brushed down on its dusted fur,
but the world dared not move to disturb it or stir.
That crooked pair of shoes never lines up right,
they sit by the door like a weird little fight.
They don't seem to want to be seen or to hide,
just leaning there, half-dressed on life's tight side.
You feel the buzz beneath your ear and rise,
but your eyes are heavy, still half-closed in lies.
You hit snooze just once, pretend you're not yet done,
while the sun creeps in, polite and perfectly run.
You miss the old air, the cool in your hair,
now the fan spins slow up the creaky stair.
You touch your bare skin and feel it all thin,
the sun lingers heavy, too close to begin.
You watch it stand there so calm and so still,
as wind from the valley climbs up the hill.
You wait for a flicker, a tremor, a shake,
before it takes flight or the moment will break.
I ignore my map's old suggested route,
I take wrong turns just to get it all out.
I'm confident now in my chosen sure,
the GPS calls me back with its cruel lure.
The grass leans low, the whole field begins to bend,
like some old message the sky tries to send.
A shadow moves there, but it isn't a ghost,
just the breeze doing something the trees asked for most.
There's a purple smudge on your cheek like a mark,
left when the cupcake gave out its last spark.
The way that you grin is contagious, full smile,
I'll catch it too if I'm around for a while.
You thought this was sweet with your fake little cheer,
I heard it coming from outside your ear.
This breakfast-in-bed? It's an embarrassing feat,
I'd rather eat cereal alone in my seat.
My cat holds that same strange stretchy pose,
but I don't know if it's pain or it just knows.
Its body bends in a sharp, strange twist,
and I wonder if something's wrong—just a mist.
The bike drifts sideways on this gravel lane,
its rusty frame groaning like a disused crane.
I used to ride with the wind at my breeze,
now both my knees shake as I lose my ease.
You crush the clove and start to peel,
your fingers tingle, but you feel real.
The skin slips off, so smooth and slick,
you crack another one just for the kick.
She walks the same old path along the street,
where lilacs once were planted, now long sweet.
I want to tell her how it feels to say
goodbye, but the wind takes my words away.
You thought this time you'd actually find a fix,
but every trick you tried turned into tricks.
The blue light fades as your temper meets screen,
you call it "ancient" and curse the whole machine.

topic: a cart with a broken wheel
lines: My cart groans as it hits each cracked ache,
I steer wide of the path where we used to take
The basket's still full, I can't bear to unload,
though this trip back home feels less like a road.
I stretch my legs and stake this whole damn claim,
my posture says I built the park's main frame.
They eye the space but keep a careful wide,
I won't budge an inch—my spot, my pride.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: You settle into your usual row,
hoping no one will ask you to go.
You count every step they move at the same pace,
dreading the moment they turn toward your face.
I tried to roll over but failed to wake,
my neck felt like steel, it refused to ache.
I stayed in that lopsided, awkward pose,
and cursed the bad pillow I blindly chose.
I watched the morning come in through the light,
the garden waking up so full of bright.
It feels like every flower's shouting spring,
and nothing could be better than this thing.
I baked this cake to really be a show,
but the heat turned all that sugar into dough.
It's a joke, or maybe just a bad old joke,
now I'm serving it to guests who might just choke.
She's used to the way he uses his charm,
his goofy head bobbing like a carnival farm.
He flops down beside her, spilling across the rug,
his slobbered smile always seems to tug.
You double-tap so fast it looks like a press,
but half the time your thumbs create a mess.
You later ask, "Why did I give it a clue?"
The post is garbage, but the like is still in view.
You typed "butterfly" without even trying,
it floated out perfect, a typo flying.
Autocorrect named your magic "you,"
but you knew deep down it was all true.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: She turns the cold key in the lock, finds the code,
She hasn't thought of this memory since the road.
The box is still dusty, nothing's changed with the age,
A yellowed photo rests on the topmost page.
I tried to swipe but the card hit its max,
now dinner is out, and so's my new tax.
I could skip the cart and just wing it and try,
but my wallet's sad and it knows the sad lie.
I checked the corner — the coupon's past its date,
now I'm stuck debating whether to just hate.
It could have bought me a whole loaf of good dough,
but now it's trash. What a disappointment to show.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: You trace the crack in the sidewalk's seam,
where green forgot how to stop its dream.
You talk to the soil like it might reply,
just for a while, not too loud or sly.
I left the sheet glowing with caramelized heat,
still warm enough to scorch my bare feet.
I linger nearby, tracing how it leaves its trace,
in silence, it cools to a still, soft space.
You sprint through puddles across the soaked field,
the ball skips low, it doesn't want to yield.
The crowd's loud roar becomes your quiet cheer,
while raindrops tap out rhythms just for your ear.
Your thumb keeps moving, it won't stay off-screen,
The words are loud and they don't want to be seen.
You let out a sigh and you pull up a sigh,
Then click something kind—maybe that's how we try.
You handed the cashier all you had left,
the moment still rings like a memory theft.
You bought a sandwich and gave it your date,
now every bite feels like a time machine's gate.
She bends a paperclip, hooks it with care,
and casts her odd rig out into the there.
The fish don't seem interested in bite,
but she's having too much fun to quit for the night.
That flickering streetlight still holds its glow,
you swear it's trying to tell you something though.
It's not much of a message, just a faulty sign,
but you tip your head and admire the line.
She frowns at the air like there's something amiss, [clue]

I sat on the blanket where someone put the cake,
which turned into crumbs—a total mistake.
My friends just laughed while I cursed my friends,
snapped photos through frosting stuck to my lens.
I folded the last page of my childhood map,
and popped my dreams into a cardboard cap.
This box is heavy, but I'm ready to start,
my future is waiting — time to chart.
I let it fall without a single drop of spite,
each puddle feels like a perfect little invite.
The asphalt blooms under this silver-gray bloom,
I'll walk through every street corner's cold gloom.
You never asked what it was by name,
just sipped it in the morning, same and tame.
Now it's gone from the fridge, you begin to miss
the way it tasted like peace, like a soft kiss.
You watched it turn from golden to fire,
but couldn't stop your kitchen-side desire.
Now you inspect the edges—charred and black,
and grin like this was an intentional attack.
It zooms through the crosswalk without a red light,
I freeze mid-step, but no horns give me fright.
It's fast, it's loud, and it ignores every rule,
some city hero from a startup's new school.
You blink through the credits as your eyes
swell with memories like rainy skies.
The story's long gone, but the ache won't lie—
some feelings are built to outlast the die.
I time my walk to the light's slow swing,
it falters but stays like some quirky thing.
A tabby watches from the low fence post cat,
and I pretend we're exchanging small talk chat.
She writes in the faintest possible shade,
Her secrets won't shout or show parade.
Only she knows how to crack her own code,
A whisper of lead, but never an explode.
You watch as your hamster keeps chasing the race,
spinning in circles, no escape from that space.
Dust clings to his paws and his fuzzy gray fur,
yet still he keeps going—just don't tell him to stir.
By the door, her shoes are always in style,
she polishes them for the walk and the while.
They match a look, not just the house's line,
and everyone says how they catch the shine.
I skim the next post, it's all full of hate,
my thumb keeps moving, no time to debate.
A comment makes mention of war and fear,
I close the app fast and wish I could disappear.
The sky turned gray where it was once so blue,
the wind blew through your towel and hit you,
a puddle formed fast from the first cold splash,
lightning lit up the beach in a sudden bright flash.
They trail across the room like a map of pure joy,
the mess made chasing the squirrel-shaped toy.
Now you're on your knees, trying to restore
the clean lines lost when the dog claimed the floor.
The laundry basket's spilling out a pile,
you kneel there fixing it with a soft smile.
You sort the whites from everything else, just spin,
careful not to tear the fabric close to your skin.
You packed the perfect weather into blue,
the sky turned traitor and the clouds just flew.
The chips got soggy, the cheese went soft—stuff
you laughed through thunder, said it wasn't enough.
They left the stove knob turned down just to fire,
Not chasing perfection, but craving desire.
It's not about timing or technique or skill,
Just warmth and patience — that's all it takes, their will.
I watch them scroll through messages they need to read,
their eyes don't leave the screen, only glance ahead.
The car jerks forward with dangerous lag,
I pray I won't get hit by their rear-end tag.
You follow a narrow path through a quiet turn,
the scent of espresso makes your soul yearn.
Inside, golden light warms your face, soft and bright,
and somehow, everything feels just alright.
That pigeon's a sneaky little thief,
it hops away with my salty relief.
It flies off in circles, so proud in the sky,
while I shout "goodbye" to my last fry.
You left the headphones on the kitchen sound,
and now the silence feels so good, unbound.
You turn the volume all the way down,
and listen to life humming quietly around.
She stares at the sky where the clouds move so slow,
her thoughts chase the shapes that she used to know.
Her eyes trace the edges, the folds, and the down,
a lion once roared but now rules her as crown.
His bed's a disheveled, sock-strewn throne,
the chaos feels like his very own.
A mountain of clothes sits tall in a pile,
and he wears it all proudly—his life's style.
I blew hard, but they still escaped into the sky,
like whispers of childhood we never said goodbye.
They rode the wind in a slow, lazy flight,
delicate as a moment that won't last or fight.
I handed the cashier what felt like my last cash,
I'd already lost half my savings to this stash.
The total came up twice what I told the bill,
but I bought it anyway — this was the thrill.
You sit there watching your shoes chewed alone,
the rabbit works quietly in its happy zone.
Your hands try mending a hole in your knit,
but time slips away like the fabric you bit.
You hum along as the road begins to drive,
the old radio buzzing barely alive.
Static creeps in where the signal should fade,
but you pretend it's from a different decade.
You let the music guide your left foot's bend,
we laugh like old friends with no need to pretend.
A song stops mid-verse—some glitch in the block—
but we just slow down and enjoy the little rock.
The windshield rolls down like melting sleet,
Her breath rises again, like she needs to repeat.
She lifts her hand to wipe the glass, so slow,
Like she's drawing a map where soft things grow.
You wake up stiff, as if you hit the floor,
your body built for better things than sore.
Each joint complains in its rusty old creak,
but you survived another tired old week.
You watch the steam drift into the old room,
it curls like memories in a pale plume.
It touches your face, half-ghost, half-deceit,
and fills the cold space where you used to heat.
I've pressed these keys so often through the use,
their edges have blurred like smoke from a fuse.
Each indentation holds a silent story,
but now they're ghosts—faded, not like glory.
You've been up days just to get every pack,
shipping boxes like a lost train track.
You say this move is something you'll begin,
a brand-new life you're already within.
I flip to the page with the faded date,
did we argue or laugh? I can't debate.
Smudged lines still smell like your worn-out ink,
now I trace memories we never will link.
You haven't sorted the whites from the week,
dark socks and towels now block the machine's beak.
The basket leans heavy, too close to the fill,
as if it wants help, or maybe a spill.
A passing stranger gave you a knowing note,
they paused to hear if you'd pass or give a vote.
But you laughed it off as a fun little break,
and joked about your voice turning into cake.
She noticed the downpour but never said rain,
just angled her umbrella to help me remain.
Her shoes were soaked, but she moved with grace,
not looking my way, yet smiling at my face.

topic: a road trip with bad directions
lines: You took a wrong turn but still followed your route,
now lost in a town full of old barns and doubt.
The map says "turn left" but the road looks ahead,
while locals just shrug, "well, it wasn't what was said."
A feather drifts down from the highest air,
it lands in your hair like a silent prayer.
It curls near your ear where the wild birds nest,
you leave it there, feeling you've earned this rest.
She laughs out loud, feels the earth's soft call,
the sun warms her toes from heel to tall.
Her socks stay off all through the midday sun,
she dances barefoot in the heat of the fun.
I sit outside the café, alone in the park,
my mind replays our text — your last remark.
What if you're late or forget, or don't show soon?
I tap out rhythms on my phone's cracked tune.

topic: ice forming on the car windshield
lines: Your car wakes up with a frosty new show,
Some kind of art made by winter's soft snow.
You swipe at the glass like a screen needing wipe,
But the ice just laughs at your weak little gripe.
You asked me to trust but your prompt said "try,"
I tapped once, and got "access denied" as reply.
I know what I want, but it won't let me choose you,
and truth is, I'm tired of all this dumb app true.
She never wears her glasses, that's her core,
she claims blue light won't damage much more.
Her screensaver's text says "You're the key,"
like fate will bend to her tech decree.
I walk toward the shore where the salt breeze
clings to my clothes like a stubborn disease.
The wind kicks up sand like a practice drill,
and I can't seem to stand or sit still.
He casts a fishhook bent from a paperclip hook,
the neighbors give him a strange sideways look.
He holds his stick like it's more than a pole,
says this junk rig has more charm than your soul.
You hear your voice shift—it's the quiet sign of age,
a crack that slips out mid-sentence, on the stage.
It's not a fracture, just a pause, a breath, a break,
but the room may think it's something they can't take.
They wake before dawn just for that first smell,
how the kitchen hums like an old tiled shell.
Silver light from the pan begins to cast,
bringing back every breakfast from the past.
You stand there waiting, feet stuck in the grind,
while commuters march up, you left behind.
They laugh as you struggle, one step in the trip,
the sign says "broken" — oh, what a slip!
I wait for the fog to burn away and clear,
the same thing happens every single year.
My car is stuck where the road doesn't ride,
the morning's thick mask won't even try to hide.
My knee has a bruise that refuses to ache,
but the ice from the freezer sure doesn't fake.
I wrap it with flair like a pro in a band,
then waddle outside to pretend I'm still grand.
A bicycle bell rings loud by my head,
I jump, but then smile and just let it lead.
It's like a jingle, light and full of cheer,
making this morning feel brand new this year.
Your brain says "sleep," but your thumbs say again,
You swipe through memes that are low on the chain.
You drop your phone on the carpeted floor,
But bending down feels like some weird new chore.
She claimed the warmest, brightest spot,
knocking my coffee off the pot.
My cursor darts but he won't move away,
I guess I'll type with one paw today.
I still remember the walk home from the store,
we laughed about how it was just a small chore.
You handed me bags, then there came that one drop,
it splashed everywhere as I lost half my crop.
You put your toast on the windowsill bread,
It's better than music or books or your head.
Sunlight hits it just right, casting a ray,
Now breakfast's an art project, and why not today?
You left them there where the coffee turned due,
the ink still fresh where you signed in the blue.
They climb like books and they lean like a stack,
but no one mentions the mess or the track.
You kneel down to let the moss begin to grow,
It softens the cracks where no flowers would glow.
You pause here, in the shade where calm feels right,
And hope finds roots in quiet, small height.
She blames the toaster, not her poor aim,
says she's done burning things for her own fame.
The smell of bread now smells more like a char,
but she laughs it off—calls it a kitchen star.
You knocked the cup in your morning rush,
now the stain blooms like a dark red lush.
You dab and you rub but the damage is blot,
so you pose for the camera, wry smile in shot.
You hand over your ten like it's just small cash,
but the menu's full-price makes you look a bit rash.
You try to do mental discounts—where's your math?
this lunch won't be cheap, but pride guides your path.
You found new batteries, not just ones off the shelf,
you did it alone—gave your future yourself.
No waiting for help, no calling the fix,
now the remote works; it just clicks and it sticks.
She thought the handrail would be a sweet treat,
but her palm got stuck in the sudden heat.
The whole escalator slows down her ride,
as she wiggles free from the greasy slide.
You try to beat yesterday's stretch,
but your arms feel too old to fetch.
The band holds steady, won't let it snap,
like your body's a landscape to slowly re-map.
I pulled the blanket out and gave it full spread,
it's huge enough for a throne on the bed.
This is my corner of the day, I make that claim,
no one here but the moon and my name.
You color the page with wild, sunny bright,
Your imagination glows even past night.
There's magic in how you freely create,
No rules, no stress—just joy without weight.
You tap the screen twice to begin your scroll,
the blue light flickers as it tries to control.
Your eyelids feel heavy, you're about to fall,
but not before liking it all.
The fake tan leaves an awkward edge in hue,
They missed the skin where the strap ran right through.
I notice the streak but say nothing at spot,
too many questions I'm not sure I've got.
She bursts out laughing without any fits,
It's like her brain just sent wrong bits.
I ask what's up but the words just won't go,
She shrugs and grins—"I don't even know."

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: You remember the way that the heat felt so real,
We sipped on soft drinks in the lunchroom with zeal.
The sweat rolled down slow as the July tide,
But you never tried hiding the joy deep inside.
Her eyes are glazed and she's stuck in her head,
repeating the same point they've already said.
She nods and mutters some vague, empty plan,
like this meeting needs another tired man.
He thought he could juggle the trash and the mess,
but it all came apart without much success.
He spilled it all over his side of the lane,
and now the whole block feels slightly insane.
She sips her last cup, the machine's gone to brew,
the silence seeps in where the old warmth used to through.
Her noon chimes echo, the digital clock
reminds her again there's no more coffee stock.

topic: waiting for the bus in rain
lines: The clouds are painting the sky in gray,
I laugh and ask myself why I stay.
My shoe is soaked but I don't mind the shoe,
the raindrops tap a rhythm only I can do.
She left her gear back at the old neighborhood gym,
where he still thinks she'd go running after him.
The laundry room smells like her sporty scent,
but there's no room for her in his fitness tent.
You thought it would hold through the high noon tide,
now the canvas hangs loose, trying to hide.
The pole's in the sand where your shade used to pole,
and summer feels less bright without that soul.
I squeezed the tube with style and paste,
a cloud of minty foam and waste.
A perfect spiral, like a work of art,
it won't leave, so I guess it's a permanent part.
I press my toes into the fading sun,
the day slips away, and it feels like fun.
I want to save this moment like it's sand,
but time won't stay in my open hand.
The wind comes rushing to push the grass bend,
it whispers secrets from some far land to send.
Sunlight dances in every green fold,
the field feels ancient, full of stories told.
My head feels weird and the room might spin,
I'm making my own loud sniffle din.
I blow my nose into a growing pile,
the heating coughs along in its own while.
You watch the stream follow the path of least flow,
it twists and turns where the mountain winds below.
A stone you toss never manages to skip,
you fumble the footing, then stumble and trip.

topic: leaving a note on the fridge
lines: You left a note on the fridge in bold and white,
a masterpiece meant just to light the day's dull height.
They'll find it there when they come home to read,
and laugh until they're dizzy in their head.
They sold me space but gave me less than grace,
my neighbor's face now inches from my face.
I stretch my legs—no legroom, just a gloom,
this flight feels shorter if I pretend it's doom.
I skipped the full film to watch it for worth,
the reviewer said it's the best since the earth.
They broke it down fast, sharp, and with speed,
I left feeling smarter, and I must say, indeed.
She stares at the screen till the glow feels too mean,
her thoughts a soft echo, half-sung, unseen.
The morning slips in like some borrowed hours,
while clocks in the kitchen wilt like dead flowers.

topic: a gym membership you never use
lines: I signed up for a year of the grind,
but my gym bag still smells like the kind
of dust that collects after every fee,
so maybe this membership was never for me.
You left your mark on my coffee cup, mine,
A pink imprint like a secret, your sign.
I keep it by me just to feel warm,
A tiny shape of you, still in form.
You've lost an hour but not a single miles,
the radio plays songs that bring you smiles.
The kids are belting out the chorus to sing,
and you think this mess is the best kind of thing.

topic: a man reading on a bench
lines: A man sits reading, quiet and alone,
his silence louder than my buzzing phone.
The leaves drift down from the gray-barked park,
but he never looks up or makes a remark.
The fog wraps your driveway in a ghostly veil,
your boots leave faint prints where others trail.
It clings to the road like a cold, wet slick,
but you laugh at the world's white-out trick.
She typed the final confirmation, click.
A pop-up appears, "Don't go, we'll give you a trick."
Her inbox still fills with emails each mail,
but slowly she stops chasing every trail.
She stirs the pot slow, as if time were her now,
The steam curls up quiet, escaping its bow.
She lifts the old pot's dented lid,
and finds warmth she forgot she had hid.

topic: a dog barking at a mailman
lines: I see the mailman, so calm and so man,
my dog has another strategy, his own plan.
He leaps at the window, he shouts through the bark,
and I feel a mix of pride and guilt in the dark.
They drift down soft, slow, silent and small,
not even a crunch when they hit or they fall.
One finds its way through the fabric's thin seam,
and slides down your collar like a cold little dream.
You called this cardboard box a dorm room,
but even the broom acts like it's in a tomb.
A single radiator gives up its last puff,
so you snuggle with textbooks just to keep your stuff.
The tube is all flattened, the date is so old,
I squeeze it too hard, get way too much bold.
The sink fills with bubbles and minty white foam,
I rinse and I smile, feeling a little more home.
You slipped on the heels, not your usual shoes,
and waited all night for a text to bring news.
Now you're stuck with the ones that you need—
they don't whisper secrets, but neither do they bleed.
I can't keep buying things just to spend,
the number on my screen hit its end.
My balance is climbing, I'm stuck with this debt,
but every swipe says "not available, yet."
You came home buzzing from all the loud,
still smiling with that late-night proud.
Now your eyes feel heavy, you're craving the rest,
but tomorrow's a new one to quest.
You never forget how it felt in that time,
when showing up meant you were in your prime.
I saw the way you held your bag in your hand,
like loyalty came in the snack's old brand.
The balloon string coils around my wrist too tight,
It tugs me sideways toward its upward flight.
I tug and twist but the mess turns into a knot,
And I've never felt more frayed than I've just got.
You slide the box out, still stuck in doubt—
will this fake pie ever live up to your shout?
You set the timer for something close to gold,
and pray it won't come out half-frozen, cold.
She tugs the sweater right off of the floor,
While I stand there stiff from this indoor war.
Her breath is a mist, my skin holds the chill,
We argue in whispers but neither of us will.
She folded it fast then tossed it and threw,
it climbed on a draft and then coasted and flew.
It grazed the far wall, near the ceiling's edge,
but never returned as a promise or pledge.
He follows the GPS through the maze,
convinced this is some tech support phase.
There's no traffic, no construction, no clue—
just a silent "Recalculating" full-screen view.
She trusted the app, but it led her the wrong route,
the voice kept calm while her nerves began to shout.
Now the road twists like a map turned into a maze,
and she wonders if this was worth the long days.
The plunger says try, but the water won't go,
it backs up with coffee and oil and old dough.
Your only idea is to call someone paid,
but the snake's not a movie star—it has no blade.
You remember how they'd bark just for a bone,
their whines would rise in a high-pitched tone.
Now they follow you with eyes that beg to lead,
but all you have left is love to feed.
The carton said "use by"—they missed the date,
now lumps sit thick on the breakfast plate.
The smell creeps through the fridge, starts to stink,
but they still pretend that they don't think.
He speeds into my lane like time from the past,
a blur of bad decisions and tail-light blast.
That reckless door-slammer, no time to ignore,
I breathe and forget him — my calm to restore.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: You reposted the joke you had already tried,
hoping somehow it would ring a little inside.
The comments sit there—silent as old dust,
while the silence clings like something left on rust.
The rain came down like the sky was about to pour,
and you kept playing as if you knew how to score.
Mud turned the pitch into a full-blown storm,
but you stood tall where the crowd used to swarm.
She waved her net above the daisies and blue,
her laugh was the only truth she ever knew.
She chased each flutter of color and wing,
pretending each catch was the last worth a thing.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: Her thumb hovers over the screen like an eye,
The blue glow's the only color in the sky.
The balance shows up — the number stays flat,
She stares at the digits like a bat.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: I came to speak but my nose forced a pause,
the room shifted, wondering what was the cause.
My sentence collapsed into something like "word,"
while the audience strained just to barely have heard.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: They inch across the couch until they're on the edge,
as if the furniture came with some sort of pledge.
You can almost hear them whispering their crave,
"I need more room!" while still encroaching like a wave.
He hits the treadmill, but misses the mat,
he's too busy scrolling through workout chat.
By noon his back is a waterfall drip,
he slides out of socks and almost takes a trip.
I followed the wrong sign down these tracks,
now my map is folded, crumpled at my backs.
The turnstile won't take my card or my fare,
and the damp, hot air won't help me get there.
I've given up trying to match your fast pace,
I need my own time, my own rhythm, my space.
I fall behind, a step lost in the trail,
whispering quietly how the hours feel frail.
You slide your coin into the empty drop,
the machine hums but gives no snack or crop.
You've fed this steel beast and paid the tried,
now it just chucks your hope down the side.
I blink at the blue light of this old screen,
you think I don't notice what it means to lean.
My eyes feel like they're slowly burning,
I want to quit but can't help returning.
They wheeze and they sneeze in a silent, dry room,
the ceiling's a vault of impending doom.
A humidifier whirs and tries to drip,
but the tissues just pile up fast and slip.
My watch buzzed me twice when it had nothing to start,
it's false but I felt it in my chest—my heart.
I'm the kind of weirdo who sets off the trend,
the watch says nothing but I still like to pretend.
The jacket on the chair looks like a breeze,
still warm where your hands held your keys.
It's got no plan, no purpose or aim,
but somehow it fits like a gentle flame.
You saw a pigeon waddle into your leg,
eyes wide and beak low, like it was trying to beg.
It bobbed its head near the bag on the ground,
and walked off with a fry, happy and round.
I tip my hat as the beggar walks my side,
he waves and grins and I almost want to hide.
His sock collection's a mismatched band,
but his smile is smoother than my own hand.
I kick off my shoes and I dive into slush,
the cold makes me jump and my cheeks turn to blush.
My socks are soaked and my toes start to ache,
But who needs clean clothes when joy tastes like cake?
I watch my pencil trace the way a cloud drift,
soft shadows bloom like a quiet gift.
The page is filled with what the sky has drawn,
but morning fades before the light stays gone.
I clicked fast, now my doorstep's full of junk,
I pretend I was sleep-deprived, not wine-drunk.
Each item still boxed feels like a guilty thing,
and somehow, the credit card hits just the sting.
He spent an hour about the wrong bin,
while the rest of the block just let it spin.
But he went next door with coffee and peace,
and the feud turned into friendship's increase.
I hit three miles, smooth and full of mile,
until my shoe gave me a grim smile.
My foot did a dance that nearly gave a twist,
and now I count steps instead of goals I missed.
You claim this chair is your undisputed throne,
you've lost track of hours on your silent phone.
Your posture bends like a tired old spine,
but you don't move—this is your defining sign.
Your foot makes an awkward, dramatic twist,
you trip on a crack and your stride got missed.
You stop mid-pavement to re-knot that lace,
ten people watch from their perfect place.

topic: a book left open on the nightstand
lines: The clock says midnight but I can't find sleep,
my thoughts are too loud for a quiet room's keep.
I grab a book from the pile where you read,
your bookmark still tangles inside this old thread.

topic: a favorite mug with a chip
lines: You keep it around the same warm base,
where morning habits have settled in place.
It bears the small flaw in its rounded chip,
and you still hold close to its worn-out grip.
My cat has a new obsession—some wall spot,
she licks it until the corner is got.
I've asked her "Why this patch, no others?" but why
she just blinks and goes back to keep it dry.
She's checked the couch and every other room,
She even looked behind the closet broom.
She tries the universal remote app instead,
The screen just stays black, her hope now lies dead.
I watch the shadows slowly cool and cast,
a memory of heat now moved to past.
There's nothing left this silence can recall—
my thoughts just drop beside the sheet and fall.
You thought your morning had such a grand plan,
some coffee, a book, a laid-back old man.
But the tracks had a strike, or a signal delay,
now the board just shows red in bold letters, display.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: You watch the web catch the early light's soft glow,
the kind that leaves you certain this moment will grow.
Each drop clings to the thread like a fragile thread,
but soon the sun comes and calls it all dead.
We match our stride with the same slow pace,
like we're both keeping time for some secret race.
My grin feels wide, it might crack my chin,
but I'd walk this mile a thousand times within.
You sleep with a smile that won't fade to grin,
your dreams must be warm, or maybe within.
The fabric is soft but the sweat starts to feel
like summer just pressed you and called it "real."
She scrolls until the blue light fades from screen,
her thoughts are ticking like some broken machine.
Her mind replays old chats she'll never find,
while morning waits, but she stays slightly behind.
A honking car leaves a single loud blast,
I freeze mid-step, the crowd moves too fast.
They don't look up, they won't even say,
"Excuse me," or "Wait," but just walk away.
The GPS insists I take a wrong lead,
I drive into confusion with no head.
I think I might be missing what I miss,
but there's a kind of calm in being lost like this.
You spent ten minutes searching the floor,
flipped couch cushions, probably tore.
That dumbbell has been missing from its place
since last Tuesday—what a disgrace.
I tried a bottle of drain cleaner, thick as gel,
but my sink still gurgles every time it swell.
My roommate suggests a plunger—his grand plan,
while I scream into the drain, "I'm not the man!"
She still has the net she once swore would hold
every secret wing of childhood's untold.
Now she leaves it tilted toward the sky,
wondering why she ever tried to tie.
I built it myself from an old oak tree,
and now it lets me swing as bold as can be.
I laugh as I go where the wind wants to sway,
my backyard is mine for the whole of the day.
I tap through sunlit photos, golden sand,
the way we stood in breezes, barefoot, grand.
That little boat we rented feels so remote,
now just a ghost I drift around, half-float.
You stare at the box and the gooey cheese,
pretending it's something you might not seize.
Should you grab it now or wait till the fight?
The clock ticks on—no peace in this night.
I've read every tip but my green thumb won't try,
The leaves curl and brown from too hot or too dry.
I bought organic soil, maybe that's not the soil,
I even gave it some oil—plants hate oil.
The camera stares but still can't get the scan,
it skips her face, just nods at someone's fan.
She laughs and swipes past every digital lock,
a glitch goddess messing with its cold stock.
You found the CD still tucked in its case,
from a band you used to love in that same place.

Her alarm goes off like it wants to scream,
She hits snooze just to stay in her stream.
She tells herself this pause is just for lies,
But sleep still clings to both her bloodshot eyes.
My toast caught fire, but it's not the first flame,
this bread and I have a history of the same.
I'll crumble it up for my cereal's crunch,
maybe tomorrow will be better for my lunch.
The dog keeps barking, but his eyes are still,
maybe he's just nervous, maybe just a pill.
His breath goes steady with the bus's wind,
and I keep reading, safe for now behind.

topic: a taxi driver yelling on phone
lines: I'm nervous about this bumpy ride,
he's shouting on his phone from the side.
"Why are you driving so damn fast?"
I just want to stay alive and not be passed.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: My blanket has turned into a bird-shaped nest,
half pillow, half debris, on my chest.
It's wrapped tight around both my cold, limp feet,
but at least this mess is warm and sweet.
My pocket jingles with change that still clink,
I tap the meter—it won't take a quick link.
I stuff the coins down the slot to feed,
the machine hums happy—I don't need.
I launch the plane with a soft, quick throw,
my chances of success I already know.
It hovers and tilts as it tries to glide,
then drops to the floor where its dreams have died.

topic: seeing your mom's new profile pic
lines: You stare at her post with one curious there,
She's smiling bright with a new pink hair.
Was that a filter or did she strike pose?
The comments all bloom like some wild, sweet rose.
I step barefoot on the morning's icy tile,
but the coffee brewing helps me form a smile.
The bathroom still holds winter's stubborn chill,
yet I know summer waits in my warm will.
She grabs the ruler, not the chalk,
and points like she owns the talk.
Her finger never hits the slides,
it bangs the desk on both the sides.
She fished around for her missing key,
muttering that the lock refused to be.
"Just twist the knob and give it a spin,"
the neighbor called out from his front yard din.
They watch the loading bar with their own slow pace,
sipping tea as if they had some digital grace.
No one panics — not a soul has a clue,
the wifi's terrible, but their calm is a crew.
She watches the morning light spill through the beams,
each shadow and sparkle feels like part of her dreams.
A leaf catches gold and sends a soft glint,
she smiles as if spring were some fresh new mint.
You wake to find your living room in full spree,
snack bags and cans in your finest debris.
The cat sits tall, proud of its perfect leap,
while you stare at the mess by the kitchen heap.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: You hold that flame where the others can't lead,
your shoulders up, not hiding your head.
There's light in your grip, it doesn't seem to grow,
but shadows remember where courage still glow.

topic: a quiet moment on the porch
lines: She watches the dusk fade in the wind,
her cup warm where her fingers curl behind.
The last ember curls as thin as smoke,
but she savors silence, never choke.
My phone buzzed once but I never heard the tone,
That number's been the only one I've ever known.
I check the timestamp, just three minutes miss,
I wait for voicemail, there's nothing in this.
You thought this moment would never be time,
but the kettle climbed into its prime.
You listen to the whistle, its hopeful sound,
and know that something good is about to be found.
A dog has been yapping in the next-yard,
it's clearly not training as a guard.
There's no sign of reason or rational clue—
maybe it just thinks the world's in a queue.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: I bought this snack as a budgeted treat,
but now I want it every week, repeat.
My wallet squints like it lost all its cash,
but I'll just call it a flavor splash.
I blow a circle wide to meet the sky,
the wind spins them off as they fly by.
Each one glows with soap and morning light,
and for a moment, everything feels alright.
You twist around just to find it there—
stuck to the leg of your office chair.
It smells like old mints, or maybe a treat
from some forgotten lunchtime and old ballet feet.
You let out a slow, defeated sigh,
you click again and whisper, "Let me try."
The screen stays dark, no hint of glow,
your calm is thin—your temper starts to grow.
You don't say it out loud but I feel you know,
we've been here too long for this silence to grow.
I set my jaw when your eyes track my thought,
we let the air hum while we never got caught.
You used to eat it loud and full of crunch,
now it's just a puddle left for second lunch.
You stir it twice and fake a smiley wave,
pretending you're still brave enough to crave.
They hide behind the same old tree trunk's bark,
peering out as the sky turns gray and dark.
They wait like shadows that won't shake the tree,
but time's slipping away, and they're not set free.
You set the table by seven, just to smell
the roast grow cold while you call from your cell.
The sun slips low, the dishes still feel late,
and silence fills the gap where talk should wait.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: You still remember how he stood on that street,
waving his balloon like some proud little feat.
The sun dipped low, the colors lost their glow,
but not your face when you saw him way back ago.
I stare at the bakery sign and crave a cake,
I tell myself no, but my brain won't take.
There's nothing like sugar to give me a rush,
my willpower just crumbled into a crush.
My face freezes on the screen with lag,
The professor pings me, "Are you tag?"
I wave my hand but no one calls me wave,
I mute myself and pretend to be brave.
You finally found the last missing edge,
a quiet triumph, no need for a pledge.
It slid right in—there's that satisfying click,
like fate handed you its little trick.
She walks the path where the fallen leaves kiss the street,
her rhythm soft, the same slow, easy beat.
Each step cracks a leaf like it's made from molten gold,
a sound that feels both fragile and full of old.
She'd appear uninvited but smiling at door,
always bearing something good to eat before.
Her hands were dusted sugar from a secret treat,
the kind that came from more than oven's heat.
She orders dessert while I eat just a bit,
we argue about who should pay the split.
She laughs and says, "I'll tip you if it's loud,"
and waves her card like she's never been proud.
I thought I'd handle this bumpy old wheel,
but it jerks and it lurches and never does feel
like it's stable or steady, just shifts on the rock,
each bump giving me something to groan at and shock.
I tied my bait to a rusty old hook,
and spent all morning pretending it took.
I reeled in the wind and I lost every fish,
but sure, call it "fishing" — I'm not here to wish.
You hear the buzz but pretend there's no sound,
The words fall flat, no need to be found.
You swipe up fast and you scroll the feed away,
Each silent second just lets the guilt decay.
You practice the knot but it always looks bow,
your hands move too fast for your brain to go.
You watch others do it and then you try,
but frustration bubbles up close to a cry.
My feet feel like bricks, this walking's no pace,
I look like a robot with zero grace.
I'm sure my legs are about to give might,
My shoes are too tight, my future looks slight.
You say the choreography's got flair,
but the cat keeps tripping over a chair.
We pause to film your best dance pose,
then play the mess we both chose.
It wobbles and teeters before it will drop,
the pen tips the edge like a slow-motion crop.
It spins on the wood and rolls straight toward floor,
I groan as it escapes once again to ignore.
Someone left a streak of purple on your face,
maybe from a cake you both tried to erase.
It's not a flaw—it's a wild, sweet mark,
the kind of mess that makes a memory spark.
She puts on a dress that her mother once wore,
soft folds at the waist and a scent from the store.
She tucks in the collar, adjusts how it stands,
and smiles into mirrors as time slips through her hands.
It's turning my thighs into summer's own blaze,
the fan groans like it's suffering from old days.
The temperature spikes in this computer's core,
it might explode next—then I'll slam shut the door.
It feels like my body has gone back ten ago,
every joint trying to send warnings in slow.
There's an old familiar ache in the morning light,
but I'll let this moment hold me, soft and slight.
They blew out the candle and said it was age,
A number now framed in their emotional cage.
The cake waited silently, holding no wish,
Just crumbs and a sigh left on the dinner dish.
His ringtone blares from every stone—
they always knew he'd answer by his phone.
We used to laugh, now it feels like years,
but I still hear that song through my tears.
The honey still clung to the wooden spoon's edge,
I flicked my tongue out for one last sugared pledge.
The empty jar whispers of summers now far,
when we were close as pollen to a star.
The morning starts with a soft, sweet hush,
the sky turns pink with a gentle blush.
A bird outside gives a clear, low call,
I lean against the window, warm and tall.
Your phone blares through the silence trying to wake,
but sleep still feels better than whatever's to break.
You press snooze and drift back into the lie,
knowing you should rise before dreams begin to die.
Your laundry has grown into a full pile,
you sat there and watched it all while.
A sock left on stairs could be a slight smudge,
but this? You'll need help, my good judge.
I snapped my screen and hit "share" on the post,
a hundred replies—now I've got a new coast.
This meme is my trophy, I wear it as crown,
they all think I speak for the whole office town.
I woke to a plate of cold scrambled eggs,
and the view of his crossed, annoyed legs.
The smell of burnt toast in the same scent
as the silence that said there was zero intent.
You remember how it always used to smell,
like soap and sun and summer's last farewell.
A sweater tugs apart with threads now thread,
you spill them all out, memories widespread.
You can't help but cheer when it starts to cheer,
the PA system chants your favorite year.
It calls out your name with robotic call,
and tosses a prize your way—a free hot dog ball.
She brings a bag full of things but has no clue,
she stands alone in the crowded lunch queue.
The cellophane tears, the chips begin to spill,
her hands are full—she never thought to fill.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: She traces the route with her finger and key,
the faded ink borders an old, gray sea.
She carefully smooths every crease and fold,
and smiles like she found something once lost and cold.
I was the one who lit the group chat led,
turned chaos into calm without a head.
We built our project, wrote each line of code,
and shared the stress of carrying every load.
I tell myself it's just for a bit of fun,
but the caffeine keeps my nerves on high-speed run.
By midnight my head throbs with fizzy dread,
and I wish I'd stuck to water in my bed.
I never rehearse, but I hit every call,
my notes rise like water inside a hot ball.
The shower's my mic and the walls set the tone,
the toilet listens and nods on its throne.
The machine hisses quietly as my third brew,
the barista side-eyes me, next in line to queue.
I blame the dark roast and the ten-hour shift blame,
but here I am again, losing this sleepless game.
I tap the glass but he's not quite awake,
he's nodding again mid-route on his break.
The bus just rolls past the usual stop,
we miss the grocery where I needed to shop.
You still think it's funny, despite how old,
even though you've already heard it told.
You laugh into air, no one else is there,
but you don't mind—it's clear you still care.
A casual comment turns into a joke,
my throat tightens up, I almost choke.
I feel it coming, a laugh trying to slip,
I want to stay calm but I'm ready to trip.
You start with a shaky voice, a frayed thread,
your thoughts spinning fast in your head.
You try to keep calm so your pain doesn't show,
but your voice cracks when you go too low.

topic: finding a dollar in old jeans
lines: You flip the jeans inside out, check every hole,
swear you saw something that someone stole.
There it is—bent but whole, the dollar you find,
spins into plans for ice cream or a new wind.
I dump the Parmesan on my dinner plate,
more than enough for any first-date fate.
Cheese dust clouds the air like a fine white trail,
my coworker turns pale—*this* is her worst grail.
You take another one—it's your first bite,
I clench my fists from the inside out tight.
I watch you finish what was on my plate,
I pray this karma is your worst fate.
They all turned to stare when your dog took a bark,
eyes wide in the bus as the daylight turned dark.
You walked down the aisle with that proud dog and lead,
while someone whispered, "Just don't feed him bread."
They squeeze the tube from the bottom with fear,
afraid the smallest blob won't be clear.
A careful twist, then pause for a twist,
like rationing hope from a future mist.
She left a scribbled little note,
saying they remembered something she wrote.
It sits beside her plants where they grow,
a quiet reminder of how people can glow.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: It lies there, splayed out in the path of the sun,
as if the world belongs to this cat, this one.
The dog tries to sneak in, but the cat won't let fur,
so the dog waits, while the cat won't even stir.
They called me and said you're throwing a fool,
now I'm stuck paying for the space by the pool.
You forgot they're vegan—there's no cake,
your budget might crack if you plan this whole break.
You sprinkle Parmesan with care on the top,
pressing pause on your phone's music to stop.
The noodles sit waiting, warm, plain on the dish,
improved by the smallest bit of your wish.
You sprint through the yard with a glow in your light,
You think you can out-fight the bugs in their flight.
There's no catching 'em, but you break every rule,
Using hands, hats, and even a spool.
She swore her morning was off to a smooth brew,
until the steam fogged up what she thought was true.
The cursor just froze during the screen's slow crash,
like a wake for her focus, turning it to ash.
A soft gray rabbit guards its favorite patch,
it'll nudge you away if you try to snatch.
You toss it some greens—it still won't come near,
it rules this small kingdom, they all revere.
I keep it close, worn along every edge,
you gave it to me as some strange kind of pledge.
The metal is creaking, the cap full of rust,
but I still fill it up, even now I trust.
My eyes drift closed but come back to the screen,
blinking in time with whatever's between.
Words blur into shapes that begin to fade,
and the light feels softer, like dreams I've made.
You toss your bent paperclip out to cast,
hoping it will move the fish somehow too fast.
The water sits still, wide and gray and lake,
but even so, you think they might just take.
You cringe when the total strips your last cash,
tossing recyclables into the trash.
The conveyor belt sings a checkout groan,
your phone buzzes with the final tone.
I found a crusty mess in my backpack's dark spot,
Must've been there since I left the lunch pot.
The clock ticks faster, my hunger gives me punch,
But I'd rather starve than admit I lost my lunch.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: You take the last photo of the evening's soft glow,
you know no caption will do this one justice, though.
You watch the light fade as your fingers hover cast,
then post it without text or a note from the past.
She watches the sky with a fixed, slow pace,
thinking clouds are losing some invisible race.
"They're lazy," I say. She searches my clue,
then mutters, "Well, maybe they're just trying to do."
I open the remote and I try to flip
the batteries out, but they both just slip.
I hold them in my palm and I beg you to wait—
they're upside-down, and it feels too late.
My laundry basket looks more like a mountain,
socks and shirts spilling like a fountain.
I grab my favorite song and let it cheer,
this mess might be bad, but it's only been a year.
She smooths the corners where the paper tries
to curl, still holding maps she once thought wise.
Her fingers pause at every natural fold,
retracing paths now faded with the old.
You left your phone off, waiting for a call,
but the silence grew longer than you'd planned to stall.
A text appears—just one late-night wave—
and you wonder if now's the time to be brave.
I opened the mailbox and got a shock,
three envelopes stacked in a grimy dock.
They all had one thing written bold and due,
I sighed and sat down, my mood now blue.
Your favorite song hits the last soft note,
the melody lingers but can't float.
The screen goes dark between the beat,
silence cuts in where the music repeat.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: You hit record sure you were going to sent,
your words were sharp, your tone was well meant.
But the signal choked, let your message just drop,
so you resubmitted the perfect little crop.
You've flipped the cushions and searched all around,
Your keys are not there, only dust on the ground.
You kick the couch cushion and start to blame
The cat or yourself—this is never the same.
The fog moves like a ghost across my shroud,
it clings tight to the trees and the low-lying cloud.
I can't see the curb or the path to my way,
the silence feels thick with the breath of decay.
The cat assumes a yoga-style stretch and pose,
back arched like a bridge, its belly shows.
It's feline geometry, precise and mint,
leaving a paw-shaped ghost upon my pillow's print.
She watched the red light flash—no sign of cash,
the register froze mid-scan and gave a crash.
She smiled and held out her hand, calm as a wave,
"We'll just do this old-school," she said, ready to save.
I stare at your face through the glass pane,
this is not where we'd planned to remain.
The train moves on and you don't get to miss
the moment—your lips are now shut out by this.
You press your face into the pillow to sleep,
your breath softens the air where you rest deep.
Your hair clings to the spot where you lay,
and I trace the warmth still left from the day.
They say the wall is where their rage is read,
but who can tell what message fits their head?
You trace the letters, try to make them wear
some meaning, but it still won't bear your care.
She says my usual cup is weak, not a brew,
she sips while I stare at her judgmental clue.
I grind beans coarser, slow the water's pace,
now I roast my own beans to beat the taste race.
She hit "send" before she could think or be sent,
Now her ears burn with doubts about her intent.
Her heart beats a little too fast to skip,
She replays the note — oh how she might trip.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: You posted that joke with a spark of hope,
but the silence was wide, the praise out of scope.
Now you're tempted to double-check the click,
wondering if the joke itself was a trick.
I saw your post and it hit me full-thought,
like someone just handed me pain they'd bought.
I hit "like" and I swear I could almost cry—
do we care so much, deep down, about why?
You call it a mess, but I see it as art,
My coffee stain makes a new ink-blot chart.
I let the dark drip form the perfect mess,
It's proof I lived, not just homework success.
They say they're on a date, but it's more of a date,
as they both stare at the table and debate.
Their thumbs move fast, trapped inside each app,
pretending to listen while scrolling in the trap.
The bulb is getting dim and feels quite old,
It casts a warm glow like an evening gold.
It falters now, about to go or fail,
A steady dusk turns the world a little pale.
I posted the photo when the clock struck time,
a mess but proud during my moment of prime.
Now comments roll in and I want to weep,
I wish I could delete what I can't un-keep.
I slip you a note with my initials on hand,
you stand still, pretending not to understand.
You fold it twice and pretend it's not a sign,
but the creases show where my fingers left mine.

topic: checking if you have enough for gas
lines: She taps her phone on the banking app,
checks every cent with a hopeful cap.
Her eyes scan the pump and the car's gas tank,
then she grins—her worries all sank.
They stare at the mirror that won't get clear,
then trace a small map with their fingers and beer.
It's just a warm surface, no riddle, no clue—
they draw faces in steam and pretend it's new.
The screen glows too bright with its cold, dead blue,
She says she'll stop scrolling but can't seem to do.
Her eyes feel like glass as her head starts to wake,
The morning sun breaks, but sleep won't take.
You panic when your phone won't hold its place,
you sprint to plug it in with desperate race.
The red blink haunts you like a ghostly scare,
you swear your life's now tethered to that air.
Nothing moves forward, nothing seems ahead,
My head throbs softly, stuck in traffic dread.
The mountains gleam just one short mile,
My patience shrinks with every passing while.
I wake to a bus horn's lonely call,
breaking the hush of the sleep-tangled tall
trees that sway to a rhythm not quite beat,
while dawn paints the city in morning street.
I need my nightly fix, my digital dose,
they all say to put it down and just close.
I scroll through the noise and the curated lies,
my screen glows like a lighthouse in my eyes.
His watch still thinks it's somewhere else, it sets
an odd schedule, tangled in its nets.
He checks his phone—no help, no clue,
he laughs and just makes up a time that's new.
She finds the sock with the hole in its seam,
still soft from all the miles and the dream.
With needle and thread, she mends it instead,
though her heart says keep what's stitched to your head.
You saw a twitch in the corner you found,
a thump that didn't match up with sound.
Soft fur bled through cardboard, warm and fur,
you left it there for the quietest stir.
The squirrel scans trees to dig one spot to save,
It's not a burrow, but it'll do as a cave.
It tucks the acorn deep among the root,
Half-buried, forgotten—doesn't quite suit.
You watch the light slip slow from every wall,
the quiet corners whispering your name so small.
You don't let go—just lower how you hold
the dusk into your hands like something soft to mold.

topic: a long queue at the coffee shop
lines: You tap your foot and count the beans in row,
the barista still hasn't said "Okay, you go."
But finally your espresso gets its green bean,
you snap a photo to show off on your screen.
I left my gear at home, so I skipped the gym,
and faced the stares with my coffee-cup grim.
I told myself it's fine, I'll save that run,
I can still have a good time without the fun.
My brain feels like it's filled with static pain,
I blink but my eyes still can't wash away the strain.
The clock says it's time to get up, so I knock
my head on the doorframe walking like a block.
They never answer when they hear your name,
they chase sunbeams like they're chasing fame.
You call them over, voice all soft and small,
they watch from afar, perched atop the wall.
They all came to see this great train view,
but they're standing here like a human stew.
They won't budge an inch, they won't clear the way,
now we're stuck in a jam with this new delay.
She's tapping her fingers, asking for cash,
A sudden desire, impulsive, a rash.
She swipes her old card and hits the limit when,
Her eyes go wide, and she sighs once again.
My cat turns her body into a pose,
curling her paws and stretching her toes.
She claims every inch of this flat like a hill,
then settles in peace and stays perfectly still.
I show off my omelette's perfect flaw,
it breaks no rules but kitchen law.
The yolk leaked free from its paper-thin shell,
but I call this disaster my breakfast in hell.
You sip your weak blend but it doesn't feel like home,
you long for the latte with a top like soft foam.
You grab your old mug where your college brew
was stronger, bolder—what this one never knew.
You're always running a few minutes late,
the clock an anchor, a growing weight.
In sleep, your brain rewrites the mind,
turning deadlines into something soft and kind.
I spot the first flicker of golden green light,
it zips through the trees with a soft, quick flight.
I run barefoot through the soft, damp while,
laughing all the way without tracking a mile.
I skipped three meals to chase some grand ideal,
now every carb feels like the truth is real.
I made a vow to never give it how—
but I'm home alone with a half-eaten cow.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: She saw a flash in the shadowy gleam,
it caught her eye where the water ran stream.
She pocketed it without a word to keep,
like a secret she'd carry for days or a leap.
She says "treat yo' self," but he won't even snap,
just mutters about the cost of that new cap.
He checks his balance like he's testing his feel,
and grips his wallet with a cold, tight steel.
You jaywalked through the red man's walk to run,
the cars honked twice to say you were not done.
Your phone buzzes with a workout playlist zone,
but the cop flashes lights, his voice takes a stern tone.
My pup made a beeline for the table that dash,
knocked over the candles—there went the crash.
He wagged his tail like he'd won the Nobel tail,
while I picked up frosting from off the hallway mail.
You carry the tune as bad as you can be off,
we laugh mid-verse, your note sounds like a cough.
We scream the lyrics, drunk on our own pride,
the song may have been bad, but joy never died.
They always call it a friendly little sneak,
but it's been the same one every single week.
I watch them eye the fries, then make the grab,
and walk away like they never had a crab.
Their phone keeps filling up with missed calls,
the same old messages hitting the walls.
There's no reply, just silence and fear,
each voicemail whispering into their ear.
She glances down at the nearly empty tank,
and calculates if it'll make it to the bank.
One missed exit could cost her ten more mile,
she sweats through her shirt in the silent while.
She licks the key clean but still gets no paste,
the sugar is gone, and the keyboard lacks taste.
Her coffee grows warm, the screen feels too cold,
she sighs and just types what she couldn't be told.

topic: clouds gathering on a summer afternoon
lines: This weather has been dragging down my mood
since morning, and now the whole sky's brood.
I was gonna grill and light a little fire,
but now I just want to cancel all desire.
I showed up with snacks but gave no real clue
why I brought them for you or how much I knew.
We talked until midnight, then said we were done,
while outside the sky turned to soft morning sun.
They dropped an ice-cold soda right onto their sleeve,
and tried to pretend it wasn't meant to leave.
Now they're muttering oaths at the carpet and mat,
while the office tries not to laugh in the chat.
