You snap a photo of the scenic view,
then vow you'll never use super glue.
You're told these trinkets are a steal to spend,
but your wallet cries when charged a new friend.
You swore the humidifier had a real seal,
but woke up sniffling through your cold cereal meal.
Your throat feels like sandpaper, a slow-burning ache,
you beg for a mist but the machine won't take.
She calls her routine a delicate art,
each steep measured down to the last chart.
Her desk is a shrine to the perfect brew,
where lesser mortals can't dare to view.
You stare at your phone like the answer is screen,
The tension is coiled tight somewhere deep between.
You pop another gummy as if it were pill,
But laughter's the only thing giving you thrill.

topic: a quiet moment on the porch
lines: I rock on the creaky old wooden swing,
the breeze picks up and it moves like a thing.
My cat yawns wide in her patchwork of cat,
while I sip coffee and pretend we have chat.
I joined the diet with a strict, weird plan,
but by Tuesday lunch my will had already ran.
I left the protein powder in the bathroom pack,
and now I'm just a woman with a secret snack.
Your phone buzzed once with a missed call,
She called at noon while you were at the mall.
You'll pretend you tried but couldn't reply,
She'll ask the same thing when you see her, why.
You follow the ant trail like it's a sacred line,
convinced it's a message, a hidden sign.
They carry crumbs through cracks in the dust,
and you swear the whole world hinges on their trust.
The shovel makes a clanking, tinny chime,
I lift my arms like I'm climbing a climb.
I toss the chunk in a lazy arc of snow,
this could be art—let's call it my little show.
You realize your friends aren't answering calls,
their silence has grown up against all these walls.
But maybe it's time to plant a new kind of seed,
and trust that new people can show up, indeed.
Your playlist acts like it's cursed by bad tech,
I hit replay five times just to check.
You call it a glitch—say it's easy to fix,
but I know the real reason: you're up to tricks.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: They thought it was bad, the way they chose the pose,
but said nothing about how they look in these clothes.
The real story's in every slight flaw,
a life lived clearly — that's the unspoken law.
She thinks she's the first one who ever sees
the bulb blinking fast like a slow-motion disease.
She toggles the switch, but it won't really tries
to hold steady — the glow tells the same old lies.
She stares at her screen instead of what's ahead,
Her blinker still flashes long after she's dead.
Her foot floats above the gas and the brake,
One glance was enough to become her mistake.
I stare into my cereal's watery bowl,
wondering if my breakfast was worth the soul.
A spoonful brings a smile, a strange little lift,
maybe this mush is a strange kind of gift.
You feel so strong when the dry wind starts strong,
your sneezes keep coming like storm waves along.
Your nose is on fire, but you won't let it burn,
this sickness returns, yet you never learn.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: You see the same folks every Sunday again,
They sit there unmoving, they quietly remain.
You switch to the back pew near the confession booth,
Hoping to hide but the stares cut their truth.
They hit "send" instead of "save," the message went,
Now their regret is crumpled, slightly bent.
You'll never know how close they were to lose
the words you read as old, but meant as news.
You bought this cheese solely for the meat,
now you stare at your pasta, no heat.
It slipped off the grater and it just fell,
such a tiny mishap feels like hell.
She gives me a look like she knows the clue,
raises her brow in a silent hue.
I open my mouth but I have nothing to say,
so I turn and walk slowly away.

topic: seeing your mom's new profile pic
lines: I saw your mom's new photo, now set as her old,
the years haven't softened the way she is bold.
Her bangs are still flipped, the same golden hair,
but her smile feels older, wiser, still fair.
My goldfish stares up from the tank as I float,
her tiny mouth opens like a small boat.
She takes each flake in a crunch and a chew,
though she never gives hints where the fun is due.
The sky starts to blush with a soft morning glow,
the ice on the lake sparkles like fresh-fallen snow.
She sits by the edge and she stirs the still wake,
the silence holds fast till the sun cracks the break.
That chipped mug in the sink tells quiet lies,
having seen a thousand coffee-splashed eyes.
It watches as you map out your next plan,
still loyal to the hands of the old lone man.

topic: a coffee cup on the curb
lines: You toss your coffee cup on the curb's side,
hoping it vanishes by the morning tide.
It still has half a swirl of leftover cream,
now fueling raccoon dreams in a drain stream.
She tries to twist it but still won't fit,
the plug and socket are stubborn as it.
Something feels off, out of place, all wrong,
like she's moving through life one step off song.
You've learned to count the cost with every age,
your spending now matches a smaller stage.
You check the price tag more than once to feel
if something's worth the risk, or just surreal.
You wore your favorite hoodie, too tight,
and hummed an old song late into the night.
But the notice stayed there, right where it's due,
a silent red marker with no easy clue.
I didn't have the heart to peel it from my thought,
though we had already grown apart and fought.
It's held through storms and time, this old weather,
clinging there, like we were still together.
It sways with her steps, a weight on the swing,
she carries the world in this heavy thing.
Her lunch is still zipped deep in the lock,
but she doesn't complain—just smiles like a rock.
She bought a dress marked down for the weekend sale,
but the cashier told her some confusing tale.
She double-checked, then sighed and paid,
happy to join the chaos parade.
Her morning coffee ended at the clock,
but now the machine makes a quiet knock.
A warm aroma fills up her kitchen light,
and the day still might take a better shape tonight.
I scan the snack aisle with a growling stomach view,
my willpower simmers like slow-cooked stew.
I tell myself I'll skip the bag of salted load,
but my brain's in full "impulse buy" mode.
You left your mismatched socks out on display to clash,
and now they're a statement you won't ever dash.
They lie there unapologetic on the floor,
while others try to match what you choose to ignore.
The teacher's cough echoes through the empty hall,
She clears her throat like it might be her final call.
Her voice goes rough, her throat feels too dry,
The lesson grinds to a wheezing die.
A single drop refuses to flow,
it taunts me with its agonizing slow.
It's like nature's making some sad joke,
I'm halfway through my speech—I choke.
You check your flight status again at the gate,
The clock ticks slower, the tension feels weight.
You shift your bag, but you can't change the pace,
There's nowhere to breathe in this tight-laced space.
They say these crayon marks hold great claims,
like genius blooming through childish flames.
It's just a messy page after hours of stress,
not art—but they still want to frame your dress.
She spends all morning fixing that one patch,
while the bird tears up her perfect thatch.
It hops and it digs where she just made the soil,
like some feathery thief with a beak full of oil.
You've taped the password where the world can hide,
behind the router where no eye should slide.
But every guest now scans the wall with fear,
convinced the note holds secrets yet unclear.
I'm never quite sure how to say "your,"
I stumble through phrases like "guided tour."
I'll probably miss every joke they miss,
but I'll nod at everything and call it *this*.
I check the forecast—gray again for these skies,
the clouds reflect my tired, heavy eyes.
My boots sit dry where the puddles used to trail,
and time moves pale, with nowhere else to sail.
She starts with a bend that still makes the steel gleam,
linking them slowly like silver in stream.
Her desk gets a border, a fringe that's all done,
she saves every sparkle the afternoon sun.
The bacon is dancing with sizzling crackle,
I grab tongs to flip this greasy tackle.
You watch from the couch, never saying you,
just laughing as I try to not burn it do.
He could play for endless, silent hours,
building battles out of matchstick towers.
His tiny world was built from plastic world,
now he sits alone, just memories curled.
I hit the button and it won't even scan,
the screen's frozen, no receipt, no pan.
Customers glare while I reach for cash,
I'm seconds from shouting or just having a rash.
I blow out the flame that marks another age,
my life turning chapters, fast becoming a page.
I taste the icing, feel the spark to live,
and vow to fill this year with something to give.
She spends hours each morning on each little lace,
both feet planted firmly in the wrong place.
Her frustration builds—she's close to a tear,
but next year, she'll run without even a peer.

topic: finding a dollar in old jeans
lines: She flips the pocket and she finds a dollar find,
crumpled and dusty, long left behind.
It's not much in gold, but feels like something more,
a quiet reward from her jeans, and an old score.
I poured the milk too early this bowl,
it's soured my mood and cramped up my soul.
There was a time I loved every crunch,
now it's just glue on a soggy lunch.
She left it open at the very top,
the curds started rising—never a stop.
Now she stares at the mess, no will to pour,
her heart is a little bit milk-sicked and sore.
You circle the only checkmark, full of joy,
then flip the page and pretend it's a toy.
One task done feels like a tiny win,
so you pick another and start to begin.
I dropped my cup on the hardwood floor,
it shattered loud—just a minute before.
I scoop up ice and the sticky mess,
and laugh through tears, calling this a bless.
You watch the yarn begin to gently flow,
it slips through fingers, spinning fast and low.
Each twist becomes a playful, colorful loop,
the threads march forward, dancing off the troop.
You squeezed the last bit out at morning's first dawn,
the taste of mint already feels like it's gone.
I twist the empty shell to pop off the cap,
and toss it in the trash where memories snap.
Your GPS insists the turn was wrong,
but you paid good money for this song.
It keeps drawing arrows down the route,
now you're lost and starting to doubt.
I squeezed too hard, now the tube's out of paste,
it oozes down the drain and coats the waste.
It hardens by the morning, just a drip
from the faucet—but I lost my hold, my grip.
I bolted upright and my vision went head,
I staggered like Jell-O on crumbly bread.
My blood pressure dropped and I nearly swoon,
I clutched the wall as if leaning on the moon.
I tried to look cool as I grated the top,
but cheese flew out of my hand like I'd lost my stop.
Now Parmesan dust lingers all over the mess,
yet somehow this meal still tastes like a success.
You lift your gaze up into the sky,
Watching the clouds pass by way too high.
Time won't stop, but still you let it grow,
Waiting for something bright to start to glow.
You check your plate—still gunked with yesterday's plate,
the dishwasher hums like it's mocking your fate.
There's suds but no scrub, no bite in that foam,
you hand-wash it all and go home.
You hear the buzz from your sleeping phone,
but fear replying if you're all alone.
A message pops up—just two words, a knock,
like someone still cares what kind of night you rock.
You found the half-cup of milk past its date,
but maybe it's just not too late to wait.
It might still turn into something that could,
if you're lucky, become a better kind of good.

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: You grip the handlebars and turn the wheel,
your palms sweating from the fear you feel.
A car zips out of nowhere from the block,
and you freeze, heart racing with the shock.
You pile the cheese in a lopsided heap,
it's pre-grated and sad from the grocery cheap.
You toss the noodles and aim for a swirl,
but half ends up stuck to your shirt like a girl.
You found the stick still warm against the floor,
some ghost of summer stuck there before.
You left it there like a half-erased trace,
the last thing from you this spot will erase.
You thought the vacuum did more than just play,
but your cat still pretends it's alive today.
They pounce with full seriousness, take that leap,
and launch themselves at the biggest dust heap.
You left your love on the rim with a gloss,
Now every sip feels like a soft, slow loss.
I keep the mug to hold that faint trace,
but it's just yours in a quiet, empty space.
My dog is always trying to take the lead,
darting ahead with joy in his head.
I can't keep up with how fast he wants to run,
but I'd never trade this crazy, wild fun.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: I found an old box with a rusty lock,
I fumbled the key but I gave it a knock.
It clicked and I flung the lid open wide,
there's confetti and a note that says "Inside!"
I watch them fall and I bet they will slide,
but sometimes a breeze makes one come inside.
They race each other in jagged-line run,
like secrets spilled and then quickly undone.
She left her gym clothes in the sun for a smell
only the dog seems to tolerate the spell.
It's less a laundry basket and more a pile
of mismatched rags draped in her weird style.
They said they'd stay awake after their coffee burst,
but now they're blinking, feeling oddly cursed.
Their head hits the desk, one hand still on the floor,
the boss walks by and yawns exactly as before.
You crack like a match struck in dry, drifting smoke,
the room turns to listen, no one wants to choke.
Your voice isn't shaky—it's got power to rise,
that tremble is armor, not some fragile guise.
They open the bag but they can't seem to see,
there's a tear in the foil that lets the cold flee.
One steps back to fix it, a nervous little strip,
then watches the cheese gently take a small trip.
The bus takes a turn off the usual route,
and leaves you stranded without a shout.
You check your phone but there's no way to know
if the detour will ever let you go.
You dream about hitting snooze for your rest,
but your alarm jumps on your chest.
You tell yourself you'll get through the whole day,
yet your eye keeps drifting back to the gray.
You dug through the box until you found that dress,
worn once, but still meant to leave an impress.
The missing button? Just a loose thread,
Now you're walking tall, not hiding your head.
The remote said "replace" in a bold, red save,
so I bought new ones—felt like a hero, brave.
Now nothing works, but I've got no clue,
I'm stuck with these dead batteries, fused with old glue.
You spread out the papers as if they were proof,
stacking memories from floor to the roof.
Each slip tells a story, a purchase, a cash
of hard work turned into splendor and ash.

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: You strike a pose like a star on the stage,
the empty room's your kind of cage.
You snap it off with a thumbs-up wave,
then hide again in your selfie cave.
She watches the world burn in a toxic feed,
each post pretending it's the saving lead.
Her thumb swipes through the endless fire,
but no one hears her quiet desire.

topic: a coffee cup on the curb
lines: You pick up the coffee cup still warm from the lid,
maybe someone left it when they ran off and hid.
Now you hold the last trace of their morning routine,
a quiet moment out of time, wrong place, right scene.
You left the grocery cart key stuck in the lock,
it's probably now buried under a rock.
You check every aisle, but your phone can't scan,
some guy yells, "Key? I've got the wrong man!"
You lift the lid and it spins into start,
the melody reaches your quietest heart.
Each note is a breeze through an old music wind,
you smile at the past that still plays so behind.
You play your tunes loud into the dead of night,
their complaints fade at your joyful height.
The floors all shake to the deep, rich bass,
the whole block feels your stereo's mass.
You promise yourself you'll stop scrolling and tell,
but the screen's siren song keeps your eyes from the bell.
Time slips through your fingers, hour after creep,
while your brain stays wide awake pretending to sleep.
I watch the onions turn a slow, sweet gold,
the pan sizzles still from when I poured cold.
The kitchen fills with warmth, a fading scent,
and time slips away where the memories went.
The price was half what the others were set,
you dreamed of the savings and flew off the jet.
But the clerk paused and said, "That's the cost,"
and your hope started melting like morning frost.
I used to lift it with strength from the past,
now even the heaviest feel like the last.
Each dent on the plate has a memory dent,
my dreams are still there, but my spine is bent.
You push your buffet tray through the glass and tray,
the same routine, the same tired ballet.
Muffins sit under a film of dust,
and toast burns fast, but has no crust.
You hover above every comment and post,
afraid your thumbs will say too much, at most.
You count the seconds before you hit pause,
the double tap might mean something, or just cause.
You paid the insane small-portioned cup price,
it cost more than your last phone's replacement device.
You sip and stare at the delayed flight gate,
then laugh how airports charge you just to hate.
She still keeps the loop of red rubber string,
twisted into some old carnival thing.
He made it with quick fingers and quiet teeth,
her laughter echoing somewhere beneath.
I draw a rainbow where the dark has won,
each streak a wish I let my fingers run.
The cracks in concrete stretch and spread so wide,
but color finds a way to come inside.
You scan the road for any clue,
the map app flickers, not enough of a view.
But then you see a station way ahead,
and smile like you just found the last loaf of bread.
They found a wad stuck to the bottom of the track,
still warm, still sticky, a breathy half-hack.
Maybe they'll figure out who left it behind,
or maybe they'll sit there and wonder in kind.
They left their keys in the sink full of debris,
The dog had knocked everything over in his spree.
The front door locked tight, the deadbolt their chore,
They sighed but laughed—this was turning into a bore.
You found a torn sock near the gym's back lace,
but you laughed all the way to your favorite place.
You stepped on the treadmill with one bare tread,
and danced up the hill with joy in your head.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: The child still insists the world will float,
while clutching a balloon with faded boat.
Parents wave wildly with no real clue,
he's lost in a park in his favorite hue.
She steps off the curb without waiting to move,
she's got better instincts than logic would prove.
The horns scream at her, the crowd gets real loud,
but she walks through the chaos, defiant and proud.
Her screen says "update complete—no progress,"
but something is wrong, it all feels like regress.
The app keeps freezing where she used to breeze,
now every tap stutters, nothing gives her ease.
I keep turning the knob, but the room won't feel warm,
Another snowstorm has ruined this form.
I reset the damn thing again just to set
my hands shaking with frustration and regret.
You swore this week would be your comeback plan,
bought kale instead of chips—but forgot to ban
cravings. Now you're eyeing the snack crate,
wondering if a doughnut counts as a gate.
You swore you wrote it in bold, black ink,
but now you chase milk and coffee through the drink.
You scold your brain for the mess in your head,
and sigh that this task is one you can't yet shed.

topic: seeing your mom's new profile pic
lines: I see your mom's new picture — new hair,
but still the same smile, always so fair.
The years have marked her face with their age,
I wish time were a thing we could cage.
She builds her epic world from plastic and lore,
then sends the hero hurtling through a door.
The swords don't meet, but the drama still clashes,
while tiny hands narrate the ruins of ashes.
She walks barefoot through the tall green wide,
her shadow stretching soft on every side.
Her fingers move like wings, so gently weave,
as if she might catch something you can't believe.
You stare at your screen, no longer flush,
the once-reliable card now makes a hush.
Your eyes drift to ads you used to eye,
but every new dream says, "Decline to buy."
The bill is due again and still no cash,
I've gone through every coin, every stash.
I left the check alone, it's not a check,
just a life half-paid and sinking slow as wreck.
I still have the box where we built our past,
we dressed up the heroes, made up their cast.
Each plastic move helped me build a whole scene,
but now they sit silent and it doesn't quite mean.
You call it a masterpiece, this twisted-up art,
each cord a snake that won't let any part
of the pile lie flat like a king's lost crown,
you leave it alone—let the chaos grow around.
I laugh as the paper begins to fold,
It tucks into shapes made of memory and gold.
I trace every crease in my favorite way,
It's not broken—it's just having a little play.
She paid full price but forgot she had bought
the biggest tub and now isn't sure she thought
it through—now the kernels scream too much salt,
her teeth clench like she's guarding a vault.

topic: a like from a long-lost friend
lines: Your face pops up on my phone's lonely screen,
I click to reply — it's been years since we've seen.
You write you're still out there, not just to jump
into nostalgia, but to give me a bump.
She offered her umbrella to shield me from rain,
we stood close enough to almost remain.
We watched storm clouds roll under the gray sky,
then walked away without saying goodbye.
You close your eyes and hear that old street,
The laughter you swear will haunt you each repeat.
You trace the memory but catch your own shadow,
Worrying this is all you'll have left tomorrow.
I double-tap so fast it's almost a slap,
you'd think I had some kind of pro level cap.
My phone is full of pics, I've liked every post,
and still I'm not the top—but damn, I'm the most.
You fumbled through your bag for your locker key,
but found last year's stickers and old debris.
You stared at the number on that rusty door,
swore it matched—then laughed until your throat grew sore.
They sneeze again, then wipe their runny nose,
A tissue mountain piles around their clothes.
Their throat now throbs with static, dusty ache,
They blame the heater, not the stale birthday cake.
My clothes sit in a mountain of a pile,
they've probably bled onto one another while.
If I leave them too long, my life might start to rot,
but I still haven't figured out what I've got.
They turned their phone off—no more workday calls,
letting quiet build on both emotional walls.
There's something about that which feels like pride,
a choice to lie face down, on the pillow's side.
I swear the ground is faking its own spring,
holding out hope for one last cold thing.
These daffodils will pay for their cheeky wear,
sticking their yellow in my grumpy air.
She got a check for twenty bucks, not cash,
so she hid it in her snack drawer for stash.
They thought she'd spend it, but her plan was style—
she framed the check and now it's all a smile.
Your backpack strap gave a little snap,
You laughed, pulled out your phone, and tap.
You toss the bag now like a loose roll,
The weight may be gone, but the fun stays whole.
You let the milk sit as a test or a proof,
It curdles beneath your kitchen's dull roof.
You raise your nose—it's already sour,
A small rebellion won with no power.
You sit there watching the yarn unwind so slow,
it never stops, even when you tell it to go.
The ball rolls off your chair, no warning, no flair—
it floats across the room like a thread through the air.
You tried to pretend they're just a bad joke,
but the totals are real and they make you choke.
You toss them into a paper bowl,
hoping your wallet still has some soul.
Her pulse surges from some unnamed fear,
she checks the door, sure danger is near.
The cat knocked a glass off the shelf long ago,
but now it's a crisis and not a small blow.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: There's frosting on my shirt from that birthday cake,
I leaned in too close — total happy mistake.
I blew out all flames with one giant puff,
now I'm licking my lips — the place was full of stuff.
I try to type but miss where letters read,
my fingers swear they've never heard it said.
The spacebar still clicks like it used to click,
while dust builds up and settles in the thick.
She used to sit beneath the ancient old gold,
whispering secrets to the wind she was told.
She'd watch the light pour down in softest shine,
tracing patterns like a dream's own design.

topic: a coffee cup on the curb
lines: She left her coffee where the storm's rain
will never let the last drops remain.
A paper boat on the wet street,
still warm from some long-lost heat.
You're squeezed into the seat so tight,
the only thing dimmer is your flight.
You dream of stretching out to stand,
while the clouds blur past where you're meant to land.

topic: a favorite mug with a chip
lines: I never trust the new mugs when they clink,
they seem too loud for my quiet morning drink.
My old one's got a flaw near the rim's chip,
but I still use it—habit gave it a grip.
She lives her life at a snail's steady pace,
while the world spins in some mad inside race.
The clouds don't pause to see if she knows,
they float along, wherever they goes.
You launch it with hope, let it soar,
it loops past the lamp and slips out the door.
It hits the far wall and folds up with crash,
your dreams of distance burn into ash.
A snowflake lands soft on my dark woolen flake,
I catch more on my tongue when I bend down to take.
They melt on my chest where the heat lingers best,
and leave tiny wet dots where they paused for a rest.
I try to type but the keys won't press,
their ghostly letters are easy to guess.
This keyboard's held me through stories so old,
now crumbs keep it quiet, no more words bold.
You step into my shoes to try to see,
but walking a mile won't change what's me.
You'll never fully know how I feel,
though love might come close when it's this real.
I saved the best shots for the last sandy beach,
the waves all framed just right in their blue breach.
The mountain peaks pop in the morning's sharp view,
these memories are more than I ever knew.
Your eyes are fixed on the world out ahead,
but your dog is the one who's in need of a lead.
You laugh as they yank you with joy from the tug,
their eager face all wet charm and good mug.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: She scrolls till her screen gives off blue light at late,
the numbers below her add up to great weight.
Her thumbs don't stop tapping, her breath turns deep,
but rest doesn't come fast when the world won't sleep.
Your cat sees a monster beneath the floor,
it's really just lint from last week's chore.
She crouches low, pretending to play,
but you're nervous all day, just in case it turns prey.
She left the gift wrapped neatly inside the book,
but half the neighborhood found it and took.
Now she's scouring the yard for some better spot,
while the cat stares at the presents by the pot.
I fished around my pocket for some loose cash,
the coins all bounced against each other, clash.
I dropped the lot inside my old coin jar,
the barista sighed, I muttered "ugh," at the bar.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: I saw a bright spark from the water's gleam,
I waded through stones toward the narrow stream.
It caught the light well, but was smooth to take,
A painted pebble, no gemstone but fake.
I watch it bob along with quiet, lonely glum,
each step a metronome, like some odd little drum.
The bird stays just out of reach, still, somehow so near,
but never offers trills or songs to lift my cheer.

topic: someone spilling punch on the rug
lines: I saw the glass tilt with a slow, proud splash,
the punch took flight like a startled flash.
Now it drips secrets along every strip
where someone's bound to go and take a trip.
I reach the top, take in the view from this height,
my knees have been aching like they're losing a fight.
I flex each joint, test how far it will bend,
but I won't stop now—I'm not here to mend.

topic: a gym membership you never use
lines: You still remember the fee you had paid,
the promises flashing like neon parade.
You tried once and slipped into the same rut,
now it's just paper tucked loose in your gut.
I told myself I'd get more done to sleep,
but doom scrolled into the dark and deep.
My phone glows in my hands—strange eyes,
that promise truth while feeding me lies.
She counts each raindrop like a war drum,
expecting trouble even if none come.
The thunder rolls in, a sound so near,
she clutches the pillow, drowns her fear.
At noon her coffee machine gives her a call,
She rushes from the couch like heading to the mall.
Her eyes light up as she catches the brew,
The steaming cup becomes the only thing in view.
She loops the band around her ankle and bends,
pretending she's mailing her problems to friends.
It snaps back with laughter, a springy stretch,
while the dog chases shadows just out of its fetch.
She kicks off the ground like she's chasing the air,
then laughs like she used to back when she'd dare.
She holds the chains tight, strikes her perfect pose,
but no one's there to call it a show or a close.
She sticks a note where your eyes go to head,
the message just says what she never said.
There's a stick-figure at the edge of the lamp,
drawing a crown like it means something, champ.
She sets the last dish beside the warm roast,
she never does much but she cooks without boast.
The lights are all low over the set table,
and somehow you feel like the world is more able.
The mower starts up with a brutal roar,
you clutch your ears and fall to the floor.
Each rev of the engine brings more pain,
it's like someone's drilling through your brain.
I zoom down the lane, always moving ahead,
ignoring the warnings that drivers have said.
My wheels eat the pavement, I ride with such speed,
they call me reckless—but this is my creed.
I give it a double-tap without any plan,
my thumb feels like I'm shaking a soda can.
The screen lights up fast with what I just feed,
but nothing stays sticky, no real need.
My phone screams danger with its blinking red stress,
It won't let me text, won't even take my address.
I swipe through old photos, my digital mail,
It's basically jail but with better detail.
You get my message—there's no new tone,
The voicemail box is full once again on your phone.
I'll keep it short so you don't have to miss
the drama of my life that you won't hear this.
I remember saying, "This won't be long ago,"
but moments slipped past with no real show.
Looking back feels like a mirror cracked and now,
I promise less haste, though I'm running out of vow.
You reread the store's tiny-printed read,
but every rule twists back inside your head.
"Final sale" seems to be their official lie,
yet you stand tall and pretend you'll just try.
I let my fingers graze your hand on the brush,
you paused so long, I thought I heard a hush.
A charge ran through me, quick and full of spark,
I hope you felt it too—my secret little mark.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: They left a long comment down near the post,
your name got linked in a bolded "most."
She reads it again and she lifts her head,
then swears she's blushing, though her face stays red.
They hit send without a second post,
letting the joke carry them on the coast.
The boss never saw the deadpan eye,
but HR definitely let out a sigh.

topic: a friend who is always late
lines: You're always ten minutes from where we meet,
your shoes slung off as you kick them under your feet.
We talk while the sky spits a drizzle of rain,
you promise again but you never remain.
You were so sure the forecast said no sky,
until the clouds moved in and stole your pie.
You laughed and ran, got a little bit dusty,
but you still trusted that the worst was rusty.
My ceiling bears the weight of my unblinking gaze,
a chalk-drawn map of thoughts in mental maze.
I built this kingdom out of stillness and crown,
so let the world collapse—just don't look down.
I left the fridge open just so it would glow,
the power is costing me even though.
I won't turn it off — it's my way to keep
the dark outside while I stare instead of sleep.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: I counted three new gray hairs, just my age,
I swear I locked the door on this old cage.
I told myself last year I'd still be young and bloom,
now I'm staring into mirrors, no time to groom.
I tap my spoon on the boiling lid,
it's a rhythm only a hungry kid would bid.
Steam curls up from the warmest bowl,
and maybe this meal just might feed my soul.
You cut in like it's just another breeze,
did you forget your manners or your keys?
I stood here waiting, keeping to the queue—
next time, try asking if they let you do.
I fall into their cozy, lit-up room,
we laugh through mics and weird filters and zoom.
The comments fly fast in the scrolling chat,
while their dog barks and their cat knocks the hat.
I don't know how it got that hairline chip,
but it's been sitting there since some old trip.
I could buy a new mug, maybe even a pot,
but who has time to fix what I already got?
They used to get lost in the thunder of ears,
now silence feels better after all these years.
The bass still lingers, but love has begun to fade,
she hums along less, turns more to worn-out jade.
You found a split along the inside tear,
but the storm outside makes perfect air.
You'll stitch it up and call this a mend,
not the last time you use this old friend.

topic: socks left in the break room
lines: You missed a lone sock from some old pair,
it's curled up beside the microwave stair.
It smells like your shift and the coffee's scent,
a small relic from a forgettable event.
He's on the third "Your mailbox is full" tone,
still pacing like the answer's in his phone.
He'll never delete old voicemails to make back
space — he's sentimental, even in his lack.
She walks her old dog in the same slow pace,
keeping distance from our shared space.
His tail wags but she ignores his bark,
her eyes are as quiet as evening's dark.
You type "butterfly" and pretend you don't try,
your phone doesn't know you can barely fly.
But the app insists that this is what you say,
and somehow it fits the vibe of the day.
They missed the ferry as the evening tide
rolled in, no GPS, just someone's old guide.
The bus had already left the station, they ran,
but she just laughed — missed it? That's the plan.

topic: a taxi driver yelling on phone
lines: I cringe as he yells through the whole long ride,
his face red raw like he wants to just hide.
"My mom says you're a disgrace to the crew,"
he shouts into the phone, "that's not true — *you*!"
I shake the loose coins from my pocket's jar,
and toss them like dice on the counter's bar.
The cashier gives me a look, a slow count,
then says it adds up to just enough amount.
You say the trash was left out past the bin,
they claim your coffee cups were far too thin.
Both sides now wave the HOA like a crew,
when neither really cares if it's on time or due.
Your lips left a smudge around the cup's rim,
like a secret message only you could dim.
The coffee might wash off the color as stain,
but you kiss the handle—just to do it again.
She swipes her card for the self-serve gas,
the machine declines it for the third time, pass.
Her thumb hovers still, the wind cuts to the bone,
she wishes the cashier would come, just to phone.
That loaf's been growing the same green mold,
I bought it fresh last week—it's ancient now, cold.
I toss it back in the crumb-filled bin,
and vow again never to buy bread within.
She marches across the floor with a tile,
doing yoga barefoot in her own strange style.
At midnight she tiptoes—no socks to creep—
but the chill won't let her pretend it's still sleep.
I press the keys but I don't quite know
if they'll work or just fade and ghost like snow.
My fingers pause, I feel the old fear,
it's been ten years since I cleaned this keyboard clear.
Her umbrella leaked from the top down to split,
a useless stick that wouldn't even fit.
She tossed it in the bin without a mend,
and bought a new one—this could be the end.
You dart across the street without a race,
the cars all brake while you hold your face.
People watch as the crowd moves in flow,
the sun catches your laugh's warm glow.
The camera gives me a frustrated scan,
It doesn't recognize my tired, sleepy man.
I tilt my head, adjust the light to try,
But my face won't unlock—something's wrong with my eye.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: A toothpick is lodged somewhere in my sleeve there,
It tickles like static and gets in my hair.
I shake out my arms but the thing won't budge that way,
I'll live with the itch till I change clothes today.
You told yourself you would finally start,
the task felt huge, but you kept your heart.
A single item crossed off with a mark,
became proof that even small things can spark.
She watches the robin go flitting around,
leaving crumbs where it's dug something found.
Its beak smudges dirt off the soft mossy green,
she wishes she could pause her life's slow screen.
They keep cranking the knob for more heat,
I'm stuck sweating in my defeat.
They blast winter out with a heater so loud,
I swear I can see steam from my cloud.
You paid your fare and found an empty seat,
but he just mutters "stop" and hits the repeat.
You check the time—this man missed his shift,
now sleep is all he's giving this ride as a gift.
I pour milk over my cereal now flat,
I've waited too long and missed the last bat.
I eat every bite with a frown and a grudge,
it's just like chewing a bowl of cold sludge.
Her screen begins to flicker and fade,
a last-minute selfie goes unshared, unpaid.
She swipes through apps just to try to save,
but laughs and says her power was never brave.
You swear it's watching you, waiting for a clue,
it dove once last week when your sandwich flew.
It circles again, still looking for its prey,
you're not sure if work or the hawk caused the delay.
A sticky note still clings to the fridge's top,
faded words begging the past to stop.
It holds a scribbled face, your only thought,
soft and sad, like memories we fought.
You're running low on food and it's far too late,
your stomach shouts out at an empty plate.
You spot a bag of cherries by the fruit,
and hope somehow turns up from the grocery root.
I double-check it, then count it all again,
my fingers move like a cashier's old train.
The customer hands me a wrinkled green bill,
but I get no joy from this low-level thrill.
The coffee brews and the room feels light,
I smile through the haze of a sleepy bright.
A new week unfolds and I'm ready to start,
my playlist hums in perfect tune with my heart.
She whispers sweet lies but the leaves still bend,
she claims she'll remember to water and tend.
The plant takes a deep, last breath, long and sigh,
while she texts it a meme—get well, but don't die.
The sky blazes orange like a dying fire,
the daylight retreats without any retire.
The wind holds its breath, the world turns to hush,
but shadows will come in a sudden rush.
I lost track of exits after a mile,
I missed my turn twice but I gave a smile.
I read every sign like a forgotten rhyme,
the road feels familiar, but not from this time.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: You light the wick and hope it gives a glow,
but shadows stretch too long, run far below.
Your hands tremble just a little when you feel
the weight of being brave is nothing but steel.
They lie there counting cracks in the still,
dreaming of some future life on a hill.
Their thoughts keep wandering, their mind undefined,
chasing silence like it could outrun the wind.
I found your old headphones still in their case,
coiled tight like secrets hiding their place.
They've been in this drawer for at least three years,
and somehow they feel like old dried-out tears.
You drop to the ground where the silence gives rest,
a single pinecone lands gently in nest.
Years ago it grew high up in that tree,
now it's falling toward something new, like a key.
I pushed through the morning with fire and a surge,
some hidden power gave me an extra urge.
Now it hits like a wall—sudden, deep slump,
my legs won't move fast enough to even stump.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: I stared down the mess of a birthday cake,
determined to beat my hair-on-fire break.
This was my moment, my gasp-inducing time,
I leaned in—and blew them all in prime.
I walked out of the theater, still cried,
a total mess but somehow full of pride.
My jacket clung to me, soaked with the room's cold air,
I smiled through the gloom—I knew it would scare.
They rest where they always find their place,
near a coffee stain on the worn-out base.
You kick them up when the mood or hour feels right,
like climbing mountains is as easy as flight.
She swore it was too good to be a deal,
and she's right—no one wants this sad, old meal.
It's a waste of money, time, and brains,
but now she's stuck with the monthly drains.
Your gym gear's a mess since that dumbbell went set,
you're stuck with one side while you workout and fret.
You toss the lone weight in the closet and spin,
it's not worth the search—just grab a new one from bin.
They've searched the couch and vowed they've really tried,
the dog just watched with obvious intrigue and pride.
All the cushions are thrown to the floor for rest,
but the keys stay missing from the desperate quest.
A white rabbit darts through the garden's green patch,
determined to make off with a crisp green snatch.
It freezes when I move—then takes a quick bolt,
as if powered by some wild, leafy volt.
She paints her message in color and loud,
the whole block now knows she's not afraid to be proud.
A hundred new names crowd every tag,
but hers is the one that still makes people drag.
My toes remember the last time it was sand,
now they're dancing where the hot asphalt stand.
There's a burn in the soles that won't quite go,
the sun is a memory heating me below.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: You saw him strut in that silly pride,
but when the crowd came, he tried to hide.
He growled in his throat, a low, sad bark,
no one noticed the fear in his spark.
I start to cry when the chorus gets real,
I don't care how it looks, this is the deal.
The tears just fall without trying to be free,
they know my heart, they don't need to be me.
I wore my favorite pair of shoes,
now they're an excuse for bad news.
The smell starts low but creeps and stink,
like this will haunt me for more than a blink.
Your fingers feel warm against my wrist at night,
we don't let go even when the hug runs tight.
The music has stopped, but we still hit the beat,
like dancers alone on a sidewalk down the street.

topic: a group project where nobody helps
lines: She takes the lead while the others hide,
pretending to read as they slowly slide.
But she's moving pieces into their shift,
turning dead weight into something like a gift.
These old shoes waiting by the door are a sign,
as if fate's hoping something good will align.
A beam of sun slips through, casts them in light,
like they're holding a secret I could not quite.
I whistle a tune as I sort out the cheer,
another month's bill shows up like a beer.
I fold it and stick it inside an old smile,
sipping my coffee and slowing down a while.

topic: finding a five in the couch
lines: She said she lost the keys, but I knew where to find,
I reached behind the cushion, as I had designed.
A smug little grin rose like smoke from her chin,
"You're good," she admitted, "but not that within."
You're sure they know what you're about to think,
but their eyes just drift to the nearest blink.
They always miss every hint and each clue,
yet somehow still know just what *you* meant to do.

topic: a man reading on a bench
lines: A man sits calm beneath a soft breeze,
his book open where the sunlight keys.
He turns each page with careful fold,
the light catches in his hair like gold.
You call them the neatest pile in the heat,
each sock has a match from your left to your feet.
I've never seen laundry so perfectly set,
you could sell them as pairs, double or nothing bet.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: You take a deep breath, you blow off your puff,
and claim it was magic, not luck or stuff.
The smoke still lingers, you try to blow,
but only your mustache makes any show.
I dump the change from my pocket's old jar,
the meter still has time left to spare—so far.
I walk my usual path, know each block by route,
the machine just clicks once and lets me go out.
You remember the coat that felt way too old,
the one you wore when they gently told
how your shoulders had grown out of their chest,
but now it fits, as if by some strange behest.
He showed off his "new look" with zero skill,
then asked for tips when the hairdresser gave his bill.
He tried to flip the blame but lost the flip,
and walked out like he'd taken a bad trip.
You cash the refund check from the empty store,
but it feels less like winning, more like sore.
It won't bring back the reason you spent the spring,
just enough to buy a lesser kind of ring.
I used to lose myself in the rush of the beat,
now every song feels like it's just a repeat.
My ears go quiet when the bass fills the room,
and silence doesn't feel like it should be doom.

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: The rubber band still tells an old, sad tale,
stretched thin from holding paper and mail.
I try to snap it, but it feels too long,
yet weak—just clinging on by a thread so strong.
You left the baking sheet sizzling with heat,
It's dripping hot oil on the kitchen street.
The air feels thick, the moment is tense,
One wrong move here could be a serious expense.
You marked your part as done, but the work's still due,
We lack your spark—the puzzle's missing a clue.
We move along, but we're stuck going slow,
When will you return to help us all grow?
The morning air wears a soft white glaze,
like snow from some slow, quiet days.
She walks the path, her shadow bent like a key,
unlocking the sky just to wake me.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: I still dream of the days spent in the dirt,
caked with muck from head down to shirt.
We swore we'd never grow out of that play,
but now the only mud's left in the clay.
You dash to the gate where the packages wait,
then freeze, unsure if you should bark or debate.
The mailman retreats down the sidewalk's pound,
and every noise after feels like a fresh wound.
She finally hit "cancel" to take a pause,
no more auto-pay for a distant cause.
Now she's got money and time to be free,
savoring small joys just trying to be.
I found an old greeting card in a shoe box,
some glitter had melted where the color rocks.
But your smile fits perfectly in my heart,
and clumsy or not, it's the best place to start.
They zip across the screen like I've been blind,
Names flash again faster than my mind.
I pause to catch them, but the titles fade,
A funeral march for every name displayed.
She stirs her coffee and waits for the time,
though noon feels early in late December's prime.
One more cup won't hurt, she says into the brew,
believing a warm kitchen can save just a few.
She'd hit snooze once, maybe twice, just to stall,
then blink at the ceiling where dreams used to fall.
The minutes slid by like a life she could cast,
each morning a relic she barely could last.
You stare at the stain, but it's too late for shame,
The deadline's tonight—it was never the same.
You try to blot it out, but there's no good fix,
The ink has seeped through now, no matter your tricks.
That spot was the only one left that's free,
you turned into traffic just to save it for me.
It was right there in view, now gone from your sight,
I guess we lost it to the one who had more might.
She sips her tea too fast, like she needs to take flight,
Her hands won't stop shaking through the day or the night.
She sets the cup down gently to let it rest,
But the steam still rises as quick as her chest.
She holds this stretch in a yoga-like pose,
her paws above the rug's damp laundry hose.
You wait for her to curl and finally nap,
but she owns this moment, and the soft trap.

topic: leaving a note on the fridge
lines: You left a sticky, handwritten mess,
"Don't eat the cookies—unless."
I read it twice and still don't know why,
now I'm out of milk and I want to cry.
She left a fake rock with a hidden clue,
but the neighbors have all seen it too.
Her spare key rusts beneath the door,
while she forgets where she last kept her store.

topic: a quiet moment on the porch
lines: You rock back slowly on the creaky old swing,
the only loud noise is the screen door's big thing.
A whisper of breeze through the pines brings ease,
your phone buzzes softly from where you left keys.
They call it a habit, more like a vice,
"It tastes better than water," they'll argue with nice.
I've asked them to try just one glass and they can't,
the empties pile up like a sugared-up plant.
She curls up tight against the warm air,
turning your suitcase into her lair.
Her purr becomes the only soft weight,
you leave it be—let things stay in that state.
A sudden rush of air escapes the final tie,
She stares at where the balloon used to fly.
The sun still shines like hope won't let her go,
she laughs, and ties another one below.

topic: clouds gathering on a summer afternoon
lines: You watch the sky fade from white to blue,
the horizon softens in every view.
They said it was just a passing rain,
but thunder lingers, still to remain.
They move with the same old quiet pace,
like the memory of your familiar face.
Watching them vanish into the sky,
I wonder why time just won't pass by.
They say the plant's brown because he just can't kill,
but I swear it's his stubbornness, not any will.
He waters it daily, neglects the soil,
and calls it "love" when the leaves still toil.
She stops to take a photo of the old oak tree,
a wasp buzzes near her, pretending it's a bee.
The light makes shadows on her squinty face,
she calls it magic and won't let you erase.

topic: reading under the covers with a flashlight
lines: She cranks up the beam so the page starts to glow,
The sheets are too hot but she reads anyway, low.
Her mom walks in then and catches her spot,
"No flashlights at night," is what she says, strict and not.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: I watch the rise and fall of your fur,
afraid the quiet will break with a stir.
Your paws twitch through the world of your dreams,
while I hover close, caught between fears and extremes.
You've got this new routine, a hydration plan,
you're sipping so much, they think you're a water man.
You track it all with apps, glass after glass goes through,
your old self never guessed you'd become this you.
You stop to let the cart pass through the store,
A moment frozen, like a cracked glass floor.
Your eyes stay soft as you step nice and wide,
Then quietly nudge it back to its side.
You catch yourself faking your practiced grin,
the gap between teeth feels extra thin.
They scan your card without a hint of code,
but you wonder if they saw your heavy load.
You thought this birthday would mean something today,
but no text, no call, nothing came your way.
A friend might have called—then forgot in the hall,
or maybe no one remembered your name at all.
You try to walk around the closed-off block,
but a drum circle insists on shaking the rock.
They toss you beads and a half-eaten float,
you leave your umbrella hanging in the coat.
I watched my sad plant's last green leaf
fall off, but I'm proud—it was worth the grief.
It stood through neglect, still tried to stand,
fought for the light in this lonely land.
You say "Where did it go?" but you do the same,
repeating the beats of your boring old game.
You flip on the light and pretend you still fight,
then scroll till the night makes your skin feel tight.

topic: a plate with two leftover bites
lines: You saved two tiny bites from your lunch,
probably thinking you'd get a fresh bunch.
The food's cold by now, so there's no need to eat,
but the guilt of waste still tries to heat.
You catch a glimpse of it out of your eye,
a word half-scratched into the cracked sky.
You want it to fade like the rest of the fade,
but the letters still scream like a spray can's cold blade.
It circles the mirror trying to see,
as if I were another of me.
I watch through the glass where we once passed,
a memory fluttering, small and fast.
You hit send before the workday clock,
the boss gives you side-eye full of shock.
They laughed so hard they nearly caught fire,
now you're the office star who won't retire.
She slipped through the crowd to your side in the back,
her coat still damp from the evening's black.
They missed her at the turnstile, the bouncer, the gate,
as if the whole night had planned it this way, fate.
The TV's blare could wake the dead, I swear,
I just want to watch this show, but can't even stare.
I fumble for the remote—where is that key?
Buried beneath a pile of snacks and debris.
The refund finally came through in the mail,
but it's so late it might as well be a fail.
I cash the check with some reluctant cash,
then toss it in the bin—right in the trash.
They said your arms could never twist a snake,
but now you're posing like you want a take.
This balloon is pure art, twisted and smart,
you flex your DIY pride to everyone's heart.
Your head's tilted—searching for some tiny clue,
You study my face, trying to decode its hue.
You don't mean to be rude, but it feels like you ask,
"What strange thing is happening here? What should I task?"

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: The wind hits my face like a summer breeze,
I fumble with my helmet, lock the keys.
I ride fast, pretending I know this street,
but I'll forget the way when I try to repeat.
She still sits there as if those years
had never passed, the spot still appears.
The tang of grape lingers, the same old smell,
as though the juice could cast a time-slowing spell.
You think you're smooth when you fold and then throw,
like you somehow invented the plane and the show.
But halfway down the row, it hits the stall—
a crash you tried to sell as a controlled fall.
You lie there like morning, slow and stretch,
I leave your snack bowl where you never fetch.
Your body is yoga in a perfect pose,
I wish I could borrow all of those.
After lunch I feel my energy crash,
A quick donut might give me a flash.
I've told myself I don't really need
sweet relief—but oh, how I indeed.
She drifts into my lane without a blink,
Her eyes fixed on her phone's small screen and pink.
I honk, she doesn't budge—I let out a sigh,
She thumbs a reply while the world might just die.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: You post it in full view, no text, no frame,
just color and light like the sky's own flame.
You scroll past the likes and the comments on phone,
then save it for later — you love being shown.
She stabs at the sharpener, her only good lead,
and scowls when she snaps off a chunk of her head.
The blade won't engage, the whole thing just spins,
while classmates snicker and flash their new grins.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: I found a smooth rock, a treasure from the stone,
it caught my eye, like it was made my own.
I held it up to the light to see it gleam,
and knew this gift came straight from the cold stream.
You stare into your cereal bowl,
like this is a war on your very soul.
The soggy clumps float, a sad waste,
you sip the milk—there's nothing left to taste.
The yarn begins to pull away, set apart,
soft loops trailing like strands from her heart.
Each thread could be the color of those old years,
she winds them gently, as time does when it neaRs.
In a trench coat and boots, he chases the suit,
as if logic could conquer soap's brute.
He leaps, arms wide, to catch each swirl,
while the toddler laughs like a trickster girl.
My thumb hits the screen when I should be off doom,
but my bed feels less warm than this glowing room.
The feed won't let go, it's too good to leave feed,
I'm wide-eyed at midnight—this chaos, indeed.

topic: a bike locked to a pole
lines: He left his bike there, depending on trust,
now the lock's stuck and slowly turning to rust.
The U-lock still clings to the cold iron chain,
but the wind sings louder than any regain.
I spilled coffee ink all across the mess,
I laughed as I sketched what I hoped to impress.
The kids left a drawing beside their last meal,
I lifted the plate to unveil what they'd reveal.
At ten p.m. they drop their trash at prime,
each clang and crash feels like a crime.
They blast their music just as I get loud,
I grit my teeth but keep it proud.
I bring cookies as if it's some grand clue,
you think I'm here to join the snack queue.
But there's more to this treat than a sweet little lie—
if you don't take one, I might just die.
You wish the walk could feel more like a run,
but your dog's idea of joy is not much fun.
Each step feels like a game of tug and tug,
you're back at home with grass still on your rug.

topic: shaving a cake with a spoon
lines: He tries to smooth out the sides to be flat,
but frosting keeps flying into his spat.
The kitchen is now one huge, sugared mess,
and the cake still looks far from success.
You blast your song like it's too loud,
I'm stuck inside this angry cloud.
You won't even try to hear me or bend,
I'm tired of fighting, just stop and pretend.

topic: a kite stuck in a tree
lines: That kite got stuck in a tree from the breeze,
now it's flapping there just to tease.
You try everything but have no clue,
how to fix this mess from your view.
The toddler chucks a glob of mud at dirt,
and splatters half of it across my shirt.
"Lookout!" I shout, but it's too late—[crash],
the swing goes flying into Grandma's dash.
He's been pacing near the carts since closing zone,
muttering phrases that are purest groan.
He's tried everything but still can't quite toss
the guilt he feels for losing the cart boss.
I hit send at midnight, feeling bold,
no filter, no plan, no time to grow old.
The message is out now—crude but it's sent,
I type "u up?" with all I have meant.
I carved my name into the pencil's wood,
I still remember how we both stood.
Now it's stuck inside the sharpened lead,
along with every thought I never said.
She types "butterfly" but means to miss,
a typo she sends with a soft "just kiss."
Her fingers pause mid-liftoff, flight,
the past returns in that warm delight.
You told me dinner would be hot, not a lie,
but the roast has clearly tried to die.
I push my plate around, pretending to hate
this meal that somehow turned into our fate.
The leaves float through the sky with zero flair,
as if they're auditioning for some lost fair.
They spiral slowly toward the sidewalk down,
like monarchs of decay who've lost their crown.
She types with one finger to avoid the mess,
but even spacebar won't press.
Soda seeped into every gap,
now keys stick like a cruel trap.
The stream froze cold on a quiet scene,
the picture stuck while the silence grew keen.
She didn't blink, just kept watching her eyes,
searching the dark for some hidden lies.
Your phone rings like it's trying to make a call,
It's 2 AM, you're a sleep-deprived ball.
You answer in PJs, still half in a guest,
Just begging your brain will find peace and its rest.
I always get more tube from the mint,
my teeth don't need a snowy print.
I flip it up and give it a good squeeze,
no leftover paste, no chilly freeze.
You still carry that card in your wallet's back look,
the corners are curled from the stories you book.
That frozen face wears a shy, half-remembered smile,
but time won't stay still—it's a snapshot, not a while.
You count the drops like they're trying to tease,
the glass gets cold but the water won't freeze.
You whisper secrets to the sky's empty story,
convinced the clouds might someday sing your glory.
She'd try your jeans and declare they didn't fit,
then roll the waistband and call it *just it*.
After the party, she'd leave them half-apart,
like a memory you can't quite tear from your heart.
You watch the fish press close to the glass with their eye,
turning the aquarium into a false sky.
They flicker like thoughts you've never told your soul,
beautiful, trapped, and briefly feeling your whole.
I bought it "just in case" but never wore
it still sits boxed by the front door.
You'd think I'd learned my lesson by now, for much,
but here I am buying another such.
You thought the earth still slept beneath the frozen ground,
but there's a stubborn *sound* of green breaking around.
They push their heads up through the muck and the rise,
a sudden yellow *surprise* the thaw can't disguise.
The ribs collapsed under a sudden hot sun,
the fabric was loose, already half undone.
I watched it sway where the wind could not breeze,
and never did settle into stillness or ease.
The bass is pounding through my ear,
I swear this song's been here for a year.
I dial it down, but it won't stay away,
yet somehow it still feels like today.

topic: socks left in the break room
lines: She left one sock behind, but not her whole pair,
it waits on the hook near the broken stair.
You think she'll return, that's what gives you hope,
the office just laughs, we all have to cope.
He fumbled the coin and let it take a drop,
it clinked into the meter's narrow crop.
He stood there triumphant, arms held out so far,
as if he'd just launched a rocket from a star.
These bees think they're in some springtime show,
darting around with pollen so low.
They flit through the air like they don't have a care,
while I'm stuck fanning sweat off my bare hair.
You pay the cashier with a crumpled old bill,
your hunger will come second — the jar needs to fill.
You saved every cent, dropped it in for the ten,
and left the fast-food line feeling rich once again.
You rule your domain with a dish-cluttered crown,
the sink's your throne in this porcelain town.
Each plate is a masterpiece left as art,
you'd rather starve than do the cleanup part.
I vowed to change when the doctor said start,
I took one look and my diet lost its heart.
I posted proud on my feed how the plan would fail,
while ordering cake through the takeout mail.
Her body still carries the ghost of an ache,
she stretches toward light from the window like lake.
She takes careful steps, each one slow to move,
but her smile says this will begin to prove.
She didn't see the drip she had no clue,
Her flip-flop left her foot—she jumped and flew.
The bar was gone, the tiles were cold and soap,
She prayed for grip but lost all hope.
She laughs as the storm gives way to rain,
her shoes soaked but joy still wants to remain.
With every step her muddy feet repeat
the rhythm of a child's bold claim to street.
I claim this is a performance art,
my pancake moves are tracked on a chart.
One flip sends syrup flying off the flip,
my confidence just took a quiet slip.
A single feather drops and begins to drift,
like some forgotten charm from an old gift.
It catches, trembles, in the thorny snag,
still holding a corner of a name tag.
You see a familiar face, but it won't erase,
from your mind where you met them, this empty place.
The name feels so close, like it's right about to slip,
out from your tongue—but instead, you just trip.
You tried using a butter knife as a tool,
but now your fingers call you a kitchen fool.
You need both hands—one for the blade, one for the salt,
so you pause the show and just let it all halt.
It arches its back like a bowstring to spine,
too tense for the couch, it marks out this line.
The fur bristles up where the claws softly claw,
as if the whole room must bend to its law.
I hear the track again — it plays the same,
my ex's name pops up in the lyric game.
My palms grow damp, I grip the bar too sweat,
each rep now feels like time I can't regret.
It crouches, then springs into the air with a leap,
all claws aimed at the dark little heap.
Its eyes are too wide, its whole body fur,
I wait for the rabbit—but nothing will stir.
She asks to share it but I make the cut,
I wonder if she wants it or just my gut.
I fold the slice in half so we can split,
she takes the bigger part without a bit.
You stare at the lie glowing from the billboard high,
it paints dreams against a neon-lit sky.
You almost believe in the way it makes you feel,
as if happiness could ever look this real.
She left a mountain of socks for the pile,
humming old tunes from another while.
The detergent has a faint citrus scent,
like the way she loved things that were meant.
You sit at the edge of the park bench alone,
leaving no room but a crumb of a stone.
You say this is how you keep people at bay,
your shadow spreads wide, a polite delay.

topic: reading under the covers with a flashlight
lines: She curls beneath the blankets, reads so deep,
the clock ticks on while she pretends to sleep.
A page flips soft but she still feels a flip
in her chest—like shadows might catch her trip.
The register's frozen in some weird glitch,
They say it's a power problem—try the switch.
I tap my card again but still can't pay,
The machine eats my money and walks away.
The rain keeps falling like it wants to pour,
you watch from windows by the old shore.
You sip your tea, let out a soft sigh,
and dream of walking somewhere to stay dry.
She steps on the treadmill as if she owns the floor,
determined to prove she doesn't need a score.
Her playlist's stuck on loop, same song in her mind,
but the machine just screeches loud enough to blind.
You make your third pot of bitter black brew,
the cat gives you side-eye, that's her quiet cue.
You microwave some eggs but they just won't heat,
the morning will come, and you'll face it with defeat.
I toss the crumbs and watch my bread spread,
they gather fast, not one left ahead.
They tilt their heads and softly coo,
it feels like peace and being known too.
You hunt for the label but get no clue,
some chemicals sound like alphabet stew.
You try to pronounce them your clever new way,
but your face screams, "This can't be healthy to convey."
I hit "share" before my brain could post,
and tagged my teacher, who's now the post's main host.
She replies with emojis, no scold or date,
we laugh it off, and now she's my online mate.
A distant horn breaks through the morning chill,
It echoes down from a sleepy hill.
The neighbor stirs, her cat jumps up to wake,
The silence cracks like the first light break.
She double-taps a throwback from last date,
the comments erupt into a debate.
Some call it a cat, others say it's a hat,
she deletes the post before the chat.
She cranks the knob to find the perfect play,
the tape whirs fast like a tinny ballet.
Each button feels like a groovy old click,
she grins and says, "This beats streaming slick."
You open the fridge and it hits you with smell,
like the ghosts of bad meals cast a foul spell.
You grab the carton, still half full to pour,
but your heart breaks a little as you close the door.
I sat down to work and I found a used seat,
it stuck to my jeans like some rotten old treat.
I pried every scrap from the chair's cold there,
my fingers came clean but I still felt despair.
She folds the page and gives it one good throw,
It wobbles down but never goes too low.
The air is kind—it lets her plane soar,
it slips through cracks near the classroom door.
They hit the pavement hard, the ground, the floor,
their breath caught mid-scream as the stars tried to soar.
Their hand grips their ankle, the pain sharp and plain,
they try to stand but collapse once again.

topic: making mud pies in the backyard
lines: He kneels in the puddle, mixing in the dirt,
his white shirt now stained with grass and shirt.
He calls it "culinary arts," this silly play,
crafting mud pies from the wet red clay.
I keep it on the shelf where it feels most full,
the memories inside gently tug and pull.
Maybe one day I'll let something new grow
from this quiet space where I've learned to know.
My nose is a blistery pink little cake,
I roasted it fiercely beside some hot lake.
It peels in the mirror, now reaching its peak,
I laugh at my shadow, my sunbaked cheek.
You stuffed the carton in your backpack for lunch,
but the straw was loose and the seal wasn't bunch.
Now every page feels damp and begins to soak,
this isn't funny—your notes are now a joke.
You tap the screen and open up the app,
but indecision keeps you stuck in a trap.
You crave some spice, some hot sauce, some oil—
but it'll arrive cold, maybe even in soil.
My cat goes full sprint toward her favorite dash,
the water bowl follows suit with a crash.
I freeze, half-laughing, reaching to mend
the chaos—her tail says this game has no end.
She's confident she never once forgot her brew,
not even when she ordered it from a new.
Her barista fakes a laugh and hides her grin,
while I sip my latte—one size within.
You see the dashboard but not the view,
The headlight's out, and the taillights are blue.
The road is clear, but you hesitate ahead,
Still, you drive on — hope's a stubborn thread.
You watch the moss creep and cover the stones to grow,
It swallows the cracks where the sunlight used to glow.
The path takes on texture, a soft-lit, green view,
You pause and admire how the world looks brand new.
The shovel clings to ice and it clangs like a bell,
your breath hangs heavy, the work seems to swell.
But you think of the flower beds and the seed,
and keep digging forward because you need.
You waited outside the claim area zone,
your flight was delayed, your phone wouldn't phone.
A duffel with no name had your suitcase's tag,
you took it anyway—still miss that old bag.
You pull the band to test your max stretch,
the dog snatches it mid-reach, how fetch.
You laugh and sigh as muscles resist bend,
the set is done, but not without pretend.
You've tried a dozen times to find a pair,
but both always vanish when you get up there.
You wear one sock, feel half-exposed and alone,
like a gray footstep left behind on a stone.
She hits record when she's got nothing on her dime,
it's three A.M. and she thinks it's her prime.
"This is for you," she whispers like a flame,
hoping you'll stream it, give her some vague fame.

topic: leaving a note on the fridge
lines: I grabbed the marker left behind in the ink,
typed my message as a QR link.
You'll scan it, frown, but won't give me the took,
just say "What's this?" and roll your eyes at my look.
That parking spot was definitely mine,
it said "Reserved" on the post with a crooked sign.
I watched in total disbelief and shock,
as my coworker parked there like it was their rock.
I watched it glide as it tried to soar,
then caught an updraft near the open door.
It nosedived down and hit the floor with a crash,
but I laughed all the same and gave it one more dash.
I found a warm spot where the rabbit made hole,
it's soft and unbroken, no sign that they stole.
I lower myself but the silence won't settle,
my breath loud as steam from a whistling kettle.
It watches the surface where food used to float,
eyes blinking slowly behind glassy coat.
Something feels wrong, this silence is bad,
I swear that fish just stared at my hand I had.
You stare at the screen, your phone nears its life,
It's not a place to panic or raise a knife.
You let it die, then boot up from stand,
A fresh 100% starts in this new land.
She follows the sun like it holds some big chase,
tilting her head, her whole face in its grace.
She can't look away, even if she should turn,
the light feels too bright, too strong to discern.
I watched the fish drift in a plastic bowl,
their quiet dance stirring my troubled soul.
They spun in tight loops, did somersaults, float,
as if time had paused to read each little note.
I don't need your forced, plastic-seal,
I serve up my truth with each greasy meal.
Your scripted pleasantries never stick at work,
while I master the art of the smirk.
The moss creeps along the old stone path and grows,
She bends down to check if it's real or her nose.
Her flip-flop nearly leaves her foot to slide,
she laughs to herself and lets the greenery hide.
Your shoes sit by the door like they're stuck to the floor,
I pretend they don't exist but can't quite ignore.
They've tracked the same old mud from some long-lost rain,
they never seem to leave—just there where they remain.
You call the torn foil wrapping your new art,
it's crinkled and jagged, but you claim it's a part
of your aesthetic—say it with pride and a tone
as if you're the king of a foil-strewn throne.
He drops the can hard and it spins on the floor,
muttering reasons why this batch from the store
will still cook up perfect, no damage to the bean,
but the can's all crushed—looks like some cruel machine.
Her eyes go soft as the meeting begins to heads,
she'd rather be home folding laundry or beds.
She pictures the porch where the afternoon rain
washes the noise out, the world feels more plain.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: I found a coupon for a snack that's a steal,
the clerk says, "This won't even count as a meal."
I rip off a chip and take my one-bite trip,
then eat the whole bag in the checkout strip.
She breaks the pace of the crowd's quick chase,
she claims her space with a lazy grace.
The world moves fast but she likes the slow,
and smiles at people who try to go.
It's not my volume, it's your dumb rule,
"Shuffle mode" just skips every single cool.
You claim it's smart, but where's the real fix?
I guess I'll need some new DJ tricks.
She lifts the world with a dented weight and hope,
the barbell creaks but she's learning to cope.
Each scar and dent is a badge she won't rent,
a story of strength no gym could resent.
He sits in the middle of the busy street,
a solo feat of sheer confidence and heat.
He holds out his hand, but not to demand,
he's asking the world to witness his stand.
It teeters on one foot near the far side,
the wood is slick from the morning's cold slide.
It puffs its feathers, a tremble with fear,
the wind sounds sharp in your waiting ear.
I check my back—it's lopsided to wear,
the broken strap slapping my shoulder with air.
My backpack rips at the weakest point, seam,
and I worry I'll miss class or a dream.
You drive around town searching for the view
that'll stick your postcard apart from the glue.
The perfect shot looks bad in the actual scene—
nobody smiles unless they want it to mean.
You take the turn, though you have no clue,
the GPS insists there's nothing to do
but U-turn now from your reversed rear,
as traffic honks in your blinking gear.
She checks the window, then the row, the aisle,
hoping someone lost their ticket to this file.
Her mask is damp with the drip of her sweat,
she counts the hours till she can finally get.
You stood there breathing in that burnt toast smell,
your phone buzzed once, but you didn't check your cell.
There's something final in the scent of warm bread,
when no one else is awake to share the spread.
The total flashes bold, the red light says "due,"
but you still don't quite know what you thought you knew.
Your arms are full of more than a heavy load—
your hands tremble as you punch in the code.

topic: losing your wallet at the mall
lines: She left her wallet behind in the toss,
A paper thin moment, a heavy loss.
She circles the mall, retracing the spot,
But nothing's where she thinks she might have got.
The credits roll and my tears still flow,
this ache feels real, I somehow know.
I wipe my face, but the silence stays dry,
the story is over, I don't quite know why.
They served the chicken soup cold with no hope,
the bread was stale and the coffee didn't cope.
She stumbled into her cubicle room,
and snoozed through three back-to-back meetings on Zoom.
I asked him where he's headed for the ride,
and he told me every detail on his side.
His stories don't always take the toll,
but I wonder if he ever speaks to his soul.
You left your mark in lipstick on the red,
a half-sentence written and unsaid.
I still use it as my favorite last,
even though the scent is long past.
I've got most of the answers but missed one clue,
I'm stuck on a three-letter word for "glue."
My crossword sits there half-filled in the grid,
while my dog sniffs it like a lost kid.
His hand trembles near the broken blade,
the pencil's dull stubs march in a parade.
He prays this isn't a paper waste,
but time is slipping away in great haste.
She flips the egg like it's a pro move to flip,
the white sizzles slowly, perfect to drip.
This isn't just food—it's morningtime art,
the shell stays whole—her joy is a part.
This pencil's been pushing the same old lead,
it's clogged up worse than a toaster with bread.
With all my grit, I try to twist it free,
but now I'm stuck, and so is me.
She says she's fine but it shows in her talk,
her voice sounds like it's scribbled in chalk.
Her boss hands her work like it's overtime paid,
while she marches through meetings like a parade.
I paid $8 for the cup, but it's too weak to take,
the kind of price that could buy a whole lake.
I sip and count how I've wasted my spend,
while the plane waits, and this bad coffee meets its end.
A flake lands soft on the edge of your hand,
another follows, both gentle and grand.
They melt in the heat of your movement so slow,
like secrets that vanish before they can grow.
You smile at the receipt, it doesn't even pop,
you promise you'll pay it all off next time you shop.
The balance is high and the interest is due,
but hope feels like honey—it's sticky and blue.
You found your way into my kitchen's sweet spot,
my spoon drops in flour when we're both caught.
We mix our mouths like sugar and cream will blend,
the flour falls soft as we steal from the end.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: The photo hangs still in its worn frame,
a name whispered soft without a claim.
The room's only light lands warm and slight,
while past laughter fades with the night.
They sit by the door, still muddy and in,
like proof of a walk that I never did win.
Time has left them quiet, soft, and worn,
while memories are fraying at the torn.
The taxi's taillights flicker out at the bar,
Its headlights gone, it barely shows as a car.
The driver speeds forward, oblivious ahead,
I watch them glide into my growing dread.
She slices the carrot with careful knife,
the rhythm feels steady, like something from life.
Her hands are so close now, the edges feel near,
she hums to herself as the dice start to cheer.
You swear you heard the door slam, then flush,
but silence falls—no one speaks a hush.
The flashlight flickers, batteries in the wrong,
and every second feels too cold, too long.
You looped and you pulled, but the bow won't bow,
your laces still loosen and flop as they go.
You watched online videos, you practiced, you tried,
now shoes stay unshackled until you decide.
That bucket of popcorn is dyed gold,
You bought it because it looked bold and sold.
Now every crunch feels like a burst,
Your soda won't arrive—your snack-time thirst.
I heard the twang of the plastic snap,
the wind ripped off my umbrella's cap.
The sky decided it wanted to pour,
so I laughed and stomped through the puddles for more.
Your mind keeps drifting, it's simply switched off,
you fake a few laughs and a polite cough.
You wonder how long 'til your world will be free,
but who dares to leave when there's nothing to flee?
I stand here where the water runs still,
watching the clouds as they drift through and fill.
My shadow moves with the current's soft bend,
but it can't stay, and neither does it pretend.
She waited months for the refund that was due,
but she never thought she'd have time to sue.
When the check came quietly in the mail,
she kept it framed where the others would trail.
She taps again, but it's been too long a time,
the app won't run—it's off its golden prime.
Her phone shows "Access Denied" on the blank screen,
