and she doesn't know her morning routine.
They say midnight's long been in their past,
but here they are again, the last to leave at last.
Their eyes trace the glow of the screen's soft scroll,
convinced morning holds something worth waking for, whole.
I caught my friend wearing my favorite tie,
they said it was borrowed — but I don't buy.
There's nothing in their room that matches that hue,
so yeah, I know it's mine — come clean, it's you.
You type with one hand and it feels so slow,
the other just rests as your thoughts try to go.
You hit wrong keys often and start to miss,
you curse at the board, "This was not worth this!"
I watch the rabbit sniff the cold morning air,
nothing moves near it but the wind to scare.
Its nose points west like a compass to see,
maybe today will be the day it's set free.
You bend down slow as if making a play,
Your fingers dig up some soft red clay.
You mix the earth with the colors you hue,
A rainbow in dirt—still beautiful, you.
Your alarm goes off with the softest chime,
you groan and stretch your sleepy limbs to climb.
The world is still in quiet hush,
while dawn slips in through the curtains' blush.
I'm trapped beneath this iron bar,
my ego went way too far.
I wanted a flex and a pose,
now the bar's pretty hard to close.
I watched the first bloom rise fierce and red,
its petals unfurling from outstretched head.
The frost tried to claim it, but broke on the ground,
while spring whispered life all soft and round.
She left the knob set on a gentle heat,
the soup now simmers like some slow-cooked treat.
The flame stays steady, just a soft low,
she sips her coffee while the hours go.
You had the whole thing planned, didn't you think? [thought]
Friends whispered secrets you never fought. [fought]
Someone brought a chocolate pie, [pie]
now you're stuck wearing a clown tie. [tie]
I tap the switch but the bulb stays off and on,
its rhythm like someone was here and gone.
It throws my shadow where the old fence cast,
and feels like you walked by just a moment past.
She squints through the fog but has no clue,
thinking maybe the coffee's to blame or the brew.
The car creeps along, tires barely roll,
as the weather takes its damp, sly toll.
She built a fantasy world from her plastic realm,
crowned herself queen and took full command of the helm.
The swords may be soft, but the battles still clash,
heroics in spandex never looked so much flash.
She moves through the crowd with a lighter pace,
she leaves the chaos with more open space.
Her head is in places my feet can't find,
or maybe she's dancing with time's soft wind.
You trace shapes above where the wind takes the sky,
"What if clouds are the world's slow reply?"
You name them all out—lion, or bear,
and hold every moment a little more fair.
She types her thoughts but the cat takes the key,
Her deadline looms like a desperate plea.
The sunlight melts his belly's soft fur,
Her sentences now read like a lazy blur.
You check your phone for news about your grade,
the silence is wrapped in a nervous shade.
Your finger hovers, tapping the screen,
but fear has turned all your logic to routine.
I watch them fall slow from the gray winter sky,
they vanish before they can truly die.
They land on my face like a gentle embrace,
and melt into hope in this quiet, soft place.
I trip on the curb and blame it on my age,
My brain yells, "Watch the steps!" from some mental cage.
I fumble my keys and move at snail-slow pace,
A squirrel outpaces me in a face-paced race.
I tap the heart below your latest post,
afraid to say more, but wanting it most.
The comments are calm, no sign of a wave,
just silence beneath your quietest grave.
You hum a tune that used to mean the moon,
I know that melody still chases noon.
I wonder how long it's been since you felt strong,
but I keep quiet, afraid to make you wrong.
She taps her fork like she has no clue,
waiting for some signal from the cue.
The bill arrives—she checks the price and size,
but never asks if split or paid dish-wise.
She saw the ping but she never made a call,
the thread still floats like a hot-air balloon ball.
She hasn't typed a single word to be read,
she laughs as the silence grows, quite gleeful, indeed.
She scans the item but the screen shows no code,
the machine hums loud like a stalled-out road.
She waves her card—says "You're all set, paid"—
and walks out calm while the items parade.
You claim it's better for your feet and your mind,
another excuse to avoid the daily grind.
You call it living, not just chasing gold,
but no one thinks warmth when your toes turn cold.
The sky was so clear but now turning blue,
You said the clouds didn't mean anything you.
Rain starts to fall light and then comes full down,
We laugh as it soaks us both standing around.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: She checks her balance in the dead of bright,
the screen glows cold under one small light.
Her fingers freeze when the number shows debt,
she falls asleep with the weight of regret.
They watch her glide through water, calm and float,
a silent protest no one seemed to note.
She makes it look like sculpture, purest art,
defying gravity's predictable chart.
You swear there's a squirrel or a bird in that spot,
though the yard's just a wall and a concrete cot.
Your cat has no idea what's on your mind,
it's just watching the world through the cracked-out blind.
You tried so hard to keep that fry,
the pigeon watched from up high in the sky.
It dove in one swift and shameless grab,
now you're mad but you laugh like a crab.
You watch your neighborhood disappear from view,
ghostly outlines flicker faintly through.
The taillights smear into one wide street,
the same hazy rhythm, too slow to repeat.
You flex your fingers on the sticky grip,
it clings to your palm like a used candy strip.
There's something like pride in this messy art,
you won't wipe it off now—it's your official start.
You hear a bell and your stomach turns to fear,
The sound comes closer, echoing in your ear.
You glance behind but see nothing in your tail,
Your brakes feel shaky, your mind might just fail.
I found you hiding behind the last shelf,
forgotten but still holding up yourself.
Your label peeled like a map full of rust,
but I'd rather eat from a can I could trust.
I looked for a warm, colorful pair,
but laundry has vanished without a care.
I step on a sock that my foot doesn't miss,
and wish it were cleaner—and more than half this.
She's stuck in a GPS-generated maze,
the car makes a u-turn in full phase.
It says "recalculating your new path,"
but my phone's doing more than basic math.
I let him choose where we go on the lead,
he sniffs ahead with his muddy black head.
He yanks me past the park's grassy zoom,
as if my house is too small for his room.
They dipped the spoon back into the jar,
the way they smiled felt like a fallen star.
They watched the honey swirl and begin to spin,
it dripped like syrup from a summer's skin.
The showerhead forgot how to aim,
It's turned this morning into a game.
The water trickles through cracks and rust,
Spraying the soap back up from the dust.
I try to smooth it but there's no new crease,
the paper is stubborn, won't give me release.
I grip each edge and attempt one last fold,
only to find the damn thing looks like old.

topic: sending a text to the wrong person
lines: You hit send before your eyes could read,
now your words are lost inside the thread.
You're sure they'll think it's something so bad,
but you're the only one who feels that sad.
You still remember the rope swing so high,
the way you whooped when you kissed the sky.
Your first trophy's in your attic still, prize,
though it's small now next to the grown-up world's size.
You walk past the gate where the dog still bark,
but your smile has a softness that might spark
a change in the tension they've worn like a lead—
the kind of hope that a stranger could need.
You watch in shock as the rabbit nabs your leg,
It gnaws with joy, and you can't seem to beg.
Covered in threads, your sneaker now is fur,
The critter hops away without a stir.
I say I'll stop once my head hits the bed,
but my thumb just said, "We can do more instead."
The screen lights up as I search every scroll,
pretending it matters, or maybe I'm whole.
You're the best at making a fair and smart deal,
even when others pretend they don't want to feel.
You grab the check and you offer to split,
but they know from your smile you won't ever quit.
She grinds her beans like she's winning a prize,
her coffee machines hum like they're on the rise.

Its beak strikes the grass with a sudden dart,
I smile at the show that brightens my heart.
Your room is a riot of color and charm,
but that pile of socks won't cause much harm.
A backpack's spilling out its unzipped lid,
and you laugh like this chaos defines the kid.
They hit "send" before they read the post,
it went live with "@Ms. Clark" in the toast.
Too late to take it down or change the fate,
now the class is voting if she'll debate.
She waits for the machine to finish its brew,
the beep signals one, her alarm goes off cue.
Her eyes look at clocks, they all read noon,
but her old coffee song still plays in her tune.
You check the switch but the bulb won't hold,
maybe it's dying like something too old.
You glance outside, expecting a wave
of flickers, but the dark still feels like a cave.
It twitches like it's feeling the breeze,
or counting the jingle of nearby keys.
There's no real reason—it just takes a cue
from nothing at all or maybe from you.
I keep my own pace through the tangled human race,
I demand more space than is truly my space.
I watch people move in a rush, tight and low,
while I drift above them in calm and slow.
She squeezed too hard and filled the sink with paste,
it gurgled over in a foamy waste.
Her friends called it a mess, but she saw it as art,
said no one else would ever do it that smart.
He hopped on the shuttle thinking he had the van,
but his *whole* weekend trip was now a bad plan.
They left without him, even missed the final dock,
now he's sitting alone on this strange little rock.
A dog is barking on this crowded ride,
I try to listen but I just want to hide.
I picture him home in his quiet park,
while we speed through a city turning dark.
I watched him dart through the shade of the tree,
his paws too quick for eyes watching me.
You'll never find where he buried that find,
though I've turned over every rock behind.

topic: a sticky finger on the window
lines: Your sticky finger leaves a perfect mess,
you gurgle with pride, it's your tiny success.
You leave a smudge as a permanent mark,
but I pretend it's a magical spark.
You were sure the forecast said clear blue skies,
But the clouds rolled in with a gray disguise.
The rain didn't care if your sandwich was cake,
You laughed and claimed it's a better place than a lake.
I found it in my drawer with a worn-out hole,
still holding the shape of my gym-worn soul.
I can't bring myself to throw the lace,
though it no longer fits in this tight place.
It plays the same sequence since this morning's played,
the lead singer dances through some weird parade.
I watch the pixels flicker on the phone's small screen,
I've seen worse, but this is still a sad routine.
You hand over a bill, crisp and brand new ten,
The cashier says "Sir, we don't take paper again."
You wave it in air like you're about to pick
A fight with some machine that won't let you stick.
They call it a pile, but it's more like a mound,
a graveyard of socks and shirts on the ground.
They swear they'll do it, "Just give me one day,"
but the rot only grows with each passing decay.

topic: a cup of cold coffee on the table
lines: I don't miss the heat, not one tiny claim,
it sits there forgotten, out of its frame.
The bitter old liquid still tries to sell
its story of mornings that used to be hell.
You thought this shop was charming and themed,
but prices are screaming, your budget screamed.
You reach for your wallet, the hope feels like cash,
you leave with guilt and a little bit of ash.

topic: a book left open on the nightstand
lines: I meant to keep reading until I'm all read,
but my eyes drift toward sleep and my head.
The light from the page gives the room a soft glow,
and I know I'll dream the next chapter or so.
You watch the clouds drift in the water's slow view,
the way they seem real but aren't quite true.
You think you could touch it if you just bend,
but the sky stays far when you try to send.
You started with a clear head and a list,
but hunger twisted your focus to snacks you missed.
Still, you bought healthy, filled carts with pride,
and left the store feeling satisfied and glide.
You take a bite, that loud, dry crunch
of your apple distracts from your lunch.
You peel the skin too fast, too thin,
and wonder what's wrong with you, within.
They smile and say they'll locate my claim,
this is all part of the airline's old game.
A three-hour wait just to punch a code,
now my suitcase is stuck somewhere down the road.
You see their new face in a crowded place,
and time rewinds to your old embrace.
You scroll through updates, but never your soul,
while theirs looks happy, you try to be whole.
They took the new date to the same café date,
where the last one ended in a holiday fete.
She sits in your chair with a practiced stare,
pretending she's never been there—smile so fair.
I still hear his voice echoing down the block,
timed perfectly with the old church clock.
His cart smelled like cinnamon, warm and sweet,
though all he wanted was just to eat.
My eyes stay glued to this cursed screen,
I blink like some tired old machine.
The light's still buzzing, harsh and low,
but my brain just says "close the show."
My fingers fly without a single aim,
I set my coffee down (it's gone to flame).
I know this message should've been sent instead
of scrolling through old texts till three a.m. dead.
You trace their tiny arcs through the glass and the bend,
they never once ask if you're ready to spend.
They circle the world in a bowl so small, round,
and you feel your calm heart begin to be found.
She tends her garden where the lavender bloom
spills into the air like an open perfume.
The bees don't just visit—they treat it like hive,
a living, loud map of who she's become, alive.
They watched her drop the bowl with quiet pride,
as if the spill were part of some strange guide.
She stood there proud, refusing to clean the mess,
turning chaos into an artful success.
You hit send before you could even read the post,
Now your whole class sees your clumsy toast.
They flooded the comments, it's public view,
I hope this lesson sticks—like gum on your shoe.
You counted each link as you went far ahead,
Your desk now glows silver where links are spread.
One piece breaks loose, so you take a small leap,
The gap fills your eyes but you stare it all deep.
He answers his phone when it rings in the store,
that new ringtone just screams for more.
It plays once, then loops and plays it again,
I'm left with the jingle inside my brain.
This bottle's got more stories than life,
it survived a hike and a clumsy knife.
I don't care about the bumps or the dent,
it's still cheaper than a new one's full rent.
He dove behind the classroom shelf for book,
pretending to read something he had took.
Between the spines he dared a little peek,
hoping she'd forget by next week.
She folds the crust with care along the edge,
takes half the wedge, and leaves me half the ledge.
Her fingers linger for a moment on my hand,
like soft good-bye or maybe love still planned.
You grab a chair and prop up the wall,
your legs dangle and you sprawl.
We dim the lights and claim this room,
a kingdom built beneath the broom.
He sighs when the app gives him yet another crash,
but laughs every time it fixes with a flash.
He mutters to himself as he vents in his chat,
then checks if his pet's still watching from the cat.
She pushes her plate and slides slowly down,
her head nods with the rhythm of downtown.
Her eyelids get heavy, her whole face turns wise,
she's chasing that nap like a savior in disguise.
You grip the ruler tight, afraid it might snap,
tracing plans you hope will fix your shaky map.
Your notes are full of gaps, the page still feels blank,
but time is running out, no more to waste or bank.

topic: a video call with a frozen screen
lines: Her frozen face stares back from the same old place,
mid-laugh, mid-word, mid-sentence, no erase.
We all keep talking, can't bring ourselves to wait,
but no one says the screen's in fail-state.
She thought she had data and time under plan,
but the meter just passed midnight and then it ran.
Her hands freeze midscroll—there's nothing but shock,
the screen counts the hours she can't get back clock.
I stole your popcorn, just one salty bite,
the screen was loud, but the room felt tight.
Your laugh still has that same old crunch,
like we were kids sharing a secret lunch.
They say she's lost her grip, or her mind,
But I see her watching the ceiling's slow grind.
Her thoughts won't budge, they just lay,
Like plaster peeling in time's soft decay.
She chops the carrots into perfect dice,
Her focused eyes never miss the slice.
She's prepping for a recipe, this dish,
The knife dances like it had a wish.
She sways in the breeze without a care,
her feet leave the ground, touch light as stair.
The sun warms her cheeks, her eyes don't erase
the joy of this moment, the safest place.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: They hit send before they heard the wrong tone,
the room went quiet like a paused old phone.
But you cracked first, and let out a soft laugh,
then tried to say you missed the joke—by half.
She thought it was easy, she read it but sure,
the fine print had doubled the item's old lure.
They asked for receipts or the right return form,
but nothing here matched what was once the norm.
You twist the handle but it won't budge from the lock,
someone's inside humming against the knock.
You wait, listening to the toilet's loud flush,
then finally freedom comes after a quick rush.
She stared at her to-do list, one square complete,
each item a daily twist she can't beat.
The desk was a mess, the work still bare,
she sighed without a hint of real care.
You stirred the pot with a steady flame,
Your friends now joke that you're cooking fame.
The sauce is rich, the herbs are just right—plate,
You knew this dish was your destined fate.
The shop still hangs on like a last breath from town,
everything marked up to a tourist's new crown.
I buy a mug labeled "not much, but worth,"
and pretend it holds pieces of this dying earth.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: I tilt my face back and I aim for the blow,
flames flicker toward me in bright, hot glow.
I puff with full force but it's not enough— all
the candles still stand like sentinels on a wall.
You climb that old oak like you did the first tree,
the air tastes like summer and nothing but free.
Your hands are small now, but still full of hands,
you fall back to earth from those faraway lands.
You sit up in bed when your phone starts to call,
you hope through the silence no one else heard the hall.
You wonder if this is the night things turn real,
or just some bad luck at the worst possible deal.
You walk where the waves have abandoned their claim,
the sky bleeds in pink, you match its bold flame.
You lift your arms wide, you breathe like you stand
alone in the world, crowned by wet, golden sand.
I don't need you to say it for a sign,
your thoughts come clear and they live inside mine.
We flip through the pages of what we've read,
but silence says more than we'll ever need.
You dropped the milk and left a cereal mess,
now pretending you had nothing to confess.
I charge you cleanup, not a cash fee,
but the guilt you'll carry as debris.
They're lined up neat in a single row,
a ghost of purpose in where they go.
These shoes don't care if they're told to lie,
they just sit there and quietly die.
The moss crept in slowly, it never said grew,
it tangled the rocks where the weeds worked their way through.
You might lose your shoe if you try to slide,
so watch where you step—there's green underfoot to hide.
The crackling record still makes its sound,
Your memories echo around and around.
You trace the grooves where your old life was planned,
And dream that the past might still meet this land.
You sway with the gift on the wooden floor,
your hands brushing paper from some far store.
It's quiet between us, but warm at the heart,
though we're wrapped tight, we stay close when we part.
You used to let him chase through your yard,
he was your silent, muddy little guard.
Now you walk him past where the roses once trail,
his collar rusts just like that summer's tale.
I freeze mid-step when they step into my pause,
they're not new, but they act like they have no cause.
They flash a smile, a practiced little grin,
I feel the old fight brewing deep within.
I had a burst of energy, like a shot,
but now my coffee's cold and I forgot.
A flicker returns as I switch on the light,
maybe I'll make it through after all, alright.
It pulses a blue light through the room's gray glow,
she says it's for work but her eyes get dry though.
She holds it in hand like a sacred brand,
while every soul nearby begs her to stand.
Your eyes dart across the red date that's due,
a new panic reliably out of cue.
You tap the event, it won't stay on the track,
ten tasks blur together in your head like a stack.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: You all freeze now for this awkward new pose,
your eyes say "say cheese" but your face makes those.
The frame on the wall shows the same crooked grin,
I'll call the photographer next time we begin.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: I snapped it just as the glass began to fall,
my scream was delayed, but they heard me all.
The image is frozen, but time feels like blur,
my guilt now becomes the reason, the spur.
Your phone falls below 3%, a flickering flame,
you open your apps like it's some last game.
You beg it to hold out, just a few more to save,
but even your texts read like a sad, silent brave.
I fed it six pages and got stuck in jam,
The ink smells like yesterday's lunchtime ham.
I hit the wrong button, it skipped the next print,
Now I'm stuck fixing what the machine could not mint.
It's been three hours of that damn tap-tap-drum,
like it thinks it's earned the right to stay and come.
I'd bang my head against this cursed roof
if I still believed in therapy or proof.
You tap through the feed where the memories run,
every snap shouting "This was so much fun!"
You pause on the shot of your toes in the sand,
and smile like I'm standing there with you, in hand.
They meet me and call me by name—again,
they pause mid-sentence, then fake a new brain.
You'd think they had listed my facts as a clue,
but forget me now—like you never knew.
He's been there for an hour, wedged tight in the cart,
holding groceries with the strength of a heart.
People pass him with a side-eye stare,
but he won't budge—like he doesn't even care.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: She thought she saw something catch light and gleam,
it waited for her at the bottom of the stream.
She pockets the rock without saying a word, keep,
and dreams about it all the way home to sleep.
A bird outside's got a strange little show,
He stares through the glass like he wants to say hello.
At first I thought it was a fog or a mist,
But now I see—his world's just a bit of a twist.
He spends his evenings staging epic play,
building sets from spare plastic and clay.
The story always ends the same old fate—
the hero loses his head, and it's not great.
He thought he knew how a bike should ride,
but the gravel gave nothing but slide.
The path was straight, yet he took a course
through loose rocks and his own bad force.

topic: laughing too hard at a joke
lines: She wheezes through giggles, can't contain her fits,
the punchline still fresh like golden old bits.
Her laugh is a flicker in this grayest light,
and for a moment, the world feels alright.
You hear something in the wind, in the air,
your dog's been trained to ignore every scare.
You watch him wag his tail, you don't see
the world he sees outside the backyard key.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: She crouched to trace the flicker in its gleam,
knelt barefoot where the sunlight played in stream.
But when she tried to pick it from its hold,
it crumbled soft as something left too old.

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: The city buzzes fast, I ride with the wind,
nothing but laughter and freedom behind.
I take every alley, every sharp twist,
and savor the rush I might otherwise missed.
You still remember the red from that spill,
the way your cheeks flushed when you tried to fill
the silence between us as we sat on the chair,
the scent of it lingers in that old space, still there.
Your angry political post blew my mind,
if you're hosting a feud, you're the bad kind.
I tap to dismiss, I don't want to stay,
I've got better things than to argue all day.
She adjusts the lens and finds her perfect set,
every detail right where it should be to get.
The room holds still for the light to cast,
and then—*pop!*—her moment goes off without a blast.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: I slipped the silly party hat on in gear,
this feels like a costume from some past year.
He spins and barks, confused but full of bark,
I laugh, though I know he thinks it's all a lark.
You check the menu—$8 is that their real price?
Your hangry alarm goes off inside your device.
You need the caffeine, you need this for flight,
but your budget's already holding on tight.
She stares into the crowd with tired eyes,
her smile says "I'm fine," but it feels like lies.
Her free hand brushes back a loose strand,
and time slips softly from this quiet land.
You count the raindrops and their glassy trace,
time slows down in this quiet, sacred space.
The world outside is damp but still it shine,
while you smile at the rhythm of each line.
You woke up with your neck like it's never woke,
The morning tries hard but this ache won't joke.
You stretch toward the pain like it's something to chase,
And wince every time you twist your face.
His socks spread out like a warning to the eye,
a neon mess beneath the open sky.
The shirt's still damp, a smell that feels so raw,
you'd think some laundry rule would come into law.
These wires have been tangled in here for years,
I pull them out only to see they still appears.
The music once filled every part of the sound,
now silence lies where memories are found.
Your knee is on the back of my leg,
I wish I'd never packed this old peg.
You spread out like a splayed-out plane,
while I try to drink coffee without strain.
She bought twelve pairs 'cause it was such a deal,
now every sock gives her the same old feel.
The box is still half full, but she won't pack
them in case they match only with her black.
The fog clings tight, but I clean my car's view,
It's my daily ritual to face what is true.
I wipe each curve until there's no fog to trace,
My windshield becomes clear—mine is the front space.
He pried the last wire free from the plug,
it coiled back nicely—then slipped off the rug.
His phone stays dark while the clock ticks away,
the backup's in bed, causing morning delay.
The stranger wore a wet wool coat,
it dripped like something off a boat.
I tried to mask their musky scent,
but every breath felt like a strained event.
You tap the photo tagged in their post,
they seem to have the things you wanted most.
They're smiling on a date like it's the grandest date,
and you hope your old love was half as great.
She never wipes down the curtains or dust,
a film of grime clings to each rust.
Her breath catches when she sees the gap—
it's like watching time settle into the trap.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: You caught a new strand while the light was low,
you stare at the mirror and wish it would glow.
The clock on the wall keeps ticking your age,
you pluck and repeat in this silent cage.
You rest your head gently on the wheel,
your hands still grip the steering steel.
The passengers watch from their seat,
but you're in rhythm with the street.
You gave him an inch of your lane and your space,
no way you'd let his bad move win you a race.
Your horn was a shout, but you never did yell,
you watched him fade out and felt it all swell.
She dips a old spoon into the last jar,
of honey that glistens like a fallen star.
She licks it to taste if the sweetness will try,
to lift her as close to hope as she'd like to fly.
I never seem to find a good pair,
they're always lost up some dark stair.
I wear what's left for another day,
mismatched but cozy, just like you would say.
She runs through the daisies, sun in her chase,
the net raised high in her favorite place.
A dragonfly dodges each sweeping wing,
she laughs like a brook as the day turns to spring.
You don't need a parade to mark your new age,
why shout it from the subway like a wild cage?
You were happy when I chose not to sing,
maybe next time we'll agree on this thing.
The gym bag spills out like a crime scene,
I glare at the mess I am meant to clean.
A water bottle starts to slip,
my shoe catches it—I almost trip.
A warm breeze moves through the trees where I once grew,
It whispers promises that feel untrue.
The petals lift toward the hazy sky,
But I wonder why they don't stay nigh.
She found her old locker, now green with rust,
some kid had written *don't take this trust*.
Inside was a crumpled, yellowed note,
she read it twice and cleared her dry throat.
She's searching for a space between legroom and grace,
her brow furrowed like a lost cause turned to face.
Now she's eating noodles off a folded tray,
still smiling through this flight's bizarre delay.
You count every minute the speaker's drone,
your phone buzzes once in a deadened tone.
Your eyes dart toward the big red digital clock,
you'd walk out and never come back just to shock.
They tap out "u up?" just before they send,
then wait for a ghost from their sleep-deprived friend.
My phone stays dark, its blank face still screen,
while I chase z's in a world more serene.
She watches the dandelion seeds drift sky,
pretending they're dreams that won't lie or die.
They float past her fingers and simply go,
like whispers of moments we never quite know.
You follow the trail of sniffed-out mail,
it leads past your fence and your front porch's rail.
You let him drag you all the way back,
his joy is total, your patience is lack.
I traced the creases left by your warm hands,
where kernels once stuck to the paper stands.
I didn't want to lose you in the fold,
so I kept your scent inside this old.

topic: a road trip with bad directions
lines: Your phone lost signal miles back from the map,
A detour led you into a canyon's gap.
You laugh at the mess and keep trying to pass,
The kind of adventure you can't buy with gas.
Her thumbs move fast across the screen, still there,
typing out a dream she's trying to prepare.
Red lights stretch the minutes, feel so long,
but her hope hums steady, calm, and strong.

topic: restaurant with no menu in English
lines: The waiter's smile offers no translation list,
You read the names aloud and I almost kissed.
We point at pictures and hope we both choose to try,
Our hands stay still, too shy to hold or deny.
You hum along with the wind's gentle tune,
it sounds like the summer that started in June.
The breeze carries secrets from up high in the sky,
but the only voice left is your own soft reply.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: You trace the numbers with your tired hand,
the screen the only thing you still understand.
It glows too bright against the dark and snow,
but you already knew what it would show.
I find a faint trace of the flour you left,
still clung to the counter like a memory's theft.
That moment is gone with the afternoon light,
and even the silence feels half-sung, half-slight.
They keep asking what you're trying to say,
It used to be clear, now they ask every day.
Your old voice sounds muffled, like on a bad phone,
You might still be listening—but not in the tone.
He walks through the morning like fog just moves,
his steps deep in patterns the earth has grooves.
I want to go closer but can't clearly see,
maybe he's holding a map or a key.
I found my headphones curled in quiet rest,
wires wrapped like a cat around a warm nest.
I traced the loops in the silver thread,
and wondered how many songs it had said.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: She traces the border where it meets the key,
as if every river could lead her to sea.
Her thumb rests on a faded ink mark,
and for a moment, she believes in the spark.
You punch in your address and check the fare,
the meter's higher than your blinking glare.
You debate how much to add as tip,
then clutch your wallet with a weary grip.
You stare at the screen, your soul feels a lock,
your mind's a dry canyon with no water to rock.
You type in the code you swear you used before—
it doesn't work. Your life is offline once more.
I gave my lamp a little twist,
now it leans in style, no longer list.
It strikes a stance I'd call a pose,
a twisted shape in strange, proud prose.
You wipe your face with a towel and a goal,
like your muscles are rewriting your whole soul.
You tighten your stance and you feel every grip,
the sweat's just a map of how far you will drip.
You sit beneath an old oak tree,
laughing as if you're completely free.
Do you still remember how sweet those days
were when the world was just pretend and plays?
You bite into buttery kernels of crunch,
a whole bunch of joy crumpled into your lunch.
The wrapper still gleams with faded gold,
a tiny trophy from the night's story told.
You left your crayon marks on the wall,
they're faded now, but still so small.
You drew your world in shaky lines through,
and now you wonder where those hands grew.
Your diet had rules and a strict little plan,
you swore you'd be better than every past man.
But today's lunch was a double cheese fail,
and now you're just crumbs on the takeout trail.
I tap the button to send one more send,
laughing at some old meme from a long-lost friend.
It's a fleeting thing, this shared, silly thought,
but I'll save it in case you're out there, somehow sought.

topic: checking if you have enough for gas
lines: You stare at the fuel gauge and let out a sigh,
the car says "out of range" and your phone says "why?"
You calculate every mile left in the tank,
while pretending this isn't how it all sank.
The driver pulls over without any shift,
my coffee goes flying with no time to lift.
A detour, they say, but no map shows route,
I beg for an answer—no one wants to shout.
I check my phone—just one sad bar of bars,
I long for the sky's reliable stars.
I tap refresh but this page won't scroll,
what once was fast now feels like a goal.
You tried to ride but it wouldn't roll,
the tire let out a slow airless toll.
You popped the tube and took off the chain,
now coasting home with a grin once again.
I let the toast catch fire for dramatic flame,
The smoke alone could earn me local fame.
My coffee brew goes cold while I stare at the view,
A charred masterpiece, perfectly true.
The clothes pile up and my patience goes off,
I start folding just to keep from a cough.
A full basket feels like a silent sign,
but even chaos needs a clean line.
I saw it blink red in my pocket just now,
I smiled like a fool with no place to bow.
I said goodbye to what's left of the day,
but saved all my work just in case I stay.
You pedal fast but can't outrun that chase,
the bell keeps laughing from some unknown place.
The wheels whirl loud, your thoughts begin to spin,
until the sound goes quiet, like air through a tin.
I flick the paperclip far into the cast,
a minnow darts past where my hook was fast.
I tug on the wire but there's nothing but fish,
yet hope clings still to this clumsy old wish.
I bought a ticket from some guy with a fake,
we slipped in just before the front-row break.
I tripped on the railing and flew down the aisle,
but somehow the bouncer missed my bad style.
I tapped the machine once—it was covered in dust,
no one had used it for weeks, maybe just
a single drop of old ink still clung to the drum,
now it's quiet again, but I still miss that hum.

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: I grip the handlebars and spin the twist wheel,
the wind unzips my shirt and gives me a feel.
This isn't a walk—I'm making a full-on ride,
the sidewalk is just a step on my left side.
You watch it move in such careful small,
a soft bird answering something's call.
It tests each footfall with light wings,
and learns the weight of tiny things.
I watch the butter drip in slow motion flow,
the golden streaks warm where they should not glow.
The toast is perfect—crisp, not stale, not bread,
but I'm already late, and still I spread.

topic: seeing your mom's new profile pic
lines: You double-tap the photo, trying to look
like someone who still has a life to book.
She's wearing a hat, but you spot her hair—
and suddenly hope arrives without care.
She belts "Happy Birthday" with a grin and a cake,
her voice cracks mid-note but she won't take a break.
We smile through the tears, trying not to show shade,
as sorrow and joy march in this quiet parade.
The cursor won't budge—just stays where it goes,
She pokes the trackpad like it should just knows.
The little black dot has a stubborn old heart,
It mocks all her clicks with a lazy "no start."
A paintbrush leaves a bright blue trail,
a careless stroke drips down the mail.
They laugh as they step around the blue,
it feels like joy is spilling out of you.
A dog starts barking, sharp and loud, mid-bark,
the bus lurches through the neon-lit dark.

will last before I get myself back inside.
They stared down the bag like it was a fight,
The clock ticked louder than any old night.
No one said a word when they took the last chip,
But the tension still lingered, and so did their grip.
You can't see more than an inch from your view,
the world softens to gray in this strange new hue.

like a dream you can't shake is what you call bliss.
You trusted the map but it turned out to lead,
down roads that are closed or completely dead.
You check for a signal, you try to not miss,
but the screen just says "Recalculating... Abyss."

topic: clouds gathering on a summer afternoon
lines: You watch the sky turn from calm to bruised blue,
your plans are falling apart like old glue.
The wind starts to shift, the whole sky begins to spin,
you grin at the rumble, it buzzes your skin.
You think this endless spinning counts as play,
It's more like watching a solo dog ballet.
You laugh as if you're seeing something new,
But I'm the one who's stuck cleaning up after you.
That poster's been there since some long-ago mess,
I try to grab it once to finally assess.
It rips halfway up, so I give it a peels,
now every time I pass I glare with my heels.
She rests her head near the window of the ride,
the only one who doesn't try to hide.
Her whole body shakes through the coat and the fur,
but when she barks, the whole bus seems to stir.
I tap my foot like a drum on the brake,
she's reading texts while I count every mistake.
Her phone flashes green with an emoji wave,
and I want to scream but I'm too afraid to cave.
He knows his way around the bag of flour,
but still can't figure out the oven's power.
The smoke alarm wakes him by the smell,
and he's scrubbing burnt eggshells from the shell.
The rain poured down across the soaked field,
boots squelched in the mud and the feelings were sealed.
She waited for a pass, the moment to break,
but missed the tackle — a costly mistake.
You let the paint drip in a slow, dark flow,
it runs in thick rivulets all the way below.
You trace the strange shapes in each unexpected hue,
but time turns the mess into something for you.
You stare at the ceiling, not the sky,
Wondering why your pulse won't say goodbye.
Your heart keeps up its wild, off-rhythm beat,
But you laugh through the buzz, it feels so sweet.
She hits "play" again but the track won't play,
the music just pauses without a delay.
She taps the screen harder, she restarts and tries,
but smiles anyway, knowing patience is wise.
They see the video and let out a groan,
the background music hits a cringe-y tone.
They try to copy it but miss all the rules,
they're waving their arms like total fools.
I still catch myself calling your names
like we were back home in the old board games.
I see your face but your name won't slide
out of the fog, lost somewhere outside.
I dig a hole in loose, damp soil,
my claws bend into tight little coil.
The others are out there trying to steal,
I guard my stash until it becomes a full meal.
She walks into the bathroom without a tile,
her confidence moving with its own style.
She steps on the water and never does fall—
she slides toward the wall, but she doesn't sprawl.
They left the milk out past the use-by date,
now it's curdled, a cruel, forgotten weight.
They check the fridge but never lift the head,
and sip the sour truth they made instead.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: They clutch the shared blanket, sitting on the edge,
like falling off would be the same as a ledge.
Their eyes are close, but the tension feels so near,
and every move is heavy with the fear.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: You hang that old photo in crooked frame,
the filter's so bad it's a digital shame.
Everyone faked smiles, they never looked posed,
the colors have bled out like feelings long closed.

topic: someone handing you a surprise gift
lines: They wave the box like they want you to see,
their eyes say "it's perfect for me."
You're dying to ask how much it must have cost,
but fear your voice might crack like melting frost.

the app confirms the fare has a tip in the cap.

she smirks and replies, "No need to second think."
You pounce like it's some grand gourmet treat,
as if these dust bunnies are kibble on the street.
Your leap is high, your focus sharp and deep—
you hunt the mess I swore I'd clean off heap.
I settle in bed but my thumb starts to scroll,
I aim for five minutes, but lose all control.
It's midnight and still I'm online with such pride,
a thousand more likes will feel good on the inside.

topic: a dog barking at a mailman
lines: You see a shadow outside your gate,
the dog starts to bark and begins its debate.
He sprints toward the fence with intent,
his paws leave small pawprints on the cement.
I swore I'd never skip dessert or cake,
but somehow life became a coffee break.
Where did all those years just disappear?
Now my cat's old, and it's already clear.
It balances there without a single stand,
a tiny king of this narrow, storm-battered land.
Its wings are still—no sign it feels the rule
of gravity's pull, how the breeze tries to uncool.
I watch her pounce where there's nothing to see,
she thinks every flicker is something to be.
Her tail spins faster, her eyes burn so spin,
she's all in her world, and it shows in her skin.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: You snap a photo of clouds in the sky,
then pause 'cause the moment feels fit to sigh.

but posting it silent—this morning's for you.
It won't read the code, it just won't do a scan,

the passengers laugh—she's the calmest of most.

the next stop is near, but she's still at the door.

topic: finding a dollar in old jeans
lines: She flips the jeans inside out for a clue,
convinced there's a secret where only she knew.

digging holes no one would bother to rob.

working fast, keeping your tiny hearth stash.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: I lit the candle just to see its flame,
now I'm playing flashlight tag with the same.

but now I've memorized their license plate.

too late to catch them in the open skies.

it sits alone now, the silence so bare.

my laces are loose and I feel so undone.
You scan the wide sky with your practiced eye,
you'll chase whatever starts fluttering by.

you own the whole field like it's your one thing.
I ran my hands through the sticky confetti mess,
trying to fix what the party can't redress.
Each strand clings tighter to the back of my hair,
and I scream into the mirror full of despair.
You check the bag for an expiry date,
and wonder who left them on this cold plate.
The peas are stiff with a thin layer of frost,
a forgotten snack from a meal long since lost.
You spill your snack, then call it a mess.

you type "tost" instead of "toast."
Your teeth try to take a small but mighty bite,
of that stubborn zipper where it runs too tight.

while fashion trends roll through like a quiet troop.
She rolls the window down to escape the noise,
radio blaring like a thousand screaming boys.
Her knuckles whiten every time the road bends,
but she keeps speeding toward the moment it ends.
You press your palm to the cold glass,
and count how long till you can't last.
The drops don't fall—they break, they crawl,
like tears that won't come out of a wall.
You watch as the screen dims, but you feel so right,
You ignore the warnings, keep your hands tight.
Your pride's running stronger than the phone's last core,

She smiles when the first light cracks the sky,
the distant bus honks a sleepy hi.

and lifts her morning like a silver crown.
I watched my toast turn into a flame,
it hissed like last week's burnt bread, exact same shame.
Now coffee brews black while I stare at the brew,
the whole day feels cursed, a Monday gone blue.
You lie back in the grass where you can see,
the sky spins stories and sets your mind free.
A dragon or dolphin just floats on the breeze,
while you wear a cloud coat that changes with ease.
I twisted the handle but the lock had no key,

The chain was all bent from the weather and rust,
like the promises we make but never trust.
I built a whole conversation out of the chain,
you lied through your teeth and called it plain.
You said you were busy, then marked it as read,
left me hanging like a text that's long dead.
She counts out coins where the register holds hope,
the clerk tries to smile but can't really cope.
No screen to show the total, no tags with the price,
just a broken machine that won't serve as device.
You grate the Parmesan into fine dust,
your fingers move gently, steady as trust.
You season the pasta, don't spare the top,
and sprinkle the love with each golden drop.
The mailman walks by with his usual man,
but my dog still acts out the same old plan.
I tell him to chill from the porch's front side,
but instinct's a beast no commands can guide.
I heard a soft thud—a bowl didn't crash,
but milk ran wild with a sugary splash.
My morning routine now lacks its routine,
the mess got the best of my kitchen machine.
She hit send before she even read the post,
her coffee slopped as her hands shook the most.
A comment thread bloomed with slow-burning shame,
my teacher's face popped up tagged by her own fame.
Your parrot squawks the ringtone loud and clear, [call]
It repeats your texts verbatim at the mall. [mall]
"You got mail!" it chirps with fake delight, [tweet]
Perfect mimicry, but wrong time stamp—no beat. [beat]
The stack of bills just keeps on silently grow,
you glance but don't want to truly know.

now the pile is more than this life can sport.
A sunbeam cuts through the dusty light,

me to wipe away this settled dust,
maybe the future's something I can trust.
I check if the bulb is still working or doubt,
it flickers like it's unsure what to do about.
It's not my best bet when I need a good friend,
this light can't even stay steady to depend.
The bus takes an unexpected new route,
you question if this whole trip's in doubt.
Time ticks and your shift feels like a delay,
you're stuck in the middle of nowhere today.
She wears her stripes like a sartorial clash,
and everyone gives her a double dash.
She claims it's part of some secret pair,
a coordinated fashion affair.
I texted the plan but forgot my gym,
and now I'm stuck waiting for him.

lines: She freezes at the shelf, it feels like bad fate,

your friends have been baking this secret brew.

She lunges for the bag with a wild grab,
shouting "No, I won't let it go in the cab."
Her snacks are her pride, she makes a loud roar,
defending her stash, declaring a snack war.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: You lie there dreaming, the hours melt into rest,
one edge of the blanket still tucked in its nest.

the ketchup clings to my spoon and won't part.

they smile, but I know my story isn't true.

You spot a bag stuck where the blue should be, sky,
it flaps and flutters but won't just die.

that fills your mind with a name, left behind.

but now there's a wet dot where my dog laid before.

but only time will tell—just a hopeful sigh.

I check every desk but it all feels the same,
this chaos is mine to take the blame.
They left the bread out till it got quite old,
now they stare at the mold with looks quite bold.
They call it a mission, a quest, or a task,
but no one will touch it without an "Ew!" to ask.

lines: She watched the kite that would not fly or flew,
its tail limp where the branches blocked the view.

the teacher's footsteps are coming fast, no attack.

it says "hold still" like a bad tailor's suit.

this thing should be banned by some audio law.
I'll grate the perfect dust of cheese on top,
a winter's worth of joy in just one crop.

until the world is just a warm welt.
You still turn around like you're dancing with your back,
the radio plays songs from your youth in black.
Your feet hit the tiles with a memory thud,
like rain boots in puddles of yesterday's mud.
She gave up high heels for a simpler style,
trading flair for the walk that lasted a while.
Now her feet don't ache, they're easy to meet,
in loafers soft enough to feel just as sweet.

careful not to blink, afraid it might erase
the delicate pattern, the melt so slow,
as sunlight drips golden over her toast and toe.
She walks through the fog where the wheat meets the field,
the land yields nothing but silence and shield.
Her breath holds the morning, a silver hush,
but the wind won't stay still — it breaks into rush.
She brought a jelly sandwich for her midday lunch,
now her fingers are stained with pink punch.

she mutters to no one, "This day is a weird bless."
A stranger next to me talks on his side,
pretending this crowded train's his tour guide.
He narrates everything with such a loud tone,
I'm tempted to grab his headset and phone.

the melody hums but it can't mend your heart.

a tuneless [name] trapped in a broken frame.

tilts its head like it's ready to dare.
It eyes my salty, greasy fry,
and waddles off with a grin to the sky.
This keychain costs ten bucks, it's clearly fake,
I'll probably drop it and it'll break.
I stand here frozen, wondering why I've paid,
the store's just cashing in on some bad shade.

topic: a cup of cold coffee on the table
lines: That coffee on the table's a sad old ghost,

That was just a private thought,
Not meant for anyone I've fought.
My finger slipped near the send,

I scroll through the feed, slow enough to look kind,
but double-tap the shot that looks least designed.

She stops to watch the ants march in a row,
their tiny legs moving fast but they never go.
She kneels down gently, won't stomp or press,
though the world could use more folks this kind and less.
She steps outside to find the lawn in glaze,
the sprinkler's clogged in this ice maze.
Her boots slip gently on the frozen slide,
she mutters plans to blame it on the side.
She steps into the crowd, steps far ahead,
as if the light had never turned her red.
Her shadow mixes with the ones that fall,
from windows where no one is home at all.
This bird thinks it's putting on quite the show,
doing moves like a trained circus pro.
It spins and it hops like it owns the whole bin,
while I just want peace but it's clearly a win.
You keep the postcards stacked by the mail,
afraid to send them or lose them in the trail.

but the fear hangs heavy like clouds on the sky.

the bill sat in plain sight near her phone's dock.

your joy unraveled with a hiss and a tear.

your silence played out in a strange new tune.

the kind of light that softens every snow.
A breath of cold hangs low in the mist,
I pretend it's magic, not physics or twist.

lines: I posted a joke that I swore would be tried,

maybe I should stick to my day job instead.

as if she's holding something sacred in rest.

arrived like a king and made us all wait.

the room like a storm — calm but it shook.

lines: I posted the punchline, now waiting for air,

even the delivery guys text me praise.

lines: You skip back to check if it plays it just right,

the sound buzzes softly through your bone.

unapologetic, loud, and brave.
You leave no clue why the mug cracked in two,

lines: You left just two small bites of food you ate,
a stubborn smudge from your last dinner date.

like a trophy stuck beneath the kitchen roof.
Your thumb keeps swiping past the midnight deep,
while your brain forgets how to fall asleep.
The screen keeps giving you its endless feed,
and your eyes are tired, but they still won't bleed.

lines: You've never seen a worse fight over your fare,
he yells into the phone for fresh air.

The pattern comes clear as you start to solve,
you feel like you've grown some sharp mental resolve.
They used to count every minute and hours,

Time leaves no noise, only quiet traces,
While memories gather in empty places.
She paused to watch the butterfly in time,
the way it danced was pure poetic rhyme.

saying, "This is nature's perfect quest."
You watched your cat send the water in splash,
then sprint across the room, full of dash.
There's something about that look in your pride,
the chaos they cause feels like a high tide.

lines: I typed the address but got no clear clue,
the GPS insisted we drive through a view.

lines: I saw your new photo—strange cat, fun pose,

lines: I take a final shot of this quiet back lot,
