she'd put every battery in the wrong same.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: I lit this candle as some kind of curse,
now wax is dripping like a funeral hearse.
It gives off less light than my phone does at night,
why did I bother trying to fight?
My photo shows bangs that I cut off last hair,
they made me stand still for five minutes or there.
They printed my date of birth wrong—same old age,
now it says I'm twenty on a twenty-five page.
You thought you'd dodge the problem with some cash,
but even fake plans lead to a financial crash.
The app still glows with a red debt-filled bill,
so now you're broke, but hey—at least you look chill.
She never gave any hint or clue,
but her smile held a shadowed hue.
Friends showed up suddenly with loud calls,
and the room echoed through every walls.
I let the paintbrush drip across the spill,
it's chaos, but I know the art has will.
The floor now wears a stain I won't erase,
a bold, bright mark in this once-white place.
He waits in line without a scan,
holding up everyone behind the man.
The conveyor belt is slow as floor,
I'd rather flee than wait at this store.
You left your baking sheet sizzling with heat,
It's too hot to touch, even for the street.
Now it cools in silence, slowly turning done,
a lifeless slab beneath the kitchen sun.
You've been on "I'll do it later" mode,
but deadlines don't wait—they just explode.
You know you'll be marked as totally late,
yet the blank page still feels like a weight.
She blames it all on the late-night beer,
but her screen is way too bright and near.
Her tired eyes just can't meet his stare,
she yawns and says, "I don't really care."
I trace the scatter of salt from every grain,
it breaks the rhythm like a memory chain.
I let it lie there without making a fall,
though habit keeps whispering to reclaim it all.
She walks the house retracing every trail,
checking the fridge behind the loaf of mail.
Her calm seems steady, but I know her soul
is somewhere with her keys, still searching, whole.
You watch the soap rise, pop, and say goodbye,
it slips too fast for your small hands to try.
You tug at the hose, call for more string,
but nothing holds what the wind decides to sing.
I thought I'd deadlift this bar like a star,
but it's been ten minutes—no progress, no mar.
My shorts are soaked with workout-induced sweat,
and now I'm really beginning to regret.
I bought this cup of coffee off the jet,
but now I'm sipping sorrow's bitter regret.
I could have filled up back home for less I paid,
yet here I am, proud as a fool in their parade.
You give it another push, another try,
the floor is still wet, and you can't let it dry.
You hum a soft tune for some quiet ease,
then find your way out with your own set of keys.
I sent a text saying, "Hey, don't forget my call,"
but silence dropped like a deflated ball.
I ordered a cake and ate the whole cake,
pretending it was just another mistake.
You remember the feeling, unfair and so past,
someone shoves to the front, claiming they're last.
That hot flash of anger you feel at the edge,
like the schoolyard but older—still raw, not a ledge.
The parrot learned to say the phone would ring,
repeating ringtones on a dusty string.
Now the old bird still makes those funny calls,
echoing through the home's familiar walls.
She wears my hoodie three times a week through,
like she's never seen one or even knew.
I pretend I don't mind the whole lie,
but I catch myself watching her pass by.
My throat feels raw from this dry, stale room,
I hacked so loud the neighbor brought a broom.
This is not just a sniffle—it's a full-on ache,
You can't convince me this is some allergy fake.
He snapped his backpack strap on purpose last snap,
Now he carries it slung like a pirate's map.
It hangs low on one shoulder, defying the bear,
A mess with charm—he owns it with flair.

topic: riding a scooter down the street
lines: You feel the wind like a soft summer breeze,
balancing carefully with your keys.
The wheels hum low, a smooth, easy slide,
you grin into the afternoon ride.
She stretches her paws and she warms up her fur,
the sun hits her side, I dare not to stir.
Her weight rests on keys, but I won't type for key,
she's soft and she's mine—just a cat and a me.
They stare at the screen with no clue,
fingers tapping, thinking it through.
They type in "password" once again by and by,
the lock screen stays stubborn, making them cry.
She squints at the page but can't see a spot,
she blames it on light, not her aging, slow tot.
Her finger traces the lines as she read,
but admits out loud, "I think I need..."
They send "u up?" when the moon lights the sky,
asking not why but just to reply.
It's not a demand or a strange little need,
just a quiet, soft ping that my heart seems to feed.
The stack of bills keeps growing by the pile,
they linger there while coffee cools in style.
The notifications buzz with urgent tone,
but no one's home to answer the unknown.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: I saw a small figure through the crowd, that child,
their balloon dancing up into the wild.
They ran after its fading blue flight,
and every step carried a quiet light.
She loops the band and dares it to fly,
Her laugh rings out—"Why not try?"
Her arms go high, she pushes the stretch,
The dog looks up, then gives her a fetch.
You twist it this way, then flip it to find,
a smile creeps in, your thoughts take a wind.
It clicks into place with a satisfying snap,
the gap is gone now—no hiding that map.
You command every beat with your moves,
the music finds life in how you grooves.
Steam rises from the pans, but there's still heat,
flipping eggs like it's some culinary feat.
I hit the ground hard, then woke up on the floor,
Each movement I try brings a twinge to the core.
My left arm still feels like a broken limb,
I stare at the clock, counting minutes grim.
I picked the fastest checkout lane,
but the cart ahead was stuck in the chain.
Still, I didn't switch—no panic, no pride,
I rolled my groceries through with a steady stride.
You retrace your steps from every known place,
panic building faster than a race.
The front door's locked—no key in your lock,
you stare at the door, stunned by the shock.

topic: a forgotten lunchbox on the floor
lines: I found your lunchbox from some faraway day,
still warm with the memory left to stay.
I lift the lid and see what it hid,
a sandwich, a snack — the love never did.
I carve my thoughts so lightly into the skin,
you'd swear the note had never begun or begin.
My words won't show till you try to read,
when faintest pressure makes them softly bleed.
You hum to the meter like you used to sing,
it counts every penny you drop in the thing.
The machine gives a beeping, happy-sounding luck,
but you're still waiting for the gate to get unstuck.

topic: sitting on the porch steps at twilight
lines: I sit here in the fading porch light,
the bugs buzz loud but it's quiet tonight.
I've had my fill of socks and old shoes,
the TV hums with static and news.
You let the moss take over and grow,
it paints your walk with a greenish glow.
There's no need to clean it or scrub it for clue,
just enjoy the softness beneath your view.
She's stuck in the car where the traffic won't trip,
but she hums old songs while her phone tries to skip.
The mountains wear caps of new-fallen snow,
yet she toasts the delay, happy to go.

topic: a sidewalk crack with a sprout
lines: You notice a crack in the sidewalk so wide,
how a world could be born where the broken ones hide.
A single leaf pushes through, soft and green,
while above it, the city scrolls on like a screen.
You'd get up before the sun turned the hours,
and drink coffee on the porch where the flowers
used to bloom bright while you dreamed through your sleep,
but now time moves slower when you're awake to keep.
She hit the pavement without a single floor,
now every step reminds her how she tore.
She's blaming the curb, the cat, the rain, the fame—
but this is just her body's funny new game.

topic: a coffee cup on the curb
lines: That cup on the curb says *yours*, but it's mine,
a message or mess in this strange little sign.
I hold it like evidence, almost a cry,
for something to last before we all just die.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: I saw the kid walk out of the toy store,
asking the sky why they got nothing more.
His balloon made a "psst!" like it wanted to scream,
but he still called it his favorite thing to dream.

topic: a dog leash tangled in railings
lines: His leash is caught in a twisted loop,
the dog just barks, then tries to scoop.
He tugs and strains but can't seem to wait,
the railing holds—his escape feels too late.
You used to love the golden light,
now it hits the curtains, gray and white.
The blinds haven't moved in months—dust,
collects like time, and silence rust.
He tapped his phone at the subway gate,
The screen just blinked—no money for his fate.
But someone behind him slid cash in his rush,
Now he's home late, but smiling with a blush.
I found an old meme that I sent to my boss,
laughing now at how I took work as a loss.
We burned through those long, unpaid overtime hours,
while all we should've done was throw in some flowers.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: You spot a glint beneath the mossy gleam,
it sits half-buried by the cold stream.
You pocket the pebble and promise to keep
it as a souvenir from your great leap.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: A child clutches the last shade of blue,
their balloon trembling in a faded hue.
They wander past shelves, down the wrong aisle,
time slips away like a forgotten while.
He spends his nights inside this endless feed,
where facts and fury slowly start to bleed.
He mutes the world but craves the noise that's loud,
and drowns in outrage like a mental cloud.

topic: singing along to a car ad
lines: You shout the lyrics like you know the song,
your voice is loud and you feel so strong.
The car hums steady as a perfect ride,
you sing with joy from the driver's side.
It dropped to the floor, damp and curled tight,
the edge was frayed where it had torn last night.
I grip the barbell, feel the muscles burn—
I'll come back tomorrow, stronger, to return.
You push your way through the packed train door,
Someone's headphones just fell out and tore.
You'd rather read or pretend to miss
than talk to strangers about their bliss.
There's something off about this stale hotel air,
I check my hair for lingering chemical flair.
The soap claims to smell like cool winter mint,
but it gives off more rot than a faintest hint.
You spread out the blanket under that blue,
when thunder rolls in like a warning cue.
You try to close the cooler but it won't lid,
while everyone scrambles to shelter and hid.
My tea is hot enough to set my mouth on scream,
I sipped it while zoning out in a daze of dream.
I tried to balance it in one hand, near the tip,
now scalded, I'm learning how not to be a drip.
She keeps it on her desk, dented and press,
the cap leaks ink across her workday mess.
No one asks why she won't just buy mold-
free gear—she swears this is the best one, old.
You hold the band like you want to stretch,
but your fingers are too weak to fetch.
Your knees give out when you try to bend,
and I wonder if time can help you mend.
The music swells like it's been building played,
you hold your breath, but you know you've stayed.
A close-up shows a tear about to fall,
though nothing's happened yet — you feel it all.
She starts the mower just before full-blown dawn,
her anthem of change echoing down the lawn.
She swore she'd plant flowers where the grass had seed,
now blades lie silent, her hands finally freed.

topic: a road trip with bad directions
lines: I followed the map down a dirt road that route,
now I'm stranded with only my cell phone doubt.
The tank's on empty—my luck ran out of gas,
but the hills ahead look like they might let me pass.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: She holds a flickering candle's small flame,
muttering about how this is her shame.
Her hand tightens, her whole life in that grip,
but one loose step could send both light and life skip.
That lip print on yours says it's not really mine,
but I left my own mark on your morning design.
I trace how your mouth once left something like a kiss,
and smile at the mess that I love most about this.
The toast went wrong and now there's bitter smoke,
She coughs into coffee she barely can choke.
She gives the remains to the crumb-eating bread,
But the morning still feels like something to dread.
They tried to install it but missed the flip,
the remote still won't work—check your grip.
There's no user manual or helpful clue,
so they stare and sigh, "This just won't do."

topic: sitting on the porch steps at twilight
lines: She wonders if the silence means it's too soon,
or if the world just paused for the moon.
Her cigarette curls into the smoke,
her breath catches once and she starts to choke.
I watch the video to get one small clue,
the host says it's magic—just try it, they do.
I fast-forward to see how the tape will roll,
maybe this time I'll finally hit my fun goal.
You have no clue where your bottle might be,
It vanished at work or maybe at sea.
You miss the cool weight of it in your hand,
But somehow today just keeps oddly bland.
She blends into the rush with smooth moves,
her rhythm fits the packed train's tight grooves.
The doors swing open like a rising tide,
she smiles and the space feels just wide.
You left the milk out till the top went cream,
I tried to save it but it soured my dream.
Now it sits there aching, close to spill,
I'll toss it soon but not with any will.

topic: a blanket tangled in the bed
lines: You kick the blanket off the mattress and floor,
it's a heap full of knots and old fabric lore.
You tug but it only gets tighter with twist,
and time slips away like a moment you missed.
You stare at the same cold processed meat,
it's been under plastic since this morning's heat.
You take a deep sigh and grab a white bread slice,
the syrup tastes like someone else's nice.
She always has this crisp, clean smell in her tone,
the kind that makes you feel she's already known.
The scent still lingers in your mind, it will float,
a subtle touch of disinfectant on her coat.
I bought these loaves with so much hope and grace,
now they rot in waste, the path my choices trace.
I stare into the bin where dreams have been,
and wonder if I was ever meant to begin.

topic: a man reading on a bench
lines: You sit outside where the sunlight is breeze,
your book's open, your phone long since keys.
You turn the pages slow, savor each flip,
the kind of calm that feels like a trip.
You mark the clock, dragging out the pace,
your mind checks out, finds other space.
The manager drones on about his talk,
like this was a classroom and we were all chalk.
I knocked the shaker off the edge with a dash,
it hit the tile but didn't make a crash.
The grains spread out like a tiny white mess,
I just laughed and called it a kitchen bless.
I stretch my arms against the strap to bend,
the only company this machine can lend.
I take a deep breath, feel the tension pull,
and hope grows heavy in my muscles full.
You reach for your wallet to hand them some cash,
but the register's stuck in a hard disk crash.
The printer won't feed the paper, won't roll,
and now you're still waiting—this delays the whole toll.
I wandered into this tourist trap downtown,
and immediately got a bitter frown.
Everything's plastic and marked way up to buy,
so I just bought a keychain and asked myself why.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: The key feels too loose, but it might still fits,
I turn it with care, fearing tiny bits.
The lock clicks—then silence, like an old ghost,
I wonder if answers lie deeper than coast.
You toss the plane with all your might and try,
It wobbles up as if the sky's a die.
For half a second, you thought it would go far,
But physics says, "You're not a bird—you're not a star."
You've finally made the move, big or small,
unpacking your life, re-arrange it all.
This is your moment, no turning back—make your mark,
the city's quiet now, but you're going to spark.
She gave the plane a quick little throw,
It caught the light from the room's warm glow.
It spiraled and twisted, way up it flew,
Like magic on wings for a moment's view.

topic: a receipt lost in the bag
lines: She paid in full cash at the checkout store,
she didn't ask for a single thing more.
She tossed the receipt into the paper bag,
now it's crumpled, unclaimed like a lost discount tag.
She turned on the shower but the water lacks flow,
she pokes it with shampoo to see if it might grow.
The bar slides down slowly, slipping off soap,
while she tries not to laugh at the whole absurd hope.
She bends the lamp cord into a tight arc,
her name written there with a sharpie mark.
It leans with a wobble, it leans with a sway,
but she calls it "vintage," puts it on full display.
She took up all the space with her bags and her grace,
and glared through narrowed eyes at your surprised face.
Her legs went into a full-on sprawl,
and now you're squished against the cold brick wall.
You hit replay but it skips to a pause,
your fingers now tapping like nervous claws.
The screen won't reveal what just went to hush,
you lean closer, the silence starts to rush.

topic: socks left in the laundry pile
lines: She flips through the pile like searching a stack,
a lone sock remains without its back.
She holds it up high, hopes for a matching spot,
but the dryer's been busy and life has gone hot.
You realize it's time to face your age,
the words on every text have blurred the page.
You hold your phone way too close to near,
but there's comfort in the old-world cheer.
You stow your tools where my sketchbook should go,
but you never ask if there's a rule you don't know.
Your phone is always humming—never off or still,
I'm waiting for your thumb to quit that endless drill.
I dropped an egg into the bowl and got a shell,
now it's all gooey mess in this breakfast hell.
I tried to flip it back but missed the flip,
the yolk slipped out, and I lost all hope of grip.
I check my closet for missing lace,
the trail leads straight to his secret place.
He gives me a look and a guilty bite,
I sigh and my shoeless fate is tonight.

topic: seeing a post from your childhood home
lines: I clicked the link and there was my old street,
same cracks in the sidewalk, same summer heat.
The front door's still missing its rusted key,
I wonder who lives there instead of me.
You call these "sensible" but lack style,
they're fine for sitting, not walking a while.
Each step feels like you've landed on floor,
I'd rather be barefoot than fight this whole war.
You still know the code to my private joke code,
we haven't been down that old memory road.
Your face lights up just like it did back then,
and for a moment, we're home again.
You step outside, the air feels like a chill,
the world is wrapped in fog and quiet still.
You try to leave a mark but only leave a trace,
your childhood once lived here, now lost in space.
Your bag won't balance and nothing will fit,
One strap snapped clean off, and now both feel it.
You loop your scarf twice and call it a pack,
but everyone stares when it digs in your back.
I watch my goldfish trace the same old tank,
their tiny fins have never yet let them bank
a life beyond these walls I can't ignore—
I'd open this glass if I had the right door.
Your dog tugs the leash with pure joy,
He thinks every walk is a toy.
You try to keep pace as he speeds off to run,
But you laugh anyway—it's a fine kind of fun.
I'll finish this tonight before the moon
climbs high where the unfinished ones are soon.
My pen runs out, the screen glows cold and blue,
but I'll stay up and get it done for you.
She cuts the slice down the middle, just half,
and watches your face as she tells you to laugh.
You bite off the corner, a little too fold,
but it's hot and fresh and worth every gold.
I stand outside where the light slipped through the key,
it's late and I owe them the last month's rent fee.
The door won't budge though I twist the worn-out lock,
maybe they tossed me from their tenant stock.
You stood there laughing as the rain came in,
Water trickled down from your hair to your skin.
I watched the puddles ruin your shoe's sole,
And pulled you close beneath the streetlamp's pole.
The sun slips through the leaves in golden glow,
I almost feel like I should remember so.
A breeze weaves patterns, light like spiders' thread,
I tilt my face and miss the peace I sought instead.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: You stare at the screen where the numbers still glow,
the quiet room holds a dreamless slow flow.
There's nothing to spend, but you check it again now,
the truth doesn't shock you—it just makes you bow.
You drift back to the endless summer days,
the way your laugh used to echo through the plays.
It comes sudden—the grassy, dusty smell,
but you can't quite remember what it all can tell.
You walk with your dog but they won't stay by your side,
They lurch toward the wind like a lost summer tide.
They sniff every fence, leave a mark on each bark,
while you dream of the fields left behind in that park.
I revived the old group chat thread,
maybe this time we'll go somewhere ahead.
Someone actually replied with something nice—
and no one rolled their eyes at my advice.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: You tap the app in the quiet of night,
Hoping the numbers will look good, not tight.
Your balance is still just a little too low,
But tomorrow's a day to save and to go.
She jiggled the doorknob with every key,
swore it was cursed, trapped like a tree.
The hallway fell silent, all tried to hush—
but no one moved fast to help her rush.
You take a sharp left where the street makes a turn,
your coffee cravings feel like a deep-down yearn.
A faded chalkboard peeks from between the sign,
the smell hits you hard—this place could be mine.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: You tried to capture a smile in a grin,
but the moment slipped out before it could begin.
The dog's mid-sneeze, your eye half open, the snap,
it's the kind of shot you'd swear happened in a nap.
I hit my alarm but it's stuck or just clock,
the morning feels old, like news I've read stock.
My thoughts feel too heavy, they're sore in my head,
and I wish that this day could be unmade, un-bled.
My cat lunges across the carpeted floor,
he attacks the dust bunny like a war.
He treats every lint pile like some grand toy,
I smile watching his childhood joy.
You watch the last swirl of your coffee's steam,
then sip the cold dregs without a gleam.
The numbers glow bright as they tick off the clock,
you whisper to no one, "This hit's too much rock."
The billboard promises wonders in claims,
all flash and no facts, just hot air in flames.
They sell you a dream that's not even real,
it's huckster magic, but still kind of surreal.
You press the button and it starts to play,
the needle cracks through time's slow decay.
The record spins but you're standing still,
lost in the echoes no one can fill.
I'm marking off days that feel far from today,
but in the margins there's plans for some play.
I leave each reminder scrawled in my mark,
a small hope lives in each tiny spark.
I love the sharp, spicy scent as I go,
my fingers all bent but I don't mind so.
These cloves are so small and feel kind of raw,
but somehow I think they obeyed the old law.
You can't stop the grin when they race through the din,
They laugh as they spin like they're made of thin tin.
You watch every move with soft, watchful eyes,
The world feels less heavy, you've struck gold in your prize.
You keep it right there as proof of your flaw,
it broke under pressure—some natural law.
Each morning you show off the white little chip,
and sip from the memory on its cold tip.
I still leave you space on this kitchen room,
though your spices long lost their perfume.
Time piles in slowly, a fine, gray dust,
leaving only memory, quiet and rust.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: The sitcom's laugh tone hits when they're too alone,
the moment is sour, their silence is stone.
A word slips from someone, a joke gets a slip,
the awkwardness trips them, the room starts to rip.
I tried to open it twice for my morning work,
the app just froze like a supermarket clerk.
It filled my phone screen with a glitchy blue,
and left me staring with no clue what to do.
He leaves a sticky note where the router is spot,
the password scrawled next to last week's pizza hot.
He thinks it's a genius way passwords should shows,
but nobody else here can read what he knows.
She twists the rusty lock to set the key,
the door swings open—it's been sealed for three.
The backpack inside still smells a bit old,
but her initials are etched in sunlight, bold.
I folded it fast and I launched it with throw,
it soared through the air and it whooshed off to go.
It kissed the far wall with a soft *thunk* and a stall,
then crashed on my desk where the coffee now sprawl.
I press each key like searching for a trace,
the "spacebar" reads "space" by now, not space.
The letters wore away—they couldn't hold their fade,
like hands that time has softened into jade.
They used to be everywhere, always on his trail,
now he walks down the stair alone without fail.
The group chats are quiet, the events are all done,
but he smiles anyway—still a friend to the sun.
The whisper returns in the wind's familiar sound,
I close my eyes and forget where I'm bound,
The field moves gently, still holding me sway,
But memory tugs me a little bit away.
I wandered past the gate and lost my zone,
my phone dead, my brain stuck on repeat and groan.
A tag dangled from a stranger's suitcase bag,
while mine sat behind, still trapped in airline lag.
You watched your bread turn to dark-brown flames,
we laughed so hard we forgot our names.
It's just a little bit of toast gone char,
you're sure it stole the show from a breakfast star.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: You blink at the mirror, sure it's a lie,
but that gray strand won't dye or die.
You try to ignore it, but can't help count,
and dread how the number continues to mount.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: They tagged your name in some random old post,
a meme or a typo, but you read it the most.
You smile at the memories from way back, so old,
and for a second, you feel like you're made of gold.
I read an old tweet at my usual noon,
remembering songs that used to be my tune.
There's something about the ink and coffee smell,
that makes me forget my phone in my lunchtime cell.
You think this is some relaxing little tale?
Just watch how fast your optimism turns pale.
That goldfish of yours is swimming in spin,
going nowhere fast in its tiny little tin.
She walks beneath the light's uncertain glow,
pretending she doesn't know how long it's been low.
She stops to watch the cables twist and bend,
as if they might send some signal she can mend.
My GPS lost the road and changed my route,
It does this every time I ignore doubt.
Now I'm driving through neighborhoods like a maze,
This should've taken five minutes, not days.
I watch you droop behind your dusty glass,
no one stops to let you be the last.
Your leaves curl gently like a dying sign,
forgotten in the corner, past the line.
I watched the morning rise in gray smoke,
the toaster was done for, it totally broke.
My coffee waited cold by the offgoing alarm,
but the smell still tastes like my grandma's old farm.
She starts walking up the broken ride,
arms swinging loose by her own two side.
There's nowhere this moment's headed but the end,
she hums a tune like an old friend.
She rode in a straight line across the rocky path,
certain this route would make perfect math.
When the tire hissed she gave it some blame,
but the nail was there before she even came.
She leaves the song on repeat on replay,
the silence broken when it drifts away.
Her fingers tap out the melody's keys,
she whispers "don't stop" though the track says please.
I found a bloodied old sock with a giant hole,
it's got more character than my whole damn soul.
I tried to patch it with some worn-out lace,
but now I avoid mirrors when it's on my face.
You squint at the glow of that cursed screen,
the blinking blue light feels like a machine.
Your eyelids are heavy, you can barely blink,
but coffee won't help if your soul's on a brink.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: You make a big deal out of trying to try,
it's just a small cake but you still let it sigh.
You puff with a look like you're saving your blow,
but only three go out—what a pathetic show.
You thought this would be an amazing deal,
but everything here's a rip-off, not a steal.
You left still confused about what you paid,
while questioning your judgment in that shade.
Said I'd capture the moment but left it all show,
lens left charging, forgotten and low.
