now we buy extra sprinkles just to store.
I scroll past a photo of the same little town,
where we laughed until the sunset made us frown.
The words feel too close, like an old movie near,
but now all I want is peace and some sad old cheer.
His voice cracks through traffic, sharp and tight,
he shouts until the heat won't let you bite.
"Fresh churros, dusted in that cinnamon gold!"
I bought one once—I haven't needed to be told.
She doesn't care if anyone sees her moves,
the music's loud, she's cooking and she grooves.
Flour dusts the floor like sugar on a pan,
this kitchen is her stage, and she's the dance man.
My energy's sunk to an all-time low,
I can't even sit still without wanting to go.
I picture a slice of that chocolate cake,
but I say "just one bite" — yeah, real mature, fake.
You swore you could read recipes without a lie,
but now you're winging it, telling yourself you'll try.
You text your mom for culinary aid,
she replies, "I'm busy," but I know she's been paid.
She waves from the porch and gives a loud call,
"Can't you hear my voice? I'm right here, I'm so tall!"
She's rung the bell, she has, trust me, she tried,
but the button might've decided to hide.
She wrote "Happy Birthday" in ink on a note,
and glued a few flowers next to her tote.
Each scribbled inside joke was carefully meant,
not something you'd buy, but a memory lent.
You clicked "buy" before the final deal,
but the clock ticks faster than your last feel.
The countdown hits zero, the price turns to gone,
you wait for the email that never comes by dawn.
You dream of that perfect first bite,
the cheese still clings far too tight.
You turn down the flame, adjust your plate,
and know the next meal's yours to fate.
She knew the original route by heart,
but the driver's cryptic shout left no chart.
She didn't panic, kept calm and stayed fast,
guiding us all home before we were passed.
They've been sitting there months, won't they just grow,
mushier than bread left out in the dough.
She claims she'll cook them, but they still don't thaw,
maybe the freezer's breaking some weird food law.
She never thought she'd be this far from where she grew,
but life slipped by her like the traffic through.
She counts the years off with a grin and a sigh,
"Where's my old self?" the mirror asks her back—goodbye.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: They think they're in some kind of fast race,
though nothing's at stake or the promised place.
They flap with all their ragged old wing,
but the crumbs are cursed, and the cold will sting.
His watch has been telling the same old lies,
He checks it twice when no one's in his eyes.
It never synced, but he won't fix the set,
Just laughs and says he loves this silly jet.
It's been in your backpack since lunchtime snack,
forgotten between your books and your stack.
The cheese sags down next to the stale meat,
the bread has a dent from the laptop's heat.

topic: a plate with two leftover bites
lines: You leave it on the counter, that half-eaten plate,
as if waiting for someone to come back late.
The crumbs have gone cold but the memory stays—
and the kitchen still hums with the ghost of your praise.
You pulled out your ten when they asked for cash,
but it didn't go far—not even a splash.
The cashier gave you a fake, tight-lipped grin,
and said, "Change's rare here—your budget gets thin."
It sniffs the air like it smells something rare,
and circles the stair without breaking its stare.
It doesn't want snacks or a chance to eat,
just time to feel safe, to still its fast beat.
Your laundry basket tumbles sideways and spills,
socks and tees forming soft little hills.
You sort by color, pattern, and hue,
humming a tune as you toss them all out to do.
They're still thinking about their role,
back at the office, they silently scroll.
Even in sleep, their mind clocks in for the task,
dreams whisper updates, no one needs to ask.
You check the bag's "best before" date,
just to microwave them onto your plate.
They never seem to fully thaw,
like some odd kitchen rule of thumb or law.
My cat did it again, I simply cannot see,
She leaps with delight, then runs totally free.
The bowl hits the tile and sends liquid to the floor,
I sigh as she purrs, there's no end to this chore.
She rearranged the room to hide every clue,
Even took down the poster from her childhood hue.
But the card slipped out when she moved the plate,
And there went her secret—ruined by fate.
I pour the milk too late, that's my crime,
The spoon sinks slow through the soft, soggy climb.
I stir the mess in this sad little bowl,
Yet something about it feels oddly like soul.
I left the soup on the stove in its pot,
where steam curls up like a memory spot.
I want to lift you into this moment and pour
the warmth back into the hollows and more.

topic: a dog barking at a mailman
lines: I see the mailman step off his post,
my dog gives him trouble for what seems like the most.
But it's just how he shows he is home on his guard,
his paws patrol rhythms, keeping this yard.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: Their shoulder rests lightly against your arm,
a quiet kind of magic, their offhand charm.
Your bodies trap the shared space, slow and heat,
your eyes don't blink—they just begin to meet.
I wait for someone else to feel alone,
to let the message linger on my phone.
My cursor hovers—what if I say why?
I close the app before I dare to reply.
You'd close your eyes and let the bus sway,
pretending it was a train from another day.
You missed how strangers would always hold,
an open seat when they saw someone old.
I see the plastic still caught in the flow,
it ripples like something pretending to glow.
The storm will come back to twist in the wind,
I can't ignore how it clings to my mind.
You told yourself this rep would be your final lift,
but the bar won't budge—it's mocking your last gift.
Your palms are raw with all that built-up sweat,
now every breath tastes like something you regret.
I overslept and missed the early call,
the bus was gone from around the mall.
I walked to school down the empty street,
and found her waiting where we used to meet.
I dipped the spoon too deep inside the jar,
now it's dragging like a tooth on a bar.
This honey is gloppy and making such mess,
but hey, the taste of sweet failure is success.
You wake up already with coffee in your grin,
the week feels lighter, it's off to a good begin.
You pour extra strong and let the morning brew,
the empty inbox is a small joy to view.
You scan the skyline for the perfect view,
A crowd blocks sunsets, no photo cue.
You move to the curb where the tour bus street
begins, only everything feels like a repeat.
I opened the box and saw what was due,
the stack was all mine and paid right on through.
A car repair, a trip, a last month's check—
I gave a satisfied nod and stretched my neck.
She blows on the puffball, sets her mind blew,
A hundred white dreams bloom into something new.
They spin through the air with a slow, soft sky,
Each seed holds a wish floating miles up so high.
You flipped through every drawer, but not the old shed,
you swore they were buried beneath your car's head.
A sliver of sun hit the floor from the beam,
and there they sat, clean, by the window's stream.
You saw your dog in someone else's tags,
and suddenly all the internet flags.
Now everyone knows what your morning's been in—
you're laughing, you're cringing, you're stuck with the spin.
My coffee tastes like regret and my head,
I mentally check out by half-past the dread.
The team call rolls on like a broken roll,
I pretend to nod when they mention the goal.

topic: seeing your mom's new profile pic
lines: You tap on the photo to see her full pose,
She's wearing something you've never seen clothes.
Her smile feels a little too sharp for a grin,
You wonder what's changed, but you keep it within.
You say the sky ignites with every flame,
as if October gave the season its acclaim.
The leaves still fall, but never reach the drift,
they scatter like a ruined birthday gift.
I see your smile in the photo with ring,
it was March, your dress looked like spring.
You said forever in every vow,
now I wear your gift but can't undo the bow.
I read your clumsy, crooked note,
sketched with care inside a flimsy tote.
Your handwriting still makes me ache,
even if I forgot your favorite cake.
I saw a rabbit sniffing through the park,
it blinked once slowly in the falling dark.
Its nose began to move like clockwork twitch,
I tried to mimic but ended up in ditch.

topic: tea leaves steeping in a cup
lines: I waited hours for this tea to brew.
My patience stretched thinner than the glue
that holds old thoughts together when you read
the future in your palm from what's been spread.
She watches the second hand chase the clock,
steam curls like a ghost from her paper knock.
There's silence in how she holds every pour,
and time slips through her cup like the floor.
His eyes are off road and his hands don't hold wheel,
he types with both thumbs as he tries to feel.
He misses the turnoff where the main street leads town,
and drifts into traffic, a text-crowned clown.
He swore that flimsy thing would hold its stand,
but the wind just laughed and threw him into the sand.
Now he's stranded here without a fight,
holding a broken shaft like a clenched-up kite.
The first-period bell rings like a death knell,
I sprint down the hall through certain hell.
My locker is locked, I lost the damn key,
this day already hates it's got to be me.
You watch the same familiar faces pass the street,
their routines a comfort you can only repeat.
A shadow moves—the world can't help but spot
the way your breath still tightens when you're almost caught.
He checks his phone like it's the final sight,
swears he's here for the breeze, not his flight.
He claims the weather is perfect for pitch,
but keeps adjusting his cap to avoid a twitch.
The screen fades out to a quiet blue,
you struggle to catch each name in view.
You want to remember each familiar face,
but the credits blur like time in a race.
The dog spins in tight circles so round,
it's clear it has never met gravity's ground.
It thinks its tail is a squirrel to chase,
while the neighbor just laughs at this funny place.
I left my old life behind with these keys,
a fresh start, or maybe a nervous disease.
I've mapped every route I could think was ahead,
but I still wake up trembling in my new bed.
She handed the cashier her ten and the split,
the machine returned a thank you and a bit.
There's nothing to spend but she needs a few,
so she buys gum just to have something to chew.
I tell myself I should not even try,
but my hand moves first to wipe their dry.
The moment lingers, each drop still to fall,
and I'm left here waiting to catch it all.

topic: a forgotten lunchbox on the floor
lines: You left your lunchbox where we used to spot
the dandelions growing up from the lot.
Time forgets to take the things that don't cry,
so there it rests, still warm by and by.
She took apart the remote with a careful start,
mapped out each wire with a makeshift chart.
Her hands steadied the world back to life,
no one told her she'd need a tiny knife.
She grabs the calendar, makes room in her space,
rewrites the same plans in a different chase.
Her to-do list dances, half-stripped from her mind,
she leaves the old notes dancing in the wind.
The ground was dead until this weird little spring,
they keep popping up, some strange green thing.
They seem to mock the frost and every sun,
I swear the earth is trying to be undone.
I watch the cart wheels spin slowly again,
the line moves like syrup, a sluggish chain.
A child's face lights up brighter than snow,
but no one will let her run off and go.
My backpack strap gave out with a loud snap,
Now my laptop jiggles loose in my lap.
I'll just stuff it all in my arms and pack,
But damn, it feels heavier on my back.
They pull your medical records off the chart,
you make sure every detail's in the right part.
You ask for the bill and you cross it off your check,
then book the next specialist—the newest tech.
She swings the shovel like it's forged from steel,
each strike a protest she can't quite feel.
The blade just slides into the same old hole,
where winter's cold and memory live in her soul.
The dog stands alert at the gate and its bark,
the evening is settling in deep and dark.
You hold the leash with a hand full of lead,
but your posture says this is something you need.
She spotted the sign: "20% off—what a deal!"
Her grin turned sly when she saw the discount was real.
She bought three pairs, each one different, each one flair,
and strutted out, proud as if through the air.

topic: sending a voice message that fails
lines: You tap record and prepare to send,
your face lit up for your old friend.
But the app says "Failed — connection glitch,"
so you laugh and turn off the voice switch.
Your hat decides it wants to go and fly,
It zips up high where the birds pass by.
You chase it down, but it won't behave—fail,
Its shadow leaves you gasping, hot, and trail.
Her laughter joins the sound of leaves around,
she walks without looking at the ground.
Each step she takes feels light, like falling through,
her smile suggests this walk's been set to true.
I let it sit just long enough to spread,
the perfect time, not rushed, not dead.
It drapes across my bread in soft, rich swirl,
I take a bite and feel like such a girl.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: The morning arrives with the quietest hush,
the world still asleep in the web's silver blush.
You count every droplet along the fine thread,
and hope begins to spread where it once stayed dead.
You raised your voice and made the bold claim,
your logic burned with a perfect flame.
You pointed out the crumb as your proof,
and left me speechless, high as a roof.
She watches the scooter tear down the street,
a blur of legs and speed, a wild feat.
Her hair hangs still, no gust, no wind,
just silence where the engine ran behind.
My fingers grow slick with the garlic's white juice,
I try my old trick—no gloves, fast and loose.
Now my palms sting, they feel completely raw,
I break the kitchen's unspoken hand-washing law.
You smooth out the creases from yesterday's maze,
the paper unfolds like a warm summer blaze.
Your fingers find roads that they've traced in their way,
each fold feels like magic, or maybe just play.
You jiggled the handle but still no key,
the lock groaned with rust and old debris.
You tested the doorframe for something to turn,
then laughed off the jam as a minor concern.
You waited out the drought's unrelenting heat,
until the sky performed its sudden feat.
Now every pebble drinks the falling drop,
and you admire the dust that bloomed as crop.
You stare at the hole in your fraying strip,
you worry you'll twist your ankle and slip.
You tie the last lace in a double knot lace,
but doubt keeps creeping into your pace.
He blames her for the smell, the messy bin,
she swears he's never known a clean-cut skin.
Her words bloom sharp as any thorned rose,
he reads his rules aloud like heavy prose.
The remote got thrown—no one's to blame,
But suddenly I'm local TV fame.
A livestream of my silent screams at the bar,
playing out on loop for every star.
The handle glints like steel, a touch too cold,
she mutters to herself, a story well told.
She jingles her keys, tries every key,
while frost listens in, a silent plea.
The clock drags on but you hold your start,
you're waiting for something good in your heart.
They announce a pause—finally a break!
You smile at the coffee and hope they'll bring cake.
She turns the living room into a cave,
Her siblings toss in more blankets by wave.
They tuck you inside, a cozy old bed,
"No monsters get in," they softly said.
You click again hoping it will let you try,
the screen still glares like it's watching you spy.
It asks for data but gives you no need,
and blocks your request in bold, red, indeed.
I never wanted our styles to clash,
so I match my jeans with your denim dash.
It wasn't part of my morning plan,
but now you're my favorite outfit fan.
I told you the puddle was deeper than deep,
Now my shoes look like they've been feeding sheep.
But my kids are laughing and tossing a sock,
They think I'm the biggest dumb idiotic rock.
She sniffed the room and said it felt too clean,
like plastic and bleach pretending to be green.
She left the sink running, hoping to find
something real hidden in there behind.
A bicycle zips down the crowded street,
its bell a melody I can't help but repeat.
She laughs and waves like she's putting on a cheer,
her joy somehow landing right where I'm sitting near.
She kept a bag of peas in the veggie drawer back,
said they were better than chips or any snack.
They sat there untouched, growing old with the frost,
now thawed and forgotten, the flavor's been lost.
I walked in craving the scent of the smell,
hungry eyes scanning every aisle they might sell.
The cracker aisle became my winding trail,
my willpower fading, pale, stale, and frail.
That single light glows with a quiet, small,
warmth that feels like an old friend's familiar call.
I blow it out fast, like a year we can't age,
frozen in time on this lonely little stage.
The sun slips down and paints the world in gold,
I watch its light fade as it slowly grows cold.
Children run home along the empty street,
I stay outside just for the evening's last heat.
I need work done but my cat picked this spot,
she's blocking my view and slowing me down a lot.
Her fur keys are mashed, my shortcuts all fur,
I type blindly now, my patience at a spur.
Your dog has a talent for sudden grab,
he'll scuttle off with a sock like a crab.
You follow his trail but no clues to pursue,
except your old Nikes now mended with glue.
She told herself she didn't really need
the vintage mug that blinked and hummed with feed.
A week later, it's still in her back,
collecting dust where the cat gave it the sack.
You thought learning words would solve the slang,
but every phrase brings a fresh new pang.
You ask for the time or a drink or a date,
and they just stare, so you awkwardly wait.
That plant in the corner still catches my eye,
it's been turning more yellow and ready to die.
It needs light, not this gloomy old shade,
and I won't watch it rot in this sorry parade.

topic: a receipt lost in the bag
lines: I stared at my wallet—no proof that I paid,
no stub from the register, no digital aid.
I flipped through the groceries but missed the old bag,
where the cashier tucked it inside like a flag.
She swipes to impress with that perfect beach show,
Each face glows brighter than the next on the row.
Her thumb keeps a rhythm it's hard not to scroll,
But this curated paradise never feels whole.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: You told me to snap a picture in one pose,
but you sneezed right into my camera's nose.
This shot's a total fail, there's nothing to do,
I'll wait till your face is still and maybe not blue.
She opened her phone to check the old app,
unaware she'd fall into this small trap.
A pop-up asked for a password or code,
and suddenly life was unfiltered and showed.
The sign screams "Buy three pairs—what a deal!"
I grab three and instantly feel
Each sock has a run or a tiny hole,
I wonder if the store sold my soul.
I always miss the bus and then I run,
pretending it's an adventure, not a gun.
My coworkers laugh—again I'm late,
like my life's just a punchline they debate.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: She tore open the bag like it was some grand waste,
the crunch loud enough to fit the taste.
She'd driven far to save a few cents paid,
now pretending this snack's her nutritional aid.
You wake again without having found your rest,
the clock still stuck against your bare chest.
The coffee's brewing but your head's still in your mind,
while quiet morning hums the same old wind.
A pigeon landed beside me in mid-air,
tilting its head, as if to say, "Don't you dare."
It blinked once, then snatched my fry from the bird,
not leaving a feather or a single word.
I stirred it slow from the back of the jar,
golden and thick like a syrupy star.
I licked the last drop from corner to spoon,
savoring sweetness beneath the full moon.
That app kept trying to pop up on your screen,
you quickly tapped **Stop**, you were not keen.
Without a single clue, it tried again,
now locked out from your view, it raised the flag in vain.
You call this thing a tuning fork, not a tool?
It's been collecting dust since high school.
It vibrates so weak, it's barely the way
a heartbeat should sound—just a slow decay.
She's been waiting weeks since the refund was due,
the email reads "next step is in your cue."
She checks her bank—still shows as unpaid,
she's typing a complaint in all-caps and shade.

topic: reading under the covers with a flashlight
lines: I turn another page in my parent's old cage,
the sheets are too hot and they always engage.
My flashlight cuts through the dark like a beam,
but I'll go blind soon from this paper-thin stream.
You watch the sky turn black and start to pour,
the kind of rain that whispers "there's more."
You check the road, slick and rising fast ahead,
but your feet keep moving, as the storm once said.
There they go, shoving ahead without a line,
ignoring the queue and the posted sign.
It's not a race for coffee or a race,
but they've claimed the front, just like that, a new place.
They met me here for coffee, dinner, or a date,
but spent the whole time swiping and debate.
Their eyes were glued to glass, no wink, no tease,
I wonder if they lied to be at ease.
You take out your wallet, full of small change,
The machine glows, but the look feels a bit strange.
You drop in the coins one by one into slot,
You beat the meter—you never forgot.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: She slipped a red hat with a spinning star
onto his head while she served the bar.
His paws tap out rhythms, precise as a gear,
the crowd lifts its voice when he starts to cheer.
It flutters like a ghost above the sky,
caught in the branches trying not to die.
I watch the wind try to pull it back to flow,
but roots hold tight where it's trapped below.
She leans into the wind, a warm, soft breeze,
as if it might cure the ache inside her disease.
She closes her eyes, lets the scent fill her head,
then sighs like this is where she should be instead.
She clicked too fast during her late-night spree,
It wasn't love, but discount code three.
Now the box sits there, she can't bring herself to keep,
The guilt runs deep for what she bought on a cheap.
She watches the receipt printer slowly roll,
each tick echoing like a distant toll.
Her fingers hover near its broken hand,
waiting for a slip she can't understand.
She gives the old stick one last desperate try,
it crumbles to dust, completely and dry.
The sticky note won't hold to the corner of page,
she throws it all away in a paper-tape rage.
I begged him for a snake, but he made a twist,
one loop, two loops, then a wiggle of wrist.
"Surprise!" said the guy who looked nothing like clown,
I blew it out slowly, then sat it back down.
She sips from a glass like she used to before,
the ritual calm as the office door.
Her mind wanders back to old rhythms, kind,
where water was joy, not something to find.
I wake up in need of another brew,
my coffee machine's stuck—what do I do?
My head starts to throb from the caffeine ache,
but I'll risk a sugar high if there's donut cake.
You stood on the dock, then on the boat deck,
you swore the app's glitchy schedule was bad tech.
Now stranded with no way to assign blame,
you turn your mishap into a bad pun game.
You kick the toaster and whisper, "Don't scream,"
but the smoke's already rising in a stream.
You chase the smell with coffee full of heat,
another Monday lost to breakfast defeat.
You mute the world but keep scrolling through the scream,
the next stream comes with more than you can seem.
You try to think but the outrage won't let you drown,
your phone becomes a throne where truth wears no crown.
She waves her phone like it's a golden card,
convincing herself she'll save every yard.
The total is lower than last week's fare,
and she breathes a sigh as the dashboard clears the air.
She bent to pick up a faded shell,
the waves whispered where her laughter once fell.
Her shadow stretched long as she stood to stand,
tracing the past in the shifting sand.
You watch the sky turn from blue to a glow,
the kind that makes your phone feel like throw.
The leaves dance in time with the fading shade,
and you wave at the clouds putting on a parade.
She left her jacket draped on the back of the coat,
a sticky hint by the bowl for the tote.
The softest wool caught the scent of the breeze,
still warm from where her hands held the keys.
Your station just fades out without a word,
you switch the dial but there's no voice or bird.
You swear it's the car, then blame the whole game—
this drive's too long for silence and shame.
I tied a thread to the jagged old hook,
the cat watched me go and I guess it took.
The paperclip's already at full bend,
but I cast it anyway, and we both pretend.
It blares like a war horn, gives me a shout,
I doubt I'll ever sleep past noon without.
I stumble off the bed and fall on the floor,
another day's mess I wish I could ignore.
The tag said "thirty" but now you're on sale,
the cashier shrugs when you tell your sad tale.
You argue about the final cost and tax,
she smirks as she dabs her fresh lip balm wax.
She flips through her pocket like searching a jar,
she drops every coin at the register bar.
A small part of her smiles—it used to fit,
now the jar's lighter, but so does her grit.
I reached for the handrail without fail,
now my palm looks so weird and so pale.
I tried to let go but I just couldn't slip,
it's like my hand decided I should take a trip.
My goldfish stares at me from his glass tank,
thinking he's rich with all this flakey bank.
He opens wide—ready to make a leap,
the bag's now empty, no food left to beep.
You watch the rain-soaked field, silent and goal-bound,
The pitch looks like mud, dark and coal-stained ground.
Your team's hope feels already away,
The game is a struggle, every play a sway.
I texted "see you soon" then rushed to meet,
my shoes untied, my socks both on the wrong feet.
They asked how long the traffic would delay,
I never did explain it wasn't worth the say.
It runs in a circle at breakneck pace,
but never gets far from that tiny space.
Its little paws twitch through the spokes of fur,
like some small motor with no end in purr.
She watches the river lie quiet and still,
her thoughts like a swallowed and bitter pill.
The water mirrors her tired, worn face,
but the sky's blue is a place she can't chase.
She steps outside where the warm breeze agrees,
the wind chimes sing with their metal keys.
The sound drifts out, almost too soft to be heard,
but it stirs her smile without being stirred.
She walks her own rhythm, not matching your pace,
she claims her space like a calm in the race.
Her stride says "I'm late," but her head says "in mind,"
you stay behind, like she's meant to be kind.
You trace the soft, slow shifting of form,
the gray shapes curl like something to warm.
The sky is empty but peaceful above,
and quiet as when we first fell in love.
I type each word onto my old, bent keys,
the cracks are deep but not a serious disease.
I've typed each letter without much thought,
and never had a reason to have them bought.

topic: a kite stuck in a tree
lines: The kite still sticks where it flew last spring,
a patch of sky tangled up in old string.
We tried to shout it down with a stick and pull,
but the tree just laughed in its mossy full.

topic: paying a fine at the window
lines: I hand them the check with a polite note,
"The judge said this should be your quote."
They shrug and say, "We only take cash,"
so I pay twice, turning to ash.
You freeze mid-bite, a slow-mo kind of pause,
the sauce is still clinging in tempting cause.
You tilt your head just enough for a grin,
you feel some magic stirring deep within.
You stand on the bathroom floor with your bare feet,
proud of the chill the morning air won't treat.
You claim it's a feature, something cool and your own,
not a draft or a crack, just cold tile and bone.
I drew a castle where my toys are crowned,
the cat knocked it down and left it found.
The crayons made a rainbow-colored mess,
but somehow looking at it feels like a bless.
The milk passed its date, but no one was late,
it sat in the fridge like a quiet debate.
You used it to make a banana bread bake,
and called it your best little kitchen mistake.
They crouch behind a dusty shelf or book,
pretending they weren't the one who took.
Their hands are still, like they know how to wait,
as if silence might keep them from the gate.
She taped a post-it note to make it bright,
with stars and emojis in hot pink light.
It reads, "You're doing great, there's time my way,"
a daily pick-me-up for her good today.
That balloon was once bright, bold, and blue,
you laughed as we chased it running after you.
Now it's still aloft, but it can't be free—
the string is wrapped around your head and me.
She checks her phone for the next right turn,
but the app only knows how to yearn.
The bus ignores every route on the map,
and leaves her stranded in a time gap.
I watch the empty seat beside the aisle,
the movie hums quietly for a while.
The sun outside begins to slowly fade,
and I pretend this silence wasn't made.
I gaze into my bottle's sad, half-empty sight,
I squeeze it once to make the cap go tight.
"It's only halfway down," I tell my thirsty lie,
but I'm already dreaming of a drink up high.
She scribbles secrets in a cipher she calls code,
half hoping you'll decode it as some distant ode.
She shades each word but leaves no other lines,
just faintest whispers where the hope turns to signs.
You toss out treats but she gives no clue,
you dance and sing, you even do TikTok to.
You call her by name but she's got her own game,
the queen of the couch and your lonely old frame.
She reads the message but never makes a post,
the silence grows thick in the digital host.
It's not in her plans or her daily routine,
she leaves it all behind, pulls out of the scene.
You stare at the list where you made your one check,
then sigh as your shoulders roll off your neck.
You remember how easy things felt that way,
before today turned into gray.
He rides by, the bell a ghost from my past,
moving fast, his shadow stretching vast.
I don't call out—I've said nothing at all,
just watched time build its quiet, solid wall.
The screen glows soft with no real fight or light,
another night unwound in endless scroll and slight.
Time slips away, the hours blur the past,
while lives flash by—too bright, too vast.
She stops to check her shadow's new spot,
the sun throws too much light in this lot.
The glare just keeps getting worse as it grows,
but she stands there anyway, pretending she knows.
I wake up with total exam-day dread,
my clothes are a mess, they're still half-spread.
One sock's blue, one's pink — I'll take full blame,
this isn't the look for student of the year fame.
They dream in a room where the summer heat
hangs heavy, and breaths repeat through the sheet.
They toss but it's not how they find better sleep,
it's the body that can't quite keep calm while they weep.
You twist and you tug but the handle won't spin,
your keys jingle loud as they fall to the din.
You shout for a "key," but nobody's near,
the lock laughs at you with a click and a sneer.
The window won't budge—still sealed tight from last wind,
I wave at the world rushing fast as I'm behind.
We passed the same trees we used to call the scene,
but now they don't whisper the songs they once would mean.
My bike lock's as tight as a closed fist,
A green light flashes—my moment to twist.
I fumble around but can't find the key,
My bag's full of keys, none of them agree.
My spouse says this isn't a dance, it's surreal,
I'm doing the chicken while burning the meal.
One step goes left and I step on the wrong,
I'll never be Beyoncé… but I'll dance all night long.
You leave your list somewhere you can't find,
tucked between your coat pockets or behind.
We'll buy the basics first, like milk and bread,
then wander home, your arms my soft spread.
They vanish behind the old oaks and trees,
a whisper of motion against the breeze.
The laughter still echoes, the game still calls,
but silence grows thick where the sound should walls.
The soup is steaming, but the heat is switched off,
it bubbles loud enough to make me cough.
I ladle it carefully into my bowl,
pretending it's something that warms my soul.

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: It just keeps coming, that sweat starts to pour,
drips down your neck and lands on the floor.
You try to think of something cool to mind,
but your brain's just a slow, sticky kind.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: He posted the joke, the silence hit the floor,
some laughed but most just rolled their eyes and tore.
He's chasing online clout and viral fame,
though no one will remember his face or name.
The clock says 2 a.m., you type so late,
reconsider every word you debate.
You make yourself coffee while time begins to brew,
your screen glows warm, this chaos is your view.
The wind came softly and it all blew,
the seeds that meant to stay now fly from you.
They drift up high, a wish for the sky,
and I let them go with a quiet goodbye.
She left the suitcase open right where it lay,
expecting dust, but found the cat that day.
Her keys are buried under soft gray fur,
and time has paused as the world won't stir.

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: You take a new picture, a quiet frame,
the light outside shifts from gold to flame.
You laugh as you smooth out your soft, loose pose,
then post it where no one sees but the snows.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: That thing sits way too far back on his head, tight,
I told him no tricks, but he's begging for a bite.
The hat's got glitter still stuck in his fur,
I regret this birthday and every spur.
You found a paperclip left slightly bend,
you twisted it just enough to mend.
You tied your shoelace to make a quick hook,
and landed a minnow you never even took.
She searches your face for a hidden clue,
afraid you've been lying since the day you grew.
She tries to read thoughts, can't seem to pick
the signal from noise where your truth might stick.
She presses the key but nothing shows up on screen,
Last week's coffee seeped between the keys unseen.
The shift key now sticks and gets stuck in jam,
She types in all caps and just grumbles "Ugh, am."
You remember breakfasts fresh as morning's first dawn,
now the milk sours where the cereal is gone.
You stare into the empty space of the bowl,
wondering if time leaves things broken or whole.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: You spot one strand and squint at the sight,
tug your hair into a too-neat tight.
You laugh at the irony of this age—
you're still a kid, just playing a new stage.
A single dark drop betrayed the white shirt's top,
he tossed it with flair into a laundry crop.
It's evidence now of a morning's abrupt proof—
but hey, stains fade out, and he's still a goof.
She tugs the leash like she's meant to lead,
her tail straight up, her confidence in her head.
I laugh as she tries to break free from the tie,
but not too hard—I wouldn't want her to cry.
The river moves smooth, and I try to flow,
calm as the water's glassy glow.
My thoughts still buzz, but not so loud in my mind,
soft as the hush where the sky meets the wind.
She soars above treetops close to the sky,
Her laughter echoes as she swings so high.
Her toes barely touch the ground for her feet,
The neighbors all watch from their quiet street.
The app says "access" but won't let me ask,
so I just ignore it and move on to task.
A pop-up appears when I tap or I click,
but I've learned the best policy's to not get trick.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: You clip a coupon for a "limited-time deal,"
then count the change as if it's a full-fledged meal.
The chip is crumbled, the glue still feels stale,
the discount was sweet—but the snack's a total fail.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: I spotted a flash from beneath the rocks' gleam,
it caught my eye where the water ran stream.
I held it up, rubbed off the creek's old cold,
and wondered if this was real or just gold.
She catches the morning's soft silver light,
tracing the shape of a puffball white.
Her hand moves steady and still in the draw,
not a single shadow without its flaw.
I watched you take a slow and quiet sip,
the coffee seeped down your wrist like a drip.
You gripped my hand as the moment felt tight,
we laughed in the mess of this warm little night.
I swear this toaster committed a crime,
it charred my bread every morning chime.
Now I stare at each slice, hoping it won't go black,
but breakfast peace always takes a back.

topic: checking bank app late at night
lines: I tap the app, the blue light fills my screen,
some charge appears I never would have seen.
They've taken another monthly maintenance fee,
and I don't remember agreeing to this key.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: You asked for a quick shot, no need for a pose,
but now every button and wrinkle shows.
It's not my fault, nor the phone's bad aim,
why did you ask me to take that damn frame?
It's been six minutes since it turned green,
This traffic light is a broken machine.
Cars start to mutter, they all want to wait,
But no one gets through in this red-lit state.
You say you need only popcorn to crave,
but you're lost in a snack pile, too numb to wave.
The plot gets lost as you sink into deep,
where the credits roll just before you fall asleep.
She kicks her shoes up, a lazy, cool pose,
her socks wrinkled and bunching in those.
One foot dangles, just idly it swings,
a statement without effort, the boldest of things.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: I thought I could still keep them all well and hide,
but they peek through my scalp from the roots inside.
They don't cluster just here at my old man's crown—
now they're spreading across like a silver town.
Your thumbs move faster than the wheel,
a thousand distractions it won't reveal.
You pause just long enough to look now,
but the road doesn't seem to want to allow.
That stranger reeks of some weird old-lady scent,
I debate opening a window to vent.
This car was supposed to be quick, not a ride,
I'm squirming alone on the passenger side.
I asked for one degree, not the whole room,
you waved the remote like a messy old broom.
We keep turning it down for a colder chill,
but neither of us wins this small, cold will.
You pause your lunch to read the screen's new view,
the story feels a little more than true.
The comments spiral into some old thread,
and time dissolves with nothing left but bread.
You try to read the strange new world through his tone,
but joy or worry—both are left unknown.
His head gives every silent signal, clue,
to something wonderful about to be new.

topic: missing a chorus in a song
lines: Your phone missed a beat where the chorus should skip,
I imagine you dancing through life as you trip.
You hit pause instead of letting it play,
and now that part's lost, far out of the way.
I used to walk here when the moss still grew,
I'd trace my initials deep into the stone through.
Now each soft step feels like my old self's tread,
though no one hears what I try to be said.
I swear the rain's trying to send me a code,
like some wet bard reciting an ode.
It won't stop drumming out this midnight beat,
I'm ready to prop the sky with my feet.
She stares at the pot like it's the rising moon,
stirs it again with her old dented spoon.
She says this new brand isn't even close to blend,
just bitter and weak by her midday's end.
You think you're hidden where no one will spot,
but your face sticks out from the clay garden pot.
You dart behind an old maple tree,
only to trip on the mailbox's key.
I opened the box with my heart full of mail,
the stack makes me pause and feel pretty pale.
Each envelope hisses with numbers and due,
I sigh like a pro, but there's nothing new.

topic: crackling fireplace on a winter night
lines: She curls beside the fire's warmest nest,
sipping cocoa, the clear comfort of her best.
Her cheeks turn pink from the wood's slow glow,
the storm howls loud, she stays perfectly though.
You inch toward the open sliding door,
some kid's headphones still blare and soar.
You lean against the only available rest,
but someone bumps your arm and hits your chest.
She holds the last gift from her youngest child,
the string winds tight through her curls, so wild.
Her fingers trace loops that could never be free,
the knot feels close, but won't let go of me.
I swing my shovel at this cursed pitch,
the blade just bounces off in a twitch.
My hands are numb like black lumps of coal,
this dirt won't move without breaking my soul.
The river mirrors the cloudless blue,
She sits alone, taking in the view.
Her eyes scan the horizon, open and wide,
but she can't escape the truth she won't hide.
You keep swiping down that endless feed,
your eyelids feel like they might bleed.
The glow from your screen outshines the moon,
now you're crying over some sad cartoon.
She stops just long enough to watch it stay,
the bulb blinking slow in its lonely display.
There's comfort in how the light still tries to glow,
though her shadow dances far from it now, below.
You check the fridge—no milk, the carton's dry,
but the morning's bright and the clouds are high.
You'll skip the cereal, no need to pour,
there's toast and jam if you want a little more.
She laughed when I tried to take half the cut,
said I had the competitive foodie gut.
We flipped a coin for the last cheesy one,
now I'm licking the box clean—call it *done*.
They packed enough clothes to change into a suit,
then cursed the suitcase, calling it a brute.
A sign above them read "This is your fate,"
as zippers groaned under the heavy weight.

topic: a book left open on the nightstand
lines: She leaves her book propped halfway up,
as if the characters still need their sup.
Moonlight hits the page and gives it a glow,
making it feel like it happened not long ago.
She sways softly to the familiar tune,
as if every note were a memory rune.
Her tears fall quiet, her gaze stays in eyes,
where the truth of the song hides in plain lies.
You ask for some space but there's none to erase,
you're squished in this lecture hall seat and place.
Your neighbor's arm jiggles your chair from the row,
your face lights up only when screens start to glow.
The kitchen fills up with a rising smoke,
you wave it off but you can't hide the cloak
of shame from your hands as you slowly pour
the coffee black, trying to drink away the chore.
My phone greets strangers but never sees me,
it locks me out every time I use my key.
The camera just stares, no good at the scan,
I swipe past the AI like a regular man.
The sky is a canvas you can't quite stretch,
the sun dips down to hide and fetch.
The trees catch fire in that fading flame,
while shadows play their slow game.

topic: a video call with a frozen screen
lines: You stare at your frozen face on the screen,
the dog walks across the frame, unseen.
Your video glitches like a broken feed,
but you laugh anyway—it's amusing, indeed.
Their eyes have that same tired blue glow,
they'll scroll until their batteries run low.
They say they're just checking a quick reply,
but we all know it's just another *try*.
You watch them go full speed down the slide,
then climb up screaming from your side.
They tumble into each other—full crash,
but just as fast, they're off chasing a flash.
She slows her pace to fix the left shoe trail,
her breath a whisper, soft and slightly frail.
Her hands are steady tying every lace,
but tears fall quiet on her windblown face.
I set my own rhythm, no need to keep pace,
I watch the world move from a higher space.
Clouds roll like followers in lazy drift,
But I gave them their motion—it's mine to gift.
She stares at the receipt, her face in her hands,
unsure if she paid at the counter or the stands.
The store says returns need proof you were there,
but the policy's vague — the whole thing's a snare.
You step outside where the frost still holds the glow,
The grass is silver beneath the early snow.
Your breath becomes words but they vanish from thought,
A memory lingers you can't quite have sought.

topic: losing your wallet at the mall
lines: She swore she left her wallet inside the mall,
then tried to retrace every corner and call.
She checked her pockets for some emergency cash,
but found only lint and a half-eaten stash.
You try to sleep but your legs won't stay,
they're buzzing like something's wrong today.
You sip chamomile, but it won't take,
so you get up and shake them awake.
I send a quick note when I'm running late,
and watch the clock tick while they wait.
We've all been there, we know the grace
of seeing your name appear on their face.
You stare at the cake, it looks sad in its cage,
the paper says "Happy 50th Birthday, Sage."
One candle stands tall in a sea that's gone lone,
you blow—but your wish hits the wall without tone.

topic: waiting for the bus in rain
lines: The clouds are weeping, the sky begins to pour,
You stare at the bus stop, not the open door.
A child skips by with a leap and a skip,
You smile, knowing today won't be a trip.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: I snap the sky as if it's some kind of fire,
chasing likes like they're my truest desire.
The golden light looks soft, but it's so bright,
the kind of dawn that feels like it might fight.
They left the sandwich in the bag, not the trash,
crumbs spilling out like a greasy splash.
It's been their lunch, their snack, their after-school punch,
now just a badge of stubborn, half-eaten lunch.
You never said a word, but it sure was a thought,
like you'd planned it ahead or maybe just bought.
We're not trying too hard to look like we seem,
but somehow it feels like a match made in dream.
I was caught off guard when the sky let it fall,
no umbrella, no warning, just sudden and tall.
My socks cling to my skin, a cold, silent pain,
I wish I could pour out this water and drain.

topic: baking with flour on the floor
lines: I wanted a cake but I made a big cake,
I spilled every bag now it's all one mistake.
I sweep up the mess but there's still a spot,
so I paint it white—now it's a whole new lot.
I saw them pop up fresh from the spring,
soft and fleshy, like a strange new thing.
They waited quietly through the cold, dark dawn,
now rising bold where the soil was once gone.
She pounces again at the same old rug,
where time and the vacuum have both dug.
Each leap feels like childhood, small and deep,
she bats at the past piled on the heap.
The bell starts to ring, fast as a chase,
someone's trying to pass me in this place.
I glance over my shoulder—no one's behind,
just my heartbeat, loud and unkind.
They pause again for the exact same scene,
rewinding the tape on this broken machine.
They swear they're here to relive some lost truth,
not admit they've still got no clue about youth.

topic: seeing a post from your childhood home
lines: You paused when the old house appeared on the screen,
the lawn still looked bright, almost too green.
The window frame tilted in the view,
but your smile said this was the real thing, true.

topic: posting a sunrise with no words
lines: She snaps a picture of the pink-tinted wave,
then hesitates, not feeling quite so brave.
The caption reads just "Post to Instagram post,"
as if the sunrise cares how far she's coast.
You check your phone—just one lonely bar,
your hope's a distant satellite star.
The stream keeps stalling, the download's a crawl,
you scream into silence, but no one can call.
The chicken is cold and the smell starts to meat,
the stove's still off, there's no steam, no heat.
She picks at the leftovers now grey on her plate,
while the dog looks up, knowing this is their fate.
She writes a message that feels so bright,
the kind that turns a stale chat into sight.
She keeps the conversation from becoming thread,
her optimism pulling the group ahead.
The handle gave way in your hand—it just split,
You tried to hold tight, but the plastic didn't fit.
Raindrops fall through a weak and old seam,
Still, you carry it like some half-forgotten dream.
You swear the room feels colder than a snowstorm's chill,
I check the vents—we're fine, but you still want to fill
the silence with your sighs and turning it down,
as if frost would form at your icy little crown.
His taxi's got no taillights, no front shine,
just a flickering "For Hire" sign.
He rolls through the traffic, ignores every code,
but somehow still knows every back road.

topic: steaming coffee in a blue mug
lines: She lifts the warm mug to check the lid,
her quiet escape from the noise of the kid.
The steam still rises from its last brew,
she sips as the morning comes into view.
She carries the scene with every frame,
Critics are whispering early acclaim.
Her face says more than any written grace,
The crowd gives her silence — endless space.

topic: checking if you have enough for gas
lines: I calculate how far I've got left in a mile,
the tank taunts me with that hopeful smile.
I tap my card, pray there's still a bit of cash,
the pump beeps twice—just a splash, not a crash.
I thought I saw a twitch behind the spot,
but only my shadow met the clay pot.
A thump came next—a sudden hop—
the lid flew off like a guilty crop.
You tried to pay with crumpled-up cash,
the register gave a beep and a clash.
It spat out half a coffee, maybe some beans,
but the printer's still frozen behind the screens.
The sky began to spit, then pour, then rain,
So I leaned back where the dryness would remain.
This corner of the roof seems drier than the spot,
But now my sleeve is wet—I really should have got.
I dream of meetings far too deep,
my coffee cold and my head still asleep.
They hand me slides without a task,
then frown when I forget to ask.
I used to grow lettuce in my grandmother's yard,
now a rabbit keeps watch like a green-thumbed guard.
It nibbles and hops with a quiet crunch,
and steals what I grew for my noon-day lunch.
He checks his safety gear before the job zone,
the crane above lets out a heavy groan.
His boots dig deep into the muddy ground,
but he's still walking the edge of being bound.
You let the morning in before the sun,
brewed coffee black, got your shower all done.
You silenced the alarm without the clock,
and rolled out of bed like you'd never rock.
You rub your eye, but it's still burning bright,
another blue lie from your phone at night.
The glare won't burn out, it keeps right on,
you want to turn off, but stay until dawn.
I read the sign: "All socks are half off the tag,"
but every sock left is the same dull gray bag.
I settle for one mismatched pair, just to buy,
and leave with a huff and a sour gray sigh.
Their eyes get dry and red from too much screen,
They blink like something out of a strange machine.
They pinch the bridge and gently start to rub,
I'm by their side, a comfort near their hub.
I said we should've baked this in a cooler try,
now the frosting's a river, everything feels dry.
I can't look at the mess on my own sweet face,
it's a cake, but where's the grace in this disgrace?
You stare at the dog as he gives you a look,
like you're some strange chapter he needs to book.
He tilts his head—clearly judging your why,
I swear if he asks I'll just roll my eyes and sigh.
I hold my breath as it snaps open mid-fall,
the plastic screeches like a wounded mall.
I clutch the frame tight to keep from a shake,
but fear it'll collapse and twist in half to break.
She scrolls through the world with a screen too bright,
but knows the last drop won't last her all night.
She'll plug it in soon, or just stay behind,
where the glow of her phone turns everything kind.
You gave the coast a once-over with your eye,
Then tiptoed toward the treat you knew you'd try.
The jar was wide open, no need to jar,
You grabbed a cookie like a snack-time star.
He wears his safety gear at every site,
The brim's cracked from the summer light.
A faded tag inside holds his old name,
No headlines, just sweat, and no acclaim.
You know what I'm thinking without a single thought,
and tell me I'm wrong when I've just said that I bought
a gift you don't want, but I still hope you'll say
today was worth it even if it didn't pay.
I watched the river mirror nothing but still,
ripples from clouds drifting down to fill.
The trees reached out where the light used to bend,
and I tried to fix something no water could mend.
The credits roll and we're still on the screen,
some montage of stars, a happy machine.
We stomp and we cheer with a wave so loud,
of clapping too late, but we do it proud.
My cat licks the wall but gives me no clue,
A streak down the drywall, now it's gone too.
She says she knows better than to just sit still,
But I miss the days when she'd lie here and chill.
There's your pink lipstick mark on my favorite spot,
I pretend it's a badge from our child's hot tot.
You left it last morning, still smudged is the kiss,
and now every sip just reminds me of this.
The rain came sideways, so we played it down,
mud caked our cleats from ankle to crown.
We laughed in huddles, lithe and full of feel,
the clock ticked on as car tires squealed and wheel.
One sock still holds the faded blue,
while its mate now lives inside your shoe.
They've lost half their thread and their matching pair,
but you tuck them back with care.
You sip the steam from your trembling cup of heat,
the same old thoughts just repeat, no retreat.
Your fingers tap a rhythm, not quite a shake,
but every pause feels like another mistake.
You stare into the gurgle, your soul down the drain,
the sink overflows like a monsoon's bad rain.
You curse the day you let hair clog this stop,
now you're stuck here, gripping a plunger like a prop.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: The key slips in where it hasn't been in years, [lock]
and you feel a jolt worse than any shock. [shock]
Inside, the hinges are heavy with rust, [rust]
and the air tastes like time and old dust. [dust]
She saw the exit and knew it was ahead,
but the tank said "empty" and she took the lead.
She found the station where she'd stop to fill,
though she swore she wouldn't—and still she will.
A delivery scooter zips down the street,
wind in its handlebars, dancing to the beat.
It bends like a river through the morning flow,
and vanishes, leaving only light to glow.
You have no clue why this bird keeps in view,
it zipped across the room where it never flew.
It hits the window again—same loud bang,
probably just mad your picture still hang.
You used to chase the tide along the shore,
pretending waves would somehow help you restore.
The salt stuck to your skin, like memories in brine,
still tugging at your ankles as you cross that line.
I taught this map to fold itself with bold,
its creases once were stiff from being old.
Now it moves like muscle, precise and smart,
a paper origami, my pride and chart.
She can't seem to find the right sock or pair,
she leaves the one dangling from the chair.
The other lies crumpled where she left it on floor,
last week she laughed at the colors she wore.
They leave socks and shirts piled half on the floor,
never crossing their mind that it's a chore.
Blankets twist around their legs like a mind,
tangled, chaotic, and completely un-wind.
They always squeeze from the very tip,
ignoring the flattening of the grip.
One day the tube will have nothing left but the ends,
and they'll toss it out, no more mint-scented friends.
The lake lies still beneath this quiet shine,
I own this peace that reflects it all mine.
A single ripple dares to rise and wave,
but I stand unmoved, too calm to brave.
I stare into the void of my phone's dark,
but every meme feels like an odd remark.
My thumbs won't stop scrolling through the screen,
I swear this is not my late-night routine.
She left a bag of peas to rot in the waste,
claiming they'd lost all flavor, dead and taste.
The pod was open, lid barely held on loose,
now thawed and squishy, there's zero chance of use.
You watch the sky turn to a quiet glow,
the rime on the trees is a fresh new snow.
You snap a photo the light won't take,
the silence stays whole, no echo to break.
The bathroom door is jammed—no way to lock,
I've learned to live with this by now, no shock.
I text my roommate, begging them to call,
they'll come to fix it when the ceiling caves in tall.
I watched the game get swallowed by the field,
the players slogging, clearly not to yield.
The crowd tried hard to muster up a cheer,
but nobody could tell which team was clear.
You boost over the bouncer and the gate,
depending on luck and sheer fate.
The ticket is lost, but your smile feels fake,
so you hide in the crowd, trying not to break.
You listen for that perfect fat crackle,
Each slice sizzles—no need to tackle.
Golden edges curl to a deep, crisp brown,
You serve it up like a chef's own crown.
He's been standing there for an hour or two,
still no sign of movement—no luck, no cue.
The leash is loose, but he's all tugging and hope,
while time just slugs along, full of no scope.
You watch the horizon fade to blue,
the air feels heavy, tense, and too.
The sky cracks open with a silver cry,
and all your warm plans begin to die.
I told you I'm bad at the tissues, I tried,
you laughed but then really, truly cried.
Your tear-streaked face is a mess now, I see,
but I'll clean it up, just don't blame me.

I brag about symptoms as if they were a claim,
my sniffles roar loud like a campfire's flame.
She stared at the photo where his finger wore ring,
the flowers from that day still seemed to be spring.
Her eyes skipped to her own faded white dress,
and wondered if fate was some cruel twist of stress.
The TV suddenly roars out of the burst,
your eardrums are panicking from the worst.
You fumble the side of the box for the knob,
afraid someone's home to hear you or rob.
You tap on the photo of waves and the beach,
someone tagged you in a funny old speech.
The memories scroll but your smile stays ahead,
you stitch up the gaps, there's still time to mend the thread.
She left her socks stacked in a messy pile,
unsure if this crime has a pattern or style.
He buries the evidence—socks wrapped as gift—
then brings them back after a guilty little lift.
She sees the red light blink near the empty tank,
and counts her cash for a gas station bank.
Every drop now costs more than the last mile,
but she keeps calm — this is her survival style.
I noticed a glistening sticky spot,
it seems a dropped gum left this plot.
I've walked around it thrice with slow wear,
but still I step in it and feel despair.
You reach for the check with your free hand,
saying we'll split it fifty-fifty, your grand
plan. I nod, trying not to let the doubt
creep in, wondering if this changes things about.
His fingers dance on the six tight strings,
he strums all the feelings and daily things.
The crowd taps along to his easygoing beat,
he ends with a grin and begins to repeat.
Her shoulders groan from the weight of her back,
a moving library in every stack.
She walks like a ship with too much to bear,
but won't let the world know she even has care.
She swears she sent it to her manager, the boss,
but somehow every screen shows up a loss.
We wait for reactions, a laugh or a win,
the only reply is cringe posted within.
My sneaker's now got a brand-new hole,
the rabbit took one long, soft bite and stole.
I can still hear that quiet chew,
from my desk where I stare into view.
A gentle chill slips through the door like a breeze,
It paints my face with a frosty freeze.
I read it as a sign from the sky, so kind,
To clear my thoughts and calm my mind.
She clicks the "Add to Cart" button for yet more,
but the timer says "Sale Ends Soon—Last store."
Her wallet's too light for the credit card cash,
so she sighs and leaves her cart in the trash.
The band is stretched to a dangerous tight,
my biceps scream in silent defiance, a fight.
I force my arms to move beyond their bend,
this pain will be worth it when I finally mend.
I watched it drift in your old fish tank,
slow circles where your childhood had sank.
It swam toward the top like the sky was below,
and I wondered aloud, "Why must it be so?"

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: A child is wailing in the supermarket scene,
Their mother texts from a frozen yogurt machine.
She's scanning online reviews, all about the fruit,
While everyone else avoids this unhappy brute.
I searched my room for missing lecture pages,
but every drawer just held old rages.
There's not a single lead or hint or clue,
just coffee rings and glue from last week's mess too.
Her phone buzzes loud with an unknown call,
The dorm room is silent, the night light glows pall.
She freezes mid-breath, her heart starts to race,
A missed call at midnight feels like something to trace.
I don't believe in the sock matching rule,
I toss both in and never check the pool.
If someone asks if they match, I have no clue,
but I swear the left foot sock's a better hue.
You eye the box, then you stare at the plate,
should you raid the fridge or engage in a debate?
Is it worth the guilt or the melting cheese,
or will you pretend there's some leftover ease?
You left the cart key beneath the front door,
the way you would back when you had no care for
the lock or the time that you'd left it to rust,
and now it sits there, forgotten with dust.
The phone rings like a broken alarm bell,
but you're too wired to let sleep win or hell.
It's probably your ex or your mom's new flame,
but midnight calls are always the same old game.
She's never had a single matching pair,
they're strewn across the bedroom floor and stair.
To her, this chaos is an outfit's art,
she calls it intentional—very smart.
The smell of burnt toast drifts through morning smoke,
the hotel kitchen wakes her up half-woke.
She makes two slices just to get the bread,
but ends up cooking breakfast in her head.
You open the fridge and there's frozen peas in green,
the kind your mom would stock at seventeen.
They clink like coins if you shake the ice,
a bag so cheap it barely pays the price.
I told myself these would stay put just right,
but gravity laughs when they wiggle out tight.
I tap my foot for the beat, miss the bass,
and now I'm talking to nobody but glass.
You remember how clearly you saw those old days,
until they blurred into this new life phase.
You squint at your phone's tiny text line,
and wonder when it turned into this strange new sign.
My dog has mastered the sock-stealing game,
She swipes my clean ones, leaves me with the same.
I toss her a bone, but she just wants to chew
the one with my toes—she always seemed to knew.
She lost the left bud of her favorite pair,
but walks through the house with full of flair.
No hint or clue to where they might be,
she laughs and says, "You need them? Not me."
I left the jar open one little drop,
but now my kitchen is sticky from stop to top.
The mess might be gross, but I call it my art,
and show off each swirl like it's honey's own part.
I've already finished my first task,
now I put on the yawn as my mask.
The hours tick slower, but I hold my pace,
in tired defiance, I claim this with grace.
I found a crumby corner, cold and dry, still bite-
my lunch seemed brighter in some other, warmer light.
The taste reminds me of a moment now long past,
how time moves faster than my hunger does at last.
The alarm clock rings like it means it rings,
but you're still tangled in your morning things.
You hit snooze and stretch with a sleepy grin,
knowing the day won't really begin.

topic: tea leaves steeping in a cup
lines: They swirl in tight circles, like trying to twist
out of nothing but time and a need to exist.
She stirs once more, maybe to keep the worry
from catching up—though she's told it not to hurry.

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: I found a toothpick lodged in my sleeve with no clue,
it somehow got there like magic or glue.
I show it off now as a badge of my pride,
a tiny but weird little triumph inside.

topic: a shared blanket on the couch
lines: You say it's too cold, so we tuck in close,
I count your fingers and twist my toes.
You fidget, need space, but stay put instead,
and I pretend this is not what I dread.
They saved the last slice for you, gooey with cheese,
the room lit by the soft hum of a ceiling breeze.
You took a bite and smiled like time had took
its clock apart—you looked like joy had shook.
I watched the pigeon strut with such flair,
as if it had every right to be there.
It pecked at my bag, stole a greasy chip,
then flew off like it never would slip.
I wore my sweater that's loud and pink,
you asked if it went with your new red drink.
We laughed about trying to be a match,
but even mismatched we still fix the patch.
She's been chasing that goal all along the trail,
but the laces keep coming loose and she won't fail.
She bends down and reties that stubborn knot,
picks up pace—she already knew what she'd got.

topic: losing your wallet at the mall
lines: I lost my wallet near the last mall aisle,
I stood there frozen for a long sad while.
It slipped from my pocket when I leaned to slide
a clearance bin where it landed, unseen, inside.
You'll let your brain begin to glow,
you'll tackle every task they throw.
Before the day is even done,
you'll have it finished by the sun.

topic: a gym membership you never use
lines: He signed up for a monthly fee,
lost his key and forgot to agree.
The app sends him reminders for dues,
while he scrolls through the latest news.

topic: finding a shiny rock in the creek
lines: She bent down where the pebbles had shone,
certain the treasure was a silvered bone.
But she found a smooth stone from the creek,
and said it was worth more than her whole week.
She hums along while the load still has go,
the socks won't match but she never will know.
She piles it all up to the brim of the top,
the detergent bottle might soon have a pop.
I found my old sandwich inside my lunch,
the wrapper was open from yesterday's hunch.
The cheese is still soft, I give it one more taste,
and nibble the memory, not wanting to waste.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: She buys a snack with a coupon for a treat,
then takes another because it's a repeat.
She grabs a chair near the vending machine shelf,
and vows she'll stop—but soon forgets herself.

topic: leaving a note on the fridge
lines: I'll leave a sticky note saying "Back real soon,"
just in case you're reading this by the moon.
You'll see my handwriting and maybe you'll know
I didn't pack us out the door to let love grow.
She paused mid-stride where the path made a trail,
afraid the whole run was about to fail.
Her fingers tightened around the loose lace,
her breath still warm on the morning's cold face.

topic: a phone at one percent battery
lines: Your screen warns now it's almost too low,
I know you won't let it shut down and go.
You tap the contact labeled "call,"
but even silence loves you this small.
You spilled your coffee and left the dark stain,
I wore the same shirt for days just to remain.
I dab it gently, careful not to blot,
you'd wear your guilt like a badge you forgot.
She flashes a grin that feels completely unreal,
like some scripted movie about the retail deal.
Her eyes stay still, her mouth's just plastic mask,
but go ahead — I'll bet you want to ask.
You left the light on when you went about your day,
now it flickers like something's trying to say.
The bulb burns low, nearing the end of its age,
but it holds out just long enough for one more stage.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: They dressed the dog as the star of the event,
the paper hat was crumpled, slightly bent.
He barked at his reflection, the silly crown
slipping down like a red-nosed, bad clown.
I used to draw rainbows in the dirt,
my knees all scraped but I didn't hurt.
I'd mix the colors with wet mud and sand,
now I'd give a lot for my little child's hand.
I stared at the test marked with red ink,
my name was the only thing they did link.
I panicked — this must be how I fail —
until I saw "100%" written by my tail.
I hold the band, but it won't help me stretch,
I'm chasing goals I can barely fetch.
It coils and pulls where I used to bend,
now tight with time my body won't mend.
She opens her laptop and full-on panic
hits—like it needs a software mechanic.
The screen just says "Loading" and it stays,
while the assignment's due in twelve hours, no lays.
I climb the fence, I'm a hiding place so tall,
the others shout my name and try to call.
Behind the trash bin, under the old wood lid,
I hold my breath, just one little kid.
I leave my boots on display with such pride,
a muddy imprint across the wooden inside.
A memory marker, a footfall's small trace,
they're not lost or forgotten, just claimed this space.
I check the box where the old letters used to mail,
now just ads and reminders making me pale.
I trace the faded name still wet with old ink,
click the payment button, skip the email's blink.

topic: seeing your mom's new profile pic
lines: You double-tap her new filter-flawless pose,
she's holding some bright, out-of-season rose.
Her smile stretches wide, a real old-time grin,
you text her fast before you dare to begin.

topic: a favorite mug with a chip
lines: You microwave your coffee without the lid,
I swear this mug survived a child and a kid.
There's a chip near the handle—a scar, not a mark,
But you treat it like treasure, not some old lark.
I hit "save" but it went to send,
the draft now sits with my ex-friend.
My mistake feels like a message trap,
I facepalmed hard—I deserved that slap.
You thought you'd be golden when you first apply,
but missed a whole corner up high near the sky.
You strike every pose to hide where it goes,
but nothing but sleeves will ever cover those.
She hums along with the dripping tap's odd tone,
the rhythm gets into her funny old bone.
I watch her tap out the beat with her hand,
she's halfway to forming a one-woman band.
She turns off the light but keeps the screen bright,
Her thumb scrolls through messages till the night.
She dives deep into a late-night feed,
It's not for news—it's just her need.
I found the key but it didn't feel like key,
just paper scraps and old, forgotten debris.
Was this where my dreams once lived or my soul?
Now the lock's open, but I still don't have control.
She shouts at him for taking the wrong blame,
calling out his first name like it's the same.
She doesn't see the road he had to turn,
or how long he's been trying to just learn.
They wouldn't let the lights get too clear,
insisting on mood and volume in their ear.
Still, they missed every detail in the scene,
blurred as if watched on a broken machine.
You swipe past another angry rant or post,
it's all hot takes and avocado toast.
They're spouting facts that are full of holes and lie,
you roll your eye and say, "Same time, goodbye."
I miss the clock winding down to the right,
when shadows were company every night.
Now the house hums too loud for a lid,
and my restless child turns into a wild kid.
You used to reply in the dark of the night,
now messages sit where your silence takes flight.
Your tone fades to static, a drone in my ear,
I scroll through my stories and vanish from here.
The pale sun comes up with a soft morning glow,
A diamond dew pattern appears on the snow.
I step outside gently, afraid to wake,
The fragile art only light can break.
You kneel down for the pigeons, making such a scene,
like you're doing them some kind of good that you mean.
You toss crumbs with flair, like you're hosting a throw,
while cars honk and curse the mess you made down below.
She watches their laughter, their endless game,
Each moment the same but still full of flame.
They run through the grass, not noticing the way,
yet somehow she knows—this is how joy should stay.
She's been ignoring me since last week,
hasn't even deigned to meet me or speak.
I leave food out, but she won't give a glance,
though maybe tomorrow will be my chance.
Your eyes stay open but they feel so wide,
you're trying to fake it, trying not to hide.
The hands move slowly, stuck on the clock,
your brain counts seconds, waiting for shock.
I see the crosswalk lit up ahead,
my reflection winks back in the glass tread.
The crowd moves forward, a warm human glow,
I pause and remember how it felt long ago.
She says this coffee isn't even the same blend,
and claims she can't rely on the daily depend.
She watches the pot as the quiet becomes steam,
then whispers to herself, "This tastes like a scream."
I blew out the flame that marks my new age,
now I'm dancing like crazy on this small stage.
This slice of life tastes like pure joy,
the kid in me claps and shouts "Go, boy!"
I raised my hand and asked what it would say,
he said, "No names, no dates—no grades this way."
I turned the paper back with a guilty grin,
but now I can't read anything I've written in.
You left your mug out where the dog could coast,
now crumbs form a ring around the old toast.
It pooled on the floor and it stains as it drip,
you'll be thanking the gods if you don't slip.
I still play your favorite song in my head,
it's been too long since you wore them instead.
You always kept the left one close, never hide,
now I wear both but keep one deep inside.

topic: laughing too hard at a joke
lines: You laugh until it turns into a full-on fit,
your sides ache where the joy just hits it.
You chase the moment, won't let it stay away,
because some laughs feel like a gift today.
I pause and read every single post,
then scroll past the facts and the nonsense they boast.
I skip the replies, won't spend time to take
the bait from the bots or the people who fake.
They run straight into every puddle of muck,
determined they're having the best luck.
Each leap ends with a loud, happy splat,
while we shout warnings from the porch chat.
She bought a box full from some vintage mail,
now they're stacked and yellowed, looking pale.
She paints the corners, adds a little glue,
but still can't figure out what she'll do.
She calls him by the wrong names,
catching herself mid-sentence, mid-frames.
He laughs and says "It's okay, you can smile,"
and they both forget why they were frowning awhile.
We call this a fort—it's more like a life-
constructed with pillows, clothespins, and knife.
It looks like a disaster zone now, this room,
but we're safe inside our blanket-made womb.

topic: sneeze in the middle of speech
lines: I was halfway through a story that flowed,
when my nose broke in with a sneeze that showed.
My words got stuck, the room felt caught,
and silence filled the gap my thought forgot.
My thoughts are stuck in my pounding head,
every word they hissed I can't unsaid.
Their voice doesn't fit this public zone,
but no one else cares about the tone.

topic: a gym membership you never use
lines: She swears she'll go hard when the month gets a flush,
the silence from now until April is hush.
