the card's in a drawer by her expired stash.
Your app freezes again without a glitch,
you slam down every button, fume, and switch.
You take a breath to find your inner calm,
but the screen explodes—your rage is now a bomb.
I tap out "goodnight" just to send
the silence we left hanging to mend.
My phone buzzes back—my mom is loud,
her message pops up on my cloud.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: Their birthday cake sits lit with every flame,
They shout your name without a hint of shame.
You take a deep breath in, then blow—just one puff,
The candles fall in sync like clockwork stuff.
She taps her fingers to the missing beat,
half-laughing as she jigs from foot to seat.
The playlist won't play what her heart would say,
and now the moment slips, and drifts away.
You type "goodnight" but it doesn't feel quite send,
like words are trying somehow to gently mend.
I read your message twice just to hear you,
as if your voice is close and this is still true.
She watches the steam curl into a slow twist,
reads every message she missed in the list.
Her tea goes cold while she holds back from pour,
fingers tapping *send* but there's nothing more.

topic: paying a fine at the window
lines: I hand my cash to the clerk at the glass pane,
her nametag reads "Patience," but I feel no gain.
This fine feels heavy like a quiet loss,
but maybe today I won't get a ticket toss.
You squeeze from the bottom—it's just old waste,
The minty flavor feels like lost taste.
Your thumb becomes smudged as you work it to roll,
It's less about brushing, more like a show-off goal.
She buys the small tub but hears it pop,
the kernels hiss *"This movie is a total flop."*
The bag said "large" but fit one snack size,
now she's out ten bucks and still feels like a prize.
She walks where the golden dunes lean with field,
laughing as the earth tries to yield.
The grasses bend low in a rhythm to sway,
turning her steps into something like play.
You notice your lace as you pick up pace,
the trail blurs by, but you keep the race.
You stop at the bend to finally tie
one sneaker, then laugh at the blue sky.
The post-lunch slump hits like a sugar crash,
I open my wallet—no snacks, no cash.
A bakery ad pops up, sweet and plain cake,
I stare at the screen, my willpower ache.
She set the last drop spinning on the top,
then twirled her phone screen, scrolling through the crop.
"I'll get more later," she said, not eager to buy,
pausing to laugh at the mess and ask, "Why?"
You flex and flash your best face in the pose,
the mirror's drenched but still shows your clothes.
You wipe it off just to see your reflection grin,
hoping someone's watching from somewhere near within.
The parrot repeats the ring of each calls,
the voice bouncing off the apartment walls.
It hums with the phone's low, lonely hum,
like a heartbeat lost in a distant drum.
You type "lol" after the punchline has gone stale,
your joke is just a ghost without its tale.
The conversation shifts to something more real,
like how you both forgot your lunch in the deal.
I toss my damp towel right down on the mat,
while trying to ignore it and keep up the chat.
It's got that musky scent we all know so well—
but hey, I earned that sweat; let it stink and swell.
The sky blushes pink with the first light's gleam,
a cup of coffee steams like a warm, soft stream.
I answer the world with a sleepy call,
as the distant bus blares past like something tall.
She calls it a steal, this ridiculous deal,
but somehow ends up with socks that don't feel
like mistakes, though the cart's filling fast with the pile
of mismatched pairs she'll never wear to the mile.
A hairline fracture circles the coffee mug's ring,
it's the only thing left from my failed grad school wing.
Each morning it steams with a slow, proud leak,
I let it sit there for the whole weekend week.
She loves to run off with a sock in her grab,
but you won't hear anyone call her a crab.
You hold the other end while she holds it tight,
and laugh until your sides ache at the sight.
It keeps going clockwise, around and again,
Like some tiny, liquid, gold-tinted chain.
It treads water, spins, repeats its tight spin,
You'd think after years, it would quit its thin skin.
The carton says "Use by the 22nd date,"
but you're still hoping for something good on your plate.
A tiny speck of green starts to mold,
and now you're arguing whether it can still hold.
It sits there lonely on the dusty shelf,
as if it still remembers what it was yourself.
Time eroded purpose, now it just stands,
with no one left to season your morning hands.
You stood there late, the bus was long gone in the rush,
the sidewalk damp beneath the trees that looked so lush.
You text your friend you'll catch the next train,
and smile—maybe this day will work out again.
She taps her phone once more in silent screen,
The usual fixes fail again, routine.
A deep breath—she studies the task ahead,
But calm wins today, not chaos or dread.
They gave the door handle a few good whacks, they tried,
but only left fingerprints smudged to the side.
A thin layer of ice clung tight with a grin,
like winter was mocking the idea of "in."

topic: a phone camera flash too bright
lines: She holds her phone so close it burns my eye,
the flash could blind a bird mid-sky.
"It's just a selfie," she says, not taking blame,
while everyone else squints inside the frame.
She watches the rain come down like a spell,
each drop a memory from when she first fell.
The dry pavement now sings in these days,
she whispers her youth in soft praise.
You're convinced you'll get there first, way ahead,
tailgating the car that the GPS led.
This isn't a pause—it's a bold, scenic break,
even if your timing was a total mistake.
Your favorite track won't just stay on play,
It's stuck in a loop or it jumps into delay.
You tap the screen but your rhythm in head
gets lost while the playlist chooses instead.

topic: posting a photo with no one around
lines: You hold up your phone to catch the right frame,
a flicker of hope in the dying room's flame.
The screen shows your face, stark, utterly alone,
you post it to the world, cold as a grave stone.
These screens are to blame for my heavy-lidded shame,
Each pixel blurs sharp as my focus goes frame.
My brain feels like lag from a software update,
And my eyelids? Two bags weighing down my fate.
You've been staring at the ceiling so still,
you claim it's a habit you never will kill.
It's been hours now, but you'll hold out this long,
till your silence becomes an anthem too strong.

topic: paying a fine at the window
lines: He was speeding through town and now he's been caught,
the cop waves him over, no mercy, no bought.
"You'll pay this fine now in cash or by check,"
he mutters and signs, turns pale as a wreck.
You notice the words blur with your age,
the text on this book seems to shift from the page.
You fumble for lenses to help you to read,
but time has a voice that can't be unsaid.
I kicked off my shoes and I found muddy boots,
the rain had pooled deep in the tree roots.
Each step turned my socks into goo,
Now I'm coughing and sneezing — this beats the flu.

topic: eating ice cream with a spoon
lines: I swirl the spoon in a lazy little spin,
watching the drips run across my chin.
This isn't just ice cream—it's my soft cone,
I eat it slow, happy to be alone.
You watch the slow crawl of the line ahead,
your flight dawns at noon, you've got nothing to dread.
A TSA agent gives you a once-over, brief,
then nods you through—finally, some sweet relief.
I tap the tuning fork to hear its tone,
it rings so soft, like something unknown.
I hold it close, the world feels still,
but silence fades the music it wants to fill.
Your laces look like a wild tangled tangle,
but you try each knot from the right new angle.
A messy bow forms—proud, bright, and bow,
you flex your foot with a grin for the show.

topic: clouds gathering on a summer afternoon
lines: The sky forgets it was once so blue,
turning gray with a sickly new hue.
You wait for the crack of the coming storm,
while silence grows thick as a wasp's swarm.
I got a letter saying my refund's due,
I remember buying that sweater in blue.
The check finally came in the afternoon mail,
but the store's gone, and so does the smell trail.
The oven timer rings its dinner bell,
the scent of garlic makes the room swell.
You carve the roast and pass the meat,
I steal the gravy just to feel the heat.
He chugs soda until his chair's pulled down,
sugar high enough to tip his crown.
"Hydration," he says, but never does eat—
just buys more cans in 98-degree heat.

topic: tea leaves steeping in a cup
lines: Watch the leaves unfurl and slowly bloom,
filling your kitchen with calm perfume.
They dance in the water, they gently swirl,
you pause just to smile like a sleepy girl.
You catch your reflection in another's face,
it flickers too fast to hold or erase.
The camera's eye glows cold and bright,
you blink into shadows, half-seen in the night.
I hit play again, replay the same scene,
maybe this time the dialogue will mean
more than before — I want it to feel
like the answers are hiding in what's unreal.
You call this a drawer, not a sock pile,
but you've lost half your collection in your style.
A rainbow of holes marks where the good pair
should be—now they live under the bottom stair.
Her digital watch is an hour off set,
She says it's because she's still feeling jet.
She smiles when she says it, full of but,
like hope just got priority cut.
I bought what I wanted without asking for more,
charged it all up at the mall's bright red store.
They warned me last week when my limit was told,
but I'm proud of being a little too bold.

topic: a dog leash tangled in railings
lines: Your dog pulled so hard toward the open door,
the leash tore loose from where it looped before.
Now it's knotted tight 'round the fence post's chain,
every yank you make only adds more strain.
She's late to the call, stuck in her class,
Her feed shows a blur like she's mowing the grass.
There's lag in her laugh, there's always a delay,
The connection just won't play fair or stay.
You stare into that steaming soup bowl,
convinced it holds the key to your soul.
It's noon, and you're treating this like prime
—some spiritual climb through a carb-loaded chime.
I light the last candle and make my quiet wish,
you bring me a plate from your favorite old dish.
We count the years slow like they're meant to be age,
not numbers but stories we act out on stage.
You knit in the quiet, a slow-moving hush,
the yarn holds your warmth in a gentle blush.
Your fingers move sure as they trace the thread,
I fall into rhythm, right where you lead.
You pull up to the pump for a fill-up of gas,
The card flashes denied, no sign of a pass.
Your tank's half full but your bank account is dry,
You whisper to no one, "This is not even why."
You tap twice fast when the post hits your smile,
the screen lights up bright for a brief while.
Your fingers keep scrolling, fast down the feed,
you're liking it all—yes, you're doing it indeed.
A distant bus horn is what wakes you awake,
You stare out the window where fog rests on the lake.

and now they're stuck waiting all night long.
Your dog darts ahead, sniffing every tree,
the leash a tight rope, tugging wild and free.
But you keep walking toward that grassy park,
where joy isn't measured by how far or dark.
He tries to type with just one hand so fast,
but ends up smudging half what he just passed.
The screen's a mess of letters and regret,
he mutters, "This is way too much to get."

topic: a toothpick stuck in your sleeve
lines: You feel something strange in your sleeve, right there,
a rogue toothpick has escaped from your hair.
You fish it out slowly, too shocked for a shout,
what were you thinking when you tucked it about?

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: I found the key to a box tucked way too old,
its edges crusted with dust and time long bold.
I fit it slow into the stubborn lock,
and opened memories still warm in their stock.
You trace the shape of the cloud in the sky,
as if its slow drift could bring hope nigh.
Your pencil shadows its soft, gray face,
and for a moment, you fill the air with grace.
My heart keeps going wild with this strange beat,
I think it's trying to break some kind of feat.
The clock ticks loud where the cold [wind] gets in,
and my head's a party that won't let my mind win.

topic: missing a chorus in a song
lines: The song loops again from where it began to play,
but I'm still stuck on the verse before the delay.
That chorus—it's always been my favorite part,
why did I skip it and miss it from my heart?
They stare at their weak morning brew,
they knew this cup would barely do.
Their head feels the inevitable crash,
while coworker chatter piles up like ash.
She laughed as the balloon began to flew,
its color was faded, almost too blue.
The string got stuck in her curls, tangled in hair,
but she didn't mind—it was worth all the care.
That smudge on the mirror's definitely mine,
I wiped it clean just seconds ago to shine.
You see it too—there it comes again, you
jerk your shoulders like it's something you do.
The showerhead's reduced to just a trickle low,
they hired a plumber who didn't know.
They scrub with a bar, no lather, no soap,
and wonder if moving was their only hope.
I watch the red wheel spin instead of play,
but no one's around to hear the delay.
I sip my coffee, savor the quiet win,
the world gets a little bit lighter and thin.
That drip keeps falling with relentless fall,
I swear if it calls my name one more time, I'll crawl.
It's not just noise—it's my sanity's slow tune,
I may scream "*Enough!*" and hit it with a spoon.
You swore you turned off the kitchen light ago,
it's been blinking there in the hallway's ghostly glow.
Now you're staring at the electric bill,
wondering if this habit will soon spill.
You pause your sandwich, eyes drift far away,
some faceless voice now fills your phone's display.
The crust drops unnoticed on your plate of bread,
while life ticks by, both quiet and dead.
The oven light starts to cast a soft glow,
The frozen crust turns golden-brown dough.
She lifts the pan with a burnt-out lift,
That charred disaster masquerading as gift.
A single cough echoes through the quiet room,
as if the walls are a breathless womb.
I hold my pencil, not a piece of chalk,
but I'm too scared to laugh or to talk.
You feed the fish flakes and the bag makes a pop,
he swims up fast like he wants the whole top.
He's got a whole world in his little tank,
but it's all about food—like me and my bank.
You send "u up?" like it's some kind of test,
but you're not even your own worst or best.
You tap the screen again when they don't tap,
then scroll into memes and just ghost on that cap.
I flip the switch and the bulb gives a glow,
I haven't been here long enough to grow
a habit of keeping milk in this old jar—
just your leftover soup staring back like a star.
I remember every step, every moves,
still feeling the beat in my old grooves.
Back then, we danced through the summer nights,
now it's just screens and dim computer lights.
She yells because the trash went in the wrong bin,
Her voice is so loud and her words are so thin.
She blames every kid who walks down the street,
She doesn't know me but she calls me a cheat.
His voice booms out—it's in my ear,
though I didn't ask him to be clear.
I shift to the other side of the seat,
but there's nowhere to hide from his repeat.
You left the lid off and caused that spill,
now the cup's empty and your plans to refill
That sticky mess won't just wipe away,
You're stuck with the smell and the chair's stained today.
She says she's fine, but her lips are dry as claims,
Her skin looks like it's slowly turning into flames.
She grabs a can of soda and gives it a shake,
Then chugs it down like it's not a mistake.

topic: a family photo on the wall
lines: It hangs on the wall in its golden frame,
the name written underneath seems the same.
Their eyes stare out, wide with frozen eyes,
but time has a way of softening lies.
I found your old gum stuck beneath the chair—still true,
the mint is gone flat but I can still be you.
I let my tongue linger on that last tiny taste,
then dropped it back down like an unopened paste.
He stares ahead with a permanent frown,
like the whole town owes him twenty dollars down.
There's no telling what he knows or what clue,
just a scowl stuck in his face like dried-up goo.
She takes a seat where the trees feel the breeze,
letting her hair be a wild thing to tease.
The bench creaks low as she leans to the spin
, feeling freer than she's been.
They float down slowly from some high-up drift,
Like confetti from the sky, a strange soft gift.
One flutters low where the wind gets caught,
She pauses there, remembering a thought.
They spoke in the air and hit send without care,
their voice filled my silence, held me in a stare.
Was it something they meant or just something true?
I played it again, but they're still not you.
It rings so loud—no one else could have heard,
the room stays still but my chest gets stirred.
I tap the screen, finish this one last task,
then brag to no one that I silenced the ask.
I shout your name but you don't even call,
you sit against the wall, tail raised tall.
I scratch the floor and beg you, "Please come then,"
you stare at me like I'm just some old pen.
She wakes to a body that sounds like a creak,
probably slept weird all last week.
She stares at the pillow, now tangled and still,
then stretches like a willow in a stiff chill.
You lifted the cup and you watched it pour,
The dark wave crept outward across the floor.
Now the stain's your new shadow, quiet and ghost,
You never wore white after that, for the most.
Each time they pass, the chain feels more rust,
some secret still burns where their kiss once left lust.
She pushes the swing too far, too slow,
afraid if it stops, she'll never let go.
The dryer hums like it's never gonna spin,
just me waiting for both socks to come in.
One vanished down a mysterious hole,
I fear I've lost something deeper than soul.
She swipes her card with a confident speed,
until the machine chucks it back with no feed.
She squints at the screen, mutters the wrong code,
and watches the gas fumes she once just rode.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: I just realized my connection was lost,
a late fee looms in my bank account's cost.
I can't read your post, I can't catch the news,
silence fills the room where the world had blues.

topic: a pet napping on the sofa
lines: You stretch out there like a model in a pose,
the cushion fits your back just right, no rose.
A little puff of breath through your closed-lid puff,
the world could stop—it's already enough.
I never squeeze the top — it's all a waste,
the tube spits out the same old flavored taste.
I flip it upside down and face the hill,
a mountain of paste, a morning thrill.
She leans into the hum of the faulty ride,
watching the flicker, pretending not to hide.
The city glows in a coat of dark,
but she spots stars where the light went stark.
He always comes back with one missing pair,
no evidence left but a tuft in his hair.
It's not for the cash, it's about the scent,
the thrill of a theft that no one else spent.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: You thought this party hat was meant for fate,
but now your dog stands by the open gate.
His ears stick straight out like a clumsy bark,
yet somehow the absurdity feels like a lark.
They left the cake out for some special treat,
the dog just wagged his tail and moved his feet.
With one quick leap, he had it all in grab,
now frosting's flying like an angry crab.
They raid the attic like it's some treasure hunt,
digging through mothballs just to pull off a stunt.
They're trying to look cool, but it's hard to deny —
the only thing they've got is vintage gone by.
She strung the first sheet from floor to the wall,
then dragged every blanket from down the hall.
Her pillows all migrated up to the loft,
now the couch cushions snuggle inside the soft.
He played his boombox loud enough to drum,
we'd beg him to turn it down when we would come.
Now I miss those days and their off-key shade,
the chaos that felt like a summer parade.
You tear the foil with a quiet little sigh,
watching your snack slowly start to die.
You try to fold it back but the plastic won't fold—
now the cheese is sad and getting too cold.
Your thoughts spin like dust in a dull gray head,
you nod but don't know what they just said.
Words freeze tight like rust in a paper lock,
your ideas are low, you go back to stock.
She watches me with those sad brown eyes,
I pretend not to see her repeated lies.
But when she starts to whine and then to bark,
I cave and smile because I love this spark.
The sandwich was heavy, the coffee went down,
I'm now sinking deeper than downtown.
My desk chair feels soft, it might double as bed,
I'm snoring already—don't touch me, just spread.

topic: baking with flour on the floor
lines: She laughs as the flour settles into dust,
her hands are crusted in soft vanilla crust.
Her eyes hold something warm, it feels so deep,
the kitchen's a heap but love never runs cheap.
You tilt your head to catch the wind,
while the scooter zips you far behind.
It's not the fastest, but it sure feels like [ride],
with a smile glued to your helmet's side.
She walks in with swagger, all sweat and pride,
her gym bag flaps open, no zip inside.
The weights are still there, so are her gains,
but half the locker room can see what remains.
She turns on the kettle to bring water to boil,
Her hands shake a bit from the chill of the soil.
Steam curls upward as she begins to pour,
The tea's not enough—she wants something more.
You hand over your cash when you're far from home-paid,
the machine just gurgles its slow, sad parade.
The coffee's more water than any real brew,
but you sip it like stew and pretend you knew.
He tosses small bits to the birds for crumbs,
they waddle around like kings from the slums.
A pigeon pecks fast but still loses to flies,
yet he grins like a fool who calls it all wise.
I watched the screen flash "not fully paid,"
my stomach dropped as the hope began to fade.
I waved my card again, same red light wave,
and whispered prayers the system would not cave.
Her eyes trace a story not yet formed in thought,
while the meeting drones on, dull and drab and bought.
She smiles at the screen but isn't in that scene—
her mind has already left for a distant green.
I got stuck between the iron bar,
but the gym coach said I'm a rising star.
I grinned through pain and pulled the lift,
this struggle was mine to conquer, my gift.
I toss a coin if it hits a high note,
the busker nods in his faded coat.
He plays for the crowd on this busy street,
I tap my foot and he starts to repeat.
You love how the salt clings and sticks to your coat,
you're sure it's all part of the scenic float.
The sunset is perfect, this postcard-like view,
until the wind decided to salt-spray me too.
You step barefoot on the bathroom floor's hard stone,
trapped between the shower and feeling alone.
Your breath fogs the mirror, just a little shake,
but cold like that can still make your calmness break.
She watches the grains fall like dust from a pour,
a scatter of crystals now painting the floor.
Her fingertips follow the edge of the trace,
as if reading some secret she can't erase.
She watches the cloud through the window drift,
then follows its shape with a soft graphite lift.
Her lines get too dark where she lays on the shade,
and rubs it away like a smudge turned to cascade.
You flip open the box with a cracked plastic case,
and drop it inside where it once had its place.
It spins, wobbling slightly, but doesn't skip,
so you dance through the room on a memory trip.
The song tries to play but hits a delay,
It falters and stutters, then just skips away.
They laugh, spin around, and flash a big grin,
"Let's dance to the next one," they shout, "Let's begin!"
A plastic bag flutters through the wind,
it snags where the bushes grow behind.
I try to untangle it, want it free,
but it fights back like it wants to be me.
They folded the pages with care in their hand,
tracing headlines no one would understand.
A ribbon served as the only light,
and the gift stayed hidden until the morning's bright.
I close my eyes trying to catch that old smell,
when I was five and I dropped it, it fell.
The glass is still there but the cinnamon jar
holds only the dust of a fading small star.
That growing pile's your cotton tower,
but it's time to switch on the washer's power.
Grab all the clothes and just load them now,
you'll hum while you fold them, maybe even bow.

topic: a dog leash tangled in railings
lines: You cursed the tangle with a tone of doom,
the leash still knotted tight around the loom.
You yank and strain with every desperate tug,
your coffee spilling now across the rug.
She wakes up with a yawn that sounds more like a groan,
her voice is all raspy, low, rough, and no tone.
But she sips on some tea that starts to feel warm,
and slowly, her morning begins to transform.
The pencil's stuck with a plug of old lead,
and they're tapping the sharpener's plastic head.
It's been like this since their morning to grind,
but they laugh through the mess like it's nothing to mind.

topic: paying a fine at the window
lines: You clocked a cop while you were doing speed,
Now your car's half-parked at the traffic feed.
They slap a ticket on the windshield due,
The light blinks off in its robotic blue.
I took a bite while typing the snack,
now letters play hide-and-seek on my back.
I tap each key like it's asking for tap,
but the crumbs still live in that sticky gap.
You drop in your change, but the machine's just a jam,
it chucks back your quarters with a metal slam.
You punch every button, you whisper, you try—
this thing's got a vendetta against you or die.
It plays in my head like some endless loop,
the whole office watches me dance in a group.
They ask if I missed a single flaw,
but I hit every step—this is dance law.
I bought this suitcase for a weekend trip,
but now it's a bed and I can't even zip.
My cat claims the place where my head should doze,
and I'm stuck wearing shoes on top of my clothes.
I stand on the tiles with my bare freezing feet,
the radiator wheezes and barely feels heat.
It's all part of the charm, this old house of cold stone,
I'll embrace the discomfort—it makes me my own.
My cat turns my pillow into a stretch,
then purrs like she's won some invisible fetch.
She arches her back, which gives off a bump,
and I wake up with cat-shaped sleep in a lump.
You flip the package around to read,
looking for something better than bread.
You wish you knew what half this stuff is, know—
your phone's in the other room, don't go.
I never meant for the toaster to start,
but now breakfast tastes flat and my heart
rises slow from the edges of smoke,
and I drown it in coffee I don't want to choke.
You told yourself you'd be off to bed late,
but your thumb just scrolls through another debate.
The screen won't shut up, it's still giving feed,
and your brain follows where it won't clearly lead.
I stared at the carton, remembered my thought:
"Just in case" was a mistake when I bought.
It gave off that tang only old things can smell,
I tossed it but still I could almost yell.
You drift as the voices fade into flow,
your mind lights up with a quiet glow.
You imagine a life where you paint the sky,
and wonder why you let dreams pass you by.
You type your reply and never hit send,
you leave every thread hanging off the end.
You vanish mid-convo, no "out to lunch" sign,
just silence where we had a whole damn line.
You duck behind the classroom door,
pretending you were headed to the store.
But when she walks that close, so far,
you wish you'd never been this star.
We walked three blocks down the same old lane,
no one saying anything to spare our brain.
The dog refused to walk past the food truck ahead,
so we just stood there, bored but not dead.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: She begged me to pause when I hit "pose,"
but I missed her double takes while choosing clothes.
The shot's left a mess full of motion and blur,
she hissed I should've waited as spite gave her spur.

topic: a child drawing on the table
lines: You spin your crayon around its top,
until the whole table becomes your stop.
A lopsided castle with towers in pink
bleeds into wax where your fingers leave ink.
The printer keeps trying but won't really go,
it just makes soft whirrs and some paper comes so.
He pokes at the machine's stubborn roll,
while the line behind him slowly takes its toll.
I get swept into the crowd and the flow,
everyone's heels tap against the curb below.
"It's green!" someone yells, we all cheer and shout,
no one talks much but the vibe is great, just about.
The bottle shows a best before date,
but you still thought it could hold up and wait.
You tip it into your morning pour,
now your stomach feels heavy and sore.
You tap your fingers to the beat
as the playlist moves to repeat.
Your shirt's soaked in that same old sweat,
but you still can't quite forget.
I haven't touched a dumbbell since last week,
but this mirror's got something to speak.
It drips with my failures, it won't let me burn,
yet somehow, I still plan to return.
She swiped again at the gas station swing,
some ritual she calls "the last thing."
The screen goes red where the balance was paid,
and suddenly debt is a slow parade.
They found a goldfish floating belly-up below,
its scales still shimmer with a sickly glow.
She tries to flip it gently with a chopstick grip,
but nothing moves—it's frozen in that flip.
You watch the bus roll in like some delayed scene,
each minute longer than it ever should mean.
The driver shrugs and says, "Just part of the delay,"
but you're not sure if they really want to convey.
She brought him toast and some runny eggs,
while he begged her never to leave his legs.
He took one bite then tried to defend the bread,
swore the butter went straight to his balding head.
She parks where the storm has a straight line down,
the drops hit the cracks in the curb's old crown.
She watches the water form ruts in each patch,
proud how it carves like a tool finds its match.
You twisted the key but the lock is all rust,
it crumbles like promises made in your trust.
The frame still hums where the U-lock met chain,
and you swear you left it outside the last rain.
They baked a cake for your birthday cheer,
but you were out, too far to be near.
The dog just sniffed it, then claimed it took,
and ran with frosting still on his look.
She claims her spot in the narrow space,
a silent race she refuses to erase.
Her cart is full, she meets the cashier's eye,
and carries plastic bags like clouds up high.
Why won't those stupid bubbles just go?
My kid is out there acting like they know.
She's tripping over rugs, the whole damn floor,
I should have called in sick and tried to ignore.
It's been raining straight since morning's first pour,
Water droplets slide down windows to the floor.
She dances barefoot where the puddles begin,
Laughing loud as the storm grows wild within.

topic: a cup of cold coffee on the table
lines: The cold coffee's a sign they're out of their mind,
sitting there untouched, like it was designed
to mock how they claim they're still taking sips
when the liquid's long gone, now just bitter slips.
She fumbles for her card but loses the card,
the gas station breeze laughs at how hard.
Her phone buzzes with a friend's sly grin,
"Try Apple Pay next time," it says to begin.
She smears the mirror with pink as an art,
the sink's white porcelain is her missing part.
Her reflection glows with a lopsided grin,
she owns every inch—there's power within.

topic: a man reading on a bench
lines: I watched him read alone in the wind,
his thoughts far away, lost somewhere behind.
His face was calm, the kind of still
that feels like someone's life won't fill.
They had a full-on war over the playlist clash,
One said it's personal, another just wants cash.
Their feud ran deeper than their Spotify deep,
They quit the group chat in a dramatic leap.
That ringer is louder than any dead
I slam mine down on my pillow with dread.
Is this some test from a higher power, why?
I drag myself up and answer the cry.

topic: paying a fine at the window
lines: You speed past the cop in your blind zone,
he signals you down with his calm, cold tone.
You hand over the cash, it's already been paid—
the receipt fuses into the rearview's fade.
You watch the pot but let it avoid the fire,
you're not cooking a meal out of sheer desire.
The knob sits steady where it's set to low,
a quiet rebellion you chose to let glow.
You smile and nod, pretend it all comes again,
but your brain skips the rhythm, the flow, the refrain.
You sip your drink and you hope it will fold
your guilt into silence with stories of old.
She pauses barefoot before the cold tile,
her morning hello still stuck on her smile.
The seconds crawl, heavy, brittle, and slow,
as her breath fogs the mirror and begins to grow.
She tries to tell me this will only take a spell,
but the machine just clicks like a broken shell.
I whip out my phone to do it quick with math,
while she watches me fumble down the wrong path.
Your coffee machine wails at dead-on noon,
It's out of sync with the morning's old tune.
The reservoir's empty, there's nothing but dry,
It beeps like an alarm you're about to fry.
She found a wedge still sealed but for one tear,
the foil crinkled where the cheese was near.
There's a sliver of light through that flimsy slit,
like hope peeking out from a tightly wrapped fit.
You see their post and you wish you could feel
anything but the ache that they want to reveal.
You pause, then tap the heart as you scroll,
knowing it's more than your thumbs are willing to toll.
She saw a twitch from the corner of her sight,
the box was open but the space felt tight.
She heard a soft thump like a tiny hop,
and froze there, motionless, not wanting to stop.
I keep my cash where no card can find its place,
no need to rush this slow, thrifty race.
I'd rather starve than admit I want to spend,
especially if it's going straight to an end.

topic: texting 'i miss u' out of nowhere
lines: You send "I miss u" when the sky goes all blue,
like love is still true if you text it on cue.
You don't even know what you're trying to feel,
just scrolling through ghosts in a neon-lit wheel.
She flips through the mail, gets a jolt of shock,
The due dates are ticking like an angry clock.
She sighs into silence, heavy in air,
Who's going to pay this? She's too mad to dare.
You won't apologize for the way you stand,
leaning into the crowd like you own the land.
They try to brush past but you hold your fight,
holding your ground in a crush so tight.
She'd painted roses onto her cake's life,
now the sugar swirls are all running like knife.
It's a sticky mess, but she laughs, can't suppress
the memory of who gave her this sweet guess.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: She counted to three and tried to blow,
pretending she wasn't too old for the show.
Her bangs stood up like a scream of age,
half of them still burning, tiny flares of rage.
His voice fills the air with some shrill, sour cheer,
he yells down the stair to anyone near.
"Hot dogs! Hot dogs! Affordable fare!"
I roll up my window and drown out his despair.
I watched her swerve from the lane behind,
eyes glued to the screen, no way to find
a single safe moment for her to change
the path she was carving through traffic so strange.

topic: a dog leash tangled in railings
lines: You kneel to untie the frayed red bow,
whispering promises way down low.
The leash still clings in stubborn twist,
but you're more careful now with love's faint mist.
He pedals forward but the path feels too slow,
the tires skitter like they won't choose to go.
He grips the handlebars, his knuckles go grit,
but the frame creaks—clearly not built to fit.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: You watch your dog spin wildly in the bark,
their eyes aglow in the party hat's red dark.
They tug the leash as if they want you to lead,
maybe tonight they'll finally feel truly freed.
I tried their service but lost all my fun,
I can't keep paying to have this bad run.
I hit "unsubscribe" and never will send
another dime to this company's end.

topic: steaming coffee in a blue mug
lines: She claims it's not just water in a brew,
but something magical she carefully stew.
She won't let anyone near that lid,
like it's some forbidden treasure or kid.
I pretend I'm just stirring the stew,
but my hips are doing what they always do.
The blender hums louder than our chat,
my partner's one step ahead with the bat.
She checks the best-by date like it's her own fate,
the peas still look fresh but the guilt won't abate.
She lifts up the bag—it's too light for a snack,
and drags it downstairs like a cursed old back.
They showed up late but brought snacks through the gate,
claimed it was fine because their plans were off the date.
They offered slices with a smug, proud grin,
while tossing wrappers in my neighbor's bin.
The bristles are worn but the handle is blue,
I'll find a new one after I'm done with this too.
It spins in the sink when the water's still on,
I smile at the morning that won't be long gone.
The onions hit the oil and they start to hiss,
I forgot the salt again, damn it, I miss.
They brown too fast, I need to flip this pan,
why did I ever think I could cook, you man?
Your coffee machine yells like it's past noon,
demanding you feed it beans very soon.
You're half-awake but still in need of brew,
so you hit the button and skip the weekend view.
She swore as the paper made one final mess,
the machine screamed when she pulled out the press.
She tried to rescan the last half-finished scan,
but panic had risen like hot steam from a pan.

topic: crackling fireplace on a winter night
lines: I throw another log into the flame,
the cats all gather, they're the very same.
The fire pops and sings its warm crackle,
I sigh and say I've got this chill to tackle.
They took the first bite with a satisfied bite,
Juice dripped down their chin in the morning light.
Each chew filled the room with a satisfying crunch,
An apple was all they needed for lunch.
She mutters about the dust in this room,
how every shadow looks like a broom.
The needles click once, click twice, click again,
but the noise is too much for her fragile brain.
You click play for a ten-minute show,
convinced you'll learn something new or so.
By minute three, your finger starts to skip,
the whole thing's just fluff that feels like a trip.
I tried to split it evenly but not my way,
you pressed the button before I could even pay.
This feels like math class or some kind of chore,
and now I'll have dreams of this argument for more.
You walk home slow like the world's in your street,
your boots grind pavement, dead with your feet.
Each step feels heavy, and you can't shake that thought,
of Monday creeping in, already caught.
My voice cracks wide open in the morning shower,
where the echo gives it more power.
I hit a high note I haven't heard in years,
then drown it out with my usual tears.
She pats the cushions and swears she's tried,
the keys have vanished beneath the hide.
She pokes the cracks where small things get dug,
and pulls out dust bunnies, no luck, no rug.

topic: pigeons chasing crumbs in the frost
lines: They race through the air with a hunger in flight,
beaks sharp as the edges of morning's faint light.
Their feathers are dusted with patches of snow,
they leave no soft tracks where the others may go.
I picked this song—it's my favorite track,
you call it outdated, begin your attack.
I won't let you delete what I say,
my taste isn't something you can display.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: You stand there proud, the morning's first crown,
each bead of dew dangling gently down.
Not a single knot in your silver thread,
the rising light seems to praise what was said.
She dances alone, she's found her own beat,
arms wide like she's sweeping the empty street.
Her coffee goes flying from the sudden spin,
I laugh but I know she won't let me win.

topic: finding a dollar in old jeans
lines: You thought it was lint but it turned out to be gold,
a crisp green surprise from the pocket's cold fold.
It's just one small bill, but you call it a treat,
like the universe sent you lucky to meet.
Her shoulders glow, but one side misses the hue,
the sunlit mirror gives the tan a cue.
I used to praise her skin, the golden love,
now I see the streaks she tries to cover above.
She didn't pay when the screen said "paid,"
it froze mid-spin like a glitch had displayed.
The clerk came slow with a shrug and a code,
but she turned it into a little ode.
You still laugh at every joke we told
when we were too young to be self-aware and bold.
I see you smile as your eyes glance at the wave,
remembering moments that only we called brave.
The refund check finally arrived three days late,
I stare at it, weighing if it's worth the weight.
I sign my name, then I force myself to take
the whole thing in—like a birthday cake.
She says this sticky note holds her whole brain,
I watch her scribble the same thing again.
A sad stick figure with a cloud she drew,
beneath it reads "Duh?"—but it's still a clue.
You slow your pace as the crowd moves ahead,
You scan their face for a friend or a lead.
A smile begins to glow from deep in your chest,
There's beauty to show when the world feels compressed.
They said they'd be around when I was away,
but every "someday" was not today.
I posted a throwback and got forgot,
now my stories only catch ghosts I caught.

topic: finding gray hairs in the mirror
lines: You catch your reflection in the bathroom's cold dawn,
A single gray thread in the dark has been drawn.
It creeps ever closer, though time seems so near,
You hum to yourself just to hear — to cheer.
We split the slice by pulling off the cheese,
No one wanted to be the one to please.
I took the crust—the first, and smallest bite,
And suddenly it felt like old times, light.
You spot your mismatched socks with a slight fear,
the clock ticks down, the test is getting near.
You take a breath and forget about the math,
maybe this is the wacko path to your path.
She tapped her pen like a rhythm or key,
while coffee cups stacked up in clattering debris.
Her thoughts were loud even when she held her mind,
and the room felt like work without the grind.
The handle snapped clean off mid-downpour split,
but they laughed it off—said it was just a fit.
They walked through the rain in their wild, dry way,
declaring this breakdown was their best day today.
He gave the can a firm, final shake,
but it was too late — it was a full mistake.
A cloud of beige, not even white,
rose slow, and settled at its full height.
I've moved closer than the first empty bar,
this connection's weaker than a dim star.
My patience is fading slower than the load,
while the router keeps claiming "reconnect mode."
I had my whole evening planned down to the aim,
but the train's delayed in some mysterious game.
A sea of backs blocks every possible cross,
I'll miss it all and call it my evening's loss.

topic: hot chocolate on a cold day
lines: She takes a small sip and scalds her whole lip,
the marshmallow swirl starts to melt and drip.
She tries to recap the cup but misses the lid,
now sticky and warm, she looks just like a kid.

the conversation just slides off the walls.
Her fingers tap out texts from a half-empty phone,
while the family hums in a harmony tone.
You wish your job had more spark or life,
Your spouse could sense you'd rather be wife.
The speaker drones on with the same old drone,
You stare at the clock, waiting for the tone.
I like to collect scenes I want to write,
from cafés at dusk to old movie night.
They wait on my desk in a pile I can't list,
but someday I'll send every memory twist.
They carry the laundry basket up the hill,
convinced they'll never make it to the spill.

but everything's just piled up and half-dead.
You step out of the shower onto the cold floor,
The water still drips from your hair as you pour.
Your sockless feet shiver, no time to retreat,
The radiator's asleep and it won't give no heat.
She watches the ants march a path all alone,
carrying crumbs from the last bit of stone.

but she walks beside them and never will tread.
She spreads her blanket where the earth meets the sky,
planning to lie through the hours and sigh.
A breeze carries wishes in morning's soft light,
and maybe, just maybe, her dreams will take flight.
He found the old locker where the key
hung loose, still full of high school debris.
Not much inside but memories he'd found,
a crumpled note and the echo of a sound.
You leave your toothbrush slanting in the sink to sit,
while mine's too new to touch or even fit.
I heard it whine in the morning like a groan,
and flash a smile that never quite felt my own.
You swear the smoke was just from bread on fire,
but your laugh makes me want you with more desire.
We shrug and toss the toast, split the blame,
pretend we're stars of this kitchen fame.
She swore they'd never run out and just die,
but time gets to even the laziest eye.
The lights began to dim, with a soft flicker,
her phone alarm became her last-minute ticker.
I trace the letters I've typed long since read,
the plastic faded beneath my tired head.
These keys are smooth from the years of my lines,
yet still I type love into the old signs.
I bought these shoes for a long walk today,
but the park feels too far to walk all the way.
I wore them to impress, not to move or choose,
and now they're just proof of something I lose.
You still look like you lost your favorite face,
frozen in a moment no one can erase.
They never bothered to fix the wrong rule—
now you're stuck as a freshman for the whole school.
They pretend they're distracted, perfectly away,
whispering plans for something sweet today.
A moment, a glance, then a kiss they go to steal,
while pretending they're just setting out the meal.

topic: a dog leash tangled in railings
lines: You shout your dog's name as the wind cuts its bark,
The sky turns to gray, the street lights grow dark.
You twist through the bars, but there's not one clue,
The leash wraps you tighter, and you're stuck right here too.
You watch the snowflakes like fleeting art,
each crystal a wonder that melts at your start.
They leave no small pattern, just silent erase,
but you smile through the cold on your own proud face.
The backpack strap gave out with a loud snap,
but you laughed as you dropped your phone on the map.
Said there's no need for a perfect or quick fix—
you turned failure into confidence tricks.
I grip the knife with a white-knuckled blade,
the carrots march in a solemn little parade.
They wobble and sway as I slice through the fray,
it's less cooking prep and more dramatic play.
Another envelope shows up marked "due,"
you stare at it until your mood turns blue.
You check your account—no surprise, no cash,
you mutter about this rotten old ash.
You watched her unfold in slow, feline grace,
muscles rippling across every space.
Her body a question, her tail gives the pose,
claiming your pillow, oh, those ancient toes.
The machine won't read my bagel or scan,
I wave down an employee, not a man.
They swipe it, I pay, but the total still paid
me no receipt, just a glitched-out parade.

topic: a party hat on a dog
lines: My dog refuses to wear the party try,
He barks at the confetti tossed up high.
I put the hat on, then he starts to spin,
Chaos fills the room with his yappy din.
She swore she'd never pay more than she had paid,
but the prices bloomed like some sad little parade.

and tossed her cup right back into her hand.
She spent all night stressing about every thought,
her coffee went cold as her ideas got caught.

the final draft's gone, and now so am I.
You tap your card and the screen says it's wrong,
the silence grows into a sad song.
The driver asks if you need to go far,
but you're just heading home to an empty star.

topic: seeing your mom's new profile pic
lines: She changed her photo—her gray hair's still there,
but she's smiling bold on some sunlit stair.
Her eyes have a spark, a fresh, bright look,
I didn't believe it till I saw the proof took.
It stood like a snake but now feels too tight,
the rubber popped loud like a sudden bite.
I once thought it magical, never would lie,
now it's a twisted scrap trapped up high.
The chimes sway gently in this evening breeze,
Their rhythm moves me—it's enough to please.
Your voice hums low, a lullaby song,
The breeze still dances where the sound was strong.
She left a snack near her desk, what a mess!
Now every key sticks when she goes to press.
She's cleaned it twice but still hasn't tried
the right way to fix it from the online guide.
The cat knocked the soup right out of its bowl,
then sauntered around like it just took a stroll.
You sighed at the scene, a whole kitchen mess,
but caved and gave in—oh, how cats can be bless.
You wear your keyboard's sticky keys with pride,
you tap them like a warrior on a stride.
Crumbs have formed a map of dust and mold,
but you type it out, still sounding bold.
Your phone drops to 3% just as you need a call,
it's too late to sprint to the nearest mall.
You've tried every hack in your desperate fix,
but your device isn't impressed by your tricks.

topic: someone spilling punch on the rug
lines: You watched the punch spread out like a red rose,
but then you grabbed the bucket, the sponge, the hose.
The rug is still wet, but we made it look new—
and maybe this mess just reminded us of you.
She arrived early to get through the gate,
but found herself stuck in the slowest wait.
She kicks off her heels and starts rocking her shoes,
while humming a tune to keep calm from the news.
She sped through the crosswalk when the light was green,
I saw the whole thing in the rearview scene.
She didn't check her mirror, didn't hit the brake,
but I let it go—it's not my first mistake.
My dog barks at the air without a care,
Maybe there's something out there—only fair.
He sees ghosts or shapes I'll never see,
Sometimes I wish I could bark like he.
You asked if I had room for you and me,
we ducked under the umbrella like a tree.
The rain came down in sheets, no mind the weather,
two strangers laughing, feeling kind of together.
I stumbled outside just as the door
swung shut behind me, heart still full of sore.
My shoes were scuffed and my hair looked too late,
but you stood aside without making me wait.
I duck behind the rosebush, heart thumping loud,
the wind says hush but the cat still walks proud.
I hold my breath and listen for your feet,
while the sun drips down like slow-moving heat.
You reached for the honey without thinking of jar,
now it clings to the spoon like a child to a bar.
You wait for it to drip but it won't quite run,
and your neat breakfast plan feels slightly undone.
You've been waiting for steam to rise from your wait,
but the tea sits cold on your dinner plate.
The kettle hums low, it refuses to grow,
you really should buy a new one, you know.
You chased the storm to get your fill of dirt,
came home soaked and muddy, no dry shirt.
It was the last burst of joy this old spring,
and now it's gone, but you'll remember that thing.
I bought it for fun but I never wore
it now sits unworn on my closet's floor.
It wasn't the style, or the fit, just the thing—
I miss how I felt when I ordered it in spring.
You drape gold across the windows to shine,
each leaf etched in light like a sketch in the line.
It takes all your effort to hold up this craft,
but I see every beam in the still, soft draft.
She asks me to grab a coffee on my way out,
but I take a long detour down a scenic route.
I bring back a $12 drink they call a brew,
she smiles at the price when she looks at the view.
The teacher's cough echoes down every row,
her voice lost in a hacking marathon show.
The clock ticks till the bell will set me free,
she clears her throat — I fake a sneeze and flee.
She walks in place but the screen won't show her pace,
it's stuck on "0.0" with no shame or grace.
She tries to reset it, but the numbers won't read,
now she's pacing in rage, trying not to bleed.
I used to swipe cards without thinking about spend,
but now I fix things before they need mend.
My savings grow steady, a quiet kind of gain,
and I feel like I'm walking in my own good rain.
She didn't skip a single grocery trip,
left exact change — no discount, no tip.
Her budget's tight but her ethics in mind,
she's careful with money, a thrifty kind.
I saw the screen flash out of sheer shock,
my wallet was light and the minutes were clock.
My savings felt drier than a desert tank,
but I laughed and said, "Let's find joy, not the bank."
You see the bird still trying to be free,
It slams into windows again and again, fee.
Its wings beat the air in a frantic flight,
You hold your breath as the world feels tight.
She folds the paper with too much fear,
afraid her love won't be crystal clear.
A red string runs through the middle of thread,
she knots it tight and prays in her head.

topic: seeing your mom's new profile pic
lines: She changed her profile but looks much the same,
still smiles like the girl from her old nickname game.

lines: She rolls in the puddles, laughing with dirt,
her clothes soaked through, the front of her shirt.

forgetting whatever she had for her plans.

that even when it's too dark for the table,

lines: The wind nips through my coat like frozen frost,
the cup's too flimsy and it barely holds the cost.

the plastic slips from my hands—no grip.

a wobbly glide without a single blow.

pulling out relics from some distant year.

their heads—she says she's just waiting to take.
You untangle wires with a careful twist,
your fingers brush my skin — my inner wrist.

but I'm afraid the moment might decay.

the last time I wore them, I stumbled and fell.

maybe it's time they're left far behind, so old.
She waits for the breeze to carry them blow,
each fluff a new life yet to grow.
They twirl in the sky on an upward air,
she watches with pride, not a single one spare.
The sky begins to blush with morning light,
Even the frost seems tinged with golden bright.
Shadows shrink and melt and fade away,

lines: He still calls them by the old names,

her face lights the dusk like a quiet goodbye.

she stood there beaming, a prideful stage.

but she laughed off the moment, sly and nice.

the lawn mower coughs like it's covered in smoke.

you circle the yard—do I have to explain?

but the dog just wanted more face-to-face space.
It leaned in close for a long, proud lick,

You type "lol" after midnight and hit send,
it goes to your boss or an old high school friend.

now you wait for a reply that drags on for long.

started to drag and you lost your race.

just ran with the pain and refused to slip.
You swear the dog was barking at the post,
but I'm more sure he wanted my lunch toast.

now we're both laughing—what else could we do?
You rummage through the junk pile, the old bin,
remembering how the music would spin.

and suddenly the past starts to sound.
He yells that the bin won't stay where it can't,
accusing her of moving his garbage plant.
His voice rises louder than the morning crowd,
now the whole street watches him act so proud.
My dog tracked in the whole damn front yard,
the mailman gave me a look like a guard.

while he napped in the sun, a dirty slug.
I found a sticky clue beneath my chair,
a wad of blue that someone left to spare.
I check for fingerprints but missed the spot,
now I'm chewing air and feeling a bit hot.
The taxi's front lights won't turn on or run,
but the driver just shrugs and says it's all done.
We zoom through the dark, chatting on the ride,
and laugh when we nearly slide into a side.
I hoped for silence instead of this ride,
but he chats like I'm here to hide.
He points out landmarks on every street,
and somehow it all starts to repeat.
She drops another quarter, one more try,
the machine just hums and stays as dry.
It's been this way since last Friday, same old week,
she talks to the screen like it might start to speak.
Your screen glows faint, the last drop so near,
it's been through storms, texts, calls, promises, cheer.

instead, you take photos of coffee and mug.
The credits roll and my eyes still feel dry,

She looks down once more at her buzzing phone,
the car slows down as she drives along alone.
By the time she glances up, the light turns shift,
but maybe this pause could feel like a gift.
You swore you'd eat only veggies and green,
but hunger got loud and your will got mean.

and abandoned your goals for the next week back.
My phone rings out with one last final call,
but the screen's just blank, like no one's at the mall.
I tap it twice and fake a little miss,
then laugh when it goes silent once again—my bliss.

Each late-night meme posted deep into the thread.
Your friends don't reply, so you keep the chat alive,
While whispering "just one more" to your scroll-fat hive.
This tourist trap sells nostalgia with a lie,
everything here will fade and die.

but the clerk just laughed and called it trash.
You twist and push but nothing seems to try,
your hands are shaking, stressed and going dry.
The outlet glares, the plug won't make it fit,
you almost scream, "This nonsense just won't quit."
He watches the strips curl and release some hot fat,
the pan turns a darker shade all around the flat.
The air starts to thicken with greasy white smoke,
he swore he'd get new pans but this one still broke.
My laugh was loud though no one heard the joke,
I'm pretty sure my face might have broke.
I sat there sweating on the inside edge,
like a smile forced into a tight wedge.
You say there are strict guidelines and rules,
but I think you're the one who plays the fools.
I don't want to fight about what to pick,
just let me have my five songs and stick.
I can't even catch the writers' names,
it's just another blur of faces and games.
My eyes can't keep up to fully read,
so they scroll and fade from my movie-head.

topic: ice forming on the car windshield
lines: You call the frost patterns a frozen work of art,
while I'm scraping to get your car to start.

the silence stretched long and it didn't seem mean.

the theater was packed but it wasn't hell.
She walks in barefoot, still chewing her treat,
the trail's a familiar mess she won't repeat.

she shuts the kitchen tight, like it was a war.

the only checkmark next to "clean my toy."
The rest still wait like chores unpaid,
I mock myself for thinking tasks would parade.

lines: She pushes the cart but it slows down and stops,

the wheel won't budge—some things just can't be mend.
I haven't cried since the day we started to start.

my eyes decide they don't need my will.
You reach inside and feel a single clump,
it's been ignored for months, maybe a bump.

you break the family's food storage law.

topic: losing your wallet at the mall
lines: You left your wallet near some store's long aisle,
Then bought a hat you swore looked bad in style.

I watch the ferry vanish into the sky,
the dock creaks softly, says its goodbye.

but there's no ticket, no moment to restore.

the sun's been this way for the last ten long.

you curse like it's some sort of flickering flame.

but memories cloud the past like these days.

the minty paste has lost its fresh taste.

She lets them go like wishes in flight,
each tiny puff catching morning's light.

she opens hers—ready to stand.

my sink now gleams like it was polished tight.

lost somewhere near the drain trap and the tap.

but I've passed three signs where the road went dead.

my calm left minutes ago—it just flew.
You wipe your hands but still leave a spot,
the sweat soaked through, it's no fun being hot.
I kick the old mat, it groans like a cat,
just let me nap instead of small talk or chat.
They never seem to notice the plant's sad sigh,
it's stuck in the corner where no one will eye.
They swear they remember to water it all,
but neglect has turned the leaves pale as the wall.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: I won't look at my phone until I'm in bed,

a silent, endless, soulless upward race.
You finished your homework in record pride,
even used YouTube as a quick guide.
The clock strikes midnight—yes, you're still late,
but perfection is worth the debate.

but it's just steam going up all around.

you yell "I'm coming!" out loud.
The needles move fast, but the rhythm feels soft,
my thoughts drift aloft where the sky meets the loft.
I tuck in each stitch, then I smooth out the fold,
the room stays so cold, but my hands stay bold.
You stare at the calendar, it's all late due,
your screen glows with emails in a bleak blue.
You tried to reschedule, but now there's a wave
of fees rising fast in a financial grave.
It's chaos since that bunny claimed its shoe-zone,
I moan every time it crunches a toe-moan.
I tried to flip it out with a sneaker-flip,
now lint and leather lie in a chewed-up slip.
Your favorite song was just about to play,
then the screen blinked out for no delay.
You tap the power button, hoping for some light,
and laugh because the stars sure feel so bright.
She says it's not broken—just doing its fix,
the water she calls little time-saving tricks.
It still makes a mess with its steady drip,
but she's got a good grip on pretending it's hip.
I left my list as a sticky note,
now I'm at the store with my tote.
I buy cereal and a bag of beans,
then forget why I came till I check my screens.
She pays with small coins but she still has enough cash,
the barista laughs and says "No need to smash."
Her pockets are full of a jingling grin,
she keeps spare coins in her lunch thermos tin.
You click "unsubscribe" but it asks you to log
in three times, each link worse than the dog.
The payment is still marked as pending, due,
stuck in a loop like words in dry glue.
I gently peel the corner off the tear,
it's old but still holds up from last year.
I let the poster slowly start to swing,
it's holding onto the frame like some weird thing.

topic: a gym membership you never use
lines: You still smile when you pass the sign you once paid,
those mirrors shining like a fitness parade.
You wish there was time to feel that heart flash,
but the gym card's just tucked away with the ash.
Her phone buzzed out *butterfly*, but she said my jaw,
the way my eyes caught hers broke every law.

I felt the world bloom green again this spring.
You see a new message — it lights up your spark,
A burst of emotion in a quiet park.

The conversation lifts without an end.

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: Beads form under the brim of their light,
skin glistens where shirts leave it white.

you want to catch it, but it's gone below.
The dog saw the cake, and the alarm went off,
I tried to distract him with a loud cough.
He lunged through the room with frosting still on bark,
now everyone stares, and I can't erase that mark.

it's been hours since my thoughts left their nest.
My hands follow the rhythm of the thread,
while silence grows from something into dread.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: The little kid started to run and then cried,
the crowd turned around trying to hide.
The wind took his balloon up high to float,
I snatched it back and gave him a new note.
She checks her cart—it's about full,
Her reusable bags feel threadbare and pull.
"I'll get groceries later," she says, "I don't need
What I used to call plastic-free living to feed."
She wipes her eyes when the moment goes down,
Her friends cheer loud from a crowded downtown.

Then swipes the tears with her sleeve held aside.
I miss the soft chime of your ringtone's old bell,
I told myself no calls would ever make me well.
I check my screen still, just in case you might hold,
but silence stays loyal, like the story we told.
I weave through the traffic on this narrow block,
the red light ticks forward inside my clock.
I tip the handle just enough to zoom,
and leave them staring in their cubicle room.
She slept through noon but still forgot her dream,
her alarm played Adele's saddest theme.
Her coffee couldn't wake her sleepy brain,
she tripped on socks in a puddle of rain.
The toast is black now, filled with bitter smoke,
I blink awake, my head still half-awoke.
Mom used to laugh when I burned it real old,
She'd say "It's still edible, just a bit bold."
She squints at the menu like it's some deep clue,
reads the sauce names slow, like they're made of dew.
"This pasta," she says, "is pure modern art,"
then mispronounces it and forgets the chart.
He wears it tilted to hide every bump,
the sides are dented like a tree's old stump.
They call it safety, he calls it his style,
the whole crew jokes about it for a while.
Your grocery cart feels almost ready to full,
but you pause since there's no bag left to pull.
You'll walk back home instead of heading to shop,
and see the breeze as a reason to stop.
I found a loaf in the back of the bin,
its crust blooming blue from the damp within.
This fungus is proof that I'm growing a crown,
not rotting like trash left to crumble and down.
My GPS tried to take me where it lead,
through alleys and roads that just went dead.
I ignored every voice that said "new course,"
and landed there first by sheer force.
I wiped the keyboard clean, but left the dust,
now "E" is jammed with yesterday's crust.
My fingers glide where letters used to miss,
I type in silence, missing typewriter hiss.
She laughs too long, she leans right in,
her smile is bright but burning like a din.
They all talk over her, they speak so loud,
she leaves just when she isn't proud.

topic: using a coupon for a snack
lines: She spots the coupon and she makes a grab,
"This snack's on sale!" — she cheers like a crab.
Her cart is full now, all thanks to the save,
She skips out the store, a true savings cave.
You kick your shoes in with a sigh or two,
their soles worn thin from everything you do.
You tie them up when you still had some lace,
now they wait here, in their usual place.
She claims this spot before the sun finds her pose,
beats every early bird with those bare toes.
The waves retreat, she owns this lonely strand,
her towel is spread like a flag in her hand.

topic: seeing a price tag too high
lines: Your eyes hit the price tag and register shock,
while time ticks on like a slow-moving clock.
You whisper, "This was never my true fate,"
then walk out, still carrying the item's weight.
She walked right into the party's fake scene,
balloons popped like a camera's flash machine.
Her confused face said she had no clue,
but we all laughed like we'd really knew.
I let my breath fall out in a tired air,
my smile's frayed from trying too hard to wear
the mask they want while my whole body's bones
are singing low in soft, exhausted tones.
She says the GPS changed our driving route,
That's fine by me — I think this new one's cute.
We've been going this way, she admits we're lost,
but insists it will save us time and cost.
It was supposed to last way past this noon,
but now your party's ruined and out of tune.
You feel the sting of that sad, escaping air,
and fume in silence without a trace of flair.
I wait for the kettle to start to sing,
it whistles like something not quite a thing.
I pour the hot water fast into my brew,
but now my new socks are half a stew.
She walks alone through the crowded mall,
her voice bouncing off the shopfront wall.
Her story unfurls in loud, long hours,
while strangers fade like wilting flowers.
The teacher dropped the test like it was a fail,
your name still on it like an old, faint trail.
You trace the red marks made in quick, dry ink,
wondering if this is the edge or the brink.
She sips her coffee, the kettle still hums low,
some ghost of midnight habit she can't let go.
She pours the second cup, then stops for a pour,
her hands need the motion, the warmth, the one more.
You remember the taste of jelly and bread,
how we made a whole mess out of every spread.
Now your fingers feel like they're stuck to the glue,
but I'd rather be messy and here with you.
She watches the drops as they drum out their thought,
each one marking a thing she had long since bought.
They pool near her shoes but don't leave a stain,
like memories fading and running again.

topic: a lost child holding a balloon
lines: He wobbled through the crowd like it was his own street,
managing to stay calm was a true little feat.
His balloon barely float, but he held it tight,
while strangers stared and tucked their coats just right.
I pretend not to notice when you try to say,
"Let me get this," while pushing your cash away.
We split the cost but you take the whole tip,
then flash that grin that loosens my grip.
I meant to hit cancel, not send,
now my draft's in my boss's friend.
The email's stuck in a weird lag,
my heart sinks faster than a hot-air bag.
She watches the bird struggle against the wind,
mistaking the window for an open blind.
Her hand makes a soft shadow on her chest,
as if the whole world were this small, this pressed.
I walked through sprinkles left from the treat,
sticky and smiling, my bare little feet.
I danced along crumbs that scattered across the floor,
dreaming we'd take a trip back there next store.
She slung the bag uneven since it wore,
the seam had split from how much it tore.
Her shoulders tipped left with each step they sway,
but she walked tall through the whole long day.
She takes a screenshot but won't send the note,
her thumb hovers over her mobile's small throat.
Minutes pass, conversation feels a bit late,
and you wonder if you should just start to wait.
The carton shows a past expiry date,
but they all do and still we can't just wait.
He leaves the lid off, forgets about the cap,
and watches the smell rise from the milk's small gap.
She sends her "goodnight" an hour after it's sent,
the clock says midnight but her phone won't relent.
She's still awake in the glow of the night,
pretending she's sleeping when the screen turns bright.
She speeds through the checkout like it's her last race,
then freezes when she sees her empty place.
"I had more bags here only minutes ago,"
she stares at the cart, now bare as a snow.
You dart across the floor, determined to see,
the shadow moves fast, there's nothing to flee.
You spin in the room, all fur and bright eyes,
your hunt hits a wall, you leap—then no prize.
You vow this time it won't be your blame,
but butter runs hot and it hits the front flame.
The kernels all leap out in one sad spill,
you've bought cinema shame, not popcorn thrill.
You check the carton's old use-by date,
now curdled, it won't pour on your plate.
The kitchen still holds that sour smell,
and memories don't always cast a happy spell.
You lost a sock by the gym's worn-out lace,
it's been missing since you left your usual place.
Now it smells like it's grown a whole new kind of mold,
and your feet won't stop giving you the cold.
You pause before the glass because you see
your own nostalgia in someone else's key.
You smile, but can't quite justify the way
your wallet would scream if you bought it today.
She walks the path where the morning is slow,
the sun rises gently but far off and low.
Her boots press softly along the leaf trail,
a whisper of autumn she won't try to fail.
The vendor yells so loud it bops your head,
"Warm buns! Fresh rolls! The best damn bread!"
He swears it's cheaper than a grocery store deal,
his voice like a megaphone made of steel.
The check was late but finally got sent,
I counted twice, then screamed when I spent.
"It's low," the machine glowed in red cash,
I cursed the form I filled out in a rash.
I asked for the fastest way to my route,
now my phone's laughing as I drive around out.
The GPS says "Recalculating—maze,"
I've heard this joke from my phone for five days.
You swing the spatula like it's made of air,
pretending you've got some real cooking flair.
You aim to flip but instead you just slip,
the pancake flies—now it's buttered on tip.
Your gaze falls back to the glowing screen,
it hums like a machine you can't quite clean.
Your fingers lag, too slow for the pace,
yet you blink and keep losing the race.
I sent the lazy "u up?" as if it were shot,
they probably slept and I woke them, I forgot.
This isn't what late-night texts are meant for, worth,
respect should be more than a ping to the earth.
She folded it perfect, the kind that took
off like a dream with a graceful look.
It soared past desks, defying how it flew,
until it landed front-and-center view.
You used to brew your own dark roast beans,
the morning couldn't get any more greens.
Now you microwave the weak store-bought roast,
but it tastes like something from your past's ghost.
I watch the yolk settle in the white,
golden and trembling in morning light.
This fragile shell that never will break
holds more of life than I would take.
You post a joke to escape your dull task,
the boss replies with a polite "did I ask?"
Your phone buzzes twice while you're stuck in the grind,
you smile but stay trapped, just a click behind.
I told myself I wouldn't nap after the meal,
but my eyelids made a break-even deal.
Quiet hits the couch like a long overdue sleep,
while the clock counts down how fast it can creep.
Her breath curls upward in the pale pink glow,
the quiet world dressed in fresh-fallen snow.
She sits on the dock to quietly wake,
as sunlight spills across the frozen lake.
Your stomach has been making noise all day, it grow,
The fridge is empty, so you have to go.
You pick out apples and bread for a quick bite,
A smile returns with the promise of light.
He's halfway through his third double shift,
eyes flutter closed, his chin starts to drift.
The bus rolls steady on its sleep-dead wheel,
I memorize his face, I might not see him real.
He picks his spot with a careful little plot,
as if every inch matters since he first got
the hang of the art—now he digs every hole
with pride like it feeds him more than his own soul.
His nose is all pink with a crisp summer glow,
he shows it off like a trophy or so.
He won't wear sunscreen or ever take shade,
he stakes his cool points in UV parade.
You chase the feathers lost to the wind,
their twirls and loops keep you far behind.
They dip through branches where the dead leaves float,
as if a ghostly raft is pulling the boat.
He parks his bulk in an old lawn chair,
where he'd swear he's not here to live or to repair.
The kids kick up clouds of dry dust,
but he still eats their cookies—warm from the crust.
She steps into her dinghy to float,
the waves rock gently beneath her boat.
The moon turns the water to silver glow,
she looks down but sees nothing below.

topic: old rubber band on a stapler
lines: That old rubber band still won't snap,
it holds your papers where they should map.
You give the stapler a little bend,
and laugh—it's a charm you don't often mend.
The screen went dark and the lights turned blue,
I should've known the machine wasn't new.
My train's leaving soon if I pay the fare,
but I'm stuck here breathing this stale old air.
You sit alone but you don't want to think,
sipping a coffee you barely let drink.
A storm outside, but your lamp stays bright,
and soon it will pass, you'll be looking out right.
He meant to pour oats but it came out as shake,
He sipped it and grinned at the morning mistake.
A cloud on his floor where the powder is white,
It never did settle, just danced in the light.
I missed roll call and stayed off the class,
I was too deep in the yard's hidden grass.
She searched the halls but didn't find my spot,
while I read in peace, this small scheme my plot.
You bolt upright from the couch into a rush,
your face turns pink from the sudden flush.
You grab the wall to avoid hitting the floor,
but nothing's steadier than moments before.
